records_other.title: EU sanctions listing of M23 and RDF figures, a Rwandan mining official and a Kigali gold refinery (European Union, 17 March 2025)
records_other.perpetrator_as_alleged: M23 and RDF figures, the RMB chief executive and Gasabo Gold Refinery, as named in the EU listing

records_other.title: Residents flee the Buliriko quarter after a military camp attributed to AFC/M23 is set up (Kavumu, Kabare, about 2 August 2026)
records_other.perpetrator_as_alleged: AFC/M23 (camp attributed to its fighters), per Enquete.cd

claims.text: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) reported, as an example, that from 12 to 15 January in several localities of Rutshuru territory, North Kivu, at least 10 children, nine women and eight men suspected of collaborating with Wazalendo groups were killed by AFC/M23 combatants.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verified in the retained PDF (section on non-State armed groups, 'A titre d'exemple'). UN body's documented monitoring: grade A. Researcher's note arithmetic ('17 plus 10 = 27') is muddled; the categories sum to 27 but no total is printed, so none is stated. The report gives the example by category only (10 children, nine women, eight men); it prints no total and does not name the localities.
claims.researcher_note: Publication date of the monthly report not printed in the extracted text; 2026-01-31 is the date shown in the search listing and the file sits under a 2026-04 upload path. Localities not named in the excerpt. 17 plus 10 = 27 victims by the sum of the categories printed (10+9+8); the report does not print a total in the excerpt.

claims.text: BCNUDH reported that on 2 January 2026 the FARDC used armed drones in Masisi territory, North Kivu, against AFC/M23 positions, and that several strikes hit densely populated areas in Masisi-centre, injuring 42 people and killing seven others, including two women, a girl and a boy, and destroying houses.
claims.verification_note: Verified in the retained PDF; 'sept' is spelled out (flag on '7' is a format false positive). UN body documentation: grade A. BCNUDH lists this under 'Dommages collatéraux résultant de l'utilisation de drones'.
claims.researcher_note: Described by BCNUDH as 'dommages collatéraux' (collateral damage) of drone use. No FARDC or government statement on this strike was found in these searches.

claims.text: UN News, citing a MONUSCO press release, reported that a French UNICEF employee was killed on Wednesday 11 March 2026 in a drone attack on a building housing humanitarian workers in Goma, and that the attack also killed two civilians and damaged civilian homes.
claims.place_as_written: Goma (Himbi quarter per UN Group of Experts), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by UN News (attribution contested)
claims.verification_note: Verified on the page. The researcher's note that the victim is unnamed is wrong; the page names her (see note). Both sources are the same page and origin (MONUSCO via UN News): grade B, not A. The same UN News page names the victim as Karine Buisset (UNICEF statement: 'notre collègue Karine Buisset'); the stored excerpts do not, so the name is not yet on this claim (lead: add_excerpt). UN News does not attribute the strike. MONUSCO's acting head Bruno Lemarquis said attacks on UN personnel 'pourraient constituer des crimes de guerre' and called for an independent inquiry.
claims.researcher_note: Goma is described by UN News as under M23 control for over a year. Perpetrator not stated by UN News; see the separate claim on the Group of Experts. Victim not named in this source.

claims.text: Beto.cd, in an article credited to AFP summarising the UN Group of Experts report S/2026/466, reported that the experts reconstructed the strike that killed UNICEF worker Karine Buisset in Goma on 11 March as an aerial fragmentation munition fired by a drone coming from Lake Kivu, and that attribution remains contested.
claims.verification_note: Byline 'AFP La Rédaction': credited to AFP. Single wire relay of a UN report not opened: B. Party accounts on the same AFP page (not in the stored excerpt; lead for add_excerpt): 'L’AFC/M23 a accusé l’armée congolaise d’avoir lancé les drones ; Kinshasa a présenté ses condoléances et ouvert une enquête sans désigner de coupable, tout en pointant une « agression technologique » rwandaise.' The page places the strike in the Himbi quarter around 4 a.m. The Group of Experts report itself was not opened. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: article credited to AFP 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-009: Checked the AFP summary against the retained GoE report: its annex supports it ('high-explosive fragmentation', platform 'approaching from over Lake Kivu', per witness accounts and damage analysis) and the Group names no perpetrator. Amended only to show the relay: the page is Beto.cd's, credited to AFP.; excerpt-support: added the headline and byline ('AFP La Rédaction', 2 July 2026) as an excerpt for the AFP credit
claims.researcher_note: Page carries an AFP credit; cited as relayed by Beto.cd. The report S/2026/466 itself was not opened. Earlier lead (not cited): Goma strikes were reported by local social media as attributed to the FARDC; no party statement on responsibility was fetched.

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported that AFC/M23 military spokesperson Willy Ngoma was killed on Tuesday in a drone strike attributed to the FARDC near Rubaya, Masisi territory, according to concordant sources and movement officials.
claims.verification_note: Verified on the page (byline David Lupemba, no wire credit). Flag on '7' comes from the outlet name 7sur7. Single local outlet: grade C (lowered from B). Who attributes the strike to the FARDC is not specified by the outlet. Tuesday = 24 February 2026 from the article date.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and the page's dateline (Tuesday 24 February 2026). A search listing (Africanews) reported at least nine dead in the same strike; that page was not opened, so no figure is given. Ngoma is a combatant; recorded as a military event, not as a civilian atrocity.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported on Monday 25 May that aerial strikes attributed to military drones, whose origin remained undetermined and which no party had claimed, hit Rubaya (Masisi) and Rumangabo (Rutshuru) the day before; a strike on Sunday around 07:30 hit a training centre for the women and widows of ICCN rangers in the Virunga National Park compound at Rumangabo, with no loss of life confirmed, and an earlier strike around 00:15 targeted a guest house in Rubaya.
claims.actor_as_written: unidentified; not claimed by any party (source)
claims.verification_note: All clauses verified on the retained page. Radio Okapi (UN-run) as a single credible non-partisan origin: B. No official human toll at the time of the report; the Rubaya guest house reportedly housed several people ('hébergerait').
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date (Monday 25 May 2026; strikes 'au lendemain'). The AFC/M23 accused the FARDC of the strikes (Kivu Morning Post headline of 24 May 2026, in search results, page not opened); no FARDC statement found. No official toll at the time of the report.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the villages of Ihula, Katobo and Mukohwa in Kisimba groupement, Walikale territory, were retaken by AFC/M23 rebels on Tuesday 26 May after intense fighting against the FARDC and allied Wazalendo; according to its sources, the rebels used drones to bomb loyalist positions.
claims.place_as_written: Ihula, Katobo, Mukohwa (Kisimba groupement), Walikale territory
claims.verification_note: The retake is the outlet's own narration; only the drone use is attributed to its sources. Attribution re-ordered accordingly. Same page: loyalist forces held Ngambi and Buhimba; households fled towards Kalinga and Mpombi.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet citing unnamed sources; no AFC/M23 or FARDC statement found. Source says the clashes caused mass displacement towards Kalinga and Mpombi.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing several local sources, that fighting between Wazalendo armed groups and AFC/M23 rebels was reported on Wednesday 10 June in Masisi territory, notably at Kishanja and Kasenyi, with heavy and light weapons heard.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23; Wazalendo (Maï-Maï Lamuka coalition and Groupe Armé des Volontaires per local sources)
claims.verification_note: Verified on the retained page. Single report citing unnamed local sources: C. Same page: local sources say Maï-Maï Lamuka and GAV elements responded to an AFC/M23 attack from 5 a.m. at Kashovu (Ufamandu groupement); fighting also on Tuesday at Kazinga (Nyamaboko groupement). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 10 Jun 2026, carries every clause; the stored excerpt lacks the date and the heavy and light weapons, added here.
claims.researcher_note: Frontline context only. The same page reports local civil society saying the escalation caused population displacement.

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported that the FARDC announced in a communiqué that 10 civilians were summarily killed by the M23 in the locality of Kiseguru, near Virunga National Park, Bwito chiefdom, North Kivu, on Tuesday 02 June 2026, and that the FARDC condemned this as a new violation of international humanitarian law; the same communiqué said several other citizens were arrested and transferred to Kanyangambi central prison in Rutshuru on the pretext that they were FDLR.
claims.place_as_written: Kiseguru, Bwito chiefdom, near Virunga National Park, Rutshuru territory
claims.actor_as_written: M23 (as alleged by the FARDC communiqué)
claims.verification_note: Verified on the page (byline Alphonse Muderwa). Partisan communiqué relayed by one outlet: C. Flag '7' is from the outlet name. Party allegation (FARDC); the legal characterisation is the FARDC's own. 'Rutshuru' for Kiseguru rests on the prison clause and Bwito chiefdom (which is in Rutshuru territory); the page does not print 'Rutshuru' beside Kiseguru. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: FARDC condemnation as quoted 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-010: Legal label must sit inside an attributed quote: the page prints 'condamnent cette nouvelle violation du droit international humanitaire' in the sentence that continues source 0 (add_excerpt needed). Fresh search found only relays of the same FARDC communiqué (MediaCongo, Enquete.cd), no independent account and no M23 response. Place lead: other reporting places Kiseguru in Binza groupement (Bwisha chiefdom, near Nyamilima), not Bwito; keep 'Bwito' as printed and flag it.; excerpt-support: added the communiqué sentence with 'condamnent cette nouvelle violation du droit international humanitaire' as an excerpt 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: 7sur7.cd, 4 Jun 2026 (Alphonse Muderwa). The phrase 'cette nouvelle violation du droit international humanitaire' is the outlet's paraphrase of the FARDC condemnation, not a quotation from the communiqué, so it should not be presented as 'what it called'. Otherwise all clauses are on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Single account relaying a party communiqué (FARDC); victims not named; the communiqué itself was not found. An AFC/M23 response to this allegation was searched for and not found (see gaps). Arrests are as described in the same communiqué (an allegation against M23).

claims.text: The Kivu Morning Post reported that at least 54 people were killed in attacks by ADF-MTM since January 2026 in the Baswagha chiefdom and the Bapere sector of Lubero territory, according to a provisional toll compiled on Thursday by the Comité local de protection communautaire (CLPC), whose president Vianney Kitsamba cited 33 deaths in Baswagha and 21 civilians in the Bapere sector.
claims.place_as_written: Baswagha chiefdom and Bapere sector, Lubero territory
claims.verification_note: Verified on the page. Local civil-society tally via one local outlet: C. Kept separate from the North Kivu civil society coordination tally (52 in Lubero as of 3 February, Radio Okapi): different compiler, area and cut-off; not merged. 'Terroristes' is the outlet's wording.
claims.researcher_note: Local civil-society tally, provisional. Differs from the North Kivu provincial civil society coordination tally reported by Radio Okapi on 6 February (62 in Beni and Lubero, of which 52 in Lubero, as of a statement of 3 February): different compilers and cut-off dates; figures are not merged. The Thursday is 22 January per the page date.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that in a statement published on Tuesday 3 February 2026, the provincial coordination of North Kivu civil society said at least 62 civilians had been killed since the start of the year by suspected ADF rebels in Beni and Lubero territories, 52 of them in Lubero and 10 in Beni.
claims.verification_note: Verified on the page. Civil-society tally: C. Differs from the CLPC figure of 54 (Baswagha and Bapere only, 22 January); the two tallies are kept separate.
claims.researcher_note: Civil-society tally; see the Kivu Morning Post claim for the differing 22 January figure. Same page lists one health post burned (see separate claim).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the North Kivu civil society tally of violence by suspected ADF rebels in Beni and Lubero since January 2026 included one health post burned, 67 shops and 10 houses burned, 23 motorcycles burned and the destruction of a local chief's 'barza' meeting place.
claims.place_as_written: Beni and Lubero territories (health post not located by the source)
claims.verification_note: Verified on the page; 'un poste de santé' carries 'one' (flag is a format false positive). The health post is not named or located. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: suspected ADF rebels 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-008: The statement calls it a tally 'of ADF violence', firmer than the source's 'rebelles presumes des ADF' in the same article; restored 'suspected'. Health post still unlocated.; excerpt-support: added the article's opening sentence ('rebelles présumés des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF)') as an excerpt 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Excerpt reproduces the page's typo ('Le ban fait état de d'un'). The health post is not named or located by the source.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing health sources, that the health centres of Mausa, Pombi, Mandelya and Musenge and the reference health centre (CSR) of Masoy had ceased activities in the Mwenye groupement of Lubero territory, along with several health posts, following persistent insecurity marked by killings of civilians attributed to suspected ADF rebels; the reference health centre of Masoya, chief town of the groupement, had closed about a week earlier.
claims.actor_as_written: ADF (suspected; killings of civilians cited as the cause of insecurity)
claims.verification_note: Statement used 'Masoya' where the cited passage prints 'Masoy'; aligned to each passage and added the 'several health posts' and the one-week closure the page states. The page spells the reference centre both 'Masoy' and 'Masoya'. Closures are attributed to insecurity, not to a direct attack on the facilities. A civil society leader on the same page also cites pressure on the Biambwe health centre (armed group members and their wives treated without paying).
claims.researcher_note: Closures attributed to insecurity, not a direct attack on the facilities. The same page quotes a civil society president saying pressure on the Biambwe health centre pushed nurses to close; that passage is not relied on here. Spelling 'Masoy'/'Masoya' as printed on the page.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, according to local sources, an ADF incursion in the night of 21 to 22 July 2026 in the Bapere sector of Lubero territory cost the lives of at least seven civilians and several homes were burned, forcing many households to flee.
claims.verification_note: Verified on the page; 'sept' spelled out (flag false positive). Village of the attack not named; the alert concerns villages of Bapakombe groupement (Mambau, Maakele, Makumo, Souma).
claims.researcher_note: Zone named by the article title as the Bapere sector. A search listing (Instagram, not opened) mentions at least seven civilians killed on Thursday 23 July at Kazaroho; not cited.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that five civilians were killed and about ten houses burned in a new attack attributed to ADF combatants in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 21 January at the village of Mavwe-Mavwe, in the Mandelya locality, and that four women were among the victims.
claims.place_as_written: Mavwe-Mavwe, Mandelya locality, Mwenye groupement, Lubero territory
claims.verification_note: Verified on the page; figures spelled out (flag false positive). 21 January 2026 was a Wednesday, so the 20-21 range is consistent.
claims.researcher_note: Date given as 'Tuesday to Wednesday 21 January'; recorded as the range 20-21 January. Reported in passing in an article about health centre closures.

claims.text: MediaCongo, carrying a report credited 'Gloire Kamandi/Butembo, Actu30 / MCP', reported that the Karisimbi communal youth council alerted on Wednesday 8 July 2026 to the abduction of more than 50 young people by armed men in the Kasika and Mabanga Nord quarters of Goma, and that the council fears their possible forced enrolment into the March 23 movement (M23/AFC).
claims.place_as_written: Kasika and Mabanga Nord quarters, Goma
claims.actor_as_written: armed men; youth council alleges vehicles belonging to M23/AFC elements
claims.verification_note: Added the council's stated fear of forced enrolment (excerpt 1). The conditional vehicle attribution stays in the note because the stored excerpts do not carry it. Origin is Actu30.cd. Single unverified account: C. The page (Actu30 / MCP relay) also quotes the council president, Claude Rugo, saying the youths were forced into more than four vehicles 'qui appartiendraient aux éléments du mouvement du 23 mars (M23/AFC)', and that they include boys, girls and children. That attribution is conditional and not in the stored excerpts (lead for add_excerpt). 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: MediaCongo, 8 Jul 2026, credited 'Gloire Kamandi/Butembo, Actu30 / MCP'; the council president Claude Rugo spoke to Actu30.cd and said the youths were taken in vehicles that 'appartiendraient' to M23/AFC elements. All clauses are on the page; the statement should credit Actu30's copy.
claims.researcher_note: Single claim by a youth council relayed by Actu30/MCP. Search listings (Ouragan.cd, Instagram, not opened) place the abduction in the night of 7 July and attribute it to the AFC/M23, one saying 'police de l'AFC/M23'; no AFC/M23 statement found. Council president named in the page as Claude Rugo. Youth include boys, girls and children according to the council president (page text); not quoted here.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that the AFC/M23 announced six members of one family, a woman and her five children, were killed in an attack it said was carried out by the FDLR in Rutshuru territory, and that, according to AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, the attack took place in the night of 2 July 2026 in the Kabizo/Butare area of Bwito chiefdom.
claims.verification_note: Verified on the retained Kinyarwanda page; all six names printed. Partisan origin: C. Single-party account (AFC/M23). The outlet itself notes the information comes from one side. Kanyuka also accused the DRC government of working with the FDLR. Names of the dead are as the outlet prints them (source 1).
claims.researcher_note: Single-party account (AFC/M23) relayed by a Rwandan outlet; the page itself notes that the information comes from one side and no independent confirmation or DRC government response was found. The page also says a UN experts' report of late June 2026 found the FDLR still active in North Kivu, in places cooperating with Congolese forces and Wazalendo (not relied on). The children are described as 'abana' (children); ages not given. Treat as partisan_afc_m23 for the claim.

claims.text: Actualite.cd, relaying Reporters sans frontières (RSF), reported that Espoir Mbata, director of the community radio Top Buzi FM, was held in a container at the North Kivu Provincial Assembly in Goma by the AFC/M23, forced to film an interview of the M23 spokesperson and then released, according to RSF on Friday 24 April.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts verified. The detention ran from 29 March to 3 April per the page, so the date is widened from April to March-April; exact dates are in the note pending add_excerpt. RSF investigation through one relay: B. Per RSF as relayed on the same page (not in the stored excerpts; lead for add_excerpt): Mbata, based in Minova, was arrested on 29 March at his radio's premises by three individuals presenting as M23, transferred to Goma the next day, held four days in a container, and on 3 April taken to the offices of M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka and filmed interviewing him before release. The page says M23 had earlier denied RSF's container revelations as 'des informations totalement infondées'.
claims.researcher_note: RSF accusation relayed by Actualite.cd; exact detention date not given ('quelques jours' after RSF's earlier report); recorded as April 2026. No AFC/M23 response found in these searches. RSF's earlier report is said to concern at least two journalists held incommunicado in containers in eastern DRC (not detailed here).

claims.text: Amnesty International reported in a September 2026 briefing that it documented the summary killing of 18 artisanal miners by M23 or their collaborators in mines in North and South Kivu, at least nine of whom were beaten brutally and died at health centres or before they reached the hospital.
claims.place_as_written: M23-controlled artisanal mines incl. Rubaya and Lomera (North and South Kivu)
claims.actor_as_written: M23 or their collaborators (as alleged by Amnesty International)
claims.verification_note: Verified in the retained PDF. Dropped '26 interviews' and 'between January and April', which the stored excerpt does not print (they are in the note). Documented major-NGO investigation: A. Date not stated: the briefing gives no date range for the 18 killings. The cases it does date all fall in the window (a Rubaya miner beaten to death in February 2025; two Lomera detainees shot after a June 2025 detention; a pit-boss killing in December 2025; seven miners who died at a health centre after beatings between January and March 2026). Not all 18 are dated, so some may fall outside these dates. Interviews ran January-April 2026. Amnesty wrote to M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka on 11 August 2026 and had no response at publication.
claims.researcher_note: The briefing does not give incident dates in the passage; interviews were January-April 2026 and a miner mentions events 'last year'. Some incidents may predate 2026. The Rubaya mine is in Masisi territory (North Kivu); Lomera is in South Kivu. Amnesty wrote to the M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka on 11 August 2026 and reported no response from M23 at publication (passage in the same document).

claims.text: Amnesty International reported that more than 20 miners from Rubaya were kept in a pit and beaten three times a day by M23 fighters.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 fighters (as alleged by Amnesty International)
claims.verification_note: Narrowed to what the stored excerpt prints: the ndake depth figures are not in the excerpt (they are in the note). The undated summary and the February 2026 testimony are surfaced, not merged. Major-NGO investigation: A. Date not stated for this summary figure. Amnesty says M23 uses underground cells known as ndake, roughly 1.5 to 2 m deep. In the body, a Rubaya miner says M23 detained and beat him in February 2026 in a pit inside a wooden house at Kanyenzuki, west of Rubaya, and that 'There were 20 of us in the pit'; he was released the next day after paying about US$32. Discrepancy: the summary says 'more than 20', the witness says 20, and Amnesty does not say they are the same case.
claims.researcher_note: Incident date not stated in the passage (interviews January-April 2026). Same briefing describes forced recruitment threats of transfer to the Rumangabo and Tchanzou training sites in Rutshuru.

claims.text: Health Policy Watch reported that UN experts, in a statement the previous week, called for an end to what they described as a 'reign of terror' by the Rwanda-backed M23, citing a growing volume of civilian testimony, and said rapes, gang rapes, violent assaults and killings of civilians are a common feature of M23's modus operandi, adding that 'while these crimes are not exclusive to M23, the number of individuals affected is staggering and must end'.
claims.place_as_written: M23-controlled areas of eastern DRC (North and South Kivu; place not specified in the excerpt)
claims.verification_note: Verified on the page (Stefan Anderson, 30/07/2026). Relay of a UN statement whose original was not opened: B. Secondary relay; the OHCHR original was not fetched. The same page says the experts described arbitrary detention, 'torture including sexual torture', forced labour and forced recruitment, with detainees held in unofficial sites 'with little or no medical access' (not in the stored excerpt; lead for add_excerpt). The experts also said the crimes 'are not exclusive to M23'. Not tied to a specific place. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: 'these crimes are not exclusive to M23' 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-028: Read the retained page: the experts' very next sentence qualifies the attribution ('not exclusive to M23'), which the claim omitted. Added it; still a relay of the OHCHR statement (original not fetched), so B stands.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): 'these crimes are not exclusive to M23' 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
claims.researcher_note: Secondary relay of an OHCHR press release listed in the search results as dated 21 July 2026 ('M23's reign of terror by torture in eastern DR Congo must end'); the OHCHR page could not be fetched, so the original wording is unverified. An earlier OHCHR experts' release of 26 February 2026 on M23 violence against human rights defenders in North and South Kivu was also found in listing only. Experts' statement is general and not tied to a single territory.

claims.text: Witnesses and relatives told Human Rights Watch that drone attacks in the highlands killed at least two Banyamulenge people in March 2026: an 86-year-old man near Minembwe on 23 March and a 14-year-old boy near his village in Fizi territory on 30 March. HRW said it was unclear if the attacks intended to target military objectives.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe and Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: drones, operator not established by the source
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verified on retained HRW page; same event, same figures. Operator of the drones not established by HRW for these two deaths; victims unnamed.
claims.researcher_note: Victims unnamed in source. Minor (14) unnamed.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that a community radio station in Madegu, near Minembwe, was damaged in an apparent drone attack on 9 March 2026, and that an apparent drone attack was carried out on a church in Ilundu village at night, also in March. Human Rights Watch said it could not establish responsibility with certainty but that the targets suggest the Congolese army or allied fighters controlled the drones; Human Rights Watch said it had asked the Congolese army's regional commander for information on the strikes and had not received a response.
claims.place_as_written: Madegu and Ilundu, near Minembwe, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: drones; operator not established; HRW infers from the targets that the Congolese army or allied fighters controlled them (HRW's inference)
claims.verification_note: Removed the '4 April' figure no excerpt prints (date kept in note); 'contacted' changed to HRW's wording; drone-control inference kept attributed to HRW. Responsibility is HRW's inference from the targets, not an established finding. HRW spoke to the commander on 4 April (page text).
claims.researcher_note: Church attack dated only 'in March'. Two excerpts from one page.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that, according to Minembwe residents and UN and diplomatic sources, the Twirwaneho had forced families to provide a fighter or financially compensate the armed group and retaliated if they refused, and that, according to the same sources, the Twirwaneho had also blocked civilians from leaving Minembwe.
claims.verification_note: Blocking clause is on the page in the next sentence, not the excerpt; attribution to 'the sources' made explicit.
claims.researcher_note: Undated ongoing practice as of HRW's April 2026 report.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported, citing security sources, that the Burundian army had about 4,000 troops deployed to Fizi and Mwenga territories to fight alongside Congolese armed forces.
claims.place_as_written: Fizi and Mwenga territories, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed 'against Twirwaneho and M23 armed groups', which the excerpt does not state; the irrelevant SOS Medias note is not supported here. Figure from unnamed security sources as relayed by HRW.
claims.researcher_note: Figure is from unnamed security sources per HRW; Burundian authorities per SOS Médias Burundi gave no casualty figures.

claims.text: Fizi territory administrator Samy Badibanga reported that Rwandan air force fighter jets had once again bombed Rugezi, Mulima, Point Zéro, Kazaroho, Bilalo Mbili and Mikenge on Wednesday 8 July 2026, causing enormous material and human damage; the territorial authority said several civilians were wounded in these bombings.
claims.place_as_written: Rugezi, Mulima, Point Zéro, Kazaroho, Bilalo Mbili, Mikenge, Fizi, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Rwandan air force (as alleged by DRC authority)
claims.verification_note: Wounded clause rests on a page passage, not the excerpt; 'heavy' changed to 'enormous' per the source; discrepancy in the article surfaced. Discrepancy: the same Radio Okapi article later says 'Ces bombardements attribués aux Twirwaneho et à leurs alliés'. claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Mikenge, in the Itombwe sector of Mwenga territory, was retaken on Sunday by the FARDC, supported by the Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB) and the Wazalendo militia, after remaining for over a year under the control of Twirwaneho fighters and allied rebels.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to independent UN experts, the AFC/M23 had reportedly set up a system of control based on fear in the areas it administers, and that the experts' statement reported arbitrary arrests and detentions, acts of torture including sexual violence, and cases of forced labour and forced recruitment of civilians.

The UN statement itself should be retrieved as the primary source.
claims.researcher_note: Region-wide; not specific to South Kivu. Excerpt does not mention abductions/arson/investigations/21 July/Geneva (those are in adjacent sentences), so the verifier should narrow. Territory field is a placeholder.

claims.text: MSF reported that between January and April 2026 its support to Baraka general referral hospital (Fizi territory, South Kivu), through medical and logistical supplies and staff training, helped treat 426 war-wounded patients arriving in the influx of violence-related injuries.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that Rwanda deployed over 8,000 RDF troops, including special forces, and heavy equipment to the Ruzizi Plain frontlines, and that BM21 rockets were fired from Kamanyola on 4 and 5 December, with cross-border shelling on 5 December causing civilian casualties in Cibitoke, Burundi.

claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. Reported by the Group from multiple sources; no direct quotation of President Tshisekedi.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 leaders alleged that FARDC and FDNB committed a premeditated, systematic and targeted campaign of extermination against the Banyamulenge population, including through aerial bombardments; the Group stated it did not substantiate intentional targeting and that Banyamulenge community members reported three civilian deaths.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that on 11 March 2026 two successive detonations were reported near a residential compound in the Himbi neighbourhood of Goma, the second causing the death of a UNICEF staff member; M23 military personnel deployed to the scene shortly after the strike and removed all ballistic remnants; AFC/M23 attributed the strike to FARDC while Congolese authorities announced an investigation, and the Group's investigations continue.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 continued to forcibly or voluntarily recruit adults and minors, and that former recruits denounced systematic torture and executions in training camps, notably in Rumangabo.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 was the leading perpetrator of conflict-related sexual violence according to cases documented and verified by the United Nations, and that humanitarian actors recorded a dramatic increase in cases of such violence since 2024, disproportionately affecting women and girls.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that in January 2026 the UN in the DRC verified at least 46 cases of conflict-related sexual violence affecting 61 victims in conflict-affected provinces of eastern DRC, with North Kivu the most affected province (33 victims: 22 women and 11 girls), followed by South Kivu (22 victims: 13 women and nine girls) and Ituri (six victims).
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed in this passage (see next claim)
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported, citing a UN source, that for the January 2026 verified cases armed groups were responsible for cases affecting 52 per cent of victims (M23 most, with 21 victims, then Nyatura four, Raïa Mutomboki three and ADF two), while State agents were responsible for 46 per cent of the cases, with FARDC soldiers ranking first, followed by the PNC and one official from the Ministry of Mines and Energy.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu and South Kivu (and Ituri)
claims.actor_as_written: M23; Nyatura; Raïa Mutomboki; ADF; FARDC; PNC
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 annex 4. The cited figures cover all conflict-affected provinces in the data (includes Ituri). Excerpt may need tightening.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that IPS inspectors of the AFC/M23-run Provincial Health Inspection Department inspected the premises of humanitarian actors after an 11 February 2026 AFC/M23 'Note Explicative', requested aggregate data on sexual violence incidents and access to confidential patient files containing names of victims, and that some humanitarian actors were ordered to cease distributing dignity kits to curb what AFC/M23 alleged were 'fake' victims.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.

The Group notes AFC/M23's stated intention not to impede access to assistance (annex 5 para. 6) and that its actions may deter victims from seeking assistance (para. 8).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that at a joint meeting in late March 2026 AFC/M23 officials reprimanded humanitarian actors and accused them of inventing data about sexual violence, affirmed that AFC/M23 did not tolerate sexual violence, and criticised the lack of perpetrator data in patient files; the officials present included Colonel John Imani Nzenze and Ms. Chantal Kayitaba Murekatete.
