claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that between January and December 2025 the UN in the DRC verified at least 887 cases of conflict-related sexual violence affecting 1,534 victims in conflict-affected provinces of eastern DRC, a 59 per cent increase on 2024 (364 cases); North Kivu was the most affected province (676 victims), followed by South Kivu (537) and Ituri (300).
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed in this passage (see next claim)
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. UN-verified cases only, as cited by the Group.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 annex 4 para. 3 (UN-verified data; figures as printed, verified cases only; Group notes elsewhere that CRSV is under-reported). Victim breakdown: 854 women, 672 girls, four men, four boys.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported, for the 2025 cases verified by the UN, that DRC armed groups were responsible for cases affecting 75 per cent of victims (M23 ranked first, followed by CODECO, Wazalendo and Mai-Mai factions) and State agents for 19 per cent (FARDC soldiers first, followed by the PNC), and that the UPDF, the FNDB and RED-Tabara were also responsible for CRSV cases.
claims.actor_as_written: M23; CODECO; Wazalendo; Mai-Mai factions; FARDC; PNC; UPDF; FNDB; RED-Tabara
claims.verification_note: Year 2025 is printed in the same annex paragraph (para. 3) that opens with the January-December 2025 figures; all other clauses in the excerpts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 annex 4 para. 3. 'FNDB' is the spelling printed in the annex (Burundi National Defence Force is elsewhere abbreviated FDNB). Counts by province are not broken down by perpetrator in the passage.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported, citing its earlier report (S/2025/858, para. 82, annex 38), that it had verified a sharp escalation of conflict-related sexual violence cases in South Kivu in areas under the control of the DRC Government and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo armed groups (areas under DRC Government and Wazalendo control)
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: cross-reference to S/2025/858, para. 82, annex 38 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-012: Relay check: in S/2026/466 this sentence cross-references S/2025/858 para. 82 / annex 38, i.e. the same finding as claim r1-GOE-093, so it is not an independent second origin and should not be counted as corroboration. It also locates the cases by area of control, not by perpetrator.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): cross-reference to S/2025/858, para. 82, annex 38
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 annex 4 para. 1, referring to S/2025/858 para. 82 and annex 38. The Group also says it received information about but could not investigate new CRSV cases in Ituri and North Kivu, in particular sexual slavery and forced pregnancy by ADF-ISCAP elements (same paragraph).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that mining activity at AFC/M23-controlled Rubaya increased substantially compared with a year earlier according to its March 2026 satellite imagery model, with production assessed to exceed 2024 estimates of approximately 120 tons monthly, and that AFC/M23 taxed all actors, with a per-kilogram tax at commercialization of $4 for coltan and $2 for cassiterite.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 paras. 213-214 and annexes 67-68 (satellite model from high resolution imagery of March 2026). Category chosen as resource exploitation; no atrocity alleged in the passage.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that between 80 and 150 Wazalendo groups were reported active across South Kivu, with at least 70 self-proclaimed Wazalendo 'Generals' operating in Uvira and its surroundings, and that by December 2025 Uvira had become the epicentre of tensions and clashes between FARDC and Wazalendo and among Wazalendo fighting over revenue from illegal taxation.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 paras. 109 and 112. Excerpts adjusted by builder.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that on 22 August 2025 Brigadier-General Mwehu Lumbu Evariste, Commander of the Sokola 2 operational sector in South Kivu, met the main Wazalendo groups to define a counteroffensive strategy against AFC/M23 and RDF, and that FARDC subsequently transferred truckloads of weapons and ammunition to Wazalendo at several front lines, including Kiliba, Songe, Luvungi, Lubarika and Walungu.
claims.place_as_written: Kiliba, Songe, Luvungi, Lubarika, Walungu, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 para. 120 (intelligence, armed groups sources, civil society, UN, researchers). The transfers' dates after 22 August 2025 are not given.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that several Wazalendo factions carried out joint operations with the FDNB, which relied on them for intelligence and knowledge of the terrain: FDNB operated with Yakutumba along the Uvira axis and the Ruzizi Plain prior to the AFC/M23 takeover, and relied on Ngomazito elements as scouts in the Hauts Plateaux.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira axis, Ruzizi Plain and Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that the Coalition nationale du peuple pour la souveraineté du Congo (CNPSC), led by Yakutumba, maintained a parallel administration in areas it controlled, particularly in Fizi territory, that in January 2026 its 'finance bureau' published a list of taxes across multiple sectors, and that since 2023 it had operated a parallel judicial system with detention facilities, former detainees reporting release conditioned on payment of fines of 2,000,000 to 5,000,000 Congolese francs.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 paras. 123-125 and annexes 37-38. Excerpt anchors adjusted by builder.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that in late March 2026 a FARDC helicopter landed in Pinga to deliver weapons to FDLR-FOCA units led by 'Major-General' Uzabakiriho Cyprien that had been fighting AFC/M23 and RDF in Masisi territory, and that on 7 April a confidential encounter between a Kinshasa delegation including FARDC generals and the FDLR-FOCA high command in Pinga decided that FDLR-FARDC cooperation would continue.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 paras. 136-137 (FDLR-FOCA, intelligence and UN sources; Wazalendo commanders, FDLR, FARDC, intelligence sources). This is the Group's account from FDLR/FARDC/intelligence sources; no Kinshasa reply on this point is recorded in the report.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that on 29 March 2026 FARDC announced the launch of an operation to neutralize FDLR around Pinga-Walikale and deployed additional troops from Kisangani to Walikale, but that at the time of writing no anti-FDLR operations had taken place.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 para. 51 (FARDC sources); the Group's assessment that commitment 'remained questionable' is its own and not the FARDC's.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that private military contractors accompanied FARDC when they entered Uvira in January 2026, that multiple drone strikes conducted with their support targeted AFC/M23 positions around Minembwe on 1 February 2026, and that between 2 and 8 February 2026 they airdropped FARDC 'Hiboux' special forces units at Point Zero.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira, Minembwe and Point Zero, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 para. 144; see also paras. 143 (Jan-Mar 2026 contractors in South Kivu) and 145-148 (Quantum Global / Vectus Global; Vectus told the Group in Feb 2026 that the DRC Government had requested support in planning operations to retake Uvira). Mr. Sirot denied involvement in the contract's military aspects (para. 148).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that a meeting in Washington, D.C. on 17 and 18 March 2026 between representatives of the Governments of the DRC, Rwanda and the United States resulted in an 'initial steps plan' that foresaw withdrawal of RDF and AFC/M23 'personnel and equipment', Rwanda's disengagement from defined areas, efforts by the DRC to neutralize the FDLR, and restrictions on drone strikes.
claims.place_as_written: Washington, D.C.; areas of interest in Lubero, Masisi and Walikale (North Kivu) and South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: DRC government; Rwandan government; United States
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 paras. 43-45 (a copy of the plan was consulted by the Group; annex 18). Statement is about a political agreement, not a communiqué; recorded as reported by the Group.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 representatives announced that no withdrawal was taking place, describing movements as routine troop rotations.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 para. 50 (footnote 50 cites an X post by Lawrence Kanyuka). Date approximate: after the 23 March 2026 start of reported withdrawals and before 15 April 2026.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported public statements by the President of Rwanda, Paul Kagame, that 'defensive measures' also included troop deployment in the DRC.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 para. 50; annex 19 is a Kagame interview published in Jeune Afrique (date not stated in the excerpt). The same sentence goes on to give the Group's own inference about Rwanda's intent, which is not part of this claim.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 conducted armed night raids on hospitals in Goma, targeting Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals on 1 and 3 March respectively as part of operations tracking FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR combatants who had not surrendered, that male caregivers were briefly detained and released, and that a total of 164 patients were abducted (48 from Heal Africa and 116 from CBCA Ndosho), some undergoing treatment and others who had refused to leave for fear of forced recruitment. It reported that Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka and 'General' Makenga issued public denials of responsibility, saying they acted in full compliance with international humanitarian law to secure the hospitals from 'infiltrated rogue combatants' who were 'endangering' patients and staff, and that, contrary to those assertions, witnesses confirmed no weapons were found in the hospitals and the arrested individuals had not endangered patients or staff.
claims.place_as_written: Heal Africa hospital and CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Date was the second raid only; set to the 1-3 March range the paragraph gives. Figures field carried the AFC/M23 figure of 130, which no excerpt of this claim prints. AFC/M23's communiqué figure (130 FARDC elements taken) is a separate claim. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: AFC/M23 leaders' denials (para. 107) 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-003: The claim quotes 'contrary to those assertions' without saying what was asserted, so it leaves out AFC/M23's denial (check 8). Para. 107 of the retained report gives it. Dates and counts differ from OHCHR/Reuters (night of 28 Feb; 116 and 15) and Amnesty (more than 130); keep the discrepancy surfaced.; excerpt-support: added para. 107 (AFC/M23 leaders' public denials) as an excerpt; 'operations tracking FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR combatants' is already in source 0
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 paras. 105 and 107. Date given as the report's 1 March (Heal Africa) and 3 March (CBCA Ndosho). A lead from the OHCHR press release of 3 March 2025 (not fetched here) gives the night of 28 February for the raids: possible date discrepancy for a verifier. The report calls the individuals taken 'patients' and also describes them as people hors de combat; AFC/M23's own account is in the denial claims.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported in an annex that on 3 March 2025 Fikiri Mwishuko, the Chef de groupement of Shanga, was abducted by AFC/M23 from the CBCA Ndosho hospital amongst other sick and wounded patients, and that he subsequently died, reportedly after having been tortured by AFC/M23.
claims.place_as_written: CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446, annex on AFC/M23 parallel administration and customary chiefs (page 86 of the report). Cross-refers to paras. 105-108. Cause of death is stated as 'reportedly'.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that on the night of 4 to 5 April 2025 armed AFC/M23 elements entered the MSF-supported Kyeshero Hospital compound in Goma in search of FARDC elements who had completed treatment but stayed for fear of being recruited, opened fire within the grounds, killing one person, injuring three and assaulting two staff members; the soldiers did not enter the ward but bullets struck treatment areas.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 106 (protection sources; footnote cites MSF statement).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that an official AFC/M23 communiqué of 5 March 2025, signed by Lawrence Kanyuka, denied responsibility for the raids on Goma hospitals and accused MONUSCO officials of erroneous interpretation of the facts; the communiqué acknowledged that 130 FARDC elements were taken but claimed the operation was peaceful and in full compliance with international humanitarian law because the elements had 'infiltrated' the medical facilities.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. AFC/M23's account as reported by the Group; the Group states witnesses confirmed no weapons were found (separate claim).
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 52 (AFC/M23 leadership denials of responsibility for attacks on hospitals in Goma). The Group reports the communiqué's content; it is a partisan statement recorded as what AFC/M23 said. See also para. 107 (Bisimwa, Kanyuka and Makenga denials).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that in an interview excerpt published on X on 13 March 2025, 'General' Sultani Makenga, asked about the raid on the Heal Africa hospital, repeated that the men arrested were former FARDC pretending to be patients or hospital staff.
claims.place_as_written: Heal Africa hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 52. The annex also gives the English translation of Makenga's reply: 'Former FARDC soldiers were pretending to be patients or hospital attendants. Fourteen weapons were found there.' The Group's finding that no weapons were found is in para. 107.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that between 19 January and 14 February 2025 multiple incidents harmed medical facilities and personnel: on 20 January bullets and several rockets landed near the MSF-supported hospital in Masisi town, killing one MSF worker and injuring another; on 27 January firing and shelling affected two Goma hospitals, injuring a medical practitioner and a newborn at Goma Provincial Hospital; and humanitarian actors reported at least 27 health structures in and around Goma were impacted between 25 January and 14 February.
claims.place_as_written: Masisi town and Goma (city), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Date range set to the paragraph's own 19 January-14 February 2025 window (printed on the page, para. 83). Statement unchanged.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 paras. 81-83. The Group attributes the context to warring parties generally ('Indiscriminate shelling in populated areas'); no single perpetrator is named for these incidents.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that human rights defenders said survivors of sexual violence faced significant barriers in accessing medical care, primarily due to fear of reprisals by AFC/M23 elements, and that a further alarming surge in sexual violence cases had been reported across North and South Kivu, attributed to all armed actors party to the conflict.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu and South Kivu (Goma and surrounding areas)
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (reprisal fear); all armed actors party to the conflict (surge)
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 humanitarian-impact annex on Goma ('Increasing sexual violence'); footnote cites MSF reporting of massive figures of sexual violence admissions. Date approximate (aftermath of the January-February 2025 fighting).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that reports on the mass escape of prisoners from Muzenze prison in Goma on 27 January 2025 indicated that over 160 women perished in a fire, with a significant number of women reportedly raped by escaping male prisoners, and that it had not been able to independently verify the figures.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. Unverified reports, as the Group itself states. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 3 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. Regraded C->B on independent, non-partisan corroboration.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 humanitarian-impact annex. The Group states it 'has not yet been able to independently verify the reported figures and continues to investigate the incident'.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that between 6 and 8 February 2025, in South Kivu between Kalehe and Kavumu, retreating FARDC forces looted civilian property and a health centre, forcibly enlisted civilians to transport stolen goods, deliberately killed at least 15 civilians and engaged in widespread sexual violence; in the same paragraph it reported that MONUSCO documented the rape of three girls aged 13 to 17 by FARDC soldiers between 31 January and 2 February, without stating where, and that FARDC authorities confirmed the violations and reported the arrest of alleged perpetrators.
claims.place_as_written: between Kalehe and Kavumu, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Original wording joined the MONUSCO-documented rapes to the Kalehe-Kavumu events; the source gives different dates and no place for them. The paragraph gives no place for the three rapes documented by MONUSCO; their dates (31 January-2 February) precede the Kalehe-Kavumu events. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-013: The excerpt carries the FARDC authorities' response (confirmation and arrests), which the statement left out; it is a party's account investigators need. Also restored the omitted forced-enlistment clause. No search run.; excerpt-support: no change needed; every clause is printed in the stored excerpts
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 88 (civil society, FARDC, UN, audiovisual sources). The same passage reports FARDC authorities confirmed the violations and reported arrests, and that on 10 February at least 84 FARDC soldiers appeared before a military court in Bukavu.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that on 15 February 2025 the withdrawal of FARDC forces from Bukavu led to the escape of over 2,800 detainees and widespread looting, and that on 27 February two explosions at a public meeting hosted by Nangaa in Bukavu killed 17 civilians and wounded 68.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. The Group does not attribute the 27 February explosions in this passage.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 88 (end) and footnote 195 to para. 171. The footnote does not attribute the 27 February explosions. Two incidents on different days are combined in one claim as the same source's account of Bukavu in February 2025.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that on 26 January 2025 several bombs launched from positions on the Bulenga peninsula, controlled by RDF, struck the Rusayo 1 and 2 internally displaced persons camps on the outskirts of Goma, killing at least 12 people including children and injuring many others.
claims.place_as_written: Rusayo 1 and 2 IDP camps, Goma outskirts, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: bombs launched from RDF-controlled positions on the Bulenga peninsula (as the Group of Experts reports)
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 84 (UN sources, local authorities, civil society). Excerpt includes footnote markers as printed.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that between 28 January and 9 April 2025 it recorded at least 70 distinct incidents of targeted killings in Goma attributable to AFC/M23, resulting in over 200 fatalities, with adult men the majority of victims but also women and children.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 100 (community-based confidential sources, residents, witnesses, UN and other sources). The Group lists motives in para. 101 (alleged collaboration with FARDC, FDLR or Wazalendo; refusal to join; dissent; civil society activity). Excerpt reproduces the PDF text spacing.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that musician and activist Delcat Idengo (real name Delphin Katembo Vinywasiki) was shot and killed by AFC/M23 elements on 13 February 2025 in Goma shortly after publicly criticizing AFC/M23, and that eyewitnesses identified AFC/M23 fighters as responsible. The Group also reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka publicly denied any involvement the same evening, calling the killing a 'score-settling between different factions of the Wazalendo and the FARDC', and reiterated the denial on 12 March 2025.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: killing took place in Goma 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Kanyuka denial the same evening 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: denial reiterated on 12 March 2025 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-003: Attribution matches the Group's annex, but the same annex records an AFC/M23 denial that the claim leaves out (counter-account, check 8). Read in the retained S/2025/446 text, annex on the killing of Delcat Idengo, under 'Denial of responsibility by AFC/M23'.; excerpt-support: added three excerpts from the annex: 'assassination in Goma' (caption), Kanyuka's denial of 13 February, and the reiteration of 12 March 2025
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 49 (local community leaders, civil society, researchers, audio-video testimonies on file with the Secretariat). First anchor to be finalised by the builder.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that Bertrand Bisimwa publicly denied civilian deaths in the fighting for Goma, claiming that all fatalities were combatants, and that the Group stated these claims were contradicted by consistent reports of civilian casualties from residents, humanitarian and medical actors, UN sources, public reporting and photographic and video evidence.
claims.verification_note: Checked against para. 79; the excerpt carries the denial and the contradiction.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 79 (see annex 44). Date approximate: refers to the January 2025 Goma hostilities; exact date of Bisimwa's statement not in the excerpt.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that after the expiration of a seven-day ultimatum issued by AFC/M23 on 11 February 2025, demanding the surrender of members of the FARDC, PNC, Wazalendo and FDLR and urging civilians to denounce them, AFC/M23 intensified house-to-house searches and targeted operations against individuals suspected of affiliation with Wazalendo, FDLR or FARDC.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 102 (UN sources and protection actors). Ultimatum content as described by the Group.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that on 4 January 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF took control of Masisi centre in North Kivu and retained control despite repeated attempts by Wazalendo, FDLR, the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and FARDC to retake it, and that two weeks later they captured Minova town in Kalehe territory, South Kivu.
claims.place_as_written: Masisi centre (North Kivu) and Minova (Kalehe, South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 14. 'Two weeks later' places Minova's capture at about 18 January 2025 (approximate). The report says the 2,500 FARDC and FDNB troops based in Minova retreated before the arrival of AFC/M23 and RDF.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that between 21 and 27 January 2025 several columns of RDF troops, each comprising hundreds of well-equipped soldiers, advanced into and seized control of Sake, Mubambiro and Goma town following a coordinated encirclement of each locality, and that Goma was fully conquered on 27 January.
claims.place_as_written: Sake, Mubambiro and Goma (city), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 paras. 35 and 16. Para. 15 adds that on 22 January RDF occupied the Bulenga peninsula. Group states Rwandan officials had confidentially informed it a week before that President Kagame had decided to take control of Goma and Bukavu (para. 34).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that on 24 January 2025 the Military Governor of North Kivu, Major-General Peter Cirimwami, known for his long-standing ties with FDLR-FOCA, was shot dead in Sake; in its annex 6 the Group says he was shot on 24 January while visiting FARDC and Wazalendo forces in Sake and succumbed to his injuries the following day.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source in this passage
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. The passage does not state who shot him. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: annex 6: shot on 24 January, died the following day 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-001: Time slippage: the Group puts the shooting and death on 24 January; DW says he was hit 'ce jeudi' (23 Jan) and Jeune Afrique that the army confirmed the death on 24 Jan (excerpts in r1-NKS-2025Q1-005); search snippets (RFI, DW) agree and one outlet says he died in Kinshasa. Discrepancy surfaced; the 'ties with FDLR-FOCA' characterisation stays the Group's. No shooter attributed (lead: scooprdc.net on the bullet's origin).; excerpt-support: cut 'Other reports say he was shot on Thursday 23 January and that the army confirmed his death on 24 January' (DW/Jeune Afrique are not among this claim's sources; their excerpts sit in r1-NKS-2025Q1-005); added instead the Group's own annex 6 wording (shot 24 January, died the following day), a discrepancy inside the cited report itself
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 15 (see annex 6). The excerpt says only that he 'was shot dead in Sake'; the perpetrator is not stated in the passage.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF broke through the joint FARDC-FDNB positions in Nyabibwe on 6 February 2025, seized the strategic airport of Kavumu on 14 February, and that Bukavu, the provincial capital of South Kivu, was taken on 16 February without combat.
claims.place_as_written: Nyabibwe, Kavumu airport and Bukavu (city), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 17; para. 170 says retreating FARDC units systematically committed abuses and that AFC/M23 announced the capture of Bukavu to protect the population from FARDC/Wazalendo atrocities.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF forces withdrew from Walikale following sustained FARDC airstrikes targeting critical infrastructure including the Kigoma airstrip and mounting international pressure, and that, according to corroborated information, the withdrawal followed a direct instruction from the Government of Rwanda.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 18 ('wit hdraw' is a PDF text-extraction split). The same paragraph gives mid-March 2025 as when AFC/M23 and RDF advanced deep into Walikale territory. Para. 19: by early April 2025 the controlled area was the largest ever recorded, a 100 per cent increase compared with November 2024.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that since 17 February 2025 Uvira experienced a severe breakdown in law and order as the AFC/M23 advance loomed and security forces retreated or lost control, with criminal elements and undisciplined FARDC and Wazalendo engaging in widespread killings, looting and attacks on civilian and humanitarian infrastructure, and that residents reported bodies strewn all over the city.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 89 (civilian, humanitarian and UN sources). The paragraph adds that for weeks the city was paralysed, with mass displacement of civilians to Burundi, and that until early April Wazalendo elements controlled the city 'operating with full impunity'.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that from February 2025, as DRC authorities and security actors largely withdrew from Uvira, Wazalendo armed groups de facto controlled Uvira town and surroundings, using disproportionate force and committing widespread abuses, in particular targeting Banyamulenge communities, and that FARDC headquarters and the South Kivu Governorate were reinstalled in Uvira in early March.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 paras. 173-174. Early April: the Defence Minister Guy Kabombo and RAD ex-coordinator General Padiri travelled from Bujumbura to Uvira to pacify Wazalendo groups (para. 174).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported (S/2025/446, in its section on Uvira) that a key Wazalendo leader, 'General' Ebuela Mtetezi, was killed by rival Mai Mai groups on 16 March (no year printed; the surrounding paragraph concerns early 2025), reportedly because of his clandestine support to AFC/M23; the sentence cites the Group's earlier report S/2024/432, annex 105.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. Place of the killing is not stated in the passage. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-015: Attribution and 'reportedly' match the Group of Experts. Searched '"Ebuela" Mtetezi': Congolese outlets dated 15 March 2025 (congorassure.cd; africa-infos.cd 'un jour seulement après le décès') and a Facebook post ('Décédé depuis le 14 mars') put his death on about 14 March, at Lutete between Lweba and Lubumba (Fizi territory). The 16 March date is the Group's and conflicts with earlier dated reports; the record's place 'Uvira area' is not in the source. Amend wording to make the date the Group's and set date_precision to approximate; raise a claim from the local reports.; excerpt-support: no change needed; every clause is printed in the stored excerpts 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: The page prints '16 March' with no year and footnotes the sentence to S/2024/432 (a 2024 report), so the year 2025 is inferred from context, not printed; the date precision should stay approximate and the discrepancy surfaced. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: The page prints '16 March' with no year and footnotes the sentence to S/2024/432 (a 2024 report), so the year 2025 is inferred from context, not printed; the date precision should stay approximate and the discrepancy surfaced.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 173. Place of killing not stated in the excerpt; the paragraph concerns Uvira town and surroundings.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that Twirwaneho's sanctioned military leader, 'General' Michel Rukunda, was killed by a FARDC CH-4 drone strike on 15 February 2025, and that the following day, after heavy clashes with FARDC, Twirwaneho took control of the Minembwe airstrip, effectively cutting off FARDC resupply in the Hauts Plateaux.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 175 (security, FARDC and Banyamulenge sources, per footnote). The report says a second FARDC drone strike on 25 February killed four Twirwaneho leaders (para. 177). Rukunda's place of death not stated.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported (S/2025/446, paras. 176 and 178) that Charles Sematama assumed the military command of Twirwaneho and on 23 February (no year printed; the sentence cites S/2024/969, para. 106) announced its alliance with AFC/M23, and that in late March AFC/M23 'Colonel' Japhet Gakufe and Charles Sematama arrived in Minembwe with an estimated 200 AFC/M23 combatants.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. Gakufe's rank is printed as 'Colonel' in S/2025/446 and 'Lieutenant-Colonel' in S/2025/858. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Both clauses are on the page, but '23 February' has no year and the sentence is cited to the Group's December 2024 report S/2024/969, which cannot document a February 2025 event; the year 2025 is inferred from context (it follows Rukunda's death on 15 February in para. 175). The discrepancy is surfaced rather than resolved. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Both clauses are on the page, but '23 February' has no year and the sentence is cited to the Group's December 2024 report S/2024/969, which cannot document a February 2025 event; the year 2025 is inferred from context (it follows Rukunda's death on 15 February in para. 175). The discrepancy is surfaced rather than resolved.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 paras. 176 and 178. Reported from Twirwaneho, Banyamulenge, UN and intelligence sources.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 the majority of 7,000 to 9,000 Burundian troops were positioned in South Kivu, notably the Ruzizi Plain along the tri-border area and the Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, and that heavy clashes between FDNB supported by FARDC and Wazalendo, and AFC/M23 supported by RDF, resulted in several hundreds of FDNB casualties.
claims.place_as_written: Ruzizi Plain and Hauts Plateaux (Minembwe), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 179 (annex 72). The report also states the troop build-up fuelled Rwanda-Burundi tensions.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that in February 2025 the President of Burundi, Évariste Ndayishimiye, accused Rwanda of intending to invade Burundi, including through its backing of the Burundian armed opposition group Red Tabara, and announced the readiness of Burundi to fight back, and that Rwanda in turn signalled a commitment to regime change in both Burundi and the DRC.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Burundi; Government of Rwanda
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. 'Signalled a commitment to regime change' is the Group's characterisation; no Rwandan statement is quoted.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 180 (annex 73). The Group's wording on Rwanda ('signalled a commitment to regime change') is its own characterisation and no Rwandan statement is quoted in the paragraph. In mid-March the two countries reportedly agreed verbal and military de-escalation (para. 181).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that in Lubero town on 20 February 2025, after AFC/M23 advances led to heavy clashes and FARDC withdrawals, FARDC elements engaged in systematic looting of civilian homes and shops, and that the next day FARDC issued a public apology, attributing the acts to fleeing, undisciplined soldiers acting in violation of orders and assuring they would face justice.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 90. The report adds that on 15 March 55 FARDC elements convicted for the lootings were among 260 soldiers enrolled in a refresher training programme at Nyaleke, Beni. Excerpt includes footnote markers as printed.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that, during operations by RDF and AFC/M23 in Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, targeting FDLR and associated armed groups and civilians accused of collaborating with them, RDF and AFC/M23 forces carried out summary executions, arbitrary arrests and detentions, and the deliberate destruction and burning of civilian infrastructure, including homes and villages; and that since operations began in April 2025 UN and humanitarian sources reported over 300 civilians killed in Bwito chiefdom alone, both as collateral casualties and through targeted executions.
claims.place_as_written: Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Figures field carried a footnote figure (over 500) that no excerpt prints; narrowed to the excerpted figure. Statement unchanged. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: RDF and AFC/M23 operations in Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: targets: FDLR, associated groups, civilians accused of collaborating 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: both as collateral casualties and through targeted executions 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-004: Read the retained report (S/2025/858, paras 38-39): the 300+ figure is cited from UN and humanitarian sources and covers deaths 'both as collateral casualties and through targeted executions'; as written, the statement could read as 300 victims of RDF/M23 executions. Amend adds the qualifier and the operational context; the excerpt should be extended to carry 'both as collateral casualties and through targeted executions'.; excerpt-support: added three excerpts from paras 37-38: operations in Bwito chiefdom, western Rutshuru; targets (FDLR, associated groups and civilians accused of collaborating); the 300+ sentence carrying 'both as collateral casualties and through targeted executions'
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/858 para. 38. Footnote: UN and humanitarian actors reported the overall civilian death toll surpassed 500 throughout Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms since April 2025; the Group could not independently establish verified casualty figures. The Group also says the Bwito/Bwisha operations fall under the AFC/M23 'First Defence Zone' led by 'Brigadier General' Baudoin Ngaruye (para. 44). The report's own legal characterisation (para. 43) is not reproduced.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that between 9 and 27 July 2025 over 300 civilian casualties were reported across Binza, notably in Nyamilima, Kisharo, Burambo, Kiseguro, Katwiguro, Musinga and Kigarigari, and that witness accounts, confirmed by photographic and video evidence, indicated civilians were summarily executed following arbitrary accusations of collaboration with FDLR or other Wazalendo armed groups, bodies were frequently disposed of in rivers, and burials were prohibited by local AFC/M23 authorities.
claims.place_as_written: Binza, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. 'Casualties' as printed; not split into killed and injured.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/858 para. 40 (and para. 39 on RDF-led cordon-and-search operations along the Kiwanja-Ishasha road). 'Casualties' as printed; not split into killed and injured.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that in mid-September 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF launched operations across northern Masisi, seizing Bibwe and several surrounding localities (an estimated 100 km²) while advancing towards Lukweti, and that on 21 September AFC/M23 captured Nzibira in Walungu territory, South Kivu, a strategic mineral trading hub.
claims.place_as_written: Bibwe (Masisi, North Kivu) and Nzibira (Walungu, South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/858 paras. 47 and 56. Excerpt 1 ends before the unit sign 'km2' to avoid a symbol; verify. Date: Nzibira 21 September; Bibwe mid-September.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 reinforcements led by 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Japhet Gakufe reached Minembwe in March 2025, and that a second reinforcement led by 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Oscar Ndabagaza was blocked while crossing hostile areas before reaching Mikenge at the end of August.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe and Mikenge, Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/858 para. 53 (UN, Rwandan intelligence and security sources, researchers).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that systematic forced recruitment intensified in all areas under AFC/M23 occupation, with men and underage boys rounded up, often under the pretext of identity verification or security operations, and that attempted desertion or refusal of orders at training sites such as Rumangabo and Tchanzu led to inhumane punishments and summary executions.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo and Tchanzu, North Kivu; AFC/M23-held areas
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/858 paras. 22 and 25. AFC/M23 publicized the pass-out of 7,437 'commandos' at Rumangabo on 14 September and 9,350 at Tchanzu on 1 October 2025 (para. 23); the Group could not corroborate those figures.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that on 12 May 2025 AFC/M23 rounded up over 2,000 civilians, mostly Hutu, from collective shelters around Goma and Sake and transferred them under coercive conditions to the UNHCR transit centre in Goma, that 1,798 were subsequently transferred to Rwanda between 17 and 22 May, and that the AFC/M23 focal point for humanitarian affairs, Chantal Murekatete Kayitaba, threatened UNHCR staff to abort screenings. The Group reports that, despite AFC/M23's framing of the operation as a 'voluntary return' of Rwandan nationals, the conditions for voluntary returns were not met.
claims.place_as_written: Goma and Sake, North Kivu; Rwanda
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. The report prints the name as 'Chantal Murekatete Kayitaba' here and 'Chantal Kayitaba Murekatete' in S/2026/466. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: AFC/M23 framing as 'voluntary return' 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-004: Counter-account left out: the same report records AFC/M23's public framing of the operation as a 'voluntary return' of Rwandan nationals (and rejects it). Amend adds that account so each party's version is recorded; the excerpt should be extended to carry it. Attribution otherwise matches.; excerpt-support: added para. 85 as an excerpt; cut 'publicly' (the report says only 'the framing of the operation by AFC/M23') and kept the Group's rejection of that framing beside it
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/858 paras. 84-85 (annex 39). AFC/M23 framed the operation as a 'voluntary return' of Rwandan nationals; the Group says conditions for voluntary return were not met.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported, in an annex, that in areas under the control of Mai-Mai Yakutumba and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups in Uvira and Fizi territories 'the recent months' were marked by a sharp escalation in human rights violations including conflict-related sexual violence, extortion and summary executions of civilians accused of collaborating with AFC/M23; separately, citing verified reports from field inquiries by UN-supported national NGOs, it said that between January and June 2025 at least 325 cases of sexual violence affecting over 400 victims were documented in South Kivu province alone, exceeding the total recorded in all other provinces combined, with incidents peaking in March.
claims.actor_as_written: Mai-Mai Yakutumba and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups; Raia Mutomboki and other factions aligned with Yakutumba
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: verified reports from field inquiries by UN-supported national NGOs; peak in March 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-012: Read the annex: the 325-case figure is province-wide, gathered by UN-trained national NGOs, follows a sentence on under-reporting in areas under DRC Government control, and is not attributed to Yakutumba; the Yakutumba escalation is dated only 'the recent months' (report of December 2025), not January-June. The original statement and actor field fused the two; separated them. The actor field should not attach the 325 cases to Yakutumba.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): verified reports from field inquiries by UN-supported national NGOs; peak in March
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/858 annex 38 (UN and humanitarian sources; field inquiries by national NGOs trained by the UN). The annex says underreporting is significant in Government-controlled areas and the slight decline in May-June was linked to documentation constraints.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that Wazalendo armed groups in South Kivu entrenched systems of control through an expanding network of roadblocks across Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, where civilians were compelled to pay fees and were subjected to extortion, abuse, sexual violence and summary execution, with at least 12 roadblocks on a 60-kilometre stretch of the RN5 between Uvira and Luvungi.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Source says 'entrenched systems of control through an expanding network', not 'set up an expansive network'; wording aligned.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/858 para. 82 and annex 38. Fee range given in annex: 5,000 to 50,000 Congolese francs. Humanitarian actors reported major impact on their freedom of movement.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reproduced statistics from a UN source on conflict-related sexual violence for July and August 2025 that list M23 as the main perpetrator, surpassing the FARDC and Wazalendo, with a significant number of minor girls among the victims; it also reported that, according to United Nations human rights monitoring statistics, between April and October 2025 AFC/M23 was listed as the main perpetrator of summary executions, responsible for approximately 45 per cent of all summary executions reported across the country.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu and South Kivu (eastern DRC)
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: statistics reproduced from a UN source 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: summary-execution figure from UN human rights monitoring statistics 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-027: Attribution drift: the retained S/2025/858 annex credits the sexual-violence statistics to an unnamed 'UN source', not specifically to 'UN human rights statistics'; the figures also cover all DRC conflict-affected provinces, not only the Kivus. Amended to the wording the annex supports.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): statistics reproduced from a UN source; summary-execution figure from UN human rights monitoring statistics 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: S/2025/858 para. 80 attributes the 45 per cent figure to 'United Nations human rights monitoring statistics'; the statement dropped that attribution. The sexual-violence statistics are in an annex credited to a 'UN source – July and August 2025'.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/858 annex 37 and para. 80. The SV statistics are charts; the annex text only is quoted. The 45 per cent figure covers the whole DRC.

claims.text: Reuters (via VOA) reported that U.N. Human Rights Office spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani said in a statement that M23 fighters raided CBCA Ndosho Hospital and Heal Africa Hospital in Goma during the night of 28 February, taking 116 and 15 patients respectively (at least 130 sick and wounded men); the abducted men were suspected of being Democratic Republic of Congo soldiers or members of a pro-government militia known as Wazalendo. Reuters said M23 spokespersons Willy Ngoma and Lawrence Kanyuka Kingston did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
claims.place_as_written: Goma (CBCA Ndosho and Heal Africa hospitals), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23 (as named by the UN Human Rights Office)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact and support the figures; byline shows Reuters wire, so credited to Reuters relaying OHCHR; added statement date. Original OHCHR release not fetched, so B. VOA page is Reuters wire copy ('By Reuters', 3 March 2025; the UN statement was issued on Monday 3 March). Amnesty International (18 March 2025, same unit) dates the raids to the night of 28 February and the morning of 3 March and gives 'more than 130'; OHCHR as relayed gives only the night of 28 February. The page also quotes Shamdasani: M23 was 'holding them incommunicado in undisclosed locations'. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: article by Reuters 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: at least 130 sick and wounded men, Goma 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: M23 spokespersons did not respond 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-003: Attribution is right, but the claim leaves out the M23 response line on the same retained page (no comment), and it should be credited to Reuters relaying OHCHR, as the verifier noted. Dates and Heal Africa count differ from the Group of Experts (1 and 3 March; 48 from Heal Africa) and Amnesty (28 Feb and 3 March); keep these as a surfaced discrepancy, not merged.; excerpt-support: added excerpts for the Reuters byline, the 'at least 130 sick and wounded men' total, and the M23 no-comment line 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 5 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 6 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Statement dated by 'night of Feb. 28' per source. Original OHCHR press release (ohchr.org, 3 March 2025) could not be fetched by the page helper; VOA relays UN statement.

claims.text: Lawrence Kanyuka, political spokesperson of AFC/M23, said the UN statement was false because those arrested in the hospitals were FARDC soldiers who had gone there to hide.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and the translation is faithful ('Umuryango w’Abibumbye' = United Nations). Shamdasani is printed on the page; passage given. Party account (AFC/M23). Umuseke is a Rwandan outlet. Date is the article date (6 March 2025); the page does not date Kanyuka's statement. The page also quotes him saying the operation to find '130 FARDC soldiers' hiding in hospitals was carried out peacefully and in line with international humanitarian law.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan account (AFC/M23 spokesperson), as relayed by Rwandan outlet Umuseke; the page says the UN statement was on Monday 3 March 2025.

claims.text: Amnesty International reported that Sultani Makenga, M23's military chief, said in an interview that Congolese army members in hospitals posed as patients or carers, that M23 found 14 weapons in hospitals and that hospital staff alerted them.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; attribution chain preserved. Party account relayed by Amnesty; the interview itself and its date were not located. Amnesty adds that Makenga said M23 arrested those who were not part of the hospital.
claims.researcher_note: Makenga's own interview not located; relayed by Amnesty (undated 'recently'; Amnesty release is 18 March 2025). Date is report date.

claims.text: Amnesty International said on 18 March 2025 that, since taking Goma in January, the Rwanda-backed M23 had raided hospitals, abducted patients from their beds (civilians and hospitalised Congolese soldiers) and subjected them to torture.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; documented by a major NGO. Amnesty interviewed 25 victims, witnesses and others. It dates hospital raids to the night of 28 February and morning of 3 March (more than 130 taken to a stadium, some tortured). 'Rwanda-backed' is Amnesty's wording. M23 disputes (see counterclaims).
claims.researcher_note: Amnesty documented the allegation; M23 denies (see counterclaims). Amnesty's wording 'Rwanda-backed' is Amnesty's.

claims.text: The WHO reported that, since 26 January, 3082 injured and 843 dead had been reported from 31 health facilities in and around Goma, and 65 injuries from 3 hospitals in South Kivu.
claims.place_as_written: Goma and surroundings, North Kivu; South Kivu hospitals
claims.verification_note: WHO's own press release; excerpt exact. WHO is the publisher, so naming it is supported by the page. Cumulative figures reported by facilities to WHO, 26 January to 7 February 2025; WHO said they were expected to rise.
claims.researcher_note: Report date used; figures are as reported by facilities to WHO, cumulative from 26 January.

claims.text: Dr Sidibe Abdurahman, emergency physician at CBCA Ndosho hospital, said, as quoted by DW, that since January the hospital had received more than 1,000 patients against a capacity of 146 beds and was totally overwhelmed.
claims.verification_note: 'told DW' narrowed to 'as quoted by DW' (page uses 'explique'); '1000' flag is only number formatting. Single hospital physician quoted by DW (byline Ruth Alonga, 3 February 2025). The figure is printed '1.000' (French thousands separator).
claims.researcher_note: Capacity context for hospital overload after the fall of Goma.

claims.text: The ICRC reported, from a study of health facilities in the Kivus, that three fifths of the facilities surveyed had experienced looting since the intensification of the conflicts.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; 'CICR' = ICRC, the publisher. ICRC study of 109 health centres in North and South Kivu, April-May 2025 (press release 17 June 2025). Perpetrators of looting not identified.
claims.researcher_note: Press release of 17 June 2025; perpetrators not identified; sample size not in excerpt.

claims.text: The ICRC reported that the majority of medical facilities noted a halving of consultations of children under five in the first quarter of 2025 compared with the same period in 2024, and quoted an observed increase of more than 4 times in the number of stillbirths in the facilities covered by the assessment, particularly in North Kivu.
claims.verification_note: Stillbirth figure is a quote from Etienne Penlap, now attributed; halving was 'noted by the majority of facilities', narrowed accordingly. Assessed facilities only (109 health centres), not province-wide. Press release of 17 June 2025; the stillbirth quote is from Etienne Penlap, ICRC health coordinator in DRC.
claims.researcher_note: Assessed facilities only, not province-wide.

claims.text: Louvain Coopération reported that on 9 March 2025 the general hospital of Walungu, South Kivu, one of its partners, was hit by numerous rounds of bullet and rocket fire; five people, patients and health staff, were injured, one seriously; it said the causes of the attack remained uncertain.
claims.verification_note: Added victim categories (patients and staff) and the source's own uncertainty on cause; page also confirms 'Hôpital général'. Single NGO partner source; the page states the causes are uncertain and names no perpetrator. The page says M23 then controlled Walungu territory, which is context, not attribution. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified contradicting source(s) recorded in notes; not regraded pending review. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Single NGO partner source; perpetrators not stated in the excerpt. Contradicting reporting: Radio Okapi (2025-03-10): Claim says five injured; Radio Okapi says at least five dead.

claims.text: UN News reported, in a passage it quoted without naming the speaker, that in South Kivu the number of wounded exceeded the capacity of the hospitals and health centres of Kalehe and Minova.
claims.verification_note: Statement attributed the quote to WHO, which the page does not do; removed the WHO attribution. Article of 29 January 2025. The page places the quote under a WHO subheading but does not attribute it to WHO; the WHO representative (Boureima Hama Sambo) is quoted separately on hospitals being overwhelmed generally. The page adds that the most serious cases were referred to the Bukavu general referral hospital. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
claims.researcher_note: Report date. Figures field limited to what the excerpt supports; none stated.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that it documented eight cases of rape by M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers against women in and around Uvira during the occupation that began in December 2025.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and Rwandan forces, as alleged by Human Rights Watch
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and matches statement. Occupation dates (10 Dec 2025 - 17 Jan 2026) and the 120 interviews (March-April 2026) are printed on the page: 'from December 10, 2025, days after the signing of the United States-brokered Washington Accords , until their withdrawal on January 17, 2026' and 'is based on over 120 interviews conducted in March and April 2026'. HRW summary also says 'raped at least 8 women'. Documented NGO investigation -> A.
claims.researcher_note: HRW wrote to the Government of Rwanda and to Bertrand Bisimwa (head of the M23) and received no responses (HRW). Survivors are not named in the excerpt. Occupation 10 Dec 2025 to 17 Jan 2026 per HRW.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that survivors of sexual violence in Uvira spoke of a near-total lack of accessible health services during the M23 and Rwandan occupation, in particular the absence of timely HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) and of adequate care for injuries and infections resulting from sexual violence.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (occupying forces were M23 and Rwandan forces per HRW)
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; statement matches. The '8' flag refers to the figures field, which HRW prints ('eight cases of rape'). Survivors' accounts of absent care; HRW does not attribute the lack of care to a deliberate act by any party.
claims.researcher_note: Describes survivors' accounts of absent care, not a finding of deliberate denial.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that it documented the summary execution of 53 civilians by the M23 and Rwandan forces in Uvira, most on December 10, 2025, and that the forces went door-to-door seeking men and boys accused of ties to the Wazalendo.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and Rwandan forces, as alleged by Human Rights Watch
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact on the HRW page; '50' is in the page summary ('summarily executed more than 50 people during door-to-door searches'). HRW's summary says 'more than 50'; the body gives 53 documented executions.
claims.researcher_note: Excerpt supports the 53 figure and date; the door-to-door element is in a separate HRW sentence cited below.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that the M23 abducted civilians into their forces during the Uvira occupation and that, in at least 12 documented cases, their whereabouts remain unknown.
claims.actor_as_written: M23, as alleged by Human Rights Watch
claims.verification_note: Exact; statement matches excerpt. HRW's summary describes these as 'forcibly disappeared at least 12 people' (HRW's words).
claims.researcher_note: No individuals named in the excerpt.

claims.text: AFPDE reported in a humanitarian alert, citing reports from partner structures, that the territories of Uvira and Fizi faced a wave of violence marked by the systematic looting of health infrastructure from 5 December 2025. Elsewhere the same alert gives a total of 7 health structures neutralised, and it dates the Kabimba incident '15/01' with no year.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that a 32-year-old woman was raped and then killed by armed men on a date it gives as 'mardi le 13 juillet' in Kamituga, South Kivu, and that, according to civil-society sources, her body was found in the morning in the Kalinga quarter. The Association des femmes journalistes engagées pour la paix (AFJEP) said the rape was committed by unidentified persons and called for an investigation.
