The source does not attribute the rapes or the looting of the Muliki health centre to either party, and does not say in which chiefdom Muliki lies. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-006: The draft put the Muliki looting under 'according to civil society', but the page narrates the damage itself (see the verifier note on sibling claim r1-SV-NK-2025-004); separated, and the absence of attribution for rapes and looting made explicit. No search.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; checked the retained page, which names no perpetrator for the rapes or the looting
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet citing civil society; perpetrators of the rapes and of the looting are not attributed in the passage. The rapes are recorded here only as part of the civil-society tally; no survivor is named. Muliki is placed in Bwito chiefdom by inference from the article's list of affected groupings only in the sense that it is in the affected area; the page does not state the territory of Muliki explicitly.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the toll of the ADF attack in Byambwe/Biambwe, Lubero territory, on the night of Friday 14 November was revised from 20 to 28 killed, including 17 patients executed at the reference health centre, per Lubero territory administrator colonel Kiwewa Mitela Alain, who called the figures provisional. A caregiver quoted by Actualite.cd said the maternity ward and operating theatre were burned and medicines looted, and that 17 people including four breastfeeding women were executed in their hospital beds.
claims.place_as_written: Biambwe/Byambwe health centre, Lubero territory (Biena health zone), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: ADF (Allied Democratic Forces, called islamistes ADF by Actualite.cd)
claims.verification_note: Single outlet (one credible origin with an official and a health worker); graded B on its own sources rather than A. Figures provisional and vary across sources (Vatican News: 15 in the clinic and 5 nearby; UN News/MONUSCO: 17 shot in the health centre). The page headline says 'une dizaine de patients'.
claims.researcher_note: Headline of the page says 'une dizaine de patients' while the body says 17 patients; the body text is cited. Initial reports gave 18 (AFP via TV5Monde/La Libre) and later ~29-30 (AA, Congo Rassure); figures vary by source and are provisional. Place is spelled Byambwe in the body text and Biambwe in the headline/URL. See also UN News (next claim) and Vatican News.

claims.text: UN News reported that, according to information gathered by MONUSCO, at Byambwe 17 people were shot dead in a health centre, including women patients who had come to give birth, and that in other localities (Mabiango, Tunarudi, Sambalysa) homes were burned, civilians abducted and medical supplies looted, in a wave of ADF attacks that killed at least 89 civilians in Lubero territory between 13 and 19 November.
claims.place_as_written: Byambwe health centre; Mabiango, Tunarudi, Sambalysa; Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Supported. Graded B: UN News relaying MONUSCO information, not a published investigation.
claims.researcher_note: UN News relays MONUSCO information; the 89 figure is stated in the page's lead-in text (the same sentence appears as the article's standfirst). Independent of Actualite.cd's local sources, though both may derive from local health staff.

claims.text: UN News reported that UN Secretary-General António Guterres, in a press release, 'fermement condamné' (strongly condemned) the attacks attributed to the ADF in North Kivu and expressed his condolences to bereaved families, and that the UN Security Council, in a statement, reaffirmed its 'détermination' to support the peace process and demanded humanitarian access that is 'total, sûr et sans entrave'.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu (statement issued at UN headquarters)
claims.verification_note: Grammar fixed; the Security Council clause rested only on the page, now given as a replacement quote. The page says both statements came 'samedi'; 22 November 2025 is computed from the weekday and the 24 November publication date.
claims.researcher_note: The article (24 November, Monday) says the statements came 'samedi'; that implies Saturday 22 November, computed from the weekday and the publication date. Context statement by a mediator-side body; recorded because the Lubero toll includes the health-centre killings.

claims.text: Vatican News reported that at around 10:00 PM on Friday ADF militants entered the town of Byambwe and attacked a diocesan health centre run by the Sisters of the Presentation, massacred patients and set the facility ablaze, killing several women in the maternity ward. Italian missionary Fr Giovanni Piumatti, who confirmed the attack to Vatican News, was quoted as saying fifteen people were killed in the clinic and another five in the surrounding area, that the attackers set fire to the facility and twenty-seven nearby homes, and that they looted all the medical supplies.
claims.place_as_written: Byambwe diocesan health centre (Diocese of Butembo-Beni), Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: The narrative of the attack is Vatican News's own; only the toll, the burning of homes and the looting are Piumatti's words. Attribution split. Graded C: a relayed, second-hand account. Second-hand account from a missionary now in Italy; figures differ from Actualite.cd (28 killed incl. 17 patients) and UN News/MONUSCO (17 shot in the health centre).
claims.researcher_note: Second-hand account: the missionary is in Italy and relays information; figures differ from Actualite.cd (28, incl. 17 patients) and UN News (17 shot in the health centre). Kept as a separate claim because the figures conflict. 'Friday' = 14 November computed from the 16 November publication date and the other sources.

claims.text: UN News reported, citing OCHA's health cluster, a worsening cholera outbreak in and around Goma, with at least 420 cases and 1 death over two consecutive weeks (3 to 15 February), more than a third of the 1,280 cholera cases recorded in North Kivu since the start of the year, and suspected cholera cases in the MONUSCO camp in Goma where disarmed FARDC members had taken refuge, with one death and 24 suspected cases under treatment.
claims.place_as_written: Goma and surroundings; MONUSCO camp in Goma, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not applicable (epidemic context following M23/AFC capture of Goma)
claims.verification_note: '1,280' is the page's '1.280'. Graded B: UN News relaying cluster data, one origin. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 4 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Figures are OCHA/health-cluster reporting relayed by UN News; Actualite.cd (2025-02-24) gives a different, more cautious count for the MONUSCO camp ('une vingtaine de cas dont un décès'); not merged. The article does not attribute the outbreak to a cause.

claims.text: UN News reported that the health cluster said three mpox treatment centres had been destroyed at Kalehe, Minova and Miti Murhesa as a result of bombings.
claims.place_as_written: Kalehe, Minova and Miti Murhesa (Kalehe territory), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: The 2-8 February range came from an unrelated mpox caseload sentence; the source dates only the report. Marked as a related event outside the unit's province. The source gives no date for the destruction or the bombings, and no perpetrator; the date is the report date. South Kivu (Kalehe territory), outside this North Kivu unit. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Outside North Kivu (South Kivu, Kalehe territory); recorded here as an epidemic-response effect found while researching the North Kivu cholera claim.

claims.text: UN News quoted Dr Boureima Hama Sambo, WHO Representative in DRC, as saying that WHO aid teams 'cannot move freely to support the hospitals, even ambulances cannot run', calling it a public-health nightmare, and he warned that mpox patients had fled at least one camp's treatment centre and were living in host communities.
claims.actor_as_written: not applicable (M23 advance on Goma; M23 fighters in control of a significant portion of the city per UN agencies)
claims.verification_note: Quoted statement; not a finding on who blocked access. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
claims.researcher_note: Statement of a WHO official, 29 January (Wednesday per the article); the quote is not a finding of who blocked access. The page spells 'Representive' and 'living now in'.

claims.text: Insecurity Insight reported, in an attacks-on-health-care news brief, that since late January reports had increased in North Kivu as M23 rebels expanded control, attacking ambulances and looting vital medical supplies, and that in one incident a baby in an incubator at Virunga General Hospital in Goma was injured by an M23-fired bullet that pierced the ceiling of the neonatal unit during clashes between M23 and the Congolese army.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu; Virunga General Hospital, Goma
claims.verification_note: Brief's date range removed from the statement (it is in the source title). Insecurity Insight is a compiler; its attribution of the bullet to M23 is its own and stays attributed. Monitor summary of open-source reports; the brief gives no date, place or source for the ambulance and looting incidents. Its global figures (247 incidents in 20 countries, 1 January-17 March 2025) are not North Kivu figures. 2026-10-28: confidence edited: red-team rt-002: The 'M23 fired bullet' attribution rests only on a compiler's brief (Insecurity Insight) that gives no source. A search for the incident found contemporaneous reports (UNICEF DRC Facebook post about an 18-day-old baby, Faraja; social posts from about 27 January 2025) that describe a bullet piercing the ceiling onto an incubator in a Goma hospital, some calling it a stray bullet ('balle perdue'), without naming who fired it. Keep the attribution strictly as Insecurity Insight's; the ambulance and looting clause is also undated and unsourced.
claims.researcher_note: Monitor summary built from open-source reports; the page gives no dates, places or sources for the ambulance and looting incidents (the event-level data sits in the HDX dataset, which no longer carries descriptions). The global figures are not North Kivu figures. ReliefWeb page, original published 1 Apr 2025.

claims.text: The EastAfrican reported that the AFC (Congo River Alliance) 'strongly denies' the UN human rights office's allegations of attacks on hospitals, saying it never targeted civilian establishments, that the UN mission MONUSCO had manipulated the details, and that its raid was aimed at securing medical infrastructure it said had been infiltrated by fighters; the AFC claimed the heads of the hospitals corroborated in the operation.
claims.place_as_written: Goma, North Kivu (CBCA Ndosho and Heal Africa hospitals)
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; the 'never targeted ... manipulated' clause added as a replacement quote. Graded B for the fact of the statement, from a credible outlet. Party statement (AFC/M23): what the AFC said, not a finding. The OHCHR said on 3 March that M23 fighters took 116 patients from CBCA Ndosho and 15 from Heal Africa in the night of 28 February (quoted by the same article).
claims.researcher_note: Party statement reported by a Nation Media Group correspondent in Kigali; recorded as what the AFC said, not as fact. The headline says M23 'admit attacks on hospitals', but the text has the AFC denying the allegations while describing a 'raid' to secure the infrastructure; the article does not clarify the fate of the abducted patients. Existing claim r1-HC-2025-002 records the AFC spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka's version via Umuseke; this is an additional outlet. The OHCHR statement itself (3 March) could not be fetched by the retrieval helper (via=none), so only the EastAfrican's quote of it is used.

claims.text: Radio Télévision Communautaire la Référence (RTCR) reported that in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 25 June 2025 presumed armed bandits visited several homes and the Centre hospitalier La Providence in the Kamesimbonzo quarter, Bulengera commune, Butembo, and that, according to John Kameta, president of the Bulengera communal civil-society core, two of the bandits came into the hospital around midnight and took one hundred thousand Congolese francs belonging to patients, as well as telephones.
claims.place_as_written: Centre hospitalier La Providence, Vukonderya cell, Bulengera commune, Butembo, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: 'présumés bandits armés' (RTCR); not linked to any armed group by the source
claims.verification_note: Kameta's title corrected to the page's wording ('président de la société civile noyau communal de Bulengera', not 'coordinator'); his name was on the page only, now in a replacement quote. Criminal incident; the source does not link it to any party to the conflict.
claims.researcher_note: Criminal incident in an M23-free area (Butembo), not linked to the armed conflict by the source; recorded for completeness on obstruction of health care. Radio Okapi, Radio Moto and Congo Quotidien also reported it on 26 June (seen in search results, not fetched/cited). Local community radio, one civil-society source.

claims.text: Insecurity Insight, citing Radio Maendeleo, reported that on 10-11 August 2025 the Ludaha Health Centre in Ludaha village, Cirunga group, Kabare territory, South Kivu, was looted overnight by armed men who took medical equipment including a microscope, a printer, telephones and money; nurses and other health workers were also attacked while treating patients.
claims.place_as_written: Ludaha village, Cirunga group, Kabare territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed men (not further identified by the source)
claims.verification_note: Page (PDF p.1) prints the entry verbatim with 'Source: Radio Maendeleo'. Single origin relayed by a monitor; Radio Maendeleo original not fetched.
claims.researcher_note: Aggregated monitor entry; original report is Radio Maendeleo (not fetched). Perpetrator not attributed.

claims.text: Insecurity Insight, citing Radio Maendeleo and RTR, reported that on 11 August 2025 in Katana village, Kabare territory, South Kivu, a hospital under construction was destroyed by the local population, who also looted the residence of the vice-president of the Senate, and that AFC/M23 rebels had reportedly asked residents to attack his properties because, according to them, he was serving his individual interests.
claims.place_as_written: Katana village, Kabare territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: local population; AFC/M23 reportedly asked residents to act (as reported by the source)
claims.verification_note: Supported; reworded to keep the M23 instigation as the source's 'reportedly', and lowercase title to match the excerpt (which prints 'VicePresident'). C: unverified instigation claim relayed by a monitor. The AFC/M23 instigation is 'reportedly' in the source and unverified; the vice-president of the Senate is not named by the source. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: sources cited: Radio Maendeleo and RTR 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-017: Searched (FR) for other accounts of the 11 August Katana looting. Radio Okapi (12 Aug 2025, page not retained; seen only as a cached extract, so it must be fetched and verified before use) says residents of Katana looted property of senator Bahati Lukwebo at the 'site SMAL', a four-storey building under construction, in a zone under M23 control, and that 'the exact reasons ... remain unclear, according to local sources'. It does not call the site a hospital or report any M23 instigation. Kivu Morning Post (social-media snippet) speaks of destitute neighbours looting after the departure of soldiers. The M23 instigation therefore rests on one monitor relay, and a more direct report says the motive is unclear; the statement should carry that counter-account.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): sources cited: Radio Maendeleo and RTR | cut the Radio Okapi sentence (senator Bahati Lukwebo, SMAL site, reasons unclear) and its pending note: the claim cites no Radio Okapi page
claims.researcher_note: The AFC/M23 request to residents is 'reportedly' and unverified here. The facility was a hospital under construction, not an operating one.

claims.text: Insecurity Insight, citing La Prunelle and Radio Okapi, reported that on 14 August 2025, around 7pm, the water tank at Panzi General Hospital in Panzi district, Ibanda commune, Bukavu, was damaged amid heavy gunfire by unidentified gunmen; the leak flooded a large part of the hospital grounds and disrupted medical activities. It added that a fruit vendor was shot and killed by a stray bullet.
claims.place_as_written: Panzi General Hospital, Panzi district, Ibanda commune, Bukavu, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Both passages are in the same entry on PDF p.1, credited 'Sources: La Prunelle and Radio Okapi'. Both sources are the same page and one relay; not two origins. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Originals (La Prunelle, Radio Okapi) not fetched; a site:radiookapi.net search returned zero results.

claims.text: Insecurity Insight reported that on 6 November 2025 in Kasheke village, Kalehe territory, South Kivu, three health workers from the General Reference Hospital were attacked and seriously injured by M23 rebels on accusations of treating Wazalendo fighters and their families, and the medical director was evacuated to Bukavu for intensive care treatment.
claims.place_as_written: Kasheke village, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23 rebels (as reported by Insecurity Insight)
claims.verification_note: Entry on page verbatim. Graded C (not B): the M23 attribution rests on two little-known local outlets not fetched, with no other cited corroboration. Perpetrator attribution rests on two small local outlets (Info Plus, Le Haut Panel) relayed by a monitor; not independently corroborated. AFC/M23 account not found.
claims.researcher_note: Originals (Info Plus, Le Haut Panel) not fetched. Facebook snippets (not cited) mention a Kasheke health-centre director beaten by M23. The AFC/M23 account was not found.

claims.text: Insecurity Insight, citing only unnamed personal communications, reported that on 22 November 2025 in Katana town, Kabare territory, South Kivu, the Chahoboka Health Centre was attacked by M23 members when they raided the town, and four people, including two health workers and a patient, were taken outside and shot and killed.
claims.place_as_written: Chahoboka Health Centre, Katana town, Kabare territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23 members (as reported by Insecurity Insight)
claims.verification_note: Text confirmed on the ReliefWeb page and on the PDF (pp.1-2), where the entry ends 'Sources: Personal Communication and Personal Communication II'. Judged strictly: anonymous single-channel origin, so C and the statement now states the sourcing. No corroboration found in one extra search. Unverified lead: the monitor's only sources are two unnamed personal communications. No media, UN or NGO corroboration found (a verifier search on 'Chahoboka Katana' found none); uncited social-media posts reportedly give a different toll and night. AFC/M23 account not found. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified contradicting source(s) recorded in notes; not regraded pending review. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: The monitor's named sources are 'Personal Communication' only: single-origin, not independently verified. No Radio Okapi, Actualite.cd or OCHA page found (only Facebook-group snippets, not cited). Needs corroboration; the AFC/M23 account was not found. Contradicting reporting: Agence Fides (2025-11-25): Gives 23 November (about 22:00) and three people killed, not 22 November and four.

claims.text: Insecurity Insight, citing OCHA DRC, reported that as of 17 November 2025 a shipment of medicines belonging to an international organisation was blocked at Baraka port, Fizi territory, South Kivu, delaying operations and causing a shortage of medicines and supplies in the health facilities the organisation supported.
claims.place_as_written: Baraka port, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Entry verbatim on PDF with 'Source: OCHA DRC'. 17 November 2025 is the report date; the blocking date and the party that blocked the shipment are not given.
claims.researcher_note: Date is the report date ('As reported 17 November 2025'); the blocking date and the party responsible are not given.

claims.text: Insecurity Insight reported that Forces de défense nationales du Burundi (FDNB) soldiers stopped a truck of a local NGO transporting materials to support medical facilities in the fight against cholera in South Kivu and forced it to turn back, despite an intervention by provincial authorities in Uvira.
claims.place_as_written: South Kivu (provincial authorities in Uvira intervened); exact place not given
claims.actor_as_written: FDNB soldiers (as named by the source)
claims.verification_note: Sentence on PDF p.4 with footnote 3 = incident 113648. Single sentence, single source. Date, location of the stop and the NGO are not given; event dated only to 2025 by the report's scope. Burundi's account not found.
claims.researcher_note: Annual report; the date, place of the stop and the NGO are not stated. Report date given as May 2026 (publication) for the chapter; the event is in 2025. Burundi's account not found. The expansion of FDNB as a Burundi force is the source's elsewhere in the chapter; the statement uses the name as printed.

claims.text: Insecurity Insight reported that in March 2025 M23 fighters occupied a hospital in South Kivu and installed artillery to defend themselves against attacks from local armed groups.
claims.place_as_written: a hospital in South Kivu (not named by the source)
claims.actor_as_written: M23 fighters (as reported by the source)
claims.verification_note: Sentence on PDF p.5, footnote 6 = incident 121172. Hospital unnamed.
claims.researcher_note: Hospital and place not named; the dataset row (incident 121172) was not retrievable here.

claims.text: Insecurity Insight reported that in South Kivu five health workers and four patients, including one child, were killed when a hospital was hit by shelling of an unidentified origin.
claims.place_as_written: a general hospital in South Kivu (not named by the source)
claims.actor_as_written: shelling of unidentified origin (per the source)
claims.verification_note: The cited excerpt says 'a hospital'; 'general' comes from a separate passage (p.4, footnote 5, same incident 96787), so the statement is narrowed to the excerpt. Hospital and date not named. Elsewhere the same report calls it 'a general hospital in South Kivu' (same incident 96787). Possibly the 9 March 2025 Walungu Hospital shelling, but the UN Fact-Finding Mission gives five killed including two children; the tolls differ and the link is not established. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: none_found; added 0 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2 verified counter-reporting source(s) recorded in notes.
claims.researcher_note: Possibly the same event as the 9 March 2025 Walungu hospital shelling (Louvain Coopération; UN Fact-Finding Mission), but the report names neither hospital nor date, so the link is not asserted. The tolls differ between sources and are not merged. Counter-reporting: Radio Okapi (2025-03-10): Figures and victim categories differ (5 patients killed vs 5 health workers + 4 patients killed incl. a child); source attributes the shell to M23 whereas claim says unidentified origin. Only relevant if same event.; Louvain Coopération (2025-03-20): Five people wounded, none reported killed, vs nine killed in the claim. Only relevant if same event.

claims.text: The UN Fact-Finding Mission on North and South Kivu reported that on 9 March a shell reportedly hit the pediatric ward of Walungu Hospital, killing five people including two children.
claims.place_as_written: Walungu Hospital, Walungu territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source in this passage
claims.verification_note: Para 28 of A/HRC/60/80 prints it verbatim; UN investigation so A, hedge kept. The UN report words this as 'reportedly' and does not attribute the shell. Toll differs from the Insecurity Insight hospital-shelling figure (five health workers and four patients).
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates the existing Walungu claim (HC-2025-009, Louvain Coopération) and supplies the UN figure. The report words it as 'reportedly' and gives no attribution in this passage.

claims.text: Insecurity Insight reported that between February and November 2025, 41 health workers were kidnapped in 20 incidents in eastern DRC, and that half of the recorded kidnapping incidents occurred in South Kivu, most of them in the Kalehe and Shabunda territories.
claims.place_as_written: Eastern DRC; half of incidents in South Kivu, mostly Kalehe and Shabunda territories
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed in these passages (the report elsewhere says mainly accusations of supporting armed groups, and ransom demands)
claims.verification_note: Both sentences on PDF p.5. Aggregate; perpetrators not named.
claims.researcher_note: The 41 figure is for eastern DRC; the South Kivu share is given only as half of recorded incidents, not a count of victims. Perpetrators are not named in the excerpts.

claims.text: Insecurity Insight reported that, among health workers kidnapped in eastern DRC in 2025, a nurse was raped then kidnapped by men armed with guns and taken away to an undisclosed location.
claims.place_as_written: Eastern DRC (place not given by the source)
claims.actor_as_written: men armed with guns (not further identified)
claims.verification_note: Sentence on PDF p.5, footnote 12 = incident 123714. Scope (South Kivu) not established, kept as a lead. Province and date not given; the case sits in the eastern-DRC kidnapping paragraph and may not be in South Kivu. Lead only (dataset incident 123714).
claims.researcher_note: Province and date not given. It sits in the kidnapping section, where half the incidents were in South Kivu, but South Kivu is not stated for this case. Recorded as a lead only.

claims.text: Actualite.cd, in an article on an OCHA bulletin, wrote that in June 2025 consignments of medicines intended for health structures in the Minembwe and Itombwe health zones in South Kivu were blocked at Mulima (45 km north of Fizi centre) for about two months.
claims.place_as_written: Mulima (45 km north of Fizi centre), serving the Minembwe and Itombwe health zones, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed actors present on the roads (OCHA, as reported); not named in this passage
claims.verification_note: Removed 'released in November 2025' (not in the excerpt) and softened 'reporting' to 'in an article on', because the Mulima passage is in the outlet's context section rather than a direct OCHA quote. The passage sits in the article's 'Contexte' section, not inside a quotation from OCHA. The same article says the main axes were closed 'en raison de la présence d’acteurs armés' and that armed actors met at Point Zéro in August 2025 reaffirmed their refusal of humanitarian access; no party is named. Kivu Morning Post relays the same Mulima point. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: OCHA's wider finding (access to Minembwe, Itombwe and Hauts Plateaux 'extremely limited, even almost impossible'; armed actors met at Point Zero in August 2025 reaffirmed refusal of humanitarian access) appears in the same article but is not in the excerpt. OCHA names no party here. The OCHA original was not fetched.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post, relaying an OCHA communiqué, reported that the health system in the Minembwe area was on the verge of collapse with a prolonged shortage of medicines, and that at Minembwe General Reference Hospital between July and September 2025 more than 60% of deaths concerned children.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe General Reference Hospital, Minembwe, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not applicable (access restriction; armed presence on roads per OCHA)
claims.verification_note: Page attributes to an OCHA communiqué; excerpt verbatim. The excerpt_en flag is a translation artefact (Hôpital Général de Référence rendered in English); translation covers the excerpt only. Actualite.cd, relaying the same OCHA bulletin, gives the count as 25 of 40 deaths. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 source_type edited: variant spelling of the existing key partisan_afc_m23 (party account of AFC/M23 vice-governor Gaddy Mukiza, relayed by Radio Maendeleo) 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Relay of the OCHA communiqué; the OCHA original was not fetched. The article also says that since January 2025 these areas saw armed clashes, attacks on civilians and looting of health structures by armed groups, and that since May the region has been almost wholly isolated.

claims.text: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) reported that heavy violence and clashes broke out in Uvira in February 2025 between the Congolese army (FARDC) and their presumed allies, the Wazalendo fighters, and quoted a mother who said they heard gunshots inside the hospital where her 10-month-old son was admitted at the mpox treatment centre of Uvira General Hospital.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira General Hospital, Uvira, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: clashes between FARDC and Wazalendo (as described by MSF); who fired inside the hospital is not stated

claims.researcher_note: Period of the abductions not stated; date is the December 2025 publication (visit "last month"); survivors not named. Exact territory of interviewed survivors not stated; Lubero/Beni inferred from the visit context only, so treat territory as unconfirmed.

claims.text: An Amnesty International researcher wrote that witnesses told her ADF fighters arrived at Byambwe as a nondescript group including women and children, asking for directions to the local hospital, after which gunshots rang out at the medical facility, and that in total the fighters killed more than 30 people, including 17 at the health facility.
claims.verification_note: Date narrowed to what this source supports (month). Clauses verified on the page. Amnesty gives no date for the Byambwe attack; it occurred during the researcher's visit to North Kivu 'last month' relative to the 19 Dec 2025 article, i.e. November 2025. The 14-15 Nov date came from other claims. Tolls differ by source: Amnesty more than 30 (17 at the health facility); Actualite.cd at least 15 patients and their guards; 7sur7.cd civil society about ten. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 3 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. Regraded B->A on independent, non-partisan corroboration. 2026-10-29: source 4 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Byambwe attack already recorded in existing claims (GOE-033, HC-NK-2025-012/014/015); this adds the NGO witness account and a differing toll. Date from existing claims; the page says Byambwe attack without a date in these excerpts.

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported, citing local civil society, that five reference health centres in Lubero territory, in the Manzia and Mwenye groupements, had stopped operating because of repeated ADF attacks; the head of Biambwe civil society, Nzanzu Achille, said that since the Biambwe attack the health centres of Biambwe, Biena, Kaumo, Masengi and Masoyi were closed.
claims.place_as_written: Biambwe, Biena, Kaumo, Masengi and Masoyi (Lubero), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; the name Nzanzu Achille and the groupement names are printed on the page (not in the stored excerpt), passages given here. Local civil-society account relayed by 7sur7.cd (correspondent Bantou Kapanza Son, Beni). The civil-society leader puts the Biambwe toll at about ten, lower than other sources. The retained page carries unrelated injected spam links in its footer; the article text itself is intact.
claims.researcher_note: Local civil society sources, per 7sur7.cd, interviewed on Thursday 20 November 2025. Toll quoted by the civil society leader ("une dizaine") differs from other sources.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that after the ADF attack on the Biambwe hospital, health services in the Biena and Manguredjipa health zones were slowed, and an anonymous health worker of the Biena health zone said colleagues were hesitant to resume work for fear for their safety.
claims.place_as_written: Biena and Manguredjipa health zones (Butembo-Manguredjipa axis, Lubero), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page. The same article reports that five of six doctors at Manguredjipa general hospital left for Butembo, and that the Biambwe health centre was attacked and burned. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Single anonymous health-worker source named only as an employee. The article headline gives the toll for Biambwe as at least 15 patients and their guards killed.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that fighting broke out on Sunday 26 October at Kalangira, in Baswagha chiefdom, between armed youths identified as Wazalendo and AFC/M23 rebels; according to the North Kivu governor the FARDC were not involved, and the incident was reportedly linked to an attempt to free three notables abducted five days earlier by an AFC/M23 official.
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; conditional kept as 'reportedly'. FARDC non-involvement is the North Kivu governor's account only (Kinshasa side). The abduction link is conditional in the source ('serait lié'). No AFC/M23 account found. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 27 Oct 2025, carries every clause, with the link to the release attempt in the conditional ('serait lié'), as the statement keeps; the stored excerpt lacks that sentence, added here.
claims.researcher_note: Date of the event: Sunday 26 October 2025 stated in the page. Detention claim is a relayed allegation (conditional "serait lié"). The governor is a military governor of the Kinshasa side (his name is not in the excerpt).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the North Kivu governor denounced the installation of new AFC/M23 positions at Vuvatama and Kanyamitala, warned of the risk of a resumption of hostilities and reaffirmed the FARDC's determination to defend their positions in case of attack.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verified; governor's words reported, attribution intact. Government (North Kivu governor) account only; the new AFC/M23 positions are his allegation. No AFC/M23 or Rwanda statement found. Date is the article date; the statement's own date is not given.
claims.researcher_note: Government claim only; the AFC/M23 account was not found. The same article states a Ugandan-army buffer zone had been deployed for eight months to contain the rebels' advance towards Lubero-Centre.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Kalangira clashes took place near the buffer zone controlled by the Ugandan army, deployed for eight months to contain the rebels' advance towards Lubero-Centre.
claims.place_as_written: Buffer zone south of Lubero-Centre (Lubero), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Category was unit_commander; this is an actor-presence/control item, recategorised with a control field. Radio Okapi's own description; not a statement by Uganda. The buffer zone's extent is not given.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi's own statement; Ugandan role in Lubero is also an actor-presence lead. Not an official statement from Uganda.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that large AFC/M23 reinforcements had been reported since Sunday 15 March in the south-west of Lubero territory, where the rebels had occupied many villages for several months; that, according to its sources, vehicle shuttles carrying men and materiel had been observed for about two weeks at Mbingi and at Bunyatenge; and that security sources confirmed the arrival of the reinforcements and said it could be preparation for offensives against FARDC and Maï-Maï positions in the Kanyabayonga groupement.
claims.place_as_written: Mbingi and Bunyatenge (Batangi chiefdom), Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Original statement placed Mbingi/Bunyatenge inside the 15 March clause; the page ties those villages to the separate two-week shuttle observation by Actualite.cd's sources. Narrowed and split. excerpt_en flags are English weekday capitalisation only. Single outlet relying on unnamed sources. The page dates the reinforcements 'since 15 March' but says the vehicle shuttles at Mbingi and Bunyatenge had been seen for about two weeks; the two time frames are kept separate.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet, anonymous 'sources'. Date is the Sunday named in the text (15 March 2026). Same page also reports AFC/M23 reinforcements at Kashebere and Kibati in Walikale (not claimed here).

claims.text: Anadolu Agency, relaying Radio Okapi citing security sources, reported that AFC/M23 rebels began moving out on Monday from several villages in Lubero territory that they had occupied for more than a year, and that after leaving Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese they were said to have set up camps in the Alimbongo, Kirumba and Kanyabayonga areas.
claims.place_as_written: Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi, Kipese; Alimbongo, Kirumba, Kanyabayonga; Lubero territory
claims.verification_note: Both passages on page (AA / Kigali / James Tasamba byline). Figure '23' is only the inferred date, not in the statement. Statement keeps the relay chain and the conditional. Date is inferred: AA's piece is dated 27 March 2026 (a Friday) and says 'lundi', taken as 23 March; approximate. AA relays Radio Okapi; the 'camps' clause is conditional ('auraient').
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('lundi') and the AA piece of Friday 27 March 2026 (Monday = 23 March). AA is a relay; original Radio Okapi item not opened. Wire credit: AA / Kigali / James Tasamba. Pairs with the Governor's statement claim. Compare with the 15 March reinforcement report (Actualite.cd): reinforcements at Mbingi/Bunyatenge were reported eight days earlier.

claims.text: Anadolu Agency reported that North Kivu Governor Evariste Kakule Somo told local media in Lubero on Thursday that he had observed an 'effective withdrawal' from several areas, called on the population to stay calm and said the rebel movement was part of 'the implementation of the peace agreements, notably those negotiated under US auspices'.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC (North Kivu provincial governor)
claims.verification_note: Passage verbatim on page; replacement extends the excerpt to include 'Plus tôt jeudi' so the weekday in the statement is carried. Official statement by the North Kivu provincial governor, known only through AA's relay of local media. 'Jeudi' in a piece dated Friday 27 March 2026 is taken as 26 March (approximate). The same AA piece reports no official Kinshasa communication on separate M23 drone allegations at Mikenke.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from 'Plus tôt jeudi' in a piece dated Friday 27 March 2026 (Thursday = 26 March). The same AA piece says no official communication from Kinshasa on M23's drone allegations at Mikenke (South Kivu; not claimed here). No AFC/M23 statement on the Lubero withdrawal found in this unit's searches.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that at least fourteen houses, a health centre and part of the Catholic church of Musenge, Baswagha chiefdom, south Lubero territory, were burned on Monday 26 January at around 20 heures (as printed) in an attack attributed to the ADF, and that two soldiers died during the army's counter-attack; Lubero territory administrator Colonel Alain Kiwewa was quoted as saying that no civilian death had been recorded so far and that the village had been emptied of its population.
claims.place_as_written: Musenge village, Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; corrected to add the administrator's verbatim quote (name was not in the stored excerpt) and to remove the Actualite.cd figure (25) from this claim's figures. Internal date/time inconsistency surfaced. CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS, kept separately: Radio Okapi (26 Jan) dates the attack to Monday 26 January about 20:00 and quotes the administrator as saying no civilian was killed; Actualite.cd (27 Jan) dates it to the night of 24-25 January and cites local 'forces vives' for at least 25 civilians killed. Radio Okapi's page is timestamped 26/01/2026 11:28, earlier than the 20:00 time it gives for an attack 'ce lundi', so the printed date may be wrong. Neither account is preferred here.
claims.researcher_note: CONFLICT: Radio Okapi dates the attack to the evening of Monday 26 January; Actualite.cd (27 January) quotes the same administrator dating it from the night of 24 January and local 'forces vives' dating it to the night of Saturday 24 to Sunday 25 January and counting at least 25 civilians killed. Radio Okapi's 'no civilian killed' is the administrator's account only. Not reconciled here.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the village of Musenge, Baswagha chiefdom, was attacked in the night of Saturday to Sunday 25 January 2026, in attacks it attributed to ADF fighters, and that according to local 'forces vives' at least 25 civilians were killed, 63 houses burned, two motorbikes burned and one person seriously wounded.
claims.place_as_written: Musenge village, Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Figures verbatim on page. Corrected to carry the page's own ADF attribution (it opens the article), to remove the Radio Okapi figures from this claim's figures, and to give the night as a date range. CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS, kept separately: Radio Okapi (26 Jan) quotes the Lubero administrator as saying no civilian was killed; this Actualite.cd account (27 Jan) cites local forces vives for at least 25 civilians killed. Actualite.cd's own headline says 'une dizaine de civils', which also differs from the 25 in its body text. Victims unnamed.
claims.researcher_note: CONFLICT with the Radio Okapi claim on the same village (date 26 vs 24/25 January; no civilian deaths per the administrator vs 25 per forces vives). Perpetrator attribution is made by the article's framing and by the administrator quoted in the next claim, not in this excerpt. Victims unnamed.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Lubero territory administrator Colonel Kiwewa Mitela Alain said that since the night of 24 January 2026 the ADF had carried out a deadly attack on Musenge village, burning almost the whole village, a health centre and a Catholic church, and that two soldiers were found burned.
claims.place_as_written: Musenge village, Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: ADF (as stated by the Lubero administrator)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim; replacement extends it to the sentence naming the administrator and the 'provisional' toll. Name and figures now carried by the stored passage. Same administrator as in the Radio Okapi item (spelled 'Alain Kiwewa' there), here dating the attack from the night of 24 January; toll described as provisional. See the conflicting Musenge accounts. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified counter-reporting source(s) recorded in notes. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates the Radio Okapi item that a Musenge health centre was burned. Same page reports that five health structures (Mausa, Pombi, Mandelya, Musenge, Masoya referral centre) closed in Mwenye groupement; that point is already held by r1-ATR-NK (actualite.cd 26 Jan). Counter-reporting: Radio Okapi (2026-01-26): Date: Radio Okapi says "ce lundi 26 janvier" (possibly publication day), others say the evening of Saturday 24 January. Also says the two soldiers died in the army counter-attack, not that they were found burned.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, according to the president of Bapere civil society Kakule Kagheni Samuel, six more bodies were found on Monday, bringing to 21 the number of civilian victims of the attack attributed to the ADF at Mambimbi-Isigo (Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector), carried out in the night of Friday 6 to Saturday 7 February 2026; several people remained missing.
claims.place_as_written: Mambimbi-Isigo, Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: All clauses verbatim. Replacement extends Actualite.cd's excerpt to the opening paragraph carrying the place, ADF attribution and 'missing'. Grade B on one credible non-partisan origin, not A. Both outlets rest on the same origin (Bapere civil society president); SOS Médias Burundi (Goma, 11 Feb) follows Actualite.cd's article point by point and is not independent. Victims unnamed.
claims.researcher_note: SOS Médias Burundi (Goma dateline, 11 Feb) repeats the same civil-society figure and appears to relay local reporting; not independent of Actualite.cd. The same Actualite.cd page also reports displacement towards Njiapanda and unburied bodies. Distinct from the 1-2 January 2026 Lubero attack (15-16 dead per other outlets), which this unit did not open.

claims.text: Actualite.cd, in a passage saying that ADF violence had also intensified in neighbouring Beni territory, reported that six civilians were killed in an ambush at Malibo on the Oicha–Mamove road in the evening of 'mardi 4 février 2026' (as printed; that weekday and date do not match), a few hours after another ambush on the same stretch that killed four others, making at least ten civilians killed in a single day on that road, where several motorbikes were also burned.
claims.place_as_written: Malibo, Oicha-Mamove axis, Beni territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: ADF (per Actualite.cd's framing; the passage does not name the perpetrator of the ambushes themselves)
claims.verification_note: Figures verbatim. Corrected: the statement now carries the outlet's ADF framing as framing, keeps the weekday mismatch explicit with the printed French, and gives the date as a range. DATE DISCREPANCY: the source prints 'mardi 4 février 2026', but 4 February 2026 was not a Tuesday; the ambush may be 3 or 4 February. SOS Médias Burundi's 12 Feb piece also gives 4 February and at least six dead at Malibo, but follows Actualite.cd closely. Possible overlap with the civil-society report of 3 February. Victims unnamed.
claims.researcher_note: DATE FLAG: 4 February 2026 was a Wednesday, but the source prints 'mardi 4 février'; the day may be 3 or 4 February. The article was published 10 February and the attack may be the one counted in the civil-society 3 February report already held (r1-ATR-NK-2026-011), which would make it a likely overlap. The excerpt does not name the perpetrator of this ambush.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Ntoyo health centre, Lubero territory, had reopened and resumed its activities five days earlier, six months after a deadly attack attributed to the ADF; that it had been forced to close after the attack of 8 September 2025, which local authorities said killed more than 100 civilians; that a large part of its medical equipment and medicines had been looted or destroyed in that incursion; and that consultations remained limited by shortages of medicines and equipment, which deputy head nurse Joseph Lungabo said complicated care for residents who had returned.
claims.place_as_written: Ntoyo, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Corrected: removed 'March 2026' (no excerpt prints it) and the 'about five days before publication' gloss; added Bapere and the shortages clause from passages now stored. Reopening is dated only as 'five days' before the 17 March 2026 article (about mid-March 2026; month precision). The 8 September 2025 attack itself is outside this unit.
claims.researcher_note: Reopening date computed from 'depuis cinq jours' in a piece published 17 March 2026 (about 12 March). The underlying September 2025 attack is outside this unit's period and is held by other rounds; this claim records the 2026 consequence (closure for ~6 months, looting of supplies, shortages).

claims.text: Amnesty International reported that it interviewed five women and two girls who were abducted by the ADF and forced into 'marriages', and that interviewees mentioned incidents of sexual violence by ADF fighters towards women and girls outside of 'marriage'.
claims.place_as_written: ADF camps and affected areas, eastern DRC (report covers North Kivu and Ituri)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on the English page (source language is en, not fr). Figures narrowed: removed the '6 of 7 pregnant' detail, which no stored excerpt carries. Documented NGO investigation (Amnesty says it researched in North Kivu in November 2025 and documented attacks in Ituri and North Kivu). The incidents are not dated or located individually; the report was published 5 May 2026. Survivors unnamed. Amnesty's own legal characterisations are not adopted here. 2026-10-29: source 0 language edited: QA 0.4 A3: the stored excerpt is English (Amnesty International English text) but the source was tagged fr
claims.researcher_note: Report published 2026-05-05; incidents are not individually dated or located in this excerpt and may span 2025-2026 (the report also cites August and November 2025 attacks). Province/territory assigned from the report's North Kivu focus; location is approximate. Survivors unnamed in the report. Grade A proposed as a documented NGO investigation, verifier to decide.

claims.text: Amnesty International reported that the ADF has repeatedly attacked health facilities and raided supplies, and that in November 2025 a health centre in the village of Byambwe was targeted, with at least 17 civilians killed and four wards set on fire.
claims.place_as_written: Byambwe village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Statement verbatim-supported. Corrected only the location (Lubero not printed by the page) and source language (en). The Amnesty page does not say which territory or province Byambwe is in; the Lubero placement in the draft came from elsewhere and is not supported here. The event (November 2025) falls outside this unit's period; this records the May 2026 NGO documentation. 2026-10-29: source 0 language edited: QA 0.4 A3: the stored excerpt is English (Amnesty International English text) but the source was tagged fr
claims.researcher_note: Byambwe's location in Lubero territory is not stated in this excerpt (Actualite.cd's Facebook page lists a Byambwe health centre in Lubero; not opened). Other rounds may already hold the November 2025 attack; this is the 2026 NGO documentation of it.

claims.text: Radio Moto Butembo (RMBB) reported that the flagrante-delicto hearing of the Butembo garrison military tribunal against four people, two of them Wazalendo, continued on Wednesday 24 June 2026 at the Kitulu roundabout, Mususa commune, Butembo; that the defendants were being prosecuted for criminal association, abduction and extortion; and that they were accused of having arrested Egyptian itinerant traders and 9 other Congolese citizens, including 6 girls, on Monday 22 June at Wayene and taking them, some tied up, to the Kafekit compound, where some were subjected to torture.
claims.place_as_written: Wayene, Bulengera commune; Kafekit compound; trial at Kitulu roundabout, Mususa commune, Butembo
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (two of the four defendants) and two civilians, as accused
claims.verification_note: Corrected: 'charged ... for arresting' changed to prosecuted/accused as printed; added the defendants' names exactly as Radio Moto prints them (policy v1); removed Radio Elimu's '3 Egyptians' from this claim's figures. Defendant names are on the page but not in the stored excerpt, so the script refuses them in the statement; they are in the note and extra.entities_named; suggest add_excerpt for source 0 so they can be restored. Radio Moto names the defendants as Nzanzu Mushakulu Boika and Katembo Madisha Joel (both Wazalendo) and Kambale Kapupa Gédéon and Kasereka Mukama Jean-Baptiste (both civilians); the names sit on the page outside the stored excerpt (see replacement_quotes). Prosecution stage only on 24 June: accused and prosecuted, not convicted (see the Radio Elimu claim for the 25 June judgment). Defendants' names are spelled as Radio Moto prints them; Radio Elimu UOR spells two differently (NZANZU MUSYAKULU Boika, KATEMBO MADIRISHA Joël). Victims unnamed. Radio Moto does not give the number of Egyptians.
claims.researcher_note: Local outlet (RMBB, Butembo). Accusations are those of the prosecution as reported; victims are unnamed. Defendant names are spelled differently by Radio Elimu UOR ('NZANZU MUSYAKULU Boika', 'KATEMBO MADIRISHA Joël'); see the trial-outcome claim. The Egyptian nationals' company is named 'FUDA' by Radio Elimu.

claims.text: Radio Elimu UOR (Butembo) reported that the Butembo garrison military tribunal sentenced to death on Thursday 25 June 2026 four defendants (named in the source and listed in entities_named), whom the prosecution had pursued, two of them as Wazalendo, for criminal association, abductions followed by torture, and extortion, in the case of the abduction of 3 Egyptians and 9 Congolese; the defence said it would appeal.
claims.place_as_written: Vuhakatwa, Wayene quarter, Bulengera commune, Butembo city
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (two of four defendants) and two civilians, as convicted by the tribunal
claims.verification_note: Corrected 'the defence was appealing' to the stated intent to appeal; the 22 June date and Vuhakatwa place are not in the stored excerpt, so they moved to the note and location; suggest add_excerpt for source 1 so they can return to the statement. Defendants as Radio Elimu prints them: NZANZU MUSYAKULU Boika, KATEMBO MADIRISHA Joël, KAMBALE KAPUPA Gédéon, KASEREKA MUKAMA Jean-Baptiste. Radio Elimu places the events on Monday 22 June 2026 at Vuhakatwa, Wayene quarter, Bulengera commune, Butembo (page passage in replacement_quotes, outside the stored excerpt). First-instance judgment of a military garrison tribunal; the defence 'promet d’interjeter appel' (has said it will appeal to the North Kivu Military Court), not an appeal already lodged. Names spelled as Radio Elimu prints them; Radio Moto spells two differently (Nzanzu Mushakulu Boika, Katembo Madisha Joel). The page does not say which two defendants were Wazalendo.
claims.researcher_note: Judicial outcome reported by a single Butembo radio (Radio Elimu UOR, Université Officielle du Ruwenzori). Spelling of two defendants' names differs from Radio Moto's 24 June report. The wider article states the defence will appeal; no statement from FARDC or Wazalendo leadership on the case was found.

claims.text: Grands Lacs News reported that between 1 and 4 January 2026, armed clashes broke out between Wazalendo factions in the Bashu chiefdom and north of Butembo city, pitting the group of self-proclaimed general Tango Fort against the Maï-maï Wazalendo RNL led by Baraka Lolwako, with a certain Fiston Nzoli reportedly involved, and that according to local sources several Tango Fort camps at Kitovo, Misugho and Rwamiso were burned.
claims.place_as_written: Bashu chiefdom (Kitovo, Misugho, Rwamiso) and north of Butembo, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo factions: Tango Fort group vs Maï-maï Wazalendo RNL (Baraka Lolwako); Fiston Nzoli
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; replacement extends the excerpt to carry the burned-camps clause. Single outlet relying partly on anonymous local and security sources. The page spells the camp both 'Rwamiso' and 'Lwamiso'. An unnamed armed chief's death is reported 'in this context'. The economic motive is the outlet's and its sources' interpretation. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Grands Lacs News (7 Jan 2026, Fred Mastaki) supports every clause; the burned-camps clause is in the sentence after the stored excerpt and is added. The same sentence also reports the death of an armed leader presented as a warlord.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet (Grands Lacs News, Fred Mastaki), partly citing anonymous local and security sources. Chiefdom of Bashu is in Beni territory. A reported death of an armed chief is not named. The article attributes the fighting to competition over mining and taxation, which is the outlet's interpretation.

claims.text: Grands Lacs News reported that the Synergie Wazalendo Front Grand Nord claimed the January 2026 operations against Tango Fort, saying it wanted to neutralise him and his supporters, accused of illegal detentions, torture, killings and arbitrary taxation, and that it welcomed the release of at least 11 illegally detained people, including minors, during the attack on the Lwamiso camp.
claims.place_as_written: Lwamiso camp, Bashu chiefdom, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Synergie Wazalendo Front Grand Nord (claim); Tango Fort group (accused)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; attribution to the party kept throughout. Partisan: a claim by a Wazalendo coalition about a rival faction, usable only as 'Synergie Wazalendo Front Grand Nord says'. The accusations against Tango Fort and the release figure are the coalition's, not established. No statement from Tango Fort's group found.
claims.researcher_note: Party claim by a Wazalendo coalition about a rival faction; the outlet itself says the real stakes were economic. The detainees are unnamed. No statement from Tango Fort's group found.

claims.text: Agence congolaise de presse (ACP) reported, in a dispatch from Lubero, that three large agglomerations of Lubero territory (Kanyabayonga, Kayina and Kirumba) are occupied by M23 rebels supported by Rwanda.
claims.place_as_written: Kanyabayonga, Kayina, Kirumba (Lubero territory), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23 rebels, described by ACP as supported by Rwanda
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports the attributed statement; state-media source on a contested fact, so partisan and C. ACP is Congolese state media; the occupation of the three places and Rwandan support are ACP's own wording, recorded as the DRC government side's account.
claims.researcher_note: Incidental sentence at the end of an ACP (state news agency) dispatch about a health walk in Lubero-centre; Lubero-centre itself not described as M23-held. Frontline claim only for the three named places; consistent with the Radio Okapi/ACP pattern since June 2024. Speaker framing 'rebelles du M23 soutenus par le Rwanda' is ACP's own wording.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that, in Lubero where the AFC/M23 permanent secretary was visiting development projects, he told residents of Kanyabayonga that they would not be abandoned and said: 'we are still here, we are going nowhere', rejecting social-media claims that the group would leave.
claims.verification_note: Removed 'Kigali-based' (not in the excerpt). Party statement, C. Party statement (AFC/M23) relayed by Bwiza (by Denis Nsengiyumva, dated 19 Nyakanga 2026); the Kanyabayonga remarks are not dated on the page. The page names the permanent secretary as Benjamin Mbonimpa ('Umunyabanga Uhoraho, Benjamin Mbonimpa'), outside the stored excerpt: extend the excerpt to add the name.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan statement relayed by a Rwanda-focused outlet; page dated 19 July per search listing (page body gives no explicit date).
