claims.researcher_note: Partisan: cited only for what Rwanda said. Excerpt is a single contiguous passage; check word count.

claims.text: UN News (Swahili) reported that Mr Lacroix, speaking to journalists, confirmed the deaths of three MONUSCO peacekeepers (one from Uruguay, two from South Africa) and wished a quick recovery to 12 other peacekeepers wounded during clashes with M23 rebels.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 (as described by the source: 'waasi wa M23')
claims.verification_note: The page names him in full as Jean-Pierre Lacroix, head of UN peacekeeping operations (replacement quote), but the stored excerpt prints only 'Bwana Lacroix'; extend the excerpt to name him in full. 'watatu' = three. Narrowed 'said 12 were wounded' to the source's wording (wished recovery to 12 wounded). The page links the wounding, not explicitly the three deaths, to clashes with M23.
claims.researcher_note: Context event (MONUSCO). Figures as of 27 January 2025 briefing; later totals may differ. Excerpt is 50-60 words; translation provided.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that at least 19 soldiers from South Africa, Malawi and Tanzania were killed when the M23 took the city of Goma in January.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 (as the capture's actor per the source)
claims.verification_note: Exact; publication date 29 March 2025 confirmed on page. Mubambiro appears on the page only as a location of SADC bases, not of the deaths.
claims.researcher_note: Publication date taken from search result (2025-03-29, approximate); verify. The page also lists a SADC-M23 meeting attended by Sultani Makenga; names not cited here. SAMIDRC are SADC troops (context).

claims.text: Studio Hirondelle reported that Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, at a briefing in Kinshasa on 3 February, speaking of the massacre and carnage committed in Goma, said that his colleague the Health Minister had been told by his services that morning that there were more than 2,000 bodies to bury.
claims.verification_note: Clarified who was informed (the Health Minister, by his services), per the full quotation. Page ends 'Studio Hirondelle RDC, avec AFP' - credited accordingly. Removed year (not printed in the passage).
claims.researcher_note: The page also prints provisional figures of nearly 3,000 dead and about 2,880 wounded (not attributed in that sentence; not recorded here). Excerpt begins mid-quotation. Figures conflict with BBC English (at least 700 killed per UN and government) - see next claims.

claims.text: BBC News Afrique reported that the UN said at least 2,900 people were killed in the fighting, that 2,000 bodies had been buried and that 900 others were still in the city's morgues.
claims.actor_as_written: Fighting between M23 and FARDC and allies, as described by the source
claims.verification_note: Exact ('2 900' with a space). Figures conflict across sources (BBC English: at least 700; Muyaya: more than 2,000 bodies); unclear whether combatants are included.
claims.researcher_note: Conflicts with the BBC English figure (700 killed per UN and government) and with the Rwandan government's later characterisation of '3,000 casualties' as exaggerated (not collected here). Unclear whether the 2,900 figure includes combatants.

claims.text: BBC News reported that at least 700 people in Goma were killed and close to 3,000 injured as the rebels clashed with the DR Congo army and its allies, according to the UN and the Congolese government.
claims.actor_as_written: Fighting between M23 and the DRC army and allies, as described by the source
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (brief rule; page date 3 February 2025 shown with the source). Lower than other contemporaneous figures (2,900 per UN in BBC Afrique of 6 Feb).
claims.researcher_note: Published date from search result (3 Feb 2025). Figure is lower than the BBC Afrique / Muyaya figures: report all three.

claims.text: BBC News Afrique reported that, according to an internal UN document it consulted, between 165 and 167 women were assaulted by male detainees during the escape from Munzenze prison in Goma, and that most of the women were killed after detainees set fire to the prison; the BBC said it could not verify the information.
claims.place_as_written: Munzenze central prison, Goma (city), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: male detainees per an internal UN document, as reported by BBC
claims.verification_note: All clauses on page; caveat kept. BBC could not verify the UN document. 'Lundi dernier' plus 'after M23 began to seize the city' points to 27 January, but the range is kept.
claims.researcher_note: BBC (published Thursday 6 Feb 2025) says the escape was 'lundi dernier'; this is either Monday 27 January or Monday 3 February, so the date is given as a range (AFP of 27 Jan reported the prison 'totalement incendiée' after a mass escape, which points to 27 Jan; verify). Survivors are not named by the source. Headline attributes the figures to the UN; body says an internal UN document seen by the BBC.

claims.text: Belga, in La Libre, reported that a local official told the German news agency DPA that at least 160 female detainees were raped during an escape from the Goma prison; Belga added that it was not yet known whether the rapists were escaped prisoners, M23 rebels or members of other local militias.
claims.place_as_written: Munzenze central prison, Goma (city), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not established: escaped prisoners, M23 or other local militias (source says unknown)
claims.verification_note: The 'not yet known' sentence is the agency's own narration, not the official's; reworded so it is not attributed to the official. Origin of source 1 set to Belga (not BBC). Anonymous local official via DPA: C.
claims.researcher_note: Wire/relay: page carries a Belga credit and says the BBC saw the UN document and DPA quoted a local official (originating sources DPA and BBC). Restricted to single-origin. The page calls M23 a 'milice'.

claims.text: UN News reported that the destruction of prisons caused by the offensive led to the escape of many prisoners from the central prisons of Goma and Bukavu, and also in Kabare in South Kivu; Patrice Vahard, director of the BCNUDH, said in an interview with UN News on Wednesday evening that escapees may include people imprisoned for atrocities, notably rape and gender-based violence.
claims.place_as_written: Goma (city), North Kivu; Bukavu and Kabare, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23 offensive (as described by the source)
claims.verification_note: Misattribution fixed: the prison-destruction sentence is UN News narration, not Vahard's words; Vahard's quote is the escapee risk. The escapes themselves date from late January (Goma) and mid-February (Bukavu); 2025-02-19 is the interview date.
claims.researcher_note: Interview on the Wednesday before 20 Feb (Wed 19 Feb); date computed from weekday and publication date. Covers both provinces; Bukavu/Kabare belong to South Kivu units.

claims.text: MSF's emergency coordinator in Goma said that on Wednesday 29 January, the first day the fighting had eased, the team received nearly 140 wounded at the hospital triage, many of whom were hospitalised, and that wounded people who had stayed at home had been unable to access care until then.
claims.actor_as_written: fighting in Goma (M23, Congolese army and respective allies, per MSF)
claims.verification_note: All on page; hospital is Kyeshero per page context ('MSF teams were working in Kyeshero hospital').
claims.researcher_note: Interview-style statement of MSF's emergency coordinator (MSF is named in the page title, not in the excerpt; 'we' in the excerpt is MSF per the page). Hospital is Kyeshero (stated in the page's preceding text, not in this excerpt).

claims.text: The Guardian reported that Chadrack Kabumba, 20, was treated at Virunga hospital for bullet wounds to his knee and shoulders after being shot four times on his way to check whether his property had been vandalised, the day after M23 entered Goma.
claims.verification_note: Date corrected from 28 to 27 January: the same Guardian page says M23 entered the city on 26 January, so 'the day after' = 27 January (approximate). The page also names another patient, Mamy Esther, 40 (pelvic injury in a bombing; lost her six-year-old son) - not part of this claim; lead for victim names. Shooter not identified by the source. Date approximate.
claims.researcher_note: 'The day after M23 entered Goma' - date computed from the Guardian's own framing (entry 26/27 Jan per other sources) so approximate. Named victim aged 20 (adult).

claims.text: Amnesty International said on 18 March 2025 that armed M23 fighters stormed the Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals in Goma on the night of 28 February and the morning of 3 March and abducted more than 130 people, including Congolese soldiers (some wounded) and health workers, who were taken to a stadium where some were tortured. Amnesty also reported that M23 military chief Sultani Makenga had said in an interview that Congolese army members in the hospitals were posing as patients or carers, that M23 had found 14 weapons in hospitals and that hospital staff had alerted them, and that M23 had arrested those who were not part of the hospital.
claims.place_as_written: Heal Africa hospital and CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Amnesty documented research (25 interviews stated on page): A. More specific than existing r1-HC-2025-004 (same page), not a duplicate. OHCHR second origin not retrieved. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Makenga's justification 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-003: Attribution is right, but Amnesty's own page carries M23's justification (Makenga), which the claim leaves out (check 8). The Group of Experts later reports witnesses saying no weapons were found (r1-GOE-055), so the two accounts should sit side by side.; excerpt-support: added Amnesty's passage on Sultani Makenga's interview as an excerpt
claims.researcher_note: Amnesty's own research (25 interviews). OHCHR press release of 3 March and Reuters/AP exist (search results) but their pages could not be retrieved by the page helper, so they are not cited; the UN figure is 'at least 130 sick and wounded men'. Check for an independent second origin (OHCHR) in the verification round. health category: patients_removed / health_worker_harmed.

claims.text: Actualite.cd, relaying Amnesty International, reported that armed M23 fighters burst into the Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals in Goma on the night of 28 February and the morning of 3 March, abducting more than 130 people including wounded Congolese soldiers and health workers who, according to Amnesty, were taken by force to a stadium where some were tortured. Actualite.cd also reported that M23 military chief Sultani Makenga said some of the abducted soldiers had posed as patients or carers, that his group had found 14 weapons in the hospitals, and justified the abductions by saying medical staff had reported the presence of Congolese soldiers.
claims.place_as_written: Heal Africa hospital and CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Stadium/torture clause is on the page but not in the stored excerpt; supplied as replacement quote. Not independent of r1-HC-2025-004 (same Amnesty origin). Relay of Amnesty's 18 March release; not an independent origin. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: stadium and torture, according to Amnesty 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Makenga's justification 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-003: The stadium/torture clause had no stored excerpt in the input; I found it on the retained Actualite.cd page ('Selon l'organisation...'), so it holds but is attributed to Amnesty. The same page carries Makenga's justification, which the claim omits (check 8). Relay of Amnesty, not an independent origin.; excerpt-support: added two excerpts: the stadium/torture sentence ('Selon l'organisation...') and Makenga's justification 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
claims.researcher_note: Relay of the Amnesty release (not independent); health-care angle of the same event as the preceding claim. 'a dénoncé Amnesty International mardi' = Tuesday 18 March.

claims.text: Amnesty International said humanitarian organisations had reported a sharp rise in rape and sexual violence in North Kivu and South Kivu, and that victims told it they were raped by M23 fighters and threatened with death; in one account, a woman said M23 fighters suspected her of being a spy and five armed fighters in military uniforms raped her collectively; in another case, two men in Congolese military uniform raped a pregnant woman and abducted her husband.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu and South Kivu (places of individual cases not stated in the excerpts)
claims.actor_as_written: M23 fighters; two men in Congolese military uniform (per Amnesty)
claims.verification_note: The draft placed the victims' accounts 'in North Kivu and South Kivu'; the page gives the two provinces only for the humanitarian reports of a rise, so the geography is now attributed to that sentence. B (testimonies without place/date) rather than A. Places and dates of the individual incidents are not given; survivors unnamed. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
claims.researcher_note: Report date 2025-03-18; incident dates and places not given. Survivors are unnamed in the source. Amnesty's line 'Le M23 et l'armée congolaise... doivent répondre de ces viols' appears on the page. The preceding sentence of the page places the humanitarian reporting of rises in North Kivu and South Kivu.

claims.text: UN News reported that UNFPA's country representative Mady Biaye said that the 895 rape cases reported by UNHCR for the first half of February concerned only survivors who received medical care at the 23 UNFPA-supported sites in Goma.
claims.verification_note: Name 'Mady' and 'first half of February' are on the page (supplied). Graded B: UN-reported data in a news interview, not a documented UN investigation. Counts are of survivors reaching care at supported sites; a floor, not a total. No perpetrator attributed.
claims.researcher_note: Original data from UNHCR (announced Monday 3 March per the page) and UNFPA. UN News translation-neutral; no perpetrators attributed in these passages; counts are of survivors reaching care and are a floor. Excerpt 1 is 57 words. Survivors unnamed.

claims.text: UN News reported looting of contraceptives, damaged health centres and depleted aid stocks as sexual violence proliferated in eastern DRC, with tens of thousands of women and girls struggling to access emergency care; UNFPA's DRC representative Mady Biaye said UNFPA health infrastructure in Goma had been damaged by the fighting and its Goma warehouse looted (no perpetrator named). The article set the US decision in January to suspend almost all foreign aid programmes for three months against these difficulties; Biaye said the US had been due to contribute 10 million dollars in 2025 for contraceptives in the DRC, 'Mais tout ça c'est arrêté', and the article notes that contraceptive stock-outs were already being felt.
claims.place_as_written: Eastern DRC (North Kivu and South Kivu; places not itemised in the excerpt)
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (brief rule). The 'meant' causal link is the standfirst's juxtaposition; kept as UN News framing. Standfirst-level summary; places and dates of looting not given. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Mady Biaye, UNFPA DRC representative 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Goma infrastructure damaged; warehouse looted 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: US aid suspension; contraceptive funding stopped 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: contraceptive stock-outs 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-027: The standfirst juxtaposes looting/damage and the access problem; the retained page (UN News, 8 March 2025) gives the concrete basis: UNFPA representative Mady Biaye said UNFPA health infrastructure in Goma was damaged by fighting and its Goma warehouse 'littéralement pillé' (no perpetrator named), and links contraceptive stock-outs in part to the US aid suspension. 'meant' overstates causation; the specifics make the claim stronger and more precise.; excerpt-support: added 4 excerpt(s): Mady Biaye, UNFPA DRC representative; Goma infrastructure damaged; warehouse looted; US aid suspension; contraceptive funding stopped; contraceptive stock-outs | replaced 'linked contraceptive stock-outs in part to the US suspension of foreign aid' (the page does not print Biaye making that link in one passage) with what the page prints
claims.researcher_note: Standfirst of the article; geography is 'eastern DRC'; the text identifies Goma-based sites later. Dates of the looting are not given. Consider the UNFPA claim as the basis; look for the underlying UNFPA/OCHA report for place and date.

claims.text: Studio Hirondelle reported that on 3 February 2025 the rebels unilaterally declared a ceasefire 'because of the humanitarian crisis caused by the Kinshasa regime', to take effect on 4 February, and said in a communiqué circulated notably on X that they had 'no intention of taking control of Bukavu or other localities'.
claims.verification_note: Exact; page credited 'Studio Hirondelle RDC, avec AFP'. 'Les rebelles' = AFC/M23 in page context. Fighting resumed in South Kivu on 5 February per the same page.
claims.researcher_note: Communiqué relayed by the outlet; original post on X not opened. The same page reports fighting resumed in South Kivu on 5 February (Nyabibwe) - South Kivu unit.

claims.text: Studio Hirondelle, citing AFP, reported that Patrick Muyaya told AFP that this was proof that the unilateral ceasefire decreed was, as usual, a decoy.
claims.place_as_written: Eastern DRC (reaction to ceasefire declared 3 February)
claims.verification_note: Fixed a stray ',.' and kept the quote's context (5 February fighting) in the note, since the stored excerpt does not print it. 'M23's' removed (the excerpt says only 'the unilateral ceasefire decreed'); the decreeing party is the rebels per the page. Per the same page, Muyaya was reacting to fighting launched in South Kivu at dawn on 5 February by the armed group and the Rwandan soldiers supporting it (replacement quote).
claims.researcher_note: Muyaya's reaction followed the 5 February fighting in South Kivu (Nyabibwe), described in the preceding sentences of the page; place of fighting is in a South Kivu unit.

claims.text: Imvaho Nshya, a Rwandan outlet, reported that M23 deputy spokesperson Dr Oscar Balinda said the group issued a communiqué calling on FARDC soldiers hiding in houses to gather at the Goma unity stadium, and that Balinda said more than 1,500 were then taken to the military camp at Rumangabo; the outlet said the soldiers were taken there on Thursday 30 January 2025.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo military camp, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (per M23 deputy spokesperson Oscar Balinda)
claims.verification_note: All exact; kept attributed to Balinda. M23 account via a Rwandan state-owned paper; the page frames it as surrender and political training. Not independently corroborated.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan Rwandan state-owned paper relaying M23; treat as 'M23 says'. The page frames the soldiers as having surrendered ('zishyikirije') and being taken for M23/AFC political training; coercion is neither stated nor ruled out. Needs corroboration (UN, HRW). Excerpt 3 begins inside Balinda's quotation.

claims.text: Umuseke, a Rwandan outlet, reported that FARDC soldiers began fleeing to Rubavu via the Grande Barrière border crossing on Monday 27 January 2025.
claims.place_as_written: Grande Barrière border crossing, Goma, North Kivu / Rubavu, Rwanda
claims.verification_note: Exact. The page adds that the soldiers surrendered to Rwandan security services and were searched and disarmed. Single Rwandan outlet. 2026-10-29: control edited: Frontline data fix (FRONTLINE_NOTES.md): control.held_by names only the holder (for a withdrawal, the side withdrawing), so the side class is not 'both sides named'; the other side stays in the statement. Wording from the stored excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Single Rwandan outlet's report from Rubavu; the page adds that the soldiers surrendered to Rwandan security services and were disarmed (not claimed here; see page). Corroboration from wires or UN needed. 'Rubavu' is the Rwandan town opposite Goma.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that M23 rebels retook the localities of Kishishe and Bambo in Rutshuru territory from Wednesday 14 May 2025 after fighting Wazalendo fighters, whom they dislodged from the area.
claims.place_as_written: Kishishe and Bambo, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries every clause; excerpt_en's 'Radio Okapi reported that' is framing, not translation (excerpt itself is exact). Radio Okapi says M23 had voluntarily left both places more than a year earlier. Actualite.cd (18 May) repeats the 14 May retaking, likely not independent.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet citing local sources; Radio Okapi says M23 had left both places voluntarily over a year earlier (outside window). Actualite.cd (18 May) corroborates 'since 14 May'.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that a notable of the region said two people were wounded the day before at Kishishe and that several shops were looted at Bambo; it said a large part of the population stayed confined at home during the heavy-weapon fighting.
claims.verification_note: Supported; date approximate. 'La veille' is relative to an article dated 16 May; the article also mislabels 16 May as Thursday, so the wounding date (about 15 May) is approximate.
claims.researcher_note: Date: article of 16 May says 'la veille' for Kishishe wounding (15 May); the looting date is not given. Anonymous notable.

claims.text: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) said it treated about twenty wounded people, including six serious cases and one death, after violent clashes on Thursday 15 May in and around Bambo, Rutshuru territory, between M23/AFC and Wazalendo fighters of the CMC group.
claims.verification_note: Statement supported (figures are printed in words); figures field rewritten in words to match the excerpt. Actualite.cd's 4 June article dates this MSF figure differently ('une semaine plus tôt' than 14 May), an internal inconsistency in the outlet's reporting. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: MSF communiqué relayed by Actualite.cd. See next claim for the hospital-related statement.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that MSF condemned the holding of clashes in populated areas close to care centres, regretting that gunfire hit a hospital service; the outlet said the fighting at Bambo took place close to the MSF-supported hospital and that the use of heavy weapons forced medical teams to take temporary shelter, limiting their capacity to provide emergency care.
claims.verification_note: Hospital proximity is on the page (preceding sentence), not in the excerpt; added the shelter/limited-care clause the excerpt carries.
claims.researcher_note: Source says 'hôpital appuyer par l'organisation MSF' in the preceding sentence; the statement is the outlet's report of MSF's communiqué.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, in an article on an MSF appeal, that since 15 May Bambo had been the scene of intense clashes between AFC/AFC rebels (as printed) and Wazalendo militiamen of the CMC group, which had caused more than 900 families from Bwito chiefdom to flee to the town.
claims.verification_note: Raw said the figure came 'from an MSF document'; the page does not attribute it to MSF. 'M23' removed because the excerpt prints 'AFC/AFC'. The 900-families figure is the outlet's narration, not attributed to MSF on the page; the same outlet gave the same figure on 25 May ('depuis trois semaines'). The page's lead names the rebels AFC/M23.
claims.researcher_note: Reported 4 June; the source text says 'AFC/AFC' (typo for AFC/M23). Displacement count is MSF's per Actualite.cd.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that at least 29 civilians, described as collateral victims of clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo over the previous six days, were buried on Tuesday 27 May in Kirumba, Lukarara, Rukano and Kagando villages in Rutshuru territory; six more bodies were buried at Runzenze the same day.
claims.place_as_written: Kirumba, Lukarara, Rukano, Kagando, Runzenze (Tongo and Bambo groupings), Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; figures field carried other articles' numbers, now limited to this source. Tolls differ by source and period and are kept separate: Radio Okapi 27 May (at least 14 civilians killed to 25 May, claim 8), Radio Okapi 10 June (at least 75 killed 18 May-10 June, claim 10), Bwiza.com (about 38 killed in Mutanda 26-31 May, claim 20). 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-004: Attribution matches (collateral victims of clashes, no side blamed; local sources). Amend only corrects 'civils' to 'civilians'. The URL is dated 2025/05/29 while the source date is 2025-05-28; check the page date.; excerpt-support: nothing to add
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi (27 May) gave 'at least 14 civilians killed up to Sunday 25 May'; Radio Okapi 10 June gave 'at least 75 killed' for 18 May to 10 June from regional sources. Figures differ by source and period; not merged. Perpetrator not attributed (collateral victims of clashes).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that several dozen villagers' houses were burned and that goats and other goods were reportedly looted, while young villagers were reportedly taken hostage by M23 rebels to carry these goods, in villages of the Tongo and Bambo groupings in Rutshuru territory.
claims.place_as_written: Tongo and Bambo groupings, Rutshuru territory
claims.actor_as_written: M23 (as to hostage-taking; burning not attributed)
claims.verification_note: Removed the report date (no excerpt prints 28); kept conditional wording. Looting and hostage-taking are conditional in the source; burning is not attributed to any party.
claims.researcher_note: Conditional wording in source ('auraient été', 'seraient'); local sources unnamed. Also records a detention/abduction element (porters). Dates approximate: report of 28 May about the preceding days.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that since Thursday 22 May AFC/M23 elements had been conducting an operation to hunt presumed Rwandan FDLR rebels in several villages of the Bambo, Tongo, Bukombo and Mutanda groupings in Bwito chiefdom, in particular at the edge of Virunga National Park.
claims.place_as_written: Bambo, Tongo, Bukombo and Mutanda groupings, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Single clause carried verbatim by the excerpt. 'Presumed FDLR' is Radio Okapi's framing; the same outlet and Actualite.cd describe the fighting as M23 against Wazalendo.
claims.researcher_note: The framing 'presumed FDLR' is Radio Okapi's wording; other outlets describe the same fighting as M23 against Wazalendo CMC. 'Depuis' = start date, operation ongoing at publication (28 May).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that since Thursday 22 May near-daily clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo groups had occurred in Bambo, Tongo, Bukombo and Mutanda groupings of Bwito, and that sources reported at least 14 civilians killed, dozens wounded and several houses burned up to Sunday 25 May.
claims.place_as_written: Bambo, Tongo, Bukombo, Mutanda groupings, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; figures field no longer carries the article date. Lower toll than the 29 burials Radio Okapi reported on 28 May for a slightly longer period; tolls kept separate.
claims.researcher_note: Lower toll than the 29 buried (Radio Okapi 28 May) for a slightly longer period; shown separately.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that after violent clashes between Wazalendo and M23 on the previous day, at Nyamilima in Rutshuru territory a girl of about 10 years was killed and houses were burned at Mulema (Walikale), as of Tuesday 10 June.
claims.verification_note: Supported; 'citing local sources' rests on the article's later 'Selon des sources locales'. The source does not say who killed the girl.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed: article of Tuesday 10 June says clashes began 'la veille' (9 June). Actualite.cd (9 June) also reports Nyamilima fighting. Perpetrator of the child's death not attributed. Mulema is in Walikale territory.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that in fighting in Rutshuru territory about ten houses were hit by bomb fragments and several civilians were arrested ('interpellés') by M23/AFC rebels after the Wazalendo withdrawal.
claims.place_as_written: Rutshuru territory (place of the arrests not specified in the excerpt)
claims.verification_note: Removed the date (no excerpt prints 10); added the bomb-fragment clause the excerpt carries. The page places this in the Nyamilima fighting (Rutshuru), which it dates to the day before its 10 June article. Number, names and fate of those arrested not stated.
claims.researcher_note: The exact village is not given in this sentence (context: Nyamilima fighting, 9-10 June). Names, number and fate of detainees not stated.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, according to several concurring sources, M23 elements attacked FARDC positions supported by the Volunteers for the Defence of the Homeland (VDP, commonly called Wazalendo) at Lushebere in Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory; a local youth parliament president quoted by the outlet placed Lushebere between Kishishe and Kirima and said M23 had just progressed on the Lushebere-Kishishe-Bambo axis.
claims.place_as_written: Lushebere, between Kishishe and Kirima, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Source 1 is inside the Mafula quote, not the outlet's narration; reattributed. Day number removed from the statement (no excerpt prints 25). Discrepancy: the outlet's lead places Lushebere between Kishishe and Bambo; the quoted youth leader says between Kishishe and Kirima. The same speaker calls M23 'terroristes' and says it was supported by the RDF (his claim). Date (25 May) is printed in the article lead and the testimony, not in the stored excerpts. Toll 'à vérifier'.
claims.researcher_note: The second excerpt is part of a quoted testimony by Chirac Mafula (president of the youth parliament of Bwito, then in Lubero), who calls M23 'terroristes' and alleges RDF support in the sentence before it; that allegation is not reproduced as fact. Casualties 'à vérifier'.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to a communiqué of the DRC Interior Ministry published on Saturday 12 April 2025, at least 52 people were killed in an attack described as 'organised and simulated' and attributed to AFC/M23 rebels supported by the Rwandan army.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC (Ministry of the Interior)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries the claim; attribution to the ministry retained. Government claim. Radio Okapi reports that local sources spoke of an attempted Wazalendo incursion, which the government rejects (claim 14). No AFC/M23 or Rwanda reply in this article.
claims.researcher_note: Government claim reported by Radio Okapi. Radio Okapi's same article states that local sources spoke of an attempted Wazalendo incursion to retake the city, a thesis the government rejects; the AFC/M23 account is not in this article. Clashes in the night of 11-12 April.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that local sources spoke of an attempted incursion by Wazalendo to retake Goma, while the government rejected that thesis and instead accused M23 of having orchestrated a premeditated attack against civilians.
claims.verification_note: Two attributed accounts, carried verbatim.
claims.researcher_note: Two competing accounts in one article; neither independently verified there. No AFC/M23 reaction in this article.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the official document (the Interior Ministry communiqué) listed 297 assassinations and summary executions, 72 rapes, hundreds of disappearances, more than 146 cases of bodily torture and the looting of more than 2 000 head of cattle and vehicles between 6 and 11 April 2025.
claims.place_as_written: Goma area (not specified in this sentence)
claims.verification_note: Removed the communiqué date (no excerpt of this claim prints 12). Government figures only, unverified; place and perpetrator not stated in the figures sentence.
claims.researcher_note: Government figures only; place not stated in this sentence and perpetrators are not named in it (the preceding sentence attributes the 'attack' to AFC/M23). No survivors named; no independent verification. Do not merge with BCNUDH figures.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the Congolese government, by an official communiqué of 8 May, denounced violence perpetrated by the AFC/M23 supported by the Rwandan army, citing more than 308 assassinations, 124 cases of rape, 315 cases of torture and hundreds of forced recruitments between April and May 2025.
claims.place_as_written: Goma and surrounding areas (not specified in excerpt)
claims.verification_note: Supported as government statement. Government figures only. The page attributes the 'crimes de guerre' label to the government and quotes Interior Minister Jacquemin Shabani Lukoo Bihango.
claims.researcher_note: Government figures only; the legal label 'crimes de guerre' is the government's wording as reported. Place not in excerpt. No AFC/M23 reply found in this source. Compare with the 12 April Interior Ministry communiqué (72 rapes for 6-11 April).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that MSF said, in a communiqué published Friday 11 April, that about twenty armed men affiliated with M23/AFC entered the compound of the Kyeshero hospital in Goma looking for people who had taken refuge there; one person died, three were injured and two hospital staff were violently assaulted.
claims.verification_note: Removed the day numbers 4 and 5 from the statement (no excerpt prints them); figures in words. Grade A not justified on this claim's own single source (no existing claims in packet): B. Incident dates (4-5 April) and the hospital name are on the page, not in the stored excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: MSF's own communiqué via Radio Okapi; the UN Group of Experts already reports the same incident (existing claim r1-UC-M23-021). Independent of the GoE text.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that MSF warned of an alarming increase in violence targeting medical facilities and staff in eastern DRC since the start of 2025, saying it had faced about fifteen violent incidents directly affecting hospitals it supports in North and South Kivu.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu and South Kivu (MSF-supported hospitals)
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; figures field in words as printed.
claims.researcher_note: MSF statement of 11 April as relayed; covers both provinces, individual incidents not listed here.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing OCHA, that violent clashes took place on 9 April in the localities of Mutaho, Mujoga and Karungu in Nyiragongo territory and reached Goma two days later; OCHA also reported a clear rise in crime around Goma and Nyiragongo since the advance of the AFC/M23.
claims.place_as_written: Mutaho, Mujoga, Karungu (Nyiragongo territory) and Goma
claims.verification_note: Supported. OCHA report not retrieved directly; clash parties not named in the passage.
claims.researcher_note: Relays an OCHA report (original not retrieved); the clash parties are not named in this excerpt. Links to the 11-12 April Goma fighting. 'Supported by Rwanda' is Actualite.cd's wording of OCHA's report.

claims.text: Bwiza.com, a Kigali-based Kinyarwanda-language outlet treated here as Rwanda-aligned, reported, without citing a source for the figure, that about 38 people, including women and children, were killed between 26 and 31 May 2025 in Mutanda grouping, Rutshuru territory, an area it described as controlled by the AFC/M23 rebels.
claims.place_as_written: Mutanda grouping, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports; source_type set to partisan given the outlet's Rwanda base. Bwiza.com is a Kigali-based outlet (page footer: 'Kigali, Rwanda'); treat as a Rwanda-aligned source. No named source for the toll; perpetrators not attributed. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Kigali-based outlet 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-004: Partisan-only support: the single source is Rwanda-aligned and unsourced, and 'Kinyarwanda-language outlet' alone does not signal that. Amend adds the outlet's alignment and makes 'controlled by AFC/M23' the outlet's description. No perpetrator named, as in the source; grade C stays.; excerpt-support: added the page's masthead line (Kigali, Rwanda) as an excerpt for 'Kigali-based'; changed 'without naming its sources' to 'without citing a source for the figure', because the next sentence on the page attributes the 30 May killing at Kashalira to local residents ('Amakuru yaturutse mu baturage baho'); the page calls itself 'kigenga' (independent)
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet (Bwiza.com, Rwanda-based, Kinyarwanda); no named source for the toll; perpetrators not attributed. Compare Radio Okapi 27-28 May (14 killed to 25 May; 29 buried 27 May) in overlapping areas.

claims.text: Bwiza.com reported, citing local residents, that Muhindo Sabuni Philémon, head of Kirima village, was killed at Kashalira market on Friday 30 May by unidentified armed men; the outlet said he had reportedly been recently appointed by the M23 administration.
claims.place_as_written: Kashalira market, Kirima village, Mutanda grouping, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Name printed exactly as in the excerpt; both clauses carried. Single Rwanda-based outlet; the M23 appointment is 'bivugwa' (it is said).
claims.researcher_note: Single Kinyarwanda outlet; appointment by M23 is 'bivugwa' (said). Name printed as 'Muhindo Sabuni Philémon'.

claims.text: Bwiza.com, a Kigali-based Kinyarwanda-language outlet treated here as Rwanda-aligned, reported that 'other information' it did not source confirmed about 543 houses were burned, notably in Marangara, Runzenze, Butare, Kanyangiri, Kasali, Kanyatsi, Mashango, Kibwe, Nyenyeri and Buhambi hamlets in North Kivu, and that at the end of May Wazalendo fighters burned about ten houses in Butare village where they suspected the owners of working with M23.
claims.place_as_written: Marangara, Runzenze, Butare and other hamlets, Mutanda/Bwito, Rutshuru territory
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (for the ten houses at Butare); not attributed for the 543 houses
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; figures field in words as printed. Rwanda-based outlet; compare Radio Okapi's 'more than 600 houses' for 18 May-10 June (claim 10). Tolls kept separate. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Kigali-based outlet 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-004: Partisan-only support: the sole source is a Rwanda-aligned outlet, and the burning by Wazalendo rests on it alone, yet the statement does not tell the reader that. Amend flags the outlet's alignment and that the 543 figure is unsourced; grade C stays.; excerpt-support: added the page's masthead line (Kigali, Rwanda) as an excerpt for 'Kigali-based'; 'other information' unsourced is in source 0 ('Hari kandi n'andi makuru yemeza'); the page calls itself 'kigenga' (independent)
claims.researcher_note: Unattributed 'other information' for 543; the source does not date the burning. Grade C.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the NGO TRIAL International, in a communiqué, said that several escaped prisoners, convicted or prosecuted for international crimes, had quickly joined armed groups including M23 and Wazalendo militias and were taking part in the fighting, and that it denounced killings, death threats, torture, rapes and extortion targeting those who contributed to their indictment or conviction.
claims.place_as_written: Eastern DRC (North Kivu and South Kivu prisons escapes)
claims.actor_as_written: escaped prisoners now in M23 and Wazalendo (per TRIAL International)
claims.verification_note: Removed the communiqué date (no excerpt prints 18). The outlet's headline frames the escapees as AFC/M23 fighters; TRIAL's own words name both M23 and Wazalendo.
claims.researcher_note: NGO statement as relayed; no individual incidents, places or victims given in this excerpt. Scope region-wide; assigned North Kivu because Goma's Munzenze prison escape is cited in the article.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, at a meeting of North Kivu civil-society coordinations, participant Pepin Kavota said that between January and May 2025 more than 200 civilians were killed by the M23/AFC/RDF in Rutshuru, 76 in Masisi, and '9600 à Goma' (figure as printed), alongside 3500 people wounded by weapons in Nyiragongo territory and Goma city.
claims.verification_note: Supported as attributed figures. Civil-society figures with no stated method; '9600' for Goma is printed so and is out of scale with the other figures (possible typo or different measure). RDF attribution is the speaker's. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-001: Figures check: '9600 à Goma' is out of scale with the other figures and may be a typo or a different measure; amended to mark it as printed so it is not read as a verified toll. The RDF attribution is the speaker's; single civil-society origin at C.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; '9600 à Goma' is printed in source 0
claims.researcher_note: Civil-society figures with no stated method; the '9600' for Goma is printed so and looks implausible next to the other figures (possible typo or different measure) - reported as printed. Attribution to RDF is the speaker's.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that Pepin Kavota, a participant in the North Kivu civil-society meeting, also mentioned kidnappings and forced recruitment within the rebel armed groups.
claims.verification_note: Supported.
claims.researcher_note: Generic statement; no dates, places or numbers. Date is report date (15 June 2025).

claims.text: Jeune Afrique reported that AFC/M23 was multiplying sweeping operations in the North Kivu capital to flush out soldiers and militiamen who refused to surrender, and that, amid arbitrary arrests, forced disappearances and sometimes killings, Goma residents were bearing the full brunt of an explosion of insecurity denounced by NGOs and citizen movements.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date, byline and dateline (no excerpt prints them). Only the free lede was readable; the article is paywalled. The byline (Yassin Kombi) and publication date are on the page, not in the excerpt. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-005: Attribution drift, minor: in the excerpt AFC/M23 is the subject only of the sweep operations; the arrests, disappearances and killings are listed as part of an 'explosion de l'insécurité' that residents suffer, without a stated perpetrator. The amended wording follows the excerpt's structure; the perpetrator field 'AFC/M23' should read 'not stated for the arrests, disappearances and killings; context of AFC/M23 sweeps'. 'Forced disappearances' stays as Jeune Afrique's wording. No search (paywalled single source).; excerpt-support: nothing to add; the wording follows source 0
claims.researcher_note: Only the paywall-free teaser/lede was retrievable; the rest of the article is paywalled and was not read. AFC/M23 response not in the visible text.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch said that between 10 and 30 July 2025 M23 fighters summarily executed local residents and farmers, including women and children, in villages, fields and near the Rutshuru River across the Binza groupement, Rutshuru territory, and that witness accounts, the UN and military sources indicate the Rwanda Defence Force were also involved in the M23 operations.
claims.place_as_written: Binza groupement, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; figures 140/141/300 are printed on the page (quotes supplied); figures field narrowed to HRW's wording, incl. the hedge on 300. Documented NGO investigation -> A, attributed to HRW. All figures and the RDF involvement are Human Rights Watch's findings; the 'may exceed 300' figure is HRW citing unnamed credible reports. Rwanda and AFC/M23 deny (separate claims).
claims.researcher_note: HRW did not independently verify all killings per Rwanda's response; HRW says it interviewed 36 people by telephone. Contested: see AFC/M23 and Rwanda statements below. Existing claims cover the UN GoE and MSF accounts; this adds HRW's own documentation.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch said its research indicates the M23 military operations in Binza in July 2025 were carried out by the 1st Battalion of the 1st Brigade, commanded by Col. Samuel Mushagara and Brig. Gen. Baudoin Ngaruye, respectively, and noted General Ngaruye is under UN sanctions.
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; attribution kept to HRW. Graded B (single origin for a command attribution) conservatively. Unit and commander attribution is Human Rights Watch's ('research indicates'); not independently corroborated. Being named is not a finding of individual responsibility.
claims.researcher_note: Attribution of command responsibility is HRW's research finding, not an adjudicated finding. Excerpt contains HRW's own legal label in a sentence about sanctions; the statement does not repeat it.

claims.text: UN News reported that the UN human rights office (OHCHR) said it had received first-hand accounts indicating that at least 319 civilians were killed by M23 fighters, aided by members of the Rwanda Defence Force, between 9 and 21 July in North Kivu province, and that Rwanda has repeatedly denied its forces support the M23.
claims.actor_as_written: M23, aided by members of the RDF (as OHCHR says)
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; UN body's documentation -> A; kept attributed to OHCHR. Note location in source is 'North Kivu province' only. The 319 toll and the RDF role are OHCHR's, based on first-hand accounts; the UN News item does not name Binza or Rutshuru.
claims.researcher_note: Place named as Rutshuru in HRW's quote of the OHCHR statement; UN News excerpt says North Kivu province. Compare GoE figure of over 300 casualties for 9-27 July in existing claim.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that AFC deputy coordinator Bertrand Bisimwa, at a press conference in Goma on 7 August 2025, called the UN report on the alleged massacre of more than 300 civilians in Rutshuru in July 'non factuel'; according to Bisimwa, the villages named as massacre sites would lie in the protected zone of Virunga National Park and therefore be uninhabited, and he said there is no family in mourning in Rutshuru and that the figure of 300 dead is implausible.
claims.place_as_written: Goma, North Kivu (press conference); Rutshuru territory (subject)
claims.verification_note: Kept Bisimwa's conditional ('seraient') and quoted the 300 figure as he did; the 'over 300 civilians' report description is the outlet's narration (quote supplied). Source 1 excerpt_en is a faithful translation ('Virunga National Park' renders 'parc national des Virunga'); flag resolved. Partisan denial: AFC/M23's account only, kept separate from the HRW, OHCHR and Rwanda claims. The 'over 300' description of the UN report is Actualite.cd's.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement reported by a Congolese outlet; cited for what AFC/M23 said only. Article also calls Bisimwa 'président du M23'.

claims.text: The Government of Rwanda (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) said in a statement that it rejects the false accusations in the recent OHCHR statement, that OHCHR alleges 'without any evidence' that the Rwanda Defence Force 'aided' in the killing of '319 civilians' in farms in eastern DRC, and that the gratuitous inclusion of the RDF in these allegations is 'unacceptable'.
claims.verification_note: Date '11 August 2025' printed on page (quote supplied). Narrowed to the statement's own words. Date left to the date field (2025-08-11) and source date, as the stored excerpt does not print it. Partisan statement: Rwanda's position only. This statement does not name any other perpetrator; Human Rights Watch reports that on 11 August the Rwandan government claimed an armed group opposed to the M23 carried out the killings, which must be recorded as HRW reporting Rwanda's position, not from this page.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan party statement. HRW (20 Aug) says that on 11 August Rwanda also claimed an armed group opposed to the M23 carried out the killings; that detail is not in this communiqué's text and is not recorded here.

claims.text: The Government of Rwanda (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) said in a statement that it firmly rejects the findings of Human Rights Watch, OHCHR and UNJHRO alleging mass killing of civilians in Binza, that 'Human Rights Watch itself admits that it did not independently verify the alleged killings', and that only an independent investigation will shed light on these allegations.
claims.verification_note: Date printed on page; 'admits' framing kept as Rwanda's quoted words; 'alleged' restored. Date left to the date field (2025-08-22) and source date. Partisan statement: Rwanda's characterisation of HRW's report is Rwanda's, not a finding.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan party statement. The page's first paragraph (rejection of HRW, OHCHR and UNJHRO findings) is quoted from a second part of the page and is not in this excerpt.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that eight bodies were buried over the weekend after deadly attacks on 8 August in the fields of Kihito and at Nyamilima (Binza, Rutshuru); it said seven victims, five wood-sawyers and two farmers from one family, were killed by gunfire or bladed weapon and, according to local sources, were reportedly targeted during an operation by AFC-M23 rebels to hunt alleged FDLR; the eighth victim, a local official of Kiheka neighbourhood, was found dead at home after a night incursion by unidentified armed men.
claims.place_as_written: Kihito fields and Nyamilima, Binza groupement, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: 'Sept' printed (7). excerpt_en of source 1 faithful ('Kiheka' etc. in original); flag resolved. Perpetrator attribution is local sources' and conditional ('auraient'); the eighth victim was killed by unidentified armed men. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-006: The source's attribution is conditional ('reportedly'), which the statement dropped; restored, and the eighth victim's unidentified attackers added so the AFC-M23 attribution is not read as covering all eight. Search (Kihito/Nyamilima M23 FDLR août 2025) found consistent reporting (Critical Threats, HRW on the wider July-August Binza killings) and no AFC/M23 denial for this incident.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; 'auraient été' and the eighth victim are in source 1
claims.researcher_note: Local sources. Victims not named. Date of attacks is stated by the article as 8 August.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that a fragile calm prevailed on Wednesday 16 July in Binza groupement (Rutshuru) after several days of intense fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and various local armed groups along the Kiwanja–Nyamilima–Ishasha axis, and that, according to local sources, the most recent clashes took place on Tuesday in Nyabanira and Kasave.
claims.place_as_written: Binza groupement; Nyabanira, Kasave; Kiwanja–Nyamilima–Ishasha axis, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Date 16 July printed on page (quote supplied).
claims.researcher_note: 'Tuesday' = 15 July (date computed from weekday and publication date). Nyabanira and Kasave are among the localities HRW lists for July killings.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, the disappearance of about a hundred farmers, notably in the Kongo-paysannat area west of Nyamilima, and said about twenty farmers had been missing since Monday 21 July; it linked the loss of access to farmland to fighting between AFC/M23 and alleged FDLR fighters near Virunga park.
claims.place_as_written: Kongo-paysannat, west of Nyamilima, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Raw statement matches the page: figures in the excerpt; the link to AFC/M23 vs alleged FDLR fighting near Virunga park is in the lead paragraph (quote in clause_support; extend excerpt with add_excerpt). '23' flag is the 'M23' in 'AFC/M23', printed in the lead paragraph. The article prints two figures, about a hundred and about twenty missing farmers; both stand as printed and the article does not reconcile them. No perpetrator is named for the disappearances.
claims.researcher_note: The two figures in one article differ (about 100 vs about 20) and are not reconciled by the source. Fate unknown. Weekday 21 July is as printed in the article.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that Kahumiro, near Kibirizi in Rutshuru territory within the Virunga park zone, had been the scene of violent clashes since 20 August 2025 between AFC-M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters and alleged FDLR elements.
claims.place_as_written: Kahumiro, near Kibirizi, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Single exact excerpt carries the whole statement. excerpt_en faithful ('Virunga National Park' renders 'parc national des Virunga'); flag resolved.
claims.researcher_note: Local outlet; single source.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing several local sources, that M23 rebels 'under the command of Makenga' launched an operation to hunt alleged FDLR rebels at Kahumiro, while community leaders said there was no longer an active FDLR presence in the area.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 under the command of Makenga (per local sources)
claims.verification_note: Exact; name kept as printed. The source prints only the surname 'Makenga'; no first name or rank is given. Command attribution rests on unnamed local sources.
claims.researcher_note: 'Makenga' as printed; the source gives no first name or rank.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that local sources spoke of about ten deaths among residents, mainly Hutu and other local ethnic groups of Bwito chiefdom, in the Kahumiro clashes, and that hundreds of households fled to Kibirizi and neighbouring villages.
claims.verification_note: Exact; excerpt_en faithful; flag resolved. Toll from unnamed local sources; the article does not say who killed the residents.
claims.researcher_note: Single local source, unverified figures.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the chief of Kimoka locality (Kamuronza groupement), named as Kibihira Bauma, was shot dead at his home in Sake in the night of Saturday to Sunday 3 August 2025, in a zone it described as totally under M23 control according to testimonies; the authors were not identified and no official report had been issued.
claims.place_as_written: Sake, Masisi territory (about 20 km north-west of Goma), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Date 3 August 2025 and Kamuronza/Kimoka printed on page (quote supplied); name spelled as printed. Perpetrators not identified by the source; the M23 control of the area is context, not an attribution.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date (3 August 2025 is a Sunday). Same article recalls the killing of Charles Kilibiri, chief of Malehe village, on 21 March (outside this unit's period; not recorded here).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that a report by the North Kivu provincial youth council documented 47 deaths, 75 cases of sexual violence, 14 abductions, 66 armed robberies and 63 cases of arson between 7 June and 3 July 2025 in Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories and Goma city.
claims.place_as_written: Goma city, Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Exact single excerpt carries the statement; excerpt_en faithful; origin set to the youth council. Figures are the North Kivu provincial youth council's, relayed by Actualite.cd; the report itself was not seen, and the period (7 June-3 July 2025) mostly precedes this quarter. No perpetrator is named. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Second-hand report of a civil-society document not seen; no perpetrator or per-incident detail. Method of the youth council count unknown.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that two people were killed by armed bandits on the evening of Wednesday 9 July 2025 in Goma; according to local sources, the first was a motorcycle taxi driver killed in Kasika quarter and the second a woman killed in Katoyi quarter, Karisimbi commune; it described Goma and Nyiragongo territory as under AFC/M23 control since late January 2025.
claims.place_as_written: Kasika and Katoyi quarters, Karisimbi commune, Goma; Nyiragongo territory
claims.actor_as_written: armed bandits (as described by the source); not attributed to a group
claims.verification_note: 'shot' removed from the statement (excerpt says 'assassinée'; the shooting is in a witness quote with a variant quarter name). 'Deux' printed (2). A civil-society witness quoted in the article says armed men shot the wife of a money changer at home on avenue Bukonde, giving the quarter as 'Kayoyi'; the article's narration says Katoyi. Perpetrators not identified beyond 'armed bandits'.
claims.researcher_note: Statement's 'at least four wounded' detail comes from a later sentence in the same article and is not in this excerpt; verifier may narrow. Victims unnamed.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC accused armed men likened to M23 fighters of abducting at least 42 women in Bukombo centre grouping, Rutshuru territory; according to the communication officer of the 34th military region, Dieudonné Kasereka, the events took place on Sunday 28 December in Bwito chiefdom, and the 42 victims reportedly underwent torture before being abducted, according to the army citing testimony from inhabitants.
claims.actor_as_written: armed men likened to M23 fighters, per FARDC 34th military region
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact; raw statement matches the Radio Okapi lead and the FARDC attribution. Congo Quotidien states 'Source: radiookapi.net' and is AI-written: a relay, not independent. '23' flag is from 'M23' in the page lead. Single origin: the FARDC 34th military region, a party to the conflict. Congo Quotidien is an AI-written relay of Radio Okapi, not independent. No AFC/M23 response found; no independent confirmation. The FARDC officer said the women's destination was not yet known. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: the FARDC as accuser 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: armed men likened to M23, 42 women, Bukombo centre 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-008: Single partisan origin (FARDC 34th military region); Congo Quotidien is a relay. Lead clause made to name the accuser. Fresh search: Actualite.cd (15 Jan 2026, seen via search/extract only, not retained) says three of '30' women abducted by AFC/M23 at Bukombo in December 2025 remained captive, accused of being Wazalendo wives: a different figure (30 vs 42) to research and record separately. No AFC/M23 denial found (query 'M23 dement enlevement 42 femmes Bukombo').; excerpt-support: added the headline ('Les FARDC accusent...') and the lead sentence (armed men 'assimilés à des combattants du M23', 42 women, Bukombo centre) as excerpts; cut 'No independent confirmation or AFC/M23 response was found', which records the searches run, not anything a cited page prints (keep it in the notes or the no-statement record)
claims.researcher_note: Single origin: FARDC 34th military region communication officer; both outlets relay it. Destination of the women unknown per source; no independent confirmation and no AFC/M23 reply found (searched). Possible sexual-violence element not stated by source. Later follow-up exists (Actualite.cd Facebook post: three women still in captivity), not fetched.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported on 15 October 2025 that civilian sources gave a toll of at least seven people killed, including two women, in the tenth day of fighting between AFC/M23 and CMC-Nyatura Wazalendo in Bwito chiefdom, with nearly ten other women reportedly raped and more than a quarter of the houses of Mashango village burned.
claims.place_as_written: Mashango and Karambi, Bukombo grouping, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.actor_as_written: not specified for the rapes; fighting between AFC/M23 and CMC/FDP-Nyatura (Dominique Ndaruhutse) Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; raw statement accurate (page dated and describing fighting on 15 October 2025). Rapes not attributed to any party by the source. Local civilian sources via Radio Okapi; rapes reported conditionally ('auraient été violées') and not attributed to any party.
claims.researcher_note: Local civilian sources via Radio Okapi; perpetrator of rapes not attributed by the source. Same page attributes the 39 earlier deaths (Chirumba, Kagango) to AFC/M23 reprisals per civil sources (see next claim).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported on 15 October 2025 that at least 39 people were killed more than a week earlier in the villages of Chirumba (Tongo) and Kagango (Bambo); according to civilian sources in the area, the killings and abuses were reportedly committed during reprisal operations by AFC/M23 rebels.

claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; raw statement accurate. Same page as claim 1. Date is approximate: before about 7 October 2025 ('more than a week' before the 15 October report). Attribution to AFC/M23 is by civilian sources and conditional. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-006: The source's conditional ('auraient été perpétrées') was dropped; 'reportedly' restored. Search ('"Chirumba" OR "Kagango" M23 tués Bwito 2025') found only relays of the same Radio Okapi text, no independent account and no AFC/M23 denial.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; 'auraient été perpétrées' is in source 0
claims.researcher_note: Date computed as 'more than a week before 15 Oct'. Possible overlap with the 9 Oct Radio Okapi claim already in the register (13 missing, 8 women raped in Bwito/Bahunde); not checked for identity.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources on 7 November 2025, that at least four people were killed and seven wounded in successive incursions by armed men over the previous two nights in Katsiru, Bwito chiefdom; per local notables, unidentified armed men attacked local defence units set up by AFC-M23, which occupies the area.
claims.actor_as_written: unidentified armed men attacking local defence units set up by AFC-M23

Discrepancy between 4 dead (lead) and 5 dead incl. 4 civilians (body) noted, not hidden. The page also says several wounded were admitted to the Katsiru reference health centre; the body gives five dead (four civilians) on the night of Wednesday to Thursday, differing from the headline's four.
claims.researcher_note: Single local-source report. Page adds the night of Wed-Thu had 5 dead incl. 4 civilians and one local-defence fighter, and wounded admitted to the Katsiru reference health centre; those details are not in the excerpts above and are not claimed. The same page names Katsiru as a long-running AFC-M23 vs CMC/Nyatura front.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, after clashes on Tuesday and Wednesday between AFC/M23 rebels and wazalendo in the villages of Muko, Karambi and Mashango (Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru territory), one person was killed, several others wounded and about ten houses burned, according to its sources; several local sources said AFC/M23 rebels searching for CMC-FDP wazalendo initiated the fighting, causing displacement, and burned houses in the three villages.
claims.place_as_written: Muko, Karambi and Mashango, Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Removed the publication date '19 December 2025', which no excerpt prints; numbers otherwise in words. Added displacement, which the excerpt prints. Dates 16-17 December 2025 are computed from 'Tuesday and Wednesday' and the 19 December publication date. No AFC/M23 account found.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday (Tuesday/Wednesday) and publication date Friday 19 Dec 2025. Local-source report; AFC/M23 account not found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that an AFC/M23 unit on patrol on the Goma-Rutshuru road inside Virunga National Park fell into an ambush set by Wazalendo near Rumangabo on Wednesday 24 December; several sources said a vehicle of the rebels was burned, and one anonymous source spoke of rebel casualties.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo, Goma-Rutshuru road (Virunga National Park), Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; casualty clause placed by a replacement quote from the same page. excerpt_en flag concerns 'National Park' capitalisation only.
claims.researcher_note: Local-source report. Casualty remark by one anonymous source on the page is not claimed.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, a series of robberies attributed to armed groups in Rutshuru and Masisi over two days; in Rutshuru, three women fish sellers returning from Vitshumbi by motorbike were attacked on Friday 19 December on the Rwindi-Kibirizi road in Virunga park and lost their goods, money and phones.
claims.actor_as_written: armed groups (the source says identifying the perpetrators is difficult in an AFC-M23-occupied zone where Wazalendo and FDLR also operate)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and supports the statement. Radio Okapi says the perpetrators are hard to identify in an AFC-M23-occupied zone where Wazalendo and FDLR also operate.
claims.researcher_note: Single local-source report. Same page notes a similar ambush on choristers from two Vitshumbi churches the day before. Actualite.cd (20 Dec) separately reported a double robbery on Kiwanja-Kanyabayonga road (not fetched for excerpt).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC, in a communiqué issued on Saturday, accused the rebel coalition, which it said is backed by Rwanda, of intensifying attacks in the east of the country in violation of commitments made in the Washington and Doha peace processes; according to the text signed by army spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekeng Bomusa Efomi, the rebels attacked several military positions in South Kivu and North Kivu over the previous 72 hours.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; '8' not printed (page says 'samedi'), removed from statement and kept in date field as computed. Accusation framing added from page lead. Party statement (FARDC). Date 8 November 2025 is computed from 'samedi' and the 9 November publication date. The page names Bulambula, Kibanda Mangobo, the Mudugwe bridge and Tuwetuwe (South Kivu) and Kasopo, Kajinga and Mont Irimwi (North Kivu) as positions attacked. The coalition accused is the AFC/M23, as the article's headline and lead state.
claims.researcher_note: Page says 'samedi' and was published Sunday 9 Nov, so date computed from weekday and publication date. Page also reports that wounded from Katsiru (Rutshuru) were being treated at Mweso hospital (medical sources, Masisi). No AFC/M23 reply found in this unit.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that on Monday 15 December 2025 vehicles carrying support troops were seen crossing Kirumba towards the north of Lubero territory, coming from the PENA centre in Rutshuru territory; the article attributes the positions in Lubero to AFC/M23 and cites Lubero civil society.
claims.place_as_written: Kirumba, Lubero territory (from PENA centre, Rutshuru)
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (per Lubero civil society and local sources)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; raw statement correctly says the article (not the excerpt) attributes the Lubero positions to AFC/M23 and cites Lubero civil society; clause support from the page. The page does not explicitly say whose troops the 15 December vehicles carried; it reports them in the context of AFC/M23 reinforcements. The FARDC-appointed military administrator called the reports rumours. Lubero military administrator Lt Col Kiwewa Mitela Alain neither confirmed nor denied, calling the reports rumours.
claims.researcher_note: Excerpt does not name AFC/M23 in itself; page headline and body attribute these movements to AFC/M23 positions. The Lubero military administrator, Lt Col Kiwewa Mitela Alain, neither confirmed nor denied. Lubero is outside this unit's geography; kept as reinforcement movement from Rutshuru.

claims.text: MSF reported that in October two health centres supported by MSF were hit by stray bullets in Masisi and Rutshuru territories in the same week, and that in total three MSF staff have been killed in North Kivu in 2025.
claims.place_as_written: Health centres in Masisi and Rutshuru territories (not named by the source)
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (stray bullets)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date '9 December 2025' from the statement. The staff-deaths sentence is on the page (replacement quote), so kept with its own clause support rather than left unsupported. MSF does not name the facilities, give exact dates or say who fired. The October date is October 2025 by context (project update of 9 December 2025).
claims.researcher_note: Facility names, dates and the party responsible are not given in the excerpt. Only the October stray-bullet incident is claimed; the 'three MSF staff killed in North Kivu in 2025' sentence is in a separate passage and is not claimed here.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that violent fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters, allies of the FARDC, continued on Thursday 15 January in the Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru territory, around the town of Mweso, and that according to local sources the fighting involved Wazalendo of the Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC).
claims.place_as_written: Bukombo grouping, around Mweso (Bumbasha, Mubirubiru), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23; Wazalendo (CMC), allies of the FARDC, as named by the source
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the retained page; translation flag is only the expansion of FARDC, which the excerpt prints. Radio Okapi narration plus local sources.
claims.researcher_note: Local sources via Radio Okapi. Overlaps in time with BCNUDH r1-ATR-NK-2026-001 (12-15 Jan, Rutshuru); this is the fighting narrative, no casualty total.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that several civilians, including displaced people, were wounded in the villages of Bumbasha, Kivuma and Kanyangohe during fighting in Rutshuru territory, and that a local customary source said a precise toll was hard to establish.
claims.place_as_written: Bumbasha, Kivuma, Kanyangohe, Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru territory
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (fighting between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo)
claims.verification_note: Removed '15 January' from the statement (not in this claim's excerpt); the date stays in the date field and is carried by the page lead. No perpetrator is named by the source.
claims.researcher_note: Single local report.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that several dozen civilians mobilised by AFC/M23 fighters for community work were targeted by CMC militiamen ambushed in the locality of Kiyeye, in the Kihondo grouping; separately, according to MSF as relayed by Radio Okapi, at least 32 wounded, mostly civilians, victims of shell fragments and direct fire, were evacuated and treated at the Nyanzale health centre (the source does not say all were wounded in the Kiyeye ambush).
claims.place_as_written: Kiyeye, Kihondo grouping, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory; Nyanzale health centre
claims.actor_as_written: CMC militiamen (as named by Radio Okapi)
claims.verification_note: Removed '19 January 2026' from the statement (excerpt says 'Ce jour-là'); the page prints the date, kept in the date field. Wording kept to 'community work' without implying forced labour. The source says the civilians were 'mobilisés ... pour des travaux communautaires'; it does not say whether this was forced. MSF's figure (at least 32 treated at Nyanzale over three days) is not explicitly limited to the Kiyeye ambush. MSF's own communiqué was not fetched. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-008: The excerpts place the CMC attribution on Radio Okapi and the 32-wounded figure on MSF, but MSF's figure is not limited to the Kiyeye ambush; the statement joined them. Amended to separate them. Fresh search: Radio Okapi (20 Jan) first reported 'au moins vingt civils' seriously wounded at Kiyeye on 19 January (search snippet, not retained), a different early toll.; excerpt-support: nothing to add
claims.researcher_note: The 19 January date and attribution are in Radio Okapi's own narrative; the 32-wounded figure is attributed to an MSF communiqué of 23 January. Not seen on MSF's own site. 'Travaux communautaires' may be forced labour; the source does not say so.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the humanitarian organisation MSF, in a communiqué, also reported that several civilian houses were burned in the area after the attack in Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory.
claims.verification_note: Removed '19 January' and 'Friday 23 January' from the statement (not in the excerpt); the page carries them, and the date range stays in the date field.
claims.researcher_note: Weekday 'vendredi' = 23 January per the page's own text ('publié vendredi 23 janvier').

claims.text: Actualite.cd, summarising an OCHA report for January, reported that between 12 and 16 January fighting occurred in more than ten villages of the Bukombo, Kihondo and Mutanda groupings, as well as Bambo and Tongo, in Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, where about fifty civilians were killed, and that the report noted the displacement of several hundred people.
claims.place_as_written: Bukombo, Kihondo, Mutanda, Bambo and Tongo groupings, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.actor_as_written: not named in the excerpt; the article's lead says the fighting notably opposed AFC/M23 rebels and wazalendo militiamen affiliated with the Congolese army
claims.verification_note: Statement narrowed to the excerpt's wording (no '2026' in the report title clause; 'groupings' list as printed). Figures field dropped the 'close to one hundred across three territories' total, which is page-only; actor marked as from the lead. Attributed to OCHA via Actualite.cd. Figure is OCHA's as relayed by Actualite.cd; OCHA's own report was not fetched. Headline ('plus d’une cinquantaine') and body ('une cinquantaine') differ slightly.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates BCNUDH r1-ATR-NK-2026-001 (12-15 January, Rutshuru). Headline says 'plus d’une cinquantaine', body says 'une cinquantaine': both recorded in figures. Original OCHA report not fetched.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that fighting pitted AFC/M23 rebels against wazalendo early on the morning of Tuesday 3 February at Kivuma and Kanyangohe, two localities of Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory), and that after several hours of violent clashes the AFC/M23 rebels were forced to fall back to Mweso, their starting base; Radio Okapi also reported that AFC/M23 rebels launched an attack on Wazalendo positions in Kivuma and Kanyangohe, in the Bukombo grouping.
claims.place_as_written: Kivuma and Kanyangohe, Bukombo grouping, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory (about 5 km from Mweso)
claims.verification_note: Removed the Radio Okapi '4 February ... fragile calm' clause: neither the date nor the calm is in the excerpt. Category set to military_operation: the source reports a repelled attack, not a change of control. The outcome (AFC/M23 forced to fall back) rests on Actualite.cd's sources only; no AFC/M23 account found.
claims.researcher_note: Two Congolese outlets agree on the attack; the 'repelled' outcome is Actualite.cd's sources only. Both outlets are Kinshasa-leaning-neutral national media; no AFC/M23 account found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing concordant local sources, that a convoy of travellers from Rutshuru territory heading to Butembo was ambushed by unidentified armed men on Sunday 1 February on the Rwindi-Kanyabayonga stretch, in an area under AFC/M23 control, with several wounded and no deaths, and that travellers' valuables were looted.
claims.place_as_written: Rwindi-Kanyabayonga road, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: All excerpts on the page; 'no deaths' and 'concordant local sources' are on the page next to the excerpts.
claims.researcher_note: Single local report; victims taken to health facilities at Kanyabayonga.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that in the village of Kabanda, near Kibirizi (Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory), an incursion by unidentified armed men was reported between 3 and 4 a.m.; the attackers looted the population's belongings, a young boy known by the name Jade was killed, and three civilians were wounded and admitted to the Kibirizi reference health centre.
claims.place_as_written: Kabanda, near Kibirizi, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Removed 'night of Sunday to Monday 16 February' from the statement (not in the excerpt and, on the page, tied to Kibirizi/Bambo rather than explicitly to Kabanda). Jade is printed in the excerpt. The page dates the night of violence in Kibirizi and Bambo to the night of Sunday to Monday 16 February; the Kabanda incursion is reported in the same article without its own date.
claims.researcher_note: Date is the night of Sunday to Monday 16 February (date computed from the page's own text). Single local report.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to local sources, the instability in Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory) is notably linked to a hunt operation led by the AFC/M23 against the Rwandan Hutu FDLR rebels and their local allies, including fighters of the Collectif des Mouvements pour le Changement (CMC/Nyatura).
claims.place_as_written: Bambo and Kibirizi, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 against FDLR and CMC/Nyatura (as named by local sources)
