claims.researcher_note: 'Rebelles hutu rwandais FDLR' is the outlet's wording. Single local-sources report.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that despite a ceasefire announced for 18 February at noon, fighting continued between the FARDC and AFC/M23; it said that since early Friday 20 February AFC/M23 had been fighting Wazalendo of PARECO at Mitimingi, Kaunda and Mbiso in Masisi territory, and that other clashes were reported in some areas of Rutshuru territory.
claims.place_as_written: Masisi and Rutshuru territories, North Kivu (Mitimingi, Kaunda, Mbiso named for Masisi; no Rutshuru places named)
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact and cover the statement; translation flag is only the FARDC expansion.
claims.researcher_note: Context: the same article says the truce was proposed 11 February by Angola after a Luanda meeting. Rutshuru clashes are not located by the source.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources reached from Mweso, that two civilians (a young girl and a cattle guard) were killed by stray bullets on Thursday 26 February in an exchange of fire between AFC/M23 elements on patrol and an unidentified armed group in the JTN concession, Bwito chiefdom, near Mweso; twelve cows were also shot dead, and no official toll was communicated by the parties.
claims.place_as_written: JTN agro-pastoral concession, Bwito chiefdom, near Mweso
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 and an unidentified armed group
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; 'twelve cows' and 'on patrol' are page-only, next to the excerpts. Location discrepancy within the source: the headline says Rutshuru; the body places Mwesso in Masisi territory and the JTN concession in Bwito chiefdom.
claims.researcher_note: Headline places the event in Rutshuru; the body places Mwesso in Masisi territory and the concession in Bwito chiefdom. Location discrepancy within the source.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that on Wednesday 18 March armed men fired on and stopped a vehicle on the Kanyabayonga-Kiwanja road inside Virunga park, Rutshuru territory, wounding two passengers, a woman and her son, who were evacuated to the Kanyabayonga reference health centre; the assailants' identity remained unknown, though several security sources said this part of the territory is under AFC/M23 influence.
claims.place_as_written: Kanyabayonga-Kiwanja road, Virunga park, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; 'under influence' is not attribution of the attack, and the statement keeps it that way.
claims.researcher_note: Single local report. Complements the 1 February ambush on the neighbouring Rwindi-Kanyabayonga stretch.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, according to local sources, the head nurse of the Kalembe health centre (Mweso health zone, Masisi territory), identified as Kapita Lucien, was shot in the hand after being violently beaten, and that the local Red Cross coordinator, Byamungu Mauwa Samson, also suffered physical abuse on the same occasion; the outlet attributed the incident to armed elements of the AFC/M23 and reported that the two men were reportedly accused, without formal proof, of links with the wazalendo and were taken away by motorbike by their abductors to an unknown destination. The article said AFC/M23 officials had not yet reacted.
claims.place_as_written: Kalembe, Mweso health zone, Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 elements, as named by the source
claims.verification_note: Removed 'Monday 30 March' from the statement (not in any excerpt; the page lead carries it and the date field keeps it). Both names are printed in excerpts 0 and 1, spelled as printed. The headline calls the second man a Red Cross volunteer ('volontaire') and says both were 'arrêtés'; the body calls him the local Red Cross coordinator and their captors 'ravisseurs'. The accusation of wazalendo links is reported in the conditional ('seraient accusés').
claims.researcher_note: Masisi territory (edge of the NKS unit). Single local report; the page states an AFC/M23 non-reaction as of publication. Source also relays a call for ICRC/MSF to intervene.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that Bruno Lemarquis, Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in the DRC, on a mission in Goma since Monday 16 March, called on the leaders of the AFC/M23 rebellion to guarantee absolute respect for humanitarian space, in a statement made during a meeting with the de facto authorities of Goma and its surroundings, led by Corneille Nangaa.
claims.place_as_written: Goma (city), Sake and Nyiragongo territory visited
claims.actor_as_written: UN (Bruno Lemarquis); AFC/M23 de facto authorities led by Corneille Nangaa
claims.verification_note: Removed 'left Goma on Wednesday 18 March' from the statement (not in the excerpts); the date is now the mission range 16-18 March, since the page does not give the meeting's exact day.
claims.researcher_note: Page published 18 March, modified 23 March. The statement is generic, no incident named.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, in an exchange with the diplomatic corps accredited in Kinshasa on Wednesday 25 March 2026, called the situation 'préoccupante', said the reopening of Goma airport for humanitarian flights had not happened, and accused the AFC/M23 of lacking political will.
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; the airport clause is a direct quote on the page outside the excerpts.
claims.researcher_note: Government account; the AFC/M23 reply on the same page is in the next claim. The 21 February AFC/M23 airport statement is already in POL-2026.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 maintains that the humanitarian situation is improving in the zones it controls and alarming in the zones controlled by Kinshasa, in the context of the dispute over reopening Goma airport.
claims.verification_note: Flag '23' is the '23' in 'AFC/M23', which the excerpt context prints. Paraphrase correctly attributed. Actualite.cd's paraphrase of the AFC/M23 position, undated on the page; not a verbatim AFC/M23 statement.
claims.researcher_note: Paraphrase by Actualite.cd, not a verbatim M23 quote; the outlet then cites Corneille Nangaa speaking in Goma on 20 February.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the AFC/M23 confirmed it carried out a drone attack on Kisangani airport (Tshopo) as a 'warning' to Kinshasa, as its leader said, and that the movement said its drones destroyed a military drone base at the airport 'where attacks killing civilians were prepared' in Masisi, Walikale, Rutshuru, Minembwe and elsewhere; BBC said it could not independently verify either side's claims.
claims.place_as_written: Kisangani (Bangoka) airport, Tshopo (statement concerns attacks on Masisi, Walikale, Rutshuru, Minembwe)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; the BBC caveat sits on the page directly after excerpt 1. Party claim ('AFC/M23 says'); BBC says it could not independently verify either side. Strike date computed from 'ku Cyumweru' and the 4 February publication date.
claims.researcher_note: Kinyarwanda article published 4 February 2026 (page header 'Yatangajwe 4 Ukwa kabiri 2026'). The strike was on 'Ku Cyumweru' (Sunday) per the Tshopo provincial account; date computed from weekday and publication date = 1 February 2026. Outside North/South Kivu; recorded because M23's stated rationale concerns Rutshuru and Masisi.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Tshopo provincial government said eight bomb-carrying drones tried to attack Bangoka airport at Kisangani on Sunday but were all shot down before reaching their target, and that the government side condemned the attack on a civilian airport and blamed the M23 and Rwandan forces.
claims.actor_as_written: Tshopo provincial government; DRC government side
claims.verification_note: The blame clause is on the page (one sentence after the BBC caveat), not in the excerpt; kept with that page quote. Flag '23' is 'M23'.
claims.researcher_note: Counter-account to the AFC/M23 claim. Date computed from weekday and publication date. The 'blamed M23 and Rwandan forces' element comes from a separate sentence on the page and is not in the excerpt, so it is not claimed here beyond what the excerpt supports; reviewers may narrow the statement.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that clashes between wazalendo and AFC/M23 were reported from the morning of Friday 10 April 2026 in the locality of Rwankuba (Kihondo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory), with heavy gunfire heard in the villages of Kiringa and Bwuma.
claims.place_as_written: Rwankuba, Kiringa and Bwuma (Bwito chiefdom), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: wazalendo and AFC/M23, as named by Actualite.cd
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact on the retained page (Actualite.cd, 10/04/2026 11:26); statement matches, attribution to the outlet's sources kept. No control change reported.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet citing its own sources; no control change reported. Place names as printed. Weekday and date both stated by the source.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that six civilians were killed on 23 April 2026 in their fields at Bushenge, Gisigari groupement (Rutshuru territory), and that, according to several local sources, the killings were attributed to the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) operating through the AFC/M23 rebels. The outlet said the circumstances were not clearly established and the motive was unknown.
claims.place_as_written: Bushenge, Gisigari groupement, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) operating through AFC/M23, according to local sources cited by Actualite.cd
claims.verification_note: All six names printed in the source 1 excerpt, spelled as printed. excerpt_en flag is benign ('Rwandan Defence Forces' renders 'Forces de défense rwandaises'). The 'circumstances not established' hedge is on the page (page-only clause), kept because it limits the claim. Perpetrator attribution rests on unnamed local sources; the outlet says the circumstances are not established.
claims.researcher_note: Single local-sourced report; attribution rests on unnamed local sources and the outlet says circumstances are not established. No RDF or AFC/M23 response found.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch said, in a report, that Rwandan military forces and the M23 armed group carried out a campaign of forced recruitment and abusive detention of thousands of captured combatants and civilians in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo; the report documents large-scale roundups and arrests in North and South Kivu and grave abuses against detainees at the Rumangabo and Tshanzu training camps in North Kivu between mid-2024 and December 2025. HRW said its researchers found that M23 fighters, backed by Rwandan military personnel, committed murder, torture and corporal punishment and used forced labor and child soldiers.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo and Tshanzu training camps, North Kivu (Rutshuru territory per Actualite.cd's account of the report)
claims.actor_as_written: M23 backed by Rwandan military forces / Rwanda Defence Force, as alleged by Human Rights Watch
claims.verification_note: Removed '10 June 2026' from the statement: it comes from the page's 'released today', not from an excerpt (the date stays in the claim's date field and source date). Rest exact; legal labels on the page ('war crimes') left out per vocabulary rule. Publication event of the report (source dated 10 June 2026); the abuses documented run mid-2024 to December 2025. HRW states Rwandan government and M23 officials have long denied, but failed to investigate, allegations of abuse.
claims.researcher_note: Report published in the window but the abuses it documents run mid-2024 to December 2025 (largely before the window). Entered as the report's publication event, not as events of the quarter. HRW interviewed former detainees; the report also uses geolocated video and satellite imagery. Rwandan and M23 response: none found in this unit (Actualite.cd and HRW both state they have long rejected such allegations without investigating). Overlaps existing r1 claims citing hrw.org; check for duplicates.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that a communiqué published on Thursday 4 June 2026 by the spokesperson of the 34th military region, Major Dieudonné Kasereka, said that 204 AFC-M23 rebels had surrendered to the FARDC and their allies in Lubero, Rutshuru and Masisi (North Kivu) in waves during April and May.
claims.place_as_written: Lubero, Rutshuru and Masisi territories (North Kivu), and Kalehe (South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Exact; figure stays attributed to the FARDC communiqué. excerpt_en flag benign (expanded 'Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo'). Party claim relayed by a credible outlet: C kept for the unverified figure. FARDC figures, not independently verified; the page body adds Kalehe (South Kivu) as a further surrender zone and quotes Kasereka saying the recruits were 'recrutés par force'.
claims.researcher_note: Party claim (FARDC) reported by Radio Okapi; AFC/M23 reaction not found. The same spokesperson also said the recruits were 'recruited by force'.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that on Wednesday 8 April 2026 the command of the 34th military region of North Kivu confirmed the voluntary surrender of 263 elements from the ranks of the AFC/M23 between February and March 2026.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu (Lubero, Rutshuru and Masisi) and Kalehe, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Exact; 'confirmed' is Radio Okapi's verb for the command's statement; figure stays attributed. FARDC figure, not independently verified. Page body: four officers among them; surrenders in Lubero, Rutshuru, Masisi and Kalehe per Major Dieudonné Kasereka.
claims.researcher_note: FARDC claim; surrenders themselves dated Feb-Mar 2026, statement dated 8 April. Territories named in the page body: Lubero, Rutshuru, Masisi, Kalehe.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that a kamikaze drone hit the headquarters of the Congolese Institute for Nature Conservation (ICCN) at Rumangabo, Rutshuru territory, on the morning of Sunday 24 May 2026; Virunga National Park public-relations officer Méthode Uhoze confirmed the facts to the outlet and said the attack came around 8 a.m. The outlet reported that the building was burned and the frame destroyed, that no toll was yet available and that the author of the attack had not been identified.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo (ICCN headquarters, Virunga National Park), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: All excerpts exact; 'no toll' clause is page-only but verbatim. excerpt_en flags benign (expanded ICCN name). Times differ: about 8 a.m. per Virunga (Actualite.cd); 07h35 per AFC/M23 (Kivu Morning Post). Author unidentified per Actualite.cd; AFC/M23 blames Kinshasa's forces (claim 6).
claims.researcher_note: Complements existing r1-ATR-NK-2026-006 (Radio Okapi, 24-25 May) with the ICCN/Virunga confirmation. Rumangabo is also named by HRW as an M23 training camp; the AFC/M23 account (KMP claim below) says the strike hit a densely populated area and the eco-guards camp. Time: Actualite.cd ~8:00, Kanyuka 07:35.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a statement on X, accused government forces of 'un bombardement criminel et indiscriminé' on Rumangabo; he said it took place on Sunday 24 May 2026 at 07h35 against the densely populated area of Rumangabo and the eco-guards camp of Virunga National Park, using CH-4 combat drones.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 accuses 'les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa' (partisan account)
claims.verification_note: Statement unchanged and exact; corrected source_type: Kivu Morning Post is a Goma-based media outlet (labelled 'media' in claim 7), the partisan origin is Kanyuka's X statement, recorded in originating_source. Second quote is Kanyuka's words ('a-t-il déclaré' on the page). Partisan account (AFC/M23), cited only as what AFC/M23 said. Kanyuka also claimed loss of life without a figure. The page says Congolese authorities had not reacted.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan claim (AFC/M23), cited only for what it said. The page also reports Kanyuka claiming 'pertes en vies humaines' without a figure. FARDC statement on Rumangabo: none found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that from Saturday 23 May 2026 the North Kivu governorate under AFC/M23 administration suspended passenger transport between Goma and Butembo until further notice, announced in a communiqué of Friday 22 May 2026 as a preventive measure against Ebola (Bundibugyo strain). Kivu Morning Post reported the same communiqué.
claims.place_as_written: Goma–Butembo road (Goma city; Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories on the route), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: North Kivu governorate under AFC/M23 administration
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact; Ebola/Bundibugyo clause is on the Actualite.cd page (page-only). Both outlets relay one communiqué, so B for an authority announcement. excerpt_en flags benign. Kivu Morning Post does not itself name AFC/M23 as the administration; the date and content match the same communiqué.
claims.researcher_note: Two Congolese outlets agree. Goods transport stays allowed with driver and assistant only (per both pages). Related Ebola-in-Goma announcement is in existing r1-POL-2026-009. Reaction of the Kinshasa government: not searched in depth.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Rwanda's foreign minister (printed 'Oliver Nduhungirehe'), in a statement the day after the Mushaki drone attack, deplored the silence of the international community and of the UN mission in the DRC regarding 'crimes du gouvernement de la République du Congo'; he said that on 11 March 2026 FARDC attack drones struck Goma, killing UNICEF humanitarian Karine Buisset and two other civilians.
claims.place_as_written: Goma (the 11 March 2026 strike alleged); statement made from Rwanda
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Rwanda (Olivier Nduhungirehe) accusing FARDC
claims.verification_note: Statement exact and attributed (the page frames the 11 March passage with 'Il ajoute que'). Corrected source_type: Kivu Morning Post is a media outlet; the partisan origin (Rwandan government, via X) is in originating_source. Karine Buisset printed in source 2 excerpt. Rwandan government allegation, cited only for what Rwanda said; the page spells the minister both 'Oliver' and 'Olivier' Nduhungirehe. Statement date approximate (page: 'le lendemain' of the Mushaki attack, which he dates 8 May 2026, and 'le week-end dernier').
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan government allegation, cited only for what Rwanda said; the 11 March strike itself predates the quarter. Date computed: page says he spoke 'le lendemain' of the Mushaki attack (8 May, per same page) and also 'le week-end dernier' (publication 11 May); date approximate. FARDC/Kinshasa response to this statement: none found. Same page also cites Mushaki (Masisi) 8 May strike, outside this unit.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said FDLR fighters infiltrated the Kabuye and Kabanda areas in the night of 18 May 2026 (time given as 'saa Saba z’igicuku'), killing a 77-year-old named Nzirorera Nsekuye at Kabanda and abducting Munenge Samuel and Karuhije Innocent at Kabuye; the outlet placed the incident in Bambo centre, Rutshuru territory.
claims.place_as_written: Kabanda and Kabuye, Bambo centre, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FDLR, per AFC/M23 spokesperson (partisan account relayed by Rwandan state-aligned outlet)
claims.verification_note: 'around midnight' was a mistranslation of 'saa Saba z’igicuku' (seventh hour of the night, about 1 a.m.); replaced with the source's own phrase rather than adding an unprinted number. All three names and the age printed in source 0 excerpt. Partisan, grade C. Single partisan claim: AFC/M23 spokesperson relayed by a Kigali outlet that adopts the FDLR attribution in its own voice. 'saa Saba z’igicuku' is the seventh hour of the night in Swahili/Kinyarwanda time-reckoning (about 1 a.m.), not midnight.
claims.researcher_note: Single partisan claim: AFC/M23 spokesperson relayed by Rwandan state-aligned media (Umuryango.rw, Kigali), which itself adopts the FDLR attribution in its own voice ('terrorist group'); treat as 'AFC/M23 says'. Time given as 'saa Saba z'igicuku' (not converted). FDLR/FARDC response: none found.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that local sources, including notables, said at least nine civilians were killed on Thursday 17 July in the village of Hohé, Tongo groupement, Rutshuru territory, and attributed the attack to AFC/M23 fighters on patrol.
claims.place_as_written: Hohé, near Rushege, Tongo groupement, Rutshuru territory
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 fighters on patrol (as attributed by local sources)
claims.verification_note: Page supports every clause; single outlet relaying local notables, no party response found. Toll is provisional per Radio Okapi; attribution to AFC/M23 rests on local sources only.
claims.researcher_note: Local sources only; no AFC/M23 or FARDC response found. 'Thursday 17 July' stated by the source. Same page says the area sees AFC/M23 operations against FDLR and alleged collaborators.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that at least five people were killed, one wounded and two missing in the last six days in the north of Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory. It said these incidents came a few days after the killing of five people on 28 July in the same area; among the victims were Justin Kahiti, chief of the village of Kirima recently appointed by the AFC/M23, his motorcycle driver and two of his bodyguards, who were killed in an ambush at Kasesero.
claims.place_as_written: Kibirizi, Kasesero, Kilambo; Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.actor_as_written: not identified; local sources attribute some acts to M23 elements and others to reprisals by presumed Wazalendo combatants (unconfirmed)
claims.verification_note: Draft said five were killed in the ambush; the page lists four ambush victims. Draft's actor read 'combatants' where the page says presumed Wazalendo. The page does not say all five 28 July victims died in the Kasesero ambush: it names four killed there (Kahiti, his driver, two bodyguards) and separately reports a notable of Kinyatsi shot the same day. Whether the 28 July deaths are inside the 'six days' toll is unclear on the page. The page also says that, according to local sources, some of these acts are attributed to M23 elements and others to reprisals by presumed Wazalendo combatants, accusations not confirmed by official sources (page text, not in the stored excerpt).
claims.researcher_note: Local sources. The page describes mixed attributions (some acts attributed by local sources to M23 elements, others to reprisals by combatants); the excerpts support only the toll and the ambush. Date range runs to the article date.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, the day before Sunday 2 August, two people were abducted in their fields around the village of Kilambo, Kanyabayonga groupement, and that their families said they were still without news; on the evening of Sunday 2 August unidentified armed men burst into a civilian's home in Kibirizi, Mutanda groupement, and shot him.
claims.place_as_written: Kilambo (Kanyabayonga groupement) and Kibirizi (Mutanda groupement), Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Both passages verbatim on the page; date of abduction (1 August) is computed from 'la veille'. The Kibirizi victim survived the shooting and was taken to a local health facility, per the page.
claims.researcher_note: 'La veille' = day before Sunday 2 August, i.e. 1 August (computed). Victim not named. Single local-source report.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that at least about fifty young people were arrested on Tuesday 7 July during an operation by AFC/M23 police elements near the disused Katindo military camp in Goma, and that no official information was given on their place of detention or the reasons for their arrest.
claims.place_as_written: Avenues Salongo 3 and Katoyi 1 (per the article), near Katindo camp, Goma
claims.verification_note: Statement is supported; figures field normalised to the source's 'une cinquantaine' (no '50' is printed). The cited existing claim was not in the packet, so independence from it is not checked here. Residents said the youths had been denounced over thefts and alleged cannabis use; these are residents' allegations, not an official reason.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates existing r1-ATR-NK-2026-016 (MediaCongo/Radio Okapi 8 July) from an independent Congolese outlet. The page says residents had reported the youths for thefts and alleged cannabis use (alleged grounds, not an official reason). Radio Okapi 2026-07-08 also carries it (headline seen in search, not fetched).

claims.text: The outlet reported that a teacher died in detention in Goma after his arrest by AFC/M23 elements, according to several sources close to his family, who accused elements of the movement and their allies of responsibility for his death. According to these sources, he had been arrested after demanding the return of his plot, which he believed had been occupied since the AFC/M23 took control of the city, and was reportedly taken to a place of detention known as 'Chien méchant', where, the family sources said, he reportedly suffered violence before succumbing to his injuries.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 elements (as alleged by the family)
claims.verification_note: Draft said the family accused 'the movement and its allies'; page says 'elements of the movement and their allies'. Restored the source's conditionals; removed stray punctuation. Anonymous family sources; the page uses the conditional for the detention site and the violence. Victim not named. The page adds that his body was reportedly transferred to the Hôpital général de Goma morgue and the family had difficulty recovering it.
claims.researcher_note: Date of death not stated in the cited excerpts; date is the article date (6 September 2026). Victim not named. Anonymous family sources; no AFC/M23 comment found.

claims.text: Radio Okapi and Actualite.cd reported an explosive-device explosion on Saturday in Jomba groupement, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, with differing accounts. Radio Okapi, citing concordant sources, placed it at Nyirubara village, said it happened while children were handling an explosive device they had just picked up, and gave seven dead (five children and two women) and about ten seriously injured taken to health facilities. Actualite.cd placed it at Gikoro, gave at least seven dead and more than ten seriously injured, said according to several sources that the device had reportedly been abandoned by persons not yet identified, and that the victims were reportedly mainly farmers; it called the toll provisional.
claims.place_as_written: Nyirubara (Radio Okapi) / Gikoro (Actualite.cd), Jomba groupement, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Draft said both outlets gave 'seven' dead; Actualite.cd says 'at least seven' and calls the toll provisional. The 12 September date is printed in each article's lead but not in the stored excerpts, so the statement says 'Saturday' and the date sits in the date field. Discrepancy kept visible: place (Nyirubara vs Gikoro), circumstances (children handling a picked-up device vs a device abandoned by unidentified persons) and victim profile (five children and two women vs mainly farmers). Both agree on at least seven dead on 12 September in Jomba groupement. Neither attributes the device to a party.
claims.researcher_note: Discrepancy to surface: place (Nyirubara vs Gikoro) and victim profile (5 children + 2 women vs mainly farmers). Both agree on 7 dead, 12 September, Jomba groupement. Igihe (Kinyarwanda) also headlined 7 killed by a buried device; its page could not be fetched. Context, not a clash-related attack by a named party.

claims.text: La Prunelle Verte reported that the AFC-M23 administration announced stricter movement restrictions: people coming from Beni, Butembo and Oïcha were no longer allowed to enter the territories under AFC-M23 control until further notice, and vehicles from those areas must be checked, as a measure it presented as preventive against Ebola.
claims.place_as_written: Territories under AFC-M23 control (entry from Beni, Butembo, Oïcha)
claims.verification_note: Every clause on the page. A de facto authority's announcement as relayed by one outlet; no finding on its effect on access to care.
claims.researcher_note: Epidemic context (Ebola) for access to care; no finding that care was denied to patients. Zonebourse (20 Aug, seen in search only) carries a similar item.

claims.text: Enquête.cd reported that the health crisis cell set up by the rebel administration announced on Thursday 3 September a new confirmed Ebola case in the Kayna health zone, a 21-year-old man from Butembo identified at a health checkpoint in the Itsu health area and transferred to the Kirumba quarantine site; it said Reuters also reported on 4 September a new case in an AFC/M23-controlled zone after the epidemic had been declared over in the territories under its control.
claims.place_as_written: Kayna health zone (Itsu health area; Kirumba quarantine site)
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 health crisis cell (de facto authority)
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; the Reuters clause is Enquête.cd's own citation of Reuters, kept attributed. Kayna is outside the unit's core territories (rebel-held Lubero); de facto health administration context. The Reuters report was not opened.
claims.researcher_note: Outside strict unit geography (Lubero territory, rebel-held) but relevant to the de facto health administration in North Kivu. Epidemic context only.

claims.text: Bwiza (Kigali) reported that the AFC/M23, through its spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, said FDLR fighters attacked civilians at Mulala in Rutshuru territory on the night of Monday 31 August, killing four and wounding ten, and that two women going to their fields were abducted; the movement accused Kinshasa of failing to stop FDLR activities.
claims.place_as_written: Mulala, about 20 km from Vitshumbi, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Every clause is on the page and stays attributed to the AFC/M23; partisan source, grade C. Party account only: Bwiza (Kigali) states the FDLR attack in its own voice, but the confirmation it cites is the AFC/M23's. No independent source and no FDLR or Kinshasa response found. Time given as about 21:45 ('saa tatu n'iminota 45 z'ijoro').
claims.researcher_note: Party account only (AFC/M23 claim carried by a Rwandan private outlet; the article's own voice asserts the FDLR attack as fact, but the confirmation it cites is the AFC/M23's; no independent source). No Kinshasa/FDLR response found in searches. Kinyarwanda source. Cite 'AFC/M23 says'. Possibly same series as umuryango.rw existing claims on FDLR in Rutshuru.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, in a declaration on Tuesday 21 July in Mangina, Beni territory, the coordination of North Kivu civil society implicated the ADF in the north and the AFC/M23 coalition in the south in the worsening security situation; its coordinator John Banyene said: 'Le M23 continue de massacrer, torturer, violer, piller les ressources naturelles et les biens de la population'. Radio Okapi, summarising the declaration, said the rebels were deploying recently trained troops at Tchanzu with logistical support from the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF).
claims.actor_as_written: coordination of North Kivu civil society (speaker); M23, ADF and RDF (as alleged)
claims.verification_note: Attribution of the Tchanzu sentence made precise: it is the outlet's summary of the declaration, not a quoted line of the declaration. General civil-society allegations (including rape) with no incident detail. The Tchanzu/RDF sentence is Radio Okapi's narration of the civil society's assessment, not a quotation. Banyene's quote continues on the page (illegal occupation of homes and fields, illegal taxes, forced recruitment of youths, targeted killings).
claims.researcher_note: Civil-society allegation, general, not an incident. The page does not state where Tchanzu is. General allegation including 'violer' without incident detail.

claims.text: Congovirtuel reported, citing Africa Intelligence, that Théo Binamungu, described as a close political adviser to Nangaa, was arrested at the end of August by loyalists of Makenga, interrogated by the military intelligence of the Armée de la révolution congolaise (ARC) and then by the Direction pour la sécurité et les renseignements (DSR), and transferred to Munzenze central prison on 8 September.
claims.actor_as_written: loyalists of Sultani Makenga; ARC military intelligence; DSR (as reported by Africa Intelligence)
claims.verification_note: Draft wrote 'AFC/M23 military intelligence'; the page names the ARC's military intelligence. Origin credited to Africa Intelligence. Single paywalled origin (Africa Intelligence) relayed by an editorialising analysis site; not independently verified. No AFC/M23 comment found.
claims.researcher_note: Single, paywalled-origin report relayed by Congovirtuel (analysis outlet; editorialised). Not verified independently; reported by Africa Intelligence per the page. The ARC is the AFC/M23 army wing as the page uses the name. Unit/commander lead: Sultani Makenga.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that fighting was reported on the morning of Tuesday 13 October around Kiseguro, Rutshuru territory, between presumed Wazalendo fighters and those of the AFC/M23, described as recently renamed the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN). Local sources said the attack on an AFC/M23 (FRN) position began around 5 a.m. and no toll was available.
claims.place_as_written: Kiseguro (Binza groupement), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the retained page and about this event; 'Tuesday' translates 'mardi' (flag spurious). Toll clause is on the page. Radio Okapi does not say who held Kiseguro after the fighting; Actualite.cd and Les Volcans News give differing accounts (separate claims).
claims.researcher_note: Local sources, no toll. Kiseguro said to be about twenty km north-east of Kiwanja. Sibling reports: Actualite.cd 14 Oct, Les Volcans News 13 Oct.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that the Wazalendo launched the attack on a Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) position at Kiseguro on Tuesday morning and, after several hours of fighting, withdrew from the area, leaving the positions in the hands of the FRN rebels.
claims.place_as_written: Kiseguro (Binza groupement), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Supported; date is computed from a weekday so date_precision set to approximate. Actualite.cd's account of control; Les Volcans News said control was not clearly established. Keep the accounts separate. The article dates the attack only as 'mardi' (date computed from the 14 Oct publication).
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('mardi') and publication date 2026-10-14. Conflicts in emphasis with Les Volcans News (control 'not clearly established'), see next claim.

claims.text: Les Volcans News reported, citing local sources, that clashes broke out on Tuesday 13 October 2026 at about 5 a.m. at Kiseguro, and that control of Kiseguro by either side was not clearly established when the article was written.
claims.place_as_written: Kiseguro (Binza groupement), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts verbatim on page; flagged capitalised word is a translation of 'RDC'/'mardi'. Differs from Actualite.cd (FRN kept positions). Both accounts recorded separately.
claims.researcher_note: Same morning's event as Radio Okapi and Actualite.cd; accounts differ on who held the place afterwards.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that around 22:00 the night before the 13 October clashes, explosions were heard at Kalengera, Kisigari groupement, Rutshuru territory, and that a military drone strike was said to have targeted a rebel position there; no toll was communicated.
claims.place_as_written: Kalengera (Kisigari groupement), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: military drone, unattributed by the source; targeted a 'rebel position'
claims.verification_note: Supported; flagged figures 13 and 22h are on the page (22 heures = 10 p.m.). Drone strike is conditional ('aurait visé') and unattributed. Actualite.cd and Les Volcans News describe 'combats' at Kalengera the day before, not a drone strike.
claims.researcher_note: Night before 13 Oct, so approx 12 Oct. Actualite.cd 14 Oct and Les Volcans News speak of 'combats' at Kalengera the day before, not a drone strike.

claims.text: FNTV reported, citing a family source quoted by the Agence congolaise de presse (ACP), that Martin Dushime, 27, a final-year medical student said to have been forcibly enrolled in the AFC/M23, surrendered to the FARDC; the article states he had been abducted in Goma on 6 July 2025. The accusation of abduction and forced recruitment comes from the family source and the outlet and is not confirmed by AFC/M23 in the article.
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; flagged '23' is from 'AFC/M23'. Replacement adds the family quote that carries the forced-recruitment allegation. The surrender date is not stated; 8 Oct is the day ('jeudi') ACP cited the family source, computed from the 9 Oct publication. Anonymous family source; no AFC/M23 response found. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: FNTV (9 Oct 2026, Lionel Kibuluku) supports the statement; the 'final-year medical student', 'forcibly enrolled' and 'surrendered' clauses are in the outlet's lead paragraph, not in the stored excerpts, so it is added. The body later calls the forced enrolment 'présumé' (alleged), which matches the statement's caveat.
claims.researcher_note: Single anonymous family source via ACP. 'jeudi' = day before publication on 9 Oct (date computed from weekday and publication date). Abduction itself dates to 2025-07-06 (within window); consider a separate record. No AFC/M23 response found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) provided care to more than 10 300 survivors of sexual violence at Sake, Masisi territory, over 13 months of intervention, and announced the transfer of its medical activities at Sake to Première Urgence Internationale (PUI).
claims.verification_note: Supported; the 10 400 psychological-support figure is on the page and now in the replacement excerpt. A care-provision count reported by MSF, not an incident count; no perpetrators or assault dates given. The article says MSF rehabilitated the Sake reference health centre, 'lourdement endommagé par les combats'. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Care-provision count, not an incident count; the article gives no perpetrators or dates of assaults. Article says MSF began in February 2025 and rehabilitated the Sake reference health centre 'lourdement endommagé par les combats'. MSF says it will refocus on Katoyi. MSF country coordinator Christine Januel quoted in the article.

claims.text: Enquete.cd reported that the 33rd Military Region spokesperson, Captain Dieudonné Kasereka, as cited by several Congolese media, confirmed on Sunday 4 October that twenty-nine fighters presented as belonging to the AFC-M23 laid down arms and surrendered to the FARDC and Wazalendo groups between 1 and 4 October 2026 in Lubero, Masisi and Walikale territories; according to the military authorities, several of them were reportedly young recruits enrolled by force.
claims.place_as_written: Lubero, Masisi and Walikale territories, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and Wazalendo (recipients); AFC-M23 fighters (surrendering), as the FARDC says
claims.verification_note: Forced-recruitment clause was attributed to Kasereka but the page attributes it to 'les autorités militaires' and in the conditional; narrowed. The page also reports ten further captures at Remeka, Mohololo, Biriko and Miko (in figures; not in any stored excerpt, so left out of the statement). FARDC account only, not independently verified; no AFC/M23 response found. Discrepancy: Enquete.cd names the 33rd Military Region, while Radio Okapi (8 Oct) credits the communication service of the 34th military region for the 4 October announcement of the 29 surrenders. Both stated as printed. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Enquete.cd (5 Oct 2026, Josué Kid, Kinshasa dateline) supports every clause, but says the spokesperson's confirmation was relayed 'cité par plusieurs médias congolais'; the statement dropped that second-hand sourcing, which is restored. 4 October 2026 is a Sunday.
claims.researcher_note: FARDC account only; party claim, not independently verified (Top Africa News says independent verification remains limited). Radio Okapi 8 Oct credits the '34e région militaire' communication service for related statement: unit number differs between outlets. No AFC/M23 response found.

claims.text: Top Africa News reported that African Union facilitators held closed-door talks with AFC/M23 leaders in Goma on Monday, meeting political coordinator Corneille Nangaa and his deputies Bertrand Bisimwa and Freddy Kaniki; AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the movement received the mission in the framework of efforts toward a political, durable and African-led resolution of the conflict, and no joint communiqué or concrete agreements were announced.
claims.verification_note: Supported; added the AFC/M23 leaders named in source 1 and moved the opening sentence into source 1's excerpt. Graded C: one digest outlet of uncertain independence, partisan quote. Single digest-style outlet ('We Digest News'); the page prints no date, only 'on Monday' and '3 weeks ago', so 5 Oct is computed from the URL date 2026/10/06 (approximate). Kanyuka's words are AFC/M23's account. Corroboration from AU or wire copy not found.
claims.researcher_note: Page says 'on Monday' and is dated 6 Oct (published '3 weeks ago' as scraped); date computed from weekday and publication date: Monday 5 October. Search results also carried AFC/M23 posts dating the reception to 5 October 2026 (leads only). Delegation per Top Africa News: Kenyatta, Masisi, Zewde. Digest-style outlet; corroborate with Reuters/AFP or AU.

claims.text: Tic-Tac Hebdo reported that AFC/M23 North Kivu governor Bahati Musanga Erasto signed communiqué n°01/007/CAB/GP-NK/2026 of 2 October, setting the Grande Barrière border post at Goma to open daily from 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. the following day; the document was circulated by Lawrence Kanyuka.
claims.place_as_written: Goma, North Kivu (Grande Barrière, Goma-Rubavu crossing)
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 provincial governorate of North Kivu
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; flagged '23' is from 'AFC/M23'. De facto authority's decision as reported by a local outlet; the communiqué itself was not retained.
claims.researcher_note: Reported by a local outlet from a communiqué it says was circulated by Kanyuka; the document itself was not seen. Source type: media reporting a partisan (AFC/M23) document, cite for what the de facto authority decided only.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing several military sources, that the FARDC-Wazalendo coalition was said to have retaken the centre of Katoyi on Tuesday, but was said still to be struggling to retake Kasake, which was reportedly still occupied by AFC/M23 rebels.
claims.place_as_written: Katoyi and Kasake, Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Supported verbatim; Tuesday date computed (approximate already set). Military-source claim in the conditional. The same article says fighting was still concentrated around the centre of Katoyi from dawn on Wednesday 7 October, so control remained contested. No AFC/M23 account found.
claims.researcher_note: Masisi edge of the unit. Date computed from weekday (Tuesday) and publication date 2026-10-07 (article says 'depuis l'aube de ce mercredi'). Military-source claim only; no AFC/M23 account found.

claims.text: Les Volcans News reported, according to local sources, that families displaced by armed clashes had taken refuge in Ngungu, Masisi territory, and that they said they had received no food aid since arrival and lacked sufficient means for medical care of their family members.
claims.place_as_written: Ngungu (Ufamandu 1er groupement), Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: health 'access_denied' implied a denying actor the source does not allege, and the field applies only to health_care_access claims: cleared. Date is the publication date of an ongoing situation: approximate. Added the Ngungu refuge sentence to the excerpt. Self-reported situation; no actor is alleged to block access to care. The article also says several health facilities in the area were reportedly closed for lack of medicines (not in this claim). Date is the report date.
claims.researcher_note: Displaced people's self-report via a local outlet; health obstacle is lack of means, no actor blocking access is alleged. Category kept as displacement_humanitarian.

claims.text: Enquete.cd reported, citing journalist Daniel Michombero who cited the group's spokesperson, that three fighters of the 'FRN-M23-RDF coalition' were killed in an attack attributed to the Wazalendo of the CMC/FDP movement in Rutshuru territory (the article goes on to quote Me Héritier Gashegu); two bodyguards of the new commander were also killed and another fighter wounded; according to the same sources, a woman presented as the presumed wife of the commander, and her infant, reportedly also died, hit by gunfire during the attack.
claims.place_as_written: Rutshuru territory, North Kivu (exact place not stated)
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo CMC/FDP (alleged by their own spokesperson)
claims.verification_note: 'Were also killed' upgraded the source's conditional; figures 'incl. two bodyguards' was an inference; 'Kabizo area' is not where the article places the attack. Date set to month. Rests on the attacking group's own spokesperson relayed by a journalist; civilian deaths are in the conditional and unverified. Attack date and exact place not stated (reported 27 Oct). 'FRN-M23-RDF' is the outlet's label. No FRN/AFC-M23 or Rwandan account found; Rwandan outlets reportedly described killings at Kabizo on 25-26 Oct attributed to FDLR/Nyatura (not fetched; lead only). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: two bodyguards killed, another fighter wounded 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Me Héritier Gashegu quoted after the spokesperson reference 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-011: Search found a retained counter-account: the FRN-appointed administrator (a party) describes a CMC FDP/FDLR attack at Kabizo on 25-26 Oct as killing five civilians, whereas Enquete.cd, via the attacking group's spokesperson, describes coalition fighters killed. Re-reading the Enquete.cd page also gives the spokesperson's name. Both accounts are partisan; the amendment sets them side by side without merging them.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): two bodyguards killed, another fighter wounded; Me Héritier Gashegu quoted after the spokesperson reference | cut the Kivu Morning Post / Euphrem Kabasha counter-account of a Kabizo attack (25-26 Oct, five civilians killed) and the sentence on whether the two reports describe the same attack, because the claim cites no Kivu Morning Post page; the counter-account needs its own claim from that page. Softened 'Me Héritier Gashegu, per the article' as spokesperson: the page names the spokesperson and then quotes Gashegu but does not say in one passage that Gashegu is the spokesperson
claims.researcher_note: Source is the Wazalendo's own spokesperson relayed by a journalist; the attack date is not stated in the article (reported 27 Oct; Kabizo named only in a reference to the Ruza killing). The coalition label 'FRN-M23-RDF' is the outlet's. Civilian deaths are unverified and no other party's account (FRN/AFC-M23, Rwanda) was found. Separate Rwandan outlets (Igihe, others in search results) reported five people killed at Kabizo on the night of 25-26 October, attributed to FDLR and Nyatura: page could not be fetched, so not cited; possible competing account of related events, lead only.

claims.text: Enquete.cd, relaying journalist Daniel Michombero citing the group's spokesperson, reported that three fighters of the FRN-M23-RDF coalition were killed in an attack attributed to the Wazalendo of the CMC/FDP movement; according to Me Héritier Gashegu, quoted in the article, one of the fighters killed had just been deployed to replace Nshimiye Kabo, described as head of the coalition's operations in that part of Rutshuru territory, who had been killed on 16 October at Ruza, about six kilometres from Kabizo.
claims.place_as_written: Ruza, about six km from Kabizo, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (killing of Nshimiye Kabo); speaker Me Héritier Gashegu

Single partisan-side source; the article does not say who killed Nshimiye Kabo, nor state Gashegu's role. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: relay via journalist Daniel Michombero citing the group's spokesperson; attack attributed to the CMC/FDP; FRN-M23-RDF coalition 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-012: The page does state Gashegu's role: he is the spokesperson of the CMC/FDP group that carried out the attack, relayed via a journalist, so this is a party-says account (the attacking side) and should read as such. 'Coalition FRN-M23-RDF' is the outlet's/speaker's label. A search for "Nshimiye Kabo" found nothing independent; who killed Kabo remains unstated. Grade C appropriate.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): relay via journalist Daniel Michombero citing the group's spokesperson; attack attributed to the CMC/FDP; FRN-M23-RDF coalition | cut the identification of Me Héritier Gashegu as the spokesperson (the page does not print it in one passage; it names 'le porte-parole du groupe' and then quotes Gashegu)
claims.researcher_note: Single partisan-sourced (Wazalendo spokesperson) report; no independent confirmation found. Not clear from the article whether Gashegu speaks for the CMC/FDP.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC announced the surrender of seventeen fighters of the AFC-M23/Twirwaneho coalition in Fizi territory, South Kivu, and that operation Sokola 2 Sud-Kivu spokesperson Sub-Lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi said one of them was a young civilian who had been kidnapped and forcibly recruited in Goma, North Kivu, by the M23; the army also said several children aged 14 to 16 were among the 17.
claims.place_as_written: Abala, Nyaruhinga and Kabanja, Fizi territory, South Kivu (abduction in Goma, North Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Supported; dates and places of surrender are on the page but not in the stored excerpts, so moved to the note; date field 2026-10-06 is printed on the page. FARDC account only; no AFC-M23/Twirwaneho response found. The article says the FARDC announced on Wednesday 7 October surrenders on Tuesday 6 October at Abala, Nyaruhinga and Kabanja in the Fizi highlands; its body spells 'Twiraneho' (title and tag 'Twirwaneho'). Event is in Fizi (South Kivu); the Fizi unit should integrate it. The same article credits the 34th military region for the 4 Oct announcement of 29 surrenders (cf. Enquete.cd's '33rd'). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, published 7 Oct 2026 (modified 8 Oct): FARDC announced on 7 Oct the surrender on 6 Oct of 17 AFC-M23/Twirwaneho fighters in the Fizi highlands (at Abala, Nyaruhinga and Kabanja); spokesperson Reagan Mbuyi's account of the kidnapped civilian and the army's mention of children aged 14-16 match. The stored excerpts did not carry the announcement or Fizi, so the lead sentence is added.
claims.researcher_note: Event in Fizi (South Kivu), kept here because the alleged abduction/recruitment took place in Goma; Fizi unit should integrate. FARDC account only; no AFC-M23/Twirwaneho response found. Page labelled 'Publié le mer, 07/10/2026'; title in the page differs slightly (AFC-M23/Twiraneho).

claims.text: The news site reported that FARDC-Wazalendo coalition elements recovered Masisi-Centre from the M23/RDF rebels on Wednesday 8 January 2025 after a counter-offensive; the president of the Masisi territory civil society confirmed this to the outlet and said fighting continued around the town.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt real and on-event; statement narrowed to name the civil-society speaker the page prints and to place the 'fighting continues' clause with him. 7sur7 says unnamed official sources confirmed but gave no comment; not used. Single local outlet, contradicted by other sources: C. The civil-society president is named on the page as Voltaire Batundi Sadiki. Contested: the UN Group of Experts and BBC Afrique (4 January) report M23 capture of Masisi, and Radio Okapi (3 April) says M23 had occupied the Masisi chef-lieu for several months. Accounts recorded separately, not resolved.
claims.researcher_note: Conflicts with the UN Group of Experts claim (draft r1/GOE#70, r1/UC-BI-FDLR#18) that AFC/M23 and RDF took Masisi centre on 4 January 2025 and retained it despite repeated Wazalendo/FARDC attempts. 7sur7 relays civil society and unnamed official confirmation; Radio Okapi 3 April 2025 says M23 had occupied the Masisi chef-lieu for months. Surfaced, not resolved.

claims.text: The news site reported that Guillaume Ndjike Kaiko, spokesperson of the military governor of North Kivu, announced on his X account on Tuesday evening that the Tuesday counter-offensive had allowed FARDC-Wazalendo to recover several localities from the enemy, which suffered heavy losses, without naming the localities.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu (Masisi territory localities, not named)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt real; added the page's own framing (X post, Tuesday evening, localities not named). Date computed from weekday, so precision set to approximate. Party claim of enemy losses stays attributed. Party statement (FARDC) as relayed by 7sur7.cd; the X post itself was not opened. Date 7 January computed from 'mardi dernier' relative to the 9 January article.
claims.researcher_note: Statement was reported as posted on X by the spokesperson (per 7sur7); post not independently opened. Localities not named. Date: the Tuesday before 9 Jan 2025 = 7 Jan.

claims.text: The news site reported that, according to first accounts, a bomb reportedly came from the rebel zone during fighting in the heights of Sake, where FARDC and presumed rebels had been clashing since the morning, and that its sources on the spot said the explosion killed three civilians; the local civil society said the bomb struck them in their house.
claims.actor_as_written: Bomb attributed by witnesses to the rebel (M23) zone; not otherwise attributed
claims.verification_note: Split the attributions as the page does: origin of the bomb = first accounts (conditional), deaths = sources on the spot, 'in their house' = local civil society quote. Victims not named. Single local outlet: C.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet; victims not named; perpetrator attribution is 'according to first accounts', 'would have come'.

claims.text: BBC News Afrique reported that the M23 rebellion took control of Masisi, about 80 km north of Goma, on Saturday, and, citing Radio Okapi, that the army and its Wazalendo allies had retaken the town of Ngungu in Masisi territory.
claims.verification_note: Dropped the 'a few days earlier' timing: the page says Okapi reported it 'yesterday' in an article updated later, so the relative order is not fixed. Parts of the page quote Reuters; the Masisi sentence carries no credit, so credited to BBC. Date approximate as flagged. The page is a running explainer published 6 January and updated 23 January 2025; 'samedi' is read as 4 January from the publication date (approximate). The Ngungu passage says Okapi reported it 'hier' without a fixed reference date, so its timing is not given. Contested with 7sur7's 8 January FARDC-Wazalendo recapture claim.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date (Saturday before 6 Jan 2025 = 4 Jan). Page text mixes a Reuters-attributed passage; not relied on. Consistent with UN GoE 4 Jan claim; 7sur7 reports FARDC recapture 8 Jan (see separate claim).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing witnesses, that Walikale's general hospital and an NGO logistics base were damaged during the fighting, causing deaths and injuries, after the Walikale area passed under rebel occupation.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt real and on-event (hospital = Walikale hospital named in the prior sentence). Perpetrator unattributed as in the source. The MSF corroboration cited in the draft notes is not in this packet, so graded on its own source: single outlet relaying witnesses, C. The source does not say who caused the damage, nor name the NGO. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates MSF's account (existing r1-HC-NK-2025-006) that crossfire hit its base on 19 March; Radio Okapi does not name the NGO. Perpetrator not attributed.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that on the same Thursday scenes of looting were reported in the mining centres of Mubi and Ndjingala, while gunfire continued to be heard.
claims.place_as_written: Mubi and Ndjingala mining centres, Walikale territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: The page does not say who reported the looting ('ont été signalées'); removed 'citing local sources'. Perpetrator not named by the source.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet; perpetrator not named.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that FARDC soldiers and their Wazalendo allies were reported to have fallen back toward Mubi-Lubutu on the road to Kisangani.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 (supported by the Rwandan army, per Radio Okapi)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; hedge ('se seraient repliés') kept as 'were reported to have'. Single outlet, conditional: C (draft B lowered).
claims.researcher_note: Hedged ('se seraient repliés'). The page also says M23 had a few days earlier attacked Kashebere and Kibati before the final assault.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to the population, armed men in military uniform carried out systematic looting in several villages, including Mubi, Ndjingala, Logu, Biruwe, Makana and Kangama in Walikale territory.
claims.place_as_written: Mubi, Ndjingala, Logu, Biruwe, Makana, Kangama, Walikale territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed men in military uniform (not further attributed by the source)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim, attributed to the population. The page gives no date for the looting, so precision set to approximate. The source does not date the looting; 2025-03-21 is the report date.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet; no unit attributed. Complements existing Radio Okapi hospital-looting claims (r1-HC-NK-2025-007/008).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that six days after its announced withdrawal, the AFC/M23 was still present in Walikale's chef-lieu.
claims.place_as_written: Walikale chef-lieu, Walikale territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Verbatim outlet narration; page dates the withdrawal announcement to Saturday 22 March 2025.
claims.researcher_note: Consistent with Kanyuka's 24 March communiqué (existing claims) that withdrawal was blocked by FARDC drones and aircraft; GoE places withdrawal in early April. Note Okapi's page says the announcement was 'six days' earlier (22 March).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the compound of Walikale general referral hospital, which already held more than 600 displaced households, recorded an influx of new households, and that hospital sources said the assistance of MSF Holland could not cover needs.
claims.place_as_written: Walikale general referral hospital, Walikale territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Both clauses on the page; MSF shortfall attributed to hospital sources as stated.
claims.researcher_note: Figure is the outlet's, from hospital sources. A second passage on the page attributes the MSF shortfall to 'certaines sources de l'hôpital'.

claims.text: A statement from the office of the government spokesperson of Rwanda said Rwanda welcomed M23's announcement on the repositioning of its forces from Walikale in support of peace initiatives underway, as well as the DRC's announcement that all offensive operations by FARDC and Wazalendo would be halted.
claims.place_as_written: Walikale, North Kivu (statement issued from Kigali)
claims.verification_note: Removed the date from the statement (the English page prints none; the date is in the date field). Speaker attribution rests on Xinhua. Xinhua is a relay of the Rwandan statement, not independent of it. Partisan source: recorded only as what the Government of Rwanda said. The English post carries no date; 23 March comes from Xinhua's 'on Sunday' (article of Tuesday 25 March) and the dated French and Kinyarwanda versions listed on gov.rw.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan state source cited only for what Rwanda said; Xinhua (Chinese state agency) confirms the Sunday (23 March) statement. Date 23 March from the gov.rw listing and Xinhua 'Sunday'. Note Rwanda denies supporting M23 in other statements; this statement does not address it.

claims.text: Xinhua reported that, in response to the AFC announcement, the Congolese military urged Congolese self-defence forces to de-escalate the same day, stressing the need to prioritise peace talks and advance the Luanda and Nairobi dialogue processes.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; date computed from 'Saturday' relative to the 25 March article, so approximate. Xinhua does not name the speaker or quote the FARDC text; 'the same day' refers to the Saturday (22 March) AFC announcement.
claims.researcher_note: Relays the FARDC statement without naming the speaker; existing KMP claim (r1-ST-M23-2025-018) records the FARDC 24 March position. Xinhua is a state agency.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that violent clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters in villages around the Masisi chef-lieu, near Kanii on Thursday, left residents hiding; some sources said Wazalendo launched an offensive to dislodge the M23, others a M23 counter-offensive against Wazalendo coming from the Nyabiondo axis.
claims.place_as_written: Kanii and Masisi-centre, Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and Wazalendo (as the source says)
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; competing accounts kept separate. Who attacked is contested between sources on the page; no toll was available.
claims.researcher_note: Contested account of who attacked; no toll available per the source. Also states M23 had occupied the Masisi chef-lieu 'for several months', which conflicts with the 7sur7 8 Jan claim of an FARDC recapture.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that M23 rebels took Kilambo (Buabo grouping, south of Masisi chef-lieu) at the end of the previous week and were attacked by Wazalendo on Tuesday 15 April, and reported that on the morning of Wednesday 16 April the rebels were counter-attacking to reoccupy the whole area.
claims.place_as_written: Kilambo, Buabo grouping, Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; capture date approximate as the draft says. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 16 Apr 2025. The capture and the 15 April Wazalendo attack are attributed to local sources; the Wednesday-morning counter-offensive is in Radio Okapi's own voice and was not in the stored excerpt. Passage added and attribution separated. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 16 Apr 2025. The capture and the 15 April Wazalendo attack are attributed to local sources; the Wednesday-morning counter-offensive is in Radio Okapi's own voice and was not in the stored excerpt. Passage added and attribution separated.
claims.researcher_note: Local outlet only. Capture date is 'end of last week' (about 11-13 April). Residents fled toward Nyamaboko.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that Wazalendo fighters of the Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC) attacked M23 positions at Buleusa, Walikale territory, around 6 a.m. on Thursday 17 April, a locality occupied by the M23 for several months.
claims.verification_note: Removed the year, which the passage does not print (it is the page's publication date). Otherwise verbatim.
claims.researcher_note: The page adds that about half the population had fled toward Pinga and southern Lubero. Local outlet only; no toll.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that the villages of Bibatama, Luke and Mungote in Masisi territory were the scene of violent clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters for almost all of Sunday, and that hundreds of residents fled.
claims.place_as_written: Bibatama, Luke, Mungote, Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; date approximate as in draft. Article published Monday 21 April 2025 (modified 22 April); 'dimanche' = 20 April, computed.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date (published 21 April, Monday; Sunday = 20 April). No toll available per the source.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that local sources denounced extortion of residents of Ufamandu 2 by fighters of the group Union des patriotes et démocrates pour la défense du Congo, 'd'un certain Noah Maachano', who were said to be imposing since the previous week a parallel tax of 10 000 Congolese francs (3.5 USD) per household.
claims.actor_as_written: Union des patriotes et démocrates pour la défense du Congo, of 'un certain Noah Maachano' (as the source prints it)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; conditional kept. Name spelled as the source prints it; being named is not a finding of responsibility. Allegation is conditional ('imposeraient'). 2026-10-28: source 0 date edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi page carries the statement verbatim, conditional kept ('imposeraient'). The page is dated 'Publié le lun, 21/04/2025 - 23:01' although the URL path says 2025/04/22; source date corrected to 2025-04-21.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet; hedged ('imposeraient'). The source does not label the group Wazalendo. Date: published 21-22 April, 'since last week'.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that fighting broke out on Friday 25 April between M23 rebels and APCLS Wazalendo fighters in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi territory despite the truce declared at Doha; sources at Nyabiondo-Centre said the rebels reportedly launched simultaneous attacks on Wazalendo positions around 5 a.m., while other sources said APCLS fighters were the first to open fire on M23 positions.
claims.place_as_written: Kinyumba, Burubi, Kibanda, Kikomo, Kasopo (Osso Banyungu sector), Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Nyabiondo sources say the rebels 'auraient lancé simultanément leurs attaques', not that they attacked first; reworded with the conditional. Removed the year the passages do not print. The page spells the group 'APCLC' in its lead and 'APCLS' later. Who fired first is contested between sources.
claims.researcher_note: Contested account of who opened fire. The page spells the group 'APCLC' once and 'APCLS' elsewhere. Families sheltered at the MSF base and Nyabiondo hospital per the page. Local outlet only.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to other sources, the rebels were also said to have repositioned at Kibati, Walikale territory, where they set up forward positions after withdrawing from Walikale, and that a local notable said their objective would be to conquer all of Masisi and retake control of the chef-lieu of Walikale territory.
claims.place_as_written: Kibati, Walikale territory, and Nyabiondo, Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Added the page's attribution ('d'après d'autres sources') carried into the Kibati sentence ('Ils se seraient également'). The '23' flag is from 'M23'. The notable's statement is an opinion about intent, not an observed fact. A 26 April Okapi report says M23 withdrew from Kibati on the night of 25 April.
claims.researcher_note: Hedged ('se seraient'). Page continues: a local notable says their aim is to conquer all of Masisi and retake Walikale chef-lieu (opinion, not cited). Complements the 26 April claim that M23 pulled back from Kibati.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that Wazalendo fighters of the Alliance des patriotes pour un Congo libre et souverain (APCLS) retook the villages of Kasopo, Lushali and Burubi in Masisi territory after violent clashes with the M23 on Friday 25 April; that, according to local sources at Nyabiondo, Kinyumba remained under rebel occupation; and that the same sources said M23 withdrew from its forward position at Kibati (Walikale territory) on the night of Friday 25 April, falling back toward Kashebere, 15 km away.
claims.place_as_written: Kasopo, Lushali, Burubi, Kinyumba (Masisi); Kibati, Kashebere (Walikale)
claims.verification_note: Draft dated the recapture to 25 April 2025; the page only says it followed the 25 April clashes. Narrowed; removed the year the passages do not print. The page does not give the exact day the villages were retaken; it follows the 25 April clashes and was reported on 26 April. No M23 or FARDC account found.
claims.researcher_note: Local sources at Nyabiondo only; no M23 or FARDC account found.

claims.text: The UN Secretary-General reported that on 19 March 2025 the M23 took control of Walikale town and withdrew from it shortly afterwards, while peace-negotiation initiatives were under way in Qatar and Washington.
claims.place_as_written: Walikale town, Walikale territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Verbatim in paragraph 19 of S/2025/403 (the PDF text has a stray space in 's ’est'). UN report: A. The report does not date the withdrawal.
claims.researcher_note: The report does not date the withdrawal; GoE (existing claim) puts it in early April after FARDC airstrikes, and Radio Okapi on 27 March says M23 was still in the chef-lieu.

claims.text: The UN Secretary-General reported that on 2 May 2025 the M23 clashed with the FARDC as it expanded west into Lubero, toward the shores of Lake Edward, and that in mid-May the group resumed its expansion in the northern part of Walikale territory.
claims.place_as_written: Northern Walikale territory and Lubero, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Verbatim in paragraph 19 of S/2025/403. UN report: A. The report adds that the northward expansion was then halted by increased FARDC and UPDF deployments around Lubero under Operation Shujaa.
claims.researcher_note: Lubero lies outside this unit; recorded for context. The report adds in its following sentence that the northward expansion was halted by increased FARDC and UPDF deployments around Lubero under Operation Shujaa.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local civil sources, that between 200 and 400 young people, including some secondary pupils, were seized by the AFC-M23 rebels in a cordon operation on Wednesday 5 November and taken to the Materdei parish compound in Masisi; the local sources described it as forced recruitment, while the report said there had been no communication about the operation on the movement's digital platforms.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt real and on-event. Day number and 'M23' removed from the statement because the stored excerpt does not print them; date 2025-11-05 and actor AFC-M23 rest on page passages in clause_support. The page also says those rounded up included minors ('jeunes mineurs et adultes confondus').
