claims.researcher_note: Relation tagged counterclaim to pair with the AFC/M23 'generalised offensive' claim above (Kinshasa/FARDC's own account of this offensive not found).

claims.text: Congoprofond.net reported that a violent fire broke out on Monday 19 January 2026 around 23:00 at the logistics base of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) and spread to much of the Masisi General Reference Hospital (HGR) in Masisi-Centre; at publication the fire was still burning, no official source had given a cause and no casualty toll had been communicated.
claims.place_as_written: Masisi-Centre, Masisi (HGR Masisi and MSF logistics base)
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed; cause not established by the source
claims.verification_note: Verified on page; health relevance as damage to a facility, not as an attack. Cause unknown: the source lists a short circuit, a domestic accident or a malicious act as open questions. This is a fire, not a reported attack; no party is alleged responsible. Single local outlet, first-hours report; no follow-up found. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. Regraded C->B on independent, non-partisan corroboration. 1 verified counter-reporting source(s) recorded in notes. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet, first-hours report; cause unknown (short circuit, accident or malicious act all open per the source). No claim of deliberate attack. Health relevance: HGR Masisi is MSF-supported. Follow-up on cause and damage not found. Counter-reporting: Actualite.cd (2026-01-20): Claim says no official source had given a cause and no toll was communicated; this later report gives an electrical fault as cause and four patient deaths (three children). Says nothing on the MSF logistics base.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing customary and local security sources, that the town of Katoy, seat of Katoy sector in Masisi territory, returned to Wazalendo control on Sunday 12 July after fighting with AFC/M23; the Wazalendo offensive was said to have been launched by fighters from Waloa Loanda groupement in Walikale, and AFC/M23 were said to have withdrawn towards the Ngungu axis.
claims.verification_note: Page supports every clause; withdrawal kept conditional ('se seraient repliés'). Single outlet relaying unnamed local sources: C. Actualite.cd says the information is hard to verify independently; no toll given. Katoy is spelled Katoyi in other reports.
claims.researcher_note: Actualite.cd says information is hard to verify independently and no casualty figures were available. Katoy is spelled Katoyi in later reports; a later draft claim (NKS-2026Q4#9) has Katoyi centre retaken 6 Oct.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the NGO Groupe d'action pour la protection de l'enfance (GAPE) said, in an interview on Wednesday 15 July 2026, that at least fifty-six children had been recruited by local armed militias, notably Wazalendo factions, in Walikale territory during the first two weeks of the school holidays; according to testimonies cited by GAPE's coordinator, the children had reportedly left their families voluntarily to join the groups.
claims.place_as_written: Walikale territory (groupements Waloa Uroba and Bakano)
claims.actor_as_written: local armed militias, notably Wazalendo factions (per GAPE)
claims.verification_note: Flagged '15' and '56' are printed on the page (interview date; coordinator quote '56 enfants au total'); the excerpt prints the figure in words (cinquante-six). Single NGO account: C. excerpt_en flag: 'NGO' renders 'ONG'; translation is faithful. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: interview on Wednesday 15 July 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Walikale territory 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: children reportedly left voluntarily, per testimonies cited by GAPE's coordinator 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-010: Category forced_recruitment overstates the source: GAPE speaks of recruitment/enrolment of children, and on the same page its coordinator says the children reportedly left voluntarily ('auraient quitté volontairement'). Child recruitment stands as GAPE's allegation, but the 'forced' element is not in the source; add the voluntary-departure caveat (add_excerpt needed) and consider category child recruitment rather than forced.; excerpt-support: added three excerpts: the interview of Wednesday 15 July, the Walikale territory survey, and the coordinator's account that the children 'auraient quitté volontairement leurs familles'
claims.researcher_note: Single NGO account. Page also lists groups 'Uhuru' of 'général Machite' and 'Kalomendo' and says children reportedly left families voluntarily, per GAPE testimonies; see next claim.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that GAPE's inquiries covered several localities of the Waloa Uroba and Bakano groupements (Walikale), notably in the ranks of the armed groups 'Uhuru' of 'général Machite' and 'Kalomendo'; GAPE's coordinator, Bayomba Mishiki Bam’s, said that according to testimonies the children had reportedly left their families voluntarily.
claims.place_as_written: Waloa Uroba and Bakano groupements, Walikale
claims.verification_note: Raw statement attributed the Uhuru/Kalomendo identification to the coordinator; on the page it is Radio Okapi's narration of the NGO's inquiries. The 'left voluntarily' point is conditional ('auraient quitté') and is kept so. The coordinator's name is printed on the page but not in the stored excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Roster lead: 'Uhuru' and 'Kalomendo' Wazalendo-type groups, Walikale. 'général' is a self-style rank as printed.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported on 1 August 2026 that violent fighting between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo self-defence groups began in the early hours of Saturday 1 August at Shango village, Butsike locality, Nyamaboko 1 groupement, Masisi territory; per local sources AFC/M23 attacked Wazalendo positions and gunfire was heard in neighbouring Shoa and Mahanga, with no casualty or damage figures available.
claims.verification_note: Flagged '1' (1 August, Nyamaboko 1) is printed on the page; every clause supported. Page also says it was unclear which force controlled the area afterwards.
claims.researcher_note: Reclassify as military_operation if preferred; no civilian harm reported beyond panic and sheltering.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to local sources, clashes on Monday 3 August in the Ikobo and Kisimba groupements (Walikale) between AFC/M23 and a coalition of Wazalendo groups were accompanied by looting; notables reported important looting at Buleusa, seat of Ikobo groupement, and nearby Rusamambu, where kiosks and shops were entirely emptied. Local sources said Wazalendo fighters led by self-proclaimed general Jonas Bigabo launched simultaneous attacks on AFC/M23 positions between midnight and 4 a.m.
claims.place_as_written: Buleusa, Rusamambu, Kalonge, Kasopo, Kateku (Ikobo and Kisimba groupements), Walikale
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo coalition led by self-proclaimed general Jonas Bigabo; AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Flagged '3' and '4' are printed on the page ('lundi 3 août', 'quatre heures du matin'). All clauses supported. Looting perpetrators are not named by the source.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi; local sources and notables. Looting perpetrators not named. Wazalendo reportedly occupied some localities for a few hours before calm returned; both forces remained present.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing concordant and administrative sources, that AFC-M23 fighters retook Remeka, seat of Ufamando groupement in Masisi territory, on Thursday 20 August 2026 after intense fighting against FARDC allied with Wazalendo; Kashukano, Kamuobe, Miano and Buuli were also said to have fallen to AFC-M23.
claims.verification_note: Date 20 Aug matches the excerpt. Flag '23' is the 'M23' in the group name. Single local outlet (Goma-based): graded C, not B. Remeka changed hands again: FARDC say they retook it on 15 Sept (FARDC communiqué); fighting resumed there on 25 Sept (Actualite.cd).
claims.researcher_note: Local outlet in Goma (M23-held). Remeka changed hands again: FARDC claim reconquest 15 Sept (separate claim).

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23, in a communiqué, accused government coalition forces of summarily executing several civilians at Luntukulu, on the Nzibira axis; according to AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka the victims allegedly included women and children.
claims.place_as_written: Luntukulu, Nzibira axis (location as printed by the source)
claims.verification_note: Statement matches page, attributed throughout, conditional kept ('allegedly'). Kanyuka's name is printed on the page (not in the excerpt). Outside the unit's Masisi/Walikale area, so relation new_related_event; province South Kivu. Partisan allegation (AFC/M23 says); not verified. Luntukulu is in South Kivu; the source does not name the territory. No FARDC response found in this unit.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan allegation, reported date approximate (communiqué date not given; page published 2026-08-21). Location is outside Masisi/Walikale (Nzibira is in South Kivu); kept as related to the unit's news page. Province/territory not established by the source. No FARDC response found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing several local sources, that on Tuesday 8 September wazalendo dislodged AFC/M23 from Rutoboko and then retook Kibahemula in Nyamaboko 1er groupement, Masisi; the Humura commercial centre was said to remain under AFC/M23 control.
claims.verification_note: Date 8 Sept and every clause printed on the page. Kept separate from the Kazinga/Humura claim, which is a different account. Separate account from Kivu Morning Post's report (published 8 Sept) of AFC/M23 taking Kazinga and Humura; both describe contested, shifting control in Nyamaboko 1. Actualite.cd on 18 Sept says FARDC and wazalendo had retaken Humura and Rutoboko.
claims.researcher_note: Conflicts with Kivu Morning Post report of AFC/M23 taking Kazinga and Humura around 7 Sept (separate claim); the two reports describe fluid, contested control. Actualite.cd says no precise toll available.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing concordant sources, that AFC/M23 took control of the villages of Kazinga and Humura in Nyamaboko 1 groupement, Masisi, dislodging the Congolese army and Wazalendo militias who had retaken the area; an anonymous health source quoted said AFC/M23 had also retaken Ngomashi, Mwima, Humura and Burinda.
claims.place_as_written: Kazinga, Humura, Ngomashi, Mwima, Burinda (Nyamaboko 1), Masisi
claims.verification_note: Statement supported. Date corrected: 7 Sept on the page is a different event (fighting on another axis); the capture is dated only by the report's publication, so 2026-09-08, approximate. Flag '1' is 'Nyamaboko 1', printed. Capture day not stated; dated to the report (8 Sept). The only 7 Sept on the page concerns fighting on the Minjenje-Pinga axis in Walikale. Separate account from Actualite.cd's report of wazalendo retaking Rutoboko and Kibahemula on 8 Sept. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Kivu Morning Post (8 Sep 2026) supports every clause, but the stored excerpt carried only the dislodging sentence; the capture sentence and the health-source quote are added. The page gives no exact date for the capture (8 Sep is the publication date). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Kivu Morning Post (8 Sep 2026) supports every clause, but the stored excerpt carried only the dislodging sentence; the capture sentence and the health-source quote are added. The page gives no exact date for the capture (8 Sep is the publication date).
claims.researcher_note: Page dated 2026-09-07/08; exact capture day not stated. Same page says AFC/M23 had also taken Katoyi-Centre. Contrasts with Actualite.cd 9 Sept (Humura still AFC/M23-held; Rutoboko/Kibahemula retaken by wazalendo).

claims.text: Mediacongo, carrying a report credited 'DMK, La Tempête des Tropiques / MCP', reported that, according to certain sources, the army allegedly used air strikes on Tuesday 8 September at around 5 p.m. against rebel positions at Malemo (Bahali Mokoto groupement, Masisi) and Luola (Walikale); local sources said they heard loud detonations.
claims.verification_note: Statement supported and kept conditional. '5 p.m.' renders '17h'. End-of-page credit shows the origin is La Tempête des Tropiques, so originating_source set to it. Republished by Mediacongo from La Tempête des Tropiques; the article is written in the conditional and uses pro-government wording elsewhere ('l'ennemi rwandais'). No toll given; no FARDC confirmation seen. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Mediacongo, 10 Sep 2026, credit line 'Par DMK, La Tempête des Tropiques / MCP, via mediacongo.net' (originating_source already records it). All clauses are on the page, in the conditional; no toll available. The statement should credit La Tempête des Tropiques.
claims.researcher_note: Conditional ('aurait fait usage'); unnamed sources; no FARDC confirmation seen.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing anonymous local sources, that violent fighting began at about 5 a.m. on Thursday 10 September 2026 at Kibati, Luberike groupement, Walikale, when a Wazalendo-FARDC coalition launched an offensive on AFC-M23 positions; it described Kibati as having been under AFC-M23 control for several months, and a resident said no inhabitants remained in Kibati.
claims.verification_note: Date '10' printed on the page. All clauses supported. Single local outlet relaying anonymous sources: graded C, not B. excerpt_en flags: 'AFC-M23'/'Kibati' renderings, translation faithful.
claims.researcher_note: Outcome reported by Actualite.cd on 18 Sept (next claim).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported on 18 September that the centre of Kibati, in Luberike groupement (Walikale), had returned under AFC/M23 control after the withdrawal of the FARDC and wazalendo, who had briefly occupied Kibati and advanced to Milonge, about five kilometres along the Kibati-Kashebere axis.
claims.verification_note: Every clause supported. Flag '18' is the publication date, printed on the page ('ven 18/09/2026'). Day of the retaking not given; dated to the report (18 Sept).
claims.researcher_note: Date is publication date; exact retaking day not given. Page also describes an AFC/M23 push toward Hembe aimed at Pinga via Bushimoo, met by a FARDC counter-offensive.

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported that the FARDC, in a communiqué signed by Lieutenant Marc Elongo, spokesperson of operational sector Sokola 1 Grand-Nord and Front Nord, said on 20 September they observe the ceasefire on all North Kivu front lines while denouncing attacks they attribute to AFC/M23-RDF on the Walikale-Masisi axis, which they said violate the Doha and Washington accords and cause displacement toward Walikale, with villages burned and fields destroyed.
claims.verification_note: All clauses printed on the page. Flagged '20', '23', '7' are the receipt date, 'M23' and '7sur7'; all printed. 'said on 20 September' is read as the date the communiqué was made public/received (noted). Party statement (FARDC says). 20 September is the day a copy reached 7sur7.cd; the communiqué's own date is not printed. The communiqué also cites the North Kivu military governor, général-major Somo Kakule Évariste, on the army's right to defend its positions. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: 7sur7.cd, 20 Sep 2026 (Bantou Kapanza Son): every clause is on the page (communiqué copy received on Sun 20 Sep). The stored excerpt only carried the displacement clause; added the ceasefire and accords passages. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: 7sur7.cd, 20 Sep 2026 (Bantou Kapanza Son): every clause is on the page (communiqué copy received on Sun 20 Sep). The stored excerpt only carried the displacement clause; added the ceasefire and accords passages.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan statement of the Congolese army. Same page: military governor of North Kivu and operations commander is général-major Somo Kakule Évariste (named as printed 'Somo Kakule Évariste').

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported a communiqué from major Dieudonné Kasereka, communication officer of the 34th military region, in which the FARDC, supported by VDP, said they neutralised 14 AFC/M23 elements over three days of fighting in Masisi, Walikale and Rutshuru, with thirteen other fighters wounded, three captured and two VDP fighters killed; the FARDC said they retook the Miko hill and Remeka centre (Masisi) on Tuesday 15 September 2026.
claims.place_as_written: Masisi, Walikale and Rutshuru territories; Miko hill and Remeka centre (Masisi)
claims.verification_note: Every figure is printed on the page (14 in the title and lead; two VDP killed and eight weapons, conditional, later in the article). Attribution to FARDC kept throughout. date_precision 'range' with a single date was incoherent: set approximate. Party figures (FARDC says), unverified. The three days of fighting are not dated on the page; only the Remeka/Miko retaking is dated (15 Sept). Actualite.cd (18 Sept) separately reports Miko and Remeka back under government control. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: 7sur7.cd, 19 Sep 2026 (Reagan Bin Kakani): every clause is on the page, but the stored excerpts do not carry the headline figure (14 AFC/M23 neutralised) or the two VDP killed; added. The page dates the retaking of Miko and Remeka to Tue 15 Sep 2026; the article itself is dated 19 Sep. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: 7sur7.cd, 19 Sep 2026 (Reagan Bin Kakani): every clause is on the page, but the stored excerpts do not carry the headline figure (14 AFC/M23 neutralised) or the two VDP killed; added. The page dates the retaking of Miko and Remeka to Tue 15 Sep 2026; the article itself is dated 19 Sep.
claims.researcher_note: Army figures, unverified. The 14 'neutralised' figure appears in the page's first sentence ('affirment avoir neutralisé 14 éléments') and two VDP killed in a later sentence. Date range: three days ending around 19 Sept; 15 Sept for the Remeka claim. 34th military region (page spelling).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting resumed early on Friday 25 September between AFC/M23 and the FARDC supported by wazalendo at Remeka, Ufamandu 1er groupement (Masisi), about a week after the FARDC and wazalendo retook the centre of Remeka in a counter-offensive; AFC/M23 reportedly attacked with reinforcements from Ngungu.
claims.verification_note: Date 25 Sept and every clause printed on the page. Flags '1' (Ufamandu 1er) and '23' (M23) printed. Outcome of the 25 Sept fighting not stated. 'About a week after' is consistent with the FARDC's 15 Sept retaking claim.
claims.researcher_note: Outcome of 25 Sept fighting not stated.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Médecins Sans Frontières was transferring its medical activities at Sake, Masisi territory, to Première Urgence Internationale after 13 months; in that period MSF teams treated more than 10 300 survivors of sexual violence, and MSF said it was redirecting resources to other areas including Katoyi in Masisi.
claims.actor_as_written: Médecins Sans Frontières; Première Urgence Internationale
claims.verification_note: Statement and figures supported by the page. Recategorised from health_care_access/facility_closed to displacement_humanitarian, since the facility did not close (care handed over to PUI). Handover of care to PUI, not a closure or an attack: PUI continues care at the Sake reference health centre. The sexual-violence figure (survivantes, female survivors) covers 13 months of MSF activity at Sake. Figures are MSF's, relayed by Actualite.cd.
claims.researcher_note: Handover of care, not an attack or denial of access; 'health' field set as nearest allowed value is questionable: reviewer may recategorise as displacement_humanitarian. Page says MSF in Feb 2025 rehabilitated the heavily damaged Sake reference health centre. Complements existing draft NKS-2026Q4#5 (Actualite.cd 17 Oct).

claims.text: BBC News reported that, responding to the US sanctions, Rwanda's foreign ministry said the sanctions would not resolve the conflict.
claims.verification_note: Supported by BBC (Wycliffe Muia). Party statement relayed by BBC. Date is the BBC publication date (21 Feb 2025); the BBC does not give the day of the ministry statement.
claims.researcher_note: Headline calls the sanctions 'unjustified'; the body's 'unjustified and unfounded' wording sits in a passage with a link artifact so is not quoted. Publication date used.

claims.text: The DRC foreign ministry said in a press release that the comprehensive peace accord with Rwanda was signed in Washington in the presence of US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and described it as a decisive step towards ending the conflict.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
claims.verification_note: Supported by the communiqué itself. Partisan source, grade C as party statement. Party (DRC government) communiqué; recorded as what Kinshasa said.
claims.researcher_note: Party communiqué, cited for what the party said only.

claims.text: The Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that Minister of State Dr. Mohammed bin Abdulaziz bin Saleh Al Khulaifi affirmed that the signing of the Doha Framework Agreement for Peace between the DRC government and the Congo River Alliance (March 23 Movement), which took place Saturday, represents an important step.
claims.verification_note: Supported; dateline 15 Nov 2025, which was a Saturday. Mediator's own statement.
claims.researcher_note: Mediator's own statement; dateline 15 Nov 2025 (a Saturday).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe told the press on Thursday 30 October 2025 that any decision on reopening Goma airport must be taken within the Doha negotiations, and that Paris could not reopen an airport while those concerned were not present.
claims.place_as_written: Goma airport, North Kivu (statement made in Kigali/Rwanda)
claims.verification_note: Statement supported. Location of the remark is inferred in draft location field; flagged in note. The page does not say where Nduhungirehe spoke; the location 'Kigali/Rwanda' in the draft is not supported.
claims.researcher_note: Context: French President Macron announced at a Paris conference the planned reopening of Goma airport for humanitarian flights. DW (2025-10-31) independently reports Rwanda's opposition.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya recalled that the reopening of Goma airport would take place only with the authorisation of the Congolese authorities and exclusively for daytime humanitarian flights.
claims.place_as_written: Goma airport, North Kivu (statement in Kinshasa)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact, supports statement. Date is the Actualite.cd publication date; the page does not date Muyaya's remark.
claims.researcher_note: Exact date of the remark not stated; publication date used.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa asked on X how the reopening of Goma airport for humanitarian reasons could be discussed while Walikale and Masisi in North Kivu and Fizi, Walungu and Mwenga in South Kivu were, in his words, subjected daily to bombardments by the Kinshasa regime targeting civilian sites, factories, bridges, airfields and humanitarian aircraft.
claims.place_as_written: Walikale, Masisi (North Kivu); Fizi, Walungu, Mwenga (South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Supported as party statement; 'AFC/M23' printed on page. Partisan allegation by AFC/M23; not corroborated. Date is the article's publication date.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan allegation of strikes by Kinshasa; cited only as what AFC/M23 said. Not independently corroborated here (lead for attack/health-access units).

claims.text: Jeune Afrique reported that, after several days of pressure from the US administration, the Kigali-backed rebel group announced in the night of 15 to 16 December its intention to withdraw from the city of Uvira, which it had taken the previous week.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (the 'groupe rebelle soutenu par Kigali', per Jeune Afrique)
claims.verification_note: Supported; JA byline 'Par Jeune Afrique' (photo credit AFP only). Announcement only; Anadolu reported no withdrawal movement observed by 07:00 GMT on Tuesday 16 December. 'Kigali-backed' is Jeune Afrique's characterisation.
claims.researcher_note: Capture of Uvira roughly 10 Dec 2025 (BBC page dated 11 Dec); exact day not in excerpt. Announcement only; actual withdrawal not established here (Afrikarabia, 24 Dec, says fighting continued around the city; not fetched).

claims.text: BBC News Afrique reported that, in a press release published Tuesday, AFC/M23 leader Corneille Nangaa said the unilateral withdrawal followed a request from the American mediators. Anadolu Agency quoted a communiqué signed by Corneille Nangaa: "The AFC/M23 will unilaterally withdraw its forces from the city of Uvira, as requested by the American mediation".
claims.verification_note: Both sources verified independently (BBC: Makumeno/Chothia/Muia; AA: Pascal Mulegwa, Kinshasa). Statement now says which clause rests on which outlet; date widened to the communiqué date/publication range. Anadolu and Jeune Afrique say the communiqué is dated 15 December; the BBC says it was published Tuesday (16 December). Anadolu reported that no withdrawal movement had been observed by 07:00 GMT Tuesday. The communiqué also sets conditions (demilitarisation, neutral force).
claims.researcher_note: BBC page dated 11 Dec, updated 16 Dec; 'mardi' = 16 Dec 2025 computed from weekday and update date; JA says communiqué dated 15 December. Date computed from weekday and publication date.

claims.text: The US Department of the Treasury announced on 2 March 2026 that its Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) had imposed sanctions on the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) and four of its senior officials, stating that the RDF is actively supporting, training, and fighting alongside the M23.
claims.actor_as_written: United States Department of the Treasury (OFAC)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; the date (March 2, 2026) is printed in the page header next to the title. Statement matches the page. The US government's own position (it is a mediator and party to the Washington Accords). The page names the four designated officers: Vincent Nyakarundi, Ruki Karusisi, Mubarakh Muganga and Stanislas Gashugi (not yet in a claim).
claims.researcher_note: US government is a mediator/party to Washington Accords; statement is its own position. Page dated 2 Mar 2026 per search result; excerpt checked against fetched page. Rwanda's response not yet searched (see gaps).

claims.text: The US Treasury said that, days after the Washington Accords signing, M23 captured Uvira, a strategic city on the border with Burundi, in an offensive that resulted in civilian deaths and forced thousands of residents to flee their homes; it said that despite M23's subsequent exit from Uvira, its continued presence near the border with Burundi, and the RDF's continued support for M23, carried the risk of escalating the conflict into a broader regional war.
claims.actor_as_written: United States Department of the Treasury (OFAC)
claims.verification_note: The draft said the Uvira events were 'part of its rationale for sanctions'; the page says instead that M23's presence near the border and RDF support 'carries the risk of escalating the conflict into a broader regional war'. Narrowed to the page's own wording. US government characterisation; the Treasury does not give dates for the capture of or exit from Uvira.
claims.researcher_note: Attribution is the US Treasury's own wording. Overlaps UV-2026Q1 on Uvira withdrawal; adds the US characterisation.

claims.text: Sosoyamboka.net reported that, in a declaration published on Sunday 18 October, Congolese government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya denounced the creation of the FRN as a new label masking the actors in the crisis, and said: "Quelle que soit sa dénomination, ce groupe armé relooké est appelé à disparaître au terme du processus de Doha".
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; the spokesperson title is printed in the article lede. excerpt_en flag is sentence-initial only. Single local outlet; the original declaration was not located. The same page reports Muyaya also accused Rwanda of seeking to present the conflict as an internal Congolese crisis (not yet a claim).
claims.researcher_note: Single local aggregator; the original declaration not located. Spokesperson's full title/channel not verified.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa said in Goma, in front of EU commissioner Hadja Lahbib and then the press, that the 'premiers demandeurs' for reopening the Goma international airport were the authorities in Goma, i.e. his movement, and that the AFC/M23 now said it accepted 'the principle' of discussions on the reopening process, 'taking into account the constraints' of the area it controls.
claims.verification_note: Name and date are on the page (lede) but not in the stored excerpt, so the date moves to the date field and the statement keeps the name the draft already had; added the 'principle' clause from source 1. Party statement reported by one Congolese outlet. The name Corneille Nangaa and the date 20 February are printed in the article's first sentence, not in the stored excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan statement reported by a Congolese outlet. Airport closed since late January 2025 (same article). Relevant to civilian access to health (humanitarian flights).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Congolese Ministry of Higher Education (ESU-RSI) firmly condemned on Monday 10 August the AFC/M23's appointments at several public higher-education institutions in Goma and Bukavu, calling the appointments publicised on 7 August 2026 by the de facto authorities a 'grave and unacceptable interference'.

claims.verification_note: Statement matches the excerpts. Removed 'Lawrence Kanyuka' from entities_named: the page does not print that name. Institutions named on the page include ISTM/Goma and ISTM/Bukavu (medical-technique institutes), ISC/Goma, ISDR/Bukavu, ISP/Goma and the Université Officielle de Bukavu. The ministry warned that anyone acting on the appointments faces sanctions.
claims.researcher_note: Both Kinshasa position and AFC/M23 action; the institutions include medical-technique institutes (ISTM Goma/Bukavu).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC-M23 confirmed that a case of Ebola virus disease had been reported in Goma, an announcement made on Sunday 17 May 2026 by its spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and matches. excerpt_en flag is sentence-initial only. Party statement (AFC/M23 communiqué) reported by one Congolese outlet; the page also reports the AFC/M23 set up a special Ebola response cell. No independent health-authority confirmation in this unit. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-009: Wording aligned with the source ('confirme qu'un cas ... a été signalé'). Searched (fr): no counter-account; the case is independently corroborated (Le Monde 17 May, 'un premier cas confirmé à Goma'; MSF citing North Kivu authorities' confirmation on 16 May), a lead for corroborate.py.; excerpt-support: nothing to add 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Epidemic context: health response in an M23-held area; RFI 21 May 2026 (not opened) reports Mukwege calling on M23 to reopen Goma airport for the response. Possible leads: DW 19 May, IRIS 8 June.

claims.text: Amnesty International said on 25 June 2026 that the Wazalendo member group CMC-FDP, backed by the Congolese army, has killed and tortured civilians, looted property, and abducted women as sexual slaves in Rutshuru territory; Amnesty interviewed 16 victims, survivors and family members about abuses between June and December 2025.
claims.place_as_written: Bukombo area, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: CMC-FDP (Collective of Movements for Change-People’s Defence Forces), a Wazalendo member group
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; the date 25 June 2026 and the Wazalendo membership are printed on the page (passages given). Amnesty's allegations, based on remote interviews; CMC-FDP operates in the Bukombo area of Rutshuru, which Amnesty says is controlled by M23. The page describes two survivors held in conditions Amnesty calls sexual slavery (one abducted in June 2025, held at a base in Mudugudu, Bukombo); survivors are unnamed. Legal characterisations on the page are Amnesty's.
claims.researcher_note: NGO investigation (remote interviews). Perpetrator is as alleged by Amnesty; CMC-FDP denial recorded separately. Area is under M23 control per Amnesty. No individual names recorded here (survivors unnamed).

claims.text: Amnesty International reported that CMC-FDP spokesperson Héritier Donald Gashegu responded in writing on 16 June 2026 and denied responsibility for the abuses Amnesty documented, asserting that CMC-FDP remains committed to respecting human rights.
claims.place_as_written: Bukombo area, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and matches. Party denial as reported by Amnesty; per the same page CMC-FDP 'categorically rejects' the sexual violence allegations.
claims.researcher_note: Party denial reported by Amnesty; counter to the claim above.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch and the Congolese organization SOFEPADI said that conflict-related sexual violence in eastern DRC had escalated, and that HRW had documented sexual violence by members of at least five non-state armed groups and the Congolese army.
claims.place_as_written: Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu provinces
claims.actor_as_written: M23, other armed groups and Congolese army, as HRW says
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; the 'escalated' clause and SOFEPADI co-authorship are on the page (passage given). Date checked: header 2026, dateline typo 2025. The page header dates the release 'January 12, 2026'; the body dateline reads '(Kinshasa, January 12, 2025)', which is inconsistent with the November 2025 interviews the release describes, so 2026 is taken as correct. HRW's interviews were with SOFEPADI's Beni and Bunia offices (northeastern Congo); the release covers Ituri as well as the Kivus.
claims.researcher_note: The page's dateline reads 'January 12, 2025' but the URL path and search metadata say 2026; the dateline is probably a typo — verifier to check. Regional (Ituri included); only North and South Kivu relevant to phase 1.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch and SOFEPADI said that expanded fighting in Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu, funding cuts and limited access to health services made it harder for survivors of sexual violence to get support, and that many clinics offering health care and other support had been forced to close.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu and South Kivu (and Ituri)
claims.verification_note: Statement matches. Removed 'Évariste Ndayishimiye' from entities_named: a copy error, the HRW page does not name him. See the date note on the companion HRW claim (header 2026, dateline typo 2025). The page links the clinic closures in part to US aid cuts.
claims.researcher_note: See date caveat in the previous claim.

claims.text: Beto.cd reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye said on France 24 on 23 September 2026, on the margins of the UN General Assembly, that he saw no sign of disengagement of Rwandan forces from eastern DRC and judged that the FDLR were only a pretext.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and matches; the year 2026 is in the page's dateline (29 SEPTEMBRE 2026) and the 81st UNGA session reference. excerpt_en flags are capitalised words that are also capitalised in the French (FDLR, DRC equivalents). Relay by a Congolese outlet of a France 24 interview; the France 24 original was not opened. Per the same page Ndayishimiye spoke as a head of state whose army fights in South Kivu and as AU chairperson; it quotes him: 'nous sommes dans l'impasse'.
claims.researcher_note: Same page notes the UN Group of Experts has not established Burundi army–FDLR collaboration in its last three reports (not cited). Rwanda's reply not searched.

claims.text: Al Jazeera, citing AFP and Reuters, reported that on Monday the UN and government sources said a ceasefire monitoring team had arrived to track the Qatari-mediated truce, and that the UN said the mission had deployed to Minembwe in South Kivu, where intense fighting had persisted in recent months.
claims.actor_as_written: ceasefire verification mission (Congolese government, M23, ICGLR observers)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact (stored excerpt 0 omits the space before the final period; verbatim passage given). Monday = 24 Aug 2026, the publication date. Byline 'Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and Reuters', published 24 Aug 2026 (a Monday). Per the page the mission is composed of members of the Congolese government and M23 plus ICGLR observers, with MONUSCO logistical support reported by local journalists, and will visit Uvira and Kalehe. Lead: the same page reports a DRC statement that day accusing M23 of killing 'more than 300 people' in June and July, rejected by M23.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date. The same article says the mission will visit Uvira and Kalehe. Caption dates a photo as 12 May 2026 for FARDC in Ruzizi Plains.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the villages of Muzinzi and Bwahungu in Walungu territory were the scene of fighting between the FARDC supported by the Wazalendo and the M23.
claims.verification_note: Day number came only from the page header (sam 01/03/2025), not the excerpt or body; removed from the statement, kept in the date field. 'Citing several witnesses' dropped: the excerpt is the outlet's narration. Article dated 1 March 2025; witnesses quoted say the fighting had gone on since the morning.
claims.researcher_note: Local single outlet.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, according to several local sources, fighting resumed early on 1 March 2025 in Bilalombili village near Mikenge, Mwenga territory, where the Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and Android elements allied to the M23 attacked Wazalendo positions.
claims.place_as_written: Bilalombili village near Mikenge, Itombwe, Mwenga territory
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho, Red Tabara, Android (allied to M23); Wazalendo

claims.researcher_note: Local civil-society sources named elsewhere in the article (Pacifique Kararuka, Parisien Ngini) are not in the excerpt. The article says Twirwaneho and Wazalendo had clashed in Itombwe villages since 23 February.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that local civil-society groups denounced the burning of houses in Bilalombili village, which had hosted people displaced from Mikenge and elsewhere, without giving a number.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports; perpetrator correctly left unattributed.
claims.researcher_note: Article quotes civil society saying all houses were burned and no toll was yet known; perpetrator not stated in the excerpt; the same article reports the Twirwaneho/M23 attack that morning.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, after fighting with Wazalendo militiamen, the AFC/M23 rebels entered Mwenga territory late on Monday 3 March 2025 via the locality of Kilungutwe.
claims.place_as_written: Kilungutwe, Mwenga territory (from Walungu across the Kadubo river)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports; title names AFC/M23 and Mwenga.

The page qualifies the six-territory count 'par le fait de l'allégeance du groupe Twirweneho à cette rébellion'; the statement dropped that qualifier, which overstates direct AFC/M23 presence (notably in Uvira and Fizi). Excerpt is verbatim.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 rebels seized Kaziba Centre late at night on 10 March 2025 after a full day of fighting against the FARDC supported by Wazalendo militiamen.
claims.place_as_written: Kaziba Centre, Kaziba chefferie, Walungu territory
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports exactly. Kaziba later changed hands: Wazalendo control reported from 15 March or 17 March (two Actualite.cd articles disagree); AFC/M23 retook it on 27 April.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing several local sources, that Kaziba in Walungu territory and the localities of Kigarama and Rurambo in the Uvira highlands had been occupied by Wazalendo since Saturday 15 March 2025, and that residents saw no AFC/M23 rebels in Kaziba.
claims.place_as_written: Kaziba, Walungu territory; Kigarama and Rurambo, Uvira highlands
claims.verification_note: The '23' flag is the '23' in 'AFC/M23', not a figure. Residents' observation is on the page, not in the excerpt (page-only clause). The article also says Kigatama/Rurambo were retaken by Wazalendo and 'certains éléments de la Task Force dont font partie les troupes burundaises': a lead on Burundian troops for a separate claim. Date conflict: this article says Wazalendo held Kaziba from Saturday 15 March; Actualite.cd's 24 and 28 April articles say they retook it on 17 March, a week after the 10 March capture.
claims.researcher_note: Discrepancy to surface: the same outlet's 24 April article says the Wazalendo retook Kaziba on 17 March (a week after 10 March); this article says occupied since 15 March.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that two people died and many others were wounded in violent clashes on Tuesday 18 March between Wazalendo and the M23 in the Burhale groupement, Walungu territory.
claims.verification_note: Statement unchanged; category changed from attack_on_civilians to military_operation because the source does not say the victims were civilians or name a perpetrator. The '2' flag is 'Deux' in the excerpt. The article does not say whether the dead and wounded were civilians or combatants, or who caused the casualties.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that on Sunday 13 April M23 rebels and various Wazalendo groups opened a new front in Butondo village (Luindi chefferie, Ihanga groupement, Mwenga territory), and quoted a local source denouncing the looting of cows, saying the M23 left with 16 cows the first time.
claims.place_as_written: Butondo village, Ihanga groupement, Luindi chefferie, Mwenga territory
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page; locality detail is on the page next to the excerpt; quote correctly attributed to 'une source locale'. The cattle-looting allegation rests on one anonymous local source quoted by the outlet.
claims.researcher_note: Alleged livestock looting by M23 rests on one anonymous local source; the quote is attributed in the article to "une source locale" (after the quoted words). The article says more cows were taken later, number not stated. The article calls these the first clashes to reach Luindi chefferie.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that clashes on Thursday 17 April between Wazalendo fighters and the AFC-M23 rebels in the Kamanyola groupement, launched by Wazalendo from the hills above Kamanyola against M23 positions in Kamanyola-Centre, began at 8:30 in Kalunga and lasted five hours, with wounded taken to a local medical institution according to sources on the spot.
claims.verification_note: All three excerpts from the same page support their clauses. excerpt_en flags: added 'DRC'/'Walungu'-type capitalisation in translation only; translations are faithful.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that M23 troop reinforcement was also seen on its positions in the rural areas under its control, a list that included Nyangezi, Walungu-Centre and Muzinzi.
claims.place_as_written: Nyangezi, Walungu-Centre, Muzinzi and other positions around Bukavu
claims.verification_note: Report date (18 April) came only from the page header; removed from the statement, kept in the date field. Condition described as current at the report date.
claims.researcher_note: Report date; reinforcement described as ongoing.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that Kaziba chefferie had been the scene of violent clashes since the evening of Saturday 26 April, that the AFC-M23 was trying to dislodge Wazalendo to reach the Minembwe highlands where its allies Twirwaneho, Androïd and Gumino are based, and that residents said five truckloads of soldiers arrived at Tchofi and Kasheke.
claims.verification_note: First two clauses in the excerpt; the trucks clause is on the page next to it (page-only). Witness claim of arrivals from Rwanda by speedboat correctly left out (conditional 'auraient'). excerpt_en flag: 'South Kivu' translation, faithful. The article is internally inconsistent: it says the clashes began on the evening of Saturday 26 April and later that they began on 'samedi 27 avril' around 17:00 (27 April 2025 was a Sunday). Tchofi and Kasheke are in Kalehe/Kabare, outside Kaziba.
claims.researcher_note: Internal date inconsistency in the source: the article first says clashes began Saturday 26 April and later says Saturday 27 April around 17:00 (27 April 2025 was a Sunday). The claim of arrivals from Rwanda by speedboat is attributed to witnesses ("certains auraient même emprunté...") and is not repeated here. Radio Okapi 25 April (fetched) also reports FARDC against M23 at Kaziba from Mushenyi.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 rebels retook control of Kaziba, Walungu territory, on Sunday 27 April after clashes with the Wazalendo, who were forced to pull back, and that several residents who fled Kaziba took refuge in neighbouring villages and chefferies, notably Luhwinja.
claims.verification_note: 'Plusieurs' is 'several', not 'many'; the withdrawal is on the page, not in the excerpt (page-only clause). This article dates the earlier Wazalendo retaking of Kaziba to 17 March; Actualite.cd's 17 March article says 15 March. Radio Okapi (27 April) puts the start of the fighting on 26 April.
claims.researcher_note: Article dates M23 capture to 10 March and Wazalendo retaking to 17 March (cf. 15 March in the 17 March article).

claims.text: Amnesty International reported that, after a security incident in Walungu Centre on 9 March, M23 fighters fired heavy weapons in the direction of the General Reference Hospital in Walungu, damaging the main hospital and injuring patients.
claims.place_as_written: General Reference Hospital, Walungu Centre, Walungu territory
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim in the retained PDF; attribution to M23 is Amnesty's own documented finding. Amnesty International's finding; it says it interviewed 13 people about the hospital incidents and received information from four others.
claims.researcher_note: Independent NGO attribution to M23; existing claims cite the UN fact-finding mission (shell hit paediatric ward, five killed) and Louvain Coopération. Amnesty section 6.8 says M23 fighters reportedly pursued suspected thieves and fired heavy weapons that hit the hospital; it interviewed 13 people about the hospital attacks overall. M23/Rwanda response on this incident not found.

claims.text: The OHCHR-mandated fact-finding mission reported that in June and July M23 summarily executed dozens of individuals following confrontations with Government forces in Walungu and Kabare territories, South Kivu, as apparent collective punishment.
claims.place_as_written: Walungu and Kabare territories, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim in the retained PDF (paragraph 30). Finding of the UN fact-finding mission; the period runs into July, past this unit's window. No village, date or toll is given in this passage.
claims.researcher_note: Range spills past the unit window (July); only June is in scope. Consistent with the FARDC allegation on Munzinzi (22 June) and CNDH claims already recorded.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that an official FARDC communiqué signed on Monday 23 June by army spokesperson General Sylvain Ekenge denounced a massacre by the RDF/AFC/M23 coalition that cost the lives of 17 civilians on Sunday 22 June around 18:30 at Munzinzi village, Walungu territory.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports every clause; Radio Okapi relays the communiqué, so the origin is the FARDC. excerpt_en flag: 'DRC'/'Armed Forces' rendering of the full name, a faithful translation. Party statement (FARDC). The same communiqué is relayed by Ouragan.cd; one origin. No M23 or Rwandan response and no independent confirmation found.
claims.researcher_note: Party claim only (partisan_drc_government content relayed by Radio Okapi and Ouragan.cd). No M23 or Rwandan response found; no independent confirmation found. Radio Okapi calls the speaker "le général Sylvain Ekenge", Ouragan.cd "général-major".

claims.text: Ouragan.cd reported, citing the FARDC communiqué signed by spokesperson Sylvain Ekenge, that seventeen civilians were executed on the evening of Sunday 22 June at Munzinzi and that the army said the assailants acted in reprisal for military failures, accusing residents of collaborating with the regular army.
claims.verification_note: The 17 and 22 June figures are printed on the page (and 17 in the title), not in the excerpt (page-only clause). Same communiqué as claim 17, so not independent of it. Single-origin allegation by the FARDC, relayed by Ouragan.cd and Radio Okapi; not independent corroboration. Ouragan.cd states the killings in its own voice before attributing them to the army. Radio Okapi calls the spokesperson 'général', Ouragan.cd 'général-major'. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Single-origin allegation (FARDC). Second-outlet relay of the same communiqué, not independent corroboration. Ouragan.cd page text states 24 June 2025.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant sources, that after fighting continued late on Tuesday in Kaziba chiefdom and at Kamanyola (Walungu territory), about ten civilians were killed by shells at Kaziba and three children in central Kamanyola.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that on Tuesday 2 December violent clashes broke out from 3am in Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu territory, between the FARDC and the AFC rebels linked to M23, with heavy weapons fire heard into the morning.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that a Médecins Sans Frontières convoy was attacked by Wazalendo militiamen on "vendredi 3 mai" (as printed; 3 May 2026 was a Sunday) at the former hot spot called Kalimoto, a few kilometres from Kalambi in Lwindi chiefdom (Mwenga territory), while heading to Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu to assess humanitarian needs; it reported that the agents were looted and that MSF staff came out unharmed.

claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page. Single outlet, own reporting; MSF statements are paraphrased. Weekday mismatch kept stated; date_precision approximate. Date uncertain: the article (5 May 2026) says 'vendredi 3 mai', but 3 May 2026 was a Sunday; the weekday and day number do not match. The source states the staff were looted; it does not say medical supplies were taken. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-023: Counter-account and date: MSF's own statement (claim r1-SKS-2026Q2-001) dates the incident to 1 May 2026 (a Friday, so 'vendredi 3 mai' is likely an error), describes a stop at a Wazalendo-controlled checkpoint followed by armed men 'firing among themselves', names no attacker and mentions no looting. A later Actualite.cd article (10 May 2026, found by search) itself dates the incident to 1 May. The Wazalendo attribution and the looting are Actualite.cd's alone and should sit beside MSF's account.; excerpt-support: cut MSF's own account (incident dated Friday 1 May; team stopped at a Wazalendo-controlled checkpoint; armed men firing among themselves): the claim cites no MSF page; it needs its own claim 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified contradicting source(s) recorded in notes; not regraded pending review.
claims.researcher_note: The article is dated 05/05/2026 (Tuesday) and says "vendredi 3 mai"; 3 May 2026 was a Sunday, so the weekday/day-number do not match and the exact day is uncertain. Existing claim r1-SV-2026-020 (Kivu Morning Post) dates the incident 2026-05-01. The "attack" is a robbery of staff; no medical supplies are stated looted. Page body also has no byline wire credit. Contradicting reporting: Médecins Sans Frontières (2026-05-08): Date is 1 May, not 3 May ('vendredi 3 mai' is also not a Friday in 2026; 1 May 2026 is). MSF describes armed men firing at each other with the team caught in between and does not mention an attack on or looting of the convoy.

claims.actor_as_written: armed men identified as M23-AFC-RDF rebels (as Radio Okapi reports)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; names as printed; Kabare/Karambi and the local-sources attribution carried by an extended source-1 passage. excerpt_en flag is the translation of 'vendredi' as 'Friday' (faithful). Perpetrator attribution is Radio Okapi's ('identifiés comme des rebelles du M23-AFC-RDF'), citing local sources; not independently verified. The source says Balume Mulingwa was killed on the Friday and was suspected of Wazalendo affiliation; the other four were 'exécutés le lendemain'.
claims.researcher_note: Single local-source report (Radio Okapi, 'selon des sources locales'). Source gives Friday for the first victim and 'the next day' for the rest; the range follows the article's 11-12 July. Perpetrator attribution is the outlet's report of local sources, not verified.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, in an article on a night of terror at Bukavu and Nyantende, that at around 19 heures armed men burst into the local hospital at Nyantende, first neutralising the security guards and then turning on patients; according to local sources the assailants looted goods, extorted phones from patients and violently assaulted an on-duty doctor, then withdrew unhindered to an area reputed to be under rebel control.
claims.actor_as_written: armed men (not identified by the source); the article's lead speaks of incursions by 'bandits armés'; they withdrew to an area 'réputée sous contrôle rebelle'
claims.verification_note: Removed '19:00', the computed '15' and the unprinted '16 July' from the statement (the night of 15-16 July stays in the date field, carried by the page passage in replacement_quotes). Perpetrator kept exactly as the source gives it. Perpetrators are not identified by the source; 'réputée sous contrôle rebelle' describes the area they withdrew to, not who they were. Doctor and patients not named. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Single local-source report. Night of 'mardi à mercredi 16 juillet' per the article (published 16 July). A 17 July La Prunelle press review snippet (laprunellerdc.cd) appears to repeat this (doctors assaulted, medical equipment looted in Kabare) but was not opened.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, in an article on a night of insecurity in Bukavu and Nyantende, that those events came only a few days after a cordon operation carried out by the M23 rebels in the Nyamugo neighbourhood of Kadutu commune, which it said led to the seizure of four AK-47 weapons and the arrest of about thirty young people suspected of criminal activity.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 rebels (as Radio Okapi calls them)
claims.verification_note: Removed '16 July' from the statement (not in excerpt); the article title carries Bukavu and Nyantende. Exact date not given (a few days before the article of 16 July). Fate of those detained not reported.
claims.researcher_note: Exact date not given ('quelques jours' before 16 July). Fate of the detainees not reported. Operation described only in passing.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that violent fighting broke out on Wednesday 30 July in Kamakombe village (Kabare territory) between M23-AFC rebels, described as allied to the RDF, and a Wazalendo group; it said the clashes had begun on the Tuesday in Mbayo village (Bugorhe groupement) following a reinforcement of M23 troops coming from Kavumu airport, and, according to several local sources, these troops launched an offensive against the Mouvement décisif de la libération du Congo (MDLC/RRADRDC), a Wazalendo branch present in the area.
claims.place_as_written: Kamakombe and Mbayo, Bugorhe groupement, Kabare territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23-AFC with RDF (per source); Wazalendo MDLC/RRADRDC
claims.verification_note: Narrowed the 'several local sources' attribution to the clause the source attaches it to (the offensive), not the start of fighting at Mbayo. The Tuesday (29 July) is computed from the weekday and the 30 July date. The source does not say who controlled Kavumu airport.
claims.researcher_note: Single local-source report. The Tuesday is 29 July (date computed from weekday and publication date). Places M23 troops at Kavumu airport (sources' wording) but does not state who controlled the airport.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, under a headline on fighting between M23 and Wazalendo resuming despite the accord, that at dawn M23-AFC-RDF insurgents launched an offensive in Bugorhe groupement against positions of the Wazalendo of the Mouvement décisif de la Libération du Congo (MDLC) at Kamakombe village (Kabare territory); after a brief M23 occupation of half the village, the Wazalendo pushed the attackers back towards the heights of Kavumu; the same day another attack attributed to the M23 targeted the Muzinzi subgroupement in neighbouring Walungu territory.
claims.place_as_written: Kamakombe, Bugorhe groupement, Kabare territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed the unprinted date and the Doha clause from the statement (date stays in the date field, carried by the page passage); Muzinzi attack worded as the source does ('attribuée au M23'). Walungu (Muzinzi) attack is context outside the unit's main area; the source attributes it to the M23 ('attribuée au M23'). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, Sat 2 Aug 2025, carries every clause, including Kamakombe in the lead. The Muzinzi attack was on no stored excerpt; that passage is added. Statement unchanged.
claims.researcher_note: Single local-source report. The article's Walungu attack is outside this unit's geography and recorded only as context.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that four civilians were killed on Thursday 7 August in fighting between AFC-M23 rebels and Wazalendo of the MDLC group at Kasheke village, on the border of Kabare and Kalehe territories; according to local sources, the M23 attacked MDLC positions at Kamakombe and opened a second front against the MDLC headquarters at Kasheke, headed by the self-proclaimed general Imani Shabani, and the toll was described as provisional.
claims.place_as_written: Kasheke (and Kamakombe), border of Kabare and Kalehe territories, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC-M23; Wazalendo MDLC (self-proclaimed general Imani Shabani)

claims.researcher_note: Single local-source report. Victims not named. Article text says clashes continued around 14:00 at 'Chez Mbayo', 3 km from the centre of 'Kavumo' (as printed).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, in an article on fighting at Kasheke and Buzunga, that witnesses spoke of generalised panic, looted goods, houses visited and even cases of abduction, notably at Buhama.
claims.verification_note: Removed '10-11 July' (not in the excerpt); the article title carries Kasheke and Buzunga. The page ties Buhama to new departures on the Friday morning (passage in replacement_quotes). Witness-based; no numbers, victims or perpetrators. The Friday is the article's 'ce vendredi' (article of 11 July). Radio Maendeleo separately reports that 'des éléments incontrôlés' looted and took people to unknown destinations (not cited here).
claims.researcher_note: Witness-based, no numbers, no victims or perpetrator named. Lead only.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that a communiqué of the FARDC Third Defence Zone, signed by Major Nestor Mavudisa Kamba Mayoyo, spokesperson of 'cette zone militaire', said that 'ces ennemis de la paix' attacked FARDC positions at Kamatembe and Kalao (Mubuku groupement, Kalehe territory) on the morning of 12 July 2025, and that, according to the FARDC, another position was attacked at Batanga, Irambi Katana groupement, Kabare territory.
claims.verification_note: Removed the communiqué date (15 July, page only; kept in the date field), the 'AFC-M23' and Rwandan-army clauses (headline and page only; the excerpt says only 'ces ennemis de la paix'); the accused party stays in extra.perpetrator_alleged. Graded C as a single partisan statement relayed by one local outlet. Partisan official statement (FARDC): evidence of what the FARDC said, not of the attacks. The article's headline says the FARDC accuse the AFC-M23; the article also says the army accuses the Rwandan army of supporting them (not in the excerpts). The communiqué was published on 15 July per the article. The Batanga date ('en cette même date') is ambiguous (12 or 14 July).
claims.researcher_note: Party statement relayed by a Goma-based outlet; evidence of what the FARDC said, not of the attacks. The M23 side's account for these dates was not found in this unit (the article itself mentions an earlier Kanyuka accusation against the army, not opened for this unit). The communiqué's date of 15 July is as reported; the Batanga attack date follows the article's 'same day' reading (14 July).

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported that fighting between Wazalendo and AFC/M23 broke out again on Wednesday 16 July 2025 on the hills above Kabulungu village (Bughore, Kabare territory), according to local civil society, and quoted a resident saying 'Des civils ont même été tués'; socio-economic activity had been paralysed there since the previous Monday.
claims.place_as_written: Kabulungu, Bughore, Kabare territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Date and 'paralysed since Monday' clauses were only on the page; extended passages added. '23' flag is 'M23'. Killing of civilians rests on one anonymous resident's quote; no toll, place or perpetrator for the deaths.
claims.researcher_note: Anonymous resident quote; no toll. Walungu part of the article is outside this unit.

claims.text: MSF said that an assessment it carried out in March, following violent clashes in the area in early 2025, found that of 24 health facilities evaluated in the Katana and Kalehe health zones, 15 had had to close, 10 had been damaged and 16 had been looted; Radio Okapi, reporting the same assessment, gave about 15 closed, 10 damaged and 'une quinzaine' looted.
claims.place_as_written: Katana (Kabare territory) and Kalehe health zones, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed the unprinted '12 August 2025' from the statement; date changed from the report date to what the excerpt says (early 2025 to March); Radio Okapi credited as a relay of MSF. Dates: the damage followed clashes 'début 2025' and was found by an assessment in March 2025 (date range Jan-Mar 2025 per the excerpt; the MSF page's English summary puts the heavy fighting in January and February). The MSF release of 12 Aug 2025 is the source date, not the event date. Radio Okapi relays MSF and is not independent; its looted count ('une quinzaine') differs slightly from MSF's 16. Perpetrators not named. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
claims.researcher_note: Damage dates to early 2025 (Jan-Feb fighting per MSF) and the assessment to March; the report date is 2025-08-12. Counts differ slightly between MSF (16 looted) and Radio Okapi (about fifteen); MSF is the primary. Perpetrators are not named. Katana health zone lies in Kabare territory.

claims.text: MSF said that, besides the damage to health facilities, patients faced barriers to care such as economic difficulties and insecurity, and that insecurity and the closure of the Bukavu and Goma airports continued to limit humanitarian access.
claims.place_as_written: Katana and Kalehe health zones, and Bukavu airport, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed the unprinted '12 August 2025' from the statement. General NGO statement on conditions, not a discrete incident; dated by the MSF release (12 Aug 2025).
claims.researcher_note: General statement by an NGO on a health system, not a discrete incident. Lead for the airport closure's effect on access.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that pastor Kelly Bahati Kazibaziba was shot dead on Monday 11 August by armed men on Michombero avenue in Kadutu commune (Bukavu); according to several local sources it was a premeditated murder, with suspicion of a link to the stance of his brother Joseph Kazibaziba, a businessman and president of the South Kivu Chamber of Mines, known for denouncing abuses attributed to the M23 rebellion.
claims.verification_note: Last clause was only on the page; extended source-0 passage added. '23' flag is 'M23'. Motive is local suspicion as reported ('il s’agirait'); perpetrators unidentified.
claims.researcher_note: Single local-source report; motive is local speculation. No party claimed or denied the killing in the source. Related lead on civilian insecurity in M23-held Bukavu.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that gunfire spread panic in the Panzi neighbourhood (Ibanda commune, Bukavu); according to the neighbourhood chief, armed individuals appear at nightfall and fire in the air, and on jeudi at around 19 h a fruit seller was fatally hit by a stray bullet as she was walking home; the outlet said rumours placed members of the Wazalendo group in the area but that no proof had been provided.
claims.verification_note: Removed '19:00' format and the unprinted '15 August'; place and date carried by the page passage in replacement_quotes. Victim not named. Thursday = 14 August, computed from the article of 15 August. Shooters not identified; the Wazalendo presence is a rumour the source says is unproven.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('jeudi') and publication date 15 August. The same night's bullet through the Panzi General Hospital water tank is already recorded (r1-HC-SK-2025-003, citing Radio Okapi / La Prunelle); this claim adds the fatality and the context.

claims.text: CongoRassure, in an article summarising OCHA-RDC's latest report, reported that OCHA-RDC said a relative calm was observed across Bukavu during August, but that local sources reported several cases of burglaries, killings and arbitrary arrests attributed to armed men.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; OCHA report attribution carried by an extended passage. Graded C because the OCHA document was not seen and the relay is a small outlet. Second-hand relay of an OCHA situation report that was not itself opened; OCHA in turn cites local sources. Retrieve the OCHA document to confirm and upgrade.
claims.researcher_note: Secondary relay of an OCHA situation report (the OCHA document itself was not opened). Not an incident-level source.

claims.text: CongoRassure, in an article on OCHA-RDC's latest report, reported that persistent clashes that broke out on 17 July in Kabare territory continued throughout August, and that on 13 August at least four civilians were killed by armed men at M'bayo, a locality where about 43 000 people were displaced following armed violence between 17 and 26 July.
claims.verification_note: The 17 July/August clause and the OCHA attribution were not in the stored excerpt; extended passage added. Numbers kept in the source's form. Graded C as an unseen OCHA document relayed by a small outlet. Relay of an OCHA report not itself opened. The source does not say whether the 43 000 were displaced from or into M'bayo. M'bayo is probably the Mbayo (Bugorhe) of Radio Okapi's 30 July report, not confirmed.
claims.researcher_note: The attribution to OCHA-RDC comes from the article's opening ('Dans son dernier rapport ... OCHA-RDC'), not from this excerpt. Likely the same place as Mbayo (Bugorhe) in Radio Okapi's 30 July report. Not checked against OCHA's own document.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that school activities had been paralysed since Tuesday 9 September in several schools of Kabare territory and at Kamisimbi (Walungu); according to local sources, armed men presenting themselves as Wazalendo burst into schools to send pupils home, arrested teachers and forced them to join the armed struggle against the M23 rebels, which the Nouvelle Dynamique de la société civile condemned.
claims.place_as_written: Schools in Kabare territory (and Kamisimbi, Walungu), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed men presenting themselves as Wazalendo

claims.researcher_note: Single local-source report; no numbers or names of teachers. Armed men 'se présentant comme' Wazalendo, so identity is unverified. Tuesday 9 September 2025 matches the calendar.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that M23 officials suspended all mining activities at the Lomera site in Luhihi (Kabare territory) from 'lundi 9 septembre' (as printed), for security reasons according to them, and demanded prior identification of all operators; it said thousands of people were affected by the measure of the M23, which it said occupies the region, and that the reopening date was unknown.

claims.actor_as_written: M23 officials (as Radio Okapi calls them)
claims.verification_note: Identification, 'thousands' and reopening clauses were only on the page; extended passage added. 'Thousands of artisanal miners' narrowed to 'thousands of people' as printed. Weekday mismatch kept stated; precision set to approximate. Date discrepancy in the source: it prints 'lundi 9 septembre', but 9 September 2025 was a Tuesday; the suspension began on Monday 8 or Tuesday 9 September. The source says 'des milliers es personnes' (people), not specifically miners. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 10 Sept 2025, carries every clause (it prints 'Des milliers es personnes' and 'lundi 9 septembre'); the stored excerpt lacks the thousands-affected, identification and reopening clauses, added here.

claims.text: Caritasdev.cd, summarising a Caritas Bukavu assessment report on Kalehe, listed under protection and abuse 7 cases of sexual violence documented in October, and reported child enlistment, extortion and cruel treatment.
claims.place_as_written: Luzira and Kasheke health areas, Kalehe health zone

Statement narrowed to what the excerpt and title print (assessment dates and health-area names were not in this claim's excerpt; they are carried in the related displacement claim). Documented cases from one assessment, not prevalence; no perpetrators, victims, places or dates within October are given. The assessment covered the Luzira and Kasheke health areas, Kalehe health zone, 20-27 October 2025 (see the Caritas displacement claim). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one

claims.text: Actualite.cd, quoting an OCHA DRC report, reported that between 6 and 12 November two international organisations had to temporarily suspend their movements for monitoring nutrition and health activities in the Chabombo health area because of intensified fighting in Katasomwa, Lumbishi and Chambombo, and that, in addition, four humanitarian workers were arrested by armed actors in the Minova health zone.

claims.actor_as_written: armed actors, not named by the source

Relay of OCHA; the OCHA sitrep retained for this unit does not show this passage in its retained text. The date of the arrests is not stated; the 6-12 November range belongs to the suspension sentence. The armed actors are not named.
