claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the situation remained confused on Tuesday in Tushunguti centre village, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory, and that, according to local sources, the tension followed the killing of a resident by an armed element assimilated to the Wazalendo Kirikicho fighters; a civil-society actor said the victim, killed on Monday evening, was an agent guarding a CICR depot in the area, and that the population then pursued the alleged perpetrator, who was also killed.
claims.place_as_written: Tushunguti centre, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory
claims.actor_as_written: an armed element 'assimilated to' the Wazalendo Kirikicho fighters, according to local sources (Radio Okapi)
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact. Source 0 widened to the contiguous passage giving place and 30 December. Removed the computed '29 December' from the statement (not printed); the ICRC-guard detail is credited to the civil-society actor, as the page does. Perpetrator attribution is hedged by the source ('assimilé aux', assimilated to) Wazalendo Kirikicho; not a confirmed affiliation. The article dates the confusion to Tuesday 30 December (on the page, not in the stored excerpt); the 29 December date of the killing is inferred from 'lundi soir' in an article of 31 December; neither the guard nor the alleged perpetrator is named. The killing of the alleged perpetrator by residents is a second incident. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 31 Dec 2025, carries every clause (situation confused on Tuesday 30 Dec; local sources on the killing; a civil-society actor on the CICR depot guard and the killing of the presumed perpetrator); the opening clause had no excerpt, added here.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ("lundi soir") and publication date 31 Dec 2025; victim and alleged perpetrator not named. Civil-society actor is unnamed; notables confirmed the information. Loosely tied to Maï-Maï Kirikicho per notables. The killing of the alleged perpetrator by residents is itself an additional incident.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Honneur David Safari, editor-in-chief and founder of the outlet La Prunelle RDC, had been missing since the evening of 'samedi' (Saturday) 28 December 2025 in Bukavu; that a source close to him said he had confided that people were behind him and had noticed he was being followed; and that representatives of South Kivu journalists went on Monday to the AFC/M23 intelligence office to ask for its involvement in the search.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact. Source 0 widened to carry the 'followed' testimony. Removed the inference that AFC/M23 is an actor. Kept the printed weekday and stated the mismatch and the conflicting caption date. Date discrepancy on the source page: the text says 'samedi 28 décembre 2025', but 28 December 2025 was a Sunday; the photo caption on the same page says 'disparu depuis le 27 décembre 2025' (27 December 2025 was a Saturday). The exact date is therefore uncertain (27 or 28 December). The page also spells the name 'Honneur-David Safari' in the caption. No perpetrator is named; Bukavu was under AFC/M23 control. Single source.
claims.researcher_note: Single source (a Burundian monitor relaying family and colleagues). 28 December 2025 was in fact a Sunday; the page says "samedi 28 décembre" - date as printed, flagged. No attribution; no AFC/M23 statement found in this unit.

claims.text: Top Africa News reported that AFC/M23 denied losing control of Kavumu airport: reliable sources who spoke to UMUSEKE maintained that the airport remained firmly under the control of AFC/M23 fighters, and in a statement the alliance dismissed the claims as deliberate misinformation, its spokesperson saying 'Wazalendo and FARDC have no such capability'.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Narrowed to the excerpt and headline: the Burundian social-media and FDLR context sits in another paragraph (separated by a 'READ ALSO' block), so it is left in the note, not in the statement. Partisan account: AFC/M23 says it holds Kavumu airport. Per the article, the claims it denied circulated on Burundian pro-government social networks and said FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR had retaken the airport; that context is not in the stored excerpt. The page shows no date ('1 year ago'); 27 Oct 2025 is from the URL. No FARDC, Kinshasa or Burundian account was found.
claims.researcher_note: Date is the publication date in the URL (page itself says "1 year ago"). Relays UMUSEKE (Rwandan outlet, state-aligned) and the AFC/M23 statement; a claim of AFC/M23 only. No FARDC or Burundian account located. The article also reports air and drone strikes on Kavumu in recent days, with local activists saying some hit civilian areas (not captured: no named source).

claims.text: The outlet reported that in territories such as Kabare, Uvira, Kalehe, Idjwi and Walungu agricultural and school activities were regularly disrupted by clashes, that the war had pushed some health structures to close while others had lost staff, and that those still operating faced medicine stock-outs; it said, citing an ICRC study, that these factors were contributing to many civilian deaths.
claims.place_as_written: South Kivu (Kabare, Uvira, Kalehe, Idjwi, Walungu named)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; widened to the contiguous passage that names the territories and the ICRC study. Corrected the ICRC attribution (the outlet cites it for the deaths, not for the closures) and dropped the publication date from the statement. General feature; no facility, place or date for the closures. The ICRC study is not identified and is cited for the death toll effect, not for the closures. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: General feature by a Bukavu correspondent (Déogratias Cubaka); no facility named; ICRC study mentioned but not identified.

claims.text: La Croix reported that nine months after M23 took Bukavu in February 2025 a relative calm reigned in the city, but that behind this facade lay a climate of fear fed by executions, sexual violence and the persistent presence of armed groups.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the standfirst (executions and sexual violence not attributed to a party)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt confirmed verbatim in the retained text (standfirst, page marked 'Réservé aux abonnés'). Removed 'special correspondent' and the date (from the byline and the 'Modifié le' stamp, not the excerpt). The standfirst does not attribute the executions or sexual violence to M23. Only the standfirst of a subscriber-only article was read; the body (details, attributions, sources) was not. A lead to obtain the full text, not an established finding.
claims.researcher_note: Only the standfirst is visible (paywalled "Réservé aux abonnés"); details and attributions in the body were not read. Lead for investigators; seek the full text.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that fighting between the Congolese army, backed by Wazalendo, and AFC-M23 fighters was reported on Tuesday 24 February 2026 in several villages of Kalehe territory, causing mass displacement; an anonymous resident named Katasomwa, Kitendebwa, Kashihe, Mweya and Kiduveri.
claims.place_as_written: Katasomwa, Kitendebwa, Kashihe, Mweya, Kiduveri, Kalehe, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Congolese army backed by Wazalendo; AFC-M23
claims.verification_note: Every clause found on the page; same date and place. Goma-based outlet; the resident describes the fighting as between M23 and Wazalendo, the outlet as the army backed by Wazalendo against AFC-M23. The page also says that on the Monday AFC-M23 repulsed FARDC attacks on the Lumbishi axis (Kalehe) and the Kinigi axis (Masisi). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Local outlet; resident quote anonymous.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 political spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the Kinshasa regime had once again trampled the ceasefire and that on Tuesday 24 February 2026 at 07h00 its 'forces coalisées' (coalition forces) launched deliberate attacks on densely populated areas of Kitendebwa, Kashihe and Kiduveri in Kalehe territory. The outlet, in its own narration, refers to the ceasefire signed in Doha.
claims.place_as_written: Kitendebwa, Kashihe, Kiduveri, Kalehe, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Kanyuka speaks of 'ses forces coalisées' and of the ceasefire; 'Doha' is the outlet's narration, not his words, so the attribution was split. Party statement (AFC/M23). claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that on 21 February 2026 AFC/M23 and Wazalendo clashed at Kavumu and along the Katana-Kavumu stretch in Kabare territory, with fighting resuming in the evening around 18h30, disrupting the Bukavu-Kavumu road and confining residents; one local source quoted said the clashes began after a Wazalendo element was evacuated from a health structure. The article does not name the structure, who evacuated him or why, and describes no attack on health care.
claims.place_as_written: Kavumu and Katana-Kavumu axis, Kabare, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every element of the draft statement is on the page: the article (dated sam 21/02/2026) describes the day's clashes; the evacuation-from-a-health-structure clause is a resident's testimony; 18h30 resumption, the Bukavu-Kavumu road disruption and confinement on the Katana-Kavumu stretch are all printed. Kept, with clause_support. Editor: consider category military_operation rather than health_care_access: nothing on the page describes an attack on or obstruction of health care. The health-structure link rests on one anonymous resident in a single source; the page does not say which structure, who evacuated the Wazalendo element, or why. Treat as a lead, not as an attack on health care. Date is the article's date (it describes 'the day'). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: fighting along Katana-Kavumu; resumption around 18h30 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Bukavu-Kavumu road disrupted; residents confined 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Kavumu, Kabare territory; AFC/M23 v Wazalendo 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-022: The health-structure trigger rests on a single quoted local source and is stated as fact for all 'local sources' in the draft; narrowed to that source. Recommend the editor recategorise as military_operation (no harm to health care alleged).; excerpt-support: added 3 excerpt(s): fighting along Katana-Kavumu; resumption around 18h30; Bukavu-Kavumu road disrupted; residents confined; Kavumu, Kabare territory; AFC/M23 v Wazalendo 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 4 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Single local-source account; it does not say who evacuated the Wazalendo element or why, nor which structure. Included as a possible health-facility link; investigators should verify.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, that an incident occurred around 12h, at midday, in a part of the province under AFC-M23 control, at Mugeri sub-village (Mwanda village, Irhambi-Katana groupement, Kabare territory): armed men entered the home of a man known as Huit MUCIGA and shot him and his wife at the same time. The article's body says a child beside them died on the spot and that the man, taken to Mugeri health centre and then to FOMULAC Katana hospital, died later the same day, while the woman remained in very critical condition; its lead gives a toll of one dead and two wounded, inconsistent with the body. The headline attributes the incursion to Wazalendo; the body does not name the attackers. Sources close to the family said the man had reportedly been accused of collaborating with AFC-M23.
claims.place_as_written: Mugeri, Mwanda, Irhambi-Katana, Kabare, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed men (body); attributed to Wazalendo in the headline
claims.verification_note: The page says 'mi-journée' and 'aux environs de 12h', not 'afternoon': corrected. Every other element found on the page; inconsistency stated rather than resolved. The article's figures are internally inconsistent: the lead says one dead and two wounded, the body describes two deaths (a child and Huit MUCIGA) and one critically wounded woman. Not resolved here. The Wazalendo attribution appears only in the headline. The child and the wife are not named. The page dates the incursion to midday on Tuesday 24 March 2026 and the man's death to about 16h the same day (not in the stored excerpt). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Community radio, Bukavu. Internal inconsistency in figures (lead 'un mort et deux blessés' vs. body: child dead, father died at 16h). Victim reportedly accused of collaborating with AFC-M23 according to sources close to the family. The excerpt does not itself print the Wazalendo attribution (only the headline does); verifier should confirm. Article also says the couple was taken to Mugeri health centre then FOMULAC Katana.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that at least seven civilians were killed and fifteen wounded during an incursion by Wazalendo, militiamen allied to the Congolese army, at Shanje, Kalehe territory, on the night of Sunday to Monday 30 March 2026; citing local sources and an anonymous resident, it said the militiamen fired on civilians in the market around 18h30 and looted the population's property.
claims.verification_note: Statement supported. Figures field corrected to this source's figures only (the other accounts are separate claims 9 and 10). One of three accounts of the Shanje attack, which differ on perpetrator and toll: Kivu Morning Post (Wazalendo; 7 killed, 15 wounded), 7sur7.cd (armed men of unknown identity; at least 9 killed, 20 wounded) and AFC/M23 (the 'Kinshasa coalition'; 7 executed, more than twenty wounded). Not reconciled. A related KMP headline on the same page reads 'Sud-Kivu : le marché de Shanje incendié par des Wazalendo' (not opened; lead). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Contested attribution/figures: see AFC/M23 claim and 7sur7.cd claim. Shanje is in the area the AFC/M23 was reportedly evacuating around 27-28 March (Minova withdrawal).

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that on 29 March 2026 at 18h30 'la coalition de Kinshasa' infiltrated the densely populated centre of Shanje, Kalehe territory, where it 'executed 7 innocent civilians', whom he named; the outlet reported that he also said more than twenty people were wounded, and he alleged that the Kinshasa regime continues to ally itself with FDLR elements and deploy them on various fronts.
claims.verification_note: Statement narrowed to Kanyuka's words; 'more than twenty' is the outlet's paraphrase of him and is written as a word, as printed. Under policy v1 the names are listed exactly as printed, split on the only even reading, with the uncertainty stated. Party statement (AFC/M23). The page prints the seven names as one run of fourteen words with no separators: 'Shadai Ndagije Bisengi Mpenze Étienne Gitinywa Gashimye Hitimana Daniel Hategeka Ndayambaje Muhire Iradukunda Nzanzumuhire'. The split into seven two-word names is an editorial reading of that run (fourteen words, seven victims), not printed by the source; other splits are possible (e.g. 'Mpenze Étienne', 'Hitimana Daniel'). Verify each identity before relying on it. No Kinshasa, FARDC or Wazalendo account found. The other accounts (claims 8 and 10) give different perpetrators and tolls. 'AFC spokesperson' = spokesperson of the AFC/M23, as the page prints it; the stored excerpt begins after that attribution. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Party account only. The page prints seven names run together without separators (starting 'Shadai Ndagije Bisengi Mpenze Étienne Gitinywa Gashimye Hitimana Daniel Hategeka Ndayambaje Muhire Iradukunda Nzanzumuhire'); name boundaries cannot be determined, so none listed in victims_named. No Kinshasa/FARDC/Wazalendo account found.

claims.text: The outlet reported that at least 9 people were killed and 20 wounded in the night of Sunday to Monday 30 March 2026 at Shanje village, Kalehe territory, during an incursion of armed men; it cited a local church official, speaking anonymously on Radio Maendeleo, who said the bandits arrived and fired, and said wounded were taken to a medical facility and that the real identity of the armed men was not yet known.
claims.verification_note: The draft tied the toll to the church official; on the page the toll is the outlet's own and the official gives the time and a description. Split the attribution accordingly. Signed Alphonse Muderwa. One of three accounts of the Shanje attack (see claims 8 and 9): figures and perpetrator differ and are not reconciled. The toll is given in the outlet's voice, not attributed to the church official; the witness quote comes from Radio Maendeleo. Times differ between accounts (about 19h here, 18h30 in KMP and AFC/M23). The church official dates the incursion to about 19h (not in the stored excerpt). The statement does not name the publisher (7sur7.cd) only because the check reads its digits as figures; the source is shown with its publisher. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Figures differ from Kivu Morning Post (7/15) and AFC/M23 (7/20+). Radio Maendeleo is the underlying source cited on the page.

claims.text: BETO reported that AFC fighters left the localities of Pitakongo and Bunyatenge on Saturday 28 March 2026, after having already withdrawn on Thursday and Friday from at least twelve localities of Lubero territory and from the strategic town of Minova; it said the disengagement did not seem to result from a military rout but rather from a planned manoeuvre, citing information relayed by other media and local sources that the move would fit within the ongoing peace processes, and it reported that the rebel mayor of a city under AFC administration described the moves as tactical repositionings.
claims.verification_note: The draft turned BETO's hedge ('ne semble pas') into a firm description; restored the hedge and the conditional on the peace-process link, and added the Goma mayor's characterisation from the page. Dates for Minova are approximate: 'Thursday and Friday' before Saturday 28 March, i.e. about 26-27 March, computed from the weekdays. CONFLICT: Actualite.cd (claim 12) reports AFC/M23 elements arrested a radio director at Minova on Sunday 29 March, which suggests AFC/M23 presence there after the reported withdrawal; both accounts are kept. The BETO byline reads 'AFP Rédaction Kinshasa' while the piece is signed Azarias Mokonzi and is partly commentary; whether it relays AFP copy is unclear. 'AFC fighters' = the AFC/M23 named in the headline (the excerpt says 'ils'). The page names TV5Monde as one of the relaying media. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Mediacongo (2026-03-31, 'Le M23 au pied du mur') also says Minova was evacuated on Saturday 28 March, but its excerpt failed the mechanical check so it is not cited. CONFLICT: Actualite.cd reports AFC/M23 arrested a Minova radio director at Minova on 29 March. Weekday dates (Thursday and Friday before Saturday 28 March = 26-27 March) computed from weekday and publication date. Page attributes details to TV5Monde and local sources. No AFC/M23 or FARDC statement on Minova captured: search results showed a social-media post saying AFC/M23 announced withdrawal from Minova, not fetched.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Espoir Mbata, director of the community radio Top Buzi FM, was arrested on Sunday 29 March at Minova, Kalehe territory; according to local sources and colleagues at the station he was reportedly detained by AFC/M23 elements, and a journalist close to the radio, speaking anonymously, said the arrest was reportedly linked to an on-air comment by Espoir Mbata about a possible withdrawal of AFC/M23 elements from Minova. The outlet said some journalists had left Minova that morning fearing arrest.
claims.verification_note: Kept the source's conditionals ('reportedly') for both the perpetrators and the motive; the draft stated the motive link without the conditional. Perpetrator attribution is conditional in the source ('aurait été interpellé'), as is the motive ('serait liée'). CONFLICT with claim 11: BETO reports AFC/M23 withdrew from Minova on about 26-27 March; this arrest on 29 March implies AFC/M23 elements were still there. Both kept. Release not found. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Page says some journalists left Minova that morning fearing arrest. This indicates AFC/M23 presence at Minova on 29 March, in tension with reports that Minova was evacuated on 26-28 March. No AFC/M23 comment found; release not found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that around 16:00 on Monday 6 April 2026 several places in the Ziralo groupement, Kalehe territory (Kaziba, Katale, Kafufula, Katanga, Mpanama, Braza, Bushege and Lulamba) had already passed under AFC/M23 control after fighting with wazalendo.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt and page support each clause; date 'ce lundi 6 avril' and Ziralo/Kalehe printed in the article lede (page, not excerpt). Year from article date 07/04/2026. Single outlet (Actualite.cd, unnamed sources); no AFC/M23 or FARDC account for the day.
claims.researcher_note: Single local-outlet account citing unnamed sources; no AFC/M23 or FARDC account found for this day.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that on 6 April 2026 in Ziralo groupement (Kalehe) the AFC/M23 fought wazalendo from several local armed groups, including the COPACO led by Kirikicho Mirimba Mwanamayi, the MCDPIN of Grevisse Nsimparingira and the group of Haguma Kanyengwenye.
claims.verification_note: All three names and groups match the page character for character. Leader names spelled as Actualite.cd prints them; the outlet does not name Haguma Kanyengwenye's group.
claims.researcher_note: Leaders as printed by the outlet.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the town of Tushunguti, chef-lieu of Ziralo groupement in Kalehe territory, fell under AFC/M23 control on Tuesday 7 April 2026 after fighting with wazalendo, according to its sources; it said no official toll had been communicated.
claims.verification_note: Every clause on the page; date 7 April 2026 in the excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Single local-outlet account.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Tushunguti (Kalehe) was again under FARDC control, supported by wazalendo fighters, after a brief AFC/M23 occupation that began on 7 April 2026; it said the counter-offensive was launched from the Biriko and Busurungi axes in Walikale.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact and on topic; the two sources are one article (not independent). Date range kept as approximate. Retaking date not printed: 'less than 48 hours' after the 7 April fall, article published 10 April 08:05, so 9-10 April is approximate. Kivu Morning Post (9 April, claim on displacement) instead said AFC-M23 was consolidating its hold on Tushunguti that day; the 5 May Actualite.cd article says AFC/M23 retook the town 'nearly two months' after losing it, which does not fit a 9-10 April loss. Discrepancies unresolved.
claims.researcher_note: Date range: article dated 10 April says retaken less than 48 hours after 7 April. Single outlet; AFC/M23 account not found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing several of its sources, that Tushunguti again passed under AFC/M23 control on Sunday 3 May 2026 after two days of fighting against wazalendo, who withdrew towards Biriko in Walikale.
claims.verification_note: Supported; year 2026 from the article date 05/05/2026. The same article says the retaking came 'près de deux mois après en avoir perdu le contrôle' (nearly two months after losing control), which conflicts with the outlet's own 10 April report of a loss on about 9-10 April (under four weeks).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing several local sources, that on 12 April 2026 AFC/M23 elements carried out a cordon-and-search operation in Minova under a curfew, and that several men aged 18 to 40 were arrested and held for several hours at the 'Mille arbres' stadium.
claims.verification_note: Supported by the page. The outlet says the women's and children's mobilisation 'aurait contribué' (reportedly contributed) to the release: conditional.
claims.researcher_note: The outlet adds the operation reportedly aimed at identifying people without Salongo tokens and those suspected of being a threat; it says the detainees were released after women and children mobilised. Perpetrator attribution is the outlet's.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that several houses were burned along the Bunje-Katale axis, notably in the villages of Bunje and Nyalugusha, during fighting between the belligerents; it did not say who burned them or on which day.

claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (AFC/M23 and wazalendo were the belligerents)

Removed the sequence and the date from the statement; date widened to the reporting window. Undated in the source: the article (17 April) reports renewed fighting at Chambombo on 13 April and fighting in Ziralo since 6 April; the burning is not tied to a day or a perpetrator. Actualite.cd's 7 April article spells the locality 'Bundje'.
claims.researcher_note: Exact date of burning not given; range from article context.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Kalehe civil society said SEBUTAGWIRA HARERIMANA JACQUES, director of the EP Chambombo, was shot dead during fighting between Wazalendo and AFC-M23 at Chambombo on Wednesday 29 April 2026.
claims.place_as_written: Chambombo, Nyalugusha village, Ziralo groupement, Kalehe territory
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (fighting between Wazalendo and AFC-M23)

claims.researcher_note: Name printed in capitals by the source. Article says Wazalendo attacked Chambombo and were repelled by AFC-M23.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that five people were shot dead and one seriously wounded in a shooting attributed to presumed AFC/M23 rebels on Thursday 21 May 2026 at Mbayo village, Kabare territory; according to a civil society official of Bugorhe groupement, the assailants gathered their victims and executed them one by one.
claims.place_as_written: Mbayo village, Bugorhe groupement, Kabare territory
claims.actor_as_written: presumed AFC/M23 rebels, per Radio Okapi
claims.verification_note: Hedge kept; figures and date match the excerpt. Perpetrators are 'présumés rebelles de l’AFC/M23' (presumed) in Radio Okapi's wording. Radio Okapi says, citing local sources, the assailants had attacked Wazalendo at the Mbayu plantation, were routed and then attacked civilians making charcoal; victims were civilians from Kamakombe and Kashwago. No victim named. No AFC/M23 account found.
claims.researcher_note: No names of victims printed in the excerpts. Radio Okapi says victims were civilians (woodcutters, farmers) from Kamakombe and Kashwago; AFC/M23 account not found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that on 9 June 2026 school and commercial activities were disrupted in Mbayo and Kamakombe villages (Kabare) by fighting between AFC/M23 elements and wazalendo militiamen from morning until late evening; it said this followed fighting a week earlier at Kafurumaye, near Kahuzi-Biega National Park.
claims.verification_note: Supported by one article; year from article date 10/06/2026.
claims.researcher_note: Same villages as the 21 May killings (separate claim).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that an explosive device killed one child and seriously wounded three others on Tuesday 28 April 2026 near Kavumu airport (Kabare); the victims, all minors, were scavenging scrap metal when they found an abandoned crate of explosives, and the three wounded were transferred to the Bukavu general referral hospital.
claims.place_as_written: Businde, Bugorhe groupement, near Kavumu airport, Kabare territory
claims.verification_note: Supported; title on page matches. Place per the page: a valley at Businde, Bugorhe groupement. Radio Okapi notes the area was, per several sources, the FARDC's last line of defence before the fall of Bukavu in February 2025; no party is said to have left the explosives.
claims.researcher_note: Title truncated in URL; title reconstructed from Radio Okapi listing. Children not named.

claims.text: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) reported that on 5 April 2026 at Cirunga, Kabare territory, eight men and two women were arrested by AFC/M23 elements for demonstrating spontaneously after learning they were to be removed from posts in that village.
claims.verification_note: Checked in the retained PDF (April 2026 monthly analysis). UN-body documentation: grade A under the rubric. Excerpt keeps the PDF typo 'postesdans' verbatim. The report gives this as an illustration and does not say what posts or what happened to the ten afterwards; it calls the AFC/M23 'auteurs présumés' in the next sentence.
claims.researcher_note: Excerpt keeps the PDF extraction artefact "postesdans". Report is for April 2026; publication date taken from the file path (2026-07), exact day unknown.

claims.text: DW reported on 22 May 2026 that the first positive Ebola case in South Kivu was recorded in the Miti-Murhesa health zone, Kabare territory, in the area held by the AFC-M23; it said the alert was confirmed by the AFC-M23 governor Patrick Busu Bwa Ngwi and by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka.

Busu Bwa Ngwi (AFC/M23 governor) and Kanyuka (AFC/M23 spokesperson) are de facto authorities; their confirmation is reported by DW, not quoted. The alert itself came from the province's health authorities. claims.researcher_note: Epidemic context, not an attack on care. DW is a German public broadcaster; correspondent Mitima Delachance in Bukavu.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to the South Kivu provincial health division chief Dr Aimé Alengo, the focus of the Ebola outbreak in South Kivu was in the Miti-Murhesa health zone of Kabare; Radio Okapi said the zone lies in a region affected by insecurity linked to armed groups, notably the AFC/M23 rebellion, which further complicates the response, and that Health Minister Roger Samuel Kamba announced diplomatic initiatives aimed at guaranteeing secure humanitarian and health access to areas under armed-group control.

Kamba also said he wrote to the Prime Minister asking for Goma airport to reopen and for access to South Kivu for health and humanitarian teams.
