claims.researcher_note: Quote attribution of Dr Alengo and Minister Kamba is as stated by the page; excerpts do not name them, entities taken from page text near the excerpts (verify at promote).

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that on Tuesday 26 May 2026 North Kivu health authorities, at a briefing in Goma, announced that Bukavu city had three new positive Ebola cases, according to Dr Biya Kizinkinko, health division head and member of the AFC-M23 Ebola response task team.
claims.verification_note: Supported by the page. The 'North Kivu health authorities' at the Goma briefing are those of the AFC/M23 administration (de facto); the Bukavu count is theirs, not independently confirmed.
claims.researcher_note: Figure is the de facto authority's; no independent count seen. Epidemic context only.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that heavy-artillery fighting resumed early on Tuesday 11 August 2026 in several localities of Kalehe territory, South Kivu, between AFC/M23 rebels and the FARDC, supported in some sectors by Wazalendo; first shots were heard around 5 a.m. in Chambombo, Lumbishi, Kaziba de Rumbishi, Kwisimbi, Gafufura and Kazinga.
claims.place_as_written: Chambombo, Lumbishi, Kaziba de Rumbishi, Kwisimbi, Gafufura, Kazinga (Kalehe), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the retained page, same event and date. excerpt_en flag is only the expansion of FARDC; translation is faithful.
claims.researcher_note: Same-day local detail on first shots (5 a.m., localities) is in the same article; excerpt covers the first paragraph only.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing its own sources, that the bombardments in Kalehe territory on 11 August 2026 caused deaths and injuries among civilians and that several houses and other property were reportedly damaged; it added that the intensity of the fighting forced several families to leave their homes for safer areas.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (fighting between AFC/M23 and FARDC/wazalendo)
claims.verification_note: Kept the conditional on the damage; the displacement clause was only on the page, so the excerpt was extended to the contiguous passage that prints it. (Excerpt extensions proposed in clause_support; replacement_quotes are not applied to exact sources.) No casualty figure given; the damage is reported conditionally ('auraient'). Excerpt gap: the stored excerpt does not carry this; the passage in clause_support is on the retained page (extend with source_edits.py add_excerpt).
claims.researcher_note: No figure; LPA (20 Aug) gives FARDC and local figures for 11-14 Aug.

claims.text: Enquete.cd reported, citing several local sources contacted on the ground, that after several hours of fighting on 11 August the Wazalendo retook control of the localities of Chambombo and Kazinga from AFC-M23-RDF elements in Kalehe territory; it said that according to local civil society Lumbishi was reportedly shared between the two sides, each occupying some positions.
claims.verification_note: Source 1 excerpt said only 'la localité'; extended to the preceding sentence that names Lumbishi. Shared-control clause made conditional as printed. Year comes from the dateline, now in the source 2 quote. (Excerpt extensions proposed in clause_support; replacement_quotes are not applied to exact sources.) 'AFC-M23-RDF' is the outlet's label. The shared-control report on Lumbishi is conditional ('serait'). Excerpt gap: the stored excerpt does not carry this; the passage in clause_support is on the retained page (extend with source_edits.py add_excerpt).
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet citing local sources; Wazalendo/AFC accounts of the event not found in this source. The article also recalls late-June fighting at Lumbishi/Chambombo in which AFC-M23 retook Chambombo (outside this quarter).

claims.text: Enquete.cd reported, citing medical sources, that several AFC-M23-RDF fighters wounded in the Kalehe fighting were reportedly admitted to the hospital of Numbi, among them a Rwandan officer presented as a colonel who was reportedly gravely wounded; the outlet said this information could not be independently verified.
claims.verification_note: Passage on page under 'Sur le plan sanitaire'; hedges kept. Grade C. Unverified by the outlet itself: the presence of a wounded Rwandan colonel is a lead, not an established fact.
claims.researcher_note: Unverified; Rwanda's presence is a contested claim. Report date used for the date (the wounded are linked to the 11 Aug fighting).

claims.text: La Presse Africaine reported that during fighting between the FARDC (supported by Wazalendo) and AFC/M23 from 11 to 14 August 2026 in Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe, the spokesperson of the 34th military region, Major Dieudonné Kaseraka, reported five civilians killed and four FARDC soldiers wounded at Chambombo and Lumbishi, while local sources put the toll higher, at least six civilians killed, among them a woman and her two children.
claims.place_as_written: Lumbishi, Chambombo (Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Supported; figures written as the excerpt prints them (words) and spokesperson name added from the excerpt. Two tolls kept per source. Tolls differ by source: FARDC 34th military region spokesperson five civilians killed; local sources at least six. Byline Jean Bujenje, LPA Minova. A woman and her two children are also cited by the FARDC for the 7 August Lumbishi explosion; possible overlap, not merged.
claims.researcher_note: Outlet is La Presse Africaine (LPA), Uvira-based; byline Jean Bujenje, Minova. Victims unnamed. Locations in the article: Lumbishi, Chambombo, Katale, Mpanama. Possible overlap with the 7 Aug Lumbishi explosion (FARDC cited a woman and two children there too): not merged.

claims.text: La Presse Africaine reported that local civil society said population movements towards Walikale were noted, that cattle pillage and losses of property were reported, and that several health structures remained difficult to operate, following the 11-14 August 2026 fighting in Kalehe's Buhavu chiefdom.
claims.place_as_written: Hauts Plateaux of Kalehe, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: All clauses on page and in excerpts. Health structures unnamed and no cause given: a lead only.
claims.researcher_note: Health point is vague (unnamed structures, no cause stated); recorded as a lead only. Date is the report date.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that a relative calm was observed on Monday 13 July in Kasake (Masisi, North Kivu) and Lumbishi (Kalehe, South Kivu) after three days of fighting between Wazalendo and AFC-M23 rebels, and that according to several local sources both localities were reportedly now under Wazalendo control.
claims.place_as_written: Lumbishi (Kalehe), South Kivu; Kasake (Masisi), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Control is conditional in the source ('seraient'); hedge restored. Year dropped from statement (not in excerpt; page dated 13/07/2026). Enquete.cd (12 August) later reported control of Lumbishi as shared between the sides.
claims.researcher_note: Enquete.cd (12 Aug) says control at Lumbishi was later shared between the sides.

claims.text: La Prunelle RDC reported that at least five people were killed and several wounded on Friday 7 August 2026 in the explosion of an explosive device in the centre of Lumbishi (Ziralo grouping, Kalehe highlands), and that the wounded were evacuated to the Numbi hospital centre.
claims.place_as_written: Lumbishi centre, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Figures field had mixed in the party tolls, which belong to claims 9 and 10; narrowed to this source's figure. Attribution to local sources added from the contiguous page passage. Grade B: one credible local outlet, the occurrence of a deadly blast corroborated by both parties' statements. Per the article, the toll of at least five came from initial information from local sources. Contested event, three accounts kept separate: local sources at least five killed; FARDC three killed by RDF-AFC-M23 82 mm mortar fire; AFC-M23 five then nine civilians killed in a government-side bombing of the market. The outlet says neither party's accusations could be independently verified, and the timings differ (local sources about 10 a.m.; AFC-M23 about 17:45).
claims.researcher_note: Contested event: FARDC and AFC/M23 accounts are the next two claims. Outlet La Prunelle, Bukavu/Uvira-area local outlet. Victims unnamed.

claims.text: La Prunelle RDC reported that in a communication published on Friday 7 August the FARDC operational sector Sukola 2 Nord–Sud-Kivu said RDF-AFC-M23 coalition fighters had tried an incursion into Bunje (Ziralo grouping) before firing several 82 mm mortar rounds towards inhabited areas, which according to the army killed three people, including a woman and her two children, and seriously wounded several; the sector's spokesperson, Second Lieutenant Meya Gbé Jérémie, said the coalition had fired 'à l’aveuglette' into densely populated areas.
claims.place_as_written: Bunje, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Rank corrected: 'lieutenant de second classe' is a second lieutenant. The 'à l’aveuglette' quote was not in the stored excerpt; source 2 extended to the full quoted sentence. Conditionals kept. (Excerpt extensions proposed in clause_support; replacement_quotes are not applied to exact sources.) Party statement (FARDC), not verified independently according to La Prunelle RDC. Contradicts the AFC-M23 account (claim 10) and the local-source toll (claim 8). Excerpt gap: the stored excerpt does not carry this; the passage in clause_support is on the retained page (extend with source_edits.py add_excerpt).
claims.researcher_note: Source type partisan: cited only for what the FARDC said. The excerpt carries the FARDC toll; the attribution to the mortar rounds, Bunje and the spokesperson is in the adjacent sentences of the same article.

claims.text: La Prunelle RDC reported that Lawrence Kanyuka, spokesperson of the armed movement, in a communication on X accused the coalition forces of the Kinshasa government of having bombed the Lumbishi market, the movement first reporting five civilians dead and several wounded and then, in an update, 9 dead.
claims.verification_note: Supported; figures written as printed and source 1 extended to the full quote so it names the Lumbishi market. (Excerpt extensions proposed in clause_support; replacement_quotes are not applied to exact sources.) The armed movement is AFC-M23 (named in the article's paragraph heading 'Une version différente de l’AFC-M23'). Party statement (AFC-M23); the X post itself was not opened. La Prunelle RDC says the accusations could not be independently verified. Excerpt gap: the stored excerpt does not carry this; the passage in clause_support is on the retained page (extend with source_edits.py add_excerpt).
claims.researcher_note: The nine-dead update is in a later sentence of the same article. The X post itself was not opened. Party statement only.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the South Kivu provincial government, which depends on the central government in Kinshasa, denounced the pressure and predation to which it said the population of Bukavu is subjected under the administration of AFC/M23, citing levies including so-called sanitation taxes and taxes on commercial activity and, according to several testimonies, acts of intimidation, violence and flogging.
claims.verification_note: Taxes/flogging clause is in the page's quoted communiqué, not in the stored excerpt (excerpt gap). The fire toll cannot enter the statement until the excerpt is extended; recorded in the note as the province's account. Date 2026-09-12 was unsupported; set to the range the page supports. Prompted by the 10 September fire at Funu B, Cimpunda quarter, Kadutu, Bukavu. DISCREPANCY (for the register): in the same article the provincial government, citing health structures, gives a provisional fire toll of more than 26 children dead (19 girls, 7 boys), mostly pupils of École primaire FARAJA; this is the province's account. The page's appended report says at least 20 pupils died and about twenty were wounded at the Ujamaa and Furaha primary schools (medical sources and AFC/M23 authorities), and existing claim r1-ST-DRC-2026-004 gives about twenty wounded. Not reconciled. Date is a range: the communiqué reached the outlet on 10 September per the article; the article is dated 13 September. AFC/M23 response not found. The province's toll should be added as its own claim once the excerpt is extended (source_edits.py add_excerpt) with: 'Selon un communiqué du gouvernement provincial parvenu à la rédaction de ACTUALITE.CD jeudi 10 septembre 2026, les premières informations recueillies auprès des structures sanitaires font état de plus de 26 enfants décédés, dont 19 filles et 7 garçons, en majorité des élèves de l’École primaire FARAJA.'
claims.researcher_note: Statement prompted by the 10 Sept Funu B fire in Kadutu (existing claim r1-ST-DRC-2026-004). The same article gives a provisional toll of more than 26 children dead (19 girls, 7 boys), mostly pupils of École primaire FARAJA, per the provincial government citing health structures; the existing claim says about twenty wounded: reviewer to reconcile. AFC/M23 response to this statement not found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the DRC higher-education ministry (ESURSI), headed by Marie-Thérèse Sombo, issued a ministerial order, announced on Tuesday 25 August 2026, suspending academic activities for academic year 2026-2027 at several institutions in Goma and Bukavu, including the Université Officielle de Bukavu, ISC-Bukavu, ISTM-Bukavu, ISP-Bukavu, ISDR-Bukavu and ISAM-Bukavu.
claims.verification_note: All clauses on page; excerpt_en flags are only expansions of acronyms. The order also lists Goma institutions (UOG, ISC-Goma, ISTM-Goma, ISP-Goma); final-year 2025-2026 students may complete elsewhere.
claims.researcher_note: Relates to de facto AFC/M23 control of universities; RFI/Yahoo says the ministry also suspended the salaries of 48 agents accused of joining AFC/M23.

claims.text: RFI (carried by Yahoo Actualités) reported that, alongside Kinshasa's suspension of academic activities, a separate decision suspended the salaries of 48 agents accused of having joined AFC/M23, pledged allegiance to it or accepted positions under its authority, and that in response AFC/M23 deputy coordinator Bertrand Bisimwa announced a substitute mechanism; RFI added that UN experts' December 2025 report had said AFC/M23 ordered universities to cut their links with the Congolese higher-education ministry.
claims.verification_note: Narrowed 'accused of allegiance' to the three grounds the page states; 'separate decision' kept as printed. Read on the Yahoo Actualités copy credited to RFI; the RFI original was not opened. The page does not say which authority issued the salary decision.
claims.researcher_note: Yahoo page carries an RFI credit; the RFI original was not fetched. The 'Bukavu' scope is partial: article covers Goma and Bukavu.

claims.text: La Presse Africaine reported that an appeal on the Ziralo situation demanded the release of 'le patriote' Kirikocho Mirimba Mwana Mayi, who the appeal said had been in detention for several weeks.
claims.verification_note: Name printed on page exactly; policy v1 allows naming detainees. Name as printed. Who holds him and where is not stated; the appeal's author is not named beyond the article's 'la même source' context. Lead only.
claims.researcher_note: Who holds him, and where, is not stated: gap. Lead only.

claims.text: La Presse Africaine reported that the body of a woman bearing traces of violence and of bladed weapons was found in Nkola village, Rubenga chiefdom, Idjwi, on a Sunday in early August 2026 (the article gives two different dates for that Sunday); a source on the spot said she was reportedly killed during the night by unidentified individuals who used knives and machetes, her body found with a serious neck wound, and village chief Doris Habiragi confirmed the information and said investigations were under way.
claims.place_as_written: Nkola village, Rubenga chiefdom, Idjwi, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Supported; inconsistency stated in the statement with both dates as printed; killing account and neck wound added from the quote on the page. (Excerpt extensions proposed in clause_support; replacement_quotes are not applied to exact sources.) Date inconsistent on the page: the summary says 'dimanche 01 août 2026', the body 'dimanche 2 août 2026'; 2 August 2026 is a Sunday, so 2 August is used, precision approximate. Headline says the woman was decapitated. The source presents it as criminality; no armed-group link stated. Victim unnamed. Byline Richelieu Byamana, LPA Sud-Kivu. Excerpt gap: the stored excerpt does not carry this; the passage in clause_support is on the retained page (extend with source_edits.py add_excerpt).
claims.researcher_note: Non-conflict criminality as far as the source says. The page is internally inconsistent: 'dimanche 01 août 2026' in one place, 'dimanche 2 août 2026' in another; 2 Aug 2026 is a Sunday, so date computed from weekday and publication date. Victim unnamed. Related LPA item on a young man found dead with bound arms in Idjwi (about mid-August) was seen only as a headline.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that after intense fighting since 3h on Monday 5 October 2026, Wazalendo fighters were said to have retaken control of Kafufula, Katale, Katoke, Bikari/Kuma Dépôts, Chambombo and Bishaka in the Ziralo grouping, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory, from AFC-M23 troops.
claims.place_as_written: Kafufula, Katale, Katoke, Chambombo, Bishaka (Ziralo grouping, Buhavu chiefdom), Kalehe territory
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo; AFC-M23 (as named by the source)
claims.verification_note: Page supports every clause; the '23' flag is the AFC-M23 name. Corroborated in part by Enquete.cd 6 Oct (FARDC-allied forces announced retaking Katale, Kafufula, Chambombo, Bishaka). Hedged by the source ('auraient repris'). The source says FARDC and Wazalendo launched the assaults; Bikari/Kuma Dépôts is not in its list of Ziralo axes. 2026-10-29: control edited: Frontline data fix (FRONTLINE_NOTES.md): control.held_by names only the holder (for a withdrawal, the side withdrawing), so the side class is not 'both sides named'; the other side stays in the statement. Wording from the stored excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Local community radio (Bukavu), hedged ('auraient'). Same event drafted from Radio Okapi (r1/UCD-FARDC-WZ#34-35); independent local outlet. Source says FARDC and Wazalendo launched the assaults.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local leaders, that at about 11h on Monday a presence of Wazalendo fighters was reported in the town of Lumbishi, about 8 km from Numbi, Kalehe territory.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim support; Monday is 5 Oct per the same page.
claims.researcher_note: Date is the Monday of the 6 Oct article, i.e. 5 Oct (article text says 'lundi 5 octobre' earlier). Single local source.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing an occasional correspondent, that in the morning of Monday 05 October an unusual presence of fighters claiming to be Wazalendo was seen on the hills of Mabingu village, Irhambi-Katana grouping, Kabare territory, and that several school heads sent pupils home fearing clashes.
claims.verification_note: Supported; excerpt_en flag is only 'Wazalendo' vs 'Wazalendos' spelling.
claims.researcher_note: Only item found placing armed activity in Kabare territory in this window; single local correspondent, no fighting reported at Mabingu.

claims.text: Enquete.cd reported, according to local sources, that the FARDC, supported by Wazalendo fighters, had retaken control of the centre of Numbi, Kalehe territory, and that clashes had reportedly preceded the retaking.
claims.verification_note: Statement said the retaking happened 'on 6 October'; the page only reports it on 6 Oct. Narrowed; date flag set approximate. Reported in a 6 October 2026 dispatch ('informations recueillies ce mardi'); the day of the retaking itself is not stated. The page says AFC/M23 had been present there for several months. Radio Maendeleo (20 Oct) later reported FRN troops retook Numbi. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Enquete.cd (6 Oct 2026, La Redaction) supports both clauses; the 'clashes reportedly preceded' clause is not in the stored excerpt, so the passage is added. The headline says the FARDC and Wazalendo 'announce' the retaking, while the body cites local sources.
claims.researcher_note: The same page says AFC/M23 had been present there for several months and reports local sources describing an AFC/M23 pull-back toward Numbi and Byonde on 5 October. Later retaken by FRN troops per Radio Maendeleo 20 Oct (separate claim).

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported on 20 October that after the Wazalendo offensive that led to their entry into Shanje, Lumbishi and Numbi between 5 and 6 October, a counter-offensive had allowed troops of the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) to retake control of them.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; '20' is the publication date (Last updated 2026/10/20). The date of the FRN counter-offensive is not given; only that it preceded the 20 October report.
claims.researcher_note: The date of the FRN counter-offensive is not given by this source; only that it preceded 20 Oct. Conflicts in time with Enquete.cd 6 Oct (FARDC holding Numbi): control changed afterwards. Single local source.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported a still-provisional toll of at least 8 dead, including civilians, and several wounded in new clashes that had pitted AFC-M23 troops against Wazalendo fighters for nearly three days in several villages around Shanje, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe highlands; the same article quoted a source in a medical structure receiving some cases as reporting several wounded civilians in addition to about ten deaths near Shanje and in the Bogamanda-Nyamutwe area.
claims.place_as_written: Shanje area (Kirwa, Bunyata, Igali axis) and Bogamanda-Nyamutwe, Kalehe territory
claims.actor_as_written: AFC-M23 troops; Wazalendo (parties to the fighting)
claims.verification_note: 'more than ten deaths' mistranslated 'en plus d'une dizaine de décès' (= in addition to about ten deaths); corrected. Both sources are one article, one origin: C. Two tolls from the same outlet differ (at least 8; about ten): kept per source. Deaths not attributed to a party; civilian/combatant split not given. The headline says FARDC backed by Wazalendo fought AFC-M23.
claims.researcher_note: Page shows 'Rédaction 14 octobre 2026 / 6 octobre 2026' (modified/published); article text refers to 'mardi 6 octobre', so event date 6 Oct. Two figures kept separate. Deaths not attributed to a party; civilian/combatant split not given.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing witnesses, that returnees found homes destroyed or burned, goods looted and fields devastated in Kalehe highlands, and that at Shanje almost all shops were burned in the night of 6 to 7 October. Actualite.cd reported separately that a large fire broke out around 4 a.m. on Wednesday 7 October in Shanje, affecting homes and the local market.
claims.verification_note: Both pages checked; two independent outlets agree on the Shanje burning of 6-7 Oct; no attribution added. Neither source states the cause of the fire or who burned or looted; not attributed by the source.
claims.researcher_note: Cause of the fire and perpetrators of looting are not stated by either source; Radio Maendeleo speaks of 'incendiées' without attribution. Shanje was contested 5-7 Oct (Wazalendo entered, FRN retook). Two local/national outlets, independent bylines.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing a local civil-society source, that in the health areas of Matutira, Mianda, Kusisa and Lumbishi (Kalehe highlands) health facilities had difficulty caring for the sick because they too had been looted, and schools struggled to resume.
claims.place_as_written: Matutira, Mianda, Kusisa and Lumbishi health areas, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory
claims.verification_note: Verbatim support; looting unattributed as in the source. Which facilities, when and by whom they were looted is not stated.
claims.researcher_note: Which facilities, when looted and by whom are not stated; the sibling health-area sentences in the same article place this after the 5-7 Oct changes of hands. Also the same article says there was no humanitarian assistance. Lead for investigators: ask the Bunyakiri/Minova health zone offices.

claims.text: Kivutimes (project Habari za Mahali) reported on 21 October that MSF Spain gave PEP kits for survivors of sexual violence to four health structures (Tushunguti, Matutira, Mianda, Kusisa) in the Bunyakiri health zone, Ziralo grouping, and that, according to Katabana Monde, head nurse at Matutira, the structures record cases of sexual violence among their populations, notably in the context of displacement caused by the fighting; providers had had difficulty obtaining PEP kits in time.
claims.place_as_written: Bunyakiri health zone (Tushunguti, Matutira, Mianda, Kusisa health centres), Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; single local outlet with one named informant, so C rather than B. No case numbers, perpetrators or incident dates given; the nurse's testimony is the only basis.
claims.researcher_note: No perpetrator, count or dates of incidents. Article produced under 'Habari za Mahali' (RATECO / REMEL-GL consortium with Media4dialogue), local reporting; a nurse's testimony. Ties to PEP supply gap (access to care within the 72-hour window is the lead). Names of survivors not given.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that journalist Laurent Vainqueur Muliro of community radio Walikale Amka (RTCWA) was shot dead on the evening of Wednesday 21 October in an ambush attributed to presumed Wazalendo militiamen near Bitale, Kalehe territory; the page says two other people were also killed and two seriously wounded, with the travellers' property looted.
claims.actor_as_written: presumed Wazalendo militiamen (as attributed by the outlet)
claims.verification_note: Name printed exactly; hedge kept; figures on the page. Perpetrators are 'présumés' (presumed) Wazalendo per the outlet; the page says the spot was under Wazalendo control and that survivors reported the facts. UNPC Walikale condemned the killing and called for an inquiry.
claims.researcher_note: Two other victims (a student and a moto-taxi driver) are unnamed in the page. The page says the convoy used the Bukavu-Hombo detour because the Goma-Walikale road had been closed by FRN rebels, and the ambush spot is in a Wazalendo-controlled area. No Wazalendo or FARDC reaction found. The injured and bodies went to Hombo Sud hospital centre.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that the local youth council of the villages of Kabulungu and Mulangala, Bugorhe grouping, Kabare territory, denounced insecurity attributed to unidentified armed persons: intimidation of farmers, theft of livestock and extortion of money, and 'inhuman treatment' of people who resist.
claims.place_as_written: Kabulungu and Mulangala, Bugorhe grouping, Kabare territory
claims.verification_note: Attributed allegation, supported verbatim. Allegations by a local youth council, in the conditional; incidents undated.
claims.researcher_note: Allegation by a local civil-society body; date is publication date (27 Oct), incidents undated. Do not read 'inhuman treatment' as any legal category.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that the same Kabulungu and Mulangala (Kabare territory) youth council also reported cases of arrests followed by detention in unknown places, the victims reportedly being released only after payment of a sum of money.
claims.place_as_written: Kabulungu and Mulangala, Bugorhe grouping, Kabare territory
claims.verification_note: Restored the source's conditional ('ne seraient libérées'); otherwise verbatim. Who carried out the arrests is not stated.
claims.researcher_note: Who arrests (the source does not say whether armed groups or authorities) is not stated. Area in contested zone (FRN vs Wazalendo clashes reported per the same page).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Hombo civil society, after an assessment mission of 25 to 27 September 2026, said the local hospital centre at Hombo Sud (Kalehe territory) was receiving a large number of displaced people needing care, as well as people wounded by violence, with limited capacity.
claims.place_as_written: Hombo Sud, Kalehe territory (and Lukaraba, Walikale, North Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Flagged numbers (2350, 25, 27) are printed on the page. Capacity strain, not an attack on care.
claims.researcher_note: Assessment dates fall in September (25-27 Sep), report date 4 Oct. The Hombo Sud hospital centre is the same one where the 21 Oct ambush victims were taken (see journalist claim). Capacity strain, not an attack.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the South Kivu provincial government (Kinshasa-appointed), in a communiqué of Monday 5 October signed by its spokesperson Didier Kabi, expressed concern at the extension of the closing hours of two border posts controlled by the AFC/M23, Ruzizi 1er in Bukavu and Grande Barrière in Goma, saying it could facilitate the entry of new populations and their settlement in AFC/M23-controlled zones.
claims.place_as_written: Ruzizi 1er border post, Bukavu; Grande Barrière, Goma
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; '23' flag is the AFC/M23 name. Party account (provincial government loyal to Kinshasa): its reading of the measure is its claim. 'Kinshasa-appointed' is a gloss; the page contrasts the provincial government with the AFC/M23-controlled posts.
claims.researcher_note: Party account: the provincial government's reading (population-settlement concern) is its claim, not established fact. The AFC/M23 side of the Grande Barrière measure is in an existing claim (r1-NKS-2026Q4-009, Tic-Tac Hebdo, 2 Oct communiqué); no AFC/M23 answer to the Kinshasa concern found.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that FRN vice-president Bertrand Bisimwa, in a speech at Bukavu on Thursday, defended continued teaching in FRN-held zones despite measures by the Congolese government, and that the FRN promised to support teachers whose pay had been suspended by Kinshasa.
claims.actor_as_written: FRN (Front pour la refondation de la nation), as named by the source
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; actor 'AFC/M23 political structure' is not what this page prints, so set to the source's own name. De facto authority (FRN) statement: 'the FRN says'. The page describes the FRN as a politico-military movement led by former president Joseph Kabila, while Actualite.cd (27 Oct) calls it the AFC/M23 rebellion 'devenue' the FRN: naming discrepancy kept, not resolved.
claims.researcher_note: Kivu Morning Post is Goma-based; the page reports the FRN's own speech (party statement). The page says the Kinshasa suspension of academic activities in Goma and Bukavu was contested by the authorities in place.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Higher Education minister Marie-Thérèse Sombo, launching the 2026-2027 academic year in Kongo Central on Monday 26 October 2026, said the provisional suspension of academic activities at Goma and Bukavu institutions aims to protect students and staff, preserve the legality of university governance and prevent irregular academic acts from compromising the value of diplomas.
claims.place_as_written: Kongo Central (statement); applies to Goma and Bukavu institutions
claims.verification_note: Verbatim support; '26' is printed on the page. Kinshasa government account.
claims.researcher_note: Kinshasa's account, opposing the FRN's 15 Oct restart in Bukavu (see Bisimwa claim). Context for civilian access to education/health training in Bukavu; the suspension affects Bukavu medical students (Actualite.cd 7 Oct reports about 200 medical students moving to Unikis).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Twirwaneho said Minembwe and surroundings were 'liberated', that a regional source confirmed to it that all of Minembwe was controlled by Twirwaneho, and that, according to several sources, Mikenge in the Itombwe sector (Mwenga territory), 28 km from Minembwe, had also come under Twirwaneho control after fighting with the Congolese armed forces on Tuesday.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe (Fizi) and Mikenge, Itombwe sector (Mwenga), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the retained Actualite.cd page (26/02/2025). 'Liberated' clause rests on the page (not the stored excerpt). Grade B: one credible national outlet relaying unnamed and partisan sources. Control is per an unnamed regional source and 'several sources'; the 'liberated' wording is Twirwaneho's own announcement. Kivutimes (4 Mar) gives a different Mikenge sequence (Wazalendo dislodging on 3 Mar and same-day Twirwaneho retake); both accounts kept. 2026-10-29: territory edited: Frontline data fix: the claim's own location places Minembwe in Fizi and Mikenge (its control place) in Mwenga territory, as the excerpt says ('territoire de Mwenga').
claims.researcher_note: Date: report date 2026-02-26 article says 'ce mercredi' (Wednesday 26 Feb 2025); Mikenge combat on 'Mardi' (25 Feb, computed from weekday and publication date). Minembwe capture itself already in r1-UV-2025Q1-032 (SOS Medias Burundi). A Facebook snippet (lead only, not opened) claims FARDC/Wazalendo retook Mikenge on 24 Feb 2025; unverified, conflicts in sequence.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that after being sighted at Kamanyola and then Luvungi, M23 rebels were now visible at Sange in Uvira territory, South Kivu, and that residents confirmed their presence although the rebels had not yet made a public statement.
claims.place_as_written: Luvungi and Sange (Ruzizi plain), Uvira territory
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on page (byline Blaise Basabose). No visible dateline; date from URL path, as noted.
claims.researcher_note: Article date taken from URL path (2025/02/20); no byline date visible in fetched text. Corroborates Radio Okapi r1-UV-2025Q1-006 (Sange, 19 Feb) and adds Luvungi.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post quoted Paul Byamungu, a member of Uvira civil society, as saying that after the meeting at Kamanyola, M23 was now with them, that they had communicated nothing, and that there had been no public meeting so far.
claims.verification_note: Removed 'in the Sange area': the quote says only 'avec nous'; placing it at Sange is the article's framing, not the speaker's. Civil-society statement, not an official one; the quote does not say where 'with us' is.
claims.researcher_note: Implies an M23 meeting at Kamanyola before 20 Feb; the page gives no date for it.

claims.text: URN (via The Observer, Uganda) reported that M23 president Bertrand Bisimwa released a statement on Monday accusing FARDC soldiers and their allies of deploying Sukhoi fighter jets and attack drones to bomb several villages in Minembwe, and that, according to Bisimwa, the strikes were aimed at areas populated by Banyamulenge civilians, as well as Minembwe airfield.
claims.verification_note: Narrowed title to the source's 'M23 president' and the Banyamulenge clause to the page's own attribution wording ('According to Bisimwa, the strikes were aimed at...'); that clause rests on the page, not the excerpt. Byline 'by URN'. Party statement (AFC/M23). The page calls him 'M23 president'; other sources call him AFC/M23 deputy coordinator.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan claim (AFC/M23). Date computed from weekday 'Monday' and page date 12 Mar 2025 (Monday 10 Mar). Role: source says 'M23 president'; New Times calls him deputy coordinator of AFC/M23. Matches Kinshasa side below.

claims.text: URN (via The Observer, Uganda) reported that, on Tuesday night, South Kivu vice-governor Jean Jacques Elakano announced that the operation by the army and coalition forces had destroyed all aircraft transporting M23 rebels from Bukavu city, resulting in the deaths of over 10 fighters.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on retained URN copy. Contrasts with Bisimwa's account (claim 3); both kept. Party statement (provincial government, Kinshasa side); the death toll is the vice-governor's claim, not independently confirmed.
claims.researcher_note: Kinshasa-side account of the Minembwe airfield strikes; contrasts with Bisimwa's claim of civilian targets. Date computed from weekday 'Tuesday night' and page date 12 Mar 2025 (11 Mar). Statement kind uncertain; source says 'announced'. Other Elakano comments (airfield used to supply Twirwaneho and Red Tabara; Kaziba as strategic) are on the same page.

claims.text: The New Times (Kigali), a Rwandan state-aligned outlet, reported that, according to AFC/M23's Bertrand Bisimwa on X, no Munyamulenge could travel to Baraka, Fizi, Uvira or Mwenga, that the Minembwe airstrip was the only means of evacuation for the sick and of delivery of medicine and essential supplies, and that it had been damaged by a government plane.
claims.verification_note: Both passages verbatim on the page (byline James Karuhanga, 10 March 2025). Party statement (AFC/M23) relayed by Rwandan state-aligned media; evidence of what Bisimwa said, not of the damage or its effect on health access.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan (AFC/M23 post on X, relayed by Rwandan state-aligned media); evidence of what Bisimwa said, not of the fact. The page calls him 'deputy coordinator' and 'the M23 leader'. The 'government of my country' phrase is Bisimwa's; the page says Sukhoi jets bombed Minembwe villages 'twelve minutes ago' at his posting.

claims.text: OCHA reported in its South Kivu situation report that at least 127 women and minor girls were victims of rape in Uvira city during the forced confinement caused by the violent clashes of 15 to 22 February 2025, of whom 54 (43 percent) received medical care within 72 hours.
claims.verification_note: 127, 54, 43 % and 15-22 February all verbatim; 'Uvira city' carried by the preceding sentences on the page. Grade B: a single UN situation report, not a documented investigation. No perpetrator named by the source. Figures are OCHA's (compiled with humanitarian partners), for Uvira city ('dans la ville', under 'Territoire d’Uvira' / 'Dans la ville d'Uvira').
claims.researcher_note: Uvira city, adjacent to this unit's area; included because it is the main sexual-violence figure in the window and may not be held by the Uvira unit. Perpetrators not attributed by OCHA in this passage. Figures are humanitarian-actor estimates.

claims.text: OCHA reported that many sexual-violence cases in Uvira city went without medical care because of a shortage of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) kits in several health structures.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; the sentence directly follows the 127/54 passage, so 'cases' refers to the rape cases in Uvira city. Supply shortage; no actor attributed by the source.
claims.researcher_note: Shortage reason is stated as a supply shortage; no actor attributed. Classified access_denied as the nearest allowed health value.

claims.text: OCHA reported that a cholera epidemic was affecting the Uvira and Ruzizi health zones, that 242 cases and ten deaths had been recorded in the two zones as of 10 March 2025, and that the Ruzizi cholera treatment centre, located in Sange, faced a stock-out of medical supplies while case numbers kept rising.
claims.place_as_written: Sange (Ruzizi health zone) and Uvira health zones
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; 'cases kept rising' rests on the page beyond the stored excerpt. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: MSF reinforced its support from 4 March (same OCHA page) - not in the excerpt.

claims.text: OCHA reported that between 1 and 14 March 2025 clashes between the FARDC and the M23 continued in the Uvira Hauts Plateaux, affecting the localities of Kahololo, Kageregere, Kitembe, Bijombo, Mugete, Mitamba, Magunda and Muranvya.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira Hauts Plateaux: Kahololo, Kageregere, Kitembe, Bijombo, Mugete, Mitamba, Magunda, Muranvya
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on OCHA page, under 'Territoire d’Uvira'. Single UN situation report.
claims.researcher_note: Complements Actualite.cd r1-UV-2025Q1-030 (Rurambo, Kigarama, 12-13 Mar).

claims.text: Kivutimes reported that Twirwaneho and Wazalendo (led, it said, by Ebuela Seba alias Mtetezi) fought at Mikenge, Itombwe sector, from the morning of Monday 3 March 2025; according to local sources Wazalendo dislodged Twirwaneho, which had held the centre for more than two weeks, and Twirwaneho fighters fled toward Kalingi; around 18 heures men of Sematama counter-attacked with heavy weapons and reoccupied Mikenge.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (led by Ebuela Seba alias Mtetezi, per the source); Twirwaneho (men of Sematama)
claims.verification_note: Every clause verbatim on the retained page (byline Lubunga lavoix, 4 March 2025). Single local outlet relaying local sources. The same page closes saying Mikenge 'reste sous contrôle des Twirwaneho, qui ont profité du retrait des FARDC'. Conflicts in sequence with Actualite.cd (26 Feb: Mikenge passed to Twirwaneho after fighting with the FARDC on Tuesday); both kept. The page's grammar leaves it slightly ambiguous whether 'dirigés par Ebuela Seba' qualifies Wazalendo only. 2026-10-29: control edited: Frontline data fix (FRONTLINE_NOTES.md): control.held_by names only the holder (for a withdrawal, the side withdrawing), so the side class is not 'both sides named'; the other side stays in the statement. Wording from the stored excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Local outlet (Kivutimes, Bukavu/Uvira area), single source. Page says Twirwaneho held Mikenge 'for more than two weeks' before 3 March (since before 17 Feb), which does not support the Facebook-snippet lead of a FARDC/Wazalendo recapture on 24 Feb; that lead was not confirmed by any outlet I could open. Actualite.cd (26 Feb) says Mikenge passed to Twirwaneho after fighting on Tuesday 25 Feb. Spelling 'Twigwaneho' in headline, 'twigwaneho' in text.

claims.text: Kivutimes reported that after occupying Mikenge the Wazalendo set fire at midday to the camp of internally displaced people that housed mostly members of the Banyamulenge community, and that no source had confirmed a precise human toll although there were victims on both sides.
claims.place_as_written: Mikenge IDP camp, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on page; perpetrator as the source names it. Allegation by a single local outlet citing local sources; the 'victims on both sides' line refers to the day's clashes generally, not specifically to the camp.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborated in kind by the NHRC statement carried by Kivutimes on 13 March (separate claim).

claims.text: Kivutimes reported that the NGO New Hope Réconciliation Centre called on humanitarian organisations to help victims of the attacks that targeted the Mikenge displaced camp, which the article described as a devastating attack carried out by Mai Mai armed groups called Wazalendo, and that the camp, which housed about 310 households mainly of Banyamulenge families, was reduced to a heap of ashes.
claims.place_as_written: Mikenge IDP camp, Itombwe, Mwenga territory
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (Mai Mai), as described in the Kivutimes article on the NHRC appeal
claims.verification_note: Narrowed attribution: the excerpt's grammar makes the Wazalendo description and the 310 figure the article's narration, not explicitly NHRC's statement. The page does not say whether the Wazalendo attribution and the 310-household figure come from NHRC or from Kivutimes's own reporting; they are credited here to the article. Attack date not on this page (Kivutimes 4 Mar places the burning on 3 Mar).
claims.researcher_note: Date is the publication date (13 Mar); the attack date is not on this page (Kivutimes 4 Mar places the burning on 3 Mar). The page also says, per local sources, the attacks caused significant loss of life and looting; not quantified, not excerpted.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that fighting resumed in the Minembwe Hauts Plateaux between the FARDC supported by Wazalendo fighters and the coalition of the armed groups Twirwaneho and Gumino, and, according to the Fizi territory administrator, that the FARDC supported by Wazalendo militiamen launched an assault on the coalition's positions.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe Hauts Plateaux: Mukoko toward Kakenge; earlier Gahwera and Kivumu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and Wazalendo; Twirwaneho and Gumino coalition
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on Radio Okapi page (published 21/03/2025). Location detail (Mukoko, Kakenge, Gahwera, Kivumu) is on the same page (Nyarugabo tweet; 'La veille ... Gahwera et Kivumu').
claims.researcher_note: Page also reports fighting on the previous day (20 Mar) at several villages, notably Gahwera and Kivumu.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing several concordant sources, that the rural town of Kamanyola, in Walungu territory, had been under occupation by the M23 and their Rwandan allies since Tuesday 18 February, late in the evening.
claims.place_as_written: Kamanyola, Walungu territory (Ruzizi plain border with Rwanda and Burundi)
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and their Rwandan allies, per Radio Okapi
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on Radio Okapi page (published 19/02/2025); 'M23 and their Rwandan allies' is Radio Okapi's wording citing several concordant sources.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates BBC Gahuza r1-SKN-2025Q1-010 (M23 entered Kamanyola Tuesday night). Page says Kamanyola is in Walungu territory; it is the access to Uvira and Fizi.

claims.text: Agence France-Presse reported that military and official sources said Burundian troops were being discreetly withdrawn despite official denials; a senior officer told AFP 'Nous avions érigé une ligne de défense à Kamanyola' to try to stop the advance of the M23 and Rwandan soldiers but had to make a tactical retreat under enemy attack on Tuesday, adding that part of 'our troops' deployed in eastern DRC were returning home on foot, which a senior Burundian official confirmed to AFP.
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian troops (per anonymous military and official sources to AFP) vs M23 and Rwandan soldiers
claims.verification_note: The page calls the speaker 'un haut gradé' only; his Burundian affiliation is implied by context (Bujumbura withdrawing, 'nos troupes ... regagner le pays'). Statement now carries the article's own framing and the denial. Grade C: anonymous sources. Anonymous sources to AFP; Burundi officially denied withdrawing, and the article itself notes 'les démentis officiels'. Both accounts kept.
claims.researcher_note: Anonymous military and official sources; Burundi officially denied withdrawing (see existing claim citing Anadolu, r1 aa.com.tr). Date computed from 'hier [mardi]' and page date 19 Feb 2025 (Wednesday), so 18 Feb.

claims.text: MediaCongo, relaying nouveaumedia.cd / MCP, reported that, after the capture of Kamanyola, the M23 and allies of the Rwandan army were said to have taken the villages of Luvungi and Sange, a few kilometres from Uvira, causing panic in Uvira where shops closed and some people crossed the border into Burundi, and that clashes between uncontrolled elements of the army and Wazalendo were said to have killed civilians.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and allies of the Rwandan army; uncontrolled army elements and Wazalendo (clashes)
claims.verification_note: All passages verbatim; credit line 'nouveaumedia.cd / MCP, via mediacongo' (byline Hornella MANSANGA). Conditional ('auraient') kept; no toll or names given.
claims.researcher_note: Conditional tense ('auraient'); early report. Byline Hornella MANSANGA, credit 'nouveaumedia.cd / MCP, via mediacongo'.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that honorary senator Moïse Nyarugabo, in a tweet on Friday 21 March, said that since 6h that morning the FARDC and Wazalendo, coming from Fizi via Mukela and Mulima, had resumed their attack at Mukoko toward Kakenge, and that the inhabitants of the Fizi and Mwenga Hauts Plateaux, especially Minembwe, were again waking up under bombs.
claims.place_as_written: Mukoko toward Kakenge, Minembwe Hauts Plateaux, Fizi/Mwenga
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and Wazalendo; Twirwaneho and Gumino coalition
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on Radio Okapi page (21/03/2025). Statement by an individual politician as reported by Radio Okapi; the original tweet was not opened.
claims.researcher_note: Post by an individual politician as relayed by Radio Okapi; evidence of what he said. Original tweet not opened.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that intense fighting had been reported since the morning of Friday 9 May 2025 in Fizi territory, between AFC-M23 rebels allied to Twirwaneho and Wazalendo at Rugezi, sector of Mutambala; Wazalendo spokesperson Aimable Nabulizi said Wazalendo of the Biloze Bishambuke self-defence force of General Ngomanzo were attacking Rugezi.
claims.place_as_written: Rugezi, Basimukuma Sud, Mutambala sector, Fizi
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (Biloze Bishambuke, Gen. Ngomanzo) vs AFC-M23/Twirwaneho/Red Tabara, as stated by a Wazalendo spokesperson
claims.verification_note: Page checked (retained copy): excerpts exact and on this event; date printed. excerpt_en flag is sentence-initial words only. Single Goma outlet relaying a party spokesperson: C. The Wazalendo advance is claimed by the Wazalendo spokesperson ('selon la même source, qui revendique l’avancée des Wazalendo'). The commander's name is printed 'Ngomanzo' here and 'NGOMANZITO' in other Kivu Morning Post and SOS Médias Burundi pieces.
claims.researcher_note: Local outlet, Bukavu/Goma; one Wazalendo spokesperson is the only attribution. Spelling Ngomanzo here, Ngomanzito/NGOMANZITO in other KMP and SOS pieces.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 fighters were said to have taken Katogota on Thursday, 80 km north of Uvira city; Uvira resident Elias Muhasha told the BBC that M23 fighters took Katogota after heavy fighting that began on Wednesday; the M23 side neither confirmed nor denied reaching Katogota, but social-media video posted on Thursday showed some M23 fighters indicating they were in Katogota.
claims.actor_as_written: M23, as reported by BBC Gahuza
claims.verification_note: Kinyarwanda checked against the retained page: 'ku wa kane' = Thursday, 'ku wa gatatu' = Wednesday, 'ku ntera ya kilometero 80' = at a distance of 80 km (the draft's 'about' is not in the source; removed). Translations of the three excerpts are faithful. Date computed: the article is dated 9 May 2025 (a Friday) and says 'ku wa kane' (Thursday), so 8 May 2025 is approximate. 'bivugwa ko' = 'it is said that': the capture is reported, not confirmed.
claims.researcher_note: Single resident quoted; M23 neither confirmed nor denied. Date computed from weekday ('ku wa kane' = Thursday) and publication date 9 May 2025 (Friday); Thursday = 2025-05-08. Distance 80 km as printed. Existing claim r1-UV-2025Q2-018 covers 5-6 May fighting at Katogota (Radio Okapi).

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that from the morning of Friday heavy fighting was reported at Lugezi/Rugezi, Basimukuma-Sud grouping, Fizi, between Wazalendo and Twirwaneho fighters, and that many civilians fled; a Fizi resident who did not wish to be named told the BBC when the fighting began; some people were said to have been killed, but their number and the number of displaced civilians were hard to establish; local journalists said Wazalendo of the Biloze Bishambuke group were the ones fighting Twirwaneho fighters.
claims.verification_note: Draft cited the anonymous resident for the whole account; the page cites him only for the start time. Restored the source's 'some were said to have died' hedge. Removed the day number (not in any excerpt; date field carries 2025-05-09). Independent of the Kivu Morning Post claim (own sourcing): B for the fact of fighting. The article is dated 9 May 2025; 'uyu wa gatanu' = this Friday. The resident gave the start time as about 5 a.m. ('saa kumi n'imwe z'igitondo').
claims.researcher_note: Independent of the Kivu Morning Post claim above (own sourcing); corroborates date and parties.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post quoted a communiqué of the Twirwaneho (MRDP-Twirwaneho) saying that the Rurambo region had been violently attacked by government forces in coalition with Burundian troops and Wazalendo elements, that these acts deliberately targeted Banyamulenge civilians, and that it would take all necessary defensive and offensive measures; in the same article Wazalendo spokesperson Aimable Nabulizi said intense fighting had been reported at Rugezi since the morning of Monday 19 May 2025, where the Wazalendo of General NGOMANZITO faced AFC Twirwaneho M23 rebels.
claims.actor_as_written: MRDP-Twirwaneho (party statement); Wazalendo of Gen. Ngomanzito
claims.verification_note: Two attribution fixes: the Rugezi sentence is the Wazalendo spokesperson's quote, not the outlet's own attribution; and the page does not date the communiqué to 19 May, so the date now attaches only to the fighting Nabulizi described. The 'defensive and offensive measures' clause is on the page, outside the stored excerpt (excerpt gap). excerpt_en flag: sentence-initial word only. Party statements on both sides. The communiqué is undated on the page; it appears in the article of 19 May 2025. Its 'actes de guerre' wording is the Twirwaneho's own.
claims.researcher_note: Twirwaneho is a party; its accusation is cited only as what it said (partisan_twirwaneho); the outlet reproduces it in quotation marks and the page attributes it to 'le Twirwaneho' in a communiqué. Counter-account to the FARDC/Wazalendo account.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Wazalendo fighters allied to the Congolese army claimed to have taken control of Rugezi, Basimukuma grouping, Fizi, on Tuesday 20 May 2025 after night fighting with Twirwaneho allied to AFC-M23; the claim came from Wazalendo spokesperson Aimable Nabulizi, who said the enemy had been dispersed.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (Biloze Bishambuke, Gen. Ngomanzito), as claimed
claims.verification_note: Every clause is on the retained page; date and day are in Nabulizi's quote (outside the stored excerpts, so excerpt gap). Kept as a claimed recapture, not as established control. Party claim. The night fighting is also attributed to unnamed 'sources sécuritaires'. Nabulizi said firing was continuing at NAMUROMWA at 12:05. Control of Rugezi changed hands several times (12 April, 9, 19 and 20 May, about 9 June); no Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 account of 20 May found.
claims.researcher_note: Party claim only. Later Radio Okapi (14 Jun) says Rugezi was taken by Twirwaneho/Red Tabara coalition about five days before 14 Jun (see separate claim); control of Rugezi changed hands more than once. No AFC-M23/Twirwaneho account of 20 May found.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that nearly 4,000 displaced households were registered in the Ruzizi plain, in the cité of Sange and the Kabunambo grouping, caught between FARDC positions to the south and AFC/M23 to the north, having fled Kamanyola, Katogota, Luvungi, Bwegera and Luberizi, hosted since 20 February; Uvira territory administrator Jean de Dieu Masibwa, who visited on Saturday 28 June, called for humanitarian assistance.
claims.place_as_written: Sange and Kabunambo; origin Kamanyola, Katogota, Luvungi, Bwegera, Luberizi (Ruzizi plain), Uvira
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the retained page; Sange/Kabunambo sentence is outside the stored excerpts (excerpt gap). Radio Okapi (UN-backed, non-partisan) own reporting: B. The page also says the displaced lack medicines and latrines, with a risk of waterborne disease. Frontline indicator for end June: FARDC south, AFC/M23 north of Sange/Kabunambo.
claims.researcher_note: Also a frontline indicator: the page places FARDC south and AFC/M23 north of Sange/Kabunambo at end June.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that intense fighting took place on Saturday 12 April at Rugezi and Kabanju, Fizi territory, between Burundian forces allied to the FARDC and the Mai-Mai Biloze Bishambuke and fighters of the Twirwaneho armed group; according to a Twirwaneho fighter contacted by the outlet, who spoke on condition of anonymity, at least 17 Burundian soldiers were killed and the Twirwaneho captured one of them with radios and rifles.
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian forces allied to FARDC vs Twirwaneho (and Mai-Mai Biloze Bishambuke as reported)
claims.verification_note: Draft wrote the clash as Burundians 'with Twirwaneho fighters and Mai-Mai Biloze Bishambuke', which takes a side on an ambiguous sentence; restored the source's wording. Dropped the year (not printed in the excerpts; date field carries it) and the 'dozens over the months' aside (page only, unofficial sources, not about this event). Added the captured-soldier clause, which is in the excerpt. The toll is an anonymous party claim (Twirwaneho), not verified; the outlet's headline and lede state it without the hedge. The source's sentence on the parties is ambiguous: elsewhere it says the Mai-Mai Biloze Bishambuke 'have also suffered losses against the Twirwaneho rebels', i.e. on the FARDC/Burundian side. Lead: one Burundian soldier reported captured (unnamed). No Burundian government account found.
claims.researcher_note: Single anonymous party source for the toll (Twirwaneho); the outlet's headline says 'Uvira' though the fighting is in Fizi. The Burundian government's account not found. The sentence about Mai-Mai Biloze Bishambuke is ambiguous in the source (it lists them with the Twirwaneho side in one place and with FARDC allies elsewhere).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that since Wednesday new Burundian troops had crossed Lake Tanganyika into the territories of Uvira and Fizi; that on Thursday 22 May several Burundian soldiers stationed at the port of Mboko, in the Tanganyika sector, told residents they were heading to Bijombo to confront the rebels; and that these movements followed a strategic meeting held on 14 May in Uvira between the Congolese and Burundian military high commands.
claims.place_as_written: Mboko port, Bijombo, Swima, Uvira and Fizi territories
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian troops (FDNB) with FARDC and Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date and 'citing local sources' (the page states the troop crossing in its own voice; 'local sources' are cited for the earlier clashes). Meeting is the outlet's narration; 'security sources' are cited only for what it marked. Burundian outlet in exile; anonymous local and security sources; Burundi has not confirmed. The page also reports Burundian units seen in Swima en route to Gihamba and Kajembwe (Bijombo groupement), and 'approximately 10,000 Burundian soldiers' 'reportedly' engaged in the DRC.
claims.researcher_note: Burundian outlet in exile, anonymous local sources; Burundi government has not confirmed. The same article places earlier clashes at Kahololo (Uvira) the previous week and at Rugezi (Fizi) between Burundian forces, Wazalendo, FARDC and Twirwaneho (not used as a claim: no excerpt on detail). The 14 May meeting is attributed to security sources.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported on 4 June 2025, citing several local and humanitarian sources, that more than 3,000 people in the Burundian refugee camps of Mulongwe and Lusenda in Fizi territory had reportedly joined Wazalendo militias; a refugee quoted said he earned up to 10,000 Congolese francs a day at a Wazalendo checkpoint in Baraka, and refugees said some returned to the camps armed and in uniform.
claims.place_as_written: Mulongwe and Lusenda refugee camps; Baraka, Fizi
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the retained page (dateline, quote and camp passage outside the stored excerpts: excerpt gap). Hedge kept. 'auraient intégré' = reportedly joined: an unverified estimate; NGOs on site called it plausible. Enrolment as described is voluntary (pay, end of food aid), not forced. UNHCR withdrew from the two camps in January per the page. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi, Bukavu 4 June 2025: per several local and humanitarian sources, more than 3,000 people in Mulongwe and Lusenda camps (Fizi) reportedly (auraient) joined Wazalendo. All clauses are on the page; the stored excerpts lacked the 10,000 FC checkpoint quote and the 'several refugees say' passage, now added. 2026-10-28: source 1 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi, Bukavu 4 June 2025: per several local and humanitarian sources, more than 3,000 people in Mulongwe and Lusenda camps (Fizi) reportedly (auraient) joined Wazalendo. All clauses are on the page; the stored excerpts lacked the 10,000 FC checkpoint quote and the 'several refugees say' passage, now added.
claims.researcher_note: Figure 'plus de 3 000' is an unverified estimate ('auraient'); NGOs on site said it was plausible. The page says UNHCR withdrew from Lusenda and Mulongwe in January and that CNR Baraka reminded that refugees may not join armed groups. Voluntary enrolment as described, not forced.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Congolese army drones reportedly bombed on Thursday 15 May 2025 the positions of Twirwaneho fighters allied to AFC-M23 at NDAKE/Mikenge, Itombwe sector, Basimukindji 1 grouping, Mwenga; an anonymous security source claimed dozens of officers were eliminated, a figure the page does not corroborate.
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the retained page; location sentence outside the stored excerpts (excerpt gap). Conditional ('auraient bombardé'). The toll is an anonymous, pro-government security source's claim (it calls the Twirwaneho a 'mouvement terroriste') and is unverified. 'NDAKE' is described by that source as the name commonly given to the camps/positions at Mikenge. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Anonymous security source; casualty claim unverified. Conditional ('auraient bombardé'). Mikenge is in Mwenga territory (Itombwe) per the page.

claims.text: Kivutimes reported on 1 May 2025 that the Hôpital général de référence d'Itombwe at Mikenge, in the Hauts-Plateaux of Mwenga territory, was the victim of systematic looting of its medical equipment during violent clashes between the Twirwaneho armed group, allied to AFC/M23, and Wazalendo groups in March 2025; Nakiele hospital centre donated a binocular microscope and caesarean, delivery and hernia kits.
claims.place_as_written: Hôpital général de référence d'Itombwe, Mikenge, Itombwe sector, Mwenga
claims.actor_as_written: Not attributed by the source for the looting (clashes between Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 and Wazalendo)
claims.verification_note: Every clause on the retained page; donation and byline date outside the stored excerpts (excerpt gap). In the investigation window although before this unit's quarter; dated as the source dates it. Looting dated by the source only to March 2025 (month precision), during clashes; the source does not say who looted. The page spells the group 'twigwaneho'. Health authorities authorised temporary relocation of the hospital to Kipupu or Kiseke because Mikenge had become unliveable. Named on the page: Dr Sumaili Enas Prince (Nakiele) and the Itombwe hospital accountant Ebulaca Ngulumina (received the equipment on Friday 1 May). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that more than thirty people were killed on Sunday evening in the town of Sange after a bomb exploded in the middle of an inhabited area; according to several testimonies, the blast followed internal clashes between FARDC soldiers, a group of Congolese soldiers returning from the front and trying to flee towards Uvira having reportedly been stopped at the Sange bridge by another FARDC detachment; the provisional toll was at least 7 Burundian soldiers and 7 civilians, plus an undetermined number of Congolese soldiers and Wazalendo.

Tolls differ across leads.

claims.text: Congovirtuel reported that the Burundian lieutenant-colonel killed in the Rusizi plain was identified as Lt-Col Athanase Minani, a former FAB officer who commanded the 8th battalion of the Burundian contingent in the DRC; it said the incident, around 4 December 2025, also killed three of his guards and at least 20 Burundian soldiers during fighting intensified that week. Congovirtuel's headline attributes the death to an M23 drone strike; SOS Médias does not give a cause.
claims.researcher_note: Two independent-looking outlets name the same officer; both are local/analysis outlets and Burundi's own confirmation was not fetched (a Burundian presidential decree of 1 July 2025 promoting an 'MINANI Athanase' to Lt-Col appeared in a search snippet; not fetched, lead only). A further 'Rwandan outlet' IGIHE report (6 Dec) and africa-insight (9 Dec) not retrievable/fetched. The Congovirtuel page says 'around 4 December'; SOS Médias dates the clashes from 1 Dec. SOS also says 'several other young officers' were killed. Congovirtuel is a Kinshasa-leaning analysis site.

claims.text: SOSOYAMBOKA.NET, relaying an OCHA communiqué, reported that OCHA recalled that since January 2025 the Minembwe, Itombwe and Hauts Plateaux area had seen a resurgence of armed clashes with serious incidents, including attacks on civilians and the pillaging of health structures, that since May 2025 the Fizi–Lusuku–Point Zéro–Mikenge–Minembwe axis had been completely closed, controlled or blocked by armed groups, and that in August 2025 armed actors at Point Zéro reaffirmed their refusal of any humanitarian access; it added that, according to South Kivu's Commission Mouvement de Population (October 2025), close to 172 000 displaced and returnees were enclaved without access to essential goods or aid.

claims.actor_as_written: armed groups controlling or blocking the axis (not named by the source)

Relayed from OCHA by an aggregator; OCHA's original communiqué was not located. The 172 000 figure is a Commission Mouvement de Population estimate cited by OCHA.
claims.researcher_note: Relay: the page (published 2025-11-25) is an aggregator that presents the OCHA mission communiqué; the OCHA original was not located (Actualite.cd of 2025-11-25 carries a related OCHA alert already cited elsewhere). The page's text also gives June 2025 medicine blockage at Mulima and July-September 2025 child mortality at Minembwe HGR (not claimed here: before the unit period). Armed actors are not named in the page; Twirwaneho and Burundian-army roles are claimed by other parties (see Kivu Morning Post claim).

claims.text: The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani stated in its civic barometer that Burundi, whose troops fight alongside the FARDC, had deployed more than 10 000 soldiers in the high and middle plateaux of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga. The figure carries a footnote (6) to a Koaci.com article whose URL is dated 7 February 2025 and refers to 10 000 additional Burundian soldiers deployed. The same barometer says that after the clashes in the Ruzizi plain and the capture of Uvira by the AFC-M23 many Burundian soldiers fled the fighting to return to their country, and 'quelques milliers' (a few thousand) remained in the high and middle plateaux of Mwenga, Fizi and Uvira.
claims.place_as_written: High and middle plateaux of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed the issue number and coverage dates from the statement (no excerpt prints them; they are in the source title). The figure is not the coalition's own count: its footnote 6 cites a Koaci article URL dated 2025/02/07 headed '10000 soldats burundais supplementaires deployes', i.e. a February 2025 report of additional troops, which the barometer presents as a deployment total. The same page adds that after Uvira's fall many Burundian soldiers fled home but 'quelques milliers' remained in the Mwenga, Fizi and Uvira plateaux. The 10 000 figure is footnoted to a February 2025 press report of additional Burundian troops, not a December 2025 count; the barometer also says only a few thousand Burundian soldiers remained after Uvira fell. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: footnote 6 to a Koaci.com article dated 2025/02/07 on 10 000 additional Burundian soldiers 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: after the fall of Uvira many Burundian soldiers went home; a few thousand remained 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-020: The statement presents the 10 000 figure as a current deployment. The barometer footnotes it to a Koaci article of 7 February 2025 about 10 000 additional troops, and the same page says only a few thousand remained after Uvira fell. The statement needs both caveats so that a February 2025 press figure does not read as a December 2025 count.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): footnote 6 to a Koaci.com article dated 2025/02/07 on 10 000 additional Burundian soldiers; after the fall of Uvira many Burundian soldiers went home; a few thousand remained | cut 'The figure is not the coalition's own count' (an inference; the page prints only the footnote)
claims.researcher_note: Local civil-society coalition (South Kivu); the figure is footnoted to another source in the PDF and is not an independent count. The superscript '6' is part of the extracted text. Burundi's official acknowledgement of troop numbers not found here.
