claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the village of Point zéro, on the boundary between Fizi and Mwenga territories on the Mitumba range, in the high plateaux, passed under the control of Twirwaneho fighters, allies of the AFC/M23 rebels, from the morning of Friday 16 January 2026; according to its sources in the area, the fighters attacked the FARDC position that morning, forcing the army to withdraw.
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho (described as allies of AFC/M23); FARDC
claims.verification_note: Removed 'two days of fighting' and 'FARDC supported by Wazalendo': this page prints neither (those details are in the SOS Médias Burundi article, claim 1). Page says fighting had been intense at Tuwetuwe since Thursday 15 January. Same event as existing Point Zéro lines; separate local outlet.
claims.researcher_note: Same event as existing r1-UV-2026Q1-007 / UC-BI-FDLR-025 lines (Ebuteli, GoE) but a separate local source; SOS Médias Burundi also dates the fall to 16 January.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several local sources, that after Twirwaneho took Point Zéro on Friday 16 January, elements of FARDC, of the Burundian national defence force (printed 'FNDB') and Wazalendo groups withdrew to the localities of Mulima and Mutambala.
claims.place_as_written: Point Zéro to Mulima and Mutambala (Fizi)
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho; FARDC, FDNB ('FNDB' in source), Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: Figure 16 is printed on the page ('ce vendredi 16 janvier'), not in the stored excerpt; page also says the fall followed two days of fighting against FARDC backed by Burundian soldiers and Wazalendo.
claims.researcher_note: Single Burundi-based outlet citing local sources. Source date 17 Jan; fall dated 16 Jan by the source.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that FARDC, supported by the Burundian defence force (FDNB) and Wazalendo militiamen, retook the locality of Point Zéro in Fizi territory on 'Friday', from Twirwaneho fighters.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and supports the retake; excerpt_en flag is only translated proper nouns (Armed Forces of the DRC). Local sources in Minembwe say combat drones were used. Date 30 January computed from 'ce vendredi' in an article datelined Bukavu, 31 January 2026, which also reports fighting 'ce samedi 31 janvier'.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date: the article has a Bukavu dateline of 31 January and also says fighting continued 'ce samedi 31 janvier', so the Friday is 30 January. Single outlet citing local sources in Minembwe; mentions combat drones used.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that residents said a Congolese army drone had reportedly bombed the commercial centre of Madegu, wounding three civilians.
claims.verification_note: Removed '31 January' from the statement (no excerpt prints it) and kept the conditional. Date stays approximate: page says 'Après la reprise de Point Zéro, les affrontements se sont poursuivis ce samedi 31 janvier'. Residents' account; the source uses the conditional ('aurait bombardé'). The strike's day is not given; the article reports it right after fighting 'ce samedi 31 janvier'.
claims.researcher_note: Residents' account relayed by one outlet; the day is not stated for the strike itself. No FARDC account found in this source.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Moïse Nyarugabo, an honorary Congolese senator, said that on Thursday 12 February 2026 the FARDC coalition, supported by drones and mortars aimed at the villages of Minembwe, killed a 101-year-old woman named Mukuzakabano Elisabeth; the outlet's next sentence says two other women were wounded in this attack, during which the hospital of Bidegu was bombed.
claims.place_as_written: Bidegu and Minembwe villages (Hauts Plateaux, Fizi)
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC coalition (drones, mortars), per Moïse Nyarugabo
claims.verification_note: Narrowed attribution: the hospital/wounded sentence is the outlet's narration, not a quoted Nyarugabo statement. Name printed as given. Single account from an interested party (Banyamulenge political figure), relayed by one outlet; the wounded women and the hospital bombing are in the outlet's narration following his account, not in a direct quote. No independent confirmation found; the FARDC says it does not fight in populated areas (Radio Okapi, 2 Feb).
claims.researcher_note: Single account from a Banyamulenge-community political figure (an interested party), relayed by a Goma outlet; not independently verified. FARDC account of the same period: see the Radio Okapi 2 Feb claim (denies fighting in populated areas). Article also says shelling of Kalingi, Bidegu, Rubemba, Karongi, Mukoko and Ilundu on 10-12 Feb per Nyarugabo.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Angolan Presidency announced in a communiqué on Thursday a ceasefire between Kinshasa and AFC/M23 from 18 February 2026, an announcement it said came as the FARDC had launched an offensive on several villages of Minembwe.
claims.verification_note: Removed '(12 February 2026)' from the statement: the excerpt prints only 'Jeudi'. Second clause is on the page. Announcement date (12 February) computed from 'Jeudi' in an article dated 13 February; the Angolan communiqué itself was not fetched.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('Jeudi') and article date 13 Feb. Context for the highlands fighting; the Angolan communiqué itself was not fetched.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 accused the FARDC of multiple ceasefire violations despite the negotiation process under way in Doha, and said it was open to any peace and de-escalation initiative.
claims.verification_note: Party statement relayed by media; second clause on the page, not in the excerpt. Date is article date.
claims.researcher_note: Party account relayed by media; the AFC/M23 communiqué itself not found. Date is article date.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the Sukola Sud operations in South Kivu, Sub-Lieutenant Mbuyi Reagan, said on Monday 2 February that the army had been fighting for five days to retake Minembwe, regarded as the stronghold of Twirwaneho and its allies.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC (Sukola Sud operations) vs Twirwaneho, AFC/M23, RED Tabara, Gumino
claims.verification_note: Statement as reported is accurately captured; the date 2 February is on the page. Grade B is for the fact that he said it; the content is a party account. He also claimed 'more than 35 combatants neutralised' the day before and described the enemy as M23-AFC backed by the Rwandan army allied to Twirwaneho, Gumino and RED Tabara: party claims, unverified.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi (local radio). Casualty claim ('more than 35 combatants neutralised') is the FARDC's own and unverified.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that Sub-Lieutenant Mbuyi Reagan, FARDC spokesperson, said the enemy was dropping bombs blindly in populated areas where civilians were, while the regular army 'does not fight in agglomerations' and protects the population.
claims.verification_note: Quote verbatim, attributed on the page. Partisan denial; contrasts with residents' and Banyamulenge-community accounts of FARDC drone and mortar strikes (SOS Médias Burundi 1 Feb; Kivu Morning Post 13 Feb).
claims.researcher_note: FARDC account only; set against Twirwaneho-side and community accounts of FARDC drone/mortar strikes on Minembwe villages (Kivu Morning Post 13 Feb; SOS Médias Burundi 1 Feb). Quote is in the source inside quotation marks, attributed to Mbuyi Reagan in the preceding sentence.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the administrator of Fizi territory, Samy Badibanga Kalonji, said the number of internally displaced people was approaching one million across Fizi territory, and that fighting on Thursday 5 February at 'Point Zéro' caused a new mass displacement.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC vs armed groups Twirwaneho, Red Tabara, FNL Zabampema, Android and Vijana Power (per Radio Okapi)
claims.verification_note: Statement accurate. Actor corrected: the page names the armed groups as Twirwaneho, Red Tabara, FNL Zabampema, Android and Vijana Power ('Les combats ont opposé les FARDC aux groupes armés Twirwaneho, Red Tabara, FNL Zabampema, Android et Vijana Power'); it does not name Gumino or Wazalendo for this fighting. Single official's estimate; his direct quote says 'plus d'un million'. He says it includes people from Fizi, Uvira city, Mwenga, Kabambare (Maniema) and parts of Tanganyika.
claims.researcher_note: Single official's estimate, unverified and not broken down; he says it includes people displaced last year and recently, from Fizi, Uvira city, Mwenga, Kabambare (Maniema) and parts of Tanganyika. Compare Mercy Corps/OCHA household counts.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that FARDC supported by Wazalendo have recovered Mikenge since Sunday 1 March, according to Pacifique Kararuka, president of the Nouvelle société civile congolaise at Kipupu.
claims.verification_note: Supported; second outlet to SOS Médias Burundi with a named local civil-society source. '1 March' comes from the outlet's lede ('depuis ce dimanche 1 er mars'), not from Kararuka's quote.
claims.researcher_note: Also reported by SOS Médias Burundi (existing r1-ATR-SK-2026-008); this is a second outlet with named local civil-society source. Actualite.cd also states AFC/M23 elements have occupied Mikenge since March 2025 (outlet's own wording).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that FARDC spokesperson in the region, Lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, said villages including Mikenge, Kakenge, Bilalombili and Bidegu 1 had been retaken, and that five elements were captured, 17 surrendered and 11 bodies left on the ground, among them a brigade commander of AFC/M23 and a logistics officer of Twirwaneho.
claims.verification_note: Quote supported in full on the page; brigade-commander clause is on the page beyond the stored excerpt. FARDC figures, unverified party claims. Rank printed 'lieutenant' here and 'sous-lieutenant' by Radio Okapi on 2 Feb; name order also differs.
claims.researcher_note: FARDC figures, unverified; the source says the quote concerns the FARDC riposte in Fizi. The spokesperson's name is printed 'Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji' here and 'Mbuyi Reagan' by Radio Okapi. The excerpt's 'en même le sol' is the page's own wording. AFC/M23 reply not found.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported, citing local sources, that FARDC, FDNB and Wazalendo now control strategic areas in the centre of Mikenge, including the main hospital, while Twirwaneho actors were reportedly still in the surrounding area.
claims.verification_note: Supported. Date approximate (article datelined 2 March, published 4 March). Swahili edition of SOS Médias Burundi's own reporting; same origin as its French report, not independent.
claims.researcher_note: Swahili edition of an existing French-language SOS Médias Burundi report (r1-ATR-SK-2026-008); counts as the same origin, not independent. Hospital named only as 'main hospital'.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that on Sunday fighting was also reported in several villages of Minembwe including Bidegu, Ilundu, Rugezi, Kalingi, Kalongi and Kakenge.
claims.place_as_written: Bidegu, Ilundu, Rugezi, Kalingi, Kalongi, Kakenge (Minembwe, Fizi)
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC, FDNB, Wazalendo vs Twirwaneho and M23
claims.verification_note: Supported. The article adds that FARDC, FDNB and Wazalendo attacks were reportedly repelled by Twirwaneho and M23 ('waliripotiwa kufanya mashambulizi lakini wakazuiwa na wapiganaji wa Twirwaneho na M23'). Sunday = 1 March from dateline 'Machi 2, 2026'.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from 'Jumapili hii' (this Sunday) with dateline 2 March; Sunday = 1 March. Machine-style Swahili; the same article elsewhere says the attacks were repelled by Twirwaneho and M23.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that intense fighting opposed the FARDC/Wazalendo coalition and AFC/M23 rebels from the morning of Tuesday 17 March in the villages of Kabunango and Runingu in the Uvira grouping, South Kivu, and that traffic was cut on the RN5 linking Bukavu and Uvira; Martin Mafikiri of the Nouvelle société civile congolaise said both sides had reinforced in the Ruzizi plain.
claims.place_as_written: Kabunango, Runingu, Kabunambo, Sange, Biriba, Kasambura (Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory)
claims.verification_note: The opening account is the outlet's own narration, not Mafikiri's; Mafikiri is credited only with the remark that both camps reinforced in the Ruzizi plain. Attribution fixed. Another civil-society actor reported heavy fighting toward Kabunambo and Sange; the outlet also lists Biriba and Kasambura.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates existing Radio Okapi claim r1-UV-2026Q1-049 (Luvungi/Kabunambo) with a different set of villages; the page also names Biriba, Kasambura. Source is Martin Mafikiri's civil-society account.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, according to the rebellion (AFC/M23), the 17 March fighting in the Ruzizi plain was a 'guerre généralisée' (generalised war) waged by the government army and its allies.
claims.verification_note: Supported; 17 and M23 printed on the page and in the title. Party position reported secondhand; the outlet says 'la rébellion' in an article about AFC/M23 fighting on 17 March; no direct AFC/M23 communiqué cited.
claims.researcher_note: AFC/M23 position reported secondhand; no FARDC/Kinshasa account of who started the 17 March fighting found in this source.

claims.text: MSF said that on 1 May 2026 its team travelling between Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu in South Kivu for a needs assessment was stopped at a checkpoint controlled by Wazalendo elements, and that armed men then fired among themselves while the team was caught in the middle. MSF said all staff later returned safely to Bukavu.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo elements (checkpoint), as described by MSF
claims.verification_note: All three excerpts exact on the retained MSF page; the safe-return clause is on the page (lead paragraph). MSF statement, attributed as MSF's. MSF's own account of its own incident (press release 8 May 2026). MSF does not say who fired; the team was afterwards urged to continue towards Mwenga.
claims.researcher_note: Primary MSF statement; existing claim r1-SV-2026-020 relays this via Kivu Morning Post. MSF says incidents are 'neither isolated nor limited to one armed group'.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing local sources, that on 17 June 2026 FARDC (supported by the Burundian army and Wazalendo) and Twirwaneho allied to AFC-M23 fought on three axes around Minembwe centre: axis 1 (Mikenge to Gitavi) led by the army and Wazalendo; axis 2 (Bidegu-Kalingi) led by the special forces Hiboux and Serpent noir using combat drones; axis 3 (Kakenge) led exclusively by the Burundian army and FDLR units, according to local and security sources.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe centre, Gitavi, Bidegu, Kalingi, Ilundu, Kakenge (Hauts Plateaux), Fizi/Mwenga
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC, Wazalendo, FDNB, forces spéciales Hiboux, Serpent noir, FDLR (per local sources) vs Twirwaneho/AFC-M23
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; figure flags are axis numbers and the 'M23' name, both printed on the page (clause quotes). excerpt_en flags are capitalisation/translation artefacts only. Single outlet, anonymous sources: C. Order of battle (Hiboux, Serpent noir, FDNB, FDLR units) is Kivu Morning Post's, from unnamed local and security sources; not confirmed by FARDC or Burundi.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet, anonymous local sources; FDLR role on axis 3 is an allegation by local sources. FARDC/Kinshasa account of the same days is in the Actualite.cd claim.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported, in an account of the 17 June 2026 fighting around Minembwe whose opening it attributes to local sources, that on axis 1 (Mikenge towards Gitavi) several houses of Banyamulenge civilians were burned by the army and Wazalendo militiamen in the first village of Gitavi. The article gives no specific source for this incident and carries no FARDC response.
claims.actor_as_written: the army and Wazalendo militiamen, per Kivu Morning Post's local sources
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; the page does not date the burning itself, so the day was removed from the statement and date_precision set to approximate. No FARDC response on the page. The article (17 June 2026) does not give the day of the burning; it is reported in its account of that day's fighting, so the date is approximate (on or shortly before 17 June). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: account attributed to local sources 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: 17 June 2026; axis 1 (Mikenge towards Gitavi) 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-024: Read the retained page: the burning sentence carries no attribution of its own; 'selon des sources locales' attaches to the article's opening account of the fighting. The article's framing is sympathetic to the Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 side (e.g. it says they 'ont réussi à stopper l’offensive'), so the allegation is single-outlet and unconfirmed; grade C is right. Amend to show how the sourcing actually runs.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): account attributed to local sources; 17 June 2026; axis 1 (Mikenge towards Gitavi)
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet; no FARDC response found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the spokesperson of operation Sukola 2 Sud-Kivu, Lieutenant Reagan Kalonji, said FARDC had since the evening of Tuesday 16 June retaken total control of Kitavi village, the Irundu agglomeration and positions at the Ugeafi school at Madegu near Minembwe centre, and that on 17 June the army was trying to retake the Minembwe-centre airfield. The Fizi territory administrator Sammy Badibanga said the clashes created a catastrophic humanitarian situation.
claims.place_as_written: Kitavi, Irundu, Madegu (Ugeafi school), Minembwe centre airfield, Fizi
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC supported by Wazalendo, vs Twirwaneho/Red Tabara allied to AFC/M23 (as the source states)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; every clause found on the page. Grade B is for the fact that FARDC made this announcement (credible outlet), not for the control change itself. FARDC announcement only; contested by residents and a human rights defender quoted by DW Swahili (18 June) and by the Twirwaneho/M23 account carried by SOS Médias Burundi (dateline 19 June). The page also spells the spokesperson 'Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji'.
claims.researcher_note: FARDC announcement relayed by an established outlet; contested by residents (see DW Swahili claim). Note the page prints 'Sammy Badibanga' here and 'Samy Badibanga' in Mediacongo/Radio Okapi.

claims.text: DW (Swahili) reported that the Congolese army claimed to have controlled Minembwe since Wednesday evening and that Twirwaneho had fled, but that residents denied it. Human rights defender Maniragaba Byashonyi said no FARDC soldiers were in the centre of Minembwe and that the centre was controlled by MRDP/Twirwaneho.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC (claim); MRDP/Twirwaneho (as described by local residents)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; Byashonyi's name and role are on the page. Credible outlet reporting two opposing accounts, both attributed. DW Swahili published 18 June 2026 (Thursday), so 'Wednesday evening' is 17 June. Residents' and the defender's account contradicts the FARDC announcement (Actualite.cd, 18 June); each account is kept separately.
claims.researcher_note: Directly contradicts the FARDC announcement (Actualite.cd 18 June). Date of 'Wednesday evening' computed from weekday and publication date (17 June 2026). The Byashonyi quote is cited as printed; the page's excerpt begins mid-quotation.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, after fighting around Minembwe, the FARDC, the FDNB and their allies had reportedly withdrawn to the localities of Lwiko, Mutunda and Miko, leaving several peripheral positions of Minembwe under the control of Twirwaneho/M23 fighters. It said the FARDC had not published a detailed communiqué at the time of writing, while local military sources confirmed a strategic repositioning after particularly violent clashes in the Ilundu and Bidegu areas.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe periphery, Lwiko, Mutunda, Miko, Ilundu, Bidegu, Fizi/Mwenga
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Raw statement turned the outlet's conditional narration into 'local sources said ... withdrew'; corrected to keep the conditional and the outlet as narrator. Dateline day moved to the date field. The withdrawal is reported in the conditional ('se seraient retirés'); dateline Minembwe, 19 June 2026, after 'près d'une semaine' of fighting. Contradicts the FARDC announcement of 16-18 June gains; each account kept separately.
claims.researcher_note: Burundian outlet with Banyamulenge-leaning sourcing; conditional tense ('se seraient retirés'). Conflicts with the FARDC claim of 16-18 June gains. Date range approximate: 'près d'une semaine' to 19 June.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi quoted former national deputy Moïse Nyarugabo as saying 'La menace sur Minembwe est écartée', that despite Sukhoi bombardments, drones and heavy artillery the forces engaged had been pushed back beyond the Lwiko river; it reported he accused the coalition of bombardments causing civilian losses and mass displacement.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; name and accusation on the page. Party-aligned claim reported by one outlet: C. Speaker is a former national deputy; the page does not state a party affiliation. Date is approximate (article dateline 19 June, published 21 June).
claims.researcher_note: Speaker is a former deputy, not an office-holder; his affiliation to Twirwaneho is not stated in the excerpt.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing residents' testimonies, that clashes had intensified since Friday 3 April 2026 in the Bijombo area of Uvira territory between FARDC supported by FDNB elements, Wazalendo and Gumino fighters on one side and Twirwaneho fighters affiliated with the M23 on the other, displacing thousands of civilians; Muramvya, Masata, Nyakirango, Irango and Kajembwe were among the most affected localities.
claims.place_as_written: Bijombo (Muramvya, Masata, Nyakirango, Irango, Kajembwe), Uvira territory
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC, FDNB, Wazalendo, Gumino vs Twirwaneho (per testimonies gathered by the outlet)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; all clauses on the page. Party line-up is from residents' testimonies gathered by SOS Médias Burundi (dateline Bukavu, 6 April 2026); no FARDC or Burundi response on the page. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi (English), dateline Bukavu 6 Apr 2026, posted 8 Apr: per residents' testimonies, FARDC with FDNB elements, Wazalendo and Gumino fight M23-affiliated Twirwaneho in Bijombo, intensified since Friday 3 April 2026. All clauses are on the page; displacement and affected localities were in no stored excerpt, now added.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet; dateline Bukavu 6 April 2026. Residents' accounts only; no FARDC/Burundi response found in the page.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi quoted a resident of Muramvya village (Bijombo area), 'Yohana', as saying residents were fleeing because 'the Wazalendo are threatening civilians and stealing our livestock', and that some residents were hiding in the bush, others had fled to the forests and many had taken refuge in churches in Masoro and Gahuna.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; Masoro/Gahuna clause is on the page. One resident's testimony, first name only as printed. Date is the article dateline (6 April 2026). 2026-10-28: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi (English), dateline Bukavu 6 Apr 2026, posted 8 Apr. The hiding/churches clause is part of Yohana's own quote, not the outlet's report, so it is attributed to him; the stored excerpt omitted it and is replaced by the full contiguous quote. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi (English), dateline Bukavu 6 Apr 2026, posted 8 Apr. The hiding/churches clause is part of Yohana's own quote, not the outlet's report, so it is attributed to him; the stored excerpt omitted it and is replaced by the full contiguous quote.
claims.researcher_note: Single anonymous-style resident testimony (first name only, as printed); date is the dateline (6 April).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Burundian army spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, acknowledged on the BBC that Banyamulenge are trapped in areas 'where the enemy is', saying 'It’s understandable that those who go to buy food for the enemy are trapped.'
claims.place_as_written: not stated by the source (article on Bijombo, Uvira territory, and Minembwe)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Date was '2026-04' with month precision, which implies the interview took place in April; the page gives no date, so it is set to the report date with approximate precision. Location is not given for the remark. The BBC interview is undated on the page; 8 April 2026 is only the date SOS Médias Burundi reported it, and the interview may be earlier. 'Acknowledged' is the outlet's verb.
claims.researcher_note: Date of the BBC interview not given by the page; reported 2026-04-08 and may predate April. Original BBC item not located.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that in a communiqué MRDP-Twirwaneho denounced ongoing attacks on civilians in Minembwe and Mikenge, rejected FARDC accusations that Minembwe served as a sanctuary for Burundian RED-Tabara rebels, demanded the immediate withdrawal of Burundian forces from Congolese territory and called for an independent international investigation into human rights violations in the region. The outlet quoted Colonel Kamasa Ndakize Welcome, in the communiqué, as calling those accusations false.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe, Mikenge (Hauts Plateaux de Fizi, Itombwe, Uvira)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Raw said the communiqué 'cited' the colonel; the page says he made the statement in the communiqué, so that clause was narrowed to what he is quoted as saying. Date stays in the date field. Party communiqué, cited only as what MRDP-Twirwaneho said. Dated by the article ('ce jeudi', 11 June 2026). The communiqué also alleges massacres, forced displacement, sexual violence and hostage-taking by the coalition, with no incident detail.
claims.researcher_note: Party communiqué, cited for what the party said only. The communiqué also alleges massacres, forced displacement, sexual violence and hostage-taking by the coalition, with no incident detail. Outlet publisher is KMP; communiqué is Twirwaneho's.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that from 08:00 on Friday 15 May 2026 Kinshasa had ordered the deployment of heavily armed combat helicopters from Kalemie to join strikes on Minembwe and surroundings, in addition to combat drones, heavy artillery and Sukhoi-25 jets. Fighting was reported at Kakenge, Kalonge, Bidegu and Kalingi (Fizi) and at Mikenge (Mwenga).
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe, Kakenge, Kalonge, Bidegu, Kalingi, Mikenge, Fizi/Mwenga
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; speaker name and Sukhoi-25 clause are on the page. AFC/M23 claim, not verified. The headline says 'avions de combat' while the quoted statement speaks of combat helicopters.
claims.researcher_note: Party claim, not verified; the headline says 'avions de combat' while the quote says helicopters. No FARDC reply to this claim found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported (9 June) that Mikenge village (Mwenga) was hit by bombardments on the night of Sunday to Monday '7 juin', leaving at least two dead and 6 wounded including two children; it said the army attributed the bombardments to the AFC/M23-Twirweneho rebel coalition and, according to an army communiqué, the air attacks hit FARDC positions at Mikenge and its surroundings, causing heavy material damage.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; attribution clause on the page. Date range 2026-06-07/2026-06-08 with 'range' precision is the honest rendering of the inconsistent date. Date as printed is internally inconsistent: 7 June 2026 is a Sunday, but the page says 'la nuit du dimanche au lundi 7 juin'; the night of 7-8 June is kept as a range. The casualty figure is the outlet's, not attributed; the perpetrator attribution is FARDC's. The page spells the group 'Twirweneho'. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: army attributed the bombardments to the AFC/M23-Twirweneho coalition 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-024: Read the retained page: the FARDC attribution sentence is printed (not in the stored excerpt, which only carries the 'positions des FARDC' clause). Possible double count: the 8 June Actualite.cd article (r1-SKC-2026H1-015) gives the identical toll for Ilundu on Sunday 7 June, and SOS Médias Burundi and Kivu Morning Post report that same toll for Ilundu; Kivu Morning Post attributes the Ilundu strike to FARDC drones. The FARDC communiqué as relayed describes hits on its own positions, not on civilians. claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on X that at 14:00 on Wednesday 24 June 2026 'les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa ont bombardé, à l’aide de drones de combat, l’hôpital général de Minembwe, y compris le pavillon pédiatrique'. claims.text: Mediacongo, carrying a report credited 'Radio Okapi / MCP', reported, citing local sources, that clashes took place on Wednesday 24 June in the villages of Ilundu and Alengei between FARDC and the fighters of the Twirwaneho armed coalition and their allies; the militia accused FARDC of drone bombardments on its positions, while local actors called this a 'fuite en avant'. It also reported that at the sixth meeting of the Joint Oversight Committee (Comité mixte de surveillance, CMS) on the security situation in the DRC, held on 24 June 2026 in London, Kinshasa and Kigali reaffirmed their commitment to defuse tensions over Minembwe.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC vs Twirwaneho and allies (described as backed by Rwanda by the source)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Raw named the London body 'Joint Security Mechanism'; the page says Comité mixte de surveillance (CMS), rendered here as Joint Oversight Committee per the stored translation. 'Supported by Rwanda' is the outlet's description of the Twirwaneho coalition. The local sources spoke on Friday 26 June. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Mediacongo, 28 Jun 2026; the credit line reads 'Radio Okapi / MCP, via mediacongo.net', so the text is Radio Okapi's copy and the statement should say so (originating_source already records Radio Okapi). Every clause is on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi-originated copy (Mediacongo credit 'Radio Okapi / MCP'; Radio Okapi original dated 27 June not opened). 'Supported by Rwanda' is the outlet's characterisation. Relevant to the AFC/M23 hospital claim of the same day.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 political spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that forces his movement calls the 'coalisées du régime de Kinshasa' intensified their ground attacks on the Point Zéro area at around 04:45 in the early hours of the morning; he also said these forces attacked Kasika (Mwenga territory) early that morning, and that government forces attacked Nyaruhinga and Mukoko in the Minembwe area. This is the AFC/M23 account.
claims.place_as_written: Point Zéro, Kasika, Nyaruhinga, Mukoko (Fizi / Mwenga territories, Minembwe area), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (Lawrence Kanyuka); Kinshasa 'coalised' forces as described by AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; the date '31' is printed only in the page lede (not in a stored excerpt), so it is removed from the statement; the date field keeps the article's 31 August. Kept as party account only. Party account (AFC/M23) relayed by Kivu Morning Post, which says it was a message on social media; the original post was not seen.
claims.researcher_note: Party account only (AFC/M23). Kivu Morning Post article is a relay of a Kanyuka social-media message; the post itself was not seen. Same article says the spokesperson described the opposing side as FARDC, Wazalendo and the Burundian army. Complements existing Aug 30-31 claims (Actualite.cd, SOS Médias Burundi) giving the Kinshasa-side account.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to the Fizi territory administrator, at least eighteen people were killed and many others wounded in drone bombings 'du M23 et de ses alliés' on the morning of Friday 3 July in the village of Mulima; the administrator said there were many victims among women, men and children, as well as livestock losses. The attribution to the M23 and its allies is the administrator's.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and its allies (as alleged by the Fizi territory administrator)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; '18' is the title's figure and 'dix-huit' in the excerpt. Removed the year (not in excerpt) and added the livestock clause the excerpt prints. Toll differs from other accounts of the same strike (e.g. civil society about 16 killed); figures kept separate, not merged. The same page quotes humanitarians as reporting more than eighteen dead among displaced people.
claims.researcher_note: Single official local source relayed by Radio Okapi (Kinshasa-side administrator); no M23 or Rwandan reply found in this page. Other outlets cited by search leads gave 17 or 21 dead (leads only, not opened). Existing claim r1-ATR-SK-2026-006 (Radio Okapi 9 Jul, civil society: about 16 killed, 12 wounded) covers the same event with a different figure; figures not merged.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Badibanga, said: 'Les infrastructures sanitaires et scolaires ont été détruites, et plusieurs élèves ont vu leurs écoles anéanties dans les villages de Mulima, Kangouli et leurs environs' (health and school infrastructure destroyed; several pupils' schools wiped out in Mulima, Kangouli and surroundings). The source does not name or number the health facilities.
claims.place_as_written: Mulima, Kangouli, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and its allies (as alleged by the Fizi territory administrator)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; date and the M23 attribution are not in this excerpt (they are in claim 1's), so the statement is narrowed to the quoted wording. claims.researcher_note: Which health facilities were hit is not specified; seek UN/health-cluster confirmation. The sentence is quoted from the administrator.

claims.text: Radio Okapi's press review reported that the Agence congolaise de presse (ACP) reports the discovery of eleven mass graves in South Kivu, seven months after massacres attributed (attribués) to the M23 in the towns of Sange and Luvungi, Uvira territory; according to ACP the announcement was made on Monday 27 July by the Auditorat militaire supérieur du Sud-Kivu after an investigation conducted jointly with the 33rd military region.
claims.place_as_written: Sange and Luvungi (Ruzizi plain), Uvira territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Auditorat militaire supérieur du Sud-Kivu (announcement); massacres 'attribués au M23' per ACP
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; kept all attribution to ACP; no perpetrator beyond the excerpt's 'attribués au M23'. Lead for add_excerpt: the page also quotes colonel-magistrat Kumbu Ngoma, auditeur militaire supérieur du Sud-Kivu, on identified burial sites and gathered evidence. High-stakes: single state-media relay (ACP) of a Congolese military-justice announcement; the announcement itself, body counts and the identity of the victims were not seen. 'Attribués au M23' is ACP's wording; who made the attribution is not stated. No independent confirmation. 2026-10-28: source 0 publisher edited: fact-check fc1: The retained page is Radio Okapi's press review of 28 Jul 2026 (radiookapi.net) summarising ACP; the statement says so correctly, but both sources list ACP as publisher. Publisher set to Radio Okapi; ACP stays as originating source. 2026-10-28: source 1 publisher edited: fact-check fc1: The retained page is Radio Okapi's press review of 28 Jul 2026 (radiookapi.net) summarising ACP; the statement says so correctly, but both sources list ACP as publisher. Publisher set to Radio Okapi; ACP stays as originating source.
claims.researcher_note: Relay of a state-agency report of a Congolese military-justice announcement (a Kinshasa-side authority); the underlying announcement was not seen. Related to existing claim r1-UV-2026Q3-022 (governor: up to 49 mass graves in the Uvira sector). Months of the massacres (Dec 2025) fall before the window; only the July 2026 discovery announcement is recorded. Sange/Luvungi lie on the Ruzizi plain.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo recalled, in a later article on fighting at Point Zéro, that on 4 July Twirwaneho elements, allies of the AFC/M23, had taken control of Point Zéro after dislodging the FARDC.
claims.place_as_written: Point Zéro (Mwenga/Fizi highlands, Itombwe), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; removed the publication date (29 August), which no excerpt prints. Retrospective line in an article published weeks later; the year is inferred from 'le 4 juillet dernier'.
claims.researcher_note: Recap line in a later article; independent of existing r1-UV-2026Q3-003 (SOS Médias Burundi, Twirwaneho statement). FARDC spokesperson on 7 July (existing claim) said the army made a 'repli stratégique' from Point Zéro. The article places Point Zéro in Mwenga territory (Itombwe) and 74 km from Fizi-Centre; other outlets say Fizi.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that violent clashes had pitted AFC/M23 elements and their allies against the FARDC, backed by Wazalendo groups, since Friday morning at Point Zéro, Itombwe highlands, Mwenga territory. claims.place_as_written: Point Zéro-Centre, Itombwe highlands, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 and allies; FARDC supported by Wazalendo groups

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing testimonies and local sources, that the FARDC, the FDNB and Wazalendo militiamen had lost several localities, notably Point Zéro, Kakenge, Rubemba, Mikenge and Kalongi, a loss these sources attributed to Twirwaneho fighters allied to the AFC/M23, and that FARDC and FDNB soldiers had reportedly withdrawn from the Rugezi, Kakenge and Point Zéro sectors towards Mukera, while others had reportedly headed towards Misisi.
claims.place_as_written: Point Zéro, Kakenge, Rubemba, Mikenge, Kalongi, Rugezi, Mukera (Fizi highlands), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho (allied to AFC/M23) per local sources; FARDC, FDNB, Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; wording aligned to the conditional and to 'testimonies gathered'. Anonymous local sources; the losses are described as recent ('ces derniers jours') as of the article date, not dated precisely.
claims.researcher_note: Anonymous local sources via a Burundian exile-run outlet; the article itself says the information could not be independently confirmed. Mikenge and Kalongi are named here as lost; the existing FARDC statement (7 July) claimed three villages retaken near Minembwe - a contested picture.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing local sources in Fizi territory, that three vehicles carrying ammunition and Burundian soldiers had reportedly been targeted by drones at Mulima during the past week, and that according to these sources several soldiers had reportedly been killed, among them a colonel and a major of the Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB); it said no official toll was available at the time of publication and that the information could not be independently confirmed.
claims.actor_as_written: drones, operator not stated by the source; FDNB targeted
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. The outlet's caveat (no official toll, not independently confirmed) is in the next sentence on the page, not the stored excerpt: kept because it only lowers certainty; please extend the excerpt with add_excerpt. Unconfirmed local reports; no Burundian official statement found. The drone operator is not named by the source.
claims.researcher_note: Unconfirmed; Burundi government has not, in this source, commented. Article dated 9 July 2026 (Fizi). Same article reports, from the same sources, a boat carrying soldiers bombed on Lake Tanganyika off Ubwari (not claimed here).

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, that new clashes between Wazalendo fighters and AFC-M23 troops broke out on Tuesday 1 September 2026 in the Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga territory, on the road to Kigogo; the sources said the Wazalendo launched the assault first, that heavy artillery was used, and that civilians were reportedly hit by bullets.
claims.place_as_written: Lwindi chiefdom (Kasika, Kalambi, road to Kigogo), Mwenga territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: All three excerpts exact and on the same page; statement matches with conditionals kept.
claims.researcher_note: Local radio, anonymous sources. Follows existing r1-ATR-SK-2026-010 (Kasika held by AFC/M23, Wazalendo at Kalambi, 30 Aug). Same article reports clashes at Kahungu and Mulangala near Kahuzi-Biega (Kalehe/Kabare area, not in this unit).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC said they shot down a kamikaze drone at Ruyengo, Fizi territory, on Thursday 20 August 2026 around 8 a.m.; the report attributed the device to RDF/M23 elements and their allies Twirwaneho/Red-Tabara. The spokesperson of the Sukola 2 operations (south sector, South Kivu), sous-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi, said this came a few hours after the FARDC foiled several rebel attacks on their positions in the Fizi highlands.
claims.place_as_written: Ruyengo, Fizi territory (Fizi highlands), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: RDF/M23 and Twirwaneho/Red-Tabara (as attributed by FARDC); FARDC
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; operation name was shortened wrongly ('Sukola 2 Sud'); page prints 'Sukola 2 Sud-Sud-Kivu'; attribution of the drone kept as the report's. FARDC claim only; no AFC/M23, Rwandan or Twirwaneho reply found.
claims.researcher_note: FARDC claim only; no AFC/M23 or Rwandan reply found. Page names the spokesperson 'sous-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi' (existing claims render the name differently). Names the allied group as 'Red-Tabara' as printed.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that violent clashes broke out from the evening of 26 September 2026 in several villages of the Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, which several local sources placed notably in the Basimukindji 2 groupement at Maheta, Magunda, Nabuhera, Kakuku and Musonjo; a local leader said AFC/M23 fighters sought to advance to Masango before being pushed back, and the article said the clashes caused a massive displacement of the population.
claims.place_as_written: Maheta, Magunda, Nabuhera, Kakuku, Musonjo (Basimukindji 2 / Bijombo), Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Displacement destinations (Basimukindji 1 etc.) and the local sources' attribution of the attack to 'AFC/M23 Twirwaheno' are on the page but not in stored excerpts: narrowed out (leads for add_excerpt). Local, unnamed sources; the attack is attributed to AFC/M23 'Twirwaheno' (spelling as printed) by those sources; no party statement in the article.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates and extends the existing Itombwe youth council claim (24-27 Sept, draft r1/SKC-2026H2#11) with place names and the start (evening of 26 Sept). No named FARDC or AFC/M23 statement in the article.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that local civil society said that on 27 September 2026 the government coalition (FARDC, Wazalendo and Burundian forces) intensified attacks at Rugezi, Gipimo and Kuwihene (Basimunyaka Sud groupement, Lulenge sector); it added that sources close to the FARDC said they shot down a drone at Rugezi, while AFC/M23 'Twirwaheno' sources said they repelled an attack in the area.
claims.place_as_written: Rugezi, Gipimo, Kuwihene (Basimunyaka Sud, Lulenge sector, Minembwe area), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC, Wazalendo and Burundian forces (per local civil society); AFC/M23 Twirwaheno
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact and match the statement clause by clause. The headline says Fizi but the article places Rugezi on the periphery of Minembwe in Mwenga territory. Burundian participation is civil society's claim.
claims.researcher_note: Both sides' accounts are given as unnamed sources. The article headlines Fizi but describes Rugezi as a peripheral village of Minembwe in Mwenga territory; territory field follows the article text. Note the claim of Burundian forces' participation comes from civil society, not from Burundi.

claims.text: MediaCongo reported that UN Secretary-General's spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric on Monday condemned drone attacks reported in Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories, South Kivu, without identifying their authors, and that according to the UN violent clashes since 4 July, including reported drone attacks, had reportedly left at least five dead and dozens wounded among civilians.
claims.place_as_written: Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; kept the conditional ('auraient fait'); removed the 16 and 18 cross-references from figures, which these excerpts do not print. UN figures; they differ from the Fizi administrator's (at least 18 at Mulima) and civil society's; not merged. Original UN transcript not fetched.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('lundi') and publication date 7 July 2026 (Monday 6 July). Relayed by MediaCongo from a UN noon briefing; the original UN transcript was not fetched (look for press.un.org / news.un.org). UN figures differ from local official figures; not merged.

claims.text: MediaCongo reported that Stéphane Dujarric said fighting had disrupted supply routes, causing critical shortages of medical supplies needed to treat the wounded, and that at least 6,000 people had fled to Kipupu and Malanda in Mwenga territory.
claims.place_as_written: Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories; Kipupu and Malanda (Mwenga), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; statement matches. UN figures. A supply-route disruption causing medical shortages, not a reported targeted attack on or denial of health care.
claims.researcher_note: Supply disruption, not a targeted denial of care; categorised access_denied as the closest value. Date computed from weekday and publication date.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Congolese government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, at a press briefing, said of the Hauts-Plateaux that 'le Rwanda excelle avec des tirs de drones à partir de son territoire', calling this once again proof of bad faith in not advancing the peace process, and added that the armed forces were well mobilised. This is the Kinshasa government's accusation.
claims.place_as_written: Hauts-Plateaux of Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC (Patrick Muyaya); Rwanda accused
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; the date ('mardi 7 juillet') is printed only in the page lede, so it is removed from the statement (date field kept). Actualite.cd is an independent outlet reporting a government statement: source_type set to media. Partisan statement (Kinshasa), recorded as what was said; not a finding that Rwanda fired the drones. No Rwandan reply found.
claims.researcher_note: Government statement, cited only for what was said. Rwandan reply not found in this unit (see gaps). The article recalls that Kigali and Kinshasa held a joint oversight committee meeting in London in late June.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing Fizi territory administrator Samy Badibanga, that sixteen fighters of the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN) and their allies surrendered to the FARDC on Tuesday 27 October in the highlands of Fizi territory, South Kivu, and that they had reportedly decided to lay down their arms; the outlet said this information, reported by the administrator, could not be confirmed by independent local sources at the time of publication.
claims.place_as_written: Hauts plateaux, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Page confirms all facts, but the surrender itself rests on the administrator ('Ces informations, rapportées par l'administrateur'); attribution moved to the whole claim and the conditional 'auraient décidé' kept as 'reportedly'. excerpt_en flags are translation artefacts (Armed Forces/DRC/Tuesday). Per the Fizi administrator only; Radio Okapi says it could not be independently confirmed.
claims.researcher_note: Single-source, official claim by Kinshasa-appointed administrator; the outlet states it is unconfirmed. Radio Okapi page is dated 2026-10-28 08:44. Distinct from the 6 Oct Fizi surrender already in the packet (r1-NKS-2026Q4-014).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that Fizi territory administrator Samy Badibanga said the surrenders concerned the zones of Mikenge-Minembwe, Mulima, Rugezi, Bikarakara and Kabandja, and that FRN fighters and their allies kept surrendering to the FARDC for protection, citing Twiraneho, AFC-M23, Red Tabara and FNL Zabampema among the allies.
claims.verification_note: Every clause on the page, attributed to the administrator. Government-side (territorial administration) statement; spellings as printed.
claims.researcher_note: Party (government) account only; place names and group spellings as printed. No FRN/Twirwaneho response found in the page.

claims.text: Kinpressactu.cd reported, citing local sources, violent clashes on Sunday in several villages south of Minembwe in the Fizi highlands between the FARDC supported by Wazalendo fighters and a coalition of Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and AFC/M23.
claims.place_as_written: South of Minembwe, Fizi highlands, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and Wazalendo vs Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Matches page (byline La Rédaction / Assumani Mukendi Abdoul); local-source attribution kept.
claims.researcher_note: Single local-source report; no place names of the individual villages given. Page dated 11 Oct 2026.

claims.text: Kinpressactu.cd reported, citing local sources, that the Sunday clashes south of Minembwe took place amid recurrent use of drones said to strike government-force positions and inhabited areas; it added that accusations of drones attributed to Rwandan forces and of bombardments hitting civilians could not be independently verified for these clashes.

The page gives two dates for the looting: Wednesday 19 August and the night of Monday to Tuesday (17-18 August, given publication on Thursday 20 August). Both are stated; neither is preferred. Perpetrators unidentified.
claims.researcher_note: Page says looting on Wednesday 19 Aug and also 'night of Monday to Tuesday' (possible internal date inconsistency, flagged). Date computed from weekday and publication date.
