claims.text: MediaCongo reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame reminded the African Union facilitators on Wednesday that Rwanda would maintain its posture as long as the root causes of the conflict are not resolved; the outlet wrote that by root causes he mainly alluded to the 'continuing presence' of the FDLR in eastern DRC, and that according to Kagame the FDLR represent a direct and existential security threat.
claims.verification_note: Draft presented the outlet's interpretation ('fait principalement allusion') as Kagame's words; re-attributed. 'génocide' appears only inside the outlet's description of the FDLR and is not used in the statement. The posture and FDLR lines are MediaCongo's paraphrase of Kagame; the Rwandan presidency readout it quotes speaks only of root causes and next steps in the AU-led process. Meeting date (Wednesday 7 October) computed from the weekday and publication on 9 October.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('mercredi') and publication 9 Oct 2026. Rwandan presidency readout quoted by MediaCongo; Kagame's own words on the FDLR are paraphrased by the outlet. Outlet's framing of Kagame as 'designated by the Congolese government as a destabilising actor' is the outlet's characterisation. Meeting: AU facilitators Sahle-Work Zewde, Uhuru Kenyatta, Mokgweetsi Masisi, Yackoley Kokou Johnson.

claims.text: Imvaho Nshya, a Rwandan outlet, reported that AFC/M23 announced it had closed the airspace of Goma in order to stop DRC forces from continuing to use Goma airport to drop bombs on the population.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt (Kinyarwanda) states AFC/M23 announced closing Goma airspace for the stated reason; page dated 26 Jan 2025 and says the M23 statement came out on Sunday. Rwandan state-linked outlet relaying a party statement. excerpt_en flag is a translation artefact (country name rendered in English), not added content. Party statement relayed by a Rwandan state-linked outlet; the DRC conduct alleged is M23's claim, not established.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan state-linked outlet relaying an M23 communiqué dated Sunday 26 January 2025 (page dated 26 Jan). Evidence of what M23 said, not of the DRC conduct alleged. Kinshasa response not found.

claims.text: Al Jazeera reported that M23 announced the capture of Goma on Monday, which the DRC government described as a "declaration of war" by Rwanda.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries both the M23 announcement and the DRC government characterisation as reported by Al Jazeera. The same page separately quotes FM Therese Kayikwamba Wagner at the UNSC on Sunday calling it 'a declaration of war'; the 'described' wording is Al Jazeera's paraphrase.
claims.researcher_note: Records both the M23 claim and the government characterisation, as reported by Al Jazeera; the government characterisation is not a first-hand quote on this page.

claims.text: BBC News reported that Corneille Nangaa, who heads an alliance of rebel groups that includes the M23, said their ultimate aim was to topple President Félix Tshisekedi's government and vowed to continue the offensive to Kinshasa.
claims.verification_note: BBC page (Plett-Usher and Rukanga, 30 Jan 2025) prints both clauses in the excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Page published Thursday 30 January 2025; the statement was made on or shortly before that date.

claims.text: BBC News reported that on Thursday Nangaa presented the rebels as the new administrators of Goma, telling journalists they were there to stay and would get services up and running again.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt matches statement exactly; Thursday = 30 Jan 2025 (page dated Thursday 30 January).
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date (page dated Thursday 30 January 2025).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the M23 installed a new North Kivu provincial administration with Bahati Musanga Joseph alias Erasto, until then adviser to the M23 military coordinator, as governor, assisted by vice-governors Minani Ngarambe Willy and Amani Bahati Shadrack, and that the Alliance Fleuve Congo also announced other appointments including Julien Katembo as mayor of Goma.
claims.verification_note: Page says the M23 installed the new administration (Thursday) and that Bahati Musanga Joseph alias Erasto 'est le nouveau gouverneur'; only the 'other appointments' (including the Goma mayor) are explicitly said to have been announced by the AFC. Narrowed so the governor/vice-governor appointment is not presented as an AFC announcement the page does not state. Spelling of the governor's name differs across outlets: 'Bahati Musanga Joseph alias Erasto' (SOS Médias Burundi), 'Erasto Bahati Musanga' (Al Jazeera), 'Bahati Musanga Erasto' (Radio Elle FM), 'Jean Bahati Musanga' (Actualite.cd, EU sanctions list report, 17 Mar 2025). Date: page (8 Feb) says installed 'jeudi' and sworn in 'vendredi'; photo captions date the Goma stadium presentation 6 February 2025.
claims.researcher_note: The page text names the installation as 'jeudi' and the swearing-in as 'vendredi' (page dated Saturday 8 Feb); a photo caption on the page dates the Goma stadium event 6 February 2025. A different source (Les Souverain Libre / social media) spells the governor 'Bahati Musanga Joseph'; the page also prints 'Bahati Musanga Erasto' elsewhere in other outlets. Another outlet (Radio Elle FM Goma, Nov 2025) prints 'Bahati Musanga Erasto'. Kinshasa's own appointment of a military governor is out of this unit.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the new governor, speaking in Kinyarwanda, said he had identified three main threats to security: former prisoners released by the Congolese authorities as M23 fighters were about to enter Goma, the local militias known as the Wazalendo, and the Hutu FDLR.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts are on the page as one continuous quote; 'S'exprimant en Kinyarwanda' is in the preceding sentence on the page. Characterisations are the speaker's. excerpt_en flags are translation artefacts. Party statement; the labels used for the Wazalendo and FDLR are the speaker's as relayed by the outlet.
claims.researcher_note: Party account only; the characterisations (including 'génocidaires') are the speaker's, relayed by the outlet. Date: event 6 Feb 2025 per photo caption on the page; see previous claim.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Corneille Nangaa, head of the Alliance Fleuve Congo, promised "une administration responsable qui doit rendre des comptes" (a responsible administration that must be accountable).
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and matches statement; party promise relayed by one outlet.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement as relayed by a Burundian exile outlet; see appointments claim for date reasoning.

claims.text: Al Jazeera reported that the AFC/M23 said in a statement posted on X that, in response to the humanitarian crisis it attributed to the regime in Kinshasa, it declared a ceasefire starting 4 February 2025 for humanitarian reasons; Al Jazeera added that there was no immediate comment from the DRC government.
claims.verification_note: Statement text is in the excerpt; the 'no immediate comment' clause is printed on the same page (not in the stored excerpt). Al Jazeera adds the announcement was made late on Monday for a ceasefire from Tuesday.
claims.researcher_note: Announced late Monday 3 Feb for effect from Tuesday 4 Feb. The 'no immediate comment' observation is from an excerpt other than the one quoted; Studio Hirondelle (existing claim NKS-2025Q1#25) and the later Muyaya 'decoy' quote (NKS-2025Q1#26) cover Kinshasa's reaction.

claims.text: Al Jazeera reported that a rebel alliance that includes M23 said, in a statement read on local radio on Monday, that it would assist the population of Bukavu who were "abandoned" by the army and allied combatants, and that its forces had been working to restore security.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries both clauses; party statement read on local radio Monday 17 Feb 2025.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement; the claim of satisfaction among the population is the party's own.

claims.text: Al Jazeera reported that Erasto Bahati Musanga, the rebel-appointed governor of North Kivu, announced that ports in Bukavu and Goma would reopen on Tuesday.
claims.place_as_written: Bukavu and Goma, North and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Statement supported. Date corrected: the claim is an announcement; the page (dated 17 Feb 2025) gives no announcement day, only that ports would reopen 'on Tuesday' (18 Feb). Date set to the page date as the latest possible announcement date. Announcement made on or before 17 Feb 2025 (page date); the reopening was announced for Tuesday 18 Feb.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date (page dated Monday 17 Feb 2025; reopening on Tuesday = 18 Feb). Announcement made on or before 17 Feb.

claims.text: DW reported that, after two explosions at an M23 rally in Bukavu, M23 accused the Congolese authorities of being behind the attack and said in a statement that it condemned "the criminal regime of Kinshasa, which just implemented its plan of exterminating civilian populations".
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries the M23 accusation and quote; 'two explosions' and the figures are printed in the DW page body (headline prints 'at least 11'). DW byline: 'Emmy Sasipornkarn with Reuters, AP, AFP'. Party accusation, not an established finding. Casualty figures are DW's (with wire agencies).
claims.researcher_note: Party accusation, not an established finding. DW credits Reuters, AP and AFP in its byline.

claims.text: DW reported that Congo's president, Felix Tshisekedi, called the Bukavu rally attack "a heinous terrorist act".
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; DW with Reuters, AP, AFP.
claims.researcher_note: Government account of the same event; Reuters (28 Feb) headline says the government and M23 traded blame, but the Reuters page could not be fetched with the helper so it is not cited.

claims.text: The New Times (Rwanda) reported that Bertrand Bisimwa, president of M23, pointed an accusing finger at Burundi after the Bukavu rally explosions and said preliminary investigations indicated that the explosives belonged to the Burundian army.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries both clauses; Rwandan state-aligned outlet (byline Alice Kagina); party allegation. Party allegation; no Burundian response was found by this unit.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan state-aligned outlet; a party allegation. No Burundian response found (see gaps).

claims.text: The New Times reported that, according to the group's leader, the explosives at the AFC/M23 rally in Bukavu on 27 February killed at least 11 people and injured 65, six of them in critical condition.
claims.verification_note: Statement supported by the excerpt. Figures field corrected: it cited DW, which is not a source of this claim; figures now only as The New Times attributes them to the group's leader (the page goes on to say Nangaa gave them at a press conference).
claims.researcher_note: Figures attributed by the outlet to the group's leader (the page names Nangaa as having given a press conference); the two blast casualty figures match DW's.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, in a communiqué published on Monday, AFC/M23 announced it would not take part in the Luanda talks planned for Tuesday 18 March under Angolan mediation, denouncing individual European Union sanctions on several of its leaders.
claims.place_as_written: Luanda (Angola); statement concerns North and South Kivu conflict
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and supports statement; excerpt_en flag is translation artefact (weekday/EU names).
claims.researcher_note: Geography: statement about a process concerning the Kivus; location outside phase-1 area kept as statement-only.

claims.text: Anadolu reported that the Alliance Fleuve Congo, a rebel alliance that includes M23, announced on Saturday that it was withdrawing from the town of Walikale and its surroundings, a few days after taking control of the area; Anadolu said residents saw rebel elements still in the town that afternoon.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the Anadolu page (byline James Tasamba, Kigali, 22 Mar 2025); Anadolu says the announcement was a communiqué by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka on X. Day of the communiqué differs: Anadolu and Kivu Morning Post say Saturday (22 Mar); Kanyuka's later post refers to 'the communiqué of Sunday 23 March 2025'.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday (page dated 22 March 2025, Saturday). A Kivu Morning Post page refers to a 'communiqué du dimanche 23 mars 2025'; the two outlets differ on the communiqué's day.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Lawrence Kanyuka, spokesperson of AFC-M23, said on X that, contrary to the communiqué of Sunday 23 March 2025, the FARDC and their coalition forces had not withdrawn their attack drones from Walikale, delaying the repositioning of AFC/M23 forces.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries the quote; 'delaying the repositioning' is the next sentence of the same quote on the page, and the page says Kanyuka said it on X on Monday 24 March 2025. Goma-based outlet ('La Rédaction').
claims.researcher_note: Party statement. The same outlet reports M23 residents' accounts that M23 had not left; see next claim for the FARDC response.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the FARDC took note of the announced M23 withdrawal from Walikale and committed to avoiding any offensive action, calling on the Wazalendo to do the same.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. The '23' flag is from 'M23' (false positive). The outlet narrates the FARDC position without a named spokesperson, channel or date; date field is the page date. The FARDC position is the outlet's narration; no FARDC spokesperson, channel or date is given on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Counterpart account; the page does not give the date or channel of the FARDC statement and does not name a spokesperson.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 announced the break of its agreement with the SADC after violent clashes in Goma, accusing SAMIDRC regional forces, in coordination with the FARDC, of military operations including attacks on the night of 11 April 2025.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact and support the statement. Date discrepancy kept visible: the page prints 'vendredi 12 avril 2025', but 12 April 2025 was a Saturday. Source date inconsistency: 'vendredi 12 avril 2025' (12 April 2025 was a Saturday). Party accusation.
claims.researcher_note: DISCREPANCY: the page says 'vendredi 12 avril 2025' but 12 April 2025 was a Saturday; date kept as 12 April as printed. Party account of an incident; no SADC/SAMIDRC or FARDC response found in this search.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the DRC government delegates and the AFC/M23 rebellion, after talks in Doha under Qatari auspices, agreed to work towards a truce in view of an effective ceasefire, in a joint declaration made public on Wednesday 23 April 2025 and read on RTNC.
claims.place_as_written: Doha (Qatar); concerns North and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt 0 carries the agreement; the 'joint declaration made public on Wednesday 23 April 2025 and read on RTNC' clause is printed on the same page.
claims.researcher_note: Page printed 'Porte-parole civile' as written. Statement is bilateral; each side's own account of it is not separately recorded here.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23, led by Corneille Nangaa, said on Monday it took note of the agreement signed in Washington on 27 June between the DRC and Rwanda while expressing strong reservations and reaffirming demands for a more inclusive peace process.
claims.place_as_written: Place of statement not stated (concerns North and South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Statement supported by excerpt. Location corrected: the page does not say where Nangaa made the statement (it calls it a message published on DRC independence day).
claims.researcher_note: Party position; place where Nangaa made the statement is not stated on the page.

claims.text: KT Press (Rwanda) reported that Corneille Nangaa, political coordinator of AFC-M23, announced that the movement regretted the widespread violation of the ceasefire on all front lines by what he called the regime in Kinshasa, which he said trampled point II of the Declaration of Principles signed in Doha on 19 July 2025.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries the quote (byline Vincent Gasana); page says the conference was held in Goma on Monday with Nangaa and Bisimwa presiding. '23' flag is from 'M23' (false positive). Party accusation relayed by a Rwanda-based outlet.
claims.researcher_note: Rwanda-based outlet; page dated 2 Sep 2025 and refers to a conference 'held in Goma on Monday' (Monday = 1 Sep 2025, computed from weekday). Party accusation, not an established fact. The page says Nangaa and Bisimwa jointly presided.

claims.text: KT Press reported that, in a formal statement before the Q&A at a Goma media briefing, Nangaa accused Tshisekedi of tearing up the Doha peace agreement signed in July 2025 and of choosing war over dialogue, and said Kinshasa's coalition forces had launched fresh offensives across eastern Congo in violation of the ceasefire.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries both clauses; page places the briefing in Goma; caption says 'speaking on Monday'. Party accusation relayed by a Rwanda-based outlet.
claims.researcher_note: Same briefing as the previous claim, separate article. Date computed: page dated 2 Sep 2025, photo caption says 'speaking on Monday'. The page also quotes Nangaa alleging that over 30,000 men and combat aircraft and drones were used by Kinshasa's coalition; that is a party figure and is not repeated as fact.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Congolese government and the AFC-M23 rebels signed on Tuesday 14 October 2025 in Doha, under Qatari mediation, a mechanism to monitor and verify the ceasefire in the provinces of North and South Kivu.
claims.place_as_written: Doha (Qatar); applies to North Kivu and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; Radio Okapi, 14 Oct 2025. Page adds that actors and modalities of implementation were not yet revealed.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi (UN-founded, Congolese). The page says the actors and modalities of implementation had not yet been revealed.

claims.text: KT Press reported that AFC/M23 rejected French President Emmanuel Macron's announcement of the planned reopening of Goma International Airport, calling it "premature, disconnected from reality, and made without consultation", in a statement issued by Corneille Nangaa.
claims.verification_note: Narrowed attribution: the excerpt has the group (AFC/M23) calling the decision 'premature, disconnected from reality, and made without consultation'; the page says this came in a statement issued by Corneille Nangaa (next sentence), not that Nangaa used that exact phrase. Statement date not printed; page dated 31 Oct 2025 and says Macron's announcement was on Thursday 30 October.
claims.researcher_note: Rwanda-based outlet; date is the report date (31 Oct 2025); Macron's announcement is stated to have been on Thursday 30 October. Statement date itself is not printed. The page also says AFC/M23 accused government forces of drone strikes and of the destruction of humanitarian planes; those are party allegations not repeated here.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 announced in a communiqué that it would unilaterally withdraw its forces from the city of Uvira, presenting the decision as a confidence-building measure to support the Doha peace process; it said the withdrawal was conditional on security guarantees including demilitarisation, protection of civilians and deployment of a neutral force. BBC Gahuza reported Nangaa said M23 would withdraw at the request of United States mediation.
claims.verification_note: Actualite.cd (Clément Muamba) and BBC Gahuza (Didier Bikorimana) independently report the announcement; Actualite.cd also prints the communiqué's 'comme demandé par la médiation des États-Unis'. Date discrepancy kept: Actualite.cd says 'ce mardi'; BBC Gahuza says a Monday statement announced Tuesday morning; date field 15 Dec (statement day per BBC Gahuza). Statement of intent, not evidence the withdrawal occurred. Day discrepancy: Monday 15 Dec (BBC Gahuza: statement of Monday, released Tuesday morning) vs 'ce mardi' (Actualite.cd).
claims.researcher_note: DATE DISCREPANCY: Actualite.cd (posted 00:14 on 16 Dec) says 'ce mardi'; BBC Gahuza says the statement was of Monday and announced Tuesday morning; TRT Afrika (citing Reuters) says Nangaa posted on X on Monday (15 Dec). The date field uses 15 Dec; reconcile at verification. Party statement of intent, not evidence that the withdrawal occurred.

claims.text: TRT Afrika, relaying Reuters, reported that M23 spokesperson Willy Ngoma told Reuters on Wednesday that "we are ready to leave (Uvira), but our conditions have to be reviewed", adding that the citizens of Uvira needed protecting and that the city should be occupied by a neutral force; residents told Reuters the rebels had not withdrawn.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries the Ngoma quote; the residents clause is in the page's lede. TRT Afrika page ends 'SOURCE : Reuters'.
claims.researcher_note: TRT Afrika republishes Reuters reporting; the original Reuters piece was not fetched. Date computed: page published Wednesday 17 Dec 2025.

claims.text: BBC News reported that M23 leader Bertrand Bisimwa said on Wednesday that the withdrawal from Uvira was "under way", with spokesman Willy Ngoma adding that this was "for the sake of peace", and that Bisimwa in a post on X urged mediators and international partners to ensure the city was protected from "reprisals, violence and remilitarisation".
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries all clauses; BBC (Rukanga and Makumeno), 18 Dec 2025; Wednesday = 17 Dec. The same page reports Uvira residents telling the BBC on Thursday it was not clear the M23 were leaving.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date 18 Dec 2025. Same page reports Uvira residents telling the BBC on Thursday that it was not clear M23 were leaving; that is not part of this statement claim.

claims.text: TRT Afrika, relaying Reuters, reported that DRC Communications Minister Patrick Muyaya dismissed the announced M23 withdrawal from Uvira as a "diversion", alleging it was an attempt to relieve pressure on Rwanda; the page also says Rwanda's government spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the TRT Afrika page ('SOURCE : Reuters'). '23' flag is from 'M23' (false positive). Rwanda's 'did not immediately respond' is not a finding that Rwanda said nothing.
claims.researcher_note: Government account; Rwanda's silence is only 'did not immediately respond', which is not a finding that Rwanda said nothing.

claims.text: BBC News reported that Muyaya described the M23's decision to leave Uvira as a "positive sign" but said the government needed to confirm the situation on the ground, having earlier called for "vigilance" in response to the "alleged withdrawal".
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries both clauses; statement day not printed (date is the page date). The same BBC page also reports DR Congo's government calling the reported withdrawal a 'diversion'.
claims.researcher_note: Date is the page's date; the statement's exact day is not printed. Compare the same speaker's 'diversion' remark to Reuters on 17 Dec.

claims.text: Radio Elle FM Goma reported that the de facto governor of North Kivu, Bahati Musanga Erasto, launched a large reforestation operation in Goma on a Salongo day, saying "Nous avons trouvé une ville et un parc dévastés"; in the same report the outlet wrote that disorderly felling of trees by armed groups such as the FDLR and Mai-Mai militias had profoundly affected biodiversity.
claims.verification_note: The tree-felling attribution is not clearly the governor's: on the page it follows 'Selon lui...' as the outlet's own sentence. Narrowed to keep that as the outlet's wording. Governor title and Salongo launch are printed on the page; title prints 'Le Gouverneur Bahati Musanga Erasto'. '23' flag is from 'M23'. Local outlet operating in M23-controlled Goma. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Elle FM (8 Nov 2025, byline Grace Wasingya Nestor) supports every clause; the stored excerpts carry only the quote and the FDLR/Mai-Mai sentence, so the launch passage is added. The FDLR sentence directly follows 'Selon lui' (according to him) and may be the governor's view paraphrased; the statement's 'the outlet wrote' is literal to the page.
claims.researcher_note: Local outlet operating under M23-controlled Goma; the page is dated 8 Nov 2025 and the event is described as taking place 'ce samedi' (8 Nov 2025 was a Saturday). Attribution of tree felling to armed groups is the governor's/outlet's wording on the page, not independently verified.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa said in a recent statement that 'À ce jour, pas un seul prisonnier n’a été libéré, en violation flagrante des accords signés', accusing the Kinshasa government of blocking implementation of the Doha commitments.
claims.verification_note: Page confirms quote and accusation; '23' flag is from 'AFC/M23'. Party statement, cited only for what was said. The page says 'déclaration récente'; the date is the publication date.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement; cited only for what the party said. The article says 'déclaration récente'; date taken from publication date (jeu 01/01/2026). Kinshasa's position on prisoner releases not located in this unit.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Corneille Nangaa said that in the zones controlled by the AFC/M23 'la population vit désormais dans la paix, la dignité et la sécurité retrouvées', and accused the central government of promoting hate speech, saying 'Le discours de haine est désormais devenu une doctrine d’État'.
claims.place_as_written: AFC/M23-controlled areas, North and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Both passages on page; same article. Party claim about conditions in its own zones; not evidence of those conditions. Made in Nangaa's end-of-2025 address to the nation. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Party claim about conditions in its zones, not evidence of those conditions; contrast UN/HRW claims recorded by other units. Kivu Morning Post is Goma-based.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that in a statement posted on X on 3 February, Corneille Nangaa presented as a response to what he called an indiscriminate military campaign by the central government the AFC/M23's claimed operation against what it described as the Congolese army's drone command centre in Kisangani (Tshopo).
claims.place_as_written: Kisangani, Tshopo (claimed target); statement on Minembwe and Hauts-Plateaux, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Supported verbatim. Claim of responsibility is the party's own. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Claim of responsibility is the party's own. Kinshasa/Tshopo side recorded in the next claim. Elsewhere than the Kivus, kept as a statement about this conflict.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Tshopo provincial authorities and the FARDC announced they had neutralised eight explosive-laden kamikaze drones in the night of 31 January to 1 February 2026, and that the Tshopo authorities accused the AFC/M23 of trying to target Bangoka airport.
claims.verification_note: Supported; grade lowered B->C: one local outlet relaying a party (government) statement. Meeting dates (13-17 April) are on the page outside the stored excerpt. Commitments are the signatories' own words, not evidence of implementation.

claims.text: UN News reported that MONUSCO head James Swan told the Security Council that the security situation in the east remained highly unstable, with heavy fighting between AFC/M23, supported by Rwandan forces (as UN News wrote), and the FARDC allied with Wazalendo, and that clashes were mainly in Rubaya and around Rutshuru in North Kivu and in the high plains of South Kivu.
claims.verification_note: Page supports each clause; the 'supported by Rwandan forces' wording is flagged as UN News's. Briefing date not printed; article dated 26 June 2026.
claims.researcher_note: The 'supported by Rwandan forces' phrasing is UN News's paraphrase of the briefing. Briefing date from article date 26 Jun 2026 (Swan briefed the Council that week).

claims.text: UN News reported that Swan said the use of offensive drones, artillery and heavy weapons had sharply increased risks to civilians and infrastructure, that AFC/M23 had partially withdrawn from some areas but continued to consolidate parallel administrative structures, and called for swift deployment of the ceasefire monitoring mechanism under the Doha process.
claims.verification_note: All three clauses on the page; two only on the page, supplied as quotes.
claims.researcher_note: Single UN-sourced article (UN News is the UN's own outlet).

claims.text: A joint statement by the governments taking part in the Sixth Joint Oversight Committee for the Peace Agreement between the DRC and Rwanda, published by the US State Department, said that the DRC updated on its work to neutralize the FDLR and Rwanda updated on the process of its disengagement of forces/lifting of defensive measures.

claims.verification_note: Credited to all the governments that released it (page: 'released by the Governments of the United States of America, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Republic of Rwanda, the State of Qatar, the Republic of Togo ... and the African Union Commission'); the meeting was held on 24 June 2026 in London per the page. Progress claims are the signatories' own, not verified.
claims.researcher_note: Joint statement; claims of progress are the parties' own, not verified. Page also records the JOC concern over escalating fighting and drone strikes and the Ebola outbreak.

claims.text: A joint statement by the representatives of the DRC Government and of the AFC, published by the US State Department after meetings in Switzerland, said the Parties developed a roadmap setting out sequenced steps and timelines for negotiations under the Doha Framework Agreement and agreed on the importance of a standardized method for reporting allegations of ceasefire violations.
claims.actor_as_written: Joint: DRC Government and AFC/M23 representatives, released with Qatar, US, Togo (AU mediator), Switzerland, AU Commission
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date (shown with the source); credited the statement's authors; added the clause carried by source 1. Page gives meetings August 17-21.
claims.researcher_note: URL as returned by search (path ends 'doha-proce', truncated by the search display; fetch succeeded). Page also mentions a reconnaissance mission on 20 August ahead of the first EJVM+ verification mission scheduled for 24 August in Minembwe.

claims.text: A joint statement by the governments taking part in the sixth Joint Security Coordination Mechanism meeting in Geneva (DRC, Rwanda, US, Qatar, Togo as AU mediator, AU Commission), published by the US State Department, said the DRC and Rwanda agreed to advance two initiatives to strengthen monitoring and verification of Washington Accords implementation on the ground.
claims.actor_as_written: Joint: Governments of the US, DRC, Rwanda, Qatar, Togo (AU mediator), AU Commission
claims.verification_note: Credited all authors; the page itself gives the meeting dates (12-13 August), so the date is a range, not approximate.
claims.researcher_note: Meeting date: page published 13 Aug 2026; lead US post says representatives met 12-13 August. Date precision approximate.

claims.text: UN News reported, in its own account around a Security Council meeting, that fighting continued in the highlands of Mwenga, Fizi and Uvira in South Kivu, causing new displacement and hindering aid delivery, and that the first two missions of the ceasefire verification mechanism had gone to Minembwe (South Kivu) and then Masisi (North Kivu).
claims.actor_as_written: UN News (its own reporting of the Security Council meeting)

claims.researcher_note: Descriptive lines are UN News's own reporting around Swan's briefing, not direct quotes of Swan.

claims.text: UN News reported that Néné Bintu Iragi, president of South Kivu civil society, told the Security Council that in territories controlled by AFC/M23 there were killings, arson, arbitrary detentions and 'collective punishments' and a parallel administration imposing taxes on the population.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (as alleged by Néné Bintu Iragi)
claims.verification_note: Page supports name, role and allegation. Allegation by a civil-society leader; no specific incidents named; no AFC/M23 reply on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Allegation by a civil-society leader, relayed by UN News; no AFC/M23 reply found in this page. Not a party statement; a mediator/UN-forum statement. No specific incidents named.

claims.text: UN News reported, in its account of an address by Deputy High Commissioner for Human Rights Awa Dabo to the UN Human Rights Council, that OHCHR documented at least 1.080 victims of conflict-related sexual violence across the country (a national figure) between June 2025 and May 2026, mainly women and children, that the real figures are probably much higher, and that armed groups were reportedly responsible for 74% of the victims recorded.
claims.verification_note: The excerpt alone does not say 'conflict-related sexual violence'; the page's preceding sentence does, supplied as quote; national scope made explicit; 'probably much higher' caveat added. National figure for the whole DRC, not specific to North or South Kivu. Dialogue date not printed; article dated 2 October 2026.
claims.researcher_note: UN News heading places the dialogue at the Human Rights Council; the 2 Oct date is the article's. Figures nationwide, not Kivu-only; OHCHR said real figures are probably much higher. Sexual-violence figure is national; separate from the 9 Mar 2026 UNJHRO report claim already held.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye, according to the outlet, said that a momentum had been interrupted because of Rwanda's expansionist aims expressed through the AFC/M23 rebellion in South Kivu, and the outlet added that he alluded to the rebels' occupation of Uvira and their announced withdrawal under US pressure, a withdrawal the outlet said Kinshasa disputed.
claims.verification_note: Date corrected from the article date to the speech date the page prints (outside the stored excerpt); weekday mismatch flagged. Per the article, the speech was given at the New Year exchange of wishes with the diplomatic corps in Burundi on 'jeudi 14 janvier 2026'; 14 January 2026 fell on a Wednesday, so the date is approximate. The Uvira passage is the outlet's paraphrase, not a quote.
claims.researcher_note: Burundi government position; Rwanda's response not found here. Statement date approximate (article 17 Jan 2026; the speech date is not given in the excerpt). Ndayishimiye assumed the AU chair in Feb 2026 per other pages. The 'withdrawal disputed by Kinshasa' is the outlet's wording.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, despite the ceasefire announced for 18 February at noon, clashes continued in eastern DRC between the FARDC and AFC/M23; it said the truce had been proposed on 11 February by Angola after a meeting in Luanda, and that the DRC officially adhered to it while AFC/M23 had committed to an immediate halt to hostilities under the Doha process.
claims.place_as_written: Masisi and Rutshuru territories, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC; AFC/M23; Wazalendo (PARECO) as named by the outlet

The page also reports fighting in Fizi (South Kivu) around 'Point Zéro' and in Masisi and Rutshuru. 2026-10-28: source 2 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 20 Feb 2026, carries every clause; the stored excerpt for the adherence clause omits its first half ('Si la RDC a officiellement adhéré ...'), so the full sentence is added.
claims.researcher_note: Local reporting (Radio Okapi, Kinshasa/Goma) on the 18 Feb ceasefire after the Angolan proposal; complements the Actualite.cd claims. Fighting localities named in the page: Mitimingi, Kaunda, Mbiso (Masisi).

claims.text: Reuters reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame said he agreed with the U.S. government on the need for a ceasefire in eastern Congo but gave no indication of bowing to calls for Rwandan troops and M23 rebels to withdraw from Goma.
claims.verification_note: Reuters copy on VOA (byline By Reuters); excerpt carries the statement verbatim.
claims.researcher_note: Reuters copy on VOA. Kagame posted on X per the same page; the post URL is a lead only.

claims.text: CNN reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame, asked in an interview whether there were Rwandan troops inside the DRC, answered 'I don't know' and said Rwanda would do anything to protect itself.
claims.verification_note: CNN exclusive interview; both clauses on page; second clause is on the page, not in the stored excerpt. Kagame's full answer: "is there a problem in Congo that concerns Rwanda? And that Rwanda would do anything to protect itself? I'd say 100%".
claims.researcher_note: Interview on Monday; CNN article published 2025-02-03, so the date is the publication date and Monday is 3 February.

claims.text: Al Jazeera reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame, at a news conference in Kigali, said that the FDLR's presence in the DRC is Rwanda's main concern and that 'if this problem is not resolved, it is natural for Rwanda to remain involved' in the conflict; Al Jazeera added that Rwanda denies Kinshasa's allegations against it.
claims.verification_note: Draft said Rwanda denies 'allegations of sending troops'; Al Jazeera's denial sentence covers both the M23-support and troop allegations, and is Al Jazeera's narration, not a quoted Rwandan statement. Kagame is named on page. Al Jazeera's denial sentence follows its statement that Kinshasa accuses Kigali of supporting the M23 and of sending Rwandan troops into Congolese territory; it is Al Jazeera's narration, not a quoted Rwandan statement.
claims.researcher_note: Date is Al Jazeera's publication date; the conference date was not given in the excerpt.

claims.text: Al Jazeera reported that Kagame said Rwanda has information that Congolese authorities 'are arming the FDLR and integrating its members into their own forces'.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim; attribution kept. Rwandan allegation against Kinshasa, attributed; Kagame said the evidence includes testimony from former FDLR members.
claims.researcher_note: Counter-claim against Kinshasa; Kinshasa's account of the same issue to be found in the DRC statements units.

claims.text: The Government of Rwanda said in a statement that responsibility for ceasefire violations, ongoing attacks and fighting in South Kivu cannot be placed on Rwanda, and condemned the FARDC and the Burundian army (FDNB), together with the FDLR, Wazalendo and foreign mercenaries, which it said have been systematically bombing civilian villages close to the Rwandan border using fighter jets and attack drones.
claims.place_as_written: South Kivu, near the Rwandan border
claims.verification_note: Bombing clause was on the page, not in the excerpt (clause_support maps it); dateline moved to the note since the excerpt does not print it. Party statement, dated 'Kigali, 10 December 2025' on the page. The ministry's own wording is 'DRC-backed FDLR genocidal militias'. It adds that AFC/M23 'has said it has been forced to counter' the bombing.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement. Contested event: Kinshasa and Burundi accounts of the December 2025 Uvira fighting are for other units.

claims.text: The Government of Rwanda said in its statement on ceasefire violations that, as a result of the past week's bombing of Kamanyola from Burundi, over 1000 Congolese citizens had fled across the border to Bugarama in western Rwanda, where they were accommodated at the Nyarushishi Transit Camp.
claims.place_as_written: Kamanyola, Walungu/Uvira area; Bugarama and Nyarushishi, Rwanda
claims.verification_note: Removed the '10 December 2025' date from the statement (not in the excerpt; the claim date and source date carry it). Content is Rwanda's allegation only; no independent confirmation in this unit. Rwandan government allegation; not independently confirmed.

claims.text: The Government of Rwanda said in its statement on ceasefire violations that the Burundian Army had amassed close to 20,000 troops in South Kivu in the service of the Government of DRC and had laid siege to Banyamulenge villages in Minembwe in a deliberate attempt to starve the residents.
claims.verification_note: Removed the '10 December 2025' date from the statement (not in the excerpt; the claim date and source date carry it). Content is Rwanda's allegation only; no independent confirmation in this unit. Rwandan government allegation; not independently confirmed.

claims.verification_note: FDLR clause is on the page, not in the excerpt (clause_support maps it). Date removed from statement text. Rwanda's characterisation of Kinshasa's position; no Congolese statement to that effect is cited here.
claims.researcher_note: Excerpt covers the first clause (DRC would not observe ceasefire); the FDLR sentence is in the same page but not in this excerpt.

claims.text: Jeune Afrique published an interview with Rwandan President Paul Kagame under the headline quote 'N’attendez pas de moi que je lève nos mesures de défense alors que vous laissez Félix Tshisekedi faire ce qu’il veut' (Do not expect me to lift our defence measures while you let Félix Tshisekedi do what he wants).

claims.text: Kigali Today (Rwandan outlet) reported that Minister Nduhungirehe, answering an RFI journalist, said 'Nta munsi n’umwe utambuka hatabayeho ibitero byo mu kirere bigabwe na Guverinoma ya Congo, ku birindiro bya AFC/M23' (not a day passes without air attacks by the Congolese Government on AFC/M23 positions), which he called a violation of the ceasefire agreements.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim on page; excerpt_en flag is the capitalised 'Government' for 'Guverinoma', a correct translation. Rwandan outlet relaying an RFI interview (journalist David Baché); party statement only. The excerpt_en is an accurate translation (Guverinoma = Government).

claims.text: Taarifa (Rwandan outlet), in an article on remarks by Nduhungirehe, wrote that following the capture of Uvira by the M23 on 10 December 2025 (Taarifa's date), Rwandan and Burundian security officials held meetings at the shared border on 14 and 28 December to discuss confidence-building measures and de-escalation mechanisms; Taarifa narrates this sentence itself and attributes the surrounding remarks to Nduhungirehe.

Taarifa relays a Jeune Afrique interview, set as originating source. The 10 December Uvira capture date is Taarifa's alone and is narrated by Taarifa, not attributed to the minister; other sources give other dates. Taarifa relays an interview Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe gave to Jeune Afrique, and quotes him next: 'These contacts were aimed at calming tensions and avoiding further deterioration'.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan state-aligned outlet; the 10 December capture date is Taarifa's wording and other sources give other dates for the capture (to be reconciled by the Uvira unit). The excerpt does not itself carry the 'Nduhungirehe said' attribution: the page attributes the paragraph to him in the following sentence and the sentence before.

claims.text: The New Times (Rwandan state-aligned outlet) reported that President Kagame told EAC and SADC leaders that the ongoing war in eastern DR Congo was started by the Congolese government.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim; partisan outlet cited only for what Kagame said. Party statement via Rwandan state-aligned outlet; the page places it at the joint EAC-SADC summit in Dar es Salaam on 8 February 2025 and adds Kagame's words "and not anything from Rwanda".
claims.researcher_note: Party statement; date from listing (8 Feb 2025), summit date not in excerpt.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that accusations of Rwandan involvement in the conflict in eastern DRC, supported by several international reports including those of the UN Group of Experts, are ones that Kigali continues to reject.

Actualite.cd's own characterisation in an article on an HRW report; not a quoted Rwandan statement and not a reply to the HRW report.
claims.researcher_note: General rejection, not a specific reply to the HRW January 2026 sexual-violence report; no direct Rwandan reply to that report found.

claims.text: The BBC reported, citing an internal UN document it had seen, that between 165 and 167 women were assaulted by male inmates during the jailbreak at Munzenze prison in Goma, and that the report states most of the women were killed after inmates set fire to the prison; the BBC said it could not verify the reports.

claims.actor_as_written: male inmates, as reported by an internal UN document seen by the BBC

Figures differ across sources: 165-167 (internal UN document via BBC), at least 165 (UN rights chief citing judicial authorities), 160 female inmates (OHCHR FFM), 'a few hundred' (MONUSCO deputy head). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one

claims.actor_as_written: not identified (per the Guardian, identity of perpetrators unclear); account of MONUSCO deputy head Van de Perre

Speaker's full name on the page: Vivian van de Perre, deputy head of the UN peacekeeping force (MONUSCO) based in Goma. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-001: The clause 'the Guardian said the identity of the perpetrators remained unclear' has no excerpt in the input. 'A few hundred women' is out of line with 160-167 elsewhere; it stays as the speaker's figure.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; the quote is in source 0 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: UN official named by the Guardian only as Van de Perre (deputy head of UN peacekeeping per page); figure 'a few hundred' differs from BBC/OHCHR figures; shown separately.

claims.text: UN News reported that the UN human rights chief said that according to judicial authorities at least 165 women prisoners were raped during the mass escape from Muzenze prison in Goma on 27 January, and that most of them were reportedly killed afterwards in a fire whose circumstances remain unclear.
claims.place_as_written: Munzenze Central Prison, Goma (gereza ya Munzenze), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (prisoners escaping)
claims.verification_note: Speaker named from page; grade lowered A->B: a statement relaying judicial authorities, not a documented UN investigation. 'auraient été tuées' is conditional (reportedly). Origin is judicial authorities as cited by Türk; no perpetrator named in this passage. The page names the human rights chief as Volker Türk. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Excerpt kept as one passage; Turk quoted by UN News.

claims.text: The OHCHR summary report of the fact-finding mission on North and South Kivu included satellite imagery of Munzenze Central Prison, Goma, captioned as showing its condition after a prison break and fire which killed the majority of the prison's 160 female inmates on 27 January 2025.
claims.place_as_written: Munzenze Central Prison, Goma (gereza ya Munzenze), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Body is the OHCHR FFM (mandated by HRC resolution S-37/1), not an HRC mission; wording narrowed to the caption. FFM's figure (160 female inmates) differs from 165-167 (internal UN document via BBC) and 'a few hundred' (MONUSCO deputy head). Caption attributes no perpetrator.
claims.researcher_note: Figure of 160 female inmates differs from 165-167 women assaulted (BBC/UN News); kept separate. Caption does not mention sexual violence; the summary map text on the same page says 'mass prison break at Munzenze (a larger number inmates), including sexual violence'.

claims.text: BBC Gahuza reported that Délion Kimbulungu, secretary of AFC/M23, presenting a report of AFC/M23, said the events at Munzenze prison happened in the morning while M23 arrived in the evening, and that their investigation found the prison escape had begun a few days before M23 arrived; the BBC said it could not independently verify the claims of M23.
claims.place_as_written: Munzenze Central Prison, Goma (gereza ya Munzenze), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Role and BBC's non-verification added from page. Publisher BBC is media; the content is the partisan account, kept as attributed. Party X says: AFC/M23 account, made 30 May 2025 (BBC Gahuza, Kinyarwanda). Translation: 'umunyamabanga' = secretary. The page's headline differs from the recorded title (current headline: 'DR Congo: M23 yahakanye ibirego bya leta birimo ko i Goma hapfuye abantu 3,000').
claims.researcher_note: Party account relayed by BBC; cite only for what AFC/M23 said. Kimbulungu is described on the page as AFC/M23 secretary. Date 30 May 2025 is the page publication date (Ukwa gatanu 30).

claims.text: BBC Gahuza reported that the Kinshasa side said the M23 group had a role in what it called the 'amahano kuri gereza ya Munzenze' (the horror at Munzenze prison).

claims.researcher_note: Government speaker not named by the source; the BBC does not give the date or channel of the statement. Date is the page date.

claims.text: OHCHR's Fact-Finding Mission reported a pattern of widespread rape and other sexual violence, primarily against women and girls but also men, boys and LGBT individuals, by M23 during cordon-and-search operations, house-to-house searches and in detention, and by FARDC and Wazalendo during their retreat from the frontlines in January and February.

Report A/HRC/60/80 is the report of the OHCHR Fact-Finding Mission, submitted to the Human Rights Council. 2026-10-28: source 0 publisher edited: fact-check fc1: A/HRC/60/80 (advance unedited, 5 September 2025), para. 49, carries the passage verbatim. The page titles itself the report of the OHCHR Fact-Finding Mission, established by the High Commissioner at the Council's request and submitted to the Council, so 'Human Rights Council fact-finding mission' is corrected to the OHCHR mission.
