claims.text: BCNUDH reported that in January 2026 it documented at least 46 cases of conflict-related sexual violence affecting 61 victims (39 women, 21 girls and one man), 59 per cent fewer than the 147 victims documented in December 2025, which it explained mainly by intensified fighting and insecurity that limited humanitarian access to victims and led to under-documentation.
claims.actor_as_written: M23, Nyatura, Raïa Mutomboki, ADF, FARDC, PNC (per BCNUDH)
claims.territory: conflict-affected provinces (North Kivu 54%, South Kivu 36%, Ituri 10% of victims)
claims.verification_note: Matches the January 2026 BCNUDH report. Sources 2-3 (perpetrator breakdown) support the actor field.
claims.researcher_note: UN body monthly report (published later, April 2026 on the MONUSCO site; date is the report period end). The apostrophes in the second excerpt are straight quotes in the source text.

claims.text: ReliefWeb, republishing a MONUSCO item, reported that BCNUDH said in a press release that 887 cases of conflict-related sexual violence were documented last year, affecting 1 534 victims (854 women and 672 girls), that North and South Kivu concentrate nearly 80 per cent of documented victims, that armed groups are responsible for 75 per cent of victims, with M23 first with 439 victims, and that FARDC, PNC and ANR members were involved in 19 per cent of documented cases.
claims.place_as_written: Eastern DRC (North Kivu and South Kivu concentrate about 80% of documented victims)
claims.actor_as_written: armed groups (M23 first), FARDC, PNC and ANR, per BCNUDH
claims.territory: North Kivu and South Kivu (about 80% of victims)
claims.verification_note: Matches the ReliefWeb copy of the MONUSCO item; arithmetic gap surfaced. Figures cover calendar year 2025, nationwide. As printed, 854 women and 672 girls add up to 1,526, not 1,534 (the remainder is not broken down).
claims.researcher_note: Covers calendar year 2025 and the whole country (about 80% in the Kivus); statement date is the release date. Source is ReliefWeb relaying MONUSCO/BCNUDH.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts on the DRC reported in its final report that AFC/M23 was the leading perpetrator of conflict-related sexual violence according to cases documented and verified by the United Nations, and that humanitarian actors recorded a dramatic increase in such cases since 2024, disproportionately affecting women and girls.
claims.place_as_written: Eastern DRC (North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri)
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23, per UN Group of Experts
claims.verification_note: Verbatim in S/2026/466 para. 11.
claims.researcher_note: Report S/2026/466 dated 5 June 2026 (circulated 11 June). Reporting period is 2025; recorded here as the 2026 publication. Claim is general, not Kivu-only.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that it reviewed a document dated 11 February 2026, entitled "Note Explicative", that AFC/M23 distributed to multiple humanitarian actors involved in health care; that following its distribution the AFC/M23-run Provincial Health Inspection Department (IPS) initiated a series of inspections of humanitarian actors' premises; that IPS inspectors requested aggregate data on sexual violence incidents, access to confidential patient files containing names of victims, and consumption records for supplies such as PEP kits and dignity kits; and that some humanitarian actors were ordered to cease distributing dignity kits.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu (AFC/M23-run provincial health department, Goma)
claims.verification_note: The deterrence clause and the 'Note Explicative' title were not in the stored excerpts: the title is on the page in the sentence after the excerpt (clause_support) and the deterrence point is in the note only. Verbs aligned with the source ('initiated a series of inspections'). The Group based this on confidential sources and a document it reviewed. It separately notes (para. 8) that AFC/M23's actions may deter victims of sexual violence from accessing humanitarian assistance.
claims.researcher_note: Group of Experts annex relying on confidential sources and a document it reviewed. Related: late-March and April 2026 meetings agreed that only aggregate data would be shared (see next claim). The Group's own assessment in para. 8 (not cited) says the actions may deter victims.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that at a joint meeting in late March 2026 between humanitarian actors and AFC/M23, attended by AFC/M23 officials including Colonel John Imani Nzenze, AFC/M23 Director of Intelligence and liaison with humanitarian actors, and Ms. Chantal Kayitaba Murekatete, Special Adviser on Gender, Family and Children, Education, and Social and Humanitarian Affairs, AFC/M23 reprimanded humanitarian actors and accused them of inventing data, affirmed that it did not tolerate sexual violence and criticised the lack of perpetrator data in patient files; further meetings in late March and April 2026 resulted in an agreement that only aggregate data on sexual violence would be shared.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu (meeting between AFC/M23 and humanitarian actors, late March 2026)
claims.verification_note: Added the two officials the source names as present (source 1 prints them), for investigators; otherwise unchanged. The Group's account (confidential sources) of what AFC/M23 said at a closed meeting, not a public AFC/M23 statement. Being named is not a finding of individual responsibility.
claims.researcher_note: Excerpt may exceed 60 words; trim if check_raw complains. Report of what AFC/M23 officials said by the UN Group of Experts (confidential sources), not a public statement by AFC/M23.

claims.text: Amnesty International said that the two sexual violence survivors it interviewed about abuses by CMC-FDP fighters in Rutshuru territory were held in conditions that amount to sexual slavery.
claims.place_as_written: Bukombo area, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu (Mudugudu base)
claims.verification_note: The rest of the draft (CMC-FDP abuses, 16 interviews, June-December 2025) is already r1-POL-2026-011 from the same page; narrowed to the one finding not stated there.
claims.researcher_note: Amnesty NGO research (remote interviews). Events 2025, report 2026; included because it concerns Wazalendo SV in North Kivu. Survivors unnamed. The area Bukombo is described as controlled by M23. CMC-FDP denial recorded separately.

claims.text: Amnesty International reported that CMC-FDP said it "categorically rejects" the allegations that its fighters raped, sexually enslaved or forced women to "marry" its commanders, and that no complaints, official reports or referrals had been brought to the attention of its internal disciplinary or judicial bodies regarding the incidents.
claims.place_as_written: Bukombo area, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: The general denial by spokesperson Gashegu on 16 June 2026 is already r1-POL-2026-012; narrowed to the specific denial of the sexual-violence allegations, which that claim does not state. Party denial as reported by Amnesty.
claims.researcher_note: Denial as reported by Amnesty; the party's own channel was not located.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23, in a clarification dated 22 September signed by Bertrand Bisimwa, "formally and in their entirety" rejected the accusations in Amnesty International's report on abuses at mining sites in areas under its control, calling them "not established and insufficiently substantiated".
claims.verification_note: Page read in full from the retained capture. Party statement; recorded only as what AFC-M23 said.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan statement relayed by a Goma outlet; answers the 21 September 2026 Amnesty report.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that UN independent experts, in a communiqué published on 21 July in Geneva, denounced serious and systematic violations against civilians; according to Radio Okapi, the experts said AFC/M23 had reportedly set up a system of control based on fear in the areas it administers, and the communiqué reported arbitrary arrests and detentions, acts of torture including sexual violence, and cases of forced labour and forced recruitment of civilians.
claims.place_as_written: AFC/M23-controlled areas of North Kivu and South Kivu
claims.territory: AFC/M23-controlled areas of North Kivu and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Attributed to Radio Okapi reporting the experts' statement; 'had set up' put back to the conditional. The OHCHR release itself could not be retrieved; this rests on Radio Okapi's account of it. The outlet's conditional (aurait) is kept.
claims.researcher_note: Relayed by Radio Okapi; the OHCHR press release (ohchr.org, 21 July 2026) could not be retrieved by the page tool, so it is not cited. Conditional "aurait" in the outlet's wording.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported, based on interviews with 102 former detainees and dozens of other sources, that the M23 detained thousands of captured fighters and civilians, some as young as 12, and that the M23's apparent aim of taking security measures to locate soldiers, militiamen and officials opposed to it gradually turned into a vast, systematic campaign of mass arrests and incommunicado detention targeting civilians with real or perceived links to the army, in particular young men and adolescents.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo and Tshanzu, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu; Goma; Bukavu
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and Rwandan forces, per HRW
claims.verification_note: 'began with soldiers and police in Goma and Bukavu' is not what the excerpt says; rewritten to the excerpts. Category changed from forced_recruitment to detention_abduction, which the cited passages describe. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: HRW French report (10 Jun 2026) supports both clauses. In the stored excerpt 'Celui-ci' refers back to the M23's 'objectif manifeste' of taking security measures, a sentence the excerpt leaves out; it is added and the wording is aligned to it. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: HRW French report (10 Jun 2026) supports both clauses. In the stored excerpt 'Celui-ci' refers back to the M23's 'objectif manifeste' of taking security measures, a sentence the excerpt leaves out; it is added and the wording is aligned to it.
claims.researcher_note: NGO report of 10 June 2026 (87 pages) on events from January 2025; sexual violence is not a focus in the cited passages. Report not previously cited in the period packet. Second excerpt may exceed word limit; trim if flagged.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that, according to several witnesses, M23 captain Gaston executed a certain colonel Amurabi at Rumangabo around June 2025, and that Amurabi was a defence lawyer in the military justice system in Goma according to a former detainee and Congolese judicial and military intelligence sources.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 commander "capitaine Gaston" (nicknamed Longangi), per HRW
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on the page; 'M23' rests on the preceding sentence (page) and the report title. Names spelled as printed. Event of about June 2025, published by HRW in June 2026. The victim was a military officer held at the camp, per HRW. HRW names only 'capitaine Gaston' (nicknamed Longangi by detainees). Being named is not a finding of individual responsibility.
claims.researcher_note: Event dated 2025 (before the unit period); included because the report was published in 2026 and names a victim and a commander. The excerpt spans HRW footnote markers. Names as HRW prints them.

claims.text: BCNUDH reported that of the 2 607 violations and abuses documented in the first half of 2026, 78 per cent (2,068) were committed by armed groups, 20 per cent (536) by State agents and 25 by foreign armed forces, and that AFC/M23 remained the main perpetrator among armed groups, followed by the Wazalendo groups.
claims.actor_as_written: armed groups (AFC/M23, Wazalendo, ADF), State agents
claims.territory: conflict-affected provinces (North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Maniema)
claims.verification_note: Matches the report. Context claim; not Kivu-only.
claims.researcher_note: The report gives a province split (North Kivu 1,655 = 63%, South Kivu 544 = 21%, Ituri 376, Maniema 32) and ADF 230, FARDC 392, not cited in an excerpt. Context claim.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the NGO "Rien sans les femmes" raised the alarm over rising rape cases against women and girls in Lubero-centre, Lubero territory, North Kivu, and that more than 250 rape cases had been documented in local hospitals since the start of 2025, according to Bernadette Kurabe, the organisation's focal point. Radio Okapi's report gave 253 cases between January and April 2025; the source does not attribute the cases to a perpetrator.
claims.verification_note: All excerpts on retained page; single local NGO via Radio Okapi; no perpetrator named. excerpt_en flag is only capitalisation of translated names (Radio Okapi/North Kivu); translation matches the excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Single local NGO figure relayed by Radio Okapi; hospital-based count, not a UN-verified figure. Date range: start of 2025 to publication date, since the page states no other period.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that a local human rights NGO based in Walikale-centre said at least about thirty cases of sexual violence were recorded among displaced people in the villages of Njingala, Mafombi, Mubi, Logu and Makana between 17 and 23 March, and that in Makana two young girls who allegedly resisted attempted rape were shot dead at point-blank range by their armed attackers. Radio Okapi said the displaced had fled Walikale-centre since its occupation by rebel forces on 17 March. According to the head of the NGO, rape victims were referred to the health centres of Ndjingala and Bisie, which are struggling to meet needs for lack of medicines and because of the massive influx of displaced people.
claims.place_as_written: Njingala, Mafombi, Mubi, Logu and Makana villages (Walikale-Kisangani axis), Walikale territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed men (not further identified by the source); source refers to "forces rebelles" occupying Walikale-centre on 17 March
claims.verification_note: Page attributes the health-centre strain to the NGO head ('selon le responsable de l’ONG'), not to Radio Okapi; attribution corrected. Excerpt_en flags are capitalisation only. The NGO is not named; the source spells the village both Njingala and Ndjingala. The source does not attribute the rapes to a named group.
claims.researcher_note: Single local NGO (unnamed in the article), relayed by Radio Okapi. Village spelled "Njingala" in one sentence and "Ndjingala" in another by the source. Perpetrators not identified; the article ties the displacement to rebel occupation of Walikale-centre on 17 March but does not attribute the rapes to a named group. Includes health-centre strain (shortage of medicines) as context.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that violent fighting between AFC-M23 rebels and the FARDC took place in the Bwito (Rutshuru territory) and Bahunde (Masisi territory) chiefdoms of North Kivu between 28 September and 8 October 2025, and that, according to civil society, the fighting caused at least 4 deaths, 13 disappearances and the rape of 8 women.
claims.place_as_written: Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru) and Bahunde chiefdom (Masisi), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC-M23 and FARDC (fighting parties); the source does not attribute the rapes to a party
claims.verification_note: Both passages on retained page; rapes not attributed to a party. Excerpt_en flag is capitalisation only.
claims.researcher_note: Civil-society tally relayed by Radio Okapi; perpetrator of the rapes not stated. The same article mentions the looting of Muliki health centre (see separate health claim) and says civil society criticised reprisals attributed to M23.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the fighting between AFC-M23 and the FARDC in the Bwito and Bahunde chiefdoms between 28 September and 8 October 2025 also caused heavy material damage: several dozen houses were burned, including the Nyabiteja primary school in the Kihondo grouping, and the health centre of Muliki was also looted, along with the theft of about twenty cattle. The source does not say who looted the health centre.
claims.place_as_written: Muliki health centre, Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: The draft said 'citing civil society' for the looting; the page narrates the damage itself ('Ces affrontements ont aussi causé...'), so attribution narrowed. Territory set to both since Muliki's chiefdom is not stated. Source 0 retained as context. Muliki's chiefdom is not stated by the source; the damage is narrated by Radio Okapi in a civil-society report, but the looting is not explicitly attributed to civil society or to any party.
claims.researcher_note: Same civil-society source as the sexual violence claim for the period; no perpetrator named for the looting. Whether Muliki is in Bwito or Bahunde is not stated; the source names Muliki without a chiefdom, so location is given at the level of the fighting zone only (reviewer: check). Supplies looted is the closest fit of the health tag (centre looted).

claims.text: CSDF, a Congolese women's health and rights organisation, said that June 2025 marked a notable deterioration in the security and human rights situation in Masisi, Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories; that, according to protection monitoring data covering 22 health zones, 842 violations were documented; that serious incidents rose by more than 35 per cent compared with May, with Masisi alone accounting for 50 per cent of the cases, followed by Nyiragongo (21 per cent) and Rutshuru (12 per cent); and that June 2025 was the annual peak of gender-based violence, with 247 documented cases (17 per cent of all violations of the month), of which 93 per cent were rapes.
claims.place_as_written: Masisi, Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (the source cites fighting between M23 and Wazalendo groups as context)
claims.verification_note: The page does not print the expansion 'Centre de Santé et Développement de la Femme' (removed) and does not say the monitoring is CSDF's own ('Selon les données du monitoring de protection'), so narrowed. Removed 'mainly women and adolescent girls in displacement and return areas' wording compression; kept figures. Single local organisation: grade C, not B. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: serious incidents up more than 35% on May 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-005: Figure-scope problem found on the retained page: the '50 % des cas' for Masisi follows a sentence on a more than 35% rise in serious incidents compared with May, not the 842 violations; the statement attaches the shares to the 842 violations. Also the page says the 842 violations affected more than 1,100 returnees (64% of identified victims). No perpetrator named, which the statement respects.; excerpt-support: added the sentence on the more than 35% rise in serious incidents compared with May as an excerpt
claims.researcher_note: Local NGO monitoring (protection-cluster style data); no perpetrator breakdown given. The 22 health zones are not named by the source. The 50/21/12 per cent split is of the month's violations/cases generally (the source says "des cas"), not of GBV cases only.

claims.text: UNFPA said in a statement in February 2025 that nearly 500 cases of sexual violence were reported within a single week in the Goma area, including more than 150 involving children, and that this number likely represents only a fraction of the actual survivors, namely those who managed to reach care.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on retained UNFPA page dated 21 February 2025; the week is not dated. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Mediacongo (2025-02-23, relaying the UNFPA statement) dates the UNFPA declaration 17 February; the week itself is not dated in the UNFPA text. Existing drafts hold UNHCR's 895 cases figure for the first half of February; this is a separate UN figure.

claims.text: UNFPA said in a statement in February 2025 that its eight UNFPA-supported mobile clinics, safe spaces and listening centers were only partially functional, that the other facilities providing treatment and counselling to survivors in displacement camps had been looted, that medical supplies and equipment worth millions of dollars had been looted from storage facilities in Goma, and that Goma, with more than 2 million inhabitants, had only three functioning hospitals able to provide clinical care to survivors of sexual assault.
claims.place_as_written: Goma and displacement camps around Goma, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: All three passages verbatim on retained page; no looter named.
claims.researcher_note: UNFPA does not name who looted the facilities or supplies. The same statement says movement restrictions imposed by "the de facto authorities in control of Goma" hampered aid delivery (not recorded here as a separate claim).

claims.text: MSF said that between January and April 2025 more than 7,400 victims and survivors of sexual violence received treatment at Ministry of Health facilities supported by MSF in Goma, and that an additional 2,400 were treated in Saké during the same period.
claims.place_as_written: Goma and Saké (Masisi territory), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on retained page; the page's context is 2025 (M23/AFC takeover of Goma). MSF places Saké 'west of the city'; Masisi territory is not stated by the source.
claims.researcher_note: Health-facility data. Existing drafts hold MSF's UN Security Council briefing (about 28,000 in the first six months of 2025); this is the Goma/Saké breakdown. The MSF text places Saké "west of the city" of Goma; the territory (Masisi) is the reviewer's geographic knowledge, not stated in the excerpt.

claims.text: MSF said that in February 2025 the M23/AFC armed group ordered the dismantling of displacement camps, effectively forcing their residents to leave, and quoted a patient it called Nasha (MSF says patients' names have been changed), who said that after the Rusayo displaced persons camp was destroyed she moved to the courtyard of a school, where armed men broke in one evening at 10:30 pm, attacked her and shot her husband dead when he tried to protect her.
claims.place_as_written: Goma area (Rusayo displaced persons camp and a school courtyard), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23/AFC (camp dismantling, as MSF states); "armed men" (attack on Nasha, not further identified)
claims.verification_note: Pseudonym made explicit with the page's own footnote; Nasha listed in victims_named as a pseudonym per policy v1. Date of the attack on Nasha is not stated (she visited MSF in May). The armed men are not identified.
claims.researcher_note: The date of the attack on "Nasha" is not stated (she visited MSF in May); the asterisk indicates a changed name, so she is not listed in victims_named. The article places this in a section on sexual violence but the quoted words say "They attacked me" without specifying rape, so the claim is filed under displacement/attack context. Which camps were dismantled is not stated beyond Rusayo in the quote; the MSF text describes "a displaced persons camp alongside some 650,000 others on the edge of Goma" (not used here).

claims.text: The BBC reported that a 22-year-old woman, Pascaline, said she was raped by two men at Munzenze prison in Goma in the early hours of 27 January, and that her attackers came over the wall from the men's block right next door called "Safina"; a second woman, Nadine, 22, said she was also raped by two men. The BBC said it could not verify how many women were raped that night, out of a total of 167 who, sources say, were being held, and reported that 132 female prisoners and at least 25 children burned to death, according to two sources.
claims.actor_as_written: attackers from the adjoining men's block, per the survivors quoted
claims.verification_note: Supported on retained page; Nadine's age placed with a replacement quote; 'two sources' attribution kept with the figure; detainee status added to victims_named. The BBC says Pascaline is willing to be identified; it does not say whether Nadine is a real name. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 5 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: First-person testimony to the BBC in Goma; Pascaline is quoted as willing to be identified. Existing drafts (SV-2025#0-3) hold the BBC/UN figures of 165-167 women assaulted; this claim adds survivor testimony and names. "Nadine" is printed without a surname. Nadine's age (22) is in the preceding sentence of the article ("Nadine, 22, has also come back to the prison").

claims.text: The BBC reported that a survivor who does not want to be identified, whom the BBC calls Florence (a name the BBC gave her), said that in this case the attackers at Munzenze prison were fellow inmates, who were not armed or in uniform; the BBC noted that the fire and the rapes are "shrouded in confusion, with all sides eager to blame someone else".
claims.verification_note: Pseudonym made explicit with the BBC's own words (replacement quote); age left out because no stored excerpt prints it. Florence also told the BBC that soldiers and police surrounding the prison fired bullets and tear gas into the women's section instead of putting out the fire (not part of this claim).
claims.researcher_note: "Florence" is a name the BBC assigns ("We are calling her Florence") to a survivor who asked not to be identified. The sentence before the excerpt in the article records that human rights groups say rape is widely used as a weapon of war by M23 and government forces; the BBC treats the prison case as unclear.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH), in its report on the main trends of human rights violations in the DRC for the month of January, recorded in North Kivu eight victims of conflict-related sexual violence, of whom three were attributed to M23 members, three to the FDLR and two to the FARDC.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 (3 victims), FDLR (3), FARDC (2), as attributed by BCNUDH
claims.verification_note: Removed the year 2025 from the statement because no excerpt prints it (date field keeps 2025-01). Graded B, not A: a single UN origin relayed by media, report not opened. January 2025 by the article's date (22 March 2025, 'janvier dernier'); the UN report itself was not opened. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Verified-case count of the UN office, relayed by Actualite.cd (which says the report reached the outlet). The UN report itself was not opened. The page headline attributes most cases nationally to CODECO (Ituri). The excerpt does not give the year of the report; the page is dated 2025-03-22 and the article says January "dernier".

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported, from a survivor account, that in February, after the M23 took control of Goma, four M23 fighters forced their way into the house of a 22-year-old woman called Patience (a pseudonym, per HRW), tied her to her bed and two of them raped her; HRW said the fighters then forced her out of the house and took her to a nearby camp, where for three days multiple fighters raped her and three other women who had been taken there.
claims.place_as_written: Goma and a nearby camp, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: All passages verbatim on retained HRW page; pseudonym marked.
claims.researcher_note: Page dated 2026-01-12 (the dateline text reads "January 12, 2025", apparently a typo). Survivor testimony gathered by HRW with SOFEPADI. Pseudonym, not a real name.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that M23 fighters abducted a woman it called Justine (a pseudonym, per HRW) from her home in Goma in March 2025 during an apparent forced recruitment operation, beat her and her 20-year-old son and forced her to walk to their camp near the city, where two men took her to a secluded area, beat her and raped her; HRW said she arrived at the hospital within 72 hours but the hospital had no PEP kits.
claims.place_as_written: Goma and an M23 camp near the city, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: All passages verbatim on retained HRW page; pseudonym marked. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
claims.researcher_note: Survivor testimony via HRW; pseudonym. HRW adds that she later fled to Uganda and tested HIV positive (not used in the statement).

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that, according to UNFPA, in May 2025 only 7 of 34 health zones in North Kivu had a minimal supply of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) kits, and that by September only 895 complete kits were available for the entire province, where hundreds of cases occur each week; HRW also said IMA World Health had ordered 116,000 kits in early 2025 but the funding was withdrawn so the kits never made it to health centres in eastern Congo.
claims.actor_as_written: not applicable (funding withdrawal and supply shortage; not an attack by a party)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on retained page. The health tag 'supplies_looted' does not fit (nothing was looted); editor should retag (no 'supply shortage' value in the list; closest is facility/access context). A supply shortage after funding withdrawal, not an attack on facilities.
claims.researcher_note: A supply shortage context, not an attack on a facility; the "supplies_looted" tag is the nearest fit in the allowed list and should be reviewed (closer to epidemic/supply context). HRW is relaying UNFPA.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing humanitarian sources, that five young girls of the same family were raped by armed men in the locality of Kalungu, 15 km south of Minova in Buzi grouping, and were treated at a local hospital centre.
claims.place_as_written: Kalungu, Buzi grouping, Kalehe territory (South of Minova), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed men (not further identified by the source)
claims.verification_note: Statement said 'Kalehe territory' as a fact about Kalungu and 'health centre'; the article only places Kalungu relative to Minova/Buzi in an article on Kalehe clashes, and says 'centre hospitalier'. Narrowed. Exact date of the Kalungu rapes not stated (article of 22 January 2025). Perpetrators' group not named. The article is about clashes in Kalehe territory. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet, anonymous humanitarian sources. The article's headline places the event in the context of M23/RDF-FARDC clashes in Kalehe but the text does not name the perpetrators' group. Exact date of the Kalungu rapes is not stated (reported 22 Jan 2025).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that at Bihovu, in Lowa-Numbi village (Shanje), two women were also victims of rape on 14 January.
claims.place_as_written: Bihovu, Shanje, Lowa-Numbi village, Kalehe territory, South Kivu

Shanje'. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet. The excerpt gives no perpetrator.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that a court in Bukavu, which it calls the 'tribunal de grande instance' (a civil-party lawyer quoted in the article thanks the Bukavu 'tribunal militaire de garnison'), sentenced to death on Friday 14 February 2025 212 soldiers accused of murder, attempted murder, rape and fleeing the enemy, for acts committed during the M23 advance in localities and villages of Kalehe, Kabare and Walungu territories.
claims.place_as_written: Bukavu (verdict); offences in Kalehe, Kabare and Walungu territories, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC soldiers (as tried by the Bukavu military court)
claims.verification_note: Raw statement called it the 'garrison military court' as a fact; the article's own narration says tribunal de grande instance. Both names now attributed. First-instance verdict as reported. The article names the court inconsistently; the headline (latest capture) says 72 acquitted while the text says 'Septante' (70). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: The page says 'tribunal de grande instance' in the first sentence and 'tribunal militaire de garnison' later; the source treats these as the same trial. The article describes it as an accelerated trial held as the M23 took Kavumu airport that day. See also the next claim for the dates and villages of the acts. Conviction is a first-instance military-court verdict as reported by the outlet.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that from 6 to 8 February 2025, acts of vandalism and killings were committed by soldiers deployed in the villages of Katana, Kabamba, Miti and Kasheke as far as Kamanyola.
claims.place_as_written: Katana, Kabamba, Miti, Kasheke to Kamanyola, Kabare and Walungu territories, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: soldiers deployed in those villages (FARDC soldiers per the context of the trial)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt matches; force not named in the sentence, actor field already hedged. Territory widened: Kamanyola is not Kabare; source gives villages only.
claims.researcher_note: The excerpt says 'militaires' without naming the force; the paragraph is part of an article about FARDC soldiers tried at Bukavu. Casualty numbers not given.

claims.text: The UN fact-finding mission report said that civil-society organisations reported more than 1 000 victims of sexual violence in South Kivu between January and June, mainly women and adolescent girls, while official sources reported 127 cases of sexual violence in South Kivu in the first two weeks of February alone.
claims.verification_note: Text matches; figure '1000' flag is the formatting '1 000'. Graded B, not A: the mission relays unverified third-party figures. The mission relays these figures from civil-society and official sources; it does not present them as its own findings.
claims.researcher_note: French text of the UN fact-finding mission report A/HRC/60/80; the English advance version is already cited by existing claims (SV-2025#6-12) but not for these figures. The footnote numbers 47 and 48 are part of the page text. The report does not give the underlying organisations; footnotes 47-48 are not reproduced here.

claims.text: The UN fact-finding mission report said that in South Kivu a man was stripped completely naked, beaten until he lost consciousness, and raped by several members of the FARDC and Wazalendo who were going from house to house looting.
claims.verification_note: Para 56 of A/HRC/60/80; date range from para 55 context (retreat in January-February 2025), kept as range.
claims.researcher_note: Sexual violence against a man; no locality or exact date in the text. The surrounding paragraph concerns the retreat of FARDC and Wazalendo from the front lines in January and February 2025 (the preceding sentence of the report).

claims.text: The UN fact-finding mission report said that, according to the UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH), 199 people convicted of sexual and gender-based crimes escaped from the prisons of Goma, Bukavu and Kabare.
claims.place_as_written: Goma, Bukavu and Kabare prisons (North and South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Para 70 matches. Territory field said Bukavu only; the figure covers three prisons incl. Goma. The report does not date these escapes in this sentence; the range follows the Goma (January) and Bukavu/Kabare (14 February) escapes described elsewhere in the report.
claims.researcher_note: Figure covers three prisons, including Goma (North Kivu), so it is not South Kivu only.

claims.text: The UN fact-finding mission report said that on 14 February two further prison escapes, in Bukavu and in Kabare, allowed detainees to flee, some of them convicted of crimes under international law; a footnote cites BCNUDH figures of 2 285 detainees escaping from Bukavu central prison and 221 from Kabare prison.
claims.place_as_written: Bukavu central prison and Kabare prison, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Para 14 and footnote 18 match.
claims.researcher_note: The numbers come from a footnote (18) of the report; the main text gives the date and the categories of escapees.

claims.text: The UN fact-finding mission report said that from 15 to 17 February 2025 soldiers of the FARDC units Guépard and Satan II summarily executed at least 20 civilians in Kamanyola after hundreds of their soldiers died in clashes with the Wazalendo; it said most victims were men and adolescents suspected of being Wazalendo members or supporters, and that according to credible sources the number of victims would be much higher, although further investigation would be needed to confirm it.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC units Guépard and Satan II
claims.verification_note: Raw statement turned the report's conditional ('serait ... seraient nécessaires') into 'credible sources put the number much higher'; restored the hedge. Territory/location 'Walungu/Uvira border, Ruzizi plain' is the researcher's, not the source's. The higher toll is conditional in the report and unconfirmed.
claims.researcher_note: Territory of Kamanyola entered as Walungu following standard administrative usage; the source says only Kamanyola, South Kivu. The existing claim SV-2025#12 covers the Kamanyola/Uvira clashes of mid-February but not these executions. No FARDC response found (see gaps).

claims.text: The UN fact-finding mission report said girls were victims of sexual violence and were used for sexual purposes by commanders and other members of armed groups, and as cooks or messengers; the sentence sits in its section on the recruitment and use of children (which opens on Wazalendo groups), in a paragraph (para. 61) that otherwise describes boys apparently under 18 at Wazalendo checkpoints in South Kivu, patrolling in Uvira and carrying weapons in Fizi territory. The sentence itself names no group.
claims.place_as_written: South Kivu (locality not given in the sentence)
claims.actor_as_written: commanders and other members of armed groups
claims.verification_note: Para 61 matches; context sentence on page. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: section on the recruitment and use of children 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: para. 61: boys at Wazalendo checkpoints, patrolling Uvira, carrying weapons in Fizi 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-013: Read para. 60-61 on the retained PDF: the context is recruitment of children by Wazalendo groups (Fizi, Uvira), which the claim's vague 'passage on the use of children by armed groups' hides; amended to give the context while keeping the sentence's own 'armed groups' (no attribution to Wazalendo added). No fresh search.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): section on the recruitment and use of children; para. 61: boys at Wazalendo checkpoints, patrolling Uvira, carrying weapons in Fizi
claims.researcher_note: The sentence does not name the armed group or place. The surrounding paragraph (para 61) concerns boys seen armed at Wazalendo checkpoints in South Kivu, patrolling in Uvira and carrying AK-47s in Fizi territory; that context is not asserted here. Period is the mission's reporting window (January to July 2025).

claims.text: The UN fact-finding mission report said that on 9 March a shell reportedly hit the paediatric ward of Walungu hospital, killing five people, including two children.
claims.place_as_written: Walungu hospital, Walungu territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Para 28 matches; 'reportedly' preserves the conditional. The mission hedges ('aurait touché') and does not attribute the shell.
claims.researcher_note: Attribution differs by source: Radio Okapi (next claim) cites several sources in Walungu saying M23 fired the shell. Walungu centre was held by M23 at the time per Radio Okapi.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that at least five people hospitalised at the Fonds social du Kivu (FSKI) hospital in Walungu died on Sunday, a day the article prints as '9 janvier' (9 January) although it was published in March, after a shell hit the roof of the paediatric ward; it said several sources in Walungu said the shell was fired by the M23 rebels, who it said were occupying the administrative centre of Walungu territory.
claims.place_as_written: FSKI hospital, Walungu centre, Walungu territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23 (according to several sources in Walungu quoted by Radio Okapi)
claims.verification_note: Raw dated the claim 2025-03-09 and silently read 'janvier' as March; a claim may not state a date its excerpt does not print. Discrepancy now in the statement; date set to the month. Date discrepancy: the article prints 'dimanche 9 janvier' but is dated 10 March 2025, cites testimony 'ce lundi 10 mars' and refers to the fright of 'la veille'; the UN mission (A/HRC/60/80, para 28) gives 9 March. 9 March is likely but is not printed by this source. M23 attribution rests on unnamed local sources. Radio Okapi is UN-run (MONUSCO); the UN mission may share its origin.
claims.researcher_note: The page prints 'dimanche 9 janvier' but is dated 10 March 2025 and refers to testimony 'ce lundi 10 mars'; the UN mission gives 9 March, so 'janvier' is read as a typographical error (flagged, not corrected in the excerpt). Attribution rests on unnamed local sources; the UN mission does not attribute. No M23 or FARDC statement found.

claims.text: The Congolese National Human Rights Commission (CNDH-RDC) reported that on 19 April 2025 Pascaline NGWASI, coordinator of the Association des Mères Célibataires pour le Bien-être des Enfants Abandonnés, was arrested, beaten and raped by M23/AFC members in the Mabenga neighbourhood of Bukavu.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt matches; name printed. Attribution kept as the CNDH's. CNDH-RDC is a Congolese state human rights commission (an organ of a party to the conflict); this is its uncorroborated account.
claims.researcher_note: Single source: a Congolese state commission whose report is addressed to national authorities and the UN; treat M23/AFC attribution as the commission's account. M23/AFC position not found. The report prints the survivor's name and a photograph; name listed under policy v1 and censored in the edition.

claims.text: The CNDH-RDC reported, in a section on violations of the right to health, that on Friday 2 May 2025 five decomposing bodies of Wazalendo members were found who had been abducted on 24 April 2025 by M23/AFC-RDF rebels from the hospital of Mushenyi, where they were being treated for gunshot wounds after the fighting at Nyanfunze, towards Kaziba; it named the five.
claims.place_as_written: Mushenyi hospital, South Kivu (the CNDH files the case under the heading 'KALEHE'; territory otherwise not stated)
claims.verification_note: Raw territory 'Walungu' and location '(Walungu territory)' were the researcher's inference against the source's own heading. Territory now says what the source prints, with the discrepancy noted. CNDH-RDC is a Congolese state human rights commission (an organ of a party to the conflict); this is its uncorroborated account. Territory discrepancy: the report files Mushenyi under 'KALEHE'; Mushenyi/Kaziba are generally placed in Walungu territory. Unresolved; check before relying on the location. Victims were combatants receiving medical care, per the source.
claims.researcher_note: Single source (CNDH). The report files the case under 'Cas d'atteinte au droit à la santé à KALEHE' although Mushenyi and Kaziba are in Walungu territory; location is reported as the source prints it. Wounded combatants removed from a hospital: recorded here under health care access, with the victims' status as combatants per the source's own description (Wazalendo).

claims.text: The CNDH-RDC reported that on 23 April 2025 AFC/M23 elements perpetrated what it calls a 'massacre' in the village of Kakaba-Bushwege (Mushenyi sector), summarily executing five civilians and wounding several others after, it said, mistaking villagers wearing traditional boots called 'GODIO' for Wazalendo; it named three victims and two young boys of the Chibwana family.
claims.place_as_written: Kakaba-Bushwege village, Mushenyi sector, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: 'Massacre' put in quotes as the CNDH's word; territory 'Walungu' was inferred, not printed. CNDH-RDC is a Congolese state human rights commission (an organ of a party to the conflict); this is its uncorroborated account. The source gives the sector only; its Mushenyi hospital entry is filed under 'KALEHE'.
claims.researcher_note: Single source (CNDH). 'Massacre' is the source's word. The two boys of the Chibwana family are not individually named. Territory (Walungu) inferred from Mushenyi sector as in the same report's other entries; the excerpt gives sector only.

claims.text: The CNDH-RDC reported that on Monday 30 June 2025 M23 soldiers entered the locality of Muku, Kamisimbi grouping, Walungu territory, and killed 6 civilians in reprisal for the alleged presence of Wazalendo in the area under their control; a caption names one victim, Francis, from Kalebero.
claims.place_as_written: Muku, Kamisimbi grouping, Walungu territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts match. CNDH-RDC is a Congolese state human rights commission (an organ of a party to the conflict); this is its uncorroborated account.
claims.researcher_note: Single source (CNDH). The UN mission separately reported M23 summary executions of dozens of people in Walungu and Kabare in June and July (collective punishment); this CNDH entry may be one of them but the sources do not link them.

claims.text: The CNDH-RDC reported that on Sunday 29 June 2025 M23 soldiers killed 4 civilians in the locality of Kaniola (Walungu territory) and set fire to several civilians' houses.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt matches; Walungu from the section heading on the page. CNDH-RDC is a Congolese state human rights commission (an organ of a party to the conflict); this is its uncorroborated account.
claims.researcher_note: Single source (CNDH).

claims.text: The CNDH-RDC reported that on 23 May 2025 the lifeless body of Pascal KILOZO was found in the Kavimvira neighbourhood of Uvira, on the shore of Lake Tanganyika; it said the circumstances of death were unknown but raised concern about a possible extrajudicial execution or murder.
claims.place_as_written: Kavimvira neighbourhood, avenue Nyagaa, Uvira, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt matches. CNDH-RDC is a Congolese state human rights commission (an organ of a party to the conflict); this is its uncorroborated account.
claims.researcher_note: Uvira was then under FARDC/Wazalendo control (per the same report's introduction). Cause of death not established.

claims.text: The CNDH-RDC reported that during the night of 4 to 5 April 2025 a child musician was killed in Bukavu by elements identified as belonging to M23-AFC; it said several consistent testimonies suggested the child had recently performed a song about freedom.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt matches; motive clause on the page. CNDH-RDC is a Congolese state human rights commission (an organ of a party to the conflict); this is its uncorroborated account. The motive is conditional in the source ('aurait').
claims.researcher_note: Single source (CNDH); the child is not named in the text and the motive reported by the CNDH is its reading of witness accounts.

claims.text: The CNDH-RDC report said that the Council of Ministers of 28 February 2025, in its record, established for South Kivu that up to 27 February 2025 the city of Bukavu had recorded more than 1.130 wounded, more than 29 deaths in care establishments and 16 people who died at the rally.
claims.verification_note: Date moved from the end of the counting period (27 Feb) to the date of the statement (28 Feb); figures written as printed ('1.130'). Government figures relayed by a state commission; the Council of Ministers record itself was not opened.
claims.researcher_note: Government figure, relayed by the CNDH (the report says it is based on government figures from the city's health structures); the Council of Ministers record itself was not opened. The 'meeting' is not described in the excerpt.

claims.text: UM News reported that during an attack by armed men on the night of March 18 on the United Methodist Irambo Health Center in Bukavu, a nurse was sexually assaulted and another beaten, according to the centre's medical director Dr Jimmy Kasongo; medicine and money were also stolen.
claims.place_as_written: Irambo Health Center, Bukavu, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed gunmen (not identified by the source)
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts match; Ntumba's transfer to Bukavu General Hospital is printed on the page. Church news service reporting on its own facility; byline is a communicator for the church's Kivu Conference. Attackers not identified.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet (church news service) relaying the medical director. Which nurse was sexually assaulted is not stated; the nurse named in the article was beaten. The same article says Irambo was ransacked a month earlier by 'armed rebels' (February) and that Majengo Health Center in Goma was attacked on 19 March.

claims.text: UM News reported that gunmen looted the medicine supplies of the United Methodist Irambo Health Center in Bukavu during an attack on the night of March 18, with more than $4,500 dollars and 789,200 Congolese francs also stolen, and that pharmacist Sandra Bontamba said the attack came 24 hours after the hospital had received essential medicines.
claims.place_as_written: Irambo Health Center, Bukavu, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Text matches; removed a stray ';.' and used the source's 'gunmen'. Church news service reporting on its own facility. Attackers not identified. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
claims.researcher_note: Same single outlet as the previous claim. The same page also says it was the second time in a month the centre was ransacked (February, by 'armed rebels'); not asserted here.

claims.text: The Guardian reported that patients at hospitals in Bukavu described sustaining serious injuries during the chaotic withdrawal of the Congolese army and its allies in the days before M23 rebels marched in: Priscilla Nabintu, 22, said a bullet hit her [in the shin] as she lay on her bed at home near Katana; Ghislaine Ntakwinja, 41, said unidentified gunmen shot her in her right hand in her house; and Mugisho Shalukoma, 20, was recovering from a leg amputation, the result of gunshot wounds. Esperance Mwamini Birindwa, an ICRC nurse, said 162 people had been admitted with injuries related to the M23 takeover between 14 and 24 February.
claims.place_as_written: Bukavu (general hospital) and near Katana, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: unidentified gunmen; the article ties the shooting to the withdrawal of the Congolese army and its allies
claims.verification_note: Raw said all three were at the general hospital and blended the article's framing with the patients' own accounts; rewritten so each clause carries its own source. Individual patients do not name who shot them (Shalukoma: 'I didn't see the person who shot me'); the link to the withdrawal is the Guardian's framing. The article dates M23's arrival in Bukavu to 14 February; the UN mission says 16 February.
claims.researcher_note: Reporting by Prosper Heri Ngorora in Bukavu and Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi. The article gives 14 February for M23's arrival in Bukavu; the UN mission says M23 entered on 16 February (existing claims differ). Three of those with gunshot and shrapnel injuries died per the same ICRC nurse (not asserted here).

claims.text: The Guardian quoted ICRC project manager Emmanuel Konin as saying that, despite all efforts, evacuations sometimes take longer than expected because of access difficulties and that some patients whose lives could have been saved had died of their injuries.
claims.place_as_written: Eastern DRC (ICRC operations; place not stated)
claims.verification_note: Dropped the Goma warehouse clause: it is not in the excerpt and is North Kivu. The quote is not tied to Bukavu by the source, so territory 'Bukavu (city)' removed.
claims.researcher_note: Quote is about ICRC operations in the conflict zone generally; the article does not state that it applies to South Kivu only. Goma warehouse looting is on the same page and is North Kivu.

claims.text: DW reported that a woman it called Riziki (not her real name) said that three soldiers broke into her house to loot and that one of them came into her bedroom to rape her but she resisted; DW said the crime took place in February in Kavumu village, about 30 km north of Bukavu.
claims.place_as_written: Kavumu village, about 30 km north of Bukavu, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: three soldiers (force not named in the passage)
claims.verification_note: Raw statement 'the others told him to leave' omitted 'but he refused'; narrowed to the excerpts. 'Kabare territory' was inferred. Pseudonymous survivor; force of the soldiers not named. On the page she says the others shouted at him to leave 'but he refused', and that they left after her son came to her rescue.
claims.researcher_note: Single survivor account relayed by DW; the survivor is identified only by a pseudonym and is not listed as a named victim. The text calls it an attack she 'survived'; the incident is an attempted rape as she describes it. DW's text 'Congolese military and allied Wazalendo militias from the North Kivu province' is from its introduction and is not tied to this case.

claims.text: DW reported that in South Kivu MSF had assisted almost 700 people in the Kalehe and Uvira regions since the start of 2025, and that according to MSF's report the vast majority of attacks reported by victims in 2025 were committed at gunpoint, with perpetrators remaining unaccountable.
claims.place_as_written: Kalehe and Uvira regions, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Raw attributed the 700 figure to 'MSF's report' (DW states it in its own voice); end date 2025-04 was borrowed from the North Kivu figure. Territory now includes Uvira. The South Kivu sentence says 'people', not explicitly victims of sexual violence; the article is about sexual violence. End of the count period not stated (article of 30 June 2025).
claims.researcher_note: Context in the article is MSF's report on sexual violence (the article's subject); the South Kivu excerpt itself says 'people' and 'attacks', so the sexual-violence framing comes from the article's headline and the neighbouring excerpt on North Kivu. The end date of the South Kivu count is not stated; the report date is 30 June 2025. MSF report itself not opened.

claims.text: Christianity Today reported that on a recent visit to Panzi Hospital in Bukavu, 185 of its 450 patients were receiving treatment for sexual violence, and that after the rebels captured Bukavu in February the hospital remained operational in the following weeks, treating injuries and gunshot wounds and delivering 110 babies.
claims.verification_note: Removed 'M23' (a number the excerpts do not print; the excerpt says 'the rebels'). Visit date unknown, so precision is approximate. The visit date is not given ('recent'); the article is in the May/June 2025 issue. The page's preceding sentence names the M23 as the rebels.
claims.researcher_note: Magazine feature; visit date not given ('recent'); publication date from URL path (2025/05) and search listing (7 May 2025). The page dates it May 2025; the search listing for the page shows 15 June, probably an update.

claims.text: The Global Protection Cluster's March 2025 protection update said that further mass prison escapes from Bukavu, Kabare and Uvira followed during the offensive towards the South Kivu capital, and that some escapees had been convicted or were suspected of serious human rights violations, including sexual and gender-based crimes.
claims.place_as_written: Bukavu, Kabare and Uvira prisons, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Wording 'followed during' restored; territory widened from Bukavu to the three prisons named. Interagency analysis, not an investigation; gives no dates or numbers for these escapes.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates the escapes at Bukavu and Kabare (UN mission) and gives Uvira (also in FIDH; existing claim SV-2025#13). Interagency protection cluster document, not an independent investigation. The same document repeats the BBC/UN figure of at least 165 women raped at Munzenze (Goma).

claims.text: The UNFPA situation report covering April 2025 said that in Minova, South Kivu, activities were still paused due to limited access, though implementing partners were prepared to resume operations as soon as the situation improved.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt matches the sitrep (covering 1-30 April 2025, issued 30 June 2025).
claims.researcher_note: The excerpt does not specify which activities (the section concerns sexual and reproductive health and GBV response). The cause 'limited access' is the sitrep's wording; the sitrep does not attribute it to a party.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the traditional FDLR-RUD area of operations was in the Bwisha and Bwito chefferies, Rutshuru territory, and that at the time of drafting FDLR-RUD units were particularly active in Jomba, Binza, Busanza and Bukoma, overlapping with the FDLR-FPP area in Rutshuru territory.
claims.place_as_written: Bwisha and Bwito chefferies; Jomba, Binza, Busanza, Bukoma, Rutshuru territory (North Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Matches excerpt.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that since April 2025 RDF units had led joint operations with AFC/M23 aimed at neutralizing the FDLR, and that RDF and AFC/M23 systematically destroyed and burned civilian settlements inhabited by members of FDLR, their families or alleged supporters.
claims.verification_note: Both clauses verbatim in the Group's report (paras 36, 41); the page places operations in Nyiragongo and Rutshuru (Bwito, Bwisha).
claims.researcher_note: Two excerpts, same document. Report says photographic evidence, satellite imagery and NASA fire data corroborated several incidents.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that since June 2025 VDP/Wazalendo units, often operating jointly with FDLR, had conducted incursions and ambushes against AFC/M23 and RDF, either to recapture strategic positions or to disrupt their advances and supply lines.
claims.place_as_written: Masisi, Rutshuru, Nyiragongo, Walikale territories and outskirts of Goma (North Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Single clause, verbatim (para 73).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that between mid- to late September and October 2025 FARDC increased air strikes, notably in Bibwe, Mpeti and Minjenje between 19 and 21 September, relying on VDP/Wazalendo and FDLR elements to conduct asymmetric ground operations.
claims.place_as_written: Bibwe, Mpeti, Minjenje (northern Masisi / Walikale, North Kivu)
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC with VDP/Wazalendo and FDLR elements
claims.verification_note: Statement verbatim; location corrected: the page places Bibwe in northern Masisi on the Rutshuru-Masisi-Walikale corridor, not a Lubero axis.
claims.researcher_note: Territory not named in the excerpt; verify (the report places Bibwe on the Bibwe-Pinga axis).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government of the DRC expressed its commitment to neutralizing the FDLR, publicly stated that it did not support the FDLR and called on FDLR combatants to disarm and surrender.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim. The Group reports the Government's public position; it does not itself assess whether the Government supported FDLR in this sentence (see claim 12).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the bulk of FDLR forces operated in areas controlled by AFC/M23 and RDF, beyond the operational reach of the FARDC, affecting the latter's ability to neutralize FDLR elements that refused to surrender.
claims.place_as_written: AFC/M23- and RDF-controlled areas of North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Verbatim.

claims.text: Congolese media reported that on Friday 10 October 2025 the FARDC issued a communiqué, signed by army spokesperson Major General Ekenge Bomusa Efomi Sylvain, calling on all FDLR factions to lay down their arms and warning that in case of refusal the FARDC would proceed to disarmament by constraint or by force; the UN Group of Experts likewise reported that FARDC issued a communiqué on 10 October 2025 calling on FDLR to disarm and surrender, warning of forced disarmament.
claims.verification_note: Date and weekday come from the 7sur7 page lead (not the stored excerpt), supplied as replacement quote; GoE independently confirms the date. excerpt_en flag is a false positive (faithful translation).
claims.researcher_note: The 7sur7 excerpt gives the date in the lead sentence of the same page (10 October 2025), not in the excerpt; the UN report gives the date. The communiqué is also described as implementing the operational order of 1 October 2025 (7sur7).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that DRC Minister of Regional Integration Floribert Anzuluni confirmed at a press briefing in Kinshasa on Tuesday 28 July that the FDLR had signed a protocol of demilitarisation, demobilisation and cantonment.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; excerpt_en flag false positive. This is the DRC government's announcement; no FDLR statement confirming the signature was opened in this round.
claims.researcher_note: Whether the FDLR confirmed signing was not found in this page.

claims.text: Afrikarabia reported that Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe considered the DRC's announcement of an FDLR surrender protocol a 'grossière manipulation' that is in no way consistent with the Washington accords.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim attributed quote. Party statement ('Rwanda says'); the page does not give the date or venue of the minister's remark.
claims.researcher_note: Exact date of Nduhungirehe's remark not given; page dated 2026-08-05, after Kinshasa's 28 July announcement.

claims.text: Afrikarabia reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo, on X, rejected a 'protocole négocié avec une milice génocidaire que le gouvernement de la RDC continue d'armer et de soutenir' and said the FDLR remain integrated in the Congolese army and active on the front lines.
claims.verification_note: Attributed party statement; quote kept as printed. Party statement. 'Milice génocidaire' is Kigali's wording, quoted. Afrikarabia's rendering of the Makolo quote is garbled ('restent intégrés ... actifs sur les lignes de fronts ne changent rien'); the original X post was not opened.
claims.researcher_note: The X post itself was not opened; attribution rests on Afrikarabia. The page text has a spacing artefact ('r estent').

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 1 March 2025 AFC/M23 transferred several FDLR captives to the Government of Rwanda, including 'Brigadier-General' Ezechiel Gakwerere; according to AFC/M23 they had been arrested during their raid on Goma, while the Group itself reported that most, including Gakwerere, were arrested during armed operations targeting hospitals, and it records 'controversies around his arrest and transfer' in an annex.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; name printed. Arrest circumstances are AFC/M23's account as reported by the Group. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Group's own finding on the arrests 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: annex on controversies around his arrest and transfer 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-003: Better explanation in the same source: the next sentence of para. 73 gives the Group's own finding on the arrest circumstances (hospital raids), which the claim omits and which links this to the hospital-raid claims (r1-GOE-055).; excerpt-support: added two excerpts: para. 73 ('Most, including Gakwerere, were arrested during armed operations targeting hospitals') and the annex 39 title
claims.researcher_note: The report adds that most of these arrests occurred during operations targeting hospitals (see the health-care claims of other units, Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho, 1 and 3 March).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 4 January 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF took control of Masisi centre and retained it despite repeated attempts by Wazalendo, FDLR, the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and FARDC to retake it.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 and RDF; counter-attacks by Wazalendo, FDLR, FDNB and FARDC
claims.verification_note: Verbatim.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that about two weeks later AFC/M23 and RDF captured Minova town in Kalehe Territory, South Kivu, and that the 2,500 FARDC and FDNB troops based in Minova retreated before their arrival, leaving behind significant quantities of military equipment.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 and RDF; FARDC and FDNB retreating
claims.verification_note: Supported; 'about' is a slight softening of the Group's 'Two weeks later', acceptable. The Group says 'Two weeks later', counting from the 4 January 2025 capture of Masisi centre in the preceding sentence (claim 18).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 the majority of 7,000 to 9,000 Burundian troops were positioned in South Kivu, notably in the Ruzizi Plain along the tri-border area and in the Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, and that heavy clashes between FDNB (supported by FARDC and Wazalendo) and AFC/M23 (supported by RDF) resulted in several hundreds of FDNB casualties.
claims.place_as_written: Ruzizi Plain and Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; footnote sources confirmed on page. Troop-strength figures differ across sources: GoE 7,000-9,000 (April 2025); SOS Médias Burundi 'more than 10,000'; Actualite.cd relaying CRG/CIC 12,000-15,000 (claim 42). Casualty footnote 211 cites FDNB, security, Government of Burundi, FARDC and intelligence sources.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in February 2025 the President of Burundi, Évariste Ndayishimiye, accused Rwanda of intending to invade Burundi, including through its backing of the Burundian armed opposition group Red Tabara, and announced Burundi's readiness to fight back; it also reported that in mid-March the two countries agreed on verbal and military de-escalation, reportedly concluding a non-aggression agreement.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim. Burundi's accusation is a party statement reported by the Group; 'reportedly' hedge kept.
claims.researcher_note: Report also cites a Rwandan Minister of Foreign Affairs message on X for the mid-March de-escalation (reportedly).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that during more than a month of controlling Uvira, AFC/M23 forced the withdrawal of FDNB, captured large FARDC bases and dominated the entire Ruzizi plain along the Burundian border, and that AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026 following sustained international diplomatic pressure.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (forced FDNB withdrawal); AFC/M23 and RDF (withdrawal from Uvira)
claims.verification_note: The Group attributes the forced FDNB withdrawal to AFC/M23 alone, not RDF; 'diplomatic pressure' clause is on the page (para 77), supplied as replacement quote.
claims.researcher_note: Report states AFC/M23 had captured Uvira on 10 December 2025 (para. 74, not excerpted here).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in late January 2026 FARDC, with support from Wazalendo, FDNB and private military contractors, launched an offensive from Uvira towards Minembwe against MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23, who had reinforced MRDP/Twirwaneho in August 2025 and February 2026.
claims.place_as_written: From Uvira towards Minembwe, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC with Wazalendo, FDNB and private military contractors
claims.verification_note: Verbatim single sentence.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in late January 2026 the AFC/M23 coalition, including Twirwaneho combatants, temporarily seized Point Zero, Kanguli and Tuwe-Tuwe along the Mwenga-Fizi road, and that FARDC-FDNB forces regained these positions on 29 January.
claims.place_as_written: Point Zero, Kanguli, Tuwe-Tuwe, Mwenga-Fizi road, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 coalition incl. Twirwaneho; FARDC-FDNB forces
claims.verification_note: Verbatim.
claims.researcher_note: The 29 January date refers to the regaining; the seizure is 'late January 2026'.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that several Wazalendo factions carried out joint operations with FDNB, which relied on them for intelligence and knowledge of the terrain; for example FDNB operated with Yakutumba along the Uvira axis and the Ruzizi Plain prior to the AFC/M23 takeover and relied on Ngomazito elements as scouts in the Hauts Plateaux.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira axis, Ruzizi Plain, Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Verbatim.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 leaders alleged that FARDC and FDNB committed a premeditated, systematic and targeted campaign of extermination against the Banyamulenge population, including through aerial bombardments; the Group stated it did not substantiate intentional targeting of the civilian population.
claims.actor_as_written: MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 (allegation); FARDC and FDNB (accused)
claims.verification_note: Allegation and the Group's finding kept separate. 'Campaign of extermination' is the wording of MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 leaders as reported by the Group; the Group did not substantiate intentional targeting.
claims.researcher_note: Party allegation attributed to the parties. The Group states it did not substantiate intentional targeting.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that additional AFC/M23 public justifications for the offensive on Uvira cited the presence of FDLR-FOCA elements operating alongside FARDC and FDNB, and said it did not identify evidence that such elements posed a direct threat to Rwanda justifying military intervention in the DRC.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 spokespersons (as described by the Group of Experts); FARDC, FDNB
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; attribution to AFC/M23 justifications supported by the preceding page sentence (replacement quote). '23' flag is from 'AFC/M23'. The 'additional claims' follow, on the page, public justifications 'including statements by AFC/M23 spokespersons and affiliated social media networks'.
claims.researcher_note: The sentence before names AFC/M23 spokespersons and affiliated social media networks as the source of the public justifications.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts assessed that control of Katogota and surrounding heights strengthens the influence of AFC/M23 over the northern 'gate' of the Ruzizi Plain and offers options of advancing toward Uvira by bypassing strong FDNB and FARDC/Wazalendo blocking positions along RN5.
claims.place_as_written: Ruzizi Plain, Katogota, RN5, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Source uses present tense ('offers'), not 'would offer'; 'defensive lines' clause narrowed out (page-only). Assessment by the Group: graded A as a documented UN finding, but it is analysis, not an event. Month '2025-09' not printed; narrowed.
claims.researcher_note: Analytical assessment by the Group of Experts, not an incident report; date is approximate.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several local sources, an attack on Saturday by Burundian soldiers in the town of Mikalati, Fizi territory, against residents returning from the weekly market in Bijombo (Uvira territory); its headline section gives four civilians killed, mass abductions and over 100 missing.
claims.place_as_written: Mikalati (Mu Mikarati), Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian soldiers (FDNB), as attributed by local sources
claims.verification_note: Supported as attributed; grade C (anonymous local sources, single outlet). Rests on unnamed local sources; the casualty figures appear only in a section heading, not in sourced body text. The date (6 December 2025) is inferred from 'Saturday' in a report datelined 7 December 2025. No official statement from Burundi or the DRC as of 7 December.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('Saturday') and publication date 2025-12-07. No victims named. Unverified local-source account; no official statement from Burundi or DRC as of Sunday morning per same page.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that a survivor, now a refugee in Mikenge, described meeting Burundian soldiers at Mikalati who attacked, looted and abducted many people, especially women.
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian soldiers, as described by one survivor
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; attributed to survivor. Single unnamed survivor account relayed by one outlet.
claims.researcher_note: Single anonymous witness. Date computed from weekday and publication date 2025-12-07. 'Women abducted' is not described as sexual violence by the source.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the survivor said the military commander ordered the soldiers 'to kill the men and collect their belongings', that the Wazalendo community claims 45 people, mostly women, are being held at the Mikalati military site, and that no official statement had been issued by the Burundian or Congolese governments as of Sunday morning.
claims.place_as_written: Mikalati military site, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian soldiers (alleged); Wazalendo community (claim on detainees)
claims.verification_note: Each clause attributed as on the page. The '45 held' figure is a claim by the Wazalendo community (a party aligned against the FDNB's adversaries but also a belligerent); the order quote is from one unnamed survivor.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan-side figure (Wazalendo community). Burundi and DRC governments: no statement as of the page, see gaps.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that OCHA had already warned of difficulties accessing food and healthcare in Minembwe, due, according to local sources, to a blockade imposed for a month by the Burundian army.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe, Fizi/Mwenga Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian army (FDNB), as alleged by local sources
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; attribution kept with SOS Médias and local sources. The OCHA warning itself was not opened; the blockade attribution to the Burundian army is 'according to local sources'. FDNB's own account of the road closures is in claims 34-35; the demonstrators' account in claim 36. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: OCHA's own warning not opened; relayed by SOS Médias Burundi. FDNB spokesperson's account is a separate claim.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the FDNB spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, acknowledged on the BBC that some Banyamulenge are trapped in areas 'where the enemy is' and said it is understandable that those who go to buy food for the enemy are blocked.
claims.verification_note: Date of the BBC remark is not 7 Dec; narrowed to a range. Origin is the BBC, so not independent of claim 35. Relay of a BBC interview; the BBC Gahuza article of 12 November 2025 (claim 35) carries a similar Baratuza quote ('Point-zero ... is the route they must use to fetch food they give to the enemies, that is why it is closed'). The SOS Médias English wording is a translation of that interview, not the original.
claims.researcher_note: Relay of a BBC interview; see the BBC Gahuza claim for the primary report (dated 2025-11-12).

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Burundian army stated that its troops in South Kivu had blocked the roads of people leaving the Minembwe area in order to 'protect Uvira and the Burundi border', and that FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza told BBC Gahuzamiryango that in Minembwe there was not one Burundian soldier.
claims.verification_note: 'Confirmed' upgraded the verb; corrected to 'stated'. excerpt_en flags are false positives (proper-noun renderings). Party statement (FDNB). Kirundi 'kimenesha' = makes known/states; rendered 'stated' rather than 'confirmed'. On the same page Baratuza says Burundian troops are at Muramvya, Mugeti and Majembwe. Translations are the researcher's, from Kirundi.
claims.researcher_note: Publication date read from the page header '12 Ukw'icumi na rimwe 2025' (Kirundi, month 11 = November). The page dateline is read as 12 November 2025.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that demonstrators in Minembwe (an area controlled by the Twirwaneho group together with AFC/M23) accused Burundian troops and those working with them of blocking the roads that bring supplies, mainly from Uvira, at Mu Mikarati, Point-zero and elsewhere, and asked that the Burundian troops return home.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe; Mu Mikarati; Point-zero, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian troops (FDNB), as alleged by demonstrators
claims.verification_note: Attributed account; translation faithful. Demonstrators' account (in an area held by Twirwaneho with AFC/M23); FDNB's account is claim 35.
claims.researcher_note: Demonstrators were in a Twirwaneho/AFC/M23-controlled area (partisan context). Demonstrators' words quoted in the same page also describe the blockade as hunger-inducing; no legal label recorded.
