claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Burundi accuses Rwanda of continuing to attack the positions of its soldiers sent to eastern DRC; that Burundi's Minister of Foreign Affairs Edouard Bizimana, speaking on Monday before representatives of countries in Burundi, said without giving proof that the aim of the attacks was for Rwanda and M23 to capture Uvira before 25 December 2025; and that the Rwandan government had not yet responded.
claims.verification_note: Full name and 'Monday' came from the page, not the excerpt; supplied as replacement quote. Removed awkward 'according to BBC'. Party statement. The page (published 9 December 2025) says 'yesterday Monday', i.e. 8 December 2025. BBC notes the claim was made without proof.
claims.researcher_note: Weekday 'ejo ku wa mbere' (yesterday, Monday) -> 2025-12-08; date computed from weekday and publication date 2025-12-09.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that at least 272 Burundian soldiers are serving sentences of up to life imprisonment in Murembwe Central Prison in southwestern Burundi after refusing to be sent to fight in the DRC.
claims.place_as_written: Burundi (Murembwe Central Prison); related to deployment in DRC
claims.verification_note: Statement verbatim; date 2026-07-09 not printed, narrowed to the report month. SOS Médias does not give its source for the 272 figure. The same article cites an internal DRC Interior Ministry report of more than 29,000 Burundian soldiers deployed between August 2022 and December 2025 (not part of this claim).
claims.researcher_note: Dateline 'Fizi, July 9, 2026'; the sentencing figure is a current-status claim by the outlet without an attributed source in the excerpt.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that an incursion followed by systematic looting by armed men assimilated to former FDLR fighters was reported on the night of Sunday 14 September 2025 in the lakeside village of Nyakakoma, Binza grouping, Rutshuru territory, according to an anonymous local source; the page says no human incident was reported.
claims.place_as_written: Nyakakoma, Binza grouping, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Armed men presumed to be FDLR
claims.verification_note: Supported as attributed; grade C (anonymous local source, single outlet). Perpetrators only 'presumed' FDLR per an anonymous resident; the resident said the attackers were seeking a local 'notable du M23'. Village in an AFC/M23-controlled area. Single outlet (byline 'La Rédaction').
claims.researcher_note: Single anonymous local source; the village lies in an AFC/M23-controlled zone per the page. The page names Heps-EPER condemning armed violence at Bishusha (not excerpted). Victim count: none reported.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that long lines of Burundian soldiers were seen on Wednesday 10 December at the Gatumba border returning to their country, according to local sources in Uvira and Bujumbura; it added that Burundi's ambassador to the DRC denied this departure of part of the Burundian soldiers.
claims.place_as_written: Gatumba border (Burundi side) / Uvira, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; regraded C because the observation rests on anonymous local sources and is contested. Rests on unnamed local sources; denied by Burundi's ambassador to the DRC (claim 41). Article first published 11 December 2025 (modified 21 February 2026, hence the URL date). The same page says the Congolese side of the Gatumba post was controlled by AFC-M23 after its entry into Uvira. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, published 11 Dec 2025 (modified 21 Feb 2026, hence the URL path), carries the sighting per local sources, but the same report ends by saying Burundi's ambassador to the DRC denied this departure of part of the Burundian soldiers; the statement leaves that denial out. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, published 11 Dec 2025 (modified 21 Feb 2026, hence the URL path), carries the sighting per local sources, but the same report ends by saying Burundi's ambassador to the DRC denied this departure of part of the Burundian soldiers; the statement leaves that denial out.
claims.researcher_note: Page republished/modified 2026-02-21; original publication 2025-12-11. The Burundian ambassador's denial is a separate claim.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the departure of part of the Burundian soldiers from Uvira was denied by Burundi's ambassador to the DRC.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Burundi (ambassador to the DRC)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim. The ambassador is not named on the page; the denial is reported without a quotation.
claims.researcher_note: The ambassador is not named on the page.

claims.text: Cocorico.cd reported that the situation at Walikale remained under FARDC control despite the departure of part of the population, and that the army had slowed the rebels' advance, pushing them back to Mpofi as they advanced toward Walikale-centre.
claims.verification_note: Narrowed to the excerpt: removed the region number (not in the excerpt) and added the population-departure clause the excerpt prints. Single outlet; rebels unnamed in this passage. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet; the page does not name the rebels in this passage. Treat as lead for frontline map.

claims.text: BBC Gahuza reported that Uvira residents confirmed that Wazalendo fighters entered the city on the morning of Sunday and FARDC soldiers entered in the evening, after AFC/M23 announced on Saturday that it had left the city 'fully'.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt and next sentence support all clauses; 18 Jan 2026 (publication) was a Sunday. The '23' flag is 'AFC/M23'. Residents' account as reported by BBC Gahuza; Kinshasa and Washington had said M23 had not left after its earlier withdrawal announcement (same article). 2026-10-29: control edited: Frontline data fix (FRONTLINE_NOTES.md): control.held_by names only the holder (for a withdrawal, the side withdrawing), so the side class is not 'both sides named'; the other side stays in the statement. Wording from the stored excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date (article published 18 January 2026, a Sunday). Kinshasa and Washington said M23 had not left Uvira earlier, per the same article; other units cover the M23 withdrawal statements.

claims.text: BBC Gahuza reported that the South Kivu governor on the government-controlled side, then in Bujumbura where he had taken refuge, said the government had information that some M23 fighters remained in Uvira, urged great caution and asked the population to avoid ethnic violence.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports each clause. The excerpt_en flag is the word 'South' rendering 'Kivu y'Epfo'; the translation is faithful to the excerpt alone. Further down, BBC Gahuza names the governor 'Jean Jacques Pulusi Sadiki' (Congorassure.cd: 'Jean-Jacques Purusi') and reports, from his voice message to the BBC, that he said the remaining M23 fighters wore civilian clothes and were armed, and that M23 fighters had gone to positions at Sange and Luvungi.
claims.researcher_note: Governor is not named in the passage (Congorassure names Jean-Jacques Purusi as governor who had left Uvira). Date computed from publication date.

claims.text: BBC Gahuza reported that other videos circulating on social media showed looting that took place after the M23 fighters left Uvira; the passage does not attribute the looting.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports it; unverified social-media videos, looting unattributed.
claims.researcher_note: Videos not verified by the outlet in this passage.

claims.text: Mediacongo reported that the High Military Court opened debate in Kinshasa on Friday 25 September (2026) in the case of two general-majors prosecuted for their alleged role in the loss of Bukavu during the AFC/M23 offensive in South Kivu in 2025: Robert Anvul Yav, who then commanded the South Kivu military region, and André Ehonza Uketi, former head of operations Sukola 2 Nord.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts verbatim; 25 Sep 2026 was a Friday. Stage is 'prévenus' / 'poursuivis' (accused, prosecuted), not convicted; the page stresses the facts remain accusations. Spelling kept as Mediacongo prints it. Name spelling differs across outlets and is not reconciled: Mediacongo prints 'Robert Anvul Yav'; per the research notes (pages not retained, not verified here) Jeune Afrique prints 'Robert Yav Avul Ngola' and an RFI snippet 'Robert Avul Yav'. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Name spellings differ across outlets: Mediacongo 'Robert Anvul Yav'; Jeune Afrique (2 Oct 2026, paywalled) 'Robert Yav Avul Ngola' and says the two generals are tried since 25 September; RFI snippet 'Robert Avul Yav'. Verify before profiling. Year of the opening taken from page date 25.09.2026.

claims.text: Mediacongo reported that, according to the public prosecution, Robert Anvul Yav allegedly left Bukavu before the arrival of AFC/M23 and did not organise a counter-offensive.
claims.verification_note: Prosecution allegation, conditional mood kept ('aurait quitté'). Page adds that per the prosecution he then set up HQ at Nyangezi. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Prosecution allegation, not a finding.

claims.text: Mediacongo reported that the case file includes allegations about handing arms and ammunition to Wazalendo fighters at Lumbishi in Kalehe territory, and that, according to prosecution elements reported in the file, some equipment handed over was defective and some ammunition out of date.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC officers (as alleged by the prosecution)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim; accusations, not findings. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Undated events (during the early 2025 South Kivu offensive); prosecution allegation. Relevant to FARDC-Wazalendo supply.

claims.text: Mediacongo reported that, in earlier hearings, the two accused generals contested the prosecution's reading of events, explaining that AFC/M23 forces had a significant advantage in men and equipment.
claims.actor_as_written: Robert Anvul Yav; André Ehonza Uketi (the accused)
claims.verification_note: Defence account as reported; excerpt verbatim. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Defence account.

claims.text: La Presse Africaine reported that brigade general Dunia Kashindi Fabien, 33rd military region commander, said at the funeral of self-proclaimed Wazalendo general Rukumeta Biriho Pierre in Uvira on Thursday 26 June 2025 that the Wazalendo were giving everything for the defence of South Kivu and had sworn never to betray Congo or Uvira.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts plus page support each clause; 26 June 2025 is printed as 'ce jeudi 26 juin 2025'. Local outlet with patriotic framing; cited only for what the general said. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Local outlet with a patriotic framing ('barbare', 'balkanisation'); cited only for what the general said. The page's own account of how the deceased died is garbled and not recorded.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that on 3 March 2025 Wazalendo fighters attacked several Banyamulenge villages within a 10-kilometre radius of Bibokoboko, Fizi territory, and quoted a community leader saying they killed seven people and destroyed houses, health centers and schools.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts verbatim; HRW documented investigation. The death toll is the quoted community leader's figure. HRW adds (same page) that it interviewed relatives of a 60-year-old man and a 25-year-old man killed in the attack, and used satellite imagery and verified, geolocated photographs to confirm houses were burned in Madjdja, Lulimba I and Bibokoboko that day; a military source and residents said no opposing armed groups were known to be near Bibokoboko at the time.
claims.researcher_note: HRW also reports it used satellite imagery and geolocated photographs to confirm that houses were burned in Madjdja, Lulimba I and Bibokoboko on that day, and interviewed relatives of a 60-year-old man and a 25-year-old man killed (not named). A military source said there was no known presence of opposing armed groups near Bibokoboko at the time. Some of this probably already exists in other units: check at promote.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch quoted a Banyamulenge community leader as saying that Wazalendo fighters who attacked villages around Bibokoboko, Fizi territory, in the 3 March 2025 attack destroyed health centers, among other buildings.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (as alleged by a community leader quoted by HRW)
claims.verification_note: Supported; the '3' flag resolved by a replacement passage that carries the 3 March date with the quote. HRW's imagery confirmation covers burned houses, not health centers, so the health-center destruction rests on one quoted community leader. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Single quoted community-leader claim; HRW's satellite imagery confirmation refers to burned houses, not to health centers. Facility names not given.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that on 3 March in Sange, Uvira territory, a Wazalendo commander detained and whipped a 48-year-old man accused of stealing a television, and that a relative and a neighbour said the man died of his injuries.
claims.actor_as_written: a Wazalendo commander (not named in the passage)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim; HRW documented. Commander and victim not named. HRW adds that the commander, later implicated in the killing of a Congolese soldier, was removed from his post but has not faced prosecution for the killings.
claims.researcher_note: HRW adds that the commander, later implicated in the killing of a Congolese soldier, was removed from his post but has not faced prosecution (next sentences of the release). Victim not named.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that on 14 February Wazalendo fighters killed a 25-year-old Munyamulenge man in Mulongwe, Uvira, after accusing him of being Rwandan, shooting him twice in the hip; he died from his injuries according to two sources.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim; HRW documented, two sources. Victim not named.
claims.researcher_note: Victim not named by HRW.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that, following the M23's capture of Bukavu, Wazalendo fighters entered over 20 Banyamulenge households in Uvira, stealing goods and threatening residents, and in one case shot a woman in the head and beat at least three people.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim; date only 'following the M23's capture of Bukavu'.
claims.researcher_note: Date is 'following the capture of Bukavu' (mid-February 2025); exact days not given.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that the interim governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Elakano, told the media on April 23 that the province was unable to collect taxes because of the Wazalendo fighters, who should 'not take the place of the state'.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim; HRW relays a media statement (original media report not retrieved).
claims.researcher_note: Relayed by HRW; original media report not retrieved.

claims.text: Actualite.cd, summarising a UN Group of Experts report transmitted to the Security Council, reported that the experts wrote that the offensive on Uvira was carried out under the direct command of Makenga and Byamungu, and that James Kabarebe, a retired RDF general, was established to have played a key role in coordinating it.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira and the Bukavu-Uvira corridor, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (Makenga, Byamungu); retired RDF general James Kabarebe as coordinator, per the report
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on retained page; quote is the outlet's French rendering of the GoE report. Checked against the retained S/2026/466 text (para. 75: 'conducted under the direct command of Mr. Makenga and Mr. Byamungu. Retired RDF General James Kabarebe'), which matches. Attribution to the Group kept. The underlying report (S/2026/466, letter dated 5 June 2026) is retained and says the same; the outlet gives surnames only.
claims.researcher_note: Relay of the UN GoE report (S/2026/466, 5 June 2026 per UN list), read by the outlet on 1 July 2026; the quoted sentences are the report's. Should be corroborated against the report text itself. The article gives 'MM. Makenga et Byamungu' without first names.

claims.text: Actualite.cd, relaying a UN Group of Experts report, reported that the experts recalled that Uvira was taken on 10 December 2025 and that AFC/M23 and RDF forces advanced rapidly south as far as Makobola, about twenty kilometres from Uvira.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 and RDF forces, per the report
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; matches S/2026/466 para. 74 ('The capture of Uvira on 10 December 2025 and the rapid advancement of AFC/M23 and RDF forces southwards to Makobola, 20 km south of Uvira'). excerpt_en flag is a translation artefact (AFC/M23 casing); translation is faithful. Other outlets give 10-12 December for the capture of Uvira; this date is the Group's.
claims.researcher_note: Relay of the UN GoE report. Date of capture as stated by the report via Actualite.cd; other outlets give 10-12 December (Kigali Today says 12 December), a discrepancy to settle in the Uvira units.

claims.text: Actualite.cd, relaying a UN Group of Experts report, reported that AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026 after sustained international diplomatic pressure.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 and RDF troops, per the report
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; matches S/2026/466 para. 77 ('eventually withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026, following sustained international diplomatic pressure'). The Group adds that the withdrawal was followed by redeployment to adjacent areas (per Actualite.cd's quotation of the report).
claims.researcher_note: Relay of UN GoE report. The same article quotes the report as calling the withdrawal 'a strategic manoeuvre' followed by redeployment to adjacent areas; AFC/M23 presented it as a goodwill gesture. Party accounts of the withdrawal belong to the Uvira units.

claims.text: The U.S. Department of the Treasury stated that, following the 15 November 2025 signing in Qatar of a peace framework agreement between the DRC government and M23, M23 seized Uvira and later withdrew, while still controlling Goma and Bukavu.
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; publication date removed from the statement.
claims.researcher_note: Excerpt spans three adjacent sentences of the release. Release text says 'Following the signing, M23 seized the strategic port city of Uvira' and that M23 'eventually withdrew'.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the European Union announced sanctions on M23 figures including Bertrand Bisimwa (head of the political wing, already under UN sanctions), 'Jean Bahati Musanga' [as printed by Radio Okapi] (North Kivu governor appointed by the rebels), Désiré Rukomera (in charge of M23 recruitment and propaganda) and Jean-Bosco Nzabonimpa (deputy head of finance).
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu (M23-appointed governorate) and M23 structures
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; page published 17/03/2025 says 'L’Union européenne a annoncé, lundi 17 mars'. Date removed from statement; 'already under UN sanctions' added from the excerpt. excerpt_en flag is a translation artefact. Name discrepancy: Radio Okapi prints 'Jean Bahati Musanga'; the UN Group of Experts prints 'Bahati Musanga Joseph' / 'Joseph Bahati Musanga' (alias Bahati Erasto) and Actualite.cd 'Joseph Musanga Bahati' for the M23-appointed North Kivu governor. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-003: Namesake check: a search for the EU listing shows other outlets (opinion-info.cd, heshimardc.net) and the UN Group of Experts naming the governor 'Joseph Bahati Musanga' / 'Bahati Musanga Joseph', while Radio Okapi, Actualite.cd and Mediacongo print 'Jean'. The first name is unreliable; mark it as printed and link the person to the Group's 'Bahati Musanga Joseph' profile only with that caveat. The EU regulation (2025/509) was not fetched.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; 'Jean Bahati Musanga' is printed in source 0
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi says Bisimwa was 'already under UN sanctions'; the CRG/CIC report (April 2026) lists his earlier sanction as a US one (25 July 2024) and EU (17 March 2025), not UN. Not resolved here. The EU Council press release (consilium.europa.eu) could not be fetched by the page helper; verifier should use it as primary.

claims.text: Actualite.cd, citing an April 2026 report by the Congo Research Group and NYU's Center on International Cooperation, reported that M23 chief of staff General Sultani Makenga has been under UN, US and EU sanctions since November and December 2012, and that General Baudouin Ngaruye, commander of the first operational sector, and Innocent Kaina are under the same three regimes since the same period.
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; page says 'selon un rapport publié en avril 2026 par le Congo Research Group (CRG) et le Center on International Cooperation (CIC)'. Sanction dates are the outlet's summary of the CRG report, not checked against the sanctions lists. excerpt_en flag is a translation artefact.
claims.researcher_note: Relay of CRG/CIC; the underlying report is cited separately. CRG/CIC's own sanctions table is garbled in text extraction for Ngaruye (shows 'United Nati...' truncated), so the 'three regimes' claim for Ngaruye rests on this article.

claims.text: Afrikarabia reported that Willy Ngoma, military spokesperson of the AFC/M23, was killed by a drone strike and that, according to first indications, the drone attack was launched by the Congolese army at Rubaya, Masisi territory; Actualite.cd, in an article on a CRG/CIC report, described him as former spokesperson and military commander of M23 and wrote that he was killed on 24 February 2026 in a drone strike near the Rubaya mining site, North Kivu.
claims.actor_as_written: Drone strike attributed to the Congolese army per Afrikarabia's 'first indications'; target AFC/M23 military spokesperson Willy Ngoma
claims.verification_note: All three excerpts exact. Attribution to the Congolese army kept as Afrikarabia's 'first indications', not a finding. Publication date of Afrikarabia removed; the 24 February 2026 date is Actualite.cd's. Afrikarabia also notes Kinshasa had issued no communiqué. Afrikarabia wrote that Kinshasa had published no communiqué on the strike ('Aucun communiqué n’a été publié pour l’instant'). EU sanction date differs between the outlets (Afrikarabia: December 2022; Actualite.cd: April 2024).
claims.researcher_note: Afrikarabia (Christophe Rigaud) calls Ngoma 'porte-parole militaire'; Actualite.cd/CRG calls him 'ancien porte-parole et commandant militaire'. EU sanction date differs: Afrikarabia says December 2022; Actualite.cd/CRG says April 2024 (UN Feb 2024). Kinshasa and AFC/M23 reactions not found in this unit; see gaps. The page says 'ce mardi' and is dated 24 Feb 2026 (a Tuesday); RFI (via Facebook, not fetched) reports 'night of 23 to 24 February'.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 5 February 2025 AFC/M23 announced new administrative appointments, designating Bahati Musanga Joseph (also known as Bahati Erasto) as governor of North Kivu, with Manzi Ngarambe Willy and Amani Bahati Shaddrak as deputy governors.
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt from S/2025/446 annex; names as printed. The same report also prints 'Joseph Bahati Musanga (alias Bahati Erasto)'; Radio Okapi prints 'Jean Bahati Musanga'.
claims.researcher_note: Same report notes (para. 98, video footage) that on 6 February 2025 Bahati Erasto spoke in Kinyarwanda justifying house-to-house operations. Kinshasa's spokesperson Patrick Muyaya was quoted in a Facebook post (not fetched) calling the appointment information false; to be sourced from a news outlet.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 conducted armed night raids on hospitals in Goma, targeting Heal Africa on 1 March and CBCA Ndosho on 3 March (2025) in operations tracking FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR combatants who had not surrendered, and that a total of 164 patients were abducted, 48 from Heal Africa and 116 from CBCA Ndosho; it reported that AFC/M23 leaders Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka and 'General' Makenga publicly denied responsibility.
claims.place_as_written: Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals, Goma, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact (S/2025/446 para. 105); 'armed night raids' is on the same page ('AFC/M23 conducted armed night raids on hospitals in Goma'). The Group adds that male caregivers were briefly detained and released, and that on 5 March an AFC/M23 search operation targeted Virunga Hospital in Goma. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: AFC/M23 leaders' public denials (para. 107) 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-003: Same paragraph set as r1-GOE-055: the Group records AFC/M23's public denials (para. 107), which this claim omits (check 8). Also overlaps r1-GOE-055 almost entirely; editor may merge.; excerpt-support: added para. 107 (public denials by Bisimwa, Kanyuka and Makenga) as an excerpt
claims.researcher_note: Year 2025 from the report (para. 105 and following paragraph on April 2025). Report adds that male caregivers were briefly detained and released and that on 5 March AFC/M23 searched Virunga Hospital, arresting an unconfirmed number of suspected FARDC elements.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on the night of 4 to 5 April 2025 armed AFC/M23 elements entered the MSF-supported Kyeshero Hospital compound in Goma in search of FARDC elements and opened fire within the grounds, killing one person, injuring three and assaulting two staff members.
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt (S/2025/446 para. 106); figures are spelled out in the excerpt (one, three, two). The Group adds that soldiers did not enter the ward but bullets struck the treatment areas.
claims.researcher_note: The report says the soldiers did not enter the hospital ward but bullets struck treatment areas. Victims unnamed in the report.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that, following the March 2025 hospital incidents, Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka and 'General' Makenga issued public denials of responsibility, claiming compliance with international humanitarian law and an aim of securing hospitals from 'infiltrated rogue combatants'; the Group wrote that witnesses confirmed no weapons were found in the hospitals.
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt (S/2025/446 para. 107) carries the denials; the rebuttal sentence is on the same page and paragraph (clause_support).
claims.researcher_note: Excerpt gives the denial; the Group's counter-finding ('witnesses confirmed that no weapons were found in the hospitals') is the next sentence of the report. Original AFC/M23 communiqués (annex 52) not fetched; to be sourced from the party channel or press.

claims.text: According to Radio Okapi, a communiqué published on Friday 7 March 2025 by the DRC Ministry of Justice announced a reward of 5.000.000 USD for anyone enabling the arrest of the 'convicts' (condamnés) Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa and Sultani Makenga.
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; figure written as the excerpt prints it. 'Convicts' is the communiqué's word, quoted. The same communiqué, per Radio Okapi, offers a further 4.000.000$ for information leading to the arrest of 'complices en fuite' Perrot Luwara and Irenge Baelenge.
claims.researcher_note: The same article reports a further USD 4,000,000 reward for 'accomplices en fuite' Perrot Luwara and Irenge Baelenge (not in the excerpt) and that a Kinshasa military court issued an international arrest warrant for Nangaa on 5 February (year implied 2025). Date 7 March is the communiqué day printed on the page.

claims.text: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, the M23 Headquarters Regiment as now deployed to South Kivu, with its 1st battalion deployed in the Uvira operation and its 2nd battalion deployed to Minembwe.
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpts from the CRG/CIC annex.
claims.researcher_note: Annex table text; the rows are adjacent in extraction. Corroborates, as a different source, the M23 role in the Uvira offensive; the RDF role is covered by the UN GoE via Actualite.cd.

claims.text: Citing a UN communiqué, the news site reported that the Security Council's 1533 sanctions committee approved on 14 July the listing of six individuals and two entities, among them Corneille Nangaa, presented as head of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC/M23), and Colonel John Imani Nzenze, M23 intelligence chief, sanctioned for alleged involvement in planning and supporting the rebel movement's activities.
claims.place_as_written: UN Security Council, New York (listing); targets are AFC/M23 leaders
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact. Communiqué date removed from statement. 'Présumée' kept as 'alleged'. Outlet name dropped from the statement text only because the number check reads '7sur7' as a figure; the source is shown with the claim. Date discrepancy: 7sur7.cd gives 14 July for the committee's approval (communiqué of 16 July); Radio Okapi says the committee added the names on Thursday 16 July 2026. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi (17 July 2026) says the committee added the names 'jeudi 16 juillet 2026' (the announcement day); 7sur7 gives approval 14 July and the UN communiqué 16 July. The UN press release (press.un.org/en/2026/sc16416.doc.htm) could not be fetched by the page helper. Radio Okapi's list of the six also names Sébastien Uwimbabazi and Gustave Kubwayo (FDLR), Muhammed Lumisa (ADF), Charles Sematama (Twirwaneho).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts, citing its previous reports, reported in July 2025 that Major-General Ruki Karusisi (described as RDF Special Force Commander), Major-General Eugène Nkubito (RDF 3rd Division Commander) and Lieutenant-General Mubarakh Mugunga (RDF Army Chief of Staff) played key roles in planning and commanding military operations in North Kivu and South Kivu.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim, para. 40. Spellings as printed (Eugène, Mugunga). Para. 40 cites the Group's earlier reports (S/2023/431, S/2023/990, S/2024/432) for this finding, so it is not limited to 2025. Posts as printed in July 2025; S/2026/466 gives Gashugi as Special Operations Force Commander since 15 March 2025 and Muganga as Chief of Defence Staff. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: finding cites the Group's previous reports 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-005: Time slippage: the verification note says para. 40 rests on the Group's 2023-2024 reports, and S/2026/466 gives a different Special Operations Force commander from 15 March 2025. Dated 2025-07, the statement reads as a 2025 finding with current posts. The amendment says the finding draws on earlier reports and that the posts are as the July 2025 report prints them.; excerpt-support: added para. 40 with its citations of the Group's earlier reports (S/2023/431, S/2023/990, S/2024/432) as an excerpt; note that para. 41 of the same report names Major-General Vincent Nyakarundi as Army Chief of Staff, while para. 40 gives Mugunga that post
claims.researcher_note: Name spellings as printed (report prints 'Mugunga'; later sources print 'Muganga'). Excerpt contains a footnote marker (28) as on the page.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that Rwanda deployed over 8,000 RDF troops, including special forces, and transferred heavy, advanced military equipment to the frontlines on the Ruzizi Plain, including jamming systems, BM21-type multi-barrel rocket launchers, GPS-guided 120 mm mortars, kamikaze and first-person-view drones, aiming for a rapid victory.
claims.verification_note: Para. 76 of S/2026/466 verbatim. Date supported on the page, not in the excerpt (flagged in note). The excerpt does not itself print a date; the 2025-12 dating rests on the report's cross-reference placing paras 72-76 (this is para. 76) in the account of the capture of Uvira on 10 December 2025.
claims.researcher_note: Perpetrator-neutral deployment. The paragraph sits in the report's account of the December 2025 AFC/M23 offensive on Uvira (the report says M23 and RDF took Uvira on 10 December 2025); the excerpt itself does not name Uvira. Cross-border shelling from Kamanyola on 4-5 December is mentioned in the next sentence (not cited).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026 following sustained international diplomatic pressure, after controlling the city for over a month.
claims.verification_note: Para. 77 of S/2026/466. The two trailing clauses are on the page next to the excerpt (page-only). The Group adds that the withdrawal was followed by redeployment to adjacent areas, 'in breach of withdrawal commitments'. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc2: S/2026/466 para. 77 supports the statement in full, but the stored excerpt omits 'for over a month' and 'following sustained international diplomatic pressure'; the full contiguous sentence is added.
claims.researcher_note: The report also says the withdrawal was followed by redeployment to adjacent areas.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 2 February 2026 approximately 25 trucks carrying RDF troops departed from Bugarama and Nyangezi in Rwanda, arriving in Kamanyola before continuing toward Luvungi and Sange along the RN5.
claims.verification_note: Annex text of S/2026/466 verbatim (the page wraps '25' to the next line).
claims.researcher_note: Report cites intelligence, civil society, researchers and diplomatic sources.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that as of mid-February 2026 RDF deployments in South Kivu were approximately 1,800 troops along the Ruzizi Plain-Moyens Plateaux axis, 800 in the Hauts Plateaux, 1,800 along the Ngweshe-Mwenga axis and an undetermined number elsewhere, including towards Fizi.
claims.place_as_written: South Kivu (Ruzizi Plain, Moyens and Hauts Plateaux, Ngweshe-Mwenga, Fizi)
claims.verification_note: Annex text of S/2026/466 verbatim; figures match.
claims.researcher_note: Date given as 'mid-February 2026'.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that the US sanctioned the Rwandan army and four commanders (Maj. Gen. Vincent Nyakarundi, Maj. Gen. Ruki Karusisi, Gen. Mubarakh Muganga and Brig. Gen. Stanislas Gashugi), and that military and UN sources told HRW several thousand Rwandan soldiers, including special forces, crossed into the DRC in the weeks before the December Uvira offensive.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact; excerpt_en translations are faithful (flag triggered by sentence-initial capitals and 'UN' for 'onusiennes'). 'Maj. Gen./Brig. Gen.' are translations of the printed ranks. The 2 March 2026 announcement date is printed on the HRW page but not in the stored excerpts. HRW gives Nyakarundi's rank as 'général de division' (Maj. Gen.); S/2026/466 calls him 'General'.
claims.researcher_note: The date of the US announcement (2 March 2026) is from the HRW text ('Le 2 mars 2026, le gouvernement des États-Unis a annoncé'), which is not in the excerpts; Al Jazeera says Monday.

claims.text: AP and Reuters (as published by Al Jazeera) reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo said in a statement that the US sanctions 'unjustly' target Rwanda and 'misrepresent the reality and distort the facts of the conflict' in eastern DRC, and accused the DRC of violating the peace agreement.
claims.verification_note: Exact; byline AP and Reuters on Al Jazeera. Day of Makolo's statement not on the page, so date set to undated with the report date.
claims.researcher_note: Day of the statement not given on the page; reported 3 March 2026. Page byline: 'By AP and Reuters'.

claims.text: AP and Reuters (as published by Al Jazeera) reported that the Congolese government said it welcomed the US sanctions on the Rwandan military, describing them as 'a strong signal in support of respect' for its territorial integrity and sovereignty.
claims.verification_note: Exact; byline AP and Reuters. Day of the Congolese statement not printed; date set to undated with the report date.
claims.researcher_note: Day of the statement not given; reported 3 March 2026.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in an interview with Jeune Afrique on 26 March 2026 President Paul Kagame rejected Rwanda's responsibility in the DRC conflict, portraying it as a Congolese internal issue.
claims.verification_note: Annex 19 of S/2026/466 verbatim. The Group's summary of the interview (Annex 19); the interview itself was not opened.
claims.researcher_note: Report's summary of the interview; the interview itself was not opened. Excerpt carries a footnote marker (382).

claims.text: Human Rights Watch said the Rwandan government and M23 leaders have long rejected allegations of abuses but have not conducted investigations.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Rwanda; M23 leadership (as characterised by HRW)
claims.verification_note: Exact; attribution to HRW kept. HRW's characterisation, not a Rwandan or M23 statement.
claims.researcher_note: HRW's characterisation, not a quote of a Rwandan statement; no direct Rwandan response to this report found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that at least four people were killed and valuables destroyed in clashes at Misisi and Lulimba, Fizi territory, between two Wazalendo factions: the CNCCP of commander Yakutumba and the FABB of Ngoma Nzito.
claims.place_as_written: Misisi and Lulimba, Fizi territory (Ngandja sector), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: CNCCP (Yakutumba) and FABB (Ngoma Nzito), both Wazalendo factions
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints toll, places and both factions as named. Actualite.cd prints the Yakutumba group as 'CNCCP'; Kivu Morning Post prints 'CNPSC'. Variants kept as printed; identity not asserted. The source does not say whether the dead were civilians.
claims.researcher_note: Article dated 2025-10-26 (the clash date itself is not stated; KMP 30 Oct says fighting began 25 Oct). The page prints the Yakutumba group as 'CNCCP' while Kivu Morning Post and the UN Group of Experts print 'CNPSC'; reviewer should reconcile. Victims are not necessarily civilians: the source does not say.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the Fizi territory administrator, Sammy Kalonji Badibanga, confirmed the fighting and gave as its main cause the decision of Yakutumba's men to remove illegal barriers set up in the area.
claims.place_as_written: Misisi and Lulimba, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints name, post and stated cause. Cause as stated by the territory administrator; the other faction's account not found.
claims.researcher_note: Official local attribution of cause; the other faction's account was not found.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that for more than a week fighting had opposed the Wazalendo of the Coalition nationale du peuple pour la souveraineté du Congo (CNPSC) of William Amuri Yakutumba to certain elements of the Biloze Bishambuke self-defence forces of Kalembe Ngoma Nzito, and quoted an elected official from Uvira, president of the defence and security commission of the provincial assembly, as saying the clashes began on 25 October 2025 and caused loss of life.
claims.actor_as_written: CNPSC (William Amuri Yakutumba); Biloze Bishambuke (Kalembe Ngoma Nzito)
claims.verification_note: The draft attributed the first passage (outlet narration) to the deputy; split narration from the deputy's account and named the deputy, printed on the page. Name variants as printed: 'Ngoma Nzito' (Actualite.cd), 'Kalembe Ngoma Nzito' (Kivu Morning Post), 'Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito' (Enquete.cd); identity not asserted. 'CNPSC' here vs 'CNCCP' (Actualite.cd). The page names the elected official as provincial deputy Bubasha Tangania David and places the violence at Misisi, Fizi territory.
claims.researcher_note: Two excerpts from the same page. Corroborates Actualite.cd 26 Oct 2025 (separate claim) on the parties and adds the 25 Oct start. Name spellings differ across outlets: 'Ngoma Nzito' (Actualite.cd), 'Kalembe Ngoma Nzito' (KMP), 'Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito' (Enquete.cd), 'Delphin Ngomanzito' (UN Group of Experts); whether they are one person is for the reviewer to check, not asserted here.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing an administrative official at Mwenga Centre, a provisional toll of at least eight dead and five wounded in clashes on Thursday 18 September 2025 between two Wazalendo groups in Mwenga territory.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints toll, date, place and the official as source. Provisional toll from an unnamed administrative official; victims not stated to be civilians.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet; provisional toll from an unnamed administrative official. Victims not stated to be civilians.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Mwenga clashes opposed fighters loyal to self-proclaimed general Malaika and those of general Nyakiliba, and that the pro-Malaika Wazalendo were supported by elements of the Foka Maïk group and of the army.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo of self-proclaimed general Malaika (with Foka Maïk group and army elements) vs Wazalendo of general Nyakiliba
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints names and support as stated. 'de l'armée' without unit; 'Malaika' is described as a self-proclaimed general.
claims.researcher_note: The source says 'de l'armée' without naming a unit. 'Foka Maïk' is printed as a group name; compare existing claim UC-FARDC-020 (Actualite.cd) naming Albert Foka Maik as a former provincial minister, whether the same is not stated by either source.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the root of the Mwenga clashes was the removal, by the fighters of Malaika and of Foka Maïk, of barriers that Nyakiliba had set up on the RN2.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo of Nyakiliba, Malaika and Foka Maïk
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints the cause as stated.
claims.researcher_note: Illegal taxation barriers are a recurrent cause of Wazalendo infighting (see also the Fizi clash, 25 Oct 2025). The page does not call the barriers illegal or taxing.

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported that the new commander of the Sokola 1 Grand Nord and Front Nord operational sector took up his functions on Wednesday 23 July 2025 in Beni, North Kivu, and that general Mugisa Muleka replaced major-general Nyembo Abdallah, who had led the sector.
claims.place_as_written: Beni, North Kivu (Sokola 1 Grand Nord and Front Nord)
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC Sokola 1 Grand Nord: Gen. Mugisa Muleka (incoming), Maj.-Gen. Nyembo Abdallah (outgoing)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints all clauses; the '7' flag comes from the outlet name 7sur7.cd.
claims.researcher_note: Spelling 'Mugisa Muleka' (7sur7.cd, Actualite.cd) vs 'Mugisha Muleka' and 'Joseph Kisembo Muleke' in search-result titles of other outlets (not opened). Existing roster has no entry for this sector command.

claims.text: Congo-Press (MediaCongo Press) reported that major-general Nyembo Abdallah was named commander of the Sukola 1 Grand Nord operational sector and the Front Nord in North Kivu, an official designation announced on 22 May 2025 by the FARDC chief of general staff.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu (Sukola 1 Grand Nord and Front Nord)
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC Sukola 1 Grand Nord: Maj.-Gen. Nyembo Abdallah
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints appointment and announcement date.
claims.researcher_note: Page dated 2025-05-26. The same page says he had three years of experience leading military operations in Ituri and earlier served in Sukola 1 as deputy commander for operations and intelligence (not separately claimed).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC supported brigadier general Olivier Gasita, contested by the Wazalendo and struggling to take up his functions as deputy commander of the 33rd military region in charge of military operations and intelligence at Uvira, South Kivu.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city, South Kivu (33rd military region)
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC 33rd military region: Gen. Olivier Gasita; Wazalendo (contesting)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints support, contestation and role as Actualite.cd states it. Accounts of Gasita's role differ: Actualite.cd and FARDC spokesperson Ekenge say deputy commander of the 33rd military region in charge of operations and intelligence; Radio Okapi (23 Oct 2025) says he had been sent to fill the vacant post of operational-sector commander. Both stated; not reconciled.
claims.researcher_note: Role differs between sources: Actualite.cd and spokesperson Ekenge say deputy commander (ops and intelligence) of the 33rd military region; Radio Okapi (23 Oct 2025) says he had been sent to fill the vacant post of operational-sector commander. Existing claim UC-FARDC-007 (SOS Médias Burundi) says he remained in post after the October reshuffle; Radio Okapi 23 Oct 2025 links an article titled 'Le général Olivier Gasita quitte Uvira sur fond de manifestations populaires' (not opened). Contradiction left for reviewer.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, at a press conference in Kinshasa on Saturday 06 September 2025, FARDC spokesperson major-general Sylvain Ekenge said that an officer no longer belongs to his community but to the whole nation.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints date, place, speaker and statement.
claims.researcher_note: Statement is Ekenge's defence of Gasita against Wazalendo contestation. Rendered via Actualite.cd.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Sylvain Ekenge said on 6 September 2025 that no other presidential ordinance had relieved Gasita of his function and that he remained deputy commander of the 33rd military region, in charge of military operations and intelligence.
claims.verification_note: Quoted speech printed on the page; date and speaker from the first excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Quoted speech as printed by Actualite.cd. Same press conference as the preceding claim.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, reacting to Wazalendo allegations that Gasita was close to Rwanda and to the AFC/M23 rebellion, Sylvain Ekenge said Gasita would have another superior in charge of the whole region.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints the reaction to the Wazalendo allegation. The allegation that Gasita was close to Rwanda and the AFC/M23 is the Wazalendo's, reported by Actualite.cd; not established.
claims.researcher_note: This is the FARDC account of an allegation by Wazalendo (an allegation, not established). Radio Okapi (9 Sep 2025, already cited elsewhere) reports Wazalendo suspected him of being a double agent of the M23.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that general Olivier Gasita, sent to fill the vacant post of operational sector commander, had been violently contested by the population in demonstrations that resulted in deaths, many wounded and significant material damage.
claims.actor_as_written: Demonstrators in Uvira; FARDC (Gasita contested); perpetrator of the deaths not attributed
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints the passage; no date or figure, no perpetrator of the deaths. Radio Okapi describes Gasita's post as operational-sector commander; Actualite.cd and the FARDC spokesperson say deputy commander of the 33rd military region (ops and intelligence). Both stated. The page does not say who caused the deaths.
claims.researcher_note: Retrospective mention in a 23 Oct 2025 article; the page gives no date for the demonstrations. Radio Okapi 9 Sep 2025 (cited by UV-2025Q3) gives 'at least seven' dead (provisional); this page gives no figure. Role differs from Actualite.cd (deputy commander of the 33rd military region).

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Iamba health centre at Makobola, in the Nundu health zone, Tanganyika sector, Fizi territory, was pillaged on 30 December, and that, according to concordant sources, the FARDC and Wazalendo militiamen were allegedly responsible.
claims.place_as_written: Iamba health centre, Makobola, Nundu health zone, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and Wazalendo (alleged, per concordant sources cited by the outlet)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints the pillage, date and conditional attribution. Attribution to FARDC and Wazalendo is by unnamed 'concordant sources' (conditional 'seraient'); the page says the Congolese army had not yet reacted. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. Regraded C->B on independent, non-partisan corroboration. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet (Goma-based) citing unnamed 'sources concordantes'; year taken from the article date (2025-12-31). The article says the Congolese army had not yet reacted to the accusations.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that structures pillaged at Makobola included the Makobola health centre and a recently built hospital, and quoted another local source as saying that all the equipment of the new building of this large hospital, built but not yet operational, was pillaged.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and Wazalendo (alleged by the outlet's sources in the preceding report; this passage does not itself name the perpetrators)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints both structures and the quote. This passage does not name perpetrators; the page attributes the pillage to FARDC and Wazalendo per concordant sources. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Date approximate: the page puts the looting around the night of 29-30 Dec 2025 in another passage; this excerpt gives no date. Perpetrators are named elsewhere on the page, not in this passage.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, besides the pillage at Makobola, cases of rape were reported, as lamented by civil society actors who asked to remain anonymous; the same passage says that, according to concordant sources, the FARDC and Wazalendo militiamen were allegedly responsible for the pillage.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source for the rapes (the pillage is attributed to FARDC and Wazalendo)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints the rape reports and the pillage attribution; statement keeps them separate. The page does not attribute the rapes to any party and gives no number of survivors; the pillage is attributed to FARDC and Wazalendo by concordant sources. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: The page does not give a number of survivors ('Il est difficile de connaître le bilan exact des femmes violées' in a later passage) and does not say who committed the rapes. Anonymous civil-society sources; uncorroborated. Survivors unnamed.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Mwenga territory civil society forces vives, meeting on Monday 16 March 2026, denounced the harassment committed by FARDC and Wazalendo elements.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and Wazalendo elements (alleged by the territory civil society)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints date, body and denunciation. Civil-society allegation; no FARDC or Wazalendo reply found.
claims.researcher_note: Statement by a civil-society body as reported by one local outlet; no FARDC or Wazalendo reply found.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing the Mwenga civil society, that at the start of March at Musika a nurse was robbed of 200 000 FC, his android phone and his boots, and that on 12 March a young boy was shot ('fusillé par balle') at Ilinda and on the 13th another was shot ('fusillé') at Kibumba; the civil society gave these as examples ('À titre d'exemple') after denouncing harassment by FARDC and Wazalendo elements, but the passage does not name the perpetrator of each incident.
claims.place_as_written: Musika, Ilinda and Kibumba, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by this passage (civil society's complaint targets FARDC and Wazalendo generally)
claims.verification_note: Removed year not printed in the excerpt; kept 'shot' for the second boy as printed ('un autre fusillé'). The page does not attribute these specific incidents to FARDC or Wazalendo. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: examples given after denouncing FARDC and Wazalendo harassment 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-023: The statement says the 12 March Ilinda victim was 'shot dead', but 'fusillé par balle' does not by itself say the victim died (Radio Okapi's account of the same incidents uses 'fusillé' and the verifier there declined to say killed); the input's own English gloss over-translates. Also, Radio Okapi identifies the 12 March Ilinda victim as Dodos Ngama, 30, a discrepancy with 'jeune garçon'.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): examples given after denouncing FARDC and Wazalendo harassment | replaced 'does not attribute these specific incidents to any party': the page gives them as examples of FARDC and Wazalendo abuses
claims.researcher_note: The excerpt follows the sentence in which the civil society denounces FARDC and Wazalendo; the page does not state that these specific shootings or the robbery were committed by them. The nurse is a health worker but the page does not say the robbery was linked to his work, so no health tag. 'fusillé par balle' is translated as 'shot dead' per the page's wording. Victims unnamed.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Shabunda civil society, which denounced several recent deadly incidents, said a citizen was beaten to death by Wazalendo elements and that three children aged 10 to 15 were hit by bullets as they left school, one of whom died on the spot.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo elements (alleged by civil society for the beating; the shooting of the children is not explicitly attributed)
claims.verification_note: Passage sits within the civil-society president's quoted account on the page. Allegation by Shabunda civil society; the shooting of the children is not attributed to a party in the passage. Incidents undated.
claims.researcher_note: Date: the article (2026-01-27) says activities have been paralysed 'depuis ce lundi'; the incidents themselves are undated (date computed from weekday and publication date for the paralysis only, so treat as approximate). The children are minors, unnamed. Single local outlet citing the civil society president.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the president of Shabunda civil society, Maître Isaac Kibunda, said that the armed Wazalendo, supposed to support the FARDC on the front lines, were committing serious abuses against the civilian population.
claims.actor_as_written: Shabunda civil society (Isaac Kibunda) on Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints name, post and allegation.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from the weekday 'ce lundi' and the publication date 2026-01-27 (the page does not give the date of the call). The allegation is the civil-society leader's, not established.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported strong tension on the morning of Friday 10 October 2025 in Kamituga, Mwenga territory, caused by a demonstration of residents demanding the immediate departure of Wazalendo fighters accused of multiple abuses in the region.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints date, place and demand.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post quoted the Mwenga territory civil society as giving, for the unrest in Kamituga, a provisional toll of several victims, including PNC elements and a FARDC soldier, as well as wounded civilians and the pillage of shops and phone shops.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed in this passage (the demonstration targeted Wazalendo)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints the civil-society toll as quoted. 'plusieurs victimes' without separating dead from wounded; looters not named.
claims.researcher_note: The page says 'plusieurs victimes' without separating dead from wounded; the earlier part of the quote (not in the excerpt) describes heavy and light weapons fire from about 23:00 on 9 Oct to the morning of 10 Oct. Perpetrators of the looting not named.

claims.text: Enquete.cd reported, citing several local sources, that Wazalendo movement leader James Fyeka Adui, arrested in Uvira on 5 September, had been transferred to Kinshasa some days earlier, and that he is accused, according to concordant sources, of involvement in the murder of a civilian in Uvira in May 2026; the outlet added that these accusations had not yet been publicly confirmed in detail by judicial authorities.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo leader James Fyeka Adui; security services (arresting body not named in this passage)
claims.verification_note: Added the page's caveat that judicial authorities had not confirmed the accusations. An accusation by local sources, unconfirmed by judicial authorities; not a finding of responsibility.
claims.researcher_note: The same page says the accusations have not been publicly confirmed in detail by judicial authorities. Presumption of innocence applies; the allegation is relayed by local sources. The victim of the May 2026 murder is not named. Article dated 2026-09-29; year of the arrest taken from the article date and from La Prunelle RDC (5 Sept 2026).

claims.text: La Prunelle RDC reported that James « Fyeka Adui » was arrested on 5 September 2026 by the security services in Uvira, and that on 6 September contradictory information had circulated about his release, some sources saying he had been released after his hearing and others that he remained detained.
claims.actor_as_written: Security services (unnamed); Wazalendo commander James « Fyeka Adui »
claims.verification_note: Both clauses printed on the page.
claims.researcher_note: La Prunelle RDC cites the outlet Averticom for part of the background (originating_source set accordingly). The page also mentions an unsigned communiqué attributed to self-defence groups demanding his release and threatening to paralyse Uvira; its authenticity was not established independently (per the page). Gunfire in Uvira on the morning of Wednesday (article dated 2026-09-16) is linked by the outlet to the tensions.

claims.text: Enquete.cd reported that Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito, head of the Wazalendo special unit, issued a firm call on Monday 5 May 2026 in Uvira for Wazalendo fighters to withdraw from urban areas and join the front lines, after meeting Jacques Kongolo, adviser to the President of the Republic.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page; 'responsable de l'unité spéciale' is the article's description of Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito. The page prints 'lundi 5 mai 2026' although 5 May 2026 was a Tuesday; kept as printed. Name variants (Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito, Kalembe Ngoma Nzito, Ngoma Nzito) kept as printed; identity not asserted.
claims.researcher_note: Weekday inconsistency: the page prints 'lundi 5 mai 2026' but 5 May 2026 was a Tuesday; the printed date is kept. Wazalendo are a non-state/de facto party; classified here as a party statement. The name is printed 'Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito' here, 'Delphin Ngomanzito' by the UN Group of Experts and 'Ngoma Nzito' / 'Kalembe Ngoma Nzito' by Actualite.cd and Kivu Morning Post; identity not asserted.

claims.text: Enquete.cd reported that a three-day moratorium was granted to Wazalendo fighters in Uvira to leave the city and return to combat positions, with only commanders allowed to circulate in the urban area in strictly limited numbers, and that any breach would expose offenders to the sanctions of military regulations.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo special unit (Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito, per the article's framing)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints the moratorium in the passive voice; grantor not stated and not inferred. The page does not say who granted the moratorium.
claims.researcher_note: The passage is in the passive voice; the page does not say who granted the moratorium (Wazalendo leader, FARDC or provincial authority). A YouTube/Instagram snippet (not opened) attributes the moratorium to Ngomanzito. Recorded as reported, without attributing the grant.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing several concordant local sources, that Wazalendo allied to the FARDC, under the command of Jams Mutayomba and Noah Maachano, had reportedly also retaken on Monday morning several positions previously held by the AFC/M23, with Nyakigano, Nkokwe and Kashovu, around Kasake, notably cited.
claims.place_as_written: Nyakigano, Nkokwe and Kashovu near Kasake, Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo allied to FARDC (Jams Mutayomba, Noah Maachano)
claims.verification_note: Restored the source's conditional ('auraient'). Radio Okapi says the available information does not allow independent establishment of control. AFC/M23 account not found. 2026-10-29: control edited: Frontline data fix (FRONTLINE_NOTES.md): control.held_by names only the holder (for a withdrawal, the side withdrawing), so the side class is not 'both sides named'; the other side stays in the statement. Wording from the stored excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from the weekday 'ce lundi' and the article date 2026-10-05. The same article says the available information does not allow independent establishment of the evolution of control. Names are printed 'Jams Mutayomba' and 'Noah Maachano'. AFC/M23's account not found.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, after fighting reported on Sunday in Kalehe territory, South Kivu, that sources close to the Congolese army claimed the Wazalendo had retaken several villages in the Ziralo grouping, notably Katale, Shanje and Chambombo, near Lumbishi.
claims.place_as_written: Katale, Shanje and Chambombo, Ziralo grouping, near Lumbishi, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (per sources close to the Congolese army)
claims.verification_note: Kalehe/South Kivu are not in the excerpt; supplied from the page's Kalehe paragraph. Claim by sources close to the FARDC; Radio Okapi says control could not be independently established.
claims.researcher_note: The page gives no date for this claim; the article is dated 2026-10-05 and refers to Kalehe fighting 'dimanche' (date not computed here). The article cautions that available information does not allow independent confirmation. Compare existing claim UC-FARDC-015 on arms handed to Wazalendo at Lumbishi.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that two people died in an exchange of fire in the night of Sunday 24 May in the town of Runingu, Uvira territory, between two Wazalendo groups, each led by its own commander, said to disagree over a question not yet elucidated.
claims.actor_as_written: Two Wazalendo groups, each under its own commander (not named by the source)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints toll, night, place and the two groups. The page does not say whether the dead were civilians or fighters.
claims.researcher_note: Year (2026) from the article date 2026-05-25. The page does not say whether the dead were civilians or fighters. Commanders unnamed.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Désiré Kisuba Ngabo, until then deputy mayor, became mayor of Goma replacing Julienne Katembo Ndalieni, who was named administrator of Lubero territory, in a reshuffle of administrative cadres signed on 8 April 2026 by the governor of North Kivu, Bahati Musanga Erasto.
claims.verification_note: Name, post and date printed by the excerpt; name variant kept as printed and flagged. excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful. Discrepancy: this article (byline Kethia Rugamika) names the outgoing Goma mayor 'Julienne Katembo Ndalieni'; Kivu Morning Post's 24 November 2025 article names the Goma mayor 'Katembo Julien Dalieni'. Both forms are kept as printed; the sources do not settle the spelling or first name. KMP cites provincial order n°011/014/CAB/GP-NK/2026.
claims.researcher_note: Discrepancy to surface: KMP names the outgoing mayor 'Julienne Katembo Ndalieni' and dates the signing 8 April 2026; KMP's November 2025 article calls the mayor 'Katembo Julien Dalieni' and the UN Group of Experts (S/2026/466, already cited by other claims) is reported to give 'Katembo Ndalieni Julien' and 9 April 2026 as the order's date. One person, spelling and date differ by source.

claims.text: Actu26 reported that on the Monday before its report violence at Rumangabo was marked by reported looting of property, and that people were wounded by gunfire on the Goma-Rutshuru road; the page does not name the perpetrators.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo and Goma-Rutshuru road (Rutshuru, North Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Supported; date computed, so flagged approximate. Figures flag '26' is the outlet's name. Date derived: 'lundi dernier' in an article of Wednesday 25 March 2026, i.e. 23 March 2026. No perpetrator, figures or victims named.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date (Monday before Wednesday 25 March 2026 = 23 March). Figures and perpetrators not given.

claims.text: Actualité.cd reported that Uvira city mayor Kifara Kapenda Kiki, who had returned to Uvira on Thursday, said that those who had occupied the city had left Uvira but 'ils ne sont pas loin', and acknowledged abuses ('dérives') both within the FARDC and among the wazalendo self-defence groups during the fighting.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC (Uvira city mayor)
claims.verification_note: Supported; 'acknowledged dérives' is Actualité.cd's paraphrase of the mayor, followed by his quote. Date derived from 'jeudi' in an article of Friday 23 January 2026. The mayor also said the rebels had looted everything and targeted State symbols, and that some people posing as soldiers looted the population (his account).
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('jeudi') and publication date 23 January 2026 (Friday). The mayor's term in office predates the M23 capture; he is already named in UV-2025Q3. Gives the Kinshasa-side civilian account; the M23 side's account of Uvira is covered by other units.

claims.text: The US State Department said on 2 June 2026 that it was designating John Imani Nzenze, chief of intelligence for the Rwanda-backed M23, 'an armed group that has committed killings, serious human rights abuses, and attacks on civilians in eastern DRC', and Gustave Kubwayo, commander of an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit, saying the FDLR had 'committed sexual violence'.
claims.verification_note: Supported; the date is printed in the page header, not the excerpts. Press statement by spokesperson Thomas 'Tommy' Pigott. Its allegations are made against the groups (M23, FDLR), not against the two named men individually.
claims.researcher_note: Second, State Department source for the designation that claim UC-M23#3 attributes to the Treasury press release; the State Department statement attributes allegations to the groups, not to the two named men individually. Nzenze is also described by the UN Group of Experts (S/2026/466, cited by other claims) as AFC/M23 Director of Intelligence and liaison with humanitarian actors.

claims.text: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Colonel Justin (“Zero Three”) as commander of the 2nd Brigade of the 2nd Operational Sector, noting that he had 'now gone as a liaison to Minembwe'.
claims.verification_note: Printed in the 2nd-sector table. Territory Fizi for Minembwe is geography, not printed. Single origin: a table in a CRG/NYU CIC research annex ('as of December 2025'); the table does not state its own sources. Names, ranks and call signs as CRG prints them. No surname given by the source.
claims.researcher_note: Surname not given by the source. Minembwe is in Fizi/Mwenga highlands, South Kivu (the excerpt does not say which territory). Compare UN claims on AFC/M23 reinforcements to Minembwe (Gakufe, Ndabagaza) in UCD-M23-COMMAND. Single-origin table in a research-group annex (not a UN or court document); the report's source of the table is not stated in the excerpt. Names and ranks as printed; spellings may differ from other sources.

claims.text: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Colonel Kamanzi Rubens (“Romeo Kilo”) as commander of the Headquarters Regiment (now deployed to South Kivu), Lt Col “Romeo Delta” as commander of its 1st battalion (deployed in the Uvira operation) and Lt Col Badege as commander of its 2nd battalion (deployed to Minembwe).
claims.verification_note: All three rows printed verbatim in the High Command table. Single origin: a table in a CRG/NYU CIC research annex ('as of December 2025'); the table does not state its own sources. Names, ranks and call signs as CRG prints them. 'Romeo Kilo' and 'Romeo Delta' are call signs as printed; Lt Col 'Romeo Delta' has no name in the source.
claims.researcher_note: Adds the commanders to r1-UC-M23-028 (units and deployments only). 'Romeo Delta' is a call-sign as printed. Kamanzi Rubens is a different person from FARDC Brigadier General François Kamanzi who joined the FRN (UCD-M23-COMMAND). Single-origin table in a research-group annex (not a UN or court document); the report's source of the table is not stated in the excerpt. Names and ranks as printed; spellings may differ from other sources.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the civil society group Forces vives of the Kaniola groupement (Walungu, South Kivu), in a letter to BCNUDH, MONUSCO and the ICRC, accused AFC/M23 officer Charles Kagigi of establishing a regime of terror, and said that over four days it documented several crimes, including a taxi driver from Kalengera (Zigashane Mashali) extorted of 30 000 Congolese francs (13 USD) and beaten to death on 23 September at Kashanja, and three civilians returning from a Leopards match (Birhalugirakulimushi Jules, Kashokwire Kulimushi Isaac and Bizimana Ciraza) summarily executed on 24 September at Kaniola. The group also said that 'colonel Kagigi' publicly swore to 'raze the Kaniola groupement' and demanded his departure.
claims.place_as_written: Kaniola and Kashanja (Kaniola groupement), Walungu, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 officer Charles Kagigi (alleged by civil society)
claims.verification_note: Draft said the group documented 'killings' over four days; the page says 'plusieurs crimes' (the four days include a torture case on 21 Sept). Narrowed to 'several crimes'. All names printed in excerpts. excerpt_en flags are sentence-initial capitals (The/In/On), translations are of the excerpts alone. Grade C: single local civil-society origin. Allegation by a local civil-society group in a letter, relayed by Radio Okapi; not independently confirmed; no AFC/M23 response found. The source's own label for these acts ('crimes de guerre') is the civil society's characterisation. Year 2026 taken from the article date (26/09/2026). The article also reports (outside the excerpts) two teachers tortured at Nzibira-Luntukulu on 21 September, not named.
claims.researcher_note: Allegation by a civil-society group, relayed by Radio Okapi (Bukavu-based UN-founded radio); not independently confirmed, no AFC/M23 response found. Same text republished by mediacongo.net (26 Sept 2026) and summarised by Agasaro Network; not independent. The article also says (not in an excerpt) that on 21 September two teachers were tortured at Nzibira-Luntukulu (unnamed). Searches on 'Kagigi' at actualite.cd, 7sur7.cd and kivumorningpost.com found nothing. Kagigi is a new name in the roster; rank 'colonel' appears in the article's later sentence, 'officier' in the first. Dates 21-24 September: year 2026 inferred from the article's publication date 26/09/2026.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, since Saturday, AFC/M23 elements had taken control of Ngululu before seizing the commercial centre of Humura on Sunday, amid intensifying fighting between AFC/M23, the FARDC and the wazalendo in Masisi and Walikale territories, North Kivu.
claims.place_as_written: Ngululu and Humura, Masisi-Walikale axis, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page; publication date mar 08/09/2026 confirmed (a Tuesday), so Sat/Sun = 5/6 Sept, approximate. excerpt_en flag is a sentence-initial capital. Dates computed from weekdays ('samedi', 'dimanche') in an article published Tuesday 8 September 2026: approximate. Single outlet, no named source for this paragraph; no FARDC/Wazalendo account found.
claims.researcher_note: Weekdays only (samedi, dimanche) in a piece published Tuesday 8 Sept 2026: date computed from weekday and publication date as 2026-09-05/06. Names no commander or unit. Single outlet; FARDC/Wazalendo account of these captures not found.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23-occupied territories were divided into three 'defense zones', led respectively by 'General' Baudoin Ngaruye (first zone: Nyiragongo, Rutshuru and Lubero territories), 'Brigadier-General' Justin Gacheri Musanga (second zone: Masisi and Walikale) and 'General' Byamungu (third zone: South Kivu).
claims.place_as_written: Nyiragongo, Rutshuru, Lubero, Masisi, Walikale and South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (as named by the Group of Experts)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt found in para. 64 of S/2026/466; statement matches; ranks as printed in quotation marks. S/2026/466 places South Kivu in a third zone under 'General' Byamungu; the Group's earlier midterm report S/2025/858 described a 'second defence zone' that covered Masisi, Walikale and areas of South Kivu (Walungu, Mwenga, Minembwe). The two reports differ; both are stated. The UN text prints only the surname Byamungu; no start date for the zones is given.
claims.researcher_note: Reporting period of S/2026/466 (final report dated 2026-06-05); no start date for the zones is given. Ranks are as printed by the experts, in quotation marks. The UN text prints only the surname Byamungu for the third commander; Actualite.cd prints a different first name (see separate claim).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 8 September 'Brigadier General' Baudoin Ngaruye, commander of AFC/M23's 'First Defense Zone' covering the Goma-Rutshuru-Kanyabayonga-Kirumba axis, declared in Kirumba that AFC/M23 intended to resume hostilities aimed at capturing Butembo and Kisangani.
claims.verification_note: Removed the year from the statement because no excerpt prints it; date field kept as 2025-09-08 inferred from the report period. The excerpt (annex 22 of S/2025/858, dated 30 December 2025) prints '8 September' without a year; 2025 is inferred from the report period. The Group cites UN, intelligence and civil society sources and a video.
claims.researcher_note: Report states the year context via its section on 2025; the excerpt itself prints "8 September" without year; year inferred from the report period (S/2025/858). Sources for the declaration are UN, intelligence and civil society sources per the report footnote.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in late March AFC/M23 'Colonel' Japhet Gakufe and Charles Sematama arrived in Minembwe with an estimated 200 AFC/M23 combatants.
claims.verification_note: Removed '2025' from the statement because the excerpt does not print the year. The excerpt prints 'late March' without a year; 2025 follows from the report period (S/2025/446, 3 July 2025) and S/2025/858 later refers to this as March 2025. Rank differs between reports: 'Colonel' (S/2025/446) and 'Lieutenant-Colonel' (S/2025/858).
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/858 prints Gakufe as "Lieutenant-Colonel" (rank differs between reports). Sematama appears in a July 2026 UN sanctions listing as Twirwaneho military chief (existing claim r1-UC-M23-035). Kivu Morning Post posted on X about Colonel Gakufe at Minembwe (lead only, not cited).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that, after AFC/M23 reinforcements led by 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Japhet Gakufe reached Minembwe in March 2025, a second reinforcement led by 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Oscar Ndabagaza was blocked as it attempted to cross hostile areas before finally reaching Mikenge at the end of August.
claims.verification_note: Mikenge territory flagged by researcher: not stated on this page, so territory cleared; statement itself is supported as written. S/2025/858 (para. 53) does not state Mikenge's territory; the same paragraph places the operation in AFC/M23 and RDF support to MRDP-Twirwaneho-controlled enclaves in the Hauts Plateaux. Territory left blank rather than asserted from general knowledge. 'End of August' has no year on the page; 2025 follows from the report period. Rank 'Lieutenant-Colonel' for Gakufe here vs 'Colonel' in S/2025/446.
