claims.researcher_note: "End of August" is the report's wording; the year follows the reporting period (2025). Territory of Mikenge is not stated in the excerpt; listed as Mwenga on the strength of general knowledge only, so verifier should confirm or set to "Hauts Plateaux".

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 confiscated identification documents, including voter cards and land titles of the refugees, and publicly burned them in the presence of AFC/M23 officials, including AFC/M23 spokesperson Oscar Balinda, military spokesperson Willy Ngoma and Goma's military commander, 'Colonel' Nsanze Nzamuye Jimmy, and in the presence of local media.
claims.verification_note: Researcher flagged the undated event; placed it in the annex's May 2025 context as approximate, and narrowed the statement to the document burning, which is the event the passage reports. Undated event: the burning sits in annex 39 of S/2025/858, which concerns the transfer of 1,798 people to Rwanda on 17-22 May 2025; the passage gives no date for the burning itself. Nsanze's role as Goma military commander is referenced to an earlier report (S/2024/432, annex 24). The Group cites witnesses, UN, humanitarian and civil society sources.
claims.researcher_note: The excerpt does not date the burning; the surrounding passage concerns transfers of refugees to Rwanda in May 2025. The date shown is the report date only; verifier should place the event from the report text.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that 'General' Makenga held overall military command of AFC/M23, although his position had become increasingly contested within the movement and by Rwanda.
claims.place_as_written: AFC/M23 territory, North and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Para. 61 of S/2026/466 matches. Adds to r1-UC-M23-011 (S/2025/446): the later report adds that Makenga's position was contested within the movement and by Rwanda.
claims.researcher_note: Complements r1-UC-M23-032 (leadership reshuffle). Reporting period of S/2026/466.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that FARDC drone operations also targeted AFC/M23 leadership: on 14 January 2026 a drone strike targeted the 'Blue Cat' bar-restaurant in the Kalundu district of Uvira during a meeting of senior AFC/M23 and RDF officers, causing significant casualties, and on 7 March 2026 a strike in Mushaki targeted a house associated with a high-ranking AFC/M23 commander.
claims.place_as_written: Kalundu district, Uvira (Blue Cat bar-restaurant); Mushaki (Masisi) on 2026-03-07
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC (drone operations, per the Group of Experts)
claims.verification_note: Added the paragraph's own framing so the FARDC attribution comes from the source rather than the actor field. Para. 165 of S/2026/466. The Group gives no casualty figure for the Blue Cat strike and names no commander for Mushaki; the Mushaki sentence says 'a strike' and sits in the paragraph on FARDC drone operations.
claims.researcher_note: Casualty numbers are not given in the excerpt. Mushaki is a different location (the excerpt gives no territory). The report attributes the strikes to FARDC drone operations; no named commander is given for either strike.

claims.text: BBC Gahuza, relaying Reuters, reported that the drone strike that killed AFC/M23 military spokesperson Lt Col Willy Ngoma at dawn on Tuesday near Rubaya killed at least nine people but narrowly missed AFC/M23 military chief Gen Sultani Makenga, who escaped unharmed according to four people who told Reuters.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC drone (per other sources); AFC/M23 target
claims.verification_note: Page and date confirmed; Rubaya location added by a replacement quote; credited to Reuters. BBC Gahuza page published 26 February 2026 ('Yatangajwe 26 Ukwa kabiri 2026'); the information is Reuters', from four unnamed people. 'uwari umuvugizi' means 'who was the spokesperson' (Ngoma, killed in the strike), not a former spokesperson. The page says BBC could not reach M23 or FARDC for comment. Tuesday 24 February 2026 agrees with the UN Group's date for the Rubaya strike.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ("Tuesday") and the UN Group of Experts date of 24 February 2026 for the Rubaya strike (existing claim r1-UC-M23-010); BBC page date shown is approximate (page header not clearly dated, verifier to confirm). Reuters story not fetched. Language: Kinyarwanda/Kirundi (BBC Gahuza). Wazalendo spokesperson claim that Makenga sheltered in a church is in the page but not recorded here.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that its research and the United Nations indicate that the M23's Léon Kanyamibwa and Bertin Masozera directed military training with support from other M23 officers, and that Rwandan military trainers operated in both Rumangabo and Tshanzu.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Narrowed to the passage's own structure: the sentence ties Rumangabo and Tshanzu to the Rwandan trainers clause. The passage is in HRW's section on 'M23 and Rwandan Commanders and Forces at the Centers'. HRW also writes that Rumangabo and Tshanzu are the M23's two main training centers.
claims.researcher_note: Date shown is year-level (HRW says conduct was in 2025). HRW also names Kanyamibwa and Masozera in its recommendation to sanction M23 camp commanders and instructors (not recorded as separate claim). Kanyamibwa is also in r1-UC-M23-016 (UN GoE).

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported, in its section 'Summary Executions and Beatings' on former detainees from Rumangabo, that one M23 commander, 'Captain Gaston', was named by a dozen former detainees as having been particularly brutal in his treatment of recruits, and that detainees often referred to him by the nickname Longangi.
claims.verification_note: Camp attribution checked against the page: Rumangabo is supported by the following sentence, not by the excerpt; statement left as written. Allegation by former detainees as reported by HRW, in its section on executions and beatings at Rumangabo. The excerpt does not name the camp; the next sentences on the page do: 'Several witnesses said that Gaston executed a Colonel Amurabi in Rumangabo around June 2025.' HRW adds that Amurabi was a legal defender in the military justice system in Goma, and that former detainees said Gaston was reprimanded after the execution but returned to the camp the following month. LEAD: extend the excerpt (source_edits.py add_excerpt) to record the Amurabi execution allegation as its own claim with Amurabi in victims_named. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: HRW section on summary executions and beatings at Rumangabo 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-001: Place slippage: the excerpt does not tie the brutality allegation to Rumangabo; the camp comes from the section heading and the next sentence (the Amurabi execution 'in Rumangabo'). Amended so the camp is HRW's section context, not part of the detainees' allegation. Allegation stays with 'a dozen former detainees'.; excerpt-support: added the section heading and opening sentence as an excerpt; wording follows the heading ('Summary Executions and Beatings') and its first sentence ('Many former detainees from Rumangabo')
claims.researcher_note: Allegation by former detainees as reported by HRW; the excerpt itself does not name Rumangabo, the surrounding section concerns Rumangabo (HRW elsewhere in the report quotes a detainee held at Rumangabo in May 2025). Verifier to confirm camp attribution against the page and shorten the statement if unsupported.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that senior AFC/M23 leaders including Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, Maj. Gen. Sultani Makenga and Bertrand Bisimwa, and commanders such as Gen. Baudoin Ngaruye, Bertrand Byamungu, John Imani Nzenze and Willy Ngoma, were all reported to have been seen at the Rumangabo and Tshanzu training centers in 2025.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo and Tshanzu training centers, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Passage matches; the identity of 'both training centers' is supplied by another passage on the same page. HRW's wording is hedged ('reported to have been seen'). HRW prints 'Bertrand Byamungu'; other sources print Bernard (Maheshe) Byamungu, the UN only 'Byamungu'. Being seen at a site is not a finding of responsibility.
claims.researcher_note: HRW writes "Bertrand Byamungu" here; the UN and other sources print Bernard (Maheshe) Byamungu. Presence at a site is not a finding of responsibility for abuses there.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that on Monday 29 December, at an exchange of wishes of senior AFC/M23 cadres in Goma, the military coordinator of the AFC/M23 and ARC chief of staff, General-Major Sultani Makenga, told participants: 'Soyez en état de guerre, cette guerre nous allons la gagner'.
claims.verification_note: All three passages match one page. Byline Blaise Basabose, Kivu Morning Post, 30 December 2025. Titles as printed by the outlet.
claims.researcher_note: Titles as printed by the outlet. Three excerpts from one page (one contiguous passage each).

claims.text: FNTV reported on 23 May 2026 that, after checking with several local sources and Wazalendo movements, it could give a clear denial that General Bernard Byamungu of the AFC/M23 had died: the man killed in the drone attack was a Wazalendo commander with the same name, colonel Byamungu Ruduga Abdallah, active in the Uvira high plateaux.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (colonel Byamungu Ruduga Abdallah, per FNTV); AFC/M23 (General Bernard Byamungu)
claims.verification_note: Passage matches; Ruvungi placed by the page's opening paragraph. UNCONFIRMED. FNTV (byline Freddy Tshiyoyo) says it had first relayed the rumour without full cross-checking; its sources are unnamed. It says witnesses attributed the drone strikes at Ruvungi locally to the rebels. Conflicts with the Enquete.cd report of 24 May 2026; neither is established.
claims.researcher_note: Outlet states it had first relayed the rumour without full cross-checking. The URL slug and title in search results ("Tiger One tombe") differ from the corrected page title. Single local outlet; its sources are unnamed. Conflicts with Enquete.cd claim of the same week.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that FARDC brigadier general François Kamanzi, commander of operations of the 12th military region in Kongo-Central, had joined the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) led by Joseph Kabila; FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said he joined the ranks of the 'Lions de Sarambwe' within the Armée révolutionnaire congolaise (ARC).
claims.actor_as_written: FRN / ARC (partisan account by FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka)
claims.verification_note: Both passages match; kept at C as a party account. Party claim (FRN spokesperson). The page says 'official sources' (unnamed) had him travel via Lufu and Luvu (Angola) before reaching Goma, and quotes the AFC/M23-appointed North Kivu vice-governor. No FARDC or government statement found. Event outside the Kivus apart from the Goma arrival.
claims.researcher_note: Party claim (FRN/AFC-M23 side, spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka); no FARDC/government statement found yet. Page is dated 28 October 2026 ("6 hours ago" at search time); the 12th military region is a FARDC region (Kongo-Central), not an AFC/M23 unit, which resolves the roster lead "12e région militaire". Relevant to ARC (M23 army) recruitment of FARDC officers.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the staff of the 34th military region announced it had detained at Walikale two Wazalendo commanders accused of indiscipline and of violence that seriously affected civilians: self-proclaimed generals Kirikicho Mirimba, alias Mwana Mayi, of the COPACO movement (Coalition des Patriotes au Congo), and Musubao Kalimba, alias Kasilasi.
claims.actor_as_written: 34th military region staff (FARDC); Wazalendo/VDP commanders of COPACO
claims.verification_note: Excerpt matches the page and supports every clause; attribution to the army kept. The arrests and the accusations are the army's account (34th military region communiqué relayed by Actualite.cd); no response from the two commanders was found.
claims.researcher_note: Army communiqué relayed by Actualite.cd; the arrest is the army's account. The two commanders' response not found. Not in the existing UC-FARDC or UCD-FARDC-WZ claims (which hold the South Kivu Wazalendo).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, according to the military authorities, the two Wazalendo commanders had been engaged in fratricidal clashes for nearly 17 months, the most recent being the fighting of 15 to 18 February 2026 in the groupements of Tushunguti and Zirhalo, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory (South Kivu); according to the army, these clashes caused 14 civilian deaths, 7 seriously wounded and 7 women victims of rape.
claims.place_as_written: Tushunguti and Zirhalo groupements, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe (South Kivu)
claims.actor_as_written: the two Wazalendo commanders detained by the army, as characterised by the military authorities
claims.verification_note: Statement reordered so the link to the two commanders is explicitly the army's; figures field had a unit ordinal; actor no longer names people the excerpts do not print. Toll and the link between the Kalehe fighting and the two commanders are the army's account; the page does not say which side committed the rapes. Survivors not named. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Figures are the army's, via one outlet; no UN/NGO figure found for this clash. Location is in South Kivu (Kalehe) but the units are those arrested in North Kivu (Walikale).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that fifty-four soldiers of the 3415th regiment of the FARDC had been appearing since Monday 26 October before the Goma garrison military tribunal, sitting in a circuit hearing at Walikale, North Kivu, prosecuted notably for murder, abandoning post, dissipation of war munitions and refusal to obey.
claims.verification_note: Figure spelled as the excerpt prints it; actor no longer asserts the regiment's parent region, which the page does not state. Prosecution stage only: the page says the verdict was expected in early November. Being prosecuted is not a finding of guilt.
claims.researcher_note: First North Kivu source for the 3411th/3415th regiment numbering in this unit. Verdict not yet reported at the date of the page.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to major Dieudonné Kasereka, communication officer of the 34th military region, the defendants were arrested on 20 October following incidents at Ntoto, Waloa Loanda groupement, on the border with Masisi territory, which left two dead, a soldier and a civilian; the page says the facts allegedly occurred during an altercation between the soldiers and Military Police elements trying to stop them from leaving the combat zone without authorisation.
claims.place_as_written: Ntoto, Waloa Loanda groupement, Walikale (territory), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC soldiers (the defendants) and Military Police elements, per the 34th military region spokesperson
claims.verification_note: Supported; figures field rewritten without bare numerals; actor narrowed to what the page says. 20 October is the arrest date; the incident date is not printed. The page also reports two wounded (a soldier and a civilian). The cause is conditional on the page ('se seraient produits').
claims.researcher_note: Date of the incident is not stated; the arrest date (20 October) is given. The page's 'a soldier and a civilian' dead and wounded are not named.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that another group of ten soldiers of the same regiment had been convicted on 1 September to sentences ranging from ten months of prison to principal penal servitude for opening fire on their company commander.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC soldiers of the same regiment as the Walikale defendants
claims.verification_note: Removed the regiment number that this excerpt does not print; territory not stated by the page. 'The same regiment' is the 3415th regiment named earlier in the same Radio Okapi report (see the claim on the 54 defendants). Year inferred from 'le 1er septembre dernier' on a page dated 27 October 2026. Court findings concern the convicted soldiers only; the court and place are not stated.
claims.researcher_note: The year is not printed in the sentence; the page is dated 2026-10-27 and says 'le 1er septembre dernier'. Place of the 1 September trial not stated in the excerpt.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that three FARDC soldiers, all from the 21st principal defence brigade, were sentenced to twenty years in prison each for collective rape in Lubero: the court found them guilty of sexually assaulting a 28-year-old woman in the village of Kimbulu during the night from Sunday to the previous Monday, and ordered them to pay jointly 10,000 US dollars to the victim in reparation.
claims.place_as_written: Kimbulu village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: three soldiers of the 21st principal defence brigade, FARDC (convicted)
claims.verification_note: Supported by excerpts and title; statement no longer depends on page-only details (tribunal name, fines moved to note); figures rewritten. Court findings concern the three convicted soldiers only. The tribunal is the Butembo-Lubero garrison military tribunal per the page; each was also fined 250,000 Congolese francs. The survivor is not named by the source. Offence date not printed; relative to a page dated 9 July 2026. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Victim not named. Date of the assault computed from 'dimanche à lundi dernier' relative to a 9 July 2026 publication (verdict given 'il y a deux jours'); the exact date is not printed. First FARDC-unit-named sexual violence case for Lubero in this unit's scope. Single outlet.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that a FARDC soldier was sentenced to seven years of penal servitude for the rape of a 15-year-old girl; according to the court, the facts took place in the village of Kaviseghe, and the soldier allegedly had sexual relations with the adolescent several times in his room.
claims.place_as_written: Kaviseghe village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: a FARDC soldier (unit not stated, convicted)
claims.verification_note: Tribunal name and Kipese hearing are page-only (not in the excerpt): moved to the note; 'citing local sources' applied only to the hearing details on the page, so removed from the statement. The victim is a minor and is not named by the source. Per the page, the Butembo-Lubero garrison military tribunal ruled 'lundi dernier' at a circuit hearing at Kipese, Lubero territory, 'selon des sources locales'. Court findings concern the convicted soldier only. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Minor victim; not named by the source. Hearing 'lundi dernier' (Monday before 21 August 2026, computed 17 August); date of the offence not stated.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that a FARDC soldier was found guilty of the murder of three people (his partner, their child and another soldier) in facts dating back to 12 August at the village of Katundu; according to the elements retained by the court, he had opened fire point-blank on his partner in a context of jealousy.
claims.place_as_written: Katundu village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: a FARDC soldier (unit not stated, convicted)
claims.verification_note: Sentence, damages and hearing place are not in the excerpt: moved to the note; statement limited to the excerpt. Per the page, the Butembo-Lubero garrison military tribunal, at a circuit hearing at Kipese (Lubero territory), sentenced him to death and to 20,000 US dollars in damages; the child was a girl ('leur fillette') who, with the other soldier, died of wounds. Victims not named. Court findings concern the convicted soldier only.
claims.researcher_note: Family/intimate-partner killing by a soldier; recorded because the brief asks for all alleged violations by FARDC personnel. Victims not named.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that a member of the Wazalendo movement called « Far West » was sentenced to death on Wednesday 6 May, the Butembo garrison military tribunal having found him guilty of the murder of a motorcyclist and of the rape followed by murder of his female customer, facts which occurred the previous week at Kimbulu, Lubero territory; Lubero civil society also demanded the outright abolition of the « Far West » movement, which it accuses of being involved in serious human rights violations.
claims.actor_as_written: a member of the Wazalendo movement 'Far West'
claims.verification_note: 'Motard' / 'cliente' translated as printed; figures rewritten without bare numerals. The convicted man and the victims are not named. A civil society communiqué of 5 May quoted on the page dates the double killing to 'jeudi dernier' and describes the victims as a motorcycle-taxi driver and his customer. Court findings concern the convicted man only; the civil society accusation against the movement is its own. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 3 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified contradicting source(s) recorded in notes; not regraded pending review. 2026-10-29: source 3 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 4 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 5 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Offence date computed from 'la semaine dernière' relative to the 6 May hearing and a 9 May publication; the later 5 May communiqué quoted on the page says 'jeudi dernier' for the double killing (30 April 2026 if the Thursday before 5 May). Victims not named. Same village (Kimbulu) as the July 2026 collective rape by 21st-brigade soldiers. Contradicting reporting: Actualite.cd (2026-05-07): verdict date: Thursday 7 May instead of Wednesday 6 May

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that fighting between the rebels of the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) and the FARDC, supported by the Wazalendo, continued for the third consecutive day on Sunday 18 October 2026 at Kibati, Luberike groupement, Walikale territory, North Kivu, the FARDC and Wazalendo having launched an offensive against FRN positions there to dislodge the rebels; the outlet says Kibati has for about two years been one of the main foci of confrontation between the FRN and government forces supported by the Wazalendo in that part of Walikale.
claims.place_as_written: Kibati, Luberike groupement, Walikale territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and Wazalendo (offensive); FRN rebels (as the source names them)
claims.verification_note: Removed 'since Friday', which the page attaches to the fighting, not to the offensive; added the third excerpt's context. The page does not say whether the FRN is the same organisation as the AFC/M23; do not equate them on this source. The page says the human and material toll was not yet known and that FRN reinforcements reached Kibati on Saturday morning (per sources at Kashebere).
claims.researcher_note: The source does not say that the FRN is the same as the AFC/M23 (other 2026 pages in this unit use FRN and ARC for the rebel side in Rutshuru). Actualite.cd says Kibati has been a main focus of confrontation for about two years. No casualty figures yet. Excerpt is >60 words? see check.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that two AFC/M23 commanders deployed at Misinga, Ikobo groupement, Walikale territory, were kidnapped by Wazalendo in the night of Sunday to Monday 30 June, the sources not giving their identities; on the Monday the AFC/M23 searched the forest of Kirumburumbu and Muuli in vain and forced farmers to leave their fields to continue the search.
claims.place_as_written: between Kirumburumbu and Muuli villages, near Misinga, Ikobo groupement, Walikale territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (as local sources say); AFC/M23 commanders as victims
claims.verification_note: Supported; figures rewritten; search detail made precise. Per the page the captors took the two to Buhimba, where they set up their headquarters, and the commanders' fate was unknown by evening. Single outlet, local sources.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet, anonymous local sources; the fate of the two commanders was unknown at the time of publication. Captors' headquarters said to be at Buhimba.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to first reports, Wazalendo led by self-proclaimed general Ignace Dunia Sauli attacked M23 positions at Biramba, Masisi territory, causing exchanges of heavy-weapon fire, after fighting at Luhonga on Sunday 29 June.
claims.place_as_written: Biramba and Luhonga, Bashali Mokoto groupement, Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo led by self-proclaimed general Ignace Dunia Sauli; AFC-M23
claims.verification_note: Statement limited to the excerpt and title (Biramba, Masisi); the 30 June date and groupement, printed on the page but not in the stored excerpt, are in the note and the date field. Per the page, the Biramba clashes broke out on Monday 30 June 2025 at Biramba (Lwama locality near Luhonga, Bashali Mokoto groupement); much of the population had left on the Sunday evening towards Mpati or neighbouring villages. Early reports only; no casualty figures.
claims.researcher_note: Only early reports; no casualty figures in the cited passage. Identifies a Wazalendo commander (Ignace Dunia Sauli) active in Bashali Mokoto, Masisi.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that at least nine civilians were killed and several others seriously wounded, among them three children including a five-year-old girl, in an armed incursion by presumed CMC-FDP Wazalendo militiamen into Bishusha groupement, Rutshuru territory, in the night of Monday to Tuesday 28 October 2025; according to anonymous health sources at Bishusha Centre, the armed men came in around 19 h, largely targeting local traders, and goods and shops were looted.
claims.place_as_written: Bishusha groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Supported; the toll is the outlet's lead (also given by a health source), so 'citing health sources' narrowed to the clauses it carries; figures rewritten. Attribution to CMC-FDP is 'presumed'; a health source quoted on the page calls the attackers 'bandits assimilés aux CMC-FDP'. Per the page, AFC-M23 elements intervened and exchanged fire with the assailants, and the wounded were being treated at a local health facility. Victims, including the injured children, are not named.
claims.researcher_note: Area under AFC-M23 control per the page; the attribution to CMC-FDP is 'presumed' and rests on anonymous health sources and a victim quote. Excerpt must be checked for length.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the administrator of Rutshuru territory under the FRN, Euphrem Kabasha, accused the Wazalendo of the CMC of being behind an attack that killed civilians at Kabizo, saying that in the night of 25 to 26 October, at about 1:30, Kabizo, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, was attacked by the FDLR together with the Nyatura CMC FDP of Gashegu Héritier and Mbitezi, and that five people were killed.
claims.place_as_written: Kabizo, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FDLR with Nyatura CMC FDP of Gashegu Héritier and Mbitezi, as alleged by the FRN-side Rutshuru territory administrator
claims.verification_note: Statement limited to the administrator's words in the excerpts; the outlet's own 'at least five' lead (page only) moved to the note; figures rewritten. Partisan account: the accuser is the administrator of the rebel-held (FRN) administration. Kivu Morning Post's own lead says at least five people were killed in the night of 25 to 26 October 2026. The page also says the ARC intervened; it does not say whether the FRN or ARC is the AFC/M23. Actualite.cd reports the same night differently (Wazalendo ambush on an FRN convoy near Kabizo and Katovu, three rebel fighters killed); neither outlet mentions the other's account. Victims not named.
claims.researcher_note: The accusation comes from the administrator of the rebel-held administration (the page says 'sous le FRN'); treat as that party's claim. The source does not say whether FRN is the AFC/M23's new name; Actualite.cd's account of the same night is a separate claim (ambush on an FRN convoy).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, according to local sources, the Wazalendo ambushed a convoy of FRN rebels heading to Kabizo to install a new commander, near Kabizo and Katovu, Rutshuru, with a provisional toll of three rebel fighters killed, per sources in the area.
claims.place_as_written: Kabizo-Katovu road, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Statement limited to the excerpt and title; date and road detail (page only) moved to the note. Per the page, the fighting between FRN rebels and Wazalendo took place in the night of Sunday to Monday 26 October on the road linking Kabizo and Katovu (Bwito chiefdom), and farmers stayed away from their fields that Monday. A different account of the same night from the Kivu Morning Post report, in which the FRN-side administrator says five people were killed at Kabizo by the FDLR and Nyatura CMC FDP; keep both.
claims.researcher_note: A different account of the same night as the Kabizo killings reported by KMP (five civilians killed, per the rebel-side administrator). The two sources do not mention each other's toll.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the spokesperson of the Wazalendo synergy Front Nord, John Mangaiko, had declared on 6 January 2026 at Butembo that Kakule Kaputu (« Tango Fort ») was killed in an armed operation and not in a targeted assassination, describing Tango Fort as an armed fighter involved in attacks on other Wazalendo and in acts of insecurity against the population; the outlet added that in a video published on 4 March 2026 at Burondo, Lubero territory, the political-military movement Bana Bateseka, a member of the Wazalendo Front Grand-Nord, announced the dissolution of the armed group Tango Fort, and that according to the video its deputy commander, colonel Thembo, announced his rallying to Bana Bateseka with all his fighters.
claims.place_as_written: Butembo and Burondo, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo synergy Front Nord (spokesperson John Mangaiko); Bana Bateseka (Wazalendo Front Grand-Nord)
claims.verification_note: 'Joined it' narrowed to 'announced his rallying', per the video as reported; Burondo added from the excerpt. Mangaiko's account (per the page: killed in clashes with another Wazalendo faction at Vuvatsi, towards Kitovo) differs in place from civil society's (Munzambaye hill). The rally is per the Bana Bateseka video as reported, not independently confirmed. Two dates: 6 January 2026 (statement) and 4 March 2026 (video).
claims.researcher_note: Mangaiko's account (a different place name, Vuvatsi towards Kitovo, from civil society's Munzambaye hill) is the Wazalendo synergy's account of the same death. Colonel Thembo's rally is per the Bana Bateseka video as reported.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing an administrative and security source in Masisi, that the self-proclaimed general Mutayomba, a Wazalendo commander on the Katoyi axis, was wounded in fighting against the AFC-M23 at Luke, Masisi territory, on 'Friday 21 May 2026'; the administrative source said he was lightly wounded and evacuated by helicopter to Beni, while a FARDC military source confirmed the injury but described it as serious.
claims.place_as_written: Luke, Katoyi sector, Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo commander self-proclaimed general Mutayomba, FARDC allies
claims.verification_note: All clauses in the excerpts; weekday mismatch stated in the note. DISCREPANCY: the page prints 'vendredi 21 mai 2026', but 21 May 2026 fell on a Thursday; the date is kept as printed. The two sources disagree on the severity of the injury. The page is dated 1 June 2026.
claims.researcher_note: DISCREPANCY: the page says 'vendredi 21 mai 2026', but 21 May 2026 was a Thursday; the day is kept as printed. Article dated 2026-06-01 but says 'Depuis plus d'une semaine' and 'au cours du week-end' rumours of death. Links to the existing claim naming 'Jams Mutayomba' under Wazalendo command (Radio Okapi 2026-10-05).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that major-general Nyembo Abdallah, interim commander of the 3rd defence zone, had been staying in Walikale since Friday 21 November, a visit which major Dieudonné Kasereka, communication officer of the 34th military region, said was part of an inspection of the troops and of command; the delegation was received by the commander of the 34th region.
claims.actor_as_written: 3rd defence zone (FARDC) interim commander Nyembo Abdallah; 34th military region
claims.verification_note: Year removed (not printed in the excerpt); Kigoma airfield (page only) moved to the note. The page (dated 24 November 2025) does not name the 34th region commander. 'Interim' is the page's wording for Nyembo Abdallah's post at the 3rd defence zone. Per the page, the reception took place at the Kigoma airfield.
claims.researcher_note: Adds a post for Nyembo Abdallah after the July 2025 telegram that sent him to the 31st military region (existing claims): by November 2025 Actualite.cd calls him interim commander of the 3rd defence zone. The 34th region commander is not named on this page.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 reinforcements led by "Lieutenant-Colonel" Japhet Gakufe reached Minembwe in March 2025, and that a second reinforcement, led by "Lieutenant -Colonel" Oscar Ndabagaza, was blocked while crossing hostile areas before reaching Mikenge at the end of August 2025; it described these as support to MRDP-Twirwaneho enclaves in the Hauts Plateaux.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe and Mikenge, Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Para. 53 of S/2025/858 prints both reinforcements and frames them as AFC/M23 and RDF military support to besieged MRDP-Twirwaneho-controlled enclaves. Ranks in quotes as printed. 'End of August' is 2025 by context (March 2025 sentence, report of 30 Dec 2025).
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/858 is already cited by other units; this claim adds the Ndabagaza reinforcement and the dating. Ranks in quotation marks as printed by the Group.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in areas under the control of Mai-Mai Yakutumba and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups in Uvira and Fizi territories there was a sharp escalation in human rights violations, including conflict-related sexual violence, extortion and summary executions of civilians accused of collaborating with AFC/M23; it also said that Raia Mutomboki and other factions aligned with Yakutumba had expanded their operations and perpetrated abuses, and that at least 325 cases of sexual violence affecting over 400 victims were documented in South Kivu between January and June 2025.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira and Fizi territories, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Mai-Mai Yakutumba, Raia Mutomboki and other Wazalendo factions aligned with Yakutumba
claims.verification_note: All three passages exact on the retained PDF (annex 38, 'Alarming surge in conflict-related sexual violence'). Statement keeps the figure separate from the group attribution. From annex 38 of S/2025/858. The 325-case figure is province-wide, drawn from verified reports gathered by UN-supported national NGOs, and the annex says it reflects underreporting in government-controlled areas; it is not attributed to Yakutumba or any single group.
claims.researcher_note: The 325-case figure is South Kivu province-wide and is not attributed to a named group by this passage. Raia Mutomboki is named only generally (no faction leader or place).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho prevented civilians from leaving Minembwe, including through coercion and threats of violence, fearing defections and information leaks, and that, as previously reported, all boys between 10 and 12 years of age and all able-bodied men were compelled to join Twirwaneho and participate in combat.
claims.verification_note: Para. 87 of S/2026/466; 'as previously reported' kept, so the recruitment statement is the Group's restatement of earlier findings, not a new 2026 documentation. The Group says the compulsory recruitment of boys aged 10-12 and able-bodied men was 'previously reported'; the date of that practice is not fixed by this passage.
claims.researcher_note: The 'as previously reported' recruitment statement refers to earlier Group reports (S/2023/431); the time of the 2025-26 events is approximate (the report says Minembwe encircled since mid-2025). Excerpt includes the footnote marker '97' as printed in the extracted PDF text.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that RED Tabara had long-standing camps in Masango (Uvira territory), Magunda (Mwenga territory) and Kipupu (Mwenga territory), and that, although the RED Tabara leadership has repeatedly denied any links with AFC/M23, RED Tabara combatants took part in hostilities alongside AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and RDF across several axes; that FNL elements were present in the Nyaburunda forest (Uvira territory), in mountainous areas near Sange and in Magunda, where they co-locate with RED Tabara units; and that by mid-February 2026 RED Tabara and FNL combatants had physically joined the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition in the Kamombo sector of the Hauts Plateaux.
claims.place_as_written: Masango, Magunda, Kipupu, Nyaburunda forest, Sange, Kamombo sector; Uvira, Mwenga and Fizi territories, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Draft said both groups 'fought alongside MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23' and dropped RDF; the excerpt says RED Tabara fought alongside AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and RDF, and for FNL only presence and joining the coalition by mid-February 2026. Narrowed to the printed wording. From annex 26 of S/2026/466. RED Tabara's denial is recorded as reported by the Group; no RED Tabara or FNL statement was opened.
claims.researcher_note: No named RED-Tabara or FNL commander in this passage; leaders not found in the Group's text searched.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Burundi accuses Rwanda of supporting RED-Tabara, that Burundian authorities identify Alexis Sinduhije, a former journalist and president of the opposition party MSD, currently in exile in Belgium, as the group's leader, and that Kigali rejects these accusations.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Burundi; Government of Rwanda; RED-Tabara
claims.verification_note: Exact on the retained page (12 Oct 2026, section 'Gitega and Kigali accuse each other'); background summary by the outlet, attributions kept separate. Two separate attributed positions: Burundi's naming of Sinduhije as RED-Tabara leader is the Burundian authorities' claim; Kigali's rejection is Rwanda's position as summarised by the outlet. No RED-Tabara or Sinduhije response is on the page, and no named speaker or date is given for either position.
claims.researcher_note: The attribution of leadership is Burundian authorities' claim; the page does not give RED-Tabara's own position. Speaker for official_statement not named by the page.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that two ADF units, led by "Mzee" Meya Sebagala in Ituri Province and by sanctioned commander Ahmad Mahmood Hassan, alias Abwakasi (CDi.040), in Lubero territory, were responsible for most ADF mass casualty attacks, and that supply rendezvous sites were overseen by senior ADF figures including Mzee Meya, Abwakasi and Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender.
claims.verification_note: Paras. 16-17 of S/2026/466; 'They' in source 1 refers to the supply rendezvous sites of para. 17. Meya's unit is in Ituri (outside phase 1), attributed to the Group.
claims.researcher_note: Abwakasi already appears in one earlier claim; Meya Sebagala and Kasibante are new. Meya's area is Ituri (outside phase 1) and is recorded as the Group's attribution.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that throughout 2025, attacks perpetrated under the command of Abwakasi (Ahmad Mahmood Hassan), whose ADF unit it places in Lubero territory, led to the killing of over 600 civilians, making it the deadliest ADF unit, with an estimated 25,000 people displaced and at least 26 villages and 9 mining sites destroyed; it reported that the group of 'Mzee' Meya Sebagala, which it places in Ituri Province (Mambasa territory), was responsible for the killing of over 230 civilians.
claims.verification_note: Para. 23 of S/2026/466; figures exact. Location of the killings is not given in the sentence (statement does not add it). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Abwakasi = Ahmad Mahmood Hassan in Lubero territory; 'Mzee' Meya Sebagala in Ituri Province 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Meya's unit in Mambasa territory, Ituri 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-002: Place slippage: the retained report places Meya's unit in Ituri Province, not North Kivu, so its 230-plus toll is outside the Phase 1 geography and must not sit under Lubero/North Kivu. The amendment states each unit's location as the Group gives it (para. 16 and annex); Abwakasi's toll is not broken down by territory.; excerpt-support: added two excerpts from the same report: para. 16 (units of 'Mzee' Meya Sebagala in Ituri Province and Ahmad Mahmood Hassan alias Abwakasi in Lubero territory) and the ADF annex (Meya's unit in Mambasa territory)
claims.researcher_note: The preceding paragraph places Abwakasi's earlier area in Lubero; the passage itself does not state where the 600 killings occurred, so the location is the Group's attribution of Abwakasi's area of operations, and some attacks may be outside North Kivu.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that, with FARDC counter-offensive operations affected by troop shortages, FARDC relied increasingly on Wazalendo armed groups against ADF, including the UPLC led by "General" Germain Kambale Mayani, elements of the NDC-R of sanctioned individual Guidon Shimiray Mwissa, and a local APCLS detachment led by "General" Fimbo.
claims.verification_note: Para. 29 of S/2026/466; the troop-shortage clause is in the same paragraph. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: S/2026/466 para. 29 supports the statement; the troop-shortage clause sits in the preceding sentence, which the stored excerpt omits, so it is added. The page says the shortages were due to offensives against AFC/M23.
claims.researcher_note: Excerpt ends before the sentence naming Manguredjipa; statement narrowed to what the excerpt says.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Colonel Mustapha of Twirwaneho, an ally of AFC-M23, was reportedly killed in a CH-4 drone strike by the Congolese army at Rugezi in Fizi territory on Thursday 28 August 2025, according to a Wazalendo spokesperson in South Kivu, who said eleven Twirwaneho fighters died with him; it also reported that AFC-M23 and Twirwaneho fighters accused the Congolese army and its allies of launching several drone attacks in Fizi territory in violation of the ceasefire.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC (drone strike, per Wazalendo spokesperson); Twirwaneho
claims.verification_note: Exact on the retained page; conditional 'aurait été tué' kept as 'reportedly'. excerpt_en flags reviewed: translations match the excerpts (the English of source 1 drops 'de Doha'; nothing is added). The death and the toll of eleven are a Wazalendo spokesperson's claim (a party to the fighting), relayed by one local outlet and not independently confirmed. AFC-M23/Twirwaneho did not confirm or deny his death on this page.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet; death claimed by a Wazalendo spokesperson (party to the conflict) and not independently confirmed. A Facebook repost quoted the same spokesperson text (lead only, not cited). Local outlet: Kivu Morning Post (Bukavu/Goma).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Twirwaneho was structured and militarised by Michel Rukunda, alias Makanika, a FARDC deserter who had been deputy commander at Walikale, and that he was killed in a Congolese army drone strike in Fizi in February 2025; it also reported that the group was active in the Hauts Plateaux of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga.
claims.verification_note: Exact on the retained page (15 Apr 2026). The 'active in' clause is on the page in the preceding sentence, outside the stored excerpt (excerpt gap). Background written by the outlet itself, not attributed to HRW. Only the February 2025 death falls in the window; the outlet's account of the group's 2019-2020 founding is not used.
claims.researcher_note: Background sentence written by the outlet itself (not attributed to HRW). Makanika appears in earlier claims (roster); this adds the outlet's wording on his post and death.

claims.text: Actualite.cd, quoting a Human Rights Watch report, reported that residents of Minembwe and UN and diplomatic sources said Twirwaneho had forced families to provide one fighter or pay financial compensation to the armed group, and that it carried out reprisals in case of refusal.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe, Hauts Plateaux, Fizi, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Exact on the retained page as a quoted HRW passage; not independent of HRW's own report, cited by an existing claim. Local relay quoting HRW; HRW attributes the information to residents of Minembwe and UN and diplomatic sources.
claims.researcher_note: HRW's own page (hrw.org/fr/news/2026/04/14/...) is already cited by an existing claim; this is a local relay with one quote. Statement narrowed: the 'prevented civilians from leaving' clause is in a later sentence not in this excerpt, so removed.

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported that MONUSCO, in a press release of 21 November 2025, condemned ADF attacks between 13 and 19 November 2025 in Lubero territory, saying at least 17 civilians, including women admitted to the maternity ward, were killed in a Catholic Church health centre at Byambwe, 60 km west of Lubero, and four pavilions housing patients were set on fire; MONUSCO also cited abductions and looting of medicines in other localities.
claims.place_as_written: Byambwe, Bapere sector / Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: All three passages exact on the retained page. The figures flag '7' comes from the publisher name '7sur7.cd' in the statement, not from a figure. excerpt_en flags reviewed: the English translates each excerpt (MONUSCO acronym expansion shortened only). Toll and attribution are MONUSCO's (press release relayed by 7sur7.cd; the release itself was not opened). Overall toll per MONUSCO: 89 civilians killed in Bapere sector and Baswagha chiefdom. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. Regraded B->A on independent, non-partisan corroboration. 2026-10-29: source 3 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 4 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Local outlet relaying a MONUSCO press release; the MONUSCO text itself was not opened. The communique says violence against civilians in medical structures may constitute crimes; not repeated here (vocabulary rule).

claims.text: The US State Department spokesperson said that the United States was designating Gustave Kubwayo, commander of an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit, and said the FDLR has carried out ethnic violence against civilians, used child soldiers, committed sexual violence and launched cross-border attacks.
claims.verification_note: Exact on the retained State Department press statement of 2 June 2026, issued by spokesperson Thomas "Tommy" Pigott. US government statement and allegation about the FDLR, as 'the US says'.
claims.researcher_note: Official US statement (a party to diplomacy, not neutral on the FDLR). Treasury's sb0518 release (already cited by another unit) gives the unit name CRAP and alias; this State release is a separate page. The sexual-violence and child-soldier wording is the US government's allegation about the FDLR as a group, not about Kubwayo individually.

claims.text: CongoRassure reported that a new battalion, the '22ᵉ Task Force (TAFOK)', was being mobilised in the border town of Gatumba before deployment to Bukavu, bringing the total of Burundian battalions in the DRC to sixteen, five of them positioned in the Hauts et Moyens-Plateaux of Fizi and Uvira to hunt Burundian rebels; that the Burundian regiment was under the command of 'général Pontien Hakizimana, alias Mingi' and structured in four brigades of three battalions each; and that the FDNB had deployed nearly 10 000 soldiers, a strength currently fluctuating between 8 000 and 12 000.
claims.place_as_written: Bukavu, Kalehe, Kamanyola, Kavumu; Hauts et Moyens-Plateaux of Fizi and Uvira, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: All facts on retained page; added Kalehe/Kamanyola/Kavumu (location field) with quote; figures written as the page prints them (10 000 etc.). excerpt_en flags are translation artefacts (DRC/RDC, South Kivu/Sud-Kivu), translations cover the excerpts only. Single outlet (CongoRassure, byline Diddy Kambale Mastaki); the page cites no source for the commander, structure or figures. The commander attribution is a lead only. Troop figures conflict with other sources and dates; kept as printed. The page also places Burundian forward positions at Kalehe, Kamanyola and Kavumu (see the replacement quote; location field).
claims.researcher_note: Single, lesser-known Congolese outlet; the page names no original source (its content closely tracks RFI's 7 Feb 2025 report, which could not be fetched). The commander attribution appears nowhere else in the existing claims; treat as a lead. Author byline: Diddy Kambale Mastaki. Compare UN GoE S/2025/446 (14 battalions in early April 2025).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several concordant security sources, a new redeployment of Burundian soldiers to the DRC observed between 29 December 2025 and 4 January 2026, toward Fizi territory (Bibokoboko, Point Zéro, Milimba) and Tanganyika province, in particular Kalemie, carried out from the Burundian navy position near the Rumonge fishing port, with about ten military vehicles mobilised according to police and military sources; a soldier contacted said the main objective would be to reinforce two Burundian battalions left isolated in mountainous areas of eastern DRC.
claims.place_as_written: Rumonge (Burundi) to Fizi territory (Bibokoboko, Point Zéro, Milimba) and Kalemie
claims.verification_note: Supported; added vehicles figure with quote; kept conditional; graded C because every element rests on anonymous sources of one outlet. Local monitor relying on anonymous security, police and military sources; the stated objective is conditional ('serait'). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi, 12 Jan 2026 (Photo de la semaine). All clauses are on the page; the Rumonge departure point and the 'about ten vehicles' (from 31 Dec, per police and military sources) were in no stored excerpt, now added. The soldier's objective is conditional (serait), as the statement keeps it. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi, 12 Jan 2026 (Photo de la semaine). All clauses are on the page; the Rumonge departure point and the 'about ten vehicles' (from 31 Dec, per police and military sources) were in no stored excerpt, now added. The soldier's objective is conditional (serait), as the statement keeps it.
claims.researcher_note: Local Burundian monitor citing anonymous security sources. Article first appeared 9 January 2026 (same text under a different title) and was republished 12 January. Complements UN GoE S/2026/466 (FDNB role in Jan 2026 FARDC offensive from Uvira).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several security sources, that a large part of the Burundian soldiers withdrew in December 2025 following M23 advances in South Kivu and losses suffered by the FDNB; it reported that the secretary general of the CNDD-FDD had spoken of a 'strategic withdrawal' ('retrait stratégique'), saying Burundi remained master of its military decisions, and quoted Révérien Ndikuriyo as having declared: 'it is like at home, we go there when we want'.
claims.verification_note: Original statement fused two sentences into a direct naming the page does not make; narrowed to what each sentence says. The page does not itself name the CNDD-FDD secretary general in the 'retrait stratégique' sentence; it attributes the next quote to Révérien Ndikuriyo. No date or venue given for either remark. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi, 12 Jan 2026. All clauses are on the page; the stored excerpt began mid-sentence and omitted the December 2025 withdrawal clause, now added. The page does not itself state that Ndikuriyo is the CNDD-FDD secretary general; the statement rightly keeps the two attributions separate.
claims.researcher_note: Burundian party statement relayed by a local monitor; the 'retrait stratégique' wording is attributed by the outlet to the CNDD-FDD secretary general, the second excerpt gives the quoted remark. Contrast with the FDNB spokesperson's denial of any withdrawal (19 Feb 2025, separate claim) and the UN GoE statement that FDNB were forced out of Uvira (existing claim UC-BI-FDLR#22).

claims.text: Anadolu Agency reported that the Burundian army spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, said on X that, contrary to what Reuters and social networks reported, FDNB soldiers deployed in the DRC continued to carry out their missions in their sectors of responsibility.
claims.place_as_written: eastern DRC (parts not specified by the source)
claims.verification_note: Byline and quote verified on retained page. Party statement (FDNB) as reported by Anadolu (AA/Bujumbura, Jean Bosco Nzosaba). AA adds that he did not specify which parts of the DRC remain under Burundian responsibility.
claims.researcher_note: Responds to Reuters' report of 18 Feb 2025 (four sources said Burundi was withdrawing forces; Reuters page could not be fetched, so that account is not recorded). Anadolu is the original publisher of this article (AA/Bujumbura, Jean Bosco Nzosaba); the quote is from the spokesperson's X post.

claims.text: Iwacu reported that at a press conference on Thursday 16 January the FDNB spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, rejected allegations that Burundian soldiers had been captured or killed by M23 in eastern DRC, saying those captured were not Burundians, while neither confirming nor denying casualties, which he called a military secret.
claims.verification_note: All clauses on retained page; '16' carried by replacement quote. FDNB party statement as reported by Iwacu (byline Stine Akimana, 16/01/2025).
claims.researcher_note: Same press conference is summarised by SOS Médias Burundi (25 Jan 2025) and Igihe (17 Jan 2025, Rwandan outlet, page not retrievable). Iwacu is a Bujumbura outlet.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Thursday, January 23, 2025, according to its sources, the Kamenge military hospital in Bujumbura counted 81 injured and 19 dead Burundian soldiers from fighting with M23 in Congolese territory, and that the army buried Lieutenant Patience Gapara, killed in the fighting with M23 in North Kivu; by its own estimate, 7,500 to 9,000 Burundian soldiers were on Congolese soil.
claims.place_as_written: Kamenge military hospital, Bujumbura; North Kivu fighting
claims.verification_note: Verified on retained page. Casualty figures rest on anonymous medical sources; the troop range is the outlet's own estimate. The FDNB gave no figure (military secret). 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-001: Attribution drift: the casualty count rests on the outlet's anonymous sources ('according to our sources'), which the statement dropped. Restored; troop range marked as the outlet's own estimate. Exile outlet, single origin, C.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; 'according to our sources' and 'According to our estimates' are in sources 0 and 2
claims.researcher_note: Local monitor with anonymous sources; the FDNB declined to give casualty figures (see Iwacu claim). Troop estimate is the outlet's own.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on 15 May 2026 several boats carrying Burundian soldiers landed in Ruzizi near the port of Kalundu in Uvira, before troops deployed to Bijombo (Uvira territory) and Itombwe (Mwenga territory), a deployment the article said was estimated (without saying by whom) at approximately two battalions, in addition to operations in April 2026 at Point Zero, Mulima, Mikenge, Kakenge, Kalingi and Bidegu with the FARDC and Wazalendo.
claims.place_as_written: Kalundu port (Uvira), Bijombo (Uvira territory), Itombwe (Mwenga territory)
claims.verification_note: Verified on retained page; April-operations clause added to quotes. Single local monitor; no named source for the landing or the estimate. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: April 2026 operations at Point Zero, Mulima, Mikenge, Kakenge, Kalingi and Bidegu with FARDC and Wazalendo 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-023: 'A deployment it estimated' puts the estimate in SOS Médias Burundi's mouth; the page uses an agentless passive ('est estimé'), as the verifier noted on the duplicate r1-UV-2026Q2-009. Searched for a Burundian denial of the 15 May landing: none found (only a February 2026 ambassador denial about a withdrawal). Lead: Uvira had been taken by M23 on 10 December 2025 (actualite.cd 5 April 2026), so control of Uvira in May 2026 should be confirmed in the frontline data. Duplicate of r1-UV-2026Q2-009 (English vs French page).; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): April 2026 operations at Point Zero, Mulima, Mikenge, Kakenge, Kalingi and Bidegu with FARDC and Wazalendo
claims.researcher_note: Single local source, no named commander. The page also says Burundian forces with FARDC and Wazalendo have launched several offensives since December 2025 to retake Minembwe 'without managing to dislodge the M23 and Twirwaneho fighters'.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported in May 2026 that the FDNB is accused by several local and international organisations of human rights violations in the Minembwe area, including road blockades, destruction of property and looting targeting civilians, and that the FDNB spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, acknowledged that movement restrictions could be imposed on individuals considered 'collaborators with the enemy'.
claims.verification_note: Verified on retained page. The accusing organisations are not named; the page gives no date or venue for the spokesperson's remark.
claims.researcher_note: The accusing organisations are not named on the page. Compare existing claims UC-BI-FDLR#30-36 (Dec 2025 Mikalati and Minembwe) from SOS Médias Burundi and BBC Gahuza.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw (Rwandan outlet) reported, citing SOS Medias, that vehicles carrying Burundian soldiers were seen at Kitoga, Muhuzi and in the Itombwe forest and that Burundian soldiers were reinforced in other areas including Minembwe, Mikalati, Kipupu and Point Zero in Fizi; it said, without giving a source, that there were now about 20 thousand Burundian troops in South Kivu, mostly in Uvira and Fizi.
claims.place_as_written: Kitoga, Muhuzi, Itombwe, Minembwe, Mikalati, Kipupu, Point Zero; Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories
claims.verification_note: Locations relay SOS Médias Burundi (origin kept); the 20,000 figure is not attributed to SOS Medias on the page, so source 1's origin corrected to Umuryango.rw. Wording aligned with the page. Rwandan partisan outlet (byline Brenda Mizero, 17 Oct 2025): usable only as 'Umuryango.rw says'. The 20 thousand figure is the outlet's own and unsourced; it conflicts with the other figures in this unit. The article also says Burundi had been sending troops to key areas of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories to stop AFC/M23 (replacement quote).
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan state-aligned outlet (partisan on contested facts); the 20,000 figure is the outlet's own, unsourced, and far above UN GoE figures. Deployment locations relay SOS Médias Burundi. Treat the figure as a party-aligned estimate only.

claims.text: UN News reported that OHCHR spokesperson Jeremy Laurence said OHCHR has documented summary executions of at least 12 people by the M23 between 26 and 28 January.
claims.place_as_written: Goma and surrounding areas, North Kivu (place not specified in the excerpt)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on page verbatim; UN News relays OHCHR briefing. Place of the executions is not stated in the article; perpetrator as alleged by OHCHR.
claims.researcher_note: Place of the executions is not given in this excerpt; the article's context is Goma. Perpetrator as alleged by OHCHR.

claims.text: UN News reported, in the section of its article on the OHCHR briefing, that in other areas under M23 control in South Kivu, such as Minova, fighters have occupied schools and hospitals, forced IDPs out of camps and subjected the civilian population to forced conscription and forced labour.
claims.verification_note: Narrowed attribution: the page does not attribute this sentence to OHCHR explicitly. The sentence carries no explicit attribution on the page; it sits within UN News' account of the OHCHR briefing.
claims.researcher_note: The sentence itself carries no attribution; the preceding paragraph of the article reports the OHCHR briefing. Also covers occupation of hospitals (health care).

claims.text: UN News reported that OHCHR has documented cases of conflict-related sexual violence by the army and allied Wazalendo fighters in Kalehe territory, South Kivu, and is verifying reports that 52 women were raped by Congolese troops in South Kivu, including alleged reports of gangrape.
claims.actor_as_written: the army and allied Wazalendo fighters (documented cases, Kalehe); Congolese troops (52 rapes, reports being verified), per OHCHR
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; actor narrowed to the source's words (army / Congolese troops) and the two clauses separated (documented vs. being verified). The 52-women figure is unverified: OHCHR said it was verifying reports. The page does not place the 52 cases in Kalehe.
claims.researcher_note: The 52-woman figure is unverified (OHCHR 'verifying reports'). The ONU Info French version names the FARDC as 'Forces armées congolaises (FARDC)'.

claims.text: UN News reported that DRC officials report at least 165 women were raped by male inmates during the mass prison break from Goma's Muzenze prison on 27 January, as M23 began its assault on the town.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on page; origin is DRC officials, not OHCHR. Figure is from DRC officials, relayed by UN News; not stated as verified by OHCHR. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Figure from DRC officials relayed by the UN, not verified by OHCHR in this text. Corroborates BBC claims already drafted (SV-NK-2025#10/#11).

claims.text: UN News reported that OHCHR spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani said OHCHR had confirmed cases of summary execution of children by M23 after they entered the city of Bukavu, and that OHCHR was also aware that children were in possession of weapons.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; three-children figure placed in replacement quote. The 'three children' figure is UN News' summary in its lead of the OHCHR alert; exact dates not given ('last week'). 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-013: The statement turned 'We are also aware that children were in possession of weapons' into a bare fact, which can read as a finding about the executed children; restored as what OHCHR said it was aware of. Searched (FR) for an M23 denial: none in results; RFI snippet mentions three children killed in the 'quartier latin' on 16 February (lead, unverified).; excerpt-support: no change needed; every clause is printed in the stored excerpts
claims.researcher_note: The 'three children' figure is stated in the article's lead; the quoted excerpt says 'cases'. 'Last week' relative to 18 Feb 2025; exact days not given. Date computed from publication date.

claims.text: UN News reported that the OHCHR spokesperson condemned attacks on hospitals and humanitarian warehouses as well as threats against the judiciary, directly linked to the rapid advance of the M23 fighters across North Kivu and South Kivu.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on page; general, no facility named. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
claims.researcher_note: No specific facility named in this excerpt.

claims.text: UN News reported that OHCHR spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani noted break-outs from Kabare and Bukavu central prisons on 14 February.
claims.place_as_written: Kabare and Bukavu central prisons, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on page; no perpetrator stated.
claims.researcher_note: The article adds that OHCHR received protection requests from witnesses and victims who feared retaliation from escapees.

claims.text: UN News reported that UNHCR spokesperson Eujin Byun said that in South Kivu more than half of the aid groups providing critical support to survivors of sexual violence report being unable to reach those in need due to insecurity and continuous displacement.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; single UNHCR statement, graded B (not a documented investigation). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
claims.researcher_note: UNHCR (not OHCHR) briefing. Access to services for sexual violence survivors.

claims.text: UN News reported that UNHCR spokesperson Eujin Byun said that in North Kivu the destruction of health facilities, including mortuaries, and overcrowded hospitals increase the risk of spreading infectious diseases, including cholera, malaria, and measles.
claims.verification_note: 'she' is the UNHCR spokesperson named earlier on the page. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 3 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
claims.researcher_note: 'she' = UNHCR spokesperson Eujin Byun named earlier in the article.

claims.text: UN News reported, in a passage on humanitarian assessments in Goma, that WHO and partners, after an assessment with the Government over the past five days, reported that 700 people had been killed and 2,800 injured were receiving treatment in health facilities, with numbers expected to rise.
claims.verification_note: Origin is WHO and partners, not OHCHR; Goma scope narrowed to the page's framing. The page does not explicitly say the 700/2,800 figures are for Goma only; they follow a sentence on Goma. Casualty figures differ across sources.
claims.researcher_note: Place 'Goma' inferred from the article's heading context (humanitarian situation in Goma); the excerpt itself does not name it. Other sources give different casualty figures; these are per-source.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) said in a communiqué that it documented 2.767 human rights violations and abuses and IHL violations across the whole territory of the DRC in the first half of 2025.
claims.place_as_written: DRC-wide (conflict provinces include North and South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Figures field had 'H1' (stray '1'); rewritten. DRC-wide scope made explicit. DRC-wide figure, not specific to North or South Kivu. Radio Okapi relays the BCNUDH communiqué.
claims.researcher_note: DRC-wide figure; the article also gives 2,378 in conflict provinces (86 per cent) in the same passage of the report. Provincial split for Kivus is not in this excerpt.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH report on the first half of 2025 accuses State agents of responsibility for sexual violence against 70 victims, including the FARDC (69 victims) and PNC agents (one victim).
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC (69 victims) and PNC agents (one victim), per BCNUDH
claims.verification_note: 'namely' softened to 'including' (notamment); period anchored to the report's half-year scope. DRC-wide; the article gives no provincial breakdown of these victims.
claims.researcher_note: DRC-wide; the excerpt does not give the provinces. Relayed by Radio Okapi from the BCNUDH report.

claims.text: ONU Info reported that, according to BCNUDH data, 887 cases of conflict-related sexual violence were documented the previous year, affecting 1,534 victims, including 854 women and 672 girls, and that North and South Kivu account for close to 80 per cent of documented victims.
claims.place_as_written: DRC; North Kivu and South Kivu account for close to 80% of victims
claims.actor_as_written: armed groups responsible for 75% of victims; State actors in 19% of documented cases, per the report
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; UNFPA is only the photo credit, origin is BCNUDH. DRC-wide annual totals (2025, 'l'année passée' in an article of March 2026); only the ~80% share is specific to the Kivus.
claims.researcher_note: Annual figures for 2025, date_precision set to year-level (flagged 'month' only because the schema has no year value). Another figure of 1,534 victims was posted by Actualite.cd on Facebook; this page is the UN News copy.

claims.text: ONU Info reported that, per the BCNUDH report, armed groups are responsible for 75 per cent of conflict-related sexual violence victims the previous year, with the M23 first at 439 victims, followed by Wazalendo groups, and that State actors including FARDC, the Police nationale congolaise and the Agence nationale de renseignement were involved in 19 per cent of documented cases.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 (439 victims); Wazalendo; State actors FARDC, PNC and ANR (19% of cases)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim. DRC-wide 2025 figures, not Kivu-specific. 75% refers to victims, 19% to cases.
claims.researcher_note: DRC-wide, annual 2025 figures; provincial split of perpetrators not given in the excerpts.

claims.text: ONU Info reported that, per the BCNUDH report, 70 per cent of conflict-related sexual violence victims have access to emergency medical care but fewer than 2 per cent receive holistic care including legal, psychological and social support.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim. DRC-wide 2025 figures.
claims.researcher_note: DRC-wide.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH recorded 61 victims of conflict-related sexual violence in January 2026, a 59 per cent drop from December 2025.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; the page says the report is for January 2026. DRC-wide monthly figure, not Kivu-specific.
claims.researcher_note: The article says the same report names the AFC/M23, ADF, Wazalendo groups and FDLR among armed-group perpetrators. DRC-wide report; Kivu share not in this excerpt.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH report notes that 42 political actors were still detained in January 2026, amid arrests judged arbitrary.
claims.verification_note: Actor 'State authorities' was inferred; set to not stated. DRC-wide; the article does not say who detained them or where.
claims.researcher_note: Not Kivu-specific; included as BCNUDH context. Excerpt does not say who detained them.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH documented 46 cases of conflict-related sexual violence in June 2026, against 40 in May, affecting 73 victims (56 women, 15 girls and 2 men), of whom North Kivu accounts for 52 and South Kivu 12, and that the AFC/M23 is cited for 34 victims.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu (52 victims), South Kivu (12), Ituri (8)
claims.actor_as_written: Non-State armed groups (77% of victims); AFC/M23 cited for 34 victims
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; year from the article's lead. The 34 AFC/M23 victims are a DRC-wide count; the article does not split them by province.
claims.researcher_note: Report published 20 Aug 2026 per Radio Okapi. Latest BCNUDH monthly figure found. Total June 2026 violations: 657 DRC-wide.

claims.text: The ICRC reported that violence and fighting in North and South Kivu hinder the movement of sick people, limit the transport of the wounded and make medical supplies hard to deliver, and have led to health-care workers leaving and medical facilities being looted or destroyed.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu and South Kivu (109 health centres studied)
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed to a named party
claims.verification_note: Figures field had 'Q1' (stray '1'); rewritten. ICRC attributes the decline also to drastic funding cuts; no party named as responsible.
claims.researcher_note: ICRC is not a UN body but is a primary humanitarian source. Release date 17 June 2025 from search listing. The release also mentions funding cuts as a factor.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported on 17 February 2025 that calm had returned to the city of Uvira after clashes that caused the death of 12 people, civilians and soldiers, and that the violence broke out the day before after an altercation between FARDC soldiers and a group of Wazalendo fighters. It cited Serge Kigwati, president of the Société civile des nationalistes congolais, as saying the altercation began when the Wazalendo tried to disarm soldiers returning from the northern front and heading south, and the FARDC refused to hand over their weapons.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo fighters (per Radio Okapi)
claims.verification_note: Page read in full; every clause on the page. The refusal clause is in Radio Okapi's narration and in Kigwati's quote.
claims.researcher_note: Perpetrator of individual deaths not stated. Later Actualite.cd reports 17 dead on 18-19 Feb (separate claim); Fides (relaying Radio Okapi) gives 12 on 17 Feb.

claims.text: MediaCongo reported that live-fire exchanges shook the city of Uvira on Sunday 16 February 2025 at the Kalundu port, where it said the FARDC and the Wazalendo clashed, the Wazalendo trying to prevent the FARDC from boarding a boat bound for Kalemie.
claims.place_as_written: Kalundu port, Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Page supports; credited at foot to 'Le hautpanel / MCP, via mediacongo.net'. excerpt_en flag is only the expansion of FARDC.
claims.researcher_note: Credited on page to 'Le hautpanel / MCP'; single outlet, no casualty figures. Article date taken from URL context (17 Feb); event date is 16 Feb as stated.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that at least 17 people were killed on Tuesday and Wednesday in the city of Uvira in spontaneous clashes between Congolese soldiers and Wazalendo militiamen (its headline says about ten dead; the local source it quotes gives a toll of more than 17 civilians, soldiers and Wazalendo combined), and quoted an unnamed local source who said the Wazalendo refused to let soldiers leave for Kalemie with weapons and ammunition, and that soldiers seized phones, money and other goods, broke down doors and shot civilians who resisted.
claims.actor_as_written: Congolese soldiers and wazalendo militiamen (per Actualite.cd and an unnamed local source)
claims.verification_note: Page read; anonymous local source carries the looting and the refusal clause. Headline says 'une dizaine de morts'; lede says at least 17. Sits beside Radio Okapi's 12 dead (17 Feb). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: headline says about ten dead 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Wazalendo refused to let soldiers leave for Kalemie with weapons and ammunition 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: local source's toll of more than 17 civilians, soldiers and Wazalendo; unnamed local source 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-014: Read the retained page: the refusal and looting account is one unnamed local source; the toll mixes civilians, soldiers and Wazalendo and conflicts with the headline's 'une dizaine'. Statement now carries both figures and the toll's scope so it is not read as civilian deaths.; excerpt-support: added 3 excerpt(s): headline says about ten dead; Wazalendo refused to let soldiers leave for Kalemie with weapons and ammunition; local source's toll of more than 17 civilians, soldiers and Wazalendo; unnamed local source
claims.researcher_note: Headline says 'une dizaine' (about ten) while the lede says at least 17; figure from an anonymous local source. Sits beside Radio Okapi's 12 dead on 16-17 Feb. Weekday dates (Tuesday 18, Wednesday 19) computed from the 19 Feb publication date.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that all detainees of the Uvira prison (named 'prison Mulunge d’Uvira' in the article) escaped that morning, and that the mass escape from the central prison of Uvira was confirmed notably by sources of the local Catholic church. A local activist told Actualite.cd that the prison doors were broken by fleeing soldiers who wanted to free their detained comrades and that other civilians also left.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira central prison, Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: fleeing soldiers broke the prison doors (per a local activist quoted by Actualite.cd)
claims.verification_note: Removed '19 February 2025' (publication date, not in excerpt; date field keeps it). Added the activist's account of who broke the doors, printed on the page. Fides (same day) says the state authorities decided to release the prisoners; the activist also says some had been released two days earlier under a presidential pardon. Unresolved discrepancy.
