claims.researcher_note: Category is a closest fit (prison escape). Fides gives a different account (authorities decided to release prisoners; separate claim). FIDH (SV-2025-014) mentions escapes at Uvira generally. Prison name as printed ('Mulunge').

claims.text: Agenzia Fides reported that the state authorities had even decided to release the prisoners before the rebels' arrival in Uvira, and that the withdrawal of Burundian soldiers a few days after the fall of Bukavu would have favoured the rebels' advance towards Uvira.
claims.verification_note: Removed publication date from statement. Fides gives no source for the release claim; conflicts with the Actualite.cd escape account.
claims.researcher_note: Unattributed in the Fides text; conflicts in framing with the 'escape' account (Actualite.cd) - an unresolved discrepancy. Burundian withdrawal hedged ('aurait').

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that after taking Bukavu and Kamanyola, the rebels conquered the cité of Sange, about 30 kilometres from Uvira, on Wednesday 19 February, and described the M23 as supported by the Rwandan army.
claims.actor_as_written: M23, supported by the Rwandan army (per Radio Okapi)
claims.verification_note: Page supports.
claims.researcher_note: Frontline claim. Actualite.cd (19 Feb) separately says AFC/M23 rebels arrived at Sange 'at least 35 km' from Uvira (headline seen only in search results, not fetched). Weekday date explicit on page.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that acts of pillage and violence were reported in Uvira, that armed persons were looting and ransacking shops and homes, and that the office of the Uvira bishopric was vandalised and priests and the bishop were assaulted and robbed of their belongings. It said local sources attributed these acts to FARDC soldiers and to undisciplined Wazalendo fighters.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC soldiers and undisciplined Wazalendo fighters (per local sources cited by Radio Okapi)
claims.verification_note: Removed publication date from statement (not in excerpt).
claims.researcher_note: Vatican News (separate claim) gives the bishopric incident in more detail; Vatican News's local source says it is unclear who is responsible and that both FARDC and Wazalendo profit from the panic.

claims.text: Vatican News reported that on Thursday 20 February three FARDC soldiers entered the episcopal seat of Uvira, forcing Mgr Muyengo Mulombe and two priests to hand over their phones and cash, and that the priests named in the article are Ricardo Mukuninwa and Bernard Kalolero.
claims.place_as_written: Episcopal seat, Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Page read in full; FARDC identification printed in the body. Names spelled as printed. Article by Marie Duhamel; details from a local source. Actualite.cd (23 Feb) says only 'trois militaires'.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet citing a local source. Page also says the amount handed over was about 50,000 FC (150 dollars), and that another community of priests of the parish Saints Anges Gardiens was visited by armed men.

claims.text: Kivutimes reported that night attacks by 'uncontrolled soldiers' were wreaking havoc in Uvira, notably in the Kimanga, Nyamianda, Kabindula, Kilibula, Songo and Mulongwe quarters, despite measures taken by the military authorities of the Sokola 2 Sud operational sector. It added, citing sources close to the institutions, that on Thursday 20 February these soldiers looted the CENI warehouse in Uvira and a Bralima depot at the Kalundu port.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city quarters (Kimanga, Nyamianda, Kabindula, Kilibula, Songo, Mulongwe) and Kalundu port, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: 'uncontrolled soldiers', often identified as soldiers who fled M23-held areas of Goma and Bukavu (per Kivutimes)
claims.verification_note: Narrowed to what the stored excerpts print; time and origin of the attackers moved to the note with a verbatim quote. The page dates the night attacks to the night of Friday 21 February 2025 from about 21h00 and says the attackers were often identified as soldiers who fled M23-held Goma and Bukavu (see replacement quote); these details are not in the stored excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Local outlet, single source. The article's date (21 Feb) coincides with the 'Friday 21 February' night it describes, so the report may have been posted or updated later; treat the night-attack date as approximate.

claims.text: Actualite.cd, in an article built on a message by the Bishop of Uvira, reported that banks, pharmacies, markets and health centres had closed in Uvira, and quoted Mgr Sébastien-Joseph Muyengo Mulombe describing systematic looting with violence and killings, including in family homes and convents.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (armed groups including routed soldiers and unidentified fighters, per the article)
claims.verification_note: Page supports; the closure sentence is the outlet's narration. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: The closure statement is the article's own sentence following the bishop's quote; it does not say which health centres or for how long. The same article says political-administrative authorities and much of the police and army fled to Burundi, Kalemie or Tanzania (not separately excerpted).

claims.text: MSF said that the Hôpital Général de Référence in Uvira had repeatedly been caught in crossfire, endangering patients and staff, that medical activities had to be interrupted again the previous week with patients sheltering, and that armed men entered the hospital premises, moving and firing inside.
claims.place_as_written: Hôpital Général de Référence, Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed men; not further identified by MSF (MSF describes clashes between FARDC and Wazalendo in the city)
claims.verification_note: Removed publication date from statement; figures field (from 17 Feb, about ten wounded per day per structure) supported by replacement quote (page spells 'févier'). MSF does not identify the armed men. MSF testimony page dated 23 Feb 2025; staff names anonymised.
claims.researcher_note: MSF primary statement; Radio Okapi (25 Feb) relays it. Date range approximate: 'last week' relative to 23 Feb, and MSF says the situation peaked on 15 Feb. MSF names staff only anonymised.

claims.text: MSF said that it had been forced to reduce its teams in Uvira, where they had supported the Ministry of Health in diagnosing and treating mpox patients for several months, and that it redirected part of its activity to supporting the care of war wounded by delivering medical supplies to several health structures in the Uvira health zone.
claims.verification_note: Redirection clause is on the page, not in the stored excerpt; supplied. MSF says it was 'forced to reduce' its teams; Actualite.cd (3 Mar) says MSF withdrew its staff. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: redirected activity to war wounded via medical supplies in Uvira health zone 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-014: Wording only: the source says 'contrainte de réduire' (forced to reduce), which is the health-access point; Actualite.cd's 'withdrew' (in note) is a stronger version not supported by MSF.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): redirected activity to war wounded via medical supplies in Uvira health zone
claims.researcher_note: Actualite.cd (3 Mar) says humanitarian organisations such as MSF were forced to withdraw staff from Uvira; MSF's own words are 'reduce' - recorded as a discrepancy of wording.

claims.text: OCHA said it was alarmed by the escalation of violence and insecurity in Uvira, and that clashes and rising crime were putting local communities and humanitarian workers in extreme danger, with humanitarian partners reporting multiple incidents of looting and sexual violence.
claims.verification_note: Page supports verbatim. No number, date, victims or perpetrators given for the sexual violence incidents. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: UN daily briefing note; no number of incidents, dates, victims or perpetrators given. Date is the publication date (reported). Only UN-level indication found for sexual violence in Uvira city in Q1; a Facebook post (not cited) says the FARDC accused the Rwandan army and AFC/M23 of looting and sexual violence in Uvira - not verified.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the spokesperson of the Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu operation, Jérémie Meya (lieutenant Jérémie Meya Gbe), said the FARDC had begun an operation to track down fleeing soldiers and alleged perpetrators of various harassments in Uvira, with the stated aim of 'cleaning' Uvira and the localities of the Ruzizi plain so the population could go about its business safely.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city and the Ruzizi plain, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Page supports; full name, rank and the Ruzizi-plain clause supplied from the page.
claims.researcher_note: FARDC acknowledgement of indiscipline by its own soldiers; the page also quotes Meya's objective sentence on restoring order and discipline after 'acts of barbarity and indiscipline' by soldiers fleeing the front lines.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that over the previous few days at least 20 dead and more than 60 people wounded by bullets had been taken in charge in the Uvira health zone, and that humanitarian organisations had recorded a toll of about a hundred wounded; it did not say whether the dead and wounded were civilians or combatants, or who caused the casualties.
claims.verification_note: Figures field rewritten in the source's own wording ('une centaine'), not the numeral. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-014: Figure scope: the source does not say the casualties were civilians, and the same days' clashes involved soldiers and Wazalendo (Actualite.cd 19 Feb counts civilians, soldiers and Wazalendo together). Added so the claim is not read as a civilian toll under attack_on_civilians.; excerpt-support: no change needed; every clause is printed in the stored excerpts
claims.researcher_note: Article does not name who is counting or the period precisely; figures may include soldiers. Compare Radio Okapi 12 dead (17 Feb) and Actualite.cd 17 dead (19 Feb).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that political-administrative authorities, FARDC soldiers and police settled in the city of Uvira on Monday 24 February, and that governor Jean-Jacques Pulusi, his deputy and about 600 uniformed men, including police and soldiers, who had left Bukavu some days earlier for Burundi, arrived in Uvira through the Kavimvira border.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city (Kavimvira border post), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: South Kivu provincial government (Governor Jean-Jacques Pulusi)
claims.verification_note: Page supports.
claims.researcher_note: The deputy governor is not named in this article (later SOS Médias Burundi names Jean Jacques Elekano as vice-governor). The provincial government's own account is in the next claim.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing the communication cell of the South Kivu governor, that the provincial executive head and his deputy were now staying in Uvira and would continue to administer South Kivu from there because Bukavu, the capital, was under rebel occupation.
claims.verification_note: Page supports; statement is the communication cell's as relayed.
claims.researcher_note: Statement relayed second-hand through Radio Okapi; the date given is the 24 Feb arrival. The page adds that the DRC ambassador to Burundi, Willy Mulamba Mabika, facilitated the return.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several witnesses, that Wazalendo-affiliated fighters under the command of 'generals Mayele and Makanaki' had multiplied acts of pillage in the Songo, Kabindula and Nyamianda quarters of Uvira, targeting the Banyamulenge community, and that some Wazalendo justified the attacks by accusing the Banyamulenge of complicity with the M23; a community leader it quoted rejected that accusation as false.
claims.place_as_written: Songo, Kabindula and Nyamianda quarters, Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo fighters under 'generals Mayele and Makanaki' (per witnesses cited by SOS Médias Burundi)
claims.verification_note: Page supports; Banyamulenge targeting and the M23 justification are on the page, supplied. Article by Adam Ntwari (SOS Médias Burundi). A community leader quoted rejects the accusations. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: targeting the Banyamulenge community 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Wazalendo justification: Banyamulenge complicity with M23 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: community leader rejected the accusation as false 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-014: Attribution is hedged ('selon plusieurs témoins') and kept. Read the retained page: the 'community leader rejects the accusations' line in the note refutes the M23-complicity charge, not the looting; added as the counter-account. No Wazalendo response on the page.; excerpt-support: added 3 excerpt(s): targeting the Banyamulenge community; Wazalendo justification: Banyamulenge complicity with M23; community leader rejected the accusation as false
claims.researcher_note: Burundi-based outlet; witnesses unnamed except 'David M.', a trader from Kabindula (partial name), who describes theft of his phone, computer and clothes. Spellings 'Mayele' and 'Makanaki' as printed; not to be confused with Twirwaneho's Colonel Makanika (spelled differently). Date is the report date (25 Mar), activity described as ongoing in March.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Friday 21 March 2025 Wazalendo fighters attacked the premises of the organisation Ebenezer International Ministry in Uvira, taking several electronic devices, including computers and Motorola phones.
claims.verification_note: Page supports verbatim.
claims.researcher_note: Single local source; an organisation official is quoted anonymously.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the vice-governor of South Kivu, Jean Jacques Elekano, condemned the violence against the Banyamulenge in Uvira and called for respect for all communities, saying in a communiqué that surveillance had been reinforced and calling on law enforcement to act firmly against these abuses.
claims.verification_note: Page supports. Communiqué date not given; 25 Mar is the report date.
claims.researcher_note: Communiqué not found on an official site; quoted via SOS Médias Burundi only. The page also says the Banyamulenge say no concrete measure has been taken.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that on 14 February Wazalendo fighters killed a 25-year-old Munyamulenge man in Mulongwe, Uvira territory, after accusing him of being Rwandan; he was shot twice in the hip and died of his wounds, according to two sources.
claims.verification_note: Page supports.
claims.researcher_note: Report published 2025-05-23, event dated 14 Feb by HRW; victim not named. 'Mulongwe' is also a quarter of Uvira city (Kivutimes) and a Burundian refugee camp; HRW says 'in Uvira territory'.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that after the M23 took Bukavu, Wazalendo fighters entered more than 20 Banyamulenge homes in Uvira, stealing property and threatening residents, and that in one case they shot a woman in the head and beat at least three people.
claims.verification_note: The draft split 'in one case' from the beatings; HRW puts both in the one case. Figures rewritten in the source's words. HRW does not say whether the woman survived or give dates for individual incidents.
claims.researcher_note: Period not precisely dated by HRW ('after the taking of Bukavu', which other claims date 16 Feb); end of range is the report date. HRW does not say whether the woman survived. Corroborates the SOS Médias Burundi 25 Mar account of Wazalendo looting of Banyamulenge homes.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that on 3 March in Sange, Uvira territory, a Wazalendo commander arrested and whipped a 48-year-old man accused of stealing a television, and that a relative and a neighbour said the man died of his injuries.
claims.actor_as_written: a Wazalendo commander (not named by HRW)
claims.verification_note: Page supports. HRW adds that the commander was later dismissed but not prosecuted.
claims.researcher_note: Victim and commander not named in this passage. HRW adds the commander was later involved in the killing of a Congolese soldier and was dismissed but not prosecuted for those killings (not excerpted).

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that on 3 March Wazalendo fighters attacked several Banyamulenge villages within 10 km of Bibokoboko, Fizi territory, and that a military source and residents said there was no known presence of opposing armed groups near Bibokoboko at the time.
claims.place_as_written: Bibokoboko area, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Statement unchanged; figures field removed because the seven-killed figure is a community leader's quote carried by claim 26, not by this excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Outside Uvira territory (Fizi) but in the same Wazalendo/Banyamulenge dynamic and recorded here for the Uvira investigation; a community leader quoted by HRW says seven people were killed and homes, medical centres and schools destroyed (see next claim).

claims.text: Human Rights Watch quoted a community leader as saying, of the 3 March Wazalendo attack around Bibokoboko in Fizi territory, that the fighters said they had come to 'clean' the Banyamulenge, killed seven people and destroyed homes, medical centres and schools.
claims.place_as_written: Bibokoboko area, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo fighters (per a community leader quoted by Human Rights Watch)
claims.verification_note: Date and Fizi location supplied from the adjoining HRW paragraph; quote attributed to an unnamed community leader as HRW does. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified contradicting source(s) recorded in notes; not regraded pending review. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Quote of an unnamed community leader. HRW separately confirmed with satellite imagery and geolocated photographs that houses were burned that day in several villages including Madjdja, Lulimba I and Bibokoboko (not excerpted here). Which medical centres is not stated. Contradicting reporting: Kivu Times (2025-03-06): Figure: at least 8 civilians killed (including a woman), versus 7 in the claim

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing hospital sources, that the Uvira health zone faced an outbreak of cholera among soldiers, with at least 40 cases hospitalised in the cholera treatment unit of the Uvira general hospital, and a medical official quoted as saying the unit was completely overwhelmed with patients lying on the floor.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira general hospital, Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Page supports; quote supplied. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: The page also says the situation had deteriorated in preceding weeks because of Wazalendo-FARDC clashes, hospitals saw an influx of wounded, and humanitarian organisations such as MSF withdrew staff (MSF's own word is 'reduce teams'). OCHA (7 Mar via search result, not fetched) reports 200+ new cases and two deaths in Uvira over two days.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that at least 90 soldiers from the North and South Kivu fronts had been appearing since Wednesday 12 February before the military garrison tribunal of Uvira on various counts, notably fleeing before the M23 and extortion.
claims.place_as_written: Military garrison tribunal, Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: 'Tried' in figures implied a completed trial; narrowed to 'appearing'. 'griefs' rendered as counts. Trial stage only (comparaissent); no verdict reported. Prosecutor named on the page as lieutenant colonel magistrat Lwamba Songe.
claims.researcher_note: Category is a closest fit (trial of soldiers). The page says the trial runs alongside one in Bukavu with 282 soldiers; the military magistrate is named as Lt Col Lwamba Songe (not in this excerpt); the accused were allegedly caught with 59 AK-47s and some were already on a boat bound for Tanganyika.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 rebels took control of the villages Rurambo and Kigarama, in the Bafuliro chiefdom in the Uvira highlands, following the allegiance of the Rushaba wazalendo group to the AFC/M23.
claims.place_as_written: Rurambo and Kigarama, Bafuliro chiefdom, Uvira territory (highlands), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 with the allied Rushaba wazalendo group (per Actualite.cd)
claims.verification_note: Page supports.
claims.researcher_note: Page quotes a local notable describing fighting on 'yesterday' (12 March) from 04:00 to 17:00 against the wazalendo group of Ruma Hondwa; date computed from 'hier' and the 13 March publication date. Earlier in March the M23 advanced from Kaziba (Walungu).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that local civil society said Rushaba had been with Nyamusaraba in the 'Task force' together with the Burundian forces before deserting it, starting clashes at Kashama and allying with the M23. The article describes the Task force as composed of Congolese soldiers, Burundian soldiers and wazalendo, and quotes another source on site as saying there was a coalition of Banyamulenge based in Kahololo/Marungu, Rushaba wazalendo and M23 elements from Kaziba.
claims.place_as_written: Kashama, Kigarama and Uvira highlands, Uvira territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Task force of Congolese soldiers, Burundian soldiers and wazalendo; Rushaba wazalendo group (per Actualite.cd)
claims.verification_note: The coalition clause is attributed on the page to 'une autre source sur place', not to the article itself; attribution restored.
claims.researcher_note: Local civil society source; evidence of Burundian forces still working with a Task force in the Uvira highlands in mid-March. The same page says the villages Murambi, Kitoga, Babingwa, Kitembe and Kahusi remained under the government coalition's control.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Minembwe group of villages in Fizi territory fell on Friday into the hands of fighters of the armed group Twirwaneho, two days after the death of Colonel Makanika, the group's military chief, killed in a drone attack. Citing witnesses, it said Twirwaneho fighters occupied all FARDC positions in several named localities, and a Twirwaneho fighter told the outlet that the soldiers had abandoned several weapons and ammunition.
claims.verification_note: Draft attributed the fall itself to witnesses (the page states it as the outlet's own) and put 'FARDC' into the fighter's quote, which says 'les militaires'. Corrected. The fall of Minembwe is the outlet's narration; witnesses are cited for the positions. The fighter's quote is a party's claim.
claims.researcher_note: Friday date computed from weekday and the 23 Feb (Sunday) publication date, i.e. 21 Feb; Makanika's death (about 19 Feb) said to be 'two days' earlier. Single local source. Twirwaneho's allegiance to AFC/M23 after Makanika's death is reported by Actualite.cd on 13 Mar (see Rurambo claim).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi quoted residents of Minembwe, who came out to celebrate Twirwaneho's capture of the area (which the article, dated 23 February 2025, places 'ce vendredi'), as saying that FARDC soldiers and Maï-Maï militiamen had looted their cows, killed people, stolen from fields and houses and raped their women and girls; the residents gave no dates, places or numbers for these acts, and the article sets them in a context of insecurity it dates to 2017. It said it tried without success to reach a FARDC spokesperson.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC soldiers and Maï-Maï militiamen (alleged by residents quoted by SOS Médias Burundi)
claims.verification_note: Page supports; FARDC no-comment line supplied. General allegation by unnamed residents celebrating one party's capture; no dates, numbers or victims. SOS Médias Burundi says it tried without success to reach a FARDC spokesperson. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: capture 'ce vendredi' 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: residents celebrating the capture 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: tried without success to reach a FARDC spokesperson 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: context of insecurity dated to 2017 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-014: Time slippage: the residents' imperfect-tense accusations are undated and the page frames them within insecurity 'depuis 2017', so they cannot be placed in the 2025 window. Statement now says so and carries the FARDC no-comment; speakers are partisan-adjacent (celebrating one party's capture).; excerpt-support: added 4 excerpt(s): capture 'ce vendredi'; residents celebrating the capture; tried without success to reach a FARDC spokesperson; context of insecurity dated to 2017 | replaced the inferred date 'about 21 February 2025' with the article's own wording ('ce vendredi', article dated 23 February 2025)
claims.researcher_note: Unverified general allegation by unnamed residents in a context of celebration of one party's capture; no dates, numbers or victims. The article says it tried to reach a FARDC spokesperson (outcome not excerpted).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the rebels' advance, after their capture of Bukavu and Kamanyola, came as Burundian troops began to withdraw from Congolese soil, after having fought alongside the FARDC and the Wazalendo under bilateral cooperation between the Burundian and Congolese governments.
claims.place_as_written: Kamanyola / Ruzizi plain towards Uvira, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed the Fides sentence: Fides is not a source of this claim. 'FDNB' is not printed on the page; removed from actor. Agenzia Fides separately says the Burundian withdrawal 'would have' favoured the advance (claim 4).
claims.researcher_note: Burundi has not (in sources found) publicly announced this in the Q1 window beyond a Burundian interior-ministry statement that 100+ Congolese police fled to Burundi from Uvira. Reuters (found only as search results, not fetched) says Burundi withdrew most of its 12,000 troops in February; Burundi/DRC officials confirmed a troop reduction on 25 Feb per Critical Threats (digest, not cited). The Fides piece is a hedged second source in a separate claim.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that at least a hundred Congolese police officers had fled to Burundi from Uvira, as announced on Wednesday in Bujumbura by the Burundian minister in charge of internal affairs.
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian Ministry of Interior (statement relayed by SOS Médias Burundi)
claims.verification_note: Page supports verbatim; minister not named.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('Wednesday') and the 20 Feb publication date, i.e. 19 Feb. Minister is not named on the page. Burundi government statement as relayed, not seen on an official site.

claims.text: BBC News Afrique reported that Wazalendo fighters reportedly wanted to seize the Congolese army's weapons and ammunition, accusing the soldiers of having deserted the front lines and fallen back south to Kalemie. An unnamed source told the BBC that the Wazalendo rose up to oppose the abuses of the regular army and asked the regular troops to give them their weapons, and that about 15 000 Congolese had crossed into Burundi. The BBC said it could not independently verify this information.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (motive as described by an unnamed source to the BBC)
claims.verification_note: The draft put the BBC's own hedged narration ('auraient voulu') in the unnamed source's mouth; split the two and added the BBC's no-verification line, printed on the page. Byline Alfred Lasteck and Ashley Lime, published 22 Feb 2025. Event date approximate.
claims.researcher_note: BBC states it could not verify independently; page is dated by search result (22 Feb) and refers to events on Wednesday (19 Feb). Gives the Wazalendo's side of why they disarmed FARDC soldiers; no Wazalendo spokesperson found speaking directly.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that military, humanitarian and other sources expressed concern about the lack of command and control by the Congolese army over the Wazalendo, who in some cases were said to have even disarmed or attacked soldiers.
claims.verification_note: Page supports; HRW's hedge ('auraient') kept as 'were said to have'. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Context for the FARDC-Wazalendo clashes in Uvira; not itself an incident claim. HRW also names Justin Bitakwira Bihona Hayi as the National Assembly member coordinating support to Wazalendo in South Kivu and says an armed-group commander complained on 4 April that he was not distributing government funds fully (outside Q1 window; not excerpted).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing several of its sources, that two groups of Wazalendo militiamen led by self-proclaimed generals René Makanaki and Itongwa (head of the Landa Bango group) fought each other on Saturday 5 April in the Mulongwe commercial centre and its surroundings in Uvira; a local civil society actor said some wounded were taken to the Uvira general referral hospital (HGR), and the sources said Néné Rubota, spokesperson of a synergy of Wazalendo armed groups led by General Gashumba, was shot and wounded.
claims.place_as_written: Mulongwe (commercial centre), Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo groups of self-proclaimed generals René Makanaki and Itongwa (Landa Bango), as Actualite.cd names them
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the retained page; single outlet relaying anonymous sources. The same page also spells the first commander 'Makanika' in a quoted passage; spelling unconfirmed.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet citing unnamed sources. Report states calm returned the next day. Reasons for the fight per sources quoted: clearance fees and leadership (not in excerpt).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, for several days, Wazalendo of different groups controlled the city of Uvira, which it described as the provisional capital of South Kivu.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo of different groups, as Actualite.cd says
claims.verification_note: Outlet's own narration; excerpt matches.
claims.researcher_note: Contrast with UN Group of Experts (see GoE claims): Wazalendo de facto control from February; FARDC HQ and governorate re-established in Uvira early March. Excerpt also records two civil society actors denouncing attacks and threats by Wazalendo.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts on the DRC reported in its final report that from February, as DRC authorities and security actors largely withdrew from Uvira, Wazalendo armed groups took de facto control of Uvira city and its surroundings, used disproportionate force and committed widespread abuses, targeting Banyamulenge communities in particular.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city and surroundings, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo armed groups, as the Group of Experts names them
claims.verification_note: Statement supported (para. 173); end date corrected to the report's transmission date (page: 'Le présent rapport a été communiqué le 6 mai 2025 au Comité'). The Group's final report (S/2025/446) was transmitted to the Sanctions Committee on 6 May 2025 and published 3 July 2025; its 'present' is about early May 2025, not June.
claims.researcher_note: Final report of the Group of Experts; sources cited in its footnote: civil society, FARDC, UN, researchers. Report period extends to its drafting (before 3 July 2025).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that, at a meeting, Wazalendo factions complained of lack of support, military logistics and funding, and that to calm them the Defence Minister announced that all Wazalendo leaders would be placed under the authority of the RAD.
claims.actor_as_written: Guy Kabombo (DRC Minister of Defence), as the Group of Experts reports
claims.verification_note: 'in Uvira' removed: the report says only 'Lors d'une réunion' (in the passage on the Uvira visit), not where the meeting was held.
claims.researcher_note: Matches Radio Okapi 8 April 2025 account.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local civil society, that DRC Defence Minister Guy Kabombo announced in Uvira on Monday 7 April that the local Wazalendo fighters supporting the army in defending the city depend exclusively from now on on the national coordinator of the Armed Defence Reserve (RAD), General Padiri Bulenda.
claims.actor_as_written: Guy Kabombo, DRC Minister of Defence
claims.verification_note: Radio Okapi attributes the account to local civil society (headline '(société civile)'); attribution kept.
claims.researcher_note: The announcement is reported through local civil society, as the page states. Corroborated by UN Group of Experts (para. 174).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that during the Defence Minister's visit to Uvira (dateline 7 April 2025), fighters complained that the Burundian army had reportedly forbidden them from attacking M23 positions at Kamanyola, and that Defence Minister Guy Kabombo replied that the restrictions aimed to avoid uncoordinated actions that could compromise joint operations, while reaffirming the Congolese government's confidence in the FDNB.
claims.verification_note: Conditional ('aurait interdit') preserved as 'reportedly'.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet. Later SOS Médias Burundi (15 May) repeats that Wazalendo accuse some Burundian units of slowing their offensives. No Burundian government statement found (see gaps).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that FARDC and Wazalendo exchanged fire from Thursday 24 April at Rugenge and in the heights of Uvira, over occupation of certain positions; sources quoted said the cause was a camp-management dispute.
claims.place_as_written: Rugenge and the hills above Uvira, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and Wazalendo, as Actualite.cd names them
claims.verification_note: 'occupation of positions' clause is on the page next to the excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Two parties' accounts recorded in separate claims (Sukola 2 communiqué; Wazalendo discontent per Radio Okapi/MediaCongo). No casualty figure given in this source.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the army described the gunfire as a redeployment of its forces: a communiqué signed by Lieutenant Elongo Kyondwa Marc, spokesperson of the Sukola 2 operational sector, said the shots heard in the hills overlooking Uvira were due to loyalist soldiers redeploying on different ridges to ensure maximum protection of the city.
claims.verification_note: Matches page.
claims.researcher_note: Party account (FARDC); contrasts with the account of local sources that FARDC and Wazalendo clashed over positions.

claims.text: MediaCongo, relaying Radio Okapi and MCP, reported that on Friday 25 April heavy gunfire between FARDC and Wazalendo shook Uvira again; Sukola 2 Sud-Sud spokesperson Lieutenant Marc Elongo said the fighting was linked to the redeployment of FARDC from Katongo to the Hauts Plateaux of Fizi, and that the Wazalendo, displeased, expressed opposition by firing, suspecting this regular army unit of collaborating with rebels in the Fizi Hauts Plateaux.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira hills; Katongo to Hauts Plateaux of Fizi, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Page credits 'Radio Okapi / MCP, via mediacongo.net'; independent of the Actualite.cd report of the same days.
claims.researcher_note: Page credits 'MediaCongo Radio Okapi / MCP, via mediacongo.net'; the original Radio Okapi page was not opened. The page names the spokesperson as lieutenant Marc Elongo; Actualite.cd prints Elongo Kyondwa Marc.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that FARDC and their wazalendo allies clashed again on the morning of Thursday 1 May in two neighbourhoods of Uvira: according to local sources fighting began about 5:00 a.m. at Kasenga and spread to the hills overlooking the city; shooting stopped in the city centre around 10:00 but continued in the surrounding hills. The reasons given by different sources were control and management of certain positions in and around the city.
claims.place_as_written: Kasenga and Kakombe, hills overlooking Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and wazalendo, as Actualite.cd names them
claims.verification_note: All on page.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborated by Radio Okapi (2 May) and SOS Médias Burundi (2 May).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that calm returned on Friday 2 May in the communes of Kasenga, Kavimvira and Mulongwe in Uvira, 24 hours after fighting between the FARDC and Wazalendo; according to local sources the clash wounded civilians, but the number of victims was not specified.
claims.place_as_written: Kasenga, Kavimvira and Mulongwe communes, Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and Wazalendo, as Radio Okapi names them
claims.verification_note: Matches.
claims.researcher_note: Another outlet (Facebook relays of Actualite.cd/Radio Okapi, not opened) reported 11 dead in two days; no opened page I could fetch carried a death toll - not recorded as a figure.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the Sukola 2 Sud-Sud operations confirmed that the points of divergence had been smoothed out and that the FARDC were securing the city, upstream and downstream, describing a misunderstanding maintained by a small group of Wazalendo.
claims.verification_note: Spokesperson unnamed on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Party account (FARDC); names not printed by the page.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the South Kivu provincial administration continued to publicly deny any clash between FARDC and Wazalendo in the Uvira region, that it had received no official statement from the local FARDC command despite repeated attempts to contact it, and, citing several local testimonies, that the hostilities were triggered by an FARDC attempt to install new military positions at Kituntu, about ten kilometres from Uvira.
claims.place_as_written: Kasenga and Kakombe hills, Kituntu, Uvira, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: South Kivu provincial administration; FARDC; Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: Conditional 'auraient été déclenchées' kept via 'citing testimonies'.
claims.researcher_note: Provincial denial reported by an outlet; Actualite.cd and Radio Okapi independently report the clashes. Page lead says 'Malgré les dénégations des autorités provinciales'. SOS Médias dateline is Bukavu although the report concerns Uvira.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that fighting broke out between Wazalendo and AFC/M23 rebels in the territories of Uvira and Walungu, with the agglomerations of Katogota and Kamanyola in a spiral of violence since Monday 5 May; according to local sources the Wazalendo launched a surprise attack first on forward M23 positions, the clashes lasted eight hours on the hills of Rutebe, Kayange and Luzinzi, civilians were wounded, and both sides suffered losses according to a human rights activist.
claims.place_as_written: Katogota, Kamanyola, hills of Rutebe, Kayange and Luzinzi, Ruzizi plain (Uvira/Walungu border), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo; AFC/M23, as Radio Okapi names them
claims.verification_note: Matches page.
claims.researcher_note: No AFC/M23 account of this clash found (see gaps).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on the Wednesday before its publication the FARDC chief of staff, Lieutenant General Jules Banza Mwilambwe, and his Burundian counterpart, General Prime Niyongabo, head of the FDNB, crossed the border at Kavimvira escorted by a large Burundian military contingent and headed to the 'Sokola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu' operational sector, where they held a closed meeting; they left around 16:50 for Bujumbura without a statement to the press.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira (Kavimvira crossing, Sokola 2 Sud operational sector), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Sources 0 and 1 carry the same excerpt; both fine.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('ce mercredi') and publication date 15 May; a lapresseafricaine.net snippet (not opened) gives 14 May. Section 'Selon des sources sécuritaires locales' speculation about drones is not recorded. No official statement on the meeting found.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that tensions between FARDC, Wazalendo militias and Burundian troops were worsening notably in the Katogota and Kamanyola areas, and that Wazalendo militiamen accuse certain Burundian units of slowing their offensives against the M23.
claims.place_as_written: Katogota and Kamanyola areas, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Accusation stays attributed.
claims.researcher_note: Allegation by Wazalendo as reported; no Burundian response found.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 approximately 14 FDNB battalions under the 'Task Force Congo' (TAFOC) umbrella were still on DRC territory, of which 10 were reportedly in the Ruzizi Plain, two in and around Uvira and two in the Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, and that FARDC, FDNB and intelligence sources estimated at least 7,000 troops in South Kivu.
claims.place_as_written: Ruzizi Plain, Uvira and Hauts Plateaux (near Minembwe), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Annex 72 text matches. The same report elsewhere gives 7 000 to 9 000 Burundian soldiers, most in South Kivu, in early April; SOS Médias Burundi gives nearly 10.000.
claims.researcher_note: From the English-language annex text embedded in the French PDF. The Group says deployed battalions were probably not fully constituted (650 soldiers per organic battalion).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that, at the time of its final report, the AFC/M23 controlled mining areas in Kalehe, Walungu and Mwenga territories as far as Kamanyola in the south, while the FARDC, FDNB and Wazalendo kept control of the Ruzizi plain and held positions along the Kamanyola-Sange-Uvira road, blocking the AFC/M23 advance towards Uvira.
claims.place_as_written: Kamanyola - Sange - Uvira road, Ruzizi plain, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (with RDF per the Group); FARDC, FDNB, Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: Date corrected from June to the report's reference time (transmitted 6 May 2025). 'At the time of the report': the report was transmitted to the Sanctions Committee on 6 May 2025 (published 3 July 2025).
claims.researcher_note: Exact date of the situation is 'at the time of the report'; the report was dated 3 July 2025, so mid-2025 is approximate. Sources cited by the Group: FARDC, AFC/M23, civil society, UN, intelligence services, researchers.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Pulusi returned to Uvira, the provisional capital of the province, on Tuesday 20 May after four months' absence, and, in an address to residents, said he carried a message from the head of state announcing the 'beginning of the end' of the M23 war; a local civil society actor said that for them the end of the war means the withdrawal of the rebels from occupied territories, among other things.
claims.verification_note: Matches. Radio Okapi spells the name 'Pulusi' in the text and 'Purusi' in the headline and tags.
claims.researcher_note: Name spelling varies on the page and in the URL ('Pulusi' vs 'Purusi'); other outlets print 'Purusi'. The same page says some inhabitants were sceptical.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch said that in April it received credible information of Wazalendo fighters beating and whipping men and women they accused of having acted inappropriately, and quoted an Uvira resident as saying that some Wazalendo act as if they were the police.
claims.place_as_written: South Kivu (resident quoted is from Uvira)
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo fighters, as Human Rights Watch names them
claims.verification_note: Location of the April beatings not given by HRW beyond South Kivu context.
claims.researcher_note: HRW does not state in these sentences that the April beatings took place in Uvira; the Uvira quotation is a resident's general remark. Treat the location as South Kivu. Other incidents in the same HRW release (Mulongwe 14 February; Sange 3 March; Bibokoboko 3 March) fall before the 1 April start of this unit and were not recorded here.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that South Kivu's interim governor, Jean-Jacques Elakano, told media on 23 April that the province could not collect taxes because of Wazalendo fighters, who should not 'substitute for the State'; HRW also reported that in March and April Wazalendo set up roadblocks on main roads linking several South Kivu towns, where they harassed residents and collected 500 to 1 000 Congolese francs per person.
claims.verification_note: Matches.
claims.researcher_note: Discrepancy to surface: HRW calls Elakano 'gouverneur intérimaire'; the elected-appointed governor Jean-Jacques Purusi/Pulusi was reported by Radio Okapi (21 May) to have been absent from Uvira for four months, returning 20 May. HRW's roadblock sentence does not name Uvira.

claims.text: Imurenge.com, a Banyamulenge community website, reported that, since February 2025, reports indicate that over 40 Banyamulenge individuals in Uvira had been assaulted and robbed, one young man killed and a woman seriously injured, and that Wazalendo militias were preventing many Banyamulenge from returning to work at Kalundu port and the Kavimvira border post.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city (Kalundu port, Kavimvira border post), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo militias, as Imurenge.com names them
claims.verification_note: Attributed as the site's account. The same page describes two individual incidents of 17 April in Uvira with two named persons (an abduction near Maendeleo port and a seizure/robbery in Gasenga); not captured as claims; lead for a gap round. Imurenge.com is a Banyamulenge community website (an interested party); figures are its own and unsourced ('reports indicate').
claims.researcher_note: Community website; 'reports indicate' is not attributed to a named monitor. Corroborated in general terms by UN Group of Experts (para. 173) and HRW (23 May). The killing and injury may overlap with incidents HRW dates to February; not independently established. Page says the 'Uvira Security Committee' issued directives, but its members were not named.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several local sources, that Banyamulenge police officers, teachers and women travelling towards Bijombo in Uvira territory were arrested, tortured and stripped of their belongings by Wazalendo elements on Wednesday 11 June 2025 (date per the photo caption), the victims including seven police officers, four teachers and two women; the victims said they were intercepted by men of the self-proclaimed generals Landabango and Alexis Dunia while on the road to Bijombo under escort of Burundian soldiers, and the Wazalendo reportedly then arrested them, accusing them of belonging to the M23. The outlet reported that police officers and teachers were freed through the intervention of the deputy mayor of the city of Uvira.
claims.place_as_written: Road to Bijombo, Uvira territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo of self-proclaimed generals Landabango and Alexis Dunia, as the victims say
claims.verification_note: Conditional 'auraient arrêtés' restored; release narrowed to police officers and teachers as the page says; date anchored to the caption; territory is Uvira territory, not the city. An open letter from local organisations including CEPCC, quoted by the outlet, places the incident between the Bavira chiefdom and a Wazalendo camp led by 'general Dunia'. The self-proclaimed Wazalendo 'general' Alexis Dunia is not the FARDC 33rd military region commander General Dunia.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet relaying local sources and victims' statements; no named victims. Open letter to the governor by local organisations including CEPCC is reported on the same page. The article's headline and dateline say Bukavu, while the events concern Uvira territory. The 'ce mercredi' in the text and the photo caption date (11 June 2025) agree. No Wazalendo or FARDC response found. The 'général Alexis Dunia' named here may be distinct from the FARDC 33rd military region commander General Dunia (Radio Okapi, 9 April) - not established.

claims.text: MSF said that since February, in collaboration with the health ministry, it had treated nearly 400 war-wounded and 800 cholera cases in three dedicated treatment centres in South Kivu, and that Uvira was hosting more than 250 000 displaced people since the start of the fighting.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira and Ruzizi health zones, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Matches. The same MSF page reports gunfire inside a hospital and medical facilities hit in Uvira in February 2025 (outside this unit's window). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Treatment figures cover three centres, not only Uvira (Actualite.cd's relay of the MSF release places them in the Uvira and Ruzizi health zones). The '2' in 'personnes2' in the displaced-persons excerpt is a footnote marker in the page text. MSF has been present in Uvira since September 2024 for a mpox response (same page).

claims.text: MSF said that persistent insecurity had made the road between Bukavu, Kamanyola and Uvira almost impassable, making it impossible for humanitarian organisations to move between the two sides of the front line, and MSF reported adapting by crossing different countries to bring aid and provide care on each side.
claims.place_as_written: Bukavu - Kamanyola - Uvira road, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Matches.
claims.researcher_note: Date is the publication date; the access constraint is described as ongoing. MSF does not attribute the insecurity to a party.

claims.text: MSF's medical lead in Uvira, Dr Aurora Revuelta, said MSF had intensified its response to strengthen capacity to care for war wounds, cholera cases and victims and survivors of sexual violence.
claims.verification_note: Matches. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Records MSF's statement on care provision only; the page gives no incident, date or perpetrator for any sexual violence.

claims.text: MSF said that Kamanyola, close to Katogota, was under M23/AFC control and had also seen its health system weakened by violence, and that while some stability had been restored in the town, most fighting continued in the surrounding hills, making access to fields impossible.
claims.verification_note: Original implied M23/AFC control weakened the health system; MSF says the health system was weakened 'by violence'.
claims.researcher_note: Consistent with the UN Group of Experts (Kamanyola as the southern limit of AFC/M23 control).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the UN Deputy Special Representative and Humanitarian Coordinator Bruno Lemarquis, in Uvira since 28 June, said the UN was there to assess security for the physical return of UN agencies to South Kivu, to study humanitarian access and the mechanisms for opening a humanitarian corridor, and to consider support to the provincial institutions provisionally installed in Uvira.
claims.verification_note: Matches.
claims.researcher_note: Context-only (UN).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that South Kivu governor Jean Jacques Purusi, based in Uvira since the fall of Bukavu to the M23, said Lemarquis's visit proved that peace, stability and security were returning, and that the authorities would do everything to eradicate the multiple barriers erected in places to facilitate the opening of a humanitarian corridor so that the population, including in areas occupied by the 'aggressors', could receive medicines, food and other assistance.
claims.actor_as_written: Governor Jean Jacques Purusi (DRC provincial government)
claims.verification_note: Matches.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement (DRC provincial government). Second quotation: the page attributes it to the governor ("a indiqué le gouverneur Jean Jacques Purusi").

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, in a 17-minute audio message broadcast on 19 July, General Makanaki (Makanaki Kasimbira John, described by the outlet as an influential Wazalendo figure) said that any truck coming from Bukavu must be burned by the Wazalendo and would not pass the Luvingi bridge, saying 'These are the trucks that bring the M23'; the outlet described the convoy as 55 trucks of food and medicine for displaced people in Uvira, and South Kivu governor Jean Jacques Purusi had said an agreement had been reached between all parties concerned.
claims.place_as_written: Luvungi bridge on the Bukavu-Uvira route (Luvingi), Uvira territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: General Makanaki Kasimbira John (described by the source as an influential Wazalendo figure)
claims.verification_note: Page (SOS Médias Burundi, Bukavu dateline 21 July 2025) states every clause; the Purusi and 'food and medicine' clauses come from the page body, supplied as replacement quotes. Makanaki's statement is known from an audio message as reported by SOS Médias Burundi; the audio itself was not retrieved. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: 55 trucks; Makanaki Kasimbira John, influential Wazalendo figure 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: agreement between all parties concerned 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-017: Read the retained page: every clause is supported, and 'he stated' in source 1 is Governor Purusi. But the statement leaves out the reason Makanaki gave in the same quote ('These are the trucks that bring the M23') and the size of the convoy (55 trucks), both on the page; the strongest true version gives his stated reason, attributed to him. The threat is known only from SOS Médias Burundi's account of an audio not retrieved.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): 55 trucks; Makanaki Kasimbira John, influential Wazalendo figure; agreement between all parties concerned
claims.researcher_note: Threat to burn convoy, not a reported attack; the source says 55 trucks of food and medicine. Whether the convoy was ultimately blocked is not stated in the excerpts. SOS Médias Burundi (24 Jul) separately says a humanitarian corridor Bukavu-Uvira was blocked (not cited here). The 55-truck figure is on the page but outside the excerpts.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, in a communiqué published on the previous Sunday, the M23-AFC coalition denounced the reinforcement of government troops on several axes, notably Shabunda, Uvira and Kalemie, and accused the Congolese authorities of violating the ceasefire.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira, Shabunda, Kalemie (as named in the communiqué)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries the statement exactly; partisan origin, so C. Party statement (AFC/M23) as relayed by Radio Okapi; the communiqué itself was not retrieved. 'Previous Sunday' relative to an article of Tuesday 12 August 2025.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from 'dimanche dernier' and publication date 2025-08-12 (Tuesday), i.e. Sunday 2025-08-10. The communiqué itself was not opened; Radio Okapi relays it. A party statement, evidence of what AFC/M23 said only.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that on the southern axis the FARDC and Wazalendo control a large portion of the Ruzizi plain beyond the city of Uvira, while the rebels keep their hold on the Nyangezi–Kamanyola axis and on certain localities of the Ruzizi plain chiefdom; according to concordant sources cited by Radio Okapi, the rebel coalition's troops were redeploying with heavy equipment towards the Walungu and Uvira axes to consolidate their positions.
claims.place_as_written: Ruzizi plain beyond Uvira; Nyangezi–Kamanyola axis, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Attribution fixed: on the page 'concordant sources' carries only the redeployment; the Ruzizi control picture is Radio Okapi's own narration. Single outlet for a frontline picture: C.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet, 'sources locales'; the page gives no precise localities for the Ruzizi plain split. The M23 move is described as 'since the weekend' (9-10 Aug).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that a FARDC soldier was shot dead and several civilians were wounded after an altercation on Monday 25 August between the FARDC and Wazalendo fighters at Mulongwe, Uvira territory; according to local sources it was triggered by a dispute over the control of vehicles carrying people from Burundi who had come for the burial of a colonel, and the Sokola 2 South Kivu spokesperson said the soldier was hit by a stray bullet while protecting the convoy.
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; the 'stray bullet' is the spokesperson's conditional account ('aurait été atteint') and is attributed. Radio Okapi (3 September) later gave a toll of at least five Wazalendo killed and fourteen arrested for the 25 August clashes (see claim 7); the tolls differ. 2026-10-28: confidence edited: red-team rt-017: Attribution is fine (stray bullet kept as the spokesperson's conditional account), but the grade overstates independence: the three 'origins' are one Radio Okapi article (its own reporting, unnamed local sources, and the FARDC Sokola 2 spokesperson, a party). Radio Okapi's own 3 September report of the same 25 August clashes gives a different toll (at least five Wazalendo killed, fourteen arrested, per military authorities: r1-UV-2025Q3-008), which this statement does not mention. One article with a party confirmation and a conflicting later toll fits C, like the companion claim.
claims.researcher_note: Perpetrator disputed: local sources point to a Wazalendo-FARDC altercation, the military spokesperson says stray bullet. Number of civilians wounded not given. Overlaps with SOS Médias Burundi's account of the 26 Aug clashes (separate claim). The colonel's burial: Radio Okapi (3 Sep) names 'colonel Patrick'.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Tuesday the border town of Uvira saw violent clashes between the FARDC and the local Wazalendo militias, concentrated in the Kavimvira and Kasenga quarters; bodies of both sides were lying along the road linking Kasenga to Kavimvira.
claims.place_as_written: Kavimvira and Kasenga quarters, Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Supported; single outlet. The page's photo caption dates the clashes to Tuesday 26 August 2025; no body count is given.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from 'mardi' and the page's photo caption (Tuesday 26 August 2025). Single (Burundian) outlet reporting from Bukavu; no casualty figure. Source says violence 'auraient éclaté' after Wazalendo tried to deploy at the Kavimvira border and a tax directorate warehouse.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the spokesperson of the South Kivu provincial government, Luganywa Bashizi Didier Kabi, relayed the position of governor Jean Jacques Purusi, who condemned the oral and physical violence of the previous two days in certain quarters of Uvira.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries the full statement; names printed on the page. Official statement verbatim: B.
claims.researcher_note: Statement date is the publication date; no exact day given by the source.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Wazalendo and the army had clashed on 25 August over the arrival of a delegation from Burundi for the funeral of colonel Patrick, who had recently died, and that, according to the military authorities, these clashes caused the death of at least five Wazalendo fighters and the arrest of fourteen others.
claims.verification_note: 'Ces groupes' on the page are the Wazalendo and FARDC, who clashed with each other; the draft read it as the Wazalendo alone opposing the arrival. Narrowed to the page's reading. Toll is the military authorities' figure. Radio Okapi's 26 August report (claim 4) gave one FARDC soldier killed; the two accounts differ.
claims.researcher_note: Single-source military figure; the page does not say the deaths and arrests all occurred on 25 August ('ces accrochages' covers the days since). SOS Médias Burundi (27 Aug) links to an article titled 'l’inhumation du Colonel Patrick Gisore interrompue par les Wazalendo' (not opened). Names detainees: none.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Nouvelle société civile congolaise announced a partial suspension of the strike from Friday 5 September, after three days of a movement launched by Wazalendo combatants and citizen movements against the appointment of General Olivier Gasita as commander of operations and intelligence.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries all clauses.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi adds that despite the announced suspension activities remained suspended and traders hesitated to reopen for fear of looting. Coordinator Mafikiri Mashimango named on the page.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Wazalendo accuse General Gasita of being a double agent serving the M23 rebellion and of having played a decisive role in the take of Bukavu by that armed group in February 2025.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt states the accusation verbatim, attributed to the Wazalendo. An accusation by the Wazalendo, reported by Radio Okapi; not a finding.
claims.researcher_note: An accusation by a party (Wazalendo), unproven; SOS Médias Burundi (7 Sep) calls similar accusations 'non prouvées' for Gasita. Date is the article's reporting of the ongoing dispute (published 5 Sep).

claims.text: Afrikarabia reported that the deputy Justin Bitakwira, who is also coordinator of the Wazalendo in South Kivu, accuses General Gasita of collusion with the M23 and of having delivered a speech calling on the Wazalendo to let the rebels pass, which would have facilitated the fall of Bukavu.
claims.actor_as_written: Justin Bitakwira (deputy and Wazalendo coordinator in South Kivu, per source)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries the statement. Category is an accusation by a political/militia figure, not an official statement in the strict sense. An accusation by Justin Bitakwira as reported by Afrikarabia; the conditional 'aurait facilité' is kept.
claims.researcher_note: Date approximate (September 2025). Accusation, unproven. The speaker is a member of parliament; the page says he was sanctioned by the EU (not cited here).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, according to concordant sources, that on 2 September at Kalungwe two civilians, including a moto-taxi driver and his client, were wounded by a bullet fired by a Wazalendo fighter after refusing to take part in the demonstration that day.
claims.verification_note: The page attributes the incident to 'sources concordantes'; attribution added.
claims.researcher_note: 'selon des sources concordantes'. Victims not named. Place spelled 'Kalungwe' by Radio Okapi.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local medical sources, that three civilians, including two moto-tricycle drivers, wounded during the Wazalendo demonstrations against General Gasita's appointment died on Thursday 4 September.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt states it; 'Trois' printed in words; the source spells 'Wazalelendo' (typo). The deaths are reported without stating who caused the injuries. A second Radio Okapi article of 5 September also reports the three deaths, after being taken to hospital.
claims.researcher_note: The page does not say who shot them. Radio Okapi 5 Sep (second article) says they died after being taken to hospital. Overlaps possibly with the 'two new civilian deaths' reported 6 Sep (separate claim). Victims not named.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, in a communiqué published on Thursday, the deputy mayor of Uvira, Kifara Kapenda, deplored the disturbances to public order, called for the end of the demonstrations while saying the demonstrators' demands had been heard, and invited the organisers to an emergency meeting on Friday 5 September.
claims.verification_note: Meeting clause is on the page, supplied as a replacement quote.
claims.researcher_note: Thursday = 2025-09-04 (date computed from weekday and publication date 2025-09-05).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that violent clashes between the FARDC and the Wazalendo had been reported, causing two new civilian deaths according to local civil society, and that a meeting between urban authorities, military leaders and demonstrators had produced no significant progress.
claims.verification_note: Supported; meeting clause supplied from the page. Toll from local civil society. The meeting was held on Friday (5 September); the article is dated 6 September. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 6 Sept 2025, carries both clauses; the stored excerpt carries only the clashes/deaths clause, so the meeting clause (held Friday) needs its own excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Date is the publication date; the page gives no exact date of the clashes. 'Nouveaux' suggests additional to earlier deaths; may overlap with 4-5 Sep deaths. The same page states 'Les autorités militaires, de leur côté, réaffirment leur soutien à l’officier contesté.'

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that a 5-year-old child died in an explosion during the night of 6 to 7 September in Uvira.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports the statement; the date conflict within the same outlet is noted. Discrepancy: an earlier SOS Médias Burundi article (Bukavu dateline 7 September) places the death in the night 'de vendredi à samedi' (5 to 6 September); this article says the night of 6 to 7 September. The cause of the explosion is not stated.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet. Cause of the explosion not stated. The SOS article of 7 Sep says the child died 'dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi' (5-6 Sep), a one-night discrepancy between the two SOS pages. HRW (existing claim) reports on 5 September an 8-year-old boy killed when a shell struck his house; it is unclear whether these are the same or different incidents.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Mutualité des Banyamulenge denounced in a communiqué acts of discrimination, physical violence and intimidation, including women and girls beaten in Kabindula and denial of access to drinking water, some demonstrators saying 'Allez puiser au Rwanda'.
claims.place_as_written: Kabindula quarter, Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: as alleged by the Mutualité des Banyamulenge: demonstrators/Wazalendo-led protesters (not specified in the excerpt)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt states the communiqué's allegations verbatim. Allegations in a community association's communiqué; perpetrators are not identified beyond 'certains manifestants'.
claims.researcher_note: Allegation by a community organisation, relayed by one outlet. HRW (15 Sep, existing source) separately reports Banyamulenge denied access to water points. No sexual violence is alleged in this excerpt.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Mutualité des Banyamulenge denounced the abduction of a FARDC soldier and a policeman, both Banyamulenge.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports; it is the list item of the communiqué introduced by 'la Mutualité des Banyamulenge dénonce'. Allegation by the Mutualité des Banyamulenge; no perpetrator, date or names given. SOS Médias Burundi's 9 September article repeats it (1 FARDC soldier and 1 policeman).
claims.researcher_note: Allegation by a community organisation (excerpt starts at the list item; the attribution to the Mutualité is in the preceding sentence of the page). Single outlet. Persons not named. Perpetrator not specified.

claims.text: Afrikarabia reported that a Wazalendo official issued a call giving '10 jours aux Tutsi d’Uvira pour quitter la ville', and that Kinshasa said it did not know the author of the message, which could be 'une manipulation'.
claims.actor_as_written: a Wazalendo official (as reported by the source)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports both clauses. The author of the message is unidentified; Kinshasa suggested it could be a manipulation. The message's date is not given.
claims.researcher_note: A threat reported by one outlet; the message itself was not seen; authorship unverified (Kinshasa suggests manipulation). Date: after Gasita's departure on 9 Sep, before the 14 Sep publication.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, according to local sources, at least 5 people were killed and about twenty wounded, several seriously, after FARDC fire to disperse demonstrators in Uvira on 8 September, while the FARDC's official version, per the same page, was one 12-year-old child killed by a stray bullet and 9 wounded (4 soldiers and 5 civilians).
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city (town hall, Sokola 2 headquarters), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: All figures on the page; the date comes from the dateline ('ce lundi', 8 September 2025). The same page gives two civil-source wounded figures: 'une vingtaine' in the text and 'plus de 9' in the summary box. Contested toll: compare Radio Okapi (claim 23) and the later at-least-eight cumulative toll (claim 25).
claims.researcher_note: Figures differ by source and are not merged: SOS Médias Burundi cites civil sources 5 killed, 'une vingtaine' / 'plus de 9' wounded (the page gives both); Afrikarabia (14 Sep) cites civil society of Uvira for 6 dead overall; Radio Okapi (10 Sep) 'au moins huit' dead across the protests. HRW (existing claim) says an 8-year-old boy was killed; Radio Okapi/FARDC say a 12-year-old. Victims not named. Complements existing r1-SV-2025-028 (HRW).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to the spokesperson of operations Sokola 2, sub-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, the disturbances in Uvira left 1 dead (a 12-year-old child hit by a bullet) and 9 wounded (4 FARDC soldiers and 5 civilians); Radio Okapi reported that the incidents broke out when demonstrators deemed uncontrolled tried to force the entrance of a military base, and that one of them was reportedly caught with a grenade, according to the military authorities; civil society denounced a violent repression and called on the President of the Republic to intervene.
claims.verification_note: The draft put the base-entry and grenade narration in the spokesperson's mouth; on the page it is Radio Okapi's narration with the grenade attributed to 'les autorités militaires'. Source 2 (civil society) was cited but unused; added. FARDC account of a contested event; SOS Médias Burundi gives at least 5 killed per local sources (claim 22).
claims.researcher_note: FARDC account of the 8 Sep shooting; the spokesman's name appears elsewhere as 'Reagan Kalonji' (SOS Médias Burundi). Contradicts HRW's description (shots at unarmed protesters, boy aged 8) and civil-society counts. Actualite.cd (9 Sep) also reports one killed and at least nine wounded by bullets after the army's repression.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that automatic-weapon fire was heard for at least twenty minutes, at around 10 o'clock local time, near the Uvira town hall in the Kimanga quarter on Monday 8 September 2025, that law enforcement elements were firing in the air to disperse demonstrators, and that several sources spoke of dead and wounded among civilians and the security forces.
claims.place_as_written: Kimanga quarter near the town hall, Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: law enforcement elements (as described by the source)
claims.verification_note: '10:00' replaced with the source's '10 heures'; casualty sentence from the page added. Kivu Morning Post is based in Goma (under AFC/M23 control at the time).
claims.researcher_note: Wording 'tiraient en l’air' contrasts with accounts of live fire at demonstrators (SOS Médias Burundi, HRW). Titled 'Des morts et des blessés' but the cited paragraph gives no casualty figure. Procession started at the Kavimvira roundabout per the same page.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the demonstrations, organised by civil society and supported by Wazalendo fighters, had been violently repressed by the FARDC; that at least eight people died during the successive demonstrations in Uvira and about ten were wounded, including soldiers; and that the bishop of Uvira, Mgr Sébastien Moyengo, had condemned the disproportionate use of force against civilians.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC (force used, per the bishop's condemnation)
claims.verification_note: Added the page's own statement that the FARDC repressed the protests, which grounds the actor field. Cumulative toll for the protests of early September; Afrikarabia (14 Sept) cites a civil-society toll of 6 dead. Tolls vary by source.
claims.researcher_note: Cumulative toll across protests (2-8 Sep), not a single event; Radio Okapi's own sub-counts earlier are 3 (4 Sep) + 1 or more (8 Sep) + 2 (6 Sep). Deaths not itemised by date or cause.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that social and economic activities resumed on Wednesday 10 September in Uvira, 24 hours after General Gasita's departure, with shops reopening and public transport resuming, while schools remained closed because parents feared new demonstrations.
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Education access: schools closed since the strike began (2 Sep).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that after an inter-institutional meeting chaired on Monday 8 September in Kinshasa by President Félix Tshisekedi, National Assembly president Vital Kamerhe said the Head of State is preoccupied by the Uvira tensions and seeks solutions through a government mission sent to Uvira.
claims.verification_note: Meeting clause supplied from the page (the page has several captures; the passage is in the latest).
claims.researcher_note: Meeting also attended per the page by Sama Lukonde, Judith Suminwa and Dieudonné Kamuleta.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the FARDC spokesperson, Major General Sylvain Ekenge, firmly rejected the demonstrators' demands, saying the Wazalendo have no instruction to give within the Armed Forces of the DRC and calling on the 'real' Wazalendo not to fall into the enemy's trap.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries the quote verbatim. The statement's own date and venue are not given (reported 7 September 2025).
claims.researcher_note: Exact day not given on this page (published 7 Sep); the statement is placed around 6 Sep by HRW's report of a press conference (not re-cited here as the HRW page is already used in an existing claim).

claims.text: Afrikarabia reported that the spokesperson of the Congolese army supported General Olivier Gasita, saying that a soldier does not belong to communities and that 'un militaire communautaire n’existe pas'.
claims.verification_note: Supported by the excerpt. Afrikarabia does not name the spokesperson; SOS Médias Burundi names the army spokesperson as Maj Gen Sylvain Ekenge (claim 30).
claims.researcher_note: Afrikarabia does not name the spokesperson in this passage; SOS Médias Burundi names Sylvain Ekenge for a separate statement. Date approximate.

claims.text: A UN Peacebuilding Support Office briefing on the DRC (September 2025) stated that Uvira had been at the center of tensions, both in relation to a possible AFC/M23 advance and to growing strain between the FARDC and wazalendo factions.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt found verbatim in the PDF ('Briefing on the situation in the DRC – September 2025'). Analytical context, not an incident.
claims.researcher_note: Context-level UN statement; the briefing is dated 30 Sep 2025 per search metadata.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué published from Goma, AFC/M23 communication head Lawrence Kanyuka warned that AFC/M23 'will no longer tolerate the barbaric surge of hate speech in Uvira, in Ituri and in the rest of the DRC'.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries the quote verbatim; byline Blaise Basabose. Party statement (AFC/M23). The article (4 September) does not give the communiqué's date explicitly; 3 September is approximate.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan party statement (AFC/M23), cited only for what it said; the exact communiqué date is not stated in the excerpt (Kivu Morning Post article dated 4 Sep; the Twirwaneho communiqué cited on the same page is dated 3 Sep). The title says it 'threatens to intervene'; the excerpted sentence is a warning only.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the movement (identified in the quoted passage as MRDP-Twirwaneho) affirms that Burundian troops and FDLR elements crossed the border at Runingu to reinforce the FARDC and Wazalendo in the area, and that it wrote that the presence of foreign troops worsens the security and humanitarian crisis.
claims.place_as_written: Runingu border crossing, Uvira territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: MRDP-Twirwaneho (claimant); Burundian troops and FDLR (as alleged)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports; allegation kept attributed. Partisan allegation (MRDP-Twirwaneho, allied with AFC/M23); not corroborated. The quoted passage also uses the term 'génocidaire', which is the movement's wording.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan claim by an armed group allied to AFC/M23 (what it said, not established fact). The page's paragraph structure leaves it slightly ambiguous whether 'le mouvement' is MRDP-Twirwaneho; the quote is attributed to it. Not independently confirmed; Burundi's government response not found. Runingu is on the Ruzizi plain near the Rwanda/DRC border of Uvira territory.
