claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that on 10 December 2025 M23 and Rwandan forces entered Uvira after several days of fighting in South Kivu, and that witnesses said hostilities in the city had largely ended when these forces took control.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and Rwandan forces (as HRW names them)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim in HRW report summary; documented NGO field investigation. Entry date differs by source: Afrikarabia 'mardi soir' (9 Dec), BBC/HRW 10 Dec, Kigali Today 12 Dec.
claims.researcher_note: HRW report published 2026-05-14; field research after the M23 departure. Other outlets date the entry 9 Dec (evening) or 10 Dec; Kigali Today dates the capture 12 Dec. Dates differ by source.

claims.text: Afrikarabia reported that AFC/M23 rebels had entered Uvira on Tuesday evening, and that testimonies on site spoke of the flight of civil and military authorities during that day while the rebellion was at Kiliba, some fifteen kilometres north of Uvira.
claims.verification_note: Removed publication date from statement (number not in excerpt; source date shown with source). Byline Christophe Rigaud on page. 'Tuesday evening' read as 9 Dec 2025 from the article date (10 Dec). The page's own photo caption says '10 décembre 2025 au soir de l'entrée'; BBC and HRW give 10 Dec. Discrepancy unresolved.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('mardi soir') and publication date 2025-12-10. Contested the next day by the provincial governor (see BBC 10 Dec claim).

claims.text: BBC reported that the M23 said it had 'liberated' the city of Uvira, while South Kivu Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi told local media that the army and allied militia remained in control of the city.
claims.verification_note: Removed publication date from statement. Two party accounts kept attributed.
claims.researcher_note: Two accounts of control in one passage. BBC also cites AFP and Radio Okapi. The governor's denial was overtaken by events (the M23 announced withdrawal on 16 Dec).

claims.text: Al Jazeera reported, citing its correspondent in Uvira, that government forces and allied militias known as Wazalendo, which had been using the city as a headquarters, began fleeing even before M23 fighters entered.
claims.verification_note: Removed publication date; the correspondent's name is printed on the page (byline 'Al Jazeera Staff and News Agencies'). HRW (14 May 2026) separately says the Congolese army and allied militias appear to have mainly fled Uvira before M23 and Rwandan forces arrived.
claims.researcher_note: Month precision: the exact day of the flight is not stated. Corroborated in substance by HRW ('semblent avoir principalement fui Uvira').

claims.text: Al Jazeera reported that regional authorities said at least 400 civilians, including children, had been killed in violence between the cities of Bukavu and Uvira, both then under M23 control.
claims.place_as_written: Between Bukavu and Uvira, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed publication date; figures field narrowed to what this source prints (UN/HRW figures belong to other claims). Perpetrator not attributed by source. Unverified authorities' figure; the authorities are not named. UN (10 Dec) gave at least 70 civilians killed across South Kivu; figures are not comparable.
claims.researcher_note: Unverified authorities' figure. UN News (10 Dec) reported at least 70 civilians killed across South Kivu; HRW later documented 62 cases in Uvira. Figures are not merged.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that it documented 62 cases of summary executions and unlawful killings in Uvira during the M23 and Rwandan-forces occupation, the victims being 54 men, 2 women, 5 boys and one girl.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and Rwandan forces (as HRW attributes)
claims.verification_note: Figures verbatim; occupation period on the same page. HRW says these cases are only a fraction of civilians summarily executed during the occupation. HRW wrote to M23 leader Bertrand Bisimwa on 14 April 2026.
claims.researcher_note: HRW says it received no reply to its 14 April 2026 letter to M23 leader Bertrand Bisimwa. HRW states these cases are a fraction of the total. Counts are documented cases only.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that residents said that during the occupation of Uvira, M23 and Rwandan forces carried out systematic searches in several areas, in particular the Kasenga and Rugenge neighbourhoods.
claims.place_as_written: Kasenga and Rugenge, Uvira (city), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and Rwandan forces (as HRW attributes)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; attribution to residents kept.
claims.researcher_note: Context for the killings and abductions HRW documents; see the 62-cases claim.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that it documented rapes and other sexual violence by M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers against women and girls, and that survivors described being raped under threat of being killed, with a firearm pointed at them, at home or in the fields.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers (as HRW attributes)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim in HRW summary.
claims.researcher_note: Survivors are not named in this record. HRW does not state a total number of rape cases in the cited passage. A related UFMP count is reported by DW.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that the lack of operational health services in Uvira during the occupation left survivors of sexual violence without access to essential care, including HIV post-exposure prophylaxis.
claims.verification_note: Single clause, verbatim; cause of the lack of services not stated, as the draft notes.
claims.researcher_note: The cited passage does not say why services were not operational.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that M23 abducted a number of men and boys, often near military bases in Uvira, with no mention of a link to the Wazalendo, and that HRW considers they were probably forcibly recruited into M23.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; HRW's hedge ('probablement') kept.
claims.researcher_note: 'Enforced disappearance' is HRW's own term, quoted via translation, not a finding of this record.

claims.text: The Union des femmes des médias pour la paix (UFMP), in a report cited by Deutsche Welle, recorded 183 cases of rape in December in the city of Uvira, followed by 220 in January and 626 in February.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; single civil-society origin relayed by DW (byline Mitima Delachance). Year of 'December' inferred from DW's 17 April 2026 date. UFMP methodology not given. DW also reports, per UFMP, that barely 30% of victims received prevention kits (STI and pregnancy). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified contradicting source(s) recorded in notes; not regraded pending review. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Year of 'December' not printed in the excerpt; DW's article is dated 2026-04-17 so December 2025 is inferred. Methodology of the UFMP count is not given on the page. The count spans the occupation and its aftermath. Contradicting reporting: UFMP Sud-Sud-Kivu (LinkedIn post) (2026-04-01): January figure: UFMP's own post gives 320 for January and a total of 1,129; DW gives 220 for January and a total of 1,029. DW's 220 appears to be an error or a different version.

claims.text: The ICRC reported that an ICRC and DRC Red Cross team evacuated 21 people wounded by weapons, seven of them children, over 40 km to Uvira, where they were being treated by medical teams of the ICRC-supported Uvira general referral hospital; the ICRC said the fighting of the past week in Uvira, Walungu, Mwenga and Fizi territories made rescue and transfer of the wounded extremely difficult.
claims.place_as_written: Sange to Uvira, Uvira territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed release date from statement; added the territories the source names. Grade B: single (credible, first-hand operational) origin, not an investigation. ICRC release of 7 Dec 2025; the evacuation date is not given. A photo caption places a Red Cross evacuation at Sange (Uvira).
claims.researcher_note: Date is the ICRC release date; the evacuation happened in the week before. Photo caption on the page places an evacuation at Sange (Uvira). ICRC head of the Uvira office quoted: Djibril Mamadou Diallo.

claims.text: The ICRC reported that, between 2 and 16 December, more than 193 people wounded by weapons were treated in hospitals it supports, 110 of them at the Uvira general referral hospital (HGR), 63 at the Bukavu provincial general referral hospital and 20 at the Fizi general referral hospital.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira, Bukavu and Fizi hospitals, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed release date (18 Dec) from statement. Grade B: single ICRC origin. Same ICRC page quotes its medical coordinator saying Fizi HGR received 'près de 20' wounded and Uvira HGR 'plus de 100' since 2 Dec; the ICRC also supported dignified burials in Uvira and the Ruzizi plain from 11 Dec. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Another ICRC release (12 Dec) put admissions at the Uvira HGR at nearly 100 for 2-11 Dec.

claims.text: Anadolu reported that on Wednesday the Congolese government attributed the violence in Uvira to a 'widespread offensive launched in recent days by the Rwandan Defense Forces' along the Kamanyola-Uvira axis, calling it a 'blatant violation' of the ceasefire and of commitments under recent peace agreements; Kigali denied the accusations.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; party statement attributed. 'Wednesday' read as 10 Dec 2025 from the article date (Fri 12 Dec). Anadolu (byline James Tasamba, Kigali dateline) is a Turkish state agency; the government's original text was not opened.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date (2025-12-12). Anadolu is a Turkish state agency; its text is taken as reporting, with the statement attributed to the Congolese government.

claims.text: Anadolu reported that on Wednesday Rwanda accused the Congolese and Burundian armies of violating a ceasefire provided under the Washington peace deal.
claims.verification_note: Single clause, verbatim. Date from 'Wednesday' and article date. BBC (10 Dec) separately reports a Rwandan foreign ministry statement on X saying the ceasefire violation 'cannot be placed on Rwanda' and that Congolese and Burundian armies had 'systematically' bombed villages near Rwanda's border.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date (2025-12-12). Nouvel Obs (10 Dec) also describes a Rwandan communiqué condemning Congolese and Burundian armies (snippet only; not fetched).

claims.text: Anadolu reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame said on Thursday that Burundian soldiers deployed in eastern DRC spend days shelling civilians, and Anadolu noted there was no immediate reaction from Burundi.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; party claim attributed. Kagame's assertions (including more than 20,000 Burundian soldiers in Congo, shelling in Minembwe with artillery and drones) are a party's claims, unverified. Said at a swearing-in ceremony in Kigali.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('Thursday') and publication date 2025-12-12. Same article quotes Kagame saying more than 20,000 Burundian soldiers are in Congo and that they shell people in Minembwe with artillery and drones; these are Kagame's assertions, not verified.

claims.text: Anadolu reported that Burundi's Foreign Minister Edouard Bizimana warned on Monday that 'any attack targeting Burundian citizens or soldiers deployed in the DRC will never be tolerated'.
claims.verification_note: Single clause, verbatim; date approximate. 'Monday' read as 8 Dec 2025; the article does not give the date. BBC (10 Dec) separately quotes Bizimana to AFP calling M23 advances 'a slap in the face'.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday; the article is dated 2025-12-12 so 'Monday' is read as 8 Dec. The page does not give the Monday's date. Excerpt may contain curly quotes as on the page.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a communiqué that captured Burundian soldiers would be handed over to their country's authorities, and that Uvira was totally under M23 control.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; 'mercredi soir' with article dated Thu 11 Dec gives 10 Dec. Party statement. Kanyuka also called on FARDC and Wazalendo still in Uvira to surrender (same page).
claims.researcher_note: Partisan statement relayed by SOS Médias Burundi (originating: AFC/M23 communiqué). Date computed: 'mercredi soir' with article dated 2025-12-11 gives 2025-12-10. The M23 claim of captured Burundian soldiers is the party's; no independent figure given.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that a Burundian delegation was forced to go to Luvungi, in South Kivu, to demand the return of its captured soldiers and negotiate a secure corridor for its troops encircled in the Hauts-Plateaux.
claims.actor_as_written: Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Single clause, verbatim (outlet narration). Kept at C. Single exile-run outlet; its following paragraph attributes the delegation details (four senior Burundian security officials, release of soldiers including a colonel, corridor for troops in Lemera groupement) to security sources in Cibitoke. No Burundian confirmation found.
claims.researcher_note: Single local-exile outlet (SOS Médias Burundi) relying on 'sources sécuritaires' per its text; no confirmation from Burundi (Anadolu: no immediate reaction). Burundi's presence figures are contested; Kagame says >20,000, which is a partisan assertion.

claims.text: Al Jazeera reported that AFC leader Corneille Nangaa posted a signed statement on X on Tuesday confirming that fighters would withdraw from Uvira 'as per United States mediation request', and that the coalition called the move a 'unilateral trust-building measure' and called for a neutral force to monitor the ceasefire.
claims.verification_note: Removed publication date from statement; party statement attributed. 'Tuesday' read as 16 Dec 2025 (article date). Al Jazeera's correspondent said 'nothing had changed' as of Tuesday morning. The X post itself was not opened.
claims.researcher_note: Date: the page is dated 2025-12-16 and says the statement was posted 'on Tuesday' (16 Dec). Partisan statement; the post itself was not opened. Al Jazeera's correspondent in Uvira reported 'nothing had changed' as of Tuesday morning with M23 fighters still seen.

claims.text: BBC Afrique reported that M23 chief Bertrand Bisimwa said on Wednesday that the withdrawal from Uvira was 'underway', with spokesperson Willy Ngoma adding it was 'in the interest of peace'.
claims.verification_note: Removed publication date. 'Wednesday' read as 17 Dec 2025 from the article date (19 Dec). Bisimwa also urged mediators on X to protect the city from 'reprisals, violence and remilitarisation'.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('mercredi') and article date 2025-12-19. Bisimwa also urged mediators to ensure the city is protected from 'reprisals, violence and remilitarisation' (same page).

claims.text: Kigali Today reported that the rebel coalition announced it was ready to leave Uvira, asking that soldiers and all other armed people be removed from the city and that neutral forces be deployed to protect civilians and infrastructure and help enforce the ceasefire.
claims.verification_note: Removed publication date; added the demilitarisation request the excerpt carries. Kigali-based outlet (byline Jean Claude Munyantore). It states AFC/M23 seized Uvira on 12 December 2025, which differs from other sources (9/10 Dec). The statement's subject is AFC/M23 as named in the page title.
claims.researcher_note: Kigali-based outlet; party statement relayed. The page states that AFC/M23 seized Uvira on 12 December 2025, which differs from other outlets (9/10 Dec).

claims.text: Al Jazeera reported that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that Rwanda's actions in eastern DRC were a 'clear violation' of the peace deal, and said in a post on X that the United States would take action to ensure promises made to the president are kept.
claims.verification_note: Removed publication date. 'Saturday' = 13 Dec 2025 (article date). Al Jazeera (16 Dec) quotes the same post as a 'clear violation of the Washington Accords'. The X post was not opened.
claims.researcher_note: Context statement by a mediator. The post (x.com/SecRubio/status/1999829630618919050) was not opened; the page says 'Saturday' and is dated 2025-12-13.

claims.text: The International Contact Group for the Great Lakes (United States, Belgium, Denmark, the EU, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland and the UK) urged M23 and the Rwanda Defence Force to immediately halt offensive operations in eastern DRC, in particular in South Kivu, and called on the RDF to withdraw from eastern DRC.
claims.actor_as_written: International Contact Group for the Great Lakes
claims.verification_note: Removed date (number not in excerpt; it is the source date); fixed 'withdraw' to 'withdraw from eastern DRC'. Credited to all ICG members, not to the hosting State Department. Grade B: one primary origin. Joint statement dated 9 Dec 2025 (Media Note, Office of the Spokesman). It also expresses concern at increased use of attack and suicide drones.
claims.researcher_note: Official joint statement published by the US State Department. Also expresses concern at increased use of attack and suicide drones (same page).

claims.text: BBC Afrique reported that the DRC government spokesperson Me Didier Kabi called the rebels' announced withdrawal from Uvira a 'mise en scène' orchestrated by the rebels to reduce pressure from partners, and that the DRC authorities said they held credible information of a 'dissimulation teintée de retrait'; BBC Afrique noted that government forces had not returned to the city.
claims.verification_note: The 'forces had not returned' clause is BBC's narration, not the government's statement: re-attributed. Grade raised to B: a credible outlet reporting an on-record official statement. BBC says the briefing came 'au lendemain' of the AFC/M23 leaders' withdrawal announcement. Kabi also said M23 forces remained 9 km from Uvira and had not passed Kiliba (12 km). BBC describes both Kabi and Patrick Muyaya as government spokesperson.
claims.researcher_note: Government account; BBC could not independently confirm. Date: the page is dated 2025-12-19 and says the briefing came 'the day after' the M23 announcement (17 Dec), so about 18 Dec. Kabi also said M23 troops remained 9 km from Uvira and at Kiliba (same page).

claims.text: BBC Afrique reported that DRC government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya told the BBC Newsday programme that the M23 announcement aimed to 'divert the attention of the American mediation team', which he said was preparing to take measures against Rwanda, and that he called the decision to leave Uvira a 'positive sign' while saying the government needed to confirm the situation on the ground.
claims.verification_note: Kept the full quoted purpose rather than a paraphrase that dropped 'preparing to take measures against Rwanda'; date set as a range. Day of the interview not given; range runs from the 16 Dec announcement to the 19 Dec article. Muyaya also asked on X about mass graves and soldiers disguised as civilians.
claims.researcher_note: Date approximate: the page (2025-12-19) does not give the day of the interview. Muyaya also posted on X questions about mass graves and soldiers disguised as civilians (same page).

claims.text: BBC Afrique reported that a local civil-society member, speaking anonymously, said some M23 troops had begun to withdraw from Uvira but that police belonging to the same group continued to arrive, while another inhabitant expressed doubts about the withdrawal.
claims.verification_note: Removed publication date; anonymous sources kept at C. The inhabitant spoke to the BBC 'jeudi matin' (18 Dec); the civil-society member's day is not given.
claims.researcher_note: Anonymous source; BBC does not give the day (a resident refers to 'jeudi matin', i.e. 18 Dec).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported (dated Uvira, 24 November 2025) that clashes between groups claiming allegiance to the Wazalendo and the FARDC had left about six people dead and more than fifteen wounded between Sunday and Monday, 24 November 2025.
claims.actor_as_written: groups claiming allegiance to Wazalendo and FARDC
claims.verification_note: Verbatim. Category changed: the source describes armed clashes between Wazalendo-affiliated groups and the FARDC, and does not say the dead were civilians. Single exile-run outlet; the FARDC's own toll (4 killed, 14 wounded, for Sunday) is recorded separately. The page says Kalundu and Kalimabenge neighbourhoods were hit by gunfire from Monday afternoon. Victims' status (civilian or combatant) not given for this toll.
claims.researcher_note: Single exile-run outlet; toll differs from the FARDC statement (4 killed, 14 wounded) recorded separately. Neighbourhoods Kalundu and Kalimabenge named elsewhere on the page as hit by gunfire since Monday afternoon.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that in a statement published on 23 November the FARDC denounced violence by what it called 'fake Wazalendo'; per the army, Sunday's clashes killed four people (one FARDC soldier, two Wazalendo fighters, a civilian motorcycle rider) and wounded 14.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim (Swahili). The army also said it recovered three AK-47 rifles. The FARDC statement itself was not opened. SOS Médias' own toll (about 6 killed, 15+ wounded, Sun-Mon) differs.
claims.researcher_note: Official FARDC statement as relayed by SOS Médias Burundi; the FARDC statement itself was not opened.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Sunday 23 November, at Luvungi in the Ruzizi plain, a man known as Huruma, described as a 'fake Wazalendo' and as having been a guardian (mlezi) of the Holy Family Parish, fired live rounds during diocesan youth celebrations at the Holy Family Catholic Church, killing two people and wounding five; the Diocese of Uvira strongly condemned the act.
claims.place_as_written: Luvungi, Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: 'fake Wazalendo' (as FARDC and SOS Médias name them)
claims.verification_note: Narrowed the translation of 'aliyekuwa mlezi' and 'sherehe za vijana kijimbo'. Single outlet. 'Huruma' is the alleged shooter as named by the source; being named is not a finding of responsibility. 'Mlezi' (guardian/patron) is ambiguous; draft's 'former caretaker' over-translated it. Wounded were taken to Luvungi hospital and Uvira's main hospital. Victims not named.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet. The shooter is named only as 'Huruma' by the source. Victims are not named.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that in Sange on Saturday 22 November two Wazalendo were killed in clashes between two rival groups, those of Kamama and Ngomanzito, according to local sources.
claims.verification_note: Single clause, verbatim; local sources attributed.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet citing local sources; 'Kamama' and 'Ngomanzito' are names of groups/leaders as printed.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that several Uvira members of parliament, including national deputy Justin Bitakwira Bihona-Hayi, condemned abuses and killings attributed to some Wazalendo elements.
claims.verification_note: Single clause, verbatim. Category changed: a political statement by deputies, not de facto governance. Day of the condemnation not stated; article dateline Uvira, 24 Nov 2025.
claims.researcher_note: Date follows the article's Uvira dateline (24 Nov); the day of the condemnation is not stated. The response of the deputies is a political statement, not an administrative measure; category chosen for lack of a closer fit.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that during the disorder that night, FARDC soldiers and their wazalendo allies stripped and ransacked the Iàmba health centre in the Bangwe sub-village (Nundu health zone) at Makobola, and a member of the Iàmba health-area development committee said they broke the doors from the pharmacy, looted all the medicines and took all the equipment from the head nurse's office.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC soldiers and wazalendo (as Actualite.cd's sources attribute)
claims.verification_note: Statement's date figure is not in the excerpts (date is in the date field and on the page); reworded to the excerpts. Grade C: single outlet on unnamed local sources, uncorroborated. Single outlet citing local sources; FARDC not quoted. Actualite.cd calls it the main health facility serving the area. Civil society demanded an inquiry. Makobola is in Fizi territory.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet, citing local sources; the FARDC were not quoted. 'Fizi' territory, but linked by the source to troops returning from the Kigongo front at Uvira.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that multiple cases of sexual assault of women were reported in the FARDC and wazalendo expedition into Makobola; a local civil-society actor said the women were forced to help carry looted goods and returned to their homes after being raped.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC soldiers and wazalendo (as Actualite.cd's sources attribute)
claims.verification_note: Removed day numbers absent from the excerpts. Grade C: single outlet, unnamed sources. Number of survivors not given; survivors not named. Same night of 29-30 Dec as the health-centre looting.
claims.researcher_note: Number of survivors not given. Survivors are not named. A civil-society demand for an inquiry is reported on the page.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, according to its sources in the region, the Makobola disorder broke out after a disagreement, for reasons not yet clarified, between soldiers of the Guépard unit returning from the Kigongo front at Uvira and soldiers of the Hiboux unit; some sources spoke of dissension between the commands of the two units.
claims.place_as_written: Makobola, Fizi territory, South Kivu (Kigongo front, Uvira)
claims.actor_as_written: soldiers of the 'Guépard' and 'Hiboux' units (as Actualite.cd's sources describe them)
claims.verification_note: Actor narrowed to the source's wording; grade C (single outlet on unnamed sources). The page heads the story as FARDC and wazalendo looting but does not state the units' formation or commanders.
claims.researcher_note: Units are named by the source without further identification (the page does not say whether 'Guépard' and 'Hiboux' are FARDC units; it describes 'militaires'). Commanders not named. Place 'Kigongo' is a front position near Uvira per the source.

claims.text: Ebuteli (Kivu Security Barometer) reported that on 16 January the AFC/M23 rebels withdrew from the city of Uvira and repositioned at Sange, about 30 km from Uvira, a crossroads to the middle and high plateaux of Uvira and Fizi, notably towards Mulenge and Lubarika.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city to Sange, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page, in Ebuteli's January 2026 section on Uvira; statement matches. Withdrawal date differs across sources: 16 Jan (Ebuteli), Saturday evening to Sunday morning 17-18 Jan (SOS Médias Burundi), 18 Jan (FARDC communiqué), 'fin janvier' (Radio Okapi, 17 Mar).
claims.researcher_note: Conflicts with SOS Médias Burundi (separate claim), which says the last M23 elements began leaving on Saturday evening (17 Jan) and finished Sunday morning (18 Jan). Ebuteli is a local monitor; Congo Indépendant and others show M23/RDF/AFC elements still near the city (Kabunambo) on 19 Jan.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the last elements of the rebel movement began leaving the city of Uvira on Saturday evening and completed the operation on Sunday morning.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date (on 20 January) from the statement per the project rule. The movement is the M23 (actor field), named in the preceding sentence on the page; the name is kept out of the corrected statement because no excerpt prints it. Weekdays only in the source; with the article dated 20 January 2026 they fall on 17-18 January. Differs from Ebuteli (16 Jan).
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date (article dated 2026-01-20; Saturday = 2026-01-17, Sunday = 2026-01-18). Differs from Ebuteli's 16 January. Single local outlet.

claims.text: Ebuteli reported that the FARDC and the Wazalendo retook the city of Uvira on 18 January, and that several abuses, often linked to attempted extortion, followed; an army communiqué reported by Actualite.cd also dated the retaking to Sunday 18 January 2026.
claims.verification_note: The raw statement credited only Ebuteli though it rests on two sources; added the FARDC communiqué clause. Grade lowered A->B: one credible monitor plus a party's communiqué. The second source is the army's own communiqué (a party). Congo Indépendant writes 'samedi 18 janvier', but 18 January 2026 was a Sunday.
claims.researcher_note: FARDC communiqué (via Actualite.cd) and Ebuteli agree on 18 January. Congo Indépendant (2026-01-21) writes 'samedi 18 janvier', but 18 January 2026 was a Sunday. Radio Okapi (2026-03-17) elsewhere dates the M23 withdrawal to 'fin janvier 2026'.

claims.text: Congo Indépendant reported, citing local sources, that M23/RDF/AFC elements remained on 19 January in the Ruzizi plain and close to the city, notably at Kabunambo, less than one kilometre from the centre.
claims.place_as_written: Kabunambo and Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page; attributed to unnamed local sources as the page says.
claims.researcher_note: Single media outlet citing unnamed local sources; relayed in Radio Okapi/Actualite.cd framing as 'faux retrait'.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Wazalendo militias, taking advantage of the vacuum left by the M23, advanced towards Uvira and took control of the village of Kirungu, 15 km from the city, and fired on several mountains overlooking Uvira.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo militias (described as supported by Kinshasa)
claims.verification_note: Supported; 'M23' is printed in the preceding sentence on the page. Radio Okapi puts Kirungu four hours' walk upstream of Uvira and reports it fell to the rebel coalition on 16 March 2026.
claims.researcher_note: Exact date not stated; follows the M23 departure of 17-18 Jan. Radio Okapi (2026-03-17) later reports Kirungu fell to a rebel coalition on 16 March, so the village changed hands.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that the locality of Kirungu, four hours' walk upstream of Uvira, fell on the evening of Monday 16 March under the control of the rebel coalition, a site linking Uvira to the middle and high plateaux of Minembwe.
claims.actor_as_written: rebel coalition (Radio Okapi's description: Twirwaneho, Red Tabara, Ngumino, FNL-Zabampema and AFC-M23)
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page; statement matches.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet, local sources. FARDC/government account of Kirungu not found in this unit.

claims.text: Ebuteli reported that the Twirwaneho occupied the zones around the 'point zéro', a strategic position controlling the high plateaux of Fizi and Uvira, and that the FARDC had thinned out the middle and high plateaux to position themselves in the city of Uvira.
claims.place_as_written: Point zéro, high plateaux of Fizi and Uvira
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page in the January 2026 report.
claims.researcher_note: Month-level date (January 2026 report).

claims.text: Human Rights Watch said that the M23 withdrew from Uvira in January 2026 and maintains positions to its north, in the Ruzizi Plain, and in the Hauts Plateaux, the highlands southwest of the city, and that fighting continues between the M23 and Congolese forces and their Wazalendo allies.
claims.place_as_written: North of Uvira, Ruzizi Plain and Hauts Plateaux
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the HRW page. Grade B rather than A: positions are background in an interview by HRW researchers, not a documented finding of the investigation.
claims.researcher_note: HRW researchers visited Uvira in March 2026.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that an army communiqué signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Mak Hazukay Mongba, acting FARDC spokesperson, deplored the systematic pillage of the city by soldiers of the AFC/M23-RDF coalition before their evacuation, and said some twenty civilians involved in looting were arrested and would be brought before the courts.
claims.verification_note: Party statement, relayed accurately by Actualite.cd (byline Clément Muamba).
claims.researcher_note: Party statement (Kinshasa/FARDC); the pillage accusation against M23/RDF is not independently confirmed here. M23's rebuttal is a separate claim.

claims.text: Congo Indépendant reported that the army deplored systematic pillage attributed to M23/RDF/AFC elements before their evacuation, and that the rebels rejected these accusations and blamed the abuses on the army and its Wazalendo allies.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page; statement matches. The rebel rebuttal is relayed without a named speaker or link.
claims.researcher_note: Rebel rebuttal is relayed without a named speaker or primary link. Date window = FARDC communiqué (19 Jan) to publication (21 Jan).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Defence Minister Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita told the Council of Ministers that security forces had returned to Uvira to ensure public order and that the scenario of chaos foreseen by the rebellion after its withdrawal had been foiled.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page; the Council date is on the page (page-only clause).
claims.researcher_note: Government account as reported by Actualite.cd from the Council of Ministers minutes; party statement.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the DRC government announced a plan for the progressive restoration of State authority in the city of Uvira and its surroundings, including coordinated security, judicial and humanitarian measures.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi published 2026-01-20; a government communiqué dated 19 January is referred to in the same article.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the government communiqué of Monday 19 January denounced the deportation of civilian populations, in particular members of the Banyamulenge community, alleging that some were forced to leave Uvira by the AFC/M23 to be used as justification for the movement's presence on Congolese soil.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page; conditional 'auraient' kept as an allegation.
claims.researcher_note: Government allegation, unverified; AFC/M23 reply not found in this unit.

claims.text: Congo Indépendant reported that, after an emergency meeting chaired by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa, government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya gave a stocktake of 1,500 dead, 3,000 displaced and 12,000 children out of school and separated from their parents.
claims.verification_note: Supported; the spokesperson's name is printed elsewhere on the page (page-only clause). The article dates the meeting 'lundi 20 janvier 2026', but 20 January 2026 was a Tuesday. '3,000 displaced' is as printed and far below the 267,000 the same article gives.
claims.researcher_note: The article writes 'lundi 20 janvier 2026' but 20 January 2026 was a Tuesday (the same article says 'lundi 19 janvier' elsewhere), so the day is uncertain. The '3.000 déplacés' figure is as printed and is far below the ~267,000 refugees/displaced the same article cites later. The article names the spokesperson as Patrick Muyaya elsewhere (not in this excerpt). The 1,500 figure is the one the government later repeated (Radio Okapi 2026-04-07) and Ebuteli counts 151 civilians killed in Uvira territory for December; HRW says 'at least several dozen'.

claims.text: Congo Indépendant reported that government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said the withdrawal of the Rwandan forces could not be interpreted as a gesture of appeasement nor as the end of the aggression.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Exact day not stated beyond the January emergency meeting.

claims.text: Congo Indépendant reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, sceptical, spoke of a 'faux retrait' (false withdrawal) and called for vigilance, judging that the enemy remains active and cunning.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page; the article gives no date for the remark, so the date is approximate.
claims.researcher_note: Date approximate: placed in the article's account of 19 January.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa, in a letter of Thursday 15 January 2026 to UN Secretary-General António Guterres, announced that he had placed the city of Uvira under the responsibility of the international community.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page; letter itself not seen.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement relayed by a Congolese outlet that also frames it as controversial; the letter itself was not seen. Kinshasa's reading (diversion from US pressure on Kigali) is in the same article.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a message on X on Wednesday 14 January, accused Congolese authorities of repeated ceasefire violations and said drones of the Kinshasa coalition forces bombed the port of Kalundu around 2:20 p.m., causing significant material damage and loss of life.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page (English edition). SOS Médias Burundi says he gave no figures.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement; SOS Médias Burundi says Kanyuka gave no figures. Post itself not opened.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing a MONUSCO communiqué, that MONUSCO and the ICGLR (CIRGL) were on a mission in Uvira from 23 to 27 February to prepare deployment of the joint ceasefire monitoring mechanism, and quoted acting Special Representative Vivian Van de Perre as saying MONUSCO's mandate in South Kivu is focused on ceasefire monitoring and does not include protection of civilians.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Mediator/UN context. Note the PoC limitation for investigators.

claims.text: Iwacu reported that on 2 January 2026 the secretary general of Burundi's ruling CNDD-FDD party, Révérien Ndikuriyo, said at a Bujumbura press conference: 'Nous avons un accord qui nous permet d’intervenir au Congo', a reply Iwacu described as radically different from the Burundian ambassador's earlier claim of withdrawal.
claims.place_as_written: Bujumbura (statement on Burundian forces in eastern DRC)
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page (byline Stine Akimana). On the same page Ndikuriyo is also quoted: 'les militaires burundais sont toujours là'.
claims.researcher_note: Speaker is a party official, not a state office; the article also quotes him on Burundian soldiers still being there (not used as an excerpt because the page prints an ellipsis). Burundian government/army did not comment on Uvira in the pages fetched.

claims.text: Iwacu reported that on 17 December 2025 Burundi's ambassador to the EU, Thérence Ntahiraja, told the European Parliament that the Burundian army had withdrawn its troops from eastern DRC after the peace accord, and that this is why the Rwandan army and the M23 advanced easily to Uvira.
claims.place_as_written: Brussels (statement on Burundian forces and Uvira)
claims.verification_note: Supported; the 'reason' clause is printed on the page next to the excerpt (page-only clause). Statement dated 17 December 2025, before this unit's quarter.
claims.researcher_note: Outside the unit's quarter but included because it frames the Burundian presence question; contradicted by Ndikuriyo (2 Jan) and by Ebuteli, which reports FDNB-supported FARDC attacks on 7 and 10 Jan.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing residents' testimony, that from Sunday to Tuesday several civilians were killed in Uvira, some for refusing to hand over their phones, others for an appearance likened to Tutsi, or accused of collaborating with the M23; some testimonies named Wazalendo elements as perpetrators, others unidentified armed bandits.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo elements (some testimonies) and unidentified armed bandits, per SOS Médias Burundi
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page; statement matches.
claims.researcher_note: Date range computed from weekdays ('dimanche' 18 Jan to 'mardi' 20 Jan); date computed from weekday and publication date. Single local outlet; no count of victims given. Ethnic profiling element (appearance read as Tutsi).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that shops, houses and stores were regularly pillaged by armed men in Uvira from Sunday to Tuesday.
claims.actor_as_written: armed men (not identified in this sentence)
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date. Radio Okapi (2026-01-18/19) also reported pillage and gunfire in Uvira on the day of the FARDC return (headlines seen in search results, pages not fetched).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing residents, cases of sexual violence in several quarters of Uvira between Sunday and Tuesday; it wrote that a woman was reportedly killed after giving food to Wazalendo fighters, who reportedly then assaulted her ('violentée'), and that young girls were targeted for their looks or for refusing to give up their phones.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo fighters (for the woman's case, per testimony)
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page; conditionals kept. 'violentée' does not itself specify rape; the source does not say the girls' targeting was sexual.
claims.researcher_note: The French 'violentée' means assaulted/abused and does not itself specify rape; the article's general sentence refers to 'violences sexuelles'. Unverified local testimony via a Burundian outlet; no victim names given; no health-care information. Date computed from weekdays.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that security sources within the FARDC said more than twenty Banyamulenge families remained under the protection of the regular forces, as some community leaders called on their own members and on the FARDC to stop the pillage and killings.
claims.verification_note: The page says community leaders called on 'leurs éléments' (their own members) and the FARDC; it does not name the Wazalendo, so that was narrowed out. The leaders' call is page-only (excerpt gap).
claims.researcher_note: Unnamed FARDC sources. Contrast with reports of destroyed Banyamulenge property (HRW) and Banyamulenge displacement allegations. Published 2026-01-20.

claims.text: Ebuteli reported that on 19 January the Mai-Mai Kuruninga killed a boy in Kalundu quarter and a man in Kabindula quarter, and the Mai-Mai Landa Bango killed a woman in Sondo quarter, in Uvira city.
claims.place_as_written: Kalundu, Kabindula and Sondo quarters, Uvira city
claims.verification_note: Statement unchanged; figures written in words as the source prints them (the '1' figures were in no excerpt).
claims.researcher_note: Ebuteli adds that the abuses were often linked to extortion attempts. No victim names printed.

claims.text: Ebuteli reported that on 19 January a group of ten unidentified armed men killed a man in Kilibuli quarter, accusing him of collaborating with the M23, and that on 24 January, during a robbery in Kasenga quarter, unidentified armed men killed a 22-year-old civilian.
claims.place_as_written: Kilibuli and Kasenga quarters, Uvira city
claims.verification_note: Statement unchanged; '19 January' rests on the preceding sentence on the page ('le même jour'), page-only clause. Figures reworded.
claims.researcher_note: Two separate incidents grouped by source; 'le même jour' refers to 19 January in the source's sequence.

claims.text: Ebuteli counted at least 21 civilians killed in Uvira territory in January 2026, against at least 151 in December 2025, the month the M23 took Uvira.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page; figures match. Monitor tally for the whole territory, all perpetrators.
claims.researcher_note: Monitor tally for the whole territory, not just the city. Compare with the Government's 1,500 dead figure for 10 Dec-18 Jan (Radio Okapi 2026-04-07) and HRW's 'at least several dozen' for the takeover.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several eyewitness accounts, that a drone attributed to the FARDC bombed a bar called Blue Cut near the Kalundu public port around 2:30 p.m. on Wednesday, reportedly causing deaths and numerous injuries among civilians as well as significant material damage.
claims.place_as_written: Blue Cut bar, Kalundu public port, Uvira city
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page. No casualty count. The article says neither Congolese nor Burundian authorities had responded.
claims.researcher_note: Date from 'Wednesday, January 14' in the same article (dateline 15 January). No count given ('several civilians injured and some dead' per a resident). Local report; AFC/M23 sources suggest the drones came from Burundi, which could not be independently verified; FARDC/Burundi response: none found (article says neither had responded).

claims.text: Ebuteli reported that on 14 January a FARDC kamikaze drone air strike in Kalundu quarter, Uvira city, targeted and destroyed a hotel in which an M23 meeting was being held, and that the toll could be several dozen victims among civilians, fighters and M23 cadres.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page. Toll is conditional. May be the same strike as SOS Médias Burundi's 'Blue Cut bar' report.
claims.researcher_note: Same date and place as the SOS Médias Burundi report of a drone strike on the Blue Cut bar, but Ebuteli says a hotel hosting an M23 meeting; the two accounts may describe one strike or two and are kept separate. The toll is conditional ('pourrait être'). Ebuteli puts this under an intensification of FARDC air offensives.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that sources close to the AFC/M23 denied that M23 members were present at the Blue Cut bar in Kalundu when it was hit by a drone, asserting that no leaders or fighters from the movement were there.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page; the 'claims' denied are the local reports of M23 members at the bar (preceding sentence).
claims.researcher_note: Anonymous partisan-adjacent sources. The 'claims' denied are local reports that the strike was based on intelligence about M23 members gathered at the bar.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch said that the South Kivu governor and the Congolese army commander took steps to control Wazalendo groups in Uvira, that some Wazalendo had been arrested for threatening and shooting at civilians, and that HRW visited them in military detention cells.
claims.verification_note: HRW's own observation during its March 2026 visit.
claims.researcher_note: HRW's visit was in March 2026; arrest dates not given. Arrested persons not named.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch said there had been a lot of damage to houses, government buildings and property of Banyamulenge, as well as destruction and looting of goods during the military withdrawal, although it was difficult to identify those responsible.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi / Congo Indépendant list damage to State services (DGDA, DGI, DGM, DGRAD, OCC) in a separate claim.

claims.text: Congo Indépendant reported that destruction and pillage targeted essential public services in Uvira, including the customs (DGDA), tax (DGI), immigration (DGM) and administrative revenue (DGRAD) directorates and the OCC quality-control agency.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed in this passage (the army attributes pre-evacuation pillage to the M23/RDF/AFC coalition)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page; perpetrators not stated.
claims.researcher_note: Government-leaning framing; perpetrators not stated in the passage.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch said that M23 fighters committed sexual violence against women and girls, especially those who ventured out to find food on their farmlands where they were isolated and vulnerable, and that most of these women and girls had not received any medical care.
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page; HRW on-site research. HRW gives no dates or count; the date range is the occupation period (entry on 10 December 2025 per residents interviewed by HRW).
claims.researcher_note: HRW does not give a date for these assaults beyond the occupation (about 10 Dec 2025-18 Jan 2026); the range is that occupation, so part falls before the unit's quarter. HRW interviews were in March 2026. The lack of medical care is stated for most survivors; no facility attack is described. No names given.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that a Government report, presented in Kinshasa on a Tuesday by Minister of Human Rights Samuel Mbemba, said about 14,400 women were raped in five weeks of occupation of Uvira by the Rwandan army and its proxies.
claims.actor_as_written: Rwandan army and its 'supplétifs' (proxies), per the DRC Government report
claims.verification_note: Statement unchanged; `figures` narrowed to what the source says (the date range 10 Dec-18 Jan is printed for the children figure, not the rape figure). Party figure; the report's method and sources are not stated. HRW documents sexual violence by M23 fighters without a count. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 3 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Government (party) figure, a roughly ten-page report not seen; method and sources not stated; much higher than any NGO/UN figure seen in this unit. HRW documents sexual violence by M23 fighters without a count. The DW/UFMP figure of 'more than a thousand' sexual violence cases over three months (search snippet, 2026-04-17) was not fetched.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Government report presented by Human Rights Minister Samuel Mbemba on a Tuesday said more than 1,500 people died and more than 300,000 were forced to flee during the occupation of Uvira, with bombings, summary executions, abductions, sexual violence and pillage creating a climate of generalised terror.
claims.actor_as_written: Rwandan army and its proxies, per the DRC Government report
claims.verification_note: Statement unchanged; `figures` narrowed to this source (HRW and Ebuteli figures moved to the note). The 'climate of terror' clause is Mbemba's, printed on the page (page-only). Party figures. HRW says the M23 and Rwandan forces killed 'at least several dozen' when they took Uvira; Ebuteli counts at least 151 civilians killed in Uvira territory in December 2025 and 21 in January 2026.
claims.researcher_note: Party figures; contradicted in scale by HRW ('at least several dozen' killed at the takeover) and Ebuteli (151 killed in Uvira territory in December, 21 in January). Not a finding.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch said its research indicated that the M23 and Rwandan forces killed at least several dozen people when they took Uvira, adding that it is difficult to know who is buried in all reported mass graves.
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Takeover phase (10 Dec 2025) precedes the unit's quarter but is the only independent count of the killings in the Government's 1,500 claim. HRW visited three burial sites.

claims.text: The DRC Council of Ministers of 27 February heard, from Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani after his mission, that mass graves had been found in Uvira, one near the World Food Programme office on the road to Kavimvira reportedly containing about 35 bodies per local sources, and a second at Kilomoni; no official exhumation had yet taken place and the identity of perpetrators and victims remained unknown.
claims.place_as_written: Kavimvira road and Kilomoni, Uvira city
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed ('identity of the perpetrators ... unknown', per the Government)
claims.verification_note: All five excerpts on the page. Grade lowered B->C: a single outlet relaying a party's (the government's) account. Government account. The article spells the quarter both 'Kavinvira' and 'Kavimvira'.
claims.researcher_note: Government account. Spelled 'Kavinvira' in the article. Provincial government figure (151) is a separate claim. Later Government report (Radio Okapi 2026-04-07) lists three graves at Mayi ya Moto with 115 bodies and Kilomoni with 31, so site names differ across sources.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the South Kivu provincial government, in a communiqué of 28 February 2026, said preliminary findings were that 151 civilians were buried in the mass graves, 121 at the Kavinvira cemetery and 30 in an enclosure in Kilomoni quarter, and that 'these executions took place on the eve of the forced withdrawal, on 18 January 2026, of the AFC/M23 elements, supported by the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF)'. The national government's account of the Council of Ministers meeting of Friday 27 February 2026 said no official exhumation had yet taken place and the identity of perpetrators and victims remained unknown.
claims.place_as_written: Kavinvira cemetery and Kilomoni quarter, Uvira city
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 supported by the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), per the provincial government
claims.verification_note: Statement unchanged; `figures` narrowed to this source (the Council of Ministers' ~35 is a separate claim). Party account. The national Council of Ministers the day before said perpetrators and victims were unknown. The communiqué's legal characterisations are not reproduced. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Council of Ministers of 27 February 2026 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: no official exhumation; perpetrators and victims unknown 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-022: Attribution drift in the actor field: as relayed, the communiqué dates the executions to the eve of the AFC/M23/RDF withdrawal and frames them as massacres, but the quoted sentence does not itself name who carried them out; 'forced' is the provincial government's word. Quote the sentence and add the national government's contrary 'perpetrators unknown' (claim r1-UV-2026Q1-040). Actor field should read 'implied: AFC/M23 with RDF support, per the provincial government'. One search found no AFC/M23 response on a citable page.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): Council of Ministers of 27 February 2026; no official exhumation; perpetrators and victims unknown
claims.researcher_note: Party (provincial government) attribution and count; the national Council of Ministers the day before said perpetrators and victims were unknown and gave ~35 bodies at one site. HRW could not say who is buried in all graves. The communiqué's legal characterisation is not reproduced here. 121+30=151 as printed.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Government report presented that Tuesday listed three mass graves at Mayi ya Moto containing 115 bodies, one at Kilomoni with 31 bodies, one at Kala, two at Rutembo and two tombs at Kaponda.
claims.place_as_written: Mayi ya Moto, Kilomoni, Kala, Rutembo, Kaponda, Uvira area
claims.actor_as_written: Rwandan army and its proxies, per the Government report
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Report date, not the date of burial; locations are partly different from the 27-28 Feb official accounts (Kavinvira). Not independently verified; HRW says it visited three burial sites and that many more exist.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Government report presented that Tuesday said the Government had identified more than 162 trucks from Rwanda involved in organised looting operations.
claims.actor_as_written: trucks from Rwanda, per the Government report
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Party claim; no dates or evidence in the article.

claims.text: Ebuteli reported that FARDC supported by the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and the Wazalendo attacked M23 fighters at Kabimba village on 7 January and at Kifuta village on 10 January, in Kalungwe groupement, Bavira chiefdom, in the middle plateaux of Uvira territory.
claims.place_as_written: Kabimba and Kifuta, Kalungwe groupement, Bavira chiefdom
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Evidence of FDNB participation in operations in Uvira territory in January; contrast with the ambassador's 17 Dec 2025 claim of withdrawal. Burundi did not comment in the pages seen.

claims.text: Ebuteli reported that on 11 January Twirwaneho fighters allied with the M23 attacked FARDC and Wazalendo positions at Abala village in the high plateaux of Fizi, and that in reprisal the FARDC targeted Mukoko village with drones on 11 and 12 January and recovered arms and ammunition lost at Abala.
claims.place_as_written: Abala and Mukoko, Basilocha groupement, high plateaux of Fizi
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho allied with M23 vs FARDC and Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Fizi territory, included as the Uvira front's southern flank.

claims.text: Ebuteli reported that on 29 January the Twirwaneho/M23/Red Tabara coalition and the FNL attacked the Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo in the villages of Kilumbi and Abala in Fizi territory, killing three Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo.
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho/M23/Red Tabara and FNL vs Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Combatant casualties; shows Red Tabara and FNL (Burundian armed groups) in the Fizi/Uvira highlands.

claims.text: Ebuteli reported that on 29 January a grenade thrown by M23 fighters killed five civilians and wounded eleven in Rutanga quarter, Sange commune, in the Ruzizi plain.
claims.place_as_written: Rutanga quarter, Sange commune, Ruzizi plain
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page; the figures are printed in words (cinq, onze). 2026-10-28: confidence edited: red-team rt-022: Single source (Ebuteli) attributes the grenade to M23 fighters, but the attribution is contested: SOS Médias Burundi (30 Jan 2026) reported four dead and eleven wounded and, citing local sources, that 'un individu non identifié aurait lancé l'engin explosif'; The New Times (Kigali, 30 Jan 2026) reported that 'The AFCM23 rebel movement blamed the government coalition for the attack' (party X says). The toll also differs (five vs four dead). Keep the statement as Ebuteli's account, grade C, and record the SOS Médias and AFC/M23 accounts as separate claims (search leads; extract text is not verbatim, so re-fetch before citing).
claims.researcher_note: Sange is where Ebuteli says the M23 repositioned after leaving Uvira. No names printed.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant local sources, violent clashes on Tuesday 17 March between the FARDC and AFC-M23 rebels at Luvungi, near Kabunambo, with bombardments, driving civilians from Runingu towards Uvira, and described the clashes as ending the relative truce around Uvira observed since the AFC-M23 withdrawal.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page; bombardments and flight towards Uvira are page-only clauses. Radio Okapi dates the M23 withdrawal to 'fin janvier 2026'; other sources give 16-18 January.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi says the withdrawal was 'fin janvier' while other sources date it 16-18 January. Ebuteli and others report earlier fighting in the highlands in January, so 'truce' applies to the city's immediate surroundings. Critical Threats (lead only) and an unfetched Facebook post also place Ruzizi plain fighting on 5 March.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the 33rd military region had announced the closure of road traffic from Runingu on the Bukavu-Uvira axis, leaving public transport vehicles and humanitarian convoys blocked there.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on the page. 'Hier' in an article of 17 March: date computed as 16 March. Speaker not named.
claims.researcher_note: 'Hier' relative to the 17 March article, so 16 March (computed from publication date). Speaker not named.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the authorities of the DRC and Burundi agreed to reopen on Monday 23 February 2026 the common border between Bujumbura and Uvira, through the Kavimvira and Gatumba border posts, with traffic resuming immediately, after the population of Uvira had been cut off from Bujumbura since the AFC-M23's temporary occupation of the city on 10 December 2025.
claims.place_as_written: Kavimvira border post, Uvira / Gatumba, Burundi
claims.actor_as_written: Governments of the DRC and Burundi
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Closure dates differ by source: Ebuteli says the border stayed closed through January despite the M23 withdrawal. Search results (RFI, France 24; not fetched) also report the 23 February reopening and that the border was reopened militarily on 19 January. FEC-Uvira operator quoted anonymously raised concerns about harassment and taxes.

claims.text: DW (Swahili) reported that Jean-Jacques Elakano, speaking to journalists in Uvira, said the government feared AFC/M23 rebels were using trade and family travel between Bukavu and Uvira to infiltrate areas controlled by the government army; a DW photo caption said the governor of South Kivu, based in Uvira, had said travel would stay suspended until the rebels left Bukavu.
claims.verification_note: The 'suspended until the rebels leave Bukavu' line is a photo caption crediting 'the governor of South Kivu in Uvira'; the body text does not give Elakano a title or put that line in his mouth. Split the two attributions. The body also quotes Elakano: 'Sasa njia itafungwa... Lengo letu ni kuhakikisha tunairejesha Bukavu' (the road will now be closed; our aim is to retake Bukavu). The statement date is not given; the date is DW's publication date (11 May 2026, byline Mitima DeLachance). Elakano's title is not printed in the article body.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet. The statement date is not given on the page; the date is the DW publication date (11 May 2026 per the search listing). Other outlets in the search results call the official 'gouverneur intérimaire' or 'vice-gouverneur'; DW's caption says 'governor'. Civil society voices in the article objected to the closure.

claims.text: DW (Swahili) reported that since Saturday AFC/M23 fighters had been withdrawing from the Sange area and some hill villages towards the north of Uvira district, and that videos circulating online showed government soldiers and Wazalendo groups entering the village of Sange.
claims.place_as_written: Sange, Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (withdrawing); government soldiers and Wazalendo groups (entering)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and covers the statement. DW attributes the withdrawal to 'reports from the Uvira area' (taarifa kutoka eneo la Uvira) and the entry to online videos; the statement keeps both attributions. 'Since Saturday' with an 11 May article = 9 May (computed). Withdrawal date differs by source: DW says 'since Saturday' (9 May, computed from the 11 May publication date); SOS Médias Burundi says Monday (11 May, computed from its 12 May dateline); Igihe 10 May (snippet only, not verified). Each claim states only its own source's date. 2026-10-29: control edited: Frontline data fix (FRONTLINE_NOTES.md): control.held_by names only the holder (for a withdrawal, the side withdrawing), so the side class is not 'both sides named'; the other side stays in the statement. Wording from the stored excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('since Saturday') and the 11 May publication date, so Saturday = 9 May; approximate. SOS Médias Burundi dates the departure to Monday 11 May; Igihe (search snippet only) dates it 10 May. Not confirmed by AFC/M23 at the time per DW.

claims.text: DW (Swahili) reported that the Congolese army said the AFC/M23 rebels had left the villages of Nyakabere, Mutarule and Luberizi, a claim that DW said AFC/M23 had not confirmed so far.
claims.place_as_written: Nyakabere, Mutarule, Luberizi, Uvira territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; the army claim and DW's note that AFC/M23 had not confirmed it are both in the one sentence. Party claim kept attributed. Army claim, not independently confirmed; date is DW's publication date.
claims.researcher_note: Army claim, not a verified fact. Date is the DW publication date. AFC/M23's own account was not found in an opened page (see gaps).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that AFC/M23 rebels left several localities of the Ruzizi plain in Uvira territory on Monday; according to local sources they withdrew from Kabunambo, Sange, Mutarule, Luberizi, Bwegera, Lemera and Luvungi towards Katogota, and residents of Sange, Luberizi and Lemera took to the streets to celebrate their departure.
claims.place_as_written: Ruzizi plain (Kabunambo, Sange, Mutarule, Luberizi, Bwegera, Lemera, Luvungi), Uvira territory; Katogota, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: All three excerpts are on the page (dateline 'Bukavu, 12 mai 2026', byline Leila Keza). 'Ce lundi' with a 12 May dateline = 11 May (computed). The page also says some local sources link the withdrawal to US diplomatic pressure ('serait lié', conditional) and that other groups 'auraient pris la direction de Kamanyola'; not added to the statement. Withdrawal date differs by source: SOS Médias Burundi says Monday (11 May, computed); DW Swahili 'since Saturday' (9 May, computed); Igihe 10 May (snippet only). The UN Group of Experts (S/2026/466, para. 49) wrote that no RDF or AFC/M23 withdrawals were documented in South Kivu at the time of drafting.
claims.researcher_note: Dateline 12 May 2026; 'ce lundi' = Monday 11 May (date computed from weekday and dateline). The same article says some local sources link the withdrawal to US diplomatic pressure and that other groups reportedly headed towards Kamanyola (not captured as an excerpt). DW Swahili dates the movement from Saturday 9 May; Igihe (snippet only) 10 May. Discrepancy surfaced, not resolved. The UN Group of Experts (S/2026/466) wrote that RDF and AFC/M23 withdrawals amounted to tactical repositioning.

claims.text: MediaCongo reported that since dawn on Wednesday 6 May 2026 violent clashes opposed AFC/M23 rebels, supported according to several sources by the Rwandan defence forces, to FARDC and Wazalendo self-defence groups, concentrated in the Ruzizi plain at Kigoro, Kigurwe and Kabunambo about 26 kilometres north of Uvira; it said no official toll had been given and that the city remained under government-force control.
claims.place_as_written: Kigoro, Kigurwe, Kabunambo, Ruzizi plain (RN5), c. 26 km north of Uvira, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (backed per several sources by RDF) vs FARDC and Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; the 'no official toll' clause is on the page but not in the stored excerpts, so supplied as a replacement quote. RDF support stays attributed to 'several sources'. Credit at end of page: 'L.M. congo-press.com (MCP) / mediacongo.net'. RDF involvement is per unnamed 'several sources' in the article, not established.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet (credited L.M., congo-press.com / MCP). The RDF involvement is the source's 'selon plusieurs sources' attribution, not established. Kabunambo was named four days later among localities AFC/M23 left (SOS Médias Burundi, 11 May). The article says 'no official toll' had been communicated. AFC/M23's and Rwanda's accounts of 6 May were not found.

claims.text: La Presse Africaine reported that, in a security assessment presented on Thursday 7 May 2026, the chiefs of six quarters of Uvira (Kimanga, Kabindula, Songo, Kilibula, Kalundu and Nyamianda) painted a dark picture of the security situation; according to this assessment, armed robbery, killings, abductions, death threats, torture and other abuses were reported almost daily, especially at night, and the outlet wrote that this violence was reportedly attributed ('seraient attribuées') largely to uncontrolled elements of the VDP Wazalendo and of the FARDC, and in part to unidentified armed men.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira (city): Kimanga, Kabindula, Songo, Kilibula, Kalundu and Nyamianda quarters, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: as alleged in the assessment: uncontrolled elements of VDP Wazalendo and FARDC; unidentified armed men
claims.verification_note: The draft put the attribution in the chiefs' mouths ('which they said were attributed'); the page has the outlet writing a conditional ('seraient attribuées') after 'Selon ce diagnostic'. Kept the conditional and the outlet as narrator. Byline Pascal Bahunde (LPA Sud-Kivu); the meeting was a quarterly security meeting run by Search for Common Ground (project 'Tukutane Tena'). General allegations at a security meeting; no individual incidents, dates or victims given.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet reporting a local-leaders' assessment at a quarterly security meeting; allegations are general, with no individual incidents, dates or victims. Wording 'seraient attribuées' is the source's. FARDC and Wazalendo accounts not found.

claims.text: Kivutimes reported that Uvira had for more than three months faced a multiplication of arbitrary arrests without trial and that, according to several local sources, some arrests were reportedly carried out by certain Wazalendo, often to obtain ransoms from detainees' families; Mapenzi Manyebwa, coordinator of the Uvira civil society synergy, denounced arrests made without respect for legal procedures, with citizens paying fines outside any judicial logic.
claims.actor_as_written: certain Wazalendo (per several local sources, as named by the source)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact and carry each clause; the Wazalendo attribution stays with 'several local sources' and the conditional. Name spelled as printed. The Wazalendo allegation is conditional ('seraient menées') and from unnamed local sources. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Kivutimes (18 May 2026, Habari za Mahali project funded by La Benevolencija) uses the conditional 'seraient menées' for the Wazalendo arrests; the statement dropped it. The page also cites a psychologist on family harms including exposure of children to GBV and early marriage.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet; article produced under the Habari za Mahali project (funded by La Benevolencija, run in Uvira by UNPC, COMEL-RDC and UFMP) per its footer. No individual detainee named. The article also notes that only certain services (prosecutor, judicial police, and within limits ANR and military intelligence) may lawfully detain.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on 15 May 2026 several boats carrying Burundian soldiers landed at Ruzizi, not far from the port of Kalundu in Uvira, before troops were deployed towards Bijombo (Uvira territory) and Itombwe (Mwenga territory); the article said the deployment was estimated (without saying by whom) at about two battalions, aimed at rebalancing the balance of forces in the Minembwe area and controlling movements between Rurambo, Bijombo and Minembwe.
claims.place_as_written: Ruzizi near Kalundu port, Uvira (city); onward to Bijombo (Uvira territory) and Itombwe (Mwenga territory), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Draft shortened the stated aim to 'aimed at the Minembwe area'; restored the source's wording. Who made the estimate is not stated on the page ('est estimé'). Single Burundi-based outlet; no unit designation, commander or official confirmation. The same article says these forces reinforce operations 'contre le M23 et Twirwaneho dans les hauts plateaux'. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi (French), dateline Uvira 19 May 2026, posted 20 May. The page says 'Le déploiement est estimé à environ deux bataillons' in the passive, naming no estimator; the statement's 'it estimated' attributes the estimate to the outlet, so it is corrected. All other clauses match.
claims.researcher_note: Single Burundi-based independent outlet; no unit designation, commander or official Burundian/Congolese confirmation found. The article describes the deployment as reinforcing operations against M23 and Twirwaneho in the highlands. The same article says Burundian forces had run joint operations with FARDC and Wazalendo at Point Zéro, Mulima, Mikenge, Kakenge, Kalingi and Bidegu in April 2026 (not captured as an excerpt).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that at a press conference in Kinshasa on Saturday 6 June the army's interim spokesperson, Lieutenant-Colonel Mak Hazukay, firmly denounced the continuation of attacks despite ongoing diplomatic initiatives, and that, according to the military authorities, several localities of North Kivu and the highlands of Fizi and Uvira in South Kivu continued to be the scene of attacks.
claims.place_as_written: Kinshasa (press conference); North Kivu localities and the Hauts Plateaux of Fizi and Uvira, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed the year, which neither excerpt prints (the page is dated 07/06/2026). The FARDC accuse 'la coalition RDF/AFC-M23' in a direct quote on the page; the statement keeps the claim as the army's. Party statement (FARDC). AFC/M23 and Rwanda replies not found.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement: the FARDC accusation is a claim by one party. Radio Okapi is a UN-founded, Congo-based radio; the page quotes the spokesperson. AFC/M23 and Rwanda responses not found.

claims.text: The ICRC reported that between 15 May and 15 June 2026 the five hospitals it supports in North and South Kivu recorded a total of 303 casualties, 30% more than for 15 April-14 May, and that, in a sign of intensifying hostilities in the Hauts Plateaux, the hospitals in Bukavu, Uvira and Fizi in South Kivu had admitted 170 casualties (56% of the 303 patients).
claims.place_as_written: Uvira General Referral Hospital (with Bukavu and Fizi hospitals), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Figures match the page exactly. Removed the Ebola clause, which sits on the page but in no stored excerpt. The page does not name the Uvira General Referral Hospital; it says 'the hospitals in Bukavu, Uvira and Fizi'. No separate figure for Uvira; 170 is for the three South Kivu hospitals combined. The location field's 'Uvira General Referral Hospital' is not printed on the page.
claims.researcher_note: ICRC press feature. Figures are for the three South Kivu hospitals combined; Uvira alone is not broken out. The 303 figure is of casualties/patients as the page words it (the page also says 'patients admitted'). Moussa Badji (ICRC medical coordinator) appears elsewhere on the page, not in these excerpts.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, according to the Human Rights Watch report 'Nous sommes des civils !', HRW documented eight cases of rape committed by M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers against women in and around Uvira between December 2025 and January 2026, with survivors describing being raped in their fields or homes, often under threat of death or at gunpoint.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira (city) and surroundings (incl. Katala, Uvira territory), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers (as alleged in the HRW report relayed by the source)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; the 'fields or homes / under threat of death or at gunpoint' clause is printed in the page body and the headline, supplied as a replacement quote. Every finding stays attributed to HRW. A relay of HRW, so not independent of the HRW origin; graded B as relayed (the HRW report itself would carry its own grade). Relay of HRW's report; events December 2025-January 2026 (before this unit's quarter). Survivors are unnamed on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Relay of the HRW report, which another claim already cites; submitted here as a separate Congolese-media account in the unit's period. The events are dated December 2025-January 2026 (by the source), i.e. before this unit's window; the date field is the stated span at month precision. Survivors are not named in the page. HRW says survivors identified the perpetrators partly by Kinyarwanda and uniforms (not in these excerpts). Rwanda/AFC-M23 denials of the HRW findings were not found in an opened page (see gaps).

claims.text: Actualite.cd, relaying the Human Rights Watch report, reported that a woman assaulted while working in her field at Katala, Uvira territory, on 15 December, went to the Kavimvira medical centre in Uvira for care but could not be treated and left without essential medicines, receiving only a small number of tablets; HRW said survivors stressed the near-total lack of accessible health services during the M23 and Rwandan occupation, notably the absence of timely PEP treatment.
claims.place_as_written: Kavimvira medical centre, Uvira (city); Katala, Uvira territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (service unavailable during M23/Rwandan occupation per HRW)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; the passage is HRW's ('a fait remarquer HRW dans son rapport') and the woman's account is relayed from the report. The page also says she identified the assailants' uniforms as Rwandan soldiers'; not needed for this health-access claim. The clinic visit followed the 15 December assault without a stated date. Assault dated 15 December (2025, per the report's Dec 2025-Jan 2026 span); clinic visit date not given. Survivor unnamed. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
claims.researcher_note: Pre-window event (Dec 2025) reported in the window; precedes the unit's period. Date '15 December' is the date of the assault in the source; the clinic visit followed ('ensuite') without a stated date. The survivor is unnamed in the page. The page states the 'Rwandan soldiers' attribution via HRW.
