claims.text: The UN Group of Experts on the DRC reported in its final report that in South Kivu no RDF or AFC/M23 troop withdrawals were documented and fighting continued, and that additional RDF reinforcements arrived from Rwanda in April, including sophisticated weaponry and anti-aerial man-portable air defence systems.
claims.place_as_written: South Kivu (province-level statement; includes the Ruzizi plain north of Uvira)
claims.actor_as_written: RDF and AFC/M23 (as named by the Group of Experts)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is para. 49 of S/2026/466 (letter dated 5 June 2026, distributed 11 June 2026), read in the retained PDF. The section opens 'At the time of drafting', so the 'no withdrawals documented' finding is as of the drafting date. Finding as of drafting (before 5 June 2026). It is in tension with the media reports of an AFC/M23 withdrawal from the Ruzizi plain on 9-11 May (DW, SOS Médias Burundi); the discrepancy is surfaced, not resolved. Para. 47 says the North Kivu withdrawals 'amounted to tactical repositioning'.
claims.researcher_note: UN panel report, document printed 19 June 2026 (ecoi.net listing date 11 June 2026). The paragraph is written before the May withdrawals from the Ruzizi plain were reported by media; it conflicts in time, not in fact, with the 10-11 May withdrawal reports. In the report, para 77 gives 18 January 2026 as the date AFC/M23 and RDF withdrew from Uvira city; this is outside the unit's period and not captured here. Footnote markers appear in the page text after 'systems'.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, spokesperson of operation Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu, said the positions of Kimete, Wihene and Kashamata had been retaken by the army, and that AFC/M23-Twirwaneho - RDF - Red Tabara elements had been forced to fall back towards Rugezi and Bigaragara, south of Minembwe.
claims.place_as_written: Kimete, Wihene, Kashamata, highlands of Fizi, Uvira and Mwenga
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries every clause; party account kept attributed. Territory widened: the article places the fighting in the highlands of Fizi, Uvira and Mwenga around Minembwe. FARDC claim; the outlet says the area is enclaved and independent information arrives late. Date computed from 'ce lundi' in an article of Tuesday 7 July.
claims.researcher_note: FARDC claim relayed by a Congolese outlet, unverified; the article says the area is enclaved with poor phone coverage. The article is dated Tuesday 7 July and says the army 'ce lundi' announced its offensive; date 6 July computed from weekday and publication date.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC denounced drone bombings attributed to the AFC/M23 the previous weekend in the village of Bidjaga, east of Point Zéro, and other densely populated villages, killing about ten people according to the army communiqué.
claims.place_as_written: Bidjaga, east of Point Zéro, highlands of Mwenga/Fizi
claims.verification_note: Excerpt states the FARDC communiqué's allegation and toll ('une dizaine de morts, d'après le communiqué de l'armée'); kept attributed to the army. Single clause chain from one excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Army communiqué relayed by media, no independent verification. Weekend date computed from publication date (7 July).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, in a statement signed by Fidèle Rugabo, the military spokesperson for the armed group Twirwaneho, the fighters claimed to have launched an offensive on Saturday, July 4, against the Point Zero position, before taking control after several hours of fighting; the outlet said no official reaction had been recorded at the time of publication.
claims.place_as_written: Point Zero (Point Zéro), Itombwe sector, Mwenga
claims.verification_note: Original credited the claim to Twirwaneho and M23 'in a statement signed by Rugabo'; the signed statement is Twirwaneho's. Narrowed to the excerpt; the joint M23 claim and the location are on the page (lead) and in the note/location field. Party claim. The article's lead says the Twirwaneho armed group and the M23/AFC-M23 jointly claim the capture of Point Zero, in the Itombwe sector of Mwenga territory. Actualite.cd of 31 August says Point Zéro was then occupied by the AFC/M23 and under attack, so control was contested over the quarter.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan claim as reported by a Burundian outlet; the same outlet reports FARDC/FDNB withdrawal only from unverified local sources. Contradicted by FARDC claims and by Actualite.cd of 31 Aug saying Point Zéro was still occupied by AFC/M23 and under attack, so control changed hands or was contested.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that clashes at Point Zéro, on the limit of Fizi and Mwenga territories, had multiplied since Friday 28 August, with heavy weapons and drones used by both belligerents, according to local sources.
claims.place_as_written: Point Zéro, border of Fizi and Mwenga
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC, wazalendo and Burundians vs AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Supported by the excerpt; local sources attribution kept. SOS Médias Burundi (31 Aug) independently reports fighting in the same highlands from Sunday 30 August.
claims.researcher_note: Same article says Point zéro is occupied by the AFC/M23 and that the army wants to retake it; not cited in this excerpt.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that a civil-society actor in the Fizi area said that from 4 a.m. on 31 August the government force FARDC, wazalendo and the Burundians launched a drone attack at Point zéro, causing massive displacement.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC, wazalendo and Burundians (as described by a civil-society actor)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is the civil-society actor's quote verbatim; attribution kept, single unnamed source.
claims.researcher_note: Single unnamed civil-society source; Burundian participation also reported by SOS Médias Burundi (31 Aug). No Burundi government statement found.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported from Uvira that fighting had been reported since Sunday in several areas of the territories of Fizi, Uvira and Mwenga, between the FARDC supported by the FDNB and Wazalendo militias, and AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho fighters.
claims.place_as_written: Malimba, Rubarati, Ruhuha, Uvira territory (also Fizi, Mwenga)
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC, FDNB, Wazalendo vs AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports it; Actualite.cd's same-day report of fighting at Point Zéro, Malimba and Rubarati corroborates the fighting.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet (Burundian independent media) relaying local sources; 'dimanche' = 30 August (computed from weekday and publication date). The detail on Malimba, Rubarati, Ruhuha and drones is in the following sentences of the same article. The Burundian government has not been found commenting.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that a Wazalendo fighter present in the Malimba area said that the FARDC, the FDNB and the Wazalendo had retaken positions previously held by AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and Red Tabara fighters at Malimba, Ruhuha and Rubarati; SOS Médias Burundi noted this could not be independently verified.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo fighter (anonymous) on behalf of FARDC/FDNB/Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: Both clauses on the page; party claim, unverified per the outlet. Anonymous combatant. Actualite.cd (31 Aug) separately cites local sources saying Malimba and Rubarati were retaken by the FARDC and Wazalendo, also unconfirmed.
claims.researcher_note: Anonymous combatant; unverified per the outlet.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Twirwaneho spokesperson Fidèle Rugabo said his fighters had repelled several attacks by the FARDC, the FDNB, the Wazalendo militias and the FDLR, citing in a post on X Kabanju, Kipupu, Nyamabuguma and Point Zéro in Fizi and Mwenga territories; SOS Médias Burundi said these claims could not be independently verified.
claims.place_as_written: Kabanju, Kipupu, Nyamabuguma, Point Zéro, Fizi and Mwenga
claims.verification_note: Supported; party claim kept attributed. Territory is Fizi and Mwenga as the article states.
claims.researcher_note: Party claim; source_type marked partisan_afc_m23 as Twirwaneho is allied with the AFC/M23. The X post itself was not opened.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that two FDNB officers, Captain Félicien Kanjori and Major Jérémie Nitunga, were arrested after the drone strike attributed to the M23 on the Mwalu hotel in Fizi; they were reportedly arrested by mercenaries in the area and suspected of passing intelligence. The outlet said the Congolese and Burundian armies had not yet communicated on the arrests.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed beyond 'mercenaries present in the area'
claims.verification_note: Every clause on the page; names printed in the excerpt. Single outlet, unnamed sources. The outlet adds that no public, independent evidence shows the officers passed intelligence, and that their reported transfer to Kinshasa (DEMIAP) is unconfirmed.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet citing unnamed sources. Outside Uvira city but records Burundian (FDNB) presence in the Fizi/Uvira theatre. Arrest date not given (reported 1 September).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on 19 August 2026 the Mwalu hotel in Fizi was struck by drones, seriously injuring two people including the manager, Mwando Lukaba, with significant material damage; an FARDC spokesperson in the region attributed the attack to the M23 and said two bombs were dropped, which the outlet said could not be independently verified.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 (as attributed by an FARDC spokesperson)
claims.verification_note: Supported; attribution stays with the FARDC spokesperson.
claims.researcher_note: The outlet says the hotel hosted several Congolese and Burundian military officials; the target character is the outlet's account of local sources.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the citizen platform MCLA-RDC said in a communiqué published Tuesday 4 August 2026 that at least four armed incidents were recorded between 1 and 4 August, causing the deaths of four people, several injuries and concern among residents.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports the statement exactly; graded C as a single civil-society origin. Citizen-movement figures relayed by Radio Okapi; the city authorities had not communicated. Overlaps with the 'at least six killed since the start of August' figure (not additive).
claims.researcher_note: Civil-society movement claim relayed by Radio Okapi; the article places the incidents in Uvira. City authorities had not yet communicated officially, per Radio Okapi. Radio Okapi of 13 Aug (separate claim) reports at least six killed since the start of August per local sources; figures not additive.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to MCLA-RDC, on 1 August in the Kavimvira quarter of Uvira a woman identified as Aimée Vumilia, aged 31 and mother of five children, was reportedly hit by a bullet, and on 2 August the lifeless body of a man was found in the Murambia zone of the Mulongwe-Kasenga quarter.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints the name, age and the conditional 'aurait été touchée'; statement keeps 'reportedly'.
claims.researcher_note: Names-only detail on the MCLA-RDC claim. Whether Aimée Vumilia died is not stated in the excerpt.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that at least six people had been killed since the start of August in several quarters of Uvira, amid a recrudescence of night attacks attributed to armed men.
claims.verification_note: Narrowed: the vehicle-handover clause (six 4x4s on 11 August) is not in the excerpt and is not part of this incident claim. Single anonymous-local-source figure, so C.
claims.researcher_note: Figure is from unnamed local sources; overlaps with MCLA-RDC figure of 4 deaths for 1-4 August (not additive).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that users of the Uvira-Luvungi, Mwenga-Uvira and Uvira-Fizi-Baraka roads denounced barriers erected by certain Wazalendo fighters, and that according to several testimonies it collected on Tuesday 4 August, taxes of 10 000 to 50 000 Congolese francs would be demanded of travellers.
claims.verification_note: The source's conditional ('seraient exigées') was rendered as fact ('are made to pay'); restored. Figures written as the excerpt prints them. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 4 Aug 2026, carries every clause, the taxes in the conditional ('seraient exigées'); the stored excerpt lacks the roads and the barriers clause, added here.
claims.researcher_note: Testimonies gathered by Radio Okapi; the youth council of Mwenga alleges ill-treatment of those who refuse or delay payment (see separate official_statement claim).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Vice-Governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Elakano, urged all Wazalendo components to act responsibly and respect the provisions set by the Provincial Security Council, and called for the dismantling of all unauthorised barriers.
claims.verification_note: Official statement as reported; excerpt supports both clauses.
claims.researcher_note: Provincial authority statement as reported by Radio Okapi. Other pages call him interim governor (Radio Okapi 3 Aug).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that six civil-society actors of Baraka, including their president Etunda Maisha Albert, were released on the afternoon of 27 August from Uvira central prison; they had been arrested on 13 August at Baraka-Centre in Fizi territory and transferred to Uvira days later.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed in the cited passage

Actor responsible for arrest not named in excerpt.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that shots were heard in Uvira from early morning on Wednesday 16 September, at Kavimvira, Kasenga, Kalundu, Mulongwe, Kimanga, Nyamianda and elsewhere, and that a local civil-society source said a fourth-year primary pupil of EP Umoja de Kamongola was shot dead at Kalundu.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city (Kavimvira, Kasenga, Kalundu, Mulongwe, Kimanga, Nyamianda)
claims.actor_as_written: shooters not identified in the excerpt (see next claim)

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that many sources described the 16 September shooting in Uvira as an expression of 'anger' by wazalendo after one of their members was arrested by the army on 5 September, the reasons for which were not known; residents said leaflets demanding his release had circulated the previous day.
claims.verification_note: Supported; attribution to unnamed sources kept, no party statement found.
claims.researcher_note: Unnamed sources; no FARDC, provincial government or Wazalendo statement on the incident found in the searches run.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that on 15 September the Congolese National Police dispersed a C64 coalition demonstration in Uvira against changing the constitution, and that rapporteur François Igilima said four people were arrested and taken away by the police.
claims.verification_note: Supported clause by clause. Other witnesses on the page name Guylain Kikwire (Ensemble pour la République federal president in Uvira) among those arrested; the mayor had banned the event citing Ebola.
claims.researcher_note: Other witnesses in the same article name Ensemble pour la République's Uvira federal president Guylain Kikwire among those arrested, and the article says the mayor banned the event citing Ebola; these are in other passages and are not cited here. Not directly about armed conflict: records a state administration measure in Uvira.

claims.text: MediaCongo reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi said that preliminary estimates counted up to 49 mass graves identified in the Uvira sector and that more than 241 bodies had already been counted in three of them alone. This entry is dated by the article reporting the statement: the graves relate to killings during the earlier rebel occupation of the city (see actor), not to events of this quarter.
claims.actor_as_written: DRC provincial government of South Kivu (speaker); AFC/M23 and allies alleged
claims.verification_note: Statement made explicit that the entry is dated by the report while the graves concern the December 2025-January 2026 occupation. Figures field had unsourced social-media numbers (110, 340, 11 Sept); removed to the note. Party statement (provincial government), not a forensic finding: the article says forensic doctors were still awaited for exhumations and DNA sampling. Only the cited figure stands. Social-media headlines of mid-September carried a count of 110 graves that no retained page supports; the two grave counts are not reconciled. The article's next sentence gives a possible total of more than 340 bodies (not in the stored excerpt). Date of the broadcast itself not given; the article is of 30 September 2026.
claims.researcher_note: Statement by a party (DRC provincial government), not independent forensic findings; the article says forensic doctors were awaited for exhumations and DNA sampling. In the following sentence the article reports the governor's estimate of more than 340 bodies in total, attributed to massacres during the 30 days of occupation (not cited here); media on 11 Sept (Actu7/Top Congo) carried a version with 110 mass graves (not opened here: Actu7 page could not be fetched); the two grave counts (49 vs 110) differ and are not reconciled. Killings relate to the Dec 2025-Jan 2026 occupation, outside this quarter; date is the date of the statement (article date). No AFC/M23 or Rwandan response found.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that at the GENOCOST day ceremony in Uvira on Sunday 2 August, survivors of the recent occupation of the city by the RDF/AFC-M23 coalition recounted violence they said they witnessed or suffered, notably executions of civilians, disappearances and other serious human rights violations.
claims.place_as_written: Place du Monument, Mulongwe commune, Uvira
claims.verification_note: Supported; testimony stays attributed to survivors. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 3 Aug 2026, carries every clause; the stored excerpt does not name the survivors as survivors of the occupation of Uvira by the RDF/AFC-M23 coalition, so that sentence is added.
claims.researcher_note: Survivor testimony at an official commemoration, no individual accounts printed; the ceremony was chaired by interim governor Jean-Jacques Elakano M'Yewa on behalf of Governor Purusi, who announced continued identification of victims linked to the mass graves and a provincial GENOCOST memorial project in Uvira (same article). Attribution to RDF/AFC-M23 is the article's wording about the occupation.

claims.text: Global Voices, republishing an article by IciCongo, reported that health actors recorded more than 1 100 cases of rape in only three months in the Uvira health zone. This entry is dated by the article's publication; the article does not attribute perpetrators or name the data holder, and it dates the three months inconsistently (see note).
claims.place_as_written: Uvira health zone (zone de santé d'Uvira)
claims.actor_as_written: perpetrators not attributed in the excerpt
claims.verification_note: Dated by report date with the period made explicit; grade lowered to C (single outlet, unnamed data owner, period stated two ways on the page). The rape count concerns an earlier period, not this quarter: the article's subtitle gives December 2025 to February 2026, while its body refers to figures of the first quarter of 2026. The data owner is unnamed ('acteurs de santé') and the cases are not described as conflict-related. Do not use as a count of conflict-related sexual violence. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Page subtitle gives the period as December 2025 to February 2026 ('Entre décembre 2025 et février 2026, plus de 1100 cas de viol enregistrés dans la zone de santé d'Uvira'); published in this quarter. The source does not name the data owner or attribute perpetrators. Civil-society coordinator Mapenzi Manyebwa calls the figure an alarm signal in a later passage. Not for use as a count of conflict-related cases without a data owner.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that Uvira's national deputy Claude Misare, in a letter of Monday 17 August to the Minister of National Defence, asked for clarification on the destination of resources for the support of Wazalendo deployed in combat zones.
claims.actor_as_written: Claude Misare, national deputy for Uvira
claims.verification_note: Supported; elected official's statement. The deputy's claim that more than 4 million US dollars a month would be disbursed (conditional) is in another passage and unverified.
claims.researcher_note: Statement by an elected official, not the executive. The same article reports the deputy as affirming that more than 4 million US dollars would be disbursed monthly by the Treasury for these fighters ('seraient décaissés'); that is a claim in a different passage, not cited here and not verified.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that violent fighting between the FRN rebels (spelled RFN in the article's text) and the FARDC, all parties backed by their allies, was reported at Mugobe and other villages of the Itara-Luvungi groupement in the Ruzizi plain, and that according to its sources RFN elements attacked FARDC and wazalendo positions in the zone from 8h00 local time.

The article does not state the day of the fighting in its text; the date is the publication date (20 October 2026, 16:00). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing an actor of Uvira society ("un acteur de la société d'Uvira"), that some schools of the Itara-Luvungi groupement sent pupils home after weapons detonations at Mugobe, and reported that the clashes disrupted traffic between Bukavu and Uvira.
claims.verification_note: The page says 'un acteur de la société d'Uvira', not explicitly civil society; narrowed. The article places the clashes 'à près de 50 kilomètres de la Route Nationale numéro 5'; the statement no longer says the fighting was on RN5. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one

claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim on page and supports the statement. Discrepancy: Actualite.cd dates the verdict Friday 2 October; SOS Médias Burundi dates it Saturday 3 October and describes the 27 as Garde républicaine soldiers. Actualite.cd also reports 10 sentenced to six months and 21 acquitted. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: SOS Medias Burundi dates the verdict Saturday 3 October and says the 27 were Republican Guard of the 21st battalion 'Simba'; see separate claim. Date conflict between outlets not resolved.

claims.place_as_written: North Kivu (AFC/M23-held areas), from Butembo, Beni and Ituri
claims.verification_note: Exact; page dated 'mar 23/06/2026' and prints 'ce mardi 23 juin'. Single local outlet: C. AFC/M23 de facto measure as reported by Actualite.cd; the stated aim is the AFC/M23 authorities'. The page also says each transport company on the Grand Nord axis must assign two drivers per vehicle, swapping at Kitsombiro (Lubero) after disinfection.
claims.researcher_note: Health: epidemic_context (Bundibugyo strain). Page date not shown in fetched text beyond 'mardi 23 juin'; year 2026 from the 22 May 2026 reminder in the same article. Stated aim is the authorities' own. Related to Africanews 20 Aug 2026 restrictions (blocked, different measure).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, since 23 May 2026, passenger transport between Goma and Butembo had been suspended until further notice by the North Kivu governorate under AFC/M23 administration.
claims.actor_as_written: North Kivu governorate under AFC/M23 administration
claims.verification_note: Exact; one clause, one source. AFC/M23 de facto measure; reported as a reminder in a later article, which says it was announced in a communiqué of Friday 22 May 2026 and covered bus and taxis ('Leo Leo'), not goods transport. excerpt_en flag is the 'Nord/North' rendering only.
claims.researcher_note: Health: epidemic_context. 'Leo Leo' bus/taxis. Reported in a later article as a reminder.

claims.text: The FARDC, in a communiqué reported by the news site, confirmed the defection of Kasereka Kabido, head of the FPP/AP/FCR movement and a member of the Wazalendo, and that according to FARDC spokesperson major-general Sylvain Ekenge, Kabido and his group had chosen to rally to Rwanda and its M23/AFC allies.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC (spokesperson Sylvain Ekenge); Kasereka Kabido, FPP/AP/FCR
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; defection clause added from the same page via replacement quote; meta sentence moved to note. FARDC (party) account. The article (11 March 2025) says the communiqué is dated '11 mars 2024', apparently a typo. Mediacongo (10 March 2025) prints the name as 'Kabido' and once 'Kisiano Kabido'. The '7' flag comes from the outlet name 7sur7.cd and is not a figure.
claims.researcher_note: Page text says communiqué dated '11 mars 2024', evidently a typo for 2025 (page dated 11 March 2025). Mediacongo (10 Mar 2025) says Kabido 'Kisiano Kabido' - name variant. Statement of FARDC, party account.

claims.text: Mediacongo reported that the self-proclaimed general Kabido and his armed group FPP/AP had officially joined the AFC-M23, which it described as a politico-military movement backed by Rwanda according to several national and international reports, and that the self-proclaimed general Shimiray Guidon, described as the commander of the Wazalendo across North Kivu, condemned this act of treason in a communiqué.
claims.verification_note: Narrowed the attribution of 'several reports' to what the sentence supports; Wazalendo condemnation is a party statement. 'selon plusieurs rapports' most naturally qualifies the Rwanda-backed description, not the joining, which Mediacongo states itself. The same article reports the Mai-Mai Kifuafua commander also distanced his group from Kabido's FPP/AP. The excerpt_en flags are translation wording (Nord-Kivu/North Kivu), not added content.
claims.researcher_note: Excerpt includes sentence 'un mouvement politico-militaire soutenu par le Rwanda, selon plusieurs rapports nationaux et internationaux' - Mediacongo's wording, not independently verified. Date: article dated 10 Mar 2025 per search listing; verify.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 8 September (2025) 'Brigadier General' Baudoin Ngaruye, commander of AFC/M23's 'First Defense Zone' covering the Goma–Rutshuru–Kanyabayonga–Kirumba axis, declared in Kirumba that AFC/M23 intended to resume hostilities aimed at capturing Butembo and Kisangani.
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt, matches PDF text; GoE documented investigation. Group of Experts finding (annex 22, footnote 178: UN, intelligence and civil society sources). The annex prints no year; 2025 follows from the report S/2025/858. Body para. 44 names Ngaruye as leading the 'First Defence Zone' covering Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms.
claims.researcher_note: Report year inferred from S/2025/858 (reporting period 2025). Report cites 'UN, intelligence, and civil society sources'. Statements of intent attributed to Ngaruye by GoE; AFC/M23's own account not retrieved. S/2025/858 is already cited elsewhere in the investigation, but this commander/zone item may be new.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that Bahati Erasto, North Kivu's AFC/M23-appointed governor, during visits to Kanyabayonga and Kirumba between 9–11 June (2025), claimed that Lubero, Butembo and Beni would soon fall under AFC/M23 control.
claims.place_as_written: Kanyabayonga and Kirumba, Lubero, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt, matches PDF text. Group of Experts finding (annex 22, footnote 177). The annex prints no year; 2025 follows from the report S/2025/858. Statement of a de facto official as reported by the Group; no AFC/M23 account retrieved.
claims.researcher_note: Year inferred from report scope. Civilian de facto official, included as a statement of the de facto authority.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that several witnesses said that one M23 commander, 'Captain Gaston', executed a Colonel Amurabi in Rumangabo around June 2025, and that Amurabi was a legal defender (défenseur judiciaire) in the military justice system in Goma, according to a former detainee and judicial and Congolese military intelligence sources.
claims.verification_note: Narrowed to the new detail (the Amurabi execution); kept 'several witnesses said' and HRW attribution; the 'dozen detainees' clause already stands in 015. Allegation resting on witnesses quoted by HRW. The 'dozen former detainees' and the nickname Longangi are already in r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-015. HRW also writes that former detainees said Gaston was reprimanded after the execution and later returned to the camp. No M23 response found.
claims.researcher_note: Excerpt contains footnote markers [96]-[99] as printed. HRW says Gaston was reprimanded after the killing but continued abusing recruits. M23/AFC response to the report not searched in this unit.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch recommended that concerned governments sanction RDF and M23 commanders responsible for serious abuses in 'training centers' and military and unofficial detention sites, including RDF Special Force commander Brig. Gen. Stanislas Gashugi, and M23 camp commanders and instructors Léon Kanyamibwa and Bertin Mas0zera, identified in this report.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo and Tshanzu (Tchanzu), Rutshuru, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: RDF Special Force (Stanislas Gashugi); M23 (Léon Kanyamibwa, Bertin Mas0zera)
claims.verification_note: Kept HRW's own wording; removed the 'allegation' framing and the paraphrase 'which it said it identified'. A recommendation addressed 'To Concerned Governments', not a finding or a sanction. Gashugi is named only once in the report text retained, in this recommendation. 'Mas0zera' is printed with a zero here; the report body prints 'Masozera' (r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-014).
claims.researcher_note: 'Mas0zera' is printed with a zero in this recommendation; elsewhere the report prints 'Masozera' (already in claim r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-014). Gashugi appears to be new to the roster. Report date from search listing.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that on Monday 8 September 2025 civil society in Uvira marched to demand the departure of general Olivier Gasita, recently named FARDC commander in charge of operations and intelligence of the 33rd military region; the population accused him of having facilitated the capture of Bukavu by AFC/M23, and Wazalendo militiamen were at the front of the opposition, while the FARDC spokesperson had three days earlier reaffirmed that Gasita enjoyed the army's confidence.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact and match the page. The accusation against Gasita is the protesters' allegation, not a finding. The same article says the march was violently repressed, with at least four dead per local sources (provisional).
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi also reports the march was repressed with at least four dead per local sources (separate incident claim likely already in UV unit).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that one man, reportedly accused of being an M23 member due to his ethnicity, was lynched on 25 January in the Lushagala internally displaced persons camp in Goma.
claims.place_as_written: Lushagala IDP camp, Goma, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (mob violence)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Year 2025 follows from para. 78 context ('Following the capture of Goma').
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 78 (footnote: open-source video footage, UN, humanitarian and civil society sources). Year 2025 follows from context (after the capture of Goma). Paragraph says over a dozen such mob-violence incidents were documented, primarily in Kinshasa.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts (annex 43) quoted a WHO report of 7 February 2025 that since 26 January 3082 injured and 843 dead had been reported from 31 health facilities in and around Goma, North Kivu.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). WHO figures quoted by the Group in annex 43; para. 79 notes the toll remained undetermined. Figures are WHO's, as quoted by the Group; the Group says the exact toll remained undetermined and publicly reported figures varied.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 43 (para. 79), quoting WHO. Para. 79 itself notes publicly reported figures varied between 900 and 2,900 dead and over 3,000 wounded and that the exact toll remained undetermined.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that over 1,000 wounded were registered in Goma between 23 and 28 January, including civilians, many of them women and children.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). 'in Goma' carried by the preceding sentence of para. 82.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 82 (footnote cites a reliefweb ICRC/humanitarian appeal). Year inferred from the paragraph context (2025).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 27 January 2025 heavy cross-border exchanges of artillery fire between the DRC and Rwandan forces caused civilian casualties on both sides of the border; in Goma the Birere neighbourhood near the airport was severely impacted, with at least 53 civilian fatalities documented, mainly women and children, after at least five shells struck homes in Mapendo and Kahembe neighbourhoods between 27 and 28 January 2025. The Group does not say which side fired those shells; it adds that residents reported FARDC heavy artillery positioned near residential areas.
claims.place_as_written: Birere, Mapendo and Kahembe neighbourhoods, Goma, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Cross-border artillery exchange between the DRC (FARDC) and Rwandan forces; the source adds residents reported FARDC heavy artillery near residential areas
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Cross-border artillery context from the opening of para. 85. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: 27 January 2025 cross-border artillery exchange (first part of the sentence, before a page break) 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: civilian casualties on both sides of the border (second part of the sentence, after the page break) 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: FARDC heavy artillery near residential areas 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-029: Para. 85 in context: the Group places the 53 deaths in the context of a cross-border artillery exchange between DRC and Rwandan forces but does not say which side fired the shells that hit Mapendo and Kahembe, and adds that residents reported FARDC heavy artillery near residential areas, and that DRC-origin fire killed 5 civilians in Gisenyi. The statement should keep the shells unattributed and carry that context.; excerpt-support: added 3 excerpt(s): 27 January 2025 cross-border artillery exchange (first part of the sentence, before a page break); civilian casualties on both sides of the border (second part of the sentence, after the page break); FARDC heavy artillery near residential areas
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 85 (civilian, humanitarian and UN sources). The same paragraph attributes the exchange to heavy cross-border artillery fire between the DRC and Rwandan forces; shooter of the specific shells is not stated in this sentence.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 46 that, according to local sources verified by UN sources, the FARDC bombing of Nyabibwe (Kalehe territory) on 6 February 2025 caused three civilian injuries (a man and his two children) and impacted at least 35 civilian homes, with no fatalities.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Date, place and FARDC as the bomber are in the annex 46 heading and para. 86 on the same page. The Group's count (three injured, no fatalities) contradicts the AFC/M23 claim of four killed; both accounts are recorded separately.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 46 (para. 86). Para. 86 says FARDC bombarded Nyabibwe targeting AFC/M23 positions. The AFC/M23 contrary claim is recorded as a separate claim.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts recorded that an AFC/M23 communiqué issued on 6 February 2025 claimed deliberate targeting of Nyabibwe by FARDC bombing, resulting in the massacre of civilians, notably four fatalities including an infant.
claims.verification_note: Recorded only as what AFC/M23 claimed, as reproduced by the Group; the Group's own sources contradict it (para. 86). AFC/M23 claim; the Group reports three civilians injured and no fatalities.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 46; para. 86 states the bombing 'resulted in injuries to three civilians' contrary to AFC/M23 claims that four civilians were killed. Cited here only for what AFC/M23 said.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that from 26 to 27 January, in Goma, retreating FARDC and Wazalendo systematically looted civilian homes and shops, engaging in theft, extortion and the shooting of civilians resisting extortion.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 88 and annex 47 (video of 26 Jan 2025 showing three armed uniformed individuals robbing and shooting a civilian). Sources: civil society, UN, audiovisual documentation.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported, without stating where, that MONUSCO documented the rape of three girls aged 13 to 17 by FARDC soldiers between 31 January and 2 February, and that FARDC authorities confirmed the violations and reported the arrest of alleged perpetrators.
claims.verification_note: Same sentence is already in r1-GOE-063, which records it 'without stating where'; this claim adds the FARDC confirmation and arrests. The draft location/province/territory (South Kivu, Kalehe) were inferred from the surrounding paragraph about 6-8 February: the source gives no place for these rapes, so they are removed. The report gives no place for these rapes. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-032: Para. 88 places the 6 to 8 February events 'between Kalehe and Kavumu', but the rapes of 31 January to 2 February are given no place, and the paragraph opens with Goma on 26 to 27 January. The verifier said the place fields were removed, but province is still 'South Kivu' and territory is still 'Kalehe'. That is time and place slippage. The amended text says the place is not stated, and province and territory should be cleared.; excerpt-support: no change needed; every clause is printed in the stored excerpts
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 88. The paragraph discusses retreating FARDC between Kalehe and Kavumu on 6-8 February; the exact place of these three rapes is not given. Year 2025 inferred from context. Victims not named.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 10 February at least 84 FARDC soldiers appeared before a military court in Bukavu, accused of desertion, the murder of at least 12 civilians, rape, looting and other crimes committed in several villages of Kabare and Kalehe territories.
claims.place_as_written: Bukavu (military court); offences in villages of Kabare and Kalehe territories, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Accused, not convicted: procedural stage kept as 'appeared before a military court, accused of'.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 88 (UN and FARDC sources; footnote cites an AP story). Allegations as stated by the Group; not a finding of individual responsibility.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in Bukavu at least six children who had dressed up in military uniforms and played with weapons discarded by fleeing FARDC soldiers were killed by AFC/M23 soldiers conducting security sweeps on 16 February.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Year 2025 from context (Bukavu taken 16 February 2025).
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 99 (humanitarian sources, researchers, video/photographic evidence). The Group says this raises 'questions of excessive use of force'. Children not named.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 6 February the AFC/M23-appointed Governor of North Kivu, Bahati Erasto, justified AFC/M23 search operations as necessary to apprehend 'Wazalendo and FDLR, mercenaries and FARDC who are still hiding in the houses'.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Speaker as the Group names him; cited for what he said.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 98 (video footage of Bahati Erasto speaking in Kinyarwanda, 6 February 2025). Cited for what he said; the Group links the sweeps to extrajudicial killings, arrests and torture.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 imposed sentences, typically beatings or summary executions, arbitrarily, and that perceived disloyalty, theft or sexual violence were generally punished by death.
claims.place_as_written: AFC/M23-held areas of North and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Subject AFC/M23 carried by para. 95.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 95 (AFC/M23 insiders, intelligence, UN, former combatants). Date is general (2025 occupation); the paragraph also says AFC/M23 relied on civilian informants and lacked detention facilities.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 operated clandestine detention sites where detainees were held incommunicado, subjected to torture and in many cases either disappeared or later found dead, their bodies discarded in public or remote areas.
claims.place_as_written: Goma and other AFC/M23-held areas, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 104; the paragraph goes on to name sites in Goma (Mont Goma, Katindo camp, 'Chien méchant' cell, Stade de l'unité, Mugunga police academy).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 51 that multiple corroborated testimonies identified the Stade de l’Unité in Goma as a holding and detention site operated by AFC/M23 and RDF forces, notably used for detaining and forcibly recruiting individuals.
claims.place_as_written: Stade de l’Unité, Goma, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 51 (para. 103), in the context of a video of 18 March 2025; the AFC/M23 call for surrender at the Stade de l'Unité began on 27 January (annex 12).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 51 that a video filmed on 17 February 2025, two days after AFC/M23 took control of Bukavu, shows the public beating of an individual by men in military uniforms.
claims.actor_as_written: men in military uniforms; the annex attributes the assault to AFC/M23 and RDF forces
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Attribution of the assault to AFC/M23 and RDF forces and the 27 blows are in the annex 51 text.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 51 (item 1), video received by the Group on 17 February 2025 from a confidential source in Bukavu; the annex states the assault 'was carried out by AFC/M23 and RDF forces who had just taken control of the city'. Victim not identified.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 51 that video footage provided to it on 18 March 2025 documents severe corporal punishment inflicted by several armed individuals in uniform at the Stade de l’Unité in Goma.
claims.place_as_written: Stade de l’Unité, Goma, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed individuals in uniform (equipment consistent with RDF issue, one with a 'PU' military police armband, per annex 51)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Equipment consistent with RDF issue and the 'PU' armband are in the annex text.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 51 (item 4). Date is that the footage was provided to the Group; the date of the beating itself is not given. Victim not identified.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 22 February 2025 at least 17 civilian men were executed near Katindo camp, in Karisimbi commune, Goma, and verified the deaths of at least 17 male victims through photographic and video evidence corroborated by witness testimony; according to witnesses cited by the Group, the killings took place during ongoing AFC/M23 sweeping operations in the Katindo neighbourhood.
claims.place_as_written: Katindo neighbourhood (near Katindo camp, Afia Bora), Karisimbi commune, Goma, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (identified by witnesses and local population; a source close to AFC/M23 confirmed responsibility)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). The link to AFC/M23 sweeping operations rests on witnesses in annex 49, and a source close to AFC/M23 confirmed responsibility (claim 19). Figures 11 and 6 (two sites) and 50 (reported, unverified; claim 18) are on the page. The Group verified at least 17 deaths; that the killings took place during AFC/M23 sweeping operations is reported by witnesses. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: witnesses: AFC/M23 sweeping operations in Katindo 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-030: Checked the retained PDF (annex 49): the Group's own finding is the 17 executions near Katindo camp; the link to AFC/M23 sweeping operations is stated as what 'witnesses reported', though the Group also writes that AFC/M23 combatants were seen arriving in trucks and rounding up men. The statement presents the AFC/M23 context as the Group's flat finding; amended to restore the witness basis. Note the FFM (r2-G-DOC-HRC-005) places what is probably the same 22-23 February operation in Kasika neighbourhood with at least 21 victims: a discrepancy to surface, not merge silently.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): witnesses: AFC/M23 sweeping operations in Katindo
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 49 (para. 101). Annex adds: 11 bodies in one compound and six at Afia Bora; on 22-23 Feb at least 50 civilians reported killed or forcibly disappeared (unverified); roundup of men at 'Terrain des scouts' on 23 Feb. Victims not named. AFC/M23 denial recorded separately.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that during door-to-door searches by AFC/M23 on 22 and 23 February in the Katindo area of Goma, at least 50 civilians were reported to have been killed or forcibly disappeared, with executions taking place on the streets and in civilian homes.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). The 50 figure is reported and not verified by the Group (it verified 17); the door-to-door searches on 22-23 February rest on multiple witnesses. Reported figure; the Group verified 17 deaths.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 49. Reported figure, not verified by the Group (the Group verified 17).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that a source close to AFC/M23 confirmed the group's responsibility for the Katindo incident, stating that AFC/M23 acknowledged internally that it was a 'bad incident' involving the summary execution of men accused of taking 'drugs'.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (per a source close to AFC/M23)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Anonymous source close to AFC/M23, as reported by the Group.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 49. Anonymous source close to the group, reported by the Group.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that after a France24 report on the Katindo killings, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka dismissed the report as 'fake news' and blatant misinformation aligned with Kinshasa's propaganda, and denied having spoken to France24.
claims.verification_note: Quote verified. The report gives no date for Kanyuka's reply; the draft's '2025-02' is not printed. Narrowed to a range from the incident (22 February) to the report date.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 49 (links an X post by Kanyuka; exact day not stated in the text). The France24 report alleged an M23 spokesperson confirmed the killings occurred during a 'sweeping and clearing' and that victims were ex-FARDC, Wazalendo or drug users.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that Bertrand Bisimwa admitted the existence of regular daily and nocturnal patrols sweeping Goma but claimed they were carried out lawfully, in a statement published on X on 9 March 2025.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Date 9 March 2025 from footnote 310 of annex 49 (annex 52 gives 10 March for the same X link; noted). Annex 52 dates the same X post 10 March 2025.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 49 (footnote: statement published on X, 9 March 2025). The Group contrasts it with consistent reports of summary executions. Annex 52 gives 10 March for a statement with the same X link; date as footnoted in annex 49.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government of the DRC, through official communiqués regularly published by its Minister of Interior, Shabani Lukoo Bihango, denounced the scale and systematic nature of abuses perpetrated by AFC/M23 and the Rwandan army, including summary executions.
claims.place_as_written: Kinshasa (communiqués on Goma and eastern DRC)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Communiqué dates (23 February, 15 March, 12 April 2025) are in the annex 49 captions.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 49; captions reproduce communiqués of 23 February, 15 March and 12 April 2025 (images; text not extracted). Cited for what the Government said.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that following the takeover of Minova on 21 January 2025, local sources and intelligence reports indicated AFC/M23 rounded up all the local youth and men and transported them in trucks to an undisclosed location.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 12 (para. 21). Date = takeover date given by the annex (para. 14 gives about two weeks after 4 January); the round-up date follows the takeover.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that multiple sources said AFC/M23 systematically abducted men, adolescents and children in conquered territories, including in and around urban settings such as Minova, Goma and Bukavu.
claims.place_as_written: Minova, Goma and Bukavu, North and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 12 (para. 21): 'forced recruitments reached unprecedented levels' since the Group's last report. Children not named.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on the morning of 29 January 2025 social media footage showed hundreds of FARDC gathered at the Stade de l’Unité in Goma, and that images show hundreds loaded onto trucks and taken to Rumangabo for accelerated military training.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 17 that in March 2025 a prominent civil society member from the Bweza groupement, displaced in Goma, was kidnapped by Ephrem Kabasha, the AFC/M23 appointed territorial administrator of Nyiragongo, from the office of Bukuma chefferie and taken to an underground cell north of Kanyaruchinya and tortured, then released the same evening.
claims.place_as_written: Bukuma chefferie office, Goma; underground cell north of Kanyaruchinya, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Torture and same-day release are in the next sentences of annex 17 (page, not the excerpt). Territory tag removed: 'Nyiragongo' is Kabasha's title, not a stated location of the event. Discrepancy in the report: this passage and para. 27 call Ephrem Kabasha the AFC/M23 territorial administrator of Nyiragongo (annex 16 also lists him as AT for Nyiragongo), while another annex 17 passage calls him territorial administrator of Masisi.

Victim not named. Note: the annex elsewhere calls Kabasha territorial administrator of Masisi; para. 27 says Nyiragongo.

claims.verification_note: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 annex 12 (para. 21); para. 169 gives 'approximately 2,000 FARDC and PNC were captured and brought to the Rumangabo training camp'. Annex 12 says the group was taken as part of coercive recruitment.
