claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 23 October AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa publicly denied the allegations made by Twangiza Mining SA, claiming that the mine was inactive, with only artisanal miners present, and that AFC/M23 lacked the necessary expertise and resources to operate gold mines; and that AFC/M23 published a communiqué on 27 October 2025 denying the accusations.
claims.verification_note: Replacement quote extends S0 back to the preceding sentence so the company name is printed; year of the 23 October denial not printed, removed.
claims.researcher_note: Para. 66 and annex 32; the two dates (23 and 27 October) are as printed. Speaker as relayed by the Group.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that Guidon Shimiray Mwissa (CDi.033), leader of NDC-R and VDP commander, moved his headquarters from Pinga to Kibati, Walikale territory, to contain RDF and AFC/M23 advancement along the Walikale-Kibua-Kashebere-Masisi axis.
claims.verification_note: S0 and S1 are the same sentence of para. 74.
claims.researcher_note: Para. 74. Excerpt ends at "Walikale territory"; the purpose clause is cited in the second source.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that APCLS leader Janvier Karairi Boingo and his troops were based in Lukweti, Masisi territory, while CMC-FDP, led by Dominique Ndaruhutse, was in Virunga National Park fighting in areas including Katsiru, Rwindi, Bukombo, Bambo, Tongo and Kalengera in Rutshuru territory.
claims.verification_note: Matches para. 74.
claims.researcher_note: Para. 74.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reproduced, in an annex, statistics on extrajudicial or summary executions by perpetrators in all DRC conflict-affected provinces showing AFC/M23 as the actor responsible for most of the violations in August 2025 (35,6%), surpassing ADF, CODECO and Wazalendo groups; a reduction in AFC/M23 violations in September 2025 (9,47%), surpassed by ADF (36,09%), CODECO (16,57%) and FARDC (10,65%); and an increase in M23-attributed killings in October 2025 (to 19,8%).
claims.verification_note: Narrowed: the stored excerpts (annex captions) do not name the UN as the statistics' source; national, not Kivu-only, figures. National figures for all conflict-affected provinces, as printed with decimal commas.
claims.researcher_note: Annex 37 (para. 80). National (not Kivu-only) UN statistics, decimal commas as printed. The Group links the September drop to lower-intensity anti-FDLR operations in Rutshuru and RDF redeployment.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported, in a paragraph on abuses by VDP/Wazalendo groups, that Alliance des nationalistes congolais pour la défense des droits humains combatants have been implicated most frequently in serious abuses against civilians, such as abductions, lootings, rape, unlawful killings and arson.
claims.place_as_written: not specified in the source (para. 81 follows the North Kivu discussion)
claims.actor_as_written: Alliance des nationalistes congolais pour la défense des droits humains (Wazalendo group)
claims.verification_note: Replacement quote extends the excerpt to the whole of para. 81 so the VDP/Wazalendo context is printed. No place, date or count given.
claims.researcher_note: Para. 81. No place, date or victim count given; the sentence does not state the province. Footnote 102 lists UN, civil society and humanitarian sources. Sexual violence element is a general finding, no individual incidents.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that VDP/Wazalendo groups also engaged in retaliatory attacks, including summary executions or targeted assassinations of individuals accused of collusion with AFC/M23, albeit on a much smaller scale than the recent systematic violations perpetrated by AFC/M23 and RDF.
claims.verification_note: The comparative clause sat outside the stored excerpt; replacement quote extends the excerpt to the end of the clause. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Para. 81 of S/2025/858 supports the statement in full, but the stored excerpt stops before the 'much smaller scale ... AFC/M23 and RDF' clause; the full sentence (with footnote marker 101) is added.
claims.researcher_note: Para. 81. The comparative "much smaller scale" clause follows a footnote marker and is not in the excerpt; it is paraphrased from the same sentence and should be narrowed by the verifier if needed.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in early September competition over the control of roadblocks in Mwenga sparked violence among Wazalendo groups, notably Mai Mai Corbeau and Mai Mai Malaika, which forced the FARDC to intervene to dismantle the growing number of barriers.
claims.actor_as_written: Mai Mai Corbeau; Mai Mai Malaika (Wazalendo); FARDC
claims.verification_note: Supported; year removed (not printed in excerpt).
claims.researcher_note: Annex 38 (para. 82).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that, according to witnesses it interviewed, Wazalendo groups established an ever-increasing number of roadblocks in and around Uvira, including along major and secondary roads; that Wazalendo imposed taxes ranging from 5,000 to 50,000 Congolese francs on road users, traders and citizens; and that between March and September at least 10 roadblocks were identified on the Misisi-Lulimba axis.
claims.verification_note: 'In and around Uvira' was outside the stored excerpt; replacement quote extends S0 to the preceding sentence (annex 38). Roadblock count kept as printed.
claims.researcher_note: Annex 38. The Uvira-Luvungi RN5 count (12 roadblocks) is already recorded. "at least10" as printed.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 26 May AFC/M23 carried out a cordon-and-search operation in a locality in Walikale, near the Rutshuru border, during which approximately 80 young men suspected of affiliation with Wazalendo factions were apprehended, and that they were reportedly transferred by force to the Rusamambo axis two days later, dressed in AFC/M23 uniforms, and deployed to the frontlines to serve as human shields.
claims.place_as_written: Locality in Walikale near the Rutshuru border; Rusamambo axis
claims.verification_note: Supported; 'reportedly' kept; year removed (not printed in excerpts).
claims.researcher_note: Annex 8 (para. 22). "Reportedly" is the Group's wording for the transfer and human-shield use. Locality unnamed.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 3 July the Congolese Minister for Human Rights, Chantal Chambu, denounced that more than 300 young men, including minors, had been captured in Rubaya without any valid legal justification and taken to an unknown destination, and that local sources, civil society and eyewitnesses confirmed the incident.
claims.verification_note: The excerpt does not name the captors; actor narrowed to 'not attributed in the excerpt'. Year removed (not printed).
claims.researcher_note: Annex 8 (para. 22). The excerpt does not name the captors; annex 8 is about AFC/M23 recruitment, and Rubaya was AFC/M23-held. Verifier should confirm attribution wording. Minister statement relayed by the Group.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that two individuals abducted by AFC/M23 with a group of 35 young men in April 2025 escaped and testified in June; they described hunger, untreated illnesses and physical abuse including torture among trainees at Rumangabo, and said 13 individuals in their group had been executed.
claims.verification_note: Escapee testimony relayed by the Group; both excerpts match. Escapee testimony; executions not independently verified in the excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Annex 8 (para. 22). Escapee testimony; executions not independently verified in the excerpt.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that it interviewed victims of arrest who had witnessed torture, inhumane treatment, including detainees stripped naked and held without food and water, and summary executions in detention centres in Goma.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed to a named unit in the sentence (preceding sentences discuss M23/PRC operations in Goma and Bukavu)
claims.verification_note: Matches para. 28; detaining unit not named.
claims.researcher_note: Para. 28. Footnote 30 lists UN sources, researchers, civil society, A/HRC/60/80 and an Amnesty report. The sentence follows the discussion of M23/PRC arbitrary detentions; the Group does not name the detaining unit in this sentence.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the newly established M23/PRC continued to conduct large-scale operations in Goma and Bukavu, resulting in arbitrary detentions and the forcible conscription of boys and men.
claims.verification_note: Narrowed to the excerpt wording ('resulting in', not 'responsible for'); 'AFC/M23 police force' label not printed in the excerpts.
claims.researcher_note: Para. 28; the two quoted fragments are consecutive in the report but split by a page break and footnotes. Period runs from 24 August 2025 (unveiling) to report cut-off.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 September FARDC's 3rd Defense Zone command reported that it received 30 alleged AFC/M23-ARC combatants, including two minors, who surrendered voluntarily to the FARDC, while 15 others were captured during clashes in North Kivu and South Kivu.
claims.verification_note: FARDC claim relayed by the Group; year removed (not printed).
claims.researcher_note: Annex 9. FARDC claim relayed by the Group; not verified by it.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in Sake, prior to transferring the refugees to Goma, AFC/M23 screened them, separating women and children from men, amid reports of physical violence, and that at least 180 men accused of FDLR affiliation were separated and brought to Stade de l’Unité in Goma, from where they were taken to an unknown location and their whereabouts remain unknown.
claims.place_as_written: Sake and Stade de l’Unité, Goma
claims.verification_note: Wording aligned with the excerpt ('refugees', as the Group writes). Adds the 180-men detail to r1-GOE-092 (12 May roundup).
claims.researcher_note: Annex 39. Date approximate: the roundup was 12 May; the separation date is not stated. Disappeared-persons lead for investigators.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that at least 72 Congolese nationals transferred to Rwanda were returned to the DRC after successfully demonstrating their Congolese citizenship, while other Congolese citizens were unlawfully deported to Rwanda without having been given the opportunity to prove their citizenship.
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; actor field narrowed because the excerpt names no actor.
claims.researcher_note: Annex 39. The excerpt does not name the actor; the surrounding annex attributes the transfers to AFC/M23 in coordination with Rwandan authorities. Verifier may narrow actor.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 17 May Rwanda's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Olivier Nduhungirehe, stated that the transferred individuals were “previously held hostages by the FDLR genocidal force.”
claims.verification_note: Narrowed: year and 'from Goma' are not printed in the excerpt. Quoted language is the minister's, as relayed by the Group.
claims.researcher_note: Annex 39. Statement as relayed by the Group (footnote 223); original post not checked.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka echoed, shortly thereafter, the statement by Rwanda's foreign minister that the transferred individuals were “previously held hostages by the FDLR genocidal force.”
claims.verification_note: Replacement quote extends S0 back to the start of the minister's sentence so 'Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs' is printed. Kanyuka's own wording not reproduced by the Group.
claims.researcher_note: Annex 39. "This statement" refers to the Nduhungirehe statement in the preceding sentence. Wording of Kanyuka's statement is not reproduced.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in May and June 2025 the Congolese government accused AFC/M23 and Rwanda of ethnic cleansing by resettling “Rwandan families” with Rwandan identity cards in eastern DRC, and annexed an official communiqué by the DRC Minister of Interior of 14 May 2025 accusing Rwanda of orchestrating an ethnic cleansing and repopulation operation.
claims.verification_note: Garbled clause rewritten to the caption's wording. Government accusation as relayed by the Group; 'ethnic cleansing' is the government's term, attributed. 'Ethnic cleansing' is the DRC government's accusation, not a finding.
claims.researcher_note: Annex 40 (para. 88). DRC accusation reported by the Group; the Group notes the returnee origins cannot be determined without UNHCR oversight. No Rwandan or AFC/M23 reply to these communiqués is recorded in the document.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government declared it would invalidate all judicial acts undertaken by AFC/M23 in violation of the country’s constitutional order, and annexed a statement of the DRC Conseil Supérieur de la Magistrature, dated 12 September 2025, declaring all judicial acts undertaken by AFC/M23 a violation of the constitutional order of the DRC.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC; Conseil Supérieur de la Magistrature
claims.verification_note: Garbled sentence repaired to the excerpt wording.
claims.researcher_note: Para. 33; annex 16 (document provided by a DRC Government source).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in July 2025 Benjamin Mbonimpa, AFC/M23 permanent secretary and chief negotiator at Doha, stated that AFC/M23 was proposing federalism as a form of governance.
claims.verification_note: Matches para. 20; statement as relayed by the Group.
claims.researcher_note: Para. 20 (footnote cites a post on X). As relayed by the Group.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo expected AFC/M23 to withdraw and accept cantonment, while AFC/M23 leaders insisted on maintaining control of current positions and seeking integration into State structures.
claims.verification_note: Narrowed: 'under the Doha Declaration' is not in the excerpt. Group's characterisation of the parties' positions.
claims.researcher_note: Para. 16. Group characterisation of the parties' positions; dates approximate.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in a letter addressed to the US President, as facilitator of the Washington peace process, the FDLR leadership alleged that the FDLR's assigned mission consisted of protecting the Rwandese refugee community in the DRC, and expressed concern that the neutralisation plan was being implemented in an indiscriminate manner, potentially targeting civilians.
claims.verification_note: The 2 July date is only in the annex caption, not the stored excerpt: date narrowed to 2025 (approximate). 2026-10-29: date_precision edited: QA 0.4 (A4): the date is a year only (2025), so approximate in the edition vocabulary (day, approximate, month, range); precision was day
claims.researcher_note: Annex 7 (para. 15). The 2 July date is from the annex caption "FDLR letter of 2 July 2025 addressed to the President of the United States"; not in the excerpt - verifier may narrow date to 2025-07.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that VDP/Wazalendo spokesperson Jules Mulumba called for the recognition of the VDP/Wazalendo as legitimate stakeholders and requested their inclusion in peace negotiations, and stated that they rejected any agreements from Doha that did not consider their demands.
claims.verification_note: The 9 and 14 November dates are only in the annex caption, not the stored excerpt: date narrowed to 2025 (approximate).
claims.researcher_note: Annex 7. Dates from the annex caption "Letters of 9 and 14 November 2025, signed by Jules Mulumba"; not in the excerpt.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that M23 members committed retaliatory killings immediately after seizing localities, and that several civilians were summarily executed in Minova, South Kivu, in January immediately after M23 took control.
claims.verification_note: Para. 30 says exactly this; Kalehe is the compiler's placement of Minova (correct administratively).
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 30. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Territory (Kalehe) is the compiler's administrative placement; the report names only Minova, South Kivu.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in June and July M23 summarily executed dozens of individuals following confrontations with Government forces in Walungu and Kabare territories (South Kivu), as apparent collective punishment.
claims.verification_note: Para. 30 verbatim.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 30. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that from 8 to 29 July M23 members, accompanied by civilians armed with machetes and alleged RDF soldiers, attacked several farms in Bishwa chefferie in Rutshuru and allegedly executed hundreds of civilians, mainly Hutu; the FFM said it could not fully investigate these incidents given time constraints.
claims.place_as_written: Bishwa chefferie [as printed in para. 31; para. 19 prints Bwisha], Rutshuru territory
claims.actor_as_written: M23 members, with civilians armed with machetes and alleged RDF soldiers
claims.verification_note: Para. 31 checked; hedges ('alleged RDF soldiers', 'allegedly executed') kept. The time-constraints caveat sits in the next sentence of para. 31 (page, not excerpt). The report spells the chiefdom 'Bishwa' in para. 31 and 'Bwisha' in para. 19. Footnote 35 gives a separate OHCHR figure (at least 319 killed in Rutshuru, 9-21 July), a different date range from para. 31's 8-29 July.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 31. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Para. 19 describes the same offensive in Bwisha chefferie, a predominantly Hutu area and traditional FDLR stronghold.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission stated in a footnote that OHCHR reported M23 killed at least 319 civilians in Rutshuru from 9 to 21 July.
claims.verification_note: Footnote 35 verbatim; statement attributes the figure to OHCHR as cited by the FFM, not to the FFM's own finding. This is OHCHR's figure quoted in a footnote; the FFM's own text (para. 31) says 'allegedly executed hundreds' for 8-29 July.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 footnote 35 to para. 31. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Different figure and date range from the 'hundreds' and 8-29 July of para. 31; both are the report's own.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that at least 21 civilians, including adolescent boys below 18, were executed in M23 cordon-and-search operations in the Kasika neighborhood of Goma on 22 and 23 February; armed M23 members went door to door rounding up local youth, allegedly on accusations of criminality, and killed most victims at point blank range.
claims.verification_note: Para. 32 verbatim. Footnote 37: the number of victims is likely higher, some reporting up to 50 killed (citing S/2025/446 annex 49).
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 32. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Footnote 37 cites S/2025/446 annex 49 for the higher figure. Footnote 37: the number of victims is likely higher, some reporting up to 50 killed (e.g. S/2025/446 annex 49).

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 16 February in Bukavu M23 members killed a man, allegedly for failing to present identification documents; on 22 February a man was executed for stealing a telephone, and the same day two men accused of filming an M23 convoy were publicly executed, the perpetrators reportedly stating to bystanders that 'no indiscipline will be tolerated'.
claims.verification_note: Para. 33 verbatim; the report does not place the 22 February executions. The report names Bukavu only for the 16 February killing; it does not say where the 22 February executions took place.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 33. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). The report does not say in which town the 22 February executions took place (the paragraph opens with Bukavu for 16 February).

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission recorded at least 11 children deliberately shot at and killed by M23 for no discernable reason; examples given were a 17-year-old boy shot in the head at a bar in Goma in February, and a woman and her two young children shot in April.
claims.verification_note: Para. 34 verbatim. Date widened: the 'at least 11' total has no period of its own; the examples are February and April, within the report's January-July 2025 scope (para. 5). The report does not give the place of the April killing.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 34. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). The report does not give the location of the April killing.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 13 February in Goma M23 members killed Delcat Idengo, a singer and activist known for songs critical of both M23 and the Congolese authorities.
claims.verification_note: Para. 36 verbatim; name printed in the excerpt. Corroborates r1-GOE-067 (Group of Experts, a separate UN body).
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 36. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in at least four incidents in Goma M23 entered hospitals to locate suspected FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR members being treated or hiding there, detaining hundreds of people, including patients, medical personnel and accompanying family members.
claims.verification_note: Para. 38 verbatim; hospitals and dates not given, range is the report period.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 38. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Hospitals are not named and dates are not given; period is the report's Jan-Jul 2025 scope (para. 5).

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that M23 detained thousands of civilians, primarily during cordon-and-search operations conducted almost daily since January.
claims.place_as_written: M23-controlled areas, North and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Para. 38 verbatim. Territory set to not specified: the paragraph is not limited to Goma.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 38. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Ransom detail is from para. 39, not in the excerpt, so it is omitted from the claim; see next claim.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that many of those detained, mostly able-bodied men and boys around 15 and older, were loaded into trucks and taken away.
claims.place_as_written: M23-controlled areas, North and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Para. 39 verbatim; actor M23 from the context of paras. 38-39 (detentions by M23).
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 39. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement limited to the excerpt in the final text; see fix below. Para. 38-39 sit in the section on patterns of violations in M23-controlled areas; the excerpt itself names no actor.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported accounts indicating that some guards at improvised M23-run detention sites in North and South Kivu were Rwandans, and said it received credible information that senior M23 commanders, including M23's military leader, were present at some of these sites; their names were retained on file.
claims.place_as_written: Improvised detention sites, North and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Para. 44 verbatim; names withheld by the FFM.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 44. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Commanders are not named in the public text. Statement date is the report's 2025 scope; no month given. Annex IV (map of sites) is image-only in the text retrieved.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that individuals forcefully recruited or otherwise detained were transported to former FARDC camps in Rumangabo and Tshanzu (Rutshuru territory) for 're-education' and military 'training' for three to four months, before being reportedly deployed to the front line.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Para. 46 verbatim; 'reportedly deployed' hedge kept.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 46. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Para. 45 states 'Thousands of civilians – including adolescent girls and boys – were forcibly recruited after being detained during search operations'. Para. 48: recruits stated most instructors and guards were Rwandan nationals, including some RDF members in uniforms.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that guards from Tshanzu removed women from their enclosures at night, and that many women detainees, unable to endure the hunger, were subjected to sexual exploitation and forced to exchange sex for food.
claims.verification_note: Para. 47 verbatim.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 47. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Same paragraph: detainees who tried to escape were executed in front of other detainees and bodies displayed; one survivor said 'Tshanzu was hell'.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that other incidents in M23 detention included so-called 'corrective rapes', forced nudity, non-consensual touching and sexual slurs, perpetrated either by M23 guards or by co-detainees with the instigation or acquiescence of de facto authorities.
claims.verification_note: Para. 50 verbatim; adds the 'corrective rapes' sentence to r1-SV-2025-010.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 50. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that between 10 and 13 May M23 forces detained hundreds of people, mostly men and adolescent boys, during cordon-and-search operations in Goma, Nyiragongo and Sake and took them to Goma stadium, where they were grouped by presumed affiliation.
claims.verification_note: Para. 53 verbatim.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 53. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Para. 54: UNHCR stated on 22 May that more than 1,700 'Rwandan nationals' had been returned to Rwanda after screening interviews conducted 'under pressure'.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 22 May UNHCR stated that more than 1,700 'Rwandan nationals' brought to a transit center after cordon-and-search operations had been returned to Rwanda after screening interviews conducted 'under pressure'.
claims.verification_note: Para. 54 verbatim; the figure is UNHCR's as relayed by the FFM (footnote 44: RFI and UNHCR).
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 54. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in North Kivu women and adolescent girls were subjected to gang rapes by retreating FARDC and Wazalendo, and that one woman was held hostage, tied to a tree and raped daily for two weeks by multiple perpetrators until her family paid a ransom.
claims.verification_note: Para. 56 verbatim. Relation set to adds_detail: the first clause is r1-SV-2025-011; the hostage case is new detail. The report does not say the hostage case was in North Kivu or who the perpetrators were beyond 'multiple perpetrators'.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 56. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Section VII.A places the pattern in the retreat from the frontlines in January and February (para. 55). The report gives no locality.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that during their retreat soldiers from the 'Satan II' and 'Guépard' units repeatedly entered homes, looted property and raped civilians, following a consistent pattern across multiple locations and over a wide geographic area.
claims.verification_note: Para. 78 verbatim; January-February from the same paragraph ('in January and February').
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 78. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement trimmed to the excerpt.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported community mobilization campaigns with door-to-door visits and mass gatherings, particularly between February and April in Fizi territory, South Kivu, during which boys and girls were encouraged to enroll.
claims.verification_note: Para. 60 verbatim; Wazalendo from the paragraph's lead sentence.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 60. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported verified witness accounts of boys visibly under 18 carrying weapons at Wazalendo checkpoints in South Kivu, patrolling in Uvira, and bearing AK-47 rifles in Fizi territory.
claims.place_as_written: South Kivu: checkpoints, Uvira, Fizi territory
claims.verification_note: Para. 61 verbatim; the paragraph gives no date, range is the post-February period of Wazalendo control within the report scope.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 61. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement trimmed to the excerpt; girls/sexual-purposes sentence is already cited by an r1 claim.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission examined allegations of at least six children killed when M23 entered Bukavu, who had taken uniforms and weapons left behind by fleeing Wazalendo and FARDC members; it could not determine the precise circumstances of their deaths.
claims.actor_as_written: not determined by the FFM (children killed when M23 entered Bukavu)

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that after February Wazalendo groups capitalized on the security vacuum left by retreating Congolese forces to assert control over Uvira and parts of Fizi territory, establishing parallel administrative and judicial structures, conducting informal trials and carrying out illegal arrests.

claims.verification_note: Para. 63 verbatim.

claims.verification_note: Para. 63 verbatim; sites not located in the public text beyond the paragraph's Uvira/Fizi setting.

Excerpt contains footnote numerals 50 and 51 as printed; statement trimmed to the excerpt (UNICEF attribution is footnote 51). Footnote 51 gives UNICEF as the source of the tripling.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that sexual violence took place mainly in the form of gang rapes by up to seven perpetrators, during or after military operations, in the context of disruption of law and order or during the displacement of populations fleeing armed conflict.
claims.verification_note: Para. 66 verbatim.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 66. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement trimmed to the excerpt.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in some instances victims were abducted and subjected to sexual slavery; for example, a 19-year-old woman was abducted, taken to an unknown location to become the 'wife' of an FDLR element who raped her for two days.
claims.verification_note: Para. 67 verbatim; the 'in some instances ... sexual slavery' clause is the sentence before the excerpt (page). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: A/HRC/60/80, para. 67, supports the whole statement, but the stored excerpt omits the opening sentence on abduction and sexual slavery that the statement carries; the full contiguous passage is added.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 67. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Survivor unnamed; date and place not given.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported cases of sexual violence against men and boys and LGBT individuals, including a verified case of a 13-year-old boy raped along with his mother, a 14-year-old boy beaten and forced to have sexual intercourse with a female relative in front of his siblings, and a documented case of forced nudity, beatings and public humiliation of an LGBT individual by Wazalendo members.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo members (LGBT case); not attributed for the two boys' cases
claims.verification_note: Para. 68 verbatim; perpetrators of the two boys' cases not given.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 68. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Minors unnamed in the source.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that it confirmed that, during the mass escape from Munzenze prison on 27 January, most of the 160 women inmates, along with numerous infants, died, and that an undetermined number were gang-raped, in some cases in front of their children, by male inmates who had forced their way into the women's ward.
claims.verification_note: Para. 69 verbatim. Adds the FFM's confirmed finding to r1-SV-2025-004 (annex caption of the same report) and relates to r1-GOE-062 / r1-SV-2025-001/003 (165-167 women per other sources). Figures differ by source: the FFM says most of 160 women inmates died; footnote 53 cites official (DRC Government) sources for 144 women and 30 infants dead; other r1 sources give 165-167 women raped. The FFM records two accounts of the cause: prisoners setting fire to cells, and detonations from shelling.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 69. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Sources differ on cause: some reported prisoners set fire to cells, others described detonations from shelling. Annex VI (satellite images) is image-only. Likely overlaps in part existing r1 claims on the Munzenze escape. Footnote 53: official sources (Government of the DRC) reported that 144 women and 30 infants died.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission confirmed repeated rapes, other ill-treatment and death threats by an escapee previously convicted by national judicial authorities, against victims and human rights defenders who had testified against him in court.
claims.verification_note: Para. 70 verbatim. Date set to the report's January-July 2025 period (the raw '2025' had no precision flag basis); place, prison and date not given.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 70. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Date, place and prison not given.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that victims' access to appropriate healthcare remained severely constrained due to ongoing hostilities, limited financial resources, threats against healthcare personnel, non-payment of salaries to medical staff, insufficient post-exposure prophylaxis kits and a reduction in international funding to health and support providers.
claims.verification_note: Para. 71 verbatim.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 71. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that shells reportedly struck the maternity ward of Charité Maternelle Hospital in Goma on 28 January, killing and injuring several civilians, including newborns and pregnant women.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 24 January multiple projectiles, including a 122mm rocket, struck the Rusayo IDP camp, killing at least 14, mostly women and children, and injuring many others.

Discrepancy: the UN Group of Experts (r1-GOE-065) reports bombs from RDF-controlled positions striking Rusayo 1 and 2 camps on 26 January, killing at least 12; the FFM gives 24 January and at least 14, and names no perpetrator. claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 25. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement trimmed to the excerpt; the FARDC-weapons observation (para. 25) is quoted in the next claim.

claims.verification_note: Para. 27 verbatim; perpetrator not identified by the FFM.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 27. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).

claims.verification_note: Para. 27 verbatim.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 27. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported that Congolese human rights minister Chantal Mwavita said that between 28 and 29 June more than 300 young people were arrested by the M23 at Rubaya and about twenty others at Rugendo (Kabare), were presented publicly at a meeting as volunteers, and that she denounced this as forced recruitment.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 / M23-RDF, per the Congolese human rights minister
claims.verification_note: Page (4 Jul 2025) quotes the minister with the 28-29 June dates and Rugendo figure; source 1 excerpt extended to the contiguous quotation. Kept attributed to the minister; grade C (partisan). Party (Kinshasa) allegation. The page also says, citing independent sources in occupied areas, that young people have been abducted and accused of working with Wazalendo.
claims.researcher_note: Party (Kinshasa) allegation; the article also says 'according to independent sources in occupied areas' young people have been abducted and accused of working with Wazalendo. Page spells the minister's title 'ministe'. The packet categories searched did not include forced_recruitment, so overlap with other rounds is possible.

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported that the Congolese Interior Ministry, in an official communiqué, denounced actions in AFC-M23-held areas of North Kivu including more than 272 assassinations and summary executions, more than 300 rapes and more than 300 acts of torture, which it said occurred mainly between 20 September and 2 October 2025 in Rutshuru, Walikale and Masisi territories.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC-M23, per the Congolese Interior Ministry
claims.verification_note: Page (11 Oct 2025) supports every clause; AFC-M23 named in the sentence before excerpt 0, so it is extended. Statement keeps the conditional as 'it said'. Party (Kinshasa) allegation; the page uses the conditional ('auraient été commises').
claims.researcher_note: Partisan (Kinshasa) allegation, cited only for what the ministry said; not verified. 7sur7.cd names the Interior Ministry; the minister is not named in the excerpt. Related Kinshasa figures at the UN Security Council on 13 October are quoted in the Mediacongo/Radio Okapi item (next claim). Not found in the period packet (which holds the April 297-killings communiqué).

Headline says 'plus de 120', body says 'au moins 123'. The page is only fetched by page_text.py via the browser-UA route it uses for the excerpt checker; no block was bypassed by me.
