Excerpt includes an unrelated food-assistance clause that cannot be split. Contradicting reporting: OCHA (2025-08-22): Highlights name Kabare and Uvira territories, not Kalehe and Uvira as in Actualite.cd's body text; Actualite.cd's own text says Kalehe and Uvira.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that more than 74 civilians were killed and 83 wounded in South Kivu since 2 December 2025 in clashes between the FARDC and the M23 (the source adds 'appuyés par les combattants Wazalendo', supported by Wazalendo fighters); the report cites a communiqué of Bruno Lemarquis (humanitarian coordinator and acting head of MONUSCO) on the escalation of violence. The page does not say who produced the figures.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and M23, each with allied fighters (not attributed by victim)
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact and support. '7' flag is the headline's '7 jours' (figures field only). The page does not say who produced the 74/83 figures; the headline says 'at least 74', the text 'more than 74'. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-033: The English 'the M23, supported by Wazalendo fighters' reads as Wazalendo supporting M23; in the French 'appuyés' is plural and cannot agree with 'le M23' alone. Also both excerpts are from one Radio Okapi page, so independent_origins should be 1, not 2.; excerpt-support: cut the grammatical reading that 'appuyés' agrees with the FARDC, not the M23 (an interpretation the page does not print; the phrase is quoted instead)
claims.researcher_note: The page does not say who produced the 74/83 figures; Lemarquis's communiqué is cited in the next paragraph. Headline says 'au moins 74', text says 'plus de 74'. Not in packet (searched '74 civil', 'Lemarquis' only Sept ADF item). Local outlet; UN original communiqué not opened.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, in a communiqué seen on 10 December 2025, Bruno Lemarquis (humanitarian coordinator and acting head of MONUSCO) said the escalating violence in South Kivu notably hinders medical evacuations and affects schools and other civilian infrastructure.
claims.verification_note: Exact; page (10 Dec 2025) on South Kivu fighting. Generic, no incident or perpetrator. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Generic statement, no specific incident or perpetrator.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that four people were killed and eleven wounded on Thursday 29 January 2026 around 18:30 in Sange, Uvira territory, by a grenade explosion; according to local sources an unidentified individual threw the device in the middle of the town, and MP Justin Bitakwira publicly accused the M23 of being behind it. The M23 held a meeting with residents of Sange on 30 January and called on anyone illegally holding arms or munitions to hand them in.
claims.actor_as_written: unidentified individual per local sources; M23 accused by Justin Bitakwira
claims.verification_note: Byline Adam Ntwari, SOS Médias Burundi, Bukavu 30 Jan 2026. Excerpt 1 extended to carry the M23 meeting clause. Figures field trimmed to this source's numbers (r1 discrepancy moved to note). Casualty figure differs from another source in the timeline (5 killed); surface both. Attribution of the thrower rests on unnamed local sources.
claims.researcher_note: Discrepancy with Ebuteli item r1-UV-2026Q1-048 (5 killed, 11 wounded, M23 attributed): SOS gives 4 killed and an unidentified thrower per local sources. Surface both. Third source entry may fail if the excerpt boundary is wrong; see check_raw.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, in an article on the Forum des ONGI en RDC condemning drone strikes in Goma, that in January 2026 the office of the international organisation War Child in Masisi, North Kivu, had already suffered significant damage following an air attack in the area.
claims.verification_note: Removed the acronym FONGI (not in excerpt or title); used the title's name. Sentence follows the FONGI communiqué passage, so attributed to it. Exact day, attacker and casualties not given.
claims.researcher_note: Single-sentence mention; exact day, attacker and casualties not given. Lead: look for War Child / OCHA access reports. Related packet items: r1-ATR-NK-2026-003/-004 (UNICEF worker killed in Goma, 11 March 2026).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the Forum des ONGI en RDC, in a communiqué condemning drone strikes in Goma, recalled that in 2025, 13 humanitarians were killed in the region against 9 in 2024, and that 626 security incidents targeting them were recorded in 2025 against 428 the previous year, citing OCHA.
claims.place_as_written: eastern DRC (communiqué on Goma, North Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Removed the 11 and 12 March dates and the FONGI acronym (not in excerpt); page says 'communiqué ce jeudi 12 mars' on strikes 'le 11 mars'. 'This region' is not defined in the sentence; the communiqué concerns eastern DRC.
claims.researcher_note: 'Cette région' is not defined in the excerpt (the communiqué concerns eastern DRC); geography is therefore approximate. Adds detail to packet items r1-ATR-NK-2026-003/-004.

claims.text: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that about a hundred road users had been blocked at Kanyabayonga, in the south of Lubero, since 3 October 2026 (the page prints 'vendredi 3 octobre 2026') after the closure of the Kanyabayonga-Kiwanja, Kanyabayonga-Kibirizi, Kanyabayonga-Rwindi and Kanyabayonga-Vitshumbi axes, a measure it said followed the confirmation of six new Ebola cases in the Kayna and Alimbongo health zones and was confirmed in a communiqué of the AFC/M23 administration that controls the area. It said the AFC/M23 administration at Rutshuru announced the suspension of traffic on the Kanyabayonga–Kikuku, Kanyabayonga–Vitshumbi, Kanyabayonga–Kiwanja and Nyakakoma–Ishasha axes, with only goods vehicles and humanitarian vehicles with the governor's prior authorisation allowed. Users at Kiwanja asked for Ebola prevention measures to be reinforced while allowing traffic to resume.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 administration at Rutshuru, as named by the source
claims.verification_note: Original said four axes 'from Kanyabayonga' but the communiqué list includes Nyakakoma-Ishasha; narrowed to the lists as printed and added the stated Ebola reason and the Kiwanja attribution from passages contiguous with the excerpts. excerpt_en flags are translation of French weekday/month words only. Single local outlet: C. The source prints 'vendredi 3 octobre 2026', but 3 October 2026 was a Saturday; the weekday/date mismatch is the source's and is left as printed. The two axis lists in the article (blocked axes vs. communiqué axes) differ; both are given as printed.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet (Radio Moto Oicha/RMBB, Butembo-Beni). Page date taken from URL (8 Oct 2026). The page says 'vendredi 3 octobre 2026' but 3 Oct 2026 is a Saturday: weekday/date inconsistency in the source, kept as printed. The headline links the closure to Ebola at Kayna and Alimbongo; the excerpts do not state the reason for the closure. Shows AFC/M23 holding Kanyabayonga in Oct 2026. Does not duplicate r1-NKS-2026Q3-010 (Enquete.cd 3 Sep Kayna case).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that after five days of occupation the M23 rebels backed by the Rwandan army withdrew from Kasugho, an agglomeration of 21 thousand ('21 milles') inhabitants at the foot of the Tayna gorilla reserve, 45 km west of Lubero-centre, and that a resident who requested anonymity said the rebels withdrew without fighting in the night to 7 March and headed for Bunyatenge.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 rebels, as named by the source
claims.verification_note: Figure written as the page prints it ('21 milles'); weekday wording dropped. 'AP' flags come from 'FPP/AP' in the title (an armed group), a false positive: no agency credit; article signed Claude Sengenya. Conflicting account: BETO the same day says the withdrawal followed intense FARDC/VDP-M23 clashes. The 'without fighting' account rests on one anonymous resident.
claims.researcher_note: CONFLICTS with BETO of the same day (separate claim): BETO says the withdrawal followed intense FARDC/VDP-M23 clashes. Night 'jeudi à vendredi' = 6-7 March 2025, computed from the page's own 'vendredi 7 mars'. Capture date (about 2 March) is from search-result snippets only and not retained, so not stated here. Kasugho was not before in the period packet.

claims.text: BETO reported that M23 elements withdrew from Friday 7 March from three villages of Lubero territory, Kasugho, Katoyo and Kagheri, about 45 km west of Lubero centre, after intense clashes between the FARDC supported by VDP and the M23; it also said the Ugandan army (UPDF) had for some weeks occupied the neighbouring village since the M23 threatened Lubero-centre.
claims.actor_as_written: M23; FARDC supported by VDP; UPDF (as named by the source)
claims.verification_note: All three passages verified on the retained page. Byline decision: the page ends 'Merveilles Kiro' and the style (local witness quotes, VDP term) is local reporting; 'AFP' sits in a header template line beside 'La Rédaction', so originating_source is BETO. Contradicts Actualite.cd of the same day, which reports a withdrawal 'sans combat' per an anonymous resident. BETO's header reads 'AFP La Rédaction', but the article is signed by Merveilles Kiro and carries no AFP dateline or end credit; it is treated as BETO's own reporting, not AFP copy.
claims.researcher_note: Contradicts Actualite.cd 7 Mar ('sans combat'): the two outlets disagree on whether there was fighting before the withdrawal; neither names a commander. The page byline reads 'AFP La Rédaction' (BETO editorial desk, Kinshasa); treat as possible agency relay, unconfirmed. 'Neighbouring village' (UPDF) is not named in the excerpt; Actualite.cd places UPDF at Kagheri 15 km from Kasugho.

claims.text: BETO, in a 7 March 2025 article whose byline reads 'AFP La Rédaction Kinshasa' and which is signed Merveilles Kiro, reported that during their withdrawal from Kasugho the M23 rebels were accused of looting, including equipment of the RTCT Kasugho radio and villagers' shops, and quoted a witness as saying they took the new mixer, the computer and the microphones from their base at the radio; Actualite.cd quoted an anonymous resident as saying that before leaving the rebels looted, notably at radio Tayna and in shops.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 rebels (accused), as named by the source
claims.verification_note: Witness quote was on the page next to the excerpt; replacement quote extends the excerpt contiguously. Two separately reported local accounts; 'AP' flag is from 'FPP/AP' (false positive). Allegation from a witness (BETO) and an anonymous resident (Actualite.cd); BETO's 'RTCT Kasugho' and Actualite.cd's 'radio Tayna' appear to refer to the same Radio Télévision Communautaire Tayna sub-station, per BETO's wording. 2026-10-28: source 0 originating_source edited: fact-check fc1: Both pages (7 March 2025) carry every clause. The BETO page's byline credits 'AFP' alongside 'La Rédaction Kinshasa' while the text is signed by Merveilles Kiro; the page does not make clear whether it is AFP copy, so the credit is surfaced rather than resolved. 2026-10-28: source 0 originating_basis edited: fact-check fc1: Both pages (7 March 2025) carry every clause. The BETO page's byline credits 'AFP' alongside 'La Rédaction Kinshasa' while the text is signed by Merveilles Kiro; the page does not make clear whether it is AFP copy, so the credit is surfaced rather than resolved. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Both pages (7 March 2025) carry every clause. The BETO page's byline credits 'AFP' alongside 'La Rédaction Kinshasa' while the text is signed by Merveilles Kiro; the page does not make clear whether it is AFP copy, so the credit is surfaced rather than resolved.
claims.researcher_note: Two local outlets agree (Actualite.cd quotes an anonymous resident; BETO a witness). Not independent proof of who looted: both say rebels 'accused'/per resident. perpetrator_alleged: M23.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that by the evening it still could not establish who controlled Kasugho: civil society sources spoke of Ugandan UPDF soldiers, a unit of which was deployed on the axis from Lubero centre to Kasugho, while the local authority said Kasugho was controlled by Wazalendo militiamen; Paluku Kuliumbwa said the UPDF soldiers were not yet at Kasugho but at Kagheri, 15 km away, and that the Wazalendo controlled Kasugho. The outlet also reported, per its sources on the spot and confirmed by Paluku Kuliumbwa, the state's delegated official at Kasugho, that Wazalendo who returned after the rebels' withdrawal came across an armed man in a drunken state, taken to be an M23 rebel, and shot him dead.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo; UPDF; fonctionnaire délégué de l'État Paluku Kuliumbwa (as named by the source)
claims.verification_note: The excerpt for the killing began 'ils ont croisé' without the subject; the replacement quote adds the contiguous preceding sentence that names the Wazalendo. Weekday dropped. 'AP' flags are from 'FPP/AP' (false positive). Control of Kasugho after the withdrawal is disputed (UPDF per civil society; Wazalendo per the local state official); both accounts are kept. The man killed is unnamed and is described only as armed, drunk and 'assimilé' to the M23.
claims.researcher_note: Two competing accounts of who held Kasugho (civil society: UPDF presence; local state official: Wazalendo) are recorded together; the outlet itself says it could not determine control. The shot man is unnamed; killing of a man described as armed, attributed to Wazalendo by local sources, confirmed by the official. Anonymous/local sourcing.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Uganda's chief of defence staff, General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, argued in an X post the previous week that the M23 rebels backed by the Rwandan army should fall back 20 km south of their positions in Lubero (Kitsombiro, Kipese, Kasugho); the outlet noted that some said the M23 was ceding place to the Ugandan army at Kasugho.
claims.place_as_written: Lubero territory (Kitsombiro, Kipese, Kasugho), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Verified on page. Cited to the outlet. 'AP' flag from 'FPP/AP' (false positive). Second-hand: the X post was not seen; Actualite.cd paraphrases it and adds that it aimed 'en vue de libérer les espaces sous influence de l'Ouganda'. Post date is only 'la semaine dernière' relative to 7 March 2025.
claims.researcher_note: Relayed in a news article; the X post itself was not opened (lead for a statement-specific search; posts may be deleted). Date range computed from 'la semaine dernière' relative to Friday 7 March 2025 (week of 24 Feb-2 Mar); exact post date unknown. Possibly already held in the Uganda statements set; check at promote.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the rebels kept control of the stretch from Kanyabayonga to Kitsombiro, a distance of nearly 100 km towards Butembo, and were still positioned at Kitsombiro, about 30 km from Lubero-centre, described as their current target.
claims.actor_as_written: Rebels (M23), as named by the source
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verified on page; statement matches; single clause from one source. In-window 'holds' snapshot (20 March 2025). The capture of Kanyabayonga dates from 2024, before the window, and is not stated here.
claims.researcher_note: Frontline snapshot, 20 Mar 2025, Actualite.cd. Kanyabayonga/Kirumba/Kayna/Alimbongo were captured BEFORE the window (Kanyabayonga, Kayna, Kirumba late June 2024 per Reuters/DW/RFI snippets; Alimbongo 17 Dec 2024 per Radio Okapi headline; Mbingi 18 Dec 2024 per Actualite.cd snippet); in-window control is recorded as 'holds'.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that the M23 also controlled gold-bearing zones such as Musigha, in the Bunyatenge area of Lubero, forcing the self-proclaimed general Kasereka Kasiyano Kabido, leader of the FPP-AP group, to rally them to 'keep his mining interests'.
claims.actor_as_written: M23; Kasereka Kasiyano Kabido (FPP-AP), as named by the source
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verified on page; attribution to local sources kept. Rests on unnamed local sources; 'de les rallier' is ambiguous and is not evidence of a formal alliance.
claims.researcher_note: Local sources, unnamed. Relevant to Bunyatenge front: Actualite.cd on 7 Mar 2025 describes Bunyatenge as FPP/AP stronghold, while this says the M23 held Musigha and Kabido rallied; r1 holds a BETO item on Kabido's arrest in Butembo 12 Jun 2025. Whether 'rallied' means an alliance with M23 is the outlet's local-source claim only.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local and security sources, that clashes between the FARDC, backed by Wazalendo fighters, and the M23 rebels, supported by Rwanda, resumed at about 4 am on 14 January in the villages of Kamandi Gite and Kibanda, about 60 km from Lubero-Centre, with heavy and light weapons heard as far as Kayna and Kirumba; that other fighting was reported a little further east in the village of Luofu and around the rural area of Kirumba; and that, per security sources, the FARDC, keeping their initial positions, were replying to M23 attacks by shelling rebel positions with artillery and combat helicopters.
claims.place_as_written: Kamandi Gite, Kibanda, Luofu, Kirumba, Kayna (Lubero), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and Wazalendo; M23 supported by Rwanda (as named by the source)
claims.verification_note: 'Heard as far as Kayna and Kirumba' was on the page next to the excerpt (replacement quote extends it contiguously); 'west of Kayna' sat in a separate paragraph and was removed; shelling clause attributed to security sources; weekday dropped. No casualty figures given. The shelling account is from security sources (the FARDC side).
claims.researcher_note: Frontline just before the Goma offensive: M23 holds Kayna/Kirumba axis from Dec 2024, FARDC 'keep their initial positions'. No casualty figures in the article. No M23 or Rwanda account found for this date.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23, reinforced by the RDF, consolidated its positions in Lubero territory in anticipation of future operations and that in mid-October 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF redeployed additional troops from Tchanzu to the Lubero front line along the Kanyabayonga-Kirumba axis, reportedly including recruits who had graduated on 1 October.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 and RDF, as named by the source
claims.verification_note: Para. 49 verified verbatim in the retained PDF; statement matches including 'reportedly'.
claims.researcher_note: Paragraph 49 of S/2025/858; footnote markers 60 and 61 appear inside the excerpt as printed. Source is the UN report cited elsewhere for other paragraphs; this passage is new. Pairs with the 'first defence zone' claim r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-005.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that sources reported on 16 September 2025 the deployment of at least 15 fully loaded trucks with AFC/M23 combatants coming from the AFC/M23-ARC training camp in Rumangabo in Kirumba, near Kanyabayonga, in Lubero territory, two days after a pass-out ceremony.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23-ARC, as named by the source
claims.verification_note: Verified verbatim in the retained PDF (followed by footnote 122). Not a duplicate of r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-002 (Uvira/Fizi item from the same report). The report's wording 'training camp in Rumangabo in Kirumba, near Kanyabayonga' is printed as is and not corrected; Rumangabo is elsewhere known as a Rutshuru location, so the phrase may be a drafting slip and the trucks' origin/destination are ambiguous.
claims.researcher_note: Wording is the report's: it places the Rumangabo camp 'in Kirumba, near Kanyabayonga', although Rumangabo is otherwise known as a Rutshuru location; the geography may be a drafting slip, so the destination of the trucks is not stated and the place is entered as printed. 'Sources' are not named. Footnote marker 122 omitted at the end of the excerpt.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that Bahati Erasto, North Kivu's AFC/M23-appointed governor, during visits to Kanyabayonga and Kirumba between 9 and 11 June, claimed that Lubero, Butembo and Beni would soon fall under AFC/M23 control.
claims.verification_note: Annex 22 passage verified verbatim in the retained PDF. A statement by an AFC/M23 official as reported by the Group.
claims.researcher_note: Annex 22 of S/2025/858 (sources: UN, intelligence sources, civil society, per footnote). Year 2025 is from the report's reporting period; the excerpt prints '9-11 June' without a year. The Ngaruye 8 September statement from the same annex is already held (r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-004). No AFC/M23 or Kinshasa reaction found to this specific remark.

claims.text: Actualite.cd, relaying MONUSCO, reported that ninety-two defendants were appearing before the Butembo garrison military tribunal sitting at Lubero-Centre, accused of several charges including sexual violence, in hearings launched on 26 June with MONUSCO support and expected to last about ten days; MONUSCO's public information section in Beni said the defendants, including 45 FARDC soldiers and 47 civilians, were prosecuted for rapes, sexual violence, abduction of children and extortion of funds, crimes committed between 2021 and 2024.
claims.actor_as_written: 45 FARDC soldiers and 47 civilians (accused), per MONUSCO as relayed
claims.verification_note: Framed as an in-window trial event, not as 2025 offences. Tribunal and Lubero-Centre were in the lead paragraph, now supplied as a contiguous replacement quote; '92' is printed in the title and in words in the excerpts. Procedural stage kept ('poursuivis', 'comparaissent' = prosecuted, appearing). A 2025 trial event: the offences are stated as committed between 2021 and 2024, before the window. Defendants are accused/prosecuted; no verdict is reported.
claims.researcher_note: The offences date from 2021-2024, before the window; the hearings (26 June 2025) are in the window and are an accountability event for sexual violence in Lubero territory, not a front incident. Perpetrator groups (soldiers and civilians) are as stated by MONUSCO; not attributed to a party. Ligue des femmes du Nord-Kivu coordinator Hélène Makule asked for exemplary sanctions.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that three displaced adults had died of hunger at Lubero-Centre in the previous month and that the displacement site in the territory office compound faced hunger, lack of access to medical care and a total lack of humanitarian assistance. Kathungu Thamweya Charline, president of the displaced in Lubero commune, told the outlet that five children had also died, that several other displaced people were bedridden in local health facilities without adequate care, and that no humanitarian aid had arrived for more than three months. The outlet said humanitarian organisations could no longer reach the area because of persistent insecurity, and that the displaced were fleeing violent clashes between the FARDC and AFC/M23 in several entities of south Lubero, some coming from areas regularly attacked by other armed groups.
claims.actor_as_written: Not attributed (conditions); clashes FARDC vs AFC/M23 cited as cause of displacement
claims.verification_note: 'Died of hunger in the previous month' and 'more than three months' were outside the stored excerpts; replacement quotes extend the excerpts contiguously. 'At the displacement site' for the children's deaths was not stated and was removed. Added the ADF access cause and mixed displacement origins the page states, for balance. The dead are unnamed. The page attributes the lack of humanitarian access mainly to ADF activity ('principalement liée à l’activisme des combattants ADF'), not to the M23 front, and says some displaced come from areas regularly attacked by the ADF and local armed groups; the ADF is named only in passages outside the stored excerpts, so it is given here as a caveat.
claims.researcher_note: Single local source (a displaced-community leader), not independently confirmed. The article also says humanitarian organisations can no longer reach the zone 'because of persistent insecurity, mainly linked to ADF activism'; the 'three months without aid' and the causes are per the source. Dead are unnamed. Links the front displacement to health-care access (no access to medical care).

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported that the Kayna health zone was affected by the Ebola epidemic with a confirmed case, a 21-year-old man from Butembo intercepted on 2 September at a checkpoint in the Itsu health area; it said this came two months after AFC-M23 had announced the end of the epidemic in the zones under its administration, and that, per the Lubero administrator Kiwewa Mitela, surveillance was reinforced in the Kayna and Kirumba health zones.
claims.place_as_written: Kayna health zone, Lubero, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Not applicable (epidemic); AFC-M23 administration named as announcing end of epidemic
claims.verification_note: All passages verified on the retained page. The figure flag '7' comes from the outlet name '7sur7.cd' (false positive). The page does not say which authority appointed Kiwewa Mitela; nothing on that is added.
claims.researcher_note: Adds the AFC-M23 'end of epidemic' announcement and the cross-front surveillance (Kinshasa-appointed administrator for zones that the M23 holds) to r1-NKS-2026Q3-010 (Enquete.cd, 3 Sep, health crisis cell of the rebel administration). Epidemic context only; 'Kayna' here is the health zone. The page title cites 'dix-septième épidémie' in its first line; strain Bundibugyo per same article.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that in the south of Lubero territory the Kayna health zone faced serious operating difficulties, and that at Kanyabayonga the Vuvogho health centre struggled to give adequate care for lack of funds; the head nurse Paluku Mupanda said its operation rested almost entirely on patients' contributions, a consequence of the absence of partners in the health sector, and the centre regularly ran out of medicines, notably for malaria.
claims.place_as_written: Vuvogho health centre, Kanyabayonga (Lubero), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: 'South Lubero' and the funding shortfall were in the lead paragraph; replacement quote extends the excerpt contiguously. Category set to health_care_access (civilian access to care), with no attack implied. Access-to-care context only: the article does not mention the M23, the front, looting or any attack.
claims.researcher_note: Health-access context in an M23-held town (Kanyabayonga) about three weeks after the late-March 2026 pull-back from nearby villages; the article does not mention M23, the front, looting or an attack, so no cause beyond 'absence of partners' is stated. Not categorised health_care_access/attack because no violence is reported.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the town of Nyabiondo in Masisi territory passed on Sunday 9 March under the occupation of the M23/AFC rebels, which it described as backed by Rwanda, after intense fighting between those rebels and the FARDC, supported by fighters of the APCLS of Janvier Kalahiri.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 against FARDC supported by APCLS
claims.verification_note: Excerpt matches the page and this event (published 9 Mar 2025). Name Janvier Kalahiri as printed; a second Radio Okapi page of 10 Mar prints 'Janvier Karairi'. Radio Okapi spells the APCLS leader 'Janvier Kalahiri' here and 'Janvier Karairi' in its 10 March article.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi 10 Mar 2025 spells the APCLS leader Janvier Kalahiri here and Janvier Karairi in a second article of the same day. Nyabiondo is the chief town of Osso-Banyungu sector (same page). Not in period packet before this claim (packet holds Nyabiondo only for 2026 and 25 Apr 2025).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that several local sources said the M23 rebels were aiming at Walikale-centre in order to reach the Bisiye deposits.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 rebels (per local sources cited by Radio Okapi)
claims.verification_note: Anonymous local sources' allegation of intent; 'M23' is carried by the page title. Spelling 'Bisiye' as printed.
claims.researcher_note: Alleged aim reported by anonymous local sources; spelling "Bisiye" as printed by Radio Okapi (Bisie mine, Alphamin). Same page says the rebels advanced without fighting to Kaanja, 6 km from Nyabiondo, on Monday 10 March.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the company Alphamin Bisie Mining (ABM) announced the immediate suspension of its mining operations from Friday 14 March because of growing risks to the safety of its staff.
claims.actor_as_written: Alphamin Bisie Mining (company communiqué as reported)
claims.verification_note: Company announcement relayed by Actualite.cd (byline Josué Mutanava, Goma); same page quotes the communiqué.
claims.researcher_note: Company statement relayed by Actualite.cd (byline Josué Mutanava, Goma). The same page says a reduced staff would remain for minimal services including the hospital.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that clashes particularly shook the locality of Kibati, where the AFC/M23 and the FARDC-wazalendo coalition fought violently over control of the village, and that, according to its sources, at the end of Thursday 13 March the belligerents shared control of Kibati, the outcome remaining uncertain.
claims.verification_note: Matches the excerpt exactly; unnamed sources, so C.
claims.researcher_note: Single local-source account in an article about the mining company; earlier than the Kibati items in the period packet (25 Apr 2025 onwards).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, in a headline, that the Kibua general hospital in Walikale territory received medicines six months after its looting by AFC/M23 rebels, and quoted its medical director, Dr Isaac Bihango, as saying the aid would help relaunch medical activity and that medical prescriptions, which had become the system of care, would now be a thing of the past.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 rebels (as stated in the headline)
claims.verification_note: Supported. Looting date not given in the body; the headline's 'six months' before 26 Sep 2025 points to about March 2025, which conflicts with 'January' in r1-HC-NK-2025-009 (Radio Okapi). Source's wording kept; looting date approximate. Looting date conflict: Actualite.cd's headline says 'six months' before 26 September 2025 (about March 2025); Radio Okapi (r1-HC-NK-2025-009) places the looting of Walikale referral hospitals in January 2025. The perpetrator attribution rests on the headline and on the outlet's narration. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Looting date is not given in the body: "six months" before 26 Sep 2025 points to about March 2025, whereas existing claim r1-HC-NK-2025-009 (Radio Okapi 2 Oct 2025) says massive looting of four Walikale referral hospitals occurred in January: flag as a date discrepancy. Attribution to AFC/M23 appears in the headline and in the sentence calling the MP's base a "victim of pillage de rebelles de l'AFC/M23".

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the Kibua general hospital released 13 people who had been blocked at the hospital for failure to pay their bills after treatment, thanks to the medicines aid received on 26 September.
claims.verification_note: Supported; the 26 September date is on the page (page-only clause).
claims.researcher_note: Cost barrier / detention of patients for unpaid bills, not conflict violence; recorded as a civilian access-to-care lead. Not attributed to any armed actor.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local civil society, that displaced people and their host families in Walikale territory received no humanitarian assistance and that for nearly four months several health structures in the region had been deprived of supplies of medicines and other essential inputs, a crisis it attributed to instability caused by the M23's occupation of several North Kivu localities.
claims.verification_note: Supported; causal sentence is the outlet's narration and the statement says so.
claims.researcher_note: The causal sentence is the outlet's own wording, not attributed to civil society. Related to existing r1-HC-NK-2025-009.

claims.text: The ICRC reported, in a press release on access to health care in the Kivus, that a man identified as Shukuru said he was wounded at Pinga in July in Walikale territory and was evacuated to Beni for care, at the Beni general referral hospital about 300 km from where he was wounded.
claims.verification_note: Removed the inferred year '(2025)': the quote does not print it (release dated 7 Oct 2025). The release's pseudonym footnote ('[1] Prénom d’emprunt') marks 'docteur Pierre', not Shukuru. The year of the July injury is inferred from the release date (7 October 2025); the quote says only 'July'.
claims.researcher_note: Year of the July injury is inferred from the 2025 release ("Depuis le début de l’année"); the excerpt does not print the year. The name "Shukuru" is given as a first name only and the release does not say whether it is a pseudonym. Weapon type and perpetrator not stated.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to the same anonymous local human rights organisation and administrative sources, the Katoyi sector office was reportedly vandalised and looted at the beginning of April by Kigingi's militiamen.
claims.verification_note: Restored the source's conditional ('aurait même été vandalisé et pillé').
claims.researcher_note: Conditional ("aurait") and anonymous source; date is "early April" (month precision).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, in a memorandum addressed on Friday 17 October to the military and civil authorities of North Kivu, notables of the Bahunde chiefdom and Osso-Banyungu sector in Masisi territory accused three Wazalendo factions, the UPDC of Noah Maachano and PARECO-FF factions commanded by Kigingi Jean de Dieu and Mutayomba Jam's, of abuses against civilians, listing disrespect for customary authority, illegal taxes on goods and illegal exploitation of some mining sites.
claims.place_as_written: Ufamandu 1er (Bahunde chiefdom) and Nyamaboko 1er groupement, Osso-Banyungu sector, Masisi
claims.actor_as_written: UPDC (Noah Maachano); PARECO-FF factions of Kigingi Jean de Dieu and Mutayomba Jam’s
claims.verification_note: Dropped 'systematic' (the page's 'exactions systématiques' is in a conditional sentence, not the accusation itself); the page prints the name with a typographic apostrophe, 'Mutayomba Jam’s'.
claims.researcher_note: Notables' memorandum relayed by Radio Okapi; no response of the named groups found. Three excerpts of one page. Financial extortion at roadblocks (1,000 to over 2,000 Congolese francs) also described on the page.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that men of Corneille Nangaa and Sultani Makenga (AFC/M23) attacked from the morning the positions of the Wazalendo of the ANCDH at Kalungu, after reinforcing their troops in men and equipment during the past week; the article places the fighting on the Tuesday and is dated Wednesday 9 July.
claims.place_as_written: Kalungu and Kinyana, Bashali Mokoto groupement, Masisi
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (men of Corneille Nangaa and Sultani Makenga per the source) against Nyatura Wazalendo of the ANCDH led by Jean-Marie Bonané
claims.verification_note: Supported; AFC/M23 and the 9 July date are on the page outside the stored excerpt. Date 8 Jul computed from 'mardi': approximate.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ("mardi") and the 9 July publication date. ANCDH is "Alliance des nationalistes congolais pour la défense des droits humains" (same page, led by Jean-Marie Bonané). Existing claim r1-NKW-2025H2-013 mentions the ANCDH for November only.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that AFC/M23 rebels temporarily dislodged Nyatura fighters from Bupfuhi, a locality that was said to have been burned.
claims.verification_note: Conditional kept; no arsonist named. Date computed from 'mardi': approximate.
claims.researcher_note: Conditional ("aurait été incendiée"); the source does not say who burned it. Date computed from "mardi".

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local notables, that between 5 a.m. and 8 a.m. AFC-M23 fought the Wazalendo of the ANCDH of Jean-Marie Bonane on the hills overlooking the villages concerned, and that residents of Kinyana, Nyabikeri, Rwankeri and Bibwe were seen with their luggage moving towards Bulende, Kasopo and Lukweti.
claims.place_as_written: Kinyana, Nyabikeri, Rwankeri, Bibwe; Bashali Mokoto, Masisi
claims.verification_note: Supported; spelling 'Bonane' as printed on this page.
claims.researcher_note: The page spells the leader "Jean-Marie Bonane" here and "Bonané" in the 9 July article. Date 21 Oct 2025 is the publication date ("ce mardi").

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the day before, attacks by Wazalendo on the town of Nyabiondo in Masisi caused the death of a child and injured four other people.
claims.verification_note: Removed the computed date from the statement; 'la veille' relative to the 21 Oct 2025 article, so the 20 Oct date field is approximate. Child unnamed.
claims.researcher_note: Child victim unnamed in the source. "La veille" is relative to the 21 Oct 2025 article. Wazalendo faction not specified. Child unnamed in the source (not listed in victims_named).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that in a communiqué made public on Monday the AFC-M23 accused the Congolese army of using heavy artillery and drones against its positions from 3 a.m. until late in the evening.
claims.verification_note: Party statement as relayed by Radio Okapi; communiqué not seen. The Monday (27 Oct) communiqué sits awkwardly with fighting 'la veille' (28 Oct) of the 29 Oct article: date approximate, discrepancy noted. Radio Okapi dates the communiqué to 'lundi' but places the main fighting 'la veille' of its Wednesday 29 October article; the day is unresolved.
claims.researcher_note: Cited only for what AFC-M23 said. Date computed from the weekday ("lundi") in an article of Wed 29 Oct that places the fighting on "la veille" (28 Oct); Actualite.cd Facebook snippet also says Tuesday 28 October. Day discrepancy to be resolved. The communiqué itself was not found.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that other sources indicated that, after the fighting at Kibati, the Wazalendo reportedly withdrew to Mikumbi and Miba, 3 km further west, leaving the area in the hands of the AFC/M23 rebels.
claims.place_as_written: Kibati, Mikumbi, Miba; Luberike groupement, Walikale
claims.verification_note: Restored the conditional ('se seraient repliés').
claims.researcher_note: Competing account ("d'autres sources") with no casualty figures ("Aucun bilan"). Later Kibati items in the packet: 10 and 18 Sep 2026.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that the shooting at Kibati had stopped after a day of fighting reported on Thursday in the area, and that the FARDC and wazalendo maintained their presence in the centre of Kibati while the AFC/M23 rebels controlled the hills overlooking the town.
claims.verification_note: Removed the weekday-computed '(10 September 2026)'.
claims.researcher_note: Between existing claims r1-NKW-2026H2-012 (10 Sep) and -013 (18 Sep, centre of Kibati back under AFC/M23 control). Same page: traffic suspended on the Kashebere-Mungazi road.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing civilian and military sources, that on the morning of Monday 28 September two positions held by wazalendo fighters at Kaleta and Bitoyi, in the Ufamandu groupements of Masisi territory, were targeted at about 7 a.m. by air strikes attributed to the AFC/M23 rebels.
claims.place_as_written: Kaleta and Bitoyi, Ufamandu groupements, Masisi
claims.verification_note: Supported; attribution kept.
claims.researcher_note: Drone use (conditional) and the absence of any toll are stated elsewhere on the page. Journal de Kinshasa carries the same report. AFC/M23 account: none found.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that at Burungu, in the Bashali chiefdom, at least eight civilians were reportedly killed and six others wounded on Saturday evening, a toll that could not be independently confirmed at the time of publication.
claims.verification_note: Figures printed as words; unconfirmed; no perpetrator given. Date computed from 'samedi soir': approximate.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from "samedi soir" and the Monday 28 Sep 2026 publication date. Context: fighting around Miko near Remeka on 26 and 27 Sep. No perpetrator given. Burungu not in period packet.

claims.text: Journal de Kinshasa reported, citing local and military sources, that for the first time since the start of fighting in the area the town of Pinga in Walikale territory was targeted on Monday 28 September 2026 by an attack attributed to the AFC/M23, drones targeting FARDC positions and causing panic and a temporary suspension of activities in the town.
claims.verification_note: Supported; single outlet (byline Cyntiche PANDI; photo credit Média Congo).
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet; photo credit "Média Congo" on the page (not stated as the text source). The page says no official toll was available. A YouTube snippet (not opened) claims at least 5 Republican Guard soldiers were killed in a drone strike on 28 Sept at Pinga: unverified, listed in gaps. Radio Okapi item of 28 Sep covers Masisi strikes only.

claims.text: Journal de Kinshasa reported that the attack on Pinga came only 24 hours after the FARDC, supported by wazalendo, retook several positions around Mindjendje, notably Tchad, Kahongoboka, Kukibingu, Bubolwa and Luola.
claims.place_as_written: Mindjendje area: Tchad, Kahongoboka, Kukibingu, Bubolwa, Luola; Walikale
claims.verification_note: Supported; date derived from '24 heures': approximate; from whom retaken not stated.
claims.researcher_note: Date derived from "24 hours before" the 28 Sep attack (approximate). Retaken from whom is not stated in the excerpt; later Actualite.cd/Congo Quotidien items (27 Oct 2026) report renewed FARDC-FRN fighting at Luola and the Tchad hill.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting began on Saturday 24 October when the army and wazalendo attacked the positions of the FRN rebels on the Rushihe hill overlooking Katobo (Banamulindwa, Kisimba groupement, Walikale), and that the government coalition dislodged the rebels and took control of the position.
claims.place_as_written: Rushihe hill, Katobo, Banamulindwa locality, Kisimba groupement, Walikale
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC supported by wazalendo against FRN rebels
claims.verification_note: Supported; FRN is not expanded on the page.
claims.researcher_note: "FRN" is not expanded on the page; this is not AFC/M23. Existing claim r1-ATR-NK-2026-007 records M23 retaking Katobo on 26 May 2026. Check unit roster for FRN.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the Rubaya mining zone, rich in coltan, cassiterite, gold and tourmaline, remained under the control of the M23 rebels.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date '4 March 2026' from the statement (shown with the source).
claims.researcher_note: Holds-status for the frontline layer; the page adds that the M23 is "soutenu par le Rwanda selon plusieurs rapports des autorités congolaises et des experts onusiens" (outside the stored excerpt). The Amnesty 21 Sep 2026 briefing also describes Rubaya as M23-controlled.

claims.text: KT Press (Rwanda) reported that Katoyi (Gatoyi) has changed hands repeatedly since late 2025: AFC-M23 captured it in November 2025, FARDC and PARECO-Wazalendo forces retook it in December, and further fighting returned control to AFC-M23 around February and March 2026.
claims.verification_note: Rwandan state-aligned outlet: partisan, usable only as 'KT Press says'. KT Press is a Rwandan state-aligned outlet; its account is recorded as the outlet's claim only.
claims.researcher_note: Rwanda-aligned outlet: usable as "KT Press says". Existing claim r1-NKS-2026Q4-010 has Radio Okapi on the FARDC-Wazalendo retaking Katoyi centre on 6 Oct 2026. The page presents the Aug 2026 advance as targeting the FDLR (pro-AFC-M23 sources); other local reporting calls it clashes with FARDC-Wazalendo.

claims.text: KT Press (Rwanda) reported that by 24-25 August 2026 the AFC-M23-appointed administrator of Masisi had visited Remeka, taken part in community work and launched maintenance of the Ngungu-Remeka road, and had urged remaining Wazalendo fighters to join AFC-M23.
claims.verification_note: Partisan outlet; administrator unnamed on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan, Rwanda-aligned outlet; the administrator is not named on the page. Complements existing r1-NKW-2026H2-006 (Remeka retaken 20 Aug).

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post, relaying MSF, reported that MSF had documented many cases of sexual violence against women, girls and children in eastern DRC since early January 2025, and had collected testimonies in Goma, Sake, Rutshuru and Masisi, in which victims said they were forced at gunpoint.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (armed men)
claims.verification_note: KMP relays MSF (originating source). The page prints 'Ruthsuru' (typo for Rutshuru). Relay of MSF; not independent of other MSF-sourced claims (e.g. r1-SV-NK-2025-009). The page spells the place 'Ruthsuru'. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: MSF itself (not fetched) is the originating source; KMP is a relay. Excerpts are two sentences of the same page. South Kivu figure (more than 700 victims treated by MSF since the start of 2025) is on the page but outside the excerpts. Page does not date the underlying MSF release (30 Jul 2025 is the KMP URL date). Relates to existing r1-SV-NK-2025-009 (MSF, 7,400 victims Jan-Apr).

claims.text: Amnesty International reported that one interviewee said he could hear the screams of detainees being tortured inside the shipping containers that M23 uses as detention cells near the Rubaya mine.
claims.verification_note: Narrowed to the new element: the container cells themselves are already in verified r2-G-UNDOCS-012 (same Amnesty page). Amnesty's finding from an interviewee's account; date is the briefing date. Same Amnesty briefing as r2-G-UNDOCS-012 (container cells, ndake); neither M23 nor Rwanda responded to Amnesty.
claims.researcher_note: Documented investigation by a major NGO, but the interview was anonymous (names changed); date of the detentions is not given, so date is the briefing date (reported 2026-09-21). Amnesty states that neither M23 nor Rwandan government officials responded to its request for comment. Complements existing r1-ATR-NK-2026-019/-020 (killings; ndake pit).

claims.text: Amnesty International reported that seven miners recounted how M23 detained miners and threatened to send them to M23 military training centres if they failed to pay ransoms for their release.
claims.place_as_written: Rubaya (North Kivu) and Lomera (South Kivu) mining sites
claims.verification_note: Supported verbatim; a threat, not a confirmed enlistment. Same Amnesty briefing as r2-G-UNDOCS-011..014 (not independent of it).
claims.researcher_note: The English release says "seven miners"; the French full report ties it to Lomera and Rubaya. Date precision: briefing date (reported 2026-09-21). Not a confirmed case of forced enlistment: the threat is of being sent to training centres.

claims.text: Amnesty International reported that, in Rubaya, miners said Rwandans play a dual role as civilian miners or mineshaft managers but also take part in hostilities when needed alongside M23 fighters.
claims.actor_as_written: Rwandans present at Rubaya (per miners), alongside M23
claims.verification_note: Miners' accounts reported by Amnesty; graded as r2-G-UNDOCS-014 (same briefing). Rwanda: Amnesty says no response.
claims.researcher_note: Testimony of unnamed miners summarised by Amnesty; Rwandan government response: Amnesty says none received. Rwanda account: no statement found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting broke out on Sunday after an attack on AFC/M23 rebels in the village of Bangwi, where intense clashes lasted all day, causing mass displacement of the population towards Swima and Mboko.
claims.place_as_written: Makobola, Bangwi, Swima (Fizi/Uvira territories), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (attacked, per Actualite.cd's sources; attacker not named in the passage)
claims.verification_note: Narrowed to the excerpt: the Monday marine-unit clause is claim 1; names not printed in the excerpt (FARDC, wazalendo, M'massa Etùba) removed from entities_named; date narrowed to the Sunday. 'Dimanche' in an article dated Monday 22 Dec 2025 is read as 21 Dec 2025. Kivutimes (separate claim) dates the start to 'samedi 21 décembre 2025' (21 Dec 2025 was a Sunday) and says the FARDC launched the offensive on Bangwi.
claims.researcher_note: Date: article published Mon 22 Dec 2025; 'dimanche' = 21 Dec 2025 (date computed from weekday and publication date). Kivutimes (separate claim) says the fighting began 'samedi 21 décembre 2025' (21 Dec 2025 was a Sunday): weekday/date mismatch in that outlet. Marine-unit detail is in a separate claim.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that the AFC/M23 had deployed a marine unit on Lake Tanganyika that took part in the fighting at Makobola and its surroundings.
claims.place_as_written: Makobola, Lake Tanganyika, Fizi/Uvira territories, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 'marins' (marine unit), as Actualite.cd's sources describe it
claims.verification_note: Excerpt says 'les rebelles'; the AFC/M23 attribution and Makobola are in the title and the next sentence of the page. AFC/M23 is printed in the title. Single outlet citing unnamed sources. Kivutimes (23 Dec 2025) says only that the rebels used a speedboat ('hors-bord') to shell the area.
claims.researcher_note: Single-source claim about a lake-borne unit; Kivutimes (23 Dec 2025) says only that the rebels used a speedboat ('hors-bord') to shell the area.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, despite FARDC reinforcements sent to the wazalendo from Kalemie, the town of Mboko, located 55 km north of Baraka, remained under the control of AFC-M23 fighters.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and says what the statement says; the conflict with Kivutimes is surfaced, not resolved. CONTESTED, unresolved: Kivutimes (23 Dec 2025, separate claim) says Mboko 'reste sous la menace directe' of AFC-M23 fighters, i.e. threatened, not held. The two accounts are kept side by side.
claims.researcher_note: CONFLICT: Kivutimes, 23 Dec 2025 (separate claim), says Mboko 'reste sous la menace directe' of AFC-M23 fighters, i.e. threatened not held. Radio Okapi 15 Dec 2025 reports AFC/M23 occupied 'Makobola 2'. Control of Mboko is unresolved; treat as contested/unverified.

claims.text: Kivutimes reported that violent fighting had opposed AFC-M23 rebels and the FARDC, supported by Wazalendo, around Makobola since 'samedi 21 décembre 2025', and that, per the outlet, military authorities had not yet communicated an official casualty toll while families fled explosive devices.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact; quoted date kept as printed. Kivutimes prints 'samedi 21 décembre 2025'; 21 Dec 2025 was a Sunday (Actualite.cd says the fighting began 'dimanche'). The weekday/date mismatch is the outlet's and is left as printed. Kivutimes attributes Rwandan support to AFC-M23 to 'les acteurs internationaux' only.
claims.researcher_note: Kivutimes (Uvira-based local outlet) calls 21 Dec 2025 a Saturday; it was a Sunday. Actualite.cd says fighting began 'dimanche'. Date range kept. Kivutimes attributes Rwandan-force support to 'international actors' only.

claims.text: Kivutimes reported that the town of Mboko, about 55 km north of Baraka, remained under the direct threat of AFC-M23 fighters, who were maintaining pressure on that axis.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and matches the statement. CONTESTED, unresolved: Actualite.cd (22 Dec 2025, separate claim) says Mboko 'reste toujours sous contrôle' of AFC-M23 fighters. The two accounts are kept side by side.
claims.researcher_note: Contradicts the Actualite.cd 22 Dec 2025 line that Mboko 'reste sous contrôle' of AFC-M23.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that violent fighting broke out on Friday around Minembwe between Twirwaneho fighters allied to AFC-M23 and Wazalendo militiamen integrated into the Congolese army, and that the Wazalendo Biloze Bishambuke (FABB) of General Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito said they were continuing to defend their positions.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe; Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma, Kwasabuni (high plateaux), Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho/AFC-M23; Wazalendo (FABB, General Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito)
claims.verification_note: The spokesperson's allegation is split out to claim 6 so it is not merged into the outlet's narration; the date number is left to the date field (not in any excerpt); 'AFC-M23' is not printed in that form in an excerpt, removed from entities_named. The date (21 Nov 2025) is in the article's lede. The Wazalendo spokesperson's allegation that 'AFC Twirwaneho M23' attacked Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma and Kwasabuni is a party statement (claim 6). No Twirwaneho or AFC-M23 account found.
claims.researcher_note: Wazalendo account only; no Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 account found on this date (see gaps). Roster lead: FABB, Gen. Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito (Biloze Bishambuke).

claims.text: A Wazalendo spokesperson told Kivu Morning Post that the AFC Twirwaneho M23 attacked Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma and Kwasabuni, on the high plateaux south of Minembwe, on the morning of Friday 21 November 2025, in violation of the Doha framework agreement.
claims.place_as_written: Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma, Kwasabuni (south of Minembwe), Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (unnamed spokesperson) accusing AFC Twirwaneho M23
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; the date is in the article's lede, the weekday in the quote. Party statement: cite only as 'a Wazalendo spokesperson said'. The 'violation of the Doha framework agreement' is the spokesperson's characterisation. No Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 response found (see gaps).
claims.researcher_note: Partisan statement; cite only as 'Wazalendo says'.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, over the weekend, AFC/M23 rebels occupied the localities of Kipupu (Mwenga territory) and Makobola 2 (Fizi territory), a few days after the taking of Uvira.
claims.place_as_written: Kipupu (Mwenga territory); Makobola 2 (Fizi territory), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: The '15 December 2025' anchor is not printed in the excerpt; moved to the date field and the note. 'Ce weekend' in an article dated Monday 15 Dec 2025 is read as 13-14 Dec 2025 (computed, not printed). SOS Médias Burundi (Oct 2025, claim 19) lists Kipupu among places in Fizi territory; Radio Okapi places it in Mwenga territory.
claims.researcher_note: Published Mon 15 Dec 2025: 'ce weekend' = 13-14 Dec (date computed from weekday and publication date). Complements Actualite.cd 22 Dec fighting at Makobola.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Badibanga Kalonji, called on the international community, in particular the United States, to compel Rwanda to withdraw the troops that, he said, support the AFC-M23 rebels, and said 'all batteries are being put in motion' to reconquer the territories already in rebel hands.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact; the statement's attribution ('he said') matches Radio Okapi's reported speech. Official (territorial administration) statement, reported by Radio Okapi. Name printed 'Samy Badibanga Kalonji' here; other outlets may print other orders/spellings.
claims.researcher_note: Name variant in packet: 'Samy Kalonji Badibanga' / 'Sammy Kalonji Badibanga'; here printed 'Samy Badibanga Kalonji'.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported, citing residents, that a Congolese government war plane carried out strikes on Monday in the Minembwe area, controlled by Twirwaneho fighters in South Kivu.
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; the resident's name is not printed in the excerpt, so it is removed from entities_named and figures. Kinyarwanda original; translation checked ('ingabo za leta' = government forces; 'nk'uko abahatuye babivuga' = according to residents). 'Ku wa mbere' (Monday) in an article dated 11 Mar 2025 is read as 10 Mar 2025. A resident quoted on the page told BBC he knew of no one killed but had heard of injuries elsewhere.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('ku wa mbere' = Monday) and publication 11 March 2025 -> 10 March 2025. Q1 item (another agent deepens SKS-2025Q1); added because the Kinyarwanda BBC page was not in the packet. Same page also gives Twirwaneho and pro-government accounts (separate claims).

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Twirwaneho group said these air strikes also targeted Kiziba hill, on which the main hospital in Minembwe stands, as well as the University Eben-Ezer Minembwe (UEMI), two secondary schools and the Methodist church.
claims.place_as_written: Kiziba hill, Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Congolese government aircraft, as alleged by Twirwaneho
claims.verification_note: 'hit' narrowed to 'targeted' to match 'byibasiye' and the hill-hospital relation kept as the source states it. Party statement (Twirwaneho). Translation checked: 'byibasiye' = targeted/attacked; 'umusozi wa Kiziba uriho ibitaro bikuru' = Kiziba hill, on which the main hospital stands.
