claims.researcher_note: DISCREPANCY: a second Radio Okapi item of 13 Mar 2026 (https://www.radiookapi.net/2026/03/13/actualite/securite/plus-de-6-000-violations-des-droits-de-lhomme-documentees-en-2025-en) reports BCNUDH annual report 'violences sexuelles liées au conflit ont augmenté de 59 %, avec 1 479 victimes'; the figures 1,534 and 1,479 differ (possibly different scope or date of data). Do not merge. Nationwide totals.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH report on November 2025 recorded 91 victims of conflict-related sexual violence in one month, mostly women and girls, an increase of 28 per cent in thirty days, with North Kivu and South Kivu remaining the epicentres.
claims.place_as_written: Democratic Republic of the Congo; North Kivu and South Kivu named as epicentres
claims.actor_as_written: armed groups (M23, Wazalendo, ADF) and state agents per the monthly report overall
claims.verification_note: Removed '20 January 2026' (no stored excerpt prints it; the year is not printed with the date); rest verbatim. Countrywide count; the article does not give a Kivu-only figure. It uses '28 per cent' both for overall violations versus October and for sexual violence, so the sexual-violence rise may be misreported. The page says the report was published on Tuesday 20 January.
claims.researcher_note: Headline figure for the same report: 542 violations in November 2025 (title says 'plus de 500').

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH monthly report for May 2026 counted 59 victims of conflict-related sexual violence, mostly women and girls, and that state actors, mainly FARDC soldiers, were designated as first responsible for nearly half of these abuses, ahead of armed groups.
claims.place_as_written: Democratic Republic of the Congo (80 per cent of violations in Ituri and the two Kivus)
claims.actor_as_written: state actors, mainly FARDC soldiers; armed groups
claims.verification_note: Removed 'released on 24 July 2026' ('24' not in a stored excerpt); rest verbatim; inconsistency stated in note. The article is internally inconsistent: its headline and first sentence give 'plus de 1200' violations including '59 cas de violence sexuelle', while later it gives 481 violations affecting nearly 1,200 people, and 59 victims (not cases) of sexual violence. Both versions are kept as printed, not merged. Countrywide; the Kivus are not separated for sexual violence. Report released 24 July 2026 per the page.
claims.researcher_note: Same article gives 'plus de 1200' violations in its first sentence but '481 violations ... près de 1 200 personnes' later: internal inconsistency in the Radio Okapi text (violations vs victims); not used. Countrywide; the Kivus are not separated for sexual violence.

claims.text: UN News (Kiswahili), relaying Radio Okapi, reported that the DRC government announced a phased plan to restore State authority in Uvira after the departure of AFC/M23 fighters, and that a government spokesperson called the M23 departure a "short-lived event" and said the only acceptable outcome was full, effective and unconditional withdrawal of AFC/M23 and the Rwandan army from the whole DRC.
claims.verification_note: Removed 'on 20 January 2026' from the statement ('20' not in the stored excerpt; date field carries it). Plan and Radio Okapi clauses are on the page, not in the stored excerpt. Grade B: one credible relay of a party's statement. Partisan statement: this records what the DRC government said, not a finding. The spokesperson is not named on the page. The page also reports the government saying the withdrawal was accompanied by repeated looting and denying forced transfers of civilians (statement of Monday 19 January). English is a translation of the Swahili.
claims.researcher_note: Spokesperson not named in the page. The page also says the government (statement of Monday 19 January) denied claims of forced transfer of civilians, notably Banyamulenge, and said the departing group forced some people to leave Uvira; and that the government said the withdrawal was accompanied by repeated looting. Plan details (statement date 19-20 January) taken from the first paragraph; check against existing ST-DRC claims for duplicates.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported from Uvira, citing several consistent accounts, that elements believed to be affiliated with the Wazalendo militia, supported by some civilians, ransacked homes, businesses and places of worship belonging to the Banyamulenge community in various neighbourhoods of the city; it named among the victims a resident, Sifa, whose two-story house was reportedly completely looted before being destroyed.
claims.actor_as_written: elements believed to be affiliated with the Wazalendo militia (SOS Médias Burundi)
claims.verification_note: Removed '20 January 2026' (no excerpt prints it; dateline reads 19 January). Downgraded to C: one local outlet, attribution hedged. Attribution to Wazalendo is SOS Médias Burundi's ('elements believed to be affiliated'); single local outlet.
claims.researcher_note: Adds Banyamulenge-specific detail to existing r1-UV-2026Q1-023 (SOS pillage 18-20 Jan). Article datelined Uvira 19 January 2026. HRW 20 Jan 2026 independently documents looting of a Banyamulenge Methodist church (separate claim).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported (dateline Bukavu) that the burial in Uvira of Colonel Patrick Gisore, of the Banyamulenge community, and his wife Yvonne Nyamahoro, who died in a military plane crash in Kisangani, turned violent on a Monday; according to several witnesses armed elements claiming to be Wazalendo interrupted the ceremony and intercepted the funeral procession in Kilomoni, while other members of the Banyamulenge community were arrested in Mulongwe or forcibly locked inside a church; local sources said some assailants fired live ammunition at people outside the church and looting took place. Human Rights Watch separately said that since August 25 Wazalendo fighters had prevented the funeral of an army colonel from the Banyamulenge community and his wife for several days and robbed people there.
claims.place_as_written: Kilomoni and Mulongwe, Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed elements claiming to be Wazalendo (SOS Médias Burundi); Wazalendo fighters (HRW)
claims.verification_note: Dateline gives no date ('Bukavu' only); 25 August comes from HRW, so the date is attributed to HRW. Passive 'were arrested' kept passive. Two independent origins (SOS, HRW).
claims.researcher_note: Date from dateline 25 August 2025 and 'Monday' (25 Aug 2025 is a Monday); HRW gives 25 August. SOS says the Bukavu dateline; SOS says Kisangani crash 16 August. Two independent sources (local monitor and HRW). SOS also names a witness-reported car looting of Alexis Rukatura (not in a cited excerpt, so not listed).

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that on 6 September 2025 the Congolese army spokesperson, Gen. Sylvain Ekenge, said at a news conference: 'We don't control the Wazalendo, the Wazalendo are not part of the armed forces', and that it was not the army's job to 'manage' them.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on HRW page; official statement relayed by HRW. Place of the news conference not stated by HRW; 'Kinshasa' in the location field is not sourced.
claims.researcher_note: Relayed by HRW; the original press conference not opened. HRW says it is reported at a news conference without place; location is not stated by HRW.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that in Burundi on 8 September 2025 police and ruling-party youths detained hundreds of Congolese refugees and asylum seekers, according to several witnesses and media reports, giving them the 'choice' of going to an official camp or returning to Congo, which about 80 people did.
claims.place_as_written: Burundi (refugees from the Uvira area; place within Burundi not stated)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on HRW page; HRW cites witnesses and media reports; Burundi geography kept as border context.
claims.researcher_note: Outside Phase 1 geography (Burundi) but concerns refugees from Uvira border flows; keep as border context. Burundian government response not found.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that on 5 September 2025 Wazalendo fighters fired small arms and artillery within Uvira, killing an 8-year-old boy when a shell struck his house.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on HRW page. Discrepancy: SOS Médias Burundi (existing r1-UV-2025Q3-019) reports a 5-year-old child killed in an explosion in Uvira on the night of 6-7 September; HRW reports an 8-year-old boy killed by a shell on 5 September. Ages and dates differ; kept separate, not merged.
claims.researcher_note: Possible discrepancy with existing r1-UV-2025Q3-019 (SOS Médias Burundi: a 5-year-old child died in an explosion during the night of 6 to 7 September in Uvira): different date and age; may be different incidents or the same incident reported differently. Not merged.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition, dateline Bujumbura) reported that at a session of Burundi's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Bujumbura, Foreign Minister Édouard Bizimana announced that the Burundi-Congo border would remain closed until further notice, insisted that the M23 was lying when it claimed to be withdrawing from the city of Uvira, and said this apparent withdrawal hid a strategy of regrouping its fighters.
claims.verification_note: Swahili translation verified ('alisisitiza kuwa M23 inadanganya' = insisted M23 is lying; 'unaficha mkakati wa kuwakusanya tena wapiganaji wake' = hides a strategy of regrouping its fighters). The regrouping clause was not in the stored excerpt: added from page. Dateline '2' supplied by replacement quote. C: single outlet relaying a party statement. Partisan statement (Government of Burundi), reported by one outlet; recorded as what the minister said. Translation from Swahili checked.
claims.researcher_note: Swahili edition of an SOS Médias Burundi article (page dated 6 Feb 2026, dateline 2 Feb 2026). The border reopened 23 February 2026 (existing Radio Okapi claim r1-UV-2026Q1-051). Complements existing Bizimana statements r1-ST-BI-012/013.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (in Swahili) reported that the South Kivu governor, Jean-Jacques Purusi, had assured Uvira residents after crossing the border that the Burundi-Congo border would reopen within two to three days, by 30 January 2026 at the latest.
claims.verification_note: Swahili translation checked and accurate; partisan (provincial government) statement attributed. Purusi's statement is reported second-hand by SOS Médias Burundi. The article (dateline 2 February) places it 'last Friday' (Ijumaa iliyopita), yet gives 30 January as the latest reopening date: the source is internally inconsistent; month precision used.
claims.researcher_note: The article is dated 2 Feb 2026 and says 'last Friday' (30 Jan 2026) yet says the border would reopen by 30 January: internal inconsistency in the source; month precision used. Single local source.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch said it documented widespread looting, following the M23's withdrawal from Uvira, of homes, shops, churches and public buildings, including those belonging to the Banyamulenge, through witness accounts and verified photographs and videos, and that it geolocated videos showing unidentified people in civilian clothes looting the city courthouse, a Methodist church used by the Banyamulenge community, a restaurant, a government office building and the city's port of Kalundu.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city (including Kalundu port), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: The 'after the M23 withdrew' link sits in the preceding HRW sentence, now quoted; documented NGO investigation (A). Flag '23' is from 'M23'. HRW does not identify the looters in the geolocated videos beyond 'unidentified people in civilian clothes'. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: widespread looting following the M23's withdrawal 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-034: Re-read the retained HRW page: the preceding sentence names the M23, not an unspecified 'armed group' ('Human Rights Watch documented widespread looting, following the M23's withdrawal, of homes, shops...'). Amended to HRW's own wording; looters stay 'unidentified people in civilian clothes'.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): widespread looting following the M23's withdrawal
claims.researcher_note: HRW documented the looting 'following the M23's withdrawal'; the news release is dated 20 January 2026 (M23 left 17-18 January per other claims).

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that Congolese Defence Minister Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita told it in a meeting on 20 January 2026 that 'the Banyamulenge should not be forcibly displaced or deported, and should feel free to return to Uvira if they wish to do so'.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on HRW page. Official statement as relayed by HRW; location of the meeting not stated by HRW.
claims.researcher_note: Reported by HRW; no separate government communiqué opened.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported (dateline Cibitoke) that on Friday morning, around 10:00, a 12-year-old boy was injured in Rugombo, Burundi, by shrapnel, and that residents of the Congolese towns of Katogota, Lubarika, Luvungi and Kamanyola, across the border from Burundi, were also living under fire, with several shells having killed civilians in their homes in recent days.
claims.place_as_written: Rugombo, Cibitoke (Burundi); Katogota, Lubarika, Luvungi, Kamanyola (Uvira/Walungu border area, South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Dateline '5' supplied by replacement quote; otherwise verbatim. The source does not say who fired the shells.
claims.researcher_note: Spillover onto Burundian territory during the Ruzizi-plain offensive that preceded the Uvira capture. The page dated 7 Dec; dateline 5 Dec 2025 (a Friday). Burundian local authorities said the situation was 'under control'. The boy is unnamed.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that DRC Human Rights Minister Samuel Mbemba presented an official report on 7 April according to which more than 14 400 women were victims of rape during the period of occupation, sexual violence the report says was recorded in different localities of Uvira and its surroundings.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC (figures concern the AFC/M23-RDF occupation period)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints '7 avril' without year: removed '2026' from the statement (source date shows it). Locality clause added from page. Same origin as the Radio Okapi claim. DRC government figure (partisan), methodology not described; same origin as the existing Radio Okapi claim of 7 April 2026 (one origin, not independent corroboration). Far above other counts (e.g. HRW's documented cases).
claims.researcher_note: Government figure, partisan and unverified; the methodology is not described. The same page also gives 300,000 displaced (not cited here). Corroborates Radio Okapi 7 April 2026 already cited (same origin: the minister's report). Compare HRW (8 rape cases documented) and other counts (UFMP 183 in December, health actors 1,100+ in 3 months) for the discrepancy register.

claims.text: In a press release on the health crisis in the Uvira region, the WHO reported that forty health structures had been attacked or pillaged, causing the loss of equipment, the destruction of medicine stocks and the temporary flight of health workers, and that the general referral hospitals of Uvira, Fizi and Baraka were operating in permanent overload.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira and surrounding health zones (Uvira, Fizi, Baraka)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date (shown with the source). 'Around Uvira' narrowed to the page's framing (crisis in the Uvira region). Hospital overload clause placed with a page passage. WHO gives no dates, places or perpetrators for the forty attacks or pillages; the figure is WHO's count for the crisis since the end of 2025 and is not comparable with OCHA's 'more than eight' for the Ruzizi and Uvira health zones. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Source gives no date or perpetrator for the attacks; the period is the crisis since end of 2025. Overlaps with OCHA 'more than eight structures pillaged in Ruzizi and Uvira health zones' (separate claim); figures differ by scope.

claims.text: Actualite.cd, summarising an OCHA overview of the security and humanitarian situation in South Kivu for December 2025, reported that health sources said more than eight health structures had been pillaged in the Ruzizi and Uvira health zones, drastically or even totally reducing their operational capacity.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; year 2025 placed with the page's period sentence. Origin is OCHA, relayed by Actualite.cd; original OCHA document not opened. OCHA's overview relays unnamed health sources; no perpetrator, dates or names of facilities are given. The headline's 44,600 people are displaced and returnees counted by ACTED, not victims of the looting.
claims.researcher_note: The headline's 44,600 figure is about displaced/returned people (ACTED assessment), not victims of looting. Original OCHA document not opened.

claims.text: The ICRC reported that its teams and those of the Red Cross of the DRC had received many evacuation requests for dozens of wounded people stuck notably south of Uvira city and on the highlands of Fizi territory; François Moreillon, head of the ICRC delegation in the DRC, said its emergency surgical team that came to Fizi from Uvira had to travel six days by road when the trip could have taken three hours on the lake, and that the lack of access forced this detour.
claims.place_as_written: South of Uvira city, Fizi highlands; Uvira to Fizi route
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact. Removed the publication date. The six-day detour is Moreillon's quoted statement, so it is now attributed to him; role placed with the page passage. The release does not say who blocked access or why the lake route was unavailable. François Moreillon is the ICRC's head of delegation, quoted as a speaker, not a victim. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Press release concerns mainly Fizi hospital; Uvira-relevant points only. Second excerpt (same page) supports the six-day detour.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that four people had died of cholera out of 182 cases recorded in recent days in the Ruzizi health zone, Uvira territory, that the zone's head nurse (infirmier titulaire) acknowledged the teams were limited in supplies to fight the disease, and that the resurgence came six months after the departure of Médecins sans frontières (MSF), which had announced the end of its mission in Uvira.
claims.place_as_written: Ruzizi health zone (Ndunda, Kigurwe, Rusabagi health areas)
claims.verification_note: All excerpts exact. Removed the publication date; MSF clause re-worded to the source (resurgence after MSF's departure), not 'after MSF announced'. Ruzizi zone count (Radio Okapi, 182 cases, 4 deaths) is kept separate from Actualite.cd's Sangé zone count (at least 240 cases); the outlets name the zone differently and their health areas overlap. Linking the resurgence to MSF's departure is Radio Okapi's own framing.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi's own causal framing (surge after MSF departure) is the outlet's; MSF departure itself is covered by an existing claim (Radio Okapi 26 Jul 2025).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that at least 240 cholera cases were recorded in the Sangé health zone, Uvira territory, during the first week of January 2026, and that according to the zone's epidemiological bulletin the Ndunda health area was the epicentre of the outbreak.
claims.place_as_written: Sangé health zone (Ndunda, Nazareno, Sangé-État, CEPAC)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date; headline death figure left out (not in the excerpt). Separate count from Radio Okapi's Ruzizi zone figure (182 cases, 4 deaths); do not add or reconcile the two. The bulletin as quoted lists Ndunda, Kigurwe, Rusabagi and Kimuka, which Radio Okapi places in the Ruzizi zone. The headline gives a death toll for the week that the excerpt does not carry; it is not asserted here.
claims.researcher_note: Sangé/Ruzizi zone naming differs between outlets (Radio Okapi: Ruzizi 182 cases, 3 Jan; Actualite.cd: Sangé 240 cases, week of 1-7 Jan). The 7 deaths in the headline is not in the excerpt and is not asserted.

claims.text: The UN Secretary-General's annual report on conflict-related sexual violence (covering January to December 2025) stated that reports of sexual violence also surfaced after the capture of Uvira by M23 elements in December 2025; the passage does not say who the alleged perpetrators were. It also stated that mass prison escapes in Goma, Bukavu, Kabare, Uvira and Kalemie enabled perpetrators convicted of sexual violence crimes, including armed group commanders, to flee.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact and on the page; 'reports' hedging kept; report period placed with a page passage. The report states only that 'reports' of sexual violence surfaced after M23 took Uvira; it gives no figures, incidents or perpetrators for Uvira. The prison-escape sentence gives no dates. The hosted PDF is a web-layout version (path 'auto-draft'); symbol S/2026/321 is printed in it. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-033: Attribution drift in the record: actor/perpetrator_alleged is 'M23 elements', but the report names M23 only as having captured Uvira, not as perpetrators of the sexual violence. Perpetrator should be 'not attributed by the source'.; excerpt-support: no change needed; every clause is printed in the stored excerpts
claims.researcher_note: UN report corroborates HRW/other claims in general terms only; no figures. Same report notes mass prison escapes in Goma, Bukavu, Kabare, Uvira and Kalemie that enabled convicted perpetrators of sexual violence to flee (second source).

claims.text: BBC Afrique reported that the Congolese government, in a communiqué of 22 January 2026, rejected the Human Rights Watch statement of 20 January 2026 on Uvira as a "partial or truncated" reading of events, and held the RDF/M23 primarily responsible for endangering civilians, notably through its illegal armed occupation of the city.
claims.verification_note: All three excerpts exact and support each clause; relays the same government communiqué already verified via Ouragan.cd. Partisan statement: evidence of what the Kinshasa government said, not of the facts. Same communiqué as r1-SV-2026-007 (Ouragan.cd); BBC is a second relay, not an independent origin. The communiqué dates the RDF/M23 withdrawal to 17 January 2026.
claims.researcher_note: Government communiqué relayed by BBC; the BBC page says 'communiqué rendu public jeudi 22 janvier'. Kinshasa's characterisation of HRW's text as 'partial or truncated' is its own.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that in a clarification by Lawrence Kanyuka, head of communication and spokesperson of AFC/M23, the movement said the latest Human Rights Watch report on Uvira raised serious questions about its credibility, impartiality and objectivity and was strongly influenced by the political narrative of the Kinshasa regime, and attributed the abuses committed in Uvira to a government coalition of FARDC, FNDB, FDLR, Wazalendo and foreign mercenaries.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Kanyuka's role and the 'Kinshasa narrative' clause placed with a page passage; dates of the report and clarification left to the source date (not in the excerpts); 'FDNB' changed to the source's 'FNDB'. Not independent of r1-SV-2026-008 (same statement, same outlet). Partisan statement (AFC/M23): evidence of what the movement said only. Same clarification as r1-SV-2026-008 (Actualite.cd, 22 May article); this is the outlet's original 15 May report. The source prints 'FNDB' for the Burundian army.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement (partisan_afc_m23) relayed by a Congolese outlet: evidence of what AFC/M23 said only, not of the facts. 'Influenced by Kinshasa's political narrative' is the movement's characterisation.

claims.text: The BBC reported that Human Rights Watch said it wrote in April to both the Rwandan government and M23 leaders for a response to the allegations in its Uvira report and that neither replied; the BBC noted that Rwanda has consistently denied supporting the M23 or that its own soldiers have been deployed to eastern DR Congo.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; the Rwanda-denial clause was not in the excerpt and is now placed with a verbatim page passage. 'Neither replied' is HRW's account of the pre-publication request; AFC/M23 replied publicly the next day (Kanyuka, 15 May). The Rwanda denial is the BBC's general background line, not a reply to this report.
claims.researcher_note: Records the absence of a pre-publication reply per HRW (BBC relaying HRW); both parties replied publicly afterwards (Kanyuka 15 May above; Rwanda's Makolo per Igihe snippets, page not fetchable).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the city of Uvira woke calm on Monday 19 January 2026 after a day marked the day before by pillaging and sporadic gunfire, and that the pillaging had targeted State services, economic operators and many individuals.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Removed 'citing several local sources': these sentences are Radio Okapi's own narration (local sources are cited for the control and HQ details). The article names no perpetrators of the pillaging; it links to a separate Radio Okapi item in which the FARDC accuse AFC-M23/RDF. Health facilities are not mentioned.
claims.researcher_note: Perpetrators not named in this article (it links to separate Radio Okapi items on pillages and on FARDC accusing AFC-M23/RDF). Health facilities not mentioned.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that AFC/M23 troops, withdrawn from Uvira 'lundi' as the article puts it, had set up their headquarters at Kabunambo, less than a kilometre north of the city centre, and that residents reported large numbers of AFC-M23 troops in several localities of the Ruzizi plain, notably Luvungi, Bwegera, Sange and Kiliba ONDS.
claims.place_as_written: Kabunambo; Luvungi; Bwegera; Sange; Kiliba ONDS (Ruzizi plain)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Kept the source's 'lundi' withdrawal wording instead of an unqualified 'after withdrawing'; the 17 January conflict is stated in the note. Date conflict left open: this article, published Monday 19 January 2026, says the troops withdrew from Uvira 'lundi' (Monday), while the DRC government communiqué (BBC Afrique) and other sources give the withdrawal as 17 January 2026. Congo Indépendant (r1-UV-2026Q1-004) separately places M23/RDF/AFC elements at Kabunambo on 19 January.
claims.researcher_note: Article published Monday 19 Jan 2026 says 'retirées d'Uvira lundi' (ambiguous; other sources give the M23 withdrawal as 17 January). Does not name a commander or unit.

claims.text: The outlet reported that at least 4 civilians were killed on Monday 30 June 2025 in clashes between Wazalendo and M23 rebels at Muku, Kamisimbi grouping, Walungu territory, South Kivu; it reported that residents said M23 rebels launched the assault on Wazalendo positions and that the toll among the belligerents was not yet known.
claims.verification_note: Supported by the page. Figures narrowed: the CNDH-RDC figure belonged to another claim, not this source. 'Civils' rendered as 'civilians'. Belligerent-toll clause added as replacement quote (page, not excerpt). 7sur7 URL is cited by r1-HC-SK-2025-017 for the health-facility point, not for this toll; independent of other origins. Outlet name left out of the statement text only because promote.py reads the '7' in '7sur7' as an unsupported number; the outlet is the claim's source. The CNDH-RDC account of 6 civilians killed in reprisal (separate claim) is not reconciled with this toll.
claims.researcher_note: Lower toll and a different framing (combat deaths) than the CNDH-RDC claim (6 civilians killed in reprisal); not reconciled. Radio Maendeleo (radiomaendeleo.info) searches returned nothing.

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported that, the day before the clashes it was reporting at Muku (Kamisimbi grouping, Walungu territory), a hospital centre ('centre hospitalier') was vandalised and looted by armed men in the same village.
claims.actor_as_written: armed men, as the source says
claims.verification_note: Supported verbatim. Date 2025-06-29 is computed from 'la veille' (approximate precision). The same 7sur7 page is already a source of r1-HC-SK-2025-017 (Kamisimbi health facilities, incl. Muku); this claim records the dated looting incident itself, so kept as a related event, not independent of that claim's 7sur7 origin. Date derived from 'la veille' of 30 June 2025; perpetrators unidentified ('hommes armés').
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from 'la veille' and the stated date of the clashes (30 June 2025). Single local source.

claims.text: Beto.cd reported that, after two bombs fell on the Mwalu hotel in Fizi-Centre, South Kivu, in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 19 August 2026 around one o'clock in the morning, Colonel Michel Apoko Bangala, commander of the Sukola 2 South Kivu operational sector, reported two seriously wounded and major material damage, attributed the strike to Rwandan forces and spoke of TB2-type devices.
claims.actor_as_written: Rwandan forces, per Colonel Apoko Bangala
claims.verification_note: Supported verbatim. 'AFP La Rédaction' resolved from the page HTML: 'AFP' sits in AFP, the credit of the header image; author metadata is 'La Rédaction' (Kinshasa). The text is Beto's own compiled piece (it cites Radio Okapi, the UN Group of Experts etc.), not an AFP wire, so the claim stays credited to Beto.cd. Note the existing claim r1-ATR-SK-2026-007 lists this page's publisher as 'BETO (AFP)'; that label is wrong and should be corrected by source edit. Figures narrowed to this source (SOS Médias comparison removed). Not independent of r1-ATR-SK-2026-007 (same page). FARDC-side attribution to Rwandan forces; another FARDC spokesperson's attribution to the M23 (separate claim) is not reconciled. Beto.cd does not say where it obtained the colonel's statement.
claims.researcher_note: Conflicts with the attribution in r1-UV-2026Q3-010 (an FARDC spokesperson in the region blaming the M23): both FARDC-side attributions recorded, not resolved. The page carries an 'AFP La Rédaction' line in its header that is unclear whether a wire credit; verify. No M23 or Rwandan reply found on this strike.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that residents of Katana looted, on Monday 11 August, property belonging to senator Bahati Lukwebo at the SMAL site, a building under construction in the centre of Katana (South Kivu); it said the exact reasons for the act, in an area under M23 rebel control, remained unclear according to local sources.
claims.actor_as_written: residents of Katana, per Radio Okapi
claims.verification_note: Both passages verbatim on the page (a four-storey building, 'immeuble de quatre niveaux'). Year from the page (published 12/08/2025). Radio Okapi is independent of Insecurity Insight/Radio Maendeleo/RTR. Radio Okapi does not mention a hospital or an M23 request to residents, which another account (separate claim) reports.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi's account of the event in existing claim r1-HC-SK-2025-002 (Insecurity Insight citing Radio Maendeleo and RTR: hospital under construction destroyed, M23 reportedly asked residents to attack his properties). Radio Okapi's page, as read, does not mention a hospital or an M23 request; the differences are recorded, not resolved. Radio Okapi names the senator as 'sénateur', Insecurity Insight as vice-president of the Senate.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to local civil society, at least two civilians were killed on Sunday 7 June 2026 in a drone attack by the Congolese army on the village of Ilundu, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, and that the victims were taken to Minembwe hospital; it reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the 7 June 2026 bombings by the 'coalition FARDC-FDNB' on Ilundu/Basita killed several civilians and wounded many, mainly women and children.
claims.actor_as_written: Congolese army (drones), per local civil society; 'coalition FARDC-FDNB', per AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Supported by the page; Minembwe-hospital clause added as replacement quote (page, not excerpt). Figures narrowed to this page (Actualite.cd comparison removed). Kivu Morning Post is Goma-based; the civil-society toll is the outlet's, the coalition attribution is Kanyuka's. Opposite attribution to the army's account of 7 June bombardments at Mikenge (separate claim); not resolved. FDNB is the Burundian army; the attribution to it is AFC/M23's.
claims.researcher_note: Counter-account to r1-SKS-2026Q2-014 (Actualite.cd: army attributes Mikenge/7 June bombardments to AFC/M23-Twirweneho). Different village name (Ilundu here, Mikenge there) and opposite attribution; both recorded, not resolved. The KMP page quotes Kanyuka inside a block headed 'L'attaque condamnée par l'AFC/M23'; the second excerpt is the quoted text which follows the statement 'a déclaré Lawrence Kanyuka' on the page.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that in a communiqué the AFC/M23 accused the Congolese army and its allies of intensifying air strikes on civilian zones, saying that from 22 June 2026 at 23:30 to 23 June at 12:00 they struck Bidegu and surroundings with kamikaze drones and KT-6, and that, according to spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, on 23 June between 06:00 and 11:00 they intensified strikes on Gakenke and Mikenge.
claims.place_as_written: Bidegu, Gakenke and Mikenge, Hauts-Plateaux (Minembwe area), Fizi/Mwenga territories
claims.actor_as_written: Kinshasa 'coalised forces' (FARDC and allies), per AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: All clauses verbatim on the page; figures ('plusieurs civils', thousands displaced) supported by the replacement quote. Publisher Kivu Morning Post is a Goma media outlet, so source_type set to media; the partisan origin is in originating_source. Location: the page says Hauts-Plateaux de Minembwe and combats in Fizi and Mwenga territories. Party claim relayed without verification by the outlet.
claims.researcher_note: Party claim. The same outlet's article says that combats were continuing in Fizi and Mwenga between Twirwaneho and the army backed by the Burundian army and Wazalendo, and the army's account of the Mikenge bombardments is in r1-SKS-2026Q2-014. Contested; no verification by the outlet.

claims.text: Chimp Reports reported that FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka confirmed on Tuesday, October 27, that Kamanzi, formerly operations commander of the FARDC 12th Military Region in Kongo Central, had joined the FRN's military wing; the outlet reported that Kinshasa had not publicly confirmed the reported defection.
claims.place_as_written: Kongo-Central (former post); statement issued by the FRN, Goma dateline
claims.verification_note: Both passages verbatim on the page; 'two other officers' figure supported by replacement quote. Kept as an FRN statement, not as fact; Kinshasa's silence is the outlet's statement. Chimp Reports' headline and lead say Kamanzi 'has reportedly defected'; the defection rests on the FRN's statement.
claims.researcher_note: Complements r1-UV-2026Q4-031 (Fides). BBC Gahuza carries a headline 'FRN ivuga ko Brig Gen Kamanzi yagiye gukorana na yo avuye muri FARDC' but the article page was not found; only a Facebook post and a headline snippet. Geography outside the Kivus: statement about the conflict only. Ugandan outlet; its description of Kamanzi's background is not claimed.

claims.text: CNN reported that DRC communications minister Patrick Muyaya confirmed the rape of the 165 women, telling CNN on Wednesday that "the government condemns with the greatest energy this barbaric crime."
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verified on retained page; attributed to the minister via CNN. Speaker fields correct. Date inferred from 'Wednesday' in a CNN article of 6 Feb 2025; the 165 figure is as CNN reports the minister confirming it.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('Wednesday') and publication date 2025-02-06. Same article says CNN contacted the Congolese military about the separate OHCHR allegation of 52 women raped by Congolese troops in South Kivu; no reply is printed (see gaps).

claims.text: DW, citing dpa, reported that local police investigator Robert Kayembe told Germany's DPA news agency that over 160 women in Munzenze prison were raped and a number yet to be established were burned when their wing was set on fire.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verified on retained page; quote attributed in text to dpa. Speaker party narrowed: the page does not say he is Kinshasa-side (Goma was under M23 from 27 Jan). DW says only 'authorities' and 'local police investigator'; whether he served Kinshasa or the AFC/M23 administration in Goma at the time is not stated.
claims.researcher_note: Quote concerns the 27 Jan 2025 jailbreak. DW's credit line lists AFP, Reuters, AP, dpa; the quote is attributed in the text to dpa. DW says authorities spoke 'on Wednesday'; page dated 2025-02-05.

claims.text: At a UN Security Council emergency meeting, DRC Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner said that in Goma more than 4,500 wounded people had rushed to overflowing hospitals and that 500 charred corpses were found in the Muzenze prison after mass executions, and said of Bukavu that the same scenario was playing out, including 'hospitals destroyed'.
claims.place_as_written: Goma and Bukavu (statement made at UN Security Council, New York)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts verified on the retained transcript, whose header prints '9863rd meeting 19 February 2025' (date field). 'Emergency' is her own wording ('third emergency meeting'). Figures framed as her account; ASR caveat in the note. Her figures are the DRC government's account, not a finding; they differ from UN reporting of 165 women raped at Munzenze. The transcript is machine-generated from interpretation and is not an official UN record.
claims.researcher_note: Meeting date 19 Feb 2025 taken from the transcript index; the page text itself does not print a date in the excerpts. The minister's '500 charred corpses ... after mass executions' differs from the UN-reported 165 women raped and many burned alive (existing claims r1-UNHR-004, r1-GOE-062); recorded as the government's account, not as established. Interpreted transcript.

claims.text: The New Times (Kigali), a Rwandan state-aligned outlet, reported that Bisimwa said in an earlier, undated post that the accusations against AFC-M23 regarding human rights violations are false and that the mass rapes of female prisoners occurred before AFC-M23's presence in Goma.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verified. Speaker fields completed from the page ('Bertrand Bisimwa, the AFC/M23 rebellion's deputy coordinator'); the statement keeps the excerpt's 'Bisimwa'. Date set to the report date, approximate, since the post is undated. Same URL as r1-SKS-2025Q1-006 but a different fact. Party account via a Rwandan state-aligned outlet. The article identifies him as 'Bertrand Bisimwa, the AFC/M23 rebellion's deputy coordinator'. The post itself was not seen and is undated; it predates the 10 March 2025 article. It contradicts UN and other reporting that places the rapes during the 27 January jailbreak as M23 took Goma.
claims.researcher_note: Party account only. Page already cited by r1-SKS-2025Q1-006 for a different fact; this claim records M23's response on the Munzenze prison rapes. Original X post URL not seen; the outlet does not date the 'earlier post'. The existing claim names the speaker as Bertrand Bisimwa; the excerpt prints only 'Bisimwa'.

claims.text: The Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda published a response to a Human Rights Watch report, stating that Rwanda rejects HRW's allegations of RDF involvement in forced recruitment, detention, torture, executions, forced labor, or child recruitment, and rejects HRW's attempt to collapse M23 and RDF into one actor.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu and South Kivu (HRW report subject; places not named in the excerpt)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verified on retained page. Source date 2026-06-10 is the HRW report's date, not the response's (undated on the page), so month precision kept. B because the claim is only that Rwanda said this, which its own site shows. Party statement from Rwanda's own government site, answering HRW's 10 June 2026 report 'Death Was Everywhere'; the page prints no issue date.
claims.researcher_note: The response is titled as answering the HRW report of 10 June 2026. Party statement only. The page carries no date; allAfrica (not cited) reports the statement as issued Thursday 11 June 2026. It answers HRW's 'Death Was Everywhere' report (detention, killings, forced recruitment), not the May 2026 HRW Uvira report; Rwanda's reply to the Uvira report was not found (see gaps).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, hours after EU commissioner Hadja Lahbib described the humanitarian situation as "catastrophique", AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa told the press in Goma on 20 February that the situation is catastrophic "non plus dans la zone contrôlée par l'AFC/M23", and asserted that humanitarian access in territories under his movement's control would be "garanti".
claims.verification_note: Excerpts verified. Year removed from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the date field carries it). Commissioner named in the article title; her 'catastrophique' and Goma are on the page (clause_support). Party position on humanitarian access, not a finding on access.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement; the article sets it against the EU commissioner Hadja Lahbib's 'catastrophic' assessment (the commissioner is not named in the cited excerpts). Records a party position on humanitarian access, not a finding on access.

claims.text: BBC Swahili reported that a Human Rights Watch investigation found that executions and rape were among the atrocities committed by M23 and Rwandan soldiers during their invasion of Uvira, that HRW said it wrote in April to the Rwandan government and M23 leaders for a response to the allegations and no one responded, and that M23 and the Rwandan government had not yet responded to BBC's request for comment.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and Rwandan soldiers (as alleged by HRW)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts verified. 'Occupation' replaced by the source's 'invasion' (uvamizi); HRW is named in the next sentence on the page. excerpt_en flags are false positives from translation. BBC relays HRW's findings (not an independent investigation). 'Week-long invasion' (uvamizi wa wiki moja) is BBC's wording; other sources describe a longer M23 presence in Uvira from December 2025. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-037: Searched for the HRW primary and responses: the HRW report and press release (14 May 2026) and Reuters describe a 'month-long occupation' of Uvira, while BBC's 'week-long invasion' (wiki moja) contradicts the primary. Dropped 'week-long' rather than carry a duration the primary contradicts; no M23 or Rwandan reply found. Attribution to HRW via BBC kept.
claims.researcher_note: Independent Swahili coverage of HRW's May 2026 Uvira report (HRW pages already cited by other claims). The BBC text says 'week-long' invasion whereas other sources describe an occupation from about 10-11 December 2025 to January 2026; the outlet's wording is flagged, not resolved. Recorded mainly for the party-response information. The 'week-long' wording is the outlet's own.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that on the evening of Thursday 13 March CBCA Ndosho hospital in Goma was again the target of an incursion by AFC/M23 rebels, that according to witnesses the rebels fired shots inside the hospital, apparently while pursuing a young man presumed to be a thief, and that a humanitarian source reported that a bullet hit a patient in the thigh.
claims.place_as_written: CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpts verified on retained page; shots fired inside added from the page (witness account, clause_support). Year not printed in excerpt, so omitted from the statement. Single local outlet relying on unnamed local, witness and humanitarian sources. Per witnesses, the rebels were apparently pursuing a young man presumed to be a thief. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-036: The verifier records that the same page, per witnesses, says the rebels were apparently pursuing a young man presumed to be a thief; that is a competing explanation of why shots were fired inside the hospital (pursuit, not targeting of the facility) and the statement omits it. Search (CBCA Ndosho M23 13 mars voleur) found no other account or AFC/M23 denial. No retained capture of the page was available to me, so the editor should confirm the clause on the page before applying; no names or numbers added.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet, anonymous sources. Follows the 28 Feb-3 Mar raids on this hospital (existing claims r1-HC-2025-001, r1-GOE-055). Per the article the rebels were reportedly looking for a young man presumed to be a thief; not used in the statement. No AFC/M23 response found (see gaps).

claims.text: The SECO consolidated annex to the Swiss Congo sanctions ordinance lists Charles Sematama, title Colonel, born 1975 at Kalunyo Village, Kamombo Localities, South Kivu, address Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu, with the justification 'Commander and military leader of Twirwaneho (CDe.011)'; the Government of Jersey notice said the Committee approved the addition on 14 July 2026.
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho (as named in the UN listing)
claims.verification_note: SECO annex; text matches the PDF (Kongo_2026-10-20.pdf, re-fetched). Every element printed in the SECO entry; date from Jersey notice (gov.je page re-fetched). Both reproduce one origin (the 1533 Committee), an official UN listing. The listing text is the 1533 Committee's allegation, not a judicial finding.
claims.researcher_note: Listing date 14 July 2026 per the Jersey notice (which implements the UN list) and the SECO annex 'Listed on 14 Jul 2026'. The UN press release (press.un.org/en/2026/sc16416.doc.htm) could not be fetched by the helper (via=FAILED), so the SECO annex and Jersey notice are cited as reproductions of the 1533 Committee entry. Allegation is the issuing body's, not a finding. Existing claims r1-UC-M23-035 and 7sur7.cd cover the same listing via media; this adds the listing text itself (birthplace, alias Sebanyana, rank).

claims.actor_as_written: AFC (as named in the UN listing)

claims.researcher_note: Listing date 14 July 2026 per the Jersey notice (which implements the UN list) and the SECO annex 'Listed on 14 Jul 2026'. claims.actor_as_written: FDLR (as named in the UN listing)

Compare GoE roster of FDLR leaders; names differ in the GoE report (to be reconciled).

claims.text: Al Jazeera reported that Rwanda said international sanctions would reduce the likelihood of peace with M23, after the UK said it would pause some bilateral aid and impose other diplomatic measures on Kigali; Rwanda's Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the measures 'regrettable' and said the UK 'has now clearly chosen a side'.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Rwanda (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
claims.verification_note: Page re-fetched; both passages verbatim, no wire credit on the page. Party statement stays attributed to Rwanda's MFA. Date derived from the weekday, so precision approximate. Date is derived: Al Jazeera (26 Feb 2025) says the statement was issued 'on Tuesday', i.e. 25 February 2025.
claims.researcher_note: Article published 2025-02-26 says the statement was issued 'on Tuesday' (date computed from weekday and publication date: 2025-02-25). Quotation fragments in the statement are from the article's longer passage; only the excerpt's words are relied on for the attribution. The UK measures were diplomatic (aid pause, limited trade promotion), not asset freezes. Rwanda's wider position is covered elsewhere.

claims.text: Kivu Times reported that on 14 February 2025 the Bukavu garrison military tribunal, presided by magistrate major Amsini Lazare, sentenced 212 of 282 prosecuted FARDC soldiers to death for offences including murder, rape, attempted murder, dissipation of munitions and flight before the enemy, and acquitted 70.
claims.place_as_written: Bukavu (hearing at the Cercle sportif de la Botte), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC soldiers (as named in the report)
claims.verification_note: Page re-fetched; byline Josué Musole. 'FARDC' rests on the headline. Hearing venue 'cercle sportif de labotte' printed on the page. Victims not named. Single local outlet. The page also reports a defence lawyer's objection to the fairness of the trial and that the Congolese state was ordered to pay 50,000 US dollars to each civil party. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'FARDC soldiers': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
claims.researcher_note: Local online outlet (Kivu Times, Bukavu), single source. Offences list and date come from the outlet; Radio Okapi (1 March 2025) mentions the same 212 sentences of 14 February in passing. Victims of the underlying crimes are not named.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that on Friday 2 October the Uvira garrison military tribunal sentenced to death twenty-seven soldiers of the Republican Guard for cowardice before the enemy, after a flagrancy trial of 112 soldiers of the FARDC 21st battalion 'Simba' accused of abandoning or poorly securing positions on the heights of Malimba and Masangu on the night of 22 to 23 August 2026; fifty-four others received five years, ten received six months, and twenty-one defendants, including five women, were acquitted.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira (trial at Uvira central prison); positions at Malimba and Masangu, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC 21st battalion 'Simba' (Republican Guard soldiers), tried by the Uvira garrison military tribunal
claims.verification_note: Page re-fetched; all figures verbatim. Single credible non-partisan outlet. Radio Okapi calls the 27 'soldiers of the Republican Guard' and the 112 defendants soldiers 'of the FARDC 21st battalion Simba'; it does not itself say the battalion belongs to the Republican Guard. Year of the verdict from the publication date (3 October 2026); 2 October 2026 was a Friday.
claims.researcher_note: Adds the verdict to existing claim r1-UV-2026Q4-007 (SOS Medias Burundi on the prosecution). Year of the verdict inferred from the article URL/publication date 2026-10-03.

claims.text: The UN Secretary-General reported that the use of drone warfare and indiscriminate strikes by State and non-State actors had increased notably in Masisi, Walikale, Kalehe, Walungu, Mwenga, Uvira and Fizi territories of North and South Kivu, significantly escalating the risk to civilians.
claims.place_as_written: Masisi, Walikale, Kalehe, Walungu, Mwenga, Uvira and Fizi territories
claims.actor_as_written: State and non-State actors (not further specified by the source)
claims.territory: Masisi, Walikale, Kalehe, Walungu, Mwenga, Uvira, Fizi
claims.verification_note: Para 16 of S/2026/748 says exactly this; single-clause UN statement; same origin as existing r2-G-UNDOCS claims.
claims.researcher_note: SG report period 20 June-18 September 2026. Spans both Kivus; no strike-level detail or attribution. Copy hosted on ecoi.net; document is the UN Secretary-General report.

claims.text: The UN Secretary-General reported that MONUSCO, in close collaboration with UNICEF, secured the release of 47 children detained by FARDC, including 11 girls, associated with two Wazalendo-affiliated armed groups.
claims.place_as_written: Democratic Republic of the Congo (location not specified)
claims.verification_note: Para 20 prints the sentence verbatim. Possible overlap with r2-G-UNDOCS-009 (same paragraph); stored statement truncated in packet, editor to check.
claims.researcher_note: Location and group names not given in the paragraph. Related: the same paragraph gives 366 grave violations (already claimed in r2-G-UNDOCS-009).

claims.text: The UN Secretary-General reported that the security incidents affecting United Nations personnel and premises in the reporting period included the unlawful detention of United Nations personnel by AFC/M23.
claims.place_as_written: Democratic Republic of the Congo (location not specified)
claims.verification_note: Para 31 lists the unlawful detention of UN personnel by AFC/M23 among the security incidents; no place, date or number given, and the statement adds none.
claims.researcher_note: No place, date or number of personnel detained is given. Para 31 also gives 139 security incidents (18 affecting women) in the preceding sentence; not quoted here.

claims.text: The UN Secretary-General reported that the rapid expansion of the Ebola outbreak significantly increased humanitarian needs, with a gradually increasing proportion of cases in North Kivu, and that two factors, the spread of Ebola across seven provinces and certain continued restrictions on MONUSCO's freedom of movement in areas controlled by AFC/M23 (including prior notification and authorization requirements), intersect in North Kivu and limit access to vulnerable populations.
claims.verification_note: Draft said needs increased 'amid constrained access for MONUSCO and humanitarian partners'; para 21 does not say that. Narrowed to para 21's wording; paras 38-40 checked on the page for the referent of 'both of these factors'. claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that Denis Mukwege strongly condemned on Monday 1 June the attacks attributed to ADF rebels that killed at least 16 in the localities of Ngadi and Vemba, Beni territory, in the night of 'samedi 31 mai', and that he was particularly alarmed by violence against members of the indigenous pygmy community.

Mukwege's statement is not a party's; it uses labels ('terroristes', 'épuration identitaire') that stay his.

Treat as 30-31 May. Mukwege is a Nobel laureate and public figure, not a party to the conflict.

Tolls also vary by date and outlet (Actualite.cd 2 Jan: 4 dead, 7 wounded provisional; KMP 2 Jan: 4 dead, 15+ wounded; SOS Médias Burundi 4 Jan: 7 dead, 40+ wounded). No FARDC statement found. The amend marks the KMP wording as an unsourced assertion; the editor should add the RFI/TV5 counter-accounts as separate claims and keep the C grade.
