The three civilians killed are not named. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: The page does not say which of the two soldiers was linked to which count beyond what is quoted. Victims of the killings are not named. Existing claim r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-009 (Radio Okapi, 10 July 2026, Beni garrison tribunal) is a different case.

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported, in its article on the Beni garrison military tribunal's Manyama-Beu verdicts, that hearings concerning a third soldier prosecuted for the alleged rape of a 19-month-old girl had been suspended, the case file being examined at Oicha, where the victim was receiving medical care.
claims.place_as_written: Manyama-Beu / Oicha, Beni territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Beni garrison military tribunal; a FARDC soldier (not named by the source)
claims.verification_note: Page re-fetched; verbatim. Figure flag '7' is the outlet name 7sur7.cd: resolved. Neither the soldier nor the child is named by the source. Allegation only; no verdict. The source says hearings were expected to resume. The date is that of the article's verdict report, not of the alleged rape (not given). 2026-10-29: statement edited: fact-check fc3: 7sur7.cd, 29 Jul 2026, introduces this with 'Par ailleurs' and says the file is examined at Oicha; it does not say these hearings were part of the same session at Manyama-Beu, so that qualifier is dropped. Otherwise the excerpt carries the clause verbatim. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Date of the alleged rape not given by the source; the date field is the date of the verdict reported in the same article. Allegation only: no verdict. Victim is a minor and not named by the source.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the president of the Constitutional Court and of the Conseil supérieur de la magistrature, Dieudonné Kamuleta, had recalled in a communiqué published on 12 September 2025 that the country's Constitution and organic laws give the Conseil supérieur de la magistrature exclusive power to recruit and manage magistrates nationwide, and that any parallel attempt is therefore, according to him, 'nulle et de nul effet'; the Justice Minister Guillaume Ngefa had announced the forthcoming signature of an ordinance annulling all judicial decisions taken by AFC/M23 leaders.
claims.place_as_written: Kinshasa (statement); Goma and Bukavu (AFC/M23-held areas concerned)
claims.actor_as_written: Dieudonné Kamuleta; Guillaume Ngefa; DRC Government
claims.verification_note: Narrowed procedural stage: source says Ngefa announced 'la signature prochaine' (forthcoming signature) of an ordinance; the draft said he announced an ordinance annulling decisions. Kamuleta clause restated closer to the source ('avait rappelé'; exclusivity per the Constitution and organic laws). Ngefa's announcement is undated in the source and concerns an ordinance to be signed, not one already signed. The page says Ngefa accuses AFC/M23 leaders of 'ne jurer que par l'amnistie'. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Statement made before the publication date of the article (3 Nov 2025); the 12 Sep 2025 communiqué is also in r2-G-DOC-858-062 (Group of Experts). This is a separate, local-media account. Kamuleta's quoted words are a paraphrase plus a quoted phrase in the source.

claims.text: BBC News Afrique reported that, according to the government, more than 200 people, including 70 children, were killed when a landslide caused a mining area to collapse in eastern DRC; it quoted the Ministry of Mines communiqué giving a provisional toll of more than 200 dead and many injured, and said it could not independently verify the toll. It also reported that the ministry blamed the M23 rebels, that the M23 had not yet commented, that a source at Rubaya told the BBC the collapse was caused by attacks by government forces and that only six people had died, and that the government had not responded to that claim.
claims.place_as_written: Rubaya mine, Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact. Added the page's second side (the Rubaya source's six-dead account and the M23's silence), which is the discrepancy this unit is for; written as 'the rebels'/'a source at the mine' because 'M23' and 'Rubaya' are printed on the page but in no stored excerpt or title (page-only clauses; extend the excerpt with source_edits.py add_excerpt). Byline Emery Makumeno, reporting from Kinshasa. The page also mentions a separate late-January collapse at the site with more than 200 dead: a different event. Tolls conflict: the government says more than 200 dead (provisional); an unnamed source at Rubaya told the BBC only six died and blamed government attacks; an existing claim (actualite.cd) gives 'more than a hundred'. None is independently verified. Rubaya is under M23 control. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'Ministry of Mines communiqué: provisional toll of more than 200 dead, 70 children, and many injured': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'the ministry blamed the rebels': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'the rebels had not yet commented; a source at the mine said government attacks caused the collapse and only six died; the government had not responded': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: statement edited: Restores 'M23' and 'Rubaya', which the verifier generalised to 'the rebels'/'a source at the mine' only because no excerpt printed them; now carried by proposed add_excerpts on source 0 ('...imputé la responsabilité de cette tragédie aux rebelles du M23'; 'Le M23 n'a pas encore fait de commentaires, mais une source à Rubaya a déclaré à la BBC...'). The '23' of M23 may trip the number guard.
claims.researcher_note: Government toll for the 3 March 2026 collapse (existing claim r2-G-NKW-MASISI-029 cites actualite.cd with 'more than a hundred'). TV5 Monde copy could not be fetched. Ouest-France headline snippet says witnesses reported 6 dead (lead only, not cited). Rubaya is under AFC/M23 control.

claims.text: MSF said in a communiqué that on 1 May a team travelling between Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu in South Kivu was stopped at a checkpoint held by Wazalendo elements, and that armed men opened fire among themselves while the team was in the middle.
claims.actor_as_written: armed men at a checkpoint held by Wazalendo elements, as MSF describes them
claims.verification_note: All three excerpts exact (the latest of 4 captures still prints them; the page's split accented letters fall outside the excerpts). Statement matches the excerpts clause by clause; attribution kept to MSF. excerpt_en flags resolved: the capitalised words ('MSF', 'South') render 'de MSF' and 'Sud-Kivu' in the excerpts themselves. MSF's own account (press release, Bukavu, 8 May 2026). It differs from outlets that headline an attack on the convoy by Wazalendo/FARDC and one that gives 3 May. MSF also says confusion arose among the armed men over the team's identity, that the team was pushed to continue to Mwenga, and that false accusations against MSF circulated online.
claims.researcher_note: MSF's own account. 'Kalimoto' is not printed on the MSF page. Other outlets (actualite.cd, KMP) headline an attack on the convoy by Wazalendo/FARDC and one gives 3 May; MSF says 1 May and describes gunfire between the armed men: discrepancy to register. msf.org text has odd spacing in accented letters, so excerpts avoid those words.

claims.text: RFI reported that the newly built Mwalu hotel in Fizi-centre was hit by a drone strike at one in the morning in the night of 18 to 19 August, that two civilians were seriously injured, and that the Congolese army accuses the AFC/M23 of being behind the attack, citing two explosive devices dropped by drones.
claims.verification_note: All excerpts exact (latest of 4 captures). RFI copy on Yahoo France with the RFI credit on the page, so originating_source is RFI. The hotel's name is in the page sentence after excerpt 2 (page-only clause). Graded B: RFI reports the strike and injuries in its own voice; the perpetrator stays attributed to the FARDC. excerpt_en flags resolved: 'Congolese', 'FARDC', 'AFC' and 'Fizi-centre' render words of each excerpt. The attribution to the AFC/M23 is the FARDC's; no AFC/M23 reply is on the page. A Facebook post by Actualite.cd (not opened) is said to date a strike on the same hotel to the night of 16 August 2026: date to be checked. 2026-10-29: source 2 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'the newly built Mwalu hotel': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
claims.researcher_note: RFI copy on Yahoo France (RFI credit on page). Actualite.cd's Facebook post (lead only, not fetched) dates a strike on the Mwalu hotel to the night of Sunday 16 August 2026: date discrepancy to resolve. No AFC/M23 reply on this page. A YouTube title claims Rwanda bombed the hotel (lead only).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that two people were killed and six wounded in bombardments in the night of Saturday 6 to Sunday 7 June in Ilundu/Basita village, Minembwe, Fizi territory, and that the Réseau local de protection des civils dans les Hauts Plateaux, a citizens' collective based in Minembwe, said in a communiqué that the shots, attributed to the FARDC and the Burundian FDNB, targeted an inhabited area of the village; the reported toll names Prince Runezerwa Mahiyaho, aged 19, who died on arrival at the general hospital, and Résor Kigeri Mazuru, who reportedly died at the scene; the outlet said that at publication no official reaction from the FARDC or the FDNB had been obtained.
claims.place_as_written: Ilundu/Basita, Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and FDNB, as attributed by the Réseau local de protection des civils dans les Hauts Plateaux
claims.verification_note: All five excerpts exact. Flag on figure '2' resolved: the statement's 'two' is printed as 'deux morts' / 'Deux personnes ont été tuées' (excerpts 1 and 4; excerpt_en 'two dead', 'Two people'), so no digit '2' is needed. Narrowed attribution: the night and the toll are the outlet's lede (excerpt 4) and 'le bilan communiqué', not only the Réseau's words; added the outlet's no-reaction line. Byline David Yemba, Bukavu dateline 7 June 2026. Victims' names are spelled as printed (two minors, policy v1). excerpt_en flag on source 0 resolved: 'Burundian'/'Sunday' render 'du Burundi'/'dimanche'. Civil-society account; the outlet says independent verification of the circumstances was not yet available. Résor Kigeri Mazuru 'aurait perdu la vie' (reportedly died) at the scene: conditional in the source. 2026-10-29: source 4 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'Minembwe, Fizi territory': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-038: The attribution is correctly the Réseau's ('attribués aux'), and the outlet's no-reaction line is kept. One wording fix: the source says the shots 'ont visé une zone habitée' (targeted an inhabited area), not that they 'hit' it. The amend restores that wording and keeps the 'reportedly' on the second death. A search (Ilundu Basita bombardement FARDC réaction) found no FARDC or FDNB denial. Two issues to surface: (1) Kivu Morning Post and Actualite.cd place Ilundu in Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, while this outlet says Minembwe, Fizi; (2) AFC/M23 (Kanyuka, r3-G-CTR-008) makes the same coalition attribution, so the Réseau and AFC/M23 accounts may not be independent of each other.
claims.researcher_note: Civil-society (Banyamulenge-based) account naming FARDC and FDNB; existing actualite.cd/KMP claims (7 June, drones attributed to FARDC) give the same toll. Night of 6-7 June per this outlet versus 'Sunday 7 June' elsewhere. Victim list includes minors (policy v1). No AFC/M23 spokesperson account found on a fetched page.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that more than 70 bodies, including those of women, children and elderly people, were found on Saturday 15 February in a church building in Maiba village, Lubero territory; civil society believed they were people reported missing who had been abducted on 12 February by unidentified armed men, and said they were found bound and beheaded, probably killed with bladed weapons. Radio Okapi added that concordant sources in the region suspected local armed groups and ADF rebels of being the perpetrators.
claims.place_as_written: Maiba village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: unidentified armed men; civil society and concordant sources suspected local armed groups and ADF rebels
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts found on the retained page (published sam 15/02/2025 14:03); statement, date, toll ('plus de 70') and hedged attribution match. excerpt_en flag is only capitalised English weekday/month words; translation is faithful. Discrepancy: Radio Okapi gives discovery on Saturday 15 February and abduction on 12 February; Actualite.cd (separate claim) has abduction in the night of 11-12 February and bodies found 'vendredi dernier' (the previous Friday). Perpetrators are suspected, not established: Radio Okapi names local armed groups and the ADF as suspects.
claims.researcher_note: Not previously held (claim_search 'Maiba' returned 0). Radio Okapi has the discovery on Saturday 15 February and abduction on 12 February; Actualite.cd (separate claim) has bodies found the preceding Friday after hostage-taking in the night of 11-12 February. Reporter.cd (16 Feb 2025; fetched, not cited) says Friday 14 February and names a CBECA church at Kasanga near Maiba, chefferie Baswagha. Not matched to any FIRE cluster in this unit (Maiba/Manzya lies south-west of Lubero town).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that at least 70 civilians died in Lubero territory in an act attributed to ADF rebels near Maiba in the Manzya groupement, and that their bodies were found 'vendredi dernier' (the previous Friday) two days after the abduction, according to the local community protection committee. It quoted the committee's coordinator Vitwamba Vianney as saying the victims were taken hostage in the night of 11 to 12 February and that the victims, of all ages, were finished off in a local church.
claims.place_as_written: Maiba, Manzya groupement, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact on retained page (sam 15/02/2025 18:33, byline Dieubon Mughenze). Attribution to ADF is the outlet's/committee's ('attribué'; quote says 'présumés ADF'); statement keeps it attributed. Date range end (14 Feb) is an inference from the weekday, flagged in note. Same event as the Radio Okapi Maiba claim, with differing dates (Friday vs Saturday 15 February for the discovery; night of 11-12 vs 12 February for the abduction). 14 February is inferred from 'vendredi dernier' and the publication date (sam 15/02/2025); the page also quotes the coordinator saying the bodies were found at Kasanga near Maiba in a CBCA church and that the victims went missing at the hands of 'présumés ADF'. The headline says 'autres' (other) 70 bodies.
claims.researcher_note: Date of discovery computed from the weekday 'vendredi dernier' and the publication date (15 Feb 2025): 14 February. Conflicts with Radio Okapi's Saturday 15 February (separate claim). Outlet is a national online outlet citing a local civil-society committee.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that fighting between the FARDC and M23 rebels continued on Wednesday 15 January at Luofu, in Lubero territory, North Kivu, and that clashes were also reported in several villages south of Lubero, notably Kamandi Gite and Kibanda, west of the rural commune of Kayna.
claims.place_as_written: Luofu, Kamandi Gite and Kibanda (west of Kayna), Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact on retained page dated mer 15/01/2025. Page attributes detail to local and security sources and Lubero civil society.
claims.researcher_note: Adds a day (15 Jan) to existing claim r2-G-NKN-FRONT-009 (Radio Okapi, 14 Jan clashes at Kamandi Gite and Kibanda). Context for FIRE-003 (17 Jan 2025): reports found cover 14-15 January, not 17 January; whether Luofu lies near that cluster was not checked against a gazetteer.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that new fighting broke out on Monday 26 January between Wazalendo fighters and AFC/M23 rebels in Mighende village, about thirty kilometres from Lubero-Centre, Lubero territory; according to local sources, AFC/M23 elements attacked a Wazalendo position and burned its camp.
claims.place_as_written: Mighende village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; page dated mer 28/01/2026 so 26 January is 2026 (a Monday). Single report citing local sources.
claims.researcher_note: Single local-sourced report. Date 26 January is stated by the page (year from page date 28/01/2026). Not within a FIRE cluster window of this unit.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that violent fighting had opposed AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo self-defence groups since Monday 30 March in several localities of southern Lubero territory; according to local and security sources, the first clashes broke out on Monday around 5 am in the villages of Kalonge and Lubango, about thirty kilometres from the territorial capital, where AFC/M23 forces reportedly attacked Wazalendo elements of the Mouvement des résistants des patriotes congolais (MRPC) recently deployed after a partial rebel withdrawal. The fighting displaced civilians, and several sources said AFC/M23 had reportedly retaken control of the villages concerned.
claims.place_as_written: Kalonge and Lubango villages, southern Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact (page mar 31/03/2026). Category territorial_control was not carried by the statement; added the page's hedged control clause (contiguous passage containing the full stored excerpt) rather than change category. Control change is hedged by the source ('aurait repris le contrôle').
claims.researcher_note: Complements held claim r1-NKN-2026H1-002 (23 March 2026 partial M23 withdrawal from Lubero villages). Radio Okapi also reports (same page) new fighting on Tuesday at Katambi, Kirikiri and Byanze and says AFC/M23 reportedly resumed control of the villages concerned; FARDC response is cut off in the passage retrieved. Control entry is hedged ('aurait'). Not matched to a FIRE cluster (nearest FIRE-118, 16 Mar 2026, is two weeks earlier).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Lunyasenge, which it described as about fifty kilometres west of Lake Edward, was taken on 2 May by AFC/M23 rebels supported by the Rwandan army, according to Kinshasa and several international reports, and that violent fighting opposed the rebels and Congolese soldiers; the toll remained unclear, but several local sources spoke of heavy human losses.
claims.place_as_written: Lunyasenge, North Kivu (territory not stated by the source)
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23, supported by the Rwandan army per Kinshasa and international reports; FARDC
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact (page mar 06/05/2025, byline Josué Mutanava, à Goma). Figures field rested on an unexcerpted sentence: supplied the contiguous passage. Territory field (provisionally Lubero) is not stated by the page: cleared to null. The page does not name Lunyasenge's territory; the 'about 50 km west of Lake Edward' description is the outlet's and was not checked against a gazetteer. Rwandan army support is Kinshasa's and international reports' account; no AFC/M23 account was searched for.
claims.researcher_note: Territory set to Lubero provisionally from the 'Lubero' context of later claims on Lunyasenge (r1-NKN-2026H1-002); this page does not name the territory, reviewers should check against the gazetteer. Lunyasenge is among the lead settlements near FIRE-108 (Jan 2026), a different date.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that in a communiqué published on 4 May the Congolese army confirmed the loss of Lunyasenge, denouncing a flagrant violation of the ceasefire in force, and that Colonel Mak Hazukay, FARDC spokesperson in the Grand-Nord, reaffirmed the army's will to 'riposter sur tous les fronts' if the threats persisted.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Statement keeps the communiqué and the spokesperson's remark as separate reported items. Reported via Actualite.cd; the communiqué itself was not retrieved. The page does not say explicitly that Hazukay's words were in the communiqué.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement (Kinshasa). AFC/M23 account of Lunyasenge not found in the searches run for this unit.

claims.text: ACLED reported that by the end of the first quarter of 2025 the M23-RDF offensive had reached an ADF camp in Lubero territory under the leadership of Ahmad Mahmood Hassan, commonly called Abwakasi.
claims.place_as_written: ADF camp in Lubero territory (exact place not stated), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23-RDF offensive; ADF camp under Ahmad Mahmood Hassan (Abwakasi)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact on retained ACLED report page (footnoted sentence). Worded as ACLED's report; date is approximate (by end of March 2025). ACLED analytical report (18 June 2025); it gives no date or place for the encounter, and 'M23-RDF' is ACLED's own label.
claims.researcher_note: Analytical statement by ACLED, not an event report: no date or village of the encounter is given. Context for the 17 Mar 2025 lead FIRE-021 but not tied to it. Existing GoE claims r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-008 place Abwakasi's unit in Lubero.

claims.text: Radio Moto Beni-Butembo (RMBB) reported that suspected ADF rebels attacked Ngadi neighbourhood, Ruwenzori commune, in the city of Beni, in the night of Saturday to Sunday 31 May 2026, targeting among other places the Ngadi pygmy camp; the provisional toll was at least 7 killed, mostly pygmies including the comedian Shukurani Nzanzu Mangese, six bodies being found early on Sunday and the seventh victim dying of wounds in a health facility, and sources on site said several other civilians were missing.
claims.place_as_written: Ngadi neighbourhood, Ruwenzori commune, Beni city, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: suspected ADF rebels ("présumés rebelles de l’ADF")
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact (byline Rédaction RMBB). 'Beni city' was not in the stored excerpt: supplied the contiguous lead sentence. Grade lowered to C: single local radio report, perpetrators 'présumés'.
claims.researcher_note: Local community radio, Beni town (RMBB). Adds the named victim and the missing to held claim r4-G-LOCAL-NK-009 (Radio Okapi, Mukwege condemnation). The page is dated 31 May 2026. Ngadi is in Beni city, roughly 50 km from the FIRE-134 cluster at Kasindi (27-31 May 2026); not the same place.

claims.text: OCHA reported in a weekly regional 'latest events at a glance' infographic that fighting in Masisi and Lubero had displaced over 100,000 people, disrupted health services and affected food supplies to Lubero, and that a boat carrying people fleeing the fighting on Lake Edward sank, leaving 22 people missing.
claims.place_as_written: Masisi and Lubero territories; Lake Edward, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact on ReliefWeb page (Source OCHA, posted 25 Feb 2025). Grade B, not A: a single UN situation infographic, not a documented investigation. The 100,000 figure combines Masisi and Lubero and need not be limited to the 18-24 February week; the infographic gives no date for the boat sinking.
claims.researcher_note: Infographic text published by OCHA on ReliefWeb. Combined Masisi and Lubero figure, not split by territory. Health-service disruption is stated without facility names.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that Muhindo Tafuteni, president of the local civil society, said ADF activism was continuing in the Bapere sector and the Manzia and Mwenye groupements, and that 'for the month of January alone, we deplore more than 52 people killed'; he also said schools and health structures were no longer functioning in that part of the country.
claims.place_as_written: Bapere sector and Manzia and Mwenye groupements, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: ADF, as attributed by the civil society speaker
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact (page 10/02/2026). Reworded so the toll stays in the speaker's words and is not tied to the western area more tightly than the quote allows. The 52 figure is the speaker's; it is not clear from the quote whether it covers only the Bapere/Manzia/Mwenye area. Radio Okapi's own lead gives about 52 killed in January across Beni and Lubero territories. No health facility is named.
claims.researcher_note: Civil-society claim, no facility named; sits alongside held claims r1-ATR-NK-2026-010/012 (Jan 2026 tolls; one health post burned). Manzia groupement is the area of lead cluster FIRE-065 (Aug 2025) but the dates differ.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that fighting broke out on a Thursday morning in the villages of Kahwela, Kivumu and Luhemba in Fizi territory between Wazalendo forces and Twirwaneho fighters allied to the AFC-M23; it said the Wazalendo accused the Twirwaneho of launching attacks targeting cultivators in those localities.
claims.place_as_written: Kahwela, Kivumu, Luhemba (Fizi territory), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo forces; Twirwaneho fighters allied to the AFC-M23 (as the source names them)
claims.verification_note: Page read in full; excerpt and weekday sentence verified. Wazalendo accusation kept as party account. Weekday only ('ce jeudi matin'); the day is inferred from the page date (11 Sep 2025, a Thursday). 'Fizi territory' and 'jeudi' are on the page but not in the stored excerpt. The page also carries a Wazalendo CPLC/FABB spokesperson's claim to have repulsed the attack (not in this claim).
claims.researcher_note: Weekday only ('ce jeudi matin'); date computed from weekday and publication date 2025-09-11 (a Thursday). Single local outlet. Kivumu and Luhemba also appear among the settlements near fire cluster FIRE-238 (Aug 2026) but this claim is Sept 2025.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Twirwaneho fighters allied to the AFC-M23 accused the Congolese army, in coalition with the Burundian army, of a targeted attack on the village of Mikenge near Minembwe, and that according to their statements the attack took place on 10 September with the support of Wazalendo forces.
claims.actor_as_written: Congolese army (FARDC) in coalition with the Burundian army and Wazalendo, as alleged by Twirwaneho
claims.verification_note: Verified on page; attribution to Twirwaneho preserved. Twirwaneho party account relayed by the outlet; not independently confirmed. The page places Mikenge 'près de Minembwe'; other sources place Mikenge in Mwenga territory.
claims.researcher_note: Party account (Twirwaneho) relayed by the outlet; not independently confirmed in the article. Mikenge is in Mwenga territory in other sources; the outlet places it 'near Minembwe'. Relates to the Sept 2025 clusters near Mikenge (e.g. FIRE-081, settlement Kilulwe (Mikenge I)).

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that from 10 to 27 August 2026 at least 23 people were killed, 17 seriously wounded and at least six villages burned in fighting between AFC-M23-Twirwaneho troops and the DRC armed forces and their allies in the Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory; it said the figures were given by the Conseil Local de la Jeunesse d'Itombwe after monitoring.
claims.place_as_written: Itombwe sector (Mwenga territory), South Kivu; fighting also extended to the hauts plateaux of Fizi and the moyens plateaux of Uvira
claims.actor_as_written: AFC-M23-Twirwaneho troops and FARDC and allies (as the source names them)
claims.verification_note: Figures match the page exactly (23 / 17 / six). Tally from a local youth council relayed by Radio Maendeleo; villages not named; burning not attributed to a party. Itombwe sector is in Mwenga territory (as printed), not Fizi.
claims.researcher_note: Local radio (Bukavu) relaying a youth-council monitoring tally; village names not printed. Itombwe sector is in Mwenga territory, outside the Fizi packet, but the same article covers Point Zéro (Fizi) and the 'hauts plateaux de Fizi'. No burning attributed to a specific party.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that the Conseil Local de la Jeunesse d'Itombwe counted at least 1100 households, more than six thousand people, displaced in the bush or in host villages in that part of South Kivu, and that sources reported continued drone and mortar bombardments at Point Zéro in Fizi territory, causing panic and new displacement.
claims.place_as_written: Itombwe sector (Mwenga); Point Zéro (Fizi territory), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Figures field reworded to the printed form; 'Itombwe area' narrowed to the printed 'cette partie du Sud-Kivu'. Figure printed in words ('plus de six mille'), not as 6,000. Sources for the Point Zéro bombardments are unnamed; no party is named as firing. Radio Maendeleo places Point Zéro in Fizi territory; Actualite.cd (19 Sep 2026) places it in Mwenga territory.
claims.researcher_note: Same article as the previous claim. 'Sources' for the Point Zéro bombardments are unnamed.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that over the weekend and until Monday morning 31 August 2026 the Kipupu-Mikenge axis was the scene of violent clashes between the two sides as far as the area known as Filon 14 in the Itombwe massif.
claims.place_as_written: Kipupu-Mikenge axis, up to 'Filon 14' (Itombwe massif), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC-M23-Twirwaneho and FARDC with allies (as the source names them)
claims.verification_note: Verified on page. 'Les deux antagonistes' is read from the article's opening paragraph; the sentence itself does not name them. Weekend dates are approximate.
claims.researcher_note: Weekend dates computed from 'week-end dernier' and Monday 31 August; range approximate.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that nearly 41.900 people displaced by clashes between AFC/M23 elements and FARDC/Wazalendo were living in precarious conditions in villages including Nakiele, Kilumbi and Kanguli in Fizi territory; it quoted civil society as saying its assessments counted 41.952 displaced persons in 8618 households, living without sufficient access to food, drinking water, health care or shelter.
claims.place_as_written: Nakiele, Kilumbi, Kanguli health areas (Fizi territory), South Kivu; 17 villages listed incl. Point zéro, Kitasha, Mikenge 1 and 2, Kakenge, Abala
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed (displacement from AFC/M23 vs FARDC/Wazalendo clashes)
claims.verification_note: Numbers restored to the printed form; the 41.952 figure attributed to civil society rather than the outlet. Discrepancy on the page: the advocacy note is attributed to 'la société civile des moyens plateaux de Fizi' in one sentence and the quote to 'la société civile des moyens plateaux d'Uvira' in the next. Headline says 'près de 42.000'. Relevant to civilian access to health care (lack of access stated, no attack on facilities).
claims.researcher_note: Quote is from the civil-society advocacy note; the article's own headline says 'près de 42.000'. The article states the note comes from 'la société civile des moyens plateaux de Fizi' in one sentence and 'd'Uvira' in another. Sector spelled 'Tanganyika' in the headline.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that new fighting at the start of the week led to the AFC/M23-Twirwaneho troops taking the centre of the village of Kanguli since Wednesday 22 July.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23-Twirwaneho troops (as the source names them)
claims.verification_note: Verified on page. Holder as printed: 'les troupes de l’AFC/M23-Twirwaneho' took the centre of the village. Year from the page date (25 Jul 2026). The page places Kanguli about 40 km from Lusenda camp and about 65 km from Baraka.
claims.researcher_note: Year taken from the page's 'Last updated 2026/07/25'. The same article places Kanguli about 40 km from Lusenda refugee camp and about 65 km from Baraka. Kanguli is among the villages listed in the 12 Sept 2026 displacement note (health area Kanguli). Relates to FIRE-185 (23-27 Jul 2026) only in time.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, that AFC/M23 troops still controlled the village of Point Zéro and its surroundings, while the FARDC kept their positions at Kipupu, Mulima, Mukera and as far as Fizi-Centre.
claims.place_as_written: Point Zéro, Kipupu, Mulima, Mukera, Fizi-Centre (Fizi / Mwenga), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23; FARDC (as the source names them)
claims.verification_note: Verified on page. Holders as printed: AFC/M23 at Point Zéro; FARDC at Kipupu, Mulima, Mukera, Fizi-Centre. The page calls Kipupu chef-lieu of Itombwe sector.
claims.researcher_note: Kipupu is described in the same article as chef-lieu of Itombwe sector.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 seized Kipupu centre on Friday 10 July before withdrawing, that clashes over control were reported at Kipupu on 12-13 July, and that the chef-lieu of the Itombwe sector then returned to the control of the army and its allies.
claims.place_as_written: Kipupu (Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and allies; FARDC and Wazalendo (as the source names them)
claims.verification_note: 'Citing local sources in the Itombwe sector' removed: this passage is the outlet's own narration; local sources are cited for other sentences. The page places Kipupu in Mwenga territory and says calm was observed on 14 July after the government forces retook it. Year from the page date (16 Jul 2026).
claims.researcher_note: Kipupu is in Mwenga territory (Itombwe sector); it appears near FIRE-081 (Sept 2025), not near the July 2026 Fizi clusters. Same article lists displacement from Kipupu to Kiseke, Tumungu, Alenga, Nabindi, Natulonge, Mikembenge and Lubunga (conseil local de la jeunesse d'Itombwe).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the vice-governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Elakano, at a security council meeting held on Monday in Uvira, denied rumours of the fall of Baraka to the rebels and urged the population to stay calm and carry on with their activities.
claims.verification_note: Verified on page. Provincial official's statement, recorded as 'the vice-governor said'. Day inferred from 'ce lundi' and the page date (7 Jul 2026).
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from 'ce lundi' and the page's 7 July 2026 publication date. The same page reports that several sources announced the taking of Mikenge and Point Zéro by Twirwaneho fighters backed by the RDF (Radio Okapi's wording), and that the Fizi territory administrator denounced violations of Congolese airspace by drones from Rwanda.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the army announced its 'repli stratégique' from Point Zéro for tactical reasons, and that the spokesperson of operation Sokola 2 South Kivu, sous-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi, said the villages retaken by the FARDC were Kashamata, Wihene and Kimete, with the rebels forced to fall back towards Rugezi and Bigaragara, south of Minembwe.
claims.place_as_written: Point Zéro; Kashamata, Wihene, Kimete (Fizi territory), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC; Twirwaneho (as the source names them)
claims.verification_note: Operation name corrected to the printed 'Sokola 2'; 'Fizi territory' clause moved to the page's lead sentence. FARDC party account. The page spells the operation 'Sokola 2' (the draft had 'Sukola 2') and the group 'Twiraneho'. The same page says several sources reported the taking of Mikenge and Point Zéro by Twirwaneho 'appuyés par les RDF' (Radio Okapi's wording).
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates an existing Actualite.cd claim (r1-UV-2026Q3-001, 6 July) on Kimete/Wihene/Kashamata; adds the Point Zéro withdrawal statement. Radio Okapi spells the group 'Twiraneho'.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing local sources, violent clashes on Wednesday 1 July 2026 at Mikenge and its surroundings in the Minembwe highlands; it said that for a month Twirwaneho allied to the AFC/M23 had been fighting the Congolese army backed by the Burundian army and Wazalendo, and that civil-society sources said the fighting reportedly caused several victims.
claims.place_as_written: Mikenge and surroundings (Minembwe highlands), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho/AFC-M23; FARDC backed by the Burundian army and Wazalendo (as the source names them)
claims.verification_note: Each clause verified on page. 'Plusieurs victimes' is conditional ('auraient') and unquantified. Mikenge is placed in Mwenga territory by other sources.
claims.researcher_note: Several statements are in one passage. Mikenge is in Mwenga territory per other sources; tagged Fizi here as the outlet places it in the Minembwe highlands.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that violent clashes took place on Sunday 14 June 2026 at Ilundu, a few kilometres from the centre of Minembwe, between the Twirwaneho and the FARDC, and that over the weekend aerial bombardments by FARDC Sukhoï-25 aircraft were recorded at Minembwe, causing many victims.
claims.place_as_written: Ilundu and Minembwe (Fizi territory), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho; FARDC (Sukhoï-25 aircraft) (as the source names them)
claims.verification_note: 'Citing concordant sources' removed: these two sentences are the outlet's narration; 'Sukhoi' restored to the printed 'Sukhoï-25'. 'De nombreuses victimes' is unquantified and unsourced in the article. The page also says rumours of Congolese/Burundian army and Wazalendo presence in Minembwe were not confirmed by independent sources, and (citing concordant sources) that Minembwe remained under Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 control.
claims.researcher_note: The article also says rumours of Congolese/Burundian army and Wazalendo presence in Minembwe were unconfirmed by independent sources. Ilundu is also in existing claims for 24 June 2026.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that more than 53 000 people fled to localities in the Fizi and Nundu health zones between August and October 2026 after intensified clashes in the hauts plateaux of Fizi; it reported OCHA as adding that fighting in early September and from 20 to 25 September reportedly caused civilian casualties and damaged essential infrastructure.
claims.place_as_written: Fizi and Nundu health zones (Fizi territory), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not named in the stored excerpts (OCHA relayed by Radio Maendeleo)
claims.verification_note: Publication-date clause, the household figure and the FRN naming removed as not in the stored excerpts; number kept in the printed '53 000' form. Secondary relay; the OCHA report itself was not located. Excerpt gap: the page also says the report was published in October 2026 and covers 1-30 September 2026, names the armed side as the 'Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN)' against FARDC, Wazalendo and the Burundian army, and gives a further household figure for the Kimbi-Lulenge and Kabambare health zones; these are not in the stored excerpts and are left out. Casualties are conditional ('auraient') and unquantified. Internal inconsistency: an August-October displacement figure in a report said to cover September.
claims.researcher_note: Secondary relay of the OCHA report (period 1-30 September 2026 per the article); original OCHA document not located. The article names the armed side as the 'Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN)', as printed.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that violent clashes continued at Point Zéro, which it placed in Mwenga territory, from the morning of 'ce 20 Septembre 2026', while several local sources said the fighting resumed there from the morning of 19 September; sources said a coalition of the FARDC, Wazalendo and 'les burundais' faced an AFC/Red Tabara Twirwaneho coalition; it said fighting had spilled over 'since yesterday' into the villages of Biziba Irumba on the periphery of Minembwe in Fizi territory, and that on 18 September fighting was concentrated in Natulonge and Kabindo in Fizi territory.
claims.place_as_written: Point Zéro; Biziba Irumba (Minembwe periphery); Natulonge; Kabindo, Fizi / Mwenga, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC, Wazalendo and Burundians vs AFC/Red Tabara/Twirwaneho (as the source names them)
claims.verification_note: Statement rewritten to show the page's own 20 September wording beside the local sources' 19 September, to keep 'depuis hier' unresolved, and to attribute only the 19 September resumption and the coalition line to sources (the Biziba Irumba and 18 September lines are the outlet's narration). Date widened to a range ending 20 Sep. Date discrepancy on the page: the page is dated 19 Sep 2026 but its first sentence says clashes continued from the morning of 'ce 20 Septembre 2026', while local sources date the resumption to 19 September; 'depuis hier' (Biziba Irumba) is therefore 18 or 19 September. Territory discrepancy: Actualite.cd places Point Zéro in Mwenga territory; Radio Maendeleo (25 Jul and 31 Aug 2026) places it in Fizi territory. The coalition line is from unnamed 'sources du milieu'.
claims.researcher_note: The article's body says the fighting continued 'depuis la matinée de ce 20 Septembre' while the page is dated 19/09/2026: internal date inconsistency, flagged. Natulonge also appears (per Actualite.cd 16 Jul 2026) as a displacement destination south of Kipupu.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that from 01:00 on Friday 16 October 2026 the coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime were intensely bombarding Rugezi and its surroundings in the Minembwe region with heavy artillery and kamikaze drones.
claims.actor_as_written: FRN (Front pour la Refondation de la Nation), via spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, accusing the 'coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime' (FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo militias, foreign mercenaries and elements of the Burundi National Defence Force, as he listed them)
claims.verification_note: Statement verified verbatim on the full page and correctly worded as the FRN spokesperson's claim. Actor field corrected: the page does not say FRN is AFC/M23 (it describes FRN as a coalition led by former head of state Joseph Kabila), so the parenthetical equating the two was an inference and is removed. Party allegation (FRN says); no independent confirmation and no Kinshasa response on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Party allegation relayed by a Congolese outlet; no independent confirmation or Kinshasa response on the page. Rugezi is in the Minembwe highlands; the page does not tie it to the Mikenge/Senge settlements of cluster FIRE-282. The source calls the movement FRN and describes it as a coalition led by Joseph Kabila; AFC/M23 is called FRN in the 17 Oct Radio Okapi page too.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the FRN accused government forces on Monday 19 October 2026 of having bombarded Rugezi and its surroundings in the Minembwe region between the evening of Saturday 17 and Sunday 18 October 2026; it also reported that Colonel Fidèle Rugabo, described as spokesperson of FRN fighters in the Minembwe area, said the populations of Rugezi and Gipimo were attacked during the night.
claims.place_as_written: Rugezi and Gipimo (Minembwe region), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FRN, accusing government forces (FARDC, FDLR, Mai-Mai militias, foreign mercenaries, Burundi National Defence Force, as listed by the source)
claims.verification_note: Both passages are on the page verbatim; attribution kept as FRN's accusation; actor list matches the page. Both sources are the same page and the same party origin, so C. Party allegation (FRN says); the 'attacks' timing is the outlet's wording of the FRN account. No Kinshasa response on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Party allegation relayed by a media outlet; no response from Kinshasa on the page. Dates from weekday-free text (17-18 October stated).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, according to local civil society, clashes between AFC/M23 and FARDC supported by Wazalendo lasted all day Sunday at Kashaka toward Kigogo and on the national road toward Ngenga, which, in the words of the Mwenga civil society president Samuel Itebo, created insecurity at Kasika; State exam papers started late in several villages of Lwindi chiefdom as a result.
claims.place_as_written: Kashaka, Kigogo, Ngenga road and Kasika, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga
claims.verification_note: Both passages verified on the full page; publication date 2026-06-23 confirmed in page metadata. Single local civil-society origin. excerpt_en flag on source 1 is a false positive (translation matches the excerpt). Date 21 June 2026 is computed from 'dimanche' and the 23 June 2026 (Tuesday) publication date; approximate. The page elsewhere says the belligerents clashed on Sunday evening.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('dimanche') and publication date Tuesday 23 June 2026: Sunday 21 June 2026 (page also says the evening of Sunday). Local civil-society source. Kigogo here may or may not be the Kigogo of the RGC lead points for FIRE-152/FIRE-245; the page does not locate it.

claims.text: Enquete.cd reported that, according to residents and civil-society actors, several houses were burned at Kiseke (Mwenga territory) after fighting between FARDC and the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition spread to Kiseke and Nabindi, that civilian victims including women and children 'would have died in the flames', and that house fires were also reported at Muhabo, Natulinge, Nabindi, Kisemu, Kalulu and Senge; the page said no official toll had been communicated and did not say who set the fires.
claims.place_as_written: Kiseke, Muhabo, Natulinge, Nabindi, Kisemu, Kalulu and Senge, Mwenga-Kipupu axis, Mwenga
claims.actor_as_written: Not attributed by the source (fighting parties: FARDC and the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition, as the source names them)
claims.verification_note: Kiseke burnings and the list of villages match the page verbatim. Corrected to tie the burnings to the fighting only as the page does (fighting spread to Kiseke/Nabindi), to state that no perpetrator of the fires is named, and to add the page's 'no official toll'. The conditional on deaths is preserved. Deaths in the fires are conditional ('auraient péri') and unquantified; the source does not attribute the burnings to either party; drone use alleged by local and military sources lacked independent confirmation.
claims.researcher_note: Local sources, unconfirmed; the page says no official toll had been communicated and that drone use alleged by local and military sources lacked independent confirmation. Unit/commanders not named. Senge also appears among the RGC lead points of cluster FIRE-282 (14-16 October 2026), a different date.

claims.text: Enquete.cd reported that fighting was reported from the morning of 'this Sunday' in the Cidasa-Kasika zone, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga, reportedly opposing FARDC supported by Wazalendo fighters and Burundian forces to AFC-M23 elements, and that the fighting had already displaced several residents; new clashes were also reported around the village of Kaulile.
claims.place_as_written: Cidasa-Kasika zone and Kaulile, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC supported by Wazalendo and Burundian forces; AFC-M23
claims.verification_note: Both passages verified on the full page; dateline and metadata 2026-08-31 confirmed. Conditional wording preserved as 'reportedly'. excerpt_en flag is a false positive (FARDC spelled out in the translation). Each stored excerpt joins two page paragraphs; the wording of each is verbatim. Burundian forces' involvement is conditional in the source ('opposeraient'). Date 30 August 2026 is computed from 'ce dimanche' under a Monday 31 August dateline; approximate.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('ce dimanche') and the page date of 31 August 2026 (a Monday): Sunday 30 August 2026. Radio Maendeleo on the same fighting is already held (r1-ATR-SK-2026-010); this adds the Burundian-forces attribution and displacement as printed by Enquete.cd.

claims.text: MSF said that in Shabunda territory more than 260,000 people faced measles and cholera epidemics, due to limited access to drinking water and sanitation facilities, coupled with the displacement of people who fled violence; it said 1,002 cholera cases with 39 deaths had been recorded since 3 July 2026, according to local authorities, and that 7,620 measles cases had been reported, with 467 deaths notified.
claims.verification_note: All figures match the MSF page (4 September 2026). '260 000' is printed with a space in the excerpt, so the 260000 flag is a formatting false positive; '4' in the flag comes from the figures field's release date, not the statement. Corrected 'linked to' to 'due to' (dûes à) and kept the measles figures as reported/notified, as printed. Epidemic context for health access, not an attack on health care. The cholera figures are credited to local authorities; the page gives no period for the measles figures.
claims.researcher_note: Epidemic context for civilian health access in Shabunda, not an attack on health care. Actualite.cd carried the same release on 4 September 2026 (not cited). The release does not state the measles figures' period beyond the sentence quoted.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources in the region, that at least ten civilians, mostly farmers, were killed on Wednesday 22 January at Kahumiro, near Virunga National Park in Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory), and that they were executed by M23/RDF coalition elements.
claims.place_as_written: Kahumiro, Bambo groupement, Bwito chiefdom (near Virunga park), Rutshuru
claims.actor_as_written: M23/RDF coalition, as alleged by local sources
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and matches page; excerpt_en flag is a false positive (capitalised 'National Park' translates 'parc national'). Page prints 22 January (publication 23/01/2025, a Thursday; 22 Jan 2025 was a Wednesday). The same page also reports 9 civilians killed by M23 at Kihondo on Wednesday 15 January (possible lead for another claim). Single outlet; the page itself says the facts are hard to confirm with other sources. The page names the youth-parliament speaker both 'Chirac Mafula' and 'Isaac Mafula'.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet; source quoted is Chirac Mafula, youth parliament president in Bwito (named in page). Places the killing 22 Jan, 3 days after the end of cluster FIRE-001 (to 19 Jan); proximity of Kahumiro to the FIRE-001 centre not verified. M23/AFC account not found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting was reported on Tuesday in the Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory), with M23 initiating the attack, in the agglomeration of Lubwe Sud.
claims.place_as_written: Lubwe Sud, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Excerpt prints only 'ce mardi'; page is dated mar 14/01/2025, so date 2025-01-14 is consistent. Graded C rather than B: single local outlet relying on unnamed sources and a government official.
claims.researcher_note: Within the 1-19 Jan FIRE-001 window; place relation to the cluster not established.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that at least five M23/RDF coalition elements were killed in an ambush by wazalendo fighters near Kiseguro in the Binza groupement (Rutshuru), and, citing its sources, that the M23 rebels had been surprised taking agricultural produce from farmers.
claims.place_as_written: Kiseguro and Ngwenda, Binza groupement, Rutshuru
claims.verification_note: Narrowed attribution: the ambush/toll sentence is the outlet's own narration, while 'selon nos sources' attaches only to the produce-taking clause. Added the Kiseguro/Ngwenda clause the location field relies on. Date range kept, flagged as a weekday/date conflict in the source. Date conflict on the page: it prints 'lundi 14 janvier 2025', but 14 January 2025 was a Tuesday (the article itself is dated Tuesday 14/01/2025, 15:30). The ambush was on Monday 13 or Tuesday 14 January; recorded as a range. Casualty figure is the outlet's, with no party confirmation. The page also reports heavy and light weapons fire for several hours after the ambush at Kiseguro and Ngwenda (not in the stored excerpt).
claims.researcher_note: The page prints 'lundi 14 janvier 2025' although 14 January 2025 was a Tuesday; date given as a range. Single local source; pro-government framing.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that violent clashes broke out from the morning of Wednesday 12 November 2025 in the Bukombo groupement (Rutshuru), particularly in the villages of Maruho, Machazo, Manyoni and Mudugugudu, and that further AFC-M23 attacks on Wazalendo positions were reported at Kibunanwa and Busukura in Mutanda groupement, with displaced people heading to Bambo, Lusogha, Kashalira and Kishishe.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact and match the page (published 2025-11-12). Both sources are the same article. Graded C rather than B: single local outlet citing unnamed sources and an anonymous resident. The page's statement that the fighting violates the Qatar-facilitated ceasefire is the outlet's framing.
claims.researcher_note: Overlaps FIRE-098/099 window (11 Nov-8 Dec); proximity of Bukombo/Mutanda villages to cluster centres not established. Page says the fighting violates the Qatar-facilitated ceasefire (publisher's framing).

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing local sources, that at least three bodies were found on the morning of Tuesday 11 November at Manyoni, Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru), the day after violent clashes between Wazalendo and AFC-M23, and that the victims were said to be three men killed with a bladed weapon.
claims.place_as_written: Manyoni, Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; '23' flag is a false positive from 'AFC-M23'. Page names no perpetrator and no victims; actor 'not attributed by the source' is correct. Page dates the preceding fighting to Monday 10 November.
claims.researcher_note: Bodies unidentified per the page; perpetrator not named; page says it is hard to know which side controls Manyoni.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that at least five people were killed and nine wounded on the night of Friday to Saturday 6 December 2025 during an incursion of armed bandits it described as assimilated to the Wazalendo in the Katsiru agglomeration, Bukombo groupement (Rutshuru). A former presenter and journalist of Radio Communautaire de Mweso, Rachid Kazadi, was among the dead.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC-M23 patrollers; armed bandits 'assimilés aux Wazalendo'
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; '23' flag comes from 'AFC-M23', which no stored excerpt prints, so the patroller exchange was moved to the note pending an excerpt extension. Narrowed so the statement does not imply who caused the casualties. 6 December 2025 was a Saturday, consistent. Perpetrator attribution is uncertain on the page (a resident says it 'could be' Wazalendo). Health: most wounded, including women and children, treated at Mweso general referral hospital. The page also says, citing anonymous sources, that the incursion was followed by an exchange of fire between the bandits and AFC-M23 patrollers, during which the assailants opened fire, hitting several civilians, and quotes a resident saying the bandits' origin is unknown but 'could be' Wazalendo (not in the stored excerpt; extend with source_edits.py add_excerpt).
claims.researcher_note: Date: Friday night to Saturday per page; page text prints 6 December. Wounded treated at Mweso general referral hospital per page. Anonymous residents; attribution uncertain (resident says it 'could be' Wazalendo). Within the FIRE-098 window (to 8 Dec); proximity unverified.

claims.text: Opinion Info reported a provisional toll of five dead, nearly twenty seriously wounded and about ten women raped, according to local sources contacted on 4 November 2025, in fighting since the start of that week between M23-AFC rebels and CMC-FDP Wazalendo fighters in Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru; an anonymous community source also mentioned the rape of fifteen women during the fighting. The outlet does not say who committed the rapes.
claims.place_as_written: Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru (villages not named)
claims.actor_as_written: M23-AFC and CMC-FDP Wazalendo (fighting parties); perpetrators of the rapes not attributed by the source
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact on retained page. Narrowed '4 November' from a publication date to the date the local sources were contacted, as printed; kept the two rape figures separate with their own attributions; non-attribution of perpetrators stated. Both sources are passages of the same article (one origin). 'Since the start of this week' and 'anonymous' come from the page outside the stored excerpts. excerpt_en flag: capitalised Tuesday/November/North are translations of mardi/novembre/Nord, acceptable. Two different figures for rapes (about ten, per local sources; fifteen, per one anonymous community source); the page attributes the rapes to no party. 'Since the start of this week' in an article of Tuesday 4 November; start date is inferred. Page uses an illustrative photo.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet (Opinion Info, Kinshasa) citing unnamed local sources; illustrative photo only. Perpetrators of the sexual violence not stated; dates from 'since the start of this week' (week of Monday 3 November) so range is computed. Same fighting as Kivu Morning Post reports of 10-12 November (r6-F-RUT-004/005) but earlier. Does not name a village; nearby-area context for FIRE-100 (Bukombo).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the situation remained tense on the morning of Monday 10 November in the village of Kinyankuku, Bukombo groupement (Rutshuru), after fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and CMC-FDP wazalendo; citing its sources, it said hostilities began in the night from Sunday to Monday after an attack by AFC/M23 rebels on wazalendo positions. It said access to the fields on the outskirts of Kitshanga, notably on the Bukombo axis, was impossible and that farming was paralysed in the area, including at Kyahemba, a neighbouring locality also affected by the fighting.
claims.place_as_written: Kinyankuku (and neighbouring Kyahemba), Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 rebels (attack on wazalendo positions, per Actualite.cd's sources); CMC-FDP wazalendo
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. claims.text: MediaCongo, relaying ACP/MCP, reported that, according to a military spokesperson, the agglomerations of Malimba, Masango, Ruhua and Rubarati were now under the control of the loyalist army, and that the M23, Twirwaneho and allied fighters were forced to retreat towards Kashongo and Magunda.
claims.place_as_written: Malimba, Masango, Ruhua (Ruhuha), Rubarati; Kashongo and Magunda, Uvira highlands, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpts verbatim; attribution 'Selon lui' kept. Army claim only, conflicting with the local-source, civil-society and Kinyarwanda-media accounts of Malimba, Rubarati, Ruhuha and Masango (23-26 Aug 2026); each kept separate. No Twirwaneho or AFC/M23 reply found. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Army claim only. No Twirwaneho or AFC/M23 reply to this claim found in this unit. The Twirwaneho spokesperson's later claim to have retaken Rubarati and Ruhuha (12 October 2026) is held in r1-SKS-2026Q4-005.

claims.text: MediaCongo, relaying ACP/MCP, reported that the spokesperson of operations Sukola 2 Sud-Sud-Kivu said the FARDC had discovered a mass grave at Masango where civilians killed during the occupation of that agglomeration by what he called 'the forces of evil', including Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and M23, which he said were supported by Rwanda, were said to be buried.
claims.date: 2026-09-01 (statement reported 2026-09-02; dates of the killings and of the discovery not given)
claims.place_as_written: Masango, Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and M23 supported by Rwanda, as alleged by the FARDC spokesperson
claims.verification_note: Made the spokesperson's characterisations ('forces du mal', 'soutenus par le Rwanda') explicitly his. Draft date '2026-08' was an inference from another outlet; set to the statement date, with the event undated. Allegation by a party spokesperson only; conditional ('seraient enterrés'). No count, no date of the killings or of the discovery, no independent verification or exhumation reported. Lead: request access to the site from MONUSCO/UNJHRO or Congolese authorities. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Allegation by a party spokesperson only; no independent verification, exhumation, count or date of the killings or of the discovery. The article itself says Masango was occupied (no date); Bwiza.com reports capture by Twirwaneho/AFC/M23 on 26 August. Lead for investigators: ask MONUSCO/UNJHRO or the Congolese authorities for access to the site.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that local leaders said that since 20 August the inhabitants of Nzibira and surrounding localities, in Walungu territory, had been leaving their homes after violent fighting between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo, with mass displacements also reported at Lutunkulu and Luhago, and that each camp accuses the other of being behind the clashes.
claims.place_as_written: Nzibira, Lutunkulu, Luhago, Walungu territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpts verbatim; statement faithful. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Place names as printed; the page also prints 'Lutunkulu' where AfriquActu prints 'Luntukulu'. Nearness of Nzibira to the FIRE-249 and FIRE-209 clusters is not established.

claims.text: AfriquActu reported that in the locality of Luntukulu, about 75 km from Bukavu, the Congolese army supported by Wazalendo repelled on Thursday an assault by the M23 supported by the Rwandan army, and that according to local sources the fighting caused significant material damage.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and Wazalendo; M23 (the outlet says supported by the Rwandan army)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim; outlet-voice claim, single source. Pro-army framing: 'soutenu par l'armée rwandaise' is the outlet's own wording. 'jeudi' taken as 20 August 2026 (the article date, a Thursday). The same page reports an AFC-M23 communiqué accusing the FARDC of attacking its positions at Rugezi, Nyaruhinga and Mukoko (not part of this claim). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from the weekday 'jeudi' and the article's URL date 2026-08-20 (a Thursday). Pro-army framing: 'soutenu par l'armée rwandaise' is the outlet's wording, not attributed to a named source.

claims.text: The UK consolidated list of financial sanctions targets (Democratic Republic of the Congo regime, last updated 15 August 2025) lists Baudoin Ngaruye Wa Myamuro with the title 'Military Leader of the movement du Mars (M23)' and the position 'Brigadier General' (UN ref CDi.019).
claims.verification_note: All three excerpts exact and printed with the name in the retained PDF (entry 34). Statement attributes the title/position to the listing. Entry-level dates (16/02/2022, late 2014 Rwanda residence) show the listing text is stale; carried as a reader note, not in the statement. Listing's stated title/position, not a finding of the post held in 2025: the 15 August 2025 date is that of the whole list. The entry itself was last updated 16/02/2022 (listed 28/02/2013) and states he entered Rwanda on 16 March 2013 and was living in Ngoma camp, Rwanda, as of late 2014; the UN Group of Experts places him as AFC/M23 First Defence Zone commander in 2025-26.
claims.researcher_note: Issuing body's own list. The list's entry dates from the 2012 UN designation and the page does not date the title; the 15 Aug 2025 'last updated' date is that of the whole list, so this shows the listed post as held out in 2025, not an appointment date. The Group of Experts (S/2025/858 para 44; S/2026/466 para 64, already recorded) gives his operative post in 2025-26 as commander of the First Defence Zone and calls him 'Brigadier General' / 'General'. No superior is stated here.

claims.text: The UK consolidated list of financial sanctions targets (Democratic Republic of the Congo regime, last updated 15 August 2025) lists Sultani Makenga (a.k.a. 'MAKENGA, Colonel, Sultani') with the position 'Military leader of the Mouvement du 23 Mars (M23) group operating in the Democratic Republic of the Congo'.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact, name and position printed together (entry 19). Attributed as the listing's stated position. Listing's stated title/position, not a finding of the post held in 2025: the 15 August 2025 date is that of the whole list. The entry was last updated 20/01/2021 (listed 28/02/2013) and says 'In Uganda as of late 2014'. The 'Colonel' a.k.a. differs from the 'General' rank other sources print for 2025-26.
claims.researcher_note: Issuing body's own list (entry from the 2012 UN listing); shows the listed position, not a dated appointment. The Group of Experts reports him as holding overall military command in 2025-26 (already recorded). The list's 'Colonel' a.k.a. differs from the 'General' the Group of Experts prints.

claims.text: The UK consolidated list of financial sanctions targets (Democratic Republic of the Congo regime, last updated 15 August 2025) lists Bernard Maheshe Byamungu (a.k.a. TIGER ONE) with the positions 'Brigadier General' and 'Deputy Commander of operations and intelligence for M23', and its narrative says he was promoted in January 2023 to Brigadier for the Congolese Revolutionary Army and then appointed chief of staff and deputy to Sultani Makenga.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; name, ranks, posts and superior (Makenga) printed in the same entry (entry 5). The 'He' in source 1 is the same entry's narrative, contiguous with the name on the page. Listing's stated title/position, not a finding of the post held in 2025: the 15 August 2025 date is that of the whole list. Entry listed and last updated 26/10/2023; the promotion and appointment it describes date from 2023. The list prints the given names BERNARD MAHESHE; an Actualite.cd relay of the 2026 Group of Experts report printed 'Innocent Byamungu' for the third defence zone commander (name discrepancy unresolved).
claims.researcher_note: Superior stated: Makenga (CDi.008). The appointment and promotion the narrative describes date from 2023, before the window; cited only as the tie the issuing body lists in 2025. Name check: the UK/UN list prints 'BERNARD MAHESHE' Byamungu; Actualite.cd's relay of the 2026 Group of Experts report (existing claim r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-002) printed 'Innocent Byamungu' for the commander of the third defence zone, while the Group of Experts text prints only 'General Byamungu'. This list supports Bernard as the name used by an official body; the third-zone identification itself rests on the Group of Experts, not on this list.

claims.text: The UK consolidated list of financial sanctions targets (Democratic Republic of the Congo regime, last updated 15 August 2025) lists Willy Ngoma with the positions 'Major' and 'Military spokesperson for M23'.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact (entry 35); attributed as the listing's stated position. Listing's stated title/position, not a finding of the post held in 2025: the 15 August 2025 date is that of the whole list. Entry listed 21/02/2024, last updated 23/02/2024; the listed rank 'Major' may not match the rank he uses in 2025-26.
claims.researcher_note: Issuing body's own list; listed rank dates from the UN listing and may not match the rank he uses in 2025. No superior stated.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing local civil society, that Wazalendo of the MCDPIN group of 'Monsieur Haguma Kanyengwenye Maik Maik' and of 'Monsieur Grevisse Nsimparinga' systematically looted civilians' property at Chambombo, a village of Nyalugusha in Ziralo groupement, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe, on Monday 13 April 2026.
claims.place_as_written: Chambombo, Nyalugusha village, Ziralo groupement, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo of the MCDPIN group of Haguma Kanyengwenye Maik Maik and Grevisse Nsimparinga
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact on the retained page (byline 'La Rédaction'); the same page says Chambombo was taken by Wazalendo that Monday and retaken by AFC/M23 around 17h. No existing claim covers this looting or the MCDPIN tie (checked Chambombo claims). Single local outlet relaying civil society. The article prints no post or rank for either man; 'du groupe MCDPIN de' gives a group tie only. Actualite.cd (r1-SKN-2026Q2-002) spells the second name 'Nsimparingira' and treats Haguma Kanyengwenye's group as separate from MCDPIN.
claims.researcher_note: Names Haguma Kanyengwenye's group as MCDPIN (Actualite.cd 7 April 2026, already recorded in r1-SKN-2026Q2-002, prints 'le MCDPIN de Grevisse Nsimparingira, ainsi que celui de Haguma Kanyengwenye', i.e. a separate group of his, and spells the second name Nsimparingira; Kivu Morning Post prints Nsimparinga and treats the two as one MCDPIN). No post, rank or superior is printed for him in either piece. The same piece says Chambombo was taken by Wazalendo on 13 April and retaken by AFC/M23 around 17:00. Category kept as unit_commander for the unit tie; the looting allegation is the incident attached to it.

claims.text: Amnesty International described Dominique 'Domi' Kamanzi Ndaruhutse as CMC-FDP's top commander and said he has fought with various Nyatura groups for more than 10 years and has, according to the UN Group of Experts on DRC, collaborated with the FDLR, particularly in Rutshuru's Bwito area.
claims.verification_note: Page already cited by r1-POL-2026-011, r1-SV-2026-026, r1-POL-2026-012 and r1-SV-2026-027 (claim_search); none records the commander or the FDLR tie, so the claim is kept for that tie only. The Gashegu spokesperson / 16 June 2026 written reply clause is narrowed out: it duplicates r1-POL-2026-012. Source 2 no longer carries any clause. Source 1's 'He' follows directly after the name on the page (verified in the retained copy). The FDLR collaboration is Amnesty's attribution to the UN Group of Experts, not Amnesty's own finding. The Group of Experts separately reports CMC-FDP as led by Dominique Ndaruhutse (r2-G-DOC-858-031).
claims.researcher_note: RULE FLAG: this Amnesty page is already cited by existing claims (r1-POL-2026-011, r1-SV-2026-026 and others); it is re-cited here only because none of them records the command and FDLR tie below, which is the tie the brief asks for. Drop this claim if the already-cited rule is applied strictly. The 2024 EU listing the first excerpt mentions is before the window and is not asserted in the statement. The FDLR collaboration is Amnesty's attribution to the Group of Experts, not Amnesty's own finding. Gashegu is printed only as spokesperson; no command post for him is stated. Amnesty says CMC-FDP denied responsibility (existing claim r1-POL-2026-012).

claims.text: The Sentry reported that Ahmad Mahmood Hassan (also known as Abwakasi) leads operations along the Lubero-Bapere-Manguredjipa axis, with headquarters in Lohoa and positions across Batike, Baredje and Bapukara.
claims.actor_as_written: ADF (Abwakasi group), as The Sentry names it
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on the PDF (p.7). Present-tense post and positions are The Sentry's; date is the report date, precision month is correct. The Sentry's accompanying map shows 'ADF deployment areas as of October 2025'; the sentence itself is undated.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates the GoE placement of Abwakasi's unit in Lubero (existing claims r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-007/-008) with a second, independent NGO source and adds the headquarters (Lohoa) and named positions. The Sentry's map caption dates deployment areas 'as of October 2025'; the excerpt itself carries no date, so the date is the report date.

claims.text: The Sentry reported that Abwakasi reportedly commands around 600 individuals, including roughly 250 combatants since June 2024.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim (p.8); hedge kept in the statement. Grade C because the figure is hedged and its basis (fn 58) was not checked. The Sentry hedges the figure with 'reportedly'; the hedge must stay. The figure includes non-combatants (abducted civilians and dependents, per the preceding sentence of the report).
claims.researcher_note: The Sentry says 'reportedly'; no source for the figure in the excerpt (footnote 58 not retrieved). Figure is for the whole ADF Abwakasi group, including non-combatants.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that since June 2024 Bapere (Lubero) has hosted two ADF groups, including the one led by Abwakasi, which it described as known for its harsh and deadly methods.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; outlet's own narration paragraph. Single clause, single source. Elsewhere in the article, Actualite.cd attributes its identification of the Bapere ADF to security and customary sources in Bapere.
claims.researcher_note: Outlet's own sentence following a traditional chief's remarks; date is the publication date of the article.

claims.text: RFI said that the Wazalendo groups at Uvira are led by known and feared militia chiefs, citing among them the former FARDC member René Itongwa, the former soldier and CNPSC leader William Amuri Yakutumba, sanctioned by the UN, and John Makanaki Kasimbira, whom it described as long installed in the hills overlooking Uvira and very hostile to General Olivier Gasita, deputy commander of the 33rd military region.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira and the hills above it
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo groups (CNPSC of Yakutumba; groups of Itongwa and Makanaki Kasimbira), as RFI names them
claims.verification_note: Confirmed: the pressafrik copy ends with an 'RFI' credit and date, so the origin is RFI. The 'led by known militia chiefs' clause rests on the page sentence before the excerpt (an excerpt gap). Fixed the 'which/whom' wording. RFI calls Gasita 'deputy commander of the 33rd military region'; Kivu Morning Post (4 Sept 2025) says he was appointed to head intelligence supervision in the 33rd military region. The two sources give different posts.
claims.researcher_note: RFI analysis (8 September 2025), cited through a pressafrik.com copy credited 'RFI'; rfi.fr itself returned no text to the page fetcher and was not worked around. Corroborates existing claims on Makanaki (r1-UV-2025Q1-020, r1-UV-2025Q2-001) with a major-wire source and adds Gasita as deputy commander of the 33rd military region (FARDC) as the Wazalendo target. Existing claim r1-UV-2025Q2-001 spells him 'René Makanaki' (Actualite.cd): spellings differ across outlets.

claims.text: In an analysis of the cohabitation of FARDC and Wazalendo at Uvira, RFI said that Wazalendo and FARDC do not always obey the same hierarchy and that the Wazalendo are groups organised in quasi-autonomous entities, each answering directly to its chief.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; this is RFI analysis, and the copy credits RFI.
claims.researcher_note: Analytical statement by RFI, not a finding by a monitor. Same page and caveats as the preceding RFI claim.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that general 'Muzalendo' Makanaki Kasimbira, in a viral video, denounced General Gasita, saying: 'Here in Uvira, we refuse this disorder of sending us foreign faces, people who do not look like Congolese. If they have their Rwandan commanders, we will not accept them here in Uvira.'
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (general 'Muzalendo' Makanaki Kasimbira, as the outlet names him)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; the 'general' title is the outlet's wording. The remark about 'Rwandan commanders' is the speaker's allegation. Kivu Morning Post describes Gasita's new post as head of intelligence supervision in the 33rd military region, while RFI calls him deputy commander.
claims.researcher_note: Statement by a self-styled general reported by a local outlet; the video date is not given, so the date is approximate (report date). Recorded as the commander's own account and attributed; the remark about 'Rwandan commanders' is his allegation, not a finding. Rank is the outlet's wording ('général'), not an FARDC rank.

claims.text: Tumaini Africa News reported that the RAD provincial coordinator for South Kivu, Alexis Mwamba Dunia, accompanied by representatives of the VDP Wazalendo, expressed gratitude to President Tshisekedi and the central government for a 325 US dollar incentive payment called 'effort de guerre', in a press briefing held in Kalundu commune, Uvira city.
claims.actor_as_written: RAD (Réserve armée de la défense), South Kivu; VDP Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: Statement verified. Date precision changed from 'day' to 'approximate': the page gives only its publication date (20/02/2026 08:21), not the day of the briefing. 2026-10-29: date_precision edited: QA 0.4 (A4): the event date is a month only (2026-02, reported 2026-02-20); precision was 'day'
claims.researcher_note: Page date 20 Feb 2026 (publication); the briefing is described only as held on an unstated day. Single outlet (Tumaini Africa News, a Congolese online outlet); the page carries no dateline of the briefing.
