claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the RAD provincial coordinator, Alexis Mwamba Dunia, announced on Thursday 22 January 2026 security measures for Uvira: at a press conference he formally banned carrying firearms and bladed weapons in urban areas and the erection of illegal roadblocks by self-defence groups, demanded the immediate withdrawal of the Wazalendo from the city centre, and said that urban security now fell exclusively under the PNC and the Military Police; the outlet added that the RAD was setting up a special unit to secure the city.
claims.actor_as_written: RAD (Réserve Armée de la Défense), South Kivu; Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: All clauses verbatim on the page; 22 January 2026 was a Thursday.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet; the Wazalendo chain-of-command point is that a RAD coordinator, not an FARDC commander, is the one issuing orders to Wazalendo here. Whether the Wazalendo withdrew was not checked in this unit. The outlet adds that Wazalendo were accused of pillage and attacks on civilians including Banyamulenge (not cited here).

claims.text: Bunia Actualité reported that the military governor of North Kivu, Major General Évariste Kakule Somo, called on the VDP, known as Wazalendo, to show more discipline in a meeting on Friday in his liaison office in Butembo, and that John Maangayiko, spokesperson of the Wazalendo of Grand Nord-Kivu, spoke in the presence of the FARDC operations commander in the area, Brigadier General Joseph Mugisa.
claims.actor_as_written: VDP/Wazalendo (Grand Nord-Kivu front); FARDC operations command
claims.verification_note: Verbatim. Location corrected: the page does not place Butembo in Lubero territory. Grade lowered to C because this is a single local outlet and I could not check the corroborating existing claims (the packet was missing). 'Friday' before the 11 January 2026 publication (a Sunday) points to 9 January 2026; the date is derived, not printed.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('vendredi') and publication date 11 January 2026. Corroborates the existing tie of Joseph Mugisa (existing claims r1-UCD-FARDC-WZ-010/-012) and of the spokesperson (r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-020, spelled 'John Mangaiko' by Kivu Morning Post; spellings differ). The page also says two Wazalendo factions clashed at Butembo on Sunday 4 January (see existing claims on Tango Fort).

claims.text: The Agence Congolaise de Presse (ACP), the state news agency, reported from a Ministry of the Interior workshop at Uvira that Willian Amuri Yakutumba, whom ACP described as coordinator of the 'Wazalendo' in South Kivu province, said that not all armed persons are Wazalendo and that the Wazalendo must be distinguished from other armed groups or individuals in South Kivu; ACP also described Alexis Dunia as 'also coordinator of wazalendo'.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo of South Kivu (coordinators Willian Amuri Yakutumba and Alexis Dunia, as ACP names them)
claims.verification_note: The draft had Yakutumba saying that Dunia was 'also coordinator'. On the page this is ACP's own description of Dunia, so it is now attributed to ACP. Date changed from 23 September (day) to the workshop range, because the agency's weekday and day count do not agree. Titles are the state agency's wording. ACP calls Dunia 'aussi coordinateur de wazalendo' while Tumaini and Kivu Morning Post call Alexis Mwamba Dunia RAD provincial coordinator. ACP's dates conflict: the plea is dated 'mercredi' and 'the second day', but the workshop opened 21 September (a Monday), so the date is given as a range. ACP spells 'Willian'.
claims.researcher_note: State news agency (partisan_drc_government): cited for what it says of titles, not for the facts. The agency gives both Yakutumba and Alexis Dunia the title of Wazalendo coordinator, whereas the RAD sources (Tumaini Africa News, Kivu Morning Post) give Alexis Mwamba Dunia the title of RAD provincial coordinator. Existing claims (HRW r1-UC-FARDC-028; Afrikarabia r1-UV-2025Q3-014) name deputy Justin Bitakwira as coordinator of the Wazalendo in South Kivu: titles differ by source and date; not reconciled here. Dateline Uvira 23 September 2026 (workshop opened 21 September).

claims.text: Amnesty International said that the top commander of the CMC-FDP is Dominique “Domi” Kamanzi Ndaruhutse, whom the European Union sanctioned in July 2024, and that he has fought with various Nyatura groups for more than 10 years and, according to the UN group of experts on DRC, collaborated with the FDLR, particularly in Rutshuru’s Bwito area.
claims.place_as_written: Rutshuru territory (CMC-FDP operates primarily in the Bukombo area)
claims.actor_as_written: CMC-FDP (Collectif des mouvements pour le changement - Forces de défense du peuple), as Amnesty names it
claims.verification_note: Both passages verbatim on the Amnesty UK copy. The FDLR collaboration stays attributed to the UN Group of Experts. Amnesty describes the CMC-FDP as a member of the Wazalendo coalition.
claims.researcher_note: Post (top commander) is Amnesty's wording as of its 25 June 2026 release; the EU listing (July 2024) is pre-window and appears only inside the cited sentence. The collaboration with the FDLR is attributed by Amnesty to the UN Group of Experts. The CMC-FDP's own response is recorded in existing claims (r1-POL-2026-012, r1-SV-2026-027). The page is the Amnesty International UK copy of the release; the Amnesty USA copy returned no text to the page fetcher.

claims.text: Amnesty International said that the FARDC supports the armed groups financially and with weapons and ammunition, and that the DRC's finance minister told the National Assembly's Defence and Security Committee in December 2025 that the state pays Wazalendo groups US$4 million per month.
claims.place_as_written: Kinshasa (National Assembly Defence and Security Committee)
claims.actor_as_written: DRC government (finance minister, not named in the excerpt); FARDC
claims.verification_note: Verbatim. Removed the 'Kinshasa' location and territory, which the source does not print. Normalised the figure to the page's 'US$4 million'. Second-hand: no primary record of the minister's testimony was retrieved, and the minister is not named.
claims.researcher_note: Second-hand: Amnesty reports what the minister said to the committee; the minister is unnamed in the excerpt. The first sentence ('FARDC supports the armed groups...') is Amnesty's own assertion, in the context of the CMC-FDP. No primary record of the committee testimony was retrieved in this unit.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported, citing residents, that the Twirwaneho armed group took the Point-Zero area in Fizi territory after heavy fighting on Wednesday and Thursday.
claims.place_as_written: Point-Zero, Fizi territory (Fizi highlands), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho (as BBC names it, working with M23)
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; translation faithful (the capitalised-word flag is only English renderings of place names and 'BBC'). Same event as the unit's mid-January 2026 Point-Zero capture; page dated 17 Ukwa mbere 2026. BBC's headline puts 'took' in quotation marks; the page also relays Actualité saying Twirwaneho with AFC/M23 took the area on Friday, and a Minembwe resident saying 'on Friday we heard that Twirwaneho had taken Point-Zero'. BBC could not reach the FARDC or Twirwaneho spokespeople.
claims.researcher_note: Kirundi-language BBC Gahuza page (month 'Ukwa mbere' = January). Date computed from weekdays and publication date 17 January 2026 (a Saturday): Wednesday 14 and Thursday 15 January; the capture itself is reported by the page as known on Friday 16 January. Corroborates REC-0586 (16 January). The page also relays that Congolese media (Actualite) said Twirwaneho with AFC/M23 took the area on Friday.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that some Congolese media confirmed government forces with Wazalendo had pushed Twirwaneho fighters out of Point-Zéro on Thursday, an area they had held for nearly two weeks; BBC said it asked the FARDC and Twirwaneho sides and neither had replied.
claims.place_as_written: Point-Zéro, Fizi territory (Fizi highlands), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC with Wazalendo (as BBC names them) against Twirwaneho
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and translation faithful. Graded C, not B: the retake rests on unnamed Congolese media relayed by BBC (BBC did not confirm it, and its resident source hedged), and those media may be the same origin as the records it corroborates (REC-0587/0601), so not shown independent. BBC's own resident source hedged: FARDC and Wazalendo 'bashobora kuba koko bafashe Point-Zéro, nubwo nta gihamya ntakuka turabona' (may indeed have taken Point-Zéro, though we have no firm proof yet).
claims.researcher_note: Kirundi-language BBC Gahuza page; credits Reuters for the photo only (the page text credits 'Ahavuye isanamu, Reuters'). Date computed from 'kuri uyu wa kane' (this Thursday) and publication date 29 January 2026 (a Thursday). Corroborates REC-0587/REC-0601 (FARDC-FDNB retake 29 January). Party statements: BBC states neither FARDC nor Twirwaneho answered its questions at publication.

claims.text: DW Swahili reported that the FARDC spokesperson for the Sokola 2 operations in South Kivu, Luteni (Lieutenant) Reagan Mbuyi, said the aircraft brought down came from Rwanda, that 'one of those helicopters from Rwanda, we shot it down', and that 13 rebel fighters of the group DW prints as Tugwaného and of M23 AFC had surrendered to the FARDC.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe area, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Statement narrowed to the excerpts: 'Twirwaneho' replaced by DW's printed 'Tugwaného' (no excerpt prints 'Twirwaneho'); helicopter quote kept as the speaker's words. Both excerpts exact; translations faithful. Army claim only; DW's headline states the shoot-down as fact. No Rwandan response on the page. In the same quote the spokesperson also claimed Minembwe centre was held by the army ('kituo mji wa Minembwe ni mali yetu').
claims.researcher_note: Party statement (FARDC) relayed by DW; the shoot-down and surrenders are the army's claim only. DW's spelling 'Tugwaného' for Twirwaneho kept as printed. The Rwandan government's reaction was not on the page. Speaker as printed 'Luteni Reagan Mbuyi' (other outlets print Mbuyi Reagan). Related: REC-0619 (April 2026 Burundian deployment) and REC-0621.

claims.text: DW Swahili reported that, despite the army saying the situation had calmed, local sources in the war zone said fighting began again that day in the early morning at Mikenge and neighbouring areas.
claims.place_as_written: Mikenge and surroundings, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory / Minembwe highlands, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC (the army's 'calm' account) versus local sources at the front; the excerpt names no side in the renewed fighting
claims.verification_note: Same article, same day as the FARDC spokesperson's 'calm' claim (claim 2), so the counterclaim is about the same event. The stored excerpt_en rendered the Swahili clock literally ('eleven forty-five'), which an English reader takes as 11:45; Swahili 11:45 alfajiri is 05:45. Actor narrowed: DW's next sentence names the fighters as 'Twighaneho na Red_Ntabara' (its spellings), not 'Red-Tabara', and the excerpt itself names no side. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-FIZ claim 3)
claims.researcher_note: Contradicts the FARDC spokesperson's 'calm' account in the same DW article. The page gives the time in Swahili clock ('saa kumi na moja na dakika arobaini na tano alfajiri', which converts to about 05:45 local time); the statement says only 'at dawn' to avoid a conversion error. The excerpt_en renders the Swahili hours literally.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Mufashi, a civil-society leader in the Minembwe area, said that besides essential goods no longer reaching residents, international aid organisations that used to take medicines to the area were now not allowed to get there.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe, Fizi territory (Hauts Plateaux), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not stated by the speaker in this passage (the protest targeted government and Burundian forces)
claims.verification_note: Original statement said the article prints only 'Mufashi'; it prints 'Santos Mufashi' once, but outside the stored excerpt, so the first name is left out of the statement (only names a surviving excerpt prints). Dropped the protest/Uvira clause (claim 5 carries it) and the actor, which the excerpt does not attribute. Speaker's account only; he does not say who bars the aid groups. The page prints his full name as Santos Mufashi; BBC says it could not reach the South Kivu government or the army on the road closures. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Kirundi-language BBC Gahuza page published 5 November 2025; protest date computed from 'ku wa kabiri' (Tuesday) and publication date. Single named civil-society source; BBC says it tried to get a response from the South Kivu government and army on the road closures without success. Adds a Kirundi/Kinyarwanda-press origin to REC-0186 and REC-0202.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that on Tuesday residents of Minembwe protested against what they called the closure of all roads linking them to Uvira, which they attributed to government and Burundian forces.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe, Fizi territory (Hauts Plateaux), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: government forces and Burundian forces (as the protesters allege)
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; translation faithful; attribution to government and Burundian forces stays the protesters'. Page dated 5 November 2025 (Wednesday), so Tuesday is 4 November.
claims.researcher_note: Kirundi-language BBC Gahuza page. Date computed from 'ku wa kabiri' and publication date 5 November 2025 (Wednesday). Corroborates the protest reported by SOS Medias Burundi on 6 November 2025 and REC-0202.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Burundian army admitted it had closed the roads, aiming to 'protect Uvira and the Burundian border', and asked residents in Minembwe to 'separate themselves from the enemies' there.
claims.place_as_written: Roads from Minembwe toward Uvira, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian army (FDNB) as reported by BBC
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; 'caremeye' = admitted/acknowledged, faithfully rendered. Party statement relayed by BBC, which interviewed the spokesperson. The same page quotes Brig. Gen. Gaspard Baratuza, Burundian army spokesperson, in an interview with BBC. A BBC Gahuza page of 17 January 2026 says that at the time of the November protest the Burundian army spokesperson told BBC there were no Burundian soldiers in that area (they were at Muramvya, Mugeti and Majembwe). The two accounts are not reconciled.
claims.researcher_note: Kirundi-language BBC Gahuza page, dated 25 November 2025. The page does not give the date or channel of the Burundian army statement, only that it 'admitted' it ('caremeye'). Note: a BBC Gahuza page of 12 August 2025 (already cited in the edition) reports the Burundian army spokesperson saying there was no Burundian soldier at Minembwe; the two statements differ in scope (presence at Minembwe versus closing roads) and are not reconciled on the page.

claims.text: BTN Rwanda reported that FARDC launched an air strike in Minembwe, and that politician Moïse Nyarugabo said the attack was launched on a camp in the Mikenke area on the morning of 12 December 2025.
claims.place_as_written: Mikenke (Mikenge) camp, Minembwe area, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC (air strike), as alleged by Nyarugabo
claims.verification_note: Nyarugabo's excerpt says only that 'this attack' hit the camp. The FARDC and warplane attribution is BTN's own narration (its headline and first paragraph), not Nyarugabo's words, so the statement now credits each part to whoever said it. The first clause rests on the page's first paragraph and the title, not the stored excerpt. Partisan Rwandan outlet. The page gives no casualty figure and does not say what kind of camp ('inkambi') it was. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Single Rwandan outlet (BTN Rwanda) relaying a Congolese politician's statement; no casualty figure on the page. The page gives the strike date as 12 December 2025 in the text; its dateline reads only partly in the extraction. Relates to REC-0224 (12 December fighting and shelling at Rusanguku and Bilalombili) and REC-0230 (13 December MRDP/AFC-M23 allegation). Speaker is a Banyamulenge politician; treat as an allegation.

claims.text: BTN Rwanda reported that the MRDP-Twirwaneho group said that closing the paths residents of Minembwe use to reach markets and clinics was meant to kill them because of their Banyamulenge ethnicity.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe area, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: DRC and Burundian forces (as alleged by MRDP-Twirwaneho)
claims.verification_note: Statement faithful and attributed. The stored excerpt_en turned 'ugaragaza ko' (argues, asserts) into 'shows', which reads as if the claim were proven; also 'urwanirira' = fights for. Corrected. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-FIZ claim 10)
claims.researcher_note: Attributed allegation of MRDP-Twirwaneho only (partisan); the same page says DRC and Burundian forces had long closed those paths, accusing residents of working with enemies. Relates to REC-0186 and REC-0202.

claims.text: Kigali Shows reported that Colonel Joseph Nganzo Olikwa Tipi, deputy commander of the 12th Brigade of the FARDC at Minembwe, was killed at Mikenke on Tuesday 3 March 2026 in fighting between government forces with allied groups and Twirwaneho with AFC/M23; it said FARDC leadership had not publicly commented.
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 (as the outlet describes the opposing side)
claims.verification_note: All four excerpts exact; translations faithful. Page dated 4 March 2026; 3 March 2026 was a Tuesday. The capitalised-word flag on excerpt_en is only English renderings. Single partisan Rwandan outlet. Its headline says 'M23 killed' the colonel and calls him one 'who had persecuted Banyamulenge'. The page says he was 'reportedly' ('bivugwa') killed in an ambush by a sniper while commanding a FARDC unit called 'Hiboux'. Unconfirmed by FARDC.
claims.researcher_note: Single Kinyarwanda outlet (Kigali Shows, a Rwandan entertainment/news site whose headline is partisan: 'M23 killed ... colonel who had persecuted Banyamulenge'). The death is unconfirmed by FARDC at publication. The page also says the colonel was under EU sanctions; that sanction detail is not repeated here. Related to REC-0534 (FARDC retake of Mikenge 1-2 March) and REC-0609. A combatant; no individual responsibility implied.

claims.text: Radio Publique Africaine (RPA, Burundi) reported that Burundian army non-commissioned officer Ferdinand Nyabenda, nicknamed Bikorwa, fell three months earlier at Rugezi in Fizi territory and that his family was not informed.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. The 'family not informed' clause is on the page next to the excerpt and in the title, not in the stored excerpt. Single source (RPA, an independent Burundian radio) quoting a neighbour; the army did not confirm the death. Page dated 19 September 2025, so 'three months ago' is about June 2025. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Burundian independent radio (RPA) in French on a Kirundi-service site; date is approximate: 'il y a trois mois' relative to the 19 September 2025 page date (about June 2025). Single source quoting a neighbour; the army did not confirm. Relates to REC-0167 (clashes at Rugezi, about 4-9 June 2025) and REC-0160.

claims.text: UN News (Swahili) reported that OCHA, in a statement quoting its humanitarian partners, said that since the middle of July fighting in the Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga areas had caused more than 48,000 people to leave their homes.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories (highlands), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (fighting between FARDC and armed groups including M23, per OCHA sources)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; translation faithful. Added that OCHA was quoting its humanitarian partners, as the excerpt says. The figure covers Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga together.
claims.researcher_note: UN News Swahili relays an OCHA update dated around 4 August 2026. Figure 48,000 is OCHA's; REC-1280 carries a later figure of 53,000 (Fizi and Nundu health zones) and REC-0555 an earlier early-July flight. Combined area (Uvira, Fizi, Mwenga), not Fizi alone.

claims.text: UN News (Swahili), citing OCHA, reported that the health sector in the affected areas was badly affected by the destruction of health facilities and the departure of health workers, and that since January more than 80 people wounded by fighting and explosive remnants of war had been unable to get the treatment they needed.
claims.place_as_written: Highland areas of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: The excerpt says 'affected areas', not 'highland areas' ('highland' comes only from the page's first paragraph), so 'highland' was removed. Otherwise faithful; the health passage sits in OCHA's list of impacts. The page does not say who destroyed the health facilities.
claims.researcher_note: Date is the UN News publication date (4 August 2026); the OCHA text does not give a single incident date. The page does not say who destroyed the facilities. Complements REC-0555 (disrupted supply routes and medical supplies) and REC-1280.

claims.text: DW Swahili reported that Jacques Alimasi, described as the supervisor (Msimamizi) of the Fizi territory civil-society organisation, said fighting continued in Fizi, citing the previous day in Point zero village and also the villages of Rusanguku, Tuwetuwe, Mikenge, Minembwe and villages around Minembwe, and that killings were increasing.
claims.place_as_written: Point Zero, Rusanguku, Tuwetuwe, Mikenge, Minembwe and surroundings, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: 'Msimamizi' is supervisor or administrator, not 'head', so the title is now given as DW prints it. 'Point zero' is spelled as printed. Both excerpts exact; translations faithful. Page dated 19 February 2026, so 'jana' (yesterday) is 18 February. No perpetrator or casualty count given.
claims.researcher_note: Single civil-society voice quoted by DW on 19 February 2026, a day after Angola's ceasefire call took effect; 'jana' (yesterday) places the Point Zero fighting on 18 February 2026. No casualty count or perpetrator given; 'killings' is the speaker's word. Related: REC-0606 (5 February Point Zero fighting), REC-0609.

claims.text: Minembwe Capital News (a Banyamulenge community outlet) reported that on Thursday 22 May 2025 the headquarters of the Mikenke hospitals was moved to Gipupu; it said the reason was not clearly known but that the administration described it as security reasons.
claims.place_as_written: Mikenke (Mikenge) general hospital, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, moved to Gipupu (Kipupu), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (relocation for security reasons per the administration, as reported)
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; translation faithful; the statement keeps the outlet's hedges. Partisan community outlet; the account rests on 'information from those areas'. The page places Mikenke in Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, and says the receiving area (Gipupu, Mibunda) is held by Wazalendo, FDLR and FARDC with Burundian forces (the outlet's account).
claims.researcher_note: Banyamulenge community outlet (partisan) in Kinyarwanda, single source. The page also says the area where the hospital was relocated is controlled by Wazalendo, FDLR and the national army with Burundian forces, while Mikenke is held by Twirwaneho and M23 since February 2025 (the outlet's account); and that the hospitals are supported by MDM/PIN according to some staff. Not in the edition: REC-0468 covers looting of the Itombwe referral hospital in March 2025; REC-0546/0627 and REC-0534 cover 2026 hospital events at Mikenge.

claims.text: Radio Publique Africaine (RPA, Burundi) reported that, according to sources at Lusenda camp, the police commissioner in charge of the camp, Masumbuko Lutombo, personally directs recruitment operations aimed mainly at young Burundian refugees, to integrate them into the Wazalendo armed groups.
claims.place_as_written: Lusenda refugee camp, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Masumbuko Lutombo, police commissioner of the camp (as alleged by refugees and sources quoted by RPA); recruiting for Wazalendo groups
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; the attribution to sources is kept. Page dated 25 July 2026. Allegation from unnamed sources; no response from the Congolese police or UNHCR on the page. Being named is not a finding of responsibility.
claims.researcher_note: Single Burundian radio source (RPA, French text on a site that also carries Kirundi bulletins); unnamed sources; allegation not confirmed by the Congolese police or UNHCR on the page. The page says recruitment began after humanitarian organisations suspended food assistance. Earlier 2025 reports of refugee recruitment are in REC-0169.

claims.text: Radio Publique Africaine (RPA, Burundi) reported that at Lusenda in South Kivu the sick had had no access to medicines for six months; it said IDAV, a partner of the UN refugee agency (HCR), indicated that stocks of medicines were at Kalemie and being forwarded.
claims.place_as_written: Lusenda refugee camp, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: 'UNHCR' replaced by the source's 'HCR'. The source says 'À Lusenda', not 'at Lusenda camp', so the wording follows the excerpt. Both excerpts exact. Page dated 23 March 2026. The page says UNHCR's DRC office, when contacted, promised to respond soon. It describes a supply gap, not an attack.
claims.researcher_note: Single Burundian radio source quoting refugees; no UNHCR statement on the page. The cause is described as a long supply gap, not an attack. Complements the Fizi territory health-supply records (REC-0171, REC-0203).

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that Twirwaneho spokesperson Kamasa Ndakize Welcome announced on 5 August 2025 that attacks by FDLR, FARDC and another group, Mai Mai Ngomanzito, began at Irumba and Rugezi in the south of Minembwe, and that Twirwaneho confirmed Burundian forces took no part in that day's attacks.
claims.place_as_written: Irumba and Rugezi, south of Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FDLR, FARDC and Mai Mai Ngomanzito (as alleged by Twirwaneho); Burundian forces said by Twirwaneho not to have taken part that day
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact on the retained copy (the live site refuses the fetch, HTTP 406); translations faithful. Byline Isimbi Estella, 6 August 2025. Partisan statement relayed by a Rwandan outlet; the quoted statement calls FDLR 'abajenosideri' and the war 'intambara ya jenoside', which is Twirwaneho's wording. It differs from REC-0188 (6 August communique naming the Burundian army), which concerns other villages; the source does not reconcile them.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan (Twirwaneho) statement relayed by a Rwandan outlet in Kinyarwanda. Differs from REC-0188 (MRDP-Twirwaneho communique of 6 August alleging FARDC, FDLR and the Burundian army attacked Kipupu, Bilalo Mbili, Lulenge and Mikenge): here Twirwaneho says Burundian forces were not involved in the 5 August attacks at Irumba and Rugezi. The two statements concern different villages and days and are not reconciled by the source. The page also relays a Twirwaneho claim made the previous week that FDLR fighters were being trained in Burundi; not recorded here.

claims.text: Bwiza reported, citing 'various reports' coming from Goma, that the drone attack launched on Goma by the forces of the DRC government was aimed at, among others, former president Joseph Kabila Kabange; it said the attack of 11 March struck the mainly residential Himbi area near Lake Kivu, where residents said they heard two explosions at dawn.
claims.actor_as_written: Forces of the DRC government, as Bwiza states
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts are exact. Removed 'Wednesday' (only in the page sentence 'kuri uyu wa Gatatu tariki ya 11 Werurwe', outside the excerpt: excerpt gap). Page date Wednesday 11 March 2026 checked (weekday correct). Same page also gives a toll of three including Karine Buisset ('Kugeza ubu abantu batatu barimo Umufaransakazi Karine Buisset wakoreraga UNICEF ni bo byamenyekanye ko biciwe muri kiriya gitero'), which matches claim 31 (Umuryango.rw) but both are Rwandan outlets; see claim 31 discrepancy note. Bwiza's 'Amakuru atandukanye ... aremeza' = 'various reports ... affirm' — the outlet presents it as confirmed; statement keeps it attributed. Rwandan outlet; the target (Kabila, and per the same page Makenga, Nangaa and Bisimwa, all with 'bivugwa' = it is said) is Bwiza's account of unnamed reports, not established. Bwiza dates the strike to Wednesday 11 March at about 'saa kumi n'igice' (Kinyarwanda clock, about 04:30) and says the DRC government had made no statement.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0874 (Himbi drone strike) from a Kinyarwanda-language Rwandan outlet (partisan on contested facts); the target (Kabila) is the outlet's account of 'various reports', not independently confirmed. The article also gives a chronology that the DRC government received information on 10 March that Kabila was in the area.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that on Thursday 7 May Congolese government forces launched a drone attack at Muja in Nyiragongo territory, where AFC/M23 soldiers were, that the explosion was heard in Goma city, and that, in the outlet's words, no one was killed or injured.
claims.actor_as_written: Forces of the DRC government (FARDC), per Umuryango.rw; targeted AFC/M23 soldiers
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Page dated Friday 08 May 2026; Thursday 7 May 2026 checked (weekday correct). 'Mu ma saa saba y'igicamunsi' = about 1 p.m., translation correct. Wire-style credit to Bwiza set as originating source. Umuryango.rw credits the story to Bwiza ('Src: Bwiza' at the foot of the page; excerpt gap). Both are Rwandan outlets. The same page relays Lawrence Kanyuka (on X) that a government drone strike the same Thursday at Kalenga, Masisi, killed civilians: a lead, not a claim here.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan outlet, not independently sourced; no FARDC account found in this round. Date: page is dated Friday 8 May 2026 and says Thursday 7 May. 'Mu ma saa saba' in Kinyarwanda clock = about 13:00. Not in known_records (nearest are REC-0888 and REC-0889 on 24 May 2026).

claims.text: BBC Gahuza reported, citing members of Rutshuru civil society, that heavy fighting on Saturday and Sunday between M23 and Wazalendo fighters at Nyanzale (Rutshuru territory) left civilians dead and others fleeing; civil society member Kambele said he had learned of at least three civilians dead near Nyanzale, and BBC wrote that Congolese media reported that a child was among those who died in the Sunday evening fighting.
claims.place_as_written: Nyanzale and Kiyeye, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and Wazalendo, as BBC Gahuza names them
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact and support every clause; deaths stay attributed to civil society and Congolese media. BBC is a credible non-partisan origin: B. Page dated 23 June 2025 (Monday): Saturday 21 and Sunday 22 June 2025, computed. The page names the speaker 'Emile Kambele'. Same page: fighting began on Saturday at Kiyeye (Wazalendo-held); Radio Okapi relayed a CMC statement condemning M23 shelling of Nyarubande, Burambo, Muhanga, Kihondo-centre and Kiyeye; M23 had made no statement.
claims.researcher_note: New: no known record covers Nyanzale/Kiyeye fighting on 21-22 June 2025 (BBC page dated 23 June 2025 gives Saturday and Sunday; dates computed from weekdays and publication date). Same page says M23 had made no statement; CMC statement condemning M23 bombardment of Nyarubande, Burambo, Muhanga, Kihondo-centre and Kiyeye on Saturday, relayed from Radio Okapi (originating source Radio Okapi for that part).

claims.text: BBC Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 said the new Human Rights Watch report accusing it of killing at least 140 civilians, mostly Hutu, is 'a lie' with 'no foundation'; in a statement by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka it said the HRW and UN allegations are politically motivated, and that HRW deliberately avoided mentioning armed groups it says work with Kinshasa, including FDLR, Nyatura, PARECO and Wazalendo.
claims.verification_note: All four excerpts exact (byline Didier Bikorimana, 21 Aug 2025). Grade B for the fact of the statement as reported by BBC. Partisan statement, cited only as what AFC/M23 said. Same page: M23 had already denied the allegations in a document of 7 August 2025; Rwanda told BBC Newshour 'RDF nta ho ihuriye' (RDF has nothing to do with it); DRC FM Thérèse Kayikwamba also responded. Counterclaim to the Binza killings (REC-0345).
claims.researcher_note: Counterclaim to REC-0345 (Binza killings, HRW report of 20 Aug 2025). The M23 statement is dated by BBC to 7 August in an earlier communiqué plus this reaction; BBC page published 21 Aug 2025. Partisan statement cited only for what AFC/M23 said.

claims.text: UN News Kiswahili reported that a report prepared by the Fact-Finding Mission (FFM) of the UN human rights office said all parties failed to protect civilians adequately during the fighting, in particular when M23 and RDF took the city of Goma at the end of January 2025, and during attacks on schools and hospitals.
claims.place_as_written: Goma, North Kivu (and attacks on schools and hospitals, place not specified)
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and RDF (capture of Goma); the report says all parties failed to protect civilians
claims.verification_note: Removed the release date '5 September 2025', which no excerpt prints (page: 'iliyotolewa Ijumaa tarehe 5 Septemba 2025', outside the excerpts: excerpt gap). 'pande zote' = 'all parties' (statement said 'the parties'). UN fact-finding report: A. General finding: the excerpt names no hospital and no party responsible for the attacks on schools and hospitals. Do not use it to attribute the Goma hospital incidents (REC-0256, REC-0289). 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-GOMA claim 4)
claims.researcher_note: Independent Swahili-language UN News relay of the OHCHR FFM report (5 Sept 2025). The excerpt does not say which hospitals or which party attacked them; it is a general statement. Cited to add a Swahili UN origin for the Goma hospital incidents (REC-0256, REC-0289), not to attribute them.

claims.text: UN News Kiswahili reported that the UN human rights office Fact-Finding Mission (FFM) report said M23 members committed sexual violence, mainly gang rape, and other forms of sexual violence including sexual slavery; women and girls were mainly targeted, but men, boys and people UN News Kiswahili calls 'watu wa jinsia moja' (literally 'people of the same sex') were also victims, including in detention.
claims.place_as_written: M23-controlled areas of North Kivu and South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23 members, as the OHCHR FFM report is relayed by UN News
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. The draft's 'people of diverse sexual characteristics' was an interpretation, not a translation; narrowed to the Swahili wording. No place in the excerpt beyond the report's scope. The Swahili 'watu wa jinsia moja' literally means 'people of the same sex'; it probably renders the report's reference to sexual and gender minorities, but the English wording should be checked against the FFM report itself. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-GOMA claim 5)
claims.researcher_note: Swahili UN News relay of OHCHR FFM report; place not stated in excerpt beyond 'M23-controlled' areas covered by the report. Wording of the last category in the Swahili ('watu wa jinsia moja') is translated literally.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that in the night of 21 to 22 July 2025 Wazalendo fighters, suspected to have come from Virunga Park, attacked the Mugunga area and Rusayo groupement, that gunfire was heard for about three hours, and that AFC/M23 pushed the Wazalendo fighters back.
claims.place_as_written: Mugunga and Rusayo groupement, west of Goma, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo fighters (attackers) and AFC/M23 (defenders), per Umuryango.rw
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact (byline ISIMBI Estella, Wednesday 23 Jul 2025). 'bikekwa' kept as 'suspected'. Source type corrected to partisan Rwandan outlet; C. Rwandan outlet giving the AFC/M23 side; no Wazalendo or FARDC account. The page says residents of Ndosho and Kyeshero heard the gunfire and places the attack west of Goma.
claims.researcher_note: New event: no known record for an attack on Mugunga/Rusayo in July 2025 (nearest REC-0299 of 11 April 2025 and Group of Experts annex for 11-12 April). Rwandan outlet (page intro places the attack west of Goma) relaying AFC/M23 account; no FARDC/Wazalendo statement found yet. Same story carried by igihe.com and umusarenews.com (not retrievable/used).

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that Manzi Willy, whom it described as the governor of North Kivu appointed by AFC/M23, said on 22 July that their fighters continue to destroy everything that could disturb the security of Goma, and that when AFC/M23 took Goma the opposing forces had hidden guns, ammunition and bombs among the population, which the alliance uncovers day by day.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Narrowed the title to the outlet's description and translated 'ribitahura' as 'uncovers'. Year 2025 from the page date (Wednesday 23 Jul 2025). DISCREPANCY: Umuryango.rw (22 July 2025) calls Manzi Willy the AFC/M23-appointed governor of North Kivu, while Umuryango.rw itself (claim 13 of this unit, 9 April 2026) and other edition records name Bahati Musanga Erasto as that governor. The title may be an outlet error; the name and title are recorded as printed.
claims.researcher_note: The page names the AFC/M23 governor as 'Manzi Willy'; other sources in this edition name the de facto governor differently (e.g. Bahati Musanga Erasto, REC-0880 area) so the name is as printed by Umuryango.rw and may be an error; flag for verifier.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that residents of Buramba village (Binza groupement, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory) continue to complain of insecurity caused by Wazalendo and FDLR rebels who harass them, and that, it is said, those often harassed are accused of working with AFC/M23; citing Kivu Morning Post, it said these armed rebels also attack users of the Kiwanja-Ishasha road at places such as Katoro, near Katwiguru, and Cabafu, where the latest attack took place on Sunday 8 March 2026.
claims.place_as_written: Buramba (Binza groupement, Bwisha chiefdom) and Kiwanja-Ishasha road (Katoro, near Katwiguru; Cabafu), Rutshuru territory
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo and FDLR fighters, as Bwiza reports
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Removed the publication date ('10 March 2026'), which no excerpt prints; the hedge 'Biravugwa' had been dropped in the draft statement and is restored. Page dated Tuesday 10 March 2026; Sunday 8 March 2026 checked (weekday correct). Rwandan outlet; the road attacks are credited to Kivu Morning Post. 'Biravugwa' (it is said) kept as a hedge. The page also quotes an unnamed resident on looting and abductions by armed Wazalendo and FDLR (excerpt gap: 'by’umwihariko gusahura no gushimuta bikorwa n’abantu bitwaje intwaro ba wazalendo na FDLR').
claims.researcher_note: New: no known record for Buramba/Cabafu harassment (REC-0875 is a different incident on the Kanyabayonga-Kiwanja road on 18 March 2026). Bwiza is Rwandan and says it takes the road-attack information from Kivu Morning Post (second excerpt); that those targeted are accused of working with AFC/M23 is Bwiza's unattributed 'biravugwa' (it is said). Date is the latest attack date given; the harassment is ongoing.

claims.text: Bwiza, relaying Radio Okapi, reported that heavy fighting took place all morning on Monday 12 January between AFC/M23 fighters and CMC Wazalendo in many villages of Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru territory, that no toll had been announced, and that the fighting started at Bumbasha, a few kilometres from Mweso, before spreading to Karambi and Chahemba, sending hundreds of residents fleeing to nearby villages and to Mweso centre.
claims.place_as_written: Bumbasha, Karambi, Chahemba (Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru), near Mweso
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; Bwiza credits Radio Okapi ('dukesha iyi nkuru'). Page dated Tuesday 13 January 2026; Monday 12 January 2026 checked. Grade rests on the Radio Okapi origin, which corroborates existing records. Kinyarwanda relay of Radio Okapi; not independent of the Radio Okapi-based records (REC-0862, REC-0865). The page adds that the displaced sheltered in churches and schools.
claims.researcher_note: Kinyarwanda relay of Radio Okapi (originating source Radio Okapi); existing records REC-0862/REC-0865 are Radio Okapi-based, so this is a language relay, not an independent origin.

claims.text: Umunota reported that heavy fighting between AFC/M23 fighters and Wazalendo fighters of the Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC) took place from dawn on Monday, mainly at Munguli in Kihondo groupement and at Kikuro in Tongo groupement, according to information from the area.
claims.place_as_written: Munguli (Kihondo groupement) and Kikuro (Tongo groupement), Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed '1 July 2025', '30 June' and 'Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory', which the excerpt does not print (all are on the page outside it). Date 30 June 2025 is from the page sentence outside the excerpt ('ubwo Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo yizihizaga isabukuru y’imyaka 65 imaze ibonye ubwigenge ku wa 30 Kamena', Bwito chiefdom): excerpt gap. Page dated 1 July 2025; 30 June 2025 was a Monday. Rwandan outlet with no byline or credit; the page adds that gunfire was heard from 'saa kumi n'ebyiri za mu gitondo' (about 6 a.m.).
claims.researcher_note: New: no known record for fighting in Bwito on 28-30 June 2025. The page gives no byline or agency credit; the wording ('information from the area') suggests relayed local reporting, probably Radio Okapi, but the page does not say so. Monday is 30 June per the page ('ku wa 30 Kamena'). Umunota is a Rwandan outlet.

claims.text: Umunota reported that on Saturday and Sunday heavy fighting took place at Birambizo and Karambi in Bukombo groupement and in Kihondo groupement, that according to information from the area it made hundreds of residents flee their homes, and that on Sunday at least six houses were burned in Karambi town and its surroundings.
claims.place_as_written: Birambizo and Karambi (Bukombo groupement) and Kihondo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (the same article describes fighting between AFC/M23 and CMC Wazalendo)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date '1 July 2025', which the excerpt does not print. No perpetrator named for the burning. Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 June 2025 computed from the page date (1 July 2025) and its reference to Monday 30 June.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekdays and publication date (Saturday 28 June, Sunday 29 June 2025). No perpetrator named for the burning.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that an announcement of 9 April 2026 by the AFC/M23-appointed governor of North Kivu, Bahati Musanga Erasto, named Kisuba Ngabo Désiré mayor of Goma in place of Julien Katembo Ndalieni, who was made head of Lubero territory, and named Nshimiyimana Juvénal, formerly in charge of mobilisation and recruitment of new fighters in AFC/M23, deputy mayor of Goma.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact (page dated Thursday 09 Apr 2026). Corroborates REC-0881 with the date discrepancy above. DISCREPANCY: Umuryango.rw dates the announcement 9 April 2026; Kivu Morning Post claims r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-009/010 (REC-0881) date it 8 April 2026. The page also spells the new mayor 'Kasuba Ngabo' in a photo caption and names Katembo Isevisya and Radjabu Kwizera Elie as deputy burgomasters.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0881 and Kivu Morning Post claims r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-009/010; Umuryango.rw dates the announcement 9 April 2026 whereas those claims date it 8 April: one-day discrepancy for the verifier. Rwandan outlet; appointments are AFC/M23 de facto acts.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that on 11 May CADECO, a bank opened by AFC/M23 after the Congolese government closed banks in the areas the group controls, opened two counters in Goma at a ceremony led by the AFC/M23 deputy governor of North Kivu for economy and finance, Shadrack Amani.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact and support the statement. Rwandan outlet: C. Year 2026 from the page date (Wednesday 13 May 2026). The page also names the board chair Kabasha Amani and director general Javan Dusabe Sangano, and says branches were planned in Rutshuru, Masisi and Minova centres (lead).
claims.researcher_note: New de facto governance item (no CADECO record in the edition). Date: the article is dated 13 May 2026 and says '11 Gicurasi' (11 May), year taken from the page date. Rwandan outlet reporting the AFC/M23 account; the article's first sentence (bank opened last year) is not in the excerpt.

claims.text: UN News Kiswahili reported that OCHA had reported that armed men raided at least two hospitals in Goma, the capital of North Kivu, and abducted several patients.
claims.place_as_written: At least two hospitals in Goma, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Armed men (watu wenye silaha), as OCHA is quoted
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed '4 March 2025' and 'Monday of that week', which the excerpt does not print. Single UN agency report relayed, not an investigation: B rather than A. Source language is Swahili, not Kinyarwanda. OCHA's report is dated by the page to 'Jumatatu wiki hii' (Monday this week), i.e. Monday 3 March 2025 for a page dated Tuesday 4 March 2025 (excerpt gap); the raids themselves were earlier. Hospitals are not named; likely the Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho raids (REC-0286) but the excerpt does not say so.
claims.researcher_note: Swahili UN News relay of an OCHA report; corroborates the raids on Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals (REC-0286) without naming them. Date computed from 'Monday this week' (page published Tuesday 4 March 2025): Monday 3 March 2025; the raids themselves were earlier. The page text carries typographic artefacts in places but not in the excerpt.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Sunday 8 February 2026 AFC-M23 presented 7,532 new commandos who had finished military training at Tchanzu (Rutshuru, North Kivu), a ceremony it described as marking a new stage in the structure of the ARC (Jeshi la Mapinduzi la Kongo), the armed wing of the movement led by General Sultani Makenga.
claims.place_as_written: Tchanzu training centre, Rutshuru, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC-M23 / Armée révolutionnaire congolaise (ARC), under General Sultani Makenga, per SOS Médias Burundi
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Removed the dateline 'from Goma on 10 February 2026', which no excerpt prints. Kept ARC wording as printed. Source language is Swahili, not Kinyarwanda. The figure of 7,532 is AFC-M23's presentation as relayed; no independent count. The page has the dateline 'Goma, Februari 10, 2026' and is dated 12 February 2026. Whether 'inayoongozwa na' (led by) qualifies the movement or its armed wing is ambiguous in the Swahili. Different cohort from REC-0312 (Tchanzu, 1 Oct 2025). 8 February 2026 was a Sunday (checked).
claims.researcher_note: New: same site as REC-0312 (Tchanzu graduation of 1 Oct 2025) but a different cohort and date; no record of the 8 Feb 2026 ceremony. Burundian independent outlet; the figure is AFC-M23's own presentation as relayed; SOS Médias Burundi gives no named original source. Whether the trainees were volunteers or conscripts is not addressed in the excerpts.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi quoted Major General Sultani Makenga, AFC-M23 military coordinator, as saying to the new troops: 'From today you have become soldiers of the ARC, an army that emerged to liberate the people, our country is run by incompetent people living in Kinshasa'.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed 'at Tchanzu on 8 February 2026' from the statement because this source's excerpt does not print it; date field kept from the article. Partisan speech cited only as what Makenga said. Speech at the Tchanzu graduation ceremony; the date (Sunday 8 February 2026) and place are in another sentence of the same article, not in this excerpt (excerpt gap: 'Jumapili, Februari 8, 2026, ... huko Tchanzu (Wilaya ya Rutshuru, Kivu Kaskazini)'). 'wazembe' can also be rendered 'negligent' or 'lazy'.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan statement cited only for what Makenga is reported to have said; the date of the speech is the ceremony date of 8 February 2026 given in the same article.

claims.text: DW Kiswahili reported that by the end of May hundreds of men were sitting on black volcanic gravel in the streets of Murambi, north of Goma, guarded by M23 fighters; that some Goma residents said people were arrested for minor reasons such as wearing dirty clothes or not shaving, many being gathered in a sports ground then turned into an open prison; and that those not cleared by evidence considered credible were taken to private places of detention.
claims.place_as_written: Murambi (north of Goma) and a sports ground used as an open prison, Goma
claims.actor_as_written: M23 fighters, as DW Kiswahili states
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Removed the publication date '27 January 2026', which no excerpt prints. Source language is Swahili. DW feature (byline Sylivanus Karemera, 27 January 2026) that quotes AFP for one resident; parts may draw on AFP without credit. 'May' is placed in 2025 by the article's chronology (capture in January 2025, Uvira offensive in December). The sports ground is unnamed; REC-0292 (Stade de l'Unité, March 2025) may be the same site but the month differs: tentative link only.
claims.researcher_note: DW Kiswahili one-year-on feature (byline Sylivanus Karemera); it quotes AFP once for an unrelated resident account and may draw on AFP and NGO reporting more widely, but does not credit an agency for these passages. 'End of May' is taken as 2025 from the article's chronology; the stadium is not named in the Swahili ('uwanja wa michezo'); REC-0292 identifies Stade de l'Unité for March 2025, so treat the link as tentative.

claims.text: DW Kiswahili reported that Congolese government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said residents of Goma continue to face suffering.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date, which the excerpt does not print. Undated paraphrase with no channel given, in a feature dated 27 January 2026; a statement lead only.
claims.researcher_note: Only a paraphrase of Muyaya's remark with no date or channel; kept as a statement lead. Partisan: cited only for what the spokesperson said.

claims.text: BBC Gahuza reported that M23 said the more than 2,500 people who died in the recent fighting in Goma were government soldiers (FARDC) and Wazalendo; that Bertrand Bisimwa, one of the leaders of M23, said no family in Goma was in mourning because of those dead; and that he said the bodies removed from the streets and buried were those of FARDC soldiers and their collaborators, including Wazalendo, FDLR, European mercenaries and Burundian forces, who died in battle.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact (page 5 Feb 2025). Removed the publication date; 'M23 leader' narrowed to 'one of M23's leaders' (umwe mu bakuru); the figures field dropped the UN and Muyaya figures, which are not in this claim's excerpts (they belong to claims 23 and 25). Partisan statement cited only as what M23 said. BBC writes that neither OCHA nor the Red Cross confirm whether the bodies buried were civilians or soldiers. DISCREPANCY within M23's own accounts: more than 2,500 dead said to be FARDC/Wazalendo here (5 Feb 2025) vs Kanyuka's M23 report that only 874 fighters died in the fight for Goma (claim 24, 3 June 2025); compare OCHA/UN figures (claim 23) and Muyaya's (claim 25).
claims.researcher_note: Counterclaim to the casualty accounts for the fight for Goma (REC-0250 and Kinshasa's account). BBC notes that it is hard to know the truth of what the state side and Rwanda/M23 say about the dead. Partisan statement cited only for what M23 said.

claims.text: BBC Gahuza reported that the UN humanitarian office OCHA-RDC said at least 2,000 bodies had already been buried and about 900 others were in the morgues of various hospitals in Goma, and that the UN said on Monday that at least 900 people had been killed and more than 2,800 wounded in the fighting, with hospitals still struggling to treat all the wounded.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Removed the publication date, which no excerpt prints. Figures per source, not merged; the 900 in morgues (OCHA-RDC) and the 900 killed (UN) are separate figures. BBC adds that neither the UN office nor the Red Cross confirm whether the dead were civilians or soldiers. 'Monday' = 3 February 2025 (page dated 5 February 2025).
claims.researcher_note: Figures per source, not merged: BBC notes that neither the UN nor the Red Cross confirm whether the bodies buried were civilians or soldiers. 'Monday' is 3 February 2025 by the page date (computed).

claims.text: BBC Gahuza reported that M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, replying on X to the Human Rights Watch report, said that report and the recent Amnesty International report are 'propaganda tools working for the Kinshasa authorities', and cited a report published by M23 the previous week saying that only 874 fighters died in the fighting to take Goma.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact (page 3 June 2025). Removed the publication date; figures field dropped the HRW figure, which is not in this claim's excerpts. Partisan statement cited only as what M23 said; the X post itself was not retained. DISCREPANCY with claim 22: M23 said in February 2025 that more than 2,500 dead were FARDC/Wazalendo. HRW told BBC it had asked Kanyuka about its findings and received no reply.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan statement cited only for what AFC/M23 said; the X post itself was not fetched (BBC relays it).

claims.text: BBC Gahuza reported that Patrick Muyaya, spokesperson of the Kinshasa government, had recently said that more than 2,000 bodies were still in the streets of Goma needing burial, and that he accused Rwandan forces and M23 of killing civilians in the recent fighting in Goma and its surroundings.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date, which the excerpt does not print. Government account; BBC gives no date for Muyaya's remark (before 5 February 2025).
claims.researcher_note: Government account, partisan on attribution; BBC gives no date for Muyaya's remark (before 5 Feb 2025).

claims.text: BBC Gahuza reported that a Human Rights Watch report said M23 killed at least 21 civilians in Goma in February whose deaths it could confirm, with evidence of many more; that on 22 February at least three pickup trucks carrying M23 fighters went to different parts of Goma and the fighters killed seven people in Katindo, with 11 more bodies including a boy found later near a construction site; that the next day the fighters rounded people up to force them into M23 and killed three who tried to escape; and that three health workers told HRW more than 50 bodies were removed from the Kasika area between 22 and 23 February.
claims.place_as_written: Katindo and other Goma neighbourhoods (Camp Katindo, Avenue du Commandant Belge, Avenue Kasika, Avenue Mulongwe)
claims.actor_as_written: M23 fighters, per Human Rights Watch
claims.verification_note: All four excerpts exact. Removed the publication date; added the Kasika clause from source 3, which the draft cited but did not state. Kept B: a relay of an NGO investigation through a single outlet. Relay of the HRW report of 3 June 2025. 'Seven' and 'three' are printed in the Kinyarwanda excerpts as words (barindwi, eshatu, batatu). The page lists Camp Katindo, Avenue du Commandant Belge, Avenue Kasika and Avenue Mulongwe among the sites. Corroborates the Group of Experts claims on the Katindo killings of 22 February 2025 (r2-G-DOC-446-018/019).
claims.researcher_note: Kinyarwanda relay of the HRW report of 3 June 2025 (originating source HRW). Corroborates the UN Group of Experts claims on the Katindo killings of 22 February 2025 (r2-G-DOC-446-018/019).

claims.text: UN News Kiswahili reported that the UN Special Rapporteur on human rights defenders, Mary Lawlor, said she had received credible reports of human rights defenders held incommunicado, forcibly disappeared and tortured in Rutshuru and Masisi, North Kivu, and that about six defenders were reported to have disappeared after trying to flee Goma after the city was taken by M23.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed in this passage (the report concerns M23-controlled areas)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Removed the publication date. A Special Rapporteur's statement on reports received is not a documented investigation: B rather than A. The passage does not say who held, disappeared or tortured the defenders. Statement given in Geneva; page dated 5 March 2025.
claims.researcher_note: Swahili UN News relay of a Geneva statement by the UN Special Rapporteur (OHCHR special procedures). The passage does not say who held or tortured the defenders. Names of defenders are not given.

claims.text: UN News Kiswahili reported that Mary Lawlor, UN Special Rapporteur on human rights defenders, said a defender had recently told her that M23 rebels had drawn up a list of human rights defenders to be arrested in the areas they controlled.
claims.actor_as_written: M23, as alleged by a defender quoted by the Special Rapporteur
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Removed the publication date. The underlying allegation rests on one anonymous source: C. An allegation from one unnamed defender, relayed by the Special Rapporteur; not a finding. No M23 response found.
claims.researcher_note: Single-source allegation relayed by the Special Rapporteur from an unnamed defender; not a finding. Cited as an allegation only. M23 response not found in this round.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa told residents of Goma that, a year after the city's administration was installed, everything was now in order, that the war in the city was completely over, and that what remained was to continue development and to liberate all of Congo.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Removed 'on Friday 6 February 2026', which no excerpt prints. Date from the page sentence outside the excerpts: 'Corneille Nangaa yabitangaje kuri uyu wa Gatanu tariki 06 Gashyantare 2026' (Friday 6 February 2026, weekday correct): excerpt gap. Partisan statement by a Rwandan outlet.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan statement cited only for what Nangaa is reported to have said, by a Rwandan outlet. Date: 'Friday 06 Feb 2026' as printed by the page.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that in the early morning of 11 March drones of the DRC army fired on residents' homes in the Himbi area, killing three civilians including the Frenchwoman Karine Buisset, who worked for UNICEF.
claims.actor_as_written: DRC army (ingabo za RDC), as Umuryango.rw states
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date '12 March 2026', which the excerpt does not print. Translation corrected: 'saa kumi' in Kinyarwanda time is about 4 a.m., not 'ten'. DISCREPANCY: the toll of three civilians (Umuryango.rw; also Bwiza, claim 0 page) is not in the existing records on this strike (REC-0874; r1-ATR-NK-2026-003/004; r1-GOE-026). Both are Rwandan outlets and the attribution to DRC army drones is theirs. Time: about 04:00 (Umuryango.rw) / about 04:30 (Bwiza), not 10:00. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-GOMA claim 31)
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0874 and Group of Experts/UN News claims (r1-ATR-NK-2026-003/004, r1-GOE-026) on the death of UNICEF staff member Karine Buisset. The toll of three civilians is Umuryango.rw's (a Rwandan outlet aligned with the AFC/M23 account) and is not in the other claims I saw; treat as a single-source figure. The excerpt's 'Mu masaa kumi y’urukerera' follows the Kinyarwanda clock (about 04:00), not 10:00; the translation is literal.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 condemned the attack and said it was not right for the international community to keep silent while the DRC government deliberately violates the ceasefire agreement signed in Doha, Qatar.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed '12 March 2026' and '11 March drone attack on Goma', which the excerpt does not print. 'The attack' is the 11 March 2026 drone strike on Himbi, Goma (previous sentence of the page, outside the excerpt). The page gives no date, channel or signatory for the AFC/M23 condemnation; reported 12 March 2026.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan statement cited only for what AFC/M23 said; the page does not give the channel or the signatory.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that on the morning of 12 March 2026 many Goma residents gathered in a protest against the drone attack launched on the city by the forces of the DRC, asking AFC/M23 to liberate the whole country, after an invitation from civil society, and that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the protesters asked AFC/M23 to remove Félix Tshisekedi's government throughout the DRC.
claims.actor_as_written: Goma residents (protesters), as Umuryango.rw describes; AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Corrected 'Felix' to 'Félix' as printed; added the civil-society invitation from the page (excerpt gap) because it bears on whether the protest was organised. Excerpt gap: the civil-society invitation is in the page sentence 'Nyuma yo kwakira ubutumire bwa sosiyete sivile, mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa 12 Werurwe abaturage benshi b’i Goma bahagaritse ibikorwa byabo', not in the stored excerpt. Whether attendance was voluntary is not established; a protest in an AFC/M23-held city reported by a Rwandan outlet and relayed by the AFC/M23 spokesperson. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan outlet; the protest is described as called after an invitation from civil society (not in the excerpts). Whether the gathering was spontaneous or organised is not established; the page says it followed an invitation from civil society. Kanyuka's remark is partisan.

claims.text: Rwandan Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo said, in reaction to a Human Rights Watch report, that 'the RDF is not AFC/M23' and that any proper investigation requires impartiality, access to where events happen, solid evidence, respect for the law and not announcing conclusions in advance or putting calls for sanctions first, according to Igihe.
claims.place_as_written: Kigali (statement on X); subject: eastern DRC
claims.verification_note: Both Igihe pages print the quote; translation checked (accurate). Capitalised-word flag is the Rwanda/u Rwanda rendering; no correction needed. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding. Rwanda's denial of RDF involvement conflicts with UN Group of Experts findings recorded elsewhere. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan state-aligned outlet relaying its own government's statement; Rwanda's position that it has no forces in eastern DRC conflicts with UN Group of Experts findings (e.g. over 8,000 RDF troops, see existing claims r1-UC-RDF-010). The HRW report concerned is the 10 June 2026 report (78 pages per Igihe). Igihe p01 says the message was posted 'this Thursday' (11 June 2026); p02 (12 June) says posted on X.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo, in a post on X, dismissed the Human Rights Watch report as part of a 30-year pattern of anonymous claims, no site visits or forensics, and 'sanctions first and investigation later'.
claims.place_as_written: Kigali (statement on X); subject: eastern DRC
claims.verification_note: Quote verbatim in p02; p01 paraphrases the same; translation accurate. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding.
claims.researcher_note: Same statement as E-IGIHE-a-001; Makolo's own words are the quoted English text in p02; p01 paraphrases.

claims.text: According to Igihe, Makolo said that HRW itself had stated that Kinshasa arms, supports and works closely with the FDLR, Wazalendo, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian army, which she said made HRW unable to take on an impartial investigation.
claims.place_as_written: Kigali (statement on X); subject: eastern DRC
claims.verification_note: Quote printed in p01; p02 paraphrases the same list. Translation adequate; "izingiyeho intambara n’akaga ku kiremwamuntu" rendered loosely but not in the statement. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 2)
claims.researcher_note: Party statement relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet. The Kinyarwanda phrase 'izingiyeho intambara n'akaga ku kiremwamuntu' is translated closely but is awkward in the original. Existing claims record UN/HRW findings on FARDC cooperation with FDLR and Wazalendo separately.

claims.text: Igihe reported that the Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda said that no HRW investigator set foot at the places named in the report, and that there were no visits, no exhumations for investigation and no laboratory tests.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Rwanda (Office of the Government Spokesperson)
claims.verification_note: Both pages print it; translation accurate. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding. HRW describes its own methods in its report.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan government claim about HRW methodology, not a finding. HRW's own methods are described in HRW's report (interviews with 102 former detainees per existing claim r1-SV-2026-031).

claims.text: According to Kigali, as reported by Igihe, HRW's own report acknowledges that the Congolese army has supported armed groups opposed to M23, including the FDLR.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Rwanda (Office of the Government Spokesperson)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p02. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding. Rwanda's characterisation of the HRW report; not checked against the report.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan government characterisation of the HRW report; not independently checked against the report. Date is the Igihe article date (12 June 2026).

claims.text: Igihe reported that the Rwandan statement cited passages in the HRW report saying that Congolese authorities armed, financed and coordinated operations with Wazalendo militias and that government support for such groups contributed to human rights violations.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Rwanda (Office of the Government Spokesperson)
