claims.text: According to Igihe, the Rwandan government said HRW claims to have satellite images showing killings 'carried out by Rwandan forces and M23', with features resembling graves, but that HRW cannot confirm whether they are graves or other objects.
claims.verification_note: p01 carries the full clause; p02 the general point. Translation accurate. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan government characterisation of the HRW report's use of satellite imagery. Useful lead: HRW satellite imagery of alleged graves.

claims.text: Rwanda's Office of the Government Spokesperson said, according to Igihe, that 'alleged M23 conduct cannot be treated as RDF conduct' and accused HRW of 'selective accountability', saying it focused primarily on Rwanda and M23 and paid insufficient attention to abuses by Congolese government forces and their allies.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Rwanda (Office of the Government Spokesperson)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p02. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan government statement relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet.

claims.text: Igihe reported that a 78-page HRW report published on 10 June alleges that Rwandan military forces and the M23 rebel movement carried out large-scale forced recruitment and abusive detention of captured combatants and civilians in North and South Kivu between mid-2024 and December 2025.
claims.actor_as_written: Rwandan military forces and M23 (alleged by HRW, as described by Igihe)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p02; the existence of the HRW report is not contested; the allegations remain HRW's. Igihe's description of the HRW report; the alleged period begins mid-2024, only the part from 1 January 2025 is in the edition window.
claims.researcher_note: Igihe's description of the HRW report (corroborates existence and scope of the HRW report already recorded; Igihe is partisan and this is not independent evidence of the underlying facts). HRW period begins mid-2024; only the part from 1 January 2025 falls in the edition window. In p01 Igihe describes the same report as covering deaths, unlawful detention and forced recruitment of civilians.

claims.text: Makolo said, according to Igihe, that the sustainable solution to the conflict is to implement the Washington agreement and impartial mediation aimed at ending the war and promoting regional cooperation; the English edition quotes her as saying the Washington peace accords remain 'the path forward'.
claims.verification_note: Both pages print it; translation accurate ("kubahiriza" = respecting/implementing). Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Rwanda's statement highlighted the FDLR as a key security threat and accused HRW of failing to adequately examine its role and its links to Congolese government forces.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Rwanda (Office of the Government Spokesperson)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p02. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet.

claims.text: Igihe reported that the Rwandan Office of the Government Spokesperson said HRW had not named the Congolese or Wazalendo individuals for whom it was calling for sanctions, and quoted it as saying 'HRW strongly condemns Rwanda and M23, while the support Kinshasa gives to violent armed groups is described in a deceptive/vague way'.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Rwanda (Office of the Government Spokesperson)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p01. "by’amahushuka" is closer to "superficially/in passing" than "deceptively"; the statement already hedges "deceptive/vague". Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 12)
claims.researcher_note: The Kinyarwanda 'by’amahushuka' is translated 'in a deceptive way' (literally 'deceptively/with deception'); meaning in context is that the support is described misleadingly or vaguely. Party statement.

claims.text: Igihe reported that in May 2026 AFC/M23 accused Human Rights Watch of defaming it, publishing falsehoods and ignoring the truth, in response to an HRW report released on 14 May that accuses its fighters of killing civilians in Uvira city, raping women and abducting people between December 2025 and January 2026.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (statement); HRW allegation against AFC/M23 fighters
claims.verification_note: Both passages verbatim on p01. Translation corrected: the "it works in line with the DRC government" clause refers to HRW. AFC/M23 statement as relayed by Igihe. Igihe dates the HRW report 14 May here; its 14 May article (p03) says 13 May. AFC/M23 reply also recorded via other outlets. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 13)
claims.researcher_note: Placeholder: excerpt anchor corrected below if needed. Igihe gives the HRW report date as 14 May; its article of 14 May (p03) says 13 May. Existing claims r1-SV-2026-008 and r2-G-UV-SVHC-010 record AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka's 15 May reply (via Actualite.cd).

claims.text: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 said the DRC army continues to work with the FDLR, which HRW does not want to address in its reports, and that HRW's bias makes the organisation lose credibility.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p01; translation accurate. AFC/M23 statement as relayed by Igihe (partisan).
claims.researcher_note: Party statement relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Rwandan Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo said on X on 14 May 2026 that 'HRW has a way of working and Rwanda is always its yardstick showing it has worked well'.
claims.place_as_written: Kigali (statement on X); subject: eastern DRC
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p03; translation accurate. Existing list in packet is empty, so the corroboration target could not be checked here. Party statement relayed by Igihe.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates existing claim r7-L-RW-002 (Umuryango.rw) on the same X post. Igihe is partisan; this is evidence of what Makolo said, not of the facts.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Makolo was criticising an HRW report released on 13 May that accuses Rwandan forces and M23 fighters of killing civilians, abducting them and raping women in Uvira city from 10 December 2025 to 17 January 2026.
claims.actor_as_written: Rwandan forces and M23 fighters (alleged by HRW, as described by Igihe)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p03; translation accurate. Igihe's description of the HRW Uvira report. Igihe dates the report 13 May here but 14 May in its 11 June article; discrepancy left as stated.
claims.researcher_note: Igihe's description of the HRW Uvira report; the report date is 13 May here but 14 May in Igihe's p01 and in other sources (BBC claim r2-G-UV-SVHC-011 dated 14 May). HRW's own findings are recorded in existing claims (e.g. r1-HC-2026-001, r1-HC-2026-003).

claims.text: Igihe reported that the Rwandan government has often told the international community that none of its troops are in eastern DRC and that it only put defensive measures on the border.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p03; translation accurate. Rwanda's position as relayed by Igihe; it conflicts with UN Group of Experts findings that RDF troops were deployed in eastern DRC.
claims.researcher_note: Rwanda's position as relayed by Igihe. It conflicts with UN Group of Experts findings that RDF troops were deployed in eastern DRC (see existing claims r1-UC-RDF-010, r1-GOE-005). Surfaced as a discrepancy, not resolved.

claims.text: Igihe wrote that in January 2025 armed units including the FDLR fired into Rubavu town while fighting M23 in Goma, and that many of the shells fired were neutralised by Rwandan forces.
claims.actor_as_written: armed forces including the FDLR (per Igihe)
claims.verification_note: "Ibisasu byinshi mu byarashwe" means "many of the shells fired", not "most"; narrowed. Igihe's own narration (Rwandan state-aligned); attribution of the fire to FDLR-including units is Igihe's. Exact dates not given. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 18)
claims.researcher_note: Single Rwandan state-aligned source; the attribution to FDLR rather than FARDC or others is Igihe's. Date given only as January 2025.

claims.text: Igihe wrote that HRW explained that those it interviewed included Burundian and DRC officials including soldiers, and argued that this makes the report highly doubtful because they are the ones fighting M23 in areas including Uvira.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p03; translation accurate. The argument is Igihe's editorial; the factual element should be checked against the HRW report methodology.
claims.researcher_note: The argument is Igihe's, not a party statement; the factual element (HRW interviewed Burundian and Congolese officials including soldiers) should be checked against the HRW report methodology.

claims.text: Igihe reported that the DRC army coalition was accused of shooting at a civilian plane carrying medicines and food to Minembwe commune on the morning of 27 August 2026; MRDP-Twirwaneho officer Colonel Fidèle Rugabo said the plane was hit by a shell from a gun on the ground as it reached the Bikuba area.
claims.actor_as_written: DRC army coalition (accused, per Twirwaneho via Igihe)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p04; translation accurate. "Civilian" and "medicines" are the Twirwaneho account as Igihe relays it; statement keeps "was accused". Accounts of the 27 August 2026 Minembwe plane downing conflict: Twirwaneho/AFC/M23 say a civilian aircraft carrying medicines and food; the Fizi administrator (LSi Africa) says it came from Rwanda carrying soldiers; Congolese security sources (ReelActu) say a rebel resupply flight; no independent confirmation of its nature (ReelActu, LSi).
claims.researcher_note: Single partisan Rwandan source relaying Twirwaneho. Independent reports (ReelActu, LSi Africa, Kivu Morning Post, 27-28 Aug 2026) confirm a plane was shot down near Minembwe but give conflicting accounts of its cargo and origin: see E-IGIHE-a-023 to 027. LSi puts the site at Bikuba, Fizi territory. No independent confirmation of civilian or military nature (ReelActu). Records for the downing: none found in project data at time of search. A search snippet mentions a similar earlier incident on 30 June (Instagram, unverified lead only).

claims.text: Colonel Fidèle Rugabo of MRDP-Twirwaneho said, according to Igihe: 'MRDP strongly condemned the shooting down of a civilian plane that was carrying medicines and food'.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p04; translation accurate. Party statement (MRDP-Twirwaneho) relayed by Igihe. Accounts of the 27 August 2026 Minembwe plane downing conflict: Twirwaneho/AFC/M23 say a civilian aircraft carrying medicines and food; the Fizi administrator (LSi Africa) says it came from Rwanda carrying soldiers; Congolese security sources (ReelActu) say a rebel resupply flight; no independent confirmation of its nature (ReelActu, LSi).
claims.researcher_note: Party statement. ReelActu (27 Aug) separately quotes 'Rugabo Fidèle' accusing the FARDC and calling it a 'provocation'.

claims.text: ReelActu reported that a plane was shot down on Thursday near the Minembwe aerodrome in the Fizi highlands, during the mission of the expanded Joint Verification Mechanism (MCVE+), and that the circumstances of its destruction and the nature of its cargo were the subject of opposing versions.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (versions conflict)
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts verbatim on the retained ReelActu page (byline Ghislain Watongoka, 27 Aug 2026 14:20). Downing also reported by LSi Africa and Kivu Morning Post; grade B kept conservatively. LSi Africa places the hit at Bikuba, about thirty kilometres from the Minembwe aerodrome; ReelActu says near the aerodrome. Accounts of the 27 August 2026 Minembwe plane downing conflict: Twirwaneho/AFC/M23 say a civilian aircraft carrying medicines and food; the Fizi administrator (LSi Africa) says it came from Rwanda carrying soldiers; Congolese security sources (ReelActu) say a rebel resupply flight; no independent confirmation of its nature (ReelActu, LSi).
claims.researcher_note: Independent Congolese outlet (ReelActu, journalist Ghislain Watongoka, 27 Aug 2026 14:20); corroborates the Igihe account that a plane was shot down. 'Thursday' is 27 August 2026 per the page date.

claims.text: ReelActu reported that Rugabo Fidèle, a member of the Twirwaneho-M23 coalition, publicly confirmed the destruction of the plane and accused the FARDC of shooting down 'a civil aircraft carrying medicines and food', calling the incident a 'provocation' that came two days after the MCVE+ team left Minembwe.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on retained ReelActu page. Party statement. Interval after the MCVE+ visit differs: two days after the team left (ReelActu), three days after the mission (LSi), the day after (Kivu Morning Post); Igihe dates the EJVM+ visit 25 August.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement as reported by an independent outlet. Note the interval: ReelActu says two days after the MCVE+ team left; LSi Africa says three days after a MCVE+ mission, and Igihe says EJVM+ visited Minembwe on 25 August.

claims.text: ReelActu reported that Congolese security sources maintain the plane was carrying out a resupply mission for rebel positions in the highlands.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on retained ReelActu page. Anonymous security sources. Accounts of the 27 August 2026 Minembwe plane downing conflict: Twirwaneho/AFC/M23 say a civilian aircraft carrying medicines and food; the Fizi administrator (LSi Africa) says it came from Rwanda carrying soldiers; Congolese security sources (ReelActu) say a rebel resupply flight; no independent confirmation of its nature (ReelActu, LSi).
claims.researcher_note: Anonymous Congolese security sources, relayed by ReelActu; the opposing account to Twirwaneho's 'civil aircraft carrying medicines'.

claims.text: ReelActu reported that no independent source had confirmed whether the plane was civil or military, or its exact cargo, and that the Congolese authorities had not yet published a communiqué detailing the circumstances of the operation.
claims.actor_as_written: Congolese authorities (no statement found as of the article)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on retained ReelActu page. Status as of ReelActu's 27 August 14:20 article.
claims.researcher_note: Records the absence of a Kinshasa/FARDC communiqué as of 27 Aug 2026 per ReelActu (see gap party_statements).

claims.text: LSi Africa reported that Fizi territory administrator Sammy Kalonji Badibanga said the plane came from Rwanda and was carrying soldiers, equipment and food, while sources linked to Twirwaneho-AFC/M23 described it as a civil aircraft linking Bukavu to Minembwe with medicines and equipment on board and two crew members.
claims.actor_as_written: Fizi territory administrator (DRC authority) vs Twirwaneho-AFC/M23 sources
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on retained LSi Africa page. LSi also says no verifiable element allows attribution of the projectile to Wazalendo, Burundian forces or another component. ReelActu spells the administrator "Samy Kalonji".
claims.researcher_note: Two opposing accounts recorded side by side by an independent outlet. LSi adds that no verifiable element makes it possible to attribute the missile to the Wazalendo, the Burundian forces or another component, and places the hit 'dans la matinée à Bikuba, dans le territoire de Fizi' (page text). Its dateline places the aerodrome distance at about thirty kilometres. Rwanda has not been found commenting on the claim that the plane came from Rwanda.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post wrote that a civil plane carrying medicines was shot down near Minembwe on Thursday, and that the Fizi territory administrator 'under the Kinshasa regime' claimed the attack, saying the plane had been shot down by the FARDC.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on retained KMP page (28 Aug 2026, La Rédaction). Grade C: single outlet, framing aligned with one party. Kivu Morning Post is Goma-based and uses AFC/M23 framing ("régime de Kinshasa"); its "civil plane carrying medicines" is unattributed narration. Its account of the administrator conflicts with LSi Africa's; not reconciled.
claims.researcher_note: Kivu Morning Post (28 Aug 2026) wording conflicts with LSi Africa's account of the same administrator's statement (plane came from Rwanda carrying soldiers); the two are not reconciled. KMP's framing 'régime de Kinshasa' and 'revendiqué' is the outlet's own.

claims.text: Igihe reported that the plane was shot down after the international body in charge of ceasefire monitoring (EJVM+) visited Minembwe on 25 August and assessed the effects of the attacks.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p04; translation accurate. ReelActu says the MCVE+ mission was deployed in Minembwe (Bashimukaku Sud) from 24 August; Igihe says the visit was on 25 August.
claims.researcher_note: ReelActu says the MCVE+ mission was deployed in Minembwe (Bashimukaku Sud) from 24 August; Igihe says the visit was on 25 August. Different start dates reported.

claims.text: According to Igihe, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo, FDLR and foreign mercenary forces began attacking Point-Zero, Nyaruhinga and Mukoko in Minembwe at about seven in the morning and that the DRC coalition was using combat drones and heavy weapons.
claims.actor_as_written: DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo, FDLR and foreign mercenary forces (as alleged by AFC/M23)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p04; "mu masaa moya y'igitondo" = around 7 a.m., correct. AFC/M23 statement relayed by Igihe (27 Aug). Kivu Morning Post quotes a Kanyuka statement on intensified attacks on Point Zéro from 04:00 on 28 August.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement relayed by Igihe. Compare Kivu Morning Post of 28 Aug 2026 (existing claim r1-SKS-2026Q3-001) for Kanyuka's later statement.

claims.text: Igihe reported, on the basis of unspecified information ('hari amakuru avuga'), that because of defeat the Burundian army leadership had asked its soldiers to return home quickly to avoid losing more lives in the war in the DRC.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p05; hedge preserved. Hedged in the source ("hari amakuru avuga" = there is information saying); unattributed.
claims.researcher_note: Unattributed rumour in a partisan outlet; hedged 'hari amakuru avuga' = 'there is information saying'. Other sources say a large part of Burundian troops withdrew in December 2025 (REC-0231).

claims.text: Igihe reported that from the morning of 8 December 2025 many Burundian troops, Imbonerakure and Wazalendo were fleeing from Uvira city to Bujumbura, and that residents who saw them said they looked exhausted.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p05; translation accurate. Date conflict: other sources date the fall of Uvira to the night of 9-10 December 2025; Igihe describes flight from Uvira on 8 December. Not reconciled.
claims.researcher_note: Date conflict to surface: other sources date the fall of Uvira to the night of 9 to 10 December 2025 (REC-0113; SOS Médias dateline 10 Dec: city fell night of 9 December). Igihe describes flight from Uvira on 8 December, before the city was taken. Not reconciled.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Burundian, DRC and Wazalendo forces were being overpowered because they had lost many areas, and that AFC/M23 fighters who left Kamanyola the previous week had reached Sange, about 30 kilometres towards Uvira city.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p05; translation accurate. Igihe narration (Rwandan state-aligned).
claims.researcher_note: Compare REC-0212 (M23 reported advancing to Luberizi, Luvungi, 6 Dec) and REC-0214 (7 Dec Sange explosion). Igihe says AFC/M23 left Kamanyola 'last week' (week before 8 Dec); Kamanyola had been under AFC/M23 since February 2025.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Burundi had sent nearly 20 thousand soldiers ('ibihumbi 20') to South Kivu, many of whom went to areas around Minembwe in Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, closing the routes by which Banyamulenge went to markets and clinics.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe area (Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p05; "hafi ibihumbi 20" = nearly 20,000, correct. Allegation by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet; Twirwaneho makes the same allegation. Troop figure unverified.
claims.researcher_note: Allegation by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet (the same allegation is made by Twirwaneho, see E-IGIHE-a-062); existing records REC-0202 and claim r1-UC-BI-FDLR-034 (OCHA warned of difficulties accessing food and healthcare in Minembwe) record the blockade independently. Troop figure is the same as Rwanda's statement of 10 Dec 2025 (r1-ST-RW-007).

claims.text: Igihe reported that it is said ('biravugwa') that Lieutenant Colonel Athanase Minani, commander of the eighth battalion of the Burundian forces fighting in eastern DRC, was shot dead by AFC/M23; the news began circulating on the evening of 5 December 2025, with reports that he fell in fighting at Luvungi that killed many other Burundian soldiers fighting beside the FARDC.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts verbatim on p06; hedges preserved; translation accurate. Death reported, hedged by Igihe ("biravugwa", "bivugwa"); neither the Burundian army nor AFC/M23 had confirmed it as of 6 Dec 2025 (Igihe). SOS Médias Burundi (8 Dec) also lists him among the dead.
claims.researcher_note: Hedged ('biravugwa', 'bivugwa') in the source. Corroborated independently by Congovirtuel (existing claim r1-SKS-2025Q4-018) and SOS Médias Burundi (E-IGIHE-a-044).

claims.text: Igihe reported that Pacifique Nininahazwe, head of FOCODE, said on X that Lieutenant Colonel Athanase Minani (SS1564), commander of the eighth battalion of Burundian forces in the DRC (TAFOC), was shot dead the previous night with his three guards, and that he was the highest-ranking FDNB soldier killed in this war.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p06; translation accurate. The three guards are not named. Death reported, hedged by Igihe ("biravugwa", "bivugwa"); neither the Burundian army nor AFC/M23 had confirmed it as of 6 Dec 2025 (Igihe). SOS Médias Burundi (8 Dec) also lists him among the dead. Nininahazwe is a Burundian human-rights activist (FOCODE).
claims.researcher_note: Nininahazwe is a Burundian human-rights activist (FOCODE), not a party; his X statement is the originating claim. 'Last night' relative to 5 Dec evening: date approximate. The three guards are unnamed.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that among the Burundian soldiers killed since 1 December in the localities of Lubarika, Mitambili, Katogota, Luvungi and Sange was Lieutenant-Colonel Athanase Minani, the highest-ranking Burundian officer killed since the start of the official intervention in the DRC.
claims.place_as_written: Lubarika, Mitambili, Katogota, Luvungi, Sange (Uvira territory)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on retained SOS page (Adam Ntwari, 8 Dec 2025). No official Burundian confirmation recorded on the page ("Aucune communication officielle n’a été faite" refers to Sange deaths).
claims.researcher_note: SOS Médias Burundi's original text (8 Dec 2025). The page also says the Burundian authorities were silent on real losses. Independent of Igihe; consistent with Congovirtuel (r1-SKS-2025Q4-018).

claims.text: Igihe reported that neither the Burundian army nor AFC/M23 had confirmed the death of the senior Burundian soldier (Lt Col Minani).
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p06. As of the article date (6 Dec 2025).
claims.researcher_note: Absence of confirmation as of the article date. No search was run by this agent for later statements (see gap).

claims.text: Igihe wrote that information reaching it said AFC/M23 had learned that DRC, Burundian and Wazalendo forces were about to attack it at Kamanyola and decided to fire first; a person close to AFC/M23's top leadership told it that the explosions heard on the morning of 2 December were fired by AFC/M23 fighters and had seriously shaken the DRC government coalition.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (per a person close to its leadership)
claims.verification_note: The pre-emption account is Igihe's "reliable information", not the person close to the leadership; split the attribution. Translation accurate. Anonymous partisan account of who fired first; the opposing account is that AFC/M23 started the clashes.
claims.researcher_note: Anonymous partisan account; the other side's version is that AFC/M23 started the clashes (see SOS Médias claim r1-SKC-2025H2-007 on exchanges of fire at Katogota/Kamanyola on 2 December).

claims.text: Igihe reported that, on the same day as the explosions it dates to the morning of 2 December, DRC and Burundian forces fired on Kamanyola centre, held by AFC/M23 for nearly 10 months, with shells destroying civilian homes and infrastructure; three civilians died and others were injured.
claims.verification_note: Supported on p06. Replacement quote extended to the preceding sentence so the "2 December" date is printed; figures field written in the source's words. Single Rwandan state-aligned source; casualty figure unverified. Other reports of the 2 December exchanges give different civilian casualty figures.
claims.researcher_note: Single partisan source; see REC-0209 (SOS Médias: exchange of fire around Katogota and Kamanyola, five civilians wounded) and REC-0211.

claims.text: Igihe reported that since the morning of 5 December 2025 DRC, Burundian and Wazalendo forces were attacking areas of Uvira territory including Katogota, Kamanyola and Luvungi groupement, and that shells falling on Luvungi made many residents flee to areas such as Sange, Runingu, Ndolera and Uvira city.
claims.actor_as_written: DRC, Burundian and Wazalendo forces (per Igihe)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p06; translation accurate. Single Rwandan state-aligned source; Igihe attributes the attacks to the government coalition.
claims.researcher_note: Single partisan source; compare REC-0212 and REC-0211.

claims.text: Bertrand Bisimwa, Deputy Leader of AFC/M23 in charge of political activities, said, according to Igihe, that Burundian forces inside Burundi were shelling heavily populated areas of Kamanyola, Katogota and Luvungi, causing the deaths of innocent people including children and destroying houses, schools, churches and markets.
claims.place_as_written: Kamanyola, Katogota, Luvungi (Uvira territory); shelling alleged from Burundian territory
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p06; translation accurate. AFC/M23 allegation of cross-border shelling; "this morning" in an article dated 6 Dec 00:28, so probably 5 Dec. No casualty figures given.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement; date approximate ('this morning' in an article published at 00:28 on 6 Dec 2025, so probably 5 Dec). Cross-border shelling allegation. See REC-0211 and UN Group of Experts claim r1-GOE-005.

claims.text: Igihe reported that the fighting continued after Rwanda and the DRC signed a peace agreement on 4 December 2025, which AFC/M23 said does not concern it.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p06. AFC/M23 position as relayed by Igihe.
claims.researcher_note: Party position as relayed by Igihe; the place of signature is not stated in this excerpt.

claims.text: Igihe reported that earlier in the week of the article, DRC media outlets reported that AFC/M23 was withdrawing fighters from areas it listed as Lubero, Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese and relocating them to Alimbongo, Kirumba and Kanyabayonga, and that the move was prompted by pressure from the United States government.
claims.place_as_written: Lubero territory: Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi, Kipese; Alimbongo, Kirumba, Kanyabayonga
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p07 (English edition). Igihe relays unnamed Congolese media reports; the US-pressure motive is what those reports "suggested". AFC/M23 denied a withdrawal. Igihe calls the localities "territories"; only Lubero is a territory.
claims.researcher_note: Reports of a pull-back that AFC/M23 denied (E-IGIHE-a-052). Igihe lists the areas as 'territories'. Compare Anadolu/Radio Okapi account of 23 March 2026 (r1-NKN-2026H1-002, REC-1008).

claims.text: According to Igihe, North Kivu Governor Erasto Bahati (AFC/M23 administration) dismissed the reports of withdrawal in a statement, saying the activities along the front were regular troop rotations within AFC/M23 and that the rumours were fuelled by social media and the Kinshasa government.
claims.verification_note: Supported verbatim on p07; reworded only for clarity (the draft said "said ... that the reports were dismissed"). Bahati is the AFC/M23-appointed governor. Statement date is the Igihe article date (29 March 2026); the statement may be earlier.
claims.researcher_note: Governor Bahati is the AFC/M23-appointed governor of North Kivu. Statement date is the Igihe article date (29 March 2026); the statement itself may be a day or two earlier.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye said in an interview with Jeune Afrique published on 10 May 2026 that the closure of the Gatumba and Vugizo border crossings with the DRC was linked to the proximity of M23 fighters near Burundi's borders, alleging that M23 operates with Rwanda's backing.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p08 (Igihe English edition, 11 May 2026). Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked.
claims.researcher_note: Interview relayed by Igihe, which frames the remarks as 'false' in its own text. Jeune Afrique original not checked by this agent; compare existing Burundian border-closure records (REC-0115, REC-0020).

claims.text: According to Igihe, Ndayishimiye said that Burundi considers the presence of M23 fighters near its borders a security concern and expressed hope that the Washington peace agreement would increase pressure to end the tensions.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p08 (Igihe English edition, 11 May 2026). Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked.
claims.researcher_note: Interview relayed by Igihe.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye maintained that Burundian troops were sent to the DRC to assist Congolese forces against their enemies rather than to defend Burundi itself, under regional arrangements that assigned South Kivu as Burundi's operational zone.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p08 (Igihe English edition, 11 May 2026). Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked.
claims.researcher_note: Interview relayed by Igihe.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye argued that fighting continued despite regional efforts because some countries failed to contain the conflict, and that only Uganda and Burundi remained actively engaged, with Burundian troops operating under the directives of the Congolese army.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p08 (Igihe English edition, 11 May 2026). Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked.
claims.researcher_note: Interview relayed by Igihe; relevant to command and control of Burundian troops (FDNB under FARDC directives).

claims.text: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye repeated accusations that Rwanda supports RED Tabara, a group Burundi describes as terrorist, and that Rwanda has consistently denied this, insisting it does not support any group seeking to destabilize Burundi.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Burundi (Ndayishimiye); Government of Rwanda (denial)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p08. Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked. The Rwandan denial is Igihe background, not a new statement.
claims.researcher_note: The Rwandan denial is stated by Igihe as background, not as a fresh statement.

claims.text: Igihe reported that, asked about Rwanda's accusation that Burundi collaborates with the FDLR, Ndayishimiye said he had asked President Paul Kagame for intelligence on FDLR positions and that Burundi would attack the group if given such information.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p08 (Igihe English edition, 11 May 2026). Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked.
claims.researcher_note: Interview relayed by Igihe.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye acknowledged that Congolese forces work with the FDLR, but argued that Burundian troops operate separately under Congolese command structures and do not mix with those groups.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p08. Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked. The acknowledgement of FARDC-FDLR cooperation rests on Igihe's paraphrase only; check the Jeune Afrique original before relying on it.
claims.researcher_note: Significant if accurate: a head of state acknowledging FARDC-FDLR cooperation. Relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet; check against the Jeune Afrique original.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye proposed coordinated military action by Rwanda, the DRC, Burundi and Uganda against armed groups in the region, saying this could reassure Rwanda about its security concerns.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p08 (Igihe English edition, 11 May 2026). Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked.
claims.researcher_note: Interview relayed by Igihe.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Burundi had deployed more than 20,000 troops to South Kivu under bilateral agreements with the DRC, and that the deployment was reduced in early December 2025 after M23 fighters captured several areas in the Ruzizi Plain and the city of Uvira.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p08. Igihe background narration; troop figure not officially confirmed by Burundi.
claims.researcher_note: Igihe background text. Corroborates REC-0231 and the Rwandan government figure (r1-ST-RW-007).

claims.text: Igihe, relaying an AFC/M23 communiqué, reported that seven people died, three were seriously injured and one lightly injured on Saturday 12 September 2026 when an explosive device, which the communiqué describes as planted by those AFC/M23 called enemies, went off at Jomba, Gikoro, Rugunga village in Rutshuru, after a child found it in a field and began handling it.
claims.verification_note: All three passages verbatim on p09; translations accurate. Figures field written as the words the source prints (the excerpts give no digits). AFC/M23 communiqué as relayed by Igihe; other outlets report the same blast with differing details. Igihe uses Rwandan administrative terms (Umurenge/sector, Ntara/province) for Rutshuru. The child is not named and the child's fate is not stated.
claims.researcher_note: AFC/M23 communiqué relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet. Radio Okapi and Actualite.cd (existing claim r1-NKS-2026Q3-006) report the same blast with differing details. Igihe calls Rutshuru a 'province' (it is a territory). The child who found the device is not named and his status (killed or injured) is not stated.

claims.text: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 expressed deep sorrow, condoled with the families, and asked residents of liberated areas to follow instructions on avoiding explosives still in the ground, not to touch, move or try to dismantle anything they suspect may be a bomb.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p09; translation accurate. Party communiqué; "liberated areas" is AFC/M23's term.
claims.researcher_note: Party communiqué as relayed by Igihe.

claims.text: Igihe reported that DRC soldiers and fighters of the Wazalendo alliance exchanged fire in Uvira city overnight, with heavy gunfire (AK-47 and machine guns) heard from eight in the evening on 5 September 2025, because of a disagreement.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p10; "masaa mbiri y'ijoro" = 8 p.m., correct. Single Rwandan state-aligned source; no casualties reported.
claims.researcher_note: Single partisan source; casualties not mentioned. Related events: Wazalendo protests against General Gasita in Uvira from 2 September (REC-0093), and deaths from demonstrations (REC-0097).

claims.text: Igihe reported, on unspecified information ('amakuru avuga'), that the Wazalendo fighters who exchanged fire with the DRC army belonged to the armed group led by 'Général' John Makanaki, which has operated in South Kivu for a long time.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo group led by 'Général' John Makanaki
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p10; hedge preserved. Hedged in the source ("amakuru avuga" = information says). Name printed "John Makanaki"; other sources print other forms.
claims.researcher_note: Hedged ('amakuru avuga'). Name 'John Makanaki' as printed; other sources print Makanaki Kasimbira John / René Makanaki (existing claims r7-CMD-WZ-008, r1-UV-2025Q2-001).

claims.text: Igihe reported that since 2 September 2025 Wazalendo had been in a major protest in Uvira demanding that DRC Brig Gen Gasita Olivier leave the city because, they claimed, he is Rwandan, doubting his nationality because he is a Munyamulenge; Wazalendo closed the main road, halting all economic activity.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p10; translation accurate. "ngo" hedge preserved ("they claimed").
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0093 (demonstrations against Gasita). The ethnic basis of the demand (Munyamulenge identity) is relevant to discrimination.

claims.text: Igihe reported that on 5 September 2025 the acting mayor of Uvira, Kifara Kapenda Kik'v, led a meeting to calm tensions attended by Wazalendo leaders including Makanaki and 'Général' William Amur Yakutumba, but it achieved nothing as the protest continued.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p10. Igihe says acting mayor ("Meya w'agateganyo"); Radio Okapi calls him deputy mayor. Name spelled as Igihe prints it.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi (existing claim r1-UV-2025Q3-017) calls Kifara Kapenda the deputy mayor of Uvira; Igihe says 'Meya w'agateganyo' (acting mayor). Name spelled as Igihe prints it.

claims.text: Wazalendo leader William Yakutumba said at the meeting held in Uvira, according to Igihe: 'That leader who was sent here, called Gen Gasita, we do not want him here in Uvira'.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p10; translation accurate. Party statement relayed by Igihe.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement. Name printed 'William Amur Yakutumba' elsewhere on the page.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Yakutumba insisted Brig Gen Gasita must leave Uvira, and that Makanaki said that if the soldier had not left by 8 September his fighters would close the DRC-Burundi border and the Uvira port on Lake Tanganyika.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p10; translation accurate. Threat, as relayed by Igihe.
claims.researcher_note: Threat to close the border and port (a civilian-supply and humanitarian concern). Party statement.

claims.text: FARDC spokesperson Maj Gen Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa, according to Igihe, had asked Wazalendo to accept Brig Gen Gasita, explaining that he had not betrayed the country and had been appointed by the Head of State; the fighters refused and asked for his replacement.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p10; translation accurate. Igihe does not date Ekenge's appeal (pluperfect "yari yasabye"; before 6 Sept 2025).
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates existing claims r1-UV-2025Q3-031 and r1-UV-2025Q3-032 (Ekenge's statements). Date of the statement not given by Igihe (before 6 Sept 2025).

claims.text: Igihe reported that on the morning of 25 September 2025 various media reported that M23 had deployed additional troops and weapons in Lubero territory to strengthen control over Kipese, Katondi, Munyakandomi, Vulera and Kirumba.
claims.place_as_written: Kipese, Katondi, Munyakandomi, Vulera, Kirumba (Lubero territory)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p11 (English edition, 26 Sep 2025). Igihe wrongly places Lubero territory in South Kivu; it is in North Kivu. Igihe relays unnamed media reports.
claims.researcher_note: Igihe wrongly says Lubero is 'located in South Kivu Province' (it is in North Kivu); the places named are in Lubero territory. Corroborates Actualite.cd (r4-G-LOCAL-NK-002, vehicles shuttling Kirumba-Katondi).

claims.text: Igihe reported that in February 2025 M23 captured the Kitsombiro area in Lubero after intense clashes with the FARDC.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p11. Spelled "Kitsombiro" by Igihe; other outlets print "Kitsumbiro". Igihe background narration.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0973 (Kipese and Katondi taken after the fall of Kitsumbiro). Igihe spells Kitsombiro; Kivu Morning Post spells Kitsumbiro.

claims.text: Igihe reported that M23 had also reinforced its forces in the localities of Rusamambu and Bukumbirwa, which it read as signalling plans to extend control to other parts of what it called South Kivu Province.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p11; narrowed so the interpretation and the mislabelled province are Igihe's. Igihe wrongly places Lubero territory in South Kivu; it is in North Kivu. The territory of Rusamambu and Bukumbirwa is not stated; the "plans to expand" reading is Igihe's.
claims.researcher_note: Igihe does not say which territory Rusamambu and Bukumbirwa are in; the interpretation ('plans to expand') is Igihe's. Place names as printed.

claims.text: AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a statement on Thursday 3 April 2025, according to Igihe, that the group had repositioned its forces in Walikale and surroundings, and warned that if Kinshasa regime forces persisted in provocations or attacked civilians in liberated areas or AFC/M23 positions, the goodwill gesture would be cancelled and 'we will eliminate the threat at its source'.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p12 ("Walikale and its surroundings" is in the quoted statement). AFC/M23 statement relayed by Igihe (4 April 2025). The UN Group of Experts gives a different cause for the early-April withdrawal.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement; the page is the English text on fr.igihe.com. Corroborates REC-0400 (announced AFC/M23 withdrawal from Walikale and reactions). UN Group of Experts (r1-GOE-075) attributes the early April withdrawal to FARDC airstrikes, a different cause.

claims.text: Igihe reported that M23 took control of Walikale on 19 March 2025, notably seizing the Kigoma airstrip, after conquering several surrounding localities including Ngora, Kisima and Mubanda.
claims.place_as_written: Walikale; Kigoma airstrip; Ngora, Kisima, Mubanda
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p12. Igihe background narration; consistent with UN reporting that M23 took Walikale town on 19 March 2025.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0395 (UN Secretary-General: M23 took control of Walikale town on 19 March 2025 and withdrew shortly afterwards).

claims.text: Igihe reported that after taking Walikale the rebel group announced its withdrawal, describing it as 'a choice aimed at creating a climate conducive to political dialogue', and called on local authorities and residents to guarantee security in the region.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p12. Announcement date not given in the excerpt; Igihe refers to an AFC/M23 press release of Sunday 23 March 2025.
claims.researcher_note: Date of the withdrawal announcement not given in the excerpt; Igihe refers elsewhere in the article to the AFC/M23 press release of Sunday 23 March 2025.

claims.text: Igihe reported that the AFC/M23-appointed Governor of North Kivu, Bahati Musanga Erasto, changed the leadership of Goma city, and that a notice of 9 April 2026 named Kisuba Ngabo Désiré, until then deputy mayor, mayor of Goma, replacing Julien Katembo Ndalieni, who became head of Lubero territory.
claims.verification_note: Both passages verbatim on p13; translations accurate. Igihe cites a notice of 9 April 2026; another outlet dates the reshuffle 8 April 2026. Spellings as Igihe prints them (its photo caption prints "Kasuba Ngabo"); other outlets print variants.
claims.researcher_note: Date conflict: Kivu Morning Post (existing claim r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-009) dates the reshuffle 8 April 2026, Igihe cites a notice of 9 April 2026. Name spellings differ: Igihe 'Kisuba Ngabo Désiré', 'Julien Katembo Ndalieni'; KMP 'Désiré Kisuba Ngabo', 'Julienne Katembo Ndalieni'. Printed as Igihe prints them.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Nshimiyimana Juvénal, who had been in charge of mobilisation and recruiting new fighters in AFC/M23, was named deputy mayor of Goma.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p13; "gushaka abarwanyi bashya" = recruiting new fighters, correct. Name as Igihe prints it; another outlet prints "Juvénal Nshimimana".
claims.researcher_note: New detail on a de facto official's earlier role (recruitment), relevant to forced-recruitment leads (REC-0304). Kivu Morning Post prints the name 'Juvénal Nshimimana' (r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-010).

claims.text: Katembo said in an interview with Igihe in January 2026 that Goma was now safe and that all activities, including trade, were going better than before.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 de facto authority in Goma
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p13; translation accurate. Only "Katembo" is printed in this sentence (in context, apparently the outgoing mayor Julien Katembo Ndalieni). De facto official's claim; conflicts with UN and NGO reports of insecurity in Goma.
claims.researcher_note: Only 'Katembo' is printed in the sentence; the article elsewhere names Julien Katembo Ndalieni as the replaced mayor. Party claim; contradicts reports of insecurity in Goma recorded by UN and NGOs.

claims.text: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 took the city of Goma on 27 January 2025 and then installed new officials to bring it back on track in security, welfare and infrastructure projects.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p13. Igihe narration; it names AFC/M23 alone (other sources record RDF participation).
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0247 (capture of Goma by AFC/M23 and RDF, 26-29 January 2025). Igihe gives AFC/M23 alone.

claims.text: Igihe reported that MDRP-Twirwaneho had for days been saying that many Burundian troops were deployed around Minembwe, including Mikenke, Point-Zéro, Makombo, Mikalati, Gipupu, Murambya and Mwenga, to starve the Banyamulenge by closing the roads they use to go to buy supplies.
claims.place_as_written: Mikenke, Point-Zéro, Makombo, Mikalati, Gipupu, Murambya, Mwenga (around Minembwe)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p14; translation accurate. MRDP-Twirwaneho is a party to the conflict (allied with AFC/M23); relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned). The intent to starve is Twirwaneho's allegation. Igihe prints "MDRP" here, elsewhere "MRDP".
claims.researcher_note: Party allegation relayed by a partisan outlet; corroborates existing records on the Minembwe blockade (REC-0202). 'MDRP' (printed so here) is the same group elsewhere printed MRDP-Twirwaneho.

claims.text: Igihe reported that during heavy fighting in the Ruzizi Plain since the start of the previous week many Burundian troops left areas they controlled such as Sange, Runingo, Kiliba and Uvira town, fleeing along with the DRC forces, Wazalendo and the FDLR.
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian troops, DRC forces, Wazalendo, FDLR (fleeing); AFC/M23 advancing
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p14. Igihe narration; the presence of FDLR among those fleeing is Igihe's claim.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0231 (large part of Burundian soldiers withdrew) and REC-0113 (Uvira taken). The mention of the FDLR among those fleeing is Igihe's.

claims.text: Igihe reported ('bivugwa') that the Burundian troops left these areas on an order from their top command because they had lost many soldiers in the war, including one of their leaders, Lt Col Athanase Minani, and that many were taken prisoner.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p14; hedge preserved. Hedged ("bivugwa" = it is said). The claim that many were captured is uncorroborated here.
claims.researcher_note: Hedged ('Bivugwa'). Claim that many were captured (as prisoners of war) is not corroborated elsewhere in this pass; see M23's earlier presentation of captured Burundian soldiers (not in this file).

claims.text: Igihe reported that Wazalendo groups affirm that some Burundian soldiers fled with them into the Itombwe forest, where they were going to regroup to attack various areas controlled by AFC/M23.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p14. Unnamed Wazalendo groups as relayed by Igihe.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement ('Wazalendo groups') relayed by a partisan outlet.

claims.text: Mugisha Nkurunziza Alexis, Vice-President of MRDP-Twirwaneho, told Igihe on 11 December 2025 that Burundian troops were still numerous in the high areas around Minembwe and said: 'The Burundian troops are still where they were. Even now Burundians are fighting the self-defending residents there at Irango, at Ndondo'.
claims.verification_note: Name order corrected to the form the excerpt prints ("Mugisha Nkurunziza Alexis"). Translation accurate ("abaturage birwanaho" = residents defending themselves). MRDP-Twirwaneho is a party to the conflict (allied with AFC/M23); relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned).
claims.researcher_note: Party statement given to Igihe. Name printed 'Mugisha Nkurunziza Alexis' here and 'Alexis Mugisha Nkurunziza' in p15.

claims.text: Igihe reported that on 6 December Burundian troops took hostage nearly 100 civilians who had gone shopping in areas bordering Minembwe, and that Twirwaneho explained that some were taken to the Mikalati military camp and others to an unknown place; Nkurunziza said the troops had since released these civilians.
claims.place_as_written: areas bordering Minembwe; Mikalati military camp
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p14; translation accurate. MRDP-Twirwaneho is a party to the conflict (allied with AFC/M23); relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned). Igihe states the hostage-taking as fact but its account rests on Twirwaneho; no victims named; unverified figure.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0213 (attack on residents returning from Bijombo market, killings, abduction; SOS Médias Burundi). Twirwaneho allegation relayed by a partisan outlet; no names.

claims.text: Nkurunziza of MRDP-Twirwaneho said, according to Igihe, that the Burundian troops had disgraced their country in this war, that their best option was to go home, and that otherwise they would be removed by force from the high hills around Minembwe.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p14; "zatesheje agaciro" = devalued/disgraced, fine. MRDP-Twirwaneho is a party to the conflict (allied with AFC/M23); relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned).
claims.researcher_note: Party statement/threat relayed by a partisan outlet.

claims.text: Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu, AFC/M23 deputy chief of staff, arrived in Uvira city on 10 December 2025 and asked the Burundian troops still in the high hills of South Kivu to come down and go home in peace, saying 'We have no problem with the Burundians because we are neighbours'.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p14; translation accurate. AFC/M23 commander's statement relayed by Igihe; places Byamungu in Uvira on 10 December 2025.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0113 (AFC/M23 and RDF take control of Uvira, 10 December 2025) and places Byamungu in Uvira that day; UN Group of Experts (r1-GOE-004) says the offensive was under his and Makenga's command. Igihe prints 'Umugaba Mukuru Wungirije' (Deputy Chief of Staff).

claims.text: Igihe reported that FARDC's military spokesperson in South Kivu, Lt Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, said in a communiqué that FARDC had been controlling Minembwe since the night of 17 June 2026, that Twirwaneho fighters were fleeing towards Walungu territory, and that FARDC had captured many MRDP-Twirwaneho and M23 fighters, weapons, ammunition and other military equipment.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p15; translation accurate. No figures for captured fighters. Contested control of Minembwe in June 2026: FARDC claimed it (Lt Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji); MRDP-Twirwaneho denied it. Another outlet quotes Kalonji dating the FARDC advance from the evening of 16 June.
claims.researcher_note: FARDC claim relayed by a partisan outlet, contested by Twirwaneho (E-IGIHE-a-095). Existing claims: r1-SKS-2026Q2-005 (Actualite.cd, Kalonji said FARDC had since the evening of Tuesday 16 June retaken positions), REC-0634, REC-0635, REC-0637.

claims.text: Igihe reported that MRDP-Twirwaneho Vice-President Alexis Mugisha Nkurunziza said the claim that DRC forces had taken Minembwe was false, and that Col Fidèle Rugabo affirmed that the group still controls Minembwe, saying 'The lies are many. Up to now we are still in Minembwe... Long live M23'.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p15; translation accurate. Contested control of Minembwe in June 2026: FARDC claimed it (Lt Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji); MRDP-Twirwaneho denied it. Another outlet quotes Kalonji dating the FARDC advance from the evening of 16 June. Party statements given to Igihe.
claims.researcher_note: Party statements given to Igihe; the second is a direct quote. Counterclaim to the FARDC communiqué of E-IGIHE-a-094. UN Secretary-General later (July) recorded Twirwaneho and M23 regaining Point Zero (REC-0642).

claims.text: Igihe reported that MRDP-Twirwaneho President Dr Freddy Kaniki Rukema told journalists at a press conference in Goma on 18 June that DRC government forces had intensified attacks in Minembwe, that attacks on civilians there had increased and that the international community knew but was doing nothing; asked whether Minembwe had been taken, he said they had not done it and would not.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p15; removed the year "2026" from the statement because the excerpt prints only "18 Kamena" (date field keeps 2026-06-18). Contested control of Minembwe in June 2026: FARDC claimed it (Lt Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji); MRDP-Twirwaneho denied it. Another outlet quotes Kalonji dating the FARDC advance from the evening of 16 June. Party statement at a press conference in AFC/M23-held Goma.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement at a press conference in Goma (AFC/M23-held city). Second excerpt is the answer to the journalist's question about Minembwe having been taken.

claims.text: Igihe reported, citing reliable information from South Kivu, that despite the difficult mountainous terrain M23 fighters had reached Minembwe to join Twirwaneho in protecting the security of residents.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p15. Anonymous "reliable information" in a Rwandan state-aligned outlet; the protective purpose is the source's framing.
claims.researcher_note: Unnamed 'reliable information' in a partisan outlet; presence of M23 fighters in Minembwe is relevant to the Rwanda/M23 linkage question. UN Secretary-General (REC-0642) records Twirwaneho and M23 operating together near Minembwe in July.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Burundian troops had also reached the front to help the DRC forces take Minembwe commune, but that available information says they had recently lost many soldiers, some of whose bodies were loaded onto a truck and taken to Bujumbura.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p15; hedge preserved. Hedged and unattributed ("amakuru ahari avuga" = available information says); no figures.
claims.researcher_note: Unattributed claim ('amakuru ahari avuga'); no figures. Compare SOS Médias Burundi reports on repatriation of bodies (r1 / REC-0210 context).

claims.text: Igihe reported that on 25 December 2025 Wazalendo fighters appeared in Makobola centre (Fizi territory) saying they had driven AFC/M23 out, and that their spokesperson, named Winston Makufuli, said 'People should remain calm, we have taken Makobola back. We thank President Félix Tshisekedi who sent FARDC troops to protect our country's security'.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p16; translation accurate. Accounts of AFC/M23's departure from Makobola differ: Wazalendo say they drove it out; Igihe's "reliable information" and a resident say it left without fighting.
claims.researcher_note: Party claim relayed by Igihe; contested by Igihe's own reporting (E-IGIHE-a-100). Corroborates Umuryango's account (existing claim r7-E-UV-038 on AFC/M23 leaving Makobola on 25 December). Records: AFC/M23 had occupied Makobola 2 on 13-14 Dec (REC-0229).

claims.text: Igihe reported, on 'reliable information' and a resident's account, that AFC/M23 left Makobola without fighting, as 25 December was calm and residents were celebrating Christmas; a Makobola resident said that in the afternoon ("saa munani z'amanywa") they saw the fighters heading towards Uvira with their luggage and that FARDC and Wazalendo arrived a few minutes later.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p16. Replaced the numeral "2 p.m." (not printed) with the source's own time expression. Accounts of AFC/M23's departure from Makobola differ: Wazalendo say they drove it out; Igihe's "reliable information" and a resident say it left without fighting. "Saa munani z'amanywa" is 2 p.m. in Kinyarwanda time reckoning. AFC/M23 said it had left Uvira by 18 December, so its fighters heading to Uvira on 25 December is not explained.
claims.researcher_note: Unnamed resident and 'reliable information' in a partisan outlet; AFC/M23 had said it withdrew from Uvira by 18 December (E-IGIHE-a-102), so its presence heading to Uvira on 25 December is unexplained. Umuryango (r7-E-UV-038) says fighters were attacked as they left.

claims.text: Igihe reported that on 24 December there was heavy fighting in various parts of Makobola centre, caused by drone and heavy-weapon attacks launched by DRC forces and Wazalendo, at Makobola 1, Makobola 2, Kiringi, Kirambi and elsewhere, causing many residents to flee to safer areas including Uvira city.
claims.verification_note: Removed the year from the statement because the excerpt prints only day and month (the date field keeps the year from the 26 Dec 2025 article). Single Rwandan state-aligned source; attribution of the attacks to DRC forces and Wazalendo is Igihe's.
claims.researcher_note: Single partisan source; related earlier fighting: REC-0236 (Bangwi and Makobola, 21 December).

claims.text: Igihe reported that on the morning of 26 December DRC forces and Wazalendo fired on Kalundu port on Lake Tanganyika, by Uvira city, using war drones.
claims.verification_note: Removed the year from the statement because the excerpt prints only day and month (the date field keeps the year from the 26 Dec 2025 article). "adjacent to" softened to "by". Single Rwandan state-aligned source; no casualty figures. "ahaherera ku mujyi wa Uvira" read as "by/at the edge of Uvira city". 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 101)
claims.researcher_note: The word 'ahaherera' in the original is translated 'adjoining' (uncertain). Umuryango (existing claim r7-E-UV-037) reports the same Kalundu attack, adding two AFC/M23 boats were hit. No casualty figures here.

claims.text: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 affirms that by 18 December all its fighters had left Uvira city, to build confidence in the Doha talks with the DRC government.
claims.verification_note: Removed the year from the statement because the excerpt prints only day and month (the date field keeps the year from the 26 Dec 2025 article). AFC/M23's claim. The UN Group of Experts says AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026; discrepancy surfaced, not resolved.
claims.researcher_note: AFC/M23's claim (partisan). The UN Group of Experts (r1-UC-RDF-011, REC-0005) says AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026, a month later; Ebuteli dates it 16 January. Discrepancy surfaced, not resolved. See REC-0127 (AFC/M23 announces unilateral withdrawal, competing statements).

claims.text: Igihe reported that Point-Zéro was captured by AFC/M23 and MRDP-Twirwaneho fighters in the middle of the night of 4 July 2026, after heavy fighting against DRC forces allied with Burundian forces, Wazalendo and the FDLR.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p17; translation accurate. Capture date as Igihe states it ("mu gicuku cyo ku wa 4 Nyakanga 2026"); other records may give different dates for the Point-Zéro capture, not reconciled here. FDLR involvement is Igihe's claim.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0553 and REC-0642 (UN Secretary-General: Twirwaneho and M23 regained control of Point Zero). FARDC announced a 'repli stratégique' (r6-F-FIZ-012).

claims.text: Igihe reported that in January 2026 Twirwaneho fighters had captured Point-Zéro and used it to block attacks that had long been launched on Minembwe, but were dislodged by DRC government forces using drones and warplanes.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p17. Igihe does not give exact dates for the January capture or loss; another outlet dates the capture 16 January 2026.
claims.researcher_note: Compare Umuryango.rw (r7-E-FIZ-009): Twirwaneho took Point-Zéro on 16 January 2026. No record yet for the January capture or the subsequent loss.

claims.text: Azarias Ruberwa said, according to Igihe, that there is a serious humanitarian problem around Point-Zéro and Minembwe because attacks are launched as if the area were uninhabited, adding that he feared people might be displaced permanently.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p17. "kuhacika" can mean "vanish from there"; translation corrected. Ruberwa (former DRC Vice-President, from Minembwe) is quoted without a date or venue; the article also cites Jeune Afrique, so the quote may be relayed from there. Date is the Igihe article date. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 107)
claims.researcher_note: Commentary by a politician from Minembwe; not a party statement. The original contains a typo ('kgukomera').

claims.text: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 said that as long as DRC government forces continue to fire blindly at areas it controls, including Point-Zéro, without regard for civilians living there, it will continue to fight for them and protect its positions.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p17; translation accurate. Party statement relayed by Igihe; undated.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement relayed by a partisan outlet.

claims.text: Igihe reported that in recent days the alliance of forces supporting the DRC government launched drone and heavy-weapon attacks on Point Zéro, trying to retake it and continuing into the centre of Minembwe, but that Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 fighters held firm.
claims.actor_as_written: Forces supporting the DRC government (alleged); AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho (defending)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p17. Igihe narration; dates not given ("mu minsi ya vuba" = in recent days, before 25 Sept 2026).
claims.researcher_note: Compare Actualite.cd on clashes at Point Zéro and Nyaruhinga on 30 September (REC-0661) and the 28 and 31 August reports (REC-0559, REC-0657).

claims.text: According to Igihe, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on 10 October 2026 that forces including those of the DRC, FDLR, Maï-Maï groups, foreign mercenaries and Burundian soldiers launched drone attacks on the night of 9 October 2026 ("saa yine z'ijoro", about 10 p.m.) on Point Zéro village and surroundings, and similar attacks later that night ("saa saba z'ijoro" of 9 into 10 October) at Rugezi and surroundings in Minembwe; he said the attacks on inhabited areas caused deaths and mass flight.

AFC/M23 allegation; no toll published (Igihe: AFC/M23 had not given the number of dead, injured or displaced). "Saa saba z'ijoro" is 1 a.m. in Kinyarwanda time reckoning.
claims.researcher_note: Party allegation; AFC/M23 had not published a toll (p18: 'ntiratangaza umubare w'abiciwe'). Times: 'saa yine z'ijoro' = 10 p.m., 'saa saba z'ijoro' = 1 a.m. Compare Radio Maendeleo/SOS Médias on FRN claims at Rugezi in October 2026.

'Saa cyenda' is Kinyarwanda clock time, about 03:00. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 111)

Related existing records: FARDC said on 19 April that AFC/M23 drones hit its positions at Mikenge and Kakenge (REC-0621); Kanyuka's 25-26 April statement (REC-0622). No FARDC reply to the 20 April claim found in this page.

claims.text: AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said, according to Igihe, that at 5:30 government coalition forces also attacked the densely populated area of Mitimingi in Masisi territory, causing much damage and making many families flee; Igihe places this in its account of attacks on 20 April 2026.

Igihe does not say whether '5:30' is clock time or Kinyarwanda reckoning (which would be 11:30); the date 20 April comes from the preceding sentence. No casualty figure given; Igihe's own lede asserting civilian deaths is not supported by any quoted figure. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: integrator: full translation of the replaced excerpt (the earlier excerpt_en covered only its last sentences)

claims.text: Igihe reported that in the night of 18 to 19 April 2026 the DRC government forces coalition launched heavy-weapon and suicide-drone attacks on areas including Kalingi and Bidegu in Minembwe and on Mitimingi and neighbouring areas.

claims.actor_as_written: ihuriro ry'ingabo za Leta ya RDC (DRC government forces coalition), as Igihe names it

The statement's year 2026 is the article's (published 20 April 2026).
claims.researcher_note: The sentence is stated in Igihe's own voice but sits between Kanyuka's statements and is almost certainly AFC/M23-sourced; no source named. Compare FARDC's own 19 April statement (REC-0621), which says AFC/M23 drones struck FARDC positions at Mikenge and Kakenge.

claims.text: AFC/M23 spokesperson Kanyuka said, according to Igihe, that AFC/M23 continues to point to repeated, deliberate breaches of the ceasefire by the Kinshasa government and that it is fully ready to defend civilians and to set up a proper security space to protect the population.

claims.verification_note: 'Bertrand' is not printed anywhere on the page (Igihe prints 'Bertand'); removed the unprinted spelling. Otherwise verbatim. Party statement relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe (article of 11 July 2026); Igihe gives 8 July as the day of the celebration in Minembwe but not the exact date of the address.
claims.researcher_note: Existing claim r1-ST-M23-2026-014 (Umuryango) carries the same announcement under REC-0642. Date: Igihe says the leaders' celebration in Minembwe was on 8 July; the address date itself is not stated.

claims.text: Igihe reported that the DRC, Burundian, FDLR and Wazalendo forces were dispossessed of areas including Point-Zéro, Mikenke, Kalingi, Ilundu and Rwitsankuku, and that once these areas were taken senior AFC/M23 leaders visited them.
claims.place_as_written: Point-Zéro, Mikenke, Kalingi, Ilundu, Rwitsankuku (Minembwe area, South Kivu)
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 and MRDP Twirwaneho (as Igihe presents the capture)

Territorial claim in the voice of Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; the sentence does not name who took the areas or when. Other project sources describe a FARDC 'strategic withdrawal' from Point Zéro; Igihe's own p33 article dates Point-Zéro's fall to 4 July.

Compare the Radio Okapi account of a FARDC 'strategic withdrawal' from Point Zéro (r6-F-FIZ-012, REC-0642). Igihe's own dated account of Point-Zéro on 4 July is in the p33 claims.

claims.text: AFC/M23 deputy leader Bertand Bisimwa said, according to Igihe, that AFC/M23 fighters from many parts of the country and MRDP Twirwaneho had united to stop what he described as a plan by the DRC government forces to wipe out Congolese because of their ethnic origin.

claims.verification_note: Verbatim; 'kurimbura Abanye-Congo zibahora ubwoko bwabo' = wipe out Congolese because of their ethnicity. Attributed. Allegation of intent by a party leader (AFC/M23) relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; no evidence cited.
claims.researcher_note: Allegation of intent by a party leader; no evidence cited in the article. 'Kurimbura' rendered 'wipe out'; no legal label is applied.

claims.text: The AFC/M23-appointed Governor of North Kivu, Col Bahati Musanga Erasto, asked residents of the Binza groupement (Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, near the Ugandan border) to distance themselves from the FDLR, telling them its founders had shed innocent blood in Rwanda, according to Igihe.
claims.place_as_written: Binza groupement, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory (North Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Both passages verbatim on the page; attribution correct. Statement by an AFC/M23-appointed official relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; date of the visit not given (article of 26 February 2026). 'Terrorist group' is the article's wording. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 121)
claims.researcher_note: 'Terrorist group' is Igihe's/the speaker's wording, not ours. The exact date of the visit is not given; article dated 26 Feb 2026. REC-0869 covers a tour of the neighbouring Bwito chiefdom from 12 Feb 2026.

claims.text: Col Bahati Musanga Erasto, the provincial governor appointed by AFC/M23, said, according to Igihe, of the FDLR, that 'we know well that they are still in the forests, and we will not cease to fight them until we defeat them.'
claims.verification_note: Rendered as 'we' (the speaker's word) rather than 'AFC/M23 knows'; replacement quote spans the contiguous opening paragraphs so the speaker and affiliation are printed. Speaker is Bahati by context: the quote follows the paragraph on his Binza visit. 'They' is the FDLR by context. Party statement relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe.
claims.researcher_note: Speaker identified by the article's context (quote from the speech by Governor Bahati). The sentence in the excerpt is itself the continuation of a quoted speech, so the attribution is contextual.

claims.verification_note: Verbatim; replacement quote spans the contiguous sentences that name Bahati. The speaker is Bahati by context ('Yagaragaje' continues his remarks). Party statement; describes an announced AFC/M23-to-Rwanda handover pathway, no individual case.
claims.researcher_note: Describes an announced handover pathway (AFC/M23 to Rwanda) for FDLR fighters; useful lead on repatriation/transfers. No individual case named.

claims.text: Igihe reported that in November 2025 the vice-president of Rwanda's national demobilisation and reintegration commission (RDRC), Maj Gen (Rtd) Jacques Nziza, explained that in 10 months Rwanda had received more than 200 FDLR fighters.
claims.place_as_written: Rwanda (receiving FDLR fighters from eastern DRC)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on the page; figures and name match. Rwandan official figure relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; the 10-month window is not anchored to dates.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan official figure as relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet; the 10-month window is not anchored to dates in the passage.

claims.text: AFC/M23 deputy leader Bertrand Bisimwa criticised the United Nations on X, according to Igihe, after the UN sanctioned several AFC/M23 leaders, saying it had been misled and was driven by emotion, and that sanctioning only the side that respects its peace commitments showed the UN had lost its way.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; attribution correct. Party statement relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe (article of 19 July 2026); the X post is not linked or dated. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 128)
claims.researcher_note: Igihe does not link or date the X post. The article's original post is not cited by URL; per project rules, cite the outlet and treat the post as a lead only. Related existing claims on the listing: r1-UC-M23-033/-034/-035 (no record).

claims.text: Bisimwa said, according to Igihe, that putting pressure on people affected by ethnic discrimination to leave their land is a grave mistake that will have consequences.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; replacement quote extends to the contiguous sentences that name Bisimwa. Speaker is Bisimwa by context (the paragraph continues his remarks and the next sentence names him). Party statement relayed by Igihe; not stated whether this was on X.
claims.researcher_note: Speaker is Bisimwa by the article's context; the excerpt starts at the verb 'Yagaragaje' (he showed).

claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 and MRDP-Twirwaneho (Freddy Kaniki); alleged: DRC government-supporting forces

claims.researcher_note: Party statement. The Group of Experts independently describes Minembwe as encircled by FARDC and allied forces since mid-2025 (r1-GOE-020, REC-0620), and also that MRDP/Twirwaneho prevented civilians from leaving (REC-0183). Kinshasa's reply to this 21 Sept claim not found in this page.

claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 and MRDP-Twirwaneho (Freddy Kaniki); alleged: DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo, FDLR forces and 'abacanshuro b’abanyamahahanga' (foreign mercenaries)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; date and parties match. Party allegation naming Burundian forces and 'foreign mercenaries' ('abacanshuro b’abanyamahahanga', as printed); relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 132)
claims.researcher_note: Party allegation naming Burundian forces and 'foreign mercenaries'. Igihe spells 'abanyamahahanga' as printed. Related fighting on 27 and 30 Sept is in REC-0570/REC-0661.

Igihe adds in its own voice that the movement of residents was hampered by the attacks. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 133)
claims.researcher_note: Party allegation; no facility, patient or date of blockade specified. Independent context: UN Group of Experts on limits to movement and aid at Minembwe (REC-0620) and OCHA warnings on access to food and care (r1-UC-BI-FDLR-034); the GoE also reports that Twirwaneho itself restricted civilians leaving (REC-0183), so both-direction restrictions are on record.

claims.text: Igihe reported that in early July 2026 AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho fighters had restored security in Minembwe by driving the DRC government forces coalition out of surrounding areas including Point-Zéro, and that the government forces were now launching strong attacks around Minembwe, including Point-Zéro, intending to retake them.

claims.actor_as_written: DRC government forces coalition (attacking); AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho (holding), as Igihe describes

Other project sources (Radio Okapi, Actualite.cd, Kivu Morning Post) report fighting at Point Zéro in late August and late September 2026.

claims.text: Igihe reported that five people were killed in an attack in the night of 25 to 26 October 2026 at Kabizo, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory; Euphrem Kabasha, Rutshuru territory administrator appointed by the FRN, said it was carried out by the FDLR together with the Nyatura CMC FDP of Gashegu Héritier and Mbitezi.
claims.place_as_written: Kabizo, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory (North Kivu)
claims.actor_as_written: Euphrem Kabasha (Rutshuru territory administrator appointed by the FRN) as the source of the attribution
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; the toll and attribution are Kabasha's (a de facto FRN/AFC-aligned administrator) relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe. Attribution conflict: Kivu Morning Post (same origin, Kabasha) attributes the 26 October attack to 'Wazalendo CMC'; Igihe quotes Kabasha attributing it to the FDLR with Nyatura CMC FDP. Each stays as its source states. Same origin, so not independent. Time: lede 'saa saba z'ijoro' (about 01:00) vs quote 'saa 1:30'. No victim names printed. Kabizo was attacked 'again'. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 136)
claims.researcher_note: Same origin (Kabasha) as the existing Kivu Morning Post claim r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-017 (REC-0922), so no independent second origin. claims.researcher_note: Addressed to Burundian forces by implication ('those who crossed over', Cibitoke, Ngozi, Bujumbura are Burundian places); the excerpt does not name Burundian forces. Channel of the original statement is not given.

claims.researcher_note: The 30 km figure is Igihe's; Uvira was taken, according to other claims, around 10 December 2025 (r7-L-RW-005, r7-L-RN-002, REC-0127).

claims.text: Igihe reported that M23 already controlled other areas of Lubero territory, including Alimbongo, Kanyabayonga, Kayna, Kirumba and Matembe, which it said it had taken at the end of 2024.
claims.place_as_written: Alimbongo, Kanyabayonga, Kayna, Kirumba, Matembe (Lubero territory, North Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim. Position held as of the article (19 February 2025); the captures themselves (end of 2024) are outside the window. Igihe's own voice.
claims.researcher_note: The capture (late 2024) is out of window; recorded only as the position held on 19 February 2025.

claims.text: A FARDC captain shot dead Lungele Mbiso, coordinator of the communication cell of South Kivu governor Jean Jacques Purusi, on the afternoon of 5 July 2025, according to Actualite.cd (citing local civil society); Igihe reports the same killing in Uvira territory.
claims.verification_note: Actualite.cd page re-fetched and read: supports the killing, date, rank and roles. Removed the '1 killed' figure (no numeral printed) and used the governor's name as printed ('Jean Jacques Purusi'). Grade B on one credible non-partisan origin.
