Excerpt gap: the clause 'Actualite.cd cites local civil society' rests on the page passage 'Selon la société civile locale, l'incident a eu lieu aux environs de 15h', not the stored excerpt. Motive not stated by either outlet; the captain is unnamed. Actualite.cd adds the killing was on avenue Kasavubu around 15:00, not far from the governorate. Igihe's account (7 July) repeats Actualite.cd's details and is probably not an independent origin. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 200) 2026-10-29: source 1 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Actualite.cd (6 July 2025) is the independent Congolese source, fetched with tools/page_text.py; it also sources the account to local civil society. Motive not stated by either outlet. Social-media reposts of the same story exist (Facebook/X); not cited. The captain is unnamed in both.

claims.text: Uvira youth leader Kiza Tiniko said, according to Actualite.cd and Igihe, that angry residents lynched (beat to death) the captain who had killed the governor's communication coordinator; Actualite.cd adds, citing several other sources, that the soldier threw away his weapon before being chased by the population, and Igihe adds, citing news from Uvira, that he threw away the gun he had used to shoot Lungele out of fear of being prosecuted.
claims.actor_as_written: Uvira residents (crowd); victim a FARDC captain
claims.verification_note: Actualite.cd page read: it supports the lynching and the discarded weapon (replacement quote spans the contiguous passage). Removed the '1' figure; 'Mbiso' is not in this claim's excerpts, so the victim of the first killing is described by role. Motive kept as Igihe's. Excerpt gap: the clause that the soldier threw away his weapon before being chased (Actualite.cd, citing several other sources) rests on the page passage 'le militaire dont il est question a jeté son arme avant d'être poursuivi par la population', given as source 2's replacement quote, not the stored excerpt. The victim of this incident is the unnamed captain, killed by a crowd. The 'fear of prosecution' motive is Igihe's alone, from unnamed 'news from Uvira'. Igihe and Actualite.cd share one origin for the lynching (Kiza Tiniko). 2026-10-29: source 2 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 201) 2026-10-29: source 2 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Victim is a soldier killed by a crowd; categorised under the nearest available category (the perpetrators are civilians). Igihe's 'threw away the gun out of fear' is stated without attribution ('Amakuru ava muri Uvira'); Actualite.cd says only that he threw away his weapon before being pursued by the population. Igihe puts Kiza Tiniko's time at 'saa cyenda n'iminota 20' (15:20), matching Actualite.cd.

claims.text: DW Swahili reported, according to Samuel Kagheni, described as one of the civil-society leaders in the village, that on Saturday the ADF attacked the village of Ngohi Vuyinga in Lubero territory (North Kivu); 9 people were killed and many others lost their homes after their houses were burned.
claims.actor_as_written: ADF (as stated in the DW text)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt and page (DW, datePublished 2025-03-10) support every clause; translation checked. Single origin (local civil-society leader via DW). Date derived from 'Saturday' (Jumamosi) and DW's page date of 10 March 2025; the page says the toll may rise as many people were unaccounted for.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('Saturday') and DW publication date 10 March 2025 (Monday). No known record for Ngohi Vuyinga (claim_search found none). The toll 9 is DW's/Kagheni's first count; the page says the toll may rise because many people were unaccounted for. Other outlets (not fetched) give 11 killed; not used.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that about ten militiamen were killed in violent clashes between the night of Monday 3 March and the morning of Tuesday 4 March in Butembo, and that, according to civil society in Kimemi, the fighting pitted two Wazalendo militia groups against each other. It said an interim report indicated ten militiamen killed and several wounded, treated in health structures in the area.
claims.place_as_written: Butembo (Kimemi neighbourhood, Mont Tabor and Mavina area), Butembo city
claims.verification_note: Page checked; translation correct. SOS Médias is a non-partisan outlet for this conflict; one origin, consistent with BBC Gahuza/RFI. BBC Gahuza (claim 3) gives six dead per an army spokesman and up to ten per associations; figures not merged. The page notes no official comment from the authorities had been recorded.
claims.researcher_note: Page dated 7 March 2025 (URL date); French original dated 5 March. Second independent origin: BBC Gahuza (in Kirundi) citing RFI, see next claim. SOS Médias Burundi notes no official comment had been recorded from the authorities.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) quoted a resident on social media as saying that four dead bodies were discovered 'this morning', that they 'would be' young militiamen from the Mavina group, and that they had been tied up before being hanged (the verb used, kunyongwa, can also mean strangled).
claims.place_as_written: near the Université Catholique du Graben (UCG) campus, Butembo
claims.actor_as_written: not stated by the source (the resident names the presumed victims' group, not the perpetrators)
claims.verification_note: Removed 'on the morning after the clashes' (the quote says only 'this morning') and the inferred perpetrator (Tabor-based group): the page says the Mavina group attacked the Tabor group but does not say who killed these four. kunyongwa is ambiguous (hang/strangle); noted. Single unnamed resident relayed from social media; hedged ('wangekuwa'). 'This morning' is relative to the undated post; the page places the bodies near the UCG area after the 3-4 March clashes. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-NKN claim 2)
claims.researcher_note: Single unnamed resident quoted from social media; hedged ('wangekuwa' = 'would be'). The excerpt ends at 'mitandao ya kijamii'; the verb 'kunyongwa' is translated 'hanged' (could also be read 'strangled'). Reviewer: translation of kunyongwa to be confirmed.

claims.text: BBC Gahuza (Kirundi), relaying RFI, reported that news from Butembo said about ten people died in clashes between two groups of Wazalendo fighters, which broke out on 3 March and lasted several hours in the Kimemi hills of the city; it added that an army spokesman in the area said in a video that six dead were known, while non-political associations said up to ten died on both sides.
claims.verification_note: Kirundi translation checked (Ntwarante = March; 'amasaha atari make' = several hours; 'Amashirahamwe adaharanira ivyicaro vya poritike' = non-political associations). RFI is cited only for the date/duration sentence; the first sentence is BBC's own. Six dead per an army spokesman vs up to ten per non-political associations; kept separate.
claims.researcher_note: Kirundi-language text (March = 'Ntwarante'; translation by the agent, reviewer should confirm). The figures differ by speaker (six per army spokesman vs ten per associations); not merged. Same event as the SOS Médias Burundi claim; two outlets, SOS and BBC/RFI, are likely independent in sourcing.

claims.text: Vatican News (Swahili), citing local sources of the pontifical charity Aid to the Church in Need (given as ACS), reported that more than 70 bodies were found in a Protestant church at Maiba, North Kivu; it said the killings took place between 12 and 15 February 2025 at the hands of ADF fighters who entered the village and abducted about 100 people.
claims.actor_as_written: ADF, per the ACN source quoted by Vatican News
claims.verification_note: Page (dated 24 Feb 2025) checked; figures and dates match. 'Terrorist Islamic group' wording is the outlet's and is not carried into the statement. ACN's source is anonymous for security reasons, per the page.
claims.researcher_note: Adds an independent (church-network) origin and a 12-15 February killing window and 'about 100 abducted' to REC-1243 (abduction night of 11-12 Feb, bodies found 14-15 Feb). ACN's source is anonymised for security per the page. The page itself says the victims included women, children and elderly people.

claims.text: UN News Kiswahili, relaying a MONUSCO statement released in Kinshasa, reported that ADF attacks between 13 and 19 November 2025 in parts of Lubero (Bapere and Baswagha areas) killed 89 civilians, including 20 women, with the number of children not yet known.
claims.verification_note: Matches page (dated 21 Nov 2025). Swahili copy of a MONUSCO release; same origin as the English MONUSCO statement, so not independent of it.
claims.researcher_note: Swahili UN News copy of the MONUSCO release (also published in English on the MONUSCO site). Corroborates the toll in REC-0941.

claims.text: UN News Kiswahili, relaying MONUSCO, reported that in the village of Byambwe, 60 km west of Lubero, at least 17 civilians, including women who were receiving care in the maternity ward, were killed inside a health centre run by the Catholic Church, and that four wards with patients caught fire during the attack.
claims.place_as_written: Byambwe, 60 km west of Lubero, Lubero territory
claims.verification_note: Matches page. MONUSCO origin, not independent of the English release. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: The excerpt does not itself name ADF or the night of 14-15 November; both come from the same release's opening sentence (13-19 Nov ADF attacks in Lubero). Corroborates REC-0942.

claims.text: UN News Kiswahili reported that MONUSCO strongly condemned recent attacks by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in Beni and Lubero, North Kivu, between 9 and 16 August 2025, which caused the deaths of about 52 civilians including women and children.
claims.verification_note: Matches page (dated 19 Aug 2025: statement released 19 August in Kinshasa). Swahili copy of a MONUSCO statement already cited in English; same origin.
claims.researcher_note: Swahili copy of the MONUSCO statement already cited elsewhere in English (reliefweb); added here as a Swahili-language corroboration only. The page adds that the attacks were accompanied by abductions, looting and destruction of property.

claims.text: DW Swahili reported that a government official in the area, Macaire Sivikunula, said the attack happened 'last night' in the village of Ntoyo in Lubero territory, and that Lubero military administrator Colonel Alain Kiwewa told Reuters the number killed was about 60 and might rise because some people had not yet been found.
claims.verification_note: Page (dated 9 Sep 2025) checked; translation correct. DW's own headline says 50 and its lead 'more than 50' (machete attack during a funeral); the official figure quoted is about 60. Not merged.
claims.researcher_note: Early (day-after) figure of about 60; later counts in known records are higher (e.g., 64 buried of 89 in a Radio Okapi report cited elsewhere). 'Last night' is relative to DW's page date 9 September 2025, hence the night of 8-9 September. Names the two local officials by role (Sivikunula: government official in the area; Kiwewa: Lubero military administrator) for the statements-by-local-authorities requirement.

claims.text: TRT Afrika Swahili reported that suspected ADF rebels killed 19 civilians in a night attack in eastern DRC, according to two local officials. Alain Kiwewa, military administrator of Lubero, said the attack, believed to have been carried out by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), took place in the village of Mukondo in North Kivu and that the toll could rise; a local pastor who declined to be named said the attackers wore uniforms resembling those of the Congolese army and attacked people with guns, knives and clubs.
claims.verification_note: Fixed garbled opening ('TRT ... suspected') and dropped the weekday not used in the excerpt's English rendering; kept 'suspected/believed'. The text carries no wire credit (only a Reuters photo credit), so the origin is left as TRT rather than inferred as Reuters. The page also quotes civil-society leader Espoir Kambale: 19 killed, 8 wounded, 26 houses burned (not in the excerpts).
claims.researcher_note: The TRT page carries no date in its text; the date (Monday 13 October 2025) is from the search listing and confirmed by Radio Okapi and Actualite.cd items of 13 and 14 October 2025 about 19 civilians killed at Mukondo (seen in search results, not fetched). Wire copy: the page's picture credit is Reuters and the French TRT copy cites Reuters. Attack date computed from 'Monday' official statement; the attack was 'night' before. Not in known_records (claim_search 'Mukondo' found none).

claims.text: DW Swahili reported that 10 people were killed in eastern DRC by extremist rebels linked to the group calling itself the Islamic State (IS), and that these ADF rebels attacked the village of Makoko in Lubero territory, North Kivu, 'yesterday'; it said, as stated by David Sikuli, a member of parliament for the province, that at the time there were no Congolese soldiers in the village, only fighters known as Wazalendo.
claims.actor_as_written: ADF (as stated in the DW text)
claims.verification_note: 'ADF-linked rebels' changed to the page's wording (lead: rebels linked to IS; next paragraph: 'those ADF rebels'). 'mbunge wa jimbo hilo' = MP of that province (jimbo is used for the province in the same sentence), not 'the area's MP'. 'jana' relative to DW datePublished 2025-01-16 gives 15 January. DW's Makoko figure (10 killed, 15 January 2025) differs in place and toll from the Muhangi record (about 30); it may be a separate attack. Kept separate, not merged. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-NKN claim 10)
claims.researcher_note: Differs from REC-0951 (Muhangi, about thirty killed, 15 January 2025) in place name (Makoko vs Muhangi) and toll (10 vs about 30); may be a separate attack the same day, or a variant name and count. DW page dated 16 January 2025, 'yesterday' = 15 January. DW's lead sentence says 'extremist rebels linked to IS' and the next paragraph names the ADF.

claims.text: BBC Swahili reported that a six-year-old girl who was being treated for Ebola was abducted from a health facility in eastern DRC: armed people stormed a clinic near the town of Butembo in North Kivu and took the child with her mother. Dr. Lubambo Maboko Gaston, the province's Ebola response manager, told Reuters that the two had not yet been found and made an urgent call to the abductors.
claims.place_as_written: clinic near Butembo, Butembo / Lubero area
claims.verification_note: Live-page entry located (firstPublished 2026-06-17); text matches; Gaston's quote is credited to Reuters. Victim is a minor and is not named by the source. The BBC entry (17 June 2026) does not give the date of the abduction.
claims.researcher_note: Exact date of the abduction is not in the BBC Swahili entry (live-page entry dated 17 June 2026). A TRT Afrika French copy of Reuters (listed in search results with a wrong date) says the clinic was stormed 'late Monday' and a provincial notice seen by Reuters did not identify the attackers; Monday before 17 June is 15 June, but that date is not in the cited excerpt. Reuters is the originating wire. Page also notes the DRC government had not issued an official statement on the abduction at publication time. Not in known_records (claim_search 'six-year-old', 'Ebola clinic Butembo' found none).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that a new series of attacks attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) caused mourning in the Beni area of North Kivu, and that between the night of Saturday 30 May and Sunday 31 May 2026, about 17 civilians were killed in several coordinated attacks on the Vemba-Katota and Vemba-Masulukwede axes in the Beni area, according to local sources and civil-society actors.
claims.place_as_written: Vemba-Katota and Vemba-Masulukwede axes, east of Ngadi, near Beni
claims.actor_as_written: ADF (identified as ADF fighters by residents, per the page)
claims.verification_note: Page (Goma dateline 1 June 2026, URL 5 June) checked; 'yanayohusishwa na' = attributed to, preserved. Text says 'about 17', headline and later text 'at least 17'; the related record gives at least 16. Kept as the source's figure.
claims.researcher_note: Toll differs slightly from REC-1211 (at least 16, night of 30 to 31 May). The page also says seven bodies were found on the Vemba-Katota road on Sunday morning and four more in the forest on the Vemba-Masulukwede road, and that several people were missing, some believed abducted. The headline says 'at least 17'. The 'ADF' attribution is in a later sentence (not in the excerpt); reviewer may narrow.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that in the Butembo and Beni health zones, as well as Kisangani, doctors, nurses, laboratory technicians and community health workers were refusing to return to work, demanding payment of their salaries and hazard allowances.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt matches the page lead (Goma dateline 18 July 2026); translation correct ('bado wanakataa' = still refuse). Strike context, not an attack.
claims.researcher_note: Context claim on civilian access to care during the 2026 Ebola outbreak; the strike is by health workers over unpaid pay, not an attack. The excerpt does not itself print the date 18 July (the dateline 'Julai 18, 2026' is elsewhere on the page). Single outlet.

claims.text: BBC Swahili reported that the trial of about sixty FARDC deserter soldiers and two female accomplices opened on the day of the entry before the Butembo military tribunal sitting at Musienene; local journalist Seros Muyisa, present at the hearing, told the BBC the accused were charged with fleeing the enemy, theft, rape, extortion and other offences in the areas of Lubero-Centre, Kimbulu and Musienene.
claims.place_as_written: Musienene (Butembo military tribunal); offences alleged in Lubero-Centre, Kimbulu and Musienene
claims.verification_note: Entry found on the live page under 25 February 2025; quotes verbatim; 'wanashtakiwa' = are charged/prosecuted. The entry's text says 'sixty' and its headline 'about 60' ('Takriban ... 60') and 'wahukumiwa' (sentenced), while the text says the case opened that day. BBC Gahuza says the trial began on Monday (24 Feb); this entry says 'today' (25 Feb). Kept separate. Rape is a charge, not a finding.
claims.researcher_note: The BBC Swahili live-page entry's headline says 'wahukumiwa' (sentenced) but its text says the case 'opened today'; the BBC Gahuza version says the trial began on Monday (24 February) and was later updated with convictions (next claim). Day discrepancy: 'today' (25 Feb, Tuesday) vs 'Monday' (24 Feb). The rape charge is an allegation in the charge sheet as reported by the journalist, not a finding. Related to but distinct from REC-0928/0929 (June-July 2025 hearings at Lubero-centre).

claims.text: BBC Gahuza (Kirundi) reported in an update that 55 of the soldiers accused of offences including fleeing the battlefield and looting were convicted and sentenced to death, and that the trial of about 60 FARDC soldiers began on Monday in the city of Butembo.
claims.verification_note: Translation checked: 'barabihamijwe, bakatirwa urwo gupfa' = found guilty, sentenced to death; 'ku wa mbere' = Monday. Page datePublished 2025-02-25. Day discrepancy with BBC Swahili ('today', 25 Feb) kept; the update's own date is not stated. The page's quote from Seros Muyisa also lists rape ('gufata ku ngufu') among the charges.
claims.researcher_note: Kirundi text; translation by the agent, reviewer to confirm ('guhunga' = flee; 'gusahura' = loot; 'ibikorwa by'ubugizi bwa nabi' = criminal acts). The excerpt does not mention rape; the rape charge is in the BBC Swahili claim. Date of the update is not stated (page dated 25 February 2025). Conflict: Monday (24 Feb) here vs 'today' (25 Feb) in BBC Swahili.

claims.text: Mwananchi (Tanzania) reported that M23 captured the town of Kasugho on 2 March 2025 and left on 7 March, heading for Bunyatenge, a gold-mining area six hours from Kasugho.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt matches page. Origin corrected to the outlet, since the sentence itself carries no attribution. The page does not attribute this sentence; the preceding paragraph cites Kivu Morning Post.
claims.researcher_note: Adds the capture date (2 March) and the departure date (7 March) and destination (Bunyatenge) to REC-0976 (M23 withdraws from Kasugho, Katoyo and Kagheri, night of 6 to 7 March). The 'M23' wording is the page's; the sentence is not itself attributed on the page, which cites Kivu Morning Post for the previous sentence.

claims.text: DW (French) reported that the Butembo human-rights network Redho said it recorded 280 sexual-violence cases brought to justice in the city of Butembo in 2025, in a report made public in mid-March; Redho coordinator Muhindo Wasingya said the slowness of judicial procedures favours out-of-court settlements between families.
claims.verification_note: Page (dated 10 April 2026) checked; French matches; name spelled as printed. Count covers complaints filed only, per the page.
claims.researcher_note: French-language DW item (10 April 2026) found while sweeping for Swahili; used as locator for a statistic. The page notes that the figure counts complaints filed only and that women's-rights activists link the rise to the ongoing conflict. Redho's name for its coordinator is spelled 'Muhindo Wasingya' on this page; Radio Moto items cited in other records spell 'Wasivinywa'. Single local NGO origin relayed by DW. Date range is the 2025 calendar year; report published mid-March (2026).

claims.text: Deutsche Welle Swahili reported that M23 had continued its attacks in eastern Congo and entered the town of Walikale, two days after Presidents Tshisekedi of Congo and Kagame of Rwanda called for a ceasefire following their meeting in Qatar.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page date 20.03.2025 confirmed on the snapshot; same event as REC-0395 (Walikale town, 19-20 March 2025). DW page dated 20 March 2025 (byline Bakari Ubena); REC-0395 dates the taking of Walikale to 19 March.
claims.researcher_note: Independent Swahili-language corroboration of the entry into Walikale (known record dates the taking to 19 March). DW page date 20.03.2025 confirmed on page. Article byline Bakari Ubena.

claims.text: Deutsche Welle Swahili reported that the AFC/M23 alliance said, in a statement published on X, that it had decided to withdraw its forces from Walikale town and from the neighbouring areas.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). The page ends 'Vyanzo: RTRE/AFP', so the copy is credited to Reuters and AFP. Same event as REC-0400 (22-24 March 2025). Announcement of intent only; DW of 4 April 2025 reports the withdrawal took place then.
claims.researcher_note: Reports a party statement (AFC/M23, via X as relayed by DW); DW is not partisan. The announcement is of intent; DW 24 March page and the DW 4 April page say the withdrawal had not yet occurred / then occurred.

claims.text: Deutsche Welle Swahili reported that the Congolese Foreign Minister Therese Kayikwamba Wagner told journalists that the government was waiting eagerly to see whether M23 would really withdraw from the town of Walikale.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Wire credit RTRE/AFP at the end of the page. Kinshasa reaction belongs to REC-0400.
claims.researcher_note: Kinshasa reaction to the announced withdrawal (record REC-0400 covers reactions).

claims.text: Deutsche Welle Swahili reported that M23 rebels had withdrawn from the strategic town of Walikale, describing the move as a gesture of goodwill before peace talks; confirming the departure, Congolese army spokesperson Sylvain Ekenge said on Friday that his soldiers had witnessed it.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page date 04.04.2025 (a Friday) confirmed; same event as REC-0402 (AFC/M23 withdrawal from Walikale, April 2025). Both sources are the same page.
claims.researcher_note: Second, Swahili-language origin for the early-April withdrawal. Weekday only ("Ijumaa"); date computed from weekday and publication date (4 April 2025 was a Friday).

claims.text: Taarifa Rwanda (Kinyarwanda edition) said that, in a communique issued on Monday 28 September, the organisation Forces vives de Masisi said many residents had been killed or wounded and others had fled their villages, some of them killed by drone strikes; it quoted civil society member Télesphore Mithondeke as saying that a drone attack at Kaleta-Bitoyi, in Ufamandu II, killed a woman and a child, and that fighting at Burungu in Bashali killed eight residents.
claims.place_as_written: Kaleta-Bitoyi (Ufamandu II) and Burungu (Bashali), Masisi territory
claims.actor_as_written: drone strikes and fighting between AFC/M23, FARDC and Wazalendo (attribution of the drone strikes not stated in the excerpts)
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Taarifa is on the project's partisan list: source_type corrected to partisan_rwanda_government and grade C. Page 'Last updated: September 29, 2026' confirmed. Matches REC-0743 (Kaleta/Bitoyi air strike, 28 Sept 2026) and REC-0740 (Burungu, eight killed, about 26 Sept 2026). Rwanda-based outlet; the page cites Radio Okapi and appears to retell its report, so it is probably not independent of the Radio Okapi-based records.
claims.researcher_note: Taarifa is a Rwanda-based outlet; it relays civil-society statements and cites Radio Okapi. Corroborates the 28 Sept air strike on Kaleta/Bitoyi (REC-0743) and the Burungu toll (REC-0740, eight civilians killed). Also says the army had not responded at the time of Radio Okapi publication. Page date 29 Sept 2026 confirmed. The statement date is that of the communique.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that AFC/M23 denied Amnesty International's allegations that it killed and abused small-scale miners and took gold and coltan to Rwanda; in a statement it issued in Goma on Tuesday, AFC/M23 said Amnesty had not provided solid evidence that could be examined.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page dated 23 Ukw'icenda 2026 (Wednesday); 'ejo ku wa kabiri' = yesterday, Tuesday = 22 September 2026. Reply to the Amnesty briefing in REC-0727/REC-0728. Grade B is for what AFC/M23 said, not for the allegations.
claims.researcher_note: AFC/M23 reply to the Amnesty briefing of 21 September 2026 (REC-0727, REC-0728). BBC Gahuza live page dated 23 Ukw'icenda (September) 2026; statement "ejo ku wa kabiri" = Tuesday; date computed from weekday and publication date (22 September 2026). Grade B is for what AFC/M23 said, not for the underlying allegations.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that, in a report published on Monday, Amnesty had accused the movement of killings, ill-treatment of people ('ugukubagura abantu'), detention without legal procedure, forced labour and forcible recruitment into armed groups, and said these happened at the Rubaya coltan site in North Kivu and at the Lomera gold mines in South Kivu.
claims.place_as_written: Rubaya (Masisi, North Kivu) and Lomera (South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: 'ku munsi wa mbere uheze' means 'last Monday', not 'the previous day'; with the page dated Wednesday 23 September 2026, Monday is 21 September, matching the Amnesty date in REC-0727/0728. Translation corrected in extra. Relation changed from corroborates to adds_detail because BBC relays Amnesty itself (same origin). Publication date removed from the statement. The movement is AFC/M23, the subject of the BBC entry. Retelling of Amnesty International's report; not an independent corroboration of it. 'ugukubagura' is rendered as ill-treatment; the researcher's 'beating' is uncertain. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-NKW claim 6)
claims.researcher_note: Second-language retelling of Amnesty (primary: Amnesty). Translation of "ugukubagura" is "beating" (uncertain verb form). Amnesty publication date derived from "the day before" the page date; known records give 21 September 2026.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Lumumba Kambere Muyisa, spokesperson of the governor of North Kivu province, told the media that the upper parts of the mine had fallen into the mine on Wednesday because of heavy rain.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23-appointed provincial administration (as described by BBC: "M23 authorities")
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports the statement; translation checked. Same event as REC-0685. The governor is the AFC/M23-appointed Erasto Bahati Musanga (per the same page).
claims.researcher_note: Weekday only ("ku wa gatatu"); date computed from weekday and publication date (Wednesday before Saturday 31 Jan 2026 = 28 Jan). BBC places him among "M23 authorities" in the preceding sentence; the page does not say so in this sentence.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the DRC government, in a statement on the Rubaya mine collapse, said that in June 2025 more than 300 civilians had died at Rubaya in a similar way, and that a ministerial order of February 2025 had banned mining in the Rubaya zone.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports the statement. Grade raised to B: BBC is a credible origin for what the government said; the underlying toll remains unverified (noted). The June 2025 toll is Kinshasa's claim in a statement about the January 2026 collapse; not verified elsewhere here. Not the same event as REC-0420 (arrests at Rubaya, 28 June-3 July 2025).
claims.researcher_note: A June 2025 mass-casualty event at Rubaya is mentioned only in this government statement as relayed by BBC; not otherwise verified here. Kinshasa is a party. Figure of 300 is the government's. Check against r2-G-LOCAL-004 (7sur7: 300 young people arrested, 28-29 June 2025), which is a different event (arrests).

claims.text: Bwiza (Rwanda), relaying information reaching Actualite.cd, reported that on Tuesday 20 October, at Ntoto, capital of the Waloa Uroba groupement in Walikale territory, a soldier and a civilian were killed by bullets when two units of the FARDC turned on each other, and that another soldier and a civilian were seriously wounded; it said the head of the Waloa Uroba groupement, Barthélemy Mulengezi Luc, explained that the incident occurred when a group of soldiers coming from the front tried to cross Ntoto.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC soldiers (two FARDC units, including Military Police)
claims.verification_note: Date 20 October and Tuesday are in the excerpt; page dated Jumanne 20 Oktoba 2026 confirmed. Removed 'citing' wording that went beyond the page and the Military Police role (not in the excerpts). Rwandan outlet relaying Actualite.cd: grade C, not independent of the Actualite.cd-based record. Bwiza prints the groupement as 'Waloa Uroba' here but 'Waloa Loanda' in its 27 October article; REC-0750 has Waloa Loanda.
claims.researcher_note: Known record REC-0750 (about 20 Oct 2026, Ntoto, "Waloa Loanda") gives two dead; Bwiza prints the groupement as "Waloa Uroba". Bwiza is a Rwandan outlet (partisan); the content relays Actualite.cd and Congolese officials. Page date 20 Oktoba 2026 confirmed on page. Military Police role stated in the Bwiza text, not in the excerpts.

claims.text: Bwiza (Rwanda) reported that 54 soldiers of the 3415th regiment of the FARDC began to be tried before the Goma Military Court, sitting specially in Walikale, from Monday 26 October, and that they are accused of offences including murder, abandoning their duties, wasting ammunition and military equipment, and refusing to obey orders; according to Major Dieudonné Kasereka, in charge of communications in the 34th military region, the soldiers were arrested on 20 October after the events at Ntoto, in the Waloa Loanda area.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC 3415th regiment soldiers; Major Dieudonné Kasereka, communications officer, 34th military region
claims.verification_note: 'charged with' changed to 'accused of' (bashinjwa); attribution to Kasereka limited to the arrest, which is all S2 credits to him; trial and accusations are Bwiza's narration. 'guta imirimo yabo' rendered 'abandoning their duties' rather than 'desertion'. Publication date removed; date set to trial start 26 October 2026 (Monday, matches). Page dated Kuwa Kabiri 27 Ukwakira 2026 confirmed. 'bashinjwa' = 'are accused of'; the source does not state formal charges. The verdict was expected in early November.
claims.researcher_note: Adds charges, the arrest date and the army source to REC-0752 (trial of 54 soldiers of the 3415th) and REC-0750 (Ntoto). Bwiza is a Rwandan outlet; the facts are relayed Congolese army statements.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that around 'saa saba' in the night of 19 to 20 October (the seventh hour of the night, about one in the morning), Wazalendo groups attacked AFC/M23 at Nyabiondo and heavy fighting began; it placed the Nyabiondo centre in Masisi territory, North Kivu.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Removed the digit '1' (not printed); the clock reading is spelled out. Page 'Monday 20, Oct 2025' confirmed. Same place and night as REC-0447 (19 Oct 2025, Nyabiondo). Partisan Rwandan outlet: C. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-NKW claim 12)
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan outlet (partisan); page date "Monday 20, Oct 2025" confirmed. "saa saba y'ijoro" read as about 01:00. Corroborates REC-0447 (19 Oct 2025, Nyabiondo).

claims.text: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that on the evening of 18 October aircraft of the DRC army fired on AFC/M23 positions at Mpeti and Buhaya in Walikale, and that AFC/M23 deputy leader Bertrand Bisimwa condemned the attack, recalling that the DRC government was violating the agreement the two sides made in Doha, Qatar.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC aircraft (per Umuryango.rw); AFC/M23 deputy head Bertrand Bisimwa (condemnation)
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page date Monday 20 Oct 2025 confirmed; no known record for 18 Oct 2025 at Mpeti/Buhaya. Partisan outlet: C.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan partisan outlet relaying an AFC/M23 position; no independent confirmation seen here. Not in known records for 18 Oct 2025 (checked list).

claims.text: Ijambo.net (Rwanda) reported that M23 took the trading centre of Mubi in Walikale territory on Friday 21 March, with reports saying it took it without fighting because the government forces had already fled it; it said the centre lies about 36 kilometres from Walikale-Centre on the road to Kisangani.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). The hedge 'amakuru akavuga' covers both 'without fighting' and the flight of government forces; statement now keeps both inside it. Ijambo.net is on the partisan list: source_type corrected. Page 'Published: 2025-03-22' confirmed; 21 March 2025 is a Friday.
claims.researcher_note: Ijambo.net is a Rwanda-based outlet (Yirunga Ltd, Rubavu); treated as not independent of Rwandan narrative. Page "Published: 2025-03-22 11:09:56 CAT" confirmed. Related to REC-0398/REC-0399 (looting at Mubi on 20-21 March, army fall-back toward Mubi) but not the same fact; first control claim for Mubi.

claims.text: BBC Swahili reported that, in a statement issued on Sunday 23 March 2025, Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo said the government welcomed the news that FARDC and Wazalendo military activities would also be suspended.
claims.verification_note: Entry dated 23 Machi 2025 on the live page; 23 March 2025 is a Sunday. Excerpt supports the statement.
claims.researcher_note: Rwanda's account of the M23 announced withdrawal (REC-0400 covers reactions). Entry is on a BBC Swahili live page that carries multiple items; the entry is dated 23 Machi 2025 on the page. The live page was archived on 25 March per search metadata; entry date used.

claims.text: BBC News Swahili reported that the Congolese army had stepped up its campaign to get FDLR rebels to surrender to Congolese authorities or to MONUSCO peacekeepers, and that police and army officers had been using loudspeakers in the Walikale area of North Kivu to urge them to surrender; it said the operation was also in the Pinga area, on the Masisi border, where some FDLR groups are said to be camped.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Live-page entry dated 8 Novemba 2025 confirmed (photo credit AFP; no text credit).
claims.researcher_note: BBC Swahili live-page entry dated 8 Novemba 2025 (photo credit AFP; text unattributed). Context for REC-0697/REC-0698 (FDLR at Pinga 2026) one year earlier. Kinshasa army campaign; no FDLR response (page says FDLR had made no statement on the peace plan).

claims.text: Mwananchi (Tanzania) reported that M23 launched surprise attacks that broke through government forces' strongholds near the capital of the Masisi district and ended up capturing the Nyabiondo area and several neighbouring villages, from 'the day before yesterday, March 9, 2025'.
claims.place_as_written: Nyabiondo and neighbouring villages, Masisi territory
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page 'Jumanne, Machi 11, 2025' confirmed; same event as REC-0388. Mwananchi's article is a compilation credited 'with the help of agencies'; the origin of this sentence is not named.
claims.researcher_note: Tanzanian daily; article is a summary of local-media reporting (page cites Kivu Morning Post and Actualite.cd elsewhere) and does not name the origin of the Nyabiondo sentence. Page date Jumanne, Machi 11, 2025 confirmed. Corroborates r2-G-NKW-MASISI-001 / REC-0388.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that some Congolese media said that on Thursday the M23 took the Kazinga area in Masisi, but that this information had not been confirmed by any of the warring sides.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 (as reported by some Congolese media)
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source).
claims.researcher_note: Unconfirmed claim as BBC states. Weekday only; date computed from weekday and publication date (Thursday 13 November 2025). Kazinga also appears in REC-0460 (health centre looting, Nov-Dec 2025) and REC-0732 (Sept 2026).

claims.text: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that on Thursday 26 February 2026, at about 16:15, combined forces, especially those of the FDLR, entered the JTN tea area at Mweso and shot 19 cows, of which 15 died immediately and 4 were seriously wounded.
claims.place_as_written: JTN tea estate, Mweso, Masisi territory
claims.actor_as_written: combined forces "mainly of the FDLR", per AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Removed 'on X' (in the page but not in an excerpt). Kinyarwanda time 'saa kumi na cumi n'itanu z'amanywa' = 16:15, as printed. 26 Feb 2026 is a Thursday. Relation corrected from counterclaim to new (it is an allegation, not a reply to a record; no record for Mweso/JTN); category corrected to looting_or_destruction. Party allegation; the headline blames FARDC while the quoted account names combined forces 'especially FDLR'. No FARDC response found.
claims.researcher_note: AFC/M23 allegation relayed by a Rwandan outlet (partisan); page date "Friday 27, Feb 2026" confirmed. The page itself says AFC/M23 had not issued a communique on it. Clock time printed as "16:15" with a garbled Kinyarwanda expression. No Kinshasa/FARDC response found.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the fighters fired bursts of bullets at a 19-year-old girl called Wamahoro, from Kitchanga, who died immediately.
claims.place_as_written: JTN tea estate, Mweso, Masisi territory
claims.actor_as_written: combined forces "mainly of the FDLR", per AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Name spelled as printed. Relation corrected from counterclaim to new; category to attack_on_civilians. Part of the same Kanyuka account as the JTN/Mweso cattle shooting of 26 February 2026; no independent confirmation.
claims.researcher_note: Names the victim as printed by Umuryango.rw. The sentence is within the quotation attributed to Kanyuka. AFC/M23 allegation, no independent confirmation seen.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that women it interviewed on September 21, 2025 in MPATI, in the Bashali chiefdom of Masisi territory, recounted brutal acts committed by NYATURA and CMC-FDP militiamen; a resident identified as M. N. said 'almost all the women here were raped during the war' and that she herself had suffered brutal acts at the hands of the men of Jenerali Guidon. The excerpts do not date the acts.
claims.actor_as_written: NYATURA and Collectif des Mouvements pour le Changement – Vikosi vya Ulinzi vya Watu (CMC-FDP) militiamen, per the women interviewed
claims.verification_note: Removed the dateline day and the 70/2024 figures (no excerpt prints them; the 2024 period is pre-window). Added M. N.'s attribution to 'General Guidon's men', which the excerpt prints and which differs from the NYATURA/CMC-FDP attribution. M. N.'s status narrowed: she says she was 'tortured by brutal acts' and does not say in the excerpt that she was raped. Page date 30 Septemba 2025, dateline Goma 29 September 2025. Window caution: the acts are undated. Elsewhere on the page the chief of Mpati dates the rapes he counts to April-October 2024, and residents say the violence stopped when M23 took control of Mpati, so the acts may predate 1 January 2025. Only the interviews (21 September 2025) are inside the window. The page also quotes a 17-year-old (initials S. O.), not listed because no excerpt prints her.
claims.researcher_note: Local testimony reported by SOS Médias Burundi (Burundian independent outlet; page headline date 30 September 2025, dateline Goma 29 September 2025). The dates of the incidents are NOT stated: the page's chief of Mpati (Safari Mbarushimana Jean de Dieu) gives a figure of at least three women a day for April-October 2024 and "more than 70" victims in total, which falls before the project window and is not used here; the claim rests on the interviews of 21 September 2025. Witnesses are given by initials only and one is a 17-year-old ("S. O., 17"), not listed. Attribution of "General Guidon" men: Guidon Shimiray Mwissa is the NDC-R leader per other records.

claims.text: Kigali Today (Rwanda) reported that Rwandan President Kagame said that in the areas M23 controls, it does well in combating FDLR and other criminal groups, but that in Masisi, Walikale and other areas controlled by FARDC, FDLR is still found there, cooperating with government forces.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page '3 April 2026 at 17:27' confirmed. Party statement (Rwanda) reported by a Rwandan outlet; not evidence of the facts asserted.
claims.researcher_note: Rwanda's own position as reported by a Rwandan outlet (party statement, not evidence of the fact). Context: REC-0697 (Pinga, FARDC helicopter delivery to FDLR-FOCA, reported) and REC-0698 (FARDC operation against FDLR around Pinga-Walikale, 29 March 2026). The occasion of the remarks is not stated in the excerpt.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that an air strike attributed to the Congolese armed forces (FARDC) killed about seven civilians and wounded more than 40 others on Friday, January 2, 2026, at Masisi-Center.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC (air strike attributed to FARDC, per SOS Médias Burundi)
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Figures field changed to words as printed. Page dateline 'Goma, Januari 4, 2026' confirmed; same event as REC-0681. The page says witnesses put it at 'saa 1:00 usiku' local time (Swahili clock: about 7 p.m.) and that a drone 'reportedly' dropped the device on a building housing a small War Child base; not used in the statement.
claims.researcher_note: Burundian independent outlet; page headline date 4 January 2026 confirmed. Known record REC-0681 (2 January 2026 drone strike on Masisi-centre). The page reports a drone; time of day not used (clock expression ambiguous in the Swahili translation). Attribution to FARDC is "alleged/attributed" per the page; no Kinshasa response seen on this page.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that, according to Doctors Without Borders (MSF), 42 people, most of them wounded in the attack, were currently admitted to the Masisi General Referral Hospital.
claims.actor_as_written: not applicable (hospital admissions after a strike attributed to FARDC)
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). 'kwa sasa wamelazwa' = 'are currently admitted', so 'then admitted' changed.
claims.researcher_note: MSF figure as relayed by SOS Médias Burundi (MSF primary source not cited on page). Adds the hospital burden to REC-0681. No attack on the hospital is alleged here.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that MONUSCO condemned on Saturday 3 January 2026 the drone strike of the previous day at Masisi-Center.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints the date (Saturday, January 3, 2026, a Saturday) and the condemnation; single clause, single source.
claims.researcher_note: Context statement (mediator/UN, not a party). Known record REC-0681.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported, in a dispatch datelined Goma 27 November 2025, that heavy fighting broke out at dawn on Thursday between M23 rebels and local Wazalendo militiamen at the village of Kibati, in the Luberike grouping of Walikale territory.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts support each clause; page headline date 30 November 2025, dateline 27 November 2025 (a Thursday).
claims.researcher_note: Burundian independent outlet; page headline date 30 November 2025, dateline "Goma, Novemba 27, 2025"; weekday "Alhamisi" = Thursday 27 November 2025 (date computed from weekday and dateline). The page says it was the fourth Wazalendo attack on Kibati in a few weeks. Neighbouring known records: REC-0450 (27-29 Oct 2025), REC-0459 (25 Nov 2025).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that the FARDC used their air force to strike AFC/M23 positions at Kibati (Walikale) and Kasopo (Masisi), and that no official casualty figures were available.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC air force (per SOS Médias Burundi)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts support the statement; date normalised to the month (original value '2025-11 (reported 2025-11-27)' is not a date). Possibly related to REC-0457 (21 Nov 2025 Sukhoi strike near Kasopo), not shown to be the same. Time given on the page ('saa 9:00 asubuhi') is ambiguous between Swahili and Western clocks and is not used.
claims.researcher_note: The page gives no date for the strikes other than the dispatch dateline; the time of day given on the page uses an ambiguous clock expression and is not used. Related to REC-0457 (21 Nov 2025 Sukhoi bombing at Kibanda near Kasopo).

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge said M23 rebels had retaken the town of Masisi on the afternoon of Thursday, after he had announced in the morning of the same day that government forces had retaken it on Wednesday.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Added 'afternoon' ('ku muhingamo'), which the excerpt_en dropped; translation corrected. Page 'Yatangajwe 9 Ukwa mbere 2025' (Thursday) confirmed. Qualifies REC-0368 (reported recapture, 8 January). 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-NKW claim 30)
claims.researcher_note: BBC Gahuza page "Yatangajwe 9 Ukwa mbere 2025" confirmed. Kinshasa (FARDC) account; qualifies REC-0368 (reported FARDC-Wazalendo recapture of Masisi-Centre, 8 January): per the same spokesperson, the recapture was reversed on 9 January. Weekdays given on the page ("ku wa gatatu", "uno wa kane") match 8 and 9 January 2025.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge said government forces were doing well there and were the ones controlling the whole town of Ngungu and its surroundings.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Party claim of control; no independent confirmation on the page. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-NKW claim 31)
claims.researcher_note: Party account (FARDC); no independent confirmation on the page. Ngungu also named in the UN GoE conversion of villages into towns (r2-G-DOC-858-059, August 2025).

claims.text: BBC News Swahili reported that the M23 rebellion, backed by Rwanda, took control of the town of Masisi, an important town in eastern DRC, on Saturday, and that the DRC army had pulled back, saying it was avoiding losing more lives in the town of Masisi.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page 'Iliyochapishwa 7 Januari 2025' confirmed; 4 January 2025 was a Saturday. REC-0366 rests on BBC News Afrique; this BBC Swahili page is likely the same BBC newsroom origin, so it is not independent corroboration.
claims.researcher_note: Weekday only ("Jumamosi"); date computed from weekday and publication date (Saturday 4 January 2025, matches REC-0366). Page "Iliyochapishwa 7 Januari 2025" confirmed. The text relays AFP and Reuters (MP Alexis Bahunga quoted to AFP elsewhere on the page).

claims.text: BBC News Swahili reported that Alexis Bahunga, a member of parliament of North Kivu province, told AFP that it was with great sadness that he learned of the capture of the Masisi centre by M23, and that he asked the government to take steps to restore government authority across the whole area.
claims.actor_as_written: Alexis Bahunga, member of parliament for North Kivu province
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Reaction to the capture in REC-0366: relation changed from new_related_event to adds_detail. 'mbunge wa jimbo' can mean either a national MP elected in the province or a provincial deputy.
claims.researcher_note: A local elected official (not the executive). Quote credited by BBC to AFP: originating source AFP.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that AFC/M23 said FDLR fighters, together with Wazalendo, killed 10 residents in Masisi and Walikale territories; AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the attack was launched in the Malemo and Kalembe area, on the Masisi-Walikale border, in the night of 24 May 2026, and that in Malemo they killed three civilians, wounded six and abducted the local leader, whose fate was still unknown.
claims.actor_as_written: FDLR together with Wazalendo, per AFC/M23 (Umuryango.rw headline)
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Figures written as the excerpts print them (words for three/six). Same place and night as REC-0706 (Kalembe, 24-25 May 2026). Party allegation relayed by a Rwandan outlet; 'terrorist' is the outlet's/AFC/M23's label and is not adopted. No Kinshasa reply found.
claims.researcher_note: AFC/M23 account relayed by a Rwandan outlet (partisan); page date "Monday 25, May 2026" confirmed. The "10 residents" total is AFC/M23's; the page itself breaks out only three killed and six wounded at Malemo. Known record REC-0706 (night of 24-25 May 2026, Wazalendo attack on AFC/M23 positions at Kalembe, civilians killed). The word "terrorist" is the outlet's wording of AFC/M23's label, not adopted here. No Kinshasa/FARDC reply seen.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that AFC/M23 said that after leaving those areas, FDLR and Wazalendo heavily looted the Bweru area, taking 11 cows belonging to residents and many pigs.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source).
claims.researcher_note: AFC/M23 allegation via Rwandan outlet (partisan). Date: night of 24 May is that of the attack, the looting is said to follow it.

claims.text: UMUSEKE (Rwanda) reported on 10 September 2026 that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said government forces launched attacks at dawn on Thursday 10 September 2026 in areas including Ihula, Malemo, Minjenje and Kibati and their surroundings, and that, posting on X, he said the fighting was continuing and many residents had fled.
claims.place_as_written: Ihula, Malemo, Minjenje and Kibati and surroundings (Masisi and Walikale)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts print every date and place; page 'September 10, 2026' confirmed; 10 Sept 2026 is a Thursday. Party account, partisan relay: C. Same day and Kibati as REC-0734.
claims.researcher_note: AFC/M23 account relayed by a Rwandan outlet (partisan); page date September 10, 2026 confirmed. Corroborates REC-0734 (10 Sept 2026 offensive on AFC-M23 positions, Kibati) and REC-0733 (8 Sept Malemo). The Kinshasa account of the same day is in the existing records (Radio Okapi).

claims.text: UMUSEKE (Rwanda) reported that the AFC/M23 spokesperson said the escalation of fighting affected residents' security and could hinder aid work, and that aid organisations and their staff could not reach residents affected by the attacks.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts support both clauses; S1 'Yavuze' follows S0's speaker on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Party claim of humanitarian access denial attributed to Kinshasa-side attacks; no independent confirmation on the page. "Yavuze" refers to Kanyuka in the preceding sentence (excerpt starts at the claim; attribution to Kanyuka comes from the surrounding paragraph).

claims.text: Rwanda Tribune (Rwanda) reported that information from the area said AFC/M23 had taken Mindjendje hill, in the Banakindi area of the Kisimba groupement; it said fighting on Thursday 10 September 2026 began in the morning and continued in areas near the border of Walikale and Masisi, and that residents said the fighting was heavy and drones were used.
claims.place_as_written: Mindjendje hill, Banakindi, Kisimba groupement (Walikale-Masisi border)
claims.verification_note: Removed the 'last updated' day (11 not in an excerpt). The page does not tie the capture explicitly to the 10 September fighting; the statement now reports the two separately. Precedes REC-0741 (FARDC retaking positions around Mindjendje, about 27 Sept 2026).
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan outlet (partisan) citing unnamed local information; "Last updated: September 11, 2026 6:35 am" on page. Precedes REC-0741 (about 27 Sept 2026, FARDC retaking positions around Mindjendje), which implies the position changed hands; this claim records only the 10 September claim of capture.

claims.text: Bwiza (Rwanda, English edition), relaying Actualite.cd, reported that various reports from the Waloa Loanda groupement in Walikale territory indicated that a large number of armed individuals, believed to be FDLR rebels, were disturbing security in Mishipo, in the Makungurano area; that, according to several sources, a man claiming to be a general, known as Mutayonga and said to be from Masisi territory, had been in Mishipo for several days with around 100 armed men; that reports suggested the group's leader told residents to vacate the area, claiming he had bought the land; and that, according to information received by Actualite.cd, the alleged FDLR fighters had been firing shots to intimidate the population.
claims.place_as_written: Mishipo, Makungurano area, Waloa Loanda groupement, Walikale territory
claims.actor_as_written: armed individuals believed to be FDLR rebels, led by a man known as Mutayonga (per local reports)
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Kept the 'reports suggest' hedge on the eviction demand and added the S3 clause the claim cited but did not state. Page 'Tuesday, July 8, 2025' confirmed. FDLR attribution is 'believed to be'/'alleged' in the source. No casualties reported.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan outlet republishing Actualite.cd material (the page says "According to information received by Actualite.cd"); page date "Tuesday, July 8, 2025" confirmed. Alleged FDLR attribution rests on "believed to be", not established. Not checked against Actualite.cd original (French). Status: intimidation and an eviction demand; no casualties reported on the page.

claims.text: Bwiza, citing Kivu Morning Post, reported that heavy fighting with heavy weapons between AFC/M23 fighters and the Wazalendo and FARDC coalition began, from 'saa saba z'amanywa' (the Kinyarwanda daytime hour count), on Thursday 3 September 2026 at Chinono, an area linking Ziralo and Mubuku in Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory; it cited local civil society as saying the fighting made many residents flee.
claims.place_as_written: Chinono, between Ziralo and Mubuku groupements, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23; Wazalendo and FARDC coalition (as the source names them)
claims.verification_note: Page (Bwiza, byline Denis Nsengiyumva, dated 4 Sept 2026) prints both passages; it credits Kivu Morning Post for the account. 3 Sept 2026 is a Thursday. Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 0)
claims.researcher_note: Single Rwandan outlet relaying Kivu Morning Post (originating_source); not in known_records (claim_search 'Chinono' returns nothing). Hour is printed in Kinyarwanda clock style ('saa saba z'amanywa', i.e. the seventh hour of the day, 13:00 by the usual conversion); the statement keeps the printed form. Bwiza is Rwanda-based; treat as relay.

claims.text: Bwiza, citing Kivu Morning Post, reported that other fighting in the same area took place on Wednesday 2 September 2026 when the coalition attacked the village of Lomera in Kabare territory, and that an AFC/M23 communiqué said the attack killed people and made many residents flee.
claims.actor_as_written: the Wazalendo-FARDC coalition (as the page refers back to it); casualty claim from an AFC/M23 communiqué
claims.verification_note: Statement supported. Actor corrected: 'ihuriro ry'izo ngabo zirwanira ubutegetsi' refers back to the Wazalendo-FARDC alliance named earlier on the page ('forces fighting for the government'), not to unnamed 'forces fighting for power'. The deaths rest only on the AFC/M23 communiqué; no toll. Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 1)
claims.researcher_note: AFC/M23 account relayed; no toll given. Related to REC-1073 (Lomera, September 2026, Amnesty: four men detained by M23) and the 2025 Lomera mining suspension records, but a different event. Contradiction to check: none. Date 'Wednesday, 2 September' printed with day and month in the page (kuwa Gatatu, itariki 2 Nzeri).

claims.text: Bwiza (byline Bénjamin BABOU) reported that AFC/M23 had taken Tushunguti, in Ziralo groupement, Kalehe territory, after heavy fighting with FARDC and armed groups supporting it, and that information from the area said AFC/M23 fighters had driven out Wazalendo and others on the Kinshasa side.
claims.verification_note: Statement supported (Bwiza, byline Bénjamin BABOU, dated 2 Sept 2026). Date corrected to a report date: the page does not give the day of capture and itself cites a Critical Threats report that AFC/M23 took Tushunguti on 18 August 2026 ('Raporo ya Critical Threats ivuga ko ku wa 18 Kanama AFC/M23 yafashe Tushunguti'), so the capture may predate 2 September. Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says. The page also cites Critical Threats for a capture of Tushunguti on 18 August 2026; the day of the capture it reports is not given.
claims.researcher_note: Page is dated 2 September 2026 and does not say on which day the capture happened (date given is the report date; 'approximate'). The page also cites a Critical Threats report for 18-19 August captures (digest, not cited here) and says fighting resumed at Tushunguti on 17 August. Compare REC-1043/1044/1045 (Tushunguti April-May 2026) and REC-1254/1257 (Aug 2026). Control claim: Tushunguti held by AFC/M23 as of 2 Sept 2026 per Bwiza.

claims.text: Bwiza reported, citing information from the area, that FARDC supported by Wazalendo fighters retook the centre of Numbi in Kalehe territory on Tuesday 6 October 2026 after it had been controlled by M23 rebels for several months; it added that, according to some information, M23 fighters had fallen back to Numbi on Monday after losing positions at Shanje, Gasenda and the hills of Bukumba.
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page (Bwiza, dated 6 Oct 2026). Bwiza's sources are unnamed local information. Same day Bwiza published that AFC/M23 retook Numbi within hours (claim 25). Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-1080 (Numbi retaken by FARDC and Wazalendo, 6 Oct 2026) and the Shanje/Lumbishi/Numbi entries REC-1081 and REC-1083 from a Kinyarwanda outlet (Bwiza, Rwanda-based; source of 'amakuru aturuka mu gace' not named). Adds the names Gasenda and the Bukumba hills as positions the source says M23 lost on the previous days. Bwiza also published (later, per its own related-links) that AFC/M23 retook Lumbishi and Numbi hours after Wazalendo took them; not fetched.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that, according to information announced by the AFC/M23 alliance, forces fighting for Kinshasa, chiefly FDLR members, began destruction at Shanje and its surroundings (Kalehe territory) on Wednesday 7 October 2026 from 'saa yine n'igice za mu gitondo', burning many civilian houses and the market; the AFC/M23 communiqué said further information on damage and casualties would be published later.
claims.verification_note: All three passages on the page (Bwiza, dated 7 Oct 2026, published 06:34; title 'FDLR iravugwaho' = 'FDLR is alleged'). The first sentence is in Bwiza's voice but the page states the information comes from the AFC/M23 communiqué; party account only. Same event as REC-1084 (Shanje burning, 6-7 Oct 2026). Hour discrepancy: Bwiza prints 'saa yine n'igice za mu gitondo' (10:30 a.m. on the Kinyarwanda clock) but published this piece at 06:34 on 7 October, so 10:30 that morning cannot be right as converted; Umuryango prints Kanyuka's start time as 'saa Kumi n'igice' (04:30 or 16:30). Both may render 4:30 a.m.; unresolved. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 4)
claims.researcher_note: Party account (AFC/M23 communiqué relayed by a Rwanda-based outlet); cite only for what AFC/M23 said. Concerns REC-1084 (Shanje shops burned, night of 6-7 Oct 2026, Radio Maendeleo citing returnees, no perpetrator attributed in that record). Time discrepancy between outlets: Bwiza prints the start as 'saa yine n'igice za mu gitondo', Umuryango prints 'saa Kumi n'igice' (no a.m./p.m. qualifier) for what it says Lawrence Kanyuka stated (see companion claim); on the usual Kinyarwanda conversion the two read 10:30 and 04:30 and cannot both be right if converted, so the printed forms are kept. Do not read the burning as established; no independent attribution to FDLR found in this unit.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a message on 7 October 2026 that attacks by forces supporting the Kinshasa government, including FDLR fighters, in the Shanje area of Kalehe territory had destroyed civilian houses and the market, and that details of the damage and of any dead or wounded would be published later.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 spokesperson (accusing FDLR and Kinshasa-aligned forces)
claims.verification_note: All passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, byline ISIMBI Estella, 7 Oct 2026; read from the retained copy, the live site refuses plain requests). Party statement only. Same event as REC-1084 and claim 4. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 5)
claims.researcher_note: Party statement relayed by Rwandan outlet Umuryango.rw (page loaded via browser UA). Statement kind: social-media/message as reported. Time of start differs from Bwiza's report of the same communiqué (see companion claim). Concerns REC-1084.

claims.text: DW Kiswahili (Iddi Ssessanga) reported that a woman, whose name DW said had been changed for her safety, told DW that three soldiers broke into her home and one of them tried to rape her; DW said the incident took place in February in Kavumu village, 30 km from Bukavu.
claims.place_as_written: Kavumu village, about 30 km from Bukavu, Kabare
claims.actor_as_written: three soldiers (not further identified by the source)
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the DW Kiswahili page (byline Iddi Ssessanga, 2 July 2025). The survivor's name on the page, 'Riziki', is a pseudonym DW says it changed, so it is not listed as a name. The soldiers' army is not stated. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0776 (attempted rape during break-in by three soldiers, Kavumu, February 2025) from an independent outlet that spoke to the survivor (name changed by DW, so not listed). The page does not say which army the soldiers belonged to; the same article says community groups blame the Congolese army and Wazalendo for sexual violence in northern South Kivu villages (see companion claim).

claims.text: DW Kiswahili reported that, in villages of northern South Kivu that it describes as having become war zones during the fighting of January and February, women and children suffered rape and sexual violence by armed men, and that community groups and activists blamed the Congolese army and Wazalendo fighters (from North Kivu) for taking part.
claims.place_as_written: Villages in northern South Kivu along Lake Kivu (Kalehe and Kabare area, as the article frames the M23 advance on Bukavu)
claims.actor_as_written: Congolese army and Wazalendo fighters, as blamed by community groups and activists
claims.verification_note: Narrowed: the page dates the M23 advance that turned villages into war zones to 'between January and February'; it does not itself date the rapes, so the statement now ties them to that period of fighting rather than stating their dates as fact. The year is the page's (2 July 2025). 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Adds a second origin (community groups and activists, as relayed by DW) for the attribution in REC-0763 / REC-0765 (sexual violence by FARDC and Wazalendo in Kalehe and between Kalehe and Kavumu, Jan-Feb 2025). The article names no village except Kavumu and no number; place given only as 'villages in the north of South Kivu'.

claims.text: DW Kiswahili reported that in areas taken by M23, such as Bukavu and Goma, witnesses had reported a rise in rape, mostly of married women and girls, and that some women were forced to have sex to obtain certain services; it said many survivors do not report out of fear or shame.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source beyond 'areas taken by M23'
claims.verification_note: Passage on the page (DW Kiswahili, 2 July 2025). Unnamed witnesses; no perpetrator named beyond the place being M23-held. 'wake za watu' = married women.
claims.researcher_note: General statement attributed to unnamed witnesses; no date, place within Bukavu or perpetrator given. The page does not attribute the acts to M23 itself; it only places them in M23-held areas.

claims.text: DW Kiswahili, citing MSF, reported that in the north of South Kivu MSF had attended to nearly 700 victims since the start of the year.
claims.verification_note: Supported. 'wahanga' is 'victims', not 'survivors'; wording aligned. Relays MSF; the year is the page's (2 July 2025).
claims.researcher_note: Relays MSF figures (originating_source MSF); complements REC-0773 (MSF survivors assisted, Kalehe and Uvira regions, Jan-June 2025); the DW wording says 'north of South Kivu' and does not name Kalehe.

claims.text: DW Kiswahili reported that before AFC/M23 took Bukavu in February, soldiers of the Congolese army had already been convicted of sexual violence against women in several villages of Kabare and Kalehe, and that when AFC-M23 arrived in Bukavu the accused fled, together with judges and lawyers.
claims.place_as_written: Villages of Kabare and Kalehe territories; Bukavu
claims.actor_as_written: soldiers of the Congolese army (convicted, per DW)
claims.verification_note: Passage on the DW Kiswahili page (25 Nov 2025). 'wamehukumiwa' = had been sentenced; 'washtakiwa' = the accused, as translated.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0767 (Bukavu court sentences soldiers for murder and rape, 14 Feb 2025) and REC-0768/0769 (escape of detainees, convicted SGBV prisoners) from Swahili-language DW; no names or dates in this passage.

claims.text: DW Kiswahili reported that, after AFC/M23 reached Bukavu, rape cases were later witnessed although they were dismissed by AFC/M23; it quoted women's rights defender Nono Mwavita as saying women's security has not improved.
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the DW page (25 Nov 2025). The denial is reported at second hand; no wording, date or number.
claims.researcher_note: The article does not say who raised the cases, how many, or in what words AFC/M23 rejected them: a denial reported at second hand by DW. Pairs with the 'new' claim on rises in rape in Bukavu and with REC-0859 (climate of fear nine months after the capture).

claims.text: Bwiza reported a communiqué of Lawrence Kanyuka, whom it called FRN spokesperson, saying that on Monday 26 October 2026 at about 4:00 a.m. the Kinshasa-backed forces attacked Mitimbili and Munanira in Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu territory, after attacks on Kuwihene, Rugezi and Point Zéro in the Minembwe area the previous night using kamikaze drones and 120mm and 82mm mortars.
claims.place_as_written: Mitimbili and Munanira, Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu
claims.actor_as_written: joint forces supporting Kinshasa (as alleged in the communiqué)
claims.verification_note: All passages on the page (Bwiza, dated 26 Oct 2026, published 14:43). Party account. Bwiza prints 'Umuvugizi wa FRN' and 'Murenge wa Kaziba' (murenge = sector; Kaziba is a chiefdom in the DRC system); printed labels kept. Related to REC-0580. Bwiza calls Kanyuka 'FRN spokesperson' here; BBC Gahuza headlines on the same site describe FRN as an armed movement led by Joseph Kabila. The label is kept as printed.
claims.researcher_note: Party account only (the spokesperson is printed as 'Umuvugizi wa FRN, Lawrence Kanyuka'; the unit's other records call Kanyuka AFC/M23 spokesperson: FRN is printed as the source has it, not resolved here). Relates to REC-0580 (26-27 Oct: FARDC claims to retake Mitimbili) and REC-0574 (12 Oct Mitimbili). Minembwe parts belong to unit E-FIZ. Do not read the attack claims as established.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that on Monday 12 October 2026 fighting between AFC/M23 fighters and FARDC supported by Wazalendo was reported in Kaziba chiefdom, and that, according to information from the area reaching Bwiza, it restarted at 'saa kumi n'ebyiri za mu gitondo' on the Mitimbili hills in Muhumba groupement, east of Kaziba near the border with Bafulero chiefdom; it added that a second battle at Mwera in Butuzi groupement was reported on social network X.
claims.place_as_written: Mitimbili hills, Muhumba groupement, Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu; Mwera, Butuzi groupement
claims.verification_note: All passages on the page (Bwiza, dated 12 Oct 2026, published 07:19, consistent with a 06:00 start). The Mwera front rests on social-media posts only. Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 14)
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0574 (resumption of clashes on the Mitimbili hills, 12 Oct 2026) from a Kinyarwanda outlet; adds Mwera (Butuzi groupement) as a second reported front, sourced by Bwiza only to posts on X (a lead, not verified). Bwiza prints the hour as 'saa kumi n'ebyiri za mu gitondo' (twelfth hour of the day on the Kinyarwanda clock, i.e. 06:00 by the usual conversion; kept as printed).

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that the Wazalendo alliance, backed by the DRC government, expelled students and teachers from schools in Kabare and Walungu territories of South Kivu, that the expulsions began on 9 September 2025, and that videos on social media showed people fleeing while Wazalendo fighters told them studying or teaching meant nothing to them.
claims.place_as_written: Schools in Kabare and Walungu territories
claims.verification_note: All passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, byline JABO Blaise Patience, 11 Sept 2025; retained copy). Rests on videos the outlet describes. Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0847 (9 Sept 2025, armed men presenting themselves as Wazalendo empty schools in Kabare territory) from a Rwanda-based outlet that relies on social-media videos and does not give its own eyewitness source; extends the area to Walungu territory. Umuryango.rw is Rwandan and its framing is partisan towards AFC/M23; the facts rest on videos it describes, which this unit did not see.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that, in videos circulating on social media, one Wazalendo fighter was heard speaking Swahili and saying that students found studying would be killed, and another told students everyone should go home and that whoever went to school would die.
claims.place_as_written: Schools in Kabare and Walungu territories
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (as heard in videos described by the outlet)
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, 11 Sept 2025). Quotes are the outlet's Kinyarwanda rendering of videos it did not link.
claims.researcher_note: Threats as described by the outlet from videos it did not link; not independently verified here. Pairs with the school expulsions claim and with REC-0847. Quote translated from the Kinyarwanda rendering the outlet prints.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that the AFC/M23 alliance condemned the silence of the international community, aid organisations and human rights defenders while Wazalendo continued actions depriving residents of their rights, and that spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said, citing the Wazalendo statements, that 'these words push people into killings and war crimes'.
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, 11 Sept 2025). 'War crimes' is Kanyuka's phrase, quoted with attribution.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement (AFC/M23 spokesperson as reported by a Rwanda-based outlet); the legal phrase 'war crimes' ('ibyaha by’intambara') is Kanyuka's, quoted with attribution, not a finding. Statement kind: statement as reported; no date of utterance given beyond the article date.

claims.text: DW Kiswahili reported that further heavy fighting between M23 and Wazalendo took place 'yesterday, Sunday' at Burhale in Walungu district, where vehicles and houses suspected of sheltering M23 were burned by Wazalendo in an area called Mashango.
claims.verification_note: Passage on the DW page dated 14 April 2025 (a Monday), so 'jana Jumapili' is 13 April 2025. Single source, no toll.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and publication date (article dated 14 April 2025, 'jana Jumapili' = Sunday 13 April 2025). Not in known_records at Mashango (REC-0477 is Burhale, 18 March 2025). Single source; no toll.

claims.text: DW Kiswahili (Tatu Karema) reported that witnesses said heavy fighting had taken place since early morning at Kasheke village after other heavy fighting there and in the villages of Lemera and Bushaku and in some villages of Kabare and Kalehe, and that civil society sources estimated that nearly 12 villages were under Wazalendo control, which M23 had not confirmed.
claims.place_as_written: Kasheke, Lemera, Bushaku and other villages, Kalehe and Kabare
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the DW Kiswahili page (byline Tatu Karema, 11 April 2025). 'Nearly 12 villages' is a civil-society estimate.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0810/REC-0811 (9 April: Wazalendo recover Shanje, Bushaku 1, Bushaku 2, Nyawaronga) with a second origin (civil society sources and witnesses cited by DW). 'Nearly 12 villages' is a civil-society estimate, unconfirmed by M23, as DW says. The day of the Kasheke fighting is not given; date is the report date.
