claims.text: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that M23 rebels took the town of Nzibira in Walungu territory on the evening of 'yesterday, Sunday' after first shelling army positions, according to witnesses, and it cited Radio Okapi for fighting in surrounding villages including Cisaza, Cibanda, Muyange, Karhuliza and Kalongo.
claims.place_as_written: Nzibira, Walungu; surrounding villages Cisaza, Cibanda, Muyange, Karhuliza, Kalongo
claims.actor_as_written: M23 (as the source names it); FARDC with allied groups
claims.verification_note: All passages on the page (BBC News Gahuza, published 22 Sept 2025; body in Kirundi). 'ku mugoroba w'ejo ku wa Mungu' = yesterday, Sunday evening = 21 Sept 2025. Date discrepancy with REC-0506 (26-29 Sept 2025) to surface.
claims.researcher_note: Adds the capture date to REC-0506 (which is dated 26-29 Sept 2025): BBC (22 Sept) says the town was taken on the evening of 'yesterday, Sunday' (21 Sept; date computed from weekday and publication date), and r1-SKC-2025H2-017 (Radio Okapi) says FARDC counter-attacked on 29 Sept 'a week after' the occupation. Possible date discrepancy with REC-0506 for the reviewer. Page is in Kirundi although filed on BBC's 'Gahuza' service; relays Radio Okapi (UN-supported) and witnesses.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that fighting between AFC/M23 and FARDC and allied groups intensified on Sunday 21 September 2025 in Walungu territory and ended with M23 defeating the government army and Wazalendo fighters and taking Nzibira, with the heaviest fighting at Cisaza, Cibanda, Muyange, Karhuliza and Kalongo, as Radio Okapi reported.
claims.verification_note: Passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, byline ISHIMWE Jean de Dieu, 22 Sept 2025; retained copy). The localities are relayed from Radio Okapi; graded on its own sources (a partisan Rwanda-based outlet). Agrees with BBC Gahuza on 21 Sept. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates BBC Gahuza on the date (day 21 September 2025 is printed here) and the localities; both relay Radio Okapi, so they are not independent of one another or of the Radio Okapi account already in the edition. Rwanda-based outlet; framing partisan towards AFC/M23. Relevant to the date given in REC-0506 (26-29 September).

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the AFC/M23 group accused the DRC government army of 'excessively severe' drone attacks 'in areas inhabited by civilians' at Lumbishi, Kalehe territory, on Monday, and that Lawrence Kanyuka said in a communiqué that the CH-4 drone attacks 'destroyed many things and caused many civilians to flee'.
claims.actor_as_written: DRC government army (FARDC) drones, as alleged by AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Narrowed: the page does not call Kanyuka 'spokesperson' here, and the article body is Kinyarwanda (the Gahuza site carries both languages), not Kirundi. Page published 4 May 2026, a Monday. Party allegation.
claims.researcher_note: Party allegation (AFC/M23) reported by BBC with Kinshasa's denial (see companion claim); no toll given. Date: the page is dated 4 May 2026 and says 'this Monday' (4 May 2026 is a Monday). Not in known_records (no Lumbishi record for May 2026). Page is in Kirundi.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Jacques Kongolo, adviser to President Félix Tshisekedi, told BBC on Monday that the government side was not the one violating the ceasefire agreements, and quoted him as saying that the other side uses Rwandan drones to shoot at them and then lies that it was the government side that fired.
claims.verification_note: Supported; only the language label removed (the article body is Kinyarwanda, not Kirundi). Party statement as told to BBC.
claims.researcher_note: Kinshasa's response to the AFC/M23 drone allegation at Lumbishi, as printed by BBC; Kongolo's words are a party claim about Rwanda's role that this unit did not verify.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that the Lumbishi, Shanje, Kavumu and Numbi areas of Kalehe territory were retaken by AFC/M23 fighters a few hours after Wazalendo had taken them, and that on Tuesday 6 October 2026 the Kinshasa-aligned coalition, chiefly Wazalendo and FDLR, had taken Shanje town, the Gasenda area and the Bukumba hills.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23; Wazalendo and FDLR (as the source names them)
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page (Bwiza, dated 7 Oct 2026, 11:31). Same event as REC-1080/1081 (Kalehe, 5-7 Oct 2026); it contradicts their end state and their attribution (FARDC with Wazalendo vs Wazalendo and FDLR). Bwiza names no source for the retaking. Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says.
claims.researcher_note: Contradicts the end-state in REC-1080 / REC-1081 (Numbi, Shanje, Lumbishi reported retaken by FARDC and Wazalendo on 5-6 Oct; Radio Maendeleo on 20 Oct says a counter-offensive allowed troops to retake): Bwiza says AFC/M23 retook Lumbishi, Shanje, Kavumu and Numbi within hours, and attributes the 6 Oct capture to Wazalendo and FDLR (the Radio Okapi/Maendeleo-based records say FARDC with Wazalendo). Control claims from a Rwanda-based outlet that does not name its source for the retaking; the page is dated 7 Oct 2026 and does not give the hour of the retaking. Treat 'contested'.

claims.text: Bwiza reported, citing unnamed 'new information', that about 60 houses, including kiosks, were burned in Shanje centre and cattle were looted, including two herds said to belong to Gen. Gabriel Amisi Kumba, known as Tango Four.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed in this sentence; the same article attributes destruction at Shanje on 7 October to FDLR-dominated Wazalendo, citing an AFC/M23 communiqué
claims.verification_note: Passage on the page (Bwiza, 7 Oct 2026). Unnamed source; 'bivugwa ko' (it is said) hedge kept as 'said to belong'.
claims.researcher_note: Adds a house count (about 60) and a looting detail to REC-1084 (Shanje, almost all shops burned, night of 6-7 Oct 2026). Source of the figure not named; the herds' owner is a claim by 'new information', not verified. The article ties the destruction to FDLR via the AFC/M23 communiqué (see other claims); no independent attribution.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on X on Tuesday 11 August 2026 that the Kinshasa government's forces, including FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo groups, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian army (FDNB), had launched general attacks from 05:00 with heavy weapons on densely populated parts of Kalehe territory, including Chambombo, Cyangugu, Kaziba ya Rumbishi, Kwisimbi and Gafufura, with some residents killed and injured.
claims.place_as_written: Chambombo, Cyangugu, Kaziba ya Rumbishi, Kwisimbi and Gafufura, Kalehe
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo, foreign mercenaries and FDNB (Burundi), as alleged by AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: All passages on the page (Bwiza, byline Bénjamin BABOU, 11 Aug 2026, 14:40). The page says AFC/M23 made the accusation 'kuri uyu wa Kabiri tariki ya 11 Kanama 2026'. Party account only.
claims.researcher_note: Party account only (AFC/M23). It adds an allegation of Burundian army (FDNB) participation that no other record in this unit's scope carries for Kalehe in August 2026; no denial from Burundi or Kinshasa on this specific allegation was found in this unit's searches (see gap party_statements). Concerns REC-1066, REC-1067 and REC-1252 (army says it foiled M23 attacks, 11-12 Aug 2026). Bwiza notes the post came after days of calm and after the July fighting at Minembwe. Kanyuka's text quoted on the page names the same places.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 announced that on 17 August 2026 FARDC, FDLR and other armed groups working with the Kinshasa government launched simultaneous attacks (the spokesperson listing also FDLR, Wazalendo groups, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian army FDNB among the attackers) in places including Kalehe territory (Katare, Tushunguti, Nyamugari and Kivoka) and on the Minembwe line, with AFC-M23 saying 120mm mortars and KT-6 drones were used and that the attacks killed civilians and destroyed homes and schools.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo, foreign mercenaries and FDNB, as listed by AFC/M23 (the page names FDNB in the list)
claims.verification_note: All passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, byline ISIMBI Estella, 17 Aug 2026; retained copy). Party account only. 2026-10-29: source 2 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 28)
claims.researcher_note: Party account only. Bwiza's piece on Tushunguti (2 Sept 2026) also says fighting resumed at Tushunguti, Katare, Nyamugari and Kivoka on 17 August 2026; no independent source for civilian deaths found in this unit. Kanyuka is named on the page as the person who said the list of attackers included FDNB; the passage structure is ambiguous about who exactly announced which part, so the statement attributes to 'AFC/M23' and cites the spokesperson only as the page does.

claims.text: Umuseke, crediting Radio Maendeleo, reported that a large fire broke out on the morning of Thursday 10 September 2026 on Avenue Kasheke 3 in the Buholo-Kasha area of Bagira commune, Bukavu, damaging two schools (Mogo primary school and a school called Furaha), with at least 27 bodies counted by 15:00 on provisional figures; the page quotes the Buholo-Kasha area head Patrice Mugaruka Buduge as saying the fire started at about 8:00 a.m.
claims.place_as_written: Avenue Kasheke 3, Buholo-Kasha, Bagira commune, Bukavu
claims.actor_as_written: fire; cause not stated by the source
claims.verification_note: All passages on the page (Umuseke, byline Ange Eric Hatangimana, 10 Sept 2026). The page credits the whole story to Radio Maendeleo ('Radio Maendeleo dukesha iyi nkuru'). Same event as REC-1074; place, schools, toll and hour conflict with the Actualite.cd record and the AFC/M23 account (claim 30). Radio Maendeleo's own report not seen, so kept at C. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: CONFLICTS with REC-1074 and r1-ST-DRC-2026-004 (Actualite.cd: two schools in Kadutu commune, Cimpunda) and with the AFC/M23 account (24 dead, Tshimpunda area, Kadutu commune, fire in the early afternoon; separate claim): this relay of Radio Maendeleo gives Bagira commune, Buholo-Kasha, Avenue Kasheke 3, schools Mogo and Furaha, at least 27 dead (provisional), start about 8:00 a.m. The place names differ and could be different spellings or different parts of one event; this unit cannot resolve it. Umuseke is a Rwandan outlet relaying a Bukavu radio (originating_source Radio Maendeleo); original not fetched.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that the AFC-M23 alliance announced that 24 children and students, 19 girls and five boys, died in a fire that struck houses in the Tshimpunda area of Kadutu commune, Bukavu, and that spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a communiqué of Thursday 10 September 2026 that the fire happened in the first hours after noon.
claims.actor_as_written: fire; cause under investigation per AFC-M23
claims.verification_note: Passages on the page (Bwiza, byline Bénjamin BABOU, 10 Sept 2026, 19:26). Party statement by the de facto administration. Same event as REC-1074 and claim 29; conflicting details recorded separately.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement (AFC/M23 administers Bukavu; the communiqué is relayed by a Rwanda-based outlet). Toll, location (Tshimpunda/Kadutu), school names (Mosala, Nongo) and time (after noon) differ from the Umuseke/Radio Maendeleo account (27 dead, Buholo-Kasha, Bagira, Mogo and Furaha schools, from about 8:00) and from REC-1074; kept as separate claims, none resolved. Health-care note: the communiqué names the hospitals receiving the 29 injured.

claims.text: Umuseke (byline Ndekezi Johnson) reported that AFC/M23 fighters took Idjwi island, in Lake Kivu, South Kivu, and that since the evening of 12 March 2025 the island had been controlled by M23; it quoted one journalist on the island as saying government soldiers fled before M23 fighters set foot there.
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page (Umuseke, byline NDEKEZI JOHNSON, 13 March 2025). Single Rwanda-based outlet; the flight of soldiers rests on one unnamed journalist.
claims.researcher_note: New control change not in known_records (REC-0779 is the RDF base on Idjwi, REC-0819 Mugote market 12 May 2025). Rwanda-based outlet; the claim that soldiers fled rests on one unnamed journalist. Date is the evening of 12 March 2025 as printed.

claims.text: BBC News Swahili reported that, according to the United Nations, at least 42,000 people were living in temporary camps on Idjwi island, while locals estimated there might be as many as 60,000 displaced people living on the island.
claims.verification_note: Passage on the page (BBC News Swahili, byline Marina Daras and Catherine Heathwood, published 5 March 2025). 'wakimbizi' here are displaced Congolese (the page speaks of 'Wakongo waliokimbia makazi yao').
claims.researcher_note: Figures per source, not merged: UN (via BBC) at least 42,000 in temporary camps; locals up to 60,000 displaced. Page is dated 5 March 2025, before the reported M23 takeover of the island (12 March 2025).

claims.text: BBC News Swahili reported that Idjwi island had only one main hospital and few vehicles, that it was often impossible for people in remote areas to get treatment, and quoted local radio director Yves Minani as saying that sometimes they must walk 10 km with a patient on a stretcher and that patients sometimes die on the way.
claims.actor_as_written: not applicable (structural access barrier, no actor)
claims.verification_note: Passages on the page (BBC News Swahili, 5 March 2025). The excerpt prints only 'Yves'; the full name and role are printed elsewhere on the page (quoted in clause_support). Structural access barrier, no armed actor. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Geographic and resource barrier to care described by a local radio director, not an attack or denial by an armed actor; included because the brief asks for civilian access to health care. 'Yves Minani' is described elsewhere on the page as an entrepreneur and director of a local radio station. Pre-dates the M23 takeover of the island.

claims.text: Ijambo (Chief editor Yves Iyaremye) reported that M23 said the FARDC used a Sukhoï 25 warplane to bomb inhabited areas of Kalehe territory, killing 10 people and wounding 25, and that M23 political spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a communiqué, put the attack on Thursday 13 February 2025.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC Sukhoï 25 aircraft, as alleged by M23
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page (Ijambo, author Yves Iyaremye, Chief Editor, published 2025-02-14 08:04 CAT). The page says FARDC had not yet given its side. Party allegation only.
claims.researcher_note: Party allegation (M23) relayed by a Rwanda-based outlet; the page itself says FARDC had not yet given its side. No other source for the Kalehe bombing toll found in the edition (claim_search 'Sukhoi' and 'Kalehe' show no 13 Feb 2025 record). Related to REC-0786 (fall of Kalehe, 12 Feb 2025), REC-0775 (bombing of mpox treatment centres at Kalehe/Minova/Miti-Murhesa, reported 24 Feb 2025). Published 2025-02-14 08:04 CAT per the page.

claims.text: Ijambo reported that M23 said the bombing destroyed Kalehe General Hospital, which usually received many patients in the area, and many houses of residents.
claims.place_as_written: Kalehe General Hospital (Ibitaro Bikuru bya Kalehe), Kalehe
claims.verification_note: Passage on the page (Ijambo, 14 Feb 2025). M23 allegation only; extent unverified.
claims.researcher_note: M23 allegation only; extent of damage ('destroyed') is M23's wording and is unverified; no independent source found in this unit. Day of the attack comes from the paired claim (Thursday 13 February 2025 per the communiqué); the page itself places this sentence right after the toll.

claims.text: Ijambo reported that M23 said it took Kalehe-Centre to stop the violence reported in Bukavu city, where it accused FARDC and its helpers, including FDLR, Burundian soldiers and Wazalendo, of killing residents, looting their property and committing serious violence against women.
claims.place_as_written: Kalehe-Centre (taken Wednesday 12 February 2025, per the page); Bukavu (alleged violence)
claims.actor_as_written: M23 accusing FARDC, FDLR, Burundian soldiers and Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: Passage on the page (Ijambo, 14 Feb 2025); the page dates the capture of Kalehe-Centre to Wednesday 12 February 2025. Party justification only.
claims.researcher_note: M23's stated justification and accusation (party statement, relayed). The page says the capture of Kalehe-Centre took place on Wednesday 12 February 2025 ('ku wa Gatatu, tariki 12 Gashyantare 2025'). The allegation of sexual violence in Bukavu before the city's fall is not substantiated in this source. FARDC response: the page says FARDC had not yet publicly stated its side.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported on the capture of Kalehe centre by M23, quoting an unnamed Kalehe civil-society leader who said that since the evening of Wednesday M23 fighters were in Kalehe centre, the main town of Kalehe territory.
claims.verification_note: Passage on the page (BBC News Gahuza, published 13 Feb 2025, a Thursday); 'ku wa gatatu' = Wednesday 12 Feb 2025.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0786 (fall of Kalehe, 12 Feb 2025) with an independent origin (BBC's own call to a civil-society leader). Date computed from weekday ('wednesday') and publication date 13 Feb 2025 (a Thursday).

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that on Wednesday the provincial army command said that M23 attacked army positions at Kalehe Centre and Ihusi, quoting it as saying 'these attacks caused the loss of many civilian lives', and that the army says Rwandan troops fight alongside M23, which both sides deny; M23 had said nothing yet on the army's statement.
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page (BBC News Gahuza, 13 Feb 2025). FARDC account relayed by BBC; no figure.
claims.researcher_note: FARDC account relayed by BBC (the original FARDC statement not seen). The BBC sentence is garbled in the original; the translation follows its wording. 'Many civilian lives' lost is a FARDC assertion, with no figure. Pairs with the M23 account (Ijambo, 14 Feb) of a Sukhoi bombing on 13 Feb: the two accounts blame each other.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 fighters denied information spreading on social media from Burundians that they had been dispossessed of Kavumu airport in South Kivu, and that AFC/M23-Twirwaneho said the circulating information was false and urged people to beware of rumours, saying 'Wazalendo and FARDC have no strength'.
claims.place_as_written: Kavumu airport, Kabare (about 25 km from Bukavu, per the page)
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (and Twirwaneho as named on the page)
claims.verification_note: Narrowed: the excerpt says the claims were spread 'by Burundians' ('n'Abarundi'); 'mostly' belongs to a different rumour on the page (about Nangaa) and is removed. Umuryango.rw, byline Brenda MIZERO, 27 Oct 2025. Party statement; same event as REC-0853.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0853 (AFC/M23 denies losing control of Kavumu airport, 27 Oct 2025) with the party's wording; the control assertion itself is from UMUSEKE 'reliable information' per this page, i.e. the same origin as the existing record, so not independent. Party statement only; the claim of an FARDC/Wazalendo/FDLR takeover is, per this page, a social-media rumour by pro-government Burundians, which this unit did not trace.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that on the morning of Sunday 22 February [2026] security kept deteriorating in Kavumu, Kabare territory, after fighting the previous Saturday, and that a local resident said the fighting began after a Wazalendo fighter was taken to a health centre and could be heard from Katana to Kavumu.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 and Wazalendo working with FARDC
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page (Bwiza, dated Sunday 22 February 2026, 08:28). Bwiza credits ACTUALITE.CD for its account ('inkuru dukesha ACTUALITE.CD'). Single anonymous testimony for the trigger.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-1033 (clashes at Kavumu and along the Katana-Kavumu axis, 21 Feb 2026) from a Rwanda-based outlet. The year is not printed in the excerpt; the page header gives Sunday 22 February 2026. The resident's claim that the fighting began after a Wazalendo fighter was taken to a health centre is a single anonymous testimony; whether the health centre was attacked is not stated.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that on Wednesday 30 July heavy fighting took place in Kamakombe village, Kabare territory, between M23 and a Wazalendo group, that it reportedly began on Tuesday at Mbayo village in Bugorhe groupement after M23 was reportedly reinforced at Kavumu airport, and that civil-society representatives said AFC/M23 rebels set out to drive the group out of Kamakombe on Wednesday morning.
claims.place_as_written: Kamakombe and Mbayo villages, Bugorhe groupement, Kabare
claims.actor_as_written: M23; Wazalendo group (MDLC / RRADRDC as the page names it)
claims.verification_note: Supported (Bwiza, dated Wednesday 30 July 2025). Hedge restored: the page puts the reinforcement under 'ngo' (reportedly) as well as the start under 'bivugwa ko'.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0837 (29-30 July 2025, Mbayo and Kamakombe, Bugorhe) and REC-0838 (2 Aug). Year not printed in the text; the search index dates the page 30 July 2025 and the details match REC-0837. Names the Wazalendo group as Mouvement décisif de la libération du Congo (MDLC / RRADRDC) in another sentence of the page.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that, according to residents, armed men suspected to include government soldiers and Wazalendo caused fear over the weekend in Bukavu and its outskirts and in Kavumu and Katana in Kabare territory, where they were accused of looting and killing civilians, and that Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi confirmed that about seven civilians were killed at Kavumu.
claims.place_as_written: Bukavu; Kavumu and Katana, Kabare territory
claims.actor_as_written: armed men suspected to include government soldiers and Wazalendo, per residents; the governor said it could not be confirmed that they were soldiers
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, byline Joseph Iradukunda, Monday 10 Feb 2025; retained copy). Downgraded to C: the only source is a Rwanda-based outlet whose text appears to relay BBC ('yabwiye BBC') without credit; origin unconfirmed.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates and dates REC-0765 (looting, killings and sexual violence attributed to retreating FARDC soldiers between Kalehe and Kavumu, 6-8 Feb 2025) with a governor's confirmation of about seven civilian deaths at Kavumu; dates computed from 'weekend' and the page date Monday 10 Feb 2025. No sexual violence is mentioned in these passages. The page repeats RFI for one quote and reads like a relay of a larger report; byline credit of the wire is not printed.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi of South Kivu, speaking about the violence at Kavumu and nearby, said that it was not possible to confirm that those responsible were government soldiers and that they could be bandits who take advantage of the situation to buy weapons and frighten the population; he said it happened as troops at the front were being replaced by new teams.
claims.actor_as_written: South Kivu provincial governor (Jean-Jacques Purusi) on the perpetrators
claims.verification_note: Passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, 10 Feb 2025). State authority's account. Downgraded to C for the same reason as claim 45. 2026-10-29: source 2 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 46)
claims.researcher_note: State authority's account: attributes the killings to armed men whose affiliation is not confirmed, possibly bandits; contrasts with residents and civil society who blame government forces and Wazalendo (see companion claims). The governor also says a security meeting decided those responsible must be sought and punished. Date computed from 'weekend' and the page date.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that civil-society members issued a statement saying more than nine people were killed in these acts, that people were looted and others wounded, and that they blamed government forces and Wazalendo; it quoted Maitre Pascal Mupenda, a Kabare official, via RFI, as saying nine dead were being counted and that the soldiers should leave.
claims.actor_as_written: government forces and Wazalendo, as blamed by civil society
claims.verification_note: Passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, 10 Feb 2025). Figures per source (governor about seven; civil society more than nine; Mupenda nine). Downgraded to C (partisan relay, origin unconfirmed). 2026-10-29: source 1 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Figures per source, not merged: governor about seven civilians killed at Kavumu; civil society more than nine; Kabare official nine. The second excerpt names Pascal Mupenda with the title as printed ('Maitre'); his words are a quote relayed from RFI.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that on Saturday armed men fired into the air in Bukavu city before entering shops and small markets and looting, as Bukavu residents showed on social media.
claims.verification_note: Passage on the page (Umuryango.rw, Monday 10 Feb 2025), so Saturday is 8 Feb 2025.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from 'Saturday' and the page date (Monday 10 Feb 2025). Source is residents' social-media posts as described by the outlet; no number of shops or victims.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that Kinshasa government spokesman Patrick Muyaya told Top Congo FM on Sunday that M23, which he called the Rwandan army, had approached and taken Nyabibwe and that all further attacks launched from Nyabibwe had been thwarted, and that rumours reaching Bukavu of M23 being 10 or 15 km away were false as they were in fact more than 100 km away.
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, 10 Feb 2025). Government statement relayed from Top Congo FM. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 49)
claims.researcher_note: Government statement (Patrick Muyaya, via Top Congo FM as relayed by Umuryango.rw; originating_source Top Congo FM). Concerns REC-0784 (capture of Nyabibwe, 5-6 Feb 2025) and the later advance to Bukavu (16 Feb), which proved the rumours' distance claim wrong within a week. Date computed from 'Sunday' and the page date; the weekend interview date is not otherwise given.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on 28 August 2025 that since the night of Wednesday 27 August 2025 an alliance of Kinshasa's forces, which he listed as FARDC, FDLR, Mai Mai Wazalendo, mercenaries, Imbonerakure and the Burundian army, had been shelling densely populated areas of Minembwe (Mikenke) and Kalehe (Katana, Kavumu, Katasomwa, Nyabibwe) with CH-4 drones and heavy weapons.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC, FDLR, Mai Mai Wazalendo, mercenaries, Imbonerakure and Burundian army, as alleged by AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, byline ISIMBI Estella, 28 Aug 2025; retained copy). Party account; Katana and Kavumu are listed under Kalehe in the quote as printed.
claims.researcher_note: Party account only; allegation of Imbonerakure and Burundian army participation in the Kalehe/Kabare area is AFC/M23's. The page lists Katana and Kavumu under Kalehe in the quote although they are in Kabare territory; reproduced as printed. No casualty figure given here. Compare REC-0846 (25 Aug 2025 clashes in the Kalehe highlands) and REC-0781/0782 (Lomera suspensions).

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that Wazalendo fighters attacked AFC/M23 positions at Katana, Mumosho and Chirunga in Kabare territory on the morning of 18 June, with residents explaining that Wazalendo tried to dislodge AFC/M23 from these areas.
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, 19 June 2025).
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0828 (17-18 June 2025: Cirunga, Mumosho, Katana) and adds the 'attempt to dislodge' framing from residents; same-day Kalehe residents reportedly heard gunfire (not cited). Year taken from the page date (19 June 2025).

claims.text: Bwiza (English edition, byline Fred Karege) reported that on 20 May 2025 the DRC National Commission for Monitoring the Implementation of the Addis Ababa Agreement released a report detailing serious crimes against civilians in Goma and Bukavu between January and April 2025 during the occupation by AFC-M23, presented at the National Museum in Kinshasa by the commission's coordinator Alphonse Ntumba Lwaba.
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the page (Bwiza English edition, byline Fred Karege, 21 May 2025). source_type corrected: the outlet is Rwanda-based media reporting a DRC state commission, not a DRC-government publication; the report itself was not seen.
claims.researcher_note: Government-side statement (a Congolese state commission's report) known only through this Rwandan outlet's summary; the report itself (over 100 pages per Bwiza) was not located in this unit, so its allegations are not recorded here. The legal labels the page mentions ('war crimes', 'crimes against humanity') are the commission's/ministers' wording as relayed and are not adopted. No existing record covers this report (claim_search: no match). Suggest a follow-up to find the report text (Congolese government sites).

claims.text: UN News Kiswahili reported that, in Uvira city, local civil society organisations were reporting that about 12 civilians had been killed by armed groups since 18 January, and quoted UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric saying about 2,400 people had fled Uvira towards Kamanyola.
claims.actor_as_written: armed groups (makundi yaliyojihami), as the source words it
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page. The 12-killed figure is the page's report of local civil society, not a UN finding; the 2,400 figure is Dujarric's quote. Statement keeps that split.
claims.researcher_note: Kiswahili UN News relay of the UN spokesperson noon briefing; the 12-killed figure is attributed by the page to local civil society, not verified by the UN. Date is the page date (23 Jan 2026). Note destination of the 2,400 is Kamanyola, not Burundi.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that, according to Radio Okapi, calm returned to Uvira on Monday after clashes on Sunday between FARDC and Wazalendo in which 12 people, civilians and soldiers, died; Serge Kigwati, who heads civil society there, confirmed that the clashes arose because Wazalendo tried to disarm FARDC soldiers who had fled Bukavu and the FARDC refused.
claims.verification_note: Supported. Page dated 18 Feb 2025 (Tuesday); 'ku cyumweru' = Sunday 16 Feb. Toll relays Radio Okapi (already in the store per research notes), so not independent of it. The 12-dead toll is Radio Okapi's, relayed by BBC Gahuza; not an independent count.
claims.researcher_note: The 12-dead figure is relayed from Radio Okapi (already in r1-UV-2025Q1-001), so not independent; the added value is the Kinyarwanda account and the civil-society explanation of the cause. Date computed from weekday: the page is dated 18 February 2025 and says the clashes were 'on Sunday', i.e. 16 February 2025. An anonymous resident quoted by BBC said Wazalendo asked for equipment and FARDC refused it, which led to the clash.

claims.text: Deutsche Welle Kiswahili reported that, as Wazalendo and some FARDC soldiers returned to Uvira on Sunday, several incidents of looting occurred in warehouses near Kalundu port, in several government offices and in some people's homes, especially those of members of the Banyamulenge community.
claims.place_as_written: Warehouses near Kalundu port, government offices and homes, Uvira city
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (written in the context of the Wazalendo return)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on page; the Sunday return is in the article's lede (page-only for that clause). Looters not named by DW. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: The article, dated 19 January 2026, says 'Sunday' (18 January 2026); date computed from the page's own statement that Wazalendo and FARDC returned on Sunday, one day after the AFC/M23 withdrawal. The source does not name who looted.

claims.text: Deutsche Welle Kiswahili reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, in a press release, warned that some AFC/M23 fighters were allegedly hiding in Uvira to cause chaos and blame the Wazalendo and the Congolese army, and confirmed that AFC/M23 had withdrawn to the Sange area although they were supposed to withdraw to Kamanyola.
claims.verification_note: Supported; statement keeps 'allegedly' (wanaodaiwa). Date is the DW article date, not the release date.
claims.researcher_note: Statement as relayed by DW Kiswahili (author Mitima DeLachance); the press release itself was not seen.

claims.text: Deutsche Welle Kiswahili reported that Corneille Nangaa, AFC/M23 coordinator, said on X that AFC/M23 withdrew from Uvira in good faith and that he was appalled by acts of reprisal, looting of public property, targeted killings and the forced displacement of the Tutsi Banyamulenge community.
claims.verification_note: Party statement correctly attributed. Post date not given.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement (partisan) relayed by DW; the X post was not opened. The date is the DW article date; the post date is not given.

claims.text: Umuseke (a Rwandan online outlet) reported that the FARDC and the Wazalendo, usual partners in fighting the M23, shot at each other openly on Thursday 1 May, with fighting starting at about saa kumi n'imwe in the morning at Kasenga and spreading quickly to surrounding areas, and that residents of Kakombe said gunfire continued on Friday and that they had no choice but to flee.
claims.verification_note: Narrowed to the excerpts: the 'brewing for almost a week' and the mid-morning pause / afternoon resumption clauses sit only elsewhere on the page. excerpt_en mistranslated the start time as 'the eleventh hour of the morning'; saa kumi n'imwe z'igitondo is about 05:00. Parties named in the page title. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-UV claim 6)
claims.researcher_note: Umuseke is a privately owned Rwandan outlet; Rwandan media are treated as partisan on contested facts. The page is dated 2 May 2025; Thursday 1 May is stated by the page. Complements REC-0077 (Kasenga and Kakombe clashes) with the time sequence and the Kakombe residents' account. The same page claims Burundian soldiers deployed to protect Uvira declined to get involved (see separate claim).

claims.text: Umuseke reported that Burundian soldiers deployed to protect the town of Uvira refused to get involved in the FARDC-Wazalendo fighting, and that the Wazalendo said some FARDC soldiers had prepared a boat to take them to Kalemie if M23 fighters attacked Uvira.
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian soldiers (as the outlet words it: 'Abasirikare b’Abarundi'); Wazalendo; FARDC
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on page; claim attributed to the outlet. Refers to the 1-2 May 2025 fighting. The Burundian soldiers' refusal is Umuseke's own unsourced narration, from a Rwandan outlet hostile to Burundi's role; its comment on their motives is not carried.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan-leaning Rwandan outlet; the characterisation of Burundian soldiers' motives and 'the war they were pushed into for President Ndayishimiye's interests' is the outlet's own wording and is not independently verified. Month precision only because the claims are undated within the article (published 2 May 2025).

claims.text: Kigali Today (Rwanda) reported that residents of Uvira said that since AFC/M23 left, groups of young criminals backed by the Wazalendo broke into and looted the homes and churches of Banyamulenge and other Kinyarwanda speakers, and that the Impuzamashyirahamwe Iharanira Uburenganzira bwa Muntu (DPC) issued a letter on 18 January 2026 raising concern for the safety of Uvira residents, especially Banyamulenge.
claims.actor_as_written: young criminals supported by Wazalendo, according to residents quoted by the outlet
claims.verification_note: Supported and attributed (residents; DPC). Kigali Today is partisan on this; grade C.
claims.researcher_note: Kigali Today is a Rwandan outlet aligned with the Rwandan state and is partisan on Uvira (Kigali's stated line backs the Banyamulenge and AFC/M23); cite for what residents and the DPC said, not for the facts. Date 18 January 2026 is the DPC letter date; the looting dates per other sources 18-20 January. The page says AFC/M23 left Uvira 'on Saturday 17 January 2026'.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that Colonel Fureko, a Banyamulenge and a recently integrated Wazalendo officer, was arrested on Saturday 8 November at Lemera, Uvira territory, while travelling to Mulenge, that former colleagues accused him of links to M23 and Twirwaneho, and that according to several sources Fureko and eight young Banyamulenge with him were beaten, wounded and stripped of their weapons and uniforms.
claims.place_as_written: Lemera, Uvira territory, South Kivu (travelling towards Mulenge)
claims.actor_as_written: not stated by the source; his former colleagues ('Wenzake wa zamani') accuse him of M23 and Twirwaneho links
claims.verification_note: Statement supported unchanged. Actor corrected: the draft said 'former colleagues in the Wazalendo' arrested him; the page names no arresting party, only that former colleagues accuse him. Name printed as 'Fureko'. The page does not say who arrested him. It adds that he and his companions were held in a cell at Luvungi pending investigation, and that some Banyamulenge accuse him of leading Mai-Mai attacks at Kahololo.
claims.researcher_note: Single Swahili-edition article by SOS Médias Burundi (dateline Bukavu, 10 Nov 2025); no existing claim mentions Fureko. The page itself says relatives and residents of Lemera and Kitoga denounce unjustified abuse, and that some Banyamulenge accuse him of leading Mai-Mai attacks at Kahololo (not cited here). 'Fureko' printed as a single name with rank Kanali (colonel).

claims.text: Mwananchi reported, without naming a source for this passage, that Wazalendo fighters had had to stand firm to defend the town of Uvira against M23 fighters after FARDC soldiers were alleged to have fled the fighting, with others taking canoes to escape to Kalemie.
claims.verification_note: Origin corrected: the page cites Reuters only for FARDC desertions near Lubero; the Uvira sentence is the outlet's own and unattributed, so 'partly based on Reuters' and the Reuters origin are removed. 'mitumbwi' = canoes.
claims.researcher_note: Mwananchi is a Tanzanian daily; the sentence cited is the outlet's own summary after paraphrasing Reuters on FARDC desertions (its Reuters attribution concerns Lubero and desertions in general; the Uvira sentence itself has no named source). Treat as weak corroboration of REC-0049.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi edition) reported that on the third day nobody could move around the town because of looting by armed people, including of the stores of charitable organisations, and quoted a statement posted on X by MSF saying that, unable to move around the town, medical teams and other aid workers were in danger, and that hospitals in the area kept receiving wounded people every day, including ordinary civilians.
claims.actor_as_written: armed people (abantu bafise ibirwanisho), not otherwise identified in the cited passages
claims.verification_note: 'irageramiwe' means 'are endangered/at risk', not 'are blocked'; translation and statement corrected. The 'third day' is not dated by the page (published 20 Feb 2025). MSF statement already in the store per research notes, so not independent. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-UV claim 11)
claims.researcher_note: The BBC Gahuza page is dated 20 Feb 2025 (updated 21 Feb); 'the third day' is counted from the start of unrest per the article's context and is not given as a date, so the date field is the publication date. Both MSF and the looting passages are relays of reporting already in the edition (MSF statements of Feb 2025 are in r1-UV-2025Q1-011 and others). The sentence on stolen NGO stores is the outlet's own text with no named source.

claims.text: Bwiza (a Rwandan outlet) reported that on Wednesday 31 December 2025 the DRC government, through its Communications Minister and spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, accused the Rwandan forces in a statement of attacks in the Kamanyola-Uvira areas 'with bombs and kamikaze drones' that, it said, killed more than 1,500 people and displaced about 500,000.
claims.actor_as_written: Rwandan forces (Ingabo z'u Rwanda), as accused by the DRC government
claims.verification_note: Supported; the hedge 'ngo' is kept as 'it said'. Relayed by a Rwandan outlet, which adds that Muyaya showed no proof and cited civil society, humanitarian organisations and some state bodies. The communiqué itself was not seen.
claims.researcher_note: Statement relayed by a Rwandan outlet (Bwiza), partisan on this issue; the communiqué itself was not opened. Bwiza adds that Muyaya showed no proof and said his information came from civil society, humanitarian organisations and some state bodies (outlet's own comment and a summary of Muyaya's sourcing). Related existing claims: r1-UV-2026Q1-014 (Muyaya, 1,500 dead, 19-20 Jan 2026) - check whether the 1,500 figure there is the same.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that Patrick Muyaya also accused the Rwandan forces of sending three battalions of soldiers into the highlands of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga, saying they were disguised as Twirwaneho fighters.
claims.place_as_written: Highlands of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Rwandan forces, as accused by the DRC government
claims.verification_note: Supported; 'Uyu mugabo' refers to Muyaya in the preceding paragraph. The page adds Muyaya said the aim was to extend the war into Fizi and then Kalemie (not carried).
claims.researcher_note: Partisan Rwandan outlet relaying the DRC statement of 31 December 2025; the sentence 'Uyu mugabo' refers to Minister Muyaya per the preceding sentence of the article.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23, through its spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, replied that what the Kinshasa government said was propaganda and lies intended to mislead the public.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira territory and Kamanyola axis, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: The 'rejected the territory allegations in Muyaya's statement' clause is only in the following quote on the page, not in the excerpt, so it is narrowed out (lesson 1). Same event as claim 12: it is the reply to the 31 Dec statement. The page also quotes AFC/M23 rejecting 'the allegations of seizing territory made by Mr Patrick Muyaya in his statement of 31 December 2025'.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement as relayed by a Rwandan outlet; date is the Bwiza publication date (2 January 2026), the reply's own date is not stated.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 said the killings of civilians in South Kivu during the previous month's fighting came from air attacks and shells fired by Kinshasa's forces including FARDC, FDLR, Mai-Mai Wazalendo, foreign mercenaries and Burundi's national army, in areas including Kamanyola, Luvungi and Sange, with 8 killed and 55 wounded in Kamanyola alone.
claims.place_as_written: Kamanyola, Luvungi, Sange and surroundings, Ruzizi plain
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC, FDLR, Mai-Mai Wazalendo, foreign mercenaries, Burundi national army (as alleged by AFC/M23)
claims.verification_note: Supported party account. The '23' flag is 'AFC/M23', which the title prints. The 8 killed / 55 wounded figures for Kamanyola match those of the Kamanyola head and a Saint-Joseph Hospital doctor relayed by Umuryango (claims 21-22); both reach the edition through Rwandan outlets and may share an origin.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan account (AFC/M23) as relayed by a Rwandan outlet; 'last month' is relative to the 2 January 2026 article, i.e. December 2025. Compare with REC-0209 (5 civilians wounded around Katogota and Kamanyola) and REC-0211 (rockets from Kamanyola, cross-border shelling).

claims.text: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 said that, in areas that government forces had tried to retake including Uvira and Makobola, those forces carried out 'acts of rape and organised looting'.
claims.actor_as_written: government forces (Ingabo za Leta), as alleged by AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports the attributed allegation; 'ngo' (reportedly) is carried by 'AFC/M23 said'. Unverified allegation by a party to the conflict; no date, place detail or count. HRW (claim 41) attributes rapes in Uvira to M23 and Rwandan soldiers.
claims.researcher_note: Allegation by a party to the conflict (AFC/M23) as relayed by a Rwandan outlet; it is not independently verified and conflicts with the attribution of rapes at Uvira to M23/RDF in REC-0122/REC-0024. The article does not give dates or a count. The time frame (December 2025 to early January 2026) is inferred from the article's reply to the 31 December 2025 statement; mark as approximate.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 accused government forces of having fired heavy and light weapons on residents who were holding a peaceful demonstration on 22 December.
claims.place_as_written: not stated in the cited passage
claims.actor_as_written: government forces (ingabo za Leta), as alleged by AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Supported party allegation; the page does not say where the 22 December demonstration was.
claims.researcher_note: Party allegation relayed by a Rwandan outlet; the place of the demonstration is not given in the passage. Not verified.

claims.text: Umuseke (a Rwandan outlet), in a correction, reported that fighters of the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN), led by Joseph Kabila, had taken the Kadezi area, which it said is distinct from Kawezi as had continued to be reported, and that the Kadezi hills lie 70 kilometres from the town of Uvira; it said news of the capture had circulated on social media from the morning of Monday 26 October 2026.
claims.place_as_written: Kadezi hills (between the Kaziba and Lubarika hills), about 70 km from Uvira city
claims.actor_as_written: FRN (Front pour la Refondation de la Nation), described as led by Joseph Kabila and formerly AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Relation changed from contradicts to new_related_event: the correction says the place taken was Kadezi, 70 km away, not Kawezi; it does not contradict the Kawizi denials (it agrees Kawezi was not the place taken), so it is not the same event as the Kawizi rumour records. Figures field had 8-10 km numbers from other outlets that no excerpt prints; removed. 'about 70 km' -> '70 kilometres' as printed. Rests on social-media videos and unnamed sites; not confirmed by FARDC in the page. The article's original URL ('...zigeze-mu-bilometero-10-ugana-uvira', 'reached 10 km from Uvira') now carries this corrected text.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan outlet, treat as partisan; the claim rests on social-media videos and unnamed sites and was not confirmed by the DRC army in the page. Conflict with the edition: records REC-0679 and claims r1-UV-2026Q4-017/-019/-023 (Radio Okapi, Taarifa, Radio Maendeleo) concern Kawizi (Kahwizi), about 8-10 km from Uvira, where rumours of capture were denied by FARDC/civil society; Umuseke says the capture was of Kadezi hills 70 km away, not Kawizi. The earlier URL of the same article ('ingabo-za-kabila-zigeze-mu-bilometero-10-ugana-uvira', 'Kabila's forces reached 10 km from Uvira') redirects to this corrected text, so the earlier '10 km' claim appears to have been withdrawn by the outlet.

claims.text: Rwanda Tribune reported that fighting began in the early hours of Saturday 10 October 2026 and that, according to residents, at around 'saa yine' in the morning fighters said to belong to the AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and Red-Tabara alliance attacked positions of the Wazalendo groups Binjigi and Masango, which repelled the attack, with fighting continuing towards Magunda; it said that as of writing no official statement had explained how the fighting ended or whether there were dead or wounded.
claims.place_as_written: Bijombo and Masango hills, Magunda direction, Uvira territory
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and Red-Tabara (alleged attackers); Wazalendo groups Binjigi and Masango
claims.verification_note: The 'not verified by independent bodies' clause was not in any excerpt (page only); replaced by the no-official-statement clause that source 2 carries, and moved to the note. The draft blended the 'saa yine' time with the date from a separate sentence; now split. The page says the information on the attackers and the course of the fighting had not been verified by independent bodies.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan outlet (Rwanda Tribune), partisan-leaning; relays unnamed residents and social media. Page dated 11 October 2026 (last updated 12:52). 'saa yine' is Kinyarwanda clock reckoning (about 10:00); left unconverted. The same page names Wazalendo of 'MRDP-Twirwaneho led by General Masheke Radi' trying to push back the attackers, which is unclear and was not used.

claims.text: Umuryango (a Rwandan outlet) reported that the head of Kamanyola, Hassan Shabani, said that from 2 to 4 December about 150 shells fired from Burundi hit Kamanyola, killing eight residents; that a doctor at Saint-Joseph Hospital in Kamanyola said that while Burundian forces were firing on the town they received 55 wounded, including 27 seriously wounded who were sent to Bukavu general hospital; and that a resident whose wife and two children were killed told CTGL that a shell fell on their house and four people died.
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian forces (Ingabo z’u Burundi), as alleged by the Kamanyola authority and a resident
claims.verification_note: Figures field used digits ('8') no excerpt prints; rewritten in the excerpts' terms. 'zirimo 27 ... zoherezwa' reads most naturally as the 27 seriously wounded being sent to Bukavu, not all 55; statement narrowed accordingly. excerpt_en for source 2 was a summary, not a translation; corrected. Kamanyola was under AFC/M23 control (per the page), so the 'head of Kamanyola' is presumably an AFC/M23-installed authority; the page does not say so. The resident's testimony is relayed from CTGL, not gathered by Umuryango. The same eight killed and 55 wounded appear in AFC/M23's own statement (claim 15). 2026-10-29: source 2 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-UV claim 21)
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan outlet (Umuryango); testimony relayed from CTGL. Page states that Kamanyola, in Walungu territory, is controlled by AFC/M23, so the 'head of Kamanyola' appears to be a de facto (AFC/M23-installed) authority, but the page does not say so. Existing record REC-0211 reports rockets from Kamanyola and cross-border shelling; the Burundian army's own account is separate (REC-0217 etc.). Burundian official position on this shelling: not seen in this source. Resident quoted unnamed, with the line 'Abantu bane barapfuye. Abanjye ni umugore wanjye, abana babiri n’umuturanyi wari hano' (four people dead) which differs from the head's count of eight in total.

claims.text: Umuryango reported that Kamanyola head Hassan Shabani said that in the shelling of 2-4 December schools, civilians' houses and the hospital were hit, with eight people dead.
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian forces (Ingabo z’u Burundi), as alleged by Hassan Shabani
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; figures field rewritten without the unprinted digit. 'ibitaro' may be singular or plural; no hospital is named.
claims.researcher_note: The word 'ibitaro' in the quotation is plural/generic ('hospital(s)'); the page does not name which hospital. Single-source allegation by a local authority relayed by a Rwandan outlet. The doctor at Saint-Joseph Hospital in Kamanyola gives patient figures in the preceding claim but does not say that hospital was hit.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that a 12-year-old boy died of gunfire and at least nine other people were wounded during a protest in Uvira on Monday, and that the FARDC spokesperson in the area, Lt. Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, said the child was killed when the army tried to stop protesters entering the main military office in the town.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city (main military headquarters), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not stated; the FARDC spokesperson said the child was killed when the army tried to stop protesters entering the main military office
claims.verification_note: Statement supported. Figures field credited the toll to the FARDC spokesperson, but it is BBC's own narration; the spokesperson does not say soldiers shot the child, so the actor field is narrowed. Digits replaced by the printed words. The page text is Kinyarwanda, though tagged 'rn'. Toll differs by source: BBC Gahuza one boy killed and at least nine wounded; governor Purusi via AP three dead and five wounded (claim 24).
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('ku wa mbere', Monday) and the page date of 9 September 2025 (Monday 8 September). BBC states the account as the FARDC spokesperson's; the page also relays the governor's figure (separate claim). Existing: r1-UV-2025Q3-024 (Radio Okapi: 1 dead, 9 wounded) and r1-UV-2025Q3-023 (SOS Médias Burundi: at least 5 killed).

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Associated Press, repeating South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, said the dead in the Uvira protest were three people, with five wounded.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed (protest of Wazalendo-backed demonstrators against Brig Gen Gasita)
claims.verification_note: Same protest as claim 23 ('iyi myigaragambyo', Monday 8 Sep 2025): the contradiction is genuine (three dead vs one). Figures field carried other sources' tolls in digits no excerpt prints; narrowed to this source.
claims.researcher_note: Conflicting toll: governor/AP 3 dead 5 wounded versus FARDC spokesperson 1 dead 9+ wounded (Radio Okapi and BBC Gahuza) versus SOS Médias Burundi at least 5 dead; see REC-0097 (three wounded died on 4 September) for earlier deaths in the same demonstrations. Date computed from weekday and page date.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that Bertrand Bisimwa, president of M23 and deputy coordinator of the Alliance Fleuve Congo, said on X that the Kinshasa government's decision to cut internet in Uvira aimed to hide the bad acts its forces were committing there.
claims.verification_note: Supported party statement.
claims.researcher_note: Party statement as relayed by a Rwandan outlet; the X post was not opened; quoted phrase is the outlet's translation into Kinyarwanda of the post (the original language of the post is not stated). Date is the Bwiza article date.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that houses of Tutsi in Uvira were attacked by residents led by Wazalendo fighters who had returned to the town and looted everything, particularly in Tutsi homes, and that other reports said a church considered to be mostly Tutsi was looted that Sunday morning.
claims.actor_as_written: residents led by Wazalendo fighters, per Bwiza
claims.verification_note: Supported; partisan outlet, attributed.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan outlet (Bwiza), partisan; written the same day (18 January 2026, 15:22). Video on social media is mentioned but not described reliably; 'Abatutsi' is the outlet's term, other sources say Banyamulenge.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that it was said five civilians had died in Uvira after the Wazalendo and FARDC returned, though the outlet said it could not confirm this.
claims.verification_note: Supported; the outlet's own hedge ('tutabasha kubyemeza') is kept.
claims.researcher_note: Unconfirmed figure from a Rwandan outlet on the day of the return; compare UN News Kiswahili (about 12 civilians killed since 18 January per local civil society, 23 January) and REC-0010.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that the Banyamulenge organisation Amohoro Peace Association issued a statement saying Banyamulenge were in danger, that Uvira was heading into a humanitarian emergency, and that after AFC/M23's withdrawal under United States pressure Banyamulenge civilians were being hunted while Wazalendo groups were targeting, killing and looting the homes of people called 'Banyarwanda'.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo, as alleged by Amohoro Peace Association
claims.verification_note: Supported; community association statement relayed by a partisan outlet.
claims.researcher_note: Community-association statement (partisan on the conflict) as relayed by a Rwandan outlet; the association's own page was not opened.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the DRC government said it had ordered its troops not to confront the M23 as it advanced in Uvira, and explained that it wanted to avoid civilians losing their lives there.
claims.verification_note: Supported; BBC does not name the government speaker or channel.
claims.researcher_note: Statement as reported by BBC Gahuza (original BBC wording in English in the same story family: not checked). The page does not name the government source or give the date or channel of the statement. The same page says the larger part of Congolese forces left Uvira although residents say fighting continues.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a statement on X that for more than three months AFC/M23 had denounced hate speech, attacks on citizens because of their appearance, and killings 'in the liberated areas' of M23 carried out by fighters allied with the Kinshasa government and its accomplice Burundi, and that the town of Uvira was now 'liberated'.
claims.verification_note: Kirundi 'yiyamirije' (kwiyamiriza) means 'denounced/protested against', not 'endured'; translation and statement corrected. Regraded B to C: the content is a party's claim (the fact that Kanyuka posted it is well attested by BBC, but the claim records his allegations). Same X post as the BBC English claim in the store per research notes. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-UV claim 32)
claims.researcher_note: Party statement (partisan), relayed by BBC; the X post itself was not opened. Compare r1-UV-2025Q4-003 (BBC English) and r1-UV-2025Q4-021 (SOS Médias Burundi).

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Olivier Muhasha, one of the journalists in Uvira, told it that morning that the fighters had reportedly entered only two quarters, Kavimvira and Kagenge, while the others were in the hands of the government army and the Wazalendo, and that Uvira has 14 quarters.
claims.place_as_written: Kavimvira and Kagenge quarters, Uvira city
claims.verification_note: 'boba binjiye' is the Kirundi reportative conditional ('had reportedly entered'); the hedge was dropped in the draft and the translation. Figures field used digits '2' no excerpt prints. 'These fighters' = M23 per the preceding sentence. 'The fighters' are the M23 fighters named in the preceding sentence of the page, which BBC says had reportedly entered the town (unconfirmed). 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-UV claim 33) 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Qualifies the 10 December capture record (REC-0113/0218: 'AFC/M23 and Rwandan forces take control of Uvira'): on the morning of 10 December a journalist on the spot told BBC that the fighters held two quarters only. Same BBC page notes the information was not confirmed. The page text misspells 'Muhasha'; name copied as printed. The 'Kagenge' spelling is as printed (the edition elsewhere may use Kagenge/Kalimabenge variants).

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi told Radio Okapi on Tuesday that Uvira was controlled by government troops, denying rumours that M23 rebels had entered the town.
claims.verification_note: Supported; page dated 10 Dec 2025, 'ejo ku wa kabiri' = Tuesday 9 Dec. Relay of Radio Okapi.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('ejo ku wa kabiri' = yesterday, Tuesday) and the page date of 10 December 2025, i.e. Tuesday 9 December. Existing claim r1-UV-2025Q4-003 has the BBC English version of the 10 December governor statement.

claims.text: Umuryango (a Rwandan outlet) reported that AFC/M23 shot down a FARDC Sukhoi-25 combat aircraft that had been used to attack it; according to information from South Kivu, the aircraft was hit in the air over Kalundu port, Uvira territory, at about saa saba in the afternoon of 26 December 2025 and fell into Lake Tanganyika, and two people aboard were said to have died.
claims.verification_note: Supported and attributed to the outlet. Single Rwandan outlet; no FARDC or independent confirmation of the shoot-down.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan outlet, treat as partisan; no FARDC or Kinshasa statement on the aircraft was found in this source, and no independent confirmation seen (not searched further for lack of budget). The page also says it was the second Su-25 the DRC army lost, the first having been captured at Goma in late January 2025, and says Twirwaneho claimed to have shot down a helicopter carrying white mercenaries on 6 December (not cited). 'saa saba' is Kinyarwanda clock reckoning (about 13:00); left unconverted. Existing record REC-0128 covers the AFC/M23 covert presence in Uvira after the 15-16 Dec announcement.

claims.text: Umuryango reported that DRC forces attacked Kalundu port on Lake Tanganyika, where two AFC/M23 boats were said to have been hit and the fighters aboard died, and that DRC army combat drones hit AFC/M23 bases including one at Kala, Uvira territory, at the former MONUSCO base.
claims.place_as_written: Kalundu port and Kala, Uvira territory
claims.actor_as_written: DRC forces (Ingabo za RDC) and Wazalendo; AFC/M23 boats and bases
claims.verification_note: Supported; the page places the attacks on the day of publication (26 Dec 2025, 'kuva mu gitondo cy'uyu munsi').
claims.researcher_note: Single partisan Rwandan source; unverified casualty claim ('bivugwa', reportedly).

claims.text: Umuryango reported that AFC/M23 fighters left Makobola in the afternoon of 25 December 2025 and were then attacked, and that DRC forces and Wazalendo went to take control of Makobola, as residents there confirmed.
claims.verification_note: Supported. Makobola is in Fizi territory.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan Rwandan outlet; complements Radio Okapi/Actualite.cd claims of 13-23 Dec 2025 on Makobola (r2-G-SKS-FIZI-008 etc.). Igihe (Rwanda) also carried 'Fizi: AFC/M23 yavuye muri Makobola' on 26 December 2025 but its page could not be fetched. Makobola is in Fizi territory, shown here because the edition links it to the Uvira offensive (REC-0218).

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that fighting on Tuesday between Wazalendo and FARDC in Uvira left people dead and created tension according to the town's authorities, that DRC media said about eight people had died, that part of the fighting took place in the Kavimvira area near the Burundi border, and that Radio RFI said it began over a disagreement between Wazalendo and FARDC on the entry of people coming from Burundi.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city, including Kavimvira near the Burundi border
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; figures field rewritten without the unprinted digit. Page dated Wed 27 Aug 2025, so Tuesday = 26 Aug.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('Tuesday') and the page date of 27 August 2025 (Wednesday), i.e. Tuesday 26 August. Death toll is 'about eight' per unnamed DRC media as relayed by BBC; the edition's REC-0092 does not give a toll; the BBC page does not give a source for civilian versus military dead. Compare REC-0090 (25 August, Mulongwe, clash over vehicles) for a different stated cause.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that, in an official statement on the events, the provincial governor asked the Wazalendo and the government army to 'take measures to avoid falling into the enemy's trap', saying the enemy was spreading false information that he had surrounded the town of Uvira, and that Governor Jean Jacques Purusi, on the government side, convened an 'extraordinary meeting' with representatives of the army, religious leaders, youth and women, customary authorities and the leaders of the "Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie" or Wazalendo.
claims.verification_note: The draft's 'statement from the government of the part of South Kivu controlled by the government' is not what the excerpt says ('itangazo ry'ubutegetsi' = a statement by the authorities; the governor is 'of this province'); narrowed. Name spelled 'Jean Jacques Purusi' as this page prints it.
claims.researcher_note: Relayed by BBC Gahuza from the provincial government; the date is approximate (statement issued around 26-27 August 2025). Extends r1-UV-2025Q3-007 (SOS Médias Burundi on the spokesperson Luganywa relaying Purusi's condemnation).

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that Human Rights Watch said its researchers found evidence that 53 civilians (46 men, one woman and five boys) were summarily killed in attacks on residents' homes in different parts of Uvira after the Rwanda-backed fighters took the town in December, and that HRW visited three sites said to hold mass graves, one of them in a place permanently guarded by UN peacekeepers.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers, as alleged by HRW
claims.verification_note: Statement supported. Figures used digits '1' and '5' no excerpt prints; rewritten. Regraded B to A: origin is a documented HRW investigation (rubric A), though relayed by BBC and not independent of the HRW/BBC English claims in the store.
claims.researcher_note: Kirundi-language BBC version of the HRW report of 14 May 2026 (the BBC English story is already in the edition; this is not an independent origin). Note the page itself states that the BBC could not get a response from M23 or Rwanda. Page date 14 May 2026 ('Ukwa gatanu 2026'). The date range is the occupation period as given elsewhere in the edition (the page says M23 left in January).

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that Human Rights Watch said it investigated and documented eight cases of rape alleged against the M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers during their occupation of Uvira, and quoted a woman who said they stripped her, tied her hands behind her back with her clothes and raped her, and that her husband was shot dead when he tried to help her.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers, as alleged by HRW
claims.verification_note: Supported; 'abo barwanyi' = the M23 fighters named in the page title and lede. Regraded B to A on the HRW origin; not independent of the HRW claims in the store. No survivor named.
claims.researcher_note: The page carries a content warning on sexual violence; the survivor is not named and no name is searched for. Kirundi version of the HRW findings (same origin as the BBC English and HRW pages already in the edition). Compare AFC/M23's counter-allegation (Bwiza) that government forces committed rapes at Uvira/Makobola. The government's own report of 14,400 rapes (r1-UV-2026Q1-037) and the health actors' 1,100 cases (REC-0025) differ in order of magnitude and method.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwanda had continued to deny backing M23 or deploying its soldiers in eastern DRC, and that M23 and the Rwandan government did not respond to the BBC's request for comment on HRW's findings on Uvira.
claims.verification_note: Supported. Source 1's originating_source corrected from Human Rights Watch to BBC: the no-reply line concerns BBC's own request. The page also says HRW wrote to the Rwandan government and M23 leaders in April and got no reply.
claims.researcher_note: This records 'no statement found' from M23 and Rwanda in this source at publication. The Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo replied separately to HRW (Igihe, 'RDF si AFC/M23', page not fetchable by the helper); see gaps. The excerpt's 'ruhakana' sentence is BBC's own summary of Rwanda's long-standing position, not a dated statement.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that on Saturday night Burundi's foreign minister Edouard Bizimana wrote on X that it was important to stress Qatar's bad role in using its word and money to stop the United States from acting, and in the same post accused Rwanda of continuing to seize areas in eastern DR Congo contrary to the Washington agreement without the United States doing anything.
claims.place_as_written: eastern DRC (statement about the Uvira-period conflict)
claims.verification_note: Supported; page dated Sunday 4 Jan 2026, so 'Saturday night' = 3 Jan. BBC reports Bizimana later deleted the post.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('Saturday night') and the page date of 4 January 2026 (Sunday), so Saturday 3 January. BBC adds that Bizimana later deleted the post; the post itself was not opened. The statement is about the wider conflict after the Uvira capture (the page says the M23 took Uvira the previous month and said it left), not an Uvira incident.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye, in what it described as correcting his foreign minister, said on X that Burundi had always praised Qatar's 'important role' in mediation on the DRC and that it was necessary to clarify 'whatever was not clearly understood and the wrong words' about Qatar's role.
claims.verification_note: Supported; 'this Sunday evening' = 4 Jan 2026.
claims.researcher_note: Mediator-related statement (Qatar) by Burundi's head of state; not Uvira-specific. Page notes Qatar's Al-Khulaifi thanked Ndayishimiye for the clarification.

claims.text: UN News Kiswahili reported that, in South Kivu, about 20 civilians had been killed and 10 wounded since 23 March in fighting in the Uvira, Kalehe and Mwenga areas, and quoted the UN spokesperson saying that destruction of homes and livestock had forced many families to flee while access to food and health services remained limited.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira, Kalehe and Mwenga areas, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed groups (makundi yaliyojihami), as the UN page words it
claims.verification_note: The spokesperson's name and the 'citing humanitarian agencies' attribution sit only in an earlier paragraph of the page, not the excerpt; narrowed to 'the UN spokesperson' as the excerpt says. Figures supported. The figures are not broken down by area; Kalehe and Mwenga are outside Uvira. The page spells the spokesperson 'Stephen Dujarric'.
claims.researcher_note: Briefing of 2 April 2026 at UN headquarters (page text: 'tarehe 2 Aprili'). The figures are not broken down by area (Uvira, Kalehe, Mwenga); Kalehe and Mwenga are outside the Uvira unit.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, in reaction to Amnesty International's June 2026 report accusing the CMC-FDP armed group of serious abuses in Rutshuru, the CMC-FDP spokesperson categorically rejected the accusations and said that no official complaint had been filed before the movement's internal disciplinary or judicial bodies.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and supports every clause; report date 25 June 2026 printed on the page. Translation checked (flag benign: capitalised 'In'). B: one credible non-partisan outlet reporting that the statement was made. Party statement (CMC-FDP, a Wazalendo-affiliated group): the claim is that its spokesperson said this, not that it is true. Spokesperson not named on the page. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Spokesperson not named by the page. Only the CMC-FDP reacted on this page; no statement by the government or FARDC on the Amnesty report found on it. CMC-FDP is a Wazalendo coalition member (party statement, not fact).

claims.text: DW Swahili reported that Minister of Information and government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya accused the M23 of continuing the war and called their announcement of leaving Uvira 'upotoshaji' (a distortion/misinformation), saying it was a ploy to disrupt the mediator, the United States.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact; page dated 17.12.2025 (byline Byobe Malenga). Swahili translations checked: 'kumvuruga' = to confuse/disrupt, 'upotoshaji' = distortion/misinformation; correct. Flags benign (M23 read as a number; capitalised English words). Both sources are the same page, so one origin: B. Muyaya's words are DW's Swahili rendering; the original-language wording was not seen. Kinshasa's account of the M23 announcement, not a finding that M23 stayed. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Relevant to D-018 (day AFC/M23 withdrew from Uvira): this is Kinshasa's account on 17 Dec 2025 that the withdrawal was not real. Page date taken from the page (17.12.2025). Remainder of the Muyaya quote on the page is in Swahili translation of his remarks; wording is DW's rendering.

claims.text: Ouragan.cd reported a communiqué published on 6 March by Deputy Prime Minister for the Interior Jacquemain Shabani. In the article's account, Kigali deployed its troops on 28 February and on 3 and 4 March in the Ndosho and CBCA Virunga hospitals to take away patients, most of them Congolese soldiers, and their carers, and some of them were executed. The article then attributes to the Interior Ministry communiqué the statement that the Rwandan army and its M23 auxiliaries carried out incursions into Goma hospitals, taking about a hundred patients and carers, among them Congolese soldiers, and that they were summarily executed.
claims.place_as_written: Goma, North Kivu (Ndosho and CBCA Virunga hospitals)
claims.actor_as_written: DRC government (Ministry of the Interior) accusing Rwandan forces (RDF) and M23
claims.verification_note: All excerpts exact. Original statement merged the two passages and presented the 28 Feb-4 Mar passage as communiqué wording; corrected to say which passage the article attributes to the communiqué and to keep both execution wordings. 'Rwandan forces' replaced by the page's own 'Kigali'/'Rwandan army'. Year dropped from the statement (no excerpt prints it; page date 7 March 2025). Translations checked; flags benign. Kinshasa's account (party says). The relayed text is internally inconsistent: one passage says 'some of them' were executed, the passage attributed to the communiqué says 'they were summarily executed'. The communiqué itself was not seen; the 28 Feb / 3-4 March passage is the outlet's rendering and is not in quotation marks.
claims.researcher_note: Answers r1/HC-2025#3 (Kinshasa statement on the 28 Feb hospital removals) and D-011 (date and number of patients): this is Kinshasa's account (partisan, 'party says'): 28 Feb, 3 and 4 March; 'une centaine'; hospitals named Ndosho and CBCA Virunga (Heal Africa not named). The communiqué's first passage says 'certains d'entre eux' were executed; the later passage says 'Ils ont sommairement été exécutés' (all), an internal inconsistency in the outlet's wording. Ouragan.cd page is a media relay of the communiqué; the communiqué text itself was not seen.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that DRC Minister of Human Rights Samuel Mbemba presented on 7 April a report on violations allegedly committed by AFC/M23 during the occupation of Uvira and its surroundings with Rwandan support; the government said it had counted more than 14 400 women raped, and the page gives two different figures for people killed, which it does not reconcile (see note).
claims.actor_as_written: DRC government (Ministry of Human Rights) accusing AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. The original statement gave only the 15 000 figure while the page also prints 1 500 in the minister's own quoted words: a silent choice. Narrowed: the death toll moves to the note with both figures verbatim (the 1 500 passage is on the page but in no stored excerpt, so it cannot go in the statement). Figures field narrowed to numbers an excerpt prints. Weekday and date (Tuesday 7 April) are printed. Conditional 'qu’auraient commis' kept as 'allegedly'. Government (party) figures. The same Actualite.cd page prints two death tolls for the same report: 'plus de 15 000 personnes tuées' (outlet's summary) and 'Plus de 1 500 morts' (the minister's quoted words). Both are shown as printed; neither is chosen. The rape figure is the government's own and is not independently corroborated here. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-DRC claim 3) 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Government (partisan) figures, 'party says'. The same page prints 'plus de 15 000 personnes tuées' (report summary) and, in the minister's quoted words, 'Plus de 1 500 morts' - a discrepancy inside the outlet's text that cannot be resolved from the page (possible typo); both are recorded, not merged. Relevant to D-025 (mass-grave body counts) and to the sexual-violence picture at Uvira; the very large rape figure is the government's own and is not independently corroborated here.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the Congolese government said it had found several mass graves after the AFC/M23 left Uvira: three graves at Mayi Moto holding 115 bodies according to the government, one at Kilomani with 31 bodies, one at Kala and two at Rutembo.
claims.place_as_written: Mayi Moto, Kilomani, Kala, Rutembo (Uvira area), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: DRC government (Ministry of Human Rights) accusing AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; figures 115 and 31 match. 'M23' flag benign. The 'after AFC/M23 left Uvira' clause is on the page (quoted) but not in the excerpt: expect an excerpt-gap warning. Translation tightened ('avaient permis l'ensevelissement' = had been used to bury). Government count (party says); the page does not say who dug the graves or who the dead were.
