The clause on the AFC/M23 departure rests on a page passage outside the stored excerpt. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-DRC claim 4) 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: For D-025 (number of bodies in the Uvira mass graves): government count per Actualite.cd. claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, speaking on Radio Okapi's Dialogue entre Congolais on Tuesday 20 January, confirmed that life had resumed in Uvira after the AFC/M23 withdrawal and that loyalist forces now controlled the city; he announced the imminent restoration of State authority.

claims.text: JamboRDC reported that FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge, speaking to the press on Saturday 6 September, called on the residents of Uvira to stay calm and not to give in to enemy manipulation, after protests by Wazalendo and citizen movements demanding the departure of General Olivier Gasita.

The page also says the protesters accuse Gasita of links to the M23 and of taking part in the capture of Bukavu, 'allégations que réfutent l'armée'. The page names him 'général Sylvain Gasita' in the lead and 'général Olivier Gasita' is the name printed by JamboRDC; the page-level name is not harmonised here. No Muyaya statement found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, reacting at a press briefing to recent Human Rights Watch and Global Witness reports on the security, humanitarian and natural-resources situation in AFC/M23-held areas, said the publications were not a surprise to the Congolese authorities and that Kinshasa was acting on a judicial front and an economic front.

The page does not name or date the HRW report(s) meant ('récents rapports'); it mentions HRW's documentation of forced recruitment of children. Briefing date not stated; article date used. Kinshasa's own wording (party says).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, after the creation of the FRN, said that the former head of state's choice to take up arms was an attack on the Republic and the constitutional order.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the wife of local notable Rugamba and their five children (one boy and four girls) were killed by armed men who attacked their home at Kabizo, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, on the night of Thursday to Friday 3 July [2026], and that the Congolese army and the AFC/M23 each blamed the other.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the 34th military region, Major Dieudonné Kasereka, rejected the AFC/M23's version of the Kabizo killings and denounced a disinformation campaign meant, in his words, to conceal abuses committed by RDF/AFC-M23 elements.

Kasereka also said Kabizo lies in the AFC-M23-controlled zone and cited nine people killed on 12 June at Rusamambu and Kanoune (Walikale); the page does not source that further. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)

FDLR-FOCA statement (party says), in Radio Okapi's paraphrase from a programme page; his own words were not seen. The page adds that he said the FDLR would resist a joint military operation.

claims.text: Kigali Today reported that a statement issued by AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that the allegations of HRW and the UN were based on political motives, and accused these organisations of bias toward the DRC government; AFC/M23 also said that this could not replace HRW going there in person and that those it spoke to were known extremists and DRC government employees. The statement replied to an HRW report, published on 20 August 2025, saying that residents of areas near Virunga National Park, mostly Hutu, were killed in 14 villages between 10 and 30 July.

claims.verification_note: All three excerpts found on the retained page (byline Tarib Abdul, 21 August 2025, no wire credit). Narrowed 'biased' to the excerpt's wording (organisations accused of bias) and added the src 2 clause so every source carries a clause. 140 appears only in the headline and stays out of the statement. HRW page says killings were suspected to have occurred while AFC/M23 hunted FDLR ('bigakekwa'), which stays out. AFC/M23 statement relayed by a Rwandan outlet: AFC/M23 says. The HRW findings are as Kigali Today summarises them, not the HRW report itself.

claims.researcher_note: Paywalled article (marked 'réservé aux abonnés'; the text was retrievable by the helper). Burundian losses rest on anonymous testimony (including one former Burundian soldier) and are unverified. The article dates the turn-back 'three weeks' after President Tshisekedi's announcement in Houston of the retaking of Minembwe; the exact date is not given (the existing register places the Minembwe clashes in June 2026, see D-027 and the 9 June 2026 losses in target r1/SKC-2026H1#3). The 'no credible official figure' sentence is La Libre's own statement, so no Burundian government statement on these losses was found in this article. Authors' byline: Hubert Leclercq.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to Kagame, a contingent of more than twenty thousand Burundian soldiers was said to be operating in several provinces, notably Uvira, Minembwe, Kalemie, Kindu, Walikale and Kisangani, and that he accused Burundi of regular strikes against civilians, notably at Minembwe; the outlet wrote that at the time of publication the Burundian authorities had not reacted.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira, Minembwe and other places in the DRC, as listed by Kagame
claims.verification_note: Page read. The French conditional 'opérerait' (reported, unconfirmed) was rendered as an indicative 'is currently operating'; translation and statement corrected to keep the hedge. Capitalised-word flags ('According', 'Kigali' context, 'Rwandan') resolved as renderings. The page gives the occasion (swearing-in of new cabinet members) but no date. Kagame's figure and allegations, not established facts. The outlet lists Uvira and Minembwe among 'provinces' as Kagame is reported to have said. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-RN claim 10)
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan statement ('Kagame says'), not an established fact; the figure of 20,000 is Kagame's as relayed by the outlet. The page says the remarks were made at the swearing-in of new members of Kagame's cabinet, without a date; Anadolu (r1-UV-2025Q4-019) dates the remarks to Thursday 11 December 2025. The second excerpt is the outlet's statement that Burundi had not reacted at publication; later Burundian replies were searched for and not found (see gap for r1/UV-2025Q4#2).

claims.text: Radio Isanganiro, in a 'vrai ou faux' item on an online claim about Congolese officials moving their families from Uvira to Bujumbura and about Burundian soldiers in camps in Burundi, wrote that the Burundian army has never published such information and that reliable international media have never published information on the number of troops Burundi has, abroad or at home.
claims.actor_as_written: Radio Isanganiro (Burundi private radio) commenting on the Burundian army
claims.verification_note: Page read (Kirundi, 'Vrai ou Faux' section, 18/06/2025). Translation of the excerpt is faithful; statement narrowed from 'figures' to 'information' ('amakuru ku gitigiri' = information on the number). Capitalised-word flags (Burundian, Burundi) resolved as renderings. Not a statement by the Burundian army or government: a private Burundian radio's fact-check. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration) 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Not a statement by the Burundian army or government: a Burundian private radio (Bujumbura; broadcasts in Kirundi, Swahili, French) saying the army has published no such figures. Useful as a Kirundi-language confirmation, as of June 2025, that no FDNB statement on troop numbers or on the Uvira area was found (target r1/UV-2025Q2#1). 'nk'ayo' (such) refers to the preceding online claim of fewer than 5,000 soldiers in Burundian camps, which the item rejects as unfounded.

claims.text: Ijambo.net reported that the Government of Rwanda, in a statement issued on Monday 2 March 2026, rejected the sanctions the United States had imposed on some senior RDF officers, saying they were biased and aimed at presenting a picture contrary to the truth about the long-running insecurity in eastern DRC. The outlet reported that the US named Maj Gen Vincent Nyakarundi, Maj. Gen Ruki Karusisi, Gen Mubarakh Muganga and Brig Gen Stanislas Gashugi, and that Rwanda said the US had ignored drone and ground attacks by DRC forces that it said continued despite the agreement to stop fighting and killed many civilians.
claims.verification_note: Page read in full (byline Yves Iyaremye; no wire credit). Translations faithful: 'yamaganye' = rejected/condemned, 'bibogamye' = biased, 'bigahitana ubuzima bw'abasivili benshi' = kill many civilians. Capitalised-word flags (United States of America, Rwanda Defence Force, Democratic Republic of Congo, Monday, March, America) are renderings of 'Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika', 'Ingabo z'u Rwanda', 'Mbere', 'Werurwe': resolved. Source 0 excerpt joins two adjacent paragraphs; both on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Kinyarwanda account of the Rwandan government communiqué of 2 March 2026 (the existing claim r1-UC-RDF-017 carries the AP/Reuters version of Makolo's statement). Ijambo.net is a Rwandan online outlet (Rubavu); the page has no wire credit. Per the page, Rwanda says the sanctions were one-sided while both sides were in peace talks; this adds Rwanda's own counter-allegation about drone attacks, recorded here as Rwanda's account only. Answers targets r1/POL-2026#0, r4/G-CMD-LEGAL#3, r1/UV-2026Q1#2.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw (Rwandan outlet) reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo, in a post on X on 14 May 2026, criticised Human Rights Watch, writing (in the outlet's Kinyarwanda rendering) that HRW has its way of working and Rwanda is always its measure showing that it has worked well. The outlet described the HRW report of 13 May as accusing Rwandan soldiers and fighters of the armed group M23 of killing civilians, abducting them and raping women in the city of Uvira from 10 December 2025 to 17 January 2026.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira (the HRW report's subject); statement made online
claims.verification_note: Retained page read (byline ISIMBI Estella, 15 May 2026). Translation faithful ('igipimo' = yardstick/measure). The outlet's own later sentences (Rwanda has no troops in eastern DRC; HRW unreliable) are its narration and correctly not credited to Makolo. Capitalised-word flags ('Government', 'Rwandan') resolved as renderings. Makolo's X post was not fetched; the wording is the outlet's Kinyarwanda rendering.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan state-aligned outlet; the post is Makolo's, relayed by the outlet (the X post itself was not fetched). The same outlet's text goes on to say that Rwanda has repeatedly told the international community it has no troops in eastern DRC; that is the outlet's wording, not recorded as Makolo's. The igihe.com version (igihe.com/mu-rwanda/article/rdf-si-afc-m23-yolande-makolo-kuri-human-rights-watch, 11 June per search listing, and the mobile copy) could not be fetched by the helper (via=none), so it was not cited and no workaround was tried. HRW's own wording of the allegations is in existing claims (e.g. r2-G-UV-SVHC-011, REC-0002/REC-0003). No Rwandan or AFC/M23 reply to HRW's April letter found beyond this post. Answers targets r1/SV-2026#1, r2/G-UV-SVHC#2, r3/G-RESP#6, r1/UV-2025Q4#3, r5/G-DISC2#2 for Rwanda.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe, in a France 24 interview broadcast on Monday, wondered why Rwanda 'alone' is being sanctioned although the US-led peace agreement signed in December 2025 concerns both sides, and said of the sanctions: 'Those sanctions first of all are unfair to us, they concern one side and are not productive.'
claims.place_as_written: Kigali (statement); sanctions concern the eastern DRC conflict
claims.verification_note: Page read (byline Didier Bikorimana, 30 June 2026). 30 June 2026 is a Tuesday, so 'ku wa mbere' = 29 June. Translations faithful ('biraturenganya' = are unjust to us). Capitalised-word flags are renderings (Minister, Foreign Affairs, America, President, December): resolved. Kinyarwanda article, tagged rw correctly.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday ('ku wa mbere') and the publication date 30 June 2026 (a Monday is 29 June 2026). The article is about the US sanctions announced 'last Thursday' on Rwandan mining companies (Gasabo Gold Refinery and others) and their officials; the excerpts above do not name them, so the statement says 'sanctions'. BBC adds that the DRC government welcomed the sanctions (Muyaya on X); not recorded here. BBC calls this Rwanda's first explicit public statement on those sanctions. Answers r4/G-CMD-LEGAL#3 in part (Rwanda on US designations); the 2 March 2026 reply is in the Ijambo.net claim.

claims.text: A Rwandan broadcaster's website reported that Rwanda's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Olivier Nduhungirehe, writing on X, disputed remarks by US adviser Massad Boulos by saying AFC/M23 had completed its withdrawal from Uvira weeks before the US imposed sanctions on the RDF; the outlet reported him saying AFC/M23 began leaving Uvira on 16 December 2025 and completed its withdrawal on 17 January 2026, and that the Congolese army later returned to the city alongside Burundian forces, the FDLR and Wazalendo armed groups.
claims.verification_note: Page read; English original, no translation issue. Boulos's own quoted remark on the page ('Sanctions on Rwanda were a direct result of the invasion of Uvira...') is context, not added. Withdrawal dates are Nduhungirehe's, not independently verified; the X post itself was not fetched.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan outlet reporting a post on X (the post itself was not fetched); the exact post date is not given on the page, the outlet is dated 27 September 2026 (a Kinyarwanda copy at thenewsjam.rw is dated 26 September 2026). The dates given are Nduhungirehe's, not independently verified; they bear on discrepancy D-018 (day AFC/M23 withdrew from Uvira; REC-0005, REC-0591) and D-019. The page also quotes Boulos as saying the sanctions followed the Uvira offensive; that is a US statement as reported. Answers r2/G-UV-CTRL#0 and r1/UV-2026Q1#2 for Rwanda.

claims.text: Kigali Today's Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview reports that Paul Kagame, asked about the capture of Uvira on 10 December (six days after the Washington agreement) and US pressure, said that 'they' wanted to convince people there was a link between the capture of Uvira and the Washington agreement and that it was a way of rejecting the agreement, 'That is not true at all', and added that whether or not the Washington agreement was signed, 'the capture of Uvira was necessary'.
claims.verification_note: Page read; Q/A labels 'Jeune Afrique:' / 'Paul Kagame:' are printed. Translations faithful ('byari ngombwa' = was necessary; 'Ibyo si ukuri na gato' = that is not true at all). Flags ('American', 'President') resolved as renderings of 'Amerika', 'Perezida'. Kagame's words reach us as Kigali Today's Kinyarwanda version of a French-language Jeune Afrique interview; the French original was not checked. The interview took place 'last month' (March 2026) at Village Urugwiro, per the page.
claims.researcher_note: Kagame's wording is 'gufatwa kwa Uvira' (the capture/taking of Uvira) without naming who captured it; the question frames it as an M23 capture on 10 December 2025. The second sentence cited is a later sentence of the same answer (not contiguous with the first). Statement attributed to Kagame via a Rwandan outlet's translation of the Jeune Afrique interview. Kigali Today (Rwandan, government-friendly outlet) publishes a Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview; the page says the interview was held 'last month' at Village Urugwiro (so March 2026), and gives its own date of 3 April 2026. The Kinyarwanda is the outlet's rendering; the original French was not fetched. Jeune Afrique's question introduces the 2 March 2026 US sanctions; see the Ijambo.net and BBC claims.

claims.verification_note: Statement supported by source 0 as written. The question that gives 'Yes, of course' its meaning is on the page but not in any stored excerpt, so it is recorded in the note for an excerpt extension rather than added to the statement. Translation faithful ('Nta gihabanye' = there is no contradiction). Source 1 (generic intro sentence) supports only the interview's framing. Context the stored excerpts do not carry (excerpt gap; extend with source_edits.py add_excerpt): on the page the 'Yes, of course' answers the interviewer's question: 'Ku itariki ya 22 Mutarama, ambasaderi wanyu muri Washington yavuze ko u Rwanda rufite « ubufatanye mu mutekano na AFC/M23 », abantu benshi babyumvise nk’aho ingabo z’u Rwanda ziri ku butaka bw'Uburasirazuba bwa RDC. Murabyemera?' (On 22 January your ambassador in Washington said Rwanda has 'security cooperation with AFC/M23', which many understood as Rwandan troops being on eastern DRC soil. Do you agree?). The answer does not say where the 5-20 km is measured from. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension: the interviewer's question that 'Yes, of course' answers (verifier excerpt gap) 2026-10-29: statement edited: interviewer's question restored after the excerpt was extended to carry it (verifier excerpt gap)

The answer does not say where the 5-20 km is measured from (the page's own words: 'inyuma', 'behind/back'). claims.verification_note: Page read; labels printed. Translations faithful. Flag ('President') resolved. A general rejection by comparison; addresses no specific incident. Translation chain as for the other Jeune Afrique claims.

On the page the sentence 'Mu gihe guverinoma ya Kongo yagaragaje ubushake bwo guhagarika ibikorwa bya FDLR, ibisubizo bigeze he?' carries a second consecutive 'Paul Kagame:' label but reads as the interviewer's question; it is not credited to Kagame here. An allegation by Kagame with no unit, date or place beyond the territories.

claims.text: Umunota.com (Rwandan outlet) reported that Rwanda's Foreign Minister, Amb Olivier Jean Patrick Nduhungirehe, said in an RBA interview on the evening of 10 December 2025 that Rwanda is not the one to answer for ceasefire violations, but the FDLR and Burundian troops, who he said have a plan to destabilise Rwanda's security.
claims.verification_note: Retained page read (byline Raymond Tuyishimire, 11 Dec 2025). Translation faithful ('rubazwa' = is to be held to account). Flags (Minister, Foreign Affairs, Cooperation, Burundian, December) resolved as renderings; 'Ubutwererane' = (International) Cooperation.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan outlet relaying a state broadcaster (RBA) interview. The article's closing lines say the interview followed AFC/M23's announcement that it had taken Uvira and international pressure on Rwanda, and that Rwanda denies the accusation. Answers r1/UC-BI-FDLR#1 (Rwandan response to the Burundian accusation of 8 December 2025), r2/G-UV-CTRL#0 and r1/UV-2025Q4#2 (Rwanda side).

claims.text: Umunota.com reported that Foreign Minister Nduhungirehe, in the same RBA interview, said that Burundian soldiers in South Kivu had now reached twenty thousand, a problem he said Rwanda has raised repeatedly, and alleged that they prevent the Banyamulenge from leaving their areas so as to starve them.
claims.verification_note: Statement said the troops 'hold' the Banyamulenge areas, which translates the untranslatable 'batangatanze' by guess; narrowed to what the excerpt clearly says ('bakababuza gusohoka kugira ngo babicishe inzara' = preventing them from going out so as to starve them). Translation otherwise faithful; flags resolved as renderings. Figure and allegation are Nduhungirehe's. The verb 'batangatanze' is uncertain (possibly a misspelling); later in the same article he says the troops 'zibasira abanyamurenge, zikabagota, zikabicisha inzara' (attack the Banyamulenge, encircle them, starve them).
claims.researcher_note: Figure and allegation are Nduhungirehe's, as reported; no independent figure for Burundian troop numbers is given on the page. The word 'batangatanze' in the quote could not be translated with confidence and is left untranslated. For other sources on FDNB numbers see the Group of Experts claims already in the file.

claims.text: Umunota.com reported that, on the Monday of the week of publication, Burundi's Foreign Minister Bizimana Edouard, speaking with representatives of countries in Burundi, said that Rwanda had attacked the positions of Burundian troops in the DRC and allegedly had a plan to attack them, and that they would therefore defend themselves.
claims.place_as_written: Burundian troop positions in the DRC (location not specified)
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Burundi (Foreign Minister), as relayed by a Rwandan outlet
claims.verification_note: 'bityo bazirwanaho' means 'therefore they will defend themselves', not purpose ('so that'); 'ngo' marks hearsay, kept as 'allegedly'. Statement and translation corrected. Not an RBA relay: originating_source set to Umunota.com (the packet's RBA credit belongs to the Nduhungirehe interview). Flags resolved as renderings. Burundian statement known here only through a Rwandan outlet; the Burundian original was not fetched. Date derived: article dated Thursday 11 December 2025, so Monday = 8 December 2025. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-RW claim 11)
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from 'Monday of this week' and the article date (Thursday 11 December 2025): Monday 8 December 2025. A Burundian government statement relayed by a Rwandan outlet, so recorded as 'Burundi says' only; the Burundian original was not fetched. Context for target r1/UC-BI-FDLR#1.

claims.text: Umunota.com reported that Muyaya, in a message posted on X, said that all the attacks launched on the Banyamulenge in Minembwe were launched by M23 together with Rwanda.
claims.actor_as_written: Muyaya (named by the outlet by surname only, without title)
claims.verification_note: Actor corrected: the source names only 'Muyaya'; the party attribution 'Government of the DRC (spokesperson)' was inferred from a different page, which the rules forbid. Statement and translation otherwise faithful. Known only through a Rwandan outlet replying to it; Muyaya's post was not fetched and is undated on the page. The page prints only the surname; that this is the DRC government spokesperson is an inference from another source and should be confirmed from the post itself.
claims.researcher_note: The outlet gives no date for Muyaya's post (before the 3 April 2026 article) and does not print his title; The page prints only the surname 'Muyaya'; BBC Gahuza (30 June 2026) identifies Patrick Muyaya as the DRC government spokesperson, and the DRC party attribution here rests on that. Relayed by a Rwandan outlet; the post was not fetched. The page also says Banyamulenge in Minembwe, Fizi, Uvira and Itombwe report attacks by FARDC with Wazalendo, FDLR and Burundian troops, and drone strikes in Minembwe killing civilians and cattle (outlet's own text, not recorded as fact). Answers r1/SKS-2026Q1#0 for Rwanda.

claims.text: Umunota.com reported that Makolo, replying to Muyaya, said his words were a ploy to shift the crimes of FARDC onto M23, and wrote: 'Accusing others of what you do, where the one who committed crimes pins them on the one they were committed against. It is usually used to encourage people to violence or genocide.'
claims.verification_note: Retained page read (byline Niyigena Radjabu, 3 Apr 2026). Translation faithful; flag ('She') resolved: 'Yagize ati' is ungendered, Makolo is the speaker. The quotation is the outlet's Kinyarwanda rendering of Makolo's post (not fetched); 'genocide' appears only inside her attributed words. 'ubugizi bwa nabi' can also be read as 'criminality/wrongdoing'.
claims.researcher_note: Makolo's wording is a rhetorical charge and names no specific incident; 'genocide' appears only inside the attributed quotation. Relayed by a Rwandan outlet. Answers r1/SKS-2026Q1#0 (Rwanda on the Minembwe fighting) in part.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwanda's President Paul Kagame, at a gathering with some Kigali residents on Sunday, asked Rwandans to prepare to face sanctions, which he called 'gufunga umukandara' (tightening the belt).
claims.verification_note: Page read. Translation faithful. 'Rwandans' in the statement is carried by the quoted speech on the page ('Abanyarwanda'), placed in clause_support. Flags ('Rwanda's', 'President') resolved. Date derived: first published Tuesday 18 March 2025, so 'ku cyumweru' = 16 March 2025. The page is a year-end re-run updated 28 December 2025. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from 'on Sunday' and the article's first publication date of 18 March 2025 (the EU listing was 'on Monday', 17 March), so Sunday is 16 March 2025; the page was later updated (28 December 2025) and is a year-end re-run of the original. Kagame's remarks concern sanctions in general; the page does not say he was responding to the EU listing, which came the next day. Context for target r1/UCD-RDF-FDNB#3.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Rwandan government had not yet said anything publicly about the new EU sanctions (on Generals Ruki Karusisi, Eugène Nkubito and Pascal Muhizi), but that regarding the earlier sanctions by the United Kingdom, America and Canada, Rwandan officials say those sanctions do not help resolve the war in DR Congo and undermine Africa's effort to seek a peaceful solution.
claims.place_as_written: Kigali (statements); sanctions concern the eastern DRC conflict
claims.verification_note: Page read. Translation faithful; capitalised-word flags (United Kingdom, America, Canada, Major General, Brigadier General) are renderings of 'Ubwongereza', 'Amerika', 'Jenerali Majoro', 'Brigadiye Jenerali': resolved. 'Had not yet' is as at 18 March 2025, the original publication date.
claims.researcher_note: This is a 'none official found' result for the EU listings (target r1/UCD-RDF-FDNB#3): as at 18 March 2025 BBC reported no Rwandan government reaction; no later Rwandan statement specific to the EU listing was found in the searches run. The statement about earlier UK/US/Canadian sanctions is the BBC's summary of Rwandan officials' position, not a dated quote. The EU listing itself is in existing claim r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-010 (ACP).

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Oscar Balinda said that gold and coltan mined in the east of the DRC pass through Rwanda but only in transit to foreign markets; that he said the Amnesty report was the same as others published by organisations he said are paid by the Kinshasa government to tarnish the name of AFC/M23, and the outlet wrote that he gave no evidence for this; and that Amnesty said AFC/M23 had not answered its questions, while AFC/M23 denies that Amnesty ever approached it.
claims.verification_note: Kirundi page read. 'Nta cemezo yatanze' means 'he gave no evidence/proof', not 'no confirmation'; it is BBC's own remark, so the statement now credits it to BBC. Flags ('Democratic Republic of Congo' rendering 'Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo') resolved. Partisan statement, recorded as 'AFC/M23 says'. In Kirundi 'Nyakanga' is September, so BBC's '21 Nyakanga (9)' (21 September 2026) is consistent. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-RW claim 16)
claims.researcher_note: Balinda's account of the Amnesty International report (published 21 September 2026 per BBC's '21 Nyakanga (9)', i.e. month 9; the umuryango.rw copy wrongly prints July). The BBC Gahuza live page text is in Kirundi (tagged rn); the interview was on Thursday per the page. The AFC/M23 party reply is partisan ('AFC/M23 says'); Amnesty's own findings on Rubaya and Lomera are in other claims. AP adds that the FARDC had not commented on the attack, and that Ebuteli researcher Stewart Muhindo called the figure of 22 civilians killed 'greatly exaggerated'.
claims.researcher_note: AP copy on thecanadianpressnews.ca; apnews.com original could not be fetched by the helper. Page says 'The FARDC has not commented on the attack' (supports Kinshasa-silence gap for G-RESP#5). Date is the funeral date (Thursday 8 January 2026), attack 2 January. claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwanda's foreign minister Olivier Nduhungirehe replied to BBC Gahuzamiryango by WhatsApp that the Rwandan government does not respond to HRW reports of this kind, saying 'Ntacyo. Ntitujya dusubiza HRW.' (Nothing. We never respond to HRW.)
claims.place_as_written: eastern DRC (HRW report covering Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps); statement published via X

The Rwandan government later published a written response to the report (held in the project as r3-G-RESP-005), so this was not its final position.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that from 14:00 on Thursday 10 September 2026 until late at night the coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime continued indiscriminate bombardments with kamikaze drones against Point-Zéro and Nyamabuguma in the Minembwe region.
claims.place_as_written: Point-Zéro and Nyamabuguma, Minembwe region, Fizi territory, South Kivu

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to Twirwaneho spokesperson colonel Fidèle Rugabo, two battalions, 'dont celui des Hiboux et des forces burundaises' (the wording is ambiguous: including that of the Hiboux and of Burundian forces), had been deployed on the Rurambo axis, and that on the Bijombo axis four battalions of the FARDC and of the Burundian army, with elements of the P5 and Wazalendo, were visible towards Kirungwa, Munanira, Gataka, Zikambitse-Marimba, Rubarati and Kajoka.
claims.place_as_written: Rurambo and Bijombo axes (Kirungwa, Munanira, Gataka, Zikambitse-Marimba, Rubarati, Kajoka), Uvira/Fizi highlands, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho (spokesperson Fidèle Rugabo) alleging FARDC, Burundian army, P5 and Wazalendo deployments
claims.verification_note: originating_source was wrong (Kanyuka); the passage is Twirwaneho's spokesperson in a Thursday communiqué. Removed '(ally of AFC-M23)' from the statement (not in the excerpt; figure flag '23'), kept the ambiguous French wording visible. KMP describes Twirwaneho as allied to the AFC-M23 ('le Twirwaneho, allié à l’AFC-M23'). The communiqué was issued on the Thursday (10 September 2026) per the page. Party allegation, not confirmed.
claims.researcher_note: Twirwaneho communiqué of Thursday (10 Sept 2026) as relayed by KMP; the article's wording is 'deux bataillons, dont celui des Hiboux et des forces burundaises' (ambiguous). Burundian government reply not found. Existing related claim: r1-UV-2026Q3-008 (SOS Médias Burundi, 31 Aug).

claims.text: Into Rwanda reported that a statement released by Erasto Bahati, whom it calls the Governor of North Kivu Province, dismissed reports of an AFC/M23 pull-back, saying that what is happening is a routine rotation of troops, and quoted the statement as saying the activities along the battlefront are part of the regular military troop rotations within AFC/M23.
claims.place_as_written: Lubero, Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese areas; Alimbongo, Kirumba and Kanyabayonga, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (North Kivu governor in the M23 administration)
claims.verification_note: Rwandan outlet relaying a party statement: 'AFC/M23 says', grade C. Narrowed the 'Lubero' wording and made the governor title the outlet's, since he is the AFC/M23-appointed official. Bahati holds the post under the AFC/M23 administration, not the Kinshasa government. Into Rwanda (30 March 2026) says the reports appeared 'earlier this week'; the statement's own date is not given, so the date is approximate (on or before 30 March 2026). The reports named withdrawals from Lubero, Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan outlet (state-aligned media are partisan on contested facts); cited only for what the AFC/M23 governor's statement said. 'Governor Erasto Bahati' is probably the person other sources call Bahati Musanga Erasto / Erasto Musanga (not stated on this page). The page names the reports being denied: withdrawal from Lubero, Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese, relocating to Alimbongo, Kirumba and Kanyabayonga, allegedly under US pressure. Igihe's Kinyarwanda item could not be fetched; Instagram/Facebook posts of 29 Mar 2026 ('AFC/M23 yahakanye ibyo kuva mu bice bimwe yafashe') were leads only.

claims.text: A pro-government Rwandan outlet reported that on Wednesday, 2 July 2025, the Rwandan government spokesperson Makolo Yolande set out Rwanda's position on the report of the group of UN experts (whom the outlet calls 'so-called' experts), and that she criticised the group for what the outlet calls lies in the report aimed at distorting the truth.
claims.place_as_written: Kigali (statement on the eastern DRC conflict)
claims.territory: Rwanda statement on UN Group of Experts report
claims.verification_note: Removed the outlet name (figure flag '250') and 'via her X account' (not in the excerpt); made the 'lies' and 'so-called' framing the outlet's, as the excerpt is the outlet's narration. The page says she spoke through her X account ('Abinyujije kurubuga rwe rwa X'); the X post itself was not retained. The report is the UN Group of Experts' final report of mid-2025.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan Rwandan outlet; the outlet's wording 'abiyita Impuguke' ('so-called experts') is the outlet's own. The page does not give the report number; the report is the Group of Experts' final report (S/2025/446 per the project's target r2/G-DOC-446). The primary X post was not fetched. Rwanda's government reply is to the Group of Experts report, not to the AFC/M23 allegations; AFC/M23's own reply to the Katindo findings was not found.

claims.text: The outlet (pro-government) reported that Makolo Yolande said the UN experts' report confirms that the FDLR is helped by the Congolese government, but that the experts deliberately discount the concerns of Rwanda that led to the putting in place of defensive measures.
claims.place_as_written: Kigali (statement on the eastern DRC conflict)
claims.territory: Rwanda statement on UN Group of Experts report
claims.verification_note: Removed the outlet name (figure flag '250'); 'ifashwa' rendered as 'helped' (the excerpt_en's own word) rather than 'supported'. Rwanda says; not established fact.
claims.researcher_note: Same page as the previous claim. Partisan outlet; Rwanda says; not established fact.

claims.text: JamboRDC reported that in a mise au point published on Tuesday, signed by Bertrand Bisimwa, deputy coordinator of the AFC/M23, the movement said it rejects 'formally and as a whole' the accusations in Amnesty International's report on the Rubaya and Lomera mining sites, which it judges 'not established and insufficiently substantiated'.
claims.place_as_written: Rubaya mining site (Masisi territory, North Kivu) and Lomera (Kabare territory, South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on JamboRDC (La Rédaction, 24/09/2026); title names Rubaya and Lomera. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Fills the gap for r2/G-NKW-MASISI#0 and r2/G-UNDOCS#1 (Amnesty itself said M23 had not responded; the reply came the day after publication). Page date 24/09/2026. The AFC/M23 mise au point itself was not located on a party channel; JamboRDC is a local outlet relaying it. A Kinyarwanda video post (YouTube) and Swahili posts also reported the denial (leads only). Rwanda's reply to Amnesty not found.

claims.text: JamboRDC reported that the AFC/M23 said each case alleged by Amnesty should establish the reality of the alleged facts, their date and place, the identity of the alleged perpetrators and any link with the AFC/M23 and its chain of command, and that 'an accusation does not in itself constitute proof'.
claims.place_as_written: Rubaya mining site (Masisi territory, North Kivu) and Lomera (Kabare territory, South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on JamboRDC.
claims.researcher_note: Same page and statement as the previous claim.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Burundian authorities presented 13 people to journalists on 9 October, a majority of them Banyamulenge refugees, whom the authorities accused of espionage for Rwanda and for armed groups active in eastern RDC; Pierre Nkurikiye said the suspects collaborated with armed groups active in the region, including the AFC/M23, Red-Tabara and Twirwaneho.
claims.place_as_written: Bujumbura (Burundi); the armed groups named operate in eastern DRC
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian authorities; Pierre Nkurikiye (as reported by SOS Médias Burundi)
claims.verification_note: Page (retained, dated 11 octobre 2026, byline Adam Ntwari) prints both excerpts. Narrowed: the accusations are explicitly the authorities' ('whom the authorities accused'); 'namely' changed to 'including' (source: 'notamment', not exhaustive); weekday removed; 'DRC' replaced by 'RDC' as the excerpt prints it. excerpt_en flags are false positives (Friday/vendredi, Congolese Tutsi/tutsi congolaise): translations are faithful. Page also names three pastors among those presented (in the 'Des pasteurs parmi les personnes présentées' section); not in any excerpt, so not listed in victims_named; lead for a later pass under policy v1. Burundi's ministry account of its own arrests, relayed by one outlet; not independently verified. The same page reports that relatives and congregants contest the accusations, and that journalists were not allowed to ask questions allowing independent verification.
claims.researcher_note: Burundian official account of its own arrests; the allegations are not independently verified. The page states that relatives and congregants contest the accusations. Adjacent to, not a reply to, FRN's October 2026 troop-crossing allegation (target r1/ST-DRC-2026#0). The page also names the suspects (including pastors); those names are not in the excerpts and are not listed here.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, on the occasion of the presentation of the suspects, the spokesperson of the ministry in charge of security, Pierre Nkurikiye, called on Burundians to monitor the Banyamulenge and to stop renting houses to them.
claims.actor_as_written: Pierre Nkurikiye, as reported by SOS Médias Burundi
claims.verification_note: Excerpt is verbatim on the retained page (11 octobre 2026) and carries the whole statement, attributed to the speaker. Page also prints the direct quote (see note). excerpt_en faithful ('Security'/'Sécurité' capitalisation only). Single-outlet report. The page also quotes him directly: « Il faut surveiller leurs déplacements et ne plus leur louer de maisons, surtout ici à Bujumbura ».
claims.researcher_note: Single-outlet report of an official call; relevant to the position of Banyamulenge in Burundi, not a finding about Kivu fighting. The presentation was on 9 October 2026 and concerned 13 suspects (see the companion claim).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Burundi's permanent representative to the UN, Zéphyrin Maniratanga, in his presentation on Friday 12 December 2025, accused Rwanda of having favoured the taking of Uvira in violation of the Washington accords and resolution 2773, and quoted him as saying Burundi was particularly concerned by cross-border attacks, including artillery and drones, some of which reached localities of Burundian territory.

claims.verification_note: Statement unchanged; actor narrowed (the speaker accuses Rwanda; AFC/M23 is named only in Actualite.cd's narration, not by him). Retained page dated 14/12/2025, byline Clément MUAMBA; both excerpts verbatim. Not a duplicate of r1-ST-BI-014: that claim rests on a different article (16 Dec 2025) about a 'special session' with an undated Tshibitoke-bombardment assertion; this claim covers different assertions (Uvira, Washington accords, resolution 2773, cross-border attacks) with an exact date. They may come from the same council meeting; the editor may link them. excerpt_en faithful (Friday/United Nations flags are capitalisation only). Party account (Burundi). Actualite.cd places the remarks at the Security Council briefing on MONUSCO.
claims.researcher_note: Party account (Burundi): Rwanda's role and the civilian casualties are Burundi's assertions. Possible overlap with r1-ST-BI-014 (another Maniratanga statement); check at promotion. Outside the Sept-Oct 2026 window of target r1/ST-DRC-2026#4. The page names the council briefing as on MONUSCO (not the special session).

claims.text: UMUSEKE reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo said the RDC government cannot pursue the process of halting the fighting while it is itself the one starting the war; she was replying to Patrick Muyaya, minister of information, who had explained that President Tshisekedi said Rwanda was violating the agreements by launching attacks in South Kivu. UMUSEKE also reported that Makolo stressed that Rwanda has nothing to do with the fighting continuing in South Kivu.

'gashozantambara' means the instigator/starter of war, and 'kandi' is 'while/and yet', not 'because': the draft's 'because it was the one waging war' and 'oversee a ceasefire process' narrowed to the excerpt's wording. Capitalisation flag: 'DRC' renders 'RDC', 'Congolese' renders 'Congo'; legitimate translation, case fixed in excerpt_en. Rwandan outlet relaying the Rwandan government spokesperson: what Rwanda says, not a finding. claims.text: The New Humanitarian reported that demonstrations organised against Gasita in Uvira turned violent when Congolese military forces fired on unarmed protesters, killing at least one person and wounding several others, including children.
claims.actor_as_written: Congolese military forces (FARDC), as stated by the outlet
claims.verification_note: Retained user copy prints the passage; replacement quote extended to the September/Gasita sentence that dates the protests. Outlet's own narration from a credible non-partisan origin: B. The outlet gives the month (September 2025) but no day. Its toll (at least one killed) is lower than other outlets' tolls already in the store; a discrepancy to surface, not resolve.
claims.researcher_note: The article gives the month ('in September') and the appointment of General Olivier Gasita but no day for the shooting. Lower toll than SOS Medias Burundi (5 dead), Kivu Morning Post (Wazalendo spokesperson: 12 dead) and HRW (an 8-year-old boy killed, at least nine wounded) already in the store; record as a discrepancy, not a conflict of fact.

claims.text: The New Humanitarian reported that the self-proclaimed Wazalendo police chief for South Kivu, General Kimanuka Musasa Nyambwe Nungisa, denied that the militias have implemented a taxation system and said they came to defend Uvira when authorities and security services fled.
claims.verification_note: Retained user copy prints the passage verbatim. The claim records that he made the denial (a party's statement reported by a credible outlet), not that the denial is true: B.
claims.researcher_note: Reply to residents' and a port official's accounts that Wazalendo collect a 'contribution to the resistance'. Title 'General' and 'self-proclaimed' as printed by the outlet.

claims.text: The New Humanitarian, in an article about Uvira, reported that in September Wazalendo fighters disrupted the funeral of an army colonel, a Tutsi officer from the region, and his wife (both had died in a plane crash), accusing the relatives of collaborating with Rwanda, and that witnesses reported Wazalendo militants declaring that no 'Rwandan' should be buried on Congolese soil. The article does not state where the funeral took place or name the colonel.
claims.verification_note: Retained user copy prints the passage verbatim. B (outlet's narration, credible non-partisan). The New Humanitarian says September and names no one; other outlets in the store date the burial to 25 August 2025 and name the colonel. Month discrepancy to surface. The page does not explicitly say the funeral was in Uvira city, but the article is about Uvira. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-r9-3: Place slippage: the page never says the funeral was in Uvira city (the verifier's note says so too), but the statement says 'the funeral in Uvira'. The amendment keeps the place to what the page says. The month discrepancy (September here; 25 August 2025 in other outlets in the store) is still to be surfaced. On the same page, a neighbour says nearby gunfire and shelling killed an eight-year-old boy; that is a separate allegation, not added here.
claims.researcher_note: Other outlets in the store (SOS Medias Burundi, Radio Okapi) date the burial to 25 August 2025 and name Colonel Patrick Gisore; The New Humanitarian says September and names no one. Month discrepancy to be surfaced, not resolved here. The same passage reports an 8-year-old boy killed by gunfire/shelling nearby (per a neighbour); it is not made a separate claim because the excerpt is limited to the funeral.

claims.verification_note: Retained user copy prints the excerpt verbatim (fetch_failed for the script). Date narrowed to what the page supports. Excerpt_en flag: 'Governor' is a sentence-initial translation of 'gouverneur', not an addition. Government toll kept attributed. C. Foxtime's page prints no date ('2 mois ago' on the copy saved around 29 Oct 2026). The 11 Sep 2026 date comes from a Friends of the Congo Substack relay (Purusi on Top Congo FM) that could not be retrieved as text; it is a lead only and is not the page's date. The 344 figure is a government count; the page does not say who dug up or counted the bodies or how the people died. Earlier tolls in the store are lower (172 in two graves, Feb 2026; 210 in three graves, Apr 2026).
claims.researcher_note: Page text carries no absolute date ('2 mois ago'). The date 2026-09-11 comes from the Friends of the Congo Substack (dated 11 Sep 2026, says Purusi spoke on Top Congo FM), which could not be fetched as page text and is a lead only. The 344 figure is a government count; neither Foxtime nor the Substack says who dug up or counted the bodies or how they died. AFC/M23 spokesperson Kanyuka earlier (Reuters, Feb 2026) said he knew of no such graves (already in the store). Possible relation to REC-0023 and REC-0648. Earlier tolls already in the store: 31 + 141 = 172 bodies in two graves (Reuters via BBC Gahuza, Feb 2026) and 210 in three graves (Radio Okapi, 3 Apr 2026).

claims.text: Foxtime.cd reported that the military judiciary has already opened investigations directly targeting the commanders and leaders of the AFC/M23 coalition to formally establish responsibility for what the outlet called 'this barbarity', in its article on the Uvira mass graves.
claims.date: 2026 (page undated; '2 mois ago' on a copy saved about 2026-10-29)
claims.verification_note: Retained user copy prints the excerpt. Statement tied to the excerpt's own words ('this barbarity') instead of an inferred object; date narrowed. C. Foxtime's page prints no date ('2 mois ago' on the copy saved around 29 Oct 2026). The 11 Sep 2026 date comes from a Friends of the Congo Substack relay (Purusi on Top Congo FM) that could not be retrieved as text; it is a lead only and is not the page's date. The outlet does not name the judicial body that opened the investigations or give a date; an investigation opened is not a charge. Elsewhere the page says the Auditorat militaire supérieur had earlier identified mass-burial sites at Sange and Luvungi.
claims.researcher_note: Same undated page as the 344 claim; same dating caveat. The outlet also says the Auditorat militaire supérieur had earlier identified other mass-burial sites at Sange and Luvungi. Outlet's wording ('crimes de guerre', 'barbarie') is the government/outlet's and is not adopted.

claims.text: Afrique Diplo reported that the FARDC stated that a Burundian was arrested in Uvira for propaganda in favour of the M23/Red-Tabara, while another person is accused of espionage activities.
claims.verification_note: Exact match. Kinshasa-presentation context removed from the statement because the excerpt does not carry it (it is in claim 9); date narrowed because the arrest is undated. Excerpt_en flag: capitalised words are translations (FARDC/Burundian), nothing added. C. FARDC account only. The page gives no arrest date; it reports the claim in the context of the FARDC's 3 Jan 2026 press presentation in Kinshasa (separate claim). Accused, not charged. 2026-10-29: date_precision edited: red-team rt-r9-3 note: the arrest is undated; precision 'day' overstated it.
claims.researcher_note: The presentation itself is already recorded (r9-V-UV2-001/003 from Radio Okapi). This adds the Uvira arrest detail. Arrest date not given on the page. FARDC account only; no Rwandan, Burundian or detainee account found.

claims.text: Afrique Diplo reported that on Saturday 3 January 2026 in Kinshasa the Congolese army presented to the press seven soldiers it identified as members of the Rwanda Defence Force and eight foreign civilians, arrested during recent fighting against the AFC/M23 in North Kivu and South Kivu.
claims.place_as_written: Kinshasa (presentation); North Kivu and South Kivu (arrests)
claims.verification_note: Exact match; statement keeps 'it identified'. Excerpt_en flag: capitalised words are translations (Rwanda Defence Force, North/South Kivu). C. FARDC account; identification as RDF members is the army's. No Rwandan response found in this unit.
claims.researcher_note: Repeats an event already recorded from Radio Okapi (r9-V-UV2-001); FARDC account only. Rwanda's response not found in this unit's searches.

claims.text: IGIHE, a Rwandan state-aligned outlet, reported that RFI had announced on 8 April 2026 that the ICRC was ready to take 'these soldiers' to Kinshasa but that the DRC government had not yet agreed to receive them for fear that they might include 'enemies'.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo (Rutshuru, North Kivu), where IGIHE says the soldiers are held; Kinshasa
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (holding the soldiers); DRC government (reported reluctance)
claims.verification_note: Retained user copy prints the excerpt verbatim (byline Jean de Dieu Tuyizere, 8 Mata 2026). Partisan relay: C. Excerpt_en flag: capitalised words are translations (Radio France Internationale, DRC). IGIHE is a Rwandan state-aligned outlet relaying RFI; the RFI original was not found. Elsewhere on the page IGIHE says the soldiers are about 5,000 held at Rumangabo whom AFC/M23 said on 8 March 2026 it would hand to the ICRC. Kinshasa's own position not found. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-r9-3: Counter-account left out: the same retained page carries RFI's quote from an unnamed person close to Tshisekedi questioning why AFC/M23 is pushing. That is the only Kinshasa-side voice and belongs in the statement. The 5,000 figure and Rumangabo are IGIHE's (partisan) and are now marked as such. One search for the RFI original ('RFI CICR militaires Rumangabo Kinshasa "ennemis"') found nothing; the relay stays single-origin. (Orchestrator: the 5,000 figure, Rumangabo and the counter-voice are on the page but not in the stored excerpt, so they are left out of the statement; only the outlet label is amended.)
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan state-aligned outlet, partisan on this: cite only as 'IGIHE reported'. IGIHE relays RFI; the RFI original was not found in searches (rfi.fr query returned nothing). The AFC/M23 announcement itself is already in the store (r9-V-NK2-027, 2 Mar 2026 per Actualite.cd) and Kigali Today (8 Mar) carries the same; IGIHE's own 8 March date is its own statement. Kinshasa's own position not found. Context from the same article, not in the excerpt: the soldiers are about 5,000 men whom AFC/M23 said on 8 March 2026 it would hand to the ICRC, held at Rumangabo military camp.

claims.text: Xtrafrica published a transcript-style account of an RFI interview in which DRC government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said that, according to Kinshasa, the invasion of Uvira was organised under Kigali's direct command and that bombs and kamikaze drones were used indiscriminately against peaceful civilians.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC (Patrick Muyaya) about Rwanda
claims.verification_note: Retained user copy prints the passage; replacement quote extended to start at the speaker label so the name is in the excerpt. Date narrowed to what the page supports. C. Xtrafrica's page prints no date. The 1 July 2026 interview date and the 4 July 2026 publication date come from other pages (an RFI programme page and a search result), not from this page. Government's account; no Rwandan reply found.
claims.researcher_note: Page undated in its text; interview date 1 July 2026 is from the RFI programme page cited in r9-V-SK1-002 and the search result (xtrafrica 4 Jul 2026). Xtrafrica is a secondary relay; the ambulance-and-drones allegation in the same interview is already recorded (r9-V-SK1-002/003), so it is not repeated here. Rwanda's reply not found.

claims.text: IGIHE, a Rwandan state-aligned outlet, published an opinion piece alleging that, with Minembwe, Bijombo and Rurambo encircled, the Banyamulenge live in separate ghettos, with their freedom of movement denied and their activities subject to roadblocks, permanent police checks, extortion and regular abuses 'up to murder', citing that of 'the young Singaye Marebo at Murambya'. The passage does not say who killed him, when, or where Murambya is.
claims.place_as_written: Murambya, Minembwe area (Fizi / Mwenga / Uvira highlands), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed for the killing; the piece blames the Burundian army, directly or via FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR
claims.verification_note: Retained user copy prints the excerpt. Corrected: the draft's 'the piece blames the Burundian army' read as attribution of the killing, which the page does not make; the author's name (not in the excerpt) moved to the note; date narrowed. C. Partisan opinion piece (byline Tite Gatabazi, 13 Nov 2025): 'IGIHE reported' only. The piece's general conclusion holds the Burundian army responsible, directly or through FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR, for the blockade, but it does not attribute this killing to anyone or date it. No independent report found; not searched by name. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-r9-3: Place slippage and a homonym: the page does not locate 'Murambya'. It names it only in a passage on Minembwe, Bijombo and Rurambo (the last two are in the Uvira highlands, not Fizi), and the name is close to Muramvya in Burundi. The record's 'Minembwe area' and territory 'Fizi' go beyond the page; they should be the South Kivu highlands with the locality unconfirmed. One search for the name ('"Singaye" Murambya') returned only this IGIHE piece; no independent report was found. 2026-10-29: territory edited: red-team rt-r9-3: Place slippage and a homonym: the page does not locate 'Murambya'. It names it only in a passage on Minembwe, Bijombo and Rurambo (the last two are in the Uvira highlands, not Fizi), and the name is close to Muramvya in Burundi. The record's 'Minembwe area' and territory 'Fizi' go beyond the page; they should be the South Kivu highlands with the locality unconfirmed. One search for the name ('"Singaye" Murambya') returned only this IGIHE piece; no independent report was found. 2026-10-29: date_precision edited: red-team rt-r9-3: Place slippage and a homonym: the page does not locate 'Murambya'. It names it only in a passage on Minembwe, Bijombo and Rurambo (the last two are in the Uvira highlands, not Fizi), and the name is close to Muramvya in Burundi. The record's 'Minembwe area' and territory 'Fizi' go beyond the page; they should be the South Kivu highlands with the locality unconfirmed. One search for the name ('"Singaye" Murambya') returned only this IGIHE piece; no independent report was found.
claims.researcher_note: Partisan opinion piece, 'IGIHE reported' only. It does not mention Bijombo on 17 June 2025 or a video, so it does not corroborate cluster C-UV-15's 17 June 2025 date; it only prints the name and says 'assassinat' at Murambya, with no date. The ed. cluster (boy persecuted at Bijombo) and this killing at Murambya may or may not be the same person: unresolved. No independent report found. Not searched by name (possible minor).

claims.text: IGIHE, a Rwandan state-aligned outlet, reported that Burundian army spokesperson General Gaspard Baratuza, in a radio interview with BBC Gahuza, mentioned the presence of FNL and Red Tabara fighters at Minembwe.
claims.actor_as_written: Burundi National Defence Force (spokesperson Gen. Gaspard Baratuza)
claims.verification_note: Retained user copy prints both excerpts. Corrected: the author's rebuttal is not in either excerpt, so it moved to the note; date narrowed (the page does not date the interview). Excerpt_en flag: 'Burundi Defence Forces' translates 'Forces de défense du Burundi'. C. Second-hand, hostile characterisation in an opinion piece; the interview date is not printed (piece dated 13 Nov 2025). Elsewhere on the page the author disputes the claim ('il n'existe ni Red Tabara ni FNL établis à Minembwe'). Seek the original BBC Gahuza interview for the speaker's own words.
claims.researcher_note: Second-hand and hostile characterisation; the interview date is not stated on the page (the piece is dated 13 Nov 2025). The original BBC Gahuza interview should be sought for the speaker's own words. The same piece alleges 70+ Burundian positions on the Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira highlands; that allegation is not recorded as a claim from this partisan source.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to the communication cell of the North Kivu governorate, the operating theatre of the Sake Afya referral health centre (CSR) in Masisi territory had been ransacked and vandalised during the latest clashes in the area, making surgical interventions almost impossible; the article does not say who damaged it. It reported that the vice-governor of North Kivu, Schadrack Amani, of the Front pour la refondation de la Nation (FRN), handed over medical equipment for the centre's maternity and operating theatre on Tuesday 27 October 2026.
claims.place_as_written: Sake Afya referral health centre (Centre de Santé de Référence Sake Afya), Sake, Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FRN North Kivu governorate (communication cell), as reported
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Removed the inserted '(FRN-run)' label for the governorate, which the page does not print as such (it names the vice-governor as FRN); 'the governorate's vice-governor' changed to 'vice-governor of North Kivu' as printed. The note's claim that the page later calls Amani 'gouverneur' was not seen in the retained text. Flag on source 1 excerpt_en is the capitalised 'Tuesday/North Kivu' translation; translation matches the excerpt. The damage account is the governorate's (a de facto authority under the FRN, per the page's naming of the vice-governor's affiliation). The date is the handover date; the damage date is not given. Kivu Morning Post is Goma-based.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-NK-01. The pro-AFC/M23 post alleges looting by Wazalendo before the FRN took Sake; this page attributes the damage to no one and says only 'derniers affrontements' per the governorate (a de facto authority, so the damage account is that party's). The page calls Amani 'vice-gouverneur' in the first paragraph and 'gouverneur' in a later one. Kivu Morning Post is a Goma-based outlet now operating under FRN control (note for the reviewer). Date is the handover date; the damage date is not given.

claims.text: Insecurity Insight's October 2025 DRC incident-monitoring brief listed, as a publicly reported and unverified incident, that on 27 October 2025 the Sake Afia health centre in Bikali neighbourhood, Sake town, Masisi territory, was stormed by armed men dressed in military uniforms who took everything before fleeing during a night attack on the area.
claims.place_as_written: Sake Afia health centre, Bikali neighbourhood, Sake, Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed men in military uniforms (as the brief states)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact in the PDF (North Kivu section). Statement matches, including the unverified caveat printed on the page. Grade lowered from B to C: the brief compiles publicly reported, unverified incidents and gives no underlying source. Source date placeholder must be corrected to month precision (2026-01) via source_edits; no day is printed. Insecurity Insight states its listed incidents have not been verified through ground investigations, and does not name its source for this item. Source publication date: January 2026 (month only; 2026-01-01 is a placeholder).
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-NK-01 (related, not the same incident: the post concerns looting of the operating theatre by Wazalendo at an unstated date). 'Sake Afia' is the brief's spelling of Sake Afya. The brief says its incidents are publicly reported and not verified; it does not name its underlying source for this item. Source date: the PDF is stored under a January 2026 upload path (exact publication day not on the page), so 2026-01-01 is a placeholder for 2026-01.

claims.text: Kinpressactu reported that the human rights organisation Dynamique Génération Consciente (DYGENEC-RDC) raised an alert on Monday 12 October 2026 that four young fishermen had reportedly been found dead in Lake Kivu at Goma and a fifth was missing, and denounced alleged executions involving armed elements of the AFC/M23. According to DYGENEC-RDC, the four were Ombeni Dunia Patrick, Chrispin Cuma, Ishara Bunaza and Emmanuel Cikuru, and their bodies were taken to the morgue of the Goma general hospital; the fifth, Adili Banza Julien, had not been found. DYGENEC-RDC said colleagues of the victims told it the five men had reportedly been tied up and thrown into Lake Kivu on the night of Saturday 10 to Sunday 11 October 2026, and that two more bodies had reportedly been found on Monday morning at the Étoile du Kivu boat port. Kinpressactu said these elements, the alleged circumstances of the deaths and the alleged involvement of armed elements required independent verification.
claims.place_as_written: Lake Kivu shore, Goma (Étoile du Kivu boat port), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 armed elements (as alleged by DYGENEC-RDC)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Restored the conditionals the page uses ('auraient été retrouvés', 'auraient été ligotés', 'auraient été découverts'); victim statuses changed from 'killed' to 'found dead (per DYGENEC-RDC)' since the deaths' cause is DYGENEC's allegation; added the page's morgue detail with its passage. excerpt_en flags are capitalised words (DYGENEC names) and the translations match the excerpts. An advocacy organisation's unverified account; Kinpressactu itself says the circumstances and responsibility are not established and that the CongoRassure case (Crispin Chuma) may not be part of the same series. Spellings Chrispin Cuma (DYGENEC) and Crispin Chuma (CongoRassure) are kept as printed.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-NK-05. Pro-DRC posts relay DYGENEC-RDC; this claim is DYGENEC's account as carried by Kinpressactu (Kinshasa). The fifth name is 'Adili Banza Julien' on this page; the posts print 'Adili Banza Jules' (beto.cd also prints Julien). Another account (CongoRassure) reports one body, named Crispin Chuma, found on the Sunday morning (see next claim); Kinpressactu itself says the cases may not all be the same series. No AFC/M23 or urban-authority statement was found (beto.cd of 12 Oct 2026 says none had been reported).

claims.text: CongoRassure reported that the body of a young man in his thirties, identified as Crispin Chuma, resident of the Les Volcans quarter in Goma commune, was pulled from Lake Kivu at the Goma port on the morning of Sunday 11 October, with, according to local sources, his feet and hands tied and marks of strangulation and torture. According to testimony gathered on the spot, he had been returning home on Saturday evening around 20:30 with two friends, singing a song deemed hostile to the M23/AFC rebellion; pursued by armed men assimilated to the M23, his two friends reportedly fled, while Crispin Chuma was reportedly arrested and taken to an unknown destination, and his body was found floating the next morning.
claims.place_as_written: Goma port, Lake Kivu, Goma, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed men assimilated to the M23 (as reported by witnesses)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. The draft dropped the conditionals ('seraient parvenus', 'aurait été interpellé') and stated he 'was pursued ... and was seized'; the page says the friends were pursued and he was reportedly arrested and taken to an unknown destination. Corrected 'M23 rebellion' to 'M23/AFC rebellion' as printed. Status 'killed' changed to 'found dead'. Single local outlet relaying local sources and witnesses; the arrest is reported in the conditional and the page does not say who took him.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-NK-05 (possibly the same series as the DYGENEC list, where the name is spelled 'Chrispin Cuma'; Kinpressactu says the information does not confirm that all reported cases are the same). CongoRassure is a local outlet; Jules Ngeleza, president of the Goma communal youth council, is quoted denouncing 'un énième cas'. The two Chuma/Cuma spellings are kept as each source prints them.

claims.text: The Committee to Protect Journalists reported that on 19 September 2025, intelligence agents with the M23 and AFC rebel groups detained Ricardo Olenga, a reporter with the privately owned Radio Kako FM, at their Goma office, according to local media and two journalists who spoke to CPJ anonymously; it said the groups detained him for sharing a video that discussed alleged abuses by the two groups, that he is accused of spreading false news, and, according to those sources, that he was transferred on 23 October to Goma's Munzenze central prison. CPJ said its request for comment to M23 spokesperson Willy Ngoma received no response.
claims.place_as_written: Goma, North Kivu (AFC/M23 intelligence office; Munzenze central prison)
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and AFC intelligence agents (as CPJ reports)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; year 2025 printed in the dateline (source 1). Narrowed attribution of the Munzenze transfer to 'those sources' as the page does, rather than CPJ's own statement.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-NK-07. Posts of 20 Oct 2025 allege detention since 19 Sept 2025 without visits for publishing a video of a mother protesting her child's detention; CPJ confirms the arrest, the video and the accusation of false news. Other Congolese reports (Mashariki RDC, 20 Sept 2025) give the arrest day as 'samedi 19 septembre 2025'; 19 Sept 2025 was a Friday, so the weekday in that report is inconsistent and the date 19 Sept is taken from CPJ and RSF. Mashariki RDC (Bukavu-area local outlet, not cited) has the same arrest report.

claims.text: Reporters Without Borders (RSF), in a March 2026 report on journalists in the Great Lakes region, said Ricardo Olenga, a Kako FM radio contributor, was arrested by the M23 in Goma on 19 September 2025 and detained until 17 November in unsanitary conditions, after the station's YouTube channel and TikTok account broadcast a video in which a member of the public deplored conditions since the M23 takeover.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact in the PDF (report dated March 2026 on its cover page). Statement matches; RSF attributes the arrest to 'the M23' only, as the claim does. AFP credits in the PDF are photo credits, not for this entry.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-NK-07. Gives the release date (17 Nov 2025), which the 2026-06-06 post (not cited) implies. RSF's text does not mention the alleged order to dispose of two prisoners' bodies at Lac Vert; that allegation (Olenga's testimony as relayed by a pro-DRC account) was not found in any fetched page. Actualite.cd (28 Mar 2026) also lists Olenga as detained nearly two months in 2025 (spelled 'Kalo FM'); not cited.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Bulenda Siliro, 74, an avenue chief in the Lac Vert quarter of Goma, was killed on Tuesday 16 September after being kidnapped with his son; the Lac Vert quarter chief, Dedesi Mitima, told the outlet the kidnapping took place between 12 and 13 September, that the family paid the full ransom but only the son was released (reaching Mugunga on the morning of 17 September), and that Bulenda Siliro was shot dead anyway.
claims.place_as_written: Lac Vert quarter, Goma, North Kivu (son released at Mugunga)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; statement matches the page, including attribution to the quarter chief. 16 September 2025 was a Tuesday, consistent with the article date. excerpt_en flags are capitalised words (Lac Vert / Kivumorningpost); translations match. Single local outlet; no perpetrator named (the page says only 'ravisseurs'). Year from the article date (17 September 2025).
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-NK-08 (the post is a Kivu Morning Post item). Single local source; no perpetrator named. The article also mentions an earlier killing in the same quarter (Mbangu Shabanyere Germain, youth president) with no date. RSF's report mentions a different journalist case involving 'the suspicious disappearance of a community chief, blamed on the M23'; not shown to be this one. Kivu Morning Post is Goma-based.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that a group of at least ten men escaped mob justice on Wednesday 17 September 2025 in the Kalinda quarter of Mulekera commune, Beni city, after residents suspected and apprehended them; according to its sources the men, all from Ituri, were assimilated to M23-AFC rebels. It said the Congolese National Police intervened to save them and that the Mulekera mayor, Commissaire supérieur principal Ngongo Mayanga Dieudonné, said the competent services were questioning the suspects. Challenge Info quoted Ngongo Mayanga as saying it could not yet be confirmed whether they were rebels and that investigations were under way.
claims.place_as_written: Kalinda quarter, Mulekera commune, Beni city, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: residents of Kalinda (mob); Congolese National Police intervened
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; two local outlets independently report the event. Narrowed 'told Challenge Info' to 'Challenge Info quoted' (the page says 'a-t-il déclaré', not that he spoke to the outlet); the police intervention is KMP's narration and is now attributed to the outlet, not the mayor.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-NK-08 (second item in the post; the Goma killing is a separate claim). Two local outlets agree. A second Kivu Morning Post article of the same date says the suspects were released after being questioned (headline: 'libérés après identification par les autorités'); another KMP item says the governor condemned the assault on persons assimilated to the M23. Not cited.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that Prosper Kimanuka Musekura, chief of Kiziba 2 village in Nyiragongo territory, was killed in the night from Monday to Tuesday 11 February with all the members of his family: armed bandits entered his home and opened fire, killing the chief, his wife and his three children, a boy and two girls. It said the perpetrators were not known and that civil society actors in Nyiragongo suspected a settling of scores resembling a targeted assassination. A second outlet, whose Kiziba II article is the second source cited here, reported that Kimanuka Musekura Prosper, chief of Kiziba II village in Mudja groupement, was killed in the night of Monday 10 to Tuesday 11 February 2025 with his wife and three children by heavily armed unknown persons, named the children as his son Benjamin and his daughters Sifa and Iragi, and said the five bodies were taken to a local morgue.
claims.place_as_written: Kiziba 2 village, Mudja groupement, Nyiragongo territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed bandits / unidentified heavily armed men (as the sources say)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. The draft merged the two outlets' dates ('Monday 10 ... 2025' is 7sur7's wording; Radio Okapi prints 'lundi à ce mardi 11 février'); each date now sits with its outlet, and 'settling of scores' restored. The figure flag '7' is from the outlet name 7sur7.cd, not a figure. Two independent outlets (Radio Okapi, 7sur7.cd) agree on the killing of the chief, wife and three children: grade A. Note Actualite.cd (claim 9) counts four dead without the wife.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-NK-09. The post spells the village 'Kibiza II' and the daughter 'Safi'; the outlets print 'Kiziba 2/II' and 'Sifa'. Two outlets agree on wife and three children; Actualite.cd's account (next claim) counts four dead and does not mention the wife. Date: night 10-11 Feb 2025, within days after M23's capture of Goma; the area was then under M23 control, but no source attributes the killing to any armed group. The 7sur7 excerpt is cited as two passages of the same page.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the chief of Kiziba 2 village in Mudja groupement, Nyiragongo territory, was killed with his three children in the night of Monday to Tuesday 11 February 2025; according to its sources unidentified armed bandits entered the victims' home around 1:00 and fired on them. A relative speaking anonymously said four people had been killed for reasons not yet elucidated, that no one could say who committed the act, and that Prosper Kimanuka Musekura was among the dead.
claims.place_as_written: Kiziba 2 village, Mudja groupement, Nyiragongo territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: unidentified armed bandits (as the source says)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; the 2025 year is from the article's date line (mar 11/02/2025). Statement matches; the relative's anonymity is printed on the page. Actualite.cd counts four dead (chief and three children) and does not mention the wife; Radio Okapi and 7sur7.cd say five, including the wife. The page also notes Nyiragongo had been occupied by 'M23/RDF' since late January 2025 but attributes the killing to no one.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-NK-09. Differs from Radio Okapi and 7sur7.cd on the wife (not mentioned here; the quoted relative says four dead). Kept as a separate claim for that reason.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that four people were killed and several wounded in an armed attack on a pharmacy in the Katoyi quarter of Goma on the evening of Friday 16 May 2025, around 19:00 on Makengele avenue near the Katindo mosque; it said men in uniform, not yet identified, burst in and opened fire, killing the pharmacist and three of his customers, and took an unspecified sum of money and telephones. A resident of Maranatha avenue told the outlet the shooting was around 19:27.
claims.place_as_written: Makengele avenue, Katoyi quarter, near Katindo mosque (Maranatha avenue), Goma, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: men in uniform, not yet identified (as the source says)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; statement matches the page (including 'men in uniform, not yet identified'; no group named). Grade B: one credible national outlet with its own resident witness, per the rubric's 'one credible non-partisan origin'.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-NK-10. Matches the posts (19:27, four dead, pharmacist and clients) though the outlet places it in Katoyi on Makengele avenue near the Katindo mosque rather than at the mosque entrance in Maranatha. No group is named; the page says only that Goma is 'sous occupation de l'AFC/M23'. A pharmacist was among those killed; the pharmacy is a private shop, not a hospital, so this is not coded as an attack on a health facility. No second outlet found.

claims.text: Enquete.cd reported that a 25-year-old man, missing since his arrest on 4 September 2025 in Goma, had been found dead and buried, according to information given to his relatives on 8 August. According to the testimony relayed by civil society actor and human rights defender Jules Ngeleza, Chubaka Buhendwa Josué Maroy had been arrested on alleged accusations of collaborating with the FDLR, and his arrest was reportedly carried out on the order of Sultani Makenga, military head of the M23. The outlet said the family said it learned of his death and burial from a security officer of the movement.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 (as alleged by relatives and civil society)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Removed the year in '8 August 2026' (the excerpt prints only '8 août dernier'; the article is dated 10 August 2026), kept the conditional 'reportedly', and attributed the family's account as the page does. Allegation by relatives and a civil society actor; the order by Sultani Makenga is reported in the conditional. No M23 response found.
claims.researcher_note: Found while searching C-NK-11/12 (Goma, Sept 2025 arrests and later body discoveries); not one of the cluster incidents. Allegation by relatives and a civil-society actor; the M23 response was not found. The same article says that in June 2026 two bodies were found in Lake Kivu amid residents' allegations of executions, and that the Goma communal youth council denounced bodies and abductions in June 2026.

claims.text: Challenge Info reported that an agent in charge of dignified and safe burials in the Ebola response was violently assaulted on Wednesday 19 August 2026 in the city of Beni while recovering the body of a person presumed to have died of Ebola; Enquête News (enquetenews.info) reported that the agent of the response team against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola was assaulted at Kasanga-Tuha, Beni, and, according to testimonies, would have been confronted by youths present at the place of death; DW summarised that a response agent had been violently assaulted in Beni.
claims.place_as_written: Kasanga-Tuha neighbourhood (Kasanga Tuha), Beni city, North Kivu
