claims.actor_as_written: youths present at the place of death (as reported by Enquête News); not otherwise attributed
claims.verification_note: All three pages print what is attributed; Challenge Info page also prints 'récupérer le corps d’une personne présumée décédée d’Ebola'. Enquête News keeps the conditional ('aurait été pris à partie').
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-02 (video lead; posts not cited). Date of the Beni assault is printed in the Challenge Info and Enquête News texts (Wednesday 19 August 2026). The post said around 19/20 August. No existing claim on Ebola response attacks in Beni found with claim_search.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that on 19 August 2026 at about 09:00 a Red Cross team deployed for awareness and intervention activities in the Kasanga Tuha neighbourhood, Mulekera commune, Beni, was confronted by the population, who according to witnesses accused the humanitarian team amid a high number of reported deaths; a Red Cross agent identified as Querrin was assaulted but reportedly came out "sain et sauf", and the toll also lists three other victims receiving care at the Beni General Referral Hospital.
claims.place_as_written: Kasanga Tuha, Mulekera commune, Beni city, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause on the page; name 'Querrin' printed; possibly the same incident as claim 0 told differently, kept separate.
claims.researcher_note: Same neighbourhood and date as the Challenge Info / Enquête News assault (possibly the same incident described differently: Red Cross team vs. burial agent). Not merged. Kivu Morning Post is a Goma-based outlet.

claims.text: Enquête.cd reported that youths attacked and stoned on Monday 24 August a morgue of a health facility in Beni, North Kivu, before forcibly extracting a body, at a time when the DRC faces an Ebola epidemic; RTEE Kivu reported that a group of youths forced their way on Monday 24 August 2026 into the morgue of the Centre médical Ruwenzori in Beni and took away a body, and that according to first information they reportedly removed it without respecting the planned sanitary formalities.
claims.place_as_written: Centre médical Ruwenzori, Beni city, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: RTEE prints the 'sans respecter les formalités sanitaires' clause as conditional on first information ('auraient'); narrowed to keep the hedge.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-03. The post date (24 August 2026) matches both outlets. Dr Katembo Ngalika (ACP) says this was the third attack on this morgue since the outbreak began; see the following claim. Local outlets: RTEE Kivu (Beni), Enquête.cd.

claims.text: ACP (Agence Congolaise de Presse) reported that Dr Katembo Ngalika, medical director of the Centre médical Ruwenzori in Beni, said that youths came with brutality, broke doors and windows, and that the two people in the morgue were intimidated and beaten, and that the youths took the body in violation of the response norms; he said it was the third attack on this morgue since the start of the Ebola epidemic in the region and that no particular security arrangement had been put around the clinic despite alerts.
claims.place_as_written: Centre médical Ruwenzori, Beni city, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Statement unchanged; excerpts extended so that the 'violation des normes de la riposte' and 'absence de dispositif sécuritaire' clauses rest on stored text. Director's own account via state agency ACP.
claims.researcher_note: ACP is the Congolese state press agency; the account is the facility director's. Adds to the previous claim (same event).

claims.text: Enquête.cd reported that the military governor of North Kivu, Major General Evariste Somo Kakule, had recently warned that anyone who obstructed Ebola response operations or attacked the agents mobilised would be severely punished.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC (North Kivu military governor)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries the whole statement; date of the warning not given ('récemment').
claims.researcher_note: Relayed warning; date not given in the excerpt.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that a viral video shows Beni youths armed with bladed weapons manhandling Ebola response agents, one victim being a woman seen receiving blows from sticks.
claims.actor_as_written: youths of Beni (as shown in a video described by Radio Okapi)
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date added to the statement (not in the excerpt); incident date unknown.
claims.researcher_note: Describes a video as reported by Radio Okapi; date of the incident not given; related precedent to the August incidents.

claims.text: La Voix de l'UCG (lavoixdelucg.cd) reported that, according to Dr Kalima Nzanzu, president of the cell of doctors of the Grand Nord, pillaging in some hospitals, displacement of health staff and abandonment of patients, notably those with mental disorders, made an alarming picture; he said many doctors who worked in referral health centres and hospitals were now displaced in Butembo without work, that these centres were closed and, though deserted, had been pillaged, and he named the centres of Luofu and Muhangi and said the situation at Alimbongo was even more critical.
claims.place_as_written: Luofu, Muhangi, Alimbongo (Lubero territory) and Butembo, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: ADF and M23 conflict (as framed by the source); pillagers not identified
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement; S1 extended to the doctor's opening sentence (the 'many doctors from referral centres' clause). Statement given at a medical day in Butembo 'ce dimanche' (page, 23 January 2025). Perpetrators of the pillaging not named. The pillagers are not identified; the outlet frames the crisis as caused by ADF massacres and the M23 war.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-04. The original report dates from 23 January 2025 (statement made at a medical day held on a Sunday in Butembo); the video-lead post of 10 February 2025 repeats it. Same author (Georges Kisando) as the X post. Related existing records REC-0951 and REC-1242 concern the 15 January 2025 ADF killing at Muhangi and fighting at Luofu, not the health structures. No independent second outlet fetched (rtvh.net page blocked/empty; MSF 16 Jan 2025 on Lubero not fetched).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local humanitarian organisations, that at least ten people were abducted, two others killed and several goods pillaged between Tuesday and Wednesday 24 June in Rutshuru territory, in at least six localities; on Wednesday morning at least seven people were abducted between 9h and 10h on the Kibirizi–Rwindi (at Butindiri) and Kibirizi–Kibingu road axes, among them three motorcycle-taxi drivers and their clients, and the attackers also took at least eighteen packages of fish from Vitshumbi; the perpetrators of these abductions remained unknown.
claims.place_as_written: Kibirizi–Rwindi axis (Butindiri) and Kibirizi–Kibingu axis, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed the year the excerpt does not print; 'perpetrators unknown' narrowed to the abductions as the page says ('auteurs de ces enlèvements'). The two killed are, per the page, a woman and child hit by stray bullets in AFC-M23/FDLR clashes (not in excerpts, so not stated).
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-13. The pro-AFC/M23 post attributes the abductions to FDLR, FARDC and Wazalendo and mentions ransom releases; Radio Okapi attributes them to nobody and does not mention ransom. The date of the weekday (Wednesday 24 June) is stated by the article ("mardi et mercredi 24 juin"). Existing records REC-0900 (Bwito, July-August 2026) and r1-NKS-2025Q4-007 (19 Dec 2025 on the same axis) are different incidents.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the mining town of Rubaya (Masisi territory) was hit on the night of Saturday 23 to Sunday 24 May 2026 by several explosions attributed by residents to military aircraft; a first strike allegedly targeted a hotel facility known as Rubaya's Guest House, causing several injuries and significant property damage according to local sources, and a second strike allegedly hit an outlying grazing area, destroying several homes and causing livestock losses; local civil society denounced shelling affecting inhabited areas far from the front lines.
claims.actor_as_written: military aircraft (attribution by residents; not further specified by the source)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts carry every clause with the source's hedges ('allegedly', 'according to local sources'); no toll printed (the 189 figure from the lead is unsupported). Adds to r1-ATR-NK-2026-006 (Radio Okapi), not a duplicate.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-14. ALREADY RECORDED: r1-ATR-NK-2026-006 (Radio Okapi, 25 May 2026: strike around 00:15 on a guest house in Rubaya, origin undetermined, claimed by no party). This claim adds injuries, the second strike and civil-society reaction. The pro-AFC/M23 claim of 189 civilians killed is NOT supported by either source (no death toll printed). SOS Médias also notes the AFC/M23 statement of 24 May named Rumangabo, Minembwe and Kalehe (not Rubaya) and that no Congolese official response had been published; "The information advanced by the various parties could not be independently verified."

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that in a statement issued on 24 May the AFC/M23 accused the DRC Armed Forces and their allies of conducting air strikes in North Kivu and South Kivu, claiming that Rumangabo (Rutshuru) and the Virunga National Park eco-guards camp were targeted by CH-4 drones, and recalling bombings in Minembwe and Kalehe causing civilian casualties; the AFC/M23 described the operations as "war crimes". SOS Médias added that at the time of publication no official response from the Congolese authorities had been made public and that the information could not be independently verified.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (statement); accused: DRC Armed Forces and allies
claims.verification_note: Party account kept as 'AFC/M23 accused/claims'; 'war crimes' is the party's quoted wording. Different relay from r1-NKS-2026Q2-007, adds Minembwe/Kalehe and the no-response note.
claims.researcher_note: AFC/M23 party account. Overlaps r1-NKS-2026Q2-007 (Kivu Morning Post, Kanyuka statement on Rumangabo); this is an additional independent relay and records the absence of an official Kinshasa response as of 27 May 2026.

claims.text: Radio Elimu UOR (Butembo) reported that presumed ADF carried out a deadly incursion in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 6 May 2026 in Beni territory and that local civil society spoke of 24 people killed in the villages Manzungu, Musangwa, Wasafi and Mangambo (Babila-Bakaiku locality, Batangi-Mbau groupement, Beni-Mbau sector), according to KINOS KATUO; the vice-president of civil society in Oïcha commune, Samuel MAHAMBA, said 19 bodies had been counted at the morgue and feared the toll would rise; Enquête.cd reported at least 24 civilians killed in an attack attributed to the ADF, with bodies taken to the Oïcha morgue and others missing.
claims.place_as_written: Manzungu, Musangwa, Wasafi, Mangambo (Babila-Bakaiku, Batangi-Mbau), Beni territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Date and 'présumés ADF' are printed on the Radio Elimu page, not in the stored excerpt: S0 extended. Fear of a rising toll moved to a quote. Tolls kept per source (24 / 19 at the morgue / at least 24); Radio Okapi's 26 in r4-G-LOCAL-NK-008 is not merged (Radio Elimu's own 26 adds two killed at Katerrain on 4-5 May).
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-15. ALREADY RECORDED in r4-G-LOCAL-NK-008 (Radio Okapi, at least 26 killed, night of Tuesday to Wednesday 6 May, same farming blocks). The video-lead post says "night of 6-7 May"; the sources say the night of 5-6 May (Enquête.cd prints "la nuit du mercredi 6 mai"). The 24 figure is the civil-society count; 26 includes 2 killed at Katerrain the previous night per Radio Elimu. Radio Elimu adds that presumed ADF were also accused of killing two inhabitants of Katerrain on the night of 4-5 May ("26 morts en 2 jours"), not used in the statement.

claims.text: 24News Agency reported that an attack attributed to ADF fighters in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 3 June 2026 simultaneously targeted the Matete, Kitoho and Mamuli neighbourhoods of Mbau (Beni territory), killing at least sixteen civilians, burning houses and motorcycles and carrying off an undetermined number of people; at Matete the victims were surprised while taking part in a wake (veillée mortuaire), the attackers burned a hut and three motorcycles before killing people, and the toll in that neighbourhood reached nine; at least seven were killed at Kitoho.
claims.place_as_written: Matete, Kitoho, Mamuli neighbourhoods, Mbau, Batangi-Mbau, Beni territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpts carry every clause; 'attributed to' ADF kept. Weapons-in-mats detail from the lead not found and not included.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-16. The video-lead post (survivors) says ADF infiltrated a mourning gathering with weapons hidden in mats and killed about ten; 24News confirms the wake at Matete and a toll of at least 16 (9 at Matete); the detail about weapons hidden in mats was NOT found in any fetched source. Not previously recorded (claim_search on Mbau for May-June 2026 returned nothing). 24News Agency is a Congolese online outlet; the byline is Gires Kasongo.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, according to details given by local civil society on Thursday 4 June, the toll of the Mbau attack had risen from 16 to 21 dead after four bodies were found towards Kingeste and a fifth near Ngite, with several other civilians still missing; the page adds that in three days the ADF had killed more than 40 people in attacks on the city and territory of Beni and had taken several civilians hostage.
claims.place_as_written: Mbau (Kingeste, Ngite), Beni territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date added as 'reported on 4 June 2026'; the civil society update is dated 'jeudi 4 juin' in the excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Updated toll for the same event as the 24News claim.

claims.text: Congo Quotidien reported that an attack attributed to ADF rebels in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 3 June 2026 hit the localities of Matété, Mamuli and Kitoho (Batangi-Mbau groupement, Beni territory), causing the death of about ten people according to a provisional toll from local civil society; The Guardian wrote that at least 10 people were massacred in raids on those three villages and that the ADF has been blamed.
claims.place_as_written: Matété, Mamuli, Kitoho (Mbau), Batangi-Mbau groupement, Beni territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Punctuation fixed; tolls kept per source (about ten, provisional, civil society; at least 10, Guardian).
claims.researcher_note: The Guardian byline is Prosper Heri Ngorora in Goma; the Guardian page does not carry a wire credit. Early provisional toll; superseded by the 16 and 21 figures (see other Mbau claims).

claims.text: The Guardian reported that just before midnight on Saturday the militia entered Beni, where people were beheaded and others shot, causing widespread panic and sending hundreds of people running into the bush; more than 20 men, women and children were reported killed and dozens missing, according to witnesses.
claims.date: 2026-05-30 (date computed from weekday and publication date)
claims.actor_as_written: the militia (identified elsewhere in the article as the ADF)
claims.verification_note: Removed the article date the statement had added; the excerpt says only 'Saturday'. Ngandi appears on the page (not in the statement). The Guardian names the ADF elsewhere on the page; a resident calls it 'an attack carried out by the ADF'.
claims.researcher_note: Related event found while searching Mbau. 24News Agency (3 June) places the Beni city (Ngadi) massacres three days before Mbau; SOS Médias Burundi (1 June 2026, seen in results, not fetched) reported at least 17 civilians killed in under 24 hours. The "Saturday" is computed from the Guardian's publication date (Thursday 4 June 2026). No existing record found with claim_search.

claims.text: The Guardian reported that the military governor of North Kivu said in a statement on Tuesday that three patients confirmed to have Ebola had fled treatment centres in Beni after the Saturday attacks.
claims.date: 2026-06-02 (date computed from weekday and publication date)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries the whole statement.
claims.researcher_note: Health-care context: insecurity (ADF attack on Beni city) linked to patients leaving Ebola treatment centres.

claims.text: Labeur (labeur.info) reported that the Consortium International pour les Droits de l’Homme au Congo (CIDHC), in a report made public on Monday 4 May 2026, said it had documented civilians killed without investigation, citizens beaten to humiliation, and men and women arrested without warrant, detained without trial and released on payment; according to the CIDHC, at Walo Uruba (in the Kiraku locality) and at Shempunu, populations were allegedly beaten, locked up and forced to pay money on the pretext of not having shown a "salongo" token.
claims.place_as_written: Walo Uruba (Kiraku locality) and Shempunu, Walikale territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not named by the source (the CIDHC report, as relayed, blames abuse of administrative authority)
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; actor field corrected: the page names no perpetrator for these acts and does not say 'armed men in government-held Walikale' (the report says 'L’autorité administrative est utilisée pour fabriquer une faute').
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-21. Allegation by an NGO (CIDHC) about government-held Walikale; the pro-AFC/M23 post relayed it. The post spelled the locality "Walowa Uroba"; the page prints "Walo Uruba". The Goma-presentation detail and the name Jean-Paul Ngahangondi were not found on any fetched page. Kivu7.net and newsdrc.com versions could not be fetched. No response from authorities found.

claims.text: Labeur (labeur.info) reported that the CIDHC also deplored "un jeune brûlé vif à Byungu" (a youth burned alive at Byungu), without response, investigation or justice.
claims.verification_note: Removed the date 4 May 2026, which this claim's only excerpt does not print.
claims.researcher_note: Single NGO allegation; date of the killing not given.

claims.text: Labeur (labeur.info) reported that, according to the CIDHC, on the Goma–Masisi–Walikale road barriers erected by the FARDC, militiamen and Mai-Mai Wazalendo groups harass the population.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC, militiamen and Mai-Mai Wazalendo (as alleged by the CIDHC)
claims.verification_note: NGO allegation kept attributed ('according to the CIDHC').
claims.researcher_note: Allegation of illegal roadblocks and levies, by an NGO.

claims.text: Labeur (labeur.info) reported that the CIDHC condemned the case of Amani Bitahi Lucien, a civil society actor, arrested and deprived of his liberty 26 times for having denounced injustice and the poor conditions suffered by the inhabitants; the report as quoted gives no dates for the arrests and does not name who made them.
claims.verification_note: Typo fixed; name printed in the excerpt. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-r9-1: Time slippage risk: the 26 arrests are undated and likely cumulative over years (possibly pre-2025), while the claim's date range is the report's Jan-Apr 2026 window; the arresting authority is not named. Amended to say so; no search spent.
claims.researcher_note: Named per policy v1.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the CIDHC, in a report covering January to April 2026, described Walikale detention conditions as critical and said detainees are often forced to pay to access basic rights such as food, health care or even space in detention.
claims.actor_as_written: authorities in charge of detention (as implied by the CIDHC report); not named
claims.verification_note: NGO report relayed; both clauses in the excerpts.
claims.researcher_note: NGO report as relayed by Kivu Morning Post (Goma).

claims.text: Grands Lacs News reported that, on a visit to the Rumangabo training centre in Rutshuru territory at the weekend, General Sultani Makenga, head of the M23 armed branch, spoke with prisoners of war including former FARDC soldiers captured at the fall of Goma, and told them that anyone wishing to join the rebellion voluntarily was free to do so and that those wishing to return to Kinshasa could register under the prisoner-release process of the Doha process, to be facilitated with the ICRC. The page embeds an AFC/M23 post stating that the visit took place on Friday 2 January 2026.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo military training centre, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: S1 extended so the ICRC clause rests on stored text; date of the visit comes from the embedded AFC/M23 post, the article itself says 'le weekend dernier'. Statement unchanged otherwise.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-22. The page embeds a post of Lawrence Kanyuka (3 Jan 2026) giving the date Friday 2 January 2026; the page itself says "le weekend dernier". DISCREPANCY: the AFC/M23-aligned posts say the soldiers were "captured at Uvira"; this page says captured "lors de la chute de Goma" (January 2025). The outlet relays the AFC/M23 spokesperson; treat as the AFC/M23 account. Uvira was taken by AFC/M23 on 10 Dec 2025 per existing records.

claims.text: Mediacongo reported that human rights activist Jacques Sinzahera said soldiers who answered a call by Sultani Makenga at a meeting on 4 January 2026 live in extremely difficult conditions at Rumangabo, and alleged that at least two soldiers die every week for lack of medicine and food; he called on MONUSCO and the ICRC to start repatriating them.
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed (activist Jacques Sinzahera describes soldiers left at Rumangabo after a parade organised by the M23)
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; actor field narrowed: the activist describes soldiers abandoned at Rumangabo after an M23 parade but the deaths are not attributed to a named actor in the excerpts. Single activist's unverified allegation. Date is the article date (8 March 2026).
claims.researcher_note: A single activist's unverified allegation; the page text prints "Jacques Sinzahera" and dates the meeting 4 January 2026 (the AFC/M23 posts say 2 January). Congo Profond carries the same text (undated in the fetched copy).

claims.text: Enquête.cd reported that an inhabitant, in a testimony sent to journalist Daniel Michombero, denounced presumed summary executions attributed to the rebels and their Rwandan allies after two bodies were seen floating in Lake Kivu at the site known as "Bosco Lac" in Goma; according to the inhabitant, the victims were reportedly young men who had been arrested a few days earlier at their homes in the Ndosho neighbourhood by M23 elements. Enquête.cd added that the allegations could not be independently confirmed at the time of publication and that no official reaction from the M23/AFC had been recorded.
claims.place_as_written: Bosco Lac, Lake Kivu shore, Goma (Ndosho arrests), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: M23 and Rwandan military (as alleged by an anonymous inhabitant)
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date the statement added; a single anonymous inhabitant's allegation, kept attributed with the outlet's caveat. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-r9-2: The page puts the victims' identity in the conditional ('les victimes seraient de jeunes hommes') and the executions are 'présumées'; the statement asserted the victims 'were' young men. Restored the conditional and kept the outlet's caveats. One search ('"Bosco Lac" Goma corps') found a second outlet on the same discovery (CongoRassure, 11 June 2026: 'Le CCJ-Goma condamne la découverte macabre des corps... vers Bosco lac'), a lead for corroboration of the bodies (not of the perpetrators); no M23/AFC response found.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-30 related lead, NOT the Jay le Coq / Kinyogote testimony itself, which was found only in X posts (journalist Daniel Michombero, programme "Les voix de l'Est"). Same journalist; same theme (bodies in the lake). No fetched page mentions "Kinyogote" or "Jay le Coq".

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that Reporters sans frontières (RSF), in an investigation report published on Tuesday 24 March 2026, revealed inhuman detention places run by the rebel movement AFC-M23 in Goma, where at least two journalists were detained and tortured in ventilation-less metal containers; the page lists sites at the North Kivu provincial assembly (Himbi) and near Mont Goma by the RTNC, and a former detainee reportedly said up to 80 people could be packed into the containers.
claims.place_as_written: Goma, North Kivu (provincial assembly grounds, Himbi; near Mont Goma)
claims.verification_note: RSF report as relayed by Radio Okapi; findings stay attributed to RSF and a former detainee. Not a duplicate of r1-ATR-NK-2026-018 (that claim is a separate RSF alert of 24 April on one journalist); relation set to new_related_event.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates r1-ATR-NK-2026-018 (Actualite.cd relaying RSF). Context for the "Kinyogote" detention lead; "Kinyogote" itself not found. The AFC/M23 denial is the next claim.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, contacted by RSF, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka rejected the allegations about detention containers in Goma, calling them "informations totalement infondées" and "propagande", and said the movement makes no arrests of journalists.
claims.verification_note: Party denial as reported (via RSF); excerpt carries it.
claims.researcher_note: Party account (AFC/M23 denial).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 announced in a communiqué that it had once again handed over to the International Committee of the Red Cross more than 5 000 FARDC elements captured on different fronts, to be repatriated to Kinshasa under ICRC supervision, at a ceremony held on Monday 2 March 2026 at Rumangabo camp; Actualite.cd added that the rebels deplored Kinshasa's refusal to release their arrested comrades.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo camp, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Garbled final clause fixed: 'deplore' is Actualite.cd's narration of the rebels' position. S0 extended for the repatriation clause. Number is the AFC/M23's own, not verified.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-X-03. Party claim (AFC/M23 communiqué), not verified by the ICRC. Existing REC-0903 covers the August 2026 transfer of 15 detainees to the AFC/M23 under Doha, a different event. Kigali Today (8 March 2026) and IGIHE carry the same communiqué (KT Press tweets that "government for its part hasn't released any").

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that François Moreillon, head of the ICRC delegation in Kinshasa, reacted to the AFC/M23 communiqué by saying the ICRC had taken note of it and, as a neutral intermediary, stood ready to accompany such an operation with the agreement of all parties.
claims.verification_note: ICRC reaction quoted verbatim; does not confirm the number.
claims.researcher_note: Mediator/ICRC position; does not confirm the number.

claims.text: Journal de Kinshasa reported that on Thursday 12 March the Deputy Prime Minister for Defence, Guy Kabombo, received François Moreillon, head of the ICRC delegation in the DRC, to discuss the release of war detainees, which the page links to the AFC/M23 announcement from Rumangabo of the release of more than five thousand FARDC.
claims.verification_note: Removed the year, which the excerpts do not print; a meeting, not a public government statement on the number.
claims.researcher_note: Only the meeting is recorded; no government statement on the number of 5,000. Umuseke (Rwandan outlet, 20 March 2026) wrote that Congo "ntacyo yabivuzeho" (said nothing about it) — see next claim. The IGIHE piece ("Leta ya RDC yatinye kwakira abasirikare 5000 ...", Kinshasa feared receiving them) could not be fetched by the helper; that Rwandan-aligned claim is unverified.

claims.text: Umuseke (Rwanda) wrote that AFC/M23 had said it returned to Congo some 5000 soldiers and members of their families who had been stranded in the city of Goma, and that Congo "ntacyo yabivuzeho" (had said nothing about it).
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC (silence, as stated by Umuseke)
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date the statement added. Umuseke's assertion that Congo said nothing is the outlet's own, kept attributed.
claims.researcher_note: Rwandan privately-run outlet, aligned against Kinshasa; the absence of statement is its assertion. Journal de Kinshasa shows a Defence Minister-ICRC meeting on 12 March, so "nothing said" may refer only to a public statement on the 5000.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that at least 16 civilians were killed and five others reported missing on Wednesday 3 June 2026 in simultaneous attacks attributed to ADF-MTM rebels in Mbau sector (Kitoho, Matete and Mamuli localities), according to a provisional toll from Omar Kalisya, president of the Beni territory civil society; according to civil society the assailants split into three groups, the first attacking a wake (veillée mortuaire) in the Matete neighbourhood, the second striking Kitoho, and the third targeting wives of LENI police officers engaged in security operations at Matete, where according to first information two soldiers' wives and a baby were killed.
claims.place_as_written: Matete, Kitoho, Mamuli (Mbau sector), Beni territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: ADF-MTM rebels (as attributed by the source)
claims.verification_note: Every clause in the excerpts; 'attributed to ADF-MTM' and 'according to first information' kept. Tolls kept per source.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates the 24News Agency claim (wake at Matete). The detail that weapons were hidden in mats (video-lead post) is still unconfirmed. A survivor, Paluku Poshombili, is named in the page as a person who escaped (not a victim; not listed). "ADF-MTM" is the form this source prints.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that several farming entities of the village of Bapakombe-Bakondo in Beni (North Kivu) were attacked in the night of Saturday to Sunday 31 May by ADF rebels, that about twenty civilians, pygmies and Bantu, were victims, and that the Association nationale des victimes du Congo (ANVC) condemned the massacre of the Ngadi neighbourhood and demanded an independent international investigation.
claims.place_as_written: Bapakombe-Bakondo, Ngadi neighbourhood, Beni, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: ADF rebels (as attributed by Radio Okapi)
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date added to the statement. 'Une vingtaine de civils ... victimes' kept as 'victims' (title says about 20 dead).
claims.researcher_note: Same event as the Guardian claim on the Beni city attack (the Guardian says "just before midnight Saturday"; Radio Okapi: night of Saturday to Sunday 31 May; Guardian prints "Ngandi", Radio Okapi "Ngadi"). The excerpt is cut at the coordinator's name because the page text continues "estime que..."; the statement does not attribute any opinion to him. Not previously recorded.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that an attack by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters at dawn on Thursday 11 June left, as a provisional toll, at least three civilians killed and two houses burned in the Munzambayi cell, Boikene district, Ruwenzori commune, Beni; La Presse Africaine reported a provisional toll of three dead, said the attackers also burned houses and three motorbikes before withdrawing to the forest, and, citing several local sources, said motorbike-taxi drivers took to the streets to denounce the deterioration of security after the attack attributed to the ADF.
claims.place_as_written: Munzambayi cell, Boikene district, Ruwenzori commune, Beni city (Beni), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Narrowed: tolls marked provisional; the protest is attributed to 'plusieurs sources locales' as LPA does; LPA burned houses (no count) and three motorbikes. Perpetrator as the outlets name it (Actualite.cd asserts ADF; La Presse Africaine 'attribuée aux combattants des ADF'). Tolls are provisional. Neither page says bodies were carried to Beni centre.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-17. Video post alleged 2-3 killed and bodies marched to Beni centre; sources confirm the attack, the toll of 3 and a protest by motorbike-taxi drivers, but neither page says bodies were carried to the centre. Spelling variants Munzambayi / Munzambaye / Muzambayi (UNJHRO). Weekday Thursday 11 June matches the dateline. La Presse Africaine is a Congolese outlet (LPA-OP byline).

claims.text: Dépêche.cd reported that the provisional toll communicated by the army for the ADF-attributed attack on the morning of Thursday 11 June in Boikene district, Ruwenzori commune, Beni (the Munzambayi cell) was three civilians dead, one of them burned alive, and three homes burned; Lieutenant Marc Elongo, spokesperson of the Sukola 1 Grand Nord operations, said the assailants had bypassed 'the positions held strongly in depth by the FARDC-UPDF coalition'.
claims.place_as_written: Munzambayi cell, Boikene district, Beni city, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Narrowed: toll attributed to 'the army', not to Elongo; Elongo is credited only with the bypass quote. Army account. The page does not say the toll was given by Elongo personally; it says 'communiqué par l'armée'. The army toll (three houses) differs from Actualite.cd's (two houses).
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-17, army account. REC-1211 in the packet is the 30-31 May Ngadi attack, a different incident. The page also names Brigadier General Mugisa Joseph as commander of the units deployed and says the army will continue operations against 'ADF-MTN-ISCAP' (not used in the statement).

claims.text: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (UNJHRO) reported that on 11 June, in Muzambayi in the Boikene district of the city of Beni, at least three civilians were executed and several homes were destroyed by fire, prompting a protest by the local population.
claims.place_as_written: Muzambayi, Boikene district, Beni city, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Passage confirmed in the retained PDF (footnote 3 and the 'Mbau' paragraph of the June 2026 analysis); statement matches it. Source date 2026-06-12 is from the search index, not the document: the report covers June 2026, records incidents up to at least 12 June, and the file sits in a 2026-08 folder, so the publication date is not established (treat it as published after June 2026). UNJHRO does not name a perpetrator for this incident in this passage. Corroborates the 11 June Munzambayi/Boikene attack (claims 0-1); UNJHRO says 'several homes' and gives 'at least three' executed.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-17. Date on the source is from the search index (page header 12 Jun 2026) although the file sits in a 2026-08 folder; the passage is quoted with the PDF's own stray comma.

claims.text: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (UNJHRO) reported that on the night of 5-6 June, in Matiba, five civilians were summarily executed and a house was set on fire.
claims.place_as_written: Matiba, Mbau, Beni territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Passage confirmed in the retained PDF (footnote 3 and the 'Mbau' paragraph of the June 2026 analysis); statement matches it. Source date 2026-06-12 is from the search index, not the document: the report covers June 2026, records incidents up to at least 12 June, and the file sits in a 2026-08 folder, so the publication date is not established (treat it as published after June 2026). UNJHRO does not name a perpetrator for this incident in this passage.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-18. A pro-DRC post of 9 June said ADF killed 2 civilians and burned 3 motorbikes at Matiba and PK12 (Mbau sector). UNJHRO has Matiba with 5 executed and a house burned, and separately a 6 June ambush with 2 civilians killed and motorbikes burned (next claim): details differ from the post, so partly corroborated.

claims.text: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (UNJHRO) reported that on 6 June two civilians were killed in an ambush on the Mbau-Kamango axis in Kelekele, while at least two motorcycles were set on fire.
claims.place_as_written: Kelekele, Mbau-Kamango axis, Beni territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Passage confirmed in the retained PDF (footnote 3 and the 'Mbau' paragraph of the June 2026 analysis); statement matches it. Source date 2026-06-12 is from the search index, not the document: the report covers June 2026, records incidents up to at least 12 June, and the file sits in a 2026-08 folder, so the publication date is not established (treat it as published after June 2026). UNJHRO does not name a perpetrator for this incident in this passage.
claims.researcher_note: Clusters C-NK-18 and C-NK-19. This 6 June ambush (2 killed, motorbikes burned) resembles the Matiba/PK12 post of 9 June (2 killed, 3 motorbikes); it is not the 21 June PK13 ambush of C-NK-19, for which no report was found.

claims.text: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (UNJHRO) reported that on the night of 2-3 June in Mbau, in Beni territory, ADF combatants summarily executed at least 18 civilians, including women and children, and injured at least nine others.
claims.verification_note: Passage confirmed in the retained PDF; ADF named by UNJHRO. Checked the store: no verified claim on the 2-3 June Mbau attack. Source date 2026-06-12 is from the search index, not the document: the report covers June 2026, records incidents up to at least 12 June, and the file sits in a 2026-08 folder, so the publication date is not established (treat it as published after June 2026).
claims.researcher_note: Related to cluster C-NK-18 (Mbau sector). Not in the packet; check against existing records of the 2-3 June Mbau attack before promotion (TV5Monde headline of 2 June cited 21 dead in Beni attacks; not fetched).

claims.text: Imvahonshya (Rwanda) reported that Willy Manzi, the North Kivu deputy governor appointed by AFC/M23, confirmed on social media that an FDLR fighter known as Yoweri, nicknamed Tokyo, had been captured in fighting in Masisi; the outlet said news of his capture began circulating on social media on Friday 24 October 2025, when he was said to have been captured by AFC/M23 fighters.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts and page match; attribution to Manzi and to social-media reports kept as printed; 'FDLR' is in the page title. Rwandan state-aligned outlet relaying an AFC/M23 official; the capture is AFC/M23's account. The date is when news of the capture began circulating, not the capture date. No independent, Kinshasa or FDLR account found.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-23. Rwandan outlet (Imvahonshya); cited only for what the AFC/M23 official said. No independent (non-Rwandan, non-AFC/M23) report found; no Kinshasa or FDLR reaction found. The Igihe English page could not be fetched (page_text via=none).

claims.text: Imvahonshya reported that Willy Manzi, the North Kivu deputy governor appointed by AFC/M23, said on social media that Yoweri, alias Tokyo, together with others including Jean-Marie of the Nyatura group, Tiger and Ignace Dunia, had committed terrible crimes including rape, killings and the burning of countless houses; this is an allegation by an AFC/M23 official.
claims.place_as_written: Masisi, North Kivu (place of alleged crimes not stated in the quote)
claims.verification_note: Statement kept; date changed to the window in which the statement was made (news circulated from 24 Oct; article 26 Oct), since the page does not date Manzi's post. Unverified allegation by an AFC/M23 official, relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet; no date, place or victim is given for the alleged crimes. The '23' flag is from 'AFC/M23'.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-23. Unverified allegation by a party official; no dates, places or victims given. Umuseke (below) adds that the same allegations of rape, killing and burning of homes, especially against Tutsi in Burungu and Kibarizo in October 2023, were made by the outlet itself (pre-2025, not used).

claims.text: Umuseke (Rwanda) reported that an AFC/M23 fighter, Col. Samuel Nsabimana Mwendangabo, said Tokyo had been shot in the leg and then captured, and that he would first be treated; the colonel said he was captured 'aho bita i Muzimu'.
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; date changed from the publication date to the month, since the capture date is not stated. AFC/M23 officer's account via a Rwandan outlet. Umuseke places the capture in Masisi territory 'this week' (its own narration: 'Tokyo yafatiwe muri Teritwari ya Masisi muri Kivu ya Ruguru'); it also says AFC/M23 had not said what it would do with him.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-23. Rwandan outlet; statement attributed to the AFC/M23 officer. The same page says some residents disagreed that he should be treated, and that AFC/M23 had not yet said what it would do with him ('Kugeza ubu ntacyo AFC/M23 iravuga izakoresha uyu mugabo'). Pro-AFC/M23 video post carried the same alias.

claims.text: Dépêche.cd reported that FARDC military intelligence services announced in Beni the interception of a truck carrying several sacks of hemp and that, according to the Congolese army, the cargo allegedly belonged to an AFC-M23 commander identified as Zimurinda Innocent, based in Rutshuru territory.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC; AFC-M23 commander named by the army
claims.verification_note: Narrowed: the announcement is credited on the page to the military intelligence services, not to the Sukola 1 spokesperson; conditional 'appartiendrait' kept as 'allegedly'. The FARDC's allegation only ('appartiendrait'); no AFC/M23 reaction found. Existing r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-012 names a Colonel Innocent Zimurinda in the AFC/M23 command; identity not established by this page.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-24. The post (20 May) spelled the name 'Zimuhinda', said the driver named the owner, and said the commander was RDF/M23; the page spells it 'Zimurinda Innocent', does not mention Goma or the driver, and attributes the ownership claim to the army. Date: page dated 19 May 2026 and says 'mardi' (19 May 2026 is a Tuesday). No AFC/M23 reaction found.

claims.text: Dépêche.cd reported that the FARDC presented in Beni, on Tuesday, 'plusieurs personnes accusées de collaborer avec les rebelles de l'AFC-M23', among them Byamungu Zembezembe Jean-Pierre, from South Kivu, arrested in the Matongé district in central Beni; Matofali Bushu Arsène, described by the army as a member of the armed group FFPP/AP of Kabido; and a young woman, Kavira Léa, whom the military authorities say was recruited by Katembo Ndalieni, former mayor of Goma under the rebel administration.
claims.verification_note: Statement extended to the two other presented people listed in victims_named (each printed in an excerpt); the 'unverified' caveat moved to the note; spelling 'Matongé' as printed. The FARDC's account of a presentation of detainees: the accusations are the army's and unverified; no court, defence or AFC/M23 account found. Being named is not a finding of responsibility.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-24. Reported only from the army's presentation; no independent check of the accusations; no court or defence account found. The post spoke of 'alleged Rwandan spies'; the page speaks of alleged AFC-M23 collaborators. The article also mentions Paluku Kisaka Yereyere and Mapenzi Mike as contacts alleged by the army, and gives a long army description of Byamungu Zembezembe (Uvira 2023 candidate); not used in the statement.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that at least two civilians died on Friday 3 January 2025 in bombardments that hit homes in the Renga district of the Bweremana agglomeration, Masisi, and three others were wounded by shrapnel in Kashenda district; according to local civil society, the bombs were launched by the M23 from the lines of fighting against local 'wazalendo' fighters.
claims.place_as_written: Renga and Kashenda districts, Bweremana, Masisi territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page; statement keeps the toll as 'at least two' and the M23 attribution as civil society's. The attribution to the M23 is local civil society's, as the outlet reports it. The quoted civil-society president speaks of two women killed at Renga.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-29: the post (3 Jan) said M23-Wazalendo fighting on Ndumba hills near Bweremana and residents carrying two bodies of bomb victims; Actualite.cd corroborates. The 'at least two killed' is the outlet's figure; the quoted civil-society president speaks of two women killed and three injured at Renga plus 'three wounded' at Kashenda. Journal's own phrase: M23 'coalition M23/RDF' is used in the same article for 2 Jan assaults.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing the president of Bweremana civil society, that the M23 launched simultaneous attacks from 5 a.m. on wazalendo positions on several hills overlooking the Bweremana-Minova axis, including Ndumba, Kashingamutwe and Kabase.
claims.place_as_written: Ndumba, Kashingamutwe, Kabase hills, Bweremana-Minova axis, Masisi, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: The speaker's name is not printed in the stored excerpt ('Selon la même source'), so the statement names his role; the page passage naming him is in clause_support. Single local civil-society source; the speaker (Flory Musanganya) is named in the sentence before the excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-29. Single local civil-society source relayed by Actualite.cd. 'Selon la même source' refers to Flory Musanganya, named in the preceding sentence of the page.

claims.text: Ouragan.cd reported that, on the margins of the 61st session of the UN Human Rights Council, DRC Human Rights Minister Samuel Mbemba said at the rostrum that he counted more than 17 000 documented serious human rights violations, nearly 15 000 deaths and about eight million displaced.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page; statement adds nothing beyond them. Government figures as reported by Ouragan.cd; they cover eastern DRC (not only the Kivus) and differ from the figures in the social-media post that led to this search. The speech date is not given; the article is dated 6 March 2026.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-X-04: the post (28 Feb) said '17 015 morts en 12 mois', 'un viol toutes les 4 minutes', '30 000 esclaves modernes à Rubaya'. This article gives different headline figures (over 17,000 violations, nearly 15,000 deaths) and does not mention the rape frequency or Rubaya in the passage checked; the figures are not reconciled (discrepancy). The article's date line is 6 March 2026; the exact day of the speech is not stated. Earlier DRC government figures by Mbemba are in r1-UV-2026Q1-037 and r2-G-UV-CTRL-017.

claims.text: ChimpReports reported that the Tanzania People's Defence Forces (TPDF) said, in a statement by Col. Ilonda, that following consecutive attacks in the Sake and Goma areas on 24 and 28 January 2025 it had lost two of its soldiers while four others sustained injuries and were receiving treatment in Goma, and that all TPDF troops deployed in the DRC remain safe.
claims.verification_note: The excerpts print 'Col. Ilonda' only; first name 'Gaudentius' (on the page) moved out of the statement to clause_support. ChimpReports (published 3 Feb 2025) says Tanzania confirmed 'Sunday'; the date 2 Feb is computed from that. The statement does not mention any captured soldiers and does not deny captures; it does not name the attackers (ChimpReports' narration says M23).
claims.researcher_note: Cluster C-NK-28. The post (30 Jan) claimed 16 Tanzanian soldiers were captured by M23 'yesterday'. The TPDF statement (made 'Sunday', published 3 Feb 2025; date computed from weekday and publication date) reports two dead and four injured and says its troops 'remain safe', and does not mention captures; it does not explicitly deny captures. ChimpReports is a Ugandan outlet relaying the TPDF statement.

claims.text: CongoRassure reported that several FARDC soldiers captured at the fall of Goma had escaped from the military camp of Rumangabo, Rutshuru territory, where the M23 held them; according to testimonies it gathered, many of them reportedly died through summary executions, torture or forced labour, and one escapee said they were captured on 26 and 27 January 2025 in Goma and that 'beaucoup de nos frères d'armes ont été tués'.
claims.verification_note: Statement supported by the page (first clause from the article's lead sentence); date changed from the publication date to the month reported, as the escape date is not given. Unnamed testimony relayed by a local outlet; no numbers. The escape date is not stated; the article is dated 16 August 2025. Context: UN Group of Experts and HRW reporting on Rumangabo is already in the store.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster Q-07. Existing: REC-0305/0306/0879 (UN Group of Experts and HRW on Rumangabo). This adds a local outlet's account of an escape by FARDC soldiers captured in Goma; unnamed testimony, no numbers. The page continues that after fleeing the soldiers took refuge with the Wazalendo CMC/FDP group (name of leader on the page not used).

claims.text: Deutsche Welle reported that a resident of Minembwe, speaking of drone bombardments, said that even the Minembwe general referral hospital and some health centres had been targeted, and quoted him as saying that the paediatric block had been bombed 'yesterday' and that the Ilundu health centre, next to the airfield, had been bombed too.
claims.place_as_written: Ilundu health centre, near Minembwe airfield (Minembwe), Fizi
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (the resident speaks of drone bombardments)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verified on retained DW page (byline Jean-Noël Ba-Mweze, 25/06/2026). Statement matches the resident's quoted account and stays attributed. Single anonymous witness: C. One unnamed resident quoted by DW; no perpetrator named; the bombing date is 'yesterday' relative to an undated interview in an article published 25 June 2026. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-r9-2: The quote also says the paediatric block was bombed 'yesterday', a health-care detail the statement left out; added it, still attributed to the one unnamed resident and with no perpetrator. A search found PoliScoop (25 June 2026) asserting 'Les drones du régime de Kinshasa frappent l'hôpital général de Minembwe et le service pédiatrique' (a Kigali-aligned framing, usable only as that outlet's claim) and voixdespeuple.com relaying DW; neither is an independent witness. No FARDC response found.
claims.researcher_note: Lead from cluster C-SK-01 (pro-AFC/M23 post on a video filmed 22-27 July 2026). The post's further allegations (women giving birth unassisted, Methodist church hit) were not found in any fetched independent page. DW quotes one unnamed resident; the date of the bombing is 'hier' relative to the interview, so approximately late June 2026. Not the same as REC-0547 (7 June killings) or REC-0607 (church, March). DW is not a party source.

claims.text: Congolese government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said in an RFI interview that he could share images in which Rwanda uses ambulances to transport drones and carry out attacks using the medical equipment of an ambulance; he called it a serious and substantiated accusation and said: "It is a war crime."
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC (Patrick Muyaya) accusing Rwanda
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact on retained RFI page (published 01/07/2026). Narrowed to make the Minembwe context explicit (it is the question/answer setting, not an incident tie) and to quote the 'war crime' label rather than paraphrase it, per the vocabulary rule. Party statement (DRC government accusing Rwanda). The images were not shown in the interview text; the legal label is the minister's own, quoted. The interviewer's question concerned continued bombardment of the Minembwe area by the Congolese army and its allies. The answer was given in reply to a question about Minembwe ('Sur Minembwe, on en parle beaucoup, mais il se passe des choses inacceptables à Minembwe.').
claims.researcher_note: Party statement only (DRC government accusing Rwanda); RFI reproduces the interview, the minister did not show the images in the excerpt. The excerpt's setting is Minembwe ('Sur Minembwe, on en parle beaucoup'); the ambulance is not tied by name to Minembwe hospital in the excerpt. The legal label 'war crime' is the minister's, quoted. Cluster C-SK-02 posts allege FARDC drone footage and the Minembwe hospital ambulance; those details are not confirmed by any fetched page. No Rwandan or AFC/M23 reply found.

claims.text: Mediacongo reported that, speaking to the press, the Congolese government spokesperson said Rwanda uses ambulances to transport drones intended to carry out attacks on civilians in South Kivu, and that he described these practices as war crimes.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC (government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya) accusing Rwanda
claims.verification_note: Page read in full: section 'Publireportages', end credit 'Chrioni Kibungu Ouragan / MCP, via mediacongo.net', editorialising partisan tone. Date confirmed on page (10.07.2026), not just the listing. Outlet verb 'révèle' neutralised to 'said'; origin credited to Ouragan; labelled partisan. Not independent evidence of the ambulance allegation (same government source). Published in mediacongo.net's Publireportages section and credited at the end to Chrioni Kibungu of Ouragan ('Ouragan / MCP, via mediacongo.net'); the speaker is Patrick Muyaya. Publireportage-section relay of a strongly pro-Kinshasa article (it calls the Rwandan government a 'gangster' regime in its own voice); usable only as 'the DRC government spokesperson says'. Same speaker and allegation as the RFI interview of 1 July; the article places it at a press briefing ('Face à la presse'), so it may be a separate occasion. The page date 10.07.2026 is printed on the page. The same page calls Sukola 2 Sud spokesperson Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji 'sous-lieutenant', whereas Actualite.cd calls him lieutenant-colonel.
claims.researcher_note: Section is 'Publireportages' on mediacongo.net, so it may be sponsored or relayed content; date 10 July taken from the search listing, to be checked by the reviewer. Government allegation only.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Colonel Alexis Rugabisha, commander of the FARDC 12th rapid-intervention brigade, was killed on Saturday 1 February 2025 in fighting with the M23 at Nyabibwe in Kalehe territory; military sources told the outlet he was shot by snipers after his men fled.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact on retained page; every clause carried by the page; the sniper account stays attributed to military sources. B: credible outlet, corroborated on the death by the FARDC communiqué (claims 4, 5). Place differs between outlets: Nyabibwe (SOS Médias Burundi), Mukwija (Radio Okapi). The allegation in social posts that he was killed by his own side is not in any fetched page.
claims.researcher_note: Lead from cluster C-SK-03. Posts allege he was killed by comrades-in-arms (FARDC/Wazalendo) after anti-Tutsi media campaigns; that account was found only in social posts and not in any fetched page. Place variants: Nyabibwe, Mukwija (Radio Okapi), Mukwiza, Mukwidja. Excerpt is SOS Médias Burundi's own text; 'ce samedi' = 1 February 2025 as printed.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that Colonel Alexis Rugabisha, commander of the FARDC 12th brigade, was killed in clashes between the FARDC and the M23 at Mukwija in Kalehe territory, and that FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge, in a communiqué published on Sunday 2 February 2025, praised his bravery and called his death an inestimable loss for the army and the nation.
claims.verification_note: Attribution fixed: on the page the place (Mukwija) and the circumstances are Radio Okapi's own narration; the communiqué as reported only praises his bravery and calls the death an inestimable loss. The draft put the place in the spokesperson's mouth. Radio Okapi dates the communiqué Sunday 2 February 2025; Actualite.cd (published 2 February) says the army announced it on Saturday. Place: Mukwija (Radio Okapi) vs Nyabibwe (SOS Médias Burundi, Actualite.cd).
claims.researcher_note: The FARDC account: killed in combat against M23. Radio Okapi names the place Mukwija; SOS Médias Burundi says Nyabibwe; actualite.cd (below) says the colonel led a counter-offensive from Nyabibwe towards Minova. Radio Okapi dates the communiqué Sunday 2 February; actualite.cd says 'samedi' (a discrepancy within the sources).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the Congolese army announced in a communiqué that Colonel Rugabisha Alexis, commander of the FARDC 12th brigade, was killed in combat against the Rwandan army and the M23 in Kalehe territory; according to spokesperson Major General Ekenge Bomusa Efomi Sylvain, he fell 'armes à la main' after leading a counter-offensive that pushed the M23 back from Nyabibwe towards the surroundings of Minova.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact on retained page (dim 02/02/2025 - 16:22); all clauses stay attributed to the army/spokesperson as on the page. Same FARDC communiqué as claim 4 (Radio Okapi); not an independent origin for the circumstances. The attribution to 'the Rwandan army' is the FARDC's.
claims.researcher_note: Same FARDC communiqué as V-SK1-005, reported by a second outlet; do not count as independent of it. The FARDC attributes the death to the Rwandan army and the M23; the 'killed by comrades' allegation in the lead posts is not repeated by any fetched page.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that notables of northern Kabare territory denounced cases of abductions and intimidation at the Kavumu commercial centre that were pushing many young people and heads of families to leave their homes; the same report said gunfire had been heard for over a month and that deaths by bullets and injuries had been reported.
claims.place_as_written: Kavumu commercial centre, Bugorhe grouping, Kabare, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (some sources cite clashes between AFC/M23 elements and Wazalendo groups, others say the origin of shooting is unknown)
claims.verification_note: Page read in full (Last updated 2026/08/01). Statement is covered by the page; the gunfire and casualty clauses sit outside the stored excerpt (excerpt gap, quotes supplied in clause_support). Abductions are not attributed to any party. The same report says some sources cite clashes between AFC/M23 elements and Wazalendo while others say the origin of the shooting is unknown. No report of bodies of young people (the social-media lead) was found.
claims.researcher_note: Lead from cluster C-SK-07 (post of about 3 August 2026 alleging youths taken away by M23-RDF and bodies of young people in Kavumu centre). Radio Maendeleo (Bukavu community radio) reports abductions and intimidation at Kavumu in general terms, attributing them to no one; no page found reports bodies of young people found in Kavumu centre on that day. 'Selon des sources locales' type reporting; one named notable (David Chikuru) appears in an audio element, not quoted in the text.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza told journalists on Tuesday 29 September 2026 that Maj. Nitunga Jérémie and Capt Kanjori Félicien were arrested by the DRC state on 21 August 2026 and are held at the FARDC headquarters in Baraka, where they were arrested after being found with telephones, and that it is suspected they may have been used 'in improper activities or in giving certain information'.
claims.actor_as_written: DRC state / FARDC (as stated by the FDNB spokesperson)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact on retained page (byline Bénjamin BABOU, 29 Nzeri 2026). Restored the source's hedge ('may have been used'), the rank titles as printed, and the place of detention (FARDC HQ, Baraka). Not independent of the existing press-conference claims. Burundian army's account relayed by a Rwandan outlet (Bwiza); same press conference as the existing BBC Gahuza claim. The suspicion is hedged in the source ('bigakekwa ko bashobora kuba...': it is suspected they may have been). No FARDC/Kinshasa account found.
claims.researcher_note: Adds detail to existing r1-ST-BI-021 (BBC Gahuza, same press conference, which has the confirmation and the denial of Kinshasa detention) and r1-UV-2026Q3-009 (SOS Médias Burundi): date of arrest 21 August 2026, place of detention (FARDC headquarters at Baraka), and the reason the spokesperson gave. Bwiza is a Rwandan outlet relaying the Burundian army press conference; the cluster post (Kirundi, 1 Oct 2026) matches. FARDC/Congolese government account of the arrests not found.

claims.text: PoliScoop reported, according to accounts shared by Burundian sources, that two Burundian army officers held in eastern DRC since August had been repatriated to Burundi; it also reported that Major Jeremie Nitunga and Captain Felicien Kanjori had been arrested on 21 August in Baraka and detained by the FARDC and allied groups operating in the area.
claims.verification_note: Text verified on retained page (English and French versions). Split the attribution: only the repatriation is sourced to Burundian accounts; the arrest details are the outlet's narration. Date marked as 'by' the publication date since the repatriation date is not stated. Added the outlet's own caveat that neither government gave an account. Small online outlet (byline 'PoliScoop', 5 October 2026) relying on unnamed Burundian sources; repatriation date not given and not confirmed by any official statement. Its framing echoes Kigali's positions. The outlet adds that neither Bujumbura nor Kinshasa had offered a detailed public account of the detention or the terms of the release.
claims.researcher_note: Single small outlet relying on unnamed Burundian sources; the repatriation is not confirmed by any official Burundian or Congolese statement I found. Page carries an English text and a French text; the English text is cited. Spelling in the source omits accents.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, according to an anonymous Twirwaneho fighter it contacted, at least 17 Burundian soldiers were killed in the fighting at Rugezi and Kabanju, Fizi territory, and the fighter said: 'We captured one, along with their radios and their rifles.'
claims.place_as_written: Rugezi and Kabanju, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact on retained page (15 avril 2025, byline David Yemba). Removed the meta-sentence about what the article does not say from the statement (moved to note); kept attribution to the fighter. Same article as existing r1-SKS-2025Q2-009, so not an independent origin; it adds the capture detail. Party's own claim (an anonymous Twirwaneho fighter); the article dates the clashes to Saturday 12 April and names no captured person, gives no sex or rank. It does not confirm the social-media posts about a named female soldier captured in late April.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-SK-09. Same article as existing r1-SKS-2025Q2-009 (REC-0160) but that claim does not record the capture. Posts allege a named female Burundian soldier captured around 22-30 April; this article is dated 15 April, concerns 12 April, and names no captured person, so it does not confirm the posts' details. Twirwaneho is a party; account is the party's own. The article dates the clashes to Saturday 12 April.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the spokesperson of operation Sukola 2 Sud South Kivu, Lieutenant-Colonel Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, said that following the FARDC response against what he called the 'terrorist coalition RDF and its allies M23, Twirwaneho and Red Tabara' in the Hauts Plateaux of Uvira and Fizi, the FARDC had neutralised 23 rebels, 11 others had surrendered and several weapons were recovered.
claims.place_as_written: Hauts Plateaux of Uvira and Fizi (spokesperson's words); the article places the recaptured Masango, Ruhua and Rubarati in the Mwenga highlands, Itombwe sector, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC (Sukola 2 Sud), as the spokesperson says
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact on retained page (jeu 03/09/2026). Statement wording fine; location corrected: the draft placed Masango etc. in the Uvira/Fizi highlands, but the page puts them in the Mwenga highlands (Itombwe sector). Party (FARDC) figures, unverified. The article's lead places Masango, Ruhua and Rubarati in the Hauts Plateaux of Mwenga, Itombwe sector, not Uvira/Fizi. Rank discrepancy: Mediacongo (10 July 2026) calls him 'sous-lieutenant'.
claims.researcher_note: Found while searching video-lead cluster C-SK-15 (Itombwe, 'M23 Red Tabara' arrests, ~8 Aug 2026). It does not report the arrests; it is a related FARDC claim of fighting against Red Tabara in the Hauts Plateaux from 28 August. Party account (FARDC); no AFC/M23 or Twirwaneho response found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, according to the army, a mass grave was discovered at Masango, where civilians killed during the occupation of the town by the M23/Twirwaneho/Red Tabara rebel forces, supported by Rwanda, are said to be buried.
claims.place_as_written: Masango, Hauts Plateaux of Mwenga, Itombwe sector, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. The whole sentence, including the discovery, is attributed to the army; the draft attributed only the burial part. Location corrected from Uvira territory to the Mwenga highlands (Itombwe sector) as the page states; date made 'reported' since the discovery date is not given. Army allegation only (sentence ends 'selon l'armée'; burial is conditional, 'seraient enterrés'); no number of bodies, no names, no independent verification, no AFC/M23 or Twirwaneho response found.
claims.researcher_note: Army allegation only; no independent verification found. Not from a video lead; found during C-SK-15 searches. Other Masango claims exist (UN GoE camps; SOS Medias Burundi 23 Aug).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC presented to the press in Kinshasa on Saturday 3 January seven people it described as Rwandan soldiers and eight civilians, nationals of countries of the sub-region, and that Lieutenant-Colonel Mak Hazukay said these suspects had been apprehended far from the borders during military operations in North and South Kivu.
claims.place_as_written: Kinshasa (presentation of the captives); capture sites in North and South Kivu, not specified
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC (detaining party); the seven are described by the FARDC as Rwandan soldiers
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts are on the page (published sam, 03/01/2026). Dropped the publication year and the quotation marks around 'suspects' clause; numbers written as the page words (sept, huit). Rank title kept as printed; role omitted from the statement because the two outlets name the service differently. The nationality and status of the captives are the FARDC's account; no independent identification and no Rwandan response found. Radio Okapi names Hazukay as deputy commander of the FARDC 'Service de commandement et d'information'; Liberal Info writes 'Service de communication et d'information'. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-r9-2: The FARDC is a party; Radio Okapi relays its presentation, and the captives' identity as Rwandan soldiers is the FARDC's account. Amended to attribute it. A search found Grands Lacs News (3 Jan 2026) headlining 'Kigali dément' (lead for a Rwandan denial; body not read) and quoting Hazukay that a major and a captain of the RDF were among them. Grade B fits the event of the presentation, not the identities.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-UV-10. Party account: nationality and status of the captives are as claimed by the FARDC and not independently verified. Radio Okapi does not name Uvira as the capture site (compare the Liberal Info claim, which does). No response from Rwanda found. Not in the verified claims at drafting (claim_search 'sept militaires rwandais', 'Hazukay').

claims.text: Liberal Info reported that on Saturday the FARDC presented at the Collège des Hautes Études de Stratégie et de Défense (CHESD) in Kinshasa seven people described as soldiers of the Rwandan defence forces (RDF) and eight civilians, including Burundian and Tanzanian nationals, whom Liberal Info described as 'captured in the city of Uvira'; the identification of the seven as RDF soldiers is the FARDC's account.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira (city), South Kivu (capture, per Liberal Info); Kinshasa (presentation)
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC (detaining party); the seven are described as RDF soldiers
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed the page-date clause (a number no excerpt prints) and made explicit that 'captured in the city of Uvira' is the outlet's narration of the FARDC presentation, not an established capture site. Place of capture conflicts: Liberal Info's lead says 'dans la ville d'Uvira', the same page later reports the officer as saying the arrests came in operations 'dans le territoire d'Uvira', and Radio Okapi quotes him as saying 'au Nord et Sud-Kivu'. The 'Saturday' is 3 January 2026 by the page date (Publié le 3 janvier 2026). Identities are the FARDC's account. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-r9-2: The FARDC is a party and the identification of the seven as RDF soldiers is its account; the statement gave it in Liberal Info's voice as fact. Amended to attribute the identification. A search found Grands Lacs News headlining the same presentation 'Kigali dément' (body not read; lead for a Rwandan denial) and quoting Hazukay that the captives were taken 'sur le théâtre des opérations dans les provinces du Nord-Kivu et Sud-Kivu', which again contradicts Liberal Info's 'capturés dans la ville d’Uvira'.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-UV-10. Date computed from 'samedi' and the 3 January 2026 page date. Conflicts on place with Radio Okapi (captures 'au Nord et Sud-Kivu', no town named); the same Liberal Info page later says the arrests came in operations 'dans le territoire d'Uvira'. Single outlet, FARDC account.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that FARDC Lieutenant-Colonel Mak Hazukay said, at the press presentation in Kinshasa, that the occupation of Uvira, far from Rwanda's borders, proves that the defensive-measures reason advanced by Kigali is 'un pire mensonge'.
claims.place_as_written: Kinshasa (press conference) concerning Uvira, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact on the Radio Okapi page; the 'a-t-il déploré' closes a quote the page attributes to Lt-Col Mak Hazukay (named in the preceding paragraph). Single clause, single source; attribution and wording match. Party statement (FARDC). 'L'occupation aujourd'hui d'Uvira' refers to the AFC/M23 occupation at the time of the briefing. Rwanda's response: none found.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster C-UV-10. Party statement (Kinshasa). Rwanda's response to the presentation: none found.

claims.text: Opinion Info and Actualite.cd reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, at a press briefing with Patrick Muyaya on Thursday 2 April 2026, said about 210 bodies had been found in three mass graves (Actualite.cd: at least 210); Opinion Info quotes him as saying Human Rights Watch had just detected more than 61 mass graves and that 31 mass graves had been found in only three municipalities, and names the three graves as Kamvivira, Kilomoni and Kimanga.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact. The raw statement credited both outlets with the 61 and 31 figures and the grave names, which only Opinion Info prints; split clause by clause, removed the publication dates (not in the excerpts), recorded the Actualite.cd wording difference. Governor's figures, not independently counted. The '61' is in Opinion Info's quote only: Actualite.cd quotes Purusi as saying HRW showed 'des dizaines des fausses communes', and quotes him dating the discovery of the three graves to 20 February (spelled Kavinvira, Kilomoni, Kimanga). Opinion Info calls Muyaya the government spokesperson; Actualite.cd calls him minister of communication. Earlier government counts differ (151, 171-172; see REC-0023).
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster Q-01 (REC-0023 holds the earlier Feb 2026 counts: 31+141 bodies per BBC Gahuza/Reuters, 151 per the provincial communiqué of 28 Feb). The 210 / 61 figures and the 2 April briefing are not in the verified claims at drafting. Figures differ across government statements: 151 (28 Feb communiqué), 171-172 (late Feb press), 210 (2 Apr). Third grave site is Kimanga here; Kavimvira and Kilomoni in earlier counts. The '61' is the governor's attribution to HRW; HRW's own count is not in these excerpts. The '344 bodies' of Sept 2026 (foxtime.cd, listing dated 11 Sept 2026) could not be fetched by the checker: see gaps.

claims.text: African Facts reported that the group of James Bitolo, with other Biloze Bishamuke militiamen and Maï maï fighters, then attacked and pillaged the evangelical church where the funeral of Colonel Gisore took place, and quoted Muyoboke Ntabaye, president of the Banyamulenge mutuality of Uvira, as saying he was among those arrested in the church, that they shot at them, and that they stole crates of drinks, vehicles, medical equipment and telephones; African Facts wrote that videos and other testimonies it consulted corroborate the attack.
claims.actor_as_written: as African Facts attributes it: group of James Bitolo, Biloze Bishamuke militiamen and Maï maï fighters
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact in the retained PDF; byline, date and the 'président de la mutualité' passage are on the same page. Attribution is correct (outlet's narration for the perpetrators, Ntabaye's quote for the arrests, shooting and theft). Month-level date is right because the church attack has no day printed. Read from a PDF copy hosted by francegenocidetutsi.org (third-party advocacy archive), credited to African Facts; the original page could not be reached. The article dates Colonel Gisore's funeral to 25 August 2025 and places this attack 'ensuite', after the shooting that followed the funeral; no exact day is given for the church attack. The medical equipment was taken from a funeral gathering, not a health facility. Perpetrators as African Facts names them; Ntabaye's quote says only 'ils'.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster Q-02 (a pro-M23 account posted this article). Existing REC-0091 / claim r2-G-UV-CTRL-002 (SOS Médias Burundi) dates the burial to Monday 25 August 2025; African Facts gives no funeral date, so date is month-level here. African Facts is a fact-checking outlet; the PDF is a copy hosted on francegenocidetutsi.org (the africanfacts.org original page was not fetchable). The medical equipment was taken from a church funeral gathering, not a health facility. The South Kivu government's account is a separate claim.

claims.text: African Facts reported that, in a communiqué issued 'le jour même', the South Kivu government spokesperson summed up the events as a 'petite paralysie des activités dans Mulongwe' that would have caused no damage (conditional, as the article words it), and 'condamne les organisateurs des cérémonies funéraires'; the article adds that he also condemned messages aimed at tearing the social fabric between communities and spoke of a media war waged by the rebels.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed the bracketed gloss '(the Wazalendo disturbance around the funeral of Colonel Gisore)', which the excerpt does not say; kept 'n'aurait causé' as a conditional; added the communiqué's other condemnations that the same paragraph reports, so the party's account is not cut to its most damaging lines (those clauses rest on the page, not the stored excerpt). The provincial government's communiqué is known here only through African Facts, which presents it critically; the communiqué was not found or read. 'Le jour même' follows the article's account of the 25 August 2025 funeral events, but the communiqué's exact date is not printed. The spokesperson is not named.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster Q-02. Party account (provincial government) relayed by African Facts, which presents it critically. 'Le jour même' refers to the day of the events in the preceding paragraphs; the exact day is not printed in the excerpt.

claims.text: African Facts reported that soldiers and militiamen had reportedly acted together 'hier matin' in the Nyabianda quarter, and quoted Muyoboke Ntabaye, president of the Banyamulenge mutuality of Uvira, as saying that soldiers, maï maï and persons in police uniform began the cordon at 5:00 and it lasted until 13:00, that more than fifteen members of his community were arrested without valid reason, and that some were taken to the cells of the Wazalendo militias instead of government buildings; the article also quotes him describing waking up in a cordon in the quarter 'deNamyanda' where many Banyamulenge live.
claims.place_as_written: Nyabianda / Namyanda quarter, Uvira (city), South Kivu (both spellings as printed)
claims.actor_as_written: as Ntabaye states: soldiers, maï maï and persons in police uniform
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. The raw statement put 'yesterday morning' and Nyabianda in Ntabaye's mouth; on the page they are African Facts' own narration, in the conditional ('se seraient ... entendus et auraient agi ensemble'). Re-attributed and removed the publication date (a number no excerpt prints). Single community-leader account relayed by African Facts from a PDF copy hosted by francegenocidetutsi.org. The date 19 September 2025 is computed from 'hier' and the article date (20/09/2025); the article's opening also says that nine days after the 10 September audio message soldiers and militiamen were patrolling some quarters. Nyabianda and 'deNamyanda' are both as printed and may be the same quarter. No FARDC, police or government response found.
claims.researcher_note: Video-lead cluster Q-02. Date computed from 'hier' and the article date 20 September 2025. Single-source account by a community leader; the page's own spelling 'deNamyanda' kept. No FARDC or government response to the cordon found. Existing claims r1-UV-2025Q3-020/-021 (SOS Médias Burundi) record the Mutualité's other complaints (beatings at Kabindula, water denial, abduction of a soldier and a policeman).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that before their January 2026 withdrawal AFC/M23 instructed the Banyamulenge community to leave Uvira, claiming returning Wazalendo and FARDC forces would target them, and that some members of the Banyamulenge community alleged this movement was coerced to justify claims of a genocidal threat.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. The coercion claim is an allegation the Group reports; the Group does not itself conclude on it.
