claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 para. 81. The Group reports the coercion claim as an allegation 'including from some members of the Banyamulenge community'; it does not itself conclude. AFC/M23's stated reason is recorded as stated.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that after the Wazalendo return to Uvira in January 2026 the South Kivu Governor convened all Wazalendo leaders, banned unauthorized armed elements, roadblocks and any substitution for government functions, and arrested recalcitrant combatants, and that provincial authorities began a registration process with payment of $325 to each registered combatant.
claims.actor_as_written: South Kivu provincial government; FARDC; Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 paras. 114-115. Group notes payment became regular after February 2026 and led to a sharp increase in self-declared Wazalendo.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23-occupied territories were divided into three 'defense zones': a first zone covering Nyiragongo, Rutshuru and Lubero territories led by 'General' Baudoin Ngaruye, a second covering Masisi and Walikale led by 'Brigadier-General' Justin Gacheri Musanga, and a third covering South Kivu led by 'General' Byamungu.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu and South Kivu (AFC/M23-held areas)
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 para. 64; report covers investigations to 15 April 2026 so the date is approximate. Sources: military and intelligence sources, UN, diplomatic sources, civil society, researchers, AFC/M23 officers and combatants, Wazalendo combatants. Ranks are in quotation marks as in the report.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that the estimated combat strength of AFC/M23 was around 30,000 elements, and that the figure included thousands of recently graduated FARDC, Congolese national police and Wazalendo elements who were either captured or volunteered following the fall of Goma.
claims.place_as_written: AFC/M23-held areas, North and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that the RDF 3rd Division, under Major General Eugene Nkubito, operated predominantly in North Kivu, and the 4th Division was mainly deployed in South Kivu under Brigadier General Vincent Gatama until his redeployment to Mozambique in late 2025; special forces units under Brigadier-General Stanislas Gashugi supported both, and the RDF Army Chief of Staff, General Vincent Nyakarundi, oversaw operations.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 para. 99. The report notes Gatama was referenced in late 2025 as RSF Joint Task Force Commander in Mozambique (footnote). Excerpt was fixed by the builder; footnote markers appear inside the page text.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that in December 2025 RDF deployment in eastern DRC was conservatively estimated at 8,000 to 10,000 elements in South Kivu and 6,000 to 8,000 in North Kivu, with no evidence of significant withdrawals thereafter.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 para. 96. Rwanda's government has publicly denied that its troops operate in the DRC in other sources (not collected in this unit).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that President Kagame appointed retired General James Kaberebe as Senior Defence and Security Advisor on 1 December 2025 and Brigadier-General Jean-Paul Nyirabutama as his deputy on 29 January 2026, and that Mr. Nyirabutama was directly involved in operational matters in eastern DRC including communication channels with AFC/M23.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. The report spells the name both 'Kaberebe' and 'Kabarebe'.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 para. 98 (spelling 'Kaberebe' in that sentence; 'Kabarebe' elsewhere in the report). Excerpt anchors fixed below.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that Minembwe had effectively been encircled by FARDC and allied forces since mid-2025, with severe obstacles to population movements and entry of essential goods and humanitarian assistance, and that since February 2026 access was limited to air supply only.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 para. 86 (sources: military and intelligence, UN, Banyamulenge, humanitarian sources). Members of the Banyamulenge community denounced both parties for trapping civilians (para. 88).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 issued per-kilogram tax invoices in Rubaya and Mubambiro, and that once shipments were delivered in Rwanda the transporter settled AFC/M23 tax payments by depositing the amounts in an Equity Bank account held by Patient Haba, the AFC/M23 provincial financial coordinator.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 para. 217; Group also names Bazimazika Kabano Bazinga as AFC/M23-appointed coordinator for artisanal mining in Rubaya (para. 215) and Patrice Biraira as overseeing transport coordination (para. 216).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that in early December 2025 AFC/M23 introduced a codified list of taxes mirroring Congolese State tax structures, and that the national water and electricity companies (SNEL and REGIDESO) were placed under the administrative authority of the AFC/M23-appointed governor and the financial oversight of the AFC/M23 finance department.
claims.place_as_written: AFC/M23-held areas, North and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that VDP/Wazalendo groups established new geographically organized coalitions called 'synergies': the 'Synergie Front Grand Nord' (24 armed groups in Lubero and Beni, commanded by UPLC leader 'General' Mayani), the 'Synergie Petit Nord' (14 groups in Rutshuru and Nyiragongo, commanded by Jonas Bigabo), and the 'Synergie Masisi-Walikale' (17 groups, led by APCLS leader Janvier Karahiri and sanctioned individual Guidon Shimiray Mwisa).
claims.place_as_written: Lubero, Beni, Rutshuru, Nyiragongo, Masisi and Walikale territories, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 paras. 107-108 (Wazalendo commanders, combatants, FARDC and official authorities). FDLR-FOCA combatants were integrated into the Masisi-Walikale and Petit Nord synergies (same paragraph).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that at the time of drafting Wazalendo factions in South Kivu remained divided into at least three coordinations, one led by Yakutumba, another by Alexis Mwamba Dunya (the RAD-appointed coordinator in South Kivu) and a third by Ngomanzito, and that renewed efforts to establish a unified command had failed.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 para. 117. Footnote: in late December 2025 in Baraka William Yakutumba was elected overall Wazalendo coordinator but several Wazalendo leaders rejected his appointment. Spelling 'Ngomanzito' as printed in para. 117 ('Ngomazito' appears in para. 121).

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that FDLR was fragmented into three principal factions (FDLR-FOCA, FDLR-RUD and FDLR-FPP), that 'Major-General' Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) and 'General' Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro) remained FDLR-FOCA's military commander and political leader, and that UN and intelligence sources estimated total FDLR strength at between 3,500 and 4,500 combatants.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu (Nyiragongo, Masisi, Rutshuru, Walikale) and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Figures field carried FDLR-claimed and Washington Agreement estimates that no excerpt prints; narrowed to the excerpted estimate.
claims.researcher_note: S/2026/466 paras. 126-127 and 130. FDLR sources claimed over 10,000 combatants (para. 130); the Washington Agreement estimated 3,000 to 3,500. Anchors adjusted by builder.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that after taking control of Goma, AFC/M23 forcibly displaced internally displaced persons camps west of the city, ordering civilians to vacate within 72 hours, without ensuring that returns were safe, and that tens of thousands were displaced again.
claims.place_as_written: IDP camps west of Goma (city), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 para. 93 (annex 48). The Group's legal characterisation in the paragraph is not reproduced. Date approximate: after the 27 January capture of Goma.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that in January and February 2025 a conservative estimate of 6,000 RDF troops, including special forces, were active in North Kivu and northern territories of South Kivu, with a footnote citing former RDF and Rwandan intelligence reporting at least 10,000 RDF troops deployed in eastern DRC, and that by the time of writing an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 RDF troops remained active in AFC/M23-controlled territories.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu and northern South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: S/2025/446 paras. 36-37 and footnote 25. Figures are as stated by the Group per source and not merged.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that in Bwito chiefdom AFC/M23 deployed its newly constituted 'Fourth Brigade', reportedly composed of recent recruits including former Wazalendo and FARDC elements, under the command of Mapenzi, the former leader of NDC-R/M who joined AFC/M23 in March 2025, replacing RDF forces partially redeployed from the area since September.
claims.place_as_written: Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.

claims.text: The Group of Experts reported that on 24 August 2025 'General' Sultani Makenga unveiled the AFC/M23 'elite police force', named Police révolutionnaire congolaise (M23/PRC), placed under the command of 'Colonel' Guillaume Eboko, a former FARDC officer, and deployed primarily in Goma and Bukavu.
claims.verification_note: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a public declaration from Mbwavinywa, three armed groups announced their break with Kinshasa to join the M23/AFC: the FPP/AP of the self-proclaimed general Kabido, the NDC-R/M and Maï-Maï Kifuafua.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports it. The declaration's date is not stated; the article is dated 9 March 2025. Single local outlet.
claims.researcher_note: Declaration date not stated; article dated 9 March 2025. Single local outlet; the page also says the Front Commun de la Résistance joined, not detailed here. Radio Okapi (11 March) independently describes the FPP/AP leader's rallying to the M23.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that in Beni and Butembo social groups rose up to protest the withdrawal from Lubero of the Ugandan soldiers deployed in the DRC under the joint FARDC-UPDF operations.
claims.place_as_written: Beni and Butembo; withdrawal from Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: UPDF; Beni and Butembo civil society and pressure groups
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports it. The protest date and the date of the UPDF withdrawal are not given in the passage. The page quotes Clovis Mutsuva supporting the movements.
claims.researcher_note: Withdrawal date not given in this passage; reporting only the protest. The page names a political actor, Clovis Mutsuva, as supporting the movements. Not cross-checked with Uganda or UPDF statements.

claims.text: OCHA reported that on 9 and 10 April armed violence broke out in the localities of Kanune and Luhanga, then Mbwavinywa, where two civilians died, displacing about 4,000 people towards Bunyatenge and Masika.
claims.place_as_written: Kanune, Luhanga and Mbwavinywa, Lubero territory, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: The '4000' flag is formatting: the source prints '4 000'. Excerpt matches. The perpetrators are not attributed by the source.
claims.researcher_note: OCHA situation report covering 1-15 April 2025. Actualite.cd relayed it on 2025-05-16.

claims.text: MONUSCO said that on 13 and 14 August, during incidents in Mayi-Moya (North Kivu), it provided physical protection to 206 civilians, including 70 women and 93 children, who sought refuge at its military base.
claims.place_as_written: Mayi-Moya, North Kivu (territory not stated by the source)
claims.actor_as_written: MONUSCO (protection); incident perpetrators not named in the excerpt
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; territory field corrected to what the source states. The source places Mayi-Moya only in North Kivu; the Beni-territory tag was the researcher's inference and has been removed. The release does not say who carried out the 13-14 August incidents.
claims.researcher_note: Territory (Beni) is the reviewer's inference for Mayi-Moya and is not in the excerpt; verify. The excerpt does not name the perpetrators of the incidents.

claims.text: Radio Moto Butembo reported that the World Food Programme launched a food distribution at Lubero-centre on Tuesday 26 May for displaced people and host families affected by the M23 advance in the south of the territory and by massacres attributed to alleged ADF, and that Lubero-centre had for months received displaced people from Kanyabayonga, Kirumba, Mathembe, Vutsorovya, Hutwe and Alimbongo.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim. Replacement extends source 1 to carry the 10,000-households figure; the '4th WFP shipment' detail is dropped from figures as no stored passage carries it. The year is not printed in the text; 2026 comes from the article's dated URL (2026/05/27), and 26 May 2026 was a Tuesday, consistent with 'mardi 26 mai'.
claims.researcher_note: Local outlet (RMBB, Butembo). The year 2026 is inferred from the URL date path (2026/05/27) and the publication context; the excerpt gives only 'mardi 26 mai'. Residents also complain of exclusion from final distribution lists (not cited).

claims.text: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that, according to sources contacted on the spot, residents moved towards Kalimba, Kiribata, Vusesa and Vungulo, and that more than a thousand households had already been recorded in these reception areas since Wednesday 30 September.
claims.place_as_written: Kalimba, Kiribata, Vusesa, Vungulo (Lubero territory), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: The flagged '23' came from 'M23-AFC' in a clause about fighting that the excerpt does not carry; dropped that clause so the statement rests on the excerpt alone. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Same page as the preceding claim; figure is from unnamed sources.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that a 'ville morte' (general stay-at-home strike) was observed on Tuesday 11 August in Butembo after a call by youth of citizen movements and pressure groups, who denounced insecurity and the desecration of the tomb of the artist Delcat Idinco and demanded the release of activist Clovis Mutsuva, detained in Beni; the page adds that the call was launched by youths claiming to be of LUCHA to denounce killings of civilians attributed to the ADF.
claims.verification_note: Supported by the outlet's report of an observed strike. That Clovis Mutsuva is held in Beni is not in the excerpts; his detention is the protesters' demand. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Context for Butembo civic reaction to ADF killings and a detention in Beni; the page says no law-enforcement intervention was reported by midday. No official account of Mutsuva's detention found in this unit.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to sources in the region, between 18 May and 10 June more than 600 houses were burned, at least 75 people killed and 42 wounded, with more than 26 villages affected in the Bukombo, Tongo and Bambo groupings.
claims.place_as_written: Bukombo, Tongo and Bambo groupings, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Excerpt carries the claim verbatim. Aggregate from unnamed sources; not split by perpetrator or civilian/combatant status.
claims.researcher_note: Aggregate figures from unnamed regional sources; not split by perpetrator or by civilian/combatant status. Bwiza.com separately reports 543 houses burned and 38 killed in Mutanda grouping 26–31 May.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that after three months of prohibition the M23 again allowed residents of the Katwiguru–Nyamilima axis (Bwisha chiefdom, Binza, Rutshuru) to access their fields from Monday 25 August, for an expected two weeks according to local sources, and that the restriction had been imposed by the M23 to avoid confusion between civilians and alleged FDLR rebels.
claims.place_as_written: Katwiguru to Nyamilima axis, Binza, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpts support all clauses. The stated purpose of the restriction is as Radio Okapi reports it, not an M23 statement.
claims.researcher_note: The reason for the restriction is as stated by Radio Okapi's article, not attributed to the M23 itself. The article also states that the M23 and the Rwandan government contested the HRW accusations in a communiqué of 22 August.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that, to secure Goma, the AFC/M23 administration installed infrared surveillance cameras in some quarters of Goma on Wednesday 9 July 2025.
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt carries the statement; date 9 July printed (year from the article's own 9 July 2025 date line in the same paragraph sequence).
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet.

claims.text: Actualite.cd, citing an OCHA report on June 2025, reported that since 5 June more than 3,600 people (about 720 households) fled Bukombo, south of Rutshuru, after intensified fighting between armed groups, and that most of the displaced found refuge at Birambizo General Reference Hospital, the local Catholic parish and host families.
claims.actor_as_written: armed groups (not named in the excerpt)
claims.verification_note: '3 600' printed with a space (flag is a formatting mismatch); excerpt_en faithful. OCHA quoted by Actualite.cd. Event begins 5 June 2025 (before this quarter); reported in July. Displaced people sheltering in a hospital is relevant to health-care access.
claims.researcher_note: Event begins in June; report published 15 July; included as context for Q3 Rutshuru displacement. Hospital used as shelter, not an attack on health care.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the North Kivu governor under AFC/M23 administration, Bahati Musanga Erasto, began a tour of Bwito collectivity, Rutshuru territory, on 12 February 2026, visiting Tongo, Butare, Kabizo, Bambo (Kishishe) and Nyanzale, and that at the end of the tour more than twenty young people were recruited into the ARC.
claims.place_as_written: Tongo, Butare, Kabizo, Bambo (Kishishe), Nyanzale, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 de facto governor Bahati Musanga Erasto; ARC (as printed; the page does not expand the abbreviation)
claims.verification_note: Statement unchanged; actor corrected: the page prints only 'ARC' and does not expand it, so the expansion is removed. No implication about forced recruitment. The page does not say whether the recruitment into the ARC was voluntary or forced, or who carried it out. Goma-based outlet operating under AFC/M23 administration.
claims.researcher_note: Goma-based outlet; the page does not say whether recruitment was voluntary or forced. Should be read against the Bwito fighting and the MSF/OCHA reports for the same weeks. 'ARC' is the printed abbreviation; the page does not expand it.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that on Tuesday 28 July a so-called peaceful march organised by a platform presenting itself as the Société civile plurielle et Forces vives du Nord-Kivu paralysed several sectors in Goma between 7 and 11 a.m. and ended at the MONUSCO headquarters, where the organisers handed a memorandum to the mission's representatives. The call had been widely relayed the day before by neighbourhood authorities, who said the initiative was part of a decision taken by the de facto AFC/M23 authorities in the zones under their control; some residents interviewed by Radio Okapi said the mobilisation was coercive.
claims.actor_as_written: Société civile plurielle et Forces vives du Nord-Kivu; de facto AFC/M23 authorities
claims.verification_note: Attribution tightened: the link to an AFC/M23 decision is the neighbourhood authorities' account, not Radio Okapi's finding. Per the memorandum, the protesters denounced sanctions against some AFC and M23 leaders and opposed the constitutional reform project.
claims.researcher_note: Related to the UN sanctions listing of 14 July (existing claims r1-UC-M23-033/035). Page also says protesters opposed the DRC constitutional reform project and denounced the sanctions.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that on Monday 10 August 2026 the deputy permanent secretary of the AFC-M23, Delion Kimbulungu, accompanied by the deputy governor of North Kivu Bahati Shadrack, toured higher-education institutions in Goma, including the ISTM, ISTA, ISP and ISC, where he chaired handover ceremonies between the old and new management teams. It said the decision designating the new management committees concerns ten institutions in Goma and Bukavu, and was signed by Bertrand Bisimwa and submitted for approval to Corneille Nangaa.
claims.place_as_written: Goma (ISTM, ISTA, ISP, ISC); also Bukavu
claims.verification_note: Draft said he 'installed new management teams at' the four institutes; the page says he toured and chaired handover ceremonies, the four being named as places visited. The 'ten institutions' clause needed the page passage. Bahati Shadrack is the AFC/M23-appointed deputy governor ('vice-gouverneur du Nord-Kivu' as the page puts it). The purpose of the tour is given by AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka on X, per the page.
claims.researcher_note: Adds Goma detail to existing r1-POL-2026-008 (Kinshasa's rejection of the appointments, Radio Okapi 10 Aug). The page attributes the purpose of the tour to AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka on X (not cited here).

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that, after it captured Masisi in January, the M23 ordered two displacement sites dismantled, according to a humanitarian source.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on the HRW page; attribution to a humanitarian source kept. Single credible NGO relaying one anonymous source: B.
claims.researcher_note: Single anonymous humanitarian source relayed by HRW; sites not named.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that Kasopo locality (Osso Banyungu sector, Masisi) was deserted after two days of fighting from Wednesday 10 September between M23 rebels and a coalition of Wazalendo groups made up of elements of the MAC, the APCLS and Uhuru.
claims.verification_note: Every clause on the page and in the excerpt. Page also reports the Wazalendo retook two of four localities held by M23 on the Wednesday.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet. Page also says Wazalendo retook two of four localities previously held by M23 and that this back-and-forth continued since April 2025 (not used as claim).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, mass displacement and villages nearly emptied of inhabitants since Sunday 31 May in Walikale and Masisi territories after new clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo groups allied to the FARDC; it named villages affected in Masisi (Ndete, Mulema, Luke, Kasenyi, Mbizo).
claims.place_as_written: Walikale and Masisi territories (Yaki, Kasopo, Ndete, Mulema, Luke, Kasenyi, Mbizo)
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23; Wazalendo allied to the FARDC
claims.verification_note: Verified; flags are 'M23' digits and capitalisation only. No displacement figure given. Kasenyi and Mbizo are named on the page as sites of clashes in Kibabi groupement, Bahunde chiefdom (not in the stored excerpts). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 1 Jun 2026, carries every clause (Ndete, Mulema and Luke per witnesses; Kasenyi and Mbizo in the outlet's voice); the stored excerpts stop before 'allied to the FARDC' and omit Kasenyi and Mbizo, so the full sentences are added. 2026-10-28: source 1 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 1 Jun 2026, carries every clause (Ndete, Mulema and Luke per witnesses; Kasenyi and Mbizo in the outlet's voice); the stored excerpts stop before 'allied to the FARDC' and omit Kasenyi and Mbizo, so the full sentences are added.
claims.researcher_note: No displacement figure given.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that violent clashes on Monday 12 January between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo of the CMC group, starting at Bumbasha a few kilometres from Mweso, caused hundreds of residents to flee toward neighbouring villages and to Mweso centre in Masisi, where they took refuge in churches and schools; no toll was communicated.
claims.place_as_written: Bumbasha, Karambi, Chahemba (Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru) and Mweso, Masisi
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23; Wazalendo of the CMC group
claims.verification_note: Verified on page; Rutshuru location noted. The fighting itself was in Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru territory (despite the headline 'à Masisi'); the displaced fled into Mweso, Masisi. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 13 Jan 2026, carries every clause; the stored excerpts lack the date, the CMC group, the no-toll clause and the refuge in churches and schools, added here. The page places the fighting in Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru. 2026-10-28: source 1 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 13 Jan 2026, carries every clause; the stored excerpts lack the date, the CMC group, the no-toll clause and the refuge in churches and schools, added here. The page places the fighting in Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru.
claims.researcher_note: Fighting itself is in Rutshuru territory (Bukombo); relevant to this unit for displacement into Mweso. Recorded territory Rutshuru.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing a notable contacted on the spot, that fighting on Saturday around Buruso (Ufamandu I groupement, Masisi) and Biriko (Waloa Loanda groupement, Walikale) between AFC/M23 and a Wazalendo coalition allied to the FARDC caused new displacement toward Walikale-Centre, Hombo and elsewhere; Radio Okapi described the Ufamandu I and II groupements as almost entirely emptied of residents, and military sources said they shot down on Saturday in Nyamaboko I a kamikaze drone attributed to AFC/M23.
claims.place_as_written: Buruso (Masisi); Biriko, Kilambo, Busurungi (Walikale); Nyamaboko I
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23; Wazalendo coalition allied to FARDC
claims.verification_note: Raw said 'an AFC/M23 kamikaze drone'; the page says a drone 'attribué à l'AFC/M23' by military sources: attribution restored. The emptied-groupements line is Radio Okapi's own narration, not the notable's. Day number dropped from the statement (no excerpt prints it); the date field carries 29 Aug, printed on the page. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 30 Aug 2026 (fighting Saturday 29 Aug). All clauses are on the page; the stored excerpts carry only the emptied-groupements and drone sentences, so the fighting, notable and location passages are added. Statement wording stands. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 30 Aug 2026 (fighting Saturday 29 Aug). All clauses are on the page; the stored excerpts carry only the emptied-groupements and drone sentences, so the fighting, notable and location passages are added. Statement wording stands. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 30 Aug 2026 (fighting Saturday 29 Aug). All clauses are on the page; the stored excerpts carry only the emptied-groupements and drone sentences, so the fighting, notable and location passages are added. Statement wording stands.
claims.researcher_note: Page also says rebels' advance since 13 August worsens the crisis, and the army accuses rebels of multiplying attacks to extend their zone of occupation (army account, attributed on page).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Club des Filles Reporters RDC (CFR RDC), after a mission from 25 to 27 September 2026, said nearly 2 350 displaced families lived in precarious conditions at Lukaraba (Walikale) and Hombo Sud (Kalehe, South Kivu); at Lukaraba the families had fled Ziralo, Ufamandu, Remeka, Lurere and Biriko, and at Hombo Sud the hospital was said to be under strain from sick or war-wounded displaced people.
claims.verification_note: Flagged figures (2 350; 25-27 Sept) are printed in the article's first paragraph. All clauses supported. Single NGO account relayed by Radio Okapi; the headline says 'more than 2 000 families', the body 'nearly 2 350'.
claims.researcher_note: Page notes needs in food, health care and protection of women, girls and children.

claims.text: Jeune Afrique reported that the leaders of SADC and EAC, meeting in a summit in Tanzania, urged an end to fighting between the Congolese army and the M23 and its Rwandan allies, and that the defence chiefs of the two blocs were tasked to meet within five days and give technical guidance on an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, a spokesperson said.
claims.place_as_written: Dar es Salaam, Tanzania (call on North and South Kivu conflict)
claims.actor_as_written: EAC and SADC heads of state; Rwandan President Paul Kagame and (by videoconference) Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi attended, per Jeune Afrique
claims.verification_note: Both pages support the summit; JA copy is credited 'Par Jeune Afrique avec AFP', so origin is AFP; DW is its own reporting (Fréjus Quenum), independent. Statement attributed per source. The actor field's Kagame/videoconference Tshisekedi attendance is printed on the JA page: 'Le sommet, auquel ont participé le président rwandais Paul Kagame et, par vidéoconférence, son homologue congolais Félix Tshisekedi'. 'M23' (flagged '23') printed on JA page. excerpt_en flag: translation fine. Jeune Afrique's copy is credited 'Par Jeune Afrique avec AFP'. DW dates the summit Saturday 8 February 2025 (08.02.2025) in Dar es Salaam and separately reports the leaders demanded de-escalation measures.
claims.researcher_note: Two independent outlets on the same summit; DW dates the communiqué 8 Feb 2025. The Jeune Afrique excerpt does not itself print the date; date taken from DW.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Angola's earlier mediation ended after two diplomatic setbacks: it had announced the end of its mediation and said it wanted to concentrate on African Union priorities.
claims.place_as_written: Luanda, Angola (mediation on eastern DRC conflict)
claims.verification_note: Supported. The two setbacks are the failed Dec 2024 Luanda meeting and the AFC/M23 refusal of the 18 March meeting, both described just before on the page. excerpt_en flag: 'African Union' translates 'Union africaine'; acceptable. The page says the announcement came less than two weeks before 26 March 2025; the exact date of the announcement is not on this page.
claims.researcher_note: The excerpt's 'two setbacks' are described just before it on the page; announcement date not in excerpt (RFI, 24 Mar 2025, could not be fetched).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that a joint summit of SADC and EAC heads of state had resulted on Monday in the merger of the Luanda and Nairobi processes.
claims.actor_as_written: SADC and EAC heads of state
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and supports the narrow statement. Weekday-only timing kept as month precision; no date derived. The page (dated Wed 26 March 2025) says only 'lundi'; the exact Monday is not stated on the page and is not asserted here. The DW report on the 8 Feb summit also lists the merger of the Luanda and Nairobi processes as a measure retained then.
claims.researcher_note: Weekday only ('lundi') on a page dated Wed 26 Mar 2025; the page text is internally unclear on which Monday (the Feb joint summit was a Saturday, 8 Feb). Reviewer should check; do not draw a date from this claim.

claims.text: Al Jazeera reported that the US Treasury Department said on Thursday that Rwanda's Minister of State for Regional Integration James Kabarebe was being targeted because he is "central to Rwanda's support" for the M23 armed group.
claims.place_as_written: Washington, D.C. (sanctions relating to North and South Kivu conflict)
claims.actor_as_written: US Treasury Department; Rwanda (as sanctions target); M23
claims.verification_note: Supported; page published 20 Feb 2025 with 'on Thursday' (20 Feb 2025 was a Thursday). Attribution to Treasury preserved. Allegation by the US Treasury; Al Jazeera notes Rwanda denies supporting the M23.
claims.researcher_note: Date 2025-02-20 from the page URL and weekday 'Thursday'. Rwanda denies supporting M23 (see next claim). Second sanctioned person (M23 spokesperson) not in this excerpt.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the signing ceremony of the DRC-Rwanda peace agreement in Washington was presided over by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in the presence of Congolese Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner and her Rwandan counterpart Olivier Nduhungirehe.
claims.place_as_written: Washington, D.C. (agreement concerning the conflict in North and South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Supported. excerpt_en flag: capitalised words (US etc.) are translation of 'américain'; acceptable.
claims.researcher_note: Page title title_en: 'DRC and Rwanda sign a peace agreement in Washington under US auspices'.

claims.text: UN News reported that, in a statement released on 19 July, MONUSCO said the Declaration of Principles signed in Doha under Qatari mediation between the DRC government and AFC/M23 "reflects the parties’ resolve to prioritise peaceful means, establish a ceasefire, and set up a joint mechanism to define its practical implementation."
claims.place_as_written: Doha, Qatar (DRC government and AFC/M23; North and South Kivu conflict)
claims.verification_note: Supported; 'AFC/M23' (flagged '23') printed on page. Date is the MONUSCO statement date.
claims.researcher_note: UN News dates the MONUSCO statement 19 July; the page and Doha process pages date signature to 19 July 2025 (page headline-level; signing day itself is in the Qatari/AU texts).

claims.text: The Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the parties' progress included the signing of the ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism on October 14, 2025, and the detainee release mechanism on September 14, 2025.
claims.verification_note: Supported verbatim by the release. Dates as stated by the mediator; not independently checked here.
claims.researcher_note: Two dated mechanisms, as stated by the mediator.

claims.text: BBC News Afrique reported that the verdict of the Haute Cour militaire in the trial of Joseph Kabila was delivered on a Tuesday after several postponements: the former Congolese president was sentenced to death by the court, which also ordered his immediate arrest.
claims.verification_note: Supported. Not adding in-absentia detail (no fetched source prints it). The page's own 'crimes de guerre' wording is not used in the statement. Date derived from 'ce mardi' and the page update of 30 Sept 2025 (a Tuesday). The BBC page does not state the verdict was in absentia; it says his whereabouts are unknown. Joseph Kabila rejects all charges, per the same page.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday 'mardi' and the page's 'Mise à jour 30 septembre 2025' (page 'Published 25 juillet 2025'); Le Monde URL also dated 2025-09-30 (page could not be fetched). Verdict was in absentia per Le Monde headline (not fetched).

claims.text: The US State Department said, in a release on the signing of the Washington Accords for Peace and Prosperity between the DRC and Rwanda, that the DRC and Rwanda signed the Regional Economic Integration Framework, that President Felix Tshisekedi signed on behalf of the Government of the DRC and President Paul Kagame on behalf of the Government of Rwanda, and that the signing ceremony was attended by, among others, Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC; Government of Rwanda; United States
claims.verification_note: Draft tied the Tshisekedi/Kagame signatures to the REIF only; the release does not say which instrument that sentence refers to, and its main subject is the Washington Accords. Narrowed to the release's own sentences; 'Felix' spelled as printed. The release says the signing on December 4 was hosted by President Donald J. Trump.
claims.researcher_note: Official US release; mediator's own account. Date from release URL path and search listing (4 Dec 2025).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that representatives of the Congolese government and the AFC/M23, meeting from 17 to 21 August 2026 in Switzerland, agreed new steps for the Doha peace process, including a roadmap for continuing negotiations and strengthened follow-up of their commitments.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and matches. excerpt_en flag is only sentence-initial words (The, Meeting); the translation renders the excerpt alone.
claims.researcher_note: State.gov and France24 results (22-23 Aug 2026) carry the joint statement; not opened.

claims.text: BBC News Afrique reported that the creation of the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), with Joseph Kabila as president, was announced by FRN adviser Claude Ibalanky at a joint press conference at the former president's residence in Goma, a city controlled by the M23; BBC described the FRN as replacing the AFC-M23, and reported that Kabila would have as deputies the rebel leaders Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa, Freddy Kaniki and Sultani Makenga.
claims.actor_as_written: FRN (Front pour la refondation de la nation); Joseph Kabila; AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Date 2026-10-13 was not printed in any excerpt; set to a range ending on the publication date. Added the deputies clause, which source 2 prints (resolves the entities flag). excerpt_en flags are sentence-initial words only. The BBC article (published 14 October 2026) does not date the press conference; its sidebar lists a related BBC item dated 13 October 2026 ('L'ancien président nommé chef de la nouvelle coalition rebelle'). Announcement date therefore on or before 14 October 2026; exact day unconfirmed.
claims.researcher_note: Announcement date not stated in excerpts; other results say meeting in Goma 10-11 Oct, declaration dated 12 Oct (Instagram snippets, not opened); BBC published 14 Oct. Date is approximate. Kinshasa's reaction in the next claim.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the AFC/M23 made public on 6 June 2026 in Goma decision N°033/COORDO-PR/AFC-M23/2026 appointing new political-administrative authorities in South Kivu, including Kyalangalilwa Mulondani Nicolas as mayor of Bukavu.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; figure 033 is on the page (passage given). Deputy mayor Nyota Luandja Céline is printed in source 1. excerpt_en flags are sentence-initial only. The decision number is printed on the page, not in the stored excerpt. Per the page the decision modifies an earlier decision of April 2025, and also names: Shaka Muhoza and Bahaya Léon (Bagira), Mweze Prisca and Mutunwa Mbulanga (Ibanda), Ruremesha Théo and Cikuru Barhakaziga Pascaline (Kadutu), Ntambuka Pascal and Mwimbirisa Bulikoko René (Idjwi), Elie Rubabura Espoir and Kasindi Kingombe Benjamin (Kabare), Buseyi Jean Bosco and Muhamuka Mweze Amza (Kalehe), Shengamungu Anastasie and Tumusifu Félicien (Walungu), Sengimana Ruhungande Augustin and Mahombi Mutumai (Minova cité). Names-only follow-up needed.
claims.researcher_note: Party decision as reported by local outlet; the decision text itself not seen. Page also names commune and territory appointees (Bagira, Ibanda, Kadutu, Idjwi, Kabare, Kalehe, Walungu, Minova) — available for a names-only follow-up.

claims.text: A joint statement by the representatives of the Government of the DRC and of the AFC/M23, published by the African Union Peace and Security Department, said the Parties agreed on the critical importance of ensuring life-saving humanitarian assistance for the people of eastern DRC and made substantial progress toward a protocol on Humanitarian Access and Judicial Protection, agreed to refrain from attacks on objects indispensable to the survival of the civilian population, including hospital and school facilities, and agreed to respect and protect humanitarian actors.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC; AFC/M23 (joint statement also released with Qatar, the United States, Togo as AU mediator, the African Union Commission and Switzerland)
claims.verification_note: Credited the joint statement to all its authors (not the hosting AU page); removed the '18 April' date from the statement (not printed in an excerpt; it stays in the date field); added the hospital-facilities commitment, relevant to health-care access, from the same page. Joint text of the parties and mediators, hosted by the AU; meetings held 13-17 April in Montreux. It records commitments in negotiation, not implementation. The page title carries the date 18 April 2026.
claims.researcher_note: Joint party text hosted by AU; the page lists the title date '18 April 2026' (search snippet showed 19 Apr). Also covers ceasefire verification mechanism and prisoner release; the same page carries a commitment to refrain from attacks on hospital and school facilities.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the chef-lieu of Walungu territory was encircled, with the Wazalendo on one side and the M23 on the other, that the local administration was paralysed with its officials forced to live in hiding, and that the police and intelligence services were absent.
claims.actor_as_written: local administration; Wazalendo; M23; PNC and intelligence services
claims.verification_note: Report date (19 March) came only from the page header; removed from the statement, kept in the date field. Condition described as current at the report date.
claims.researcher_note: Report date; condition described as ongoing at publication.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that several residents of Kaziba, Walungu territory, left their homes on Wednesday 23 April because of clashes between the AFC/M23 rebels and various Wazalendo groups.
claims.place_as_written: Kaziba chefferie (Mushenyi, Cibanda, Nyanfunze), Walungu territory
claims.verification_note: 'Plusieurs' is 'several', not 'many'; 'according to several local sources' attaches on the page to the resumption of fighting, not to the departures, so removed. This article dates the Wazalendo retaking of Kaziba to 17 March; Actualite.cd's 17 March article says 15 March.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the administrator of Shabunda territory, Justin Balegamire Byenda, detained in Maniema for more than nine months, was acquitted by military justice and reinstated on Thursday by provincial justice minister Faustin Mayani Shindano, amid an open conflict with his deputy Konga Konga, each reportedly relying on Wazalendo militiamen to assert power.
claims.verification_note: Supported; date from the article lead. Radio Okapi says the ceremony was disrupted by unrest; the minister blamed people 'instrumentalised' by offices in Kinshasa. The acquittal concerned a murder case, per the minister.
claims.researcher_note: The article lead gives the ceremony as Thursday 26 March 2026; the excerpt itself says only "jeudi".

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that massive population displacements had been recorded for several days in the villages of Kashongo, Magunda, Msongyo and Maheta following clashes of 24 to 27 September 2026 between the AFC/M23 coalition, which it described as backed by Red Tabara and Twirwaheno, and the FARDC/Wazalendo; the local Itombwe youth council said the incidents caused large population movements.
claims.place_as_written: Kashongo, Magunda, Msongyo and Maheta, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 coalition 'appuyée par les Red Tabara et les Twirwaheno' vs FARDC/Wazalendo
claims.verification_note: The draft attributed the outlet's narration (including the Red Tabara/Twirwaheno backing) to the youth council; the page attributes it to no one. Re-attributed clause by clause; 'Mwenga territory' cut from the statement (only the title prints Mwenga). The youth-council clause is page-only. Title confirmed. C. The displacements and the description of the coalition are Actualite.cd's narration; the youth council (president Mfariji Lewis, per the page) is quoted on the incidents and movements towards Masango, Kigoma and Itombwe forest areas. The headline places the area in Mwenga territory.
claims.researcher_note: Title reconstructed from search snippet and URL; verify. Source is the local youth council (Mfariji Lewis, president), relayed by Actualite.cd. Placement in Mwenga territory is the source's. 'Twirwaheno' is spelled as printed.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, quoting a journalist who attended a meeting held by M23 in Minova, that the rebels said schools could reopen within 48 hours and promised that the RN2 Minova-Bweremana-Sake-Goma road would be reopened.
claims.verification_note: Name M23 and the meeting are printed in the replacement passage on the same page; '23' is part of the group name. Meeting date is the page's 'cet avant-midi' on a page dated Tuesday 21/01/2025, so date is approximate to the report day. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Single anonymous journalist; the date is the report date (meeting 'this morning' on Tuesday 21 January per the page).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local activists, that after fighting on Sunday 6 and Monday 7 April on the hills above Bushushu, Lemera and Ihusi, local sources said most of the population of the Kalehe highlands had displaced toward Bushushu, Mabuka and Ihusi.
claims.verification_note: Supported by the page; dates from the passage preceding the excerpt. On the page, local rights activists are cited for the recovery of localities after the 6-7 April fighting; the displacement is attributed to local sources.
claims.researcher_note: Same source also reports M23 fighters seen at Kalehe centre (Ihusi) on 9 April.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing several local sources, that violent clashes between Wazalendo and M23 since the afternoon of jeudi 10 juillet in the villages of Kasheke and Buzunga (Kalehe territory) caused a mass displacement of civilians; Radio Maendeleo likewise reported that fighting on 10 July caused a mass displacement of the population in the villages of Kasheke, Buzunga and Lemera in Mbinga Sud groupement, Kalehe territory.
claims.place_as_written: Kasheke, Buzunga, Lemera (Mbinga Sud groupement), Kalehe territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Destinations and the 'hundreds of families' / 'thousands' figures were not in the stored excerpts: removed from the statement; the Radio Okapi figure is noted with its page passage in replacement_quotes. Two Bukavu outlets, each citing local sources; whether their local sources overlap is not known. Radio Maendeleo puts the displaced 'par milliers' (civil-society sources), not recorded in the figures.
claims.researcher_note: Two local outlets (Radio Okapi, Bukavu; Radio Maendeleo, Bukavu community radio) both cite local sources; independence not established. Radio Okapi's 11 July article also says the M23 was trying to retake RN2.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that continuing clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters in the highlands of Kalehe territory were preventing parents from preparing their children's 2025-2026 school year and, according to several local sources, were causing massive displacement of the population.
claims.place_as_written: Highlands (hauts plateaux) of Kalehe territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed the unprinted '25 August' from the statement. Ongoing situation as of the article of 25 August 2025; no villages or figures.
claims.researcher_note: Qualitative, no figures or specific villages. Shows fighting in Kalehe highlands continuing in late August.

claims.text: OCHA reported that on 4 October violent fighting in the localities of Chulwe and Cishadu, Luhago grouping (Kabare territory), caused the mass displacement of families to safer areas, that figures for the recently displaced were being verified, and that several victims, including dead and wounded among civilians, were reported.
claims.place_as_written: Chulwe and Cishadu, Luhago grouping, Kabare territory
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; widened to the contiguous passage that carries 'Kabare'. Year and 'DRC' dropped from statement (not printed in excerpt); the date field carries 2025. OCHA does not name the parties to the fighting or give casualty numbers.
claims.researcher_note: Parties to the fighting not named by OCHA. Report dated 17 Nov 2025, published 18 Nov.

claims.text: OCHA DRC reported that on 12 October 2025 about 450 households, close to 2,700 people, fled new fighting between armed groups in the localities of Civanga and Kasirusiru (Kabare territory) and took refuge at Miti and Murhesa, and that humanitarian access remained strongly limited by persistent insecurity.
claims.place_as_written: Civanga and Kasirusiru, Kabare territory; refuge at Miti and Murhesa
claims.actor_as_written: armed groups, not named by the source
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and matches. '2700' flag is the French thousands separator ('2 700'). 'Kabare' is the section heading on the page directly above this passage.

claims.text: OCHA reported that between 12 and 15 October about 27,700 people fled fighting between armed groups in the mountains overlooking Katasomwa, Mbesho, Kashihe, Katoki, Mweya and other localities of Kalehe territory, and that the living conditions of the displaced and of host communities were critical, including a rupture of medical inputs and an increased risk of sexual violence.
claims.place_as_written: Mountains above Katasomwa, Mbesho, Kashihe, Katoki, Mweya, Bwangala, Kilijiwe, Kasasa, Kaitoleya, Bushushu 1 and 2, Kalehe territory; refuge in Kalehe centre, Kasheke, Tchoki, Luzira and others
claims.actor_as_written: armed groups, not named by the source
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact; widened to contiguous passages carrying 'Kalehe' and the subject of the second sentence. '27700' flag is the thousands separator. Count is OCHA's. Caritas Bukavu's own figures for the Kalehe fighting differ (see the Caritas claims) and are kept separate; the sources do not reconcile them.
claims.researcher_note: Caritas Bukavu (below) gives different displacement counts for the 7-12 October fighting: figures are kept separate.

claims.text: Caritasdev.cd, summarising a Caritas Bukavu report on the humanitarian crisis in Kalehe, reported that the fighting of 12 October displaced more than 7,700 people to the areas of Kasheke, Luzira, Bushaku and Kabamba.
claims.place_as_written: Kasheke and Luzira health areas, Kalehe health zone
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed in the stored excerpt; the page describes clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo self-defence groups
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Narrowed to what the stored excerpt and title print: the assessment dates, the table figures and the M23/Wazalendo description are on the page but not in the excerpt, so they are in the note pending an excerpt extension. Figures are Caritas's and kept separate from OCHA's. Lead for an excerpt extension (source_edits.py add_excerpt), all on the same page: the assessment ran 'Du 20 au 27 octobre 2025' in the Luzira and Kasheke health areas, Kalehe health zone; the crisis is described as 'exacerbée par les affrontements entre les rebelles du M23 et les groupes d’autodéfense Wazalendo'; a table gives 'Kasheke 2 043 10 215 Luzira 1 275 5 610' (displaced households / people), which the source does not reconcile with the 7,700 figure. OCHA, as quoted by Actualite.cd (24 Nov 2025), describes the same Caritas Bukavu assessment as running 20 to 26 October and counting close to 19,900 displaced from fighting of 7 to 12 October: dates and counts differ between the two.
claims.researcher_note: Caritas is a church humanitarian body; the table gives household and people counts per health area. The 7,700 figure and the table figures (10,215 + 5,610) are not reconciled by the source.

claims.text: OCHA reported in a flash update that since 2 December 2025 the security situation in South Kivu had deteriorated following an escalation of armed clashes in the territories of Uvira, Walungu, Mwenga, Shabunda, Kabare, Fizi and Kalehe, and that, according to estimates from local authorities, civil society and partners on the ground, more than 500,000 people were on the move across the province.
claims.place_as_written: South Kivu: Uvira, Walungu, Mwenga, Shabunda, Kabare, Fizi, Kalehe territories
claims.actor_as_written: armed clashes, parties not named by the source
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed 'of 12 December 2025' (in the URL, not the excerpt or title). '500000' flag is the thousands separator. An estimate from local authorities, civil society and partners, not a verified count.
claims.researcher_note: Estimate, not a verified count.

claims.text: Soleil du Graben reported that the humanitarian situation of more than 10.000 people who had fled fighting since 05 February 2026 in Lumbishi, Chambombo, Katasomwa, Kitendebwa, Zilaro and other places in the Kalehe highlands was very worrying; citing concordant sources, it said displaced families were sheltering with host families or sleeping in the open at Numbi, Nyabibwe and Kalungu, and that a local notable appealed for humanitarian aid. The outlet attributed the displacement to clashes between armed groups without naming them.
claims.place_as_written: Kalehe highlands (Lumbishi, Chambombo, Katasomwa, Kitendebwa, Zilaro), Kalehe, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: armed groups (not named by the source)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt real and on point. Removed 'Bukavu-based' (page does not say so). Figure written as printed (10.000) to match the excerpt. Narrowed actor to the source's wording; added sheltering and appeal clauses from the page. Soleil du Graben's own article list carries AFC/M23-administration items (e.g. 'Hommage des autorités de l'AFC-M23'), so the portal may be aligned with the de facto authority. Unsigned ('Rédaction'); sources anonymous. The notable is named on the page (see replacement quote); the name is not in the stored excerpt. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Bukavu portal that also carries AFC/M23-administration communiqués (see other r1 claims); treat as possibly aligned with the de facto authority. Anonymous 'sources concordantes'. A notable, Valentin Akilimali Maheshe, appealed for aid; displaced reported sheltering at Numbi, Nyabibwe and Kalungu.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that traffic had timidly resumed on the Kalonge-Bunyakiri axis in Kalehe territory after three months of interruption, which it attributed to persistent clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo militiamen; a civil society actor at Kalonge said motorbikes and buses were already travelling and that the situation had been catastrophic at Kalonge and Bunyakiri.
claims.verification_note: Removed '12 February 2026' from the statement: it is the publication date, not a date the page gives for the resumption. 'looting_or_destruction' did not fit; reclassified as access/humanitarian disruption. Date is the article's publication date; the page does not give the day traffic resumed. The civil society actor is named on the page as Yoweli Nyabirungu. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Category chosen for access disruption; reclassify as displacement_humanitarian if preferred. Civil society actor Yoweli Nyabirungu is quoted elsewhere on the page.

claims.text: Mediacongo reported that daily life in Bunyakiri, Kalehe territory, remained profoundly disrupted by the prolonged blockage of Route nationale 3 (RN3), which it attributed to AFC-M23/Wazalendo clashes lasting more than three months; the president of a local civil society group said the movement of goods was almost nil for lack of authorisation from the AFC-M23 authorities.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement. Added the civil-society statement about AFC-M23 authorisation, which is what supports the de_facto_governance category. Page credit at the foot reads 'MediaCongo LaPrunelle RDC / MCP'. The civil society president is named on the page as Isaya Benjamin (Force Vive Bunyakiri). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: The same page quotes civil society president Isaya Benjamin saying goods circulation is almost nil for lack of authorisation from AFC-M23 authorities (not separately excerpted: see next claim).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, relaying the MSF annual report on its 2025 activities, that the MSF emergency team helped populations displaced at Katana, Kalehe and Bunyakiri by clashes between the Congolese army, its Wazalendo allies and the armed group AFC/M23; MSF said its medical teams supported health facilities whose activities had been disrupted by the conflict and, in hospitals and health centres, cared for survivors of sexual violence among other services.
claims.actor_as_written: MSF (reporting); Congolese army, Wazalendo, AFC/M23 (named as parties to clashes)
claims.verification_note: The page reports MSF's 2025 annual activities; the statement implied a February 2026 response. Re-dated to 2025 as a range and marked new_related_event. Added the sexual-violence care clause (phase 1 focus) from the same MSF passage. Activities date from 2025 (MSF annual report), not Q1 2026; exact months not given. The page gives no separate figures for sexual-violence care. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: The MSF statement refers to MSF's 2025 annual activity report; the article is dated 2026-02-14, so the response may relate to 2025 and falls outside the window. Reviewer should likely drop or keep only as context.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that local civil society said nearly 48 000 displaced people were in an alarming humanitarian situation after fleeing fighting between AFC/M23 and wazalendo in Ziralo groupement (Kalehe), and that all schools in the groupement remained closed.
claims.verification_note: 'about' narrowed to 'nearly' (près de); figure written as printed. Civil society figure relayed by the outlet ('près de 48 000'). Kept separate from the Kivu Morning Post civil-society figure of 'plus de 38 500' (9 April); different dates and counts.
claims.researcher_note: Figure is civil society's, relayed by the outlet.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to local civil society, more than 38 500 people fled their villages following fighting in Ziralo groupement (Kalehe), most of them towards Lulambo and Biriko in Walikale territory.
claims.verification_note: Removed the day numbers no excerpt prints from the statement (moved to date); belligerents stay in the actor field. Night of Wednesday 8 to Thursday 9 April 2026 per the page. Figure kept separate from Actualite.cd's 'près de 48 000' (17 April). Same article says AFC-M23 was consolidating its hold on Tushunguti, which differs from Actualite.cd's account of a FARDC retaking by 10 April; it also reports an AFC-M23 communiqué by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka accusing Kinshasa of 'délibérées' attacks in violation of the ceasefire (a party statement not yet recorded).
claims.researcher_note: Figure differs from Actualite.cd (48,000 on 17 April); different dates and counts, not merged.

claims.text: Soleil du Graben reported that an AFC/M23 delegation led by the vice-governor in charge of political, administrative and judicial matters, Dunia Masumbuko Bwenge Doux, relaunched customary administration of the Ntambuka chiefdom on Idjwi island and installed a seven-member peace committee, in the presence of Idjwi territory administrator Pascal Ntambuka.
claims.verification_note: All names spelled as printed; three excerpts are one article. Dunia Masumbuko Bwenge Doux is an AFC/M23 de facto official (South Kivu vice-governor in the AFC/M23 administration). Soleil du Graben, byline 'admin', reads close to AFC/M23 communications; treat as the AFC/M23 side's account of its own event. Mission day not printed; 'Last updated Mai 16, 2026'. Page also says the delegation urged families to send their children into the security forces, especially the ARC (recruitment appeal). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Soleil du Graben, 16 May 2026 (signed 'Rédaction'; the site's coverage reads as AFC/M23-aligned, so treat as the movement's account). All clauses are on the page; the stored excerpts lacked the relaunch of customary administration, now added. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Soleil du Graben, 16 May 2026 (signed 'Rédaction'; the site's coverage reads as AFC/M23-aligned, so treat as the movement's account). All clauses are on the page; the stored excerpts lacked the relaunch of customary administration, now added.
claims.researcher_note: Local web outlet (Soleil du Graben, eastern DRC); tone is neutral-to-favourable to the AFC/M23 administration; treat as report of an AFC/M23 event, not independent confirmation. The event day (mission) is taken from publication date 2026-05-16.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to local sources, Wazalendo fighters led by Noah Maachano, of the Maï-Maï Lamuka group, had reportedly also deployed in several neighbouring villages, notably Shangi, Katahandwa and Shoa.
claims.place_as_written: Shangi, Katahandwa, Shoa (near Lumbishi), Kalehe/Masisi border
claims.verification_note: Removed 'around Lumbishi' (not stated) and restored the conditional ('se seraient déployés'). The source does not say which locality the villages neighbour (the article discusses Kasake and Lumbishi) nor which province they are in.
claims.researcher_note: Shangi/Katahandwa/Shoa province not stated by the source; province field set to South Kivu provisionally.

claims.text: La Presse Africaine reported, citing local sources, that clashes involving M23 fighters had reportedly caused population displacement in several areas of Kalehe, Masisi and Walikale; Olivier Kaskoti, a Tembo notable and honorary president of Buuma bwe Batembo (Beni section), said localities in Ziralo grouping and parts of Ufamandu grouping (Masisi) and Walowa-Lwanda (Walikale) faced a deteriorating security situation for several days, and alleged that M23 used drones and artillery fire, allegations the outlet said could not be independently verified.
claims.verification_note: Draft attributed the Ziralo/Ufamandu/Walowa-Lwanda displacement to local sources; the page gives the displacement at territory level (local sources) and the specific groupings as Kaskoti's account of deteriorating security. Separated; source 2 extended to the full sentence. (Excerpt extensions proposed in clause_support; replacement_quotes are not applied to exact sources.) Report date used (28 August 2026); the article gives no event date. Byline Dieudonné Hangi, LPA Beni.
claims.researcher_note: Date is report date. Byline Dieudonné Hangi (LPA Beni).

claims.text: Mediacongo reported that the ultimatum set by the United States for Rwanda to withdraw its troops from eastern DRC expired on Wednesday 15 July 2026, and that, according to security and local sources, the rebel movement, after consolidating its positions in the Hauts Plateaux and other strategic areas, would now be seeking to extend its influence towards Baraka, an important town in Fizi territory.
claims.verification_note: Restored the conditional; identity of 'le mouvement rebelle' as AFC/M23 rests on the same article's first sentence. The article identifies the rebel movement as AFC/M23 (headline and first sentence). The Baraka movement is conditional in the source ('chercherait'). Article byline Roberto Tshahe Da Cruz. Rwandan and US statements on the expiry not found in this source.
claims.researcher_note: Outside my unit's core geography (Fizi); recorded as context only. Marco Rubio named in an adjacent sentence, not in the excerpts: remove if checker flags. Rwanda/US official statements on the expiry not located.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that at the Kavumu primary school, about 4 km from Numbi, parents rushed to collect their children because of the deteriorating security situation and the approach of the battlefield.
claims.place_as_written: Kavumu primary school near Numbi, Kalehe territory
claims.verification_note: Removed the editorial disambiguation from the statement (moved to note); the rest is verbatim. This Kavumu is a place about 4 km from Numbi, not Kavumu airport in Kabare.
claims.researcher_note: Name collision with Kavumu airport (Kabare): not the same place.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported on 3 October that, according to civil society, more than 1,900 households from Kalehe highlands (mainly Ziralo and Numbi groupings) and Ufamandu grouping in Masisi had taken refuge in the Buzi grouping of Minova, having fled fighting between the AFC/M23 and the government coalition over the previous two weeks.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23; government coalition (as named by the source)
claims.verification_note: Flagged numbers are the '1 900' spacing and the wave figures, all on the page ('plus de 1 015 ménages , la seconde de plus de 466 ménages et la troisième de plus de 226 ménages'). Single local origin: C. Households, not persons. Three waves per the page: over 1 015, over 466 and over 226 households.
claims.researcher_note: Households, not persons; the source says the displaced had no assistance to date. Predates the 5-6 Oct Kalehe fighting; this is the earlier wave.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that thousands of families who fled clashes between the FRN and the FARDC supported by Wazalendo in the Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory, were living in difficult conditions at Nyabibwe, lacking food, shelter and basic necessities, mostly women and children.
claims.actor_as_written: FRN; FARDC; Wazalendo (parties named by the source)
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the page; no source named for 'thousands'.
claims.researcher_note: No source named for the figure. Nyabibwe is on the Kalehe lakeshore road.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing a video from the South Kivu governor's communication unit, that FRN vice-presidents Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo and Bertrand Bisimwa met FRN cadres from across South Kivu in Bukavu on Thursday 22 October 2026 to discuss the movement's political vision and organisation.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; partisan origin, C. Origin is the FRN-run governor's office video; what the FRN presented, not independent. This page spells the movement 'Front de la refondation nationale'.
claims.researcher_note: Source is the movement's own governor-office video as relayed by KMP: evidence of what the FRN presented, not independent. Related Ukwelitimes item also exists (lead only).

claims.text: OCHA reported that humanitarian actors estimated more than 554 000 people were affected by the crisis in Uvira city, including 270 000 internally displaced people, of whom more than 126 000 fled to the Ruzizi plain in February 2025.
claims.verification_note: All figures verbatim; estimates attributed to humanitarian actors as OCHA states.
claims.researcher_note: Estimates by humanitarian actors, as OCHA states.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that fighting between the armed groups Red Tabara and Wazalendo was reported on Thursday 20 March in Fizi territory, South Kivu, that people of the Minembwe Hauts Plateaux were fleeing toward Fizi centre, and that the territory administrator confirmed this, appealed to the belligerents to end hostilities and invited humanitarian organisations to assist thousands of displaced people.
claims.place_as_written: Hauts Plateaux de Minembwe to Fizi centre, Fizi territory
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on Radio Okapi page (published 20/03/2025 22:59). Administrator unnamed.
claims.researcher_note: The territory administrator's statement is reported without a name; Fizi territory administrator unnamed on the page.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that recent clashes between the FARDC and a Twirwaneho-Red Tabara-M23 coalition at Rugezi in the hauts et moyens plateaux of Fizi, 'five days ago', caused mass population displacement; the Fizi territory administrator Samy Kalonji Badibanga said some households were heading to Uvira, and unconfirmed information said Wazalendo had singled out displaced people heading to Uvira as belonging to rebel movements.
claims.place_as_written: Rugezi, Hauts et Moyens Plateaux de Fizi; route to Uvira
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC vs Twirwaneho-Red Tabara-M23 coalition; Wazalendo (alleged targeting of displaced)
claims.verification_note: All clauses on the retained page; the administrator's name and the Uvira sentence are outside the stored excerpts (excerpt gap). Unconfirmed allegation kept as unconfirmed. Date approximate: 'il y a cinq jours' in an article of 14 June 2025. Lead: the administrator himself refers to information that a group of Banyamulenge displaced people may have been targeted by the Wazalendo ('il y aurait un groupe de déplacés internes Banyamulenge pris pour cible par les Wazalendo'), conditional.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from 'il y a cinq jours' and publication date 14 Jun (approx. 9 Jun). The singling-out allegation is explicitly unconfirmed. The administrator also said Banyamulenge, Bembe, Fuliru and Barega displaced move together.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that on Wednesday 11 June the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Kalonji Badibanga, said more than 600 000 internally displaced people lived in precarious conditions in the sectors of Lulenge, Mutambala and Tanganyika, and that their number had grown in the Hauts et Moyens Plateaux of Fizi since the taking of Rugezi village by Twirwaneho and Red Tabara militiamen allied to AFC/M23; he said children no longer attended school, which led to their forced enrolment in armed groups.
claims.place_as_written: Lulenge, Mutambala and Tanganyika sectors, Fizi
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho and Red Tabara allied to AFC/M23 (as named by the administrator)
claims.verification_note: Draft softened the administrator's claim ('risked forced enrolment'); the source says it leads to forced enrolment (a generalisation, no specific incident). Figure written as the source prints it. Figure from one official (a Kinshasa-appointed authority), not independently verified. In source 1, 'Elle' refers to 'cette autorité politico-administrative' (grammatical gender); the stored excerpt_en's 'She' should read 'It (the authority)': the administrator is referred to as 'Il' elsewhere on the page. He also said pregnant women were giving birth in the bush.
claims.researcher_note: Single official source (territory administrator, a Kinshasa-appointed authority); figure not independently verified and exceeds typical OCHA scale for the territory; the administrator is a party-aligned authority. Forced-recruitment statement is his generalisation, no specific incident.

The Fizi territory administrator, Sammy Badibanga, warned of a grave humanitarian crisis, denounced the persistent illicit exploitation of natural resources, and called for an urgent strengthening of emergency interventions by provincial and national authorities and NGOs.

The 100 000 figure is in Radio Okapi's own voice with no stated count method. The page spells the administrator 'Sammy Badibanga' (other Radio Okapi pages: 'Samy Kalonji Badibanga'). The page also says FARDC/Wazalendo fighting against the Twirwaneho-Red Tabara-M23 coalition displaced thousands. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 10 Aug 2025. The stored excerpt carried only the displacement figure; administrator passages added. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 10 Aug 2025.
