claims.researcher_note: Figure is Radio Okapi's, apparently from the territory administrator (Sammy Badibanga); the page does not give an independent count. 'Samy'/'Sammy' spelling varies across pages.

claims.text: The DRC Protection Cluster July 2025 highlights reported that on 23 July several gunshots were heard in Kagurube/Runingu village on the RN512 north of Uvira, and that, fearing clashes, about 202 households (1,010 people) of Runingu reportedly moved preventively to Sange, Mwaba, Biriba, Kabunambo and Kiliba.
claims.place_as_written: Kagurube/Runingu (RN512, north of Uvira) to Sange, Mwaba, Biriba, Kabunambo, Kiliba
claims.verification_note: Verified verbatim in the PDF.
claims.researcher_note: Precautionary displacement; no actor named.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources in the region, that the fear of population in the Tanganyika sector of Fizi was precipitated and aggravated by the movements of FARDC, Burundian and Wazalendo soldiers fleeing the Uvira front to take refuge in Fizi; it quoted Sammy Amimo, vice-president of civil society in Fizi territory, as saying Mboko town was overwhelmed by displaced people, with more than 18 000 families having arrived although the rebels had not yet reached the Tanganyika sector.
claims.place_as_written: Mboko, Tanganyika sector, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: soldiers of the FARDC, Burundian army and Wazalendo (movements), per Actualite.cd sources
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; 18 000 families is a civil-society figure. excerpt_en flags checked: the English renders the excerpt alone (capitalisation/expanded acronyms only).
claims.researcher_note: Civil-society figure, not verified by humanitarian agencies. Marks Mboko as not yet reached by rebels on 12 Dec; Actualite.cd of 22 Dec has the AFC-M23 holding Mboko.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Kalonji Badibanga, said displaced people in Fizi territory were sheltering in schools and churches, and that the Tanganyika lakeshore, a focus of cholera and measles, exposed children to major epidemic risks.
claims.place_as_written: Lake Tanganyika shore, Makobola-Mboko, Fizi-centre, Point Zéro Kwa Mulima (Fizi)
claims.actor_as_written: not applicable (epidemic context); displacement from fighting between AFC-M23 and FARDC
claims.verification_note: Supported by page; epidemic context, not an attack on health care. Name order differs from the 7 Feb article ('Samy Badibanga Kalonji'). Schools/churches detail is Radio Okapi's narration. Date is the publication date.
claims.researcher_note: Official statement of an administrator; no case counts given. Not an attack on health care; recorded as epidemic context.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing a Mercy Corps humanitarian report for February, that 15 200 households from the highlands were recorded in Maniema province, in Kabambare and Pangi territories, and said clashes between FARDC with Wazalendo and Ngumino-Twirwaneho allied to AFC/M23 in the Fizi highlands caused the movements, while the report also attributes part of the Kabambare displacement to heavy rains.
claims.place_as_written: Kabambare and Pangi territories, Maniema (displaced from Fizi highlands)
claims.actor_as_written: displacement linked to FARDC/Wazalendo vs Ngumino-Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 fighting
claims.verification_note: Figures checked on the page. Flagged numbers are in the figures field and printed on the page. Breakdown per the quoted report: Kabambare about 11 040 households (Lusangi 7 940; Kabambare health zone 3 100); Pangi 4 160 (Kampene). The rain sentence is the outlet's narration between quotes from the report; the next sentence cites OCHA via the report.
claims.researcher_note: Figure in statement as given; the article adds that part of the Kabambare movement is due to heavy rains in Ndandalukala (OCHA cited). Breakdown: Kabambare about 11 040 households (Lusangi 7 940; Kabambare 3 100); Pangi 4 160 (Kampene).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several local sources, that Wazalendo militiamen operating at Runingu announced on Sunday the prohibition of entry into Uvira city for anyone coming from areas controlled by M23, citing suspected spying on FARDC positions; Ruzizi plain residents of Kamanyola, Luvungi, Luberizi and Sange said they were turned away from the Kashatu market at Runingu.
claims.place_as_written: Runingu, Kashatu market; Uvira city entrance
claims.verification_note: Supported by the page; single Burundi-based outlet. Sunday = 15 March, computed from publication date 16 March. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi, Uvira 16 Mar 2026: Wazalendo at Runingu announced on Sunday (15 Mar) a ban on entry to Uvira for anyone from M23-held areas; Ruzizi plain residents say they were turned away from Kashatu market. All clauses are on the page; the spying justification was in no stored excerpt, now added.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from 'ce dimanche' and publication date 16 March (Monday), so Sunday 15 March. Single Burundi-based outlet. The same article says the Ruzizi plain localities (Kamanyola, Luvungi, Luberizi, Sange) are under M23 control, and that civil society fears effects on access to fields.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the humanitarian blockage at Minembwe was intensifying, with no exit and no resupply of food and medicines, and that humanitarian access was blocked. It said the Mahoro Peace association, which groups Congolese nationals living in the United States, had indicated that 32 civilians were wounded between 8 and 11 June.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. 'blocage' rendered as 'blockage' (not 'blockade', which implies a deliberate act the source does not state); the 17 June date stays in the date field only. Figure attributed to Mahoro Peace. The figure of 32 wounded is Mahoro Peace's (a US-based association; SOS Médias Burundi describes it as grouping members of the Banyamulenge community), not verified. The outlet does not say who imposes the blockage.
claims.researcher_note: Figure from a diaspora association (Banyamulenge-linked per SOS Médias Burundi), not independently verified. Cause of access block not stated.

claims.text: Mediacongo (Radio Okapi / MCP credit) reported that, according to local civil society, repeated Twirwaneho attacks on positions retaken by FARDC were causing new displacement, and that Fizi territory administrator Samy Badibanga said victims and vulnerable people were estimated at several thousand.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; civil-society clause on the page. Official's estimate with no breakdown or method. The same official is spelled 'Sammy Badibanga' on Actualite.cd (18 June).
claims.researcher_note: Official's estimate, no breakdown or method; date is the 'Friday 26 June' reporting day.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local civil society, that at least 155 houses were damaged by torrential rain and strong winds in the villages of Magunda, Kitembe and Kitoga (Kigoma grouping, Bafuliiru chiefdom, Uvira highlands), with the weather reported to have struck since 20 October 2026.
claims.place_as_written: Magunda, Kitembe, Kitoga, Kigoma grouping, Hauts Plateaux d'Uvira, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Matches page (byline Omeur Mudekereza). Weather damage, not a conflict event; context only.
claims.researcher_note: Weather, not conflict; recorded as humanitarian context for villages (Magunda) also named in the October fighting. Page 'last updated 2026/10/27'; 7sur7.cd carried the same item on 28 Oct.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing the same local civil society, that the Rubuga health centre lost its entire roof to the winds, complicating access to care, and that Byamungu Shamamba Paul, president of the Nouvelle Société civile congolaise in Uvira territory, said about eight health centres in the northern part of the Hauts Plateaux d'Uvira health zone had attendance difficulties and insufficient humanitarian support.
claims.place_as_written: Rubuga and northern Hauts Plateaux d'Uvira health zone, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Matches page; name spelled as printed. Weather damage, not an attack on health care; health-access context only.
claims.researcher_note: Weather damage, not an attack; relevant to health-care access in the area where fighting displaced people. 'La même source' = local civil society per preceding sentence.

claims.text: Amnesty International reported that, of 14 survivors of sexual violence from North and South Kivu it interviewed, eight said they were gang raped by M23 fighters, five said they were gang raped by Wazalendo fighters and one said she was gang raped by FARDC soldiers.
claims.actor_as_written: M23; Wazalendo; FARDC (as stated by survivors to Amnesty)
claims.verification_note: Figures written as the source prints them; date widened because the page dates some cases to January 2024. Counts are survivors' accounts ('said'). Some Wazalendo cases in the sample predate the window (two in January 2024, per the same page).
claims.researcher_note: Survivors are pseudonymised by Amnesty; no names recorded.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing a Human Rights Watch communiqué of 22 May, that HRW said it had asked in April for a meeting with Rwandan President Paul Kagame to discuss abuses by the Rwandan army and the M23 in eastern Congo and had received no response.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of Rwanda (President Kagame), as characterised by HRW
claims.verification_note: Matches the page. Records HRW's account of a non-response, not a Rwandan statement.
claims.researcher_note: Records HRW's account of a non-response; no Rwandan statement on the HRW Uvira report was found (see gaps).

claims.text: Amnesty International reported that, in research into M23 abuses at the Rubaya and Lomera mines, it documented the summary killing of 18 artisanal miners by M23 or their collaborators, at least nine of whom were beaten brutally and died at health centres or before they reached the hospital; Amnesty said it wrote to the M23 spokesperson and an M23 mining representative on 11 August 2026 and had received no response at the time of publication.
claims.place_as_written: Rubaya coltan mine area (Masisi, North Kivu) and Lomera gold mine (Kabare, South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: The two mine names rest on the report's scope passage (page, not the stored excerpt): extend the excerpt with source_edits.py add_excerpt. Date range 2026-01/2026-09 was not supported. The cited passages give no dates for the killings; the date shown is the report's publication date. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: letter of 11 August 2026; no response; Rubaya and Lomera mines 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-012: Read the report: attribution ('M23 or their collaborators') holds, and dated cases in the section fall inside the window (one death in February 2025; seven deaths January-March 2026). Added the right-of-reply passage so M23's silence is recorded rather than omitted.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): letter of 11 August 2026; no response; Rubaya and Lomera mines
claims.researcher_note: Amnesty report AFR 62/1454/2026 (21 September 2026); incident dates not stated in the cited passages. Interviews were conducted January-April 2026. Province: Rubaya is in North Kivu (Masisi); Lomera is in Kabare, South Kivu.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that at the time of writing (its letter of 5 June 2026) the FDLR was fragmented into three principal factions, FDLR-FOCA, FDLR-RUD and FDLR-Force de protection du peuple (FPP), and that all three had recently adopted alternative designations to obscure their FDLR affiliation.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt states factions and designations; finding is the Group's.
claims.researcher_note: UN Group of Experts (S/2026/466), copy hosted on ecoi.net. Alias detail from FDLR, Wazalendo and intelligence sources per the report's footnote.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that "Major-General" Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) and "General" Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro) remained FDLR-FOCA military commander and political leader respectively; it named "Brigadier-General" Emmanuel Nsengiyumva as overall FDLR-RUD leader and "Colonel" Dan Hategekimana as FDLR-FPP leader.
claims.verification_note: All names, ranks (in the Group's quotation marks) and aliases are printed in the excerpt. Spelling discrepancy: S/2026/466 prints 'Ntawuguka' (alias Omega Israel); S/2025/446 prints 'Ntawunguka' (alias Omega). Both kept as printed. Aliases Faida/Fayida Hakimu and Dan Simplice are printed in the excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Spelling 'Ntawuguka' as printed here; S/2025/446 prints 'Ntawunguka'. Sanctions designations (CDi.024, CDi.003) appear in the report.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that FDLR-FOCA, the largest FDLR faction, remained active on several major front lines in North Kivu, notably in Nyiragongo, Masisi, Rutshuru and Walikale territories, and that its special unit, the Commando de recherche et d'action en profondeur (CRAP), was reported to have active units on the outskirts of Goma and infiltrated in Goma town.
claims.place_as_written: Nyiragongo, Masisi, Rutshuru, Walikale (North Kivu); outskirts of Goma
claims.verification_note: Matches excerpt; 'reported to have' hedge kept. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-010: Small precision fix: the source says 'several major front lines ... notably in' those four territories; the statement dropped 'several' and 'notably' and so read as an exhaustive list.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; 'several' and 'notably' are in source 0
claims.researcher_note: Source of CRAP claim cited in report to FDLR-CRAP and Wazalendo sources.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that FDLR sources claimed the group's overall strength exceeded 10,000 combatants, while United Nations and intelligence sources estimated total FDLR strength at between 3,500 and 4,500 combatants.
claims.verification_note: Each figure kept attributed to its stated origin. Strength figures diverge sharply: FDLR's own claim (>10,000, half active) vs UN/intelligence estimate (3,500-4,500). Both reported by the Group of Experts.
claims.researcher_note: The report also cites the Washington Agreement estimate of 3,000 to 3,500 (not in this excerpt).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported, citing United Nations sources, that on 30 May 2025 AFC/M23 ordered the evacuation of over 240 households from five villages (Burambo, Kiyeye, Mayi ya Chumvi, Ngeri and Kiganda), leading to mass displacement of civilians.
claims.place_as_written: Burambo, Kiyeye, Mayi ya Chumvi, Ngeri, Kiganda (Rutshuru territory per the report context)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; location context confirmed on the page (Burambo listed in Binza). Appears in a footnote (fn 40) of S/2025/858 attached to the Binza (Rutshuru) section; the footnote cites UN sources.
claims.researcher_note: Footnote 40 of the report, attached to the anti-FDLR operations section. Territory inferred from the report's section on Rutshuru operations; the footnote itself does not name it.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the FARDC announcement triggered tensions between FARDC and FDLR and between FARDC and certain Wazalendo factions, and that subsequently some FARDC officers and government actors sought to reassure FDLR of their continued cooperation, given the essential role of FDLR in ongoing operations on the ground.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC officers and government actors; FDLR
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; finding is the Group's.
claims.researcher_note: Group of Experts assessment from its own sources; the DRC government is not recorded here as having said this publicly.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that key FDLR commanders and combatants were compelled to relocate to localities in Rutshuru, Masisi and Nyiragongo territories, and that FDLR military commander and sanctioned individual "Major-General" Pacifique Ntawunguka (alias Omega) and other key leaders, fearing RDF attacks, withdrew to the vicinity of the Nyiragongo volcano and inside Virunga National Park.
claims.place_as_written: Nyiragongo volcano area and Virunga National Park (North Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Raw causal clause ('as AFC/M23 and RDF advances disrupted') is only on the page, not in the excerpt; narrowed to the excerpt. Date narrowed to the report period. Spelling as printed in S/2025/446 ('Ntawunguka', alias Omega); S/2026/466 prints 'Ntawuguka' (alias Omega Israel). On the page (para 71) the relocation follows the Group's statement that AFC/M23 and RDF territorial advances disrupted FDLR presence. The report does not date the withdrawal more precisely.
claims.researcher_note: Report dated April 2025; exact dates not given.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that security concerns led Burundi to close border posts with the DRC and designate several frontier areas as 'military zones' on 9 December 2025, and that on 25 February 2026 Burundi reopened a number of crossings.
claims.verification_note: Reopening clause is on the page (annex text right after the excerpt), so supported; excerpt gap flagged for add_excerpt. '25' flag resolved by that passage. The Group adds that the reopening reflected a transition to controlled, securitized border management, not diminished security concerns. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: S/2026/466 supports both clauses, but the stored excerpt carries only the 9 December 2025 closure; the next sentence, on the 25 February 2026 reopening, is added.
claims.researcher_note: 25 February 2026 reopening is in the following sentence of the same paragraph; not within the excerpt.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing an April 2026 report by the Congo Research Group (CRG) and the Center on International Cooperation (CIC), that the capture of Uvira on 10 December 2025 by the M23 and the Rwandan Defence Forces put the Burundian contingent deployed alongside the Congolese army out of action; the article also states that between 12 000 and 15 000 FDNB soldiers were deployed on the eastern Congolese front against the M23/Rwanda alliance.
claims.verification_note: 'Capture of Uvira' wording is in the page lead (replacement quote); the troop figure sentence is not explicitly attributed to CRG/CIC, so stated as the article's. The CRG/CIC report itself was not opened. Troop figures diverge: 12,000-15,000 here; GoE 7,000-9,000 (April 2025, claim 20); SOS Médias 'more than 10,000' (Dec 2025).
claims.researcher_note: The CRG/CIC report itself was not opened (a lead: cic.nyu.edu, April 2026). UN GoE (S/2025/446) gave 7,000 to 9,000 Burundian troops for early April 2025, a different date.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the DRC Ministry of Defence announced on 29 January 2025 that, by presidential order of Tuesday 28 January, general-major Evariste Somo Kakule was appointed military governor of North Kivu province under the state of siege.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC / Ministry of Defence of the DRC

Radio Okapi relays the Ministry of Defence's X account. Radio Okapi says he succeeds général-major Peter Cirimwami Nkuba, who died of wounds after being shot at the front (the page prints this name in full; the research note's 'truncated' remark is wrong). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 29 Jan 2025, carries every clause; the stored excerpt gives the 29 January announcement but not the 28 January presidential order, which is in the next sentence (quoting the ministry's X account). Excerpt added; statement unchanged. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Page also says he previously commanded the 31st rapid reaction brigade at Kindu; the page text names his predecessor only in a truncated line. Appointment came days after the fall of Goma.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the new military governor of North Kivu had been commander of the 31st rapid reaction brigade of the FARDC based at Kindu in Maniema province.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt states it verbatim. Page adds he was until then also commander of the southern axis of the Grand Nord operational sector, south of Lubero. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one

claims.text: Cocorico.cd reported that brigade general Muhondosi Muyusa Constantin was named commander of the 34th military region in North Kivu, whose headquarters had been relocated from Goma to Walikale because of the occupation of Goma by AFC/M23 forces.

Page also says he took up post after joining the HQ at Walikale and previously handled operations and intelligence in the 21st and 31st military regions. The actu30.cd 18 March date was not fetched and is not used. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported on 22 October 2025 that newly appointed FARDC commanders had arrived in Uvira, among them brigade general Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques as new commander of the 33rd military region and general AMULI CIVIRI as commander of operational sector Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports arrival date, names and posts verbatim. SOS Médias Burundi (same day) independently prints 'Général de Brigade Amuli Civiri' and 'Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques' and says the two took office that Wednesday arriving from Kinshasa. 22 Oct 2025 was a Wednesday. The '7' flag is the outlet name 7sur7.cd. 33rd military region commander sequence in the sources is not reconciled: La Presse Africaine names brigade general Dunia Kashindi Fabien as commander on 26 June 2025; 7sur7.cd and SOS Médias Burundi say Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques (Oct 2025) replaced the late general Mwaku Mbuluku Jean-Daniel; Congorassure.cd (Jan 2026) says Dunia Kashindi Fabien was designated provisional commander. No source found says when Mwaku took over or what became of Ilunga Kabamba. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Kivu Times (kivutimes.com) dates the arrival to 'mercredi 23 octobre 2025' in its text; 22 October 2025 was a Wednesday, so the Kivu Times date looks like an error.

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported that the army spokesperson of operational sector Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu, sub-lieutenant Mbuyi Kalonji Reagan, said the new 33rd military region commander replaces the late brigade general Mwaku Mbuluku Jean-Daniel, who died after feeling unwell while on duty, and that general Civiri replaces general Mwehu Lumbu Evariste.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports every clause (spokesperson's statement). SOS Médias Burundi gives a different cause of death for Mwaku Mbuluku ('décédé récemment des suites d'une maladie') and the border post as Kavimvira-Gatumba (7sur7.cd: 'Kamvivira-Bujumbura'); both kept as each source prints. Cause of death differs: 7sur7.cd quotes the spokesperson as 'décédé de suites d'un malaise pendant son service'; SOS Médias Burundi writes 'décédé récemment des suites d’une maladie'. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Predecessor chain for the 33rd military region and Sukola 2 Sud.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that general Olivier Gasita, in charge of intelligence and operations in the 33rd military region, was not affected by the October 2025 reshuffle and remained in post despite demonstrations in Uvira in September; the same report said that, according to several local sources, he had left Uvira on 8 October 2025 and was staying in Kinshasa.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt supports the statement verbatim, but the same page qualifies 'remains in post' (see note). Single exile-based Burundian outlet. Same SOS Médias Burundi page: 'Selon plusieurs sources locales, le Général Gasita a quitté Uvira le 8 octobre 2025 et séjourne actuellement à Kinshasa.' It also says the September demonstrators denounced 'mauvaise gestion des opérations militaires' and cited his Banyamulenge origin, accusations some observers call a pretext. Actualite.cd (20 Sep 2025, cited in this unit for the Mwenga memorandum) separately says Wazalendo and some civil society actors in Uvira refused the posting of general Olivier Gasita as 'commandant second en charge des opérations et renseignements de la 33e région militaire'. A Facebook snippet naming Amuli Civiri as Gasita's replacement was not verified. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: left Uvira on 8 October 2025, staying in Kinshasa 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-019: 'Remained in post' leaves out a qualification printed on the same page: according to several local sources, Gasita left Uvira on 8 October 2025 and was in Kinshasa. A search found DW ('Retour au calme après "le départ" du général Gasita d'Uvira') and Kivu Morning Post ('Le Général Gasita quitte Uvira…'), which both report his departure from Uvira. 'In post' must not be read as 'present in Uvira'.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): left Uvira on 8 October 2025, staying in Kinshasa 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Kivu Times (23 Oct 2025) separately says Gasita remained 'Commandant Région Adjoint' in charge of operations and intelligence, with no official communication on a replacement. The page goes on to say organisers' accusations referred to his Banyamulenge origin; not recorded here because the excerpt is cut in the source text I retained. A Facebook snippet earlier names Amuli Civiri as replacing Gasita in an operations post: unresolved, treat as conflict.

claims.text: Congorassure.cd reported on 26 January 2026 that brigade general Dunia Kashindi Fabien had been designated provisional commander of the 33rd military region, covering South Kivu and Maniema, according to an official note from the FARDC chief of general staff that the outlet said it had seen.

The same note, per the outlet, names colonel Babadi Bakenge Jean-Philippe deputy commander for operations and intelligence, and colonel Kavungiro Balimenyere Marc for administration and logistics. See the 33rd military region sequence note on the 22 October 2025 arrival claim: Dunia Kashindi Fabien is also named commander in June 2025 (La Presse Africaine), before Mwaku Mbuluku and Ilunga Kabamba. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one

Dunia Kashindi Fabien is already named 33rd military region commander in earlier coverage (12 April 2025 meeting at Runingu per Facebook snippets; 26 June 2025 per La Presse Africaine) and Ilunga Kabamba was named in October 2025: commander sequence in the 33rd region needs reconciliation. Page text also says the colonel Kavungiro Balimenyere Marc is assigned administration and logistics.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that on April 4 an armed group commander wrote to President Félix Tshisekedi complaining that Justin Bitakwira Bihona Hayi, a National Assembly member who coordinates support for the Wazalendo coalition in South Kivu, was not fully distributing government funding to all Wazalendo armed groups.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that military and other sources estimate about 20,000 Wazalendo fighters, although the exact figure is unknown, and that in September 2023 some members of the coalition formed the Patriotic Defense Volunteers (VDP), an 'official' auxiliary force.

claims.researcher_note: Estimate, with HRW's own caveat. Date is the report date; the VDP formation (Sept 2023) is background.

claims.researcher_note: Context for FARDC-Wazalendo relations; see also the Umunota 8 May 2025 claim.

The same paragraph states that Rwandan-Congolese national Fred Ngenzi Kagorora and Brigadier General Patrick Karuretwa were in frequent contact with Makenga and Bisimwa and 'Colonel' Imani Nzenze, and that Nangaa was gradually sidelined by Rwanda.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Rwandan-Congolese national Fred Ngenzi Kagorora and Brigadier General Patrick Karuretwa remained in frequent contact with Makenga, Bisimwa and 'Colonel' Imani Nzenze, and that the military and political leadership of AFC/M23 continued to receive instructions and support from the Government of Rwanda and its intelligence services.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 28 February AFC/M23 announced new administrative appointments in South Kivu, naming Emmanuel Birato Rwihimba as governor with Dunia Musumbuko Bwenge and Gishinge Gasinzira Juvénal as deputy governors.

Crisis Group (snippet, not fetched) says M23 quickly replaced Birato; CRG/CIC annex lists Patrick Busu Bwa Ngwi / Manu Birato moved to Goma (garbled table), so later governor changes need a separate claim once fetched.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 maintained two principal intelligence entities: the Directorate of Security and Intelligence, headed by Basile Gasigwa (a.k.a. 'Gas'), and a military intelligence unit led by 'Colonel' Imani Nzenze.
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt from S/2025/446 para. 96; the Group's finding. The report adds that Gasigwa reports to Makenga.
claims.researcher_note: Report date used. The next sentences in the report say these bodies are responsible for surveillance, arrests, identity checks and internal punitive actions and that Gasigwa reports to Makenga.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 sources confirmed 'Colonel' Léon Kanyamibwa was in command of all training centres, with the support of AFC/M23 and Rwandan trainers.
claims.place_as_written: AFC/M23 training centres (locations not given in excerpt)
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (Léon Kanyamibwa) with Rwandan trainers, per the Group of Experts

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 August 2025 'General' Sultani Makenga unveiled the AFC/M23 'elite police force' under the movement's internal security structure, named Police révolutionnaire congolaise (M23/PRC), placed under the command of 'Colonel' Guillaume Eboko, a former FARDC officer.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 14 September AFC/M23 publicized the 'pass-out' of 7,437 'commandos' who had finished their training in Rumangabo; that the graduation ceremony was presided over by 'General' Sultani Makenga and AFC Political Coordinator Corneille Nangaa, who said the cohort would form four brigades of 'commando' units; and that the Group could not independently confirm the number of 7,437 announced by AFC/M23.

claims.text: BBC News reported that former president Joseph Kabila was named leader of a new rebel coalition, announced at a press conference at his residence in Goma by the coalition's adviser Claude Ibalanky, with M23 leader Sultani Makenga as one of Kabila's four deputies and the other three also from the AFC-M23 alliance; BBC said the Congolese government had not commented.

BBC names the coalition the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN); its unveiling was 'on Monday' (12 October 2026). Kabila had previously denied links to M23.

This is a leadership change relevant to the AFC/M23 command structure; the UN GoE (S/2026/466, para. 58) separately reported a forthcoming reshuffle. Radio Okapi (snippet, not fetched) reports the C64 coalition rejecting Kabila-linked FRN positions; see party-statement gap.

claims.researcher_note: Attribution to named sources is in the report paragraph before the excerpt; the excerpt starts at the finding.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that RDF soldiers were briefed by 'Colonel' Espoir Rukinisha about their tasks, and that according to RDF sources interviewed by the Group, Rukinisha was the commander of the third bataillion in Bigogwe, Rwanda, before joining M23 in 2023.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact (annex to S/2025/446). The draft's 2025-01/2025-02 date was inferred, not printed; removed. 'who arrived in Goma' is page-only, so dropped from the statement and kept as context. 'bataillion' spelled as printed. The report (annex) does not date the briefing; it places Rukinisha's role 'during the takeover of Goma'. The date field is left undated rather than inferred.
claims.researcher_note: Date not stated in the excerpt; the page places the briefing around the takeover of Goma (late January 2025). Reviewer to confirm.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 25, 26 and 27 January 2025 RDF troop reinforcements, including RDF Special Forces, arrived from Kitchanga, Kibumba and Kanyamahoro in the DRC, as well as from Gisenyi, Rwanda.
claims.place_as_written: Goma area (Kitchanga, Kibumba, Kanyamahoro), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Annex text of S/2025/446, verbatim; dates and places match.
claims.researcher_note: Part of the report's account of the capture of Goma.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that it documented the presence of soldiers of the following RDF brigades and battalions in North Kivu in February and March 2025: 107 Brigade (55th, 79th, 87th, 85th, 57th, 15th, 03rd, 06th and 04th Battalions), 135 Brigade (27th and 29th Battalions) and 109 Brigade (69th, 85th, '72rd' [as printed] and 75th Battalions).
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact (annex, S/2025/446). Corrected '72nd' back to the printed '72rd' and moved the sourcing into a note with its footnote quote. The report prints '72rd Battalion' (likely 72nd) and lists an 85th Battalion under both 107 and 109 Brigades; both as printed. Footnote 246 gives the source as 'RDF and intelligence sources.'
claims.researcher_note: The report prints '72rd Battalion'; this record reads it as 72nd in the statement only. Source line: 'RDF and intelligence sources'. Brigade list is split into two excerpts of the same page.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that elements of the RDF 3rd Division, under Major General Eugene Nkubito, operated predominantly in North Kivu, and the 4th Division was mainly deployed in South Kivu under Brigadier General Vincent Gatama until his redeployment to Mozambique in late 2025, both supported by special forces under Brigadier-General Stanislas Gashugi.
claims.verification_note: Para. 99 of S/2026/466; both excerpts exact. Spelling 'Eugene' as printed here (S/2025/446 prints 'Eugène').
claims.researcher_note: Report cites intelligence, AFC/M23 sources, captured RDF soldiers; footnote says Gatama was referenced in late 2025 as RSF JTF commander in Mozambique.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 1 December 2025 President Kagame appointed retired General James Kaberebe as his Senior Defence and Security Advisor, and on 29 January 2026 appointed Brigadier-General Jean-Paul Nyirabutama as his deputy.
claims.place_as_written: Rwanda (decisions concerning operations in eastern DRC)
claims.verification_note: Para. 98 of S/2026/466, verbatim. The report spells the name both 'Kaberebe' and 'Kabarebe' in the same paragraph.
claims.researcher_note: Spelling 'Kaberebe' / 'Kabarebe' as printed in the report. Appointment dates are Rwandan-side decisions; the report links both to AFC/M23 liaison.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that new RDF troop and materiel reinforcements were documented in April passing through Nyangezi-Kamanyola towards the Ruzizi Plain, Lemera in the Moyens Plateaux and the Hauts Plateaux of Uvira and Mwenga, and that RDF positioned anti-aerial defence systems (MANPADS) and conducted attacks with kamikaze and armed drones, notably between 10 and 19 April.
claims.place_as_written: Ruzizi Plain, Lemera, Hauts Plateaux of Uvira and Mwenga
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact (annex, S/2026/466). Removed the inferred '(2026)' from the statement and date. The passage does not print the year of 'April'; the context (final report of 5 June 2026, after the January 2026 withdrawal from Uvira) points to April 2026, but this is an inference.
claims.researcher_note: Year inferred from the section (post-January 2026 withdrawal from Uvira; report dated 5 June 2026). Reviewer to confirm.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the US designated Vincent Nyakarundi (Chief of Staff of the RDF), Major-General Ruki Karusisi (commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division and former Special Operations Force Commander), General Mubarakh Muganga (Chief of Defence Staff) and Stanislas Gashugi (Special Operations Force Commander since 15 March 2025) for their leadership roles within the RDF.
claims.verification_note: Annex of S/2026/466 verbatim; US and March 2026 printed elsewhere on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates the Treasury designation already cited in POL-2026; adds the UN report's wording of the four officers' posts.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that former detainees identified Rwandan soldiers during roundups and among instructors and commanders in the Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps (North Kivu), based on uniforms, equipment, accents and inability to speak French or Kiswahili, and that military, intelligence and UN sources confirmed Rwandan forces' involvement.
claims.place_as_written: Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Rwandan forces and M23 (as alleged by HRW)
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact; camp names and period printed in the same release (page-only). excerpt_en faithful (omits the dash clause 'langues peu parlées au Rwanda', no additions). HRW's period (mid-2024 to December 2025) starts before the 1 January 2025 window. HRW interviewed 102 former detainees.
claims.researcher_note: HRW interviewed 102 former detainees; the report period is mid-2024 to December 2025 (partly pre-window). Location Tshanzu per HRW text is in North Kivu.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Mouvement des Patriotes pour la Défense de la Patrie (MPDP), a Wazalendo armed group, announced its creation on Saturday 11 October 2025 in the city of Uvira, South Kivu.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints creation announcement, date and place; flag is a translation artefact (expanded acronym). Rugenge location printed on page.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet (Goma-based). Article dated 2025-10-12; the creation date 11 Oct is the page's own.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the MPDP is led by Pascal Biriho, alias Makanika, as commander of the forces, and by A. Byadunia Meschak Alexis as president of the political branch, and that both are former close collaborators of the warlord and former PNC officer Nyerere Bunana.
claims.actor_as_written: MPDP (Wazalendo): Pascal Biriho (commander of forces); A. Byadunia Meschak Alexis (political branch)
claims.verification_note: Names and roles printed verbatim in excerpt. Being named is not a finding of responsibility.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet. 'Nyerere Bunana' is described by the source as 'seigneur de guerre et ex-officier de la PNC'; being named is not a finding of responsibility.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that at the MPDP launch the RAD provincial coordinator for South Kivu, Alexis Dunia Mwamba, congratulated the MPDP commander while insisting on discipline and respect for the laws of the Republic, and symbolically handed a weapon to commander Pascal Biriho as a sign of support.
claims.actor_as_written: RAD South Kivu (Alexis Dunia Mwamba); MPDP (Pascal Biriho)
claims.verification_note: Both clauses printed on the same page (two excerpts).
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet. The excerpt says the RAD coordinator handed a weapon 'à titre symbolique'. RAD is not expanded on the page (the Group of Experts calls it the Réserve armée de la défense).

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported, citing the recent national defence telegram, that general Nyembo Abdallah was sent to Kisangani to lead the 31st military region based in Tshopo province.
claims.place_as_written: Kisangani, Tshopo (outside the Kivus; rotation of the former Sokola 1 commander)
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC 31st military region: Gen. Nyembo Abdallah
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints the posting; '7' flag is the outlet name. The page prints 'Tsopo' for Tshopo.
claims.researcher_note: Outside the Kivus; recorded as a rotation. The page writes 'Tsopo' (sic) for Tshopo.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the appointment of general Mugisa Muleka Joseph as the new head of Sokola 1 operations was communicated in a general staff telegram made public on Tuesday 15 July, and that he was previously commander of the 31st Principal Defence Brigade at Mambasa since 17 July 2020.
claims.place_as_written: Beni, North Kivu (Sokola 1); previous post Mambasa, Ituri
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC Sokola 1 Grand Nord: Gen. Mugisa Muleka Joseph
claims.verification_note: Both clauses printed on the same page. The page gives 'mardi 15 juillet' without a year; year from the article date.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed: the page gives 'mardi 15 juillet' without a year; article dated 17 Jul 2025 (year taken from the publication date). The statement 'previously commander ... since 17 July 2020' is the source's wording (start date of the former post).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that brigadier generals Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques and Amuli Civiri, named respectively commander of the 33rd military region and commander of the Sokola 2 operational sector in South Kivu, arrived in Uvira on Wednesday 22 October 2025 via the Kavimvira border post with Burundi.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC 33rd military region (Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques); Sokola 2 (Amuli Civiri)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt prints names, posts, date and entry point.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates existing claim UC-FARDC-005 (7sur7.cd) from an independent outlet; 7sur7.cd prints 'Amuli Civiri'/'AMULI CIVIRI' and Radio Okapi 'Amuli Civiri' while a search snippet printed 'Chiviri Hamuli'/'Chiviri Amuli' (not opened).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the appointments of brigadier generals Ilunga Kabamba and Amuli Civiri as commander of the 33rd military region and commander of the Sokola 2 operational sector followed the death in August of brigade general Mwaku Mbuluku Jean-Daniel, former commander of the 33rd military region, and the replacement of general Mwehu Lumbu Evariste as commander of the operational sector.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira, South Kivu (33rd military region; Sokola 2)
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC 33rd military region (Mwaku Mbuluku Jean-Daniel); Sokola 2 (Mwehu Lumbu Evariste)
claims.verification_note: 'October 2025' was not printed in either excerpt; named the appointments instead. The page prints the first name as 'Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques'.
claims.researcher_note: Month only for the death (the source says 'en août dernier'). Compare existing UC-FARDC-006 (7sur7.cd). The Group of Experts reports that Mwehu Lumbu Evariste commanded Sokola 2 on 22 Aug 2025 (held by the GOE unit).

claims.text: La Prunelle RDC reported that a voice message attributed to James « Fyeka Adui » was circulated on social networks, in which the author accused the commander of the 33rd military region of withholding funds meant for local Wazalendo armed groups; that he was summoned by the military intelligence services of the 33rd military region a few days after the message circulated; and that the Unité spéciale des Wazalendo pour les opérations au Sud-Kivu later announced his suspension as spokesperson.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (James « Fyeka Adui », Unité spéciale des Wazalendo pour les opérations au Sud-Kivu); FARDC 33rd military region command (accused)
claims.verification_note: The draft's 'in May 2026' and 'in a letter' were not in the excerpts; supplied from page passages, kept 'attributed'. The summons document is cited by the page via Averticom. An accusation in an audio of attributed authorship; the commander is not named and the accusation is unverified. The page dates the summons document 20 May 2026 (via Averticom) and the suspension correspondence 25 May 2026.
claims.researcher_note: An accusation voiced in an audio (authorship 'attributed'), reported second-hand; the commander is not named on the page and the accusation is unverified. The page, citing the outlet Averticom, also reports a 20 May 2026 summons by 33rd-region military intelligence and says the suspension letter is dated 25 May 2026. Not a finding about any commander.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that in two decisions made public on 6 April 2025 the AFC announced appointments of territory administrators, bourgmestres, cité heads and their deputies in North and South Kivu; in North Kivu it named Kulu Musubao Jean-Louis administrator of Lubero territory with Radjabu Kwizera Elie as deputy, Munyandekwe Innocent as bourgmestre of Kirumba assisted by Kavugho Jeanine, and Kahinda Jean-Baptiste as bourgmestre of Kayna with Mumbere Siméon as deputy.
claims.verification_note: All names, posts and date printed by the excerpts. 'city heads' narrowed to 'cité heads' (chefs de cité). Page (byline La Rédaction) also names Kanyabayonga's Matimano Jean, not in this claim. excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful.
claims.researcher_note: Local outlet (Goma) reporting AFC decisions; the page says 'l'AFC' not explicitly 'M23'. Sibling claim covers the South Kivu part of the same decisions. The Lubero and Kayna/Kirumba posts were later reshuffled (see April 2026 claim).

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that in the same two decisions Buseyi Jean-Bosco was named administrator of Kalehe territory with Ndaye Faustine as deputy, Elie Rubabura Espoir named for Kabare assisted by Cikuru Barakaziga, and three new bourgmestres were named for the Bukavu communes of Ibanda, Kadutu and Bagira; Balyahamwabo Paulin became head of the Minova cité.
claims.place_as_written: Kalehe, Kabare, Bukavu (Ibanda, Kadutu, Bagira) and Minova (South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Supported as printed. excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful. The page does not name the three Bukavu bourgmestres. It also names Idjwi (Ntambuka Pascal, Muhanuka Mwezi Amzat) and Walungu appointees, not in this claim.
claims.researcher_note: The page does not name the three Bukavu bourgmestres; a search snippet from another outlet (not fetched) names Kadutu and Bagira holders and spells one differently. Names in this claim are spelled as KMP prints them.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that in a decision made public on 11 June 2025 the Conseil de l'Alliance Fleuve Congo reorganised the South Kivu administration, naming Patrick Busu Bwa Ngwi Nshombo governor and Mukiza Nzabinesha Gadi vice-governor in charge of the economy, finance and development, and that Busu succeeded Emmanuel Birato Rwihimba, recalled to new functions within the AFC/M23 coordination.
claims.verification_note: Supported as printed (byline La Rédaction). excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful.
claims.researcher_note: Fills a gap flagged in UC-M23 and SKN-2025Q1 (Busu seen only in snippets). Birato was appointed governor on 28 Feb 2025 per the UN Group of Experts (existing claim). Date is the decision's publication date; swearing-in date not captured from a fetched page.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the AFC decision named Mukiza Nzabinesha Gadi as South Kivu Vice-Governor to fill the vacancy left by the death of Juvénal Gishinge Gasinzira, and that the decisions were signed by Bertrand Bisimwa, president of the M23 and deputy coordinator of the AFC, and approved by Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, coordinator of the Alliance.
claims.verification_note: Supported as printed. excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful. The page gives no date or cause of Gishinge Gasinzira's death.
claims.researcher_note: Gishinge Gasinzira was named deputy governor on 28 Feb 2025 per the UN Group of Experts (existing claim); the page gives no date or cause of his death. Chain of signature: Bisimwa signs, Nangaa approves, as KMP prints it.

claims.text: A text published by Soleil du Graben (which styles itself 'the news portal of eastern DRC') and signed 'Celcom' said that at the first security council meeting of the year, chaired on 6 January 2026 by Governor Patrick BUSU BWA NGWI Nshombo, the vice-governor in charge of financial and development matters, MUKIZA GADI NZABINESHA, who it said had long been blocked in Minembwe, was officially presented to the participants.
claims.verification_note: Page signed 'Celcom.', so partisan_afc_m23 and attributed as the AFC/M23 side's text; name spelled as the body prints it ('Gady' was the headline form). excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful. Party account: the piece ends 'Celcom.' (communication cell) and speaks of the 'mouvement révolutionnaire AFC-M23'. Name variants as printed: 'MUKIZA GADI NZABINESHA' (body), 'Gady Mukiza' (headline), 'Mukiza Nzabinesha Gadi' (Kivu Morning Post, June 2025). The headline says he arrived after 6 months' absence. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Soleil du Graben, 7 Jan 2026, text signed 'Celcom' (AFC/M23 provincial communication cell per the claim's origin field). The page calls the site 'Le portail de l'information de l'Est de la RDC'; nothing on the page says it is Bukavu-based, so that qualifier is dropped. The meeting, date, governor and vice-governor clauses match.
claims.researcher_note: Single local portal; the headline says the vice-governor arrived 'après 6 mois d'absence'. The site calls AFC-M23 'le mouvement révolutionnaire' and its copy may be relayed from the AFC provincial administration; treat as that side's account. Spelling of the name varies across outlets (Mukiza Nzabinesha Gadi in KMP).

claims.text: A text published by Soleil du Graben and signed by a communication cell said that Nicolas Kyalangalilwa took over as head of the Bukavu city hall from Ladys Muganza Wakandwa, in a decision it attributes to the 'mouvement révolutionnaire AFC-M23', at a handover ceremony on Friday 13 March 2026 under Vice-Governor Dunia Masumbuko Bwenge Doux; it said the outgoing mayor had taken the reins of Bukavu in February 2025.
claims.verification_note: Signed 'Cellule de Communication.' at the end, so attributed as the AFC/M23 side's text rather than the portal's reporting. excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful. Party account (signed 'Cellule de Communication'). The same text names the deputy mayor 'Céline Nyota Luhanja'; Radio Maendeleo (June 2026) prints 'Nyota Luandja Celine'. It says Muganza Wakandwa became the governor's deputy director of cabinet.
claims.researcher_note: The article ends with 'Cellule de Communication', i.e. it reproduces a communications cell's text, probably the provincial or city administration's, so graded as the AFC/M23 side's own account. Kyalangalilwa was 'confirmed' as mayor in the June 2026 reshuffle (see next claim). The page does not say who named the first mayor or the exact date in February 2025.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that in Bukavu Nicolas Kyalangalilwa was confirmed as mayor of Bukavu with Nyota Luandja Celine named deputy mayor, Shaka Muhoza, who had been acting, was confirmed bourgmestre of Bagira with Léon Bahaya as deputy, and that Mweze Prisca and Ruremesha Tého were named bourgmestres of Ibanda and Kadutu.
claims.place_as_written: Bukavu (Bagira, Ibanda, Kadutu communes), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Supported as printed (byline Etienne Mulindwa); RM says it consulted the decision. excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful. Name variant: Radio Maendeleo prints the deputy mayor as 'Nyota Luandja Celine'; a Soleil du Graben communication-cell text (March 2026) prints 'Céline Nyota Luhanja'. Radio Maendeleo says the decision came from the Conseil de l'Alliance and was made 'depuis le week-end'.
claims.researcher_note: Independent second outlet (Bukavu community radio) for the June 2026 decision that Kivu Morning Post also reported (POL-2026 claim on decision N°033/COORDO-PR/AFC-M23/2026). The Radio Maendeleo article is dated 2026-06-08 and says the appointments were made 'depuis le week-end'; date given as month with report date. Territory-level appointments (Idjwi, Kabare, Kalehe, Walungu, Minova) are in the same article but not repeated here.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that Pascal Ntambuka was named administrator of Idjwi territory, Elie Rubabura Espoir was reappointed administrator of Kabare with former national deputy Kasindi Kingombe Benjamin as assistant, Buseyi Jean Bosco was named administrator of Kalehe, and Sengimana Ruhungande Augustin was named head of the Minova cité.
claims.place_as_written: Idjwi, Kabare, Kalehe territories and Minova (South Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Supported as printed. Kivu Morning Post (April 2025) printed the Idjwi appointee as 'Ntambuka Pascal' with 'Muhanuka Mwezi Amzat'; Radio Maendeleo prints 'Muhamuza Mweze Amza'. Whether these are the same person is not established.
claims.researcher_note: Kabare's Elie Rubabura Espoir and Kalehe's Buseyi Jean-Bosco were already named in April 2025 (see April 2025 claim), i.e. they were reconfirmed about 14 months later.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that in the same April 2026 reshuffle Juvénal Nshimimana became deputy mayor of Goma and Katembo Isevisya became deputy bourgmestre of Goma commune, Radjabu Kwizera Elie head of Karisimbi commune, Innocent Munyandekwe Fizi assistant administrator of Lubero territory and Jeannine Kavugho bourgmestre of Kirumba commune.
claims.place_as_written: Goma (Goma and Karisimbi communes), Lubero (North Kivu)
claims.verification_note: Supported as printed; same page as claim 8. Spellings differ from April 2025 KMP ('Munyandekwe Innocent', 'Kavugho Jeanine'); kept as printed.
claims.researcher_note: Several of these people appear in April 2025 appointments under different posts (Radjabu Kwizera Elie as assistant administrator of Lubero; Munyandekwe Innocent as Kirumba bourgmestre; Kavugho Jeanine as his deputy): rotation of the same cadres. The provincial order is cited by KMP as n°011/014/CAB/GP-NK/2026 (number as printed).

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported on 24 November 2025 that the spokesperson of the North Kivu governor confirmed that Goma mayor Katembo Julien Dalieni, appointed by the AFC/M23, had been suspended for 15 days, the decision citing a 'manquement grave aux valeurs de la révolution' without further detail.
claims.verification_note: Supported; spokesperson not named on the page. excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful. Name as printed here: 'Katembo Julien Dalieni'; KMP's April 2026 article prints 'Julienne Katembo Ndalieni'. Lead: the article (byline Blaise Basabose) says the suspension came after a video circulated on social media showing the mayor hitting a bus driver; this is not asserted in the claim.
claims.researcher_note: The article adds that the suspension followed a video on social media said to show the mayor hitting a bus driver; that sentence is not in this excerpt and is not asserted here. Mayor returned to office afterwards (an article of 2026 still treats him as mayor until the April 2026 reshuffle); the reinstatement date was not found.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that North Kivu governor Bahati Musanga Erasto signed on 1 April 2026 a provincial order designating new neighbourhood chiefs and deputies in the city of Goma, aimed at strengthening local governance.
claims.place_as_written: Goma (Goma and Karisimbi communes), North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: North Kivu governor Bahati Musanga Erasto (named as the AFC/M23 governor by Actualité.cd, 1 Feb 2026, in this unit; this page does not mention AFC/M23)
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; actor narrowed because this page never names AFC/M23. excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful. The page lists the quarter chiefs by name for Goma and Karisimbi communes (e.g. Célestin Bahemuke at Bujovu).
claims.researcher_note: The article lists about 19 quarter chiefs by name (e.g. Himbi, Mapendo, Majengo, Ndosho, Mugunga, Bujovu); not itemised here. The UN Group of Experts annex quoted elsewhere shows overlapping names (Bahemuke Célestin for Bujovu).

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that North Kivu vice-governor Amani Bahati Chadrack published a circular (n° 01-009-CAB-GP-NK-2025, dated 18 August 2025) banning unjustified price rises for cement in Goma and its surroundings and officially fixing sale prices.
claims.actor_as_written: Amani Bahati Chadrack, vice-governor of North Kivu (as Kivu Morning Post names him; the page does not say who appointed him)
claims.verification_note: Actor narrowed to what the page prints. excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful. The page does not mention AFC/M23; Kinshasa named its own North Kivu vice-governor (Louis Segond Karawa, March 2025), so the AFC/M23 link rests on other sources. The page says the circular was made public on 20 August and fixed a 50 kg bag at 10 USD wholesale and 10.2 USD retail.
claims.researcher_note: Shows Amani Bahati Chadrack (also printed Chadrack Amani Bahati and Amani Bahati Shaddrak elsewhere) in post as vice-governor in August 2025; the UN Group of Experts (S/2026/466) describes him as Vice-Governor in charge of finance, economy and development. He was named in the original 5 Feb 2025 appointments per other outlets, not verified here.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that by an order signed on Monday 8 September 2025 North Kivu governor Bahati Musanga Erasto named seven members of a Commission Provinciale de Pacification et Résolution des Conflits (CPRC), created by an order of 22 August 2025 and presented as a body for pacification in the 'liberated' zones, and that the governor's director of cabinet, Nsanzamahoro Tengera Vincent, was charged with executing the orders.
claims.actor_as_written: North Kivu governor Bahati Musanga Erasto (named as the AFC/M23 governor by Actualité.cd, 1 Feb 2026, in this unit)
claims.verification_note: Statement supported; actor tied to the printed name rather than inferred. excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful. The page lists the seven members by name (e.g. Badaga Bigirimana Jean, Mboneza Ndizihiwe Patrice).
claims.researcher_note: 'Liberated' is the AFC/M23 term as quoted by KMP. Seven member names are printed on the page but not itemised here.

claims.text: Actu26 reported that Ephrem Kabasha, described as the new administrator of Rutshuru territory recently appointed by the AFC/M23, sought to reassure transport operators and the population about the security situation in the Busendo area and announced he would hold discussions with the high military hierarchy to strengthen security arrangements on that axis.
claims.verification_note: Supported (byline Obadias Kanoba). Figures flag '26' is the outlet's name, not a figure.
claims.researcher_note: Small local outlet (Goma); appointment date not given on the page. The Kabasha appointment is not in the April 2026 Goma order and its date and decision were not found. Related incident in the next claim.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that an order designated Maître Jean-Philippe Chubaka Mashamba head of the Department of Justice and Human Rights, with Maître Shyaka Jean-Paul in charge of judicial reforms and Maître Mugisa Tibasima Emmanuel in charge of human rights as deputy heads of department.
claims.verification_note: Date corrected from the article date (6 Aug) to the announcement date the page prints (5 Aug 2026); AFC-M23 as issuer is in the actor field and the page title. excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful. KMP says the AFC-M23 announced the designations on Wednesday 5 August 2026, in a decision signed by Bertrand Bisimwa and approved by Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo.
claims.researcher_note: Lead for investigators: the de facto human-rights/justice focal points for complaints in AFC/M23 areas. Date of the order itself not given; date is the article date.

claims.text: Actualité.cd reported that the death toll of at least 226 in the collapse at the Rubaya coltan mine in Masisi territory was confirmed to it by Kambere Muyisa Lumumba, whom it described as spokesperson of the North Kivu governor appointed by the AFC/M23 rebellion.
claims.verification_note: Supported; attribution chain preserved. excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful. The toll is the de facto authority spokesperson's figure as relayed by Actualité.cd (byline Clément Muamba); the page adds that local sources say the real toll could be higher. Date is the article date; the page does not give the collapse date.
claims.researcher_note: Included for the spokesperson role (first one found for the de facto North Kivu governor in 2026). Figures: 226 at least, per the spokesperson via Actualité.cd; other sources may differ.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that President Félix Tshisekedi appointed commissioner Louis Segond Karawa vice-governor of North Kivu on Friday 7 March 2025, in the context of the occupation of Goma by the M23, and that he had been South Kivu provincial police commissioner from 2015.
claims.verification_note: Supported; 'occupation ... by the M23' and 'soutenus par l'armée rwandaise' are Radio Okapi's wording. excerpt_en flags are false positives: the flagged words are English renderings (Mrs, Doctor, Council, Governor's, etc.); translations checked against the excerpts and are faithful.
claims.researcher_note: Government-side counterpart of the AFC/M23 administration (military governor Somo Kakule, existing claims). Radio Okapi describes the M23 as 'soutenus par l'armée rwandaise' (its own wording).

claims.text: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Colonel Emmanuel Kabundi as commander of the 1st Brigade (HQ in Nyongera) and Colonel Rigobert Manga as its deputy commander, within the 1st Operational Sector (Nyiragongo to Lubero, headquarters in Rutshuru town).

claims.verification_note: Annex table (sec. B, 1st Operational Sector) prints both names, posts and HQ. Territory 'Rutshuru' for Nyongera is geography, not printed by the source; the statement does not assert it. Single origin: a table in a CRG/NYU CIC research annex ('as of December 2025'); the table does not state its own sources. Names, ranks and call signs as CRG prints them.
claims.researcher_note: Brigade-level commander not in earlier claims (UC-M23 covers sector commanders only). Nyongera is in Rutshuru territory per general geography, not stated in the excerpt. Single-origin table in a research-group annex (not a UN or court document); the report's source of the table is not stated in the excerpt. Names and ranks as printed; spellings may differ from other sources.

claims.verification_note: Table prints all names/posts verbatim. UN 'Fourth Brigade' vs CRG '2nd Brigade' kept stated, not merged. The deputy, Gakufe Jafet, appears in UN reports as 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Japhet Gakufe (Minembwe reinforcement, March 2025; see UCD-M23-COMMAND). Single-origin table in a research-group annex (not a UN or court document); the report's source of the table is not stated in the excerpt. Names and ranks as printed; spellings may differ from other sources.
