claims.text: Actualite.cd, citing an April 2026 report by the Congo Research Group and NYU's Center on International Cooperation, reported that Colonel Innocent Zimurinda is commander of the headquarters (quartier général), sanctioned by the UN since December 2010, by the European Union since the same date and by the United States since January 2013.
claims.place_as_written: M23 headquarters (Rubare, Rutshuru per CRG table), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Page prints the post and sanction dates and credits the CRG/CIC report in its lead; checked against the CRG PDF's sanctions list, which matches. excerpt_en flag is capitalised proper nouns (UN/EU) rendered in English; translation is of the excerpt alone. Actualite.cd relays the CRG/CIC April 2026 report; not independent of the CRG claims. The CRG sanctions list prints 'Innocent Zimurinda, Headquarters commander' with UN 1 Dec 2010, EU 22 Dec 2010, US 3 Jan 2013; the CRG annex table prints the name 'Colonel Innocent Zimulinda' (spelling differs within the same report).
claims.researcher_note: Zimurinda is a candidate for the HQ post in the CRG annex, where the name is printed 'Colonel Innocent Zimulinda' next to 'Headquarters Commander (based in Rubare, Rutshuru)'; the PDF table layout does not make the name-to-post pairing unambiguous, so the Actualite.cd text is cited for the pairing. A FARDC-side account (depeche.cd, 19 May 2026) names 'Zimurinda Innocent' as an AFC-M23 commander based in Rutshuru; that page did not load (see gaps).

claims.text: Actualite.cd, relaying the UN Group of Experts report, reported that 'brigadier general' Justin Gacheri Musanga led the second zone (Masisi and Walikale) and a 'general' it named as Innocent Byamungu the third zone (South Kivu) of the movement's 'defence zones'.
claims.place_as_written: Nyiragongo, Rutshuru, Lubero, Masisi, Walikale and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Page prints the passage as quoted; a relay of the UN report, not independent; graded C because the added first name is unsupported by the origin. Name discrepancy: the UN report it relays (S/2026/466, para. 64) prints only “General” Byamungu; Actualite.cd prints 'Innocent Byamungu'. HRW prints 'Bertrand Byamungu'; Actualite.cd (Sept 2025), FNTV and Enquete.cd print Bernard (Maheshe) Byamungu. The first name 'Innocent' has no support in the origin and is not established. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-010: Namesake risk: the relay adds a first name ('Innocent') that the origin does not print, while other sources print Bernard or Bertrand Byamungu. The statement should say the first name is the outlet's and that the UN text gives only the surname (input claim r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-001 excerpt).; excerpt-support: cut 'the UN report itself prints only “General” Byamungu': the UN report is not among this claim's sources (its excerpt sits in r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-001); kept 'a general it named as Innocent Byamungu' (source 0 prints that name)
claims.researcher_note: Discrepancy: the UN text prints 'Byamungu' only; Actualite.cd prints 'Innocent Byamungu'. Other sources in this unit (UN sanctions summary, Kivu Morning Post, Actualite.cd Sept 2025) refer to the AFC/M23 deputy military commander as Bernard (Maheshe) Byamungu. 'Innocent' is not established; probably a relay error. Surface, do not resolve. The page sentence is introduced by 'le rapport révèle que' (the UN report).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the AFC/M23 'First Defence Zone' command, covering Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms, was led by 'Brigadier General' Baudoin Ngaruye.
claims.place_as_written: Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms, Rutshuru territory
claims.verification_note: Para. 44 of S/2025/858 matches. Rank as printed: S/2025/858 'Brigadier General'; S/2026/466 'General'.
claims.researcher_note: Reporting period of S/2025/858 (dated 2025-12-30). The same paragraph recounts a pre-2025 UN sanction history, which is outside the window and not recorded here. S/2026/466 prints Ngaruye as "General"; S/2025/858 as "Brigadier General" (rank as printed).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that one RDF brigade operated within AFC/M23's 'first defence zone' (Goma, Nyiragongo, Binza, Bwito, Rutshuru, and Kanyabayonga, Kirumba and Kipese in Lubero), and another RDF brigade in the 'second defence zone' (Masisi, Walikale, Bibwe, Kalembe, and South Kivu areas including Walungu, Mwenga and Minembwe).
claims.place_as_written: Goma, Rutshuru, Lubero, Masisi, Walikale, Walungu, Mwenga, Minembwe
claims.actor_as_written: RDF within AFC/M23 defence zones (as named by the Group of Experts)
claims.verification_note: Para. 69 of S/2025/858 matches both excerpts. S/2025/858 (para. 69) places South Kivu areas in the 'second defence zone'; S/2026/466 (para. 64) describes a separate third zone covering South Kivu under 'General' Byamungu. The reports differ; both are stated.
claims.researcher_note: Reporting period of S/2025/858 (2025-12-30). Report counts "at least two brigades and two special forces battalions" in North and South Kivu. Note this places the second zone (with South Kivu locations) differently from S/2026/466, where South Kivu is the third zone; surface this difference between reports.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that 'Colonel' Gafishi Semikobe Simon was officially appointed AFC/M23 'Officer for Mobilisation and Recruitment' on 11 February 2025 and also carried out responsibilities relating to the 'security files'.
claims.verification_note: Annex passage matches. Annex to S/2025/446; the excerpt does not itself name Goma. Name order as printed in the annex.
claims.researcher_note: Annex to S/2025/446. The main text (para. 23) prints the name as Semikobe Gafishi; spelling as printed in each place.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that in early December 2025 more than 100 Mai-Mai fighters surrendered to AFC/M23 in Uvira in the presence of General Byamungu Maheshe, described as deputy commander of the AFC/M23.
claims.verification_note: Passage matches; kept at C as a lead. Single local outlet, unsigned ('La Rédaction'), in an aside to a report on a Masisi surrender; it gives no source for the Uvira surrender. 'Early December 2025' sits awkwardly with other reports placing AFC/M23's entry into Uvira on 10 December 2025; not resolved. Name printed as 'Byamungu Maheshe'.
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet; source for the surrender figures is not stated in the excerpt. The page prints "AF-CM23" (typo for AFC/M23).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the day after attacks on Wazalendo positions on 25 September in the groupements of Kaniola and Kamisimibi, General Bernard Byamungu, described as the movement's number two, held a public meeting at Nzibira in Walungu territory.
claims.verification_note: Passage matches; Walungu territory supported by the preceding sentence. The page does not say who targeted the Wazalendo positions; the surrounding sentence concerns M23's advance from Nzibira. 26 September is computed from 'le lendemain'.
claims.researcher_note: "Le lendemain" (the next day) is relative to 25 September; the date 26 September is computed from that. Sentence on Wazalendo positions is attributed by the page to the M23 offensive context ("le M23 a progressé depuis Nzibira").

claims.text: Enquete.cd reported from Goma on 24 May 2026, according to sources close to the rebellion, that Bernard Maheshe Byamungu, alias 'Tiger One', described as one of the main military chiefs of the AFC/M23-RDF coalition, had died after being wounded in a drone strike.
claims.place_as_written: Goma (dateline); strike location not stated in the excerpt
claims.verification_note: Passage matches; recorded only as a single partisan-sourced report, kept separate from the denial. UNCONFIRMED AND CONTESTED. Enquete.cd (byline Junior Kanyiki) relies on unnamed sources close to the rebellion and one unnamed M23 officer. FNTV, a day earlier (23 May 2026), retracted its own report and said the man killed was a Wazalendo colonel with the same surname and that Gen. Bernard Byamungu was alive. The UN Group's final report (5 June 2026) lists a 'General' Byamungu as a zone commander and mentions no death. No AFC/M23 statement found. 2026-10-28: confidence edited: red-team rt-010: Single report from unnamed sources close to the rebellion; FNTV had retracted a similar report a day earlier (Wazalendo colonel namesake, general alive), the UN Group's report of 5 June 2026 still lists a 'General' Byamungu as zone commander, and a fresh search found no confirmation and no AFC/M23 statement (earlier death rumours about 'General Byamungu' also circulated). The 'AFC/M23-RDF coalition' framing is the outlet's. Keep it only as an unconfirmed, contested report next to the retraction; if D is not in the rubric, keep C with a mandatory 'unconfirmed; contested' flag.
claims.researcher_note: CONTRADICTED the same week: FNTV (23 May) reported that the dead man was a Wazalendo colonel with the same surname and that Gen. Bernard Byamungu was alive (separate claim). The UN Group of Experts final report (5 June 2026) names Byamungu among zone leaders without mentioning a death. Treat the death as unconfirmed.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Beni garrison military tribunal (North Kivu) sentenced three FARDC officers (two lieutenants and a captain) to death for desertion and breach of orders, after they had been recruited, according to the court, by a man presenting himself as coordinator of the Comité national des patriotes (CONAP); two men presenting themselves as Wazalendo commanders got twenty years in prison for, notably, illegally recruiting soldiers and spreading false information, having set up, according to military justice, a clandestine recruitment network in the Malepe quarter of Beni using without mandate the name of the Réserve armée de la défense (RAD); the verdict came on the evening of Friday 10 July.
claims.actor_as_written: Beni garrison military tribunal; three FARDC officers; self-styled CONAP coordinator and a collaborator (convicted)
claims.verification_note: Clarified that the CONAP man recruited the three officers (per the court) and that the RAD network is military justice's finding; figures rewritten. Per the page, the self-styled coordinator was convicted with one collaborator ('Quant au prétendu coordonnateur des Wazalendu, il est condamné avec un de ses collaborateurs à vingt ans de prison'); neither is named. The convicted have five days to appeal. Court findings concern the convicted only.
claims.researcher_note: The two Wazalendo 'commanders' are not named; the page says the group presented itself as the national patriots committee (CONAP). Illustrates the RAD (Réserve armée de la défense) as a name in use; the court said the recruiters used it without a mandate.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing several local sources, that two Wazalendo factions, the ACNDH group led by self-proclaimed general Jean-Marie and another group led by Ignace Sauli, clashed at Shengesha, Masisi territory, fighting with heavy and light weapons throughout the day and driving residents to flee; the outlet also reported clashes the same day involving CMC-FDP Wazalendo in Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, concentrated in Mudugugudu village.
claims.place_as_written: Shengesha, Bashali chiefdom, Masisi; Mudugugudu, Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo ACNDH (self-proclaimed general Jean-Marie); Wazalendo group of Ignace Sauli; CMC-FDP
claims.verification_note: Date taken from the page into the date field; statement limited to the excerpts. The page dates the Shengesha clash to 'samedi 1er novembre 2025' (date field). 'Ignace Sauli' here and 'Ignace Dunia Sauli' in a June 2025 KMP report may be the same person; the source does not say so. Per the page, AFC-M23 regained control of the Mudugugudu area by Saturday evening. Per the page, Shengesha is in the Bashali chiefdom. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-007: The excerpt says clashes 'entre les Wazalendo du CMC-FDP' with no second party; the retained page goes on that the Wazalendo had reinstalled in Mudugugudu after AFC-M23's temporary withdrawal and that AFC-M23 retook the area by Saturday evening, so 'clashes between CMC-FDP Wazalendo' wrongly implies an intra-CMC-FDP fight. Amended to 'involving'. Also: independent_origins 2 is one outlet (KMP, local sources).; excerpt-support: nothing to add
claims.researcher_note: Same 'Ignace Sauli' appears as 'Ignace Dunia Sauli' in the KMP piece on Biramba (30 June 2025); the source here does not state they are the same person. Date: day not printed for the Shengesha clash; 'samedi' refers to the Mudugugudu fighting (Saturday 1 Nov 2025, computed).

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that self-proclaimed general Kakule Kaputu, alias « Tango Fort », was shot dead during fighting between his Wazalendo group and that of his rival Fiston Njoli at Butembo, according to Paluku Jean-Baptiste Muyisa, president of the communal civil society; the fighting began on a Sunday morning on Munzambaye hill, Vulamba commune, and lasted until Monday 5 January, and the body was reportedly displayed publicly at Furu.
claims.place_as_written: Munzambaye hill, Congo Ya Sika quarter, Vulamba commune, Butembo, North Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo group of Kakule Kaputu alias « Tango Fort »; Wazalendo group of Fiston Njoli
claims.verification_note: Every clause is in the excerpts; the Sunday is 4 January 2026 by calendar, which the page does not print. The Wazalendo synergy Front Nord gave a different place (Vuvatsi, towards Kitovo) and called it an armed operation, not a targeted killing (separate claim). The display of the body is reported ('aurait été').
claims.researcher_note: Single local outlet; the date of the Sunday (4 January 2026, computed from the publication date and 'lundi 5 janvier'). Civil society also condemned the displaying of the body.

claims.text: Brigadier general Muhondosi Muyuwa Constantin, commander of the 34th military region, reiterated his appeal for the surrender of the M23 members still active, the outlet reported.
claims.actor_as_written: 34th military region, FARDC (commander Muhondosi Muyuwa Constantin)
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date (shown with the source) and the outlet name, whose digits the checker reads as a figure; single clause, supported verbatim; territory 'Goma' not stated by the page. Name spelled 'Muyuwa' as this page prints it (another source spells 'Muyusa'). The page, dated 20 October 2025, reports 38 AFC/M23 fighters surrendering that day to the 34th military region.
claims.researcher_note: Shows Muhondosi still in post as 34th military region commander in October 2025 (the earlier UC-FARDC claim holds his March 2025 appointment). The page's own spelling is 'Muyuwa'; the March 2025 Cocorico.cd claim spells 'Muyusa'. Page headline: near 40 M23 fighters surrender to the FARDC (headline not cited).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported in its final report that the strength of MRDP/Twirwaneho was estimated at 2,500 to 3,000 combatants, led by Charles Sematama.
claims.verification_note: Para. 84 of S/2026/466 prints the estimate and leader.
claims.researcher_note: Sematama already appears in earlier claims; this adds the strength estimate in the final report (S/2026/466, para. 84).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that ADF commander Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender, reportedly died from injuries sustained during clashes with Shujaa forces on 14 March 2026 along the Lindi River (in Asangwa, Bapere sector), which divides Lubero territory from Tshopo Province; the Group said it could not independently confirm his death.
claims.place_as_written: Lindi River, Asangwa, Bapere sector (Lubero/Tshopo border), North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Para. 30 of S/2026/466; 'reportedly' and the Group's non-confirmation preserved. Death reported, not confirmed: the Group says it could not independently confirm it.
claims.researcher_note: Death unconfirmed by the Group; footnote marker '31' printed inside the extracted excerpt.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the FDLR-FOCA military commander was "Major-General" Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) and its political leader "General" Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro); that the overall FDLR-RUD leader was "Brigadier-General" Emmanuel Nsengiyumva (alias Faida/Fayida Hakimu); and that the FDLR-FPP leader was "Colonel" Dan Hategekimana (alias Dan Simplice).
claims.verification_note: Para. 127 of S/2026/466; spellings and aliases as printed ('Ntawuguka').
claims.researcher_note: Spelling 'Ntawuguka' as printed here; earlier claims print 'Ntawunguka' from S/2025/... Nsengiyumva and Hategekimana appear new to the roster.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported a divide among Wazalendo between "old" warlords actively engaged on the frontlines, including sanctioned individual William Yakutumba (CDi.043), Makanaki Kasimbira John, Delphin Ngomanzito, René Itongwa and Ilunga, and "new" Wazalendo leaders perceived as opportunistic entrants.
claims.verification_note: Para. 111 of S/2026/466; names as printed.
claims.researcher_note: Names as printed by the Group; the page does not give their units or places in this sentence.

claims.text: Actualite.cd, reporting on a UN Group of Experts report, said the experts wrote that Guidon Shimiray Mwissa, head of the NDC-R and VDP commander, moved his headquarters from Pinga to Kibati in Walikale territory, that APCLS leader Janvier Karairi Boingo and troops were based at Lukweti in Masisi territory, and that the CMC-FDP led by Dominique Ndaruhutse was in Virunga National Park taking part in fighting in areas of Rutshuru territory.
claims.place_as_written: Walikale, Masisi and Rutshuru territories, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Exact on the retained Actualite.cd page, which credits the passages to the UN experts. Checked against the retained S/2025/858 PDF: the Kibati/Lukweti passage is printed there, so the relay is faithful but not independent of the Group's report already cited by other units. excerpt_en flags reviewed: the English is a faithful translation of each excerpt alone (flag triggered by capitalisation/punctuation differences). Relay of S/2025/858 (para. 83 area); the same wording appears in the Group's report text retained for this project. Dates approximate (the article places VDP/Wazalendo activity 'Depuis juin 2025').
claims.researcher_note: Local outlet relaying the UN Group of Experts midterm report; the Group's own report text was not checked for these two sentences. Statement avoids dates beyond 'since June 2025' phrasing of the article, so the date range is approximate.

claims.text: ACP (Agence Congolaise de Presse) reported that EU foreign ministers adopted sanctions including three Rwandan generals, Eugène Nkubito, Pascal Muhizi and Ruki Karusisi, describing Karusisi as commander of the special forces deployed in the DRC, and listing Nkubito as commander of the RDF 3rd Division and Muhizi as commander of the RDF 2nd Division. TRT Afrika reported that those sanctioned by the EU included special forces commander Ruki Karusisi and two army division commanders, Eugene Nkubito and Pascal Muhizi.
claims.place_as_written: eastern DRC (RDF deployment); sanctions announced in Brussels
claims.verification_note: ACP narrates, it does not cite an 'EU source' for the generals; discrepancy within ACP surfaced; TRT clause separated. EU listing as reported by ACP (Congolese state agency) and TRT Afrika; the EU Official Journal text was not fetched. ACP is internally inconsistent on Karusisi's role and spelling (current vs former special forces commander; 'Ruki'/'Ruzi'). Only ACP gives the division numbers.
claims.researcher_note: The 2nd Division commander (Pascal Muhizi, Brigadier General) is not in earlier UC-RDF claims, which name the 3rd and 4th/5th Divisions; the EU Official Journal text (Implementing Regulation 2025/509) and Council press release could not be fetched (bot protection, not bypassed) and would be the primary sources. ACP is the Congolese state news agency (partisan on Rwanda). The TRT page carries no wire credit but shows a Reuters photo credit; its date is taken from the search result (17 Mar 2025). Rwanda's foreign ministry statement that day was aimed at Belgium; no Rwandan reaction to the commander listings was found in these sources.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition, dateline Goma, 3 March 2026) reported that the United States announced sanctions on Monday against the RDF and four of its senior officers, whom Washington accuses of actively supporting the M23 rebellion, and that OFAC designated General Mubarakh Muganga, Major General Vincent Nyakarundi, Major General Ruki Karusisi (commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division and former special forces commander) and Brigadier General Stanislas Gashugi (current commander of Rwandan special forces); Kigali immediately denounced the sanctions as 'unjust' and 'unilateral'.
claims.verification_note: Muganga and Nyakarundi were in no excerpt: added replacement quote. Exact date not printed for the designation; set to month. The page gives the announcement day only as 'Monday' (dateline Goma, 3 March 2026; posted 9 March); Kigali's reaction is dated 2 March. Date kept at month precision. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: dateline Goma 3 March 2026; US sanctions; Kigali's denunciation 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: OFAC designations of Muganga and Nyakarundi 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-028: Read the retained page: the names and the four-officer count are supported, but the stored excerpt omits Muganga and Nyakarundi and the claim leaves out the stated basis (alleged support to M23, a US accusation) and Kigali's immediate rejection printed in the same paragraph. Added both; Muganga/Nyakarundi need an add_excerpt with the quote below. Single relay of OFAC; the OFAC release itself was not in the input.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): dateline Goma 3 March 2026; US sanctions; Kigali's denunciation; OFAC designations of Muganga and Nyakarundi
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates UC-RDF#14/#15 (UN GoE and HRW). Swahili edition of a Burundian monitor; the dateline says 3 March 2026 while the announcement is dated 2 March elsewhere. The page also states Kigali's reaction (statement of 2 March calling the sanctions 'unilateral').

claims.text: RFI's Invité Afrique Midi episode on the state visit of the Burundian president to Kinshasa, with Jean-Jacques Wondo, a strategy and security analyst at Afridesk, as guest, was headlined: '«On peut estimer à 10 000 le nombre de soldats burundais toujours présents au Congo»'.
claims.verification_note: Headline attribution narrowed to what the page shows; the president is named on the page as 'Evariste Ndayishimiye' (replacement quote). The quoted headline is presented as the guest's estimate but the page text does not attribute it in words; the audio was not transcribed, so the basis of the estimate is unknown. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Analyst estimate from a podcast page (headline); the audio was not transcribed so the basis of the estimate is unknown. The page says nothing on the geographic split between provinces.

claims.text: MSF stated that Burundian authorities now estimated at 35'000 the number of people who would have been displaced since the start of February.
claims.verification_note: Kept the source's conditional ('se seraient déplacées') and its number format; origin is the Burundian authorities.
claims.researcher_note: Figure is the Burundian authorities' estimate as relayed by MSF; Vatican News cites UNHCR for 42,000 people reaching Burundi in two weeks (not separately claimed). Scope of the 35,000 (all of the Kivus vs Uvira) is not stated.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources on Saturday 29 March, that cohabitation between the FARDC and the Wazalendo was becoming difficult, notably in Uvira, and that the two parties had set up two parallel commands, which made operational coordination difficult.
claims.verification_note: Page supports. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 29 Mar 2025, carries every clause, attributed to local sources. The stored excerpt is cut before 'rendant difficile la coordination militaire'; the full sentence is added. Statement unchanged.
claims.researcher_note: Anonymous local sources; the page adds that Wazalendo suspect FARDC soldiers of corruption and of collaborating with the rebels, and that a reconciliation meeting was planned for that weekend.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that, to restore security, the FARDC headquarters and the South Kivu governorate were relocated to Uvira in early March, and that in early April DRC Defence Minister Guy Kabombo and former RAD national coordinator General Padiri travelled from Bujumbura to Uvira to appease the Wazalendo groups.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC; Guy Kabombo; General Padiri; Wazalendo factions
claims.verification_note: Supported (para. 174); date widened because the statement includes the early-March relocation.
claims.researcher_note: Adds that the minister travelled from Bujumbura (SOS Médias Burundi also says he came after a stay in Burundi). The Group's text calls Padiri 'ancien coordonnateur national de la RAD', whereas Radio Okapi and SOS Médias Burundi (7-8 April) call him the current national coordinator (Radio Okapi: 'général Padiri Bulenda'; SOS Médias: 'lieutenant général Padiri Bulenda') - discrepancy to surface.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that during his visit to Uvira on a Monday (dateline 7 April 2025), Defence Minister Guy Kabombo, accompanied by Lieutenant General Padiri Bulenda (national coordinator of the Wazalendo) and a Burundian army delegation, praised the commitment of the Burundian army, the Burundian National Defence Force (FDNB); SOS Médias Burundi stated in its own narration that the FDNB had deployed nearly 10.000 soldiers in the DRC.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira (arrival at Kavimvira border), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Original attributed the 10.000 figure to Kabombo ('which he said'); the page has it as a relative clause in SOS Médias's narration. The troop figure is the outlet's narration, not a quote from the minister. The UN Group of Experts gives its own, lower estimates for the FDNB deployment (see the FDNB deployment claim from the same unit).
claims.researcher_note: SOS Médias Burundi is a Burundian outlet run by journalists in the country and in exile. The figure of about 10,000 is not independently confirmed; the UN Group of Experts (annex) estimates at least 7,000 troops in South Kivu in early April and about 14 battalions (see separate claim).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that during the Defence Minister's visit to Uvira (dateline 7 April 2025), abuses were reported, notably illegal tax levies at the Kavimvira post, Kalundu port and along the road axes.
claims.place_as_written: Kavimvira post, Kalundu port, Uvira, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Unattributed abuses; page does not name who levied the taxes.
claims.researcher_note: The source places this within 'tensions internes entre les Wazalendo, les FARDC et la population civile' without naming who levied the taxes. Compare HRW 23 May (Wazalendo roadblock collections in March-April).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the new commander of the 33rd military region, General Dunia, began on Tuesday 8 April the identification of Wazalendo fighters in Uvira, to distinguish genuine from false Wazalendo and give the government a list of those deserving benefits.
claims.actor_as_written: General Dunia, commander of the 33rd military region (as Radio Okapi names him)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt matches. Not to be confused with the self-proclaimed Wazalendo 'general' Alexis Dunia named in a June 2025 SOS Médias Burundi report.
claims.researcher_note: The same page says the command relationship between Wazalendo and FARDC at Uvira had been a serious problem before the minister's visit. SOS Médias Burundi (13 June) names a 'général Alexis Dunia' as a self-proclaimed Wazalendo general; the two may or may not be the same person - not established.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that, at the time of its report, relations between FARDC and Wazalendo had improved and some Wazalendo groups had left the centre of Uvira at the request of FARDC command.
claims.verification_note: Date corrected from June to the report's reference time. 'At the time of the report': transmitted to the Sanctions Committee on 6 May 2025 (published 3 July 2025).
claims.researcher_note: The sentence is split across a page break in the PDF text ('relations entre les FARDC et les ... [footnotes] ... Wazalendo s’étaient améliorées'); the excerpt begins after the footnote block. 'At the date of drawing up this report' per the Group.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that more and more young Burundians were joining Wazalendo militias in Uvira territory, with testimonies in the neighbourhoods of Kasenga, Kavimvira, Kilibula, Kawizi and Kiliba, and that some refugees from the Mulongwe and Lusenda camps or the Sange transit centre had also been seen in Wazalendo ranks; it also cited regional security sources saying nearly 10,000 Burundian soldiers, supported by Imbonerakure, were officially in the DRC.
claims.place_as_written: Kasenga, Kavimvira, Kilibula, Kawizi, Kiliba (Uvira territory); Mulongwe and Lusenda camps; Sange transit centre, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: English edition of SOS Médias Burundi, dateline 24 May 2025; locations are in Uvira territory, not only the city.
claims.researcher_note: Recruitment is described by the source as driven by promises of pay, not as coerced; recorded as unit/actor context, not as forced recruitment. A National Refugee Commission agent in Baraka is quoted as saying refugees have had no assistance for over five months. Unverified; no Burundian government response found.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that Médecins sans frontières announced in a communiqué of Friday 25 July the end of its mission in Uvira from the end of July 2025, ending care for new war-wounded patients and cholera patients at the Hôpital général de référence d'Uvira; MSF cited the attainment of the medical objectives set when the project began in November 2024.
claims.place_as_written: Hôpital général de référence d'Uvira, Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Supported by the Radio Okapi page; the excerpt_en flag is the expansion 'Uvira General Reference Hospital', a faithful translation.
claims.researcher_note: MSF's stated reason is that objectives were met (fewer gunshot cases); the source does not link it to insecurity. Recorded because it changes civilian access to trauma and cholera care in Uvira. Ben Taleb Zied (MSF project coordinator) named on the page but not in excerpts.

claims.text: Afrikarabia reported that President Félix Tshisekedi's appointment of General Olivier Gasita as deputy commander of the 33rd military region, and his taking up duty in Uvira on 1 September, were at the heart of the unrest, with civil society organisations and above all the Wazalendo militias leading the protest; SOS Médias Burundi reported that General Gasita was entrenched in an Uvira hotel under the joint protection of the FARDC and of 'militaires burundais'.
claims.verification_note: Source 1 was cited but its fact was not in the statement; added and attributed. Leadership of the protest reworded to the page ('mais surtout les milices Wazalendo'). Actualite.cd (9 Sept) describes Gasita as deputy commander in charge of operations and intelligence 'depuis janvier', which differs from the 1 September date of taking up duty given by Afrikarabia and SOS Médias Burundi. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Titles differ across outlets: 'commandant adjoint de la 33e région militaire' (Afrikarabia, SOS), 'chargé des opérations et du renseignement' (Radio Okapi). Name printed as Olivier Gasita (Radio Okapi: Olivier Gasita Mukunda per other pages). Burundian soldiers' protection stated by SOS Médias Burundi, not independently confirmed.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing local sources, that General Gasita arrived in Uvira escorted by Burundian soldiers of the FDNB as well as FARDC elements.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt states it, attributed to local sources. Single outlet: C.
claims.researcher_note: Single outlet citing local sources. Burundi's government made no statement found on this escort (see gaps).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that since 2 September the local 'forces vives' and Wazalendo combatants had erected barricades on strategic axes, notably towards the Burundian border, paralysing cross-border trade and lake operations at Kalundu port, and that, according to several sources, the port was under the exclusive surveillance of the Wazalendo.
claims.place_as_written: Axes towards the Burundi border and Kalundu port, Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Source 1's fact (Wazalendo control of Kalundu port) was not in the statement; added with its attribution.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi's 3 Sep article says activities paralysed 'depuis la matinée du mercredi 3 septembre' naming Mulongwe, Kasenga and 'Kanvinvira' (sic, Kavimvira); other outlets and HRW say 2 September. Radio Okapi 5 Sep says the barricades were on the 'Kilomoni' axis linking Uvira to the border. Prices: tomato from 500 to 1,000 francs (Radio Okapi 6 Sep).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing military sources, that General Olivier Gasita left Uvira at dawn on Tuesday 9 September at around 3 a.m., without other details on his real destination; Afrikarabia reported that he was exfiltrated from Uvira to Bujumbura and then Kinshasa.
claims.verification_note: Departure date corroborated by two outlets; destination from Afrikarabia only, attributed.
claims.researcher_note: Radio Okapi gives no destination; Afrikarabia names Bujumbura then Kinshasa. Kinshasa's official reason is not given in these excerpts.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that a government delegation led by Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani was in Uvira with the mission of reconciling local communities, easing tensions and restoring state authority; the delegation also included Aimé Boji (Industry), Floribert Anzuluni (Regional Cooperation), Eliezer Ntambwe (minister delegate for Defence in charge of veterans), FARDC chief of staff General Jules Banza and national police commissioner general Benjamin Alongaboni. SOS Médias Burundi reported that Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo arrived escorted by Burundian and Congolese soldiers.
claims.actor_as_written: DRC government delegation; FDNB (escort, per SOS Médias Burundi)
claims.verification_note: Source 1 (delegation list) was cited but unused; members added from the excerpt. The excerpt_en flags reflect translated titles only. SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) says the delegation arrived in Uvira on Thursday (11 September 2025).
claims.researcher_note: Date: SOS Médias Burundi (dated 12 Sep) says the delegation arrived 'Alhamisi hii' (Thursday = 2025-09-11); Radio Okapi (12 Sep) says it is staying in Uvira. SOS gives his title as Deputy Prime Minister for security; Radio Okapi as vice-Premier ministre et ministre de l'Intérieur. SOS says the Deputy PM met only Wazalendo representatives at first. Burundian escort is stated only by SOS Médias Burundi (one outlet).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Wazalendo militias criticise the Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB), present in Uvira as part of bilateral military cooperation, for not conducting offensives against the M23.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt states it (SOS Médias Burundi narration of the Wazalendo's criticism).
claims.researcher_note: Date is the publication date; presence is a general condition, not an event. No numbers of Burundian troops are given in this excerpt.

claims.text: The SOS Torture Burundi Justice Newsletter stated that Burundi reportedly deployed an additional contingent of 700 soldiers to Uvira on August 21, 2025, to reinforce more than 24 battalions of Burundian soldiers already deployed in eastern DRC to counter the advance of the M23.
claims.verification_note: Removed the issue number from the statement text; the originating source is the Burundi Daily article the newsletter footnotes, so this is a relay, single origin: C. Hedged ('reportedly'); the newsletter's footnote 26 cites a Burundi Daily article of 31 August 2025 ('Uvira surrounded, Ndayishimiye dispatches military reinforcements'), which was not opened. No Burundian government confirmation found.
claims.researcher_note: Hedged ('reportedly') in the newsletter, which footnotes a source not opened here. Burundi government made no statement on this found. SOS Médias Burundi (7 Sep) says Burundi has about 10,000 soldiers on Congolese soil (different figure scope).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that in recent weeks 332 Burundian refugees in 74 households, who had lived in the Mulongwe and Lusenda camps and the Kavimvira transit centre in South Kivu, were repatriated to Burundi via the Gatumba border post; refugees trying to farm at Kahwizi and Kiliba reported being attacked, and a refugee, Niyonkuru, said that Wazalendo militiamen attack them on the way to the fields.
claims.place_as_written: Mulongwe camp, Kavimvira transit centre (Uvira), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo militiamen (as alleged by a refugee quoted by the source)
claims.verification_note: Gatumba/camp details came from the page, not the excerpt; supplied. Named the speaker Niyonkuru as printed (policy v1) and added the Kahwizi/Kiliba location the excerpt gives. The attack allegation is one refugee's account; no dates or casualties given. The same page reports that the Bukavu-Uvira humanitarian corridor was blocked by Wazalendo under Makanaki Kasimbira John, according to local sources (see claim 0). The page says the operation was run by Burundi's refugee commission (CNR) with UNHCR. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi, dateline Uvira 24 July 2025, posted 25 July: 332 refugees (74 households) repatriated in recent weeks; refugees farming at Kahwizi and Kiliba report attacks, Niyonkuru blaming Wazalendo. All clauses are on the page; the camps and Gatumba clauses were in no stored excerpt, now added.
claims.researcher_note: Allegation about Wazalendo comes from one named refugee (first name/surname 'Niyonkuru') quoted by the outlet; no date. Page also says the Bukavu-Uvira humanitarian corridor (200 tonnes of food and medicine) was blocked, per local sources (not cited). Name 'Niyonkuru' printed as a quoted refugee; not harmed per the excerpt.

claims.text: UN News reported that the UN deputy spokesperson said humanitarian partners reported more than 200,000 people displaced across South Kivu and at least 70 civilians killed in the current escalation.
claims.verification_note: Removed date; speaker name sits on the page, not in the excerpt. Grade B: one UN origin (spokesperson relaying partners), not an investigation. Province-wide figure, not Uvira alone. BBC (10 Dec) cites the UN at least 74 killed, mostly civilians.
claims.researcher_note: Figure covers South Kivu, not Uvira alone. UN spokesperson on the page: Farhan Haq (Deputy Spokesperson).

claims.text: UN News reported that between 5 and 8 December nearly 25,000 people crossed the border into Burundi, including Congolese nationals, returning Burundians and third-country migrants, and that in Uvira at least 32 WFP-supported schools suspended classes to house displaced families, depriving more than 12,000 children of school meals, the UN Deputy Spokesperson said.
claims.verification_note: Statement had attributed the border figure to the Deputy Spokesperson; the excerpt does not; reworded so the attribution covers the schools passage, which names him. Border-crossing figure covers 5-8 Dec, before the M23 entry into Uvira.
claims.researcher_note: Border-crossing figure is for 5-8 Dec (before the 10 Dec entry), as the UN states it.

claims.text: BBC Afrique reported that, according to the UN, the Uvira offensive caused dozens of deaths, at least 100 wounded and more than 200,000 displaced, and that at least 30,000 civilians fled to Burundi.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira (city), South Kivu and Burundi border
claims.verification_note: Removed publication date. Relays the UN, so not an independent origin for the UN figures. The 200,000 displaced figure is the UN's South Kivu-wide figure (UN News, 10 Dec), which BBC applies to the Uvira offensive. Not independent of the UN claim.
claims.researcher_note: The UN figure of 200,000 displaced is the same South Kivu figure reported on 10 Dec by UN News; BBC applies it to the offensive.

claims.text: BBC reported that Burundi had shut its border with DR Congo, a Burundian military source was quoted as saying by AFP.
claims.verification_note: Removed publication date; wire origin credited to AFP. SOS Médias Burundi (11 Dec) separately reports Burundian authorities closed the Gatumba-Kavimvira and Vugizo posts.
claims.researcher_note: Original source AFP (per the BBC page); the BBC text does not name the Burundian source. Border posts named in other reports (Gatumba, Vugizo) were not opened.

claims.text: Congo Indépendant reported that more than 267,000 people were now refugees or displaced, nearly 250,000 of them in Burundi, and that Minister of State Ève Bazaiba, who stayed in Burundi, called it a 'human tragedy'.
claims.verification_note: Statement unchanged; removed the Radio Okapi 300,000 figure from `figures`, which this source does not print. The source of the figures is not named ('selon les chiffres disponibles').
claims.researcher_note: Figure source not named in the passage. Radio Okapi (2026-04-07, Government report) gives more than 300,000 displaced.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that residents said a FARDC drone was shot down in Fizi territory by Twirwaneho fighters after clashes in which the FARDC, supported by the Wazalendo and elements of the FDNB, fought Twirwaneho fighters, described as a military ally of the AFC/M23 in South Kivu.
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC, Wazalendo, FDNB elements vs Twirwaneho
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page; 'Thursday' with a 15 January dateline is 15 January. The article says no independent confirmation was obtained.
claims.researcher_note: Date computed from weekday and the article's dateline: 'On Thursday' = 15 January 2026. Residents' report; no independent confirmation per the article; neither Congolese nor Burundian authorities had officially responded.

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported that Bukavu-Uvira road traffic resumed on Wednesday 1 April 2026, fifteen days after FARDC and Wazalendo elements had suspended it in the Ruzizi plain, and that since 15 March the traffic had been cut at Kasambura by FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo elements.
claims.place_as_written: Kasambura, Ruzizi plain (Bukavu-Uvira road, RN5), Uvira territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and Wazalendo elements (as named by the source)
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts are on the page (byline Alphonse Muderwa) and carry every clause. The '7' flag is the outlet's name, not a figure. The excerpt_en flags are only about the English capitalisation of 'Wednesday'/'Fifteen'; the translations are faithful. Single Congolese outlet. Transporters quoted on the page also complained of several paying barriers on the road.
claims.researcher_note: Single Congolese outlet; the 15 March start date is the source's. Transporters quoted in the article denounced several paying barriers. The road was suspended again in May (see DW Swahili claim).

claims.text: DW reported that the repatriation of Congolese refugees who had fled to Burundi during the AFC-M23 occupation of Uvira in December began on Thursday, and that in Uvira the returnees were received at a transit centre where they were expected to receive resettlement kits.
claims.place_as_written: Busuma camp (Burundi) to Uvira (city), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed '23 April 2026', which no excerpt prints (the page is dated 23/04/2026 and says 'ce jeudi'; the date field carries it). The body figure (about 500 people, about ten convoys from Busuma camp) is in the replacement quote but in no stored excerpt, so it is left out of the statement and given in the note; extend the excerpt with source_edits.py add_excerpt to add it. Byline Mitima Delachance. DW body text: 'Environ 500 Congolais ont traversé la frontière de Kavimrira' (DW's spelling, presumably Kavimvira), in about ten convoys from Busuma camp in Burundi to Uvira. Returnees Victorina Asele Ngondé and Mushombé Mbirizé are quoted on the page.
claims.researcher_note: Thursday = article date 23 April 2026 (page header states 23/04/2026). DW credits a Reuters image only. Another outlet in search results (Reuters via Facebook, snippet only) also reports Burundi starting to return Congolese refugees; not cited.

claims.text: OCHA's South Kivu situation report stated that armed clashes had intensified in the territories of Fizi, Mwenga, Uvira, Kalehe and Shabunda, and that rapid multisectoral assessments in March counted more than 542 200 returnees at provincial level, most of them concentrated in Uvira territory.
claims.place_as_written: South Kivu (Fizi, Mwenga, Uvira, Kalehe, Shabunda territories); returnees concentrated in Uvira territory
claims.verification_note: Figure written as the source prints it (542 200) to clear the figure flag. The page says the report covers 1-31 March 2026 (in replacement_quotes; note only). Grade lowered from A to B: a single OCHA situation report compiling partner assessments is one credible non-partisan origin, not an investigation. Situation report #4 (21 April 2026), covering 1-31 March 2026, before this unit's period.
claims.researcher_note: Covers March 2026 (before the unit's period); included because it is the UN baseline published in the period and quantifies returns to Uvira territory. Title wording is partly reconstructed from the URL and listing; the page title as fetched was not captured separately.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Kavimvira bridge on the RN5 in Uvira collapsed on Tuesday 16 June; according to local health sources one person died and two were injured, a medical source quoted saying three people were injured, of whom a young boy died in hospital after a blow to the head and the other two had light injuries, while the NSCC Sud-Sud civil society group said in a statement that its field investigations showed three deaths, including two minors aged 14 and 17 and an adult, plus an injured woman. Local authorities had not yet commented officially on the circumstances of the collapse or the final toll.
claims.place_as_written: Kavimvira bridge, RN5, Uvira (city), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Removed the year (not in excerpt). Replaced 'the article does not attribute the collapse to the conflict' (an inference from absence) with the page's own statement that local authorities had not commented on the circumstances. Kept the two tolls separate, each attributed. No victim is named on the page. Toll differs: one dead (local health / medical source) vs three dead (NSCC Sud-Sud). Not presented as a conflict event.
claims.researcher_note: Not a conflict event; recorded as an Uvira event at the Kavimvira border crossing area that affects movement on the RN5. claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, a year after the Washington peace accord, that the territories of Masisi, Rutshuru and Walikale in North Kivu and those of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga in South Kivu remained the most affected by violence, with civilians displaced and material destruction.

SOS Médias Burundi later (6 Oct 2026, out of window) reports a similar sentence for 27 Republican Guard soldiers at Uvira. Names of the convicted not printed.

claims.researcher_note: Para. 78; annex 36.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 continued the recruitment and training of its 'local defence' forces, tasked with maintaining security in towns and villages controlled by AFC/M23, and that these forces were frequently implicated in clashes with FDLR and Wazalendo combatants and in human rights abuses; it annexed an announcement on the graduation of 242 Local Defense Personnel in Nyiragongo, dated 23 September 2025.
claims.verification_note: The 23 September 2025 date belongs to the annexed announcement caption; worded as such rather than as the graduation date.
claims.researcher_note: Para. 26; annex 10. Date refers to the graduation announcement; the abuses are undated.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 February AFC/M23 forces issued an ultimatum to residents of Karenga, who had returned to Karenga after the dismantling of IDP camps around Goma in early February, to leave by the next day or be shot.
claims.verification_note: Supported; year removed (not printed in excerpt).
claims.researcher_note: Annex 39 (para. 86). Karenga is placed in Masisi territory in annex 40. Residents then sought refuge in collective shelters in Sake.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that since January 2025 at least 5,798 individuals were repatriated to Rwanda, primarily from Masisi territory but also from Rutshuru territory, and that a confidential source with direct knowledge of repatriation operations referred to recent repatriations, including the repatriation of 227 Rwandan refugees on 23 October, primarily Hutu women and children from Masisi and Rutshuru territories.
claims.verification_note: The 227 figure comes from a confidential source cited by the Group; attribution added via replacement quote. Year of 23 October not printed, removed.
claims.researcher_note: Annex 39. The same sentence (a confidential source) reports continued AFC/M23 pressure on those returning; not asserted here.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 16 June AFC/M23 appointed Jean-Damascène Mwigimba as provincial director for its own iteration of the Commission Nationale pour les Réfugiés (CNR), overseeing cross-border refugee movements.
claims.verification_note: Narrowed: the UNHCR-office threat and the year are not in the stored excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Annex 13 (para. 31); also annexes 39 and 40. The UNHCR-office threat is cited elsewhere (existing claim on Chantal Murekatete Kayitaba).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that local sources confirmed AFC/M23 began in July 2025 to build a centre in Karenga, Masisi territory, including a transit site, a school and a health centre.
claims.verification_note: Matches annex 40; local sources as relayed by the Group.
claims.researcher_note: Annex 40. Karenga is the area from which residents were expelled in February (see annex 39 claim). The annex adds that the facilities were meant for returning Congolese refugees and that UNHCR was not involved; not asserted here.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 9 October AFC/M23 installed Bashali Luanda Jaques on the throne of the Bashali chefferie during a ceremony in Kitchanga, in contravention of traditional succession procedures and despite objections from the Bashali royal family representing the legitimate Mwami, Bashali N'siyi Minihire Roger.
claims.verification_note: Supported; year removed (not printed in excerpt). Names as printed.
claims.researcher_note: Annex 12 (para. 30). The Group describes the appointment as unlawful.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 converted villages into towns or communes, including in Sake, Ngungu, Rubaya and Bweremana in Masisi territory, abolishing all customary rights, and that in August AFC/M23-appointed North Kivu governor Bahati Erasto announced plans to subdivide Goma into four communes instead of the existing two.
claims.verification_note: Supported; year removed (not printed in excerpts).
claims.researcher_note: Annex 13 (para. 31). Conversion date not stated; August date is for the Goma announcement.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 19 June AFC/M23-appointed North Kivu governor Bahati Erasto authorized the resumption of operations within the land registry and property title divisions in North Kivu, and that on 25 July Emmanuel Birato Rwihimba, AFC/M23-appointed governor of South Kivu, issued land management laws, including new procedures for obtaining building permits and cadastral documents.
claims.verification_note: Supported; years removed (not printed in excerpts). Elsewhere the report says Birato Rwihimba was reassigned in June; the 'governor' label for 25 July is as printed.
claims.researcher_note: Annex 13. Two decisions (19 June and 25 July) in one claim; the Group says they interfere with land administration. Annex 14 says the former South Kivu governor Birato Rwihimba was reassigned in June to an investment department, which is in tension with the 25 July "governor" label; as printed in the document.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 29 May 2025 AFC/M23 announced an arbitration court for local conflicts in Goma, that on 12 August it created a 25-member Commission pour la Restauration de la Justice presided by Delion Kimbulungu Mutangala, and that on 3 November the commission announced 378 successful magistrate candidates.
claims.verification_note: Four excerpts carry the four clauses.
claims.researcher_note: Annex 15 (para. 33). Third excerpt is short by necessity; the 3 November date is in the preceding sentence of the annex.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Peace Agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of Rwanda was signed in Washington, D.C. on 27 June 2025, brokered by the United States of America in consultation with Qatar and Togo (as African Union mediator).
claims.actor_as_written: Governments of the DRC and Rwanda; United States, Qatar, Togo (mediators)
claims.verification_note: Names spelled as printed.
claims.researcher_note: Para. 7. Recorded as political context for the Kivu conflict.

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 3 July Benjamin Mbonimpa, head of the AFC/M23 delegation in Doha, and Freddy Rukema Kanyiki, AFC/M23's deputy coordinator, reiterated the need for the DRC Government to agree to several trust-building measures, and that the Doha Declaration of Principles, brokered by Qatar, was signed by the DRC Government and AFC/M23 on 19 July 2025 and welcomed by the Government of Rwanda.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC; AFC/M23; Qatar (mediator)
claims.verification_note: Narrowed to excerpt wording (measures the DRC Government was asked to agree to).
claims.researcher_note: Annex 2 (para. 7).

claims.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the parties maintained active engagement in Doha and on 18 September signed a formal prisoner exchange agreement as part of confidence-building measures, and that on 14 October both sides concluded an agreement establishing a ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism.
claims.verification_note: Supported; year removed (not printed). The parties are the DRC Government and AFC/M23 per the preceding text, not printed in the excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Para. 11; annex 5. The parties are named in the preceding sentence of para. 11 (talks stalled; "the parties maintained active engagement in Doha"). Location Doha inferred from that sentence.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 17 February AFC/M23 issued instructions giving a one-week ultimatum for parents to retrieve their children.
claims.verification_note: Para. 41 verbatim; Goma is the paragraph's setting (children on the streets of Goma).
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 41. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement limited to the ultimatum; footnote 39 says the instructions were written and verbal ones issued by de facto authorities and collected by the FFM.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that after capturing Goma, M23 members ordered tens of thousands of IDPs living in camps around the city to dismantle their shelters and return to their villages.
claims.verification_note: Para. 51 verbatim. Date narrowed to January-February: Goma was taken by 29 January (para. 13) and para. 52 dates a return 'following the forced dismantlement' to 25 February; March was not supported.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 51. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Annex V lists camps shown emptied by satellite imagery: Don Bosco Ngangi, Bushagara, Mudja, Buhimba, Rusayo, Bulengo, Lushagala, Lwashi, Kashaka, Rego. Month assumed from footnote 42 ('End of February over 500,000 IDPs...'); the paragraph itself gives no date.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 25 February Hutu families who had returned to Karenga (Masisi territory, North Kivu) after the forced dismantlement of their camp were ordered to leave the town within a day and were threatened that if they did not comply, 'the Red Cross would come to collect [their] bodies'.
claims.verification_note: Para. 52 verbatim; actor M23 from the paragraph's lead sentence ('once again expelled by M23').
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 52. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that upon capturing Goma and Bukavu, AFC/M23 appointed 'administrators' to formalize its control as de facto authority and introduced its own 'tax collection system', and that civil servants and customary chiefs opposing M23 were replaced with individuals supportive of M23.
claims.verification_note: Para. 15 verbatim. Date widened to January-February: Goma was taken in January (para. 13), Bukavu in February (para. 14).
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 15. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Footnote 21 gives BBC as source for the mining-activities tax; footnote 19: M23 appointed new governors and other local authorities in North and South Kivu.

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission described a '10 houses system' implemented in M23-held areas as an administrative structure for local chiefs appointed by M23 to monitor residents' movements and report daily on suspicious activities.
claims.verification_note: Para. 37 verbatim (description of the system).
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 37. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement limited to the excerpt (description of the system).

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 27 June senior ministers of the DRC and Rwanda signed a Peace Agreement in Washington.
claims.actor_as_written: Governments of the DRC and Rwanda
claims.verification_note: Para. 18 verbatim. Actor and location corrected: the claim is the Washington signing only (M23 and Doha belong to claim 56).
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 18. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).

claims.text: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 19 July there followed a Declaration of Principles between the Government of the DRC and M23 in Doha, committing to reaching a comprehensive peace agreement by 18 August.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC and M23
claims.verification_note: Para. 18: the excerpt does not use the word 'signed' (para. 88 does); narrowed to the excerpt's wording.
claims.researcher_note: A/HRC/60/80 para. 18. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the occupation of Nyabiondo on Sunday 9 March caused a massive displacement of inhabitants of at least six villages, who according to local notables took refuge at the Kashebere health centre, while others went towards Kibua and the surrounding bush.
claims.place_as_written: Nyabiondo, Kashebere, Kibua; Masisi and Walikale
claims.verification_note: Supported; the date '9 March' is printed in the page's lead sentence just before the stored excerpt (page-only clause). The page lists eight place names after 'at least six villages'; the statement keeps the source's wording.
claims.researcher_note: Two excerpts from the same page. The source lists eight place names after saying "at least six villages". Health-centre use as shelter noted; no attack on it reported.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that local actors lamented the absence of humanitarian aid in the area affected by the fighting around Nyabiondo, with the exception of Médecins sans frontières (MSF), which continued to support the Nyabiondo hospital.
claims.verification_note: Supported verbatim.
claims.researcher_note: Health-access context: MSF support to Nyabiondo hospital as of 10 Mar 2025, the day after the M23 capture.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that the M23 rebellion was intensifying its campaign to recruit young people in North Kivu for what it calls the Congolese revolutionary army (ARC), through a recruitment and mobilisation committee, and that the campaign also took place in the town of Kitshanga, Bukoma groupement, which the article places in Rutshuru territory.
claims.verification_note: Supported; the committee detail is on the page outside the stored excerpts. Radio Okapi places Kitshanga in Rutshuru; territory field kept as Masisi with the source's wording noted. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 29 Apr 2025, carries every clause in its own voice, including Kitshanga 'en territoire de Rutshuru' as the statement flags. The recruitment and mobilisation committee clause was on no stored excerpt; that passage is added.
claims.researcher_note: The source describes voluntary-style recruitment through ideological sessions; it does not say it is forced. Radio Okapi places Kitshanga in Rutshuru territory; Kitshanga is commonly placed in Masisi territory (flag for gazetteer). Territory field set to Masisi on that basis, to be verified.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that, in a communiqué published on Monday 28 April by an anonymous local human rights organisation, PARECO-FF Wazalendo fighters led by the militia chief Kigingi Jean de Dieu were accused of abuses against civilians in Katoyi sector, Masisi territory, including setting up a parallel fiscal and judicial administration and levying illegal taxes, with the organisation's remarks said to be corroborated by local administrative sources.
claims.actor_as_written: PARECO-FF (Coalition des patriotes résistants congolais - Force de frappe), led by Kigingi Jean de Dieu
claims.verification_note: Allegations attributed to the anonymous NGO as relayed by Radio Okapi; name as printed.
claims.researcher_note: Anonymous NGO communiqué corroborated, per the outlet, by local administrative sources. Three excerpts of one page. Party account of PARECO-FF: no statement found.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that hundreds of displaced families who had fled recent fighting between AFC-M23 and Wazalendo groups were living in alarming conditions at Mweso, in schools and churches, without humanitarian assistance.
claims.verification_note: Supported verbatim.
claims.researcher_note: The page says they fled villages around the Ngeri tea garden (Kashanje, Bweru, Kivuye) in Masisi and Rutshuru; the displaced are concentrated in the compound of the Institut technique médical de Mweso. Number undetermined ("thousands" estimated).

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that after the fighting at Rushihe a precarious calm was observed on Monday 26 October at Katobo, and that gunfire from heavy and light weapons caused displacement, with several Katobo inhabitants fleeing to Ihula and others taking refuge in the forest.
claims.verification_note: Supported.
claims.researcher_note: Two excerpts of one page.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that a new landslide on Tuesday 3 March 2026 at the Kasasa mining site in the Rubaya mining zone (Masisi) reportedly cost the lives of more than a hundred people, mostly artisanal diggers, and said it came about a month after a collapse on 28 January 2026 at the same site that had killed more than 400 people, not counting the missing.
claims.actor_as_written: not applicable (mine collapse; Rubaya under AFC/M23 control)
claims.verification_note: Tolls kept per source and provisional ('aurait'). Conflicts with an existing Actualite.cd claim of at least 226 dead on 29 January (r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-018). Toll and date of the January collapse differ between Actualite.cd reports: more than 400 dead on 28 January (this page) vs at least 226 dead on 29 January (31 January report).
claims.researcher_note: Figures conflict with existing claims on the January collapse (Actualite.cd 31 Jan 2026: at least 226 dead on Thursday 29 January; r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-018): this page gives 28 January and "more than 400". TV5Monde snippets (not opened) refer to a 3 March slide with "200 dead, including 70 children" per the DRC government; not cited. For the discrepancy register.

claims.text: A humanitarian early-warning alert listing HEKS-EPER as its principal source, with the status 'preliminary diagnosis / awaiting assessment', reported that about 65 000 people (in 9.311 households) had arrived in the town of Baraka since 11 December 2025.
claims.verification_note: Alert number and status date are not in the excerpt; moved to the note. Figures written as the alert prints them. Alert no. 6239 on the OCHA-hosted ehtools registry, start date 15/12/2025, not yet assessed. The alert says the displaced came from Uvira city and from health areas of Nundu health zone (incl. Mboko, Swima, Lweba), fleeing FARDC-AFC-M23 clashes.
claims.researcher_note: Registry entry, not yet assessed. The alert's description (beyond the excerpt) says the displaced came from Uvira city and from health areas Kenya, Kabumbe, Lusenda, Lweba, Mboko, Munene, Nundu and Swima, fleeing FARDC-AFC/M23 clashes; cite that in a second excerpt if needed.

claims.text: The same alert reported that the threat of a possible M23 advance towards Baraka caused a large part of this population, together with the host population, to flee towards Burundi, Tanzania and the Ubwari peninsula.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and matches the statement. Partner-reported early warning, unassessed. HEKS-EPER is named on the alert page, not in the excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Alert is a partner-reported early warning, unassessed.

claims.text: The Conflict Sensitivity Hub's August 2025 note on Fizi territory listed local armed groups, including Twirwaneho, led by deserter colonel Charles Sematama after the death of Michel Rukundo alias Makanika and active in Balala Nord grouping.
claims.place_as_written: Fizi territory (Balala Nord grouping), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; statement attributes the roster to the note. The Conflict Sensitivity Hub's own roster (footnote 10 of its August 2025 note), not an official or party listing. The note prints 'Michel Rukundo alias Makanika'; BBC Gahuza prints 'Michel Rukunda' (spelling discrepancy between sources).
claims.researcher_note: The same footnote lists Gumino (Bijombo-Minembwe axis), Maï-Maï Mulumba (Mimbililo), Ebwela (Kipupu), Yakutumba (Hewa Bora, Ngandja, Kilembwe) and Biloze Bishambuke (Milimba), plus Red Tabara, FNL, MRP Abarundi, FDLR and CNRD: roster lead. Publication date given as September (URL path 2025/09); period August 2025. The note's own statement that Minembwe fell 'fin février 2025' is cited to APADEC.

claims.text: The Conflict Sensitivity Hub's note said that the most important Maï-Maï factions in Fizi territory were those of Yakutumba, Ebuela (also known as Kibukila) and Biloze Bishambuke, which now collaborate with the FARDC under the name Wazalendo against the AFC/M23 and its allies, and that a coordination of Wazalendo against the AFC/M23 in Fizi territory was set up under the direction of Willam Yakutumba.
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact; origin of the coordination clause recorded. The Conflict Sensitivity Hub's account. The coordination clause is footnoted to a congorassure.com article of February 2025, so the coordination dates from early 2025, not August. The note prints 'Willam Yakutumba' (the cited URL spells 'william-yakutumba').
claims.researcher_note: The meeting's date/venue ('plusieurs seigneurs de guerre à Fizi centre') is in the preceding sentence; the note cites congorassure.com 7 Feb 2025 for it. Name printed 'Willam Yakutumba' in this note.

claims.text: The Conflict Sensitivity Hub's August 2025 note on Fizi territory said, citing an APADEC humanitarian note of 19 March 2025, that since Minembwe and its surroundings came under the control of Twirwaneho elements allied to AFC/M23, inhabitants no longer had access to essential goods coming from Uvira via Baraka and Fizi centre, and that Wazalendo groups allied to the FARDC on that route had banned itinerant traders from going to Minembwe, raising food prices.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo groups allied to the FARDC
claims.verification_note: Both clauses are on the page (the first in the sentence before the excerpt). Grade lowered to C: single local origin (APADEC) relayed. The passage is footnoted to an APADEC humanitarian note of March 2025, so the blockade observation dates from March 2025 although it appears in the August 2025 note. Single local origin relayed by the Hub. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Both clauses are verbatim in the CS-Hub note (August 2025), but the sentence carries footnote 22, which cites an APADEC humanitarian note of 19 March 2025; the situation is therefore sourced to March 2025, not August. The statement now says so. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Both clauses are verbatim in the CS-Hub note (August 2025), but the sentence carries footnote 22, which cites an APADEC humanitarian note of 19 March 2025; the situation is therefore sourced to March 2025, not August. The statement now says so.
claims.researcher_note: Goods blockade rather than a health-specific obstruction; the note does not mention medicines in this passage (recategorised displacement_humanitarian). Excerpt omits the sentence start 'Depuis que Minembwe ... n'ont plus accès aux biens essentiels' which is in the preceding sentence of the page.

claims.text: The UN Secretary-General reported that from mid-August 2026 intensified clashes between M23 and various factions of armed self-defence forces in Walikale and Masisi territories resulted in widespread violence and drove the displacement of 70,800 civilians, according to humanitarian reports.
claims.place_as_written: Walikale and Masisi territories, North Kivu
claims.verification_note: Matches page; the displacement figure is relayed from humanitarian reports, so graded B. ecoi.net copy is the UN's own PDF of S/2026/748 (job no. 26-13360, dated 21 September 2026), so verbatim; origin is the UN Secretary-General. The 70,800 figure is the SG citing unnamed humanitarian reports; the year comes from the report's period (20 June to 18 September 2026).
claims.researcher_note: Excerpt keeps the source's line-break hyphen ('self- defence'); verify.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that on 2 September 2025 Wazalendo militias set up roadblocks in Uvira, particularly along a major route to the Burundi border, and that for several days Wazalendo fighters intermittently prevented people from fleeing across the border, witnesses said; a border officer told HRW that the Wazalendo 'did not want to see people fleeing to Burundi'.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city and road to the Kavimvira/Gatumba border, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Both passages on the HRW page verbatim; HRW finding attributed. The end date 9 September is HRW's date for the shutdown of transport, trade and education; the border obstruction is dated only 'for several days'.
claims.researcher_note: Context: protest/general strike against General Gasita's deployment (existing claims). End date 9 September from HRW 'until September 9' for transport and trade shutdown; the border-crossing obstruction is 'for several days' only.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported (dateline Bujumbura, 23 January 2026) that a delegation of South Kivu provincial authorities led by the mayor of Uvira returned to Uvira from Bujumbura via the Gatumba–Kavimvira border crossing on a day the outlet gives as 'jeudi 23 janvier 2026'; that the Burundi-Congo border at Gatumba had remained closed since 10 December 2025, after the fall of Uvira to the M23; and that since the capture of Bukavu almost a year earlier a large part of the province's Congolese officials had resided in Bujumbura.
claims.place_as_written: Gatumba-Kavimvira border; Uvira city, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: South Kivu provincial authorities; Burundian authorities (border closure)
claims.verification_note: Fixed duplicated 'from Bujumbura'; quoted the weekday as printed; excerpt_en flags are ordinary translation of the French (RDC/Thursday/January). Date discrepancy: the outlet writes 'jeudi 23 janvier 2026', but 23 January 2026 was a Friday; Actualite.cd (existing) puts the mayor's return on Thursday 22 January. Dated as a range 22-23 January. The outlet also says the delegation crossed at Gatumba–Kavimvira while describing the Gatumba border as closed.
claims.researcher_note: Date conflict: the article says 'jeudi 23 janvier 2026' but 23 January 2026 is a Friday; Actualite.cd (existing r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-020) says the mayor returned on Thursday (22 Jan), and Congorassure says the governor returned Friday 23 January. Date given as a range. Single local source.

claims.text: Iwacu reported that, according to UNHCR, more than 84,000 people from South Kivu had crossed into Burundi since the beginning of December 2025, bringing the total of Congolese refugees and asylum seekers in Burundi to more than 200,000, and that UNHCR declared a level 2 emergency for Burundi needing USD 33 million.
claims.place_as_written: Gatumba-Kavimvira border and Bujumbura province, Burundi
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on the Iwacu page; '84 000'/'200 000' match 84,000/200,000 (number format only); excerpt_en is a faithful translation. Iwacu relays UNHCR; the date of the UNHCR figures is not given.
claims.researcher_note: Adds UNHCR figures to existing Iwacu 10 Dec claim. The UNHCR figure date is not stated by Iwacu (retrospective piece published 7 Jan 2026). Province coded South Kivu for the Uvira origin of the flow; the crossing is in Burundi.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition, dateline Bujumbura) reported that at a meeting in Bujumbura the UNHCR representative in Burundi, Brigitte Mkanga-Eno, expressed concern at the humanitarian funding shortfall: of the USD 33 million needed for emergency needs only USD 6 million had been raised so far, an amount she said was insufficient, especially for health services, sanitation and access to clean water.
claims.place_as_written: Bujumbura, Burundi (response to refugees from Uvira)
claims.verification_note: The 'insufficient ... health, sanitation, water' clause was not in the stored excerpt: supplied from the page. Translation checked. UNHCR remarks relayed by a single outlet.
claims.researcher_note: Single local source. Dateline 2 February 2026; page dated 6 February.

claims.text: Human Rights Watch reported that on 17 January 2026 Banyamulenge community leaders in Uvira held a meeting and said they had received instructions from the M23 that Banyamulenge people should leave with them or face reprisal attacks by Wazalendo groups, according to two community leaders and a community member.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on HRW page; account attributed to two community leaders and a community member via HRW.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates UN Group of Experts r1-GOE-007 from an independent NGO source. AFC/M23's own account of the withdrawal and of the Banyamulenge is in the HRW release's reference to a 15 January M23/AFC statement (not opened here).

claims.text: Human Rights Watch said it had reviewed credible information that Wazalendo militias prevented people from fleeing towards the Hauts Plateaux (highlands of Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories) after the M23 withdrawal from Uvira, and noted that these concerns were heightened by the continued closure of the border with Burundi.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city and Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on HRW page; HRW's finding attributed.
claims.researcher_note: HRW states 'credible information' without naming sources.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that Javid Abdelmoneim, international president of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), speaking before the UN Security Council on 12 December 2025, denounced the trivialisation of sexual violence by state and non-state armed groups in the armed conflicts in eastern DRC; the outlet identified these as AFC/M23, FDLR, ADF, Wazalendo and some FARDC elements.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23, FDLR, ADF, Wazalendo and some FARDC elements, as named by the MSF president
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. 'Commonplace among' replaced by the source's 'banalisation by' armed groups; list of groups attributed to the outlet; made clear it is not Uvira-specific. Eastern-DRC-wide statement, not specific to Uvira; the article only mentions Uvira's capture by AFC/M23 as context. The list of groups is Actualite.cd's wording, not a quoted MSF sentence. Same briefing as r1-SV-2025-024 (MSF's own text). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
claims.researcher_note: Context for Uvira (the article ties the briefing to the M23 capture of Uvira) but the statement itself concerns the whole east; province set to 'other'. The list of groups is Actualite.cd's wording of the briefing, not a verbatim MSF quote.

claims.text: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH), in its analysis for November 2025, stated that the Wazalendo also committed abuses in the context of internal clashes and interference in the administration of justice, notably in the city of Uvira.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; statement narrowed to the excerpt (ranking and province-wide figures are outside the stored excerpt and were removed from the statement and figures). The analysis gives no Uvira incidents, dates or victims.
