claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that telecommunication network services remained suspended in the town of Baraka, across Fizi territory and part of the Itombwe sector, a measure in force for more than a month and taken by the authorities for security reasons, notably after the taking of several villages including Point Zéro by AFC/M23; local civil society said even private Starlink connections were blocked.
claims.place_as_written: Baraka, Fizi territory and part of Itombwe sector (Mwenga), South Kivu
claims.verification_note: All clauses found on the page. The authority that ordered the suspension is not named. The Baraka/Fizi/Itombwe scope and the Starlink sentence are on the page but not in the stored excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: Which authority ordered the suspension is not stated.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that on Tuesday 30 June 2026 hundreds of residents of the Banyamulenge community demonstrated in Minembwe to protest against Congolese army drone attacks, which it said had intensified, and called for the withdrawal of Burundian troops present in the highlands of Fizi, Uvira and Mwenga.
claims.actor_as_written: Banyamulenge residents (protesters); Congolese army drone attacks and Burundian troops as alleged by protesters
claims.verification_note: Verified on page. The same page reports a drone attack on Minembwe hospital the previous week, which the AFC/M23 blamed on the Congolese army, and says the army had made no communication (not in this claim; a lead for health-care access).
claims.researcher_note: Minembwe was under Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 control per other KMP reporting of 15 June 2026; protest therefore took place in a de facto-held town.

claims.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué, the association Mahoro Peace Association (MPA) said 32 civilians were wounded during offensives by the Burundian and Congolese armies in the villages of Mikenge, Gakenke, Kalingi and Bidegu between 8 and 11 June 2026.
claims.place_as_written: Mikenge, Gakenke, Kalingi, Bidegu (Minembwe highlands), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian and Congolese armies, as alleged by Mahoro Peace Association
claims.verification_note: Verified on page; figure 32 exact. Association's account relayed by KMP; the article does not describe the association or give a separate confirmation. Perpetrators as alleged by the MPA.
claims.researcher_note: Advocacy association tied to the Banyamulenge community; treat as a party-aligned account. The same article is the only found text on this tally.

claims.text: Radio Maendeleo reported that more than 31 mille (31 thousand) people displaced from the hauts plateaux of Fizi, particularly Itombwe and neighbouring villages, were in the moyens plateaux, notably the Nundu health zone, Tanganyika sector, Fizi territory; its source said the latest clashes took place 'last Sunday' in the village of Rugezi, causing new waves of displacement.
claims.place_as_written: Rugezi (hauts plateaux); Nundu health zone, Tanganyika sector (Fizi territory), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed in the stored excerpts (the page names Wazalendo and an AFC/M23-Twirwaneho coalition as the parties to the earlier fighting)
claims.verification_note: Figure restored to printed form; the named official and the bush/shelter clause removed as not in the stored excerpts; actor narrowed. Excerpt gap: the page names the figures' source (the humanitarian-affairs official of Tanganyika sector, named on the page), says numbers rose 10-25 May 2025 after fighting between Wazalendo and a coalition the page lists as AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and a third group, and says some displaced live in the bush without shelter or food; none of this is in the stored excerpts, so it is left out of the statement and figures. 'Dimanche dernier' read as 8 June 2025 from the page date (12 Jun 2025); approximate.
claims.researcher_note: Page dated 2025-06-12; 'dimanche dernier' computed as 8 June 2025. Source for figures: Kalyata Antoine, head of humanitarian affairs for Tanganyika sector (as the page states). Complements r1-SKS-2025Q2-006 (Radio Okapi, 9 June).

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local testimony, that the evacuation order affecting villages of the Binza groupement (Rutshuru), mainly Nyabanira, Kasave and Makoka, was imposed by the M23. A Binza notable said the flight began on 12 July and intensified on Friday 25 July.
claims.place_as_written: Nyabanira, Kasave, Makoka, Binza groupement, Rutshuru
claims.actor_as_written: M23, as named by local testimony
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; page published ven 25/07/2025 16:55 (URL path says 26/07, the modification date). Added the FDLR-hunt clause and the 'ongoing armed operations' wording from the page; attribution kept to testimony/notable. Flight began 12 July per a local notable; 25 July is the date it intensified. The page also says, per the same notable, that the M23 launched a hunt for the FDLR in the area (not in the stored excerpt).
claims.researcher_note: Context for FIRE-041 (30-31 Jul, Busanga/Kabingu) and FIRE-009 (Kasave named among settlements, but cluster dates are Feb 2025, not July). The page says M23 launched a hunt for FDLR in the area. M23 account not found.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that a large fire killed two people and affected more than a hundred households in the night of Friday 14 to Saturday 15 August 2026 at Cimpwiji, in the village of Nyamyera, Mudusa grouping, Kabare territory; it said the fire started around 1 a.m. while most inhabitants were asleep. The article gives no cause and attributes it to no armed actor.
claims.place_as_written: Cimpwiji, Nyamyera village, Mudusa grouping, Kabare territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim on page and matches; the 'no cause / no armed actor' clause is a description of the article, checked against the full page text. Residential fire; the article gives no cause and names no armed actor. Context only. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Residential fire, not a bush or field fire and not attributed to any armed actor; recorded as context for the FIRE-207 review only. Mudusa is not among the gazetteer places near FIRE-207 (Miti, Mudaka), so the location match is not established.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant sources, that fighting reported over the previous seven days in a large part of the Hauts Plateaux of Kalehe territory compromised the resumption of classes after the Easter holidays, with schools closed, pupils displaced and teachers fleeing in several localities of the Ziralo grouping.
claims.place_as_written: Hauts Plateaux of Kalehe territory (Ziralo grouping), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: not attributed by the source (violences opposant des groupes armés)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt verbatim; statement faithful. Date range computed from 'ces 7 derniers jours' and the 17 April 2026 publication. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Range computed from 'these last 7 days' and the publication date 17 April 2026. Place is the Ziralo groupement generally; no village-level precision; nearness to FIRE-123 (Murangu, 22 April 2026) not established.

claims.text: A Council of the European Union draft implementing regulation (document 6582/25, 11 March 2025, marked LIMITE) proposed a statement of reasons describing Major-General Eugène Nkubito as Commander of the 3rd Division of the Rwanda Defence Force, deployed in eastern DRC and more specifically in North Kivu province, in that position since August 2022.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu (as described in the draft)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact; the PDF header gives only the 2025/… placeholder, confirming draft status. Statement says draft and attributes to the Council document. Corroborates r1-GOE-014 / r1-UC-RDF-008 (Group of Experts) and r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-010 (ACP), independent origins. Council pre-adoption text (number and date left blank, 'OJ: please insert the date of entry into force of this Regulation'); the adopted act's wording was not fetched and may differ. The 'Reasons' are the Council draft's statement of reasons, not an independent finding.
claims.researcher_note: This is the Council's pre-adoption draft text (the adopted act, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/509 of 17 March 2025, could not be fetched from EUR-Lex: see gaps), so the final wording may differ. Corroborates the tie already recorded from ACP/TRT Afrika (r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-010) and the Group of Experts (r1-GOE-014) and adds the stated tenure. The post 'since August 2022' predates the window; the deployment to North Kivu is the in-window fact.

claims.text: A Council of the European Union draft implementing regulation (document 6582/25, 11 March 2025, marked LIMITE) proposed a statement of reasons describing Pascal Muhizi as Brigadier-General of the Rwanda Defence Force since June 2021 and Commander of the 2nd Division of the RDF, deployed in Eastern DRC since August 2023.
claims.place_as_written: Eastern DRC (as described in the draft)
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; statement keeps the source's own construction for 'since August 2023'. Council pre-adoption text (number and date left blank, 'OJ: please insert the date of entry into force of this Regulation'); the adopted act's wording was not fetched and may differ. The 'Reasons' are the Council draft's statement of reasons, not an independent finding. The draft's wording leaves unclear whether 'since August 2023' dates the division's deployment or his command; it does not name a province. The Group of Experts (S/2026/466) places the RDF 3rd and 4th Divisions in the Kivus and does not mention a 2nd Division: discrepancy to check.
claims.researcher_note: Council pre-adoption draft text; adopted wording not fetched. Adds tenure to the tie recorded from ACP (r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-010). The draft does not say which Kivu the 2nd Division was in; the Group of Experts (S/2026/466 para 99) places the 3rd and 4th Divisions in North and South Kivu and does not mention a 2nd Division, so the 2nd Division's location in the Kivus is a discrepancy to check.

claims.text: A Council of the European Union draft implementing regulation (document 6582/25, 11 March 2025, marked LIMITE) proposed a statement of reasons describing Major-General Ruki Karusisi as the commander of the Special forces of the Rwanda Defence Force, deployed in eastern DRC.
claims.place_as_written: Eastern DRC (as described in the draft)
claims.actor_as_written: Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), Special Force Command
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact; attributed to the Council draft. Council pre-adoption text (number and date left blank, 'OJ: please insert the date of entry into force of this Regulation'); the adopted act's wording was not fetched and may differ. The 'Reasons' are the Council draft's statement of reasons, not an independent finding. The entry's identifying information reads 'Commander of the Special Force Command'; the Group of Experts (S/2026/466, r2-G-DOC-466-018) later calls him commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division, a later change of post.
claims.researcher_note: Council pre-adoption draft text; adopted wording not fetched. The header of the draft entry reads 'Commander of the Special Force Command of the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF)'. The Group of Experts (S/2026/466, via r2-G-DOC-466-018) later describes him as commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division and former Special Operations commander: a change of post to reconcile.

claims.text: Deutsche Welle reported that the special session of the State examinations for self-taught secondary candidates was held on Tuesday 25 March in the zones controlled by the M23 rebels in North and South Kivu, and described Chantal Murekatete as an M23 cadre and principal adviser to the provincial governor.
claims.place_as_written: M23-controlled zones of North Kivu and South Kivu (ceremony venue not stated in the excerpts)
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact on the retained page (byline Zanem Nety Zaidi, 25/03/2025). 'Presided over the ceremony' narrowed out as grammatically ambiguous. The excerpt_en flag on source 1 concerns only the translated words State/North/South (Etat/Nord/Sud), a faithful translation; no change needed. DW's sentence 'conseillère principale du gouverneur de province qui a présidé la cérémonie' can be read as either Murekatete or the governor having presided over the ceremony; the governor is not named. The page also says the official launch was carried out in Goma by the parallel administration installed by the rebels.
claims.researcher_note: Gives her post independently of the Group of Experts (S/2025/858: 'AFC/M23 focal point for humanitarian affairs'; S/2026/466: 'Special Adviser on Gender, Family and Children, Education, and Social and Humanitarian Affairs', both already recorded). Byline Zanem Nety Zaidi. The governor is not named in the excerpts (the Group of Experts and EU text name the AFC/M23-appointed North Kivu governor as Bahati Musanga / Bahati Erasto, but this page does not). Local-language search results also describe her as 'conseillère du gouverneur du Nord-Kivu' (Kivu Morning Post, Actualite.cd Facebook posts: snippets only, not fetched). Gazette du Continent and La Tempête pages carrying the same title could not be fetched.

claims.text: The Sentry listed Meya Sebagala (Mzee Mayor) among key ADF leaders present along Baluku at Madina camp, citing its interviews with military intelligence, civil society representatives and local researchers in eastern DRC in January 2026.
claims.place_as_written: Madina camp (Mambasa territory, Ituri per The Sentry)
claims.actor_as_written: ADF (Seka Baluku group), as The Sentry names it
claims.verification_note: Footnote text verified (p.~19). Location corrected: The Sentry says 'near the Ituri River', not 'Ituri' province; province stays 'other'. Outside the Phase 1 provinces (province 'other'). The Sentry spells 'Kasibante (Defender)'; Actualite.cd relays an FARDC claim that 'Difenda Kasibandi' was killed. No source here says they are the same person.
claims.researcher_note: Footnote text. Location is in Ituri (outside Phase 1 geography), recorded because the GoE (existing claims r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-007/-008) links Meya's unit to ADF mass-casualty attacks including in Lubero/Beni. The Sentry spells the second leader 'Kasibante (Defender)'; Actualite.cd on 2026-03-24 reports the army saying 'Difenda Kasibandi' was killed - this page does not say whether these are the same person; not inferred.

claims.text: Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC announced on Tuesday 24 March that Difenda Kasibandi, one of the leaders of the ADF, had been killed in a joint FARDC-UPDF operation at Asangwa, on the outskirts of the Lindi river, on the boundary between Lubero and Mambasa territories. In its own narration, the outlet said the operation targeted a group of Islamists led by ADF chief Abouakas.
claims.place_as_written: Asangwa, near the Lindi river, boundary of Lubero and Mambasa territories
claims.actor_as_written: ADF (group led by 'Abouakas'); FARDC-UPDF joint operation
claims.verification_note: Draft put the 'Abouakas' clause under the FARDC announcement; on the page it is the outlet's narration. Separated, and the death attributed to the army. Draft also gave territory Lubero alone, which the source does not say. The death is an FARDC claim, not an established fact. The page spells the name 'Kisibandi' once, and calls the ADF chief 'Abouakas' (elsewhere 'Abwakasi'). The operation date was not given; 24 March is the announcement date. The site is on the North Kivu/Ituri boundary.
claims.researcher_note: Army claim relayed by the outlet; no independent confirmation found. The article spells the ADF chief 'Abouakas' (elsewhere 'Abwakasi'); this page does not itself equate the two spellings in the excerpt. The page also spells the victim 'Kisibandi' once. Whether 'Difenda Kasibandi' is the 'Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender' named by the UN Group of Experts (existing claim r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-007) is not stated in the cited excerpts and is not inferred. The excerpt gives the announcement date, not the date of the operation (the article says the exact date of the hostages' release was not communicated).

claims.text: Tumaini Africa News reported that the 'self-proclaimed lieutenant general' Makanaki said, in the same press briefing at Uvira, that the incentive payment was a pleasant surprise and a real comfort for the Wazalendo.
claims.verification_note: Verified. Date precision changed to approximate, as for claim 8. The briefing context comes from the page paragraph before the excerpt.
claims.researcher_note: The page prints only 'Makanaki'; it does not give his first names, so identity with Makanaki Kasimbira John (other claims) is not stated by this source. Rank is self-proclaimed, as the outlet says.

claims.text: Radio Okapi reported that in April 2025 the national defence minister had announced at Uvira that the local Wazalendo fighters supporting the army in defending the city now depended exclusively on the national coordinator of the Réserve armée de défense (RAD), General Padiri Bulenda.
claims.actor_as_written: RAD national coordinator (General Padiri Bulenda); Wazalendo of Uvira
claims.verification_note: Verbatim. Same outlet as the existing April 2025 claim the researcher cites, so it is not independent; it adds Padiri Bulenda's rank and post. Retrospective (16 May 2026) on an April 2025 announcement; the minister is not named in the passage.
claims.researcher_note: Same outlet as existing claim r1-UV-2025Q2-006 (Radio Okapi, April 2025), so not an independent origin; it is a later retrospective that restates the tie and gives Bulenda's rank and post.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Twirwaneho group announced it controlled Minembwe and its surroundings and, for the first time, confirmed it had allied itself with AFC/M23, according to a person in Minembwe.
claims.place_as_written: Minembwe and surroundings, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact; translations faithful. Statement keeps the announcement as Twirwaneho's; it is not stated as BBC's own finding. The page adds that some reports said FARDC retook some positions in Tuesday's fighting, 'gusa nta ruhande rurayemeza' (no side has confirmed), and that 'Ibi leta ntacyo irabivugaho' (the government has said nothing on this). BBC's second excerpt: the army and government had not answered its questions.
claims.researcher_note: Kirundi-language BBC Gahuza page. Twirwaneho communique dated 'ku wa kabiri nijoro' (Tuesday night) = 25 February 2025 (computed from weekday and the 26 February publication date). Corroborates REC-0130 and REC-0132. Party statements: BBC reports FARDC and the government did not answer its questions at publication; a government statement on the Minembwe capture was not on this page.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that Twirwaneho took Point-Zéro on the morning of 16 January 2026, a day after taking other key points in Fizi territory including Baruta hill and shooting down a drone, and that Twirwaneho's leadership said the DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo and FDLR forces fled toward Mulima and Mutambala.
claims.place_as_written: Point-Zéro, Baruta hill and Isumo, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Twirwaneho (MRDP-Twirwaneho); the page names the opposing coalition as DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo and FDLR forces
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact on the retained copy (the live site refuses the fetch, HTTP 406); translations faithful. The statement already attributes the capture to the outlet and the flight claim to Twirwaneho's leadership. Partisan Rwandan outlet: the capture and the presence of FDLR are the outlet's and Twirwaneho's account (the page calls FDLR 'umutwe w'iterabwoba', a terrorist group). Byline Angeline Mukangenzi, 16 January 2026. The timing broadly agrees with BBC Gahuza (claim 0: capture known on Friday 16 January).
claims.researcher_note: Kinyarwanda-language Rwandan outlet (Umuryango.rw), which the project treats as state-aligned on contested facts; the capture, the flight of the other side and the FDLR presence are Twirwaneho's account relayed by the outlet. The FDLR attribution is the outlet's/Twirwaneho's wording only. Corroborates REC-0586 with a place-level detail (Baruta, Isumo, Mulima, Mutambala).

claims.text: Radio Publique Africaine (RPA, Burundi) reported that, according to a source among the refugees at Lusenda camp, some women were engaging in prostitution to feed their children amid famine in the camp.
claims.place_as_written: Lusenda refugee camp, Fizi territory, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Exact excerpt; the famine context is in the title and the page. Survival-related sexual exploitation context from one unnamed refugee source; not an allegation of rape. Page dated 18 July 2026. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: Reported by RPA from an unnamed refugee source; recorded as survival-related sexual exploitation context, not as an allegation of rape or of a named perpetrator. The same page says some boys join armed groups (Wazalendo) and girls marry early. Date is the page date.

claims.text: UN News Kiswahili reported that the OHCHR Fact-Finding Mission found a pattern of widespread sexual violence, especially rape and gang rape of women and girls, and looting by FARDC and Wazalendo members as they withdrew from the front line in January and February.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu and South Kivu front-line withdrawal areas (not specified in the excerpt)
claims.actor_as_written: FARDC and Wazalendo members, per OHCHR FFM report as relayed
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact and matches the statement. UN fact-finding report: A. The excerpt names no place; do not merge with REC-0253 (looting at Goma) without a source placing these acts at Goma. The page adds a quote that perpetrators acted 'in large groups and in many places at the same time'. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-GOMA claim 6)
claims.researcher_note: Relates to REC-0253 (looting by retreating FARDC/Wazalendo at Goma) but the excerpt does not name Goma; verifier should confirm whether the same events.

claims.text: DW Kiswahili reported that civilians and former government fighters were forcibly registered, and that M23 announced it had gained 7,000 new members by September.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date and 'in Goma', which the sentence does not state. The sentence names no place; the article is about Goma. September is 2025 by the article's chronology. The 7,000 figure is M23's; compare the 7,532 commandos AFC-M23 presented at Tchanzu on 8 February 2026 (claim 16), a different date and count.
claims.researcher_note: Brief line in a feature without attribution beyond M23's own announcement of the figure; the place of the forced registration is implied by the article (Goma) rather than stated in the sentence.

claims.text: DW Kiswahili reported that in October the group began appointing its own magistrates, but that observers said the rebels' court system was not fair.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date, which the excerpt does not print. DISCREPANCY (month): DW places the start of M23 magistrate appointments in October (2025 by the article's chronology), while REC-1195 records the integration of 378 magistrates on 3 November 2025. The observers are not named.
claims.researcher_note: Date 'October' as in the article's chronology (year 2025 implied); REC-1195 records the integration of 378 magistrates on 3 November 2025, so the dates differ in month. The unnamed 'observers' are not identified.

claims.text: BBC Gahuza reported that displacement camps on the outskirts of Goma, which had held hundreds of thousands of people, were bare ground after M23 fighters took the city; an independent journalist in Goma who visited the Kanyaruchinya and Lushagara camps said almost all the tents were down; it was not clearly known whether the remaining displaced people had gone home voluntarily or by force; and Dany Kalume of Goma civil society said many had returned to areas of Rutshuru and Masisi controlled by M23 and that M23 had provided vehicles the previous week to take back those remaining in some of the camps.
claims.place_as_written: Kanyaruchinya and Lushagara displacement camps, outskirts of Goma
claims.actor_as_written: M23, as BBC Gahuza and the civil society source describe
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact. Removed the publication date '3 February 2025', which no excerpt prints; added Kalume's Rutshuru/Masisi returns, which his excerpt states. BBC states it is unclear whether returns were voluntary or forced; do not present this as forced return. Aid groups cited on the page put the pre-fighting population of Kanyaruchinya and Lushagara at 300,000-400,000 (outside the excerpts).
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates REC-0282 (forced dismantling of IDP camps around Goma, January and February 2025) with a Kinyarwanda BBC source that explicitly says it is unclear whether the returns were voluntary. The figures of 300,000-400,000 are from aid groups cited in the same article (not excerpted).

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that on the morning of 22 December 2025 residents of Goma and neighbouring areas took part in a protest against AFC/M23's withdrawal from the city of Uvira, and that AFC/M23 fighters had left Uvira on 17 and 18 December after about a week there.
claims.verification_note: Excerpts exact (page dated Monday 22 Dec 2025). Statement matches. Rwandan outlet. The page quotes a placard rejecting the return of FARDC, Wazalendo, Burundian forces and mercenaries to Uvira, and says AFC/M23 withdrew at the request of the United States; relevant to the Uvira unit.
claims.researcher_note: Goma-side political event related to the Uvira withdrawal (Uvira is another unit's area). Rwandan outlet; whether the protest was organised is not stated in the excerpts.

claims.text: Igihe wrote that the HRW report also states that the Congolese army and those allied with it carried out acts of abuse, killing, rape and unlawful detention in the outskirts of Goma.
claims.actor_as_written: Congolese army and its allies (as Igihe summarises HRW)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p01; translation accurate ("guhohotera abantu" = mistreating/abusing people). Grade C: secondhand partisan paraphrase. Igihe's paraphrase of the 10 June 2026 HRW report, placed within its account of the Rwandan government statement (the English edition says the statement "cited passages in the report"). Incident dates not given; check against the HRW report itself.
claims.researcher_note: This is Igihe's own summary of what the 10 June 2026 HRW report says; the incident dates are not stated by Igihe (date given is the report publication date). To be checked against the HRW report itself. Included because it concerns sexual violence alleged against FARDC and allies.

claims.text: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 also accused the DRC government forces of attacks in areas of Walungu territory in South Kivu, including Nzibira, Kishadu and Chulwe, and in Katoyi in Masisi territory.
claims.actor_as_written: DRC government forces (as alleged by AFC/M23)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p04; translation accurate. AFC/M23 allegation relayed by Igihe.
claims.researcher_note: Party allegation relayed by Igihe. Existing record REC-1265 covers displacement from Nzibira after fighting in Walungu (20-27 Aug).

claims.text: Igihe, citing the SOS Médias website of the Burundians, reported that the Kamenge military hospital alone was housing 87 wounded Burundian soldiers.
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian soldiers wounded in fighting with AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Statement verbatim-supported on p05; figures field narrowed to the 87 Igihe prints (the "100" came from SOS, not this excerpt). Relay of SOS Médias Burundi (8 Dec 2025, recorded separately); not independent of it.
claims.researcher_note: Relays SOS Médias Burundi (original article of 8 Dec 2025 cited in E-IGIHE-a-033). Related earlier claim for Jan 2025: r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-006.

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, in recent days, more than a hundred wounded had been reported, 87 of them admitted to the Kamenge military hospital, north of Bujumbura, and that Burundian authorities were keeping silent about the real losses.
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian soldiers wounded in fighting with M23/AFC
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on retained SOS page (Adam Ntwari, 8 Dec 2025). Figures field rewritten in the source's words: the page prints "centaine", not "100". SOS Médias Burundi is an exile Burundian outlet critical of the Burundian government; no official Burundian figure was given.
claims.researcher_note: Original reporting by SOS Médias Burundi's own reporters at the hospital (independent of Igihe).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, quoting a journalist at the Kamenge military hospital, that lack of beds forced some patients to share the same bed and that 'a single bed can accommodate up to three patients' because the two emergency wards were full.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on retained SOS page. Patients are wounded soldiers, not civilians.
claims.researcher_note: Hospital overcrowding affecting wounded Burundian soldiers in Bujumbura (hospital capacity); patients are military, not civilians, so not recorded as civilian access to health care.

claims.text: Igihe reported that other wounded had been sent to other hospitals including Tanganyika Care Polyclinic, and that many Bujumbura hospitals were severely overcrowded, with up to three patients on one bed.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p05; translation accurate. SOS Médias (the apparent origin) reports the bed-sharing at Kamenge's two emergency wards only; Igihe generalises it to many Bujumbura hospitals.
claims.researcher_note: Igihe, partly relaying SOS Médias Burundi (SOS names Tanganyika Care Polyclinic and up to three patients per bed).

claims.text: Igihe reported that the Burundian army sent many soldiers to the border to receive those fleeing, to keep calm, and that those coming from the DRC were being disarmed before continuing to where they were lodged.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p05; translation accurate.
claims.researcher_note: Single partisan source.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Lt Col Minani was formerly of the old Burundian army (Ex FAB) and had been promoted to the rank of Lieutenant Colonel in July of the year of writing.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p06. "This year" = 2025 per the article date (6 Dec 2025).
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates the Congovirtuel detail (former FAB officer). 'This year' = 2025 (article dated 6 Dec 2025).

claims.text: Igihe described TAFOC as the Burundian bilateral contingent in the DRC, which began operations in South Kivu in 2022 alongside Congolese forces against armed groups including RED Tabara, FOREBU, FNL and Twirwaneho.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p08. Igihe background used only to identify the TAFOC unit; the 2022 start is before the edition window.
claims.researcher_note: Background on a unit name (TAFOC) used by Burundian forces in the DRC; start in 2022 is outside the edition window, so the claim is dated to the Igihe article and used only to identify the unit. Minani is described by Nininahazwe as a TAFOC battalion commander (E-IGIHE-a-042).

claims.text: Igihe reported that the group had recruited 7,437 new fighters who had undergone six months of military training at the Rumangabo base in North Kivu, including former FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo members who joined M23 after the capture of Goma and Bukavu.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p11. Igihe narration; the figure matches the 7,437 recruits AFC/M23 publicised in September 2025. The composition of the recruits is Igihe's claim.
claims.researcher_note: Corroborates the figure of 7,437 'commandos' whose pass-out AFC/M23 publicised on 14 September 2025 (UN Group of Experts, r1-UC-M23-018, REC-0311). The claim that former FARDC and Wazalendo joined is Igihe's.

claims.text: Igihe reported that the Congolese government and the M23 were to begin direct talks on 9 April 2025 in Doha, Qatar, the first direct negotiation between the two parties since the rebels took two provincial capitals.
claims.actor_as_written: Government of the DRC; M23; Qatar (mediator)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p12. Forward-looking (published 4 April 2025); not confirmation the talks began that day.
claims.researcher_note: Forward-looking report (published 4 April 2025), not confirmation that the talks took place on that day.

claims.text: Igihe reported that a meeting initially planned in Angola on 18 March was abruptly cancelled after M23 withdrew in protest against European Union sanctions on its leaders, and that diplomatic efforts resumed after an unexpected mid-March meeting between Presidents Félix Tshisekedi and Paul Kagame in Doha.
claims.actor_as_written: M23; Angola; Qatar; Presidents Tshisekedi and Kagame
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p12; removed the year "2025" from the statement because the excerpt does not print it (date field keeps 2025-03-18). Igihe background on mediation (article of 4 April 2025; the year is the article's).
claims.researcher_note: Background reported by Igihe on mediation; no Kivu location. Statement-level context only.

claims.text: Igihe reported that, in the same reshuffle, Katembo Isevisya, who had been in the Lubero territory leadership, and Radjabu Kwizera Elie were given deputy burgomaster posts, Radjabu Kwizera Elie as deputy burgomaster of Karisimbi commune.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p13; statement does not go beyond the text. The source sentence is garbled ("Komite yahawe Burugumesitiri wungirije", probably a typo for a commune); which commune Katembo Isevisya serves is not clear from Igihe.
claims.researcher_note: The Kinyarwanda sentence is garbled in the source ('Komite yahawe Burugumesitiri wungirije'); translated literally. KMP (r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-010) says Katembo Isevisya became deputy bourgmestre.

claims.text: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 delegates returned to the Doha talks on 12 December, but the DRC government refused to send its delegates there, complaining that the alliance's fighters had taken Uvira city on 9 December.
claims.verification_note: Removed the year from the statement because the excerpt prints only day and month (the date field keeps the year from the 26 Dec 2025 article). Igihe puts the taking of Uvira on 9 December; other sources give 10 December (night of 9-10). No DRC government statement checked.
claims.researcher_note: Igihe puts the taking of Uvira on 9 December; UN Group of Experts and others say 10 December (REC-0113; SOS Médias: night of 9 to 10 December). No DRC government statement found by this agent.

claims.text: Igihe reported that Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, President of the Council of Ministers of Togo and the mediator appointed by the African Union, made a visit of a few hours to Kinshasa on 22 December to discuss the war in eastern DRC.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim on p16; translation accurate. Mediator activity; Igihe report.
claims.researcher_note: Mediator activity; context only.

claims.text: Igihe reported that the DRC government and AFC/M23 had agreed that the work of an international body to monitor compliance with the ceasefire in North Kivu and South Kivu would start soon, and that the agreement launching the body's activities was signed in Switzerland on 14 April.
claims.place_as_written: Switzerland (talks); body covers North Kivu and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Supported verbatim, but sole source is partisan_rwanda: grade lowered B to C per the rule for Igihe without an independent origin on the claim itself. Single partisan (Rwandan state-aligned) source on this claim; other project records (UN Group of Experts, joint statement) cover the Switzerland talks but are not cited here. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 115)
claims.researcher_note: Independently documented elsewhere in the project: the UN Group of Experts places the Doha-process talks in Montreux between 13 and 17 April 2026 (claim r2-G-DOC-466-046) and a joint statement of 19 April exists (r1-ST-MED-2026-008); neither is linked to a record. Igihe is cited only for the 14 April signing date and the 'monitoring body starts soon' wording.

claims.text: Igihe reported that once the Minembwe-area positions were taken, senior AFC/M23 leaders visited them, including Bisimwa, Dr. Freddy Kaniki (in charge of economy and finance in the alliance and President of MRDP Twirwaneho) and Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu (Deputy Commander-in-Chief of M23); it also states that 8 July was a day of songs of thanks for the residents of Minembwe.
claims.verification_note: Full first name 'Bertand' is not in either excerpt; narrowed to 'Bisimwa'. Otherwise verbatim. Roles as Igihe prints them. The visit date is not stated; 8 July is the date of the celebration. Photo captions also place Lawrence Kanyuka and 'PC Mavugo' of MRDP-Twirwaneho in Minembwe and Byamungu at Point-Zéro. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 119)
claims.researcher_note: Roles as Igihe prints them. The visit date is not given precisely; 8 July is the date of the celebration. Photo captions on the page also place Kanyuka and 'PC Mavugo' of MRDP-Twirwaneho in Minembwe.

claims.text: Igihe quoted Governor Bahati as saying FDLR members are thieves who spend their days deceiving residents, robbing them and raping women and girls. No date, place, victim or incident is given.
claims.place_as_written: Binza groupement, Rutshuru territory (North Kivu), general allegation
claims.actor_as_written: Allegation by AFC/M23 governor against FDLR
claims.verification_note: 'AFC/M23' (flagged 23) is not in the excerpt; moved the affiliation to the note. 'Gusambanya ku gahato' = rape (force). Generalised accusation by an AFC/M23-appointed governor (identified at the top of the article), relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; a lead only, no incident, victim or date.
claims.researcher_note: Generalised accusation by a party official; a lead only. 'Gusambanya ku gahato' translated as 'to rape by force'. No incident, victim count or date. Not an established finding.

claims.text: Igihe quoted governor Bahati as saying, of the FDLR ('those bandits'), that what they can do is ambush vehicles, loot, and kill those inside; the passage gives no date, place or incident.
claims.actor_as_written: Allegation by AFC/M23 governor against FDLR
claims.verification_note: Speaker is clear: 'Ati' directly follows 'Guverineri Bahati yavuze...'. Replacement quote spans the two contiguous sentences so the name is printed; AFC/M23 moved out of the statement (flagged 23). Generalised accusation by an AFC/M23-appointed governor relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; no incident.
claims.researcher_note: The speaker is Governor Bahati by context (the preceding sentences of the article); the 'Ati' attribution carries over. Generalised accusation, no incident.

claims.text: Igihe reported, citing a UN report it does not name, that FDLR fighters captured and repatriated to Rwanda since AFC/M23 took Goma in January 2025 are far more numerous than those who returned while the DRC government controlled the area.
claims.place_as_written: Areas under AFC/M23 control in North Kivu; Rwanda
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; attribution to an unnamed UN report kept as Igihe's claim. Igihe cites an unnamed, undated UN report; check against the UN Group of Experts reports before use. No figure given.
claims.researcher_note: The UN report is not named or dated; the claim should be checked against the Group of Experts reports before use. No figure given.

claims.text: Igihe reported that the UN had recently imposed sanctions on AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa, on Col Nzenze Imani, described as in charge of intelligence and military operations in the alliance, and on Brig Gen Charles Sematama, who leads Twirwaneho in Minembwe commune; Igihe wrote that Sematama was sanctioned for leading a group accused of "killing civilians, recruiting children into the army and engaging in activities that disturb the peace and security of the population."
claims.place_as_written: UN Security Council (listing); persons active in North and South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: UN Security Council (as Igihe names it); Corneille Nangaa; Col Nzenze Imani; Brig Gen Charles Sematama
claims.verification_note: Sole source is Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; grade lowered B to C (the independent UN-listing claims are separate). Statement extended with source 1, which the original did not use. Igihe's name order 'Col Nzenze Imani' differs from OFAC's 'John Imani Nzenze' in other project claims. The listing grounds are Igihe's Kinyarwanda rendering of the UN text, not the UN text itself. The page adds that the Security Council was presided by the DRC from July 2026.
claims.researcher_note: The listing is independently documented in existing claims (r1-UC-M23-033, -035 7sur7.cd citing a UN communiqué of 14 July 2026; r4-G-LOCAL/SECO r4-G-CMD-LEGAL-001); none is linked to a record. Igihe's wording 'Col Nzenze Imani' differs from OFAC's 'John Imani Nzenze' (r1-UC-M23-004). The quoted grounds for Sematama are Igihe's rendering, in Kinyarwanda, of the UN listing grounds.

claims.text: Igihe reported that from 16 February 2025 M23 fighters began searching for armed people still hiding in Bukavu and confronting soldiers who had fled to the south-east of the city.
claims.verification_note: Verbatim; 'from that day' refers to 16 February in the preceding sentence. Igihe's own voice; no detentions or abuses mentioned on this page.
claims.researcher_note: Describes search operations in Bukavu; no detentions or abuses mentioned in this passage.

claims.text: Igihe reported that in most of the areas AFC/M23 had already 'liberated' it had put its new leaders, who it said were committed to security and development of residents.
claims.place_as_written: Areas held by AFC/M23 in North and South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Verbatim. Igihe's own assertion; 'liberated' is Igihe's word for AFC/M23-held areas. No names.
claims.researcher_note: Igihe's own assertion on AFC/M23 administration; no names. The AFC/M23 South Kivu appointments of 28 February 2025 are in REC-0802.

claims.text: Igihe reported that on 2 March 2026 the United States imposed sanctions on the Rwandan army and its officials, accusing them of violating the Washington peace agreement.
claims.verification_note: Sole source is Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; grade lowered B to C. Statement verbatim. Igihe's own voice; the 2 March 2026 US sanctions on the RDF are documented independently (US Treasury) in another project claim, not cited here.
claims.researcher_note: Independently documented: US Treasury (OFAC) announcement of 2 March 2026 sanctioning the RDF and four senior officials (claim r1-POL-2026-001, no record linked). Igihe is cited only as a Rwandan outlet's confirmation.

claims.text: Igihe reported that the office of the government-appointed South Kivu governor, Jean-Jacques Purusi, relocated to Uvira in February 2025 once AFC/M23 had taken Bukavu.
claims.actor_as_written: South Kivu provincial government (Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi)
claims.verification_note: Verbatim. Igihe's own voice; the year is the article's context (published 7 July 2025). Actualite.cd's page also says Uvira became the provincial capital after AFC/M23 took Bukavu, and Radio Okapi documents the move in another project claim.
claims.researcher_note: Independently documented by Radio Okapi (24 Feb 2025, communication cell of the governor, REC-0064).

claims.text: Mwananchi (Tanzania) reported, citing DRC media and a statement signed by the Wazalendo leader Shukuru Bulenda, that the defecting groups were Mai-Mai Kabidon (FPP-AP), part of Mai-Mai Kifuafua and the Nduma Defense of Congo-Renovated (NDC-R/M) group, who were said to have joined AFC/M23 on 9 March 2025.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu (Lubero territory, per record REC-0981)
claims.actor_as_written: Mai-Mai Kabidon (FPP-AP); part of Mai-Mai Kifuafua; NDC-R/M; AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Excerpt matches the page (dated 11 March 2025); 'vinadaiwa' (alleged) preserved as 'said to have joined'; 'juzi' gives 9 March, matching the date printed.
claims.researcher_note: Tanzanian outlet relaying DRC media (the page itself cites Kivu Morning Post and Actualite.cd elsewhere); 'juzi' = the day before yesterday relative to the page date, Tuesday 11 March 2025. Names the signatory of the defection statement and the three groups. The statement was reported as 'said to have joined', not confirmed by the page.

claims.text: UN News Kiswahili reported, citing OCHA, that violence increased on 2 May in the Lubero area, forcing about 30,000 people to flee their homes.
claims.verification_note: Matches the page (dated 7 May 2025). The parties are not named in the sentence; actor correctly left unattributed.
claims.researcher_note: Gives the displacement figure for the 2 May 2025 fighting around Lunyasenge (REC-1246). The excerpt itself does not name the fighting parties; the page's wider context is the M23/FARDC conflict and WFP aid via Beni. The article also reports WFP intends to use relief supplies stored in warehouses in Beni to assist about 140,000 people in the Lubero area.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 authorities in eastern DRC said more than 200 people had died after a mine collapsed in the mineral-rich town of Rubaya.
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Removed the 226 figure from 'figures' (no excerpt prints it). BBC page 'Yatangajwe 31 Ukwa mbere 2026' confirmed. REC-0685 gives at least 226 (confirmed by the AFC/M23-appointed governorate); BBC's 'more than 200' comes from the same party, so it is not an independent count.
claims.researcher_note: BBC Gahuza (Kinyarwanda edition; published 31 Ukwa mbere 2026, updated 1 Ukwa kabiri). Known record REC-0685 gives at least 226 (Actualite.cd); this source says more than 200 per M23 authorities.

claims.text: Mwananchi (Tanzania) reported that, according to media in the DRC and a statement signed by the Wazalendo leader Shukuru Bulenda, the groups that defected included Mai-Mai Kabidon (FPP-AP), part of Mai-Mai Kifuafua and the Nduma Defense of Congo-Renovated (NDC-R/M), and that these groups were alleged to have joined AFC/M23 on March 9, 2025.
claims.place_as_written: North Kivu (location not stated in the excerpt)
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo groups (FPP-AP, Mai-Mai Kifuafua part, NDC-R/M) allegedly joining AFC/M23
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Different group and date from REC-0387 (FCR, 7 March 2025): new_related_event kept. The Mwananchi sentence is garbled; it is unclear whether Bulenda's statement announced the defection or listed the groups. The hedge 'vinadaiwa' (alleged) is kept.
claims.researcher_note: Related to REC-0387 (FCR allegiance to AFC/M23, 7 March 2025, different group named); Mwananchi names other groups and the date 9 March. Secondhand; other Wazalendo groups could have denied. No denial searched here.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that on Thursday the areas of the Nyamaboko 1 groupements in Masisi 'became the hotbed of terrifying fighting', according to Voltaire Batundi, head of Masisi civil society, and that the fighting, which began in the morning and lasted almost all day, made thousands of people leave their homes and flee.
claims.actor_as_written: M23 vs FARDC and Wazalendo (fighting); no perpetrator for displacement
claims.verification_note: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page 'Yatangajwe 14 Ukw'icumi na rimwe 2025' (Friday) confirmed; Thursday = 13 November 2025, between REC-0455 (12 Nov) and REC-0456 (15 Nov).
claims.researcher_note: BBC Gahuza page "Yatangajwe 14 Ukw'icumi na rimwe 2025" (14 November 2025). Weekday only ("ku wa kane"); date computed from weekday and publication date (Thursday 13 November 2025). Neighbouring known records: REC-0455 (12 Nov), REC-0456 (15 Nov). Toll "thousands" is civil society's figure.

claims.text: DW Kiswahili (Mitima DeLachance) reported that hundreds of Catholic women marched in South Kivu on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, representing 44 parishes of the Bukavu archdiocese, and that the march was held at the Olame centre because public demonstrations had been banned by the new authorities of Bukavu city.
claims.actor_as_written: new authorities of Bukavu city (AFC/M23 administration, as the source implies)
claims.verification_note: All passages on the DW Kiswahili page (byline Mitima DeLachance, 25 Nov 2025). The page does not name who issued the ban or when.
claims.researcher_note: Reports a ban on public demonstrations by 'watawala wapya' (new rulers) of Bukavu; the page does not name the ban's issuer or date. The march was about sexual violence used as a weapon of war and digital harassment.

claims.text: DW Kiswahili reported that local civil society organisations spoke of the deaths of at least seven people, including five civilians, and of wounded people being treated at Kavumu health facilities, after Wazalendo tried for a few minutes to take Kavumu airport before M23 forces drove them out.
claims.verification_note: Statement supported (DW Kiswahili, 14 April 2025). Date corrected: this page does not date the Kavumu attack (13 April came from REC-0812, not from this source); the claim is dated by its report.
claims.researcher_note: Adds a toll to REC-0812 (Wazalendo temporarily retake Kavumu airport, 13 April 2025): civil society sources cited by DW say at least 7 dead including 5 civilians. Date: the article is dated 14 April 2025 and describes calm after the violence; the incident date is taken from REC-0812, not from this page.

claims.text: Umuseke reported that on arriving at Idjwi AFC/M23 first gave a broadcast on the island's radio, Obuguma, before meeting residents, and that Mustapha Maomboleo, head of Idjwi territory, said the broadcast was meant to reassure the island's residents.
claims.verification_note: Passage on the page (Umuseke, 13 March 2025). The page does not say whether the territory head was a state or AFC/M23 appointee.
claims.researcher_note: Spelling 'Mustapha Maomboleo' as printed by Umuseke; BBC Swahili (5 March 2025) prints the same administrator as 'Mustafa Mamboleo'. Whether he was an AFC/M23 appointee or the previous state administrator is not stated by the page. Date is the page date.

claims.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that fighting that began on Tuesday and grew on Wednesday made residents flee in various directions, including to islands in Lake Kivu and the large island of Idjwi, and others south towards Bukavu, according to a Kalehe civil-society member who told BBC.
claims.place_as_written: Kalehe territory (to Idjwi, lake islands and Bukavu)
claims.verification_note: Passage on the page (BBC News Gahuza, 13 Feb 2025). Raised to B: BBC's own source, non-partisan, not contested.
claims.researcher_note: Dates computed from weekdays and the publication date (13 Feb 2025). No numbers given. Adds a flight route (to Idjwi) not in known_records.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that Wazalendo fighters attacked Kavumu in Kabare territory on the morning of Sunday 13 April, that videos on social media showed fighters with DRC flags in Kavumu centre heading for the airport that M23 had taken two months earlier, and that, according to information, after a short fight M23 retook all of Kavumu; it added that information reaching BWIZA said many Wazalendo were killed, including the leader of the attack.
claims.verification_note: Supported (Umuryango.rw, byline ISHIMWE Jean de Dieu, 14 April 2025; retained copy). Only the stray trailing comma removed and the retaking attributed to 'information' as printed ('Amakuru avuga'). The Wazalendo losses rest on BWIZA's unnamed information; DW's civil-society toll (claim 18) is different. Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says.
claims.researcher_note: M23-side account relayed by a Rwanda-based outlet that credits BWIZA; losses to Wazalendo are not independently confirmed here. Complements REC-0812 (Wazalendo temporarily retake Kavumu airport, 13 Apr 2025) and the DW Kiswahili claim (at least seven dead including five civilians, per civil society). The page also says many others were captured by M23 (not cited here: the sentence is garbled). The page is dated Monday 14 April 2025.

claims.text: Umuryango.rw reported that fighting at Nyangezi and Lurhala in Walungu territory began on 17 June 2025 and that, according to information from Nyangezi, about 45 km from Bukavu, many residents fled the trading centre on the morning of 18 June; it quoted a resident as saying the fighting started the day before and reached Weza.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23; Wazalendo (the article frames the fighting as between them)
claims.verification_note: Passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, byline ISIMBI Estella, 19 June 2025; retained copy). Unnamed sources. 2026-10-29: source 1 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
claims.researcher_note: No Nyangezi record for June 2025 in known_records (REC-0482 is Nyangezi, about 18 April 2025). Rwanda-based outlet; sources are unnamed 'information from the area' and a resident quote. No casualty figure.

claims.text: Deutsche Welle Kiswahili reported that in the evening FARDC soldiers removed several Banyamulenge families who feared for their safety in Uvira and took them to a safe place.
claims.verification_note: Excerpt on page and supports the statement. Regraded C to B: DW is a credible non-partisan outlet, as in claim 2 from the same article. Day is inferred from sequence, so the date is approximate. DW does not say on which day ('in the evening' follows the account of the Sunday 18 January return) or where the families were taken.
claims.researcher_note: Single media source; day computed from the article's sequence (Sunday return of Wazalendo/FARDC, 'in the evening'). The destination is not given.

claims.text: Analysons Kongo reported (dateline Uvira, 17 September 2026), citing The Great Lakes Eye, which cited an anonymous Burundian colonel, that twelve Burundian soldiers were allegedly killed by their own comrades after trying to leave their positions on the Bijombo front, in the night of 10 September at Kiliba Haut, Kagando groupement, Uvira territory; it said the FDNB had issued no communiqué confirming or denying the information.
claims.place_as_written: Kiliba Haut, Kagando groupement, Uvira territory (Bijombo front)
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian soldiers (FDNB), allegedly killed by their own comrades
claims.verification_note: All three passages on the page; the conditional (auraient, se seraient) is kept as 'allegedly'. Unconfirmed: one anonymous source, relayed twice; the outlet itself writes 'si elle était confirmée'.
claims.researcher_note: Single anonymous source relayed twice; unconfirmed, the outlet itself calls it unconfirmed ('si elle était confirmée'). Swahili-language posts on Instagram/Facebook repeat it but are not citable. The original The Great Lakes Eye article was not located. French source used because no Kirundi/Swahili/Kinyarwanda web page carrying the text was fetchable; flagged for a Burundian official statement (FDNB: none found).

claims.text: Bwiza (a Rwandan outlet) reported that the DRC government had cut internet in the town of Uvira a few days after its forces returned, and that the DRC government had said nothing on the matter, while reports said President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi gave the order.
claims.place_as_written: Uvira city and surroundings, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Supported and attributed. Single Rwandan outlet; the Tshisekedi order rests on unnamed 'reports'. No independent confirmation of the shutdown.
claims.researcher_note: Single Rwandan outlet, partisan on this; no Kinshasa statement found in the page. Not yet corroborated by an independent source in this search (searched: 'internet Uvira' in the edition returned nothing). A telecom shutdown affects health-care access and reporting but the page does not say so.

claims.text: Bwiza reported that the UN Group of Experts on Congo report said the assault on Uvira was led directly by AFC/M23 military leaders Gen. Sultani Makenga and Bernard Byamungu, and that Gen (Rtd) James Kabarebe, former Rwandan army chief of staff, 'played a major role in coordinating' the operation.
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (Makenga, Byamungu); James Kabarebe (Rwanda), as named by the UN Group of Experts
claims.verification_note: Supported; relay of the UN GoE, not independent of the existing GoE claim. Kept at B because the report itself was not opened. Relay of a UN Group of Experts report (not seen directly); same origin as the existing claim carrying the report.
claims.researcher_note: Relay by a Rwandan outlet of a UN Group of Experts report; the existing claim r1-UC-M23-001 (Actualite.cd) carries the same. Bwiza also notes (not cited) that Rwanda's foreign ministry rejected the US OFAC sanctions on Kabarebe as baseless. The page is dated 1 July 2026, the date of the article not of the report.

claims.text: UNE.CD reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi returned on Friday 23 January 2026 to Uvira, the provisional seat of provincial institutions, after the withdrawal of the AFC-M23; it said he, his provincial government and other officials had fallen back to Fizi-Baraka after the fall of Uvira on 10 December 2025. Kivutimes, reporting the same arrival, said instead that the provincial authority had been forced to flee to Bujumbura, in Burundi.
claims.verification_note: All excerpts exact; 23 January 2026 was a Friday. The original statement rested only on UNE.CD while citing Kivutimes; corrected to say which clause rests on which outlet and to surface the Fizi-Baraka/Bujumbura discrepancy. B: two local outlets agree on the date of arrival, disagree on the earlier whereabouts. Discrepancy: UNE.CD says the provincial authorities fell back to Fizi-Baraka; Kivutimes says they fled to Bujumbura (Kivutimes also says the governor returned to Bujumbura the same afternoon). Both date the arrival to Friday 23 January 2026. 2026-10-29: source 2 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-DRC claim 6)
claims.researcher_note: D-021: both outlets give 23 January 2026 for the governor's return. They differ on where the authorities had gone: UNE.CD says Fizi-Baraka; Kivutimes says the provincial authority fled to Bujumbura. Kivutimes also reports the governor visited the Kalundu port 'après les actes de pillages qui ont été perpétrés par les rebelles avant le retrait' (outlet narration, not a governor statement) and later returned to Bujumbura the same afternoon (relevant to D-020, who looted Uvira).

claims.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, according to concordant testimonies, Burundian soldiers posted at Mikalati intercepted several groups of women, men and young people from Minembwe who were trying to reach the Bijombo market to buy basic goods such as salt, sugar or soap. The outlet also wrote that an FDNB spokesperson was not available to answer these allegations and that in most cases the Burundian authorities have denied accusations of mistreating Banyamulenge.
claims.place_as_written: Mikalati, Bijombo groupement (Fizi territory), South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: Burundian soldiers (FDNB) posted at Mikalati, per witnesses
claims.verification_note: Page read in full (byline Adam Ntwari, dateline Bukavu). All clauses placed; the Minembwe/Bijombo clause rests on the page's lead paragraph (excerpt gap noted) plus source 2. Names printed as the page prints them. Single outlet relying on witnesses: C. Timing per the outlet: 'le week-end dernier' before 20 October 2025. The 'denied in most cases' sentence is the outlet's general statement, not a denial of this incident. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration) 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 3 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
claims.researcher_note: Earlier episode than the 6 December 2025 Mikalati attack (r1-UC-BI-FDLR-031..033) and the November 2025 FDNB statement on road blocking (r1-ST-BI-005). The Burundian reaction found: spokesperson 'not available' for this article; the 'denied in most cases' sentence is the outlet's general statement, not a quoted denial and not tied to this incident. The names are first names/initials of quoted residents as printed. Access to food (and, per the outlet, to care) in the Hauts Plateaux; no health-facility event in this item. Answers part of target r1/HC-SK-2025#2.

claims.place_as_written: Eastern DRC (as stated in the act)
claims.verification_note: Verified against the retained Official Journal text (pages.py import, saved_text; the live helper fetch failed because the Publications Office serves the act only on an XHTML Accept header).
