claims.text: The New Humanitarian reported that a civil society activist in Uvira said that for three months the state was completely absent in the city, that there were abuses, and that people were whipped, arrested and some died in detention; the article ties this to a militia-led policing force that residents said carried out arbitrary arrests.
claims.actor_as_written: Wazalendo (pro-government militias), as described by residents to The New Humanitarian
claims.verification_note: Retained user copy (fetch_failed for the script) prints the passage verbatim; replacement quote extended to include the residents' account of a militia-led policing force. Single anonymous testimony: C. Anonymous civil society activist; the quote itself does not name who whipped or arrested people. No dates, places or names of detainees.
claims.researcher_note: Anonymous civil society activist; no dates or names of detainees. Article says more than a dozen Uvira residents spoke to the outlet. Independent context: HRW 15 Sep 2025 on Wazalendo and army threats to civilians in Uvira (already cited elsewhere).

claims.text: The New Humanitarian reported that the Congolese army carried out raids in search of alleged M23 collaborators, mainly in hotels across Uvira, and that these operations led to arbitrary arrests and contributed to a climate of fear, particularly among Banyamulenge.
claims.actor_as_written: Congolese army (FARDC), as stated by the outlet
claims.verification_note: Retained user copy prints the passage verbatim. Credible non-partisan outlet's own reporting: B. Outlet's own characterisation; no dates, numbers or names.
claims.researcher_note: Outlet's own characterisation; no dates, numbers or names.

claims.text: 7sur7.cd reported that on 20 February the cemetery of Musigiko, in Kabare territory, South Kivu, was the burial place of 18 people who died in the fighting during the M23's capture of Bukavu, their bodies placed in body bags and laid in a mass grave in Bukavu; it said John Kashinzwe, Red Cross provincial secretary in South Kivu, specified the remains had been recovered from various places in the city, and that the Red Cross with the ICRC had earlier announced collecting 26 bodies.
claims.place_as_written: Musigiko cemetery, Kabare territory, and Bukavu, South Kivu
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts on the page; statement matches; the '7' flag is from the outlet name 7sur7.cd. The page places the cemetery in Kabare territory but the grave 'à Bukavu'. It does not identify who killed the 18 or whether they were civilians or combatants.
claims.researcher_note: Cluster Q-10 (existing REC-0793/0794: children killed 16 Feb, executions). The page has a minor internal inconsistency (cemetery in Kabare territory, grave 'à Bukavu'). This claim adds the burial and Red Cross collection figures; it does not link the 18 dead to the six children or to any perpetrator.

claims.text: Enquete.cd reported that, according to testimonies gathered on site, several residents of the Buliriko quarter of Kavumu, in Kabare territory, left their homes for Buhandahanda and Nzinzi, and that families said they feared a worsening situation after the installation on Saturday of a military camp attributed to AFC/M23 fighters.
claims.place_as_written: Buliriko quarter, Kavumu, Kabare, South Kivu
claims.actor_as_written: AFC/M23 (camp attributed to its fighters, per the source)
claims.verification_note: Both excerpts exact on retained page (2 August 2026); statement keeps the source's hedges. The camp is 'attributed to' AFC/M23 fighters; the article says no official communication had been made on the movements or the origin of the detonations.
claims.researcher_note: Related event at Kavumu on the dates of cluster C-SK-07; it does not report abductions or bodies. The article says no official communication had been made on the population movements or on the origin of detonations heard that morning. 'Saturday' = 1 August 2026, computed from the 2 August publication date (a Sunday per the article).

claim_sources.excerpt_original: du 12 au 15 janvier, dans plusieurs localités du territoire de Rutshuru, province du Nord Kivu, au moins 10 enfants, neuf femmes et huit hommes soupçonnés de collaborer avec les groupes Wazalendo ont été tués par des combattants de l’AFC/M23.
claim_sources.translation_en: from 12 to 15 January, in several localities of Rutshuru territory, North Kivu province, at least 10 children, nine women and eight men suspected of collaborating with Wazalendo groups were killed by AFC/M23 combatants.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Le 2 janvier 2026, les FARDC ont utilisé des drones armés dans le territoire de Masisi (Nord-Kivu) pour frapper des positions de l’AFC/M23. Plusieurs de ces frappes ont touché des zones densément peuplées à Masisi-centre, blessant 42 personnes et tuant sept autres dont deux femmes, une fille, un garçon et détruisant des maisons.
claim_sources.translation_en: On 2 January 2026, the FARDC used armed drones in Masisi territory (North Kivu) to strike AFC/M23 positions. Several of these strikes hit densely populated areas in Masisi-centre, injuring 42 people and killing seven others including two women, a girl and a boy, and destroying houses.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Une employée française de l’UNICEF a été tuée mercredi lors d’une attaque de drone contre un bâtiment abritant des travailleurs humanitaires à Goma
claim_sources.translation_en: A French UNICEF employee was killed on Wednesday in a drone attack on a building housing humanitarian workers in Goma

claim_sources.excerpt_original: L’attaque de drone a également entraîné la mort de deux civils et causé des dégâts à des habitations civiles, a précisé le Mission de paix des Nations Unies en RDC, la MONUSCO , dans un communiqué de presse.
claim_sources.translation_en: The drone attack also caused the death of two civilians and damaged civilian homes, the UN peace mission in the DRC, MONUSCO, said in a press release.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Le groupe d'experts de l'ONU (S/2026/466) reconstitue la frappe qui a tué l'humanitaire française de l'Unicef Karine Buisset à Goma le 11 mars : une munition aérienne de fragmentation, tirée par un drone venu du lac Kivu. L'attribution, elle, reste contestée.
claim_sources.translation_en: The UN group of experts (S/2026/466) reconstructs the strike that killed the French Unicef humanitarian Karine Buisset in Goma on 11 March: an aerial fragmentation munition, fired by a drone coming from Lake Kivu. Attribution, however, remains contested.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Frappe de drone à Goma : les vérités du Groupe d’experts de l’ONU AFP La Rédaction Kinshasa - 2 JUILLET 2026
claim_sources.translation_en: Drone strike in Goma: the truths of the UN Group of Experts AFP The Editorial Team Kinshasa - 2 JULY 2026

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Le porte-parole militaire du mouvement rebelle AFC/M23, Willy Ngoma, a été tué mardi dans une frappe de drone attribuée aux Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), ont indiqué des sources concordantes ainsi que des responsables du mouvement.
claim_sources.translation_en: The military spokesperson of the rebel movement AFC/M23, Willy Ngoma, was killed on Tuesday in a drone strike attributed to the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), concordant sources and movement officials indicated.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Les frappes, dont l’origine reste indéterminée, n’ont été revendiquées par aucune des parties impliquées dans le conflit.
claim_sources.translation_en: The strikes, whose origin remains undetermined, have not been claimed by any of the parties involved in the conflict.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: À Rumangabo, dans le territoire de Rutshuru, une frappe survenue dimanche vers 7h30 a touché un bâtiment abritant un centre de formation destiné aux femmes et aux veuves d’écogardes de l’ICCN, situé dans l’enceinte du parc national des Virunga.
claim_sources.translation_en: At Rumangabo, in Rutshuru territory, a strike on Sunday around 7:30 hit a building housing a training centre for the women and widows of ICCN ecoguards, located within the Virunga National Park compound.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Quelques heures plus tôt, vers 00h15, une autre frappe avait ciblé une maison d’accueil dans la cité minière de Rubaya, dans le territoire de Masisi.
claim_sources.translation_en: A few hours earlier, around 00:15, another strike had targeted a guest house in the mining town of Rubaya, in Masisi territory.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Les villages d'Ihula, Katobo et Mukohwa, situés dans le groupement Kisimba, dans le territoire de Walikale au Nord-Kivu, ont été repris par les rebelles de l'AFC/M23 mardi 26 mai après des combats intenses contre les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) et leurs alliés wazalendo.
claim_sources.translation_en: The villages of Ihula, Katobo and Mukohwa, located in Kisimba groupement, in Walikale territory in North Kivu, were retaken by AFC/M23 rebels on Tuesday 26 May after intense fighting against the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and their Wazalendo allies.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Selon plusieurs sources locales, des affrontements opposent les groupes armés Wazalendo aux rebelles de l’AFC/M23. Les combats ont notamment été signalés dans les localités de Kishanja et Kasenyi, où la situation reste tendue.
claim_sources.translation_en: According to several local sources, clashes pit the Wazalendo armed groups against the AFC/M23 rebels. The fighting was notably reported in the localities of Kishanja and Kasenyi, where the situation remains tense.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Des détonations d’armes lourdes et légères ont été entendues jusqu’à la matinée de ce mercredi 10 juin dans plusieurs localités du territoire de Masisi, dans la province du Nord-Kivu.
claim_sources.translation_en: Detonations of heavy and light weapons were heard until the morning of Wednesday 10 June in several localities of Masisi territory, North Kivu province.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: 10 civils ont été sommairement tués par le M23 dans la localité de Kiseguru, près du parc national de Virunga, en chefferie de Bwito au Nord-Kivu, mardi 02 juin 2026. Les Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo (FARDC) l'annoncent dans un communiqué
claim_sources.translation_en: 10 civilians were summarily killed by the M23 in the locality of Kiseguru, near Virunga National Park, in Bwito chiefdom in North Kivu, on Tuesday 02 June 2026. The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) announce this in a communiqué

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Le même communiqué indique que plusieurs autres citoyens ont été arrêtés et transférés dans la prison centrale de Kanyangambi à Rutshuru sous prétexte qu'ils seraient des FDLR.
claim_sources.translation_en: The same communiqué indicates that several other citizens were arrested and transferred to the central prison of Kanyangambi in Rutshuru on the pretext that they were FDLR.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Les Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo (FARDC) l'annoncent dans un communiqué et condamnent cette nouvelle violation du droit international humanitaire.
claim_sources.translation_en: The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) announce this in a communiqué and condemn this new violation of international humanitarian law.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Au moins 54 personnes ont été tuées dans les attaques des terroristes des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF-MTM) depuis janvier 2026, dans la chefferie des Baswagha et le secteur des Bapere, dans le territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu. Ce bilan provisoire a été dressé ce jeudi par le Comité local de protection communautaire (CLPC)
claim_sources.translation_en: At least 54 people were killed in the attacks by the terrorists of the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF-MTM) since January 2026, in the Baswagha chiefdom and the Bapere sector, in Lubero territory, North Kivu. This provisional toll was drawn up this Thursday by the Local Community Protection Committee (CLPC)

claim_sources.excerpt_original: « Comment comprendre que les ADF tuent ainsi les civils : 33 morts à Baswagha et 21 civils dans le secteur des Bapere depuis janvier 2026 ? » , s’interroge Vianney Kitsamba, président de cette structure citoyenne.
claim_sources.translation_en: “How can we understand that the ADF kill civilians in this way: 33 dead in Baswagha and 21 civilians in the Bapere sector since January 2026?”, asks Vianney Kitsamba, president of this citizen structure.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Dans une déclaration publiée, mardi 3 février 2026, la coordination provinciale de la société civile du Nord-Kivu dresse un bilan alarmant : au moins 62 civils ont été tués depuis le début de l'année par des rebelles présumés des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF) dans les territoires de Beni et Lubero.
claim_sources.translation_en: In a statement published on Tuesday 3 February 2026, the provincial coordination of North Kivu civil society draws up an alarming toll: at least 62 civilians have been killed since the start of the year by suspected rebels of the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in the territories of Beni and Lubero.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Selon les données compilées par la société civile, le territoire de Lubero est le plus durement touché, avec 52 personnes tuées, contre 10 autres en territoire de Beni.
claim_sources.translation_en: According to data compiled by civil society, Lubero territory is the hardest hit, with 52 people killed, against 10 others in Beni territory.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Le ban fait état de d'un poste de santé incendié, 67 boutiques et 10 maisons brûlées ; 23 motos calcinées ; et la destruction du le « barza » (lieu de réunion) d'un chef de localité.
claim_sources.translation_en: The toll reports a health post burned, 67 shops and 10 houses burned; 23 motorbikes burnt; and the destruction of the 'barza' (meeting place) of a locality chief.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: au moins 62 civils ont été tués depuis le début de l'année par des rebelles présumés des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF) dans les territoires de Beni et Lubero
claim_sources.translation_en: at least 62 civilians have been killed since the start of the year by suspected rebels of the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in Beni and Lubero territories

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Un poste de santé, vingt-trois motos, soixante-sept boutiques, dix maisons d’habitation ainsi que le barza du chef de localité ont été incendiés
claim_sources.translation_en: One health post, twenty-three motorbikes, sixty-seven shops, ten dwellings, as well as the local chief's barza were burned down

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Des sources sanitaires indiquent à ACTUALITÉ.CD que les centres de santé de Mausa, Pombi, Mandelya, Musenge, ainsi que le centre de santé de référence (CSR) de Masoy, ont cessé leurs activités.
claim_sources.translation_en: Health sources tell ACTUALITÉ.CD that the health centres of Mausa, Pombi, Mandelya, Musenge, as well as the reference health centre (CSR) of Masoy, have ceased their activities.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Cette alerte intervient au lendemain d'une attaque des ADF dans la nuit du 21 au 22 juillet 2026 dans cette zone. Selon des sources locales, l'incursion a coûté la vie à au moins sept civils. Plusieurs habitations ont également été incendiées, contraignant de nombreux ménages à fuir leurs villages pour se mettre à l'abri.
claim_sources.translation_en: This alert comes the day after an ADF attack in the night of 21 to 22 July 2026 in this area. According to local sources, the incursion cost the lives of at least seven civilians. Several homes were also burned, forcing many households to flee their villages to take shelter.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Pour rappel, cinq civils ont été tués et une dizaine de maisons incendiées lors d'une nouvelle attaque attribuée aux combattants ADF dans la nuit du mardi au mercredi 21 janvier dernier. L'incident s'est produit au village de Mavwe-Mavwe, dans la localité de Mandelya. Parmi les victimes figuraient quatre femmes.
claim_sources.translation_en: As a reminder, five civilians were killed and about ten houses burned in a new attack attributed to ADF combatants in the night from Tuesday to Wednesday 21 January last. The incident occurred in the village of Mavwe-Mavwe, in the Mandelya locality. Among the victims were four women.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Le conseil communal de la jeunesse de Karisimbi a alerté ce mercredi 8 juillet 2026 sur l’enlèvement de plus de 50 jeunes par des hommes armés dans les quartiers Kasika et Mabanga Nord, en ville de Goma, dans la province du Nord-Kivu.
claim_sources.translation_en: The Karisimbi communal youth council alerted this Wednesday 8 July 2026 to the abduction of more than 50 young people by armed men in the Kasika and Mabanga Nord quarters, in the city of Goma, in North Kivu province.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Le conseil communal de la jeunesse de la commune de Karisimbi, qui craint un éventuel enrôlement forcé de ces jeunes au sein du mouvement du 23 mars (M23/AFC), plaide pour l’intervention de l’opinion nationale et internationale afin que ces civils recouvrent leur liberté.
claim_sources.translation_en: The Karisimbi communal youth council, which fears a possible forced enrolment of these young people into the March 23 movement (M23/AFC), appeals to national and international opinion for the intervention so that these civilians regain their freedom.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Ihuriro AFC/M23 ryatangaje ko abantu batandatu bo mu muryango umwe, barimo umugore n’abana be batanu, bishwe mu gitero rivuga ko cyagabwe n’umutwe wa FDLR mu Teritwari ya Rutshuru, mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru.
claim_sources.translation_en: The AFC/M23 alliance announced that six people of one family, including a woman and her five children, were killed in an attack it says was carried out by the FDLR group in Rutshuru Territory, in North Kivu Province.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Abo bivugwa ko bahasize ubuzima ni Tuombe Maniragaba wari umugore wa Rugamba, hamwe n’abana babo batanu ari bo Sifiwe Rugamba, Dorika Rugamba, Emery Rugamba, Mariam Rugamba na Divine Rugamba.
claim_sources.translation_en: Those said to have lost their lives are Tuombe Maniragaba, who was Rugamba's wife, together with their five children, namely Sifiwe Rugamba, Dorika Rugamba, Emery Rugamba, Mariam Rugamba and Divine Rugamba.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Nk’uko byatangajwe n’umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, icyo gitero cyabaye mu ijoro ryo ku wa 2 Nyakanga 2026 mu gace ka Kabizo/Butare, gaherereye muri Sheferi ya Bwito.
claim_sources.translation_en: According to AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, the attack took place in the night of 2 July 2026 in the Kabizo/Butare area, located in Bwito Chiefdom.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: le directeur de la radio communautaire Top Buzi FM, Espoir Mbata a, à son tour, été séquestré. Il a ensuite été contraint de réaliser une interview filmée du porte-parole du M23, le groupe armé qui le détenait, avant d’être finalement libéré. C’est ce qu’a révélé ce vendredi 24 avril RSF.
claim_sources.translation_en: the director of the community radio Top Buzi FM, Espoir Mbata, was in turn confined. He was then forced to carry out a filmed interview of the M23 spokesperson, the armed group that was holding him, before finally being released. This is what RSF revealed this Friday 24 April.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Quelques jours seulement après les révélations de RSF sur l’utilisation de conteneurs comme lieu de détention, l’AFC/M23 a de nouveau enfermé un journaliste dans l’un de ceux situés dans l’Assemblée provinciale du Nord-Kivu, à Goma.
claim_sources.translation_en: Only a few days after RSF's revelations on the use of containers as places of detention, the AFC/M23 again locked up a journalist in one of those located in the North Kivu Provincial Assembly, in Goma.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Amnesty International documented the summary killing of 18 artisanal miners by M23 or their collaborators, at least nine of whom were beaten brutally and died at health centres or before they reached the hospital.
More than 20 miners from Rubaya were kept in a pit and beaten three times a day by M23 fighters.

In a separate statement last week, UN experts called for an end to what they described as a “reign of terror” by the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group, citing a growing volume of testimony from civilian victims. “Rapes, gang rapes, violent assaults and killings of civilians are a common feature of M23's modus operandi,” the experts said.
While these crimes are not exclusive to M23, the number of individuals affected is staggering and must end.
“Rapes, gang rapes, violent assaults and killings of civilians are a common feature of M23’s modus operandi,” the experts said in a press release.

Witnesses and relatives told Human Rights Watch that drone attacks in the highlands killed at least two Banyamulenge people in March 2026. On March 23, an 86-year-old man was killed while tending his cattle near Minembwe. On March 30, a 14-year-old boy was killed in a field near his village in Fizi territory. It is unclear if the attacks intended to target military objectives.

A community radio station in Madegu, near Minembwe, was damaged in an apparent drone attack on March 9, disrupting access to information in an area where the phone network has been disrupted for over a year.

While Human Rights Watch could not establish with certainty responsibility for these strikes, the targets suggest that the Congolese army or allied fighters controlled the drones, Human Rights Watch said.
Minembwe residents and UN and diplomatic sources said that the Twirwaneho had forced families to provide a fighter or financially compensate the armed group, and retaliated if they refused.
The Burundian army currently has about 4,000 troops deployed to Fizi and Mwenga territories to fight alongside Congolese armed forces, according to security sources.

« Les avions de chasse de l’armée de l’air du Rwanda ont une fois de plus bombardé les agglomérations de Rugezi, Mulima, Point Zéro, Kazaroho, Bilalo Mbili et Mikenge, causant d’énormes dégâts matériels et humains, ce mercredi 8 juillet 2026 » , a rapporté l’administrateur du territoire de Fizi, Samy Badibanga.
claim_sources.translation_en: "Rwandan air force fighter jets have once again bombed the agglomerations of Rugezi, Mulima, Point Zéro, Kazaroho, Bilalo Mbili and Mikenge, causing enormous material and human damage, this Wednesday 8 July 2026," reported the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Badibanga.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: L’autorité territoriale indique que plusieurs blessés civils ont été enregistrés à la suite de ces bombardements.
claim_sources.translation_en: The territorial authority says several civilian wounded were recorded following these bombings.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Selon la nouvelle dynamique de la société civile, antenne de Fizi, environ 16 civils ont été tués et 12 autres blessés. Parmi les victimes figurent des femmes et des enfants.
claim_sources.translation_en: "The fighter jets of the Rwandan air force have once again bombed the agglomerations of Rugezi, Mulima, Point Zéro, Kazaroho, Bilalo Mbili and Mikenge, causing enormous material and human damage, this Wednesday 8 July 2026," reported the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Badibanga.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: L'alerte est lancée par le député national élu de Fizi, le professeur Nyamangyoku Ishibwela. Il dénonce une crise humanitaire majeure où même les civils blessés lors de ces frappes peinent à recevoir des soins médicaux.
claim_sources.translation_en: The alert was raised by Fizi's elected national deputy, Professor Nyamangyoku Ishibwela. He denounces a major humanitarian crisis in which even civilians wounded in these strikes struggle to receive medical care.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: L’alerte a été lancée par le député national élu de Fizi, le professeur Nyamangyoku Ishibwela.
claim_sources.translation_en: The alert was raised by the elected national deputy for Fizi, Professor Nyamangyoku Ishibwela.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Le 29 juillet 2026, le député national élu de Fizi, Nyamangyoku Ishibwela, alerte sur le sort de milliers de personnes déplacées depuis le 24 juillet par des bombardements qu’il attribue à des drones kamikazes venus du Rwanda.
claim_sources.translation_en: On 29 July 2026, the elected national deputy for Fizi, Nyamangyoku Ishibwela, raises the alarm about the fate of thousands of people displaced since 24 July by bombings that he attributes to kamikaze drones from Rwanda.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: The town of Mikenge, located in the Itombwe sector of Mwenga territory in South Kivu province, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, was retaken on Sunday by the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), supported by the Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB) and the Wazalendo militia.

the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo), the FDNB (National Democratic Forces of Burundi), and the Wazalendo militia now control strategic points in the center of Mikenge, including the general hospital.
La cité de Kasika reste sous le contrôle de l’AFC/M23, tandis que les Wazalendo sont positionnés à Kalambi, à environ 20 kilomètres de Kasika, toujours dans la chefferie de Lwindi.
claim_sources.translation_en: The town of Kasika remains under the control of the AFC/M23, while the Wazalendo are positioned at Kalambi, about 20 kilometres from Kasika, still in Lwindi chiefdom.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Mu butumwa yashyize kuri X ku wa 21 Kanama 2026, Kanyuka yavuze ko mu gace ka Luntukulu, ku muhanda wa Nzibira, abasivili barimo abagore n’abana baguye mu bitero.
claim_sources.translation_en: In a message he posted on X on 21 August 2026, Kanyuka said that in the Luntukulu area, on the Nzibira road, civilians including women and children died in the attacks.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Kanyuka kandi yavuze ko ingabo za Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo zikomeje kugaba ibitero by’ibisasu mu gace ka Minembwe. Yavuze ko muri ibyo bikorwa hakoreshwa drones za kamikaze ndetse n’intwaro za TK-6
claim_sources.translation_en: Kanyuka also said the armed forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo continue to launch bomb attacks in the Minembwe area. He said these operations use kamikaze drones and TK-6 weapons.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Selon les experts onusiens, l’AFC/M23 aurait mis en place un véritable système de contrôle fondé sur la peur dans les zones qu’il administre. Le communiqué fait état d’arrestations et de détentions arbitraires, d’actes de torture, y compris de violences sexuelles, ainsi que de cas de travail forcé et de recrutement forcé de civils.
claim_sources.translation_en: According to the UN experts, the AFC/M23 has reportedly set up a genuine system of control based on fear in the areas it administers. The statement reports arbitrary arrests and detentions, acts of torture, including sexual violence, as well as cases of forced labour and forced recruitment of civilians.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Entre janvier et avril 2026, MSF a appuyé l’hôpital général de référence de Baraka en renforçant ses capacités à travers des approvisionnements médicaux et logistiques, ainsi que des sessions de formation au personnel soignant, afin de mieux répondre à l’afflux de blessés liés aux violences. Cet appui a permis de prendre en charge 426 patients blessés de guerre.
claim_sources.translation_en: Between January and April 2026, MSF supported Baraka general referral hospital by strengthening its capacity through medical and logistical supplies and staff training, to better respond to the influx of violence-related injuries. This support made it possible to treat 426 war-wounded patients.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: However, in the days preceding its signature, the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) and AFC/M23 launched a coordinated military offensive in South Kivu, taking control of Uvira on 10 December 2025

On 4 December 2025, the Governments of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda signed the Washington Agreement, 42 aimed at de-escalation and cessation of hostilities. 43 However, in the days preceding its signature, the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) and AFC/M23 launched a coordinated military offensive in South Kivu, taking control of Uvira on 10 December 2025
AFC/ M23 and RDF troops eventually withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026, following sustained international diplomatic pressure
Presented as a goodwill gesture, the withdrawal was a strategic move followed by the consolidation of AFC/M23 and RDF positions, as they redeployed to adjacent areas

At the end of November 2025, AFC/M23 and RDF launched a major offensive along the Bukavu-Uvira (RN5) corridor and adjacent axes, aiming to seize the Ruzizi Plain and Uvira, to compel Burundi’s disengagement from the conflict
The offensive on Uvira was conducted under the direct command of Mr. Makenga and Mr. Byamungu.
AFC/M23 and RDF sources signaled since early October the intent of taking Uvira, pointing at a carefully planned operation by AFC/M23 and Rwanda.
Rwanda deployed over 8,000 RDF troops, including special forces, and transferred heavy, advanced military equipment to the frontlines on the Ruzizi Plain

Heavy artillery and shelling were employed, including firing BM21 rockets from Kamanyola on 4 and 5 December. Cross-border shelling on 5 December has also caused civilian casualties in Cibitoke, Burundi.
Heavy artillery fire and shelling resulted in civilian casualties and significant population displacement from the Ruzizi Plain towards Burundi

As clashes subsided and AFC/M23 and RDF consolidated control throughout Uvira in early December, they conducted cordon -and-search operations that led to the killing of those suspected of affiliation with FARDC or Wazalendo.

When Wazalendo groups re-entered Uvira on 18 January, they triggered widespread disorder, including looting, the destruction of civilian, humanitarian and State properties and the killing of individuals accused of collaborating with AFC/M23.

Violence also affected members and properties of the Banyamulenge community, with churches and homes looted or destroyed across several neighbourhoods. 89 The Group of Experts did not document any targeted killings of Banyamulenge civilians.

Multiple sources indicated that government authorities, including the President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Félix Tshisekedi, instructed Wazalendo elements not to target civilians, particularly the Banyamulenge. FARDC placed 31 Banyamulenge families remaining in Uvira under its protection.
Overall military command of AFC/M23 remained with “General” Makenga, although his position became increasingly contested within the movement and by Rwanda

Bertrand Bisimwa and Corneille Nangaa remained the political leaders. Both the military and political leadership continued to receive instructions and support from the Government of Rwanda and its intelligence services

Withdrawals by RDF and AFC/M23 from frontlines in North Kivu began on 23 March but fell short of agreed terms and deadlines. Withdrawals – barely exceeding 15 to 20 km – represented limited strategic and territorial concessions. Movements amounted to tactical repositioning
RDF personnel, heavy artillery and sophisticated equipment (jamming, spoofing and other air defence systems) were redeployed from Lubero to the Masisi-Walikale axis

At the time of writing, RDF and AFC/M23 had retained control over most withdrawal-designated localities and maintained operational focus on Pinga and Walikale. In April, intense clashes over territorial control persisted along the Walikale-Masisi border, between AFC/M23 and RDF on the one side and FARDC, Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP)/Wazalendo and FDLR

In late January 2026, FARDC, with support from Wazalendo, FDNB and private military contractors (see paras. 143–144), launched an offensive from Uvira towards Minembwe against MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23, who reinforced MRDP/ Twirwaneho in August 2025 and February 2026.

On 31 March, FARDC launched a major offensive on Minembwe following sustained gains across the Hauts Plateaux. 93 In response, RDF supported MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 through drone strikes and aerial resupply.

MRDP/Twirwaneho prevented civilians from leaving Minembwe, including through coercion and threats of violence, fearing defections and information leaks. 97 As previously reported, all boys between 10 and 12 years of age and all able-bodied men were compelled to join Twirwaneho and participate in combat

MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 leaders alleged that FARDC and FDNB committed a premeditated, systematic and targeted campaign of extermination against the Banyamulenge population, including through aerial bombardments of densely populated areas.

the Group of Experts did not substantiate their intentional targeting. In the context of frequent aerial operations since mid-2025, members of the Banyamulenge community, including human rights organizations, have reported three civilian deaths, including one teenage boy and two elderly individuals.
Statements on X, including by Lawrence Kanyuka on 13 December 2025.

FARDC drone operations also targeted AFC/M23 leadership. On 14 January 2026, a drone strike targeted the “Blue Cat” bar-restaurant in the Kalundu district of Uvira, during a meeting of senior AFC/M23 and RDF officers, causing significant casualties.

On 24 February 2026, a FARDC drone strike in Rubaya killed sanctioned individual “Lieutenant-Colonel” Willy Ngoma (CDi.044), the military spokesperson of AFC/M23. 195 On 7 March 2026, a strike in Mushaki targeted a house associated with a high-ranking AFC/M23 commander.

Several FARDC drone operations affected civilian objects and populations. In Masisi territory, strikes in late October 2025 in Shoa and the Nyabiondo hills killed at least three civilians and caused displacement. On 2 January 2026, a drone strike in
Masisi centre damaged civilian and administrative buildings and the sub -base of the international humanitarian organization War Child, causing at least seven fatalities.

On 11 March 2026, two successive detonations were reported near a residential compound located in the Himbi neighbourhood in Goma. The second detonation impacted a residential compound resulting in the death of a United Nations Children’s
Fund (UNICEF) staff member. M23 military personnel deployed to the scene shortly after the strike and removed all ballistic remnants
AFC/M23 attributed the strike to FARDC, while Congolese authorities announced an investigation. 201 The Group of Experts’ investigations into this incident continue.

AFC/M23 continued to forcibly or voluntarily recruit adults and minors (see S/2025/858, para. 22). 70 Former recruits denounced systematic torture and executions in training camps, notably in Rumangabo.
Leon Kanyamibwa continued to be identified as AFC/M23 commander responsible for all training centres

AFC/M23 was the leading perpetrator of conflict-related sexual violence according to cases documented and verified by the United Nations (see S/2025/858, para. 80 and annex 37). Humanitarian actors recorded a dramatic increase in cases of such violence since 2024, with cases disproportionately affecting women and girls
In January 2026, the UN in DRC verified at least 46 cases of CRSV affecting 61 victims in conflict-affected provinces in eastern DRC.

North Kivu was the most affected province with 33 victims (22 women and 11 girls), followed by South Kivu with 22 victims (13 women and nine girls) and Ituri with six victims (four women, one girl and one man).
Armed groups continued to bear the main responsibility for CRSV and were responsible for cases affecting 52 per cent of victims. M23 committed most cases with 21 victims (13 women and eight girls)
the Nyatura with four victims (two women and two girls), the Raïa Mutomboki with three victims (two women and one girl), and the ADF with two victims, (both women).
State agents were responsible for 46 percent of the cases. FARDC soldiers ranked first followed by the PNC and one official from Ministry of Mines and Energy.
The Group reviewed a document dated 11 February 2026 that the AFC/M23 distributed to multiple humanitarian actors involved in the provision of health care

Following the distribution of this note, the AFC/M23-run Provincial Health Inspection Department (Inspection Provinciale de la Santé or IPS) initiated a series of inspections of the premises of humanitarian actors. IPS inspectors requested aggregate data on sexual violence incidents and access to confidential patient files containing names of victims and other personal information
Some humanitarian actors were ordered to cease the distribution of dignity kits to curb the number of what they alleged to be “fake” victims seeking humanitarian assistance.

A joint meeting was held in late March 2026 between humanitarian actors and AFC/M23 at which the issue of sexual violence data was discussed. AFC/M23 officials present at the meeting included Colonel John Imani Nzenze, AFC/M23 Director of Intelligence and the AFC/M23 liaison with humanitarian actors, and Ms. Chantal Kayitaba Murekatete

At the meeting, the AFC/M23 reprimanded humanitarian actors and accused them of inventing data. It affirmed that AFC/M23 did not tolerate sexual violence and criticised the lack of perpetrator data in patient files as this made it more difficult for it to punish perpetrators

On 15 November 2025, between approximately 19:00 and 23:00 hours, ADF elements carried out an incursion into the village of Byambwe, in Manzya groupement, Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, killing 23 civilians, including 13 women and 10 men. Among the victims were women admitted to the maternity ward who were killed inside a Catholic Church–run health center.

During the attack, four hospital pavilions housing patients were set on fire. The assailants looted and burned 27 houses, including the medical facility, from which equipment and medicines were taken.

Selon des sources locales concordantes, les ADF ont ciblé le Centre, où ils ont tué, pillé des médicaments et incendié des maisons voisines. Le bilan provisoire, pas encore confirmé par des sources officielles, est de 20 civils tués, dont 18 malades qui recevaient des soins dans cette structure sanitaire
claim_sources.translation_en: According to concordant local sources, the ADF targeted the Centre, where they killed, looted medicines and set neighbouring houses on fire. The provisional toll, not yet confirmed by official sources, is 20 civilians killed, including 18 patients who were receiving care in this health facility

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Le bilan de la récente attaque meurtrière des islamistes ADF à Byambwe, dans le territoire de Lubero, dans la nuit du vendredi 14 novembre, a été revu à la hausse, passant de 20 à 28 personnes tuées, dont 17 patients exécutés au centre de santé de référence de la localité.
claim_sources.translation_en: The toll of the recent deadly attack by ADF Islamists in Byambwe, in Lubero territory, on the night of Friday 14 November, has been revised upwards, from 20 to 28 people killed, including 17 patients executed at the locality's referral health centre.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Among the most significant incidents attributed to Abwakasi’s elements was the massacre of civilians attending a funeral in Ntuyo village, located approximately 6 kilometers east of Manguredjipa town, in Bapere sector, Lubero territory. The attack was carried out on the night of 8 to 9 September 2025
A total of 71 civilians, including men, women, and children, were killed. At least 36 houses were looted and set on fire
Abwakasi’s group massacred 71 civilians attending a funeral in Nturo village in November 2025.

Between January and December 2025, the UN in DRC verified at least 887 cases of CRSV affecting a total of 1,534 victims in conflict-affected provinces in eastern DRC. This represented an increase of 59 per cent in comparison to 2024 when 364 cases were verified.
Among the victims were 854 women, 672 girls, four men, and four boys. North Kivu was the most affected province with 676 victims, followed by South Kivu with 537 victims and Ituri with 300 victims.

The UN identified that DRC armed groups were responsible for cases affecting 75 per cent of CRSV victims. M23 ranked first followed by CODECO, Wazalendo and Mai-Mai factions. State agents were responsible for cases affecting 19 per cent of CRSV victims. FARDC soldiers ranked first followed by the PNC.
Foreign armed forces – the UPDF and the FNDB – as well as foreign armed groups – RED-Tabara – were also responsible for CRSV cases.
The Group has verified a sharp escalation of cases of CRSV in South Kivu in areas under the control of the DRC Government and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups
The Group has verified a sharp escalation of cases of CRSV in South Kivu in areas under the control of the DRC Government and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups (S/2025/858, para. 82, annex 38)
Comparison with activity observed one year earlier indicated a substantial increase in mining activity. Production levels are assessed to exceed 2024 estimates of approximately 120 tons monthly

AFC/M23 continued to tax all actors involved in the production and supply chains. The most significant revenue was generated through a per-kilogram tax imposed at the point of commercialization, 239 notably $4 for coltan and $2 for cassiterite.

Between 80 and 150 Wazalendo groups were reported active across South Kivu, with at least 70 self proclaimed Wazalendo “Generals” operating in Uvira and its surroundings 127 (see annex 35). Mobilization and recruitment increased.
By December 2025, Uvira had become the epicentre of tensions and clashes between FARDC and Wazalendo and among Wazalendo fighting over revenue from illegal taxation.
FARDC continued to supply war materiel to Wazalendo. On 22 August 2025, Brigadier-General Mwehu Lumbu Evariste, Commander of Sokola 2 operational

sector in South Kivu, met with the main Wazalendo groups to define a counteroffensive strategy against AFC/M23 and RDF. Subsequently, FARDC transferred truckloads of weapons and ammunition to Wazalendo at several front lines, including Kiliba, Songe, Luvungi, Lubarika and Walungu.

Several Wazalendo factions also carried out joint operations with FDNB, which relied on them for intelligence and knowledge of the terrain. For example, FDNB operated with Yakutumba along the Uvira axis and the Ruzizi Plain prior to the AFC/M23 takeover and relied on Ngomazito elements as scouts in the Hauts Plateaux

Coalition nationale du peuple pour la souveraineté du Congo (CNPSC), led by Yakutumba (see para. 111), maintained a parallel administration it had established in areas under its control, particularly in Fizi territory
Former detainees reported that release was conditioned on the payment of fines ranging between 2,000,000 and 5,000,000 Congolese francs

On 7 April, a confidential encounter between a high -level delegation from Kinshasa, including FARDC generals, and representatives of the FDLR -FOCA high command in Pinga decided, inter alia, that FDLR-FARDC cooperation would continue.

In late March 2026, a FARDC helicopter landed in Pinga to deliver weapons to FDLR-FOCA units led by “Major-General” Uzabakiriho Cyprien (alias Kolomboka Niyo Tedium Mugisha) that had been engaged in fighting against AFC/M23 and RDF in Masisi territory

On 29 March 2026, FARDC announced the launch of an operation to neutralize FDLR around Pinga-Walikale and deployed additional troops from Kisangani to Walikale for these operations. 51 However, the commitment of FARDC remained questionable (see S/2024/969, paras. 67–73) since at the time of writing no anti-FDLR operations had taken place

private military contractors accompanied FARDC when they entered in Uvira in January 2026 (see para. 40). 178 On 1 February 2026, multiple drone strikes conducted with the support of private military contractors targeted AFC/M23 positions around Minembwe. 179 Between 2 and 8 February 2026, private military contractors airdropped FARDC “Hiboux” special forces units at Point Zero

a meeting in Washington, D.C. on 17 and 18 March 2026 between representatives of the Governments of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda and the United States resulted in commitments defined in an “initial steps plan

The plan included coordinated steps to de-escalate tensions, commitments to sovereignty and territorial integrity, Rwanda’s disengagement from defined areas in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, efforts by the Democratic Republic of the Congo to neutralize the Forces démocratiques de libération du Rwanda (FDLR), restrictions on drone strikes
The plan foresaw the withdrawal of both RDF and AFC/M23 “personnel and equipment
AFC/M23 representatives announced that no withdrawal was taking place, describing movements as routine troop rotations
as well as public statements by the President of Rwanda, Paul Kagame, that “defensive measures” also included troop deployment in the Democratic Republic of the Congo

AFC/M23 conducted armed night raids on hospitals in Goma. Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals were targeted, on 1 and 3 March, respectively, as part of operations tracking FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR combatants who had not surrendered (see para. 21 above). Male caregivers were briefly detained and released.
A total of 164 patients were abducted – 48 from Heal Africa and 116 from CBCA Ndosho – some of whom had been undergoing treatment, others who had refused to leave for fear of forced recruitment
Contrary to those assertions, witnesses confirmed that no weapons were found in the hospitals and the arrested individuals had not endangered patients or staff

Following the incidents in March, Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka and “General” Makenga issued public denials of responsibility, claiming they had acted in full compliance with international humanitarian law and with the aim of securing the hospitals from “infiltrated rogue combatants” who had been “endangering” patients and medical staff

On 3 March 2025, Fikiri Mwishuko, the Chef de groupement of Shanga, was abducted by AFC/M23 from the CBCA Ndosho hospital (paras. 105-108), amongst others sick and wounded patients. Fikiri Mwishuko subsequently died, reportedly after having been tortured by AFC/M23.

On the night of 4 to 5 April 2025, armed AFC/M23 elements entered the MSF supported Kyeshero Hospital compound in Goma in search of FARDC elements who had completed medical treatment but remained at the hospital for fear of being recruited. The AFC/M23 elements opened fire within the facility grounds, killing one person, injuring three and assaulting two staff members.
Although the soldiers did not enter the hospital ward, bullets struck the treatment areas.

An official AFC/M23 communiqué was published on 5 March 2025, signed by Lawrence Kanyuka, denying responsibility for the raids on the hospitals, accusing MONUSCO officials of erroneous interpretation of the facts

The communiqué acknowledges that 130 FARDC elements were taken, but claims that the operation was carried out in in a peaceful manner and in full compliance with IHL, because the FARDC elements had “infiltrated” the medical facilities

On 13 March 2025, the excerpt from an interview by Alain Destexhe, a Belgian national, with “General” Sultani Makenga was published on “X”. Responding to a question about the raid on the Heal Africa hospital, Makenga repeated the claims that the men who were “arrested” were former FARDC who were pretending to be patients or hospital staff
On 20 January, bullets and several rockets landed near the Médecins sans frontières (MSF) -supported hospital in Masisi town, killing one MSF worker and injuring another.
On 27 January, intense firing and shelling affected two hospitals in Goma, injuring a medical practitioner and a newborn at Goma Provincial Hospital.
Humanitarian actors reported that, between 25 January and 14 February, at least 27 health structures in and around Goma had been impacted by attacks.

A further alarming surge in cases has been reported across North and South Kivu, attributed to all armed actors party to the conflict, both in the immediate aftermath of the fighting and during the subsequent
consolidation of AFC/M23’s control. Human rights defenders reported that survivors faced significant barriers in accessing medical care, primarily due to fear of reprisals by AFC/M23 elements.

De nombreux autres cas de violence restent non documentés en raison de divers facteurs, tels que la crainte de représailles de la part des auteurs, la stigmatisation au sein de la communauté et l’inaccessibilité et l’absence de services spécialisés.
claim_sources.translation_en: Many other cases of violence remain undocumented because of various factors, such as fear of reprisals from the perpetrators, stigma within the community, and the inaccessibility and absence of specialised services.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Reports on the mass escape of prisoners from Muzenze prison in Goma on 27 January 2025 indicated that over 160 women perished in a fire that engulfed the facility, with a significant number of women reportedly raped by escaping male prisoners.284 The Group has not yet been able to independently verify the reported figures
Hours later, inside the compound, there was a fire - apparently set by male prisoners as they tried to escape.
A total of 132 female prisoners and at least 25 children burned to death, according to two sources.
The BBC cannot verify how many women were raped that night,

Between 6 and 8 February, similar patterns were recorded in South Kivu, between Kalehe and Kavumu, as retreating FARDC forces looted civilian property and a health centre, forcibly enlisted civilians to transport stolen goods, deliberately killed at least 15 civilians 87 and engaged in widespread sexual violence.

MONUSCO documented the rape of three girls aged 13 to 17 by FARDC soldiers between 31 January and 2 February. FARDC authorities confirmed the violations and reported the arrest of alleged perpetrators.
On 15 February, the withdrawal of FARDC forces from Bukavu led to the escape of over 2,800 detainees and widespread looting
At a public meeting hosted by Nangaa in Bukavu on 27 February, two explosions resulted in 17 civilians killed and 68 wounded.

On 26 January 2025, several bombs launched from positions on the Bulenga peninsula, controlled by RDF (see para. 53 above), 79 struck the Rusayo 1 and 2 internally displaced persons camps on the outskirts of Goma, killing at least 12 people, including children, and injuring many others.

Between 28 January and 9 April, the Group recorded at least 70 distinct incidents of targeted kill ings in Goma attributable to AFC/M23, resulting in over 200 fatalities. Adult men comprised the majority of the victims, but which also included women and children.

On 13 February 2025, Delcat Idengo – by his real name Delphin Katembo Vinywasiki – a well-known “revolutionary” activist musician, famous for his politically charged songs, was shot and killed by AFC/M23 elements shortly after publicly criticizing AFC/M23
Eyewitnesses who were at the scene identified AFC/M23 fighters as responsible for his assassination.
Screenshot from the video of Idengo’s recorded speech, two days prior to his assassination in Goma.

The same evening, on 13 February, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka publicly denied any involvement in the killing of Idengo, condemning it as a “score-settling between different factions of the Wazalendo and the FARDC”
A month later, on 12 March 2025, Lawrence Kanyuka reiterated his denial of AFC/M23’s responsibility for the killing of Idengo

Bertrand Bisimwa publicly denied civilian deaths, claiming that all fatalities were combatants (see annex 44). These claims were contradicted by consistent reports on civilian casualties from residents, humanitarian and medical actors
After the expiration of a seven-day ultimatum issued on 11 February by AFC/M23 – demanding the surrender of members of the FARDC, PNC, Wazalendo and FDLR, urging civilians to denounce them

and warning that failure to comply would result in being treated as enemies – AFC/M23 intensified house-to-house searches and targeted operations against individuals suspected of affiliation with Wazalendo, FDLR or FARDC

On 4 January 2025, AFC/M23 and RDF took control of Masisi centre in North Kivu and managed to retain control despite repeated attempts by Wazalendo, FDLR, the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and FARDC to retake it. Two weeks later, AFC/M23 and RDF captured Minova town in Kalehe Territory, South Kivu

Between 21 and 27 January 2025, several columns of RDF troops, each comprising hundreds of well-equipped soldiers, advanced into and seized control of Sake, Mubambiro and Goma town, following a coordinated encirclement of each locality.
After several days of intense fighting, significant casualties were reported among combatants, including RDF, and among civilians (see paras. 65 –67 below). Goma was fully conquered on 27 January.
On 24 January, the Military Governor of North Kivu, Major-General Peter Cirimwami,
known for his long-standing ties with the Forces démocratiques de libération du Rwanda-Forces combattantes abacunguzi (FDLR-FOCA), was shot dead in Sake (see annex 6).

The Military Governor of North Kivu, Major-General Peter Cirimwami, was shot on 24 January while visiting FARDC and Wazalendo forces in Sake to encourage them and request them to continue fighting. He succumbed to his injuries the following day.

AFC/M23 and RDF broke through the joint FARDC-FDNB positions in Nyabibwe on 6 February and managed to seize the strategic airport of Kavumu on 14 February. Bukavu, the provincial capital of South Kivu, was taken on 16 February without combat

In early April, AFC/M23 and RDF forces withdrew from Walikale following sustained FARDC airstrikes targeting critical infrastructure, including the Kigoma airstrip (see para. 38 below), alongside mounting international pressure.
According to corroborated information obtained by the Group, the decision to wit hdraw was taken following direct instruction from the Government of Rwanda

Similarly, since 17 February, Uvira experienced a severe breakdown in law and order, as the AFC/M23 advance loomed and security forces either retreated (see paras. 169–170 below) or lost control of key areas. Criminal elements and undisciplined FARDC and Wazalendo engaged in widespread killings, looting and attacks on civilian and humanitarian infrastructure. Residents reported bodies strewn all over the city.
From February, as the Democratic Republic of the Congo authorities and security actors largely withdrew from Uvira, Wazalendo armed groups de facto controlled
Uvira town and surroundings, where they resorted to the disproportionate use of force and widespread abuses, in particular targeting Banyamulenge communities.
FARDC headquarters and the South Kivu Governorate were reinstalled in Uvira in early March.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Depuis début janvier, la cité de Masisi Centre et ses environs sont le théâtre d’affrontements quasi quotidiens entre combattants VDP/Wazalendo (alliés à l’armée congolaise) et le M23/AFC.
claim_sources.translation_en: Since early January, the town of Masisi Centre and its surroundings have been the scene of almost daily clashes between VDP/Wazalendo fighters (allied to the Congolese army) and the M23/AFC.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Depuis début janvier, la cité de Masisi-Centre et ses environs sont le théâtre d’affrontements quasi quotidiens entre combattants VDP/Wazalendo (alliés à l’armée congolaise) et le M23/AFC.
claim_sources.translation_en: Since early January, the town of Masisi-Centre and its surroundings have been the scene of almost daily clashes between VDP/Wazalendo fighters (allied with the Congolese army) and the M23/AFC.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: est décédé ce samedi des suites d’une blessure par balle reçue lors des affrontements du 20 février entre les combattants VDP/Wazalendo et ceux du M23/AFC à Masisi Centre, dans la province du Nord-Kivu
claim_sources.translation_en: died this Saturday from a gunshot wound received during the clashes of 20 February between VDP/Wazalendo fighters and those of the M23/AFC in Masisi Centre, in North Kivu province

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Médecins sans frontières (MSF) a annoncé samedi 22 février le décès de l’un de ses employés qui avait été blessé par balle jeudi dernier, lors de violents affrontements entre les rebelles du M23/AFC et les VDP/Wazalendo, près de l’hôpital général de référence de Masisi (Nord-Kivu).
claim_sources.translation_en: Médecins sans frontières (MSF) announced on Saturday 22 February the death of one of its employees who had been shot last Thursday during violent clashes between M23/AFC rebels and VDP/Wazalendo near the Masisi general referral hospital (North Kivu).

claim_sources.excerpt_original: La disparition tragique de Jerry Muhindo Kavali s’inscrit en effet dans un contexte de violences de plus en plus marquées affectant les installations sanitaires et humanitaires dans l’est de la RDC ». Décédé à 49 ans, Jerry a travaillé avec Médecins sans frontières durant plus de dix ans.
claim_sources.translation_en: The tragic death of Jerry Muhindo Kavali comes in a context of increasingly marked violence affecting health and humanitarian facilities in eastern DRC." Dead at 49, Jerry had worked with Médecins sans frontières for more than ten years.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Le 20 février, un radio-opérateur de MSF, alors en poste dans la base de l’ONG à Masisi centre, a été mortellement touché par des tirs entre combattants VDP/Wazalendo et du M23/AFC à proximité du bâtiment de MSF.
claim_sources.translation_en: On 20 February, an MSF radio operator, then posted at the NGO's base in Masisi centre, was fatally hit by gunfire between VDP/Wazalendo and M23/AFC fighters near the MSF building.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Dans la soirée du 18 avril, un employé de Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) a été tué par balle à son domicile de Masisi centre (Nord-Kivu) par un homme armé en uniforme. Infirmier à l’hôpital général de référence de la ville, il est le second employé MSF à être tué par balle à Masisi centre en deux mois
claim_sources.translation_en: On the evening of 18 April, a Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) employee was shot dead at his home in Masisi centre (North Kivu) by an armed man in uniform. A nurse at the town's general referral hospital, he is the second MSF employee to be shot dead in Masisi centre in two months

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Le 18 avril, deux hommes en uniforme militaire armés de fusils d’assauts ont agressé et racketté des civils dans la ville de Masisi avant de faire irruption au domicile d’un employé de MSF afin d’y extorquer les biens des résidents.
claim_sources.translation_en: On 18 April, two men in military uniform armed with assault rifles assaulted and extorted civilians in the town of Masisi before bursting into the home of an MSF employee to extort the residents' belongings.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: On the evening of April 18, a Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) health worker was shot dead in his home in Masisi town, in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) by a gunman in a military uniform.
Depuis janvier, une quinzaine d’incidents ont directement touché les équipes, ambulances, bureaux et structures gérées ou soutenues par MSF.
claim_sources.translation_en: Since January, about fifteen incidents have directly affected teams, ambulances, offices and structures run or supported by MSF.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Since early 2025, MSF teams have witnessed violent incidents on an almost daily basis – and on several occasions have been injured or lost their lives.

L'escalade de la violence entre les FARDC et le M23/AFC, et leurs alliés respectifs, dans le Nord-Kivu, en République démocratique du Congo, a atteint la ville de Walikale le 19 mars, piégeant le personnel de Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) à notre base et à l'hôpital.
claim_sources.translation_en: The escalation of violence between the FARDC and the M23/AFC, and their respective allies, in North Kivu has reached Walikale town on 19 March, trapping Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) staff at our base and at the hospital.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: La violence a gravement affecté l'accès aux soins de santé, car 80 % de la population a fui la ville en entendant les tirs d'artillerie et en craignant les hostilités. Plus de 700 personnes déplacées se sont réfugiées à l'hôpital général de Walikale, ce qui accroît la pression sur des ressources médicales déjà limitées.
claim_sources.translation_en: The violence has seriously affected access to health care, as 80% of the population fled the town on hearing artillery fire and fearing hostilities. More than 700 displaced people took refuge in Walikale general hospital, increasing pressure on already limited medical resources.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Nos équipes doivent suspendre leurs activités médicales lorsque des combats éclatent et ne peuvent pas se déplacer en toute sécurité. La sécurité de notre personnel et de nos patients est notre priorité absolue », déclare Natalia Torrent, responsable des programmes de MSF au Nord-Kivu.
claim_sources.translation_en: Our teams must suspend their medical activities when fighting breaks out and cannot move safely. The safety of our staff and our patients is our top priority," said Natalia Torrent, MSF programme manager in North Kivu.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: passé sous occupation rebelle la veille, ont provoqué des déplacements massifs de populations. Certains civils ont pris la direction de Hombo dans la province du Sud-Kivu, d’autres sont allés sur l’axe Mubi-Lubutu-Kisangani, tandis que d'autres encore se sont réfugiés près de l'hôpital de Walikale alors que quelques-uns sont restés dans leurs maisons, rapportent des sources locales. Cet hôpital général et une base logistique d'une ONG ont été endommagés lors des combats, entraînant des morts et des blessés, selon des témoins.
claim_sources.translation_en: which had come under rebel occupation the day before, caused massive displacement of the population. Some civilians headed for Hombo in South Kivu province, others went along the Mubi-Lubutu-Kisangani axis, while still others took refuge near the Walikale hospital and a few stayed in their homes, local sources report. This general hospital and an NGO logistics base were damaged during the fighting, causing deaths and injuries, according to witnesses.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: La société civile de Walikale au Nord-Kivu, dénonce le pillage systématique de plusieurs hôpitaux et centres de santé par des éléments présumés de la rébellion M23 entre le 3 et le 4 avril 2025.
claim_sources.translation_en: Walikale civil society in North Kivu denounces the systematic looting of several hospitals and health centres by alleged elements of the M23 rebellion between 3 and 4 April 2025.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Ces actes ont particulièrement touché la zone de santé de Kibua, où l’hôpital général de référence et le centre de santé de Mungazi ont été dépouillés de leurs équipements biomédicaux, administratifs et médicaux.
claim_sources.translation_en: These acts particularly affected the Kibua health zone, where the general referral hospital and the Mungazi health centre were stripped of their biomedical, administrative and medical equipment.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Selon Fiston Misona, président de la coordination territoriale de la société civile, les rebelles ont démantelé les panneaux solaires, emporté les médicaments essentiels et détruit des documents administratifs. Le centre de santé de Kishanga, situé à une dizaine de kilomètres, a subi le même sort, avec le vol d’équipements énergétiques et de stocks pharmaceutiques.
claim_sources.translation_en: According to Fiston Misona, president of the territorial civil-society coordination, the rebels dismantled the solar panels, took essential medicines and destroyed administrative documents. The Kishanga health centre, about ten kilometres away, suffered the same fate, with the theft of energy equipment and pharmaceutical stocks.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Ces pillages interviennent dans un contexte où 9 structures sanitaires sur 18 dans la zone de santé de Walikale avaient déjà été saccagées entre le 17 et le 23 mars lors de l’avancée initiale du M23.
claim_sources.translation_en: These lootings come in a context where 9 of 18 health structures in the Walikale health zone had already been ransacked between 17 and 23 March during the initial M23 advance.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Lors du retrait de leur retrait de la commune rurale de Walikale au début du mois d'avril, les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 ont pillé systématiquement les structures sanitaires dans la région. Dans la zone de santé rurale de Walikale, quatre structures sanitaires ont été dépouillées de tout et peinent à se relancer.
claim_sources.translation_en: During their withdrawal from the rural commune of Walikale at the beginning of April, the AFC/M23 rebels systematically looted the health structures in the region. In the Walikale rural health zone, four health structures were stripped of everything and are struggling to restart.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Ces hôpitaux avaient été victimes d’un pillage massif en janvier dernier lors des combats entre les Forces armées de la RDC et les rebelles du M23, causant la paralysie de nombreux services et la perte du matériel médical essentiel.
claim_sources.translation_en: These hospitals had been victims of massive looting last January during fighting between the Armed Forces of the DRC and the M23 rebels, paralysing many services and causing the loss of essential medical equipment.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: l'hôpital général de Kibua appuyé en médicaments six mois après son pillage par les rebelles de l'AFC/M23
claim_sources.translation_en: the Kibua general hospital supported with medicines six months after its looting by AFC/M23 rebels

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Tous les survivants désignent des hommes armés comme auteurs des massacres, certains citant le groupe armé M23.
claim_sources.translation_en: All survivors name armed men as the perpetrators of the massacres, some citing the M23 armed group.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Bien que MSF ne soit pas en mesure de vérifier le nombre exact de victimes, 124 personnes blessées intentionnellement ont été soignées à l'hôpital général de référence de Rutshuru en juillet et août, provenant pour la plupart des zones de santé de Binza et Bambo.
claim_sources.translation_en: Although MSF is unable to verify the exact number of victims, 124 intentionally wounded people were treated at Rutshuru general referral hospital in July and August, mostly from the Binza and Bambo health zones.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Entre janvier et aout 2025, dans l'hôpital général de Rutshuru, où MSF fournit des soins médicaux et chirurgicaux, a été traité en moyenne 59 victimes de violence par mois. Cela représente une augmentation de 15 % par rapport à la même période l'année précédente
claim_sources.translation_en: Between January and August 2025, an average of 59 victims of violence per month were treated at Rutshuru general hospital, where MSF provides medical and surgical care. This is a 15% increase on the same period of the previous year

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Selon la société civile, ce conflit a provoqué la mort d’au moins 4 personnes et la disparition de 13 autres, ainsi que le viol de 8 femmes.
claim_sources.translation_en: According to civil society, this conflict caused the death of at least 4 people and the disappearance of 13 others, as well as the rape of 8 women.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Le centre de santé de Muliki a également été pillé, avec en prime le vol d’une vingtaine de bovins.
claim_sources.translation_en: The Muliki health centre was also looted, along with the theft of about twenty cattle.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Des combats violents ont opposé les rebelles de l’AFC-M23 et les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) dans les chefferies de Bwito et Bahunde, situées respectivement dans les territoires de Rutshuru et Masisi au Nord-Kivu entre le 28 septembre et le 8 octobre 2025.
claim_sources.translation_en: Violent fighting pitted the AFC-M23 rebels against the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) in the Bwito and Bahunde chiefdoms, located respectively in the Rutshuru and Masisi territories of North Kivu, between 28 September and 8 October 2025.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Le bilan de la récente attaque meurtrière des islamistes ADF à Byambwe, dans le territoire de Lubero, dans la nuit du vendredi 14 novembre, a été revu à la hausse, passant de 20 à 28 personnes tuées, dont 17 patients exécutés au centre de santé de référence de la localité.
claim_sources.translation_en: The toll of the recent deadly attack by the Islamist ADF in Byambwe, in Lubero territory, on the night of Friday 14 November, has been revised upward, from 20 to 28 people killed, including 17 patients executed at the locality's reference health centre.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Selon le colonel Kiwewa Mitela Alain, administrateur du territoire de Lubero, joint par ACTUALITÉ.CD, ce nouveau bilan découle des fouilles menées à Biambwe et dans ses environs au lendemain de l’attaque. Il précise toutefois que ces chiffres demeurent provisoires.
claim_sources.translation_en: According to colonel Kiwewa Mitela Alain, administrator of Lubero territory, reached by ACTUALITÉ.CD, this new toll results from searches carried out in Biambwe and its surroundings the day after the attack. He specifies, however, that these figures remain provisional.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: La zone de santé de Biena confirme l’attaque. Un membre du personnel soignant évoque l’incendie du pavillon de maternité et du bloc opératoire, ainsi que le pillage des médicaments. Il affirme que 17 personnes, dont quatre femmes allaitantes, ont été exécutées sur leur lit d’hôpital.
claim_sources.translation_en: The Biena health zone confirms the attack. A member of the care staff describes the burning of the maternity ward and the operating theatre, and the looting of medicines. He says that 17 people, including four breastfeeding women, were executed in their hospital beds.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Selon les informations recueillies par la Mission des Nations unies en République démocratique du Congo ( MONUSCO ), à Byambwe, 17 personnes ont été abattues dans un centre de santé, dont des patientes venues accoucher ; ailleurs, dans les localités de Mabiango, Tunarudi ou Sambalysa, des habitations ont été incendiées, des civils enlevés, des fournitures médicales pillées.
claim_sources.translation_en: According to information gathered by the United Nations Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO), at Byambwe 17 people were shot dead in a health centre, including women patients who had come to give birth; elsewhere, in the localities of Mabiango, Tunarudi or Sambalysa, homes were burned, civilians abducted and medical supplies looted.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Entre le 13 et le 19 novembre, les ADF ont tué au moins 89 civils, dont 20 femmes et un nombre encore inconnu d’enfants dans le territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu.
claim_sources.translation_en: Between 13 and 19 November, the ADF killed at least 89 civilians, including 20 women and an as yet unknown number of children, in Lubero territory, North Kivu.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Dans un communiqué de presse, António Guterres a « fermement condamné » ces attaques attribuées aux Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF), une milice originaire de l'Ouganda voisin, et exprimé ses « plus sincères condoléances aux familles et communautés endeuillées ».
claim_sources.translation_en: In a press release, António Guterres 'strongly condemned' these attacks attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a militia originating from neighbouring Uganda, and expressed his 'deepest condolences to the bereaved families and communities'.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: At around 10:00 PM local time on Friday, militants from the ADF (Allied Democratic Forces)—aligned with the so-called Islamic State since 2009—entered the town of Byambwe, in the Diocese of Butembo-Beni. They attacked a diocesan health center run by the Sisters of the Presentation, massacred patients, and then set the entire facility ablaze, killing several women in the maternity ward.

Selon le Bureau de la coordination des affaires humanitaires de l’ONU ( OCHA ), le groupe sectoriel Santé alerte sur une aggravation de l’épidémie de choléra dans et autour de Goma.
claim_sources.translation_en: According to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), the Health cluster is warning of a worsening cholera outbreak in and around Goma.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Au moins 420 cas et 1 décès ont été signalés sur deux semaines consécutives (du 3 au 15 février), soit plus d’un tiers des 1.280 cas de choléra enregistrés dans toute la province du Nord-Kivu depuis le début de l’année.
claim_sources.translation_en: At least 420 cases and 1 death were reported over two consecutive weeks (3 to 15 February), or more than a third of the 1,280 cholera cases recorded across North Kivu province since the start of the year.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: des cas suspects de choléra ont été signalés au sein du camp de la Mission de paix des Nations Unies ( MONUSCO ) à Goma, où de nombreux membres des Forces armées de RDC (FARDC) désarmés se sont réfugiés.
claim_sources.translation_en: Suspected cholera cases were reported inside the United Nations Peace Mission (MONUSCO) camp in Goma, where many disarmed members of the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) have taken refuge.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: À ce jour, un décès dû au choléra a été enregistré, tandis que 24 cas suspects sont en cours de traitement.
claim_sources.translation_en: To date, one death from cholera has been recorded, while 24 suspected cases are being treated.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Le cluster santé a alerté sur une aggravation de l'épidémie de choléra dans et autou

claim_sources.translation_en: The cluster also reports that three mpox treatment centres were destroyed in Kalehe, Minova and Miti Murhesa as a result of bombings.

claim_sources.excerpt_original: trois centres de traitement Mpox ont été détruits à Kalehe, Minova et Miti Murhesa à la suite de bombardements
claim_sources.translation_en: three Mpox treatment centres were destroyed in Kalehe, Minova and Miti Murhesa following bombings

claim_sources.excerpt_original: Aid teams from the UN World Health Organization ( WHO ) “cannot move freely to support the hospitals, even ambulances cannot run. It’s a situation that in public health is a nightmare,” said Dr Boureima Hama Sambo, WHO Representive in DRC.
Dr Sambo warned that mpox patients had fled at least one camp’s treatment centre and were now living now in host communities and with families.
Ninety percent of the mpox patients (128 of 143) in isolation units in Goma had fled for safety

During one incident, a baby in an incubator at Virunga General Hospital in Goma city was injured by an M23 fired bullet that pierced the ceiling of the neonatal unit during clashes between M23 and the Congolese army.

Insecurity Insight identified 247 incidents of violence against or obstruction of health care in 20 countries and territories between 01 January and 17 March. In these incidents, 29 health workers were killed, 59 injured, 10 kidnapped and 19 arrested.
