statements_all.translation_en: MRDP-Twirwaneho categorically rejects the FARDC accusations that Minembwe serves as a sanctuary for the Burundian RED-Tabara rebels.

statements_all.text: Rwandan Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo said, in reaction to a Human Rights Watch report, that 'the RDF is not AFC/M23' and that any proper investigation requires impartiality, access to where events happen, solid evidence, respect for the law and not announcing conclusions in advance or putting calls for sanctions first, according to Igihe.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Yakomeje yibutsa uyu muryango ko ntaho ingabo z’u Rwanda zihuriye na AFC/M23. Ati “Bikwiriye gusobanuka neza, RDF ntabwo ari AFC/M23. Iperereza ryose rikozwe neza risaba kutabogama, kugera aho ibintu bibera, ibimenyetso simusiga, kubahiriza amategeko ndetse no kudatangaza imyanzuro mbere y’igihe, cyangwa ngo ushyire imbere gusaba ibihano.”
statements_all.translation_en: She went on to remind this organisation that Rwandan forces have no connection with AFC/M23. She said: “It should be made clear, the RDF is not AFC/M23. Any properly conducted investigation requires impartiality, access to where events take place, solid evidence, respect for the law and not announcing conclusions in advance, or putting calls for sanctions first.”

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo, in a post on X, dismissed the Human Rights Watch report as part of a 30-year pattern of anonymous claims, no site visits or forensics, and 'sanctions first and investigation later'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: In a statement posted on X, Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo dismissed the report as part of a long-standing pattern in HRW's reporting on Rwanda. “Human Rights Watch on Rwanda is a 30-year pattern: anonymous claims, no site visits or forensics, sanctions first and investigation later,” Makolo wrote.

statements_all.text: According to Igihe, Makolo said that HRW itself had stated that Kinshasa arms, supports and works closely with the FDLR, Wazalendo, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian army, which she said made HRW unable to take on an impartial investigation.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ati “Muri raporo yayo iheruka, HRW ntabwo ishobora gufata inshingano (zo gukora iperereza ritabogamye) mu gihe yirengagiza bimwe mu byo yitangarije: Kinshasa iha intwaro, igatera inkunga ndetse igakorana bya hafi na FDLR, Wazalendo, abacanshuro b’abanyamahanga n’igisirikare cy’u Burundi, byose bifatwa nk’ingabo cyangwa imitwe yitwaje intwaro izingiyeho intambara n’akaga ku kiremwamuntu mu Burasirazuba bwa RDC.”
statements_all.translation_en: She said: “In its latest report, HRW cannot take on the responsibility (of conducting an impartial investigation) while ignoring some of what it itself stated: Kinshasa arms, funds and works closely with the FDLR, Wazalendo, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian army, all of which are regarded as forces or armed groups entangled in the war and in harm to humanity in eastern DRC.”

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that the Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda said that no HRW investigator set foot at the places named in the report, and that there were no visits, no exhumations for investigation and no laboratory tests.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ibiro by’Umuvugizi wa Guverinoma byatangaje ko nta mukozi n’umwe wa HRW wageze aho ibivugwa byabereye. Biti “Nta muntu ushinzwe gukora iperereza wakandagije ikirenge cye ahantu iyi raporo ivuga. Nta kuhasura byigeze bibaho, nta gutaburura imirambo hagamijwe iperereza ndetse nta bizamini by’abahanga byo muri laboratwari byigeze bikorwa.
statements_all.translation_en: The Office of the Government Spokesperson stated that not a single HRW worker had gone to where the alleged events took place. It said: “No investigator has set foot at the places this report speaks of. There has been no visit there, no exhumation of bodies for investigation and no expert laboratory tests have been carried out.”

statements_all.text: According to Igihe, the Rwandan government said HRW claims to have satellite images showing killings 'carried out by Rwandan forces and M23', with features resembling graves, but that HRW cannot confirm whether they are graves or other objects.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Guverinoma yagaragaje ko HRW ivuga ko ifite amashusho yafashwe na satellite agaragaza ubwicanyi “bwakozwe n’ingabo z’u Rwanda na M23”, agaragaza ibimeze nk’imva zashyinguwemo abapfuye, ariko ko idashora guhamya niba ari imva koko cyangwa ibindi bintu bijya kumera nka zo.
statements_all.translation_en: The government showed that HRW says it has satellite images showing killings “carried out by Rwandan forces and M23”, showing things resembling graves where the dead were buried, but that it cannot confirm whether they are graves indeed or other things that look like them.

statements_all.text: Makolo said, according to Igihe, that the sustainable solution to the conflict is to implement the Washington agreement and impartial mediation aimed at ending the war and promoting regional cooperation; the English edition quotes her as saying the Washington peace accords remain 'the path forward'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Makolo yavuze ko umuti urambye kuri iki kibazo ari ukubahiriza amasezerano ya Washington, n’ubuhuza butabogamye, hagamijwe kurangiza intambara no kwimakaza ubufatanye bw’akarere.
statements_all.translation_en: Makolo said the lasting solution to this problem is to respect the Washington agreement and impartial mediation, aimed at ending the war and promoting regional cooperation.

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that the Rwandan Office of the Government Spokesperson said HRW had not named the Congolese or Wazalendo individuals for whom it was calling for sanctions, and quoted it as saying 'HRW strongly condemns Rwanda and M23, while the support Kinshasa gives to violent armed groups is described in a deceptive/vague way'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Bagaragaza kandi ko uyu muryango nta na hamwe wigeze uvuga amazina y’Abanye-Congo cyangwa abo muri Wazalendo usabira ibihano. Biti “HRW ijora bikomeye u Rwanda na M23, mu gihe ubufasha Kinshasa iha imitwe yitwaje intwaro igira urugomo buvugwaho by’amahushuka.”
statements_all.translation_en: They also say that this organisation nowhere mentioned the names of Congolese or Wazalendo members for whom it seeks sanctions. They said: “HRW harshly criticises Rwanda and M23, while the support Kinshasa gives to violent armed groups is mentioned only superficially (in passing).”

statements_all.setting: press statement as reported by media
statements_all.text: Dépêche.cd reported that the provisional toll communicated by the army for the ADF-attributed attack on the morning of Thursday 11 June in Boikene district, Ruwenzori commune, Beni (the Munzambayi cell) was three civilians dead, one of them burned alive, and three homes burned; Lieutenant Marc Elongo, spokesperson of the Sukola 1 Grand Nord operations, said the assailants had bypassed 'the positions held strongly in depth by the FARDC-UPDF coalition'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Trois civils ont été tués lors d’une attaque attribuée aux terroristes ADF dans la matinée du jeudi 11 juin, au quartier Boikene, dans la commune de Ruwenzori, en ville de Beni, au Nord-Kivu.
statements_all.translation_en: Three civilians were killed in an attack attributed to the ADF terrorists on the morning of Thursday 11 June, in the Boikene district, in the Ruwenzori commune, in the city of Beni, in North Kivu.

statements_all.setting: communiqué and statement to press as reported
statements_all.text: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC announced they had retaken, on the morning of Wednesday 10 June, control of Mikenge, Kakenge and Kalingi in the highlands of Fizi and Mwenga territories; according to an army communiqué these localities had been occupied the previous Monday by a coalition of Twirwaneho and M23, whose assailants reportedly used military drones, and the FARDC said the recapture followed a counter-offensive of about 48 hours with Wazalendo support. Fizi territory administrator Samy Kalonji Badibanga confirmed the recapture and gave an earlier date than the communiqué for the return of Mikenge to FARDC control (see note), and said the attack of Monday 8 June was reportedly facilitated by drones attributed to AFC/M23 and by allied armed groups, notably Red Tabara and Twirwaneho.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ont annoncé avoir repris, le matin de ce mercredi 10 juin, le contrôle des localités de Mikenge, Kakenge et Kalingi, dans les hauts plateaux des territoires de Fizi et de Mwenga, au Sud-Kivu.
statements_all.translation_en: The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) announced they had retaken, on the morning of this Wednesday 10 June, control of the localities of Mikenge, Kakenge and Kalingi, in the highlands of the Fizi and Mwenga territories, in South Kivu.

statements_all.setting: communiqué and social-media post as reported
statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a communiqué that on Wednesday 10 June 2026 the "coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime", notably the FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo and elements of the Burundian national force, launched attacks against the densely populated areas of Gakenke and surroundings in the Minembwe highlands (Lulenge sector, Fizi territory); on X he said the attacks, carried out with kamikaze-type and KT-6 combat drones and heavy artillery, caused heavy loss of life, destroyed many homes and forced civilians to flee. Kivu Morning Post said no communication was possible in the zone, telephone lines and the internet being cut.
statements_all.excerpt_original: « Ce mercredi 10 juin 2026, les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa, notamment les FARDC, les FDLR, les Wazalendo et les éléments de la force nationale burundaise, ont lancé des attaques contre les zones densément peuplées de Gakenke et de ses environs
statements_all.translation_en: "This Wednesday 10 June 2026, the coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime, notably the FARDC, the FDLR, the Wazalendo and elements of the Burundian national force, launched attacks against the densely populated areas of Gakenke and its surroundings

statements_all.text: Human Rights Watch said the Rwandan government and M23 leaders have long rejected allegations of abuses but have not conducted investigations.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Le gouvernement rwandais et les dirigeants du M23 ont longtemps rejeté les allégations d’abus, mais n’ont pas mené d’enquêtes.
statements_all.translation_en: The Rwandan government and M23 leaders have long rejected the allegations of abuses, but have not carried out investigations.

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on X that the movement strongly rejects the Human Rights Watch report as 'very biased' (ibogamye cyane), selective, containing untruths and not matching realities on the ground.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Umuvugizi wa M23 Lawrence Kanyuka yatangaje ku rubuga nkoranyambaga rwa X ko uyu mutwe wamaganye ukomeje iyo raporo "ibogamye cyane", "ihitamo bamwe, irimo ibitari ukuri kandi idahuye n'ukuri kw'ibibera ku rubuga".
statements_all.translation_en: M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka stated on the social network X that the movement strongly condemned that report as "very biased", "selective, containing untruths and not matching the reality on the ground".

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Kanyuka added that the HRW report again focuses almost entirely on AFC/M23 while greatly downplaying or ignoring the very serious abuses committed by the combined forces of the Kinshasa regime, and that this approach raises serious questions about the neutrality and credibility of its conclusions.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Yongeyeho ati: "Ku yindi nshuro, uyu muryango uribanda hafi ya hose kuri AFC/M23, mu gihe ugabanya cyane cyangwa wirengagiza amahonyora akomeye cyane akorwa n'ingabo zishyize hamwe z'ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa." Kanyuka avuga ko ubwo buryo bw'imikorere bwa HRW butera kwibaza "ibibazo bikomeye ku kutabogama no ku kwizerwa kw'imyanzuro yayo" muri iyo raporo.
statements_all.translation_en: He added: "Once again, this organisation focuses almost entirely on AFC/M23, while greatly downplaying or ignoring the very serious abuses committed by the combined forces of the Kinshasa regime." Kanyuka says that HRW's way of working raises "serious questions about the neutrality and credibility of its conclusions" in that report.

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 firmly denies 'these allegations', which in the article refer to the abduction of young men and boys and their military training, and that Kanyuka said its mobilisation activities are carried out openly, without hiding them, and 'voluntarily'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: M23 ihakana ibi birego yivuye inyuma ndetse Kanyuka yavuze ko ibikorwa by'ubukangurambaga byayo ibikorera ku mugaragaro nta kubihisha kandi ko ubwo bukangurambaga bukorwa "ku bushake".
statements_all.translation_en: M23 firmly denies these allegations and Kanyuka said that it carries out its mobilisation activities openly, without hiding them, and that this mobilisation is done "voluntarily".

statements_all.setting: message to a journalist as reported
statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwanda's foreign minister Olivier Nduhungirehe replied to BBC Gahuzamiryango by WhatsApp that the Rwandan government does not respond to HRW reports of this kind, saying 'Ntacyo. Ntitujya dusubiza HRW.' (Nothing. We never respond to HRW.)
statements_all.excerpt_original: Minisitiri w'ububanyi n'amahanga w'u Rwanda Olivier Nduhungirehe yasubije BBC Gahuzamiryango mu butumwa bwo kuri WhatsApp ko leta y'u Rwanda idasubiza kuri raporo nk'izi za HRW. Yagize ati: "Ntacyo. Ntitujya dusubiza HRW."
statements_all.translation_en: Rwanda's minister of foreign affairs Olivier Nduhungirehe replied to BBC Gahuzamiryango in a WhatsApp message that the Rwandan government does not respond to HRW reports like these. He said: "Nothing. We never respond to HRW."

statements_all.role: lieutenant-colonel, interim spokesperson of the army
statements_all.text: Radio Okapi reported that at a press conference in Kinshasa on Saturday 6 June the army's interim spokesperson, Lieutenant-Colonel Mak Hazukay, firmly denounced the continuation of attacks despite ongoing diplomatic initiatives, and that, according to the military authorities, several localities of North Kivu and the highlands of Fizi and Uvira in South Kivu continued to be the scene of attacks.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Lors d’une conference de presse tenu samedi 6 juin à Kinshasa, le porte-parole intérimaire de l’armée, le lieutenant-colonel Mak Hazukay, a fermement dénoncé la poursuite des attaques malgré les initiatives diplomatiques en cours.
statements_all.translation_en: At a press conference held Saturday 6 June in Kinshasa, the army's interim spokesperson, Lieutenant-Colonel Mak Hazukay, firmly denounced the continuation of attacks despite the diplomatic initiatives under way.

statements_all.text: Radio Okapi reported that a communiqué published on Thursday 4 June 2026 by the spokesperson of the 34th military region, Major Dieudonné Kasereka, said that 204 AFC-M23 rebels had surrendered to the FARDC and their allies in Lubero, Rutshuru and Masisi (North Kivu) in waves during April and May.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Au total, 204 rebelles de l’AFC-M23 se rendent aux Forces armée de la République démocratique du Congo et leurs alliés à Lubero, Rutshuru et Masisi (Nord-Kivu). Ces redditions volontaires se sont effectuées par vagues successives aux mois d’avril et mai derniers, explique un communiqué publié jeudi 4 juin 2026 par le porte-parole de la 34ᵉ région militaire, le major Dieudonné Kasereka.
statements_all.translation_en: In total, 204 AFC-M23 rebels are surrendering to the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo and their allies in Lubero, Rutshuru and Masisi (North Kivu). These voluntary surrenders took place in successive waves in April and May, a communiqué published Thursday 4 June 2026 by the spokesperson of the 34th military region, Major Dieudonné Kasereka, explains.

statements_all.text: Presse Actu reported that AFC-M23 rejected, on Thursday 4 June 2026, FARDC accusations implicating it in the summary execution of ten civilians in the locality of Kiseguru, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu; in a 'mise au point' the rebel movement called them 'allégations mensongères, infondées et politiquement motivées' (false, unfounded and politically motivated allegations).
statements_all.excerpt_original: L’Alliance Fleuve Congo-M23 (AFC-M23) a rejeté, ce jeudi 4 juin 2026, les accusations des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) l’impliquant dans l’exécution sommaire de dix civils dans la localité de Kiseguru, en territoire de Rutshuru, au Nord-Kivu
statements_all.translation_en: The Alliance Fleuve Congo-M23 (AFC-M23) rejected, on Thursday 4 June 2026, the accusations of the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) implicating it in the summary execution of ten civilians in the locality of Kiseguru, in Rutshuru territory, North Kivu

statements_all.text: The U.S. Department of the Treasury stated that, following the 15 November 2025 signing in Qatar of a peace framework agreement between the DRC government and M23, M23 seized Uvira and later withdrew, while still controlling Goma and Bukavu.
statements_all.excerpt_original: On November 15, 2025, the DRC government and M23 signed a peace framework agreement in Qatar. Following the signing, M23 seized the strategic port city of Uvira located in South Kivu province along the DRC-Burundi border. Although M23 eventually withdrew from Uvira, the rebel group still controls Goma and Bukavu,

statements_all.text: The US State Department said on 2 June 2026 that it was designating John Imani Nzenze, chief of intelligence for the Rwanda-backed M23, 'an armed group that has committed killings, serious human rights abuses, and attacks on civilians in eastern DRC', and Gustave Kubwayo, commander of an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit, saying the FDLR had 'committed sexual violence'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: We are designating Gustave Kubwayo, commander of an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit. The FDLR has carried out ethnic violence against civilians, used child soldiers, committed sexual violence, and launched cross-border attacks that continue to threaten Rwanda’s security.

statements_all.text: The US State Department spokesperson said that the United States was designating Gustave Kubwayo, commander of an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit, and said the FDLR has carried out ethnic violence against civilians, used child soldiers, committed sexual violence and launched cross-border attacks.
statements_all.excerpt_original: We are designating Gustave Kubwayo, commander of an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit. The FDLR has carried out ethnic violence against civilians, used child soldiers, committed sexual violence, and launched cross-border attacks that continue to threaten Rwanda’s security.

statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué, AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the whole of May 2026 was marked by intensified land and air offensives by the 'coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime' against densely populated areas and its positions, notably at Minembwe, Masisi, Numbi and Walikale, and that any attack would now receive a proportionate response; the outlet added that other fighting was reported on the Kibati axis, on the border of Walikale and Masisi territories, with AFC-M23 accusing the army of attacking its areas with heavy artillery.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Selon Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole de l’AFC-M23, toute attaque recevra désormais une réponse proportionnée et les forces du mouvement éloigneront la menace au-delà de leurs positions de départ.
statements_all.translation_en: According to Lawrence Kanyuka, spokesperson of the AFC-M23, any attack will now receive a proportionate response and the movement's forces will keep the threat away beyond their starting positions.

statements_all.setting: statement as reported by The Guardian
statements_all.text: The Guardian reported that the military governor of North Kivu said in a statement on Tuesday that three patients confirmed to have Ebola had fled treatment centres in Beni after the Saturday attacks.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The military governor of North Kivu said in a statement on Tuesday that three patients confirmed to have Ebola had fled treatment centres in Beni after Saturday’s attacks.

statements_all.text: The Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda published a response to a Human Rights Watch report, stating that Rwanda rejects HRW's allegations of RDF involvement in forced recruitment, detention, torture, executions, forced labor, or child recruitment, and rejects HRW's attempt to collapse M23 and RDF into one actor.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Rwanda rejects HRW’s allegations of RDF involvement in forced recruitment, detention, torture, executions, forced labor, or child recruitment. Rwanda also rejects HRW’s attempt to collapse M23 and RDF into one actor.

statements_all.role: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
statements_all.setting: interview with France 24 (Marc Perelman), as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe warned the United States, according to Igihe, that its biased sanctions cannot resolve the conflict between Rwanda and the DRC and instead inflame it.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Minisitiri w’Ububanyi n’Amahanga n’Ubutwererane, Ambasaderi Olivier Nduhungirehe, yaburiye Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika ko ibihano byayo bibogamye bidashobora gukemura amakimbirane ari hagati y’u Rwanda na Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, ahubwo ko biyenyegeza.
statements_all.translation_en: The Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, warned the United States of America that its biased sanctions cannot resolve the conflict between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, but that they fuel it.

statements_all.role: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
statements_all.setting: interview with France 24 (Marc Perelman), as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Nduhungirehe said, in a France 24 interview with Marc Perelman reported by Igihe, that the Washington agreement had not produced results because the DRC government kept breaching the ceasefire, kept helping the FDLR, and was hosting opponents of the Rwandan government, including Juvénal Habyarimana's son Jean Luc Habyarimana.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Mu kiganiro n’umunyamakuru Marc Perelman wa France 24, Minisitiri Nduhungirehe yagaragaje ko amasezerano ya Washington atatanze umusaruro kubera ko Leta ya RDC yakomeje kurenga ku gahenge, inakomeza gufasha umutwe wa FDLR, anakira abarwanya Leta y’u Rwanda barimo umuhungu wa Juvénal Habyarimana witwa Jean Luc Habyarimana.
statements_all.translation_en: In an interview with France 24 journalist Marc Perelman, Minister Nduhungirehe showed that the Washington agreement had not produced results because the DRC government continued to breach the ceasefire, continued to help the FDLR, and received opponents of the Rwandan government including Juvénal Habyarimana's son named Jean Luc Habyarimana.

statements_all.role: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
statements_all.setting: interview with France 24 (Marc Perelman), as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Nduhungirehe said, according to Igihe, that on 5 June 2026 US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told legislators that Rwanda was complying with the Washington agreement while the DRC government had done nothing, which he said showed weak political will.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Minisitiri Nduhungirehe yavuze ko tariki ya 5 Kamena 2026, Minisitiri w’Ububanyi n’Amahanga wa Amerika, Marco Rubio, yemereye abadepite ko u Rwanda ruri kubahiriza aya masezerano, ariko ko Leta ya RDC yo ntacyo yakoze; ibishimangira ubushake buke bwa politiki.
statements_all.translation_en: Minister Nduhungirehe said that on 5 June 2026 the US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, acknowledged to members of the House [of Representatives] that Rwanda is complying with this agreement, but that the DRC government has done nothing; which confirms weak political will.

statements_all.role: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
statements_all.setting: interview with France 24 (Marc Perelman), as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Nduhungirehe reminded Perelman, per Igihe, that Massad Boulos, an adviser to Trump, had told the UN security council that the government of RDC (as Igihe writes it) had not dismantled the FDLR, at least in the areas it controls; the sentence goes on that this showed the reason Rwanda is the one still being punished is not understandable.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Yibukije Perelman ko ku 26 Kamena 2026, Umujyanama wa Perezida Trump mu bijyanye n’ubufatanye na Afurika, Massad Boulos, yabwiye Akanama k’Umuryango w’Abibumbye gashinzwe umutekano ko Leta ya RDC itigeze isenya FDLR byibura mu bice igenzura, agaragaza ko impamvu u Rwanda ari rwo rukomeje guhanwa itumvikana.
statements_all.translation_en: He reminded Perelman that on 26 June 2026, President Trump's adviser on cooperation with Africa, Massad Boulos, told the UN Security Council that the DRC government has never dismantled the FDLR at least in the areas it controls, showing that the reason Rwanda is the one continuing to be punished is not understandable.

statements_all.role: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
statements_all.setting: interview with France 24 (Marc Perelman), as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Nduhungirehe said, according to Igihe, that DRC forces had also launched attacks on various areas controlled by AFC/M23 and MRDP Twirwaneho, killing many civilians, and asked how many civilians must die before it is understood that the DRC should respect the ceasefire.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Minisitiri Nduhungirehe yagaragaje ko ingabo za RDC zanagabye igitero mu bice bitandukanye bigenzurwa n’ihuriro AFC/M23 n’umutwe wa MRDP Twirwanehomuri, zica abasivili benshi, abaza ati “None ni abasivili bangahe bagomba gupfa kugira ngo twumve ko RDC ikwiye kubahiriza agahenge?”
statements_all.translation_en: Minister Nduhungirehe showed that DRC forces had also launched an attack in various areas controlled by the AFC/M23 alliance and the MRDP Twirwanehomuri group, killing many civilians, asking: "So how many civilians must die for us to understand that the DRC should respect the ceasefire?"

statements_all.role: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
statements_all.setting: interview with France 24 (Marc Perelman), as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Nduhungirehe said, according to Igihe, that the US sanctions on Gasabo Refinery, its head and other mining companies on 25 June could bring no solution between Rwanda and the DRC and were biased, adding that sanctions are not a mediator's role.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ku bihano Amerika yafatiye Gasabo Refinery, umuyobozi wayo n’izindi sosiyete z’ubucukuzi bw’amabuye y’agaciro tariki ya 25 Kamena, Minisitiri Nduhungirehe yagaragaje ko nta gisubizo bishobora kuzana hagati y’u Rwanda na RDC. Yagize ati “Mbere na mbere, ibi bihano birabogamye. Bibogamira ku ruhande rumwe kandi nta musaruro byatanga. Gutanga ibihano si inshingano y’umuhuza.
statements_all.translation_en: On the sanctions America imposed on Gasabo Refinery, its head and other mineral mining companies on 25 June, Minister Nduhungirehe showed that they can bring no solution between Rwanda and the DRC. He said: "First of all, these sanctions are biased. They lean to one side and would yield no result. Imposing sanctions is not the mediator's role.

statements_all.role: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
statements_all.setting: interview with France 24 (Marc Perelman), as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Nduhungirehe said, according to Igihe, that the effects of bias had begun to show because DRC forces had stepped up attacks on the Banyamulenge in Minembwe commune and on AFC/M23 positions, since President Tshisekedi saw that the US would not penalise him.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Yagize ati “Mbere na mbere, ibi bihano birabogamye. Bibogamira ku ruhande rumwe kandi nta musaruro byatanga. Gutanga ibihano si inshingano y’umuhuza. Niba umuhuza abona ko gufata ibihano ari ngombwa, kubifatira uruhande rumwe byoshya urundi.” Minisitiri Nduhungirehe yakomeje ati “Ariko ku rundi ruhande, tubwira umuhuza wa Amerika ko twagiranye amasezerano n’uruhande rwitwa RDC, rwemeye guhagarika imirwano no gusenya FDLR. Amahoro ntiyaboneka mu gihe uruhande rumwe ari rwo rwubahiriza ibyo rusabwa mu masezerano.” Yagaragaje ko ingaruka zo kubogama zatangiye kugaragara kuko ingabo za RDC zenyegeje ibitero ku Banyamulenge muri Komini Minembwe no ku birindiro bya AFC/M23 kubera ko Perezida Félix Tshisekedi yabonye ko Amerika ntacyo imutwara.
statements_all.translation_en: He showed that the effects of bias had begun to appear because DRC forces had stepped up attacks on the Banyamulenge in Minembwe commune and on AFC/M23 positions because President Félix Tshisekedi saw that America would do nothing to him.

statements_all.role: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
statements_all.setting: interview with France 24 (Marc Perelman), as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Nduhungirehe said, according to Igihe, that the US had set no deadline for Rwanda to lift its defensive measures and that Rwanda itself had offered an idea of how both sides could speed up implementation of the Washington agreement; Igihe adds that Rubio told legislators he was confident Rwanda would lift them by mid-July 2026.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Muri icyo kiganiro n’abadepite, Minisitiri Rubio yababwiye ko afite icyizere ko hagati muri Nyakanga 2026, u Rwanda ruzaba rwakuyeho ingamba z’ubwirinzi rwashyizeho. Minisitiri Nduhungirehe yasobanuye ko ibyo byashingiye ku gitekerezo u Rwanda rwatanze. Ati “Icya mbere, nta gihe ntarengwa cyatanzwe na Amerika. Ni twebwe u Rwanda, mu rwego rwo kwihutisha ishyirwa mu bikorwa amasezerano y’amahoro ya Washington agamije amahoro n’iterambere, twatanze igitekerezo cy’uburyo impande zombi zakwihutisha gushyira mu bikorwa ibyo ziyemeje.”
statements_all.translation_en: In that meeting with the legislators, Minister Rubio told them that he was confident that by mid-July 2026 Rwanda would have lifted the defensive measures it had put in place. Minister Nduhungirehe explained that this was based on an idea that Rwanda put forward.

statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a statement on X, accused government forces of 'un bombardement criminel et indiscriminé' on Rumangabo; he said it took place on Sunday 24 May 2026 at 07h35 against the densely populated area of Rumangabo and the eco-guards camp of Virunga National Park, using CH-4 combat drones.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Dans une déclaration publiée sur son compte X, le porte-parole de l’AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, a accusé les forces gouvernementales d’avoir mené « un bombardement criminel et indiscriminé » contre Rumangabo.
statements_all.translation_en: In a statement published on his X account, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka accused government forces of carrying out 'a criminal and indiscriminate bombing' against Rumangabo.

statements_all.person: Roger Samuel Kamba ; Dr Aimé Alengo
statements_all.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to the South Kivu provincial health division chief Dr Aimé Alengo, the focus of the Ebola outbreak in South Kivu was in the Miti-Murhesa health zone of Kabare; Radio Okapi said the zone lies in a region affected by insecurity linked to armed groups, notably the AFC/M23 rebellion, which further complicates the response, and that Health Minister Roger Samuel Kamba announced diplomatic initiatives aimed at guaranteeing secure humanitarian and health access to areas under armed-group control.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Elle se trouve également dans une région affectée par l’insécurité liée à la présence de groupes armés, notamment la rébellion AFC/M23, ce qui complique davantage la mise en œuvre des actions de riposte sanitaire.
statements_all.translation_en: It is also in a region affected by insecurity linked to the presence of armed groups, notably the AFC/M23 rebellion, which further complicates the implementation of the health response.

statements_all.text: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that AFC/M23 said FDLR fighters, together with Wazalendo, killed 10 residents in Masisi and Walikale territories; AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the attack was launched in the Malemo and Kalembe area, on the Masisi-Walikale border, in the night of 24 May 2026, and that in Malemo they killed three civilians, wounded six and abducted the local leader, whose fate was still unknown.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yatangaje ko iki gitero cyagabwe mu gace ka Malemo na Kalembe ku rugabano rwa Masisi na Walikale mu ijoro ryo ku wa 24 Gicurasi 2026.
statements_all.translation_en: AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka announced that this attack was launched in the Malemo and Kalembe area on the border of Masisi and Walikale in the night of 24 May 2026.

statements_all.text: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23, in a statement issued by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, said that around 22:00 on the night of Sunday 24 May 2026 FDLR fighters supported by Wazalendo attacked the villages of Malemo and Kalembe between Masisi and Walikale; Kanyuka said seven civilians were killed and three seriously injured at Malemo, and three killed, nine injured and a village chief abducted at Kalembe, and that the fighters looted 11 cows and many pigs at Bweru.
statements_all.excerpt_original: AFC/M23 mu itangazo ryasohowe n'umuvugizi wayo, Lawrence Kanyuka, yavuze ko ibyo bitero byabaye mu ijoro ryo ku Cyumweru tariki ya 24 Gicurasi 2026, ahagana saa yine z’ijoro.
statements_all.translation_en: AFC/M23, in a statement issued by its spokesperson, Lawrence Kanyuka, said the attacks took place on the night of Sunday 24 May 2026, at about ten o'clock at night.

statements_all.role: AFC/M23 statement as reported (spokesperson not named in the excerpt)
statements_all.setting: communiqué as reported by SOS Médias Burundi
statements_all.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that in a statement issued on 24 May the AFC/M23 accused the DRC Armed Forces and their allies of conducting air strikes in North Kivu and South Kivu, claiming that Rumangabo (Rutshuru) and the Virunga National Park eco-guards camp were targeted by CH-4 drones, and recalling bombings in Minembwe and Kalehe causing civilian casualties; the AFC/M23 described the operations as "war crimes". SOS Médias added that at the time of publication no official response from the Congolese authorities had been made public and that the information could not be independently verified.
statements_all.excerpt_original: In a statement issued on May 24, the AFC/M23 accused the DRC Armed Forces and their allies of conducting a series of air strikes in North Kivu and South Kivu. The movement claims that Rumangabo, in Rutshuru territory, as well as the camp of the eco-guards of the Virunga National Park, were allegedly targeted by CH-4 fighter drones.

statements_all.text: FNTV reported on 23 May 2026 that, after checking with several local sources and Wazalendo movements, it could give a clear denial that General Bernard Byamungu of the AFC/M23 had died: the man killed in the drone attack was a Wazalendo commander with the same name, colonel Byamungu Ruduga Abdallah, active in the Uvira high plateaux.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Après vérification auprès de plusieurs sources locales et de mouvements Wazalendo, nous sommes en mesure d’apporter un démenti clair : le général Bernard Byamungu est vivant. L’homme décédé dans cette attaque n’est pas le cadre militaire de l’AFC/M23, mais un commandant Wazalendo portant le même nom : le colonel Byamungu Ruduga Abdallah, actif dans les hauts plateaux d’Uvira.
statements_all.translation_en: After checking with several local sources and Wazalendo movements, we are able to provide a clear denial: General Bernard Byamungu is alive. The man who died in this attack is not the AFC/M23 military cadre, but a Wazalendo commander bearing the same name: colonel Byamungu Ruduga Abdallah, active in the high plateaux of Uvira.

statements_all.text: Africa-Infos.cd reported that in its press communiqué n°13 of 20 May 2026 the FARDC denounced attacks attributed to a coalition of the RDF and the AFC/M23 in several localities of Minembwe, said that several drone strikes targeted Kalingi and Mikenge in the Minembwe highlands from the first hours of the morning, and said that the Mikenge General Hospital was reportedly "intentionally targeted" and then completely destroyed.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Dans ce communiqué de presse n°13, les FARDC affirment que plusieurs frappes de drones ont visé dès les premières heures de la matinée les localités de Kalingi et Mikenge, dans les hauts plateaux de Minembwe.
statements_all.translation_en: In this press communiqué n°13, the FARDC state that several drone strikes hit the localities of Kalingi and Mikenge from the first hours of the morning, in the Minembwe highlands.

statements_all.text: Mediacongo, carrying a piece credited 'Patrick Kitoko, Opinion Info / MCP', reported that, according to a FARDC communiqué of 20 May 2026, the Mikenge general hospital was reportedly 'intentionally targeted' and 'completely destroyed' during drone strikes that hit localities including Kalingi and Mikenge in the early morning, with a provisional toll of several civilian victims that reportedly included hospital staff members. FARDC also accused Rwanda and its 'proxies' of being behind the offensive. The communiqué was signed by FARDC acting spokesperson Lieutenant-Colonel Mongba Hazukay Mak. Africa-Infos.cd (21 May) reported the same communiqué, no. 13.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Selon les FARDC, l’hôpital général de Mikenge aurait été « intentionnellement ciblé » et « complètement détruit » lors de ces attaques.
statements_all.translation_en: According to FARDC, the Mikenge general hospital was reportedly 'intentionally targeted' and 'completely destroyed' during these attacks.

statements_all.text: Dépêche.cd reported that FARDC military intelligence services announced in Beni the interception of a truck carrying several sacks of hemp and that, according to the Congolese army, the cargo allegedly belonged to an AFC-M23 commander identified as Zimurinda Innocent, based in Rutshuru territory.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Par ailleurs, les services de renseignements militaires ont annoncé l’interception d’un camion transportant plusieurs sacs de chanvre. Selon l’armée congolaise, cette cargaison appartiendrait à un commandant de l’AFC-M23 identifié comme Zimurinda Innocent, basé dans le territoire de Rutshuru.
statements_all.translation_en: Moreover, military intelligence services announced the interception of a truck carrying several sacks of hemp. According to the Congolese army, this cargo allegedly belonged to an AFC-M23 commander identified as Zimurinda Innocent, based in Rutshuru territory.

statements_all.text: Dépêche.cd reported that the FARDC presented in Beni, on Tuesday, 'plusieurs personnes accusées de collaborer avec les rebelles de l'AFC-M23', among them Byamungu Zembezembe Jean-Pierre, from South Kivu, arrested in the Matongé district in central Beni; Matofali Bushu Arsène, described by the army as a member of the armed group FFPP/AP of Kabido; and a young woman, Kavira Léa, whom the military authorities say was recruited by Katembo Ndalieni, former mayor of Goma under the rebel administration.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ont présenté, mardi à Beni, dans la province du Nord-Kivu, plusieurs personnes accusées de collaborer avec les rebelles de l’AFC-M23.
statements_all.translation_en: The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) presented, on Tuesday in Beni, in North Kivu province, several people accused of collaborating with the AFC-M23 rebels.

statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC-M23 confirmed that a case of Ebola virus disease had been reported in Goma, an announcement made on Sunday 17 May 2026 by its spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka.
statements_all.excerpt_original: L’AFC-M23 confirme qu’un cas de Maladie à virus Ebola a été signalé à Goma, dans la province du Nord-Kivu. L’annonce a été faite ce dimanche 17 mai 2026 par Lawrence Kanyuka, chef du département de la communication et porte-parole de la rébellion AFC/M23.
statements_all.translation_en: The AFC-M23 confirms that a case of Ebola virus disease has been reported in Goma, North Kivu province. The announcement was made this Sunday 17 May 2026 by Lawrence Kanyuka, head of the communication department and spokesperson of the AFC/M23 rebellion.

statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that from 08:00 on Friday 15 May 2026 Kinshasa had ordered the deployment of heavily armed combat helicopters from Kalemie to join strikes on Minembwe and surroundings, in addition to combat drones, heavy artillery and Sukhoi-25 jets. Fighting was reported at Kakenge, Kalonge, Bidegu and Kalingi (Fizi) and at Mikenge (Mwenga).
statements_all.excerpt_original: “Depuis 8h00 ce vendredi 15 mai 2026, le régime de Kinshasa a ordonné le déploiement massif d’hélicoptères de combat lourdement armés en provenance de Kalemie afin de participer aux frappes en cours contre Minembwe et ses environs.
statements_all.translation_en: “Since 08:00 this Friday 15 May 2026, the Kinshasa regime has ordered the massive deployment of heavily armed combat helicopters from Kalemie to take part in the ongoing strikes against Minembwe and its surroundings.

statements_all.role: head of communication department and spokesperson
statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23, in a clarification of Friday 15 May by its spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, questioned the credibility, impartiality and objectivity of the Human Rights Watch report on Uvira, said its withdrawal from Uvira took place in broad daylight and calmly, and attributed the abuses in Uvira to a government coalition of FARDC, FNDB, FDLR, Wazalendo and foreign mercenaries.
statements_all.excerpt_original: En réaction, le mouvement politico-militaire Alliance Fleuve Congo-AFC/M23 s’est montré critique à l’égard de ce rapport, affirmant qu’il suscite de sérieuses interrogations quant à sa crédibilité, son impartialité et son objectivité.
statements_all.translation_en: In reaction, the political-military movement Alliance Fleuve Congo-AFC/M23 was critical of this report, saying it raises serious questions about its credibility, its impartiality and its objectivity.

statements_all.role: head of communication department and spokesperson
statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that in a clarification by Lawrence Kanyuka, head of communication and spokesperson of AFC/M23, the movement said the latest Human Rights Watch report on Uvira raised serious questions about its credibility, impartiality and objectivity and was strongly influenced by the political narrative of the Kinshasa regime, and attributed the abuses committed in Uvira to a government coalition of FARDC, FNDB, FDLR, Wazalendo and foreign mercenaries.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Elle les présente comme démontrant l’ampleur des exactions commises à Uvira non pas par ses éléments, mais, selon Lawrence Kanyuka, par la coalition gouvernementale composée des FARDC, des FNDB, des FDLR, des Wazalendo et de mercenaires étrangers.
statements_all.translation_en: It presents them as showing the scale of the abuses committed in Uvira not by its elements but, according to Lawrence Kanyuka, by the government coalition made up of the FARDC, FNDB, FDLR, Wazalendo and foreign mercenaries.

statements_all.role: Office of the Government Spokesperson (OGS) fact-checking library
statements_all.setting: written response published on the government spokesperson office website
statements_all.text: The Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda published a "response" to the Human Rights Watch report of 14 May 2026, saying that the 14 May report claimed that the M23 and Rwandan forces, and no longer the Wazalendo, were the principal threat to the civilians covered in HRW's January 2026 statement, and that the conduct of the FARDC and Wazalendo in Uvira and the surrounding territory had not been the subject of a comparable 23-page investigative report.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Four months later, on 14 May 2026, HRW published a report claiming that it was instead the M23 and Rwandan forces, and no longer the Wazalendo, who were the principal threat to the same civilians it had reported on in its January 2026 statement.

statements_all.text: The BBC reported that Human Rights Watch said it wrote in April to both the Rwandan government and M23 leaders for a response to the allegations in its Uvira report and that neither replied; the BBC noted that Rwanda has consistently denied supporting the M23 or that its own soldiers have been deployed to eastern DR Congo.
statements_all.excerpt_original: HRW says it wrote in April to both the Rwandan government and M23 leaders for a response to the allegations in its report, but, it adds, neither replied.

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that Rwandan Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo said on X on 14 May 2026 that 'HRW has a way of working and Rwanda is always its yardstick showing it has worked well'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ubutumwe bwa Makolo bwanyuze ku rubuga X kuri uyu wa 14 Gicurasi 2026, bugira buti “HRW ifite uburyo ikora kandi u Rwanda ruhora ari igipimo cyayo kigaragaza ko yakoze neza.”
statements_all.translation_en: Makolo's message, which went through the X platform on this 14 May 2026, reads: “HRW has a way of working and Rwanda is always its yardstick showing that it has worked well.”

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that the Rwandan government has often told the international community that none of its troops are in eastern DRC and that it only put defensive measures on the border.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ni kenshi Leta y’u Rwanda yagaragarije umuryango mpuzamahanga ko nta ngabo zarwo ziri mu burasirazuba bwa RDC, isobanura ko icyo rwakoze ari ugushyira ingamba z’ubwirinzi ku mupaka kugira ngo ibibazo byo muri iki gihugu cy’abaturanyi bitarugeramo.
statements_all.translation_en: The Rwandan State has often shown the international community that none of its troops are in eastern DRC, explaining that what it did was to put defensive measures on the border so that the problems of this neighbouring country do not reach it.

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwanda had continued to deny backing M23 or deploying its soldiers in eastern DRC, and that M23 and the Rwandan government did not respond to the BBC's request for comment on HRW's findings on Uvira.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Urwanda rwagumye ruhakana ko rushigikiye M23 canke ko abasirikare barwo barungitswe mu buseruko bwa RD Congo, igihugu kirangwamwo amabuye y'agaciro menshi . Ariko HRW ivuga ko benshi mu bo yabajije bavuze ko babonye amahano yakozwe n'abasirikare b'Urwanda bambaye umwambaro ubaranga hamwe n'abarwanyi ba M23.
statements_all.translation_en: Rwanda has continued to deny that it backs M23 or that its soldiers were sent to eastern DR Congo, a country rich in minerals. But HRW says that many of those it interviewed said they saw atrocities committed by Rwandan soldiers in uniform and by M23 fighters.

statements_all.text: Umuryango.rw (Rwandan outlet) reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo, in a post on X on 14 May 2026, criticised Human Rights Watch, writing (in the outlet's Kinyarwanda rendering) that HRW has its way of working and Rwanda is always its measure showing that it has worked well. The outlet described the HRW report of 13 May as accusing Rwandan soldiers and fighters of the armed group M23 of killing civilians, abducting them and raping women in the city of Uvira from 10 December 2025 to 17 January 2026.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Umuvugizi wa Guverinoma y’u Rwanda, Yolande Makolo, yagaragaje ko umuryango Human Rights Watch uharanira uburenganzira bw’ikiremwamuntu utavuze ku Rwanda, akazi kawo katagaragara. Ubutumwe bwa Makolo bwanyuze ku rubuga X kuri uyu wa 14 Gicurasi 2026, bugira buti “HRW ifite uburyo ikora kandi u Rwanda ruhora ari igipimo cyayo kigaragaza ko yakoze neza.”
statements_all.translation_en: The spokesperson of the Government of Rwanda, Yolande Makolo, showed that the human rights organisation Human Rights Watch, if it does not speak about Rwanda, its work is not visible. Makolo's message on X on this 14 May 2026 reads: “HRW has its way of working and Rwanda is always its measure showing that it has worked well.”

statements_all.role: Office of the Government Spokesperson (OGS) fact-checking library
statements_all.setting: written response published on the government spokesperson office website
statements_all.text: The Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda published a response to a post by Muyaya and to an HRW report, saying that nowhere in the HRW document is Rwanda attributed responsibility for the mass graves, and that the same report documents summary executions and sexual violence by the FARDC and Wazalendo against South Kivu populations before and during their withdrawal from Uvira.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Nowhere in this document is Rwanda attributed responsibility for the mass graves. The report itself acknowledges that it is “difficult to know exactly who is buried in all the graves, when they were buried, and how they died.”

statements_all.role: described by DW as the South Kivu governor based in Uvira
statements_all.setting: press statement to journalists, as reported
statements_all.text: DW (Swahili) reported that Jean-Jacques Elakano, speaking to journalists in Uvira, said the government feared AFC/M23 rebels were using trade and family travel between Bukavu and Uvira to infiltrate areas controlled by the government army; a DW photo caption said the governor of South Kivu, based in Uvira, had said travel would stay suspended until the rebels left Bukavu.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Akizungumza mbele ya wanahabari mjini Uvira, Jean-Jacques Elakano amesema serikali inahofia kuwa waasi wa AFC/M23 wanatumia shughuli za biashara na safari za kifamilia kati ya Bukavu na Uvira kujipenyeza katika maeneo yanayodhibitiwa na jeshi la serikali.
statements_all.translation_en: Speaking before journalists in Uvira, Jean-Jacques Elakano said the government fears that AFC/M23 rebels are using trade and family trips between Bukavu and Uvira to infiltrate areas controlled by the government army.

statements_all.setting: army claim as reported by media
statements_all.text: DW (Swahili) reported that the Congolese army said the AFC/M23 rebels had left the villages of Nyakabere, Mutarule and Luberizi, a claim that DW said AFC/M23 had not confirmed so far.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Jeshi la Kongo pia limesema waasi hao wameondoka katika vijiji vya Nyakabere, Mutarule na Luberizi, madai ambayo hadi sasa hayajathibitishwa na AFC/M23.
statements_all.translation_en: The Congolese army also said the rebels left the villages of Nyakabere, Mutarule and Luberizi, claims that so far have not been confirmed by AFC/M23.

statements_all.role: deputy governor of North Kivu for economy and finance, per Umuryango.rw
statements_all.setting: ceremony statement, as reported by Umuryango.rw
statements_all.text: Umuryango.rw reported that on 11 May CADECO, a bank opened by AFC/M23 after the Congolese government closed banks in the areas the group controls, opened two counters in Goma at a ceremony led by the AFC/M23 deputy governor of North Kivu for economy and finance, Shadrack Amani.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Banki ya CADECO yafunguwe na AFC/M23 nyuma y’uko Leta ya Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo yari imaze gufunga amabanki yo mu bice uriya mutwe ugenzura, yatangiye gutanga Serivisi z’imari ku batuye mu mujyi wa Goma.
statements_all.translation_en: The CADECO bank, opened by AFC/M23 after the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo had closed banks in the areas that group controls, has started providing financial services to residents of Goma city.

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye said in an interview with Jeune Afrique published on 10 May 2026 that the closure of the Gatumba and Vugizo border crossings with the DRC was linked to the proximity of M23 fighters near Burundi's borders, alleging that M23 operates with Rwanda's backing.
statements_all.excerpt_original: In an interview with Jeune Afrique published on May 10, 2026, Ndayishimiye discussed the closure of the Gatumba and Vugizo border crossings between Burundi and DR Congo on the South Kivu side. He claimed the decision was linked to the proximity of M23 fighters near Burundi’s borders, alleging that the group operates with Rwanda’s backing.

statements_all.text: According to Igihe, Ndayishimiye said that Burundi considers the presence of M23 fighters near its borders a security concern and expressed hope that the Washington peace agreement would increase pressure to end the tensions.
statements_all.excerpt_original: According to Ndayishimiye, Burundi considers the presence of M23 fighters near its borders as a security concern, although he expressed hope that the Washington peace agreement would increase pressure aimed at ending the tensions.

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye maintained that Burundian troops were sent to the DRC to assist Congolese forces against their enemies rather than to defend Burundi itself, under regional arrangements that assigned South Kivu as Burundi's operational zone.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ndayishimiye maintained that Burundian troops were sent to DR Congo to assist Congolese forces against their enemies rather than to defend Burundi itself. He explained that the deployment was carried out under regional arrangements that assigned South Kivu as Burundi’s operational zone.

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye argued that fighting continued despite regional efforts because some countries failed to contain the conflict, and that only Uganda and Burundi remained actively engaged, with Burundian troops operating under the directives of the Congolese army.
statements_all.excerpt_original: He further argued that despite efforts by regional actors, fighting continued because some countries failed to contain the conflict. According to him, only Uganda and Burundi remained actively engaged, with Burundian troops operating under the directives of the Congolese army.

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye repeated accusations that Rwanda supports RED Tabara, a group Burundi describes as terrorist, and that Rwanda has consistently denied this, insisting it does not support any group seeking to destabilize Burundi.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The Burundian leader also repeated accusations that Rwanda supports RED Tabara, a group Burundi describes as a terrorist organization responsible for attacks inside the country. Rwanda has consistently denied the allegations, insisting that it does not support any group seeking to destabilize Burundi.

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that, asked about Rwanda's accusation that Burundi collaborates with the FDLR, Ndayishimiye said he had asked President Paul Kagame for intelligence on FDLR positions and that Burundi would attack the group if given such information.
statements_all.excerpt_original: In response, Ndayishimiye argued that he had previously asked President Paul Kagame to provide intelligence on FDLR positions, insisting that Burundi would attack the group if such information were made available.

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye acknowledged that Congolese forces work with the FDLR, but argued that Burundian troops operate separately under Congolese command structures and do not mix with those groups.
statements_all.excerpt_original: When asked how Burundian troops could avoid cooperating with FDLR while operating alongside FARDC, which has repeatedly been accused of collaborating with the group, Ndayishimiye acknowledged that Congolese forces work with FDLR. However, he argued that Burundian troops operate separately under Congolese command structures and do not mix with those groups

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye proposed coordinated military action by Rwanda, the DRC, Burundi and Uganda against armed groups in the region, saying this could reassure Rwanda about its security concerns.
statements_all.excerpt_original: He proposed coordinated military action involving Rwanda, DR Congo, Burundi and Uganda against armed groups operating in the region, saying such cooperation could help reassure Rwanda about its security concerns.

statements_all.setting: statement, medium not specified on page (page cites his X account)
statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Rwanda's foreign minister (printed 'Oliver Nduhungirehe'), in a statement the day after the Mushaki drone attack, deplored the silence of the international community and of the UN mission in the DRC regarding 'crimes du gouvernement de la République du Congo'; he said that on 11 March 2026 FARDC attack drones struck Goma, killing UNICEF humanitarian Karine Buisset and two other civilians.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Le ministre des Affaires étrangères de la République du Rwanda a déploré, le week-end dernier, dans une déclaration, le silence de la communauté internationale et de la Mission onusienne en RDC face aux « crimes du gouvernement de la République du Congo »
statements_all.translation_en: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Rwanda deplored, last weekend, in a statement, the silence of the international community and the UN Mission in the DRC in the face of the 'crimes of the government of the Republic of Congo'

statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that, in a communiqué, the rebel movement's spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka gave a provisional toll of at least 21 civilians killed and more than 67 wounded, among them women and children, in drone strikes the rebellion blamed on government forces against the public market of Mushaki, and that the movement called the attack a serious violation of international humanitarian law.
statements_all.excerpt_original: La rébellion accuse les forces gouvernementales d’avoir mené, une nouvelle fois, des frappes de drones meurtrières contre le marché public de Mushaki.
statements_all.translation_en: The rebellion accuses the government forces of having carried out, once again, deadly drone strikes against the public market of Mushaki.

statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Rwandan Minister of Foreign Affairs, Oliver Nduhungirehe, deplored in a statement the weekend before the silence of the international community and the UN mission in the DRC in the face of the 'crimes du gouvernement de la République du Congo', speaking the day after the Congolese army drone attack on Mushaki.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Le ministre des Affaires étrangères de la République du Rwanda a déploré, le week-end dernier, dans une déclaration, le silence de la communauté internationale et de la Mission onusienne en RDC face aux « crimes du gouvernement de la République du Congo » . Oliver Nduhungirehe l’a dit le lendemain de l’attaque de drones de l’armée congolaise à Mushaki
statements_all.translation_en: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Rwanda deplored, last weekend, in a statement, the silence of the international community and of the UN Mission in the DRC in the face of the « crimes of the government of the Republic of the Congo » . Oliver Nduhungirehe said so the day after the Congolese army's drone attack on Mushaki

statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to AFCM23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa, the Congolese army's drone attack on Mushaki, forty kilometres from Goma, killed 20 people and wounded about sixty civilians.
statements_all.excerpt_original: l’attaque de drones de l’armée congolaise à Mushaki, à quarante kilomètres de Goma, qui a fait 20 morts et une soixantaine de blessés parmi la population civile, selon Corneille Nangaa, coordonnateur de l’AFCM23.
statements_all.translation_en: the Congolese army's drone attack on Mushaki, forty kilometres from Goma, which left 20 dead and about sixty wounded among the civilian population, according to Corneille Nangaa, coordinator of the AFCM23.

statements_all.role: head of the Wazalendo special unit (per Enquete.cd)
statements_all.text: Enquete.cd reported that Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito, head of the Wazalendo special unit, issued a firm call on Monday 5 May 2026 in Uvira for Wazalendo fighters to withdraw from urban areas and join the front lines, after meeting Jacques Kongolo, adviser to the President of the Republic.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Dans ce contexte, Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito a lancé un appel ferme au retrait des combattants Wazalendo des zones urbaines, tout en plaidant pour une cohabitation pacifique entre les communautés.
statements_all.translation_en: In this context, Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito issued a firm call for the withdrawal of Wazalendo fighters from urban areas, while pleading for peaceful coexistence between communities.

statements_all.text: Enquete.cd reported that a three-day moratorium was granted to Wazalendo fighters in Uvira to leave the city and return to combat positions, with only commanders allowed to circulate in the urban area in strictly limited numbers, and that any breach would expose offenders to the sanctions of military regulations.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Un moratoire de trois jours a été accordé aux combattants pour quitter la ville et regagner les positions de combat. Seuls les commandants seront autorisés à circuler en zone urbaine, avec un effectif strictement limité. Toute infraction à ces directives exposera les contrevenants à des sanctions prévues par le règlement militaire.
statements_all.translation_en: A three-day moratorium was granted to the fighters to leave the city and return to combat positions. Only commanders will be authorized to circulate in the urban area, with a strictly limited number. Any breach will expose offenders to the sanctions provided by military regulations.

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the AFC/M23 group accused the DRC government army of 'excessively severe' drone attacks 'in areas inhabited by civilians' at Lumbishi, Kalehe territory, on Monday, and that Lawrence Kanyuka said in a communiqué that the CH-4 drone attacks 'destroyed many things and caused many civilians to flee'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Umutwe wa AFC/M23 urashinja igisirikare cya leta ya DR Congo kugaba ibitero "by'ubukana burenze" gikoresheje za 'drones' "mu duce dutuwe n'abaturage" i Lumbishi muri teritwari ya Karehe mu ntara ya Kivu y'Epfo kuri uyu wa mbere.
statements_all.translation_en: The AFC/M23 group accuses the army of the DR Congo government of carrying out 'excessively severe' attacks using drones 'in areas inhabited by civilians' at Lumbishi in Kalehe territory in South Kivu province on this Monday.

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Jacques Kongolo, adviser to President Félix Tshisekedi, told BBC on Monday that the government side was not the one violating the ceasefire agreements, and quoted him as saying that the other side uses Rwandan drones to shoot at them and then lies that it was the government side that fired.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Jacques Kongolo, umujyanama wa Perezida Félix Tshisekedi yabwiye BBC Gahuzamiryango kuri uyu wa mbere ko uruhande rwa leta atari rwo ruhonyora amasezerano y'agahenge. Komeza usome Kongolo yagize ati: "[Nibo] Bakoresha amadrones y'u Rwanda mu kuturasa bagahita babeshya ngo ni twe twarashe".
statements_all.translation_en: Jacques Kongolo, adviser to President Félix Tshisekedi, told BBC Gahuzamiryango on Monday that the government side is not the one violating the ceasefire agreements. Kongolo said: '[They] use Rwanda's drones to shoot at us and then lie that it is we who fired.'

statements_all.person: Julia Garcia Zamora, MSF programme manager, South Kivu
statements_all.text: MSF said in a communiqué that on 1 May a team travelling between Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu in South Kivu was stopped at a checkpoint held by Wazalendo elements, and that armed men opened fire among themselves while the team was in the middle.
statements_all.excerpt_original: « Après avoir franchi sans difficulté plusieurs points de contrôle tenus par des éléments Wazalendo le long du trajet, notre équipe a été arrêtée à l’un d’eux », explique Julia Garcia Zamora, cheffe de programme de MSF au Sud-Kivu.
statements_all.translation_en: "After passing several checkpoints held by Wazalendo elements along the route without difficulty, our team was stopped at one of them," says Julia Garcia Zamora, MSF programme manager in South Kivu.

statements_all.text: Antoine Kaburahe's site reported that, in a press interview, President Ndayishimiye defended keeping several thousand Burundian soldiers in eastern DRC, saying they operate in support of the FARDC under regional accords, and rejected accusations of collaboration with the FDLR; Rwandan foreign minister Olivier Nduhungirehe, interviewed by Kaburahe, rejected the president's accusations and said the FDLR collaborate openly with the army of the DRC and the Burundian army.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Évariste Ndayishimiye défend également le maintien de plusieurs milliers de soldats burundais dans l’est de la RDC, expliquant qu’ils interviennent en appui des FARDC dans le cadre d’accords régionaux. Il rejette les accusations de collaboration avec les FDLR
statements_all.translation_en: Évariste Ndayishimiye also defends the continued presence of several thousand Burundian soldiers in eastern DRC, explaining that they are intervening in support of the FARDC under regional agreements. He rejects the accusations of collaboration with the FDLR

statements_all.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported in May 2026 that the FDNB is accused by several local and international organisations of human rights violations in the Minembwe area, including road blockades, destruction of property and looting targeting civilians, and that the FDNB spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, acknowledged that movement restrictions could be imposed on individuals considered 'collaborators with the enemy'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB) is accused by several local and international organizations of human rights violations in the Minembwe area, including cases of road blockades, destruction of property, and looting targeting civilians.

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that in May 2026 AFC/M23 accused Human Rights Watch of defaming it, publishing falsehoods and ignoring the truth, in response to an HRW report released on 14 May that accuses its fighters of killing civilians in Uvira city, raping women and abducting people between December 2025 and January 2026.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Uretse u Rwanda, muri Gicurasi 2026, Ihuriro AFC/M23 ryashinje Human Rights Watch kuriharabika, gutangaza ibinyoma no kwirengagiza ukuri, mu buryo bushimangira ko ukorera mu murongo w’ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo.
statements_all.translation_en: Besides Rwanda, in May 2026 the AFC/M23 alliance accused Human Rights Watch of smearing it, publishing lies and ignoring the truth, in a way that, it said, shows HRW works in line with the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 said the DRC army continues to work with the FDLR, which HRW does not want to address in its reports, and that HRW's bias makes the organisation lose credibility.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Iri huriro ryagaragaje ko ingabo za RDC zikomeje gukorana n’umutwe w’iterabwoba wa FDLR washinzwe n’abagize uruhare muri Jenoside yakorewe Abatutsi mu 1994, ariko ko HRW idashaka kubivugaho muri raporo zayo. AFC/M23 yatangaje ko kubogama HRW yagaragaje muri raporo yayo gutuma uyu muryango utakarizwa icyizere mu buryo bukomeye, ibituma ibyo utangaza bidahabwa agaciro.
statements_all.translation_en: This alliance showed that the DRC army continues to work with the terrorist FDLR group founded by people who took part in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, but that HRW does not want to talk about it in its reports. AFC/M23 stated that HRW's bias in its report makes this organisation lose trust seriously, which means what it publishes is not given value.

statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC announced in a communiqué on Sunday 26 April that they had shot down on Saturday 25 April 2026 a UAV belonging to the Rwandan army, intercepted at Point Zéro in the Minembwe highlands, Fizi territory.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Dans un communiqué dimanche 26 avril, les Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ont annoncé avoir abattu, en plein vol, samedi 25 avril 2026, un drone de type UAV appartenant à l’armée rwandaise. L’appareil a été intercepté au Point Zéro, dans les Hauts Plateaux de Minembwe, en territoire de Fizi, au Sud-Kivu.
statements_all.translation_en: In a communiqué on Sunday 26 April, the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) announced that they had shot down in mid-flight, on Saturday 25 April 2026, a UAV-type drone belonging to the Rwandan army. The aircraft was intercepted at Point Zéro, in the Hauts Plateaux of Minembwe, in Fizi territory, in South Kivu.

statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that from Saturday 25 April to Sunday the Kinshasa regime's coalition forces carried out simultaneous, sustained bombardments at Gakenke, Mikenke and their surroundings in the Minembwe region, using kamikaze combat drones and KT-6 type drones, which the movement called a flagrant violation of the ceasefire.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole du mouvement rebelle, a déclaré que du samedi 25 avril au dimanche, les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa ont mené des bombardements simultanés, soutenus et ininterrompus à Gakenke, Mikenke ainsi que leurs environs, dans la région de Minembwe.
statements_all.translation_en: Lawrence Kanyuka, spokesperson of the rebel movement, stated that from Saturday 25 April to Sunday, the coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime carried out simultaneous, sustained and uninterrupted bombardments at Gakenke, Mikenke and their surroundings, in the Minembwe region.

statements_all.setting: written fact-check published on a government website
statements_all.text: The Rwandan Ministry of Defence website published a "fact-checking" stating that Jean-Jacques Purusi accused Rwanda and the AFC/M23 of being responsible for the massacres in Uvira, pointing to mass graves, and responding that since the AFC/M23 withdrew from Uvira the city has been in chaos, with killings, looting and sexual violence in several neighbourhoods.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Jean-Jacques Purusi accused Rwanda and the AFC/M23 of being responsible for the massacres in Uvira, pointing to the discovery of mass graves reportedly containing hundreds of bodies. Fact: Since the AFC/M23 withdrew from Uvira, the city has been plunged into chaos. Killings, looting, and sexual violence have erupted in several neighborhoods.

statements_all.setting: written fact-check published on a government website
statements_all.text: The Rwandan Ministry of Defence website published a "fact-checking" stating that in the High Plateaus of South Kivu the Banyamulenge have faced systematic attacks by a coalition of Maï-Maï groups operating in collaboration with the FARDC, involving killings, rape, the burning of villages, mass theft of cattle and "even drone strikes by the Congolese government".
statements_all.excerpt_original: In the High Plateaus of South Kivu, the Banyamulenge community has been under siege for years, facing systematic attacks carried out by a coalition of Maï-Maï groups operating in collaboration with the FARDC. These attacks involve killings, rape, the burning of villages, mass theft of cattle, and even drone strikes by the Congolese government.

statements_all.setting: written fact-check published on a government website
statements_all.text: The Rwandan Ministry of Defence website published a "fact-checking" responding to Jean-Jacques Purusi's accusation that the AFC/M23 slaughtered Banyamulenge cattle to frame the FARDC, stating that multiple recent reports describe drone strikes affecting the Minembwe area in South Kivu that hit civilians and property, including injuries and deaths.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Jean-Jacques Purusi accused the AFC/M23 of slaughtering Banyamulenge cattle to frame the FARDC. Fact: Multiple recent reports describe drone strikes affecting the Minembwe area in South Kivu that hit civilians and property, including injuries and deaths.

statements_all.setting: statement as reported by Igihe (no channel stated)
statements_all.text: AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said, according to Igihe, that from the early hours of 20 April 2026 the coalition of DRC government forces launched a suicide-drone attack on the Mikenke area in Minembwe commune.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yatangaje ko guhera mu masaa cyenda y’urukerera rwo kuri uyu wa 20 Mata 2026, ihuriro ry’ingabo za Leta ya RDC ryagabye igitero cya drones z’ubwiyahuzi mu gace ka Mikenke muri Komini Minembwe.
statements_all.translation_en: AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka announced that from about 3 a.m. (saa cyenda in Kinyarwanda time-reckoning) in the early morning of this 20 April 2026, the coalition of DRC government forces launched a suicide-drone attack on the Mikenke area in Minembwe commune.

statements_all.setting: statement as reported by Igihe (no channel stated)
statements_all.text: AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said, according to Igihe, that at 5:30 government coalition forces also attacked the densely populated area of Mitimingi in Masisi territory, causing much damage and making many families flee; Igihe places this in its account of attacks on 20 April 2026.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yatangaje ko guhera mu masaa cyenda y’urukerera rwo kuri uyu wa 20 Mata 2026, ihuriro ry’ingabo za Leta ya RDC ryagabye igitero cya drones z’ubwiyahuzi mu gace ka Mikenke muri Komini Minembwe. Kanyuka yagize ati "Saa 5:30, izi ngabo zanagabye igitero ku gace gatuwe cyane ka Mitimingi muri teritwari ya Masisi, hangirika byinshi, imiryango myinshi irahunga."
statements_all.translation_en: AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka announced that from around 3 a.m. (Kinyarwanda 'mu masaa cyenda y'urukerera', literally 'around the ninth hour of the early morning') on this 20 April 2026, the coalition of DRC government forces launched a kamikaze drone attack on the Mikenke area in Minembwe commune. Kanyuka said: "At 5:30, these forces also launched an attack on the densely populated area of Mitimingi in Masisi territory; much was damaged and many families fled."

statements_all.text: AFC/M23 spokesperson Kanyuka said, according to Igihe, that AFC/M23 continues to point to repeated, deliberate breaches of the ceasefire by the Kinshasa government and that it is fully ready to defend civilians and to set up a proper security space to protect the population.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Kanyuka yagize ati "AFC/M23 ikomeje kugaragaza ukurenga ku gahenge kenshi, gukorwa nkana na Leta ya Kinshasa. Ishimangira ko yiteguye rwose kurwanirira abasivili no gushyiraho umwanya ukwiye w’umutekano kugira ngo turinde abaturage intambara dushozwaho na Leta."
statements_all.translation_en: Kanyuka said: "AFC/M23 continues to show repeated breaches of the ceasefire, committed deliberately by the Kinshasa government. It affirms that it is fully ready to defend civilians and to establish a proper security space so that we protect the population from the war launched on us by the government."

statements_all.text: Anadolu reported that on Sunday the Congolese army said in a statement that AFC/M23 and its coalition had launched drone attacks on Saturday evening on its positions at Mikenge and Kakenge in South Kivu and on civilian areas at Point Zero, with a provisional toll of four civilians killed and eight injured, mostly women and children, while Anadolu noted there was no immediate reaction from Rwanda.
statements_all.excerpt_original: But on Sunday, the army said AFC/M23 rebels and its coalition launched deadly drone attacks Saturday evening on its positions in South Kivu’s Mikenge and Kakenge localities as well as on areas inhabited by civilians at Point Zero. “The provisional toll indicates that four civilians were killed and eight others injured, mostly women and children,” the army said in a statement.

statements_all.text: A joint statement by the Government of the DRC and the AFC, together with the United States, Qatar, Togo as African Union mediator, the AU Commission and Switzerland, on talks in Montreux, Switzerland, said the Parties agreed to facilitate rapid, unimpeded, safe and sustained humanitarian access and freedom of movement for humanitarian personnel, goods and services, and agreed to refrain from any attack, destruction or removal of objects indispensable to the survival of the civilian population, including hospital and school facilities.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The Parties agreed to facilitate rapid, unimpeded, safe, and sustained humanitarian access and freedom of movement for humanitarian personnel, goods, and services

statements_all.text: AFC/M23 told Congolese and the international community, according to Igihe, that the Kinshasa government was putting war first, while Igihe reported that DRC forces were still launching drone and heavy-weapon attacks on Minembwe and Masisi while the talks that began on 13 April were under way.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ubwo ibi biganiro byatangiye tariki ya 13 Mata byari bikomeje, Leta ya RDC yari ikigaba ibitero bya drones n’intwaro ziremereye muri Minembwe na Masisi. AFC/M23 yamenyesheje Abanye-Congo n’umuryango mpuzamahanga ko Leta ishyize imbere intambara.
statements_all.translation_en: While these talks that began on 13 April were under way, the DRC government was still launching drone and heavy-weapon attacks in Minembwe and Masisi. AFC/M23 informed Congolese and the international community that the government is putting war first.
