statements_all.text: UN News reported that, at the Security Council meeting that renewed the MONUSCO mandate, the United States said negotiations were "yet again disrupted" by M23 advances "supported by the Rwanda Defence Forces", and Ambassador Jennifer Locetta said M23 must immediately withdraw at least 75km from Uvira and return to compliance with its obligations under the Framework Agreement.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The United States said negotiations were “yet again disrupted” by M23 advances “supported by the Rwanda Defence Forces,” and urged the group to comply with its commitments under the Doha framework. “M23 must immediately withdraw at least 75km from Uvira and return to compliance with all of its obligations undertaken in the Framework Agreement,” said Jennifer Locetta

statements_all.text: UN News (French) reported that in its resolution renewing the MONUSCO mandate the Security Council strongly condemned the M23 offensive in South Kivu, carried out with the support of the Rwandan Defence Force, and demanded their immediate withdrawal from Congolese territory.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Dans sa résolution, le Conseil de sécurité « condamne fermement l’offensive menée par le M23 au Sud-Kivu, avec le soutien de la Force de défense rwandaise » et exige leur retrait immédiat du territoire congolais.
statements_all.translation_en: In its resolution, the Security Council “strongly condemns the offensive led by the M23 in South Kivu, with the support of the Rwandan Defence Force” and demands their immediate withdrawal from Congolese territory.

statements_all.text: BBC News reported that Muyaya described the M23's decision to leave Uvira as a "positive sign" but said the government needed to confirm the situation on the ground, having earlier called for "vigilance" in response to the "alleged withdrawal".
statements_all.excerpt_original: Muyaya described the M23's decision to leave Uvira as a "positive sign" but said the government needed to confirm the situation on the ground. Earlier he had called for "vigilance" in response to the "alleged withdrawal".

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 affirms that by 18 December all its fighters had left Uvira city, to build confidence in the Doha talks with the DRC government.
statements_all.excerpt_original: AFC/M23 yemeza ko tariki ya 18 Ukuboza abarwanyi bayo bose bari bamaze kuva mu Mujyi wa Uvira, mu kubaka icyizere mu biganiro biyihuriza na Leta ya RDC i Doha muri Qatar, kugira ngo impande zombi zigere ku masezerano y’amahoro.
statements_all.translation_en: AFC/M23 confirms that on 18 December all its fighters had left Uvira city, to build confidence in the talks bringing it together with the DRC government in Doha, Qatar, so that both sides reach a peace agreement.

statements_all.text: Al Jazeera reported that the DRC government described M23's pledge to withdraw from Uvira as a 'nonevent, a diversion, a distraction', and that Communications Minister Patrick Muyaya told Reuters the intention was to distract the American mediation team, which he said was preparing to take measures against Rwanda.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Earlier on Wednesday, the DRC government described M23’s pledge to withdraw from Uvira as a “nonevent, a diversion, a distraction” while the group said its conditions for a pullout were yet to be met. “The intention is to distract the American mediation team, which is preparing to take measures against Rwanda,” DRC Communications Minister Patrick Muyaya told the Reuters news agency.

statements_all.text: TRT Afrika, relaying Reuters, reported that M23 spokesperson Willy Ngoma told Reuters on Wednesday that "we are ready to leave (Uvira), but our conditions have to be reviewed", adding that the citizens of Uvira needed protecting and that the city should be occupied by a neutral force; residents told Reuters the rebels had not withdrawn.
statements_all.excerpt_original: M23 spokesperson Willy Ngoma told Reuters on Wednesday that "we are ready to leave (Uvira), but our conditions have to be reviewed." The spokesperson added that the citizens of Uvira needed protecting and it should be occupied by a neutral force.

statements_all.setting: statement and social-media post as reported
statements_all.text: BBC News reported that M23 leader Bertrand Bisimwa said on Wednesday that the withdrawal from Uvira was "under way", with spokesman Willy Ngoma adding that this was "for the sake of peace", and that Bisimwa in a post on X urged mediators and international partners to ensure the city was protected from "reprisals, violence and remilitarisation".
statements_all.excerpt_original: M23 leader Bertrand Bisimwa said on Wednesday that the withdrawal was "under way," with spokesman Willy Ngoma adding that this was "for the sake of peace". In a post on X, Bisimwa urged mediators and international partners to ensure the city was protected from "reprisals, violence and remilitarisation".

statements_all.text: TRT Afrika, relaying Reuters, reported that DRC Communications Minister Patrick Muyaya dismissed the announced M23 withdrawal from Uvira as a "diversion", alleging it was an attempt to relieve pressure on Rwanda; the page also says Rwanda's government spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
statements_all.excerpt_original: However, DR Congo's Communications Minister Patrick Muyaya dismissed the announcement of a withdrawal from Uvira as a "diversion," alleging it was an attempt to relieve pressure on Rwanda, which Kinshasa and the United Nations accuse of backing the rebels.

statements_all.text: BBC Afrique reported that M23 chief Bertrand Bisimwa said on Wednesday that the withdrawal from Uvira was 'underway', with spokesperson Willy Ngoma adding it was 'in the interest of peace'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Le chef du M23, Bertrand Bisimwa, a déclaré mercredi que le retrait était « en cours », le porte-parole Willy Ngoma ajoutant que c'était « dans l'intérêt de la paix ».
statements_all.translation_en: The head of the M23, Bertrand Bisimwa, said on Wednesday that the withdrawal was “underway”, with spokesperson Willy Ngoma adding that it was “in the interest of peace”.

statements_all.text: BBC Afrique reported that the DRC government spokesperson Me Didier Kabi called the rebels' announced withdrawal from Uvira a 'mise en scène' orchestrated by the rebels to reduce pressure from partners, and that the DRC authorities said they held credible information of a 'dissimulation teintée de retrait'; BBC Afrique noted that government forces had not returned to the city.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Pour le porte-parole du gouvernement, Me Didier Kabi, cette annonce est une "mise en scène" orchestrée par les rebelles pour réduire la pression des partenaires qui pèse sur eux. Les autorités de la RDC indiquent détenir des informations crédibles qui "font état d'une dissimulation teintée de retrait".
statements_all.translation_en: For the government spokesperson, Me Didier Kabi, this announcement is a “staging” orchestrated by the rebels to reduce the pressure that partners are putting on them. The DRC authorities say they hold credible information that “speaks of a concealment tinged with withdrawal”.

statements_all.role: ambassador of Burundi to the EU
statements_all.text: Iwacu reported that on 17 December 2025 Burundi's ambassador to the EU, Thérence Ntahiraja, told the European Parliament that the Burundian army had withdrawn its troops from eastern DRC after the peace accord, and that this is why the Rwandan army and the M23 advanced easily to Uvira.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Le 17 décembre 2025, devant le Parlement européen à Bruxelles, l’ambassadeur du Burundi auprès de l’Union européenne, Thérence Ntahiraja, s’est en effet exprimé sur la situation sécuritaire à l’Est de la RDC, aux côtés de son homologue congolais Christian Ndongala Nkuku.
statements_all.translation_en: On 17 December 2025, before the European Parliament in Brussels, Burundi's ambassador to the European Union, Thérence Ntahiraja, spoke about the security situation in eastern DRC, alongside his Congolese counterpart Christian Ndongala Nkuku.

statements_all.role: Minister of Communication and Media, government spokesperson
statements_all.text: DW Swahili reported that Minister of Information and government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya accused the M23 of continuing the war and called their announcement of leaving Uvira 'upotoshaji' (a distortion/misinformation), saying it was a ploy to disrupt the mediator, the United States.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Waziri wa Habari na Msemaji wa Serikali, Patrick Muyaya amewashutumu waasi hao kwa kuendeleza vita, siku chache tu baada ya kusaini makubaliano ya amani na kulitaja tangazo lao la kuondoka kama upotoshaji.
statements_all.translation_en: Minister of Information and Government Spokesperson Patrick Muyaya has accused the rebels of continuing the war, just days after signing a peace agreement, and called their announcement of leaving a distortion.

statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that Burundian foreign minister Édouard Bizimana wrote on X that the rebels' announced withdrawal from Uvira was "a pure lie" meant to mislead international opinion, saying the Rwandan forces and the rebels had not withdrawn from Uvira.
statements_all.excerpt_original: « C’est encore un pur mensonge destiné à induire en erreur l’opinion internationale, le président des États-Unis, le secrétaire d’État Marco Rubio et toutes les personnes éprises de paix », a écrit sur le réseau social X (ex-Twitter) Édouard Bizimana, ministre burundais des affaires étrangères.
statements_all.translation_en: "This is once again a pure lie intended to mislead international opinion, the President of the United States, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and all peace-loving people," wrote Édouard Bizimana, Burundi's minister of foreign affairs, on the social network X (formerly Twitter).

statements_all.text: Al Jazeera reported that AFC leader Corneille Nangaa posted a signed statement on X on Tuesday confirming that fighters would withdraw from Uvira 'as per United States mediation request', and that the coalition called the move a 'unilateral trust-building measure' and called for a neutral force to monitor the ceasefire.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Corneille Nangaa, leader of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) rebel coalition, which includes the M23 group, posted a signed statement on X on Tuesday that confirmed fighters would withdraw from the town located in South Kivu province, near the border with Burundi, “as per United States mediation request”.

statements_all.text: Kigali Today reported that the rebel coalition announced it was ready to leave Uvira, asking that soldiers and all other armed people be removed from the city and that neutral forces be deployed to protect civilians and infrastructure and help enforce the ceasefire.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Mu byo uyu mutwe usaba kugira ngo wubahirize ibyo wiyemeje, harimo kandi ko umujyi wa Uvira wakurwamo abasirikare n’abandi bose bitwaje intwaro bahasanzwe, hakabaho kurinda abaturage n’ibikorwa remezo, ari yo mpamvu usaba ko hashyirwaho ingabo zitabogama zanafasha kubahiriza ihagarikwa ry’imirwano (ceasefire).
statements_all.translation_en: Among what this group requests in order to fulfil what it committed to is that Uvira city be cleared of the soldiers and all other armed people found there, with protection of civilians and infrastructure, which is why it requests the deployment of neutral forces that would also help enforce the ceasefire.

statements_all.text: BBC Afrique reported that DRC government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya told the BBC Newsday programme that the M23 announcement aimed to 'divert the attention of the American mediation team', which he said was preparing to take measures against Rwanda, and that he called the decision to leave Uvira a 'positive sign' while saying the government needed to confirm the situation on the ground.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Le porte-parole du gouvernement de la République démocratique du Congo, Patrick Muyaya, a déclaré à l'émission BBC Newsday que l'annonce du M23 visait à « détourner l'attention de l'équipe de médiation américaine, qui se prépare à prendre des mesures contre le Rwanda ».
statements_all.translation_en: The spokesperson of the government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Patrick Muyaya, told the BBC Newsday programme that the M23's announcement aimed to “divert the attention of the American mediation team, which is preparing to take measures against Rwanda”.

statements_all.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 16 December 2025 AFC coordinator Corneille Nangaa posted on his X account a statement announcing that AFC/M23 would unilaterally withdraw its forces from Uvira "as per the United States' mediation request".
statements_all.excerpt_original: On 16 December, AFC coordinator Corneille Nangaa posted on his X account a statement in which he announced that AFC/M23, referring to the Doha process and the signing of the Doha Framework agreement on 15 November 2025, it will unilaterally withdraw its forces from Uvira “as per the United States' mediation request”.

statements_all.role: coordinator of the Alliance Fleuve Congo
statements_all.text: BBC News Afrique reported that, in a press release published Tuesday, AFC/M23 leader Corneille Nangaa said the unilateral withdrawal followed a request from the American mediators. Anadolu Agency quoted a communiqué signed by Corneille Nangaa: "The AFC/M23 will unilaterally withdraw its forces from the city of Uvira, as requested by the American mediation".
statements_all.excerpt_original: Dans un communiqué de presse publié mardi, Corneille Nangaa, le leader de l'AFC /M23, a déclaré que ce retrait unilatéral faisait suite à une demande des médiateurs américains.
statements_all.translation_en: In a press release published on Tuesday, Corneille Nangaa, the leader of the AFC /M23, said that this unilateral withdrawal followed a request from the American mediators.

statements_all.setting: communiqué and social-media post as reported
statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 announced in a communiqué that it would unilaterally withdraw its forces from the city of Uvira, presenting the decision as a confidence-building measure to support the Doha peace process; it said the withdrawal was conditional on security guarantees including demilitarisation, protection of civilians and deployment of a neutral force. BBC Gahuza reported Nangaa said M23 would withdraw at the request of United States mediation.
statements_all.excerpt_original: L’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC/M23) a annoncé ce mardi qu’elle retirerait unilatéralement ses forces de la ville d’Uvira, dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo, présentant cette décision comme une mesure de confiance destinée à soutenir le processus de paix de Doha, a-t-elle indiqué dans un communiqué.
statements_all.translation_en: The Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC/M23) announced this Tuesday that it would unilaterally withdraw its forces from the city of Uvira, in eastern DRC, presenting this decision as a confidence-building measure to support the Doha process, it said in a communiqué.

statements_all.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Badibanga Kalonji, called on the international community, in particular the United States, to compel Rwanda to withdraw the troops that, he said, support the AFC-M23 rebels, and said 'all batteries are being put in motion' to reconquer the territories already in rebel hands.
statements_all.excerpt_original: L’administrateur de Fizi, Samy Badibanga Kalonji, déplore cette avancée et demande à la communauté internationale, particulièrement les États-Unis, de contraindre le Rwanda à retirer ses troupes qui soutiennent les rebelles de l’AFC-M23.
statements_all.translation_en: The administrator of Fizi, Samy Badibanga Kalonji, deplores this advance and asks the international community, particularly the United States, to compel Rwanda to withdraw its troops which support the AFC-M23 rebels.

statements_all.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that an M23 spokesperson said the movement had "no problem with African people, much less with Burundians", could not be held responsible for the prolonged blockade of Burundians in Uvira, and that the border on the Congolese side had remained open under a policy of free movement in areas under its control.
statements_all.excerpt_original: One of its spokespeople clarified that the movement had “no problem with African people, much less with Burundians,” and that it could not be held responsible for the prolonged blockade of these citizens. According to him, the border on the Congolese side had remained open, and the M23 was implementing a policy of free movement in the areas under its control.

statements_all.role: AFC/M23 spokesperson (role not stated in excerpt)
statements_all.setting: social-media posts on X as reported by the Group of Experts
statements_all.text: The Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 leaders alleged that FARDC and FDNB committed a premeditated, systematic and targeted campaign of extermination against the Banyamulenge population, including through aerial bombardments; the Group stated it did not substantiate intentional targeting and that Banyamulenge community members reported three civilian deaths.
statements_all.excerpt_original: MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 leaders alleged that FARDC and FDNB committed a premeditated, systematic and targeted campaign of extermination against the Banyamulenge population, including through aerial bombardments of densely populated areas.

statements_all.text: Al Jazeera reported that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that Rwanda's actions in eastern DRC were a 'clear violation' of the peace deal, and said in a post on X that the United States would take action to ensure promises made to the president are kept.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Rwanda’s actions in eastern DRC are a “clear violation” of the peace deal US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday. “The United States will take action to ensure promises made to the president are kept,” he said in a post on X.

statements_all.role: permanent representative of Burundi to the United Nations
statements_all.setting: speech at UN Security Council briefing, as reported
statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that Burundi's permanent representative to the UN, Zéphyrin Maniratanga, in his presentation on Friday 12 December 2025, accused Rwanda of having favoured the taking of Uvira in violation of the Washington accords and resolution 2773, and quoted him as saying Burundi was particularly concerned by cross-border attacks, including artillery and drones, some of which reached localities of Burundian territory.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Dans son exposé, vendredi 12 décembre 2025, le représentant permanent du Burundi auprès des Nations unies, Zéphyrin Maniratanga, a dénoncé l’attitude qu’il qualifie de belliqueuse du Rwanda, l’accusant d’avoir favorisé la prise de la ville d’Uvira en violation des accords de Washington et de la résolution 2773.
statements_all.translation_en: In his presentation on Friday 12 December 2025, the permanent representative of Burundi to the United Nations, Zéphyrin Maniratanga, denounced what he called Rwanda's belligerent attitude, accusing it of having favoured the taking of the city of Uvira in violation of the Washington accords and resolution 2773.

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the office of President Félix Tshisekedi said on X that, at a restricted ministers' meeting on Thursday, Tshisekedi described the attack as a 'flagrant violation' of Rwanda's commitments under the peace agreements signed in Washington the previous week; the article ties this to the rebels' capture of Uvira, which it presents as a military attack by Rwanda.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ibiro bya Perezida Félix Tshisekedi byatangaje ku rubuga nkoranyambaga X ko mu nama ya bacye y'abaminisitiri yo ku wa kane, Tshisekedi yavuze ko icyo gitero ari "ihonyorwa rigaragara ry'ibyo u Rwanda rwiyemeje muri gahunda y'amasezerano y'amahoro yasinyiwe i Washington" mu cyumweru gishize hagati y'u Rwanda na DRC.
statements_all.translation_en: The office of President Félix Tshisekedi announced on X that in a restricted ministers' meeting on Thursday, Tshisekedi said the attack was a "flagrant violation of what Rwanda committed to in the peace agreements signed in Washington" last week between Rwanda and the DRC.

statements_all.setting: statement as relayed by Radio Okapi
statements_all.text: Radio Okapi reported that the departure of part of the Burundian soldiers from Uvira was denied by Burundi's ambassador to the DRC.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Mais ce départ d'une partie des militaires burundais est démenti par l'ambassadeur du Burundi en RDC.
statements_all.translation_en: But this departure of part of the Burundian soldiers is denied by the Burundian ambassador to the DRC.

statements_all.setting: speech at a swearing-in ceremony, as reported
statements_all.text: Anadolu reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame said on Thursday that Burundian soldiers deployed in eastern DRC spend days shelling civilians, and Anadolu noted there was no immediate reaction from Burundi.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Burundian soldiers deployed to the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo spend days shelling civilians, Rwandan President Paul Kagame said Thursday, highlighting Burundi’s military involvement in the conflict in South Kivu province. There was no immediate reaction from Burundi.

statements_all.text: Mugisha Nkurunziza Alexis, Vice-President of MRDP-Twirwaneho, told Igihe on 11 December 2025 that Burundian troops were still numerous in the high areas around Minembwe and said: 'The Burundian troops are still where they were. Even now Burundians are fighting the self-defending residents there at Irango, at Ndondo'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Kuri uyu wa 11 Ukuboza 2025, Visi Perezida wa MRDP-Twirwaneho, Mugisha Nkurunziza Alexis, yatangarije IGIHE ingabo z’u Burundi zikiri nyinshi mu bice by’imisozi miremire bikikije Minembwe. Nkurunziza yagize ati “Ingabo z’u Burundi aho zari ziri ziracyahari. N’ubu Abarundi bari kurwana n’abaturage birwanaho hariya ku Irango, ku Ndondo.”
statements_all.translation_en: On this 11 December 2025, the Vice-President of MRDP-Twirwaneho, Mugisha Nkurunziza Alexis, told IGIHE that Burundian troops are still numerous in the high areas around Minembwe. Nkurunziza said: “The Burundian troops are still where they were. Even now Burundians are fighting the villagers who defend themselves there at Irango, at Ndondo.”

statements_all.text: Nkurunziza of MRDP-Twirwaneho said, according to Igihe, that the Burundian troops had disgraced their country in this war, that their best option was to go home, and that otherwise they would be removed by force from the high hills around Minembwe.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Nkurunziza yatangaje ko ingabo z’u Burundi zatesheje agaciro igihugu cyazo muri iyi ntambara, bityo ko amahitamo meza zikwiye kugira ari ugutaha, bitaba ibyo na zo zikazakurwa mu misozi miremire ikikije Minembwe ku ngufu.
statements_all.translation_en: Nkurunziza stated that the Burundian troops had devalued their country in this war, so that the best choice they should make is to go home, otherwise they too would be removed by force from the high hills around Minembwe.

statements_all.setting: government report, as reported by Radio Okapi
statements_all.text: Radio Okapi reported that a Government report, presented in Kinshasa on a Tuesday by Minister of Human Rights Samuel Mbemba, said about 14,400 women were raped in five weeks of occupation of Uvira by the Rwandan army and its proxies.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Plus de 1 500 personnes ont perdu la vie et environ 14 400 femmes ont été violées en cinq semaines d’occupation de la ville d’Uvira, dans la province du Sud-Kivu, par l’armée rwandaise et ses supplétifs. Ces chiffres sont contenus dans un rapport du Gouvernement, présenté mardi à Kinshasa devant la presse par le ministre des Droits humains, Samuel Mbemba.
statements_all.translation_en: More than 1,500 people lost their lives and about 14,400 women were raped in five weeks of occupation of the city of Uvira, in South Kivu province, by the Rwandan army and its proxies. These figures are contained in a Government report presented on Tuesday in Kinshasa to the press by the Minister of Human Rights, Samuel Mbemba.

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that Makolo was criticising an HRW report released on 13 May that accuses Rwandan forces and M23 fighters of killing civilians, abducting them and raping women in Uvira city from 10 December 2025 to 17 January 2026.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Makolo yanengaga raporo HRW yashyize hanze ku wa 13 Gicurasi, ishinja ingabo z’u Rwanda n’abarwanyi b’umutwe witwaje intwaro wa M23 kwica abasivili, kubashimuta no gufata ku ngufu abagore mu Mujyi wa Uvira, kuva tariki ya 10 Ukuboza 2025 kugeza ku ya 17 Mutarama 2026.
statements_all.translation_en: Makolo was criticising the report HRW released on 13 May, which accuses Rwandan forces and fighters of the armed group M23 of killing civilians, abducting them and raping women in Uvira city, from 10 December 2025 until 17 January 2026.

statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that, in a communiqué, the Rwandan government accused the DRC and Burundi of violating the ceasefire, said the FARDC, Burundian troops (FDNB), the FDLR, Wazalendo militias and foreign mercenaries had carried out bombings near the Rwandan border, and claimed Burundi had deployed nearly 20 000 soldiers in South Kivu and besieged Banyamulenge villages at Minembwe.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Kigali affirme encore que le Burundi a déployé près de 20 000 soldats au Sud-Kivu, au service de Kinshasa, et assiégé des villages banyamulenge à Minembwe.
statements_all.translation_en: Kigali further claims that Burundi has deployed nearly 20,000 soldiers in South Kivu, in the service of Kinshasa, and besieged Banyamulenge villages in Minembwe.

statements_all.role: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
statements_all.text: The Government of Rwanda said in a statement that responsibility for ceasefire violations, ongoing attacks and fighting in South Kivu cannot be placed on Rwanda, and condemned the FARDC and the Burundian army (FDNB), together with the FDLR, Wazalendo and foreign mercenaries, which it said have been systematically bombing civilian villages close to the Rwandan border using fighter jets and attack drones.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The responsibility for ceasefire violations, ongoing attacks and fighting in South Kivu, DRC cannot be placed on Rwanda. Rwanda condemns the Congolese Army (FARDC) and the Burundian Army (FDNB), together with its coalition of the DRC-backed FDLR genocidal militias, Wazalendo and foreign mercenaries,

statements_all.role: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
statements_all.text: The Government of Rwanda said in its statement on ceasefire violations that, as a result of the past week's bombing of Kamanyola from Burundi, over 1000 Congolese citizens had fled across the border to Bugarama in western Rwanda, where they were accommodated at the Nyarushishi Transit Camp.
statements_all.excerpt_original: As a result of this past week’s bombing of Kamanyola from Burundi, over 1000 Congolese citizens have fled across the border to Bugarama, in Western Rwanda, where they are accommodated at the Nyarushishi Transit Camp.

statements_all.role: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
statements_all.text: The Government of Rwanda said in its statement on ceasefire violations that the Burundian Army had amassed close to 20,000 troops in South Kivu in the service of the Government of DRC and had laid siege to Banyamulenge villages in Minembwe in a deliberate attempt to starve the residents.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The Burundian Army has amassed close to 20,000 troops in South Kivu in the service of the Government of DRC, and notably laid siege to Banyamulenge villages in Minembwe in a deliberate attempt to starve the residents.

statements_all.role: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
statements_all.text: The Government of Rwanda said in its statement on ceasefire violations that the DRC had openly stated it would not observe any ceasefire and was fighting to recapture territories lost to AFC/M23 even as the peace process unfolded, and that the DRC's failure to neutralize the FDLR as stipulated in the June 2025 Peace Agreement continued to delay the resolution of the conflict in eastern DRC.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The DRC has openly stated that it would not observe any ceasefire, and was fighting to recapture territories lost to AFC/M23, even as the peace process unfolded.

statements_all.setting: statement to local media as reported
statements_all.text: BBC reported that the M23 said it had 'liberated' the city of Uvira, while South Kivu Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi told local media that the army and allied militia remained in control of the city.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The M23 rebel group said it had "liberated" the city, while UN-backed Radio Okapi quoted residents as saying that rebel fighters were on major streets. However, South Kivu Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi told local media that the army and allied militia remained in control of the city, which is just 27km (17 miles) from Burundi's capital, Bujumbura, across Lake Tanganyika.

statements_all.text: Anadolu reported that on Wednesday the Congolese government attributed the violence in Uvira to a 'widespread offensive launched in recent days by the Rwandan Defense Forces' along the Kamanyola-Uvira axis, calling it a 'blatant violation' of the ceasefire and of commitments under recent peace agreements; Kigali denied the accusations.
statements_all.excerpt_original: On Wednesday, the Congolese government attributed the violence in Uvira to a “widespread offensive launched in recent days by the Rwandan Defense Forces” along the Kamanyola-Uvira axis, calling it a “blatant violation” of the ceasefire and the commitments made under recent peace agreements. Kigali denied the accusations.

statements_all.text: Anadolu reported that on Wednesday Rwanda accused the Congolese and Burundian armies of violating a ceasefire provided under the Washington peace deal.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Instead, Rwanda on Wednesday accused the Congolese and Burundian armies of violating a ceasefire provided under a Washington peace deal championed by US President Donald Trump.

statements_all.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a communiqué that captured Burundian soldiers would be handed over to their country's authorities, and that Uvira was totally under M23 control.
statements_all.excerpt_original: « Les soldats burundais capturés seront remis aux autorités de leur pays dans le strict respect des droits humains », a déclaré Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole de l’AFC/M23, dans un communiqué qu’il a partagé avec SOS Médias Burundi mercredi soir. Il a ajouté que la ville d’Uvira est totalement sous contrôle du M23
statements_all.translation_en: “The captured Burundian soldiers will be handed over to the authorities of their country in strict respect of human rights,” said Lawrence Kanyuka, spokesperson of the AFC/M23, in a communiqué he shared with SOS Médias Burundi on Wednesday evening. He added that the city of Uvira is totally under M23 control

statements_all.role: Brig Gen, Deputy Chief of Staff of AFC/M23
statements_all.text: Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu, AFC/M23 deputy chief of staff, arrived in Uvira city on 10 December 2025 and asked the Burundian troops still in the high hills of South Kivu to come down and go home in peace, saying 'We have no problem with the Burundians because we are neighbours'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ubwo Umugaba Mukuru Wungirije wa AFC/M23, Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu yageraga mu Mujyi wa Uvira ku wa 10 Ukuboza 2025, yasabye ingabo z’u Burundi zikiri mu misozi miremire yo muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo ko zamanuka, zigataha mu mahoro.
statements_all.translation_en: When the Deputy Chief of Staff of AFC/M23, Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu, arrived in Uvira city on 10 December 2025, he asked the Burundian troops still in the high hills of South Kivu to come down and go home in peace.

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the DRC government said it had ordered its troops not to confront the M23 as it advanced in Uvira, and explained that it wanted to avoid civilians losing their lives there.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Reta ya Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo ivuga ko yategetse ingabo zayo kutivuna umuhari uyigwanya wa M23 mu gihe uriko uratera intambwe zikomeye mu gisagara ca Uvira, akarere ka nyuma gakomeye kari gasigaye katarafatwa mu buseruko bw'ico gihugu. Reta ya Congo isigura ko yashatse kwirinda ko abasivire bahasiga ubuzima.
statements_all.translation_en: The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo says it ordered its troops not to confront the M23 armed group as it makes major advances in the town of Uvira, the last major area remaining unseized in the east of that country. The government of Congo explains that it wanted to avoid civilians losing their lives there.

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a statement on X that for more than three months AFC/M23 had denounced hate speech, attacks on citizens because of their appearance, and killings 'in the liberated areas' of M23 carried out by fighters allied with the Kinshasa government and its accomplice Burundi, and that the town of Uvira was now 'liberated'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Mw'itangazo ryaciye ku rubuga rwa X rwa Lawrence Kanyuka, umuvugizi w'uwo murwi, avuga ko amenyesha abantu bose ko kuva mu mezi arenga atatu, AFC/M23 yiyamirije amajambo abiba urwanko, ibitero vyibasira abenegihugu kubera uko bavutse basa, n'ubwicanyi bukorerwa "mu turere twabohowe" na M23 bukozwe n'abarwanyi bafashanya na reta ya Kinshasa na somambike wabo, ari we Uburundi.
statements_all.translation_en: In the statement on the X account of Lawrence Kanyuka, the spokesperson of that group, he says he informs everyone that for more than three months AFC/M23 has denounced hate speech, attacks targeting citizens because of how they look by birth, and killings carried out 'in the areas liberated' by M23 by fighters allied with the Kinshasa government and its accomplice, namely Burundi.

statements_all.role: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
statements_all.text: Umunota.com (Rwandan outlet) reported that Rwanda's Foreign Minister, Amb Olivier Jean Patrick Nduhungirehe, said in an RBA interview on the evening of 10 December 2025 that Rwanda is not the one to answer for ceasefire violations, but the FDLR and Burundian troops, who he said have a plan to destabilise Rwanda's security.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Minisitiri w’Ububanyi n’Amahanga n’Ubutwererane w’u Rwanda ,Amb Olivier Jean Patrick Nduhungirehe, yatangaje ko u Rwanda atari rwo rubazwa ibyo kwica agahenge ahubwo FDLR n’ingabo z’u Burundi bifite umugambi wo guhungabanya umutekano warwo. Ni mu kiganiro Amb Nduhungirehe yagiranye na RBA ku mugoroba wo kuwa 10 Ukuboza 2025
statements_all.translation_en: The Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Rwanda, Amb Olivier Jean Patrick Nduhungirehe, stated that it is not Rwanda that is accountable for breaking the ceasefire but the FDLR and Burundian troops, who have a plan to destabilise its security. This was in an interview Amb Nduhungirehe gave to RBA on the evening of 10 December 2025

statements_all.role: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
statements_all.text: Umunota.com reported that Foreign Minister Nduhungirehe, in the same RBA interview, said that Burundian soldiers in South Kivu had now reached twenty thousand, a problem he said Rwanda has raised repeatedly, and alleged that they prevent the Banyamulenge from leaving their areas so as to starve them.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Minisitiri w’Ububanyi n’Amahanga n’Ubutwererane w’u Rwanda ,Amb Olivier Jean Patrick Nduhungirehe, yatangaje ko u Rwanda atari rwo rubazwa ibyo kwica agahenge ahubwo FDLR n’ingabo z’u Burundi bifite umugambi wo guhungabanya umutekano warwo. Ni mu kiganiro Amb Nduhungirehe yagiranye na RBA ku mugoroba wo kuwa 10 Ukuboza 2025
statements_all.translation_en: The Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Rwanda, Amb Olivier Jean Patrick Nduhungirehe, stated that it is not Rwanda that is accountable for breaking the ceasefire but the FDLR and Burundian troops, who have a plan to destabilise its security. This was in an interview Amb Nduhungirehe gave to RBA on the evening of 10 December 2025

statements_all.party: International Contact Group for the Great Lakes
statements_all.text: The International Contact Group for the Great Lakes (United States, Belgium, Denmark, the EU, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland and the UK) urged M23 and the Rwanda Defence Force to immediately halt offensive operations in eastern DRC, in particular in South Kivu, and called on the RDF to withdraw from eastern DRC.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The ICG urges the M23 and the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) to immediately halt offensive operations in eastern DRC, in particular in South Kivu, and calls on the RDF to withdraw from eastern DRC

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi told Radio Okapi on Tuesday that Uvira was controlled by government troops, denying rumours that M23 rebels had entered the town.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Hagati aho, mu gihe buramatari w'intara ya Kivu y'Epfo, Jean-Jacques Purusi, ejo ku wa kabiri yabwiye Radio Okapi yo muri Congo ko Uvira yagenzurwa n'ingabo za reta akabeshuza ibihuha vyavuga ko inyeshamba za M23 zoba zari zinjiye muri iki gisagara
statements_all.translation_en: Meanwhile, as the governor of South Kivu province, Jean-Jacques Purusi, yesterday on Tuesday told Radio Okapi of Congo that Uvira was controlled by government forces and denied rumours that M23 rebels had entered this town

statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that, in Gitega on Monday, Burundi's foreign minister Edouard Bizimana told diplomats that Rwanda had targeted Burundian territory and dropped three bombs, wounding two civilians, a child and a woman, and that Burundian positions in the DRC had been attacked by Rwanda since 2 December, including with drones.
statements_all.excerpt_original: « Ils ont ciblé notre territoire et largué trois bombes. Ces attaques ont fait deux blessés civils, un enfant et une femme », a déclaré le ministre des Affaires étrangères, Edouard Bizimana, devant des diplomates. Il affirme que « dès le 2 décembre », des positions burundaises en RDC ont été attaquées par le Rwanda, y compris avec des drones.
statements_all.translation_en: "They targeted our territory and dropped three bombs. These attacks left two civilians wounded, a child and a woman," said the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Edouard Bizimana, before diplomats. He states that "from 2 December", Burundian positions in the DRC were attacked by Rwanda, including with drones.

statements_all.text: Africa Insight reported that Burundian foreign minister Edouard Bizimana told diplomats on 8 December 2025 that the AFC/M23 coalition had sought to capture Uvira before the 4 December Washington peace accord but Burundian troops had intervened.
statements_all.excerpt_original: S'adressant aux diplomates le 8 décembre 2025, le ministre Bizimana a souligné que la coalition AFC/M23 avait cherché à capturer Uvira avant l'accord de paix de Washington signé le 4 décembre, mais que les troupes burundaises étaient intervenues.
statements_all.translation_en: Addressing diplomats on 8 December 2025, Minister Bizimana stressed that the AFC/M23 coalition had sought to capture Uvira before the Washington peace agreement signed on 4 December, but that Burundian troops had intervened.

statements_all.text: DW reported that President Félix Tshisekedi, in a speech to Congolese parliamentarians on Monday, said that as long as a single village, neighbourhood or hill remained under the threat of illegal arms, he would consider his task unfinished; DW added that the speech did not reassure residents of Uvira territory.
statements_all.excerpt_original: D'un ton ferme, le président Félix Tshisekedi a voulu rassurer les Congolais : "Tant qu'un seul village, tant qu'un seul quartier, tant qu'une seule colline de ce pays restera sous la menace des armes illégales, je considérerai que notre tâche n'est pas achevée."
statements_all.translation_en: In a firm tone, President Félix Tshisekedi wanted to reassure Congolese: "As long as a single village, a single neighbourhood, a single hill of this country remains under the threat of illegal arms, I will consider our task unfinished."

statements_all.setting: remarks to diplomats and press as reported
statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Burundi accuses Rwanda of continuing to attack the positions of its soldiers sent to eastern DRC; that Burundi's Minister of Foreign Affairs Edouard Bizimana, speaking on Monday before representatives of countries in Burundi, said without giving proof that the aim of the attacks was for Rwanda and M23 to capture Uvira before 25 December 2025; and that the Rwandan government had not yet responded.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Uburundi buragiriza Urwanda ko ari rwo rubandanya rutera ibirindiro vy'abasirikare babwo barungitswe mu buseruko bwa Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo, kandi ko igihugu kidashobora kurera amaboko mu gihe kizobandanya giterwa.
statements_all.translation_en: Burundi accuses Rwanda of being the one that continues to attack the positions of its soldiers sent to the east of the Democratic Republic of Congo, and that the country cannot sit with arms folded while it continues to be attacked.

statements_all.text: Anadolu reported that Burundi's Foreign Minister Edouard Bizimana warned on Monday that 'any attack targeting Burundian citizens or soldiers deployed in the DRC will never be tolerated'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: But on Monday, Burundi’s Foreign Minister Edouard Bizimana warned that “any attack targeting Burundian citizens or soldiers deployed in the DRC will never be tolerated.

statements_all.setting: briefing to diplomats, as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Burundi's Foreign Minister Dr. Edouard Bizimana said at a briefing with diplomats on 8 December 2025, according to Igihe, that AFC/M23 had aimed to take the city of Uvira before the Washington peace agreement was signed on 4 December but, he said, was held back by Burundian forces.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Minisitiri w’Ububanyi n’Amahanga w’u Burundi, Dr. Edouard Bizimana, yiteye akanyabugabo nyuma y’aho abasirikare benshi b’igihugu cye bapfiriye muri teritwari ya Uvira mu burasirazuba bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo. Mu kiganiro n’abadipolomate cyabaye ku wa 8 Ukuboza 2025, Minisitiri Bizimana yatangaje ko AFC/M23 yari ifite intego yo gufata umujyi wa Uvira mbere y’uko amasezerano y’amahoro ya Washington ashyirwaho umukono ku wa 4 Ukuboza ariko ngo yakomwe mu nkokora n’ingabo z’u Burundi.
statements_all.translation_en: At a briefing with diplomats held on 8 December 2025, Minister Bizimana announced that AFC/M23 had the aim of taking the city of Uvira before the Washington peace agreement was signed on 4 December, but it was reportedly hindered by Burundian forces.

statements_all.setting: briefing to diplomats, as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Bizimana said, according to Igihe ('uyu muyobozi', this official, read as the minister from the preceding paragraph), that Burundian troops went to the DRC to protect Burundi's borders, Burundians and their property, that they cannot leave while the problems that took them there remain unsolved, and that they went there with the agreement of the Congolese government.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Mu kiganiro n’abadipolomate cyabaye ku wa 8 Ukuboza 2025, Minisitiri Bizimana yatangaje ko AFC/M23 yari ifite intego yo gufata umujyi wa Uvira mbere y’uko amasezerano y’amahoro ya Washington ashyirwaho umukono ku wa 4 Ukuboza ariko ngo yakomwe mu nkokora n’ingabo z’u Burundi. Yagize ati “Bo bashakaga ko amasezerano asinywa bamaze gufata Luvungi na Uvira. Ariko ntibyaboroheye, ingabo zacu zahagaze neza, zirwanya umwanzi. Ndagira ngo mfate uyu mwanya nshimire abasirikare b’Abarundi bari guharanira amahoro muri Congo uko bitanze kugira ngo umwanzi ntavogere igihugu cyacu.” Uyu muyobozi yatangaje ko ingabo z’u Burundi zagiye muri RDC kugira ngo zirinde imbibi z’igihugu cyazo, kandi ko zidashobora kuvayo mu gihe ibibazo byazijyanyeyo bitarakemuka.
statements_all.translation_en: This official announced that Burundian forces went to the DRC to protect the borders of their country, and that they cannot leave while the problems that took them there have not been resolved.

statements_all.setting: briefing to diplomats, as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Igihe reported that Bizimana asserted AFC/M23's aim was to take Uvira before Christmas, and that as of 8 December 2025 AFC/M23 fighters were within 30 kilometres of Uvira city.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Kugeza tariki ya 8 Ukuboza 2025, abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 bari mu ntera y’ibilometero 30 bagana mu mujyi wa Uvira. Minisitiri Bizimana ahamya ko bafite intego yo gufata uyu mujyi mbere ya Noheli,
statements_all.translation_en: Up to 8 December 2025, AFC/M23 fighters were within 30 kilometres of the city of Uvira. Minister Bizimana asserts that they intend to take this city before Christmas,

statements_all.text: Umunota.com reported that, on the Monday of the week of publication, Burundi's Foreign Minister Bizimana Edouard, speaking with representatives of countries in Burundi, said that Rwanda had attacked the positions of Burundian troops in the DRC and allegedly had a plan to attack them, and that they would therefore defend themselves.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ubwo ku wa mbere w’iki cyumweru, Minisitiri w’Ububanyi n’Amahanga w’u Burundi, Bizimana Edouard , yagiranaga ikiganiro n’abahagarariye ibihugu byabo mu Burundi, yavuze ko u Rwanda rwateye ibirindiro by’ingabo zabo ziri muri RDcongo ndetse ko ngo rufite umugambi wo kubatera bityo bazirwanaho.
statements_all.translation_en: On Monday of this week, Burundi's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Bizimana Edouard, while holding talks with the representatives of their countries in Burundi, said that Rwanda had attacked the positions of their troops in the DRC and that it allegedly has a plan to attack them, and that they will therefore defend themselves.

statements_all.setting: statement as reported by Igihe (channel not stated)
statements_all.text: AFC/M23 military spokesperson Lt Col Willy Ngoma said on 6 December, according to Igihe, 'Those who crossed over have learned a lesson', that 'Congo is not Cibitoke, nor Ngozi or their Bujumbura', and that they come to AFC/M23's home where it is fighting for the truth.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23 mu rwego rwa gisirikare, Lt Col Willy Ngoma, tariki ya 6 Ukuboza yagize ati “Abambutse babonye isomo. Basanze abagabo turi maso kandi tuzaba maso. Congo ntabwo ari Cibitoke, ntabwo ari Ngozi cyangwa Bujumbura yabo, oya. Baradusanga iwacu, turwanirira ukuri, kandi bazabibona.”
statements_all.translation_en: The AFC/M23 military spokesperson, Lt Col Willy Ngoma, said on 6 December: "Those who crossed over have learned a lesson. They found men who are alert, and we will stay alert. Congo is not Cibitoke, it is not Ngozi or their Bujumbura, no. They come to us in our home, we are fighting for the truth, and they will see."

statements_all.role: Deputy leader of AFC/M23 for political affairs
statements_all.text: Bertrand Bisimwa, Deputy Leader of AFC/M23 in charge of political activities, said, according to Igihe, that Burundian forces inside Burundi were shelling heavily populated areas of Kamanyola, Katogota and Luvungi, causing the deaths of innocent people including children and destroying houses, schools, churches and markets.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Umuyobozi Wungirije wa AFC/M23 ushinzwe ibikorwa bya politiki, Bertrand Bisimwa, yatangaje ko ingabo z’Abarundi ziri mu Burundi ziri kurasa muri Kamanyola, Katogota na Luvungi. Ati “Muri iki gitondo, ingabo z’u Burundi ziri mu Burundi ziri gusuka ibisasu mu bice bituwe cyane muri Kamanyola, Katogota na Luvungi, zigateza imfu z’inzirakarengane zirimo abana, zigasenya inzu, amashuri, insengero n’amasoko.”
statements_all.translation_en: The Deputy Leader of AFC/M23 in charge of political activities, Bertrand Bisimwa, stated that Burundian forces who are in Burundi are firing into Kamanyola, Katogota and Luvungi. He said: “This morning, Burundian forces who are in Burundi are pouring shells onto densely inhabited areas in Kamanyola, Katogota and Luvungi, causing deaths of innocents including children, destroying houses, schools, churches and markets.”

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that the fighting continued after Rwanda and the DRC signed a peace agreement on 4 December 2025, which AFC/M23 said does not concern it.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Iyi mirwano ikomeje mu gihe ku wa 4 Ukuboza 2025, u Rwanda na RDC byashyize umukono ku masezerano y'amahoro, ibintu AFC/M23 yavuze ko ibyo biganiro n'ayo masezerano bitayireba.
statements_all.translation_en: This fighting continues while on 4 December 2025 Rwanda and the DRC signed a peace agreement, something that AFC/M23 said these talks and that agreement do not concern it.

statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a communiqué on his X account, accused the FARDC of attacks on its positions and said that at least three civilians were killed and five others injured in a FARDC strike at Kamanyola.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Dans un communiqué sur son compte X, Lawrence Kanyuka porte parole de l’AFC-M23 a accusé les FARDC d’attaques contre leurs positions. Il a indiqué qu’au moins trois civils ont été tués et 5 autres blessés lors d’une frappe des FARDC à Kamanyola.
statements_all.translation_en: In a communiqué on his X account, Lawrence Kanyuka, spokesperson of the AFC-M23, accused the FARDC of attacks on their positions. He said that at least three civilians were killed and 5 others injured in a FARDC strike at Kamanyola.

statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the 33rd military region of the FARDC, based at Uvira, said it had stopped attacks by AFC-M23 fighters, and that the region's spokesperson Captain Sylvain Bijanu said these 'enemies of peace' had also attacked its positions at Rugezi and Ngungu (Minembwe), Kaziba (Walungu), Kasika (Mwenga) and Civanga-Hombo (Kalehe).
statements_all.excerpt_original: La 33ème région militaire des Forces armées congolaise basée à Uvira a affirmé avoir stopper les attaques des combattants de l’AFC-M23.
statements_all.translation_en: The 33rd military region of the Congolese armed forces, based in Uvira, said it had stopped the attacks of the AFC-M23 fighters.

statements_all.text: Iwacu reported that, at his press conference, President Ndayishimiye spoke again about his decision to send troops to eastern DRC to support the FARDC and curb incursions by certain Burundian rebel groups based in South Kivu; Iwacu noted he gave no further details.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Il est revenu sur sa décision d’envoyer des troupes à l’est de la RDC pour épauler les FARDC et juguler les incursions de certains groupes rebelles burundais basés au Sud-Kivu, sans plus de précisions.
statements_all.translation_en: He went back on his decision to send troops to eastern DRC to support the FARDC and curb the incursions of certain Burundian rebel groups based in South Kivu, without further details.

statements_all.text: Iwacu reported that President Ndayishimiye said at his press conference that he had asked the AFC-M23 rebels whether they were really Congolese, that they admitted they were, and that he had proposed they accept being cantoned at Rumangabo so that a negotiation, disarmament, demobilisation and reintegration process could follow, "mais la guerre a repris de plus belle" (but the war resumed all the more).
statements_all.excerpt_original: « J’ai demandé aux rebelles de la coalition AFC-M23, qualifiés par la partie congolaise de pro rwandais ou carrément de Rwandais, s’ils sont réellement de nationalité congolaise et ils m’ont avoué qu’ils sont bel et bien des Congolais.
statements_all.translation_en: "I asked the rebels of the AFC-M23 coalition, described by the Congolese side as pro-Rwandan or even outright Rwandan, whether they are really of Congolese nationality, and they admitted to me that they are indeed Congolese.

statements_all.text: The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani reported that the AFC-M23 rebels had issued a communiqué asking Burundi to withdraw its forces and proposing the opening of a humanitarian corridor to facilitate their return.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Les rebelles de l’AFC-M23 ont diffusé un communiqué dans lequel ils demandent au Burundi de retirer ses forces, proposant l’ouverture d’un corridor humanitaire pour faciliter leur retour
statements_all.translation_en: The AFC-M23 rebels issued a communiqué in which they ask Burundi to withdraw its forces, proposing the opening of a humanitarian corridor to facilitate their return

statements_all.text: The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani reported that Burundi had affirmed its will to keep its troops on Congolese soil and to continue operations alongside the FARDC, in line with the bilateral partnership, according to its foreign minister, Édouard BIZIMANA.
statements_all.excerpt_original: De son côté, le Burundi a affirmé sa volonté de maintenir ses troupes sur le sol congolais et de poursuivre les opérations aux côtés des FARDC, conformément au partenariat bilatéral entre les deux pays afin d’assurer aussi la sécurité de son pays, à en croire son Ministre des affaires étrangères, Édouard BIZIMANA8.
statements_all.translation_en: For its part, Burundi affirmed its will to keep its troops on Congolese soil and to continue operations alongside the FARDC, in accordance with the bilateral partnership between the two countries in order to also ensure the security of its own country, according to its Minister of Foreign Affairs, Édouard BIZIMANA.

statements_all.text: Iwacu reported that, in an RFI interview, Burundian foreign minister Edouard Bizimana said the rebels used heavy weapons, artillery and Turkish-made kamikaze drones and "launched bombs on civilian populations, forcing people to flee".
statements_all.excerpt_original: Selon lui, les rebelles ont utilisé des armes lourdes, de l’artillerie et même des drones kamikazes de fabrication turque. « Ce que nous regrettons, c’est que ce sont des armes qui tuent à l’aveuglette. Ils ont lancé des bombes sur les populations civiles, obligeant les gens à fuir. »
statements_all.translation_en: According to him, the rebels used heavy weapons, artillery and even Turkish-made kamikaze drones. "What we regret is that these are weapons that kill blindly. They launched bombs on civilian populations, forcing people to flee."

statements_all.text: Iwacu reported that Bizimana said in an RFI interview that if the rebels and their Rwandan allies entered Uvira "all options are on the table", adding "What threatens Uvira also threatens Bujumbura".
statements_all.excerpt_original: Il avait également averti : si les rebelles et leurs alliés rwandais entrent dans Uvira, « toutes les options sont sur la table », car Uvira et Bujumbura sont deux villes côtières. « Ce qui menace Uvira menace aussi Bujumbura.
statements_all.translation_en: He had also warned: if the rebels and their Rwandan allies enter Uvira, "all options are on the table", because Uvira and Bujumbura are two coastal cities. "What threatens Uvira also threatens Bujumbura.

statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that Burundi's ambassador to the UN, Zéphyrin Maniratanga, told a special session on the crisis in the east that bombardments from Rwanda hit the commune of Tshibitoke on 4 December, wounding a woman and a child, and warned that Burundi's restraint "has limits" and that it reserved the right to self-defence under the UN Charter in case of new attacks.
statements_all.excerpt_original: l’ambassadeur burundais auprès des Nations unies, Zéphyrin Maniratanga, a affirmé que des bombardements en provenance du Rwanda avaient touché la commune de Tshibitoke le 4 décembre, blessant une femme et un enfant.
statements_all.translation_en: the Burundian ambassador to the United Nations, Zéphyrin Maniratanga, stated that bombings coming from Rwanda had hit the commune of Tshibitoke on 4 December, wounding a woman and a child.

statements_all.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that additional AFC/M23 public justifications for the offensive on Uvira cited the presence of FDLR-FOCA elements operating alongside FARDC and FDNB, and said it did not identify evidence that such elements posed a direct threat to Rwanda justifying military intervention in the DRC.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Additional claims cited the presence of FDLR-FOCA elements operating alongside FARDC and FDNB. The Group of Experts did not identify evidence th at such elements posed a direct threat to Rwanda justifying military intervention in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (see S/2025/446, annex 24).

statements_all.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several security sources, that a large part of the Burundian soldiers withdrew in December 2025 following M23 advances in South Kivu and losses suffered by the FDNB; it reported that the secretary general of the CNDD-FDD had spoken of a 'strategic withdrawal' ('retrait stratégique'), saying Burundi remained master of its military decisions, and quoted Révérien Ndikuriyo as having declared: 'it is like at home, we go there when we want'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: à la suite des avancées spectaculaires du M23 dans le Sud-Kivu et des pertes subies par la FDNB (Force de défense nationale du Burundi). Récemment, le secrétaire général du CNDD-FDD, l’ancienne rébellion hutu au pouvoir au Burundi depuis 2005, a évoqué un « retrait stratégique », affirmant que le Burundi restait maître de ses décisions militaires.
statements_all.translation_en: following the spectacular M23 advances in South Kivu and the losses suffered by the FDNB. Recently, the secretary general of the CNDD-FDD, the former Hutu rebellion in power in Burundi since 2005, spoke of a 'strategic withdrawal', stating that Burundi remained master of its military decisions.

statements_all.role: Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe, in a statement posted on his X account after an African Union Peace and Security Council meeting, said Rwanda welcomed the unilateral withdrawal of AFC/M23 from Uvira as a goodwill gesture towards the mediators and a strong signal of readiness to return to the negotiating table.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Olivier Nduhungirehe, dans une déclaration publiée sur son compte X, à l’issue d’une réunion du Conseil de paix et de sécurité de l’Union africaine. « Le Rwanda accueille favorablement le retrait unilatéral de l’AFC/M23 d’Uvira, en tant que geste de bonne volonté envers les médiateurs et signal fort de disponibilité à retourner à la table des négociations
statements_all.translation_en: Olivier Nduhungirehe, in a statement published on his X account after a meeting of the African Union Peace and Security Council. "Rwanda welcomes the unilateral withdrawal of AFC/M23 from Uvira, as a goodwill gesture towards the mediators and a strong signal of readiness to return to the negotiating table"

statements_all.role: Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Rwanda also reiterated its concerns about what it called daily ceasefire violations by the Kinshasa-backed armed coalition, saying that a ceasefire binds both parties to a conflict equally and cannot be imposed on only one.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Le Rwanda a par ailleurs réitéré ses préoccupations concernant ce qu’il qualifie de « violations quotidiennes du cessez-le-feu » par la coalition armée soutenue par Kinshasa, rappelant qu’« un cessez-le-feu engage de manière égale les deux parties à un conflit et ne peut être imposé à une seule ».
statements_all.translation_en: Rwanda also reiterated its concerns about what it calls "daily ceasefire violations" by the armed coalition backed by Kinshasa, recalling that "a ceasefire binds both parties to a conflict equally and cannot be imposed on only one".

statements_all.role: finance minister (unnamed in the source excerpt)
statements_all.setting: testimony to parliamentary committee, as reported by Amnesty International
statements_all.text: Amnesty International said that the FARDC supports the armed groups financially and with weapons and ammunition, and that the DRC's finance minister told the National Assembly's Defence and Security Committee in December 2025 that the state pays Wazalendo groups US$4 million per month.
statements_all.excerpt_original: FARDC supports the armed groups financially and with weapons and ammunition. The DRC’s finance minister told the National Assembly’s Defence and Security Committee in December 2025 that the state pays Wazalendo groups US$ 4 million per month .

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that Wazalendo groups affirm that some Burundian soldiers fled with them into the Itombwe forest, where they were going to regroup to attack various areas controlled by AFC/M23.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Imitwe ya Wazalendo ihamya ko hari abasirikare b’u Burundi bahunganye na yo mu ishyamba rya Itombwe, aho bagiye kwisuganyiriza kugira ngo bazatere ibice bitandukanye bigenzurwa na AFC/M23.
statements_all.translation_en: The Wazalendo groups affirm that there are Burundian soldiers who fled with them in the Itombwe forest, where they have gone to regroup so as to attack various areas controlled by AFC/M23.

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that, after M23 took Uvira, Burundi's foreign minister Édouard Bizimana told the news agency AFP that signing agreements and then not implementing them is contempt for everyone, first of all for President Trump.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Nyuma yuko M23 ifashe Uvira, Minisitiri w'ububanyi n'amahanga w'u Burundi Édouard Bizimana yavuze ko byabaye "gukubita urushyi mu maso
statements_all.translation_en: After M23 took Uvira, the minister of foreign affairs of Burundi Édouard Bizimana said that it was a "slap in the face

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Burundi's foreign minister Édouard Bizimana had told Radio RFI, before the capture of Uvira, that 'those troops' would leave only if the Kinshasa government asked for it, because it was with Kinshasa that they had made the agreement.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Minisitiri w'ububanyi n'amahanga w'u Burundi Édouard Bizimana yari yabwiye Radio RFI y'Abafaransa mbere y'ifatwa rya Uvira ko izo ngabo zahava gusa ari uko leta ya Kinshasa ibisabye kuko ari yo bagiranye amasezerano.
statements_all.translation_en: Burundi's Minister of Foreign Affairs Édouard Bizimana had told the French radio RFI before the capture of Uvira that those troops would leave only if the Kinshasa government asked for it, because it is with it that they made the agreement.

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwanda's ambassador to the UN, Martin Ngoga, said that Rwanda has no plan to attack Burundi, and that M23 had also said earlier that it has no such plan.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ambasaderi w'u Rwanda muri ONU Martin Ngoga yavuze ko nta mugambi rufite wo gutera u Burundi. Mbere, M23 na yo yavuze ko nta mugambi nk'uwo ifite.
statements_all.translation_en: Rwanda's ambassador to the UN Martin Ngoga said that it has no plan to attack Burundi. Earlier, M23 also said that it has no such plan.

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 had said earlier that it has no plan to attack Burundi.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ambasaderi w'u Rwanda muri ONU Martin Ngoga yavuze ko nta mugambi rufite wo gutera u Burundi. Mbere, M23 na yo yavuze ko nta mugambi nk'uwo ifite.
statements_all.translation_en: Rwanda's ambassador to the UN Martin Ngoga said that it has no plan to attack Burundi. Earlier, M23 also said that it has no such plan.

statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to Kagame, a contingent of more than twenty thousand Burundian soldiers was said to be operating in several provinces, notably Uvira, Minembwe, Kalemie, Kindu, Walikale and Kisangani, and that he accused Burundi of regular strikes against civilians, notably at Minembwe; the outlet wrote that at the time of publication the Burundian authorities had not reacted.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Selon Kagame, un contingent de plus de vingt mille soldats burundais opérerait actuellement dans plusieurs provinces, notamment Uvira, Minembwe, Kalemie, Kindu, Walikale et Kisangani. Il accuse également le Burundi de frappes régulières contre les civils, notamment à Minembwe, et déplore le silence de la communauté internationale.
statements_all.translation_en: According to Kagame, a contingent of more than twenty thousand Burundian soldiers would currently be operating in several provinces, notably Uvira, Minembwe, Kalemie, Kindu, Walikale and Kisangani. He also accuses Burundi of regular strikes against civilians, notably at Minembwe, and laments the silence of the international community.

statements_all.setting: social-media post or public reply as reported by a Rwandan outlet (platform not named in the excerpt)
statements_all.text: UMUSEKE reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo said the RDC government cannot pursue the process of halting the fighting while it is itself the one starting the war; she was replying to Patrick Muyaya, minister of information, who had explained that President Tshisekedi said Rwanda was violating the agreements by launching attacks in South Kivu. UMUSEKE also reported that Makolo stressed that Rwanda has nothing to do with the fighting continuing in South Kivu.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Umuvugizi wa Guverinoma, Yolande Makolo, yavuze ko Leta ya RDC idashobora gukurikirana inzira yo guhagarika imirwano kandi ari yo gashozantambara. Yasubizaga Minisitiri w’Itangazamakuru Patrick Muyaya, wasobanuraga ko Perezida Tshisekedi yavuze ko u Rwanda rurenga ku masezerano rugaba ibitero muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo.
statements_all.translation_en: The government spokesperson, Yolande Makolo, said that the DRC government cannot pursue [or: monitor] the process of halting the fighting while it is itself the instigator of the war. She was replying to the Minister of Information Patrick Muyaya, who explained that President Tshisekedi said that Rwanda violates the agreements by launching attacks in South Kivu.

statements_all.role: spokesperson, Ministry of National Defence and Veterans
statements_all.text: Burundi Forum reported that the FDNB published a communiqué, also relayed on its X account, in which spokesperson Brigadier General Baratuza Gaspard said that no FDNB soldier was currently in the locality of Minembwe and that comments relayed on social media questioning the conduct of Burundian soldiers deployed in the DRC were "sans fondement" (unfounded).
statements_all.excerpt_original: Le Général de Brigade Baratuza Gaspard, porte-parole du Ministère de la Défense Nationale et des Anciens Combattants , a affirmé qu’aucun militaire de la FDNB ne se trouve actuellement dans la localité de Minembwe.
statements_all.translation_en: Brigadier General Baratuza Gaspard, spokesperson of the Ministry of National Defence and Veterans, affirmed that no FDNB soldier is currently in the locality of Minembwe.

statements_all.role: Burundian army (institution), as reported by BBC
statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Burundian army admitted it had closed the roads, aiming to 'protect Uvira and the Burundian border', and asked residents in Minembwe to 'separate themselves from the enemies' there.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Igisirikare c'Uburundi caremeye ko ari co cazibiye aya mayira mu ntumbero yo "gukingira Uvira n'urubibe rw'Uburundi", kigasaba abanyagihugu bari i Minembwe "kuvavanura n'abansi" bariyo.
statements_all.translation_en: The Burundian army admitted that it is the one that blocked these roads with the aim of "protecting Uvira and the Burundian border", and asked the citizens in Minembwe to "separate from the enemies" who are there.

statements_all.text: DW Kiswahili reported that, after AFC/M23 reached Bukavu, rape cases were later witnessed although they were dismissed by AFC/M23; it quoted women's rights defender Nono Mwavita as saying women's security has not improved.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Lakini pia baadae visa vya ubakaji vilishuhudiwa licha yakuwa vilitupiliwa mbali na AFC/M23.
statements_all.translation_en: But later cases of rape were also witnessed, although they were dismissed by AFC/M23.

statements_all.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that several Uvira members of parliament, including national deputy Justin Bitakwira Bihona-Hayi, condemned abuses and killings attributed to some Wazalendo elements.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Wakikabiliwa na ongezeko hili, wabunge kadhaa kutoka Uvira, akiwemo Justin Bitakwira Bihona-Hayi, naibu wa kitaifa kutoka Uvira, walilaani dhuluma na mauaji yanayohusishwa na baadhi ya vipengele vya Wazalendo.
statements_all.translation_en: Faced with this increase, several members of parliament from Uvira, including Justin Bitakwira Bihona-Hayi, national deputy from Uvira, condemned the abuses and killings attributed to some Wazalendo elements.

statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Congolese army accused the rebels of carrying out several attacks on its positions in Rutshuru, Masisi and Kalehe and said it would not let this happen.
statements_all.excerpt_original: L’armée accuse les rebelles de mener plusieurs attaques contre ses positions à Rutshuru, Masisi et Kalehe, et affirme qu’elle ne va pas laisser faire. De son côté, l’AFC-M23 accuse les FARDC de violer l’accord signé à Doha en rompant le cessez-le-feu.
statements_all.translation_en: The army accuses the rebels of carrying out several attacks on its positions in Rutshuru, Masisi and Kalehe, and says it will not let this happen. For its part, the AFC-M23 accuses the FARDC of violating the agreement signed in Doha by breaking the ceasefire.

statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, for its part, the AFC-M23 accused the FARDC of violating the agreement signed in Doha by breaking the ceasefire.
statements_all.excerpt_original: L’armée accuse les rebelles de mener plusieurs attaques contre ses positions à Rutshuru, Masisi et Kalehe, et affirme qu’elle ne va pas laisser faire. De son côté, l’AFC-M23 accuse les FARDC de violer l’accord signé à Doha en rompant le cessez-le-feu.
statements_all.translation_en: The army accuses the rebels of carrying out several attacks on its positions in Rutshuru, Masisi and Kalehe, and says it will not let this happen. For its part, the AFC-M23 accuses the FARDC of violating the agreement signed in Doha by breaking the ceasefire.

statements_all.text: 7sur7.cd reported that, according to a communiqué of the South Kivu provincial government signed by its spokesperson Luganywa Bashizi Didier, six civilian men, including patients and health-care staff, were killed by AFC/M23 rebels in Irambi Katana grouping (Kabare) in an attack on the night of 23 to 24 November 2025 on the Cahoboka dispensary; the communiqué said the victims were forcibly taken from the facility and subjected to cruel treatment before being summarily executed.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Selon un communiqué du gouvernement provincial du Sud-Kivu et signé par son porte-parole, Luganywa Bashizi Didier, ces civils ont été tués dans une attaque perpétrée dans la nuit du 23 au 24 novembre 2025 contre le dispensaire de Cahoboka à Katana.
statements_all.translation_en: According to a communiqué of the South Kivu provincial government signed by its spokesperson, Luganywa Bashizi Didier, these civilians were killed in an attack carried out in the night of 23 to 24 November 2025 against the Cahoboka dispensary in Katana.

statements_all.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that in a statement published on 23 November the FARDC denounced violence by what it called 'fake Wazalendo'; per the army, Sunday's clashes killed four people (one FARDC soldier, two Wazalendo fighters, a civilian motorcycle rider) and wounded 14.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Katika taarifa iliyochapishwa mnamo Novemba 23, FARDC ilishutumu ghasia zinazofanywa na kile wanachoita “Wazalendo feki,”
statements_all.translation_en: In a statement published on November 23, FARDC condemned violence committed by what they call “fake Wazalendo,”

statements_all.text: UN News reported that UN Secretary-General António Guterres, in a press release, 'fermement condamné' (strongly condemned) the attacks attributed to the ADF in North Kivu and expressed his condolences to bereaved families, and that the UN Security Council, in a statement, reaffirmed its 'détermination' to support the peace process and demanded humanitarian access that is 'total, sûr et sans entrave'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Dans un communiqué de presse, António Guterres a « fermement condamné » ces attaques attribuées aux Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF), une milice originaire de l'Ouganda voisin, et exprimé ses « plus sincères condoléances aux familles et communautés endeuillées ».
statements_all.translation_en: In a press release, António Guterres 'strongly condemned' these attacks attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a militia originating from neighbouring Uganda, and expressed his 'deepest condolences to the bereaved families and communities'.

statements_all.text: A Wazalendo spokesperson told Kivu Morning Post that the AFC Twirwaneho M23 attacked Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma and Kwasabuni, on the high plateaux south of Minembwe, on the morning of Friday 21 November 2025, in violation of the Doha framework agreement.
statements_all.excerpt_original: « Le matin de ce vendredi, l’AFC Twirwaneho M23, en violation de l’accord-cadre de Doha, a attaqué Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma et Kwasabuni, sur les hauts plateaux au sud de Minembwe, devenus cibles ce matin », a déclaré un porte-parole des Wazalendo.
statements_all.translation_en: 'This Friday morning, the AFC Twirwaneho M23, in violation of the Doha framework agreement, attacked Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma and Kwasabuni, on the high plateaux south of Minembwe, which became targets this morning', a Wazalendo spokesperson said.

statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Wazalendo, in a communiqué denouncing attacks against them, stated that on 15 November 2025 the positions of the ANCDH/AFDP at Kashanje (Masisi), of the UPLC/EPLC at Mikenge (Mwenga) and of the CMC/FDP at Kitunda (Rutshuru) were attacked.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ils affirment que le 15 novembre 2025, les positions de l’ANCDH/AFDP à Kashanje (Masisi), de l’UPLC/EPLC à Mikenge (Mwenga) et du CMC/FDP à Kitunda (Rutshuru) ont été attaquées.
statements_all.translation_en: They state that on 15 November 2025, the positions of the ANCDH/AFDP at Kashanje (Masisi), of the UPLC/EPLC at Mikenge (Mwenga) and of the CMC/FDP at Kitunda (Rutshuru) were attacked.

statements_all.person: Dr. Mohammed bin Abdulaziz bin Saleh Al Khulaifi
statements_all.role: Minister of State, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
statements_all.text: The Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that Minister of State Dr. Mohammed bin Abdulaziz bin Saleh Al Khulaifi affirmed that the signing of the Doha Framework Agreement for Peace between the DRC government and the Congo River Alliance (March 23 Movement), which took place Saturday, represents an important step.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Dr. Mohammed bin Abdulaziz bin Saleh Al Khulaifi affirmed that the signing of the Doha Framework Agreement for Peace between the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and the Congo River Alliance (March 23 Movement), which took place Saturday, represents an important step

statements_all.text: The Government of Rwanda welcomed, in a statement carried on its foreign ministry's news listing, 'today's signing' of the Doha Framework for a Comprehensive Peace Agreement between the DRC Government and the AFC/M23.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The Government of Rwanda welcomes today’s signing of the Doha Framework for a Comprehensive Peace Agreement between the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and the AFC/M23.

statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that the toll of the ADF attack in Byambwe/Biambwe, Lubero territory, on the night of Friday 14 November was revised from 20 to 28 killed, including 17 patients executed at the reference health centre, per Lubero territory administrator colonel Kiwewa Mitela Alain, who called the figures provisional. A caregiver quoted by Actualite.cd said the maternity ward and operating theatre were burned and medicines looted, and that 17 people including four breastfeeding women were executed in their hospital beds.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Le bilan de la récente attaque meurtrière des islamistes ADF à Byambwe, dans le territoire de Lubero, dans la nuit du vendredi 14 novembre, a été revu à la hausse, passant de 20 à 28 personnes tuées, dont 17 patients exécutés au centre de santé de référence de la localité.
statements_all.translation_en: The toll of the recent deadly attack by the Islamist ADF in Byambwe, in Lubero territory, on the night of Friday 14 November, has been revised upward, from 20 to 28 people killed, including 17 patients executed at the locality's reference health centre.

statements_all.setting: radio interview (BBC Gahuza), as characterised by IGIHE
statements_all.text: IGIHE, a Rwandan state-aligned outlet, reported that Burundian army spokesperson General Gaspard Baratuza, in a radio interview with BBC Gahuza, mentioned the presence of FNL and Red Tabara fighters at Minembwe.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Le porte parole évoque parallèlement la présence de combattants du Front national de libération (FNL) et de Résistance pour un État de Droit (Red Tabara) à Minembwe.
statements_all.translation_en: The spokesperson also mentions the presence of fighters of the Front national de libération (FNL) and of Résistance pour un État de Droit (Red Tabara) at Minembwe.
