statements_all.excerpt_original: Subsequently, the rebel group announced its withdrawal, describing this decision as "a choice aimed at creating a climate conducive to political dialogue". Despite this withdrawal, the M23 called on local authorities and residents to guarantee security in the region.

statements_all.text: DW Swahili reported that the Congolese army said M23's claims were not true and that a video showing fighters captured in Congo being handed over to Rwanda was 'forged'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Jeshi la Kongo limesema madai hayo ya M23 siyo ya kweli na hata mkanda wa video ulioonesha wapiganaji waliokamatwa Kongo wakikabidhiwa kwa Rwanda ni wa "kughushi".
statements_all.translation_en: The Congolese army said those claims by M23 are not true and even the video showing fighters captured in Congo being handed over to Rwanda is "forged".

statements_all.text: Anadolu Agency reported that FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza said in a message on X that no Burundian soldier was deployed in the city of Bukavu, rejecting the M23's accusation after the double explosion at an M23 rally; Anadolu quoted M23 president Bertrand Bisimwa as saying preliminary investigations indicated the explosives were those used by the FDNB.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Dans un message publié sur son compte X, le général de brigade Gaspard Baratuza, porte-parole de l’armée burundaise, a déclaré qu’aucun militaire burundais n’est déployé dans la ville de Bukavu.
statements_all.translation_en: In a message published on his X account, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, spokesperson of the Burundian army, stated that no Burundian soldier is deployed in the city of Bukavu.

statements_all.role: Council of Ministers (as cited by the CNDH)
statements_all.setting: communiqué (Council of Ministers record, as cited)
statements_all.text: The CNDH-RDC report said that the Council of Ministers of 28 February 2025, in its record, established for South Kivu that up to 27 February 2025 the city of Bukavu had recorded more than 1.130 wounded, more than 29 deaths in care establishments and 16 people who died at the rally.
statements_all.excerpt_original: le Conseil des Ministres du 28 février 2025, dans son compte rendu, établit le bilan ci-après pour le Sud-Kivu, « jusqu’au 27 février 2025, la ville de Bukavu a enregistré plus de 1.130 blessés, plus de 29 décès dans les établissements de soins et 16 personnes décédées lors du meeting ».
statements_all.translation_en: the Council of Ministers of 28 February 2025, in its record, established the following toll for South Kivu: 'up to 27 February 2025, the city of Bukavu recorded more than 1.130 wounded, more than 29 deaths in health care establishments and 16 people who died at the rally'.

statements_all.text: DW reported that, after two explosions at an M23 rally in Bukavu, M23 accused the Congolese authorities of being behind the attack and said in a statement that it condemned "the criminal regime of Kinshasa, which just implemented its plan of exterminating civilian populations".
statements_all.excerpt_original: Meanwhile, M23 accused the Congolese authorities of being behind the attack. "We are accusing and condemning vigorously the criminal regime of Kinshasa, which just implemented its plan of exterminating civilian populations," the group said in a statement.

statements_all.text: DW reported that Congo's president, Felix Tshisekedi, called the Bukavu rally attack "a heinous terrorist act".
statements_all.excerpt_original: Congo's president, Felix Tshisekedi, called the attack "a heinous terrorist act."

statements_all.text: The New Times (Rwanda) reported that Bertrand Bisimwa, president of M23, pointed an accusing finger at Burundi after the Bukavu rally explosions and said preliminary investigations indicated that the explosives belonged to the Burundian army.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Moments after the attack, Bertrand Bisimwa, the president of M23, pointed an accusing finger at neighbouring Burundi, which is allied with the Kinshasa regime in the fight against the rebel group that controls much of eastern DR Congo. Preliminary investigations indicated that the explosives used in the terrorist attack belong to the Burundian army, he said.

statements_all.text: The New Times reported that, according to the group's leader, the explosives at the AFC/M23 rally in Bukavu on 27 February killed at least 11 people and injured 65, six of them in critical condition.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The explosives that hit a huge crowd of people who had turned up in their thousands for an AFC/M23 rally in Bukavu, on February 27, caused the death of at least 11 people and injured 65, of whom six are in critical condition, according to group’s leader.

statements_all.person: Jérémie Meya (printed also as lieutenant Jérémie Meya Gbe)
statements_all.role: spokesperson of operation Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu
statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that the spokesperson of the Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu operation, Jérémie Meya (lieutenant Jérémie Meya Gbe), said the FARDC had begun an operation to track down fleeing soldiers and alleged perpetrators of various harassments in Uvira, with the stated aim of 'cleaning' Uvira and the localities of the Ruzizi plain so the population could go about its business safely.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) ont entamé une opération de traque des militaires fuyards et présumés auteurs de différentes tracasseries à Uvira. A en croire le porte-parole de l'opération Sukola 2 sud Sud-Kivu, Jérémie Meya, cette opération vise le nettoyage de la ville d'Uvira.
statements_all.translation_en: The Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) have begun an operation to track down fleeing soldiers and alleged perpetrators of various harassments in Uvira. According to the spokesperson of the Sukola 2 sud Sud-Kivu operation, Jérémie Meya, this operation aims at cleaning the city of Uvira.

statements_all.text: Al Jazeera reported that Rwanda said international sanctions would reduce the likelihood of peace with M23, after the UK said it would pause some bilateral aid and impose other diplomatic measures on Kigali; Rwanda's Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the measures 'regrettable' and said the UK 'has now clearly chosen a side'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Rwanda has said international sanctions will reduce the likelihood of peace with M23 rebels in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) , after the United Kingdom said it would pause some bilateral aid and impose other diplomatic sanctions on Kigali.

statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué published on Tuesday 25 February 2025, AFC/M23 said that several villages of Minembwe, notably Irundu and Nyarujoka, were bombed that day, and alerted to a rise in persecution of the Banyamulenge community in Uvira city, which it said took the form of arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances and other repression; the outlet added that the Congolese authorities had not officially reacted to the accusations.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Dans un communiqué publié ce mardi 25 février 2025, l’AFC/M23 affirme que plusieurs villages de Minembwe, notamment Irundu et Nyarujoka, ont été la cible de bombardements.
statements_all.translation_en: In a communiqué published this Tuesday 25 February 2025, the AFC/M23 says that several villages of Minembwe, notably Irundu and Nyarujoka, were targeted by bombardments.

statements_all.text: Radio Okapi reported that Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka, opening the 58th session of the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva on Monday 24 February, called for 'dissuasive sanctions against Rwanda'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Intervenant à l’ouverture, ce lundi 24 février à Genève (Suisse) de la 58ème session du Conseil des droits de l’homme (CDH), la Première ministre Judith Suminwa Tuluka a appelé « à des sanctions dissuasives contre le Rwanda »
statements_all.translation_en: Speaking at the opening, this Monday 24 February in Geneva (Switzerland) of the 58th session of the Human Rights Council, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka called for "dissuasive sanctions against Rwanda"

statements_all.role: communication cell of the provincial governor
statements_all.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing the communication cell of the South Kivu governor, that the provincial executive head and his deputy were now staying in Uvira and would continue to administer South Kivu from there because Bukavu, the capital, was under rebel occupation.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Selon la cellule de Communication du gouverneur de province, le chef de l'exécutif provincial et son adjoint séjournent désormais à Uvira. C'est à partir de cette ville qu'ils vont continuer à administrer la province du Sud-Kivu, étant donné que Bukavu, la capitale, est sous occupation des rebelles.
statements_all.translation_en: According to the communication cell of the provincial governor, the head of the provincial executive and his deputy are now staying in Uvira. It is from this city that they will continue to administer the province of South Kivu, given that Bukavu, the capital, is under rebel occupation.

statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that Uganda's chief of defence staff, General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, argued in an X post the previous week that the M23 rebels backed by the Rwandan army should fall back 20 km south of their positions in Lubero (Kitsombiro, Kipese, Kasugho); the outlet noted that some said the M23 was ceding place to the Ugandan army at Kasugho.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Bien que des langues affirment qu'ils cèdent place à l'armée ougandaise dont le chef d'État major, le général Muhoozi Kainerugaba, fils de Yoweri Museveni, a argué, dans un post sur X la semaine dernière que les rebelles du M23 soutenus par l'armée rwandaise devraient reculer de 20 Km au Sud de leurs positions actuelles de Lubero (Kitsombiro, Kipese, Kasugho)
statements_all.translation_en: Although some say they are ceding place to the Ugandan army, whose chief of staff, General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, son of Yoweri Museveni, argued in a post on X last week that the M23 rebels supported by the Rwandan army should fall back 20 km south of their current positions in Lubero (Kitsombiro, Kipese, Kasugho)

statements_all.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government of the DRC, through official communiqués regularly published by its Minister of Interior, Shabani Lukoo Bihango, denounced the scale and systematic nature of abuses perpetrated by AFC/M23 and the Rwandan army, including summary executions.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The Government of the DRC, through official communiqués regularly published through its Minister of Interior, Shabani Lukoo Bihango, denounced the scale and systematic nature of abuses perpetrated by AFC/M23 and the Rwandan army, including summary executions:

statements_all.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that after a France24 report on the Katindo killings, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka dismissed the report as 'fake news' and blatant misinformation aligned with Kinshasa's propaganda, and denied having spoken to France24.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Lawrence Kanyuka dismissed the report as "fake news" and blatant misinformation aligned with Kinshasa’s propaganda. He further denied having spoken to France24 regarding the matter.

statements_all.text: Igihe reported that Twirwaneho, a group it describes as defending Banyamulenge who are persecuted and killed by the DRC government, announced it had joined AFC/M23 in the struggle to remove the Kinshasa government.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Umutwe wa Twirwaneho uharanirauburenganzira bw'Abanyamulenge batotezwa ndetse bakicwa na Leta ya Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, RDC, watangaje ko wifatanyije n’Ihuriro AFC/M23 mu rugamba rwo gukuraho ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa bukomeje kwica abaturage.
statements_all.translation_en: The Twirwaneho group, which fights for the rights of Banyamulenge who are persecuted and killed by the government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, DRC, announced that it has joined the AFC/M23 alliance in the struggle to remove the Kinshasa government that continues to kill citizens.

statements_all.text: BBC News reported that, responding to the US sanctions, Rwanda's foreign ministry said the sanctions would not resolve the conflict.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Responding to the US move, Rwanda's foreign ministry said the sanctions would not resolve the conflict

statements_all.text: UN News reported that the UN Security Council unanimously adopted a resolution in which it demanded that the M23 immediately cease hostilities, withdraw from all areas it controls and fully reverse the establishment of illegitimate parallel administrations in DRC territory, and in which its 15 members called on the Rwanda Defence Forces to stop supporting the armed group and immediately withdraw from Congolese territory without preconditions.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The Council demanded that the M23 immediately cease hostilities, withdraw from all areas that it controls, “and fully reverse the establishment of illegitimate parallel administrations in the DRC territory.” The 15 members called on the Rwanda Defence Forces to stop supporting the armed group and immediately withdraw from Congolese territory “without preconditions.”

statements_all.text: UN News reported that in the same resolution the Security Council strongly condemned all attacks directed against civilians and infrastructure, including UN, humanitarian and medical personnel, and condemned summary executions and maiming, sexual and gender-based violence, human trafficking and the recruitment and use of children.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The resolution strongly condemned all attacks directed against civilians and infrastructure, including UN, humanitarian and medical personnel. It also condemned summary executions and maiming, sexual and gender-based violence, human trafficking and the recruitment and use of children.

statements_all.setting: message as reported by Igihe (channel not stated)
statements_all.text: M23's military spokesperson Lt Col Willy Ngoma said, according to Igihe, in a message on 21 February 2025 accompanied by a photo of Col Rukunda, that those who think they will wipe out the Banyamulenge in the DRC are mistaken and that these Congolese will soon be liberated to move freely in their country.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ubwo butumwa yatanze ku wa 21 Gashyantare 2025, abuherekesha ifoto ya Col Rukunda, Lt Col Ngoma yavuze ko abibwira ko bazatsemba Abanyamulenge bari muri RDC bibeshya, kandi ko vuba aba Banye-Congo bazabohorwa, bidegembye mu gihugu cyabo.
statements_all.translation_en: This message he gave on 21 February 2025, accompanying it with a photo of Col Rukunda, Lt Col Ngoma said that those who think they will wipe out the Banyamulenge in the DRC are mistaken, and that soon these Congolese will be liberated, free to move in their country.

statements_all.text: Kivu Morning Post quoted Paul Byamungu, a member of Uvira civil society, as saying that after the meeting at Kamanyola, M23 was now with them, that they had communicated nothing, and that there had been no public meeting so far.
statements_all.excerpt_original: « Après le meeting à Kamanyola, le M23 est maintenant avec nous. Ils n’ont rien communiqué. Aucun meeting public jusque-là, mais nous, acteurs de la société civile, avons besoin de la paix » , a déclaré Paul Byamungu, membre de la société civile d’Uvira.
statements_all.translation_en: "After the meeting at Kamanyola, M23 is now with us. They have communicated nothing. No public meeting so far, but we, civil society actors, need peace," said Paul Byamungu, member of Uvira civil society.

statements_all.setting: text message and social-media post as reported
statements_all.text: BBC Gahuza reported that, asked about a Reuters report of Burundian troops returning home from the DRC, FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza replied by text message "Fake News" and said on X that FDNB soldiers sent to the DRC were continuing their activities in their assigned areas.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Abajijwe na BBC ku bivugwa, Général de Brigade Gaspard Baratuza avugira igisirikare c'Uburundi yishuye mu butumwa bugufi ati: "Fake News"
statements_all.translation_en: Asked by the BBC about the reports, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, spokesman for the Burundian army, replied in a short message: "Fake News"

statements_all.text: In an interview with NotreAfrik published by Wakat Séra, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka said the M23 and Rwanda are 'intrinsically linked' and that any serious negotiation should be held directly with Rwanda.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Pour nous, la position est claire : le M23 et le Rwanda sont intrinsèquement liés. Comme l’a déjà souligné le Président de la République, toute négociation sérieuse devrait se faire directement avec le Rwanda.
statements_all.translation_en: For us, the position is clear: the M23 and Rwanda are intrinsically linked. As the President of the Republic has already stressed, any serious negotiation should be held directly with Rwanda.

statements_all.text: Anadolu Agency reported that the Burundian army spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, said on X that, contrary to what Reuters and social networks reported, FDNB soldiers deployed in the DRC continued to carry out their missions in their sectors of responsibility.
statements_all.excerpt_original: « Contrairement aux propos véhiculés par Reuters et repris par d'autres réseaux sociaux, les militaires de la FDNB (forces de défenses nationales du Burundi) déployés en RDC continuent à exécuter leurs missions dans leurs secteurs de responsabilité », a déclaré le général de brigade Gaspard Baratuza sur X.
statements_all.translation_en: 'Contrary to the statements carried by Reuters and repeated by other social networks, the FDNB soldiers deployed in the DRC continue to carry out their missions in their sectors of responsibility,' said Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza on X.

statements_all.role: minister in charge of internal affairs
statements_all.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that at least a hundred Congolese police officers had fled to Burundi from Uvira, as announced on Wednesday in Bujumbura by the Burundian minister in charge of internal affairs.
statements_all.excerpt_original: At least a hundred Congolese police officers have fled to Burundi from Uvira, the Burundian minister in charge of internal affairs announced Wednesday in the commercial capital Bujumbura.

statements_all.text: BBC News Afrique reported that Wazalendo fighters reportedly wanted to seize the Congolese army's weapons and ammunition, accusing the soldiers of having deserted the front lines and fallen back south to Kalemie. An unnamed source told the BBC that the Wazalendo rose up to oppose the abuses of the regular army and asked the regular troops to give them their weapons, and that about 15 000 Congolese had crossed into Burundi. The BBC said it could not independently verify this information.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Les combattants Wazalendo auraient voulu s'emparer des armes et des munitions de l'armée congolaise, accusant les soldats d'avoir déserté les lignes de front et de s'être repliés plus au sud, à Kalemie. « Le Wazalendo s'est levé pour s'opposer aux abus de l'armée régulière et a demandé aux troupes régulières de lui donner leurs armes », a déclaré la source, ajoutant qu'environ 15 000 Congolais sont passés au Burundi.
statements_all.translation_en: The Wazalendo fighters reportedly wanted to seize the weapons and ammunition of the Congolese army, accusing the soldiers of having deserted the front lines and fallen back further south to Kalemie. "The Wazalendo rose up to oppose the abuses of the regular army and asked the regular troops to give them their weapons," said the source, adding that about 15,000 Congolese had crossed into Burundi.

statements_all.role: State Minister, Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Francophonie
statements_all.text: At a UN Security Council emergency meeting, DRC Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner said that in Goma more than 4,500 wounded people had rushed to overflowing hospitals and that 500 charred corpses were found in the Muzenze prison after mass executions, and said of Bukavu that the same scenario was playing out, including 'hospitals destroyed'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: I now give the floor to Her Excellency Ms. Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, State Minister, Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation, and Francophonie of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

statements_all.setting: communiqué read on radio, as reported
statements_all.text: Al Jazeera reported that a rebel alliance that includes M23 said, in a statement read on local radio on Monday, that it would assist the population of Bukavu who were "abandoned" by the army and allied combatants, and that its forces had been working to restore security.
statements_all.excerpt_original: In a statement read on local radio on Monday, a rebel alliance that includes M23 said it would assist the population of Bukavu who were “abandoned” by the army and allied combatants. “Our forces have been working to restore the security for the people and their property, much to the satisfaction of the entire population,” it said.

statements_all.text: Al Jazeera reported that Erasto Bahati Musanga, the rebel-appointed governor of North Kivu, announced that ports in Bukavu and Goma would reopen on Tuesday.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Erasto Bahati Musanga, the rebel-appointed governor of North Kivu, announced that ports in Bukavu and Goma would reopen on Tuesday.

statements_all.text: AFC/M23 called, in a communiqué released on the evening of 17 February 2025 by political spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka and reported by Igihe, on political and armed groups in the DRC that aim to protect civilians to join it in a struggle to liberate the country and remove the Kinshasa government.
statements_all.excerpt_original: AFC/M23 yahamagariye imitwe ya politiki n’iya gisirikare iharanira kurengera abaturage yo muri Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, RDC, kuyiyungaho mu rugamba rugamije kubohora iki gihugu, bakavanaho ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa bumaze imyaka bwarimitse ikibi.
statements_all.translation_en: AFC/M23 called on political and military groups in the Democratic Republic of the Congo that strive to protect civilians to join it in the struggle to liberate this country, removing the Kinshasa government that has for years enthroned evil.

statements_all.text: Igihe wrote that AFC/M23 indicates it is committed to talking with the DRC to resolve the country's security problems and, failing that, will only settle once it reaches Kinshasa and liberates the population.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Kugeza ubu ibice AFC/M23 yamaze kubohora ibyinshi yabishyizemo abayobozi bayo bashya, barajwe ishinga no kwimakaza umutekano n’iterambere ry’abaturage. Iri huriro rigaragaza ko rirajwe ishinga no kuganira na RDC ku gukemura ibibazo by’umutekano muke muri iki gihugu, bitakunda rikemeza rizatuza ari uko rigeze i Kinshasa rikabohora abaturage.
statements_all.translation_en: So far, in most of the areas AFC/M23 has already liberated it has installed its new administrators, who are intent on promoting security and the development of the population. The alliance indicates that it is committed to talking with the DRC to resolve the security problems in this country; failing that, it affirms it will only settle down once it has reached Kinshasa and liberated the population.

statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that the Prime Minister's office said Judith Suminwa was preparing to speak at the African Union Peace and Security Council on behalf of the Head of State with force and determination, putting forward her country's precise expectations.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Judith Suminwa se prépare à prendre la parole au nom du Chef de l'État avec force et détermination, mettant en avant les attentes précises de son pays", dit la Primature.
statements_all.translation_en: Judith Suminwa is preparing to speak on behalf of the Head of State with force and determination, putting forward her country's precise expectations, the Prime Minister's office said.

statements_all.text: DW reported that President Félix Tshisekedi intensified his accusations against Rwanda, criticising decades of what he described as 'predatory aggression' against the DRC, at the Munich Security Conference.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Congolese President Felix Tshisekedi has intensified his accusations against Rwanda , issuing a scathing critique against decades of what he described as "predatory aggression" against the Democratic Republic of Congo at the recent Munich Security Conference .

statements_all.text: The African Union Peace and Security Council adopted a communiqué that unequivocally condemned the activities of M23 and its supporters, ADF, FDLR and other armed groups.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Unequivocally condemns the activities of M23 and its supporters, Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) and other armed groups

statements_all.text: The African Union Peace and Security Council communiqué commended Angola's President João Manuel Lourenço, Chair of the ICGLR and AU Champion for Peace and Reconciliation, for mediating between the DRC and Rwanda and called on the two parties to return urgently to the Luanda Process.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Commends the efforts of H.E. João Manuel Lourenço, President of the Republic of Angola, the Chair of ICGLR and AU Champion for Peace and Reconciliation, for mediating between the DRC and Rwanda; and calls on the two parties to urgently return to the Luanda Process

statements_all.role: political spokesperson (printed 'umuvugizi wa M23 ushinzwe ibya politiki')
statements_all.text: Ijambo (Chief editor Yves Iyaremye) reported that M23 said the FARDC used a Sukhoï 25 warplane to bomb inhabited areas of Kalehe territory, killing 10 people and wounding 25, and that M23 political spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a communiqué, put the attack on Thursday 13 February 2025.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Umutwe wa M23 watangaje ko igisirikare cya Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo (FARDC) cyakoresheje indege y’intambara yo mu bwoko bwa Sukhoï 25, ikarasa ibisasu mu bice bituwemo n’abaturage muri Teritwari ya Kalehe, bigahitana abantu 10 mu gihe abandi 25 bakomeretse.
statements_all.translation_en: The M23 group announced that the army of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) used a Sukhoï 25 type warplane and fired bombs into inhabited areas in Kalehe territory, killing 10 people while another 25 were wounded.

statements_all.text: Ijambo reported that M23 said it took Kalehe-Centre to stop the violence reported in Bukavu city, where it accused FARDC and its helpers, including FDLR, Burundian soldiers and Wazalendo, of killing residents, looting their property and committing serious violence against women.
statements_all.excerpt_original: M23 ivuga ko yafashe aka gace kugira ngo ihagarike ihohoterwa rivugwa mu Mujyi wa Bukavu, aho ishinja FARDC n’abayifasha barimo FDLR, abasirikare b’u Burundi na Wazalendo, kuba barishe abaturage, bagasahura imitungo yabo, ndetse bagakora ihohoterwa rikabije ku bagore.
statements_all.translation_en: M23 says it took this area in order to stop the violence reported in Bukavu city, where it accuses FARDC and those who help it, including FDLR, Burundian soldiers and Wazalendo, of having killed residents, looted their property and committed serious violence against women.

statements_all.text: BBC News Gahuza reported that on Wednesday the provincial army command said that M23 attacked army positions at Kalehe Centre and Ihusi, quoting it as saying 'these attacks caused the loss of many civilian lives', and that the army says Rwandan troops fight alongside M23, which both sides deny; M23 had said nothing yet on the army's statement.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ku wa gatatu, igisirikare cya leta muri iyi ntara cyatangaje ko M23 mu gikorwa cyo kurenga ku gahenge kasabwe n'inama y'i Dar es Salaam, M23 yateye ibirindiro by'ingabo muri Kalehe Centre na Ihusi ko "ibyo bitero byateye kubura ubuzima bw'abasivile benshi".
statements_all.translation_en: On Wednesday, the government army in this province announced that M23, in an action violating the ceasefire requested by the Dar es Salaam meeting, M23 attacked army positions at Kalehe Centre and Ihusi that 'these attacks caused the loss of many civilian lives'.

statements_all.setting: ultimatum as reported by the Group of Experts
statements_all.text: The Group of Experts reported that after the expiration of a seven-day ultimatum issued by AFC/M23 on 11 February 2025, demanding the surrender of members of the FARDC, PNC, Wazalendo and FDLR and urging civilians to denounce them, AFC/M23 intensified house-to-house searches and targeted operations against individuals suspected of affiliation with Wazalendo, FDLR or FARDC.
statements_all.excerpt_original: After the expiration of a seven-day ultimatum issued on 11 February by AFC/M23 – demanding the surrender of members of the FARDC, PNC, Wazalendo and FDLR, urging civilians to denounce them

statements_all.text: AFP reported that President Ndayishimiye again warned Rwanda during a visit to the shared border, telling residents of Bugabira, a commune on the border with Rwanda, "Celui qui va nous attaquer, nous allons l'attaquer" (whoever attacks us, we will attack them), in a speech broadcast on Wednesday by local media.
statements_all.excerpt_original: "Celui qui va nous attaquer, nous allons l'attaquer" , a déclaré le général Ndayishimiye devant des habitants de Bugabira (Nord), une commune frontalière du Rwanda, qu'il a aussi qualifié de "mauvais voisin" dans un discours diffusé mercredi par des médias locaux.
statements_all.translation_en: "Whoever attacks us, we will attack," said General Ndayishimiye before residents of Bugabira (North), a commune bordering Rwanda, which he also described as a "bad neighbour", in a speech broadcast on Wednesday by local media.

statements_all.setting: message to the public as reported
statements_all.text: Umuryango.rw reported that Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi of South Kivu, speaking about the violence at Kavumu and nearby, said that it was not possible to confirm that those responsible were government soldiers and that they could be bandits who take advantage of the situation to buy weapons and frighten the population; he said it happened as troops at the front were being replaced by new teams.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Guverineri Jean-Jacques Purusi wa Kivu y’Epfo yatanze ubutumwa bwo guhumuriza rubanda.
statements_all.translation_en: Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi of South Kivu gave a message to reassure the public.

statements_all.text: Umuryango.rw reported that Kinshasa government spokesman Patrick Muyaya told Top Congo FM on Sunday that M23, which he called the Rwandan army, had approached and taken Nyabibwe and that all further attacks launched from Nyabibwe had been thwarted, and that rumours reaching Bukavu of M23 being 10 or 15 km away were false as they were in fact more than 100 km away.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ku cyumweru, Patrick Muyaya uvugira leta ya Kinshasa abajijwe uko ibintu bimeze yabwiye ikinyamakuru Top Congo FM ko, mu minsi yashize M23 – yita ingabo z’u Rwanda – yasatiriye igafata Nyabibwe, ati: "Guhera Nyabibwe hari ibindi bitero bakoze byo gusatira bavuye i Nyabibwe ariko byose byaburijwemo."
statements_all.translation_en: On Sunday, Patrick Muyaya, spokesman for the Kinshasa government, asked how things stood, told the media outlet Top Congo FM that in recent days M23, which he calls Rwandan troops, had advanced and taken Nyabibwe, saying: 'From Nyabibwe there were other attacks they made to advance from Nyabibwe, but all were thwarted.'

statements_all.text: The New Times (Rwandan state-aligned outlet) reported that President Kagame told EAC and SADC leaders that the ongoing war in eastern DR Congo was started by the Congolese government.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Kagame told EAC and SADC leaders that the ongoing war in eastern DR Congo was started by the Congolese government

statements_all.role: Alliance Fleuve Congo (appointments announced at Goma stadium)
statements_all.setting: public presentation of appointments as reported
statements_all.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the M23 installed a new North Kivu provincial administration with Bahati Musanga Joseph alias Erasto, until then adviser to the M23 military coordinator, as governor, assisted by vice-governors Minani Ngarambe Willy and Amani Bahati Shadrack, and that the Alliance Fleuve Congo also announced other appointments including Julien Katembo as mayor of Goma.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Bahati Musanga Joseph alias Erasto, jusqu’ici conseiller du coordinateur militaire du M23 est le nouveau gouverneur de province.
statements_all.translation_en: Bahati Musanga Joseph alias Erasto, until now adviser to the M23 military coordinator, is the new governor of the province.

statements_all.role: de facto governor of North Kivu
statements_all.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the new governor, speaking in Kinyarwanda, said he had identified three main threats to security: former prisoners released by the Congolese authorities as M23 fighters were about to enter Goma, the local militias known as the Wazalendo, and the Hutu FDLR.
statements_all.excerpt_original: le nouveau gouverneur a déclaré avoir recensé trois menaces principales contre la sécurité de ses sujets : « les anciens prisonniers qui ont été libérés par les autorités congolaises alors que les combattants du M23 s’apprêtaient à entrer dans la ville de Goma,
statements_all.translation_en: the new governor said he had identified three main threats to the security of his subjects: 'the former prisoners who were released by the Congolese authorities as M23 fighters were preparing to enter the city of Goma,

statements_all.role: coordinator of the Alliance Fleuve Congo
statements_all.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Corneille Nangaa, head of the Alliance Fleuve Congo, promised "une administration responsable qui doit rendre des comptes" (a responsible administration that must be accountable).
statements_all.excerpt_original: Corneille Nangaa, responsable de l’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) à laquelle est affilié le groupe armé, a promis « une administration responsable qui doit rendre des comptes ».
statements_all.translation_en: Corneille Nangaa, head of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) with which the armed group is affiliated, promised 'a responsible administration that must be accountable'.

statements_all.text: The UN Group of Experts recorded that an AFC/M23 communiqué issued on 6 February 2025 claimed deliberate targeting of Nyabibwe by FARDC bombing, resulting in the massacre of civilians, notably four fatalities including an infant.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Below, an AFC/M23 communiqué issued on 6 February 2025 claiming the deliberate targeting of Nyabibwe by FARDC bombing, resulting in the massacre of civilians, notably four fatalities including an infant:

statements_all.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 6 February the AFC/M23-appointed Governor of North Kivu, Bahati Erasto, justified AFC/M23 search operations as necessary to apprehend 'Wazalendo and FDLR, mercenaries and FARDC who are still hiding in the houses'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: On 6 February, the AFC/M23-appointed Governor of North Kivu, Bahati Erasto, justified the operations as necessary to apprehend “Wazalendo and FDLR, mercenaries and FARDC who are still hiding in the houses”.

statements_all.text: Studio Hirondelle, citing AFP, reported that Patrick Muyaya told AFP that this was proof that the unilateral ceasefire decreed was, as usual, a decoy.
statements_all.excerpt_original: « C’est bien la preuve que le cessez-le-feu unilatéral décrété était, comme d’habitude, un leurre » , a réagi auprès de l’AFP Patrick Muyaya.
statements_all.translation_en: "This is proof that the unilateral ceasefire decreed was, as usual, a decoy", Patrick Muyaya reacted to AFP.

statements_all.text: CNN reported that DRC communications minister Patrick Muyaya confirmed the rape of the 165 women, telling CNN on Wednesday that "the government condemns with the greatest energy this barbaric crime."
statements_all.excerpt_original: DRC communications minister Patrick Muyaya confirmed the rape of the 165 women, telling CNN Wednesday that “the government condemns with the greatest energy this barbaric crime.”

statements_all.text: DW, citing dpa, reported that local police investigator Robert Kayembe told Germany's DPA news agency that over 160 women in Munzenze prison were raped and a number yet to be established were burned when their wing was set on fire.
statements_all.excerpt_original: "Over 160 women in Munzenze prison were raped and a number yet to be established were burned when their wing at the prison was set on fire," local police investigator Robert Kayembe told Germany's DPA news agency.

statements_all.role: one of the leaders of M23
statements_all.setting: message, as reported by BBC Gahuza
statements_all.text: BBC Gahuza reported that M23 said the more than 2,500 people who died in the recent fighting in Goma were government soldiers (FARDC) and Wazalendo; that Bertrand Bisimwa, one of the leaders of M23, said no family in Goma was in mourning because of those dead; and that he said the bodies removed from the streets and buried were those of FARDC soldiers and their collaborators, including Wazalendo, FDLR, European mercenaries and Burundian forces, who died in battle.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Umutwe wa M23 watangaje ko abantu bapfuye mu mirwano iheruka i Goma barenga 2,500 ari abasirikare ba leta (FARDC) na Wazalendo.
statements_all.translation_en: The M23 group announced that the people who died in the recent fighting in Goma, more than 2,500, are government soldiers (FARDC) and Wazalendo.

statements_all.setting: communiqué posted on X, as reported
statements_all.text: Ijambo reported that AFC/M23 appointed new authorities for North Kivu and Goma city in a statement posted on X by Laurence Kanyuka, AFC/M23 political spokesperson, naming Bahati Musanga Joseph governor of North Kivu, with Manzi Ngarambe Willy as vice-governor for politics, administration and legal affairs.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ibyo byatangajwe mu itangazo ryashyizwe kuri X na Laurence Kanyuka, Umuvugizi w’umutwe wa AFC/M23 mu bya politiki, ku itariki 5 Gashyantare 2024.
statements_all.translation_en: This was announced in a statement posted on X by Laurence Kanyuka, spokesperson of the AFC/M23 movement for politics, on 5 February 2024.

statements_all.text: Al Jazeera reported that the AFC/M23 said in a statement posted on X that, in response to the humanitarian crisis it attributed to the regime in Kinshasa, it declared a ceasefire starting 4 February 2025 for humanitarian reasons; Al Jazeera added that there was no immediate comment from the DRC government.
statements_all.excerpt_original: “The Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC/M23) informs the public that in response to the humanitarian crisis caused by the regime in Kinshasa it declares a ceasefire starting 4 February 4 2025 for humanitarian reasons,” the rebels said in a statement posted on X.

statements_all.role: Minister of Communication and Media, government spokesperson
statements_all.text: Studio Hirondelle reported that Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, at a briefing in Kinshasa on 3 February, speaking of the massacre and carnage committed in Goma, said that his colleague the Health Minister had been told by his services that morning that there were more than 2,000 bodies to bury.
statements_all.excerpt_original: du massacre et du carnage qui a été commis à Goma, ce matin ses services lui ont renseigné qu’il y a plus de 2 000 corps à enterrer », a déclaré Patrick Muyaya, ministre de la Communication et des Médias, porte-parole du gouvernement, au cours d’un briefing le 3 février à Kinshasa.
statements_all.translation_en: of the massacre and carnage that was committed in Goma, this morning his services informed him that there are more than 2,000 bodies to bury,” said Patrick Muyaya, Minister of Communication and Media, government spokesperson, during a briefing on 3 February in Kinshasa.

statements_all.text: Studio Hirondelle reported that on 3 February 2025 the rebels unilaterally declared a ceasefire 'because of the humanitarian crisis caused by the Kinshasa regime', to take effect on 4 February, and said in a communiqué circulated notably on X that they had 'no intention of taking control of Bukavu or other localities'.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Le 3 février, les rebelles ont décrété unilatéralement un cessez-le-feu « en raison de la crise humanitaire provoquée par le régime de Kinshasa » , censé entrer en vigueur le 4 février. « Nous n’avons aucune intention de prendre le contrôle de Bukavu ou d’autres localités » , avaient-ils déclaré dans un communiqué diffusé notamment sur X.
statements_all.translation_en: On 3 February, the rebels unilaterally decreed a ceasefire "because of the humanitarian crisis caused by the Kinshasa regime", due to take effect on 4 February. "We have no intention of taking control of Bukavu or other localities", they had said in a communiqué circulated notably on X.

statements_all.text: CNN reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame, asked in an interview whether there were Rwandan troops inside the DRC, answered 'I don't know' and said Rwanda would do anything to protect itself.
statements_all.excerpt_original: In an exclusive interview with CNN on Monday, Kagame was asked if there were any Rwandan troops inside the DRC. “I don’t know,” Kagame said, despite the fact that he is commander-in-chief of the Rwandan Defence Force.

statements_all.role: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (statement from Kigali)
statements_all.text: Rwanda's foreign ministry said on 2 February 2025 that it rejected the accusations against the Rwanda Defence Force made in the statement of the SADC extraordinary summit of 31 January 2025, and said the RDF does not attack civilians.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Kigali, 2 February 2025 - Rwanda rejects the accusations against the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) made in the statement of the Extraordinary Summit of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) held on 31 January 2025. The RDF defends Rwanda's borders from threats and protects civilians, it does not attack civilians.

statements_all.role: Acting Director of Information and Public Relations, TPDF
statements_all.text: ChimpReports reported that the Tanzania People's Defence Forces (TPDF) said, in a statement by Col. Ilonda, that following consecutive attacks in the Sake and Goma areas on 24 and 28 January 2025 it had lost two of its soldiers while four others sustained injuries and were receiving treatment in Goma, and that all TPDF troops deployed in the DRC remain safe.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Following consecutive attacks in the Sake and Goma areas on January 24 and 28, 2025, TPDF has lost two of its soldiers while four others sustained injuries. The injured personnel are currently receiving treatment in Goma,” said Col. Ilonda.

statements_all.text: Radio Okapi reported that Colonel Alexis Rugabisha, commander of the FARDC 12th brigade, was killed in clashes between the FARDC and the M23 at Mukwija in Kalehe territory, and that FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge, in a communiqué published on Sunday 2 February 2025, praised his bravery and called his death an inestimable loss for the army and the nation.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Le colonel Alexis Rugabisha, commandant de la 12ᵉ brigade des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo, a été tué lors des affrontements entre les FARDC et les rebelles du M23 à Mukwija, dans le territoire de Kalehe au Sud-Kivu. Le porte-parole des FARDC, le général major Sylvain Ekenge a, dans un communiqué publié ce dimanche 2 février 2025, salué la bravoure du colonel Rugabisha.
statements_all.translation_en: Colonel Alexis Rugabisha, commander of the 12th brigade of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, was killed during clashes between the FARDC and M23 rebels at Mukwija, in Kalehe territory in South Kivu. The FARDC spokesperson, Major General Sylvain Ekenge, in a communiqué published this Sunday 2 February 2025, praised the bravery of Colonel Rugabisha.

statements_all.text: Actualite.cd reported that the Congolese army announced in a communiqué that Colonel Rugabisha Alexis, commander of the FARDC 12th brigade, was killed in combat against the Rwandan army and the M23 in Kalehe territory; according to spokesperson Major General Ekenge Bomusa Efomi Sylvain, he fell 'armes à la main' after leading a counter-offensive that pushed the M23 back from Nyabibwe towards the surroundings of Minova.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Le colonel Rugabisha Alexis, commandant de la 12ᵉ brigade des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), a été tué au combat contre l’armée rwandaise et ses alliés du Mouvement du 23 Mars (M23) dans le territoire de Kalehe, au Sud-Kivu, a annoncé samedi l’armée congolaise dans un communiqué. D’après le porte-parole des FARDC, le général-major Ekenge Bomusa Efomi Sylvain, le colonel Rugabisha est tombé “armes à la main” après avoir conduit une contre-offensive qui a repoussé les rebelles du M23 de Nyabibwe jusqu’aux environs de Minova.
statements_all.translation_en: Colonel Rugabisha Alexis, commander of the 12th brigade of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC), was killed in combat against the Rwandan army and its allies of the March 23 Movement (M23) in Kalehe territory, South Kivu, the Congolese army announced on Saturday in a communiqué. According to the FARDC spokesperson, Major General Ekenge Bomusa Efomi Sylvain, Colonel Rugabisha fell "weapon in hand" after leading a counter-offensive that pushed the M23 rebels back from Nyabibwe to the surroundings of Minova.

statements_all.setting: public statement as reported by the Group of Experts
statements_all.text: The Group of Experts reported that in February 2025 the President of Burundi, Évariste Ndayishimiye, accused Rwanda of intending to invade Burundi, including through its backing of the Burundian armed opposition group Red Tabara, and announced the readiness of Burundi to fight back, and that Rwanda in turn signalled a commitment to regime change in both Burundi and the DRC.
statements_all.excerpt_original: In February 2025, the President of Burundi, Évariste Ndayishimiye, accused Rwanda of intending to invade Burundi, including through its backing of the Burundian armed opposition group Red Tabara, and announced the readiness of Burundi to fight back (see annex 73). Rwanda, in turn, signalled a commitment to regime change in both Burundi and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

statements_all.setting: public remarks as reported by the Group of Experts
statements_all.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in February 2025 the President of Burundi, Évariste Ndayishimiye, accused Rwanda of intending to invade Burundi, including through its backing of the Burundian armed opposition group Red Tabara, and announced Burundi's readiness to fight back; it also reported that in mid-March the two countries agreed on verbal and military de-escalation, reportedly concluding a non-aggression agreement.
statements_all.excerpt_original: In February 2025, the President of Burundi, Évariste Ndayishimiye, accused Rwanda of intending to invade Burundi, including through its backing of the Burundian armed opposition group Red Tabara, and announced the readiness of Burundi to fight back

statements_all.role: AFC/M23 appointed territorial administrator (Masisi per this passage; Nyiragongo per para. 27)
statements_all.text: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 17 that in mid-February 2025 Ephrem Kabasha, recently appointed by AFC/M23 as territorial administrator of Masisi, prohibited all associations, including civil society, during a speech in Kaseni.
statements_all.excerpt_original: in mid-February 2025, Ephrem Kabasha, recently appointed by AFC/M23 as territorial administrator of Masisi, prohibited all associations, including civil society, during a speech in Kaseni.

statements_all.setting: statement, as reported by BBC Gahuza
statements_all.text: BBC Gahuza reported that Patrick Muyaya, spokesperson of the Kinshasa government, had recently said that more than 2,000 bodies were still in the streets of Goma needing burial, and that he accused Rwandan forces and M23 of killing civilians in the recent fighting in Goma and its surroundings.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Patrick Muyaya, umuvugizi wa leta ya Kinshasa aheruka gutangaza ko imirambo irenga 2,000 ikiri mu mihanda i Goma ikeneye guhambwa. Yashinje ingabo z' Rwanda na M23 ubwicanyi ku basivile mu mirwano iheruka i Goma no mu nkengero zayo.
statements_all.translation_en: Patrick Muyaya, spokesperson of the Kinshasa government, recently announced that more than 2,000 bodies are still in the streets of Goma needing burial. He accused Rwandan forces and M23 of killing civilians in the recent fighting in Goma and its surroundings.

statements_all.setting: interview with Jeune Afrique, as published in Kinyarwanda by Igihe
statements_all.text: Rwandan President Paul Kagame said, in an interview with Jeune Afrique as published by Igihe, that he was satisfied with the outcome of the Dar es Salaam regional summit and that what matters now is how its resolutions are implemented, especially by the Congolese side.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Paul Kagame: Kunyurwa, yego. Abitabiriye inama barebaga ahazaza, bemeranya ku ngingo zitanga icyizere. Ubu, icyo twareba ni uburyo imyanzuro ishyirwa mu bikorwa by’umwihariko n’uruhande rwa Congo cyane ko ari rwo rurebwa cyane.
statements_all.translation_en: Paul Kagame: Satisfied, yes. Those who attended were looking to the future, agreeing on points that give hope. Now, what we should look at is how the resolutions are implemented, especially by the Congolese side, given that it is the one most concerned.

statements_all.setting: interview with Jeune Afrique, as published in Kinyarwanda by Igihe
statements_all.text: Kagame said, according to Igihe's rendering of his Jeune Afrique interview, that nothing explained President Tshisekedi's non-attendance in person at the summit, and that the night before he had chosen to go to Chad to ask for military assistance.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Kuri iyo ngingo, nta mpamvu n’imwe yasobanura ukutitabira inama mu buryo bw’imbonankobone kwa Perezida wa RDC [Félix Tshisekedi]. Ijoro ryabanje, yari yahisemo kujya muri Tchad gusaba ubufasha bwa gisirikare mbere yo kwitabira inama akoresheje ikoranabuhanga. Ibyo bisobanuye imigambi ye.
statements_all.translation_en: On that point, there is no reason that could explain the DRC President's [Félix Tshisekedi's] non-attendance in person at the meeting. The night before, he had chosen to go to Chad to ask for military assistance before attending the meeting by technology. That shows his intentions.

statements_all.setting: interview with Jeune Afrique, as published in Kinyarwanda by Igihe
statements_all.text: Kagame said, per Igihe, that Rwanda had signed more than five agreements with the DRC government since 2007 that the DRC never implemented, and that a group with a genocide ideology still exists.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Twagiranye amasezerano arenga atanu na Guverinoma ya Congo kuva mu 2007 ariko ntiyigeze yubahirizwa na RDC. Umutwe ufite ingengabitekerezo ya Jenoside uracyahari.
statements_all.translation_en: We concluded more than five agreements with the Congolese government since 2007, but the DRC never implemented them. The group with a genocide ideology is still there.

statements_all.setting: interview with Jeune Afrique, as published in Kinyarwanda by Igihe
statements_all.text: Kagame said, per Igihe, that the DRC government had hired mercenaries who came from Europe.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Guverinoma ya RDC yahaye akazi abacanshuro, nk’uko mwese mubizi. Baturutse he? Ni i Burayi.
statements_all.translation_en: The DRC government hired mercenaries, as you all know. Where did they come from? From Europe.

statements_all.setting: interview with Jeune Afrique, as published in Kinyarwanda by Igihe
statements_all.text: Kagame said, per Igihe, that what Rwanda took from the statements of the presidents of Burundi and the DRC was a plan to destabilise Rwanda, and that they fuelled the war and said they would remove the Rwandan government.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Icyo twakuye mu byavuzwe na Perezida w’u Burundi n’uwa RDC, ni umugambi wo guhungabanya u Rwanda. Ni bo batumye ibintu bigera aho bigeze bahembera intambara, banavuga ko bazakuraho Guverinoma y’u Rwanda.
statements_all.translation_en: What we took from what the Presidents of Burundi and the DRC said is a plan to destabilise Rwanda. They are the ones who brought things to where they are by fuelling war, and they also said that they would remove the Government of Rwanda.

statements_all.setting: interview with Jeune Afrique, as published in Kinyarwanda by Igihe
statements_all.text: Kagame said, per Igihe, that he has sympathy for M23 'based on evidence and proof' and that the group defends many people who have long been persecuted, killed and chased out as refugees.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Naba mfitiye M23 impuhwe? Yego, nshingiye ku bihamya n’ibimenyetso. Uyu mutwe urengera abantu benshi, bamaze igihe bacunaguzwa, bicwa, bameneshejwe bakaba impunzi.
statements_all.translation_en: Do I have sympathy for M23? Yes, based on testimony and evidence. This group defends many people who have long been persecuted, killed and driven out to become refugees.

statements_all.setting: interview with Jeune Afrique, as published in Kinyarwanda by Igihe
statements_all.text: Kagame said, in rhetorical questions rendered by Igihe, that the Wazalendo were set up by the Congolese government to carry out ethnically based killings and that Burundi's leadership entered the conflict to support its Congolese counterparts in their plan to kill and wipe out those people.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ku bwa Wazalendo yashyizweho na Guverinoma ya Congo kugira ngo ikore ubwicanyi bushingiye ku moko? Cyangwa se ku bw’ubuyobozi bw’u Burundi bwinjiye muri aya makimbirane bufite intego imwe yo gushyigikira bagenzi babo b’Abanye-Congo mu mugambi wabo w’ubwicanyi no kurimbura abo bantu?
statements_all.translation_en: On behalf of the Wazalendo set up by the Congolese Government to carry out ethnically based killings? Or on behalf of the leadership of Burundi, which entered this conflict with one aim, to support their Congolese counterparts in their plan of killing and wiping out those people?

statements_all.setting: interview with Jeune Afrique, as published in Kinyarwanda by Igihe
statements_all.text: Kagame said, per Igihe, that 'they' (the FDLR, by context) are still there, that some had fled and others had gone south to regroup, and that they followed the Burundian troops from Goma to Bukavu.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Baracyahari, bamwe barahunze, abandi berekeje mu majyepfo, aho bari kwisuganyiriza. Bakurikiye ingabo z’u Burundi, bava i Goma bajya i Bukavu.
statements_all.translation_en: They are still there, some have fled, others have headed south, where they are regrouping. They followed the Burundian troops, from Goma to Bukavu.

statements_all.setting: interview with Jeune Afrique, as published in Kinyarwanda by Igihe
statements_all.text: Asked, in a question stating that M23's attacks on Goma killed more than 3000, whether Rwanda had a role, Kagame answered 'None' and said the measures Rwanda put in place are only defensive, according to Igihe.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ibitero bya M23 ku Mujyi wa Goma byahitanye abarenga 3000. Haba hari uruhare rw’u Rwanda muri ibyo? Nta na rumwe. Ingamba twashyizeho ni iz’ubwirinzi gusa.
statements_all.translation_en: M23's attacks on the city of Goma killed more than 3,000. Is there any role of Rwanda in that? None at all. The measures we have put in place are only defensive.

statements_all.setting: interview with Jeune Afrique, as published in Kinyarwanda by Igihe
statements_all.text: Kagame said, per Igihe, that most of those killed in the fighting were FARDC soldiers, FDLR fighters and Wazalendo armed groups fighting alongside them, and that the number of civilians killed is reckoned at about 500.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ku rundi ruhande, umubare munini w’abahitanywe n’imirwano bari abasirikare ba FARDC, abarwanyi ba FDLR, ndetse n’imitwe yitwaje intwaro ya Wazalendo bafatanya ku rugamba. Umubare w’abasivile baguye mu ntambara ubarirwa muri 500.
statements_all.translation_en: On the other hand, the majority of those killed in the fighting were FARDC soldiers, FDLR fighters, and the armed groups of Wazalendo who fight alongside them. The number of civilians who died in the war is counted at about 500.

statements_all.setting: interview with Jeune Afrique, as published in Kinyarwanda by Igihe
statements_all.text: Kagame replied, per Igihe, 'Yes, it is taken as though there is no doubt that Rwandan troops are there, but the FDLR is a threat to Rwanda's security', adding that mercenaries and provocations by Félix Tshisekedi and Burundi also threaten Rwanda.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Ni byo, bifatwa nk’aho nta shiti ingabo z’u Rwanda ziriyo, ariko FDLR iteye inkeke ku mutekano w’u Rwanda, rutewe inkeke n’abacanshuro hamwe n’ubushotoranyi bukorwa na Félix Tshisekedi n’u Burundi ku karubanda na byo birigaragaza.
statements_all.translation_en: True, it is regarded as though it were beyond doubt that Rwandan troops are there, but the FDLR is a threat to Rwanda's security, Rwanda is threatened by mercenaries, and the provocations openly made by Félix Tshisekedi and Burundi are also evident.

statements_all.setting: interview with Jeune Afrique, as published in Kinyarwanda by Igihe
statements_all.text: Kagame said, per Igihe, that rather than choose between threats to security and sanctions he would take up arms against what aims to harm Rwanda, regardless of sanctions.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Byumvikane neza: aho guhitamo hagati y’ibibangamira umutekano no gufatirwa ibihano, nafata intwaro nkahangana n’ibigamije kungirira nabi ntitaye ku bihano.
statements_all.translation_en: Let it be clear: rather than choosing between what threatens security and being sanctioned, I would take up arms and confront what aims to harm me, regardless of sanctions.

statements_all.setting: interview with Jeune Afrique, as published in Kinyarwanda by Igihe
statements_all.text: Kagame said, per Igihe, that he does not go to greet people and be photographed; that they were to meet in Luanda to sign an agreement prepared by their ministers and technicians, not to hold talks; and that the agreement was not agreed because Kinshasa refused to include key issues.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Kubera impamvu nakubwiye, sinjya gusuhuzanya no gufata amafoto. Twagombaga guhurira i Luanda tugasinya amasezerano yari yateguwe n’abaminisitiri bacu n’abatekinisiye, ntabwo twari tugiye kuganira. Ayo masezerano rero ntabwo yumvikanyweho kubera ko Kinshasa yanze gushyiramo ibibazo by’ingenzi byakabaye biri no mu nshingano zayo.
statements_all.translation_en: For the reason I told you, I do not go to greet people and take photographs. We were supposed to meet in Luanda to sign an agreement prepared by our ministers and technicians; we were not going to hold talks. That agreement was therefore not agreed upon because Kinshasa refused to include the key issues that should also be among its responsibilities.

statements_all.setting: interview with Jeune Afrique, as published in Kinyarwanda by Igihe
statements_all.text: Asked whether he supported the aim of M23 and AFC to remove Felix Tshisekedi from power, Kagame said, per Igihe, that he could understand what they were expressing, and that Rwanda has a problem with a Congolese government that he said was not elected, either the first or second time, and that he said aims only to persecute the population, sow more chaos and enrich itself.
statements_all.excerpt_original: M23 na AFC bifite abanyamuryango bafite gahunda ya politiki igaragara: gukura Felix Tshisekedi ku butegetsi. Ushyigikiye iyi ntego? Nshobora kumva icyo bari kugaragaza. Dufitanye ikibazo na Leta ya Congo mu by’ukuri itaratowe, haba ku nshuro ya mbere n’iya kabiri, kandi ifite gusa umugambi wo gutoteza abaturage, guteza akavuyo kurushaho no kwigwizaho byose.
statements_all.translation_en: I can understand what they are expressing. We have a problem with a Congolese government that, in truth, was not elected, either the first or the second time, and that has only the aim of persecuting the people, causing even more chaos and enriching itself with everything.

statements_all.setting: interview with Voice of America (Ijwi rya Amerika), as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Igihe reported that the new Commander-in-Chief of Twirwaneho, Brig Gen Charles Sematama, told Voice of America that Col Rukunda left them strong and that they must finish the struggle he started whatever happens.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Umuyobozi Mukuru mushya wa Twirwaneho, Brig Gen Charles Sematama yabwiye Ijwi rya Amerika ko Col Rukunda asize bakomeye ndetse urugamba yatangije bagomba kurusoza uko byagenda kose.
statements_all.translation_en: The new Commander-in-Chief of Twirwaneho, Brig Gen Charles Sematama, told Voice of America that Col Rukunda has left them strong and that they must finish the struggle he started whatever happens.

statements_all.setting: interview with Voice of America (Ijwi rya Amerika), as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Brig Gen Sentama (as Igihe prints the name in this passage; Sematama elsewhere in the article) said, according to Igihe, that they had been fighting a war of self-defence for seven years, had tried to alert foreign countries and to persuade Kinshasa to drop discrimination and protect people equally, that this kept failing, and that they were now determined to do it openly themselves.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Brig Gen Sentama yavuze ko bamaze imyaka irindwi barwana intambara yo kwirwanaho, bagerageza gutabaza amahanga, bumvisha Kinshasa ko igomba kureka ivangura ikarinda abaturage mu buryo bungana ariko bikomeza kunanirana, uyu munsi bakaba biyemeje kubyikorera ku buryo bweruye.
statements_all.translation_en: Brig Gen Sentama said that they had been fighting a war of self-defence for seven years, trying to alert foreign countries, persuading Kinshasa that it must drop discrimination and protect the people equally, but it kept failing, and today they had resolved to do it themselves openly.

statements_all.setting: interview with Voice of America (Ijwi rya Amerika), as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Brig Gen Sentama (as Igihe prints the name) alleged, according to Igihe, that all the Mai Mai groups were united with the FDLR and had begun attacking and destroying the homes of Banyamulenge, that foreign countries were shown this but stayed silent, that the killings continue to this day and that they had killed the leader.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Brig Gen Sentama yavuze ko bamaze imyaka irindwi barwana intambara yo kwirwanaho, bagerageza gutabaza amahanga, bumvisha Kinshasa ko igomba kureka ivangura ikarinda abaturage mu buryo bungana ariko bikomeza kunanirana, uyu munsi bakaba biyemeje kubyikorera ku buryo bweruye. Ati “Mai Mai zose zihuje na FDLR, barahura batangira kugaba ibitero no gusenyera Abanyamulenge, ariko twabyeretse amahanga araceceka ararebera, ubwicanyi burakomeza kugeza uyu munsi n’umuyobozi bakaba bamwishe.
statements_all.translation_en: Brig Gen Sentama said that they have spent seven years fighting a war of self-defence, trying to alert foreign countries and to persuade Kinshasa that it must stop discrimination and protect the population equally, but this kept failing, and that today they have resolved to do it themselves, openly. He said: "All the Mai Mai are united with the FDLR; they meet and start launching attacks and destroying the homes of the Banyamulenge, but we showed this to foreign countries and they stayed silent and looked on; the killings continue to this day and they have also killed the leader.

statements_all.setting: interview with Voice of America (Ijwi rya Amerika), as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Brig Gen Sematama said, according to Igihe, that in the fight to remove the Kinshasa government they had taken areas of Minembwe in Fizi territory and others, that they had driven FARDC out of where it had been, and that they had entered Mikenke and would continue.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Brig Gen Sematama yanavuze ko mu rugamba rwo gukuraho ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa ubu bamaze gufata uduce twa Minembwe two muri Teritwari ya Fizi mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo n’utundi. Ati “Minembwe twarayifashe, aho FARDC yari iri twayikuyemo. Uyu munsi twinjiye Mikenke ndetse tugomba gukomeza.
statements_all.translation_en: Brig Gen Sematama also said that in the struggle to remove the Kinshasa government they had now taken areas of Minembwe in Fizi Territory in South Kivu Province and others. He said: "We took Minembwe, we drove FARDC out of where it was. Today we have entered Mikenke and we must continue.

statements_all.setting: interview with Voice of America (Ijwi rya Amerika), as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Brig Gen Sematama said, according to Igihe, in reply to international calls to lay down arms and join talks: 'We are being killed. Should we lay down our guns and then they kill us?', adding that they had appealed to the world for a long time and nothing had been done.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Brig Gen Sematama ku bijyanye n’ibyo basabwa n’umuryango mpuzamahanga byo kurambika intwaro bakayoboka inzira y’ibiganiro yagize ati “Turi kwicwa. Turambike imbunda maze batwice? Bajye kubwira abandi bafite ibyo barwanira, twe turwanira kubaho kandi twabatakiye kuva kera kandi ntacyo bakoze.
statements_all.translation_en: Brig Gen Sematama, on what the international community asks of them to lay down arms and follow the path of talks, said: "We are being killed. Should we lay down our guns so that they kill us? Let them go and tell others who have something to fight for; we are fighting to live and we appealed to them long ago and they did nothing.

statements_all.setting: interview with Voice of America (Ijwi rya Amerika), as reported by Igihe
statements_all.text: Brig Gen Sematama, the new Twirwaneho leader, called, according to Igihe, on all young Banyamulenge men to come to the rescue and unite to remove 'this government of killers', which he said was committing 'genocide' and wiping out their parents.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Brig Gen Sematama yanavuze ko mu rugamba rwo gukuraho ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa ubu bamaze gufata uduce twa Minembwe two muri Teritwari ya Fizi mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo n’utundi. Ati “Minembwe twarayifashe, aho FARDC yari iri twayikuyemo. Uyu munsi twinjiye Mikenke ndetse tugomba gukomeza. Aho Umunyamulenge hose atuye tugomba kuhakoza ikirenge ndetse kuko twiyunze n’abandi tuzakomeza ku buryo tuzabohora RDC yose abaturage bose bakagira amahoro.” Abajijwe aho izo mbaraga bazikuye ndetse n’iby’uko baba binjije ingabo nshya, uyu muyobozi mushya wa Twirwaneho yavuze ko nta ngabo nshya binjije ahubwo icyahindutse ari uko biyemeje gukuraho ubwo butegetsi. Ati “Turacyari ba bandi. Mbere baraduteraga tukirwanaho tukabarasa tukabageza mu birindiro byabo tukagaruka ariko ubu twiyemeje kubakuraho kuko bakomeje ubwicanyi. Turabwira Abanye-Congo bose guhaguruka. Turasaba abasore b’Abanyamulenge bose kuza gutabara tukiyunga tugashyira hamwe mu gukuraho iyi leta y’abicanyi kuko ari yo iri gukora jenoside ikabamaraho ababyeyi babo.”
statements_all.translation_en: Brig Gen Sematama also said that in the struggle to remove the Kinshasa government they have now taken the areas of Minembwe in Fizi territory in South Kivu province, among others. He said: "We have taken Minembwe; we drove FARDC out of where it was. Today we entered Mikenke and we must continue. Wherever a Munyamulenge lives we must set foot, and because we have united with others we will continue until we liberate the whole of the DRC so that all the people have peace." Asked where they got this strength and whether they had brought in new troops, the new Twirwaneho leader said they had brought in no new troops; what had changed is that they had resolved to remove that government. He said: "We are still the same people. Before, they attacked us, we defended ourselves, fired at them, pushed them back to their positions and came back, but now we have resolved to remove them because they keep on killing. We tell all Congolese to rise up. We ask all young Banyamulenge men to come to the rescue so that we unite and come together to remove this government of killers, because it is the one carrying out genocide and finishing off their parents."

statements_all.text: Imvaho Nshya, a Rwandan outlet, reported that M23 deputy spokesperson Dr Oscar Balinda said the group issued a communiqué calling on FARDC soldiers hiding in houses to gather at the Goma unity stadium, and that Balinda said more than 1,500 were then taken to the military camp at Rumangabo; the outlet said the soldiers were taken there on Thursday 30 January 2025.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Aba basirikare bagejejwe i Rumangabo ku wa Kane tariki 30 Mutarama 2025.
statements_all.translation_en: These soldiers were taken to Rumangabo on Thursday 30 January 2025.

statements_all.role: coordinator of the Alliance Fleuve Congo
statements_all.text: BBC News reported that Corneille Nangaa, who heads an alliance of rebel groups that includes the M23, said their ultimate aim was to topple President Félix Tshisekedi's government and vowed to continue the offensive to Kinshasa.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The rebel leader whose fighters have captured Goma, the biggest city in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, has vowed to continue their offensive all the way to the capital, Kinshasa. Corneille Nangaa, who heads an alliance of rebel groups that includes the M23, said their ultimate aim was to topple President Félix Tshisekedi's government.

statements_all.role: coordinator of the Alliance Fleuve Congo
statements_all.text: BBC News reported that on Thursday Nangaa presented the rebels as the new administrators of Goma, telling journalists they were there to stay and would get services up and running again.
statements_all.excerpt_original: On Thursday, Nangaa presented the rebels as the new administrators of Goma, telling journalists they were there to stay and would get services up and running again.

statements_all.text: Congolese newspaper L'Avenir reported that President Félix Tshisekedi, in a live address on RTNC on Wednesday 29 January 2025, called on Congolese to show resistance and resilience in the face of an unprecedented worsening of the security situation in the east, which it said he attributed to Rwandan defence forces supporting the M23.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Au cours d’un discours à la nation en direct sur la chaine de télévision nationale, RTNC, mercredi 29 janvier2025, le Chef de l’Etat Felix-Antoine Tshisekedi a invité les Congolais à faire preuve de résistance et surtout de résilience face à l’aggravation sans précédent de la situation sécuritaire dans l’Est du pays.
statements_all.translation_en: During a live address to the nation on the national television channel RTNC, on Wednesday 29 January 2025, the Head of State Felix-Antoine Tshisekedi invited Congolese to show resistance and above all resilience in the face of the unprecedented worsening of the security situation in the east of the country.

statements_all.text: Reuters reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame said he agreed with the U.S. government on the need for a ceasefire in eastern Congo but gave no indication of bowing to calls for Rwandan troops and M23 rebels to withdraw from Goma.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Rwanda's President Paul Kagame said he agreed with the U.S. government on the need for a ceasefire in eastern Congo but gave no indication of bowing to calls for Rwandan troops and the M23 rebels they support to withdraw from Goma.

statements_all.role: Minister of Communication and Media, government spokesperson
statements_all.text: Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said on Monday in a statement posted on X that the government continued to work to avoid carnage and loss of life, as reported by AFP.
statements_all.excerpt_original: " Le gouvernement continue de travailler pour éviter le carnage et les pertes en vies humaines ", a assuré Patrick Muyaya dans une déclaration postée sur X.
statements_all.translation_en: "The government continues to work to avoid carnage and loss of life," Patrick Muyaya assured in a statement posted on X.

statements_all.text: BBC News Afrique reported that the Minister of Rural Development, Muhindo Nzangi, said the DRC army controlled 80% of the city of Goma on Monday evening while M23 had taken only a few areas on the outskirts.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Le ministre du développement rural, Muhindo Nzangi, a déclaré que l'armée de la RDC contrôlait 80 % de la ville de Goma lundi soir, tandis que le M23 ne s'était emparé que de quelques zones dans la périphérie de la ville.
statements_all.translation_en: The Minister of Rural Development, Muhindo Nzangi, said the DRC army controlled 80% of the city of Goma on Monday evening, while M23 had only seized a few areas on the city's outskirts.

statements_all.text: Al Jazeera reported that M23 announced the capture of Goma on Monday, which the DRC government described as a "declaration of war" by Rwanda.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Earlier on Monday, M23 announced the capture of Goma, which the DRC government described was a “declaration of war” by Rwanda.

statements_all.text: DW reported that Rwandan army spokesperson Ronald Rwivanga said that five civilians were killed and 25 were wounded on the outskirts of the border town of Gisenyi.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Rwandan army spokesperson Ronald Rwivanga said that five civilians were killed and 25 were wounded on the outskirts of the border town of Gisenyi.

statements_all.setting: report presented at a press event, as reported
statements_all.text: BBC Gahuza reported that Délion Kimbulungu, secretary of AFC/M23, presenting a report of AFC/M23, said the events at Munzenze prison happened in the morning while M23 arrived in the evening, and that their investigation found the prison escape had begun a few days before M23 arrived; the BBC said it could not independently verify the claims of M23.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Muri raporo yabo y'uyu munsi, Kimbulungu yavuze ko ibyabaye kuri gereza Munzenze byabaye mu gitondo mu gihe M23 yahageze nimugoroba. Yavuze ko mu iperereza ryabo basanze gutoroka gereza "byaratangiye iminsi micye mbere y'uko M23 ihagera"
statements_all.translation_en: In their report today, Kimbulungu said the Munzenze prison events happened in the morning while M23 arrived in the evening. He said their investigation found the prison escape 'began a few days before M23 arrived'.

statements_all.role: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (statement from Kigali)
statements_all.text: The Rwandan foreign ministry said in a statement dated 26 January 2025 that the recent heavy fighting around Goma was triggered by constant ceasefire violations by the FARDC in coalition with the FDLR, European mercenaries, Wazalendo, Burundian armed forces, SAMIDRC forces and MONUSCO troops.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The ongoing conflict in eastern DRC, particularly the recent heavy fighting around Goma, was triggered by constant violations of the ceasefire by the Congolese armed forces (FARDC) in coalition with UN-sanctioned genocidal militia FDLR, European mercenaries, ethnic militias (Wazalendo), Burundian armed forces, SAMIDRC forces as well as MONUSCO troops.

statements_all.role: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (statement from Kigali)
statements_all.text: The Rwandan foreign ministry said in a statement that the late Maj Gen Peter Cirimwami, Military Governor of North Kivu, who it said was killed during fighting around Sake, served as liaison with the FDLR, citing UN reports.
statements_all.excerpt_original: The United Nations confirmed in their reports that the late Maj Gen Peter Cirimwami, the Military Governor of North Kivu who was killed during fighting around Sake, served as liaison with the FDLR and was responsible for sabotaging planned operations by the FARDC to neutralize the leaders of the FDLR.

statements_all.text: Imvaho Nshya, a Rwandan outlet, reported that AFC/M23 announced it had closed the airspace of Goma in order to stop DRC forces from continuing to use Goma airport to drop bombs on the population.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Umutwe wa AFC/M23 watangaje ko wafunze ikirere cy’i Goma mu rwego rwo gukumira ingabo za Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo (RDC) zikomeza kwifashisha ikibuga cy’indege cya Goma mu kumisha ibisasu mu baturage.
statements_all.translation_en: The AFC/M23 group announced that it had closed the airspace of Goma in order to prevent the forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo from continuing to use Goma airport to drop bombs on the population.

statements_all.text: DW reported that, according to the M23, military governor Peter Cirimwami had been seriously wounded at Kasengezi while on his way to the front line, which DW said was difficult to verify; DW added that the Congolese government had still not communicated on the matter.
statements_all.excerpt_original: Selon le M23, celui-ci aurait été grièvement blessé à Kasengezi alors qu'il se rendait sur la ligne de front. Une information qu'il était difficile à vérifier. Le gouvernement congolais n'avait en tout cas toujours pas communiqué sur cette situation.
statements_all.translation_en: According to the M23, he had reportedly been seriously wounded at Kasengezi while on his way to the front line. This was difficult to verify. The Congolese government had in any case still not communicated on this situation.

statements_all.text: Iwacu reported that at a press conference on Thursday 16 January the FDNB spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, rejected allegations that Burundian soldiers had been captured or killed by M23 in eastern DRC, saying those captured were not Burundians, while neither confirming nor denying casualties, which he called a military secret.
statements_all.excerpt_original: « Ceux qui sont capturés par le M23 ne sont pas des Burundais.
statements_all.translation_en: 'Those captured by M23 are not Burundians.
